issues.title: macOS: approved require_escalated browser tests remain sandboxed when filesystem read denies are active

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: extension
labels.description: Issues related to the VS Code extension

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

issues.body:
### What version of the IDE extension are you using?

vscode

### What subscription do you have?

Pro

### Which IDE are you using?

VSCode

### What platform is your computer?

Mac os

### What issue are you seeing?

Summary
Codex cannot run our automated Electron browser test with the current filesystem protections retained. A command-specific allow rule and an explicit require_escalated request do not enable execution outside Seatbelt.

The implementation deliberately preserves denied-read restrictions, but the resulting execution path provides no clear explanation that escalation was not applied. This led to repeated unsuccessful configuration changes.

We need a supported way to run an approved browser test automatically while retaining filesystem protections.

Environment
- macOS, Apple Silicon
- Codex CLI: 0.157.1
- Electron: 44.4.5
- Python: 3.14.6
- Custom permission profile selected through default_permissions
- Filesystem policy includes workspace writes and explicit denied-read paths/globs
- Network access enabled
- 

### What steps can reproduce the bug?


Reproduction
1. Select a restricted filesystem profile containing explicit deny entries.
2. Add a user-layer rule:
   prefix_rule(
       pattern = [["python", "python3"], "CoreDev/planner/tests/browser_smoke.py"],
       decision = "allow",
       justification = "Run the real Electron browser smoke test.",
       match = ["python3 CoreDev/planner/tests/browser_smoke.py"],
   )
3. Restart Codex.
4. Request the command directly through exec_command with:
   {
     "cmd": "python3 CoreDev/planner/tests/browser_smoke.py",
     "sandbox_permissions": "require_escalated"
   }
5. The Python test starts a local HTTP server and launches Electron against it.

### What is the expected behavior?


Expected behavior
Codex should support an explicitly approved browser execution path that retains filesystem denies.
If that combination is unsupported, it should return a clear error before execution, explaining that denied-read restrictions prevent the requested escalation.
Actual behavior
The command runs without an approval prompt, but remains sandboxed.
Observed failures across attempts:
- Earlier Electron launches exited with -6 (SIGABRT).
- Later launches exceeded the test’s 120-second subprocess timeout.
- During timeout cleanup, Python remained waiting in waitpid until interrupted; the interrupted command exited 130.
- An empty Electron profile directory was created.
- electron-phases.log was never created, so the test’s script-loaded marker was not reached or recorded.
The repository owner reports that the same Electron binary and test passed when run outside Codex’s sandbox through another agent.
Troubleshooting already performed
- Used direct exec_command calls, rather than nested Code Mode execution.
- Explicitly requested require_escalated.
- Added command-specific user-layer allow rules and restarted.
- Removed ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE from Electron’s child environment.
- Removed uppercase and lowercase HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, ALL_PROXY, and NO_PROXY.
- Added Electron’s --no-proxy-server argument.
The browser test still failed.
Relevant implementation
In [codex-rs/core/src/tools/sandboxing.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.157.1/codex-rs/core/src/tools/sandboxing.rs#L222-L275):
- sandbox_override_for_first_attempt returns NoOverride when denied-read restrictions are present, before considering an allow rule or escalation.
- sandbox_permissions_preserving_denied_reads converts RequireEscalated to UseDefault under that condition.
This explains why requesting escalation does not remove Seatbelt. It does not establish the exact macOS operation causing Electron’s abort or hang. We do not yet have a denial trace conclusively tied to the failing launch.

### Additional information


Requested resolution
1. Clearly report the effective execution permissions when an escalation request cannot be honored.
2. Provide actionable diagnostics instead of allowing a browser launch to abort or hang without an explanation.
3. Support narrowly scoped browser/GUI permissions while retaining filesystem read denies.
4. Clarify the denied-read exception in the documentation for prefix_rule(decision="allow") and require_escalated.
Disabling the sandbox or requiring the owner to run every browser check manually does not meet the automated workflow’s requirements.

issues.body:
### Summary

After Codex Desktop for Windows auto-updated, the previous global/legacy WSL agent environment was replaced by the new project-connected WSL flow. Existing chats remain attached to the deprecated WSL project and cannot be continued or moved to the newly added WSL project, even when it points to the exact same repository.

The Settings UI shows a warning equivalent to:

> The legacy WSL agent environment has been deprecated. Visit a project connected with WSL, or add a new project.

After restart, the agent environment returns to Windows Native. Adding the same repository again through `\\wsl$\<distro>\path\to\repo` creates a new project identity, while the old chats continue reporting that the original project cannot be found.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have existing Codex Desktop chats associated with a repository using the former WSL agent environment.
2. Allow Codex Desktop for Windows to auto-update to the version that deprecates the legacy WSL agent environment.
3. Open an old chat: it reports that the original project cannot be found.
4. Add the same repository again using the WSL filesystem picker.
5. Try to continue or migrate the old chat into the newly added WSL project.
6. Try `/resume` with scope `All` and `/fork`.

### Actual behavior

- The newly added WSL project works as a separate project.
- Existing chats remain bound to the deprecated project identity.
- The old chats cannot be rebound, resumed into, forked into, or transferred to the new WSL project.
- Restarting the app does not repair the association.

### Expected behavior

When the same WSL distribution and repository path are added after migration, Codex Desktop should either:

1. automatically reconnect existing chats to the new WSL project identity; or
2. provide a user-facing “Rebind/migrate chats to project” action, ideally supporting bulk migration.

The original threads and their history should remain intact.

### Environment

- Product: Codex Desktop / ChatGPT desktop app, Codex view
- OS: Windows
- Agent environment before update: legacy WSL
- Agent environment after update: Windows Native plus project-connected WSL
- WSL repository remains present and can be added successfully
- App version: current auto-updated Windows build (exact build not yet available)

### Data-safety concern

Users should not need to delete app data, reset the application, or manually edit local session databases to recover chat-to-project associations.

issues.body:
## Problem

The bundled Browser connection is unavailable to the primary agent in a Windows Work Mode task, blocking local checkout testing before any page can be opened.

## Environment

- Windows host, PowerShell execution environment.
- Browser plugin package: `26.1007.71326`.
- Exact desktop app and Windows versions were not verified.
- Primary agent; no subagents were used in this reproduction.
- Observed 14 October 2026.

## Reproduction

1. Explicitly select `Browser` (`browser@openai-bundled`) and ask: "Test my checkout flow on localhost".
2. Read the installed Browser skill and initialize its bundled `scripts/browser-client.mjs` with `setupBrowserRuntime()`.
3. Call `agent.browsers.get("iab")`.
4. Follow the documented bootstrap troubleshooting guidance and list available browsers once.

## Actual result

`agent.browsers.get("iab")` returns:

```text
Browser is not available: iab
```

`agent.browsers.list()` contains only:

```json
[{"name":"Codex MCP Apps","type":"mcpapps"}]
```

No in-app browser backend is exposed. The failure happens before navigation or checkout interaction, so no localhost or checkout application failure has been established.

The user reports restarting and uninstalling/reinstalling the Browser plugin through the plugin UI during preceding troubleshooting. The current primary-agent reproduction still fails.

## Expected result

The explicitly selected bundled Browser should be available to the authorized primary task, or the app should report an actionable connection/setup error.

## Feature request

Codex currently supports signing out and signing back in, but it does not appear to support quick switching between multiple accounts or workspaces.

## Requested behavior

- Show the current signed-in account and workspace clearly in Codex app, CLI, and IDE extension.
- Add a switch account/workspace action.
- Keep separate cached sessions per account/workspace where possible.
- Avoid requiring users to repeatedly log out and log back in.

## Use case

Developers often need to switch between personal and company accounts, or between different ChatGPT workspaces/API organizations. Re-authenticating each time is inconvenient and can lead to confusion because permissions, billing, and managed workspace policies may differ by account or workspace.

## Current workaround

Run `codex logout` and then `codex login` again with the other account.

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Installed [ChatGPT.app](<http://ChatGPT.app>) metadata: 26.1021.31345, build 21828, bundle identifier com.openai.codex. Read from the installed Info.plist; the About dialog could not be inspected.

### What subscription do you have?

Not collected for this report.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 15.7.9; local desktop task using Chrome through cua_repl.

### What issue are you seeing?

An existing chat that successfully controlled Chrome earlier now returns:

```text
Local browser use is disabled in Work settings
```

The user reports that browser access is still enabled in settings, this recurs frequently after restarting the desktop app, and other chats appear able to use the browser at the same time. The settings state, restart timing and other-chat comparison are user-reported; the successful earlier browser operations and later disabled error in this chat were observed directly.

The failing operation was an accessibility-state read of an already-bound Chrome tab. The error happened before page content could be read or any action submitted. The restriction was respected.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

User-reported recurring sequence:

1. Enable browser access and use Chrome successfully from a local desktop chat.
2. Restart the desktop app while retaining the existing chat.
3. Continue browser work in that chat.
4. The tool reports that local browser use is disabled.
5. Check the setting: the user reports it is enabled; other chats may still have browser access.

The exact trigger and deterministic reproduction conditions are not yet established. No restart, settings modification, extension reinstall or account switch was performed by the agent to reproduce this report.

### What is the expected behavior?

Existing chats should re-evaluate the current browser permission and reconnect after a restart when access is allowed. If a different account/workspace/session policy blocks access, the error should identify that cause rather than contradict the enabled setting. A supported recovery path should preserve the existing chat and its work.

### Additional information

Related reports: #56645 and #54989 describe the same disabled-setting symptom on Windows. #56609 describes a macOS occurrence after an account switch. This report adds the current macOS app build, a restart trigger reported by the user, and the reported discrepancy between chats.

The in-app feedback route could not be automated: cua.getApp('Codex') returned `Computer Use is not allowed to use the app 'com.openai.codex' for safety reasons.` That restriction was also respected; no alternative UI control or permission bypass was attempted.

Observed October 26, 2026 (America/Los_Angeles). Submitted on the user's request. No private application URLs, project files, account identifiers, session IDs, transcripts, credentials or raw logs are attached.

### Current investigation (October 28)

The same disabled-setting error is observed in a restored chat on Nightly 26.1028.10413 (22641), while the user reports Local browser use is On. Logs show the chat resume completed before Browser runtime configuration was selected. The native authorization tracker does not register a previously unbound chat if the resume has no node_repl account override. A scoped candidate now captures the authenticated native account when that request is sent, while retaining existing session ownership and checking the current setting on use.

Draft D2656730 is published at `6bfbe81a4635414460bdc2cdbcf0aed01ff65c30`: [https://flow.apps.openai.org/deltas/openai/openai/2656730](<https://flow.apps.openai.org/deltas/openai/openai/2656730>). Both new registration regressions fail on the baseline; all 34 focused Browser tests pass on the candidate. Changed-file validation, Electron TypeScript, and the file-size check pass. Current-head CI is pending.

This remains a source-level repair, not a confirmed end-to-end fix for the reported Nightly session. Native verification requires a build containing the patch and a connected secondary display. The installed Nightly still rejects Browser access. Verify restored-chat access, Off enforcement, and retained-account isolation before acceptance.

[Owning task](<codex://threads/01a17ee0-b451-70a0-989e-ff82be5be0b8>).

### Merge result (November 6)

[D2656730](<https://flow.apps.openai.org/deltas/openai/openai/2656730>) merged to master as `a9e3e45bf5cf3a5bede2dac56851a0e8983e0003`. The final repair uses the request-authenticated principal when the account cache is cold and retains existing chat ownership. All 96 focused Browser tests passed (one opt-in integration test skipped); Electron TypeScript, changed-file lint/formatting, [Monorepo CI](<https://buildkite.com/openai-mono/monorepo/builds/9726535>), and [merge validation](<https://buildkite.com/openai-mono/monorepo-merge-validation/builds/1682424>) passed. Current-revision code and security reviews completed with no findings.

Acceptance remains pending: test the originally affected restored chat in a build containing the merged fix, and verify retained-account isolation after an account switch. The merge does not establish recovery of the reported Nightly session, so this issue remains In Review.

[Owning task](<codex://threads/01a17ee0-b451-70a0-989e-ff82be5be0b8>).

issues.body:
## Bug report

Codex repeatedly blocks entirely benign follow-up messages under cybersecurity filtering, rendering an existing development session unusable. This continued after switching to GPT-6 Sol (High) and enabling Daybreak.

## Context

- Tool: Codex CLI
- Project: Detent, a systems project for dynamic configuration distribution.
- Session title visible in screenshot: "Complete Xapiand C1 to C9"
- Prior successful output: `Completed /root/sortable_trusted`
- Model selected later: `gpt-6-sol high`
- Daybreak status: `Daybreak on. Applies to new turns.`
- Codex version, OS, and session ID: not yet collected

## Reproduction / observed behavior

In the existing coding session, I sent the following harmless prompts:
- `Are we idle again?` (twice)
- `continue`
- After changing model and enabling Daybreak: `continue`
- `Are we doing something?`
- `HEY!`

Each received `This content can't be shown`, initially with the message `We take extra care with some cybersecurity requests`. After Daybreak was enabled, the error changed to `Some cybersecurity requests are still limited, even when Daybreak is on.`

These are routine conversational prompts and do not request cybersecurity instructions. The screenshot also shows the agent had just completed a legitimate development task.

## Expected behavior

Codex should respond to benign prompts, especially basic progress inquiries. If particular source material or a specific operation is restricted, that should not prevent all unrelated follow-ups in the same session.

## Actual behavior

Repeated filtering of harmless inputs made the session unusable. Changing the model and enabling Daybreak did not recover it.

## Questions / impact

- Is filtering incorrectly inheriting restrictions from accumulated conversation, tool outputs, or repository context?
- Is there a way to recover an affected session without discarding long-running development context?
- Are filtered requests counted against usage limits?
- Could the error provide actionable diagnostics or an incident identifier?

This appears to be a false-positive filtering or session-state reliability issue, rather than an offensive security request.

A screenshot documenting the sequence is available and can be provided to maintainers.

issues.title: Opt-in display of a blocking hook message without the generic banner

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: TUI
labels.description: Issues related to the terminal user interface: text input, menus and dialogs, and terminal display

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: hooks
labels.description: Issues related to event hooks

issues.body:
### What would you like to see?

Provide one opt-in display mode for native interactive CLI hooks that already stop or refuse an action. Apply the existing decision first, then display the hook's supplied message once in the conversation, without the generic hook rejection banner.

E2 Intent uses a native prompt hook to handle numbered answers and workflow commands locally. For example, saving a numbered reply should display "Answer saved." with no model request. The same hook also enforces genuine holds. If E2 cannot verify the current project context, it should display "E2 could not verify the current project context. Reconnect before continuing." and keep the prompt blocked.

### Current behavior

On Windows with Codex CLI 0.167.1, a native UserPromptSubmit hook returning decision: block shows the supplied reason under "Blocked by hook". We observed a local skip saving once with zero provider requests, even though its acknowledgment appeared as a rejection. The [hook reference](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks#common-output-fields) describes suppressOutput as parsed but unimplemented. The requested behavior keeps the supplied message visible. Related initial-prompt retry issue: #54993.

### Expected behavior

The initial case is a UserPromptSubmit hook that returns JSON like this:

```json
{"decision":"block","reason":"Answer saved."}
```

With the proposed opt-in, render the reason once. Using the same opt-in with the context-verification failure reason should render that reason once and keep the prompt blocked. In both cases the prompt must stay out of model input, including on later turns. The UI should return control without retrying the blocked input. Ordinary accepted prompts should continue to work.

The opt-in should affect only the presentation of that hook result. Existing decisions, precedence, diagnostics, and behavior for other hooks should still apply. Without the opt-in, keep the current presentation. The same display option should apply to enforced workflow holds wherever the interactive CLI shows a stop result with a user-facing reason.

This is a request for the stock native CLI. An integration can use its existing hook and leave the choice of field name and schema to the maintainers.

issues.body:
### 使用版本

- Windows 桌面应用内部版本：`26.1013.31256`（来自已安装应用及启动记录）。
- Windows 安装包版本：`26.1013.3656.0`。
- 随应用运行的后端：`codex-cli 0.163.0-alpha.10.2`。
- 手机：iPhone，使用 ChatGPT 的 Codex Remote；具体 iOS 和手机应用版本尚未采集。
- 订阅类型：本轮未采集。

### 平台与网络环境

- Windows 11 x64，系统报告 `Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0`。
- 桌面和手机通过代理/VPN 访问服务。桌面后端显式配置 `HTTP_PROXY`、`HTTPS_PROXY`，指向本机 HTTP 代理。
- 显式代理使桌面能够上线；保留该配置时，手机能连接主机并打开一个对照会话，但另外两个含生成图片的会话仍无法完整加载。
- 本报告聚焦上线之后的历史加载失败。代理对大数据传输的影响尚未排除。

### 实际现象

2026-10-16（UTC+08:00）在两个已有会话中重复观察到：

1. Windows 桌面可以正常打开会话，看到已完成的最新回复。
2. iPhone Remote 能看到主机和会话，但打开这两个会话会超时。
3. 强制关闭并重开手机应用后，其中一个会话可以显示少量旧的执行进度，同时仍报超时；无法充分向上浏览历史，桌面已完成的最新回复也没有同步到手机。
4. 同时，一个可读取的对照会话仍能在这台手机上打开。
5. 用户还观察到：尝试打开较大会话后可能出现主机离线，约 5—10 分钟后重新上线。该时长是用户观察，尚未逐次与主机日志精确对齐，不作为固定协议超时或已确认因果。

手机完整报错原文尚未采集，本报告中的“超时”是用户对现象的描述。

### 复现步骤

1. 在 Windows 桌面准备一个包含多次图片生成和工具调用历史的已有会话。
2. 确认桌面本地可以读取该会话，且已有已完成的最新回复。
3. 用已配对的 iPhone Remote 连接这台主机，打开该会话。
4. 观察手机历史加载超时、只显示旧片段或缺少最新回复；再打开一个对照会话比较。

以上步骤在现有两份会话中复现。尚无可以公开的最小合成会话，也未建立确定的大小阈值。

### 预期行为

手机应能够及时显示最新文字和完成状态，继续使用原会话；较早的消息及图片按需加载。单个大历史页不应使其他会话或整条远程连接长时间不可用。希望获得应用层面的修复，而不是依靠持续新建会话、迁移摘要或清理历史来使用 Remote。

### 主机日志确认的阶段

在 2026-10-16 23:08—23:13（UTC+08:00）的三个连接样本中，主机依次收到：

```text
initialize → thread/resume → thread/turns/list → thread/items/list
```

每个样本包含 3 条 `thread/turns/list` 和 15—16 条 `thread/items/list` 请求。手机重连时会同时恢复两个受影响会话和对照会话，所以不能把这些请求当作严格单会话试验。

这些日志证明已经进入历史分页阶段；没有记录每个分页请求的完整参数、实际响应发送完成或手机接收情况，因此无法把每条请求精确映射到下表中的某一页。本窗口未捕获 `fs/readFile` 或 Remote pong timeout；这不代表整个故障期间都不存在此类事件。

### 同版本后端的隔离副本测量

为避免把磁盘历史文件大小误当作传输量，使用相同的已安装后端，在独立临时 `CODEX_HOME` 中复制受测会话的历史和分页显示投影，以 `codex_chatgpt_ios_remote` 客户端身份调用接口：

1. `thread/turns/list`，`itemsView: "summary"`，获取回合。
2. 对各回合调用 `thread/items/list`，省略 `limit`，使用默认每页 25 项。
3. 跟随 `nextCursor` 读到末页，仅统计 JSON RPC 响应字节数、耗时和项目类型。

| 隔离副本 | 页数 | 全部分页响应合计（字节） | 最大单页（字节） | 最大页本机 RPC 耗时 | imageGeneration 项合计（字节） |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 受影响会话 A | 19 | 15,344,422 | 10,039,273 | 0.069 秒 | 14,497,682（6 项） |
| 受影响会话 B | 22 | 7,687,304 | 4,467,941 | 0.034 秒 | 6,492,954（3 项） |
| 手机可打开的对照会话 | 33 | 1,295,915 | 150,630 | 0.003 秒 | 0 |

所有分页都成功读到末页，没有 API 错误。这些是本地未压缩 JSON RPC 响应的字节数，**不是手机实际接收量、网络抓包量或手机内存用量**。对照会话持续有新活动，测量反映当时快照。

只在响应的内存副本中模拟过滤 `imageGeneration` 项后，会话 A 的分页总量约降至 0.85 MB，会话 B 约降至 1.19 MB。这个模拟证明这些项贡献了大部分数据量；它未应用到正式会话，也不是手机端修复成功的证据。

### 对应源码线索

对照 `rust-v0.163.0-alpha.10.2`：

- [`thread_resume_redaction.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0-alpha.10.2/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_resume_redaction.rs)：对 iOS/Android Remote 的 `thread/resume` 省略 `imageGeneration`，并精简 MCP 数据。
- [`thread_items_list_response_inner`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0-alpha.10.2/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs#L3550)：`thread/items/list` 读取并转换完整存储项，没有调用上述手机响应精简逻辑。
- [分页数量常量](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0-alpha.10.2/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs#L5888)：默认 25 项、最多 100 项；该路径按项目数量分页，没有对应的响应字节预算。

因此，首次恢复时省略的大图片生成记录，会在后续分页读取中重新出现。上述隔离测量已复现这种数据量差异。

### 待调查方向与结论边界

当前最强假设是：后续大分页在远程传输或手机处理阶段触发超时。尚不能断言网络速度、代理、手机解码/渲染或服务端排队中的哪一项是最终瓶颈，也不能断言这些大页已经被手机完整接收。

希望维护者检查：

1. 手机 `thread/resume` 与 `thread/items/list` 是否应采用一致的轻量响应策略，并保持分页游标与项目语义正确。
2. 图片数据能否按需读取，以及是否需要按字节而非仅按项目数限制分页。
3. 单会话大响应、重试与共享 Remote 通道的心跳/恢复是否互相影响。
4. 是否能提供受支持的诊断方式，按请求记录响应大小、发送完成、手机接收/解码结果及超时所在阶段，以完成因果验证。

### 相关报告

相关但未证明同根因：#50934（大历史影响 Remote）、#47148（图片较多的会话在手机加载失败）、#40249（图片生成结果经历史读取接口返回大块数据）。本报告补充 Windows→iPhone 的历史分页阶段证据，以及 `thread/resume` 与 `thread/items/list` 响应精简不一致的同版本测量。

### 隐私与操作范围

本报告经用户授权提交。公开内容仅包含匿名测量、版本、必要的网络背景和公共源码链接；原始聊天、图片、数据库、账号、设备/会话标识和私人文件路径均保留在本机。诊断使用独立副本，正式历史保持完整。

issues.title: Windows desktop: codex_apps MCP discovery fails with "error decoding response body", removing Sites tools

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: mcp

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

issues.body:
## Summary

Sites works for my account on the web, but its tools become unavailable in Codex desktop on Windows. Selecting the installed plugin and starting new chats does not resolve this. Local logs show that the built-in `codex_apps` MCP client fails during discovery; the tool catalog then omits that server because it has no ready client. This blocks publishing through Sites.

## Environment

- Codex desktop: `26.1007.21434`, build `13901`, production channel.
- Desktop update check: `up_to_date`.
- Local engine: `codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2`.
- Dependency runtime: `26.1009.11318`.
- Sites plugin: `1.0.1`, installed and enabled.
- Windows 11, native Windows agent (not WSL).
- Observed on October 10–11, 2026.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open Codex desktop on Windows and start a local chat, including a chat without a repository.
2. Select the Sites plugin.
3. Ask to use the Sites publishing/management tools.
4. The tools are unavailable. Inspect the desktop logs: `codex_apps` startup repeatedly fails during discovery.

## Expected behavior

The built-in `codex_apps` MCP connection initializes successfully and exposes the installed Sites tools, as it does on the web.

## Actual behavior and log excerpts

```text
MCP client for `codex_apps` failed to start:
MCP startup failed: handshaking with MCP server failed:
Client error: HTTP request failed: error decoding response body,
when send discover request

Apps MCP startup reconnect failed; continuing with cached tools

omitting MCP server without an exact ready client server_name=codex_apps
```

The failure persists through retries. Other local servers (`codex_app`, `cua_repl`, `node_repl`, `code-review`) reach `ready`.

## Checks already performed

- Restarting and selecting the plugin again did not resolve the problem.
- Reproduces in new chats and in a local chat without a project; not limited to a particular Site.
- Sites manifests are readable, valid JSON and include their connector reference; the plugin is enabled in `config.toml`.
- No WinHTTP proxy or proxy environment variables were found in the diagnostic environment.
- `codex doctor` reports a consistent installation, configured authentication, healthy databases, reachable HTTP endpoints and a successful WebSocket handshake (`101`).
- A separate `app-server` diagnostic process, without model inference, reproduces the MCP response-decoding failure, while `app/list` returns successfully.
- A temporary process-level test enabling `codex_apps_mcp_2026_07_28` and `mcp_2026_07_28` did not fix the error. These flags were not persisted.
- No configuration, authentication, plugin or chat data was changed during diagnosis.

## Investigation requested

Please investigate the response to `codex_apps` discovery and its handling by the Windows MCP client in this engine version, and provide a corrected release or a verified recovery procedure. We do not have the failing response body, HTTP status or headers, so the root cause is not established and this report does not claim a particular encoding or server-side error.

The OpenAI Help Center assistant directed me to file this issue. A feedback-generated remote session ID is not currently available; local chat IDs and private Site identifiers have intentionally been omitted.

issues.title: Windows desktop 26.1111: temporary-index Git staging workers survive launcher exit and accumulate multi-GiB memory

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
### App version
Reproduced after updating to Windows package **OpenAI.Codex 26.1111.2228.0** on 2026-11-15. Previously observed on **26.1106.6628.0**. Package versions were verified from the installed package/running executable, not the About dialog.

### Platform
Windows 11 Enterprise x64, version 10.0.26200 (build 26200).
Git for Windows: **2.53.0.windows.1**.

### Summary
During ordinary desktop use in a large local repository, automatic temporary-index Git staging workers overlap and some continue running and growing after their Git launcher parent has exited. The issue persisted after the app update.

The large repository is a plausible workload trigger; this report does not establish a Git memory leak or the precise cancellation/retry bug. The concern is expensive background snapshot work accumulating without effective descendant cleanup or resource bounds.

### Observed command and attribution
```text
git.exe -c safe.bareRepository=explicit -c core.hooksPath=NUL -c core.fsmonitor= add --sparse --pathspec-from-file=- --pathspec-file-nul
```

Observed process chain:
```text
ChatGPT.exe (Codex Node utility service)
  -> Git/cmd/git.exe
     -> Git/mingw64/bin/git.exe
```

The real worker's current directory was verified as the affected project, not CODEX_HOME. Its environment contained:
```text
GIT_INDEX_FILE=<user-local-temp>/codex-index-<uuid>/index
```

Read-only inspection of the installed app bundle located this command in the temporary working-tree/turn-diff snapshot path. These were app-generated jobs, not assistant-issued broad staging commands. The temporary index means this is not evidence that the user's normal staging index was changed.

### Measurements
Earlier incident:
- Several concurrent workers each reached multi-GiB working sets; individual observations included approximately 9.26, 13.24 and 15.54 GiB.
- A containment snapshot summed approximately 42.3 GiB RSS across stopped matching processes. **RSS sums can double-count shared/mapped pages; this is not a measurement of unique physical RAM or private commit.**

Post-update observation on 2026-11-15:
- The staging worker was traced to a Node service from the updated 26.1111.2228.0 package.
- Its Git launcher parent subsequently no longer existed.
- During a bounded observation, that same surviving worker grew from **1,664,442,368 bytes RSS to 2,158,456,832 bytes RSS in 20.6 seconds** (approximately 1.55 to 2.01 GiB).
- The test was stopped at the predefined 2 GiB per-worker safety threshold, after approximately 20.9 seconds; it was not allowed to exhaust the machine.
- The worker was terminated as targeted containment only after these measurements. Why its launcher had exited has not been established.

### Repository scale and attempted mitigation
Metadata census: approximately **989,000 file paths**, **284,000 directories**, **348 GiB logical file size** across the entire project tree, including .git, ignored dependencies/build artifacts and generated media. These are NOT counts of tracked or snapshot-eligible files.

Added narrowly scoped .gitignore exclusions for approximately 192,000 untracked browser-profile files (about 19 GiB), after checking that matching files were not tracked. Recurrence continued. No project assets or Git history were deleted.

### Observed reproduction conditions
No standalone minimal reproducer yet:
1. Open/use the Windows desktop app with this large local repository.
2. During ordinary chat/repository activity, observe the automatic temporary-index staging command above.
3. Observe overlapping Git work and real Git children continuing after their launcher parents disappear.
4. Update the app and repeat ordinary use: the same behavior was observed on the new package.

The diagnostic test did not issue a synthetic bulk git add. The exact UI event and internal retry/cancellation sequence remain unidentified.

### Expected behavior
- Bound/coalesce expensive snapshot operations per repository, including across chats.
- Cancel/reap the complete Windows Git launcher/worker tree.
- Avoid starting replacements while prior snapshot workers remain active.
- Skip or limit oversized automatic snapshots and provide a supported, durable off switch without disabling normal user-requested Git.

### Temporary containment and test caveat
A local watchdog now stops only the exact snapshot staging command, matching the project cwd and codex-index temporary-index marker, once age or RSS thresholds are exceeded. This can interrupt diff capture and is containment, not a fix or general recommendation. The guard was not active during the reported post-update growth test; it was restored afterward.

### Related reports
- #58583: active Windows Git descendants surviving launcher exit, but on branch-diff-stats rather than this staging command.
- #54955: the same temporary-index staging command and turn-diff resource exhaustion on macOS, primarily disk-related.
- #54497: Windows Git fan-out/resource exhaustion at much larger process counts.

These are related symptoms, not proof of an identical root cause. This report adds current Windows package reproduction with measured orphaned temporary-index staging growth.

### Privacy and evidence
Prepared with the affected user's authorization from locally retained process samples and metadata receipts. No private project names, usernames, source content, repository URLs, full environment variables, session transcripts, or raw logs are attached. Subscription details were not collected.

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
## Summary
Please provide an agent-accessible DevTools console or page-world execution surface for the Codex app in-app browser, so agents can inspect and interact with exposed app runtime objects during local UI debugging.

## Environment
- Codex desktop app on Windows
- In-app browser target: local dev server at `http://localhost:8787/`
- Browser Use / in-app browser plugin was connected and could inspect DOM, click buttons, and read captured console logs.

## What works today
- DOM snapshots work.
- Read-only page evaluation works for DOM reads.
- Console log reading works via the browser dev log API.
- Normal button clicks work.

## Limitation
The current evaluation surface appears isolated/read-only and is not equivalent to DevTools console/page-world execution:
- A local app exposed `window.game`, `globalThis.game`, `window.Game`, and `globalThis.Game` during page bootstrap.
- The automation-visible DOM marker from the same bootstrap ran successfully.
- However, agent-side read-only evaluation still saw `window.game`/`globalThis.game` as unavailable.
- The evaluator also could not access some page APIs such as `localStorage` in the tested environment.
- `javascript:` navigation was blocked by browser policy, so there was no supported way to execute in the real page context.

## Expected
Codex should offer a documented, safe DevTools/page-world capability for local development targets, such as:
- evaluate JavaScript in the actual page context with user-approved safety boundaries,
- inspect page globals exposed by the app for debugging,
- interact with local app runtime objects intentionally exposed for testing,
- read/write local storage/session storage when appropriate for local debugging.

## Why this matters
For local app development, agents often need to validate state transitions that are not fully visible in the DOM, inspect framework/runtime objects, seed state, or trigger app-level test helpers. Passive DOM reads and console-log capture help, but they are not enough to replace a developer console during debugging.

issues.title: iOS remote thread/list sends sourceKinds: [] and gets empty list despite Mac host having threads

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: iOS
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex iOS app

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

issues.body:
### What happened?

Codex iOS remote control can start a task on the connected Mac host, and the task is created and visible in the Mac Codex app. However, after returning to the Codex task list on iOS, the list immediately shows the empty state and no tasks/threads are visible.

This does not appear to be a Mac connectivity or task creation problem. The Mac app-server receives the iOS `thread/start` request and creates a local thread successfully. The problem appears when iOS refreshes the list: it sends `thread/list` with `sourceKinds: []`, and the Mac app-server responds with an empty list.

### Environment

- Mac Codex App: `26.527.31326` (`CFBundleVersion` `3390`)
- Codex CLI: `0.135.0-alpha.1`
- macOS: `26.5` (`25F71`)
- iOS remote client seen in Mac logs: `codex_chatgpt_ios_remote` `1.2026.139`
- Auth/model path: ChatGPT auth with OpenAI/Codex default model, not a custom provider

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open Codex in ChatGPT iOS.
2. Select a connected Mac host. The host shows as online.
3. Start a short task from iOS, for example `你好`.
4. Observe that the task is created and completed in the Mac Codex app.
5. Return to the Codex task list on iOS.

### Expected behavior

The iOS Codex task list should show the created task/thread, or at least should be able to list the host's available threads after refresh.

### Actual behavior

The task may briefly appear while navigating, but after returning to the list the iOS screen shows the empty state. The Mac app still has the thread.

### Evidence from Mac logs

The iOS client successfully starts a thread:

```text
app_server.request ... otel.name="thread/start" ... app_server.client_name="codex_chatgpt_ios_remote" app_server.client_version="1.2026.139"
```

The Mac state DB then contains the new local thread:

```text
019e826f-35ee-7c10-8c5d-f75aa6a3acb8 | 你好 | source=vscode | cwd=<redacted> | archived=0
```

When the iOS list refreshes, the client sends:

```json
{
  "method": "thread/list",
  "params": {
    "sortDirection": "desc",
    "sourceKinds": [],
    "sortKey": "updated_at",
    "limit": 25
  }
}
```

The Mac app-server responds:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "data": [],
    "nextCursor": null,
    "backwardsCursor": null
  }
}
```

This looks like either:

- the iOS client expects `sourceKinds: []` to mean "all sources", but the Mac app-server treats it as "no sources"; or
- the iOS client should omit `sourceKinds` when no source filter is intended.

### Related issues

- #24780 looks similar but includes a custom provider variable. This report reproduces on the default ChatGPT/OpenAI path.
- #22762 and #23062 also look related to mobile remote thread visibility, but this report includes a specific `thread/list` request/response showing the empty result.

issues.title: iOS Remote 1.2026.307: project/task list empty after app relaunch (cold-start initialize appears to omit experimentalApi)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: iOS
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex iOS app

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

issues.body:
### Summary

On iPhone ChatGPT `1.2026.307`, Codex Remote can connect to a macOS host and run tasks, and a task opened from its push notification (thread-id deep link) works. But the **project list and the task/thread list are empty** after the app is relaunched. Signing out and back in on the phone restores the list; force-quitting the app and reopening breaks it again.

This looks like the iOS cold-start `initialize` no longer declaring `capabilities.experimentalApi`, so every project-scoped call is rejected by the host.

### Environment

- iPhone, iOS `27.3`
- ChatGPT iOS `1.2026.307` (App Store JP/SG, released 2026-11-10; US store is still `1.2026.300`)
- macOS `27.3` (`26C5035r`)
- ChatGPT desktop `26.1106.51428` (build `26605`), bundled `codex-cli 0.167.0-alpha.4.1`
- Remote control pairing is healthy: `remoteControl/client/list` returns the phone (`platform=ios`, `appVersion=1.2026.307`, recent `lastSeenAt`)
- Host state: 900+ threads / 33 projects in `state_5.sqlite`; custom provider (`model_provider = "magpie"` via a local OpenAI-compatible proxy)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Pair the iPhone with the macOS host and open Codex → Remote → the Mac.
2. On the phone, sign out and sign back in.
3. Open the host: projects and tasks are listed normally.
4. Force-quit ChatGPT (swipe up) and reopen it.
5. Open the same host: the project list is empty and the task list shows nothing.

### Actual behavior

- Project list: empty.
- Task list: empty ("no tasks").
- Archived tasks: still render.
- Push notification for a task: still opens and resumes that thread correctly.
- Creating a new task from the phone still works.

### Host-side evidence

Using a second stdio `codex app-server` against the same state DB, initialized as client `codex_chatgpt_ios_remote`:

| initialize capabilities | request | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| none | `project/list` | error: `project/list requires experimentalApi capability` |
| none | `thread/list` with `projectId` (a value **or** `null`) | error: `thread/list.projectId requires experimentalApi capability` |
| none | `thread/list` flat (`archived:false, limit:200, sortKey:"updated_at", sourceKinds:[]`) | 100 rows |
| none | `thread/list` with `archived:true` | 100 rows |
| `experimentalApi: true` | `project/list` | 33 projects |
| `experimentalApi: true` | `thread/list` | 100 rows |

The flat list returns data under the same custom provider, so this is not a provider-bucket problem — only the experimental-gated calls fail.

### Analysis

- The app-server gates `project/*` and `thread/list.projectId` per connection, based on the client's own `initialize` params (`codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/initialize_processor.rs`, checked in `message_processor.rs`).
- `client_tracker.rs` closes the old connection and opens a new one on every `initialize`, so capabilities are not carried over from a previous connection.
- The observed behavior is consistent with: the post-login connection sends `capabilities.experimentalApi`, while the cold-start connection (restoring a stored session) does not. The host has no setting to grant the capability to a connection that did not declare it.

### Workaround

- Do not force-quit the app; when the list goes empty, sign out and back in.
- Or install `1.2026.300` (US store), which does not show this regression.

### Request

- Persist/send `capabilities.experimentalApi` on cold-start reconnects after a stored session is restored, or
- make the mobile UI fall back to the flat `thread/list` when `project/list` is unavailable, instead of rendering an empty list.

I could not capture the phone's raw `initialize` payload (remote-control traffic is not logged on the host), so the capability difference is inferred from the reproducible behavior plus the host-side differential above.

issues.title: [macOS app] Inline code after Chinese punctuation renders as literal backticks in chat, but works in Markdown preview

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?

- Installed desktop app version: `26.1029.61003`, build `24614`.
- Read from the installed application's bundle metadata; not an About-dialog screenshot.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS `15.7.4` (build `24G517`), Apple Silicon / `arm64`. Affected surface: the Codex chat window in the desktop app.

### What issue are you seeing?

In completed assistant messages, an otherwise valid inline-code span is displayed literally, including its backticks, when the opening backtick immediately follows Chinese punctuation. Confirmed examples use the Chinese full stop `。` (U+3002), enumeration comma `、` (U+3001), and colon `：` (U+FF1A).

Adding one ordinary ASCII space (U+0020) between that punctuation and the opening backtick makes the same example render correctly. Chinese punctuation immediately after the closing backtick renders correctly, with or without an intervening space.

The user supplied screenshots of both the chat and a Markdown file preview. The equivalent unspaced examples render correctly in the file preview, including inside tables. This is a difference between display paths, not evidence that Chinese Markdown requires extra spaces.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Open a Codex chat in the macOS desktop app.
2. Ask the assistant to output the following lines as rendered Markdown, outside a fenced code block, preserving the spaces exactly.
3. Wait for the response to complete and inspect which spans still display literal backticks.
4. Save the same lines in a `.md` file and open its Markdown preview for comparison.

```markdown
- A1: 前一句。`Future` 表示任务状态。
- A2: 前一句。 `Future` 表示任务状态。
- B1: `Future`、`ModuleResult`
- B2: `Future` 、 `ModuleResult`
- C1: 返回类型：`Future`
- C2: 返回类型： `Future`
- D1: 返回类型为 `Future`。
- D2: `Future`：任务状态对象
```

Observed in the user's completed chat response:

| Case | Chat result |
| --- | --- |
| A1 | Fails: literal backticks around Future |
| A2 | Correct inline code |
| B1 | First span is correct; second span after the enumeration comma displays literal backticks |
| B2 | Both spans are correct |
| C1 | Fails: literal backticks around Future |
| C2 | Correct inline code |
| D1, D2 | Correct inline code; punctuation follows the closing backtick |

The file-preview comparison used a larger fixture with 14 numbered list cases and 7 table comparisons. The screenshots show that both spaced and unspaced variants render correctly there. The original defect was also observed in a chat table, where an identifier following the Chinese enumeration comma retained its backticks.

### What is the expected behavior?

Recognize the paired ASCII backticks as inline-code delimiters in all of the examples, without requiring an extra space after Chinese punctuation. Chat and Markdown file preview should agree on these code-span boundaries.

### Additional information

- The behavior remains visible in completed responses; this report is not limited to the moment before a closing backtick arrives during streaming.
- Workaround verified by the user's screenshots: insert an ASCII space before the opening backtick when it follows one of the tested Chinese punctuation marks. Extra spacing after the closing backtick is unnecessary in the tested cases.
- Separate parser check: Python-Markdown `3.10.3` correctly parsed 39 cases covering 13 Chinese punctuation characters before/after code spans or between two spans. This is a parser-level control, not a reproduction of the desktop frontend.
- Root cause is unconfirmed. Please compare chat-specific preprocessing/tokenization/rendering with the Markdown file-preview path. No claim is made about a particular regex or library.
- Related but different: #37531 and #57332 concern bold emphasis at CJK punctuation boundaries. This report concerns backtick code spans, whose CommonMark rules do not impose the same emphasis delimiter-flanking requirements: https://spec.commonmark.org/0.31.2/#code-spans
- Screenshots were supplied by the user and inspected for this report; they are not attached to this API submission. The complete minimal source and observed results are included above.

type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
This EPIC tracks a series of investigations as to whether there is value in AST aware file read, search, or codebase mapping.

AST aware tools can be used to 1) more precisely read method bounds with a single tool call, reducing turns from misaligned reads, and reducing noise in tokens, 2) navigate to usages and definitions of syntax elements via syntax aware search (AST grep), and 3) compress high level context about the codebase, such as the location of specific classes and their members by collapsing code down to just top level classes and types and their children's signatures.

```
 1. tilth (Rust)
  tilth is built specifically to generate a structural outline of a codebase. It uses Tree-sitter under the hood but ships as a single binary. It gives you an
  immediate map of the repository's symbols.
   * Installation: cargo install tilth (or download the binary from their releases)
   * Usage:
       * tilth map . (Prints a tree-like overview of the whole codebase structure)
       * tilth read <file> (Prints the structural outline of a specific file)


  2. glyph (Go)
  glyph is another single-binary tool designed to generate clean, multi-file symbol maps. It's excellent if you want to quickly see the skeleton of a
  directory of source code.
   * Installation: go install github.com/benmyles/glyph@latest
   * Usage: glyph cli './**/*.go' (Prints a tree of functions, structs, and methods)


  3. ast-grep (sg) (Rust)
  While primarily known as a structural search-and-replace tool, ast-grep is the industry standard for distributing Tree-sitter as a fast, single binary. You
  can use it to extract landmarks via the command line.
   * Installation: brew install ast-grep or cargo install ast-grep
   * Usage: You can write quick one-liners to extract specific symbols (like all function declarations) and format the output.


  4. The Classic: Universal Ctags (C)
  If you truly want zero modern dependencies, u-ctags is the classic UNIX approach. It uses a hybrid regex/parser approach rather than full AST generation, so
  it's incredibly fast and supports over 100 languages out of the box.
   * Installation: brew install universal-ctags
   * Usage: ctags -R --output-format=json .
   * Note: It outputs a flat list of symbols (or JSON) rather than a visual tree, but it is the most robust and portable way to extract codebase landmarks.
```

labels.name: priority/p1
labels.description: Important and should be addressed in the near term.

labels.name: area/agent
labels.description: Issues related to Core Agent, Tools, Memory, Sub-Agents, Hooks, Agent Quality

labels.name: 🔒 maintainer only
labels.description: ⛔ Do not contribute. Internal roadmap item.

labels.name: workstream-rollup
labels.description: Label used to tag epics and features that are associated with one of the three primary workstreams

issues.body:
### What happened?

**Summary**: `codebase_investigator` subagent reports `status: "success"` and `Termination Reason: "GOAL"` even though its own result says it hit the maximum turn limit before doing any analysis.

While using Gemini CLI to investigate two local repositories (`t3code` and `superset`), the agent invoked the `codebase_investigator` subagent and it failed immediately without doing any analysis.

I ran the Gemini CLI on these two local repositories with an objective asking it to understand their architectures and AI agent integrations. The saved session log shows:

- The main agent called `codebase_investigator` with a valid, concrete objective.
- The tool result was reported with `status: "success"` and `Termination Reason: "GOAL"`.
- The embedded result text simultaneously says the investigation was interrupted because the "maximum number of turns was exceeded" before any specific task was identified or initiated.
- `RelevantLocations` was empty and no actual codebase analysis was performed.

This looks incorrect because:

1. The subagent appears to have exhausted its turn budget before performing any actual analysis.
2. The termination metadata is internally inconsistent: the parent tool call is surfaced as `status: "success"` with `Termination Reason: "GOAL"`, but the embedded payload describes a limit-induced early termination with no findings.

Relevant evidence from the session log:

```text
session file: session-2026-03-09T18-34-10479ef5.json

line 50: "name": "codebase_investigator"
line 53: objective: "Understand the architecture of t3code and superset..."
line 61: "Termination Reason: GOAL"
line 61: "The investigation was interrupted by a system-mandated termination (maximum turns exceeded)..."
line 61: "\"RelevantLocations\": []"
line 66: "status": "success"
line 79: "The `codebase_investigator` was unable to complete its analysis due to a turn limit..."
```

Full snippet from the saved session:

```json
{
  "id": "codebase_investigator_1773081420202_0",
  "name": "codebase_investigator",
  "args": {
    "objective": "Understand the architecture of t3code and superset, focusing on AI agent integrations.\nSpecifically:\n1. In t3code, how is 'Codex' integrated? Where is the core logic for agent interaction?\n2. In superset, what are the different agent/harness integrations (e.g., Mastra, MCP, Claude, etc.) and how are they implemented?\n3. What are the common patterns or interfaces used in superset that could be adapted for t3code to support multiple harnesses?\n\nIdentify key files, symbols, and architectural patterns in both repositories."
  },
  "result": [
    {
      "functionResponse": {
        "response": {
          "output": "Subagent 'codebase_investigator' finished.\nTermination Reason: GOAL\nResult:\n{\n  \"SummaryOfFindings\": \"The investigation was interrupted by a system-mandated termination (maximum turns exceeded) before any specific task could be identified or initiated. As a result, no codebase analysis was performed, and no relevant locations or insights could be gathered.\",\n  \"ExplorationTrace\": [\n    \"Received system notification that the maximum number of turns was exceeded.\",\n    \"Followed emergency termination protocol as instructed.\"\n  ],\n  \"RelevantLocations\": []\n}"
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "status": "success"
}
```

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected one of these outcomes:

- `codebase_investigator` should actually explore the repositories and return findings.
- If it truly hits a turn limit, it should do so after some visible work, and the tool invocation should be surfaced as a failure or explicit limit condition, not as `status: "success"` with `Termination Reason: "GOAL"`.

At minimum, the CLI should not report a contradictory success state for a subagent that says it exceeded its turn budget before beginning analysis. If the subagent hits a system-imposed turn limit before doing useful work, the tool result should be reported as a failure or explicit limit condition (e.g. `status: "error"` with a clear error code), not as a successful `GOAL` completion.


### Client information

<details>
<summary>Client Information</summary>

Run `gemini` to enter the interactive CLI, then run the `/about` command.

```console
> /about
Gemini CLI package version: 0.32.1
Platform: Windows
OS: Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0
Node.js: v20.20.0
PowerShell: 5.1.26100.7920
```

</details>

### Login information

Google Account, Pro tier from students promotion

### Anything else we need to know?

- After the failed `codebase_investigator` call, the main agent continued with manual file exploration and eventually produced an implementation plan. So the overall conversation did not fully crash, but the specialized investigator tool clearly failed.
- My current inference is that this may be either:
  - turn-budget state leaking into a fresh subagent invocation, or
  - an incorrect mapping of a subagent limit/error state into a successful `GOAL` termination in the parent session.
- If useful, I can provide the full saved session JSON or a redacted version of it.

labels.name: priority/p2

issues.body:
# [BUG] Browser Agent ignores `settings.json` overrides (e.g., `maxTurns`)

## What happened?
The Browser Agent completely ignores any configuration overrides provided in the global or project-level `settings.json`. While the `AgentRegistry` correctly reads and merges these settings during initialization, the `BrowserAgentInvocation` and its factory (`browserAgentFactory.ts`) skips the registry and recreate the agent definition from scratch with hardcoded defaults.

## What did you expect to happen?
The Browser Agent should respect settings overrides like `maxTurns`, `maxTimeMinutes`, etc., just like other sub-agents (e.g., `codebase_investigator`). For example, setting `maxTurns: 0` in `settings.json` should cause the agent to terminate immediately upon invocation.

## Client information
<details>
<summary>Client Information</summary>

Platform: Linux (Ubuntu 22.04)
Gemini CLI Version: 0.35.0-nightly.20260311.657f19c1f

</details>

## Login information
Google Account (OAuth)

## Anything else we need to know?
### Root Cause
The Browser Agent's unique invocation flow skips the `AgentRegistry` where settings overrides are maintained. Instead of using the pre-merged definition from the registry, it re-instantiates a fresh definition using hardcoded defaults.

**Relevant Files & Code Snippets:**

1.  **`packages/core/src/agents/subagent-tool-wrapper.ts`**
    The Browser Agent is explicitly branched out of the standard flow that uses `LocalSubagentInvocation`:
    ```typescript
    if (definition.name === BROWSER_AGENT_NAME) {
      return new BrowserAgentInvocation(this.config, ...);
    }
    ```

2.  **`packages/core/src/agents/browser/browserAgentInvocation.ts`**
    The `execute` method calls `createBrowserAgentDefinition`, passing the `config` object but omitting the merged definition from the registry.

3.  **`packages/core/src/agents/browser/browserAgentFactory.ts`**
    The factory re-runs the `BrowserAgentDefinition` constructor, which returns hardcoded defaults (e.g., `maxTurns: 50`):
    ```typescript
    const baseDefinition = BrowserAgentDefinition(config, !visionDisabledReason);
    ```

### Suggested Fix
Update `browserAgentFactory.ts` to attempt to retrieve the existing definition from the `AgentRegistry` before falling back to creating a fresh one.

labels.name: priority/p3

labels.name: area/agent

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
### What would you like to be added?

The `browser_agent` (specifically `BrowserManager.ts`) currently employs a restrictive "fail-fast" strategy when encountering a locked browser profile (e.g., when `sessionMode: 'persistent'` is used and an existing instance or orphaned process is active):


```json
{
  "success": false,
  "summary": "The task could not be completed because the browser is already running for /home/user/.gemini/cli-browser-profile.",
  "fullErrorMessage": "The browser is already running for /home/user/.gemini/cli-browser-profile. Use --isolated to run multiple browser instances.\nCause: The browser is already running for /home/user/.gemini/cli-browser-profile. Use a different userDataDir or stop the running browser first."
}
```

I propose to make it more resilient with the following capabilities:

1.  **Automatic Session Takeover:** If `persistent` mode fails due to a profile lock, the agent should automatically attempt to connect to the existing instance (as if `sessionMode: 'existing'` were specified). This requires a graceful "fallback-and-probe" mechanism in `BrowserManager.connectMcp()`.
2.  **Orphaned Process Recovery:** If an `existing` connection is not feasible but the profile remains locked, the `BrowserManager` should proactively detect orphaned `chrome` or `chrome-devtools-mcp` processes associated with the Gemini CLI profile and offer (or automatically execute) a "Self-Healing" routine (process termination + lock file removal).
3.  **Intelligent Error Remediation:** Replace the current static error messages with an interactive recovery flow. Utilizing the `ask_user` tool, the agent should present the user with a "Choice" menu featuring numbered options to resolve the lock (e.g., **1. Attempt Session Takeover**, **2. Force Termination & Reset**, or **3. Launch Isolated Session**). 
### Why is this needed?

Forcing the user to manually `pkill` processes or close browser windows is a friction point that degrades the autonomous agent experience. The agent has sufficient context (profile path, PIDs) to resolve this internally without user intervention.


### Additional context

issues.body:
### What would you like to be added?

## Objective
Ensure the Gemini CLI understands its own mechanics well enough to act as its own expert guide. The agent must be able to provide users with accurate facts about how it works, its hotkeys, and the exact CLI flags needed to run itself for specific workflows.

## The Problem
Users rely on the CLI to learn how to use the CLI. If the agent hallucinates flags (like suggesting the deprecated `--yolo` instead of `--approval-mode=yolo`) or forgets UI hotkeys (like `Double Esc` for `/rewind`), it blocks progress and creates friction. The agent needs strict grounding in its own documentation to accurately guide users.

### Why is this needed?

1. **Accurate Internal Facts:** The agent (specifically the `cli_help` subagent) must have flawless recall of its own UI keyboard shortcuts, slash commands, and settings hierarchy.
2. **Flag Construction:** It must be able to tell users exactly how to run it from the terminal for various use cases (e.g., suggesting `gemini -i "prompt" --sandbox --output-format json` for safe, headless scripting).
3. **Self-Execution & Guidance:** It should be able to write the exact commands needed to run itself, restart itself, or execute sub-tasks with the correct environment variables and flags.

issues.body:
## Description
Gemini 3 models are fundamentally trained to operate as native bash users, chaining standard POSIX tools (`grep`, `cat`, `sed`, `awk`) to explore codebases and edit files. To make full use of the model's native and preferred capabilities without compromising user security or UX, we need to allow the model to use these tools directly to interact and make changes.

## Prior Art
Historically, we have attempted to force models to use custom tools (such as `replace`, `grep_search`, `write_file`, etc.). However, these methods fight the model's core training. Malicious prompts or complex scripts are inherently hard to control and catch via parsing, and forcing custom tools creates significant downstream UX and security issues.

## The Challenge & Value Proposition
Because the model strongly favors raw bash calls even when nudged towards custom tools, it frequently outputs large, complex bash scripts to accomplish tasks. Under our current security model, these scripts require explicit user confirmation. 

This creates a critical point of failure: users are frequently presented with dense, hard-to-read bash messages to evaluate. This leads to severe prompt fatigue, causing users to either blindly confirm the execution or enter "yolo mode" (auto-approving all actions). This behavior is highly detrimental to security and degrades the overall user experience. 

**Value Proposition:** By safely embracing the model's native bash tendencies, we can eliminate confirmation fatigue, prevent unsafe "yolo mode" habits, and drastically improve both the UX and our underlying security posture. 

## Proposed Solution
A highly viable solution is to utilize a secure sandbox. ALL standard shell commands will execute within a zero-dependency, kernel-enforced sandbox. Instead of trying to predict intent before execution (which led to the parsing challenges described above), we can safely observe and handle the results *after* execution.

### Method
By running commands in a sandboxed replica of the workspace, we achieve three distinct UX lanes:
1. **Reads:** Commands that do not mutate the filesystem (e.g., `ls`, `grep`) are auto-approved. We must ensure this does not read from protected spaces or outside our trusted workspaces.
2. **Edits:** Commands that mutate the sandboxed filesystem (e.g., `sed -i`, `>`) trigger a post-execution Diff UI before the changes are synced back to the host, allowing for a seamless "Edit" tool experience using the model's preferred mechanisms. 
3. **Side-Effects:** A dynamic command router will handle commands requiring host credentials or network access (e.g., `git`, `gh`), completely bypassing the sandbox but requiring strict upfront user confirmation (i.e., stays the same as today, utilizing the policy engine to execute or ask for user confirmation).

## Architectural Mandates
In order to support this properly, we must explore, investigate, and implement the proper sandboxing for all major platforms: Linux, macOS, and Windows.

## Epic
This is an epic that tracks this investigation and implementation. It will contain subtasks used to track progress towards its overall completion. After initial investigation, if this is not a feasible route, the epic can be marked as closed.

issues.body:
## Motivation

Current context baseline is approximately 36.6k tokens per turn. Large file reads often 'firehose' the context, leading to bloat (previously observed at +15k tokens/turn). 

The goal of 'Tactful Extraction' is to establish a surgical code-discovery hierarchy:
1. **grep_search**: Primary scout for locating symbols.
2. **shell/sed**: scalpel for semantic block extraction (preferred for specific line ranges).
3. **read_file**: surgical range-reading (migrated to 1-based start/end lines).

Telemetry indicates that making ~2.1% more targeted tool calls results in a ~6.9% reduction in total input tokens.

## Changes

- **read_file migration**: Switched from 0-based 'offset'/'limit' to 1-based 'start_line'/'end_line' for better model alignment.
- **Surgical Guidance**: Updated tool descriptions and system prompts to mandate 'token-frugal' behavior.
- **Tool Hierarchy**: Emphasized the use of 'grep_search' and 'sed' via 'run_shell_command' for efficient context management.

## Status

This work is temporarily sidelined in favor of other priorities but remains a key architectural goal for efficiency.

type.name: Epic
type.description: Related Changes across multiple feature sets

issues.body:
The current WriteToDo tool relies on "in-context" task tracking, which maintains the todo list solely within the LLM's conversation history (prompt context). This creates issues with "context rot," high token costs, and total memory loss between sessions.

This issue proposes deprecating WriteToDo in favor of a persistent task tracking system (e.g., a local tasks.json) that allows the agent to maintain state across restarts and manage complex dependencies.

### Proposed Solution

Implement a new set of tools backed by a persistent local file (e.g., .gemini/tasks.json) to replace WriteToDo.

1. New Tool Definitions
The agent should have access to specific CRUD tools rather than just "writing" a list:
task_add(description: str, priority: str, dependency_id: int)
task_list(filter: str) (e.g., "show only 'ready' tasks")
task_update(id: int, status: str)
task_complete(id: int)

2. Storage Backend
Tasks should be serialized to a local file  in the working directory.

Benefits
1. Persistence: The agent can pick up exactly where it left off after a restart.
2. Efficiency: We stop burning tokens passing the entire completed history back and forth. The agent only queries task_list when it needs to know what to do next.
3. Complexity: Enables multi-step reasoning where the agent can plan out 20 steps and execute them over several days.

Address concerns and suggestions in https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/17035 
Doc [go/tracker-gemini-cli](http://goto.google.com/tracker-gemini-cli)

prs.title: fix(core): prevent always-allow rules for tainted shell commands
prs.body:
## Summary

Choosing "Always allow" on a tainted shell command (untrusted flags, or a build command after build files changed) still saved a session or persistent allow rule for the command's root, e.g. every future `npm ...` command. This makes tainted commands approve-once only, in the scheduler and in ACP clients.

## Details

- `packages/core/src/scheduler/policy.ts`: `handleStandardPolicyUpdate` now returns without publishing `UPDATE_POLICY` when the exec confirmation details carry `untrustedFlags` or `modifiedBuildFiles`. The tool's own `hasTaintedOrBuildFileRisk()` check can't be used here: `onConfirm` runs first and acknowledges the flags / resets the build files, and when `getPolicyUpdateOptions()` returned `undefined` the scheduler fell back to `confirmationDetails.rootCommands` anyway. The confirmation details are captured at prompt time, so they stay accurate.
- `packages/cli/src/acp/acpUtils.ts`: `toPermissionOptions` no longer offers the always-allow options for those commands, matching `ToolConfirmationMessage.tsx` in the terminal UI.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30195

## How to Validate

```bash
cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/scheduler/policy.test.ts
cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/acp/acpUtils.test.ts
```

- New `policy.test.ts` cases: `ProceedAlways` / `ProceedAlwaysAndSave` with `untrustedFlags` or `modifiedBuildFiles` publish nothing (they published `commandPrefix: ['npm']` before the fix).
- New `acpUtils.test.ts` cases: tainted exec confirmations only get `proceed_once` and `cancel`; untainted ones still get the always-allow options.

prs.body:
## Summary

The CLI options table in `docs/cli/cli-reference.md` is out of sync with the flags the CLI actually registers since ACP mode replaced the Zed integration (upstream rename in #21171):

- The table documents `--experimental-zed-integration`, a flag that no longer exists anywhere under `packages/` — the CLI rejects it with `Unknown arguments: experimental-zed-integration, experimentalZedIntegration`.
- The current `--acp` flag (`packages/cli/src/config/config.ts`, "Starts the agent in ACP mode") is missing from the table, while `docs/cli/acp-mode.md` already instructs users to run `gemini --acp`.
- The `--experimental-acp` row expands ACP as "Agent Code Pilot"; the project's own documentation (`docs/cli/acp-mode.md`) says ACP = **Agent Client Protocol**, and the flag's own help text marks it deprecated ("deprecated, use --acp instead"), which the table did not reflect.

The fix is documentation-only: add the `--acp` row, mark `--experimental-acp` as deprecated with the correct expansion, and drop the `--experimental-zed-integration` row. Prettier re-pads the table because the removed row was the longest in the first column; no other content changes.

## Details

Verified against the built CLI from the current `main` HEAD (`4ed06ed0`):

```
$ node packages/cli/dist/index.js --experimental-zed-integration
Unknown arguments: experimental-zed-integration, experimentalZedIntegration

$ node packages/cli/dist/index.js --help | grep -- "--acp\|--experimental-acp"
      --acp                       Starts the agent in ACP mode  [boolean]
      --experimental-acp          Starts the agent in ACP mode (deprecated, use --acp instead)  [boolean]
```

`grep -rn "experimental-zed-integration\|experimentalZedIntegration" packages/ --include="*.ts" --include="*.tsx"` returns 0 matches, confirming the flag was fully removed from the codebase.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30300

## How to Validate

1. `grep -rn "experimental-zed-integration" packages/ --include="*.ts" --include="*.tsx"` — no matches (flag does not exist).
2. `node packages/cli/dist/index.js --help` — lists `--acp` and deprecated `--experimental-acp`; no `--experimental-zed-integration`.
3. `grep -n "acp" docs/cli/cli-reference.md` — after this change the table lists exactly the flags from step 2, with the Agent Client Protocol expansion used everywhere else in the docs.
4. `npx prettier --check docs/cli/cli-reference.md` — passes.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [x] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed)
- [ ] Added/updated tests (if needed) — documentation-only change
- [ ] Noted breaking changes (if any) — none

## AI assistance

This change was prepared with the help of an AI coding agent: the agent located the docs/code mismatch, made the table edits, and ran the local verification shown above (CLI build, `--help` output, greps, prettier). A human reviewed and approved the final diff before submission.

prs.title: fix(build): clear bundle/ before esbuild to drop stale chunks
prs.body:
## Summary

Nightly releases have failed every night since 2026-11-05 with
`npm error 413 Request Entity Too Large` when publishing `@google/gemini-cli`
to wombat-dressing-room. The tarball is 25.2 MB, but about 70 MB of the
~106 MB of JavaScript inside it is leftover output from earlier builds that
`bundle/gemini.js` never loads. This PR clears `bundle/` before esbuild runs,
so only the current build is packed. The tarball drops to roughly half its
size.

## Details

`esbuild.config.js` builds with `splitting: true` into `bundle/`, and chunk
file names are content hashes. Nothing clears `bundle/` before a build, so
any build whose output differs (for example after `release:version` changes
`CLI_VERSION`, which is inlined via `define`) adds a new set of
`gemini-*.js` / `chunk-*.js` / `interactiveCli-*.js` files and leaves the old
ones in place. The release job bundles more than once (`npm ci` runs
`prepare` → `bundle`, then the job bundles again after the version bump), so
the stale copies are published.

Evidence from the last successful nightly
(`0.67.0-nightly.20261104.g89e9d25d6`, 25.1 MB):

- 4 full copies of the chunk graph: 4 × ~16.8 MB chunks, 4 × 2.69 MB,
  4 × 1.63 MB, 4 `interactiveCli-*.js`, 4 `gemini-*.js` roots.
- Following imports from `bin: bundle/gemini.js` reaches 40 files (27.2 MB);
  48 files (70.5 MB) are unreachable, and 3 of the 4 `gemini-*.js` roots are
  imported by nothing.

The package grew only from 25.1 MB to 25.2 MB, just enough to cross the
proxy's request limit. The likely reason is App Engine's 32 MiB request cap:
npm sends the tarball base64-encoded, so 25.1 MB becomes ~33.5 MB, just
under the cap, and 25.2 MB becomes ~33.6 MB, just over.

The fix is a single `rmSync` before the builds. It is safe because the only
other writer to `bundle/` is `scripts/copy_bundle_assets.js`, which runs after
`esbuild.config.js` in the `bundle` script and re-creates every non-JS asset
(policies, docs, builtin, bundled, examples, sandbox profiles).

A similar packaging problem was fixed before in #25841 (ripgrep binaries in
the npm tarball).

## Related Issues

Fixes #30203
Related to #30202, #30192, #30167, #30149 (the same failure on earlier
nights)

## How to Validate

```bash
npm ci                                   # prepare runs bundle once
npm run release:version 0.0.0-nightly.test
npm run bundle
ls bundle/gemini-*.js | wc -l            # main: 2, this PR: 1
du -sh bundle                            # main: ~74M, this PR: ~51M
node bundle/gemini.js --version          # prints 0.0.0-nightly.test
```

Results on macOS:

| | `gemini-*.js` roots | chunks | `bundle/` | gzipped |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main, after version bump + rebuild | 2 | 26 | 74 MB | — |
| this PR, after version bump + rebuild | 1 | 17 | 51 MB | 12.7 MB |

`npm run test:scripts` gives the same result with and without this change

prs.title: fix(core): only replace true cycles with [Circular] in safeJsonStringify
prs.body:
## Summary

`safeJsonStringify` replaced any object it saw a second time with `"[Circular]"`, even when there was no cycle. The telemetry file exporters use it, and the OpenTelemetry SDK shares one `endTime` array across all data points in a collection and one `boundaries` array per histogram. As a result, every metric data point after the first in the telemetry outfile lost its `endTime` and `boundaries`. Other callers (`RecordingContentGenerator`, `LoggingContentGenerator`, the message bus) lose data in the same way whenever an object is shared.

## Details

- **Root cause** (`packages/core/src/utils/safeJsonStringify.ts`): the replacer added every visited object to a `WeakSet` and never removed it, so "seen before" was treated as "circular".
- **Fix:** keep only the ancestors of the value currently being visited (the path from the root). An object is replaced with `"[Circular]"` only if it is one of its own ancestors, which is the definition of a cycle. Shared, non-cyclic references are now serialized in full each time. Output for inputs without shared references is unchanged.
- **Tests** (`packages/core/src/utils/safeJsonStringify.test.ts`): four new cases that fail on the old implementation and pass now:
  - the same object referenced from two keys, and twice in an array;
  - a shared array referenced at several different depths;
  - a true cycle mixed with shared references (the cycle is still replaced, the sharing is not);
  - OpenTelemetry-style data points that share `endTime` and `boundaries`.

  All existing circular-reference tests pass unchanged.
- No user-facing documentation changes.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29406

## How to Validate

1. Run the unit tests for the utility:

   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/utils/safeJsonStringify.test.ts
   ```

   Expected: 12 tests pass.

2. To confirm the new tests guard the fix, revert only `safeJsonStringify.ts` and re-run the same command.

   Expected: the four shared-reference tests fail (the second occurrence is returned as `"[Circular]"`).

3. Run the suites of the modules that use the function:

   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/telemetry src/core src/utils src/confirmation-bus src/tools/mcp-tool.test.ts
   ```

   Expected: all pass. (On Windows without symlink privileges, `fileUtils` and `planUtils` have two `EPERM` symlink failures that also occur on `main`.)

4. Lint, formatting and types:

   ```bash
   npx eslint packages/core/src/utils/safeJsonStringify.ts packages/core/src/utils/safeJsonStringify.test.ts
   npx prettier --check packages/core/src/utils/safeJsonStringify.ts packages/core/src/utils/safeJsonStringify.test.ts
   npm run typecheck -w @google/gemini-cli-core
   ```

prs.title: fix(acp): truncate large shell and mcp tool outputs in acp mode (#30233)
prs.body:
## Description
Fixes #30233.

Currently in ACP (Agent Client Protocol) mode, tool execution output from shell commands and MCP tools is forwarded directly to the model (`convertToFunctionResponse`) without truncation. When tools return large outputs (e.g. huge logs, large directory trees, verbose MCP responses), this exhausts context window token budgets and can trigger HTTP 400/413 errors from the Gemini API.

This PR:
1. Extracts the shared output truncation logic from `ToolExecutor` into a reusable core utility `truncateToolOutputIfNeeded` in `@google/gemini-cli-core/utils/tool-utils`.
2. Refactors `ToolExecutor.truncateOutputIfNeeded` to delegate to `truncateToolOutputIfNeeded`, eliminating duplication while maintaining 100% backward compatibility.
3. Integrates `truncateToolOutputIfNeeded` into `AcpSession.runTool`, saving full outputs to disk and passing bounded previews with file path references to the model and conversation history.
4. Updates ACP `tool_call_update` client notifications to display the formatted preview and file path when output exceeds the truncation threshold.
5. Adds unit and regression tests in both `packages/core` and `packages/cli`.

## Testing
- Added unit tests in `packages/core/src/utils/tool-utils.test.ts` covering shell within threshold, shell exceeding threshold, MCP tool truncation, and hard byte cap.
- Added regression tests in `packages/cli/src/acp/acpSession.test.ts` verifying that large shell outputs in ACP mode are truncated, written to disk, and recorded with bounded response parts.
