issues.body:
## Problem

Copilot CLI loads the same skill twice when a repository contains a project skill and an enabled user plugin contributes the identical skill. This doubles the skill description surface in repositories that develop their own plugin.

Observed with Copilot CLI 1.0.79-9 in `rjmurillo/ai-agents`, where `.claude/skills` is the canonical source for the installed `project-toolkit` plugin.

## Reproduction

```bash
cd <repo-that-contains-the-plugin-source>
copilot plugins list --json | jq -r '
[.plugins[] | select(.kind=="skill") | {name,scope,source,description:(.description // "")}]
| group_by(.name)[]
| select((map(.scope)|index("repository")) and (map(.scope)|index("plugin")))
| [. [0].name, (length|tostring), ([.[].scope+":"+.[].source]|join(","))]
| @tsv'
```

Measured result:

```text
duplicate_names=97
identical_descriptions=97
duplicate_description_bytes=40624
```

Example name:

```text
context-optimizer  plugin  plugin
context-optimizer  repository  project
```

The installed plugin is enabled at user scope. No repository-scoped setting was found to disable that one plugin only in its source repository.

## Expected

When a repository skill and plugin skill have the same canonical name and identical content, load one entry. Project scope could take precedence, or the CLI could deduplicate by name plus content hash. A repository-scoped plugin-disable override would also provide a workaround.

## Control

This is specific to skills. A canary placed in `plugin/instructions/*.instructions.md` did not load through `--plugin-dir`, while a repository `.github/instructions` canary did load.

issues.title: Support a single unified mcp.json for both VS Code and Copilot CLI for maintainability purpose

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Description

Currently, VS Code and GitHub Copilot CLI use two different MCP configuration schemas:

- **VS Code** (`.vscode/mcp.json` or user-level `mcp.json`): uses a top-level `servers` key, and `type` is optional.
- **Copilot CLI** (`~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`, `.mcp.json`, `.github/mcp.json`): uses a top-level `mcpServers` key, and `type` is required for each server entry.

This forces users who work with both VS Code and Copilot CLI to maintain two near-duplicate JSON files and manually keep them in sync whenever a server is added, removed, or updated — which is error-prone and adds unnecessary maintenance overhead.

### Feature Request

Please support a single, unified `mcp.json` file/schema that can be used by both VS Code and Copilot CLI without conversion. For example:

- Accept the `servers` key as an alias for `mcpServers` (or vice versa), and
- Make the `type` field optional/inferable (e.g. default to `stdio`/`local` when `command` is present, or `http` when `url` is present) so existing VS Code configs work as-is.

This would let a single `mcp.json` (whether at the user/global level or per-repository) be shared across both tools, eliminating duplicate configuration and reducing drift between environments.

### Related issues

- #3835 (Incompatible mcp.json schema with VSCode)
- #146 (Respect VS Code User Settings for Copilot CLI Configuration)

issues.title: Cloud agent: MCP registry policy fetch fails with 401/403 on GHEC data residency, silently blocking all user-configured MCP servers

labels.name: area:enterprise
labels.description: GitHub Enterprise (GHE/GHES) support, org policies, and enterprise settings

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

## Summary

On a GitHub Enterprise Cloud **with data residency** instance (`<tenant>.ghe.com`), every user-configured MCP server is silently dropped from Copilot **cloud agent** sessions. Only the platform defaults (`github-mcp-server`, `playwright`) reach the model. The cause is the registry-policy fetch failing with **401/403** and falling into the fail-closed path — the same defect as #2498, where only the **404** leg was fixed.

This is the same fail-closed family as #2498, #2552, #2567, #4346 and #4349, but reached through the cloud agent, where nothing is surfaced to the user at all.

## Environment

- Surface: Copilot cloud agent (not the local CLI, not an IDE)
- Host: GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency, `<tenant>.ghe.com`
- Two MCP servers configured in repo Settings → Copilot → MCP servers: one remote `http`, one `local` (stdio). Both valid per the documented schema, both with explicit `tools` lists.
- Enterprise MCP registry: none configured. `GET /copilot/mcp_registry` (user PAT) returns `{"mcp_registries":[{"url":"","registry_access":"allow_all",...}]}`
- `GET /copilot_internal/user` reports `is_mcp_enabled: true`, `copilot_plan: "enterprise"`

## What happens

From the CLI's own log inside the session (`~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log`):

```
[ERROR]   Failed to validate SDK token (401): GitHub returned: Bad credentials
[WARNING] session.gitHubAuth.setCredentials: failed to re-resolve copilotUser for token
          credential; token swap applied, plan/quota/billing metadata degraded:
          Failed to fetch Copilot user info: 401 Unauthorized: {"message":"Bad credentials"}
[WARNING] Failed to fetch MCP registry policy: 401 Unauthorized.
          Non-default MCP servers will be blocked until the policy can be fetched.
[ERROR]   MCP server "<remote-server>" filtered: Could not verify server against any configured registry
[ERROR]   MCP server "<local-server>"  filtered: Could not verify server against any configured registry
[ERROR]   Using deferred connection for default Playwright server
```

Probing the endpoint from inside the session with **every** credential present (`GITHUB_COPILOT_API_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `COPILOT_SDK_AUTH_TOKEN`, …): **403** on `api.<tenant>.ghe.com/copilot/mcp_registry`, **401** on `api.github.com/copilot/mcp_registry`. The same endpoint returns **200 `allow_all`** to a normal user PAT.

## Why this is a bug, not policy

1. **404 is tolerated, 401/403 is not.** The client special-cases a 404 as "no registry configured, allow all", but any other failure throws into the fail-closed catch that blocks every server without `isDefaultServer`. A tenant with *no registry configured* is therefore treated as if it prohibited everything, purely because its endpoint answers 403 instead of 404. #2498 fixed the 404 leg; the auth-failure leg has the identical consequence.
2. **This filter is documented as not applying to the cloud agent.** Per the MCP-management support matrix, "Registry display" and "Allowlist enforcement" are *Not supported* for Copilot cloud agent, and the enterprise docs state private MCP registries "apply to Copilot CLI and IDEs, but not to cloud agents that run on GitHub." It is nonetheless the filter rejecting these servers.
3. **The root credential failure looks host-related.** `Bad credentials` is what `api.github.com` returns for a token minted by another host, which suggests the SDK-token validation and/or the policy fetch resolves to public github.com rather than the data-residency tenant.

## Everything upstream is healthy

Verified in-session, so the failure is purely in the policy filter:

- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/copilot/cloud-agent/configuration` returns both servers as stored.
- The `Start MCP Servers` step succeeds; the local MCP proxy serves all servers' tools (`GET 127.0.0.1:2301/tools` — 62 tools, including all of both user servers').
- The stdio server's `initialize`/`tools/list` handshake works when driven by hand on the runner.
- `COPILOT_MCP_ENABLED=true`, `GITHUB_COPILOT_3P_MCP_ENABLED=true`, `COPILOT_PERMISSION_MODE=allow_all`.

## Impact

**Nothing is surfaced.** No failed step, no warning in the pull request, no line in the session transcript. The messages above exist only in the CLI's private log inside the ephemeral runner. In our case a Microsoft Learn MCP server had been silently dead in every cloud-agent session for an unknown period, and we only found it while investigating a second server. Unlike the local CLI — where `--log-level debug` reveals it — cloud-agent users have no way to observe this.

Reproduced across three different agent runtime builds.

## Suggested fix

Either (or both):

1. Treat an **auth failure** (401/403) on the registry-policy fetch the same as 404 when no registry is configured for the tenant — i.e. extend #2498's fix beyond 404.
2. Fix host/token resolution so the policy endpoint authenticates on data-residency instances.

Additionally: surface a blocked-server warning on the pull request, the way firewall blocks already are. A silent drop is indistinguishable from the agent choosing not to use a tool.

## Ruled out

`MCP servers in Copilot` policy (enabled), registry allowlist (`allow_all`), custom agent `tools:` filter (none present), server transport (remote HTTP and local stdio fail identically), config schema (validated by the Settings UI), and any client-side override (no env var, CLI flag, or settings key reaches the gate; `isDefaultServer` is rejected by the Settings schema validator).

issues.title: Focus reporting (DECSET ?1004) is not restored on exit - [I/[O leak into the parent shell

labels.name: area:terminal-rendering
labels.description: Display and rendering: flickering, scrolling, line wrapping, output formatting

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Copilot CLI enables xterm focus reporting (DECSET `?1004`) and does not disable it when the process exits abnormally (crash, or abort during an operation). The terminal keeps emitting focus events after Copilot is gone, and with nothing left to consume them they land in the parent shell as literal input.

On Windows Terminal with PowerShell the effect is immediately disruptive. Every focus change injects `[I` (focus gained, `CSI I`) or `[O` (focus lost, `CSI O`) at the prompt, and PowerShell parses `[I` as the opening of a type literal, so the shell errors:

```
D:\Git> [I[O[I
ParserError:
Line |
   1 |  [I[O[I
     |         ~
     | Missing ] at end of attribute or type literal.
```

One `[I`/`[O` pair arrives per alt-tab or window click, so the prompt stays unusable until the mode is reset by hand.

The confirming symptom is a Copilot TUI still painted on screen with **no `copilot` or `node` process running** — the terminal has been left in TUI-oriented input mode by a process that has already exited.

### Affected version

```
GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.78
```

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Start `copilot` in Windows Terminal with PowerShell as the shell.
2. Cause the process to terminate abnormally. In my case the session died on its own (see Additional context); `taskkill /f /im copilot.exe` produces the same terminal state.
3. At the recovered PowerShell prompt, click to another window and back.
4. `[I` / `[O` appear at the prompt. Pressing Enter produces the `ParserError` above.

Manual recovery, for anyone who finds this issue while stuck:

```powershell
[Console]::Write("`e[?1004l")
```

### Expected behavior

Copilot restores the terminal modes it enabled — at minimum focus reporting (`?1004`) and mouse tracking (`?1000`/`?1002`/`?1003`/`?1006`) — on **every** exit path including abnormal ones, leaving the parent shell as it was found.

Two changes would each help, independently:

1. **Move the mode-restore into a handler that also runs on abnormal termination** (panic/abort/signal), not only on clean shutdown.
2. **Add a setting to opt out of focus reporting**, in the same spirit as the existing `terminalProgress`, whose own documentation says *"Set to `false` to suppress these escape sequences on terminals that render them as visible artifacts."* `mouse` is a second precedent. There is currently no equivalent for `?1004`, so a user hitting this has no supported way to avoid it.

The second is valuable even if the first lands, since it also helps terminals and multiplexers that mishandle focus events while Copilot is running normally.

### Additional context

Related issues:

- **#2332** — same failure class: terminal left in a bad mode after exiting a Copilot session (mouse selection rather than focus reporting).
- **#459** — the feature request that introduced focus reporting.
- This is a known cross-tool TUI hazard rather than something specific to Copilot. Claude Code has the consuming-side equivalent (anthropics/claude-code#11391 and #18363, closed as duplicates of #18208), and vim removed mode 1004 from its XM termcap over the same class of problem.

**What terminated the session** — possibly a separate issue, happy to split it out. The session log ends with repeated bridge-ack timeouts, one in the same second as a subagent launch:

```
12:49:14.535Z [WARNING] [rust:copilot_runtime::interop::bridge_backed_seam] timed out waiting for bridge event ack {"event_kind":"event","timeout_ms":30000}
12:51:54.590Z [INFO]    Completing 1 orphaned tool calls.
12:53:59.317Z [WARNING] [rust:copilot_runtime::interop::bridge_backed_seam] timed out waiting for bridge event ack {"event_kind":"event","timeout_ms":30000}
12:53:59.553Z [INFO]    SessionAgentExecutor.execute() called for "rubber-duck" (toolCallId=…)
12:54:03.747Z [INFO]    --- End of group ---
                        <process gone>
```

Fourteen such bridge-ack timeouts occurred in that one session over a day. This may relate to #4026 and #2543. The terminal-mode leak is independent of the cause of death, though — any abnormal exit produces it.

Environment:

- **OS**: Windows 11 Enterprise, build 10.0.26200
- **CPU architecture**: x86_64 (AMD64)
- **Terminal emulator**: Windows Terminal
- **Shell**: PowerShell 7.6.4 (`pwsh`)
- **Node**: v24.18.1
- **Relevant settings**: `mouse: false`, `autoUpdate: false`

Happy to provide fuller logs via `--log-level debug --log-file` if useful.

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Long links in assistant Markdown sometimes render with the OSC 8 hyperlink control payload visible as text when the link wraps in Ghostty. The output is prefixed with text resembling:

```text
]8;;id=md-<generated-id>;https://example.com/a/very/long/path/https://example.com/a/very/long/path/
```

The saved assistant response contains only a valid plain URL, with no malformed Markdown or escape sequences. This indicates the corruption occurs in Copilot CLI's terminal rendering rather than in model output.

This appears related to the `1.0.68` changelog fix, "Preserve wrapped OSC 8 hyperlink IDs in terminal output," but still reproduces on `1.0.78`.

### Affected version

```text
GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.78
```

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Launch Copilot CLI in Ghostty.
2. Have an assistant response end with a bare URL long enough to wrap at the current terminal width.
3. Observe that the URL is preceded by visible OSC 8 payload text such as `]8;;id=md-...;` and may appear duplicated.

An affected session is:

```text
250a0930-cde5-4f39-bcdd-c40ef05656a0
```

The problem is visible in the final assistant response of that session.

### Expected behavior

The response should display one clean, clickable URL. OSC 8 control sequences and generated hyperlink IDs must never be visible, including when the URL wraps across terminal lines.

### Additional context

- Operating system: macOS (Darwin), Apple Silicon
- Terminal: Ghostty `1.3.2-main-+8252871b2`
- Environment: `TERM_PROGRAM=ghostty`, `TERM=xterm-ghostty`, `COLORTERM=truecolor`
- Workaround: launching with `FORCE_HYPERLINK=0 copilot` prevents OSC 8 hyperlinks from being emitted
- The local session event log records the assistant content as normal prose followed by a plain URL, confirming the malformed text is introduced during rendering

## Summary

GitHub Copilot CLI session appeared to continue consuming AI credits after all visible tasks were completed.

## Environment

- GitHub Copilot CLI version: 1.0.75
- Mode: Interactive CLI session
- Session limit enabled: No
- Observed behavior: Session showed approximately 97.8% AI credit usage after the visible tasks completed. No further user prompts or interactions were made. Later, the session reached 100%.

issues.title: Agent View ignores remote container context when workspace is opened in ssh dev container

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

## Description

When a VS Code workspace is opened in a remote SSH dev container, the new Copilot Agent View incorrectly initializes on the host system instead of inside the container, ignoring the remote context that the main Chat interface correctly respects.

## Expected Behavior

- Workspace opened in dev container → Chat works correctly in container
- New Agent View opened → should also run in the same container context
- Both interfaces should respect the remote container environment

## Actual Behavior

- Workspace opened in dev container → Chat works correctly in container
- New Agent View opened → **starts on the host system instead of the container**
- Agent has file system access to the host (e.g., `/Users/<name>/...`) instead of container paths
- This creates a context mismatch and prevents proper interaction with container-specific tools/dependencies

## Environment

- OS: macOS (Darwin)
- Workspace: SSH remote dev container
- VS Code: Remote - Containers extension enabled
- Copilot CLI: Latest version

## Impact

- Agent cannot access container-specific dependencies/tools
- Workspace context is fragmented between Chat (container) and Agent (host)
- Potential security/privacy issue: agent operates on host file system when it shouldn't

## Suggested Fix

Agent View should automatically detect and respect the VS Code remote context (dev container, SSH, WSL, etc.) on initialization, matching the behavior of the main Chat interface.

### Affected version

latest

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Open a project in a dev container (e.g., via Remote - Containers extension)
2. Verify Chat interface works correctly in container
3. Open Agent View (or new agent session)
4. Check working directory/system info: `echo $PWD` or equivalent
5. **Observe:** Agent is on host system, not in container

### Expected behavior

- Workspace opened in dev container → Chat works correctly in container
- New Agent View opened → should also run in the same container context
- Both interfaces should respect the remote container environment

issues.title: [FEATURE]: Add provider-aware API key format validation before saving credentials

labels.name: type/feature
labels.description: New behaviour or an improvement

labels.name: area/auth
labels.description: Login and credentials

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

## Problem

OpenCode's generic API key connection flow accepts any non-empty string as an API key. For example, entering `1` can pass the connection form, be forwarded through `integration.connect.key`, and be stored as a credential. The error may only become apparent later when making a model request.

## Current implementation

- `packages/app/src/providers/connect/machine.ts` only checks whether the entered key is empty or whitespace.
- `packages/protocol/src/groups/integration.ts` defines the key as `Schema.String`, without format constraints.
- `packages/server/src/handlers/integration.ts` forwards the submitted key.
- `packages/core/src/integration.ts` persists the key as a credential without provider-specific format validation.

## Proposed behavior

Introduce declarative, provider-owned API key format constraints and enforce them in the shared server/core connection path before creating or replacing a credential.

- Reject clearly malformed keys only when a built-in provider has a documented, stable format contract.
- Do not impose a global `sk-` regex. Custom providers and OpenAI-compatible endpoints may use opaque or deployment-specific tokens.
- Keep validation local. Do not require a network request or prove that the key is currently active.
- Return actionable validation errors without echoing or logging the submitted secret.
- Do not create or overwrite credentials when validation fails.

## Scope boundary

This feature covers **local input-format validation before persistence**, not live credential verification.

Live verification and authentication diagnostics are a separate concern discussed in #56782. A syntactically plausible key should remain saveable even when the provider is offline, the endpoint is custom, or the key has limited model permissions.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Clearly malformed keys are rejected for providers with stable, declared format constraints.
2. Plausible keys are not rejected because live verification is unavailable or fails.
3. Custom and opaque-key providers are not blocked by generic regex assumptions.
4. Validation is enforced server-side for App, TUI, CLI, and SDK callers.
5. Tests cover empty/whitespace input, malformed constrained input, valid input, unconstrained providers, and ensuring credentials are not mutated after rejection.

Related: #56782 — live credential verification and authentication diagnostics.

issues.title: tool-use: streamed tool-call arguments drop to empty {} placeholder, session hangs (GLM-5.3 via ollama-cloud)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: area/model-behavior
labels.description: What the model does or says

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/windows
labels.description: Windows

issues.body:
## Summary

During a long opencode session with GLM-5.3 (ollama-cloud provider), tool-call argument payloads intermittently fail to arrive, leaving an empty `{}` placeholder. The session then either hangs (stream never completes, no reaper fires) or enters a runaway loop of repeated empty tool calls. This affects every tool with a large string payload (`shell.command`, `execute.code`, `subagent.prompt`, `write.content`, `edit.oldString`, `edit.newString`, `question.questions`), while small structured arguments (`read.path`) are unaffected. 100+ empty `shell` calls were observed in one session, including bursts of 30–50 consecutive failures.

## Environment

- opencode version: `2.2.5`
- OS: `Windows_NT 10.0.26200 (win32 x64)`
- Shell: `C:\windows\system32\cmd.exe`
- Install/channel: `latest`
- Active plugins: None found in config
- Model/provider: `GLM-5.3` via `ollama-cloud`

## Root Cause (with maintainer diagnosis)

Two independent defect chains, confirmed by upstream reports:

**1. Provider stream dies mid-tool-call (primary).** The GLM-5.3 stream stops sending argument fragments partway through a tool call. The `{}` shown in the transcript is the **streaming placeholder**, not a completed empty call — `executed: false` with no `ran` timestamp proves nothing was ever executed. No reaper clears it: the 5-minute `chunkTimeout` never fires if the provider keeps sending keepalive/empty events. This is the mechanism tracked in **#51291**, **#53433**, **#54683** (closed as dup of #51291), **#58481**, **#12233**.

**2. GLM tool-call serialization defects (secondary).** Confirmed upstream:
- vLLM MTP speculative decoding duplicates/corrupts tool-call JSON tokens (vllm-project/vllm#34449, zai-org/GLM-5#15)
- SGLang streaming passes object/array arguments through verbatim without escaping, truncating JSON (zai-org/GLM-5#15)
- GLM-5.3-Flash via Ollama Cloud emits malformed string-encoded tool calls (ollama/ollama#18506)

The empty-argument loops in this session are consistent with chain 1: the model re-emits the tool call after a stalled/failed stream, the placeholder stalls again, and the cycle repeats with no loop protection.

## Reproduction

1. Start a long session with GLM-5.3 via ollama-cloud on Windows.
2. Drive a workload with repeated large-payload tool calls (multi-line PowerShell, file writes, subagent prompts).
3. Observe intermittent `shell` calls returning `(no output)` with `command: ""`, `execute` returning `"Code cannot be empty."`, and `subagent` receiving an empty `prompt`.
4. Observe bursts of 30–50 consecutive empty calls with no loop abort.

## Expected Behavior

- A stalled provider stream is detected and reaped within a bounded time, with a structured error returned to the model.
- An empty/invalid tool-call argument payload never reaches the executor.
- Repeated identical failing tool calls trigger loop protection after a small threshold.

## Actual Behavior

- Empty `shell` commands execute as no-ops and return `(no output)`; the model reads this as success and retries.
- `execute`/`subagent`/`write`/`edit`/`question` fail validation and the model retries identically.
- No reaper fires for stalled streams (24+ minutes observed in upstream reports).
- No doom-loop abort for repeated empty calls.

## Related Upstream Issues

| Issue | Relevance |
|---|---|
| anomalyco/opencode#51291 | Provider stream disappears mid-turn, call stays running |
| anomalyco/opencode#53433 | No per-tool timeout; one unsettled tool hangs the step |
| anomalyco/opencode#54683 | Empty-input hang = streaming placeholder (dup of #51291) |
| anomalyco/opencode#58481 | Parallel streamed calls with `{}` args |
| anomalyco/opencode#12233 | StreamIdleTimeout retry loop during tool-input generation |
| anomalyco/opencode#25511 (PR) | Empty-args early-exit guard (GPT-5.5 `apply_patch`) |
| anomalyco/opencode#37110 (PR) | Doom-loop guard after 3 consecutive empty outcomes |
| ollama/ollama#18506 | GLM-5.3-Flash malformed tool calls via Ollama Cloud |
| zai-org/GLM-5#15 | Malformed tool-call JSON via NVIDIA NIM |

## Workarounds

1. **Provider-level request timeout** (from opencode maintainer, #54683): set an overall timeout on the provider so a stalled stream fails and retries:
   ```json
   { "providers": { "ollama-cloud": { "settings": { "timeout": 900000 } } } }
   ```
2. External watchdog: detect last message = tool_use with empty input + no stream activity for 60s → interrupt and re-prompt.
3. Short concrete commands; avoid very large single payloads in long sessions.
4. Start fresh sessions when failure rate climbs (long-context aggravation suspected).

## Remediation Priorities

1. **Stream diagnostics first** — capture raw provider stream, parsed representation, and executor input to localize where arguments vanish.
2. **Stream reaping / provider timeout** — bounded overall request timeout plus periodic stale-tool sweep (`settleStaleToolCalls` on a timer, not only at drain start).
3. **Argument-integrity guard** — reject empty/missing required payloads before execution with a structured error (builds on PR #25511).
4. **Doom-loop detection** — abort after N consecutive identical failing calls (builds on PR #37110).

issues.title: agent: degenerate meta-planning loop - turn produces zero output, reasoning leaks into reply

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: area/model-behavior
labels.description: What the model does or says

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/windows
labels.description: Windows

issues.body:
## Summary

A large language-model session can end in a degenerate meta-planning loop: the model repeatedly announces imminent execution ("Execute now. FINAL. Go.") with increasing compression, never emits tool calls or a final answer, and the turn produces zero output. In observed cases, internal reasoning text also leaked into the visible reply instead of staying hidden.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.1.4
- OS: Windows_NT 10.0.26300 (win32 x64)
- Terminal: Unavailable: terminal environment variables are not set (OpenCode desktop app)
- Shell: cmd.exe (harness); session tooling runs PowerShell
- Install/channel: latest
- Active plugins: @dietrichgebert/ponytail (5.3.2, supply-chain audited — no network/eval/processes), opencode-spend-tracker (local file plugin, code-read: ledger reader only)

## Reproduction

Reproduction is not deterministic; it occurred in 2–3 sessions under these conditions:

1. A previous assistant turn fails or produces an incoherent/partial response.
2. The next turn carries a large multi-step task (recover from the failure + design + implement + run + report).
3. The model enters a planning phase that never terminates: instead of tool calls or a reply, it emits endlessly repeating self-instructions of the form "Execute now. (END) OK. Final answer now. Stop. Write. Go. FINAL." — each iteration shorter, hundreds of repetitions, consuming the entire turn.
4. No tool call is ever issued; the session appears hung from the user's side until manually interrupted.

## Expected Behavior

The agent either acts (issues tool calls) or produces a final reply. A failure to plan should surface as an error or a normal reply stating the difficulty — not an unterminated repetition loop.

## Actual Behavior

- Turn output = hundreds of repeated "executing now"-style filler tokens; zero tool calls; zero deliverable.
- Chain-of-thought/scratchpad text ("Hmm, but background is safer...", "Careful with the script — no bugs") appeared in the visible reply rather than staying in the hidden reasoning channel.
- Observed in 2–3 sessions over 2026-10-30/31; always after a prior turn failure; always under large multi-step task framing.

## Additional Context

- User workaround that works: interrupt early, then issue a direct imperative ("stop planning, act now") — a fresh, imperative-heavy turn recovers immediately. Smaller task scoping per turn also prevents recurrence.
- Possibly related to a separate harness-layer symptom reported separately: an instruction block appearing in the user channel that exists in zero stored session messages (see companion issue). Both symptoms sit at the client↔model context-assembly layer, so may share a root cause in middleware (context assembly/compaction/injection ordering).
- The corrupted turn is preserved verbatim by the user if the team wants the full token-level sample.

issues.title: [FEATURE]: Auto-select reasoning effort based on task complexity
issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

## Summary
Currently, reasoning effort (variants like low/medium/high) must be manually switched by the user. It would be great if OpenCode could automatically select the appropriate reasoning effort based on the complexity of the task.
## Problem
In v1.4.0, GitHub Copilot Anthropic models moved from a hardcoded `thinking_budget: 4000` to user-selectable `reasoningEffort` variants. This is a great improvement, but users now have to manually switch between variants depending on the task.
- Simple tasks (file search, small edits) waste tokens on `high`
- Complex tasks (architecture decisions, debugging) suffer on `low`
## Proposed Solution
Automatically classify the task complexity and select the reasoning effort:
| Task type | Suggested effort |
|---|---|
| Simple questions, file lookups | low |
| Standard code edits, refactoring | medium |
| Complex design, multi-file debugging | high |
### Possible approaches:
1. **Heuristic-based**: Analyze prompt length, number of files mentioned, keywords (e.g. "debug", "architect", "refactor") to estimate complexity
2. **Two-pass**: Use a fast/cheap model call to classify complexity first, then route to the appropriate effort level
3. **Per-agent defaults**: Allow configuring default effort per agent type (already partially possible, but could be more granular)
## Additional Context
- Related change: commit 5a6d10c (v1.4.0)
- This would be especially valuable for GitHub Copilot users where rate limits matter more than per-token cost

### Description

### Description

On Windows, OpenCode 2.3.0 appears to ignore a customized `TEMP`/`TMP` environment variable when choosing its temporary directory.

In previous versions, OpenCode used `%TEMP%\opencode` (i.e. it respected the current `TEMP` value). In 2.3.0, it seems to always use the default user temp path:

```text
C:\Users\<username>\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode
```

even when `TEMP` and `TMP` have been changed to another location (for example `D:\Temp`).

This means the temporary files are written to the system default user temp directory instead of the directory configured through the environment variables.

### Environment

- OpenCode version: 2.3.0
- OS: Windows 10/11 (please fill in exact version)
- Installation method: (e.g. desktop app / CLI / npm / standalone — please fill in)
- Shell used to launch OpenCode: (e.g. PowerShell / CMD / Windows Terminal — please fill in)

### Expected behavior

OpenCode should use `%TEMP%\opencode` / `%TMP%\opencode`, i.e. it should respect the current `TEMP`/`TMP` environment variables, as previous versions did.

Alternatively, if there is a reason not to inherit them, there should be a documented configuration option or environment variable to override the temp directory.

### Actual behavior

OpenCode creates/uses:

```text
C:\Users\<username>\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode
```

even when `TEMP` and `TMP` point to a different directory.

### Additional context

- This looks related to the existing reports about OpenCode not respecting `TMPDIR`/`TEMP`/`TMP` on Windows and about the bundled Bun runtime’s temp-directory handling.
- I have not yet confirmed whether setting `BUN_TMPDIR` changes the behavior, but the regression compared with previous versions seems to be in how OpenCode resolves its temp root on Windows.
- Please let me know if you need logs, a trace, or a minimal reproduction repository.


### Plugins

It most likely has nothing to do with any plugin, because this just looks like an issue with system prompt injection.

2.3.0

issues.title: permissions: external_directory checks don't resolve links, so a link into a denied directory gets around a policy

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: area/core
labels.description: Agent loop, tools and config

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/wsl
labels.description: Windows Subsystem for Linux

issues.body:
## Summary

`external_directory` checks match the path as given, without resolving links. A `tool.use` policy that denies `external_directory:<dir>/*` blocks reading `<dir>/file`, but reading the same file through a link that points into `<dir>` succeeds. The permissions docs say "Explicit external paths are canonicalized before matching", so I expected the link to be resolved and the read blocked.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.2.5
- OS: Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64 (WSL2)
- Terminal: TERM=xterm-256color
- Shell: /bin/zsh
- Install/channel: latest
- Active plugins: none found in config

## Reproduction

1. Set up a denied directory, a link into it, and a project, all outside each other:

   ```sh
   R=/tmp/oc-linkrepro
   mkdir -p $R/project $R/denied
   echo secret > $R/denied/secret.txt
   ln -s $R/denied $R/link
   git -C $R/project init -q
   ```

2. Add `$R/project/opencode.jsonc`:

   ```jsonc
   {
     "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
     "policies": [
       { "action": "tool.use", "resource": "external_directory:/tmp/oc-linkrepro/denied/*", "effect": "deny" }
     ]
   }
   ```

3. From `$R/project`, run:

   ```sh
   opencode run --standalone --format json --auto "Use the read tool on /tmp/oc-linkrepro/denied/secret.txt, then on /tmp/oc-linkrepro/link/secret.txt. Make no other tool calls, and keep going if one is blocked."
   ```

## Expected Behavior

Both reads are blocked with `Blocked by configuration policy`, because `/tmp/oc-linkrepro/link/secret.txt` canonicalizes to `/tmp/oc-linkrepro/denied/secret.txt`.

## Actual Behavior

```text
read /tmp/oc-linkrepro/denied/secret.txt -> Blocked by configuration policy
read /tmp/oc-linkrepro/link/secret.txt   -> Read file /tmp/oc-linkrepro/link/secret.txt, lines 1-1  1: secret
```

The same happens for shell commands: `ls` through a link into a denied directory isn't blocked.

## Additional Context

1. Reproduces every time. I hit it while denying `external_directory:/mnt/c/*` so agents stay off the Windows drive in WSL: a link such as `~/win -> /mnt/c/Users/me` gets around the policy.
2. Possibly related: #30788, closed, asked for links inside a project that point outside it to go through `external_directory` consent. This report is about an external path whose link target is in a denied directory.
3. Also noticed, though the docs call shell directory inference best effort: for shell commands, only `cd` targets and the working directory are checked against `external_directory`. Path arguments, such as `ls /mnt/c/Windows` or `cat /mnt/c/Windows/win.ini`, aren't checked, even when they exist. I worked around it with `shell:*/mnt/c/*` text patterns.

issues.title: V2: preserve permission and question waits across server restart

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: core
labels.description: Anything pertaining to core functionality of the application (opencode server stuff)

issues.body:
## Summary

Pending permission requests and question forms are process-local in V2. Restarting the server destroys the request and its suspended continuation. Managed-service restart continuity may resume the Session, but it cannot restore or accept a reply to the old blocker.

We need a durable model for interactive waits that covers both permissions and questions without blindly replaying the tool call that created them.

## Current behavior

Permissions keep pending requests in an in-memory `Map` with a `Deferred` owned by the running tool fiber:

- `packages/core/src/permission.ts`
- layer finalization declines every pending request and clears the map

Questions use `Form.Service`, whose entries and `Deferred`s live in an in-memory cache:

- `packages/core/src/form.ts`
- layer finalization cancels every pending form
- the built-in question tool waits on `forms.ask(...)` inside its tool execution

On managed-server shutdown, active Sessions are suspended for restart continuity. On startup, the runner resumes the Session and reconciles stale running tools as interrupted. The old permission/form request no longer exists, so clients cannot display or answer it.

This also gives shutdown the wrong domain meaning for forms: finalization publishes cancellation even though the user did not cancel the question.

## Design pressure

Persisting the request payload alone is insufficient. The reply currently settles a process-local `Deferred` inside a tool call, and that continuation disappears with the process.

Permissions are the harder case because `permission.assert(...)` can be called from within tool execution. Re-entering the tool to reach the permission check may repeat work or side effects that happened before the check. Treating every interrupted tool as replayable is therefore unsafe.

The design should decide where the restartable boundary lives. Possibilities include:

- Make interactive blockers durable workflow records whose terminal reply can settle the owning tool call without restoring the old JavaScript continuation.
- Move authorization to an explicit boundary before the physical tool attempt, so an approved attempt can start safely after restart.
- Define a resumable tool protocol for tools that can suspend on interactive input, while ordinary tools remain non-replayable.

Questions and permissions should share the same lifecycle concepts where possible, even if permission evaluation and form rendering remain separate APIs.

## Required semantics

- A pending permission or question survives a graceful managed-service restart and remains visible through the existing list APIs.
- The original request ID remains replyable after restart.
- Server shutdown does not record a user rejection or cancellation.
- A reply settles the blocker exactly once and allows the owning Session to continue.
- Recovery does not repeat provider work or tool side effects that may already have executed.
- Saved permission rules remain distinct from one pending permission decision.
- Reconnect hydration and live events converge on the same durable blocker state.
- Location and Session ownership checks continue to prevent cross-location or cross-session replies.
- The design explicitly states whether unexpected process death is supported or remains outside the first implementation.

## Coverage

Add an integration test that:

1. Starts a Session that blocks on a permission request or question form.
2. Tears down the server/location graph while preserving the database.
3. Builds a fresh graph and performs managed restart continuation.
4. Verifies the same blocker is listed and replyable.
5. Replies and verifies the Session continues without duplicate tool side effects.

Cover permission approval, permission rejection, question answer, and question cancellation.

## Related

- #15172 tracks the same user-visible question loss in V1.
- #35447 covered V2 blocker reconciliation after reconnect and requested fresh focused issues against the current lifecycle.
- #35646 added graceful managed-service Session continuation, but intentionally reconciles ambiguous in-flight tools rather than replaying them.
- `specs/v2/session-restart-continuation.md` documents the current restart boundary.

issues.title: shell: Store PowerShell fails with 0xC0070005 in Windows pipe mode

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: area/service
labels.description: Background service and server

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/windows
labels.description: Windows

issues.body:
### Description

### Description

After updating OpenCode from 2.2.7 to 2.3.0 on Windows, shell tool calls using Microsoft Store PowerShell 7 fail before executing even a one-line command:

```text
failed to spawn C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\Microsoft.PowerShell_7.7.0.0_x64__8wekyb3d8bbwe\pwsh.EXE:
OS Error -1073283067 (FormatMessageW() returned error 317) (os error -1073283067)
```

`-1073283067` is `0xC0070005`. Expected: the command executes and returns its output. Actual: process creation fails, in both a project directory and a separate temporary directory.

#### Isolated Win32 reproduction

A standalone C# P/Invoke probe, independent of OpenCode/plugins, called `CreateProcessW` for the same packaged executable with `-NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command "exit 0"` and `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`. Changing only the job attachment strategy produced:

| Creation strategy | Store PowerShell 7.7 | Windows PowerShell 5.1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No explicit job attribute | Success, exit 0 | Success, exit 0 |
| `STARTUPINFOEXW` + `EXTENDED_STARTUPINFO_PRESENT` + `PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST` containing one newly created unnamed job | Fails: `0xC0070005` | Success, exit 0 |
| Normal creation, then `AssignProcessToJobObject` | Success, assignment succeeds, exit 0 | Success, exit 0 |

Three additional consecutive rounds reproduced the same Store executable results. Normal `ProcessStartInfo` creation also succeeds for both the real packaged EXE and its app-execution aliases. `Get-AppxPackage Microsoft.PowerShell` reports Status=Ok and IsPartiallyStaged=False.

At the failing timestamps, **Microsoft-Windows-AppModel-Runtime/Admin** records:

- Event 212, `0x80070005`: cannot add the process to the package's Desktop AppX container.
- Event 208, `0x80070005`: cannot create the package process while configuring its runtime, `[FinishPackageActivation]`.

#### Relevant implementation

The running shell process is launched through `opencode-pty` **0.5.2**, in pipe mode. [The current Windows pipe implementation](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2.3.0/packages/process-daemon/src/service/pipe/windows.rs) supplies `PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST` during `CreateProcessW`.

Its jobless retry only accepts raw `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` (`5`); the packaged EXE returns `0xC0070005`, so that retry is skipped. The standalone probe returns `5` when given the app-execution alias instead of the real packaged path. This error-code distinction appears relevant to the missed fallback.

The [2.2.7 shell service](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2.2.7/packages/core/src/shell.ts) directly spawned commands; [2.3.0](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2.3.0/packages/core/src/shell.ts) delegates local commands to the process daemon. Related introduction: #63196; follow-up: #63346. The previous 2.2.7 binary was not rerun during this diagnosis, so the version boundary is based on observed upgrade history and source comparison, not a binary bisect.

This differs from closed #62512: that issue returned exit 0 with empty output through the Store alias; this one fails to create the real packaged process.

Workaround verified: explicitly selecting Windows PowerShell 5.1 restores shell execution. MSI/ZIP PowerShell 7 was not installed or tested. No WindowsApps ACL changes or package repairs were made.

### Plugins

`@tarquinen/opencode-dcp@latest`, `oh-my-opencode-slim`. OpenCode itself was not retested with plugins disabled; the standalone Win32 probe has no plugin dependency.

### OpenCode version

`opencode v2.3.0`, latest/release channel, installed through Scoop; managed `serve --service` process. Process daemon: `opencode-pty` 0.5.2.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On Windows, use Microsoft Store PowerShell 7 (observed package: `Microsoft.PowerShell_7.7.0.0_x64__8wekyb3d8bbwe`), with OpenCode 2.3.0 selecting that shell.
2. Ask the shell tool to run `Write-Output 'probe'`.
3. Observe the spawn failure above, before any command output. Changing the working directory does not help.
4. For an API-level comparison, create that same EXE with and without `PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST`, as described in the table.

### Operating System

Windows x64, `Windows_NT 10.0.26300` (`[Environment]::OSVersion`: `10.0.26300.0`). Store PowerShell reports 7.7.0. System Windows PowerShell reports 5.1.26100.9818.

### Terminal

Exact frontend terminal application unavailable. Shell-tool environment has `TERM=xterm-256color` (injected by OpenCode); `TERM_PROGRAM`, `COLORTERM`, and `WT_SESSION` are unset. `ComSpec=C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe`.

issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

Every TUI launch restores the session tabs from the previous run by reading `tabs.json`. The only way to start clean today is `tabs.mode: "off"`, which removes the tab strip entirely.

Add a third value to `tabs.scope`:

```json
{ "tabs": { "scope": "window" } }
```

With `window`, tabs live in process memory instead of `tabs.json`:

- a new launch starts with no tabs restored,
- nothing is written to `tabs.json`, so the previous run's file and other TUI processes are untouched,
- tabs are not shared with other OpenCode windows.

`cwd` and `global` keep their current behavior, and the default stays `cwd`.

Why a scope value rather than a separate `tabs.restore` flag: persistence and cross-window sharing are the same mechanism (the file-backed store), so one setting covers both. A boolean would duplicate it and allow "shared but not persisted", which the current storage cannot represent.

Related but different:

- #47998 and #60859 report persisted tabs leaking between servers or launches. This gives users per-process tabs without changing the persisted scopes.
- #52693 (`tabs.restore`, closed) used a separate boolean.

I have a small implementation and test plan ready if the approach sounds reasonable.

issues.body:
## Summary

After running OpenCode and exiting, GNOME Terminal keeps OpenCode’s Nord light background (`#ECEFF4`) and foreground (`#2E3440`) instead of restoring the terminal profile’s previous colors. The profile palette remains Solarized, so the terminal looks inconsistent outside OpenCode.

CodeWhale 0.10.2 was also used under the same GNOME Terminal profile and has an identical custom Nord theme, so the exact writer is not yet isolated.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.2.5
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04, Linux 6.8.0-149-generic x86_64
- Terminal: GNOME Terminal 3.44.0 using VTE 0.68.0; TERM=xterm-256color; COLORTERM=truecolor
- Shell: /bin/bash
- Install/channel: latest (local)
- Theme: nord, light mode
- Active plugins: `$HOME/.config/opencode/plugins/fetch-verbose`; TUI plugins `taller-tabs`, `timestamps-final`, `find-conversation`

## Reproduction

1. Open GNOME Terminal with the Solarized profile.
2. Run `opencode`.
3. Exit OpenCode normally.
4. Observe the terminal background and foreground remain OpenCode’s Nord light colors instead of the previous profile colors.

## Expected Behavior

OpenCode restores the terminal’s previous background, foreground, and palette on exit, or leaves the terminal profile colors untouched.

## Actual Behavior

The GNOME Terminal profile now has:

- `use-theme-colors=false`
- `background-color=rgb(236,239,244)` (`#ECEFF4`, Nord light)
- `foreground-color=rgb(46,52,64)` (`#2E3440`, Nord dark)
- `palette` still Solarized (`#002B36`, `#FDF6E3`, etc.)

The background and foreground match OpenCode’s Nord light theme, while the palette remains Solarized.

## Additional Context

- Frequency: observed after using OpenCode and CodeWhale in the same GNOME Terminal profile; not yet isolated to one app.
- `printf '\033]111\007'` has not been tested to see whether it restores the background.
- Disabling the TUI plugins has not been tested.
- OpenCode sets the renderer background from the active theme in `packages/tui/src/context/theme.tsx`.
- The embedded terminal pane emits OSC 4/10/11 sequences in `packages/tui/src/component/terminal-pane.tsx`.
- CodeWhale 0.10.2 is configured with `theme = "custom:nord"`; its `~/.codewhale/themes/nord.json` defines `surface_bg: "#ECEFF4"` and `text_body: "#2E3440"`, exactly matching the leaked profile values. CodeWhale’s binary includes OSC 11 handling, and its logs show `\x1b]11;?` / `\x1b]10;?` terminal probes.
- This may be a cross-application terminal state conflict. The primary request is that the application setting OSC 10/11 restores the previous colors on exit, or preserves the existing profile colors.
- Workaround: reset the GNOME Terminal profile colors with `gsettings`.

## Steps to isolate

1. In a fresh GNOME Terminal tab, run `printf '\033]111\007'` and `printf '\033]110\007'` to test whether the terminal resets dynamic background and foreground.
2. Reproduce with the TUI plugins disabled.
3. Reproduce with only OpenCode, then with only CodeWhale, to identify which application writes the profile colors.

labels.description: Terminal interface

issues.body:
### Description

Switching to a tab that is unread (or away from one that stays unread) runs the strip's unread glow through its release (900 ms) and ignition (600 ms) at 20 fps. The glow there signals a status change, but here only the selection changed, so the screen keeps redrawing for most of a second after every switch.

Measured on a TUI with four big sessions as tabs (a strobe bench, alt+down through the tabs): the screen settles 764 ms after a switch on the current code, 163 ms with the change below (−79%); frames per run 70 → 31; keypress-to-frame latency unchanged.

### Proposed change

`TabPulse` gets a `glowMuted` prop: a mute (the tab being selected) cuts the glow or brings it back at once, while a change of `glow` itself (the status) still ignites and releases. The horizontal strip passes the status glow and `glowMuted={selected() && !attention}`, which is the same combined glow as before. Its per-tab width, selection and activity accessors also become memos, so a spring tick only reruns the tabs whose values moved.

Commit in our fork: https://github.com/cevr/opencode/commit/12b16720e4

### OpenCode version

dev (fork based on it)

issues.title: tui: prompt and steer selected subagents

labels.name: gang-grill
labels.description: Design topics queued for later group grilling

issues.body:
## Problem

The V2 TUI can select a child Session, inspect its live activity, cycle between children, and interrupt one child without affecting its siblings. The selected child inspector is read-only, however: the composer remains owned by the parent Session.

This makes the most useful recovery loop impossible when one of several parallel subagents starts going in the wrong direction:

1. Inspect the problematic child.
2. Interrupt only that child if necessary.
3. Send it corrective instructions.
4. Let that child resume with its existing context while every sibling continues.

Today the user can perform steps 1 and 2, but not step 3 from the child inspector.

## Current V2 surface

The compact TUI already has the right selection boundary:

- `session.child.first` opens the subagent picker.
- Selecting a child opens its read-only inspector.
- `composer.subagent.interrupt` interrupts that selected child Session.
- `Tab` cycles through child Sessions.
- `Esc` returns to the parent composer.

Selection currently changes only the observed child transcript. It does not retarget prompt submission.

## Proposed interaction

When a child is selected, show a composer whose target is explicitly that child Session:

```text
◔ Inspect session execution    Explore    ctrl+d interrupt    1 of 5

  Search "SessionExecution"
  Read packages/core/src/session/execution.ts
  I’m tracing the ownership path...

┃ Message Explore...
```

### Soft steer

Submitting while the child is running should admit a prompt to the selected child with `delivery: "steer"`.

```text
select child
→ type correction
→ submit
→ correction is promoted at the child’s next safe step boundary
```

The active provider request or tool is not cancelled. Sibling Sessions are unaffected.

### Hard redirect

The existing targeted interrupt remains available:

```text
select child
→ interrupt selected child
→ type correction
→ submit
→ child wakes with the correction and retained history
```

The interrupt must affect only the selected child. Prompt submission after interruption must target that same child Session, not the parent.

## Existing V2 capabilities

This should not require a new child-specific protocol:

- Child agents are real Sessions with stable Session IDs.
- `POST /api/session/:sessionID/prompt` already supports durable admission, `delivery: "steer" | "queue"`, and wake scheduling.
- `POST /api/session/:sessionID/interrupt` already targets one Session.
- A steer can be admitted while the child is running and promoted at its next safe model-step boundary.

The primary missing piece is TUI target routing and presentation: the selected child must become the composer target while the inspector is open.

## Prior art

Claude Code’s in-process teammate view is the closest interaction: selecting a teammate replaces the visible transcript, `Esc` interrupts only that teammate’s current work, and the normal composer submits into that teammate’s pending-message queue. The teammate resumes with retained history while siblings continue.

Grok Build allows inspecting and individually cancelling a subagent, but its child view is intentionally read-only.

Current Codex V2 allows inspecting and interrupting a parent-owned child thread but disables direct child input; follow-ups are mediated through the parent. Older direct-input-capable Codex threads instead route the composer to the active child thread and use steer-or-start semantics.

## Gang grill

Decisions to pressure-test before implementation:

- Should Enter in a running child always mean `steer`, or should the normal parent default of queueing active-turn submissions remain consistent?
- Is the inspector composer visibly distinct enough to prevent accidentally prompting the child instead of the parent?
- After a targeted interrupt, should the inspector remain open and focused on an empty child composer?
- Should there be an atomic “interrupt and send” operation, or is interrupt-then-submit sufficient? Ordering matters because interruption clears an advisory pending wake unless continuation is requested.
- Can completed and failed children be continued from the same inspector, or only running/interrupted children?
- Should child composer drafts be preserved independently when cycling with `Tab` or returning to the parent?
- How are child permission and form requests represented while the user is directly viewing that child?
- Does direct human prompting change parent ownership or completion-notification semantics?
- Should the parent agent receive an explicit durable fact that the human redirected its child, or is that derivable from child history?
- Is this interaction intentionally human-only, or should the parent also gain a first-class tool for steer/follow-up against an existing child Session?

## Acceptance criteria

- A selected child inspector exposes a composer clearly labeled with the child target.
- Submitting from that composer sends the prompt to the selected child Session ID.
- A running child can receive a soft steer without interrupting its current physical attempt.
- An interrupted, idle, or completed child can be continued with retained history, subject to the decisions above.
- Interrupting or prompting one child does not interrupt, prompt, or otherwise mutate sibling Sessions.
- Returning to the parent restores the parent composer and its draft.
- Cycling between children cannot send a draft to the wrong Session.
- API failures are shown in the child inspector rather than silently dropping the correction.
- Tests cover target routing, soft steer, interrupt-then-prompt, child switching, and sibling isolation.

## Related

- #41667 requests direct prompting of child sessions in web/desktop.
- #38966 requests per-subagent steer/cancel/abort across parent tools and TUI.
- #36423 tracks V2 subagent resume and steering compared with V1.

issues.title: session: an interrupted turn stores only "interrupted" — the reason (user/shutdown/superseded/inactivity) is dropped

labels.name: type/feature
labels.description: New behaviour or an improvement

labels.name: area/sessions-storage
labels.description: Sessions, history and stored data

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/windows
labels.description: Windows

issues.body:
## Summary

When a turn ends abnormally, the durable record is only this — `session_message` row of type
`idle`:

```json
{"time": {"created": 1794678199239}, "outcome": "interrupted"}
```

plus `session_v2.idle_outcome = "interrupted"`. The reason *is* known to the event schema —
`session.execution.interrupted` carries `data.reason` with `"user" | "shutdown" | "superseded" |
"inactivity"` — but it never reaches the persisted idle message, the session row, or the log. After
the fact it is impossible to tell "the user pressed Stop" from "the turn was stopped by the
runtime".

## Environment

- opencode desktop `2.2.5` (Windows 11, win32 x64; `session.version` in the DB is `1.18.25`)
- provider/model: `commandcode` / `deepseek-v4-flash` (variant `max`)
- plugin active: `@cortexkit/opencode-magic-context` (declared for transparency — it reads the
  session DB; no evidence it is involved)
- DB: `%LOCALAPPDATA%/../.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`

## What happened

One session, one turn, no user action in between:

| time (local) | event |
|---|---|
| 20:10:17 | user message "Применяй" (start of a long apply phase) |
| 20:10:17 – 20:43:18 | 116 assistant steps: normal streaming, tool calls, edits |
| 20:43:18.187 | last assistant step completes normally (`time.completed` set, its `edit` tool `completed`) |
| **20:43:19.239** | **`idle` message: `{"outcome": "interrupted"}`** |
| 20:43:19 – 04:07:39 | **no messages at all** (7 h 24 m) |
| 04:07:39 | next user message "продолжай" |

Facts that exclude two of the four reasons:

- The app was not restarted: a single `app starting` in the desktop `main.log` (2026-11-11) and the
  `run=` id in `log/opencode.log` is unchanged across the event. Also, per the client code,
  `session.execution.interrupted` with `reason === "shutdown"` does not insert an idle message at
  all — and one was inserted.
- No prompt was sent between 20:10 and 04:07, so `superseded` cannot apply.

That leaves **`user`** (someone pressed Stop) and **`inactivity`** (a watchdog). Both are plausible
from the outside, and the stored data does not distinguish them. The user reported the session as
"working for 8 hours" — from the UI he could not tell either.

## Impact

- A post-mortem cannot answer "who stopped the turn" — the only question that matters when a long
  phase ends silently. We spent ~30 minutes excluding causes by inference (app restarts, log gaps,
  CLI restarts) before we could say "either a manual Stop or a watchdog".
- Upstream support suffers the same: reports of "the session stopped by itself" cannot be triaged
  into "user action" vs "runtime bug" without asking the user to remember.
- `idle_outcome` in `session_v2` is the only machine-readable field, and `interrupted` is the union
  of four different situations.

## Proposal

1. Persist the reason next to the outcome: `{"outcome": "interrupted", "reason": "user"}` in the
   `idle` message, and/or `session_v2.idle_reason`. It is already in the event
   (`session.execution.interrupted`), so this is a write-through, not new logic.
2. One log line with the same fields (`session.execution.interrupted reason=inactivity`) would make
   `log/opencode.log` sufficient for triage.
3. If the runtime intentionally collapses the reasons (e.g. to keep the client schema small), please
   say so in the docs — then clients can at least stop guessing.

## Reproduction

Not reproducible on demand; the record is durable, so it can be inspected:

```sql
-- the idle record of the turn
SELECT seq, type, data FROM session_message
WHERE session_id = 'ses_fa89d5398ffemRwpQF9eLetB3d' AND type = 'idle';

-- what the session row keeps
SELECT idle_outcome, time_idle, time_suspended, time_busy FROM session_v2
WHERE id = 'ses_fa89d5398ffemRwpQF9eLetB3d';
```

## Additional Context

Different shape from #61490 (a `bash` call that never returns keeps its step `running` for 8 hours
until a manual stop). Here the last step completed cleanly and the *next* step never started — so
whatever ended the turn happened between steps, which is exactly the case where the reason would be
decisive.

issues.title: run --format json omits every subagent event (still in 2.x, see #49300)
issues.body:
### Description

`opencode run --format json` prints nothing a subagent does. Only events from the root session reach stdout: the subagent's shell calls, text and steps are dropped, and the root's `subagent` tool_use appears only once the subagent has finished. A headless consumer can't show progress, or see where a long subagent got stuck.

#49300 reported this against 1.18 and was closed for 2.0. It is still there in 2.2.1 and 2.2.3. `packages/cli/src/run/noninteractive.ts` skips every event whose `sessionID` isn't the root one (`:236` at v2.2.1, `:239` at v2.2.3), while `ownsSession` a few lines up already follows `parentID` so that subagent permission prompts are answered. On `dev` after #61911 the same check is at `:172`.

### Plugins

none

### OpenCode version

2.2.3 (same on 2.2.1)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Point the `openai` provider at a stub Responses endpoint (`OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` with `baseURL`) and run `opencode run --standalone --format json --auto --model openai/gpt-test -- "go"` with an empty HOME.
2. The stub answers the root's first turn with a `subagent` call (`agent: general`). It answers the child's first turn with `shell` `echo child-ran`, and every turn that carries a tool result with plain text.
3. The stub receives the child's requests, and the child's shell result (`child-ran`) comes back to it, so the subagent ran.
4. stdout has only root-session lines: `step_start`, `tool_use` (`subagent`, whose `metadata.sessionID` names the child), `step_finish`, `step_start`, `text`, `step_finish`. Nothing from the child session.

### Operating System

Linux Mint 22.3 (Ubuntu 24.04 base), x64

### Terminal

none (headless)

Downstream: alpha-omega-security/scrutineer#1318, where an 8-hour run timed out inside a subagent with no trace of what it was doing.

issues.body:
### Description

When an OpenCode directory wakes up after `location services evicted` (or immediately on boot) and sends a prompt using `github-copilot/gemini-4-hydrogen`, the step fails with HTTP 400 (`unsupported_api_for_model`):

```
Session.StepFailedError: model gemini-4-hydrogen does not support Responses API.
```

From `opencode.log` and `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/github-copilot.ts`:
- At `location services booted` (e.g. `16:12:44.176Z`), `ProviderRefresh.start` loads Copilot's `/models` list asynchronously in the background (taking ~2.4s until the second `provider.updated` / `model.updated` at `16:12:46.563Z`).
- Before that sync completes, `/api/provider/github-copilot` exposes default package `@opencode/ai/providers/openai/responses`, and `gemini-4-hydrogen` is not in `models.dev`.
- Any turn dispatched in that startup window sends `gemini-4-hydrogen` to `/responses` instead of `/chat/completions`, so Copilot rejects it with HTTP 400 (and retries inside `SessionRunner.drain` reuse the pre-sync route).
- Once the background `/models` sync completes, `/api/model` shows `gemini-4-hydrogen` updated to `@opencode/ai/providers/openai-compatible`, and the next prompt succeeds normally.

Related: #53712, #53961 (#62034 fixed `fallbackEndpoint` for `gemini-*` in `packages/core/src/github-copilot/models.ts` and #63146 cached the login `baseURL`, but the pre-sync window before `loaded.models` arrives still hits this on config-overridden / non-`models.dev` Gemini models).

### Plugins

None affecting providers (`claude-mem` local session plugin only)

### OpenCode version

2.3.0

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set `model: "github-copilot/gemini-4-hydrogen"` with a `providers.github-copilot.models["gemini-4-hydrogen"]` entry (for example `settings.reasoningEffort`) using an authenticated GitHub Copilot account whose `/models` serves `gemini-4-hydrogen` on `/chat/completions`.
2. Leave a directory idle until `location services evicted` (or restart `opencode service`).
3. Send a prompt immediately on wake/boot before `GithubCopilotPlugin`'s background `/models` sync finishes (~2–3s).
4. Observe `model gemini-4-hydrogen does not support Responses API.` (`400 unsupported_api_for_model`). Sending another prompt a few seconds later succeeds once `model.updated` switches `gemini-4-hydrogen` to `@opencode/ai/providers/openai-compatible`.

### Operating System

macOS 26.x (Darwin 25.6.0, arm64)

### Terminal

Ghostty (xterm-ghostty, truecolor)

issues.title: 2.2.5: plugin tool definitions with JSON Schema $ref are all rejected ("evaluating 'a.ref'") and the tools vanish
issues.body:
### Description

In 2.2.5, every tool definition supplied by a plugin is rejected at registration when its `args` is plain JSON Schema containing `$ref`/`$defs`. Each is logged and dropped:

```
level=ERROR message="Skipping invalid tool registration" name=read namespace=undefined
  error="Invalid tool definition read: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'a.ref')"
```

With `@cortexkit/aft-opencode` installed this is destructive: the plugin replaces the built-in `read`, `write`, `edit`, `patch`, `shell`, `grep` and `glob` tools with its own, the replacements are skipped, and nothing is registered under those names — so the session has no filesystem or shell tools at all. 21 tool names from that one plugin were rejected, every one with the identical `a.ref` error.

Same machine, same config, same plugin version on 2.2.0: zero rejections, all tools present. The breakage began with the automatic update 2.2.0 → 2.2.5.

### Plugins

`@cortexkit/aft-opencode@0.62.0`. Also reproduces with `0.60.0`, so it is not specific to one plugin release.

The plugin builds tool `args` with Zod 4.1.8 `toJSONSchema()`, so any reused or recursive shape is emitted as `{"$ref": "#/$defs/..."}` plus a top-level `$defs` block. My reading of the error is that the validator dereferences `$ref` and hits an undefined node — flagging it as a hypothesis, I did not trace the 2.2.5 code path itself.

### OpenCode version

2.2.5 — broken. 2.2.0 — works.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install `@cortexkit/aft-opencode` (0.60.0 or 0.62.0) in `opencode.json`.
2. Run 2.2.5 (or let an existing install self-update to it).
3. Send any message so plugin tools get registered.
4. Every plugin tool is skipped; `read`/`write`/`edit`/`shell` are missing from the session.
5. `opencode upgrade v2.2.0` then `opencode restart` — all tools register, no errors.

### Screenshot

```
timestamp=2026-10-31T00:19:12.857Z level=ERROR run=50c39cff message="Skipping invalid tool registration"
  name=read namespace=undefined error="Invalid tool definition read: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'a.ref')" role=server
timestamp=2026-10-31T00:19:12.857Z level=ERROR run=50c39cff message="Skipping invalid tool registration"
  name=write namespace=undefined error="Invalid tool definition write: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'a.ref')" role=server
```

Rejected names: `read write edit patch shell bash_status bash_write bash_watch bash_kill aft_delete aft_move aft_outline aft_zoom aft_safety aft_import aft_callgraph ast_grep_search ast_grep_replace aft_search aft_inspect grep glob`

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS on WSL2 (kernel 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2)

### Terminal

Windows Terminal, `TERM=xterm-256color`

### Additional context

- 2928 occurrences over ~5 hours. First at `2026-10-31T00:19:12Z`, 36 s after the 2.2.5 server came up (`cli starting version=2.2.5`, `background service starting reason=version-mismatch previousVersion=2.2.0`); last at `2026-10-31T05:02:47Z`, immediately before the 2.2.0 downgrade. Nothing since.
- Rejection happens during tool registration/validation, before any plugin subprocess is spawned, so plugin runtime behaviour is not involved.
- `opencode upgrade v2.2.0` is a complete workaround; the failure returns as soon as an update to 2.2.5+ happens.

### AI assistance disclosure

AI was used in this submission: an AI coding agent collected the log excerpts and environment details above and drafted this report. All log lines quoted are verbatim from the affected machine.

issues.title: V2: Reconcile provider catalogs with /models endpoints
issues.body:
## Problem

V2 should reconcile each provider's model catalog with the provider's `/models` endpoint instead of relying only on a static or stale catalog.

Today this can fail in both directions:

- models exposed by the provider may be missing from OpenCode
- models no longer exposed or usable by the provider may remain selectable

That leaves new models unavailable and stale or irrelevant models visible until hardcoded metadata catches up.

## Desired behavior

- Fetch model availability from supported providers' `/models` endpoints.
- Merge endpoint results with OpenCode metadata needed for capabilities, limits, variants, and display names.
- Drop models that the authoritative endpoint does not expose or marks unavailable for the current account or organization.
- Preserve explicitly configured custom models where appropriate.
- Define fallback behavior when discovery is unsupported, unauthenticated, malformed, or temporarily unavailable.
- Refresh without making startup or model selection depend indefinitely on a slow provider.

## Acceptance criteria

- A newly exposed provider model becomes selectable without a static catalog update when the endpoint supplies enough information.
- A model removed from the endpoint is no longer offered unless explicitly configured or covered by a documented fallback.
- Account- or organization-scoped model lists are respected.
- Endpoint failures retain a usable bounded fallback and surface diagnostics without silently replacing a known-good catalog with an empty list.
- Tests cover additions, removals, explicit overrides, scoped availability, malformed responses, and request failure/timeout.

## Related scope

This is broader than generic OpenAI-compatible custom-provider discovery: it covers V2's model-catalog reconciliation and filtering semantics across providers that expose authoritative model-list endpoints.

issues.title: core: remaining text cuts can split UTF-16 surrogate pairs

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: area/core
labels.description: Agent loop, tools and config

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

issues.body:
### Describe the bug
Follow-up to #63967 (`fix: keep text cuts from splitting characters`). A few remaining `.slice()` truncation sites in `packages/core/src` can cut in the middle of a UTF-16 surrogate pair (for example, an emoji at the cut boundary), leaving a lone surrogate in text sent back to the model (which providers such as Anthropic reject with a 400 `"no low surrogate in string"` error):

- `packages/core/src/session/runner/publish-llm-event.ts:626` (`value.slice(0, INPUT_EXCERPT_LIMIT)` where `INPUT_EXCERPT_LIMIT = 2048`)
- `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/mcp-events.ts:183` (`fence(data.slice(0, DATA_LIMIT))` where `DATA_LIMIT = 16384`)
- `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/edit.ts:234` (`line.slice(0, hintLineLength)` where `hintLineLength = 200`)
- `packages/core/src/mcp/stdio.ts:181` (`(stderr + output).slice(-STDERR_TAIL)` where `STDERR_TAIL = 4096`)

### Expected behavior
Use `TextBoundary.head` / `TextBoundary.tail` so truncation never splits a UTF-16 surrogate pair or produces ill-formed strings.

prs.title: fix(server): answer handler defects with a readable 500 instead of an empty one
prs.body:
A request that hits an unexpected failure in a handler now gets a 500 with a JSON body instead of an empty one. When the failure is a storage error, the body says so.

Before, a defect (anything a handler didn't turn into a declared error) reached the client as `500` with no body. The common real case is SQLite failing to write: on a full disk, sending a prompt returned an empty 500, so clients had nothing to show.

```text
POST /api/session/:id/prompt  (disk full)
  before: 500  ""
  after:  500  { "_tag": "UnknownError", "message": "Storage error: database or disk is full", "ref": "err_1a2b3c4d" }

any other defect
  before: 500  ""
  after:  500  { "_tag": "UnknownError", "message": "Server failed to handle the request. Check server logs for details.", "ref": "err_…" }
```

**How it works.** A global router middleware (`packages/server/src/middleware/defect-response.ts`) asks Effect what it would answer for the failure (`HttpServerError.causeResponse`). Only when that answer is the empty 500 does it log the cause with a `ref` and the route, and respond with the existing `UnknownError` shape instead. That's the same shape and wording as the response-encoding failure in `schema-error.ts`. Everything Effect already answers keeps its response: declared errors, route-not-found, defects that carry their own response, aborted requests. `StorageFailure.message` (`packages/core/src/database/storage-failure.ts`) finds the SQLite result code under the query error (disk full, read-only, I/O error, locked, corrupt, can't open). Only those get their reason in the message, so a buggy query never sends SQL or data to the client.

**Limits.** No status codes change and no endpoint contracts change. 500 is declared (as `UnknownError`) on only some endpoints, so the generated client parses the body on those. On the rest, including `session.prompt`, it still reports `UnexpectedStatus: 500` without reading the body. Getting the message into the TUI on a failed send is a follow-up.

**Tests** (`packages/server/test/defect-response.test.ts`):
- a prompt on a real full disk (`PRAGMA max_page_count`) returns the storage reason
- a non-storage defect returns the generic message with a ref
- an unknown route still returns 404

Both behavior tests fail without the middleware. The server suite passes (129, isolated HOME), and `bun typecheck` in server and core and `bun run check` pass.

### Issue for this PR

Part of #40111. Stacked on #60039 (per-server `tls` config); once that lands, this diff is just the first-use flow.

### Type of change

- [x] New feature

### What does this PR do?

Trusting a private-network MCP server's self-signed certificate becomes a first-use decision instead of up-front TLS config:

1. The first connect to an `https` server at a private IP fails with the presented certificate — fingerprint, subject — and the command to trust it.
2. `opencode mcp trust <url>` shows the certificate's subject, validity, and fingerprint and asks for confirmation. `--yes` skips the confirmation (required without a terminal); `--force` is only needed to re-pin after the certificate rotated.
3. The pin is stored per project in a new `mcp_trusted_host` table (new migration). Later connects are pinned by fingerprint, so a rotated certificate fails the connection instead of being silently accepted, and certificates without IP SANs work because the fingerprint is the identity check.

The trust hint is only added for actual TLS verification failures (self-signed, expired, alt-name, and the Node-style codes); network, protocol, and HTTP failures keep their original message. Hostnames never qualify — the IP literal in the config is the trust boundary, not DNS. An explicit `tls` config takes precedence.

Related: #23506, #14696, #26862, #1694

### Type of change

### What does this PR do?

Adds an optional `tls` block to remote MCP server config, so a server with a self-signed or private-CA certificate can be trusted for that one server without changing verification anywhere else (no `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`):

prs.title: fix(core): preserve UTF-8 across shell output pages
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Found while testing shell output pagination.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

If 😀 starts at byte 65,535, the default shell output page used to decode its first byte alone. Now the page ends at byte 65,535 and the next read returns the whole character. A one-byte limit can return that one character to make progress. A tail seek inside it resumes after it.

The reader checks up to three bytes on either side of the page. It holds an incomplete character while the command runs and decodes leftover bytes at exit. The TUI uses its regular poll interval when a live read cannot advance. Persisted files keep their original bytes. This fix ships without a flag.
