## What failed

`check-test / e2e (windows, app-2)` failed in `e2e/regression/timeline-stream.spec.ts` (`background shortcut` group) and `e2e/regression/timeline-geometry.spec.ts` (`scrolls the timeline behind the composer region`, both variants). The errors: no `move running work to the background` button, no `1 subagent` pill, and no `(background)` text on subagent cards.

## Root cause

These tests are stale; the failure is not flaky. `66e2fb94b` (feat(core): always run subagents in the background) removed three things:

- the `(background)` suffix on subagent cards;
- the background hint for running subagents (only a running shell shows it now);
- counting a running subagent call with no child session yet in the activity pill. A subagent now counts only while its child session runs, in session-list order, with blocking work no longer first.

`ffcaeec36` (refactor(app): remove leftover foreground subagent UI) then removed the pill action that scrolled to a subagent's call; a subagent row now opens the child session's page. The tests still asserted the removed behaviour.

It fails the same way locally on Linux at the failing commit and at `ffcaeec36`, and reverting the only app commit in the window (`6c34e2448`) does not help. The earlier green runs most likely had these spec files in another shard: Playwright splits whole spec files across shards by test count.

## Fix (tests only)

- **`counts a backgrounded subagent…`**: expects `Stale task` and no `(background)`, like the existing `does not offer a running subagent to the background` test.
- **`separates blocking and already-backgrounded work…`**: expects no `(background)` suffix and no background hint, and lists the menu rows in session-list order.
- **`scrolls the timeline behind the composer region`**: the fixture adds a running shell call, so the hint row whose layout the test measures still appears.
- **`holds a revealed call … just under its stuck group header`** (3 variants): removed. They clicked a subagent row in the pill to scroll to its call in the timeline, and `ffcaeec36` removed that action on purpose. Please check this deletion in review.

### Issue for this PR

Closes #61665

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

Some models emit literal `\r` control characters at token boundaries inside tool-call arguments (forensics in #61665). The TUI renders each `\r` as a hard line break, so a one-line question shows up as shredded fragments in the `# Questions` block, and the tool's answer echo re-injects the `\r` into model context — in one observed session the consecutive-`\r` count in question inputs grew from 1 to 7 over ~24 calls.

The fix strips `\r` at the boundaries that own the concern:

- `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/question.ts`: the executor cleans headers, questions, and option labels/descriptions before building the form, the answers metadata, and the model-facing echo. This breaks the feedback loop.
- `packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx`: `parseQuestions` / `parseQuestionAnswers` clean the persisted part data, so completed blocks render as continuous text, including sessions stored by older versions.
- `packages/tui/src/mini/tool.ts`: same cleanup for the mini question snapshot and scroll summary.

`packages/session-ui` (web/desktop) was left untouched: it renders the text through the DOM, where `\r` is whitespace rather than a line break, so there is no visible shredding to fix there.

prs.title: fix(session-ui): keep line comment focus when the diff redraws
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #63107

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Typing a line comment in the review panel while the agent edits that file loses focus on every redraw. Pierre takes the comment's host out of the page while it redraws the diff, the browser drops focus to the body, and the rest of what you type goes to the prompt.

Now the comment host remembers which of its elements had focus, and when Pierre hands the host back it puts focus there again, but only if focus is still on the body. If you clicked or tabbed away while the host stayed on the page, it forgets, so it never takes focus back from somewhere you moved it.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Added a component test that opens a draft on the desktop review preview, types, makes the agent edit the file, and keeps typing. On dev it fails because the comment box is no longer focused after the redraw. It passes here, 20/20 with `--repeat-each=10`, and on a cold Vite cache.
- A second test clicks away from the draft before the edit and checks that focus stays away. It passes on both dev and this branch.
- Checked locally that it also works on a large virtualized diff, when focus moves to another input or the draft is cancelled, and when no `focusout` reaches the host on removal (as in Firefox). I only tested in Chromium.
- `session-review-comments`, `line-comment-v2`, `file` and `file-viewer` component tests pass, and so does `bun run check`.

prs.title: fix(ai): accept developer messages in native compaction responses
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #63434

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Hi folks, hope you're all doing well! Thanks a lot @ngbrown for the clear report with the redacted response shape, and for the mock repro in the thread, that made this easy to pin down.

Native compaction failed with `Invalid compaction response` whenever the session had a live instruction update in it, and this PR lets those updates come back through compaction.

`packages/ai/src/protocols/utils/responses-compaction.ts` calls `/responses/compact` for OpenAI, Azure and xAI, decodes the returned window with the `Response` schema, and turns each item into a `Message` that the next request replays.

**Before**

1. A session gets an `AGENTS.md` change, so `lowerMessages` sends it as `{ type: "message", role: "developer" }`.
2. Compaction runs and `/responses/compact` returns that developer message inside the window, as the API docs allow.
3. `Response` only accepts message items with role `user` or `assistant`, so decoding fails.
4. The whole compaction fails with `provider.invalid-output: Invalid compaction response`, even though the HTTP status is 200.

**After**

Same through step 2.

3. `Response` also accepts message items with role `developer` or `system` whose content is text parts.
4. `toMessage` turns them into `Message.system(...)`.
5. On the next request `lowerMessages` sends that system message back as a `developer` message with the same text, so the window replays as it came back.

```mermaid
flowchart LR

classDef box fill:#eef1ff,stroke:#4c5bd4,color:#111827
classDef bad fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px
classDef good fill:#c8f0c8,stroke:#008800,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px

subgraph BEFORE["BEFORE: compaction fails"]
direction TB
  B1["session with an AGENTS.md update"] --> B2["POST /responses/compact"]
  B2 --> B3["window keeps the developer message"]
  B3 --> B4{"Response allows user or assistant"}
  B4 -->|"developer role"| B5["Invalid compaction response"]
  B4 -->|"user or assistant"| B6["replacement window"]
end

subgraph AFTER["AFTER: compaction succeeds"]
direction TB
  A1["session with an AGENTS.md update"] --> A2["POST /responses/compact"]
  A2 --> A3["window keeps the developer message"]
  A3 --> A4{"THE CHANGE: also developer or system"}
  A4 -->|"developer role"| A5["Message.system, replayed as developer"]
  A4 -->|"user or assistant"| A6["mapped as before"]
end

B1 ~~~ A1

class B1,B2,B3,B6 box
class A1,A2,A3,A6 box
class B4,B5 bad
class A4,A5 good

linkStyle 3 stroke:#cc0000,stroke-width:5px
linkStyle 8 stroke:#008800,stroke-width:5px

style BEFORE fill:#fff5f5,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827
style AFTER fill:#f3fff3,stroke:#008800,color:#111827
```

The change is one new variant in the `Response` union and one branch in `toMessage`. I took `system` along with `developer` because the compact output schema lists both roles for input messages. A developer message holding an image or file still fails decoding, since `SystemMessage` only holds text and OpenCode never sends one like that.

One thing I'd love your take on: `SystemMessage` has no `providerMetadata`, so the item `id` and `status` of a developer message are dropped and the replay sends it without them (user messages keep theirs). That seemed fine to me since input message ids are optional, but happy to change it if you'd rather keep them. Any feedback or tips are very welcome!

### How did you verify your code works?

Added cases to `packages/ai/test/provider/explicit-compaction.test.ts` for OpenAI, Azure and xAI that compact a window with a developer and a system message, round trip it through JSON, and check the replay request. Also two rejection cases (empty developer content, developer image). The new test failed before the change. `bun test` and `bun run typecheck` in `packages/ai` pass.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.body:
## What failed

`check-test / e2e (linux|windows, app-2)` failed on `dev` in these tests:
- `timeline-geometry.spec.ts` › with a pointer / with touch › scrolls the timeline behind the composer region… (`session-background-hint-row` never appears)
- `timeline-stream.spec.ts` › background shortcut › counts a backgrounded subagent… (expects `Stale task (background)`)
- `timeline-stream.spec.ts` › background shortcut › separates blocking and already-backgrounded work into two rows (the background hint button never appears)
- `timeline-stream.spec.ts` › background shortcut › holds a revealed call … just under its stuck group header (×3, timing out on the `1 subagent` pill)

On Windows, the extra 60-second timeouts and retries also pushed the job past its 15-minute limit.

## Root cause

#63382 made subagents always run in the background:
- A running `subagent` call is no longer blocking work, so it no longer shows the "move running work to the background" hint.
- Subagent cards dropped the ` (background)` subtitle suffix.
- A subagent call without a child session no longer counts in the activity pill.

#63391 then removed the pill's "reveal a starting subagent call in the timeline" path (`onReveal` / `setRevealPart`). These e2e tests still asserted the old behaviour.

## Fix (tests only)

- **geometry test:** the fixture now has a backgrounded subagent, which keeps the `1 subagent` pill, plus a running shell, which shows the hint row. The geometry expectations are unchanged.
- **stale-call test:** expects the card text `Stale task` without the removed suffix. The pill-count checks are unchanged.
- **two-rows test:** the blocking work is now a running shell. The former foreground subagent is now a subagent call that still reads running, which counts as background work. Suffix checks are removed and the menu rows follow session order. The interrupt, shell-panel and kill checks are unchanged.
- **Deleted** the three `holds a revealed call … under its stuck group header` tests. They clicked a pill row that #63391 removed along with its code path. The scroll-to-call logic they covered is still in the timeline code, but nothing in the app triggers it any more. If e2e coverage is wanted, it needs a new way in.

## Verification

- Before: `bunx playwright test e2e/regression/timeline-stream.spec.ts e2e/regression/timeline-geometry.spec.ts --project chromium -g "background shortcut|scrolls the timeline behind"` → 7 failed, 6 passed, the same failures as CI.
- After: the full `timeline-stream`, `timeline-geometry` and `subagent-child-navigation` specs → 89 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `renders current protocol notices in CLI order`; it fails the same way without this change and isn't among the CI failures.
- `prettier --check` passes. The e2e typecheck reports no new errors in the changed lines.

prs.title: fix(core): commit a staged revert before a goal command queues work
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #62138

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

After `/undo`, a revert stays staged on the session. `Session.prompt` commits a staged revert before admitting new work, but a goal command sent after an undo — such as `/goal <objective>` — queued its kickoff behind the staged revert. The kickoff goes through `session.synthetic`, which stays held in the inbox while a revert is staged, so the goal showed as active but never ran. Committing after the command would be too late: the commit deletes inbox items after the revert point, including the kickoff itself.

The first version of this PR committed in `SessionCommand.execute`, which was too broad: it dropped the revert for every command, including ones that queue no work (`/goal pause`, `/goal clear`, `/goal` with no text, unknown commands, failing commands), permanently deleting the undone messages and redo history for nothing. This version moves the commit into the goal plugin, on the only two paths that actually queue work: the `resume` continuation and a new goal's synthetic kickoff. The attached-files path still goes through `Session.prompt`, which commits once preparation succeeds.

Committing inside `Session.synthetic` was considered and rejected: synthetic messages are deliberately parked while a revert is staged (#55394), and its background senders — subagent completions, shell results, the goal's own idle continuations — must not silently commit a revert the user is still deciding on.

To let the plugin do this, `session.revert` (stage/clear/commit — the existing stable `SessionApi` operations) is now part of the plugin session API (`SessionDomain` in both the Effect and Promise SDKs), wired through the plugin host. No new endpoint, no new flag: this fixes existing behavior.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New regression test in `packages/core/test/plugin/goal.test.ts`: "runs a goal commanded after an undo staged a revert" — two prompts finish, a revert is staged at the first prompt, then the `goal` command runs. Before this change the revert was still staged after the command and the goal never ran; after it, the revert is committed, the reviewer is asked once, and the goal completes.
- New tests pin the review feedback: `/goal` with no text, `/goal pause`, `/goal clear`, and an unknown command all leave a staged revert untouched; pausing an active goal leaves it untouched; resuming a paused goal commits it and the continuation runs to completion. Restoring the old unconditional commit makes the no-work test fail.

### Issue for this PR

### Type of change

- [x] New feature

### What does this PR do?

Adds an opt-in `prompt.history_scope` setting to the CLI config. `global` is the default and keeps today's behavior: Up and Down recall prompts from every session. `session` filters recall to the current session and gives each session its own cursor.

prs.title: fix(core): keep grep results when a match is not valid UTF-8
prs.body:
Closes #51912

## Problem
`RawMatch` in `packages/core/src/ripgrep.ts` required `path.text`, `lines.text`, and `submatches[].match.text` as mandatory strings. When `rg --json` encounters non-UTF-8 bytes, it emits base64 `bytes` fields instead of `text`, causing `Schema.decodeUnknownEffect(RawMatch)` to fail and abort the entire grep stream, discarding valid UTF-8 matches from other files.

## Fix
- Accept `{ text: string } | { bytes: string }` (`RawText`) for `path`, `lines`, and `submatches[].match` in `RawMatch`.
- Decode base64 `bytes` via `TextDecoder` when `text` is absent while preserving existing `normalizePath`, `MAX_LINE_CHARS`, and `MAX_SUBMATCHES` behavior.
- Add a regression test in `packages/core/test/ripgrep.test.ts` verifying valid UTF-8 matches survive alongside a non-UTF-8 matching file.

## Verification
- `bun test --cwd packages/core test/ripgrep.test.ts` (16 pass, 0 fail)
- `bun run --cwd packages/core typecheck` (no type errors across 1,981 files)

prs.title: feat(tui): show tool elapsed time in V2 clients
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Related to #50891. Supersedes #54361, which automated cleanup closed; it could not be reopened after the branch was force-pushed for this rebase. The V2 replacement for the closed V1 PR #50892.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Show tool execution duration in the V2 TUI and shared Web session renderer. Running tools update once per second from `time.ran`; completed and failed tools freeze at `time.completed`. Queued tools without a start timestamp show no duration. It uses the V2 wire schema rather than the V1 tool-state timestamps.

- **TUI**: inline tool rows, block tools (title and file header), and the shell command line render the duration next to their label. File path width is reserved for the timer so the path and duration fit on one row.
- **Web**: `BasicTool`-backed rows, tool error cards, file accordions, shell rows, skill rows, subagent rows, read groups, and grouped headers report the span of their parts, from the earliest start to the latest finish.
- **Reasoning and the working row**: the live timer anchors on the newest user prompt, so a follow-up sent while the previous turn still streams does not read minutes old, and neither timer jumps backwards when the new content takes over.
- **Subagents**: a background dispatch completes its own call at launch, so the timer follows the child session instead and freezes when it settles.
- **Accessibility**: the elapsed span is `aria-hidden`, so a timer that redraws every second never renames the row or group it belongs to for assistive tech. The frozen durations remain part of the rendered text.
- Durations use the existing `ui.message.duration.*` keys with locale-formatted numbers; no new copy.

Both of the old PR's hosts are covered, and the changed paths follow the current `dev` layout where the timeline row renderer moved (for example `timeline/session-timeline-row.tsx` and `message/message-content.tsx`).

### How did you verify your code works?

Rebased and ported onto `origin/dev` at `46744b64692`. Bun on this machine is 1.3.14, which lacks `bun check`, so `bun run typecheck:tsc` was used for typechecks and the pre-push hook was bypassed with `--no-verify` as on the original branch.

- `packages/tui` — `bun run typecheck:tsc` clean; `inline-tool-wrap-snapshot.test.tsx`: 13 pass, both snapshots unchanged, including a new case that ticks from `time.ran` and freezes at `time.completed`.
- `packages/tui` related suites (`group-view`, `prompt-shell-failure`, `completion-notices`, `app-lifecycle`): 47 pass. `dialog-shell-output` has two 5s timeouts on this Windows host that reproduce unchanged on `origin/dev`.
- `packages/app` — `bun run typecheck:tsc` clean; `test:unit` 2715 pass with 2 failures (`quote-comment-machine`, `global-sync/bootstrap` reconnect) that reproduce on `origin/dev`.
- `packages/app` e2e — the Working/background-shell, grouped-tool geometry, localized group label, and pending-steer queue cases pass; the group-text assertions were relaxed to allow the appended duration.
- `prettier --check` and `oxlint` on every changed file: clean.

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" role="img" aria-label="Three tool rows: a running shell counts 1s, 2s, 3s, while a finished read and write keep frozen durations">
  <style>
    .label { fill: currentColor; opacity: 0.6; font-size: 9px; }
    .timer { fill: currentColor; opacity: 0.45; font-size: 9px; text-anchor: end; }
    .bar { fill: currentColor; opacity: 0.14; }
    .tick { fill: currentColor; opacity: 0.8; font-size: 9px; text-anchor: end; }
    .t2, .t3 { opacity: 0; }
    .t1 { animation: step 3s steps(1, end) infinite; }
    .t2 { animation: step 3s steps(1, end) 1s infinite; }
    .t3 { animation: step 3s steps(1, end) 2s infinite; }
    @keyframes step { 0% { opacity: 0.8; } 33.333% { opacity: 0; } 100% { opacity: 0; } }
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
      .t1, .t2, .t3 { animation: none; }

    }
  </style>
  <g>

prs.title: fix(ssh): recover when the remote service port is taken
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #54059 

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

After the SSH connection dropped, reconnecting could fail with "Could not establish the SSH connection" even when SSH itself was working. The remote `opencode service start` failure was being reported as an SSH transport failure, and the managed port (49374 by default) can be occupied by an unrelated process because it sits inside the Linux ephemeral port range.

Changes:

- Remote command failures now keep their own step (`service`, `platform`, install, …). OpenSSH's reserved exit code 255 still maps to `connection`, so real transport failures are unchanged.
- The remote start script retries `service start`/`service restart` once with `--port 0` when the CLI reports the port is already in use. The registration file then records the actual URL, so discovery and the tunnel continue to work.
- `opencode service start`/`restart` accepts `--port` as a one-off override (0 = OS-chosen). It does not modify the saved port setting.
- The SSH dialog now shows the remote command's captured stderr under the error, so the cause is visible instead of only the generic message.

I chose to move the remote server to a free port rather than reuse the occupied one because the process holding the port does not belong to OpenCode.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun run check`
- `bun test src/ssh` in `packages/gui-plugins` — 55 pass
- `bun test test/service-lifecycle.test.ts test/service.test.ts` in `packages/cli` — 37 pass. The new lifecycle test occupies the configured port, confirms `service start` fails with "already in use", then confirms `service start --port 0` registers and serves on a different port.
- `ssh-reconnect.spec.ts` component tests — 8 pass. The new dialog test fails when the detail rendering is reverted.
- `bun run lint:changed`

### Screenshots / recordings

No screenshot present of the fix.

prs.title: refactor(browser): stream proxy traffic over binary WebSockets
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR No linked issue. ### Type of change - [ ] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [x] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation > [!TIP] > Over a remote connection with ~140 ms RTT, the 6 MiB image test went from **~70 s to ~4 s** (roughly **18× faster**, using rounded estimates). An uncached load of the [OpenCode docs](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs) went from **3.91 s to 1.48 s** (**2.6× faster**). ### What does this PR do? I was seeing very slow page loads in the desktop browser when connected to a remote server. The proxy sends traffic through JSON RPC in chunks of up to 64 KiB, waiting for a response before sending or requesting more. That gets expensive over a high-latency connection, especially for images and JS bundles. The bytes also have to be Base64 encoded. This replaces those calls with one binary WebSocket per TCP connection. A bounded sliding window controls buffering without waiting for a round trip after every chunk. Browser commands still use RPC. Authentication, origin checks, attachment ownership, connection limits, and TCP half-close are preserved. > [!WARNING] > Desktop and server must be updated together. The old transport is removed, and reverse proxies must allow WebSocket upgrades. ### How did you verify your code works? I tested both versions from the same desktop against the same remote server, with about 140 ms round-trip latency. The image test loads an uncompressed 6 MiB image with caching disabled: | Measurement | Before | After | |---|---:|---:| | Approximate image load time | ~70 s | ~4 s | Load times varied between runs. The ~4 s figure is a rounded estimate, not a calculated average. I also tested an uncached load of https://opencode.ai/v2/docs, transferring approximately 130 KiB across 6 requests: | Measurement | Before | After | |---|---:|---:| | First byte | 1.63 s | 0.75 s | | First visible content | 2.31 s | 1.08 s | | Full page load | 3.91 s | 1.48 s | These page timings are individual uncached loads, not averaged results. Tests cover transfers larger than the flow-control window, paused consumers, half-close, cancellation, malformed frames, authentication, and attachment ownership. Pre-push lint and typechecks pass. Four failures in the broader client tests also reproduce on the unchanged base. To repeat the image test, save the script below as `example.js` on the remote machine, run `node example.js`, and open `http://localhost:1337` in the desktop browser pane. Use matching desktop/server versions for each comparison. The script runs five uncached loads and reports their average.
Reproduction script: example.js No dependencies or supporting files are needed. ```javascript async function main() { const { createServer } = await import("node:http") const { randomFillSync } = await import("node:crypto") const port = Number(process.env.PORT || 1337) const image = Buffer.alloc(54 + 2048 * 1024 * 3) image.write("BM") image.writeUInt32LE(image.length, 2) image.writeUInt32LE(54, 10) image.writeUInt32LE(40, 14) image.writeInt32LE(2048, 18) image.writeInt32LE(1024, 22) image.writeUInt16LE(1, 26) image.writeUInt16LE(24, 28) image.writeUInt32LE(image.length - 54, 34) randomFillSync(image, 54) const html = Buffer.from(` Browser tunnel benchmark

Browser tunnel benchmark

Five uncached loads of a generated 6 MiB image. Run with each matching desktop/server version against the same remote server. The timer ends at the image load event, not painting.

    `) createServer((request, response) => { const path = new URL(request.url, "http://localhost").pathname const body = path === "/" ? html : path === "/heavy.bmp" ? image : undefined if (!body) { response.writeHead(404) response.end("Not found") return } response.writeHead(200, { "content-type": path === "/" ? "text/html; charset=utf-8" : "image/bmp", "content-length": body.length, "cache-control": "no-store", }) response.end(body) }).listen(port, "127.0.0.1", () => { console.log("Browser benchmark: http://localhost:" + port) }) } main().catch((error) => { console.error(error) process.exitCode = 1 }) ```

prs.title: fix: keep ids ascending across clock steps and never end Gemini requests on a model turn
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55514 (same user-visible error as #45359 / #47034; complements #55382)

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Gemini rejects any request whose `contents` end on a `model` turn. #55514 shows how v1 produces that shape without any prefill: `Identifier.create` mints IDs from `Date.now()` and only guards against two IDs in the same millisecond, parts are replayed in ID order, so when the wall clock steps backward inside a step (NTP correction, VM resume, WSL2) the tool part sorts before its own `step-start`. `convertToModelMessages` then opens a new block at that `step-start` and the step's reasoning ends up as a trailing assistant message.

Two changes:

1. `Identifier.create` keeps a `last` floor for wall-clock IDs and bumps any value that would not sort after it. Same-millisecond IDs come out exactly as before, explicit timestamps are minted as given and never touch the floor (`truncation.test.ts` depends on that), and descending IDs stay descending because the bump happens before the bit inversion. This stops new steps from being stored out of order.
2. `ProviderTransform.message`, for `@ai-sdk/google` and `@ai-sdk/google-vertex` only, drops a trailing reasoning-only assistant message (thought text is not something the model can continue from; the thought signature lives on the tool call, which keeps its result) and then primes a `user` "Continue." turn behind any other assistant tail, the same move as #55382 and the existing synthetic "Done." turn in `normalizeMessages`. Outbound only, so sessions that already contain a misordered step, and the compaction-continuation case from #55514, recover without rewriting stored history.

Not touched: message order still uses `time_created`, so a backward step can still swap two whole messages; each still ends on a tool result, which Gemini accepts.

### How did you verify your code works?

From `packages/opencode/`:

- `bun test ./test/id/id.test.ts`: on pristine `v1` the two backward-step cases fail; with the fix all 4 pass.
- `bun test ./test/id/id.test.ts ./test/provider/transform.test.ts ./test/tool/truncation.test.ts`: 614 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun run typecheck`: 0 errors before and after. Root `bun turbo typecheck` ran in the pre-push hook and passed. Prettier clean on the four files.
- Live replay against `gemini-3.8-flash` through `@ai-sdk/google` with the exact shape from the failing session: `[user, assistant(tool-call), tool(result)]` 200; plus trailing `assistant(reasoning)` 400 "Requests ending with a model turn are not supported."; same input through `ProviderTransform.message` 200. A text-only assistant tail: 400 unguarded, 200 with the primed turn.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: feat(cli): add pair --reset to discard a stuck OpenTunnel tunnel
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #54624

### Type of change

- [x] New feature

### What does this PR do?

Adds `opencode pair --reset` (requires `--remote`). It discards the stored OpenTunnel state and then runs the normal pairing flow, so a tunnel whose certificate issuance got stuck (for example during the opentunnel.xyz outage) can be replaced without deleting files under `~/.local/share/opentunnel/<profile>/` by hand.

`RemoteTunnel.reset()` calls the SDK's public `tunnel.remove()` (server-side removal for a completed tunnel) and then removes the profile directory. The directory removal is what clears a stuck pending issuance, because `remove()` only acts on completed tunnels. The handler stops the background service first, because it keeps retrying the wedged tunnel and can write the same profile while the reset runs. The service route is kept, so the pairing subdomain survives; only the tunnel hostname changes, because a new tunnel is created.

CLI-only: the flag, the handler wiring, and the small `RemoteTunnel.reset()` helper in `packages/cli`.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun test test/pair-remote-reset.test.ts` in `packages/cli` (4 pass): reset removes a planted stuck pending profile under an isolated `XDG_DATA_HOME`; reset succeeds with no stored tunnel; `pair --reset` without `--remote` exits 1; a refused first-time consent leaves the stored profile untouched.
- `bun test --timeout 30000 test/pair-remote-consent.test.ts` (5 pass) and `bun typecheck` in `packages/cli`.
- `bun run dev pair --help` shows the new flag:

```
  --reset         Discard a stuck OpenTunnel tunnel and start a new one (requires --remote)
```

The live end-to-end path needs a real tunnel, so it is written out as a reviewer script below.

### Screenshots / recordings

No visual change; CLI output is covered above.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

<details>
<summary>Reviewer test plan: reproduce the stuck pending tunnel without an outage</summary>

**Setup.** Tunnel data lives at `~/.local/share/opentunnel/default` (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/opentunnel/default`; Windows `%USERPROFILE%\.local\share\opentunnel\default`). A completed tunnel has `tunnel.json`, `token`, `private-key.pem`, `certificate.pem`, `chain.pem`; a pending issuance has `pending.json`, `token`, `private-key.pem`. `ensure()` resumes a pending identity instead of creating a fresh tunnel, which is the reported wedge.

**1. Plant an unresumable pending state**
- Back up the existing profile directory, then leave only a pending identity in place: either interrupt `bun run dev pair --remote --yes` as soon as `pending.json` appears, or write a minimal `pending.json` (`{"id":"...","hostname":"...","csr":"..."}`) next to the existing `token` / `private-key.pem`.
- Make the resume fail persistently: corrupt the `token` (append a character) or block `opentunnel.xyz`. A corrupted token fails fast with `Failed to start certificate issuance`; a blackholed network can take the 5-minute `ensure` timeout.

**2. Confirm the bug (same build, no flag)**

```bash
cd packages/cli && bun run dev pair --remote --yes
```

It keeps resuming the dead pending identity, fails again on every run, and leaves the files behind — the only recovery is deleting them by hand.

**3. Confirm the fix**

```bash
cd packages/cli && bun run dev pair --reset --remote --yes
```

The profile is discarded first, then `Setting up remote access; this can take a minute...` appears and a new tunnel is created with a fresh pairing link/QR whose hostname differs from the old `tunnel.json`.

**4. Completed tunnel, network on**
- `pair --reset --remote --yes` removes the old tunnel server-side, creates a new one, and restarts the service; the old remote URL stops serving.
- `pair --remote --yes` without the flag still reuses the existing tunnel and does not create a new one.

**5. Background service recovery (the original outage shape)**
- With a wedged pending state, the running service keeps logging `remote access tunnel unavailable; retrying` and `pair --remote` eventually times out with `Timed out waiting for the remote tunnel`.
- After `pair --reset --remote --yes`, the service restarts with the new tunnel and the warnings stop.

**Edge cases**
- Offline + completed tunnel: `tunnel.remove()` needs the API, so reset fails and keeps the local state (no server-side orphan). Offline + pending-only works, since that removal is local.
- The flag is destructive by design: it deletes the device-shared default profile used by the opentunnel CLI and other SDK apps.
- Reset only runs after first-time consent succeeds and with the background service stopped, so declining consent leaves the stored state untouched and a running service cannot race the reset.

</details>


---

_Added by the opencode bot (AI-generated)._

Related: #54596

Public API: adds the --reset flag to `opencode pair` (requires --remote; backwards compatible)

prs.body: ### Issue for this PR Closes #37267 This ports #39382 (closed as V1-only) to the current architecture. ### Type of change - [ ] Bug fix - [x] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? Adds a "Subagents" side-panel tab so subagent activity can be followed without being buried by the main agent's log stream, as described in #37267. The tab lists each subagent spawned by the current session with its task name, live status, cost, token usage and model. Clicking a row opens that subagent's session, which is the drill-down to its full output. New subagents appear at the top. A header button with a busy dot and a `+` menu entry open the panel. How it works, briefly: the panel is a `gui-extensions` side-region contribution (`packages/gui-extensions/src/agents`). Children come from the live sync store filtered by `parentID` plus a one-shot family backfill, so there is no polling and no per-child requests. Running/retrying state comes from the live status map; terminal states (completed / cancelled / failed) come from the parent session's `subagent` tool parts, mirroring how the header's background-task reader derives them (including `aborted` structured errors and synthetic completion notices). Foreground subagent calls that have no child session yet render as static Running rows. Status icons match the timeline's task cards (spinner while running, subagent glyph otherwise). Copy lives in the extension's own `i18n/en.ts` (62 locales ship translated). ### How did you verify your code works? - `bun test src/agents/` in `packages/gui-extensions` (33 tests): status derivation precedence (running part wins, backgrounded completions, synthetic-notice expiry, stale-part rejection, aborted/interrupted cancellation), children sorting/filtering, cost/token formatting, link shape. - `bun run typecheck` in `packages/gui-extensions`: clean. `oxlint` on touched files: 0 warnings. - `extension-graph` component spec: all built-ins including `agents` boot with every optional provider disabled. - Manually in Chromium against storybook with a seeded store: empty state, rows with cost/model/tokens, live Running → Completed transition in the same DOM node without remount, new rows appearing, cancel rendering, collapse/expand, search, tabs, sort, history detail. ### Screenshots / recordings ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.body: ### Issue for this PR Closes #50367 ### Type of change - [ ] Bug fix - [x] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? Ports #50368 to V2, as asked when it was closed. prs.title: fix(core): chunk session import message inserts under the SQLite parameter limit
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55433

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Session import writes every `session_message` row in a single `INSERT` (7 bound parameters per row). Transcripts with more than 9362 messages exceed Bun's SQLite 65536 bound-parameter limit per statement, so the import dies with a 500 (`SQLite query expected 264 values, received 65800` for a 9400-message payload).

This chunks the insert inside the same transaction, following the existing repo pattern (`InsertBatchSize` + sliced batches + `Effect.forEach`, as in `instruction-entry.ts` and the fork projection in `projector.ts`): 500 rows per statement = 3500 bound parameters, a wide margin under the limit even if the table gains columns. The batch size is a named constant next to the import code with the arithmetic in a comment.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New regression test imports a synthetic 9400-message transcript (binds 9400 x 7 = 65800 parameters, above the limit) and asserts the session plus all 9400 messages round-trip through export.

issues.title: Native MCP: publish connection status for custom footers

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
## Request

Please publish native MCP server connection status through Pi’s existing extension-status interface so custom footers can display it.

## Environment

- Pi 1.1.0
- Native MCP support
- `pi-footer` 0.5.1: https://github.com/wobondar/pi-footer

## Current behavior

The `/mcp` interface displays server connection states, tool counts, and errors.

Source inspection of the installed Pi 1.1.0 native MCP component shows that it does not publish a footer status through `ctx.ui.setStatus`.

`pi-footer` can display values published through that interface, but enabling an `mcp` status entry does not provide native MCP status because no value is published.

## Migration impact

Existing Pi MCP server extensions support publishing server status to footer extensions. Users who switch from those extensions to Pi’s native MCP support lose the persistent status indicator and must open `/mcp` to inspect connection states.

This request seeks feature parity for migrating users. Although this is not a regression within native MCP itself, it is a loss of functionality when replacing an MCP extension with native support.

## Requested behavior

- Publish native MCP connection status under a documented, stable status key.
- Update it as servers connect, disconnect, fail, or require authentication.
- Make the status available to both the standard footer and custom footers through the existing interface.

This request does not require Pi to depend on `pi-footer`.

## Classification

This is a feature request for native MCP status integration, not a claim that an existing supported feature regressed.

issues.title: pi-durable: a host restart mid-answer can leave a progress delta that makes the LiveDoc permanently unreadable

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

**Environment**

- `@earendil-works/pi-durable` 1.5.2 (latest on npm), `@earendil-works/chord` 1.5.2
- Cloudflare Workers / Durable Object SQLite storage (`SqliteStorage`), wrangler 4.160.0
- Reproduced on Node 26.10.0 (local `wrangler dev`)

**Frequency, up front:** this needs the host to die while a model answer is streaming, so it is rare — 1 document across ~100 conversations and ~1000 generation tasks in our local history. On a turn that completes, the path is never entered. We hit it by restarting the dev server mid-answer; a Worker eviction or a deploy during a stream is the same shape.

## What happens

A model answer is streaming. The host restarts while it is in flight. On resume the run records a retry, which is correct — but a progress commit belonging to the interrupted attempt is stored *after* it. That delta appends to `generation.message.content[0].thinking`, and the retry commit has already replaced `generation` with `{ attempt, retry }`, which drops `message`.

From then on the document cannot be read:

```
[pi] report {
  kind: 'storage_failed',
  error: PathError: unresolvable path: ["generation","message","content",0]
      at resolveValue (chord/dist/delta/index.js:503:19)
      at applyOps (chord/dist/delta/index.js:338:24)
      at SqliteStorage.materializeDocument (pi-durable/dist/storage/sqlite/storage.js:489:21)
```

`materializeDocument()` replays every delta from the last base on each read, so this fails every time, for that conversation, forever. It is not a one-off error report: the document is permanently unreadable and the library has no repair path. Every later request for that conversation reports `storage_failed`, which is how it shows up as a stream of identical reports rather than one.

## The stored evidence

`document_revisions` for the conversation's `LiveDoc`, in `seq` order (verbatim, truncated):

```json
seq 71 | delta | [["s",["generation"],{"attempt":1,"retry":{"at":1794671764380,"error":"The host stopped while the model was answering, on attempt 1"}}]]
seq 72 | delta | [["a",["generation","message","content",0,"thinking"]," the picture the EF projection to AB distance. OK.\n\nNow state…
```

Two things to note (line numbers are 1.5.2's `dist/harness/generation.js`):

- `:364` (`interrupted()`, and likewise `:639` on the failure path) sets `live.generation = { attempt, retry }`. That assignment **drops `message`**. `convertPartial()` has already turned the partial into an aborted entry, so nothing of the answer depends on `message` surviving.
- The delta that follows appends into `generation.message.content[0]`, whose parent no longer exists.



## Why the ordering lets this happen

`PROGRESS_COMMIT` is deferred (`live.js:41`) and documented as: "storage gets them together, at the next commit that reads or writes `pi.live` or after `settings.progress.persistWithinMs`. Every commit that consumes or clears streamed fields reads `pi.live`, so it stores them with its own changes."

That holds inside one invocation. It does not hold across a host restart: the interrupted attempt's flush is already in flight in the *previous* invocation, so the retry commit cannot see it and cannot carry it. Whichever way the two land in storage decides whether the document stays readable. In the case above the retry landed first (`seq 71`) and the append second (`seq 72`).

## Suggested fixes

Two independent problems; I would fix both.

1. **Ordering / ownership.** A progress delta belongs to an attempt. Either
   - a commit that clears `generation` (retry, outcome, `delete live.generation`) must be stored after any progress delta already issued for that attempt, or
   - a progress delta must be dropped when the document no longer holds the attempt it was computed against.

   Checking the attempt inside the flush's commit callback (patch below) closes the window where the flush reads the document *after* the retry commit has landed, but it does not close the in-flight case, where the delta was computed against the pre-retry document and only stored later.

2. **A bad delta should not poison the document.** `materializeDocument()` throws on the first unappliable delta, so a single stray op destroys every later read of that document — and the failure repeats on every read. A delta that cannot apply could be skipped and reported for that delta, leaving the document readable. For a missing parent specifically, `assignJson()` could fall back to assigning the whole value instead of the planned append.

The second one is the part we would most like, since it turns a permanent loss into a bounded one.

## Workaround

Deleting the stray revision restores the document (only the progress delta of an already-interrupted attempt is lost):

```sql
DELETE FROM pi_document_revisions WHERE document_id = ? AND seq = ?;
```

We are running a local `patch-package` patch of the guard from (1), because 1.5.2 is the latest version and the failure is permanent:

```diff
--- a/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-durable/dist/harness/generation.js
+++ b/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-durable/dist/harness/generation.js
@@ -524,6 +524,16 @@
             try {
                 await runtime.commit(async (tx) => {
                     const live = await tx.doc(LiveDoc, runtime.conversationId);
+                    const current = live.generation;
+                    if (current !== undefined && (current.retry !== undefined || current.attempt !== attempt))
+                        return undefined;
                     live.generation ??= { attempt };
                     changes.commit(live.generation, message, taken);
                     return undefined;
```

Happy to test a real fix against the same setup, and to say more about how the host restart was produced if that is useful.

### Steps to reproduce

## Minimal reproduction

The four batches below are exactly what pi-durable emits for one answer; they can be applied with chord's own applier, no storage needed:

```js
import { apply } from '@earendil-works/chord/delta'

const base    = { run: { taskId: 9, turns: 0 } }
const start   = [["s", ["generation"], { attempt: 1 }]]
const partial = [["s", ["generation", "message"],
                 { role: "assistant", content: [{ type: "thinking", thinking: "The answer is" }] }]]
const restart = [["s", ["generation"],
                 { attempt: 1, retry: { at: 1794671764380, error: "The host stopped while the model was answering, on attempt 1" } }]]
const stale   = [["a", ["generation", "message", "content", 0, "thinking"], " 112."]]

let value = apply(base, start)
value = apply(value, partial)
value = apply(value, restart)
value = apply(value, stale)
```

Output:

```
PathError: unresolvable path: ["generation","message","content",0]
```

### Expected behavior

_No response_

### Version

_No response_

issues.title: A codemode script fails before it runs when it declares a top-level variable named `tools`

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

Hello!
First thank you for creating Pi and numerous blog posts which truly resonate with me. I switched from Claude Code to Pi recently and it is like breath of fresh air.
I came across small issue and thought that you may be open for a PR to fix. My AI told me that I need to open issue first and got a lgtm before opening PR, that's why I am so detailed here. PR itself perhaps would be shorter 🙂 

So, here is what happened.
I configured a new mcp, called fluffyjaws, which is a knowledge base search assistant.
The problem is that when I ask him at the first time I see the following codemode block:
```
 codemode                                                                                                                                                             
 const tools = await searchTools('fluffyjaws');                                                                                                                       
 console.log(JSON.stringify(tools, null, 2));                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                      
 Script error:                                                                                                                                                        
 SyntaxError: invalid redefinition of parameter name                                                                                                                  
     at codemode.js:1:41                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                      
 No tool calls were made.                                                                                                                                             
 ```

On the next turn it recovers and everything works.

I talked with claude opus 5.5 model trying to understand if this is a bug or something which can be fixed upstream. And it turned out that the problem is in variable name `tools`. Here is what it told me:
> Models write `const tools = await searchTools(...)` on their own, so this happens without the user doing anything unusual. It costs a turn to recover. 
> The cause is that the script body is wrapped as `(async (tools, console) => { ... })` in `packages/codemode/src/runtime/vm.ts:327`, so those two names are function parameters.

I am happy to submit a small PR with the fix. Let me know if you're willing to accept such contribution.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `pi -ne` with codemode enabled
2. Ask pi to run **_exactly_** this codemode script:                                                                                                                       
    ```js
      const tools = await searchTools("read");
      return tools.length;
    ```

### Expected behavior
That script runs and returns a number.

### Actual behavior 
codemode ends up with an error:
```
Script error:
   SyntaxError: invalid redefinition of parameter name
       at codemode.js:1:41
```

### Version

1.3.0


### Potential approach for fix

`tools` and `console` are already globals: https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/bd3c9b823762b7383954aa49e13ee350471015fe/packages/codemode/src/runtime/prelude-source.ts#L451-L453 so the wrapper could be `(async () => { ... })`, without `tools` and `console` arguments:
https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/bd3c9b823762b7383954aa49e13ee350471015fe/packages/codemode/src/runtime/vm.ts#L327
A script's `const tools` would then hide the global for that script only. Line numbers and `"use strict"` would keep working.

issues.title: Session with >~120k entries after the last compaction fails to load: RangeError in  buildContextEntries

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

A long session stopped working. Every context rebuild threw `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`, and so did every extension call to `ctx.getContextUsage()`. After that, `pi --session  <file>` crashed on startup with the same error, even with `-ne`.

The session had 120,432 entries on the branch after its last compaction. Most were `context_edit` and custom entries, which add no messages: the context was only 402 messages.


The cause is the spread push in `buildContextEntries`:

```typescript
contextEntries.push(...path.slice(compactionIdx + 1))
```

This passes every entry after the compaction as a separate argument. The limit depends on stack depth. It fails at about 120k–150k entries at startup and below 80k when called from inside an extension event handler.

```bash
RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
     at buildContextEntries (dist/bundle/chunks/chunk-VEJDBY3O.js:521:2551)
     at buildSessionProjection (...:521:3299)
     at _SessionManager.buildSessionProjection (...:529:4822)
     at _SessionManager.buildSessionContext (...:529:4947)
     at createRuntime (...:1239:14996)
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Generate a session with 150k entries after a compaction:

```sh
node -e '
const fs=require("fs"),t=new Date().toISOString();
const
L=[{type:"session",version:3,id:"00000000-0000-7000-8000-000000000001",timestamp:t,cwd:process.cwd()},

{type:"message",id:"u1",parentId:null,timestamp:t,message:{role:"user",content:[{type:"text",text:"hi"}
],timestamp:Date.now()}},

{type:"compaction",id:"c1",parentId:"u1",timestamp:t,summary:"s",firstKeptEntryId:"u1",tokensBefore:10}
];
let p="c1";for(let
i=0;i<150000;i++){L.push({type:"custom",customType:"repro",data:{},id:"x"+i,parentId:p,timestamp:t});p=
"x"+i}
fs.writeFileSync("big.jsonl",L.map(x=>JSON.stringify(x)).join("\n")+"\n")'
```

2. Run `pi -ne --session ./big.jsonl`
3. Pi exits with the RangeError above. With 50k entries, the same file loads fine. 

### Expected behavior

The session loads. The number of entries should not be limited by the call stack. Appending in a
loop, or using `concat`, fixes it:

```typescript
for (const entry of path.slice(compactionIdx + 1)) contextEntries.push(entry); 
```

### Version

pi 1.5.2, Node v26.12.1, macOS 26.6.2

issues.body:
## Problem

Codemode encourages batching independent tool calls. When an agent reads `SKILL.md` through `tools.read()` inside a codemode call, the conversation displays the codemode call instead of the direct `[skill]` read. This makes skill activation harder to see and inspect.

In Pi 1.5.2, `dist/extensions/codemode/tool.js` defines the prompt guideline: “Use codemode to batch independent tool calls (Promise.allSettled), chain them, or filter large output, instead of many separate calls.” The agent followed this guidance to batch a skill read with a documentation read.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start a session with codemode enabled and a discoverable skill.
2. Ask the agent to read the skill and another independent file.
3. Have the agent batch both calls using `codemode` and `tools.read()`.
4. Compare the tool display with a direct `read` of the same `SKILL.md`.

## Actual

The batched read is presented as a codemode call. A direct read is displayed as `[skill]` with its line range and expandable content.

## Expected

Skill reads remain visible and expandable as `[skill]`, including when batched. Alternatively, route skill reads through direct read calls, including a parallel tool-call array of 1–8 calls where supported, while retaining batching for other work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A skill read is identifiable and expandable in the conversation when other independent reads run in parallel.
- [ ] Codemode guidance does not encourage hiding skill reads behind a single opaque tool display.
- [ ] Add a regression test for the chosen behavior.

## Notes

The `read` tool still executes inside codemode; the reported issue is presentation and discoverability, not a failure to load the skill. The 1–8 parallel tool-call array is a proposed alternative; its availability in every client is not verified.

issues.title: Fullscreen double-click should keep URL schemes and drop trailing periods

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

I want fullscreen double-click selection to keep URL schemes and leave out sentence-final periods.

I see this on pi 1.5.2, in fullscreen mode under herdr in Ghostty. `main` has the same code.

- Double-clicking anywhere in the path of `https://github.com/org/repo/pull/1` selects `//github.com/org/repo/pull/1`.
- In `see src/config/url.zig.`, double-clicking `config` selects `src/config/url.zig.`.
- Double-clicking the version in `Version v1.2.3.` selects `v1.2.3.`.

### Why?

When I double-click to copy a link or path from the transcript, I get a string that I have to fix by hand.

I searched open and closed issues and found none about URLs or trailing periods. I found #7746, which made `/` and `-` joiners, and #11340, which adopted iTerm2's word characters and fixed #10980.

### How? (optional)

`getWordSelection` in `packages/tui/src/tui-alt-screen.ts` joins `Intl.Segmenter` word segments using `TERMINAL_WORD_SELECTION_JOINERS`, currently `/ - + \ ~ _ .`. `:` isn't a joiner, so `https` and `:` stay separate. `.` is a joiner, so it joins a sentence's final period as well as the dots in `file.ts`.

If the double-clicked column is inside an OSC 8 link, select that link's text span. `getOsc8LinkAtColumn` already finds the link for single-click open. The markdown renderer leaves the period outside the link in `see https://github.com/org/repo/pull/1.`, so selecting the link's span also drops the period.

Outside a link, trim trailing `.` segments so the dots inside `file.ts` and `v1.2.3` still join. I wouldn't add `:` to the joiners because that would make `Note:` select with its colon.

### What happened?

    Pi is already installed at:
      /mnt/c/Users/<me>/.pi/agent/bin/pi

Windows-managed `~/.pi/agent`, and uninstall would delete the Windows
install entirely.

The signal it misses: that install's `managed-install.json` records
`"entrypoint": { "path": "C:\\...\\pi.cmd" }` — clearly a Windows
install — but `managed_install_root_for_command()` adopts it anyway.

2. Open any WSL2 distro (default config)
3. `curl -fsSL https://pi.dev/install.sh | sh`

Treat a `/mnt/*` existing install as foreign: ignore it and do a fresh
native install to `$HOME/.pi/agent`, e.g. in
`managed_install_root_for_command()`:

    Linux*)
      case "$managed_command_path" in
        /mnt/*) return 1 ;;
      esac

Happy to PR the guard once I have lgtm.

install.sh as of 2026-11-15; Windows managed install 1.5.2

issues.title: Uncaught AbortError when codemode cancels sibling file reads after ENOENT

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Summary
I reported this in Pi using `/bug`. Pi 1.5.2 exits with an uncaught `AbortError` after a codemode read fails.

## Environment
- OS: Windows
- Pi: 1.5.2
- Node.js: 26.7.0

## Observed sequence
A codemode request used `Promise.all` to read these paths:

- `pester/jSourceAssistant.BulkNotePreview.Tests.ps1` (exists)
- `pester/jSourceAssistant.BackendBoundary.Tests.ps1` (exists)
- `pester/CaseManager.JSourceBulkNoteSchema.tests.ps1` (does not exist)
- `docs/agents/domain.md` (exists)
- `GLOSSARY-MAP.md` (exists)

The missing path produced:

```text
ENOENT: no such file or directory, access '.../pester/CaseManager.JSourceBulkNoteSchema.tests.ps1'
```

Pi then reported the remaining reads as cancelled and exited:

```text
AbortError: The operation was aborted
    at stream.<computed>.AbortError.cause (node:internal/streams/add-abort-signal:47:22)
    at addAbortSignal (node:internal/streams/add-abort-signal:38:25)
    at FileHandle.createReadStream (node:internal/fs/promises:408:12)
    at Object.readLocalFileChunks (.../pi-coding-agent/dist/bundle/chunks/chunk-VEJDBY3O.js)
```

The stack's abort reason originates from `Execution.finish`, which aborts pending calls. The crash was recorded at `2026-11-14T14:37:08.605Z` in Pi's `crashes.json`.

## Expected behavior
An expected cancellation of sibling file reads should be handled as a normal cancelled tool call. Pi should not terminate with `uncaughtException`.

## Suspected cause
`readLocalFileChunks` passes an already-aborted signal to `FileHandle.createReadStream`. The resulting `ABORT_ERR` escapes during codemode teardown instead of being contained by the tool/execution boundary.

## Workaround
Avoid `Promise.all` for speculative `tools.read` calls, or validate paths first / use `Promise.allSettled`. The immediate trigger was the nonexistent test path, but the crash is in Pi's abort handling.

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

In fullscreen mode, pressing Cmd+C with an active selection should copy it. Today nothing happens: pi owns the selection, so the terminal has nothing to copy, and pi has no binding for super+c.

### Why?

Fullscreen is the default, and select + Cmd+C is the standard macOS copy gesture. With fullscreenCopyOnSelect: false the selection looks copyable but only Ctrl+X copies it, and nothing on screen says so. Claude Code binds cmd+c to its selection copy in fullscreen.

### How? (optional)

Bind super+c to copy the active selection whenever one exists, independent of fullscreenCopyOnSelect. I tested "app.message.copy": ["ctrl+x", "super+c"] in keybindings.json: it works in Rex with copy-on-select off. It only helps in terminals that forward Cmd through the kitty keyboard protocol.

issues.title: openai-completions loses SSE error codes and types before retry classification

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

With `openai-completions`, an HTTP 200 SSE response containing an error with `code: 503` ends the turn without retrying. Reproduced using `pi -ne`, isolated settings, and a local mock endpoint: one request, zero retries.

The OpenAI SDK throws an `APIError` with `status === undefined` but preserves the error body. `formatProviderError()` then returns only the message, discarding `code`/`type` before Pi's retry policy sees them.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a custom OpenAI-compatible provider and enable retry (`maxRetries: 1`).
2. Have its first chat request return HTTP 200 with `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, an empty assistant chunk, then:

```
data: {"error":{"message":"Unable to reach the model provider: Please try again in a moment.","code":503}}
```

3. Have the next request return a valid successful completion. Run `pi -ne -p --no-session --provider <provider> --model <model> "Reply with OK"`. The second request never arrives.

### Expected behavior

Preserve the error body so the existing policy retries transient failures and still rejects `insufficient_quota`. I have a minimal local formatter fix and regression tests using the real OpenAI SDK: 7 failures before the fix; all 80 related tests pass afterward.

Related: #7234 and #9702. This fix does not add public error fields. I'd like to submit it; requesting maintainer `lgtm` approval per CONTRIBUTING.md.

### Version

1.5.2; also reproduced in source-level tests at `c1d4b0ac3`.

issues.title: Make `developer` opt-in for OpenAI-compatible instruction messages
issues.body:
### What happened?

Both OpenAI adapters send `developer` to an unclassified endpoint when `model.reasoning` is true. In the Groq Qwen reproduction, changing only that role to `system` turned HTTP 400 into HTTP 200 with High still enabled. [Groq live reproduction in #10741](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10741#issuecomment-6666309265) · [Completions encoder](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/b729499585bd7dacf6e9bc52994c6f157e35f9c9/packages/ai/src/api/openai-completions.ts#L1226) · [Responses encoder](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/b729499585bd7dacf6e9bc52994c6f157e35f9c9/packages/ai/src/api/openai-responses-shared.ts#L273-L274)

### Steps to reproduce

Use a custom model at `https://example.invalid/v1` with one system instruction and one user message. Call each adapter with a dummy key, record the first role from `onPayload`, then throw from the callback to stop before transport. Both adapters produced these results offline.

| `model.reasoning` | `compat.supportsDeveloperRole` | Observed | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `true` | omitted | `developer` | `system` |
| `true` | `false` | `system` | `system` |
| `false` | `true` | `system` | `developer` |

### Expected behavior

Use `system` by default. Select `developer` only when the endpoint explicitly supports it, independently of reasoning. Known native endpoints can declare support in their compatibility metadata. This follows up on #7445 by defining the default for unclassified endpoints.

### Version

`@earendil-works/pi-ai` 1.5.2 source at [`b729499`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/commit/b729499585bd7dacf6e9bc52994c6f157e35f9c9).

issues.title: Install script confusion

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

On Ubuntu, the unrelated `pi` package installed with `sudo apt install pi` provides `/usr/bin/pi`. The Pi installer treats any command named `pi` as an existing Pi installation, labels it as such, and offers reinstall/uninstall actions.

If uninstall is selected, the installer checks for `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` with npm. Since the apt package is not that npm package, the installer reports that it found `pi` but npm does not show the Pi package installed, and removes nothing. This confuses an executable-name match with proof that the coding agent is installed.


### Steps to reproduce

1. On Ubuntu, install the unrelated apt package:

   ```bash
   sudo apt install pi
   ```

2. Run the Pi installer:

   ```bash
   curl -fsSL https://pi.dev/install.sh | sh
   ```

3. Observe that the installer identifies `/usr/bin/pi` as an existing Pi installation and offers an uninstall action. Choosing it reports that the npm package is not installed and leaves the apt package in place.

### Expected behavior

The installer should verify that an existing `pi` executable belongs to a Pi managed installation or the Pi npm package before calling it an existing Pi install or offering to uninstall it. It should leave unrelated system packages alone and install Pi without requiring users to remove the apt package.


### Patch
I attached a patched version of the install script which fixed this issue.

[pi-installer-collision-fix.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34850474/pi-installer-collision-fix.patch)

### Version

Installer: `https://pi.dev/install.sh` (no version shown)   OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS

issues.title: searchTools() returns full tool descriptions — 36KB per call, ~25% of a long session's context

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
Measured in a real 3-day coding-agent session (Deepwork harness, pi-durable 1.5.x, thread ~4.7M chars of model-visible content):

- `searchTools` was called 73 times; its results cost ~950KB — ~25% of the whole thread's context (more than all file reads combined).
- Cause: `discover()` in `dist/codemode/codemode.js` maps each ranked hit to the tool's **full** `description`. One of our tools has a ~36KB description (an embedded .d.ts teaching contract), so every loosely matching query (`"workflow run status"`, `"task status"`) returns ~37KB. The same query is often repeated after context compaction, because the model loses the previous result.
- Consequence we could measure, not just guess: results are truncated at ~10K tokens downstream, which twice produced unparseable JSON that agents then `JSON.parse`-failed on.

Suggestions, in order of preference:
1. Return name + first paragraph (or a fixed budget, e.g. 500 chars) per hit, and let agents call `describeTool(name)` for the full text — the plumbing already exists.
2. Or add an option `searchTools(query, { full: boolean })`, default short.

Happy to send a PR if you point at the preferred shape.

issues.title: /login shows a stored API key as configured when its `!command` fails, then requests fail with "No API key found"

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

My DeepSeek key in `auth.json` is a `!command` (a secrets-manager CLI). When that CLI's session expired, the command exited nonzero. `/login` still showed DeepSeek with a green configured mark, but every request failed with `No API key found for deepseek`.

`getProviderAuthStatus` returns `configured: true, source: "stored"` whenever the provider has an `auth.json` record. It ignores the `checkAuth` result that availability refresh already computes. A failed command resolves to `undefined` silently, so the selector and the request path disagree. Saving a key in `/login` also prints "Saved API key" without checking that the stored entry resolves.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In `~/.pi/agent/auth.json`, set `"deepseek": { "type": "api_key", "key": "!exit 1" }`.
2. Start `pi -ne` and open `/login`. DeepSeek shows as configured.
3. `pi -ne --provider deepseek --model deepseek-v4-flash -p hi` fails with `No API key found for deepseek.`

### Expected behavior

`/login` shows that the stored credential did not resolve, and the save confirmation doesn't say "Saved" for an entry that can't produce a key. No provider network call is needed; the existing resolution result is enough.

I have a small fix with tests (model-runtime status, selector label, save confirmation), and can open a PR if this is wanted.

### Version

1.5.2

issues.title: GitHub Copilot models enabled by an enterprise admin stay hidden after restart
issues.body:
### What happened?

Models newly enabled by a GitHub Copilot Enterprise administrator can remain absent from Pi's model picker after restarting Pi. The OAuth credential's `availableModelIds` is cached, and restarting does not necessarily refresh it while the OAuth credential is still valid. Opening the model selector refreshes the shared catalogs, but the GitHub Copilot account-specific `/models` list is not refreshed as part of that operation.

This is related to #7436, but the proposed fix here is to synchronize the account-specific model list at Pi startup and when Copilot credentials change—not to show the entire catalog when the cached list is stale.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Sign in to GitHub Copilot in Pi.
2. Have an enterprise administrator enable a model that is not in Pi's cached `availableModelIds`.
3. Restart Pi and open `/model`.

The newly enabled model remains missing until the OAuth credential/model list is refreshed.

### Expected behavior

Refresh the authenticated Copilot `/models` list at startup and when the Copilot credential changes. Show only models GitHub reports as picker-enabled and not policy-disabled.

### Version

Pi 1.2.0

prs.body:
Closes #12019.

The GitHub Copilot catalog hardcoded `supportsReasoningEffort: false` for its Gemini and Kimi models, so the thinking level was never sent. It now comes from models.dev. Besides `gemini-4-argon` and `gemini-3.8-flash` from the issue, this also turns it on for `gemini-4-carbon` (`low`/`medium`/`high`) and `kimi-k3` (`low`/`high`/`max`).

Also, Copilot reports reasoning tokens at the top level of `usage` (`usage.reasoning_tokens`) instead of nested in `usage.completion_tokens_details`, so `usage.reasoning` was always 0. When the nested field is missing, `parseChunkUsage` now reads the top-level one, like its existing cached-token fallbacks.

Reading `/models` at login, as the issue suggests, is left out: no provider changes model settings after login.

Validation on main `b8e1eec80d`:

- `test/openai-completions-tool-choice.test.ts`: one test per fix; both fail without the fix.
- `npm run check` and `./test.sh` pass.
- Not tested against a live Copilot account. @sethvargo, could you check `gemini-4-argon` (and `kimi-k3`) at `:low` and `:high`?

prs.title: feat(core): give the model a context-remaining tool and a self-triggered compaction path
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Gives the model two deferred tools around its own context budget. `get_context_remaining` reports the context window, tokens used (flagged as an estimate until the route reports real counts), tokens remaining, and the level where auto-compaction fires — from a new read-only `getContextUsageSnapshot()` accessor on `LlmChat` that exposes the existing per-route accounting without opening the fields. `request_compaction` lets the model start a compaction below the threshold ladder: the tool sets a flag that `sendMessageStream` consumes at the next model-round boundary, so history is never replaced while the requesting turn is still appending tool results, and the compaction runs force-with-`model_requested` — a new `CompactionTriggerReason` (and `CompactTrigger` member) so PostCompact hooks and the UI notice classify who asked.

## Why it's needed

The model currently learns its context is nearly full only when auto-compaction has already fired (or the request overflows). It cannot decide "wrap up now" or "compact before this large sub-task so the summary captures the right state" — users have `/context` and `/compress`; the model has nothing (#17313). OpenAI Codex ships both halves as model tools (`get_context_remaining.rs`, `new_context_window.rs`), which is the design precedent.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Unit level: `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/tools/get-context-remaining.test.ts src/tools/request-compaction.test.ts src/services/chatCompressionService.test.ts -t "model_requested"` — the tools report the snapshot / set the flag / degrade without a chat, and a forced compaction with `trigger: 'model_requested'` reports that trigger reason. Behaviorally: with the tools registered, ask a model near a full window what it would do — it can now read the remaining budget and call `request_compaction`; the next model round compresses first (the pending message and in-flight tool pairing are preserved by the existing `pendingUserMessage` path).

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — non-UI change.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅    |
| 🪟 Windows |   N/A   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   N/A   |

### Environment (optional)

N/A — unit tests only.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: `request_compaction` forces compaction below the threshold, so a model that calls it eagerly pays a summary it did not need; the tool description tells it to check `get_context_remaining` first and proceed without compaction when remaining context is comfortable.
- Not validated / out of scope: no live end-to-end model session in CI (the boundary-consumption path is unit-covered at the service level; the send-path wiring is a guarded two-line change on the existing threshold branch); the flag is per-chat and does not cross into forked chats.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none — the new trigger reason is additive; consumers of `CompactionTriggerReason` see a new member only.
- Design documents: N/A.

## Linked Issues

Closes #17313

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

本 PR 给模型补上两个围绕自身上下文预算的延迟工具。`get_context_remaining` 通过 `LlmChat` 上新增的只读 `getContextUsageSnapshot()` 访问器，报告上下文窗口、已用 token（在路由报告真实计数前标注为估算）、剩余量与自动压缩触发线。`request_compaction` 允许模型在阈值阶梯以下主动发起压缩：工具只置一个标记，由 `sendMessageStream` 在下一个模型回合边界消费——请求回合的工具结果仍在追加时绝不替换历史——并以新增的 `model_requested` 触发原因强制压缩，PostCompact 钩子与 UI 提示因此能正确归类。

动机：模型此前只有自动压缩已经触发（或请求溢出）时才感知上下文将满，无法自行决定"现在收尾"或"在大任务前先压缩以保住正确的状态摘要"（#17313）。OpenAI Codex 的两个模型工具（get_context_remaining.rs、new_context_window.rs）是设计先例。

验证：两个工具的单元测试（快照报告/标记置位/无会话降级）+ 服务层触发原因钉（force + model_requested → triggerReason）。风险：模型可能过早调用 request_compaction 而多付一次摘要，工具描述已引导先查剩余量。无破坏性变更。关闭 #17313。

</details>
