prs.title: docs(serve): document the two ignored watch knobs and calibrate the bound-delivery designs
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Clears the documentation follow-ups that the PR-watch design calibration (#17250) and its reviews recorded but deliberately left out of that change because they needed files outside its ten-file set, then calibrates the three bound-delivery designs those follow-ups live in.

**The operator page.** The GitHub channel user page marked only two of the four deprecated keys. `prWatchEvents` had a **Deprecated** row and the `watch:*` keys were described in prose, but `prWatchLimit` and `prWatchBudgetReserve` appeared nowhere in the page — or anywhere else under `docs/` outside the design family. An operator carrying only one of those knobs had no way to learn that it is ignored now and due for rejection. Both now have rows saying exactly that, and the sentence that promised the channel "accepts both deprecated surfaces" now names all four keys and says the warning names them, with only the first two read as aliases. The page also gated the alias on the setting alone; the settings reference and the daemon configuration reference it links to both require the setting **and its environment override** to be unset, so the page now says the same at all three places it describes the condition.

**The predecessor design.** The design the PR-watch master design supersedes still read `Status: proposed` and described `prWatchEvents` as live, with `validateConfig` rejecting it and `pollOnce` running the state watch. A reader following the supersession pointer would implement a second poller the family forbids. Its status line now records that it shipped as #16117, carries a scoped note that the PR-state-watch part is superseded and has landed while the comment-delivery part is still live, and carries the as-designed body note the rest of the family uses.

**The prompt-language design.** It said the daemon watch is gated off by the removed internal constant and the channel is the only live producer of bound event prompts; it is now the opposite — the daemon produces them whenever the effective PR-watch subscription has an event. That condition names all three inputs: `serve.sessionPrWatch`, its `QWEN_SESSION_PR_WATCH_EVENTS` override, and, when neither is configured, the deprecated per-host channel alias. The alias matters: `resolvePrWatchSubscription` falls through to `resolveAlias` when the setting is not explicit, and `createPrWatchDeps` gates only on `anyEvents`, so a deployment carrying only `prWatchEvents` does run both the observation tick and the drain. Its decision 7 deferred the language threading to "its enablement increment", which has since landed (#17032) without doing it: `PrWatchDrainDeps` still declares no language field, so the decision now says the threading is still owed rather than scheduled elsewhere. Two further sites in the same document still called the drain producer inert — the current-state table cell and the non-goal — contradicting that decision; both now say the language is not threaded, not that the producer is inert. And the document's own subject shipped as #16773, so its status line now says so instead of `proposed`, with the two things that moved since named: the drain language is still owed, and the watch summaries belong to the daemon after PR B.

**The active-watch-gate design.** It said the observation tick "is inert today … and would need a guard before that flag flips"; the flag is gone and the tick runs when events are subscribed, so the bullet now says that, names the same three subscription inputs, and points at the measurement that answered the concern — §9 of the config-migration design measures the whole scan and decides to keep three scans. Its decision D6 bounded the polling cost by `prWatchLimit`, a knob this same PR documents as deprecated and ignored; it now names the pass's built-in budget. Its status line records that the gate shipped as #16772, and scopes it: `requireBoundWatch` and `watchGateExcludes` have no reader anywhere under the daemon's serve code, while the adapter calls its `watchGateExcludes` helper at seven sites, so the gate filters the channel's comment delivery only, never the daemon's state transitions.

**The current-state table.** An independent verification round caught that repairing only the daemon-drain row left one present-day row among five pre-implementation rows, with no marker telling them apart, in a table titled *Current state*. The watch-summary row still pointed at `watchOnePr`, which no longer exists anywhere under `packages/`, and the locale row still said the adapter does not consume a locale it consumes at four sites. All six rows now describe the shipped tree in both languages; the design body below keeps its as-designed record, where naming `watchOnePr` as the symbol the change touched is correct.

The 126-character line the triage nit named is re-wrapped, and a structural gate now holds that across all four design files.

## Why it's needed

These are the items three separate review rounds surfaced and declined to file against #17250 because they were unchanged files made stale by #17214 rather than by that diff. Declining them there was right; leaving them indefinitely is not. Two are operator-facing: a deprecated setting nobody documents is a setting an operator keeps carrying, and a superseded design that still reads `proposed` invites reimplementing a poller the architecture forbids. The others are premise errors that would mislead the next increment — one defers work to an increment that already shipped without it, one treats a live per-tick cost as hypothetical, one would let a contributor conclude that localizing the drain prompt is dead work when a zh deployment with an event subscription receives English daemon prompts today, and three would let a reader take a shipped feature for pending work.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Documentation-only; there is no runtime behaviour to exercise. What a reviewer should confirm is that each repaired statement matches the shipped code and that nothing outside the intended scope changed.

Start with the channel user page. The two new rows should say the knobs are deprecated **and ignored**, that the pass uses its built-in budget, and that they will be rejected at `connect()` after one minor release. The deprecation paragraph should name four keys, not two surfaces, and say only the first two are aliased. Compare against the single warning the adapter emits: it names `prWatchEvents`, the `watch:*` keys, `prWatchLimit` and `prWatchBudgetReserve`, and says the two limit knobs are ignored and the pass uses its built-in budget. Every place the page describes the alias condition should require the setting and its environment override to be unset, matching the two reference pages it links to.

Then the three designs. Each status line should name the PR that shipped it (#16117, #16773, #16772), carry the as-designed body note, and — where part of the subject moved to the daemon — scope the supersession rather than blanket-marking the document. The prompt-language premise should name all three subscription inputs; its decision 7 should say the threading is still owed, which is checkable: `PrWatchDrainDeps` declares no language field; neither its current-state table nor its non-goal may still call the producer inert. The gate design's scan-cost bullet should say the tick is no longer inert, name the same three inputs, and cite §9's "keep three scans" decision, present in both languages of the config-migration design; its D6 should bound cost by the built-in budget; its status note should say the gate is comment-lane only, which is checkable: no daemon serve code reads `requireBoundWatch`.

Formatting and structure, run locally:

```
prettier --check <the seven changed files>
→ All matched files use Prettier code style!
```

Because a docs diff has no runtime A/B, the load-bearing evidence is a claim ledger: each repaired claim is a scripted predicate evaluated against the shipped tree on both the base document and the head document, and a cell counts only when head agrees **and base does not**. 115 cells: 109 flip, none regresses, none is vacuous. Six hold in both arms and are reported as such rather than counted as flips — two are deliberate invariants (each design keeps its own proposal date and maintainer-confirmation record), and four are regression guards against the setting-only wording this branch's own first version used, which never existed on main.

Seventeen code oracles back them: the removed constant has no occurrence under `packages/`; `run-qwen-serve.ts` populates both deps getters; `PrWatchDrainDeps` declares no language field; the adapter's single warning names all four keys and says the knobs are ignored; the deprecation predicate covers all four; §9 of the config-migration design carries the "keep three scans" decision in both languages; #17032, #17214, #16117, #16772 and #16773 are all ancestors of main; the subscription resolver falls through to the alias and the deps builder gates only on `anyEvents`; `explicit` covers the setting key and a non-blank events override; neither limit knob is read as a budget anywhere in the adapter; both reference pages gate the alias on both inputs; the channel lane is localized (`BoundPromptLanguage`, the per-language guidance table, the adapter consuming its locale) and `watchOnePr` is gone from the adapter; and no daemon serve code reads the bound-watch gate while the adapter calls its `watchGateExcludes` helper at seven sites. Three structural gates hold: the three bilingual pairs keep identical heading sequences and table-row counts, every relative link resolves and points at its own language, and no prose line in the four design files exceeds 80 characters unless it carries an unbreakable markdown link or is a status line, which the family writes as one long line.

Each claim also has a positive control that reverts it in place and requires the **named** assertion plus exactly the declared set of siblings to go red: 42 of 42 killed, every tree restored byte-identical. The sibling sets are declared, not derived from the run. Seven are worth naming: five revert a current-state table row to its pre-implementation text, two revert a premise to this branch's first-version wording; one collapses the re-wrapped bullet back to a single long line with identical words so that only the wrap gate may redden; and two inject a stale claim into a file no per-site cell reads, to prove the family-wide cells have reach beyond the sites the per-site cells name.

The harness itself was repaired six times during this revision, and each repair is load-bearing for the evidence above. Anchors are whitespace-normalized on both arms, with the space a line break leaves between two CJK characters removed, so re-wrapping Chinese prose cannot silently turn a cell vacuous. Block anchors and literal anchors both resolve in normalized space and map back to exact source bytes, verified to resolve the same block at three different wrap widths. The family-wide alias cell is case-insensitive, so a sentence-initial "When" cannot slip past it. And one family-wide cell had its two arms written with opposite polarity, which made it report "holds in both arms" instead of flipping; the final read of the both-arm list caught it. Two more came from the verification round: a family-wide cell was scoped to the whole document when the invariant only holds for the current-state table (the design body legitimately names the historical symbol), and the ledger's exit code did not fail on a cell that is false in **both** arms — which is how that over-broad cell stayed green through a full control sweep. Both are fixed, and a vacuous cell now fails the run.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — documentation only, no user-visible or TUI change.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍎 macOS  |  N/A   |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

N/A — formatting, reference and claim-ledger checks only. No build or test run is meaningful for a prose change; the repo's own CI covers the formatting gate independently.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the three designs keep their proposal dates and maintainer-confirmation records inside the new status lines rather than being rewritten, and the scoped notes name which half moved instead of blanket-marking a document superseded. A reader skimming status values alone gets the shipped state; a reader who needs the mechanism detail is told it is historical. The alternative — rewriting the bodies — would destroy their value as the record of what was decided.
- Not validated / out of scope: no code is touched. The language threading that decision 7 now records as owed is a code change and is not attempted here; neither are the two no-deps refresh tests whose effect assertions the master design's validation plan records as owed, nor the missing `prWatchLimit` assertion in the adapter's deprecation-warning test, nor the JSDoc above `usesDeprecatedPrWatchSurface` that still names two of the four keys its body checks. Those remain code follow-ups.
- Recorded, not widened into this diff: the drain design's `## Current state` still describes the removed constant and the unpopulated deps seam, shielded by that document's as-designed note but read differently from its same-dated sibling, which adds an explicit past-tense note. The same inversion survives in two code comments at the drain call site in `session-pr-refresh.ts`. An inbound-reference sweep also found two stale statuses outside this PR's file set — the bound-PR-comment-watch design still reads `proposed` although `prCommentWatch` shipped, and the bound-session-action-templates design still reads "implemented on `feat/…` (pending review)" although #16258 merged. Both are left for a separate pass rather than widening this diff.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. The two new table rows document existing behaviour; they do not change it.

## Linked Issues

Follow-up to #17250, whose reviews recorded these items as deferred. References #17214 (which removed the internal switch and the adapter's state detection), #17032 (the enablement increment that shipped without threading the prompt language), and the three PRs that shipped the designs calibrated here: #16117, #16772 and #16773.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

清掉 PR watch 设计校准（#17250）及其评审记录、但因需要该改动十个文件之外的文件而刻意留下的文档后续项，并校准这些后续项所在的三份绑定投递设计。

**运维者页面。** GitHub channel 用户页只标了四个弃用键中的两个。`prWatchEvents` 有 **Deprecated** 行、`watch:*` 键在散文里描述，但 `prWatchLimit` 与 `prWatchBudgetReserve` 在该页——以及 `docs/` 下设计族之外的任何地方——都不出现。只带着其中一个旋钮的运维者无从知道它现在被忽略、且即将被拒绝。两者现在各有一行说明这些，而那句承诺 channel「accepts both deprecated surfaces」的话现在点名全部四个键、说明告警会点名它们，且只有前两者被读作别名。该页原先还把别名只门控在设置上；它链接的 settings 参考与 daemon 配置参考都要求设置**及其环境变量覆盖**都未设置，因此该页现在在描述该条件的全部三处都这么说。

**前驱设计。** 被 PR watch 母设计取代的那份设计仍写 `Status: proposed`，并把 `prWatchEvents` 描述为在用、`validateConfig` 会拒绝它、`pollOnce` 跑状态监视。顺着取代指路走的读者会实现一个本族禁止的第二个轮询器。其状态行现在记录它已作为 #16117 落地，带一条限定注记说明 PR 状态监视部分已被取代且已落地、评论投递部分仍然在用，并带上本族其余设计使用的「正文按设计时记录」注记。

**prompt-language 设计。** 它原先说 daemon watch 被已删除的内部常量关掉、channel 是绑定事件提示词唯一活跃的生产方；现在正好相反——只要生效的 PR-watch 订阅带有事件，daemon 就生产它们。该条件点名全部三个输入：`serve.sessionPrWatch`、其 `QWEN_SESSION_PR_WATCH_EVENTS` 覆盖，以及两者都未配置时的弃用 per-host channel 别名。别名这一条是承重的：设置非显式时 `resolvePrWatchSubscription` 会回退到 `resolveAlias`，而 `createPrWatchDeps` 只以 `anyEvents` 为门，因此只带着 `prWatchEvents` 的部署确实会跑观测 tick 与 drain。其决策 7 把语言穿线推给「其启用增量」，而该增量此后已落地（#17032）却没做这件事：`PrWatchDrainDeps` 仍未声明 language 字段，因此该决策现在说这项穿线仍欠着、而不是已排到别处。同一文档另有两处仍称 drain 生产方惰性——现状表格单元与非目标——与该决策矛盾；两处现在都说语言尚未穿线，而不是生产方惰性。而该文档自身的主题已作为 #16773 落地，因此其状态行现在这么说、不再写 `proposed`，并点名此后移动的两件事：drain 语言仍欠着，且 watch 摘要在 PR B 之后属于 daemon。

**active-watch-gate 设计。** 它原先说观测 tick「目前是惰性的……该开关翻开前需要先加守卫」；开关已不存在、订阅事件时 tick 就会跑，因此该 bullet 现在这么说、点名同样那三个订阅输入，并指向回答该顾虑的实测——config-migration 设计 §9 实测整次扫描后定案保留三次扫描。其决策 D6 用 `prWatchLimit` 约束轮询成本，而本 PR 正把该旋钮记为已弃用且被忽略；它现在点名 pass 的内建预算。其状态行记录该门已作为 #16772 落地，并限定范围：`requireBoundWatch` 与 `watchGateExcludes` 在 daemon 的 serve 代码下没有任何读取方，而适配器在七个站点调用其 `watchGateExcludes` 助手，因此该门只过滤 channel 的评论投递，从不过滤 daemon 的状态转换。

**现状表。** 一轮独立验证抓住：只修 daemon drain 那一行，会让一张标题为*Current state* 的表里出现「一行是今天、五行是实现前」且无标记区分。watch 摘要行仍指向 `watchOnePr`（该符号在 `packages/` 下已不存在），locale 行仍说适配器不消费它其实在四处消费的 locale。六行现在双语都描述已发布的树；其下的设计正文保留按设计时的记录，在那里把 `watchOnePr` 作为本次改动触碰的符号点名是正确的。

triage 小注记点名的那行 126 字符已重新折行，并有一条结构门对全部四个设计文件守住此事。

## 为什么需要

这些是三轮评审分别发现、但因属「未改动文件、其陈旧来自 #17214 而非该 diff」而未对 #17250 立为发现的条目。在那里不立是对的；无限期留着不是。其中两条面向运维者：没人记录的弃用设置就是运维者会一直带着的设置，而仍写 `proposed` 的被取代设计会诱人去重新实现架构禁止的轮询器。其余是会误导下一个增量的前提错误——一个把工作推给已发布却没做它的增量，一个把一项已在发生的每 tick 成本当作假设，一个会让贡献者得出「本地化 drain 提示词是死工」的结论（而今天一个带事件订阅的 zh 部署收到的正是英文 daemon 提示词），还有三个会让读者把已发布的特性当作待办工作。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

纯文档，没有运行时行为可跑。评审者应确认的是：每条被修复的陈述与已发布代码一致，且意图范围之外没有改动。

先看 channel 用户页。两个新行应说明这两个旋钮已弃用**且被忽略**、pass 使用其内建预算、以及一个 minor 版本后将在 `connect()` 被拒绝。弃用段落应点名四个键而非两个面，并说明只有前两者被别名化。对着适配器发出的那条唯一告警比对：它点名 `prWatchEvents`、`watch:*` 键、`prWatchLimit` 与 `prWatchBudgetReserve`，并说两个 limit 旋钮被忽略、pass 使用内建预算。该页描述别名条件的每一处都应要求设置及其环境变量覆盖都未设置，与它链接的两份参考页一致。

再看三份设计。每条状态行应点名使其落地的那个 PR（#16117、#16773、#16772）、带上「正文按设计时记录」注记，并在主题有一部分移到 daemon 时限定取代范围、而不是一律标取代。prompt-language 的前提应点名全部三个订阅输入；其决策 7 应说穿线仍欠着，这一点可核：`PrWatchDrainDeps` 未声明 language 字段；其现状表格与非目标都不得再称生产方惰性。gate 设计的扫描成本 bullet 应说 tick 已不再惰性、点名同样那三个输入，并引用 §9 的「保留三次扫描」定案（config-migration 设计双语都在）；其 D6 应以内建预算约束成本；其状态注记应说该门只作用于评论车道，这一点可核：daemon 的 serve 代码不读 `requireBoundWatch`。

本地已跑的格式与结构检查：

```
prettier --check <七个改动文件>
→ All matched files use Prettier code style!
```

由于文档 diff 没有运行时 A/B，承重证据是一份 claim ledger：每条被修复的主张都是一个脚本谓词，对已发布树在 base 文档与 head 文档上分别求值，只有 head 成立**且 base 不成立**才计一个单元。115 个单元：109 个翻转，无一回归，无一空转。六个在两臂都成立，按实报告而不计入翻转——两个是刻意不变量（每份设计保留自身的提案日期与维护者确认记录），另四个是针对本分支第一版所用「只点名设置」措辞的回归守卫，该措辞从未存在于 main。

十七条代码 oracle 支撑它们：已删除常量在 `packages/` 下 0 命中；`run-qwen-serve.ts` 填充两个 deps getter；`PrWatchDrainDeps` 未声明 language 字段；适配器唯一告警点名四个键并说旋钮被忽略；弃用谓词覆盖四个键；config-migration 设计 §9 双语都带「保留三次扫描」定案；#17032、#17214、#16117、#16772、#16773 都是 main 的祖先；订阅解析器会回退到别名、deps 构造器只以 `anyEvents` 为门；`explicit` 覆盖设置键与非空 events 覆盖；两个 limit 旋钮在适配器任何地方都不被当作预算读取；两份参考页都把别名门控在两个输入上；channel 车道已本地化（`BoundPromptLanguage`、按语言的指引表、适配器消费其 locale）且 `watchOnePr` 已从适配器消失；daemon 的 serve 代码不读绑定监视门，而适配器在七个站点调用其 `watchGateExcludes` 助手。三个结构门成立：三对双语标题序列与表行数一致，全部相对链接可解析且指向自身语言，四个设计文件中没有任何散文行超过 80 字符（携带不可折行 markdown 链接的行、以及本族写成单长行的状态行除外）。

每条主张还有一条正向控制，把它原地改回并要求**被点名**的断言加上恰好声明的那组兄弟断言变红：42 条全部击杀，每棵树字节级还原。兄弟集合是声明的、不是从运行结果反推的。其中七条值得点名：五条把现状表行改回实现前文本，两条把前提改回本分支第一版的措辞；一条把重新折行的 bullet 用完全相同的词压回一行长行，使得只有行宽门可以变红；另两条往任何逐站点单元都不读的文件里注入一句陈旧主张，以证明全族单元的覆盖面超出逐站点单元所点名的站点。

harness 本身在本次修订中修了六次，每次都对上面的证据承重。锚点现在在两臂都做空白归一化，并去掉换行在两个中文字符之间留下的空格，因此重新折行中文散文不会把某个单元悄悄变成空转。块锚点与字面量锚点都在归一化空间定位、再映射回精确源字节，已验证在三种折行宽度下解析到同一个块。全族别名单元大小写不敏感，因此句首大写的「When」不会溜过去。还有一个全族单元的两臂被写成了相反极性，使它报告「两臂都成立」而不是翻转；最终对「两臂都成立」清单的通读抓住了它。另有两次来自验证轮：一个全族单元被范围到整份文档，而该不变量只对现状表成立（设计正文正当地点名那个历史符号）；以及账本的退出码不对「两臂都不成立」的单元判失败——正是这一点让那个范围过宽的单元在整轮控制 sweep 中保持绿色。两者都已修，空转单元现在会让运行失败。

### 证据（改动前后）

N/A —— 纯文档，无用户可见或 TUI 变化。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍎 macOS  | N/A  |
| 🪟 Windows | N/A  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ✅  |

### 环境（可选）

N/A —— 仅格式、引用与 claim ledger 检查。对散文改动跑构建或测试没有意义；仓库自己的 CI 独立覆盖格式门。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：三份设计把提案日期与维护者确认记录保留在新状态行内、而不是重写，限定注记点名哪一半移动了、而不是一律标取代。只扫状态值的读者得到的是已落地状态；需要机制细节的读者会被告知那是历史记录。另一种做法（重写正文）会毁掉它们作为决策记录的价值。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：未触碰任何代码。决策 7 现在记为仍欠着的语言穿线属代码改动，不在此尝试；母设计验证计划记为仍欠着的两个 no-deps 刷新用例效果断言、适配器弃用告警测试里缺失的 `prWatchLimit` 断言、以及 `usesDeprecatedPrWatchSurface` 上方仍只点名四个键中两个的 JSDoc，同样不在此尝试。这些仍是代码后续。
- 记录、但不撑进本 diff：drain 设计的 `## Current state` 仍描述已删除的常量与尚未填充的 deps 接缝，由该文档的「按设计时记录」注记护栏，但与其同日期兄弟读起来不同（后者另加一条明确的过去时注记）。同一处倒置还残留在 `session-pr-refresh.ts` 里 drain 调用点的两条代码注释中。一次入站引用普查还在本 PR 文件集之外发现两处陈旧状态——bound-PR-comment-watch 设计仍写 `proposed`，尽管 `prCommentWatch` 已落地；bound-session-action-templates 设计仍写「implemented on `feat/…`（pending review）」，尽管 #16258 已合入。两者留给单独一轮处理，而不撑大本 diff。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。两个新表行记录的是既有行为，不改变它。

## 关联 Issue

#17250 的后续，其评审把这些条目记为转后续。引用 #17214（移除内部开关与适配器状态检测）、#17032（已发布但未穿提示词语言的启用增量），以及使此处校准的三份设计落地的三个 PR：#16117、#16772、#16773。

</details>

prs.title: fix(web-shell): show scroll-to-bottom control in Split View panes
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Split View panes now render the same floating "scroll to bottom" button the main session view already has. When the reader scrolls up inside a pane, the button appears just above that pane's composer; clicking it scrolls the pane's transcript back to the bottom and resumes following live output.

The pane previously received no scroll-position signal from its transcript, so it could not know when to offer the control. It now subscribes to the existing callback that the transcript list already reports, keeps the state locally, and reuses the pane's existing imperative scroll handle for the click. The button's styling is copied from the main view's so the two controls look identical.

## Why it's needed

In Split View, scrolling up in a pane stops its auto-follow — the same behavior as the main view — but a pane had no way back to the live tail except manual wheel/trackpad scrolling. With several panes running at once, the pane whose autoscroll you broke is exactly the one you cannot easily jump back into. The main view solved this long ago; panes just never wired the same callback.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Run the new unit test: `cd packages/web-shell && npx vitest run client/components/ChatPane.test.tsx -t "scroll-to-bottom control"`. It asserts the button is absent before the pane reports a detached scroll position, that it appears once reported, that clicking it invokes the pane's scroll handle, and that it disappears when the pane reports being back at the bottom.
2. Manually: open a session in Split View (Add to Split View on a session), send a prompt long enough to overflow the pane, then scroll the pane up. Expected: a round chevron button appears above that pane's composer. Clicking it returns the pane to the bottom and re-engages autofollow. Before the change, no button appears and the only way back is manual scrolling.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: after scrolling a split pane up, no control appeared above the composer.
After: the same round scroll-to-bottom button the main view uses appears above the pane composer and returns the pane to the live tail.

No screenshot was captured in this run — the change was verified through the unit test above, not through a live browser session.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   N/A  |
|  🐧 Linux  |   N/A  |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only (`npx vitest run` in `packages/web-shell`); no dev server or browser session was run.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the pane footer gains one absolutely-positioned overlay element when the button is visible. It is `pointer-events: none` except on the button itself, and mirrors the main view's layer, so it should not intercept composer input.
- Not validated / out of scope: not verified in a live browser (see Evidence). The `packages/web-shell` typecheck reports one pre-existing error on `main` (`session-catalog-store.ts`: `liveOnly` missing on `DaemonSessionListPageOptions`); the same error appears with this change stashed, so it is unrelated.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #16569

prs.title: test(cli): raise managed terminal wait budgets on slow hosts (#17262)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Raises the two internal watchdogs in the managed runtime terminal test suite from a flat 15 seconds to the repository's existing slow-host budget, and gives the scrollback replay case a matching per-test ceiling. The fast arm stays at the previous 15-second value for idle hosts; the slow arm is 45 seconds for the waits and 90 seconds for the replay test.

## Why it's needed

The CLI Vitest configuration already raises the per-test ceiling to 60 seconds on the shared `ecs-qwen-*` pool because PTY spawn and output replay are I/O-bound. The terminal suite's own attach and output-marker timers ignored that host class and fired at 15 seconds, so a slow-but-healthy run on a loaded pool failed with `output marker mwt-echo-ok timed out` before the suite ceiling could apply. The replay path itself was already fixed in #17194 (the replay listener is attached before `open` resolves); this is the residual watchdog-budget failure tracked in #17262.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run `npx vitest run src/serve/managed-runtime-terminal.test.ts` from `packages/cli` on an idle host, then repeat with `RUNNER_NAME=ecs-qwen-autofix` to exercise the slow-host arm. Both forms should report 20/20 passing. Confirm that the only behavior change is the ceiling: the named `ManagedRuntimeTerminals › replays scrollback on reconnect of the same Session` case still fails if the replay never arrives, because its marker assertion is untouched.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — test-only ceiling change with no user-visible behavior.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only, run through the CLI package's Vitest configuration. The sandbox build needed `COREPACK_HOME=/tmp/corepack` because the home cache was not writable.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a genuinely hung terminal now takes up to 45 seconds to fail on a slow host instead of 15 seconds. Assertions and markers are unchanged, so a terminal that never replays still fails.
- Not validated / out of scope: the original ECS run could not be re-executed locally; verification used the slow-host arm to exercise the raised budgets.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #17262

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

把托管运行时终端测试套件中的两个内部看门狗从固定的 15 秒提高到仓库已有的慢主机预算,并给滚动回看重放用例一个匹配的每用例上限。空闲主机上的快速分支保持之前的 15 秒;慢速分支的等待预算为 45 秒,重放测试的上限为 90 秒。

## 为什么需要

CLI 的 Vitest 配置已经在共享的 `ecs-qwen-*` 池上把每用例上限提高到 60 秒,因为 PTY 启动和输出重放属于 I/O 密集操作。终端套件自带的连接计时器和输出标记计时器忽略了这个主机类别,在 15 秒时就触发,导致负载较高的池上健康但缓慢的运行在套件上限生效之前就以 `output marker mwt-echo-ok timed out` 失败。重放路径本身已在 #17194 修复(重放监听器在 `open` 完成前挂载);这是 #17262 跟踪的残余看门狗预算失败。

## 审查者测试计划

### 如何验证

在 `packages/cli` 下于空闲主机运行 `npx vitest run src/serve/managed-runtime-terminal.test.ts`,然后带上 `RUNNER_NAME=ecs-qwen-autofix` 重复运行以触发慢主机分支。两种形式都应报告 20/20 通过。确认唯一的行为变化是上限:名为 `ManagedRuntimeTerminals › replays scrollback on reconnect of the same Session` 的用例在重放始终不出现时仍会失败,因为它的标记断言没有被改动。

### 证据(修改前与修改后)

不适用——仅测试上限变化,没有用户可见行为。

### 测试环境

|    操作系统    | 状态 |
| :------------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS      |  ⚠️  |
| 🪟 Windows     |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux      |  ✅  |

### 环境(可选)

仅单元测试,通过 CLI 包的 Vitest 配置运行。沙箱构建需要 `COREPACK_HOME=/tmp/corepack`,因为 home 缓存不可写。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡:真正卡死的终端在慢主机上现在最多需要 45 秒才失败,而不是 15 秒。断言和标记没有变化,因此永远不会重放的终端仍会失败。
- 未验证 / 超出范围:无法在本地重新执行原始 ECS 运行;验证通过慢主机分支来触发提高后的预算。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明:无。

## 关联 Issue

Fixes #17262

</details>

prs.title: feat(web-shell): show per-turn hook statistics
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds per-turn Hook statistics to Web Shell replies using the local records delivered in #17015. A reply footer entry opens a hover/focus summary and a paginated detail dialog; narrow screens expose the entry through a more menu. Historical navigation keeps the same read-only entry.

Statistics distinguish blocked and unsuccessful executions, cumulative execution duration, incomplete records, and background dispatch. Queries use the selected session and canonical history turn, and detail pages retain one frozen snapshot until explicitly refreshed.

## Why it's needed

Local Hook records are available after #17015, but Web Shell users cannot inspect them from a conversation. This makes those existing records accessible without changing Hook execution or collection.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run local command Hooks and open their reply's Hook statistics. The summary and detail list should match actual invocations, preserve their counts after reload, and remain separate across turns. Navigate to an older turn and return to the live conversation; each entry should show only its own records.

With more than 50 executions, load another page, retry a failed page, then refresh. Pagination should preserve the original total and snapshot; Refresh should show newly recorded executions. Check light/dark themes, keyboard focus and Enter, Escape returning focus, and the 320px more menu. Background dispatch must not be described as completed, and missing terminal records must remain unknown.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: the required global CLI 0.22.0 baseline has no statistics entry. This older release is a UI/startup baseline, not evidence about current main's data collection.

![Global 0.22.0 baseline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/codex/web-shell-hook-statistics/.github/assets/web-shell-hook-statistics/baseline-global-0.22.png)

After: actual command Hooks with the local daemon, using deterministic model responses. Two turns each executed three commands; API and UI both showed three executions per turn after reload.

![Real Hook summary](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/codex/web-shell-hook-statistics/.github/assets/web-shell-hook-statistics/real-hover.png)

![Real Hook details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/codex/web-shell-hook-statistics/.github/assets/web-shell-hook-statistics/real-dialog.png)

Local verification: full build, typecheck and bundle; 890 focused unit tests; four Chromium scenarios; changed-file ESLint and Prettier. The separate E2E report distinguishes real-command evidence from pagination/error fixtures.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :---: | :---: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ Not tested locally |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ Not tested locally |

### Environment (optional)

Node.js 26.7.0, Chromium, isolated temporary workspace/config/runtime, local bundled daemon and deterministic OpenAI-compatible model. Unit tests disable Node 26's experimental webstorage.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: canonical turn ownership and stale asynchronous reads during session/navigation changes; these paths have focused tests and browser coverage.
- Not validated / out of scope: managed Hook collection, async final-result collection, session totals, subagent aggregation, and external model/provider behavior.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none; reuses the existing read-only SDK contract and lifecycle reducer. Document exports exclude the interactive statistics component.

Design: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/web-shell-hook-statistics/docs/design/web-shell-hook-statistics.md) · [中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/web-shell-hook-statistics/docs/design/web-shell-hook-statistics.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

Follows merged data-layer PR #17015. No issue closed by this UI-only follow-up.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的改动

使用 #17015 提供的本地记录，在 Web Shell 回复中新增轮次 Hook 统计。回复底部入口支持悬浮／聚焦摘要和分页明细弹窗；窄屏通过更多菜单进入。历史导航中保留同一只读入口。

统计区分阻止与未成功执行、累计执行耗时、不完整记录和后台派发。查询绑定选中的会话及规范历史轮次，明细分页保持同一冻结快照，直到显式刷新。

## 为什么需要

#17015 已提供本地 Hook 记录，但 Web Shell 用户还无法从对话中查看。本 PR 让已有记录可见，不改变 Hook 执行或采集。

## 评审验证计划

### 如何验证

运行本地 command Hook，打开对应回复的钩子统计。摘要和列表应与实际调用一致，重载后次数不变，不同轮次相互独立。导航到历史轮次后再返回实时对话，每个入口应只显示自身记录。

超过 50 次执行时加载下一页，重试失败页，再刷新。分页应保持原总数及快照；刷新应显示新记录。检查亮暗主题、键盘聚焦及 Enter、Escape 返回焦点，以及 320px 的更多菜单。后台派发不能描述为已完成，缺失终态必须保留未知状态。

### 前后证据

修改前：按流程验证的全局 CLI 0.22.0 没有统计入口。该旧版本仅作为界面／启动基线，不用于证明当前 main 的数据采集情况。截图见上方 Global 0.22.0 baseline。

修改后：使用本地 daemon、真实 command Hook 及确定性模型响应。两轮各执行三条命令，重载后 API 与界面均显示每轮三次。上方 Real Hook summary 与 Real Hook details 分别展示真实摘要和明细。

本地验证包括全量 build、typecheck、bundle，890 项定向单测，四项 Chromium 场景，以及改动文件的 ESLint、Prettier。独立 E2E 报告区分真实命令证据与分页／错误 fixture。

### 测试平台

| OS | 状态 |
| :---: | :---: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未在本地测试 |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ 未在本地测试 |

### 环境

Node.js 26.7.0、Chromium、隔离临时工作区／配置／运行时、本地 daemon bundle 与确定性 OpenAI 兼容模型。单测禁用 Node 26 的实验性 webstorage。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：会话／导航切换时的规范轮次归属及过期异步读取；已用定向测试及浏览器场景覆盖。
- 未验证／范围外：托管 Hook 采集、异步最终结果采集、会话汇总、子 Agent 聚合，以及外部模型／提供商行为。
- 兼容性／迁移：无破坏性改动或迁移，复用既有只读 SDK 契约和生命周期 reducer。文档导出排除交互统计组件。

设计：[English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/web-shell-hook-statistics/docs/design/web-shell-hook-statistics.md) · [中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/web-shell-hook-statistics/docs/design/web-shell-hook-statistics.zh-CN.md)。

## 关联 Issue

接续已合入的数据层 PR #17015。本次仅交付界面，不关闭 Issue。

</details>

prs.title: test(web-shell): reset CPU throttle before the history-viewport live assertion
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Resets the 4x CPU throttle before the final "Scroll to bottom" phase of the 200-record history-viewport `@smoke` case, and gives the live-viewport assertion its own timeout instead of letting the global 20s expect window bound it. The 16-record sibling case is untouched: its restore is a no-op.

## Why it's needed

The case sets a 4x CDP CPU throttle for the 2,400-record fixture walk and never restores it, so the last step — send a background event, click Scroll to bottom, assert the live viewport shows the new answer — also runs at 4x throttle. That assertion is bounded by `expect.timeout` (20s, `playwright.config.ts:18`), not by the case's own `test.setTimeout`. When a loaded runner pushes the React commit past 20s, the assertion expires as `element(s) not found` while most of the test budget is still unspent — exactly the reported shape (`Expect "toContainText" with timeout 20000ms` inside `Test timeout of 120000ms exceeded`).

Raising the test budget (#15656, 120s → 300s) does not help: `test.setTimeout` and `expect.timeout` are independent budgets, so the assertion still gives up at 20s. This removes the coupling at its source rather than widening the budget again.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the case locally and confirm it still passes end to end:

```
cd packages/web-shell
npx playwright test client/e2e/web-shell.history-viewport.spec.ts --project=chromium -g "bounded 200-record" --workers=1
```

Expected: the case passes. The throttle reset is a no-op change for correctness on a quiet host — it changes headroom, not behaviour — so a green run is the check that the assertion still observes the live viewport.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: the throttle is set at the top of the case and never reset, so the final phase runs throttled; the final assertion carries only the global 20s `expect.timeout`.

After: `Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate` is restored to `rate: 1` immediately before the Scroll to bottom click, and the final `toContainText` is given its own `timeout` so a genuinely slow commit is reported as an assertion timeout rather than consuming the test budget.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   N/A  |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️    |

CI-only Playwright spec; the local run was macOS. The Linux lane is where the flake showed up, so the CI smoke job is the confirmation that matters there.

### Environment (optional)

Local Playwright run against the repo's own vite dev server, chromium project, single worker.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the 200-record case now runs its final phase without CPU throttling, so it no longer exercises a throttled click-to-live transition. The throttled walk (the expensive part, and the reason the throttle exists) is unchanged. If a throttled live transition is something worth covering, it should be its own case rather than a side effect of this one.
- Not validated / out of scope: the underlying cause of a slow React commit on a loaded runner (host contention) is not addressed; this only stops it from failing on an assertion window that is 6x smaller than the case budget. Not run on Windows or Linux locally.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

### Note on the `ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:4170` log line

The report lists that proxy error as a possible trigger. It is structural: the mock daemon has no `GET /workspace/models` handler, so the request falls through the spec's route and is proxied to a daemon port that nothing listens on. A local run of this spec reproduces the warning on every green case, which rules it out as the failure cause.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #15697

prs.title: fix(acp): treat a refused group signal as provisional, not proof of a failed shutdown
prs.body:
## What this PR does

A refused group signal is no longer latched as a shutdown failure. When the teardown loop could not signal a known process group because the kernel answered `EPERM`, that single transient error was stored for the lifetime of the tracked child and then re-thrown on the clean path — before the check that decides whether the root exited uncleanly. A child that had already exited with code 0 and left no surviving group was therefore reported as a failed cleanup, and the daemon exited non-zero.

The change makes `EPERM` provisional instead of fatal: the group stays committed and the process table decides. A group that has actually emptied is retired by the existing `ESRCH` handling on the next signal attempt or by the terminal-group pruning that runs on the same loop, while a group that is still verifiably alive at the total deadline continues to fail with the surviving pgids named in the error. Every other errno stays fail-closed.

## Why it's needed

`qwen serve` installs its shutdown handlers before ACP preheat starts, and preheat is fire-and-forget. Stopping the daemon while the ACP child is still booting can hit a window where the child has exited but the group signal is refused. The daemon then logs `could not send SIGKILL to pgid=<pid>: kill EPERM` plus `daemon shutdown incomplete` and exits 1, even though `ps`, a PGID query and `lsof` immediately afterwards find no residual process, group member or listener.

The exit code is the signal every consumer uses to decide whether the daemon stopped cleanly — the desktop shell, CI jobs and process supervisors all read it that way. Reporting a fully clean shutdown as a cleanup failure makes a mac-only timing race look like a leak on macOS.

The same file already disagrees with itself on `EPERM`: the group liveness path tolerates it, and the direct-root fallbacks swallow every error silently. Only the signalling path treated it as proof of a real failure. A unit test asserted that outcome, so the wrong answer was pinned.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the package's registry tests. The two new cases cover both halves of the contract:

```
cd packages/acp-bridge && npx vitest run src/process-registry.test.ts
```

On `main` the clean-exit case fails with `ACP child pid=1234 could not send SIGTERM to pgid=1234: EPERM`; on this branch all 39 cases pass. Expected behaviour after the change: a child that exits 0 while the group signal is refused with `EPERM` resolves instead of rejecting, and a group that is still listed in the process table at the deadline still fails with `did not exit with its owned process groups within 10000ms`.

The macOS reproduction from the issue (start an authenticated daemon with `--port 0` and an isolated runtime dir, send `SIGTERM` before ACP preheat finishes, read the exit code) was not run here.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before, on `origin/main` with the new tests applied — the clean-exit case rejects:

```
FAIL  src/process-registry.test.ts > ProcessRegistry > reports a clean exit when the group signal is refused with EPERM and the group empties
AssertionError: promise rejected "Error: ACP child pid=1234 could not send …" instead of resolving
Caused by: Error: ACP child pid=1234 could not send SIGTERM to pgid=1234: EPERM
 ❯ TrackedChild.recordCleanupProofError src/process-registry.ts:598:32
 ❯ TrackedChild.signalKnownGroups src/process-registry.ts:565:14
```

After, on this branch:

```
 ✓ src/process-registry.test.ts (39 tests) 31ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  39 passed (39)
```

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

macOS: `process-registry.test.ts` 39/39. The cases that exercise this path force `process.platform` to `linux`, so the POSIX branch is covered by unit tests, but nothing ran on a real Linux or Windows host.

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only; no sandbox or daemon was started.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a group that is genuinely alive but refuses every signal is now retired only by the process table. If that table cannot be read, the group stays committed and the total-deadline error fires with the pgid named — so the failure is still loud, just later.
- Not validated / out of scope: the macOS timing window itself was not reproduced at runtime; this is a unit-level verification of the mechanism the issue documents. Part 2 of the issue (the listener-less ACP child boot window, which is a separate design gap needing an upstream decision) is not touched here.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: the unit case that asserted `EPERM` produces a rejection now uses `EIO`, so the fail-closed contract for errnos that do prove a real failure is still pinned.

## Linked Issues

Part of #12350. This changes the first failure only; the issue's part 2 — the listener-less ACP child boot window, where `throwForUncleanExit` still reports `signalCode !== null` as unclean — is an upstream design decision, so `Fixes` would retire the issue with that cost still present.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

被拒绝的进程组信号不再被当成关停失败的证据。原来的清理循环在无法向已知进程组发信号（内核返回 `EPERM`）时，会把这一条瞬时错误永久记录在被跟踪子进程上，然后在"干净退出"分支里、判断根进程是否异常退出之前就把它抛出来。结果是：已经以退出码 0 结束、且没有残留进程组的子进程被报告为清理失败，守护进程以非零码退出。

这次改成把 `EPERM` 视为待定：进程组继续保留在跟踪集合里，由进程表来判定。真正已经清空的组会由下一次信号尝试的 `ESRCH` 处理或同一循环里的终态组清理回收；而在总超时时刻仍能被证实存活的组，依旧会在错误里列出存活的 pgid 并失败。其他 errno 一律保持 fail-closed。

## 为什么需要

`qwen serve` 在 ACP preheat 之前就安装了关停处理器，而 preheat 是"发出即不管"的。在 ACP 子进程还在启动时停掉守护进程，会命中"子进程已退出、但向进程组发信号被拒绝"的窗口。此时守护进程会打印 `could not send SIGKILL to pgid=<pid>: kill EPERM` 和 `daemon shutdown incomplete` 并以 1 退出，可紧接着的 `ps`、PGID 查询和 `lsof` 都找不到残留进程、组成员或监听端口。

退出码是所有调用方（桌面壳、CI 任务、进程管理器）判断守护进程是否干净退出的依据。把一次完全干净的关停报告成清理失败，会让一个 macOS 上的时序竞态看起来像泄漏。

同一个文件里对 `EPERM` 的处理本来就自相矛盾：进程组存活检查容忍它，直接对根进程的兜底路径则静默吞掉所有错误。只有发信号这条路径把它当成真实失败的证据，而且还有一条单测把这个错误结论固定了下来。

## 审阅方式

在 `packages/acp-bridge` 下运行 `npx vitest run src/process-registry.test.ts`。在 `main` 上，干净退出的那个用例会以 `ACP child pid=1234 could not send SIGTERM to pgid=1234: EPERM` 失败；在本分支上 39 个用例全部通过。

issue 里描述的 macOS 运行时复现（以 `--port 0` 和独立 runtime 目录启动带鉴权的守护进程，在 preheat 完成前发送 `SIGTERM`，读退出码）本轮没有实际执行。

## 风险与范围

- 主要权衡：如果某个进程组确实还活着却拒绝一切信号，现在只能靠进程表回收。当进程表读不到时，该组会保持提交状态，由总超时错误带出 pgid——失败依然会明确报出，只是更晚。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：issue 里的 macOS 时序窗口没有做运行时复现，这是对机制的单元级验证。issue 的第二部分（ACP 子进程启动期没有监听者的窗口，属于另一个需要上游决策的设计缺口）本次不涉及。
- 兼容性：原来断言 `EPERM` 会 reject 的单测改用 `EIO`，因此"确实代表真实失败的 errno 必须 fail-closed"这条契约仍然被固定。

</details>

prs.title: fix(core): don't publish a phantom cwd for brace-expanded cd targets
prs.body:
## What this PR does

When a `cd` or `pushd` target is a brace list or brace range (`cd {a,b}`, `cd sub{1..3}`), the shell-operation walker now keeps the cwd the segment started in and marks the rest of the segment `cwdUnknown`, instead of resolving the literal braces into a directory path that does not exist.

## Why it's needed

This is the last of the three phantom-cwd entrances recorded in #13139 that current `main` still reproduces; the other two (quoted trailing-backslash and newline-inside-a-quoted-cd-word) are already fixed.

Bash expands the brace list before the builtin sees its arguments, so `cd {a,b}` becomes two words and bash exits 1 with `cd: too many arguments`. The cd never runs and the segment keeps the cwd it started in. The analyzer instead published `{write_file, /repo/{a,b}/settings.json}` and returned `allow`, so a `Write(.qwen/settings.json)` deny rule (or any rule protecting a *relative* path) did not match the write that actually happened.

Marking the segment `cwdUnknown` escalates the operation to `ask` / force-review in `PermissionManager` and `autoMode` instead of allowing it, which is the fail-closed behaviour the issue asks for. A quoted `'{a,b}'`, a single-item `{a}` and a drive-letter path stay literal, because none of them is a brace list.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

With `allow ['Bash(cd *)','Bash(echo *)']`, `deny ['Write(.qwen/settings.json)']` and cwd `/repo`, the analyzer's output for the three shapes from the issue on current `main`:

```
"cd .qwen ; cd 'x\\' ; echo {} > settings.json"   -> {write_file, /repo/.qwen/x/settings.json, cwdUnknown: true}   (already fixed)
"cd 'x\\\ny' && echo hi > settings.json"          -> {write_file, .../x/\ny/settings.json, cwdUnknown: true}     (already fixed)
"cd {a,b} && echo x > settings.json"              -> {write_file, /repo/{a,b}/settings.json}   allow              (this PR)
```

After this PR the third becomes `{write_file, /repo/settings.json, cwdUnknown: true, pathMayDependOnCwd: true}`, so the write is no longer allowed outright. Four regression cases were added next to the other compound-`cd` cases in `shell-semantics.test.ts`: brace list, brace range, quoted brace list, single-item brace.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — non-user-visible (permission analyzer); the before/after operation lists are above and the new tests cover them.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

Local runs on macOS: `npx vitest run packages/core/src/permissions/` (16 files, 1411 tests passed), `npm --prefix packages/core run typecheck`, and `npx eslint` on both changed files. The full `npm run build` was not run; a core-package build was done only to satisfy the unit-test dist prerequisite.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: Brace-expanded `cd`/`pushd` targets now escalate to `ask` / force-review instead of being allowed. A legitimate workflow such as `cd {src,test}` will start prompting where it previously parsed as an allow. This is the intended fail-closed direction from #13139 — the analyzer cannot know which of the expansions the shell actually chdir'd into, so it must not keep claiming the starting cwd.
- Not validated / out of scope: Windows and Linux were not run locally (see `Tested on` above); only macOS was. Brace *ranges* with a step (`{1..9..2}`) are covered by the same code path as `{1..3}` but only the plain range has a regression test. The other two phantom-cwd entrances from #13139 are already fixed on `main` and are not touched here.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: No API or config change. Behavioural change only: a previously-`allow`ed operation on a brace-expanded `cd` target is now `ask`. Users whose allow rules covered it will get one prompt per such command.

## Linked Issues

Closes #13139

- 主要风险或取舍：花括号展开的 `cd`/`pushd` 目标现在会升级为 `ask` / force-review，不再直接放行。像 `cd {src,test}` 这样的合法工作流在以前被解析为 allow 的地方会开始询问。这是 #13139 要求的 fail-closed 方向——analyzer 无法知道 shell 实际 chdir 进了哪一个展开项，所以不能继续声称起始 cwd。

prs.title: test(web-shell): stabilize global turn navigation scroll-follow E2E (#17252)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Stabilizes the web-shell smoke test that verifies the global turn navigation rail follows transcript scrolling. The test now waits for the rail to actually reach the live tail before reading the highlighted turn, and after the narrow/wide viewport round-trip it waits for the rail to reflect an upper reading position before clicking turn 0. The click-and-jump assertions and all inputs are unchanged.

## Why it's needed

The test could fail intermittently because it read the rail highlight once the ordinal was merely non-null, before the transcript had settled at the live tail, and because it forced the rail to the top while the post-resize relayout was still following the tail. In the second case, the rail re-windowed away from turn 0 and the click waited until the test timed out with the tick detached from the DOM. Both paths are timing races in the test, not product behavior.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the named spec repeatedly from `packages/web-shell` with `npx playwright test --config playwright.config.ts web-shell.turn-navigation-scroll-follow.spec.ts --project=chromium --repeat-each=10 --workers=1`. Before the fix, the run fails at the post-widen turn-0 click because the rail re-windows to the tail; after the fix, all 10 runs pass while still asserting that clicking turn 0 jumps to `QUESTION 0` and moves the highlight to that turn.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (test-only change). Before: 2/2 local runs failed at the post-widen tick-0 click with `element was detached from the DOM, retrying`. After: 10/10 repeated runs and one `CI=1` run passed.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Playwright Chromium 149 with the web-shell Vite dev server, headless.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the test performs one extra transcript scroll before the final tick click; it changes no production code or assertions.
- Not validated / out of scope: the full two-shard web-shell smoke suite was not run locally; the named spec was repeated ten times and also run under the CI configuration.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #17252

prs.title: fix(cli): let in-session MCP enable lift glob exclusions
prs.body:
## What this PR does

`qwen serve` now logs a repeated WebSocket upgrade rejection at most once per minute per `reason@client-address`. Every other rejection still gets its 403 and is still counted — only the duplicate journal line is suppressed. An in-session `enable` now also lifts a glob exclusion from `mcp.excluded`, matching how every disable path already applied the pattern.

## Why it's needed

`logReject` in `packages/cli/src/serve/acp-http/index.ts` wrote one stderr line per rejected upgrade with no throttle or dedupe. A client whose upgrade the daemon always refuses — most often the Chrome extension retrying an origin the daemon was never told to allow — reconnects forever, so the journal accumulates thousands of identical lines a day. The issue measured ~4,000–6,000/day for a single extension origin.

Separately, every disable path matched `mcp.excluded` with `matchesAnyServerPattern`, but every enable path removed the entry with an exact `!==` / `includes` comparison. A pattern such as `foo-*` never equals the server name, so it stayed in the list and remained in the runtime union — the dialog then reported `Enabled '<name>'` while the server was still excluded.

This is the server-side third of #13966. The client halves are the extension's reconnect ladder and an autoconnect opt-out; #14022 already covers persisting that ladder across MV3 service-worker restarts.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Log throttle:

- One entry per distinct `reason@address`, holding the last time it was logged. Inside `UPGRADE_REJECT_LOG_INTERVAL_MS` the line is dropped; the socket is still destroyed with the same 403.
- The key includes the reason, not just the address, so a different rejection from the same client (say an expired token after an origin that was previously refused) is still reported immediately.
- The map is re-inserted on each log so it stays in least-recently-logged order, and is capped at `MAX_UPGRADE_REJECT_LOG_KEYS` by evicting the oldest entry. Without the cap, a daemon seeing many distinct rejected clients would grow it without bound.

Enable lifting a glob:

The enable side now filters through the same matcher, in all six places that lift an exclusion:

- `serve/routes/workspace-mcp-config.ts`
- `acp-integration/acpAgent.ts` (settings + live configs)
- `ui/opentui/dialog-data.ts`
- `ui/components/mcp/MCPManagementDialog.tsx`
- `ui/components/extensions/views/McpServerActionsView.tsx`
- `ui/components/extensions/tabs/InstalledTab.tsx`

The serve route additionally returned 409 for a glob sitting in the **target** scope — the one this call writes. That scope is owned by the caller, so its patterns are now lifted together with the exact name; only a pattern in a higher-priority scope still blocks, and that is what the 409 reports.

```sh
# from packages/cli
npx vitest run src/serve/acp-http/transport.test.ts
npx vitest run src/ui/opentui/dialog-data.test.ts
npx vitest run src/serve/workspace-qualified-rest.test.ts
npx vitest run src/ui/components/mcp/MCPManagementDialog.test.tsx src/ui/components/extensions/tabs/InstalledTab.test.tsx
```

### Evidence (Before & After)

- `transport.test.ts` — 433 passed, including two new cases: repeated identical rejections log once while a different reason still logs, and the same rejection is logged again after the window elapses.
- `dialog-data.test.ts` — 75 passed, including a new case where `srv*` sits in both the user-scope and runtime lists.
- `workspace-qualified-rest.test.ts` — 68 passed. Adds "lifts a wildcard exclusion from the scope being enabled"; retargets "rejects enabling an MCP server blocked by a wildcard" to a system-scope pattern via `QWEN_CODE_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH`, since a same-scope glob is no longer a refusal.
- `MCPManagementDialog.test.tsx` and `InstalledTab.test.tsx` — passed.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only; no dev server or sandbox.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a genuine repeat of the same upgrade rejection from the same client inside one minute is not journaled; the rejection itself is still refused and counted, and the key includes the reason so a different failure is never suppressed. On the enable side, a glob in the scope being enabled is now lifted, so an operator cannot keep a specific server excluded by a pattern that also matches it in that scope.
- Not validated / out of scope: the full `npm run build` / repo-wide typecheck. A package `tsc --noEmit` in this worktree reports ~32 errors that all pre-date this change (stale prebuilt `dist` from `main` vs. `ToolResult`/`LlmFinishedEventValue`, Node builtin typings such as `Module.enableCompileCache` and `process.execve`); none are in the files touched here.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.
- The launch-flag half of the original report ("success reported while the server stays disconnected") is not addressed: `--disable-mcp-server` is a boot-time union, so it needs a different signal than settings, and the triage note defers it until #14083 lands.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #14465

prs.title: ci(release): retry the Docker integration test suites once
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The release Docker integration script now runs its `cli` and `interactive` suites through a single helper and retries a failed suite once when the step is still within its retry budget. Before the retry it removes the containers labeled with its own job owner, so a container leaked by the first attempt cannot affect the second. A sandbox-image build failure now emits an `::error::` annotation stating that the Docker tests did not run, and a suite that fails again after the retry emits its own `::error::`; both become check-run annotations instead of leaving only "Process completed with exit code 1."

## Why it's needed

This is release-lane hardening, not the fix for the nightly failure it was originally drafted against. The motivating incident — `integration_docker` exiting 1 after 38m37s of a 120-minute job for `v0.27.1-nightly.20261110.c238beb56f` (run 42902215339, job 130132787607), with the previous nightly failing the same way (#16769) — turned out to be a **deterministic sandbox `$HOME` crash**, not shared-host transient pressure. The failed job's log is readable with a repo-scoped token (only anonymous access 403s), and the defect was fixed in #16878, which closed #16861. A bounded retry cannot change a deterministic failure's outcome: both attempts fail and the lane stays red (pinned by the `keeps the lane red when the motivating 38-minute cli failure repeats` case).

What the release lane actually lacked, and this PR adds, is the resilience and diagnosability the `sandbox:none` E2E leg already has (#10355): a suite-level retry for genuinely transient failures, and explicit build-versus-test failure annotations. The release job has 120 minutes, so a failed attempt early in the step leaves room for one more; the E2E Docker leg's 60-minute job cannot fit two attempts, which is why it does not retry. The build failure path is made explicit but deliberately not retried, because the build holds the shared host build mutex.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the focused script suite; it drives the real release Docker script against stubbed `git`, `node`, `docker`, `npm`, `npx`, `date`, `timeout`, and `flock` binaries. The cases simulate a first-attempt suite failure followed by a pass, the same for the second suite, a second failure after the retry, a failure after the retry budget is spent, a build failure, and check that job-owned containers are removed before the retry.

Expected: 135 tests collected. On Linux all 135 run; on macOS 134 pass and 1 pre-existing platform-conditional case skips (`executes the workspace wipe against guard branches`, which needs GNU `realpath -m`).

Then inspect the script: a failed suite is retried once only when `elapsed_seconds + max(attempt_seconds, expected_suite_seconds) + remaining_suite_seconds <= DOCKER_TEST_STEP_BUDGET_SECONDS` — a 6600s step budget, with `expected_suite_seconds` 2400s for `cli` and 1260s for `interactive`, and 1260s reserved for `interactive` when retrying `cli`. A failure that would overrun the budget exits with the budget `::error::` instead of retrying, and a build failure prints the new annotation without running vitest.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A for screenshots: this changes CI orchestration, not a user-visible or interactive surface. The before/after behavior is pinned by the script harness's call log and the mutation probes listed in the E2E report.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Local Linux container without a Docker daemon or socket. Build, typecheck, lint, the focused script suite, and ShellCheck 0.11.0 were run; the real Docker integration lane was not run locally because the daemon is unavailable.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a genuinely transient suite failure can add one extra suite run (roughly 30–40 minutes) before the step finishes. The budget gate refuses a retry that would overrun the 120-minute job, and a deterministic failure still fails both attempts, so the step cannot turn green on a real defect.
- Not validated / out of scope: the exact self-hosted Docker lane under real transient load. The motivating nightly failure was a deterministic sandbox `$HOME` crash, fixed in #16878, not a transient this retry absorbs; this change hardens the lane against genuinely transient failures and makes future build-versus-test failures visible through check-run annotations. Build failures are not retried because the build holds the shared host build mutex.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. No product code, settings, or user-facing behavior changes.

## Linked Issues

Part of #16861 (closed by #16878, the deterministic sandbox `$HOME` fix; this PR is release-lane hardening, not that fix).

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

发布 Docker 集成脚本现在通过一个辅助函数运行 `cli` 和 `interactive` 套件，并在步骤仍处于重试预算内时，对失败的套件重试一次。重试前，它会删除带有本任务 owner 标签的容器，避免第一次尝试泄漏的容器影响第二次。沙箱镜像构建失败现在会输出 `::error::` 注解，说明 Docker 测试没有运行；重试后再次失败的套件也会输出自己的 `::error::`；两者都会成为 check-run 注解，而不是只留下 "Process completed with exit code 1."

## 为什么需要这个改动

这是发布流水线的加固，而不是它最初所针对的那次夜间发布失败的修复。触发事件——`v0.27.1-nightly.20261110.c238beb56f` 的 `integration_docker` 在 120 分钟任务的第 38 分 37 秒以退出码 1 结束（运行 42902215339，任务 130132787607），且前一次夜间发布也以同样方式失败（#16769）——最终查明是**确定性的沙箱 `$HOME` 崩溃**，而不是共享宿主机瞬时压力。失败任务的日志用仓库作用域 token 可读（只有匿名访问才 403），该缺陷已在 #16878 修复，#16861 随之关闭。有界重试无法改变确定性失败的结果：两次尝试都会失败，流水线保持红色（由 `keeps the lane red when the motivating 38-minute cli failure repeats` 用例固定）。

发布流水线真正缺少、而本 PR 补上的，是 `sandbox:none` E2E 流水线早已具备的韧性与可诊断性（#10355）：针对真正瞬时失败的套件级重试，以及显式的「构建失败 vs 测试失败」注解。发布任务有 120 分钟，因此步骤早期的失败尝试仍留有一次重试的空间；E2E Docker 流水线的 60 分钟任务装不下两次尝试，这正是它不重试的原因。构建失败路径被显式标注，但有意不重试，因为构建持有共享宿主机的构建互斥锁。

## 审查者测试计划

### 如何验证

运行聚焦的脚本测试套件；它用桩程序 `git`、`node`、`docker`、`npm`、`npx`、`date`、`timeout` 和 `flock` 驱动真实的发布 Docker 脚本。用例模拟第一次套件失败后通过、第二个套件同样失败后通过、重试后再次失败、重试预算耗尽后的失败、构建失败，并检查重试前会删除本任务的容器。

预期：收集 135 个测试。Linux 上全部 135 个运行；macOS 上 134 个通过、1 个既有的平台条件用例跳过（`executes the workspace wipe against guard branches`，需要 GNU `realpath -m`）。

然后检查脚本：失败的套件只有在 `elapsed_seconds + max(attempt_seconds, expected_suite_seconds) + remaining_suite_seconds <= DOCKER_TEST_STEP_BUDGET_SECONDS` 时才重试一次——步骤预算 6600 秒，`expected_suite_seconds` 对 `cli` 为 2400 秒、对 `interactive` 为 1260 秒，重试 `cli` 时为 `interactive` 预留 1260 秒。会超出预算的失败将带着预算 `::error::` 退出而不是重试；构建失败会打印新注解且不运行 vitest。

### 证据（改动前后）

截图不适用：这改变的是 CI 编排，不是用户可见或交互式界面。改动前后的行为由脚本 harness 的调用日志和 E2E 报告中列出的变异探测固定。

### 测试环境

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ⚠️  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ✅  |

### 环境（可选）

本地 Linux 容器，没有 Docker daemon 或 socket。已运行构建、类型检查、lint、聚焦脚本套件和 ShellCheck 0.11.0；由于 daemon 不可用，本地未运行真实 Docker 集成流水线。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：真正的瞬时套件失败可能会在步骤结束前多跑一次套件（大约 30–40 分钟）。预算门限会拒绝将超出 120 分钟任务的重试，确定性失败仍然会让两次尝试都失败，因此步骤不会因为真实缺陷而变绿。
- 未验证 / 范围外：真实瞬时负载下的确切自托管 Docker 流水线。触发的那次夜间发布失败是确定性沙箱 `$HOME` 崩溃，已在 #16878 修复，不是本重试能吸收的瞬时故障；此改动加固流水线以应对真正的瞬时失败，并通过 check-run 注解让未来的构建失败与测试失败可见。构建失败不重试，因为构建持有共享宿主机构建互斥锁。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。没有产品代码、设置或用户可见行为变更。

## 关联 Issue

Part of #16861（已由 #16878 关闭，即确定性沙箱 `$HOME` 修复；本 PR 是发布流水线加固，不是该修复）。

prs.title: feat(acp): route live and read-only Agent Host sessions through the shared tool batch
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Sessions with live tools and read-only Agent Host sessions move onto the shared loop's tool batch, and `SendMessageOptions.toolLoopGuardsByHost` is removed from core. Concretely:

- ACP's batch gains two host inputs: a reference-based live-tool trust check (the session's three live tool instances, matched by identity rather than name) and the session's read-only refusal message. The Agent Host workspace guard stays on the session `Config` (`Config.getToolInvocationGuard()`) and is evaluated by `CoreToolScheduler` at its execute boundary, before the tool actually runs.
- `#runsToolsOnSharedBatch()` no longer special-cases either session kind and is removed outright; every ACP turn now runs its tool batch on the shared loop.
- Core no longer carries the flag: the client's always-on loop guards, the todo reminder, and result-aware duplicate recording apply to every ACP turn again.

## Why it's needed

This is the ACP row of #17045. The tracker is converging ACP onto the shared agent loop; live-tool and Agent Host sessions were the last two kinds still running their own tool step, which meant the client's loop guards and todo reminder were suppressed for exactly the turns that need them (a live session's model can still run a truncated edit; a read-only Agent Host session still wants its refusals counted by the same guards). Routing both through the shared batch restores those invariants without changing any default switch, and lets the flag — the last "host runs the guards" escape hatch — leave the public `SendMessageOptions` surface.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Behavior-level checks a reviewer can confirm:

1. Live-tool session on the shared batch: enable Live Appshot in a session, let the model request a truncated edit, and confirm the edit is refused by the shared scheduler's cut-off guard (the session reports "truncated due to max_tokens limit" and never calls the tool) while the trusted live tools themselves still run without a permission prompt.
2. Agent Host read-only session on the shared batch: create a session whose `getSessionSourceType()` is `agent-host`, then have the model request (a) a workspace read, which should execute and let the batch and turn continue (`stopAfterPermissionCancel=false`), and (b) an approval-needing call, which should settle per call as `EXECUTION_DENIED`/`not_started` with the session's refusal message carrying the real tool name, zero `session/request_permission`, and no effect on the other calls in the batch. The Agent Host workspace guard (`Config.getToolInvocationGuard()`) is evaluated by `CoreToolScheduler` at its execute boundary, so an out-of-workspace path is denied there.
3. Ordinary sessions are unchanged: a regular tool still completes the ACP permission round-trip (`request_permission` → `onConfirm` → execute).

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (non-UI refactor; the diff is driven by `Session.test.ts` and `client.test.ts` behavior assertions).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A   |
|  🐧 Linux  |  N/A   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit-level only: `packages/cli` `Session.test.ts` (1528/1528 pass) and `packages/core` `client.test.ts` (639/639 pass) under the worktree's local vitest.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a genuine live-task long-poll regression would show up as the always-on consecutive-identical guard counting identical live calls; the design notes call for recording live task tool identities by tool-instance reference in the batch's duplicate handling rather than broadening core's exemptions if that shows up; trust is by instance identity, so a same-named tool inherits none of it.
- Not validated / out of scope: full-stack integration scenarios per session kind (fake ACP client + fake daemon `extMethod` for live tools; refused edit with zero outbound `request_permission` for Agent Host) land with the row's next slice.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none for callers that never set `toolLoopGuardsByHost`; ACP no longer emits it.

Design docs: [English](./docs/design/2026-11-14-acp-live-agent-host-shared-batch.md) · [简体中文](./docs/design/2026-11-14-acp-live-agent-host-shared-batch.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Part of #17045. Stacks on #17181.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

带 live 工具的会话和只读的 Agent Host 会话迁到共享 loop 的工具批，core 里的 `SendMessageOptions.toolLoopGuardsByHost` 一并移除。具体地：

- ACP 的批拿到两个宿主输入：按引用（而非名字）匹配三个 live 工具实例的信任检查、会话的只读拒绝文案。Agent Host 的工作区围栏留在会话 Config（`Config.getToolInvocationGuard()`），由 `CoreToolScheduler` 在 execute 边界（即工具真正执行之前）求值。
- `#runsToolsOnSharedBatch()` 不再对两类会话特判并整体删除；每个 ACP 轮次的工具批都走共享 loop。
- core 不再携带该 flag：client 的 always-on loop guards、todo reminder 和结果感知去重重新对每个 ACP 轮次生效。

## 为什么需要

这是 #17045 里 ACP 的一行。追踪 issue 正在把 ACP 收敛到共享 agent loop；live 工具和 Agent Host 会话是最后两个还在跑自己工具步骤的类别，意味着 client 的 loop guards 和 todo reminder 恰好在最需要的轮次上被压制（live 会话的模型仍可能发出被截断的 edit；只读 Agent Host 会话仍希望它的拒绝被同一套 guard 计数）。把两者迁到共享批能在不改默认开关的前提下恢复这些不变量，并让这条「宿主自己跑守卫」的逃生口离开 `SendMessageOptions` 的公共面。

## 评审验证计划

### 如何验证

可以按行为核对：

1. live 会话走共享批：在会话里启用 Live Appshot，让模型请求一个被截断的 edit，确认它被共享调度器的截断守卫拒绝（会话报告 "truncated due to max_tokens limit"，工具未被调用），而可信 live 工具本身仍不经权限提问运行。
2. 只读 Agent Host 会话走共享批：创建 `getSessionSourceType()` 为 `agent-host` 的会话，让模型请求 (a) 一个工作区内的读——应正常执行，批与轮次继续（`stopAfterPermissionCancel=false`）；(b) 一个需审批的调用——应逐调用结算为 `EXECUTION_DENIED`/`not_started`，拒绝文案带真实工具名，零 `session/request_permission`，且同批其它调用不受影响。Agent Host 的工作区围栏（`Config.getToolInvocationGuard()`）由 `CoreToolScheduler` 在 execute 边界求值，越出工作区的路径在那里被拒。
3. 普通会话不变：普通工具仍走完 ACP 权限往返（`request_permission` → `onConfirm` → execute）。

### 证据（前后对比）

N/A（非 UI 重构；diff 由 `Session.test.ts` 和 `client.test.ts` 的行为断言驱动）。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A   |
|  🐧 Linux  |  N/A   |

### 环境（可选）

仅单元级：worktree 本地 vitest 下的 `packages/cli` `Session.test.ts`（1528/1528 通过）和 `packages/core` `client.test.ts`（639/639 通过）。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险 / 取舍：若真实出现 live 任务长轮询回归，会表现为 always-on 的连续相同调用守卫把相同的 live 调用计数；设计说明里约定这种情况下在批的重复处理里按工具实例引用记录 live 任务工具身份，而不是放宽 core 的豁免；信任按实例身份判定，同名工具不继承。
- 未验证 / 不在范围：每类会话一个全栈集成场景（live 用 fake ACP client + fake daemon `extMethod`；Agent Host 断言被拒 edit 且零次外发 `request_permission`）随本行的下一片段落地。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：对从未设置 `toolLoopGuardsByHost` 的调用方无影响；ACP 不再发出它。

设计文档：[English](./docs/design/2026-11-14-acp-live-agent-host-shared-batch.md) · [简体中文](./docs/design/2026-11-14-acp-live-agent-host-shared-batch.zh-CN.md)

## 关联 Issue

Part of #17045。叠加在 #17181 之上。

</details>

auto_merge.commit_title: feat(acp): route live and read-only Agent Host sessions through the shared tool batch (#17218)
auto_merge.commit_message:
* feat(cli): run each ACP round in one runAgentLoop call

With experimental.unifiedAgentLoop on, each round of an ACP prompt,
Goal, cron or background-notification turn runs its model request and
its tool batch in one runAgentLoop call, on the event-bus kernel when
experimental.eventBusAgentLoop is on too. The batch waits in onRoundEnd
for the turn to hand it the session's scheduler, the answered calls,
the batch's tool signal, its launch check and its result callback; a
turn that leaves first closes the round's call. The round helper the
Ink TUI uses takes those with the hand-off, lets the batch record its
own results, and runs the batch's tools in the async context of the
hand-off, which carries the turn's prompt ID, todo work chain and
full-turn model override. A prompt that UserPromptSubmit blocked runs
its first round in a call of its own. Sessions with live tools and
read-only Agent Host sessions keep their own tool step.

The ACP parity suite runs each scenario a third time on the kernel and
matches the event-bus adapter's log to the session's rounds.

* test(cli): run ACP's queued-input and Goal round tests on the kernel too

A response that queued input cuts short, or a turn kept at its stop
point, aborts the round's signal while the turn goes on, which the
kernel takes as a cancellation. Run those tests with the kernel off and
on, and say in the design that such a round still ends inside the cap.

* fix(cli): preserve ACP results at the cancellation deadline

* fix(cli): deliver and budget settled ACP tool results on cancel

* feat(acp): route live and read-only Agent Host sessions through the shared tool batch

Sessions with live tools and read-only Agent Host sessions no longer run
ACP's own tool step; they take the shared loop's batch through host inputs
on the batch: reference-based live-tool trust, the session's read-only
refusal message, and the Agent Host invocation guard at the batch's
launch boundary.

With every session on the shared batch, `#runsToolsOnSharedBatch()` is
removed and `SendMessageOptions.toolLoopGuardsByHost` is gone from core:
the client runs its loop guards, todo reminder, and result-aware duplicate
recording for every ACP turn again.

Part of #17045 (ACP row). Stacks on #17181.

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

* style(acp): apply Prettier to the merged batch files

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

* fix(acp): run the Agent Host invocation guard inside the executor wrapper

The shared loop's beforeToolLaunch hook is synchronous, but the Agent
Host invocation guard evaluates asynchronously. Move the guard into the
executor wrapper's beforeLaunch hook, which supports Promise<boolean>.

Also fix the test type errors main surfaced: give runEachTool's results
array an explicit type and drop the redundant RoundEvent cast.

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

* fix(acp): move the invocation guard to the scheduler's beforeToolLaunch

The loop-level beforeToolLaunch hook is synchronous, but the scheduler
option supports Promise<boolean>. Put the Agent Host invocation guard
there and drop the executor wrapper.

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

* test(cli): narrow the truncated-call mutation to its value

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

* test(cli): add the shared-batch host inputs to the tool-batch fixture

The batch host gained getTool and isTrustedLiveTool, but the runAcpToolBatch fixture was cast past the interface without them. Only the early-settling cancellation test reaches the batch-level beforeToolLaunch after the executor resolves (the fake-timer tests settle past the cap, the rest stub the loop), so the missing lookup surfaced there as 'host.getTool is not a function' plus three unhandled rejections, failing Linux unit tests shard 1. Give the fixture the two members with ordinary-session values; the hook then behaves exactly as it did before the host inputs landed.

* fix(acp): wire scheduler-level live trust and Agent Host guards on shared batch

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

* refactor(acp): drop stub-serving tolerances and the duplicate invocation guard

Restore the strict Config calls the shared-batch work had relaxed for
incomplete test stubs: `getDisableAllHooks()` and `getMessageBus()` are no
longer optional calls, and `getConfirmationDetails` is invoked directly again
instead of synthesizing an `info` confirmation. A malformed invocation now
fails instead of being silently approved; the fixtures that needed the
tolerance provide the interface themselves.

Remove `CoreToolSchedulerOptions.invocationGuard` and its schedule-phase
evaluation. It duplicated the Agent Host policy already enforced by
`Config.getToolInvocationGuard()` at the execution boundary, and the copy the
session built dropped the Config's upstream managed guard. `readOnlyRefusalMessage`
and live-tool identity trust stay on the scheduler; workspace confinement
stays on the session Config.

* docs(acp): fix by-name trust wording and stale batch guard comment

R1-10: the EN design risk bullet still said live task tool identities are
recorded by name, while the ZH version and the implementation trust tools by
instance reference. State tool-instance identity in EN and spell out in both
versions that a same-named tool inherits no trust.

R1-12: two Session comments still claimed the shared batch carries the Agent
Host invocation guard after the batch stopped forwarding it. Point the guard
at the session Config's getToolInvocationGuard(), evaluated by the scheduler
at its execution boundary.

Comment and documentation wording only; no behavior change.

* fix(acp): keep live trust to the tools ACP bypassed, and honour a hook's ask

The shared batch trusted `speak_to_user` along with the screen-context and
live-task tools, but ACP's own executor bypassed the permission flow for the
latter two only. A user's `permissions.deny` / `permissions.ask` rule for
`speak_to_user` therefore stopped applying on the move: the call scheduled and
spoke without ever evaluating the flow. The trusted set now matches the one the
executor had, so the voice tool keeps its own `allow` default and still fails
closed on a configured rule.

The trusted short-circuit also ran before a PreToolUse hook's `ask` could be
answered, discarding the user's own request for confirmation. A hook ask now
keeps the call on the confirmation path.

The scheduler's tolerance for an `ensureTool` result of `true` was serving a
test double, not a real registry: the registry resolves an instance or nothing.
The fixture returns an instance now and the dead branch is gone.

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

* test(cli): pin the live trust boundary by instance and by permission rule

The live-tool integration case asserted `isToolEnabled` was not called with
`expect.anything()` for both optional arguments, which the scheduler passes as
`undefined` — so the negated pattern never matched and the assertion stayed
green even with the trust bypass removed. It now checks the recorded argument
names, and goes red when the bypass is dropped.

Two cases pin the boundaries the design names as its security contract: a
second instance registered under a live tool's name must still reach
`isToolEnabled`, and a `speak_to_user` call under a matching deny rule must be
refused. Both fail if the predicate compares names instead of instances, or if
the voice tool is trusted again.

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

* docs(design): name the trusted live set and the Agent Host read policy exactly

The design counted "three trusted live tool instances" where it meant three
predicates; the set is `capture_screen_context` plus the five live-task tools,
and the voice tool is not in it. An auditor sizing which tools bypass the
permission gates was pointed away from the writable part of that surface. Both
languages and the `AcpToolBatchHost` comment now enumerate the set instead.

The Agent Host section promised in-workspace `glob` executes normally and named
`ls` / `grep`, neither of which is the registered name. The session registers
`read_file`, `grep_search` and `list_directory`, and the guard refuses `glob`,
`grep_search` with a glob filter, and the two media reads outright — a host
integrator reading the old text would either find every glob call denied or
"fix" the guard into the hole its comment documents.

The always-on tier has no background-task allowance: its streak is keyed on
name plus arguments and the only result-aware exemption is `task_list`. The
approach paragraph claimed one while the risk section stated the opposite, so
the known live-poll exposure read as optional hardening rather than the only
mitigation.

The umbrella document still presented the removed `toolLoopGuardsByHost` as the
live mechanism one screen after declaring it removed, and still told the next
contributor to append a row to a table that became a prose list. Both are
re-pointed, in both languages. The removal is also explained rather than merely
asserted: with the switch off an ACP turn sends through the session's own chat
and never reaches the client's reminder and guard branches, so nothing runs
twice without the option.

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: qqqys <qys177@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: qqqys <266654365+qqqys@users.noreply.github.com>
