issues.body:
## Summary

Expose a capability-specific embedding preflight/recovery diagnostic for Codex OAuth-only installations. Working Codex inference and available subscription usage do not establish that the same profile is entitled to native OpenAI embeddings.

This supplies fresh stable-release evidence related to closed #87677, whose last comment asks for a new report after retrying on the latest release. The current symptom differs from its historical missing-API-key gate: OAuth is selected, but the provider returns a quota/entitlement rejection.

## Observed setup

- Official OpenClaw 2026.10.7 (157d8c2), npm global.
- macOS 26.6.2 arm64, supported Node 24.22.1.
- Main model: openai/gpt-6.1-sol, runtime codex; OAuth route usable, no model fallback.
- No separate OpenAI API key configured for this test.
- Read-only local inspection confirms the selected profile belongs to the native Codex account. No credential is included here.
- Public docs describe Codex OAuth embeddings as conditional on account embedding access: https://docs.openclaw.ai/providers/openai/authentication

## Current-release synthetic controls

```sh
openclaw infer model run --gateway --agent main --model openai/gpt-6.1-sol --prompt 'Reply exactly OK.' --json
# ok=true, provider=openai, model=gpt-6.1-sol, transport=gateway, text=OK

openclaw infer embedding create --agent main --provider openai --model openai/text-embedding-3-small --text 'A quiet cedar forest after rain.' --json
# fails: HTTP429, insufficient_quota / credit_balance_exhausted
```

Before the upgrade, fixed-sentence controls for both text-embedding-3-large and text-embedding-3-small produced the same rejection. No private memory, email or calendar content was sent. No provider baseUrl override is configured; this is not the explicit chat-base-URL inheritance case in #165476.

## Requested behavior

1. Distinguish a usable Codex chat route from verified embedding entitlement, rather than letting agents infer that all Codex/subscription credits are exhausted.
2. Document an observable, bounded way to verify the conditional OAuth embedding access and identify the provider-owned supported endpoint.
3. If this account class has no supported subscription-only embedding route, say so explicitly and present existing keyless/local alternatives. Do not silently copy credentials, select a paid fallback or migrate an index.
4. Let callers preflight this capability before enqueueing private-document catch-up work.

## Scope and open question

This is not a claim that OpenClaw can grant upstream account entitlement, or that every Codex OAuth account must have embedding access. Which supported subscription-only embedding contract, if any, should this installation use? If there is none, the requested improvement is accurate capability diagnostics and documentation.

Existing model-auth policy accepts eligible Codex OAuth for embeddings, while the synthetic runtime result rejects this account at the provider boundary. Native Codex chat succeeds. No separate API-key purchase or provider migration is requested by this report.

issues.body:
**Component:** `agents/runtime-execution-facts` (runtime-context emitter) + `agents/bash-process-registry` (exec session registry)
**Affected versions:** confirmed on **2026.10.7** (`v2026.10.7` -> `157d8c2`, matching the installed build) and still present in **2026.10.10-beta.3**. **Partially fixed on `origin/main`** @ `906e0b06be` ("fix(agents): preserve safe inspection and outcomes during recovery", #177943) - requirement (a) only. **That commit is in NO release tag and is in neither published bundle**, so the fix is unreleased. Requirements (b)-(d) are **still unfixed on `origin/main`**.
**Severity:** low — it misreports exec-session liveness in the prompt; it does not abort turns. But it is the same family as the settle-wake loop: state that says "running" and is never reconciled when the process dies.
**Related:** `OPENCLAW_ISSUE_settle_wake_late_kill_20261026.md`

> **Verification method.** Release status was confirmed three ways: (1) `git merge-base --is-ancestor 906e0b06be <tag>` against real fetched tags (`v2026.10.7`, `v2026.10.10-beta.2`, `v2026.10.10-beta.3` - all **NO**); (2) by grepping the **published npm bundles** for the new string (`npm pack openclaw@<version>` -> `grep -rl "No active exec-tool sessions" package/dist/` -> **0 files** in both 2026.10.7 and 2026.10.10-beta.3); and (3) by `git log -S "No active exec-tool sessions" origin/main -- src/agents/runtime-execution-facts.ts`, which returns **`906e0b06be` as the single introducing commit**. A shallow clone's empty tag list is not evidence of absence.
>
> **Correction (2026-10-26, third pass - supersedes two earlier revisions).** The attribution in this draft has flip-flopped and this revision is the one verified against the GitHub API. The fix commit is **`906e0b06be92f6b17d5e5dcfe3044b4e9b9b277d`** - "fix(agents): preserve safe inspection and outcomes during recovery" (#177943, merged 2026-10-20T12:11:39Z). Verified directly against `https://api.github.com/repos/openclaw/openclaw/commits/906e0b06be`: it is a real commit touching 56 files, one of which is `src/agents/runtime-execution-facts.ts` (+7/-1), and that file's patch contains both `includeEmptySnapshots` and the literal string `No active exec-tool sessions`.
>
> The sha **`e5c1ae9166c81367e6a8e5358f2ca379583389f2`** is **"feat(ios): hide automation sessions from ordinary session lists" (#178620)** and touches exactly 8 files, **all under `apps/` (iOS/Swift) plus `docs/platforms/ios.md`** - it cannot be the fix for a Node-side runtime-context fact. A second revision of this draft had asserted the opposite (that `906e0b06be` "does not exist" and `e5c1ae916` was correct); that assertion was wrong and is withdrawn here.
>
> **What `906e0b06be` does NOT fix.** It only makes the empty-snapshot fallback *possible* (requirement a). The registry still performs **no pid-liveness check** - `git grep -E "kill\(.*, *0\)|ESRCH" origin/main -- src/agents/bash-process-registry.ts` returns **nothing** - so requirements (b), (c) and (d) remain open on `origin/main`.

---

## 1. Summary

The runtime context reports exec sessions as `running` forever, even after those processes have exited and the exec registry has already forgotten them. The stale fact is re-injected on every turn, unchanged, and no live state can correct it.

Observed on the reporter's host: the same two-entry block was re-injected **fourteen times, byte-identical**, listing two PIDs that had been dead for hours, while genuinely live exec sessions came and went without appearing.

## 2. Reproduction

1. Start a long-running exec session (e.g. `sleep 180`) from a turn.
2. Let it finish (or kill it).
3. Observe the runtime context on subsequent turns.

The session is still listed with `running pid=<pid>`.

## 3. Evidence that the fact is stale rather than live

On the reporter's host, two sessions were listed as running:

```
- plaid-reef running pid=1281178 cwd=/home/jimmylu/.openclaw/workspace-main :: sleep 180;
- quick-haven running pid=1281576 cwd=/home/jimmylu/.openclaw/workspace-main :: sleep 150;
```

Both PIDs were verified dead **six independent ways**:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `kill -0 <pid>` | fails (no such process) |
| `kill -9 <pid>` | exit 1 — "no such process" |
| `/proc/<pid>` | absent |
| `ps -p <pid>` | empty |
| host-wide scan for `comm=sleep` | no matching process at all |
| exec registry (`process list`) | **both sessions absent** |

The last row is decisive: the runtime-context emitter and the `process` tool's `list` action read the **same map** —

- `bash-process-references.ts` → `listRunningSessions()`
- `bash-tools.process.ts` → `listRunningSessions()`

— both imported from `bash-process-registry`. A live read of one map cannot show two sessions in the context while `list` shows neither. **The context is therefore not recomputed from live state; it is a persisted, replayed turn-start fact.**

A control experiment confirmed this: a session started during one turn (`pid 1290739`, verified alive) **never appeared** in the next turn's context, while the two long-dead sessions were still listed.

## 4. Root cause

### 4a. The installed emitter cannot supersede a stale fact

The 2026.10.7 bundle emits the exec-session block only when the registry is **non-empty**:

```js
// dist/messages-CfuAf9j-.mjs
if (sessions.length) {
  sections.push(["Active exec sessions:", sessions.join("\n")].join("\n"));
}
```

There is no empty-state fallback — `grep -c "No active exec-tool sessions" dist/messages-CfuAf9j-.mjs` → **0**. The same is true of the newer `v2026.10.10-beta.3` tarball (**0 files**), and its wording is still the old `Active exec sessions:`.

So once the registry becomes empty, the emitter produces **nothing**, and the last non-empty fact remains the effective one. Because the fact is persisted in the session transcript and replayed each turn, it can never be corrected: the only way to overwrite it would be to emit a fresh (empty) fact, which neither published build can do.

### 4b. Upstream main fixes the supersede problem

`origin/main` @ `906e0b06be` adds `includeEmptySnapshots`:

```ts
/** Retained carriers need explicit empty snapshots to supersede older facts. */
includeEmptySnapshots?: boolean;
...
if (sessions.length || includeEmptySnapshots) {
  sections.push([
    "Active exec sessions at turn start (snapshot):",
    ...
    sessions.join("\n") || "No active exec-tool sessions in this scope at turn start.",
  ].join("\n"));
}
```

and wires it at the call site:

```ts
includeEmptySnapshots: transcriptPolicy.appendOnlyRuntimeContext === true,
```

This is the fix for the observed symptom — but it is **unreleased**.

### 4c. A second gap remains even on upstream main: no liveness check on read

Neither `bash-process-registry.ts` nor `bash-process-references.ts` verifies that the process is still alive when listing:

```
grep -c "kill(pid, 0)\|ESRCH\|isAlive" src/agents/bash-process-registry.ts src/agents/bash-process-references.ts
→ 0, 0
```

`markExited()` (`bash-process-registry.ts:479` → `moveToFinished()`) is the **only** removal path when a process exits. If a process dies without that path being taken — e.g. the supervisor is torn down, or cleanup is interrupted — the registry entry stays in `runningSessions` forever and is reported as `running` even on upstream main.

Observed on the reporter's host alongside the stale fact:

```
service child cleanup did not complete before its hard deadline; pending:
{"closingReceipt":true,"controlClose":true,"relayExit":true,"lineageEof":true,
 "extinctionUnconfirmed":true,"stdoutEnd":true,"stderrEnd":true}
```

`extinctionUnconfirmed: true` is exactly the condition where the supervisor cannot confirm the child's death — and therefore cannot call `markExited`.

## 5. Requirements

| # | Requirement |
|---|---|
| (a) | The exec-session runtime fact must be **supersedable**: when the registry is empty, emit an explicit empty fact so a previously persisted non-empty fact is replaced rather than replayed forever. *(Partially fixed on `origin/main` @ `906e0b06be`, unreleased - requirement (a) only; (b)-(d) still open.)* |
| (b) | When listing active sessions, **verify pid liveness** (`kill(pid, 0)`) and treat a dead pid as exited — the registry must not report a process that no longer exists. |
| (c) | A session whose process died without a terminal notification (e.g. `extinctionUnconfirmed`) must be reconciled into a terminal state rather than left `running`. |
| (d) | `process kill` should settle the registry entry, not only cancel the supervisor. Today the entry is dropped only by `process remove` (`deleteSession()` → `runningSessions.delete`); a plain `kill` leaves a phantom `running` session. |

## 6. Notes for maintainers

- The wording difference is a reliable version marker: `2026.10.7` emits `"Active exec sessions:"`, while `origin/main` emits `"Active exec sessions at turn start (snapshot):"`.
- The registry exposes a test-only reset (`resetProcessRegistryForTests`) via `globalThis[Symbol.for("openclaw.bashProcessRegistryTestApi")]`.
- The exec registry is consulted by the runtime-context emitter (`bash-process-references.ts`), the `process` tool (`bash-tools.process.ts`), and `gateway-active-work` — so a stale entry can affect more than the prompt.

## 7. Environment

- openclaw 2026.10.7 (`v2026.10.7` → `157d8c2`, the installed build) and 2026.10.10-beta.3 — both affected
- node v24.22.1, Linux 6.8.0-146-generic
- `origin/main` @ `2cfde9ae7` (2026-10-26) for the upstream fix reference; fix commit `906e0b06be` (#177943) is on `origin/main` but in no release tag

issues.body:
## Summary
On Discord, subsequent replies/progress appear to stop after a user sends a clarification during active tool/delegated work, while newer assistant text is visible in the web conversation. Discord can remain on an older task/progress message with typing activity. This affects later updates, not just the initial acknowledgment.

**Status: user-observed cross-surface discrepancy with correlated real completion-wake/admission failures; no deterministic end-to-end delivery-loss reproduction or root cause established.** This report does not claim every web commentary segment was eligible for Discord or that a generated final was permanently lost.

## Environment
Observed October 25, 2026. OpenClaw core/Discord plugin 2026.10.7; release-matched investigation source 157d8c2bc3ea2fa183afdc11088e69690bf8e64e. macOS arm64, Node26.12.1. Prior read-only configuration observation found Discord progress mode and tool progress enabled. Effective per-turn queue/expectation overrides still need correlation. No live fixes or synthetic Discord sends were performed.

## User-reported sequence (not a deterministic reproduction)
1. Begin a multi-step task that uses tools and delegated children.
2. While it is working, send a clarification in the same Discord conversation.
3. Let child completions and requester continuation occur.
4. Compare newer assistant messages/progress in the web conversation against the Discord bottom/task message.

Paired screenshots around14:35–14:36 and14:49 Eastern showed newer web text while Discord remained on an older response. Private screenshots/business content are omitted. Some web presentation rows shared one assistant ID; apparent duplication is not evidence of duplicate generation or sends.

## Expected
Eligible replies/progress should reach the correct Discord turn/draft owner. Intentionally filtered commentary should not be confused with lost final delivery. Completion failures should settle/retry visibly rather than leave an apparently stuck progress message.

## Operational evidence
During the later affected continuation, bounded runtime logs report:
- 14:45:48,14:47:07,14:50:06 Eastern: completion wake `runtime_rejected`, with `queued steering message was not committed to the transcript before timeout`.
- 14:47:48,14:49:07: direct completion fallback failed with `SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED`.

These are real completion/admission failures correlated with the affected continuation, not conclusions inferred from screenshots. They do **not** establish that human input caused the failure, identify a Discord HTTP error, or locate a unique producer of SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED. The code has multiple producers, including prepared-source invalidation and command admission session disappearance/replacement. A separate expected-session revision mismatch emits UNAVAILABLE, not that code.

The earlier clarification final visibly arrived in Discord. Later recovered missing text includes intermediate commentary; no later generated final in the affected window has been recovered. Historical POST/PATCH/DELETE receipts and effective owner/adoption decisions remain unavailable. Supported message readback encountered provider/account-context prerequisites; no bypass was attempted.

## Offline investigation: what passes, and what it does not prove
- **13 scoped release-matched core cases pass**: real transcript commit, timeout/removal, consumed-but-unconfirmed input, explicit abort, admission guards and completion custody/retry. Removed queued input falls back once with original route/account; consumed input is not replayed. Rejection preserves retryable completion debt in tested paths. External model/Gateway boundaries are mocked where disclosed. No debt-loss invariant reproduced.
- **4 public Discord ingress/model/correction/lifecycle cases pass**, independently reviewed: raw inbound handling, real preflight/core dispatch, synthetic model stream, actual Discord delivery assembly against mocked REST. Active human correction durably commits once; exact REST sequence is preview POST → channel GET → original source final POST → preview DELETE → channel GET → corrected source final POST. Three POSTs mean one preview plus two different source-turn finals; zero PATCHes. Cleanup retires the test scheduler/MCP/resource host. This is ordinary partial-draft custody, **not child-owned retained progress**.
- Source-boundary checks show optional/unmentioned expectation may intentionally suppress queued progress while final delivery remains permitted, and retained child projections forward prepared tool activity rather than arbitrary commentary. Thus web presence alone does not prove Discord eligibility.
- The remaining full delegated-child composition stops **before accepted child registration**: the offline host does not supply a usable native in-process Gateway/source binding, and actual native spawn refuses credentials before any WebSocket. No accepted child/cohort/debt/adoption/wake is proved there. This is a test-host limitation, not a reproduced product delivery defect. No credentials or guard bypass were used.

The missing seam is real user-input admission + child registry/cohort + retained progress adoption + requester completion wake/fallback + eligible Discord final/retirement, in one supported isolated host. Need successful-commit control versus queued-timeout-removal and consumed input, retaining real source/session/transport guards. Do not relax lifecycle checks or replay consumed work to make it pass.

## Related reports (not established duplicates)
- #177852: intentional progress suppression for accepted unmentioned/room-event input; per-turn expectation must be checked here.
- #139217: web commentary absent from Discord, with finals arriving normally.
- #149640 (closed): older queued-followup stale-draft cleanup; installed2026.10.7 already has queued-settlement cleanup.
- #169076: older user input during sessions_yield admission/deadletter report.
- #178408: Slack post-yield tool-context failure; not proof of Discord delivery failure.

Separate from compaction-notice suppression #183657/#183658 and manual script refresh-owner #170985. No causal link to either established. No safe production mitigation selected.

issues.body:
### What happens

On a phone, a dashboard an agent built on desktop is hard to read and hard to scroll:

- **Reports are cut off and scroll inside themselves.** At phone width every widget stacks at full width but keeps the height it was given on the desktop grid. A native report pinned at the default size (6 × 4) gets a 220 px window for its content. A six-row table stacked for a phone is about 1,300 px tall, so you see one row at a time inside a small box.
- **Swiping gets caught by the cards.** Because each report scrolls inside its own box, a swipe that starts on a report scrolls the report, not the dashboard. In a test with three swipes over a report table, the report scrolled 705 px and the dashboard didn't move.
- **Lots of controls before any content.** With the dashboard opened and expanded, the first widget's content starts about 43% of the way down an iPhone screen. Above it: the chat header, the panel switcher (Details / Panels), the panel tabs, the Dashboard options button alone on its own row, the dashboard's tabs, and each widget's bar with a drag handle, title, a type label ("Report", "HTML") and a menu. Each card also has a resize corner, which on a phone only changes the desktop size.
- **The first view is a strip.** Choosing Dashboard on a phone opens it in the bottom sheet under the chat, leaving about 190 px for the dashboard until you expand it.

Raised in #clawtributors on Discord: "too dense and slippery to properly handle them on mobile", and a maintainer agreed.

### Steps

1. Pin a native report with a table of 6+ rows at the default size (or open any desktop-built dashboard).
2. Open the session on a phone (or a 390 px wide touch viewport) and choose **Dashboard**, then expand the panel.
3. Try to read the table and scroll past it.

Before (current `main`, iPhone width, synthetic data):

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/1447105c8f2657beaaecd8997c9b9d09d10f8110/images/2026/11/5915ddef-58be-4e15-bcc7-e4c15ccfe9d7.png)

### Proposed changes, one PR each

1. **Reports and progress cards show all their content on narrow boards.** When the board stacks its cards, native reports and session progress cards grow to their content. The dashboard becomes the only thing that scrolls. Website, Browser, custom HTML and other plugin widgets keep their usual height. The resize corner is hidden on stacked boards; size presets stay in the widget menu. Desktop layout is unchanged. I have this ready, with an end-to-end test that fails on `main` (145 px of the report hidden) and passes with the change.

   After (same data and viewport):

   ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/1447105c8f2657beaaecd8997c9b9d09d10f8110/images/2026/11/5e968069-9468-4528-858f-f66e5722eeef.png)

2. **Fewer rows of controls above a phone dashboard.** For example, put Dashboard options in the dashboard tab row instead of a row of its own, and drop the widget type label on narrow boards. Separate PR after (1).

3. **Open the dashboard taller on phones** instead of a ~190 px strip under the chat. This changes how panels open on phones, so it needs a decision first: should Dashboard open expanded on phones, or should the sheet open taller?

Custom HTML widgets that scroll inside themselves on touch screens are covered by draft #196797, so they're not part of this.

issues.body:
### Summary

Agents can enter a repeated no-progress `sessions_yield` loop **without any pending child, task, or eligible completion event**. The tool correctly responds `status: "nothing_pending"`, but the agent calls it again until loop detection terminates the turn. This has been observed during both delegation and session-history work, across **multiple models and OpenClaw releases**.

This report concerns **tool selection and failure to recover after `nothing_pending`**, not a claim that the yield tool itself returned the wrong status. Root cause is **not yet isolated**.

### Environment

- Linux x86_64; Node.js 24.21.0; OpenClaw Gateway and CLI from the same official install.
- Local models exposed via llama.cpp / OpenAI-compatible provider.
- `tools.toolSearch.mode: "directory"` on current 2026.10.5 runs; prior failures also occurred before that setting was enabled.
- Loop guard is enabled.
- Package integrity audit matched **13,981 packaged files byte-for-byte**; the one absent member was an install-lifecycle marker. No duplicate Gateway, stale runtime, or mixed installation found.

### Recorded occurrences (original retained session traces)

| Date (2026) | OpenClaw runtime | Model | Observed behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Oct 12 | 2026.10.1 | Gemma 4 12B | Session-history request: **22** `sessions_yield` calls, all `nothing_pending` |
| Oct 19 | 2026.10.10-beta.1 | LFM2.5 24B A2B (QAD_Q4_0) | Delegation request: **19** yield calls, no spawn |
| Oct 19 | 2026.10.10-beta.1 | Same LFM | Explicit spawn request forbidding yield: **28** yield calls, no spawn |
| Oct 21 | 2026.10.5 | LFM2.5 24B A2B (IQ4_XS), High thinking | **22** yield calls, no spawn |
| Oct 22 | 2026.10.5 | Same LFM, Tool Search `directory` | **28** yield calls, no spawn |
| Oct 22 | 2026.10.5 | Same LFM, Medium thinking | Workshop history review: **22** yield calls; model reasoning identified `sessions_list` as next action |

Representative result repeated:

```json
{
  "status": "nothing_pending",
  "message": "No pending completion or eligible active native task is owned by this turn. This call did not pause the turn or schedule a continuation. Continue unfinished work; return its final result when complete."
}
```

The generated prompt reports show `sessions_yield` in the **direct tool schema**, while `sessions_spawn` is deferred behind the Tool Search directory. Some normalized traces show the assistant's recorded reasoning identifying `sessions_spawn` or `sessions_list`, followed by an actual `sessions_yield` function call instead. Raw provider HTTP/SSE bodies were unavailable, so we cannot say precisely where that mismatch originates.

### Working control / evidence that spawn itself functions

On 2026.10.5 with the same primary LFM model, explicitly instructing the agent to:
1. `tool_describe` `openclaw:core:sessions_spawn`,
2. `tool_call` the described spawn schema with `agentId: "coder"` and a `task`,
3. wait for and report the completion event,

**succeeded end to end**. Separately, a different model successfully spawned that coding agent under the same Gateway. The requester allowlist was checked with an actual `agents_list` call, which returned the target agent.

### Expected / actual

**Expected:** When `sessions_yield` reports `nothing_pending`, the agent should proceed with the unfinished task using an appropriate tool (or report a blocker). It should not repeatedly issue the same no-progress yield.

**Actual:** Some runs repeatedly select `sessions_yield` despite the no-pending response, even when no child was ever created, until the loop guard terminates execution.

### Scope and uncertainties

- **Not** a 2026.10.5-only regression: original evidence shows this behavior on 2026.10.1 and 2026.10.10-beta.1.
- `sessions_yield` returning `nothing_pending` is appropriate. The defect/hazard appears in tool selection, tool presentation, or recovery from that response.
- Possible contributing interface asymmetry: `sessions_yield` direct-only, while relevant tools are deferred. This remains a **hypothesis**; no offending source change, model/provider/template boundary, or standalone deterministic reproduction has been isolated.
- Current installation is official and internally consistent; no reinstall, model switch, or source patch is justified by available evidence.
- Related but not identical: #106704 (yield misuse on first turn); #118776 (yield exposed where child/event-producing tools are absent).

### Request

Could maintainers review:
1. The **model-facing affordance/preconditions** for `sessions_yield` when there is no owned child or completion source;
2. The direct-only `sessions_yield` vs deferred session-tool presentation and Tool Search guidance;
3. Recovery behavior following repeated `nothing_pending` responses without sacrificing legitimate wait semantics?

We can provide redacted, selected runtime-event and prompt-report excerpts if maintainers indicate the preferred format.

## Environment and observation
OpenClaw 2026.10.5; macOS; Node 26.10.0; native bundled boot-md; SQLite session store. One observed occurrence on 2026-10-21 at 20:22 EDT. Reproducibility has not been tested with another restart.

## Steps observed
1. Enable only hooks.internal.entries.boot-md.enabled and perform one approved native Gateway restart.
2. BOOT.md uses native status, sends one startup message, and admits a main-session reconciliation turn.
3. Boot run finishes; native hook attempts to remove its temporary session.

Expected: startup work succeeds and the hook removes its temporary session.
Actual: startup notification and main pickup both succeeded, but cleanup failed and the finished temporary row remained. Hook logged startup task failed although useful work completed.

Sanitized error:
```text
boot: failed to clean up session: SQLite session entry changed before lifecycle removal for <temporary-boot-session>
hooks/boot-md: startup task failed; reason=session cleanup failed
```

## Impact / suspected area
Small cleanup/reporting defect: retained finished temporary session and misleading failure log. No observed lost startup message or duplicate execution. Installed boot handler finally calls applySessionEntryLifecycleMutation with expected session ID; exact-entry comparison in the SQLite projection rejects removal. The rejecting guard is located; the changing writer and root cause are not proven. Related finalization fallback appeared in the same run; causality is unknown and it is not a second blocker.

## Evidence and limits
The error excerpt above is sanitized from the observed Gateway log. Raw private transcripts, chat destinations, host names and user paths are not included. A maintainer can request a separately sanitized excerpt. No raw DB access, manual session deletion, installed patch, weakened guard or second restart was used.

## Status of the A/B evidence (update 2026-10-12)

The review of 2026-10-08 notes that the lost final replies were never correlated with a final-delivery exception or registry transition. I cannot add that correlation from production: every WhatsApp account on this install now runs with `streaming.block.enabled: true` (checked in `openclaw.json` on 2026-10-12), because `false` loses real users' replies. No lost reply has been observed with that setting. The A/B evidence below stands as recorded; reproducing again requires flipping a live account back to `false`, which I will do only on a test account if a maintainer asks for a specific log or trace to capture.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash). Whether it is a regression is unknown: the bot flags a suspected regression, but we have no confirmed working run of this account with `block.enabled: false` before 2026.9.8.

### Beta release blocker

No — not a plugin-compatibility blocker for the current beta window.

## Summary

On 2026.9.8, a WhatsApp direct-message account with `channels.whatsapp.accounts.<id>.streaming.block.enabled: false` never delivers the agent's final reply. The model completes (`stopReason: stop`), the reply is held in pending-final custody, and no `[whatsapp] Sending message` is ever logged for it. On the user's next inbound message, main-session restart recovery settles that custody as an uncertain delivery and sends the generic notice "I couldn't confirm whether my previous reply reached this chat…" instead of the reply. The reply content is never re-sent.

Flipping only `streaming.block.enabled` to `true` (hot reload, no gateway restart) restores delivery immediately; flipping it back to `false` breaks it again. A/B done 3 times on the same account and session within 25 minutes.

I did not isolate the exact function in the shipped bundle. The custody path that ends in the notice is `deliverOnce` in `dist/reply-dispatcher-*.mjs` → `settlePendingFinalDelivery({ kind: "pending-final", ... })`; with block streaming off, the final apparently never reaches `options.deliver` for the WhatsApp adapter, so custody stays `queued`/`prepared` until recovery picks it up. Related but distinct: #154416 (spurious notice while a queued reply is mid-send), #149325 (Telegram pending-final swapped for the notice), #81078 (closed; block streaming *on* suppressing finals).

## Steps to reproduce

1. OpenClaw 2026.9.8, WhatsApp channel, multi-account. One account with:
   ```json
   "streaming": { "chunkMode": "length", "block": { "enabled": false } }
   ```
2. Send a DM to that account's number. Agent replies (any model; reproduced with `gpt-5.6-terra` and `claude-haiku-4-5`).
3. Observe: ✅ reaction is sent, no reply arrives.
4. Send a second DM.

## Expected behavior

The final reply is delivered to the DM after step 2, exactly as with `block.enabled: true` and as on 2026.9.6 and earlier with the same config.

## Actual behavior

- After step 2: no outbound message for the reply.
- After step 4: the restart-recovery notice is sent in place of the previous reply; then the new reply is again held.
- Transcript of the session: each assistant turn with `stopReason: stop` is followed by a `delivery-mirror` entry with idempotencyKey `main-session-restart-recovery:pending-final:*`.

Gateway log (America/Sao_Paulo, -03:00), `block.enabled: false`. Each `Sending message` right after an inbound is the recovery notice for the previous turn, never the reply:

```
2026-10-07T06:29:20.242-03:00 [whatsapp] Inbound message +55119XXXXXXXX -> +5511954211992 (direct, 82 chars)
2026-10-07T06:29:20.260-03:00 [whatsapp] Sending message -> sha256:28c3e0f7e09d
2026-10-07T06:29:20.587-03:00 [whatsapp] Sent message 3EB06F041B1C499E2FA931 -> sha256:28c3e0f7e09d (328ms)
2026-10-07T06:32:28.144-03:00 [whatsapp] Inbound message +55119XXXXXXXX -> +5511954211992 (direct, 82 chars)
2026-10-07T06:32:28.170-03:00 [whatsapp] Sending message -> sha256:28c3e0f7e09d
2026-10-07T06:32:28.878-03:00 [whatsapp] Sent message 3EB0044088067334950600 -> sha256:28c3e0f7e09d (709ms)
```

Flip to `true`:

```
2026-10-07T06:32:48.811-03:00 [reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (channels.whatsapp.accounts.arnold.streaming.block.enabled)
2026-10-07T06:33:00.778-03:00 [reload] config hot reload applied (channels.whatsapp.accounts.arnold.streaming.block.enabled)
2026-10-07T06:35:23.415-03:00 [whatsapp] Inbound message +55119XXXXXXXX -> +5511954211992 (direct, 78 chars)
```

The 06:35 reply was delivered (confirmed on the recipient's device). Note: replies sent via the block-reply path do not log `[whatsapp] Sent message`, so the log alone cannot confirm block-path delivery.

Flip back to `false` at 06:36:37 → the 06:49 DM again got no reply. Flip to `true` at 06:50:43 → one residual recovery notice for the 06:49 turn, then 06:56 and 06:57 DMs answered normally.

Window affected in production: 2026-10-05 10:38 → 2026-10-07 06:56, 6 user turns lost on one account. Last good delivery with the same config: 2026-10-03 13:27 on 2026.9.6.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.8 (npm global, `npm ls -g openclaw` → `openclaw@2026.9.8`), upgraded from 2026.9.6 on 2026-10-04 09:53
- Linux 7.0.14 (Proxmox LXC), Node v24.21.0, systemd user service
- WhatsApp channel, 4 accounts on one gateway; only the affected account had `block.enabled: false`

## Provider / routing chain

WhatsApp inbound DM → agent `arnold` main session (`agent:<id>:whatsapp:direct:<peer>`) → embedded run (OpenAI `gpt-5.6-terra`; also reproduced with Anthropic `claude-haiku-4-5`) → reply dispatcher → WhatsApp outbound.

## Additional setup details

Local plugins loaded via `plugins.load.paths`: `nexus-context` (context engine), `backlog-v2`, `promise-wake`, `discord-voice-call`. None touches outbound reply delivery. One local dist patch (`dispatchTrustedPluginGatewayMethod`, #164545) unrelated to the reply path.

## Impact and severity

Silent message loss on an entire account: every DM final reply dropped, replaced by a generic notice one turn later. Time-to-notice was ~44 h because the account still sends ✅ reactions and the recovery notice, so it looks alive. Workaround: `streaming.block.enabled: true`.

## Model

OpenAI `gpt-5.6-terra`; also reproduced with Anthropic `claude-haiku-4-5` (same routing chain above). The defect sits in reply delivery, after the model returns.

issues.body:
## Requested verification and a correction (2026-10-08, openclaw 2026.9.8 `fc23bc8`)

ClawSweeper asked for the copied store's schema and foreign-key result. Measured today on a copy made with `VACUUM INTO` from a read-only connection to the live agent store, read with `node:sqlite`:

```
schema_meta.primary   schema_version=24  app_version=2026.9.8
PRAGMA foreign_keys   1
PRAGMA foreign_key_list(session_windows)
  session_key -> session_nodes.session_key  ON DELETE CASCADE
  primary_conversation_id -> conversations.conversation_id  ON DELETE SET NULL
PRAGMA foreign_key_check            0 rows (whole db)
PRAGMA integrity_check              ok
session_windows LEFT JOIN session_nodes USING(session_key) WHERE node IS NULL   0 rows
```

**The original report is wrong on one point, and the bot's objection is correct: these windows are not orphans.** Every one of the 14 stuck `:run:` windows has a `session_nodes` row. The 2026-09-28 count filtered `status='running'` in each table, and these node rows carry `status = NULL`, so they were miscounted as absent. Below, the sentences claiming "no `session_nodes` row" are struck through rather than deleted.

What the rows actually are, the key from the repro as the example:

```
session_nodes   session_key=agent:arthur:cron:4a9a487f-…:run:428d4deb-…
                current_session_id=428d4deb-…  entry_json='{}'  entry_valid=-1
                status=NULL  created_at=NULL  snapshot_revision=0  updated_at=2026-09-19T21:00:01Z
session_windows session_id=428d4deb-…  status='running'  ended_at=NULL
                created_at=2026-09-19T21:00:01Z  started_at=2026-09-19T21:00:02Z
```

All 14 share that shape (`entry_json='{}'`, `entry_valid=-1`, node `status` NULL), windows created 2026-08-19T11:30:22Z → 2026-09-19T21:00:01Z. Store-wide, 317 `session_nodes` rows carry `entry_valid=-1`; I have not checked how many of those are otherwise reachable.

Re-measured on 2026.9.8 with shipped commands only:

```
$ openclaw gateway call sessions.get --json --params '{"key":"agent:arthur:cron:4a9a487f-…:run:428d4deb-…"}'
{ "messages": [] }

$ openclaw sessions delete agent:arthur:cron:4a9a487f-…:run:428d4deb-… --dry-run --json
{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "Session delete did not complete for every requested key." },
  "dryRun": true, "results": [ { "ok": false, "status": "not_found", "error": "Session not found. …" } ] }

$ openclaw sessions list --json --agent arthur --limit all | grep -c 428d4deb
0
```

I did **not** re-run the `sessions.delete` RPC on 2026.9.8: it is the only call here that mutates, and these 14 rows are the only live specimens. The 2026.9.4 result in *Actual behavior* stands as recorded then.

**Revised reading, a hypothesis I have not verified in source:** the node row exists but its entry is empty and flagged invalid (`entry_valid=-1`), and the lookup that `sessions.get`, the CLI and `sessions.delete` share treats an invalid entry as no session. The rows remain unreachable by every shipped path and invisible to `doctor --session-sqlite inspect`; what changes is the storage state a repair has to target: an invalid-entry node with a `running` window, not a foreign-key orphan. Creation path not measured; node `updated_at` and window `created_at` are 83 ms apart and the window never got `ended_at`, which fits a run that died before its first entry commit (#141172 lineage), still unproven.

---

## Summary

`sessions.delete` reports success and does nothing when a session's `session_nodes` row holds an empty, invalid entry (`entry_json='{}'`, `entry_valid=-1`; see the 2026-10-08 correction above — ~~only surviving row is in `session_windows` with no matching `session_nodes` row~~). The RPC returns `ok: true` with `deleted: false` and `archived: []`, the row stays `status='running'` forever, and there is no other path — CLI, `doctor --session-sqlite`, or any reaper — that can retire it.

Two separate defects on the same call:

1. **The row is unreachable.** Deletion resolves the target through the session node; with the node row gone there is nothing to resolve, so the lifecycle path exits without touching `session_windows`.
2. **The result misstates what happened.** `ok: true` is what every caller reads, and `deleted: false` carries the whole truth in a field a caller has no reason to branch on. A cleanup script sees success on a row it did not remove, so the residue is invisible to the operator who "cleaned" it.

This is not the listing defect from #158180 (fixed by #158212, merged 2026-09-25, not yet in a published release). #158212 replaces the CLI's `sessions.list` resolution with a per-key `sessions.get`; measured here, `sessions.get` on one of these keys returns `{"messages": []}` — no session object — so after that release lands the CLI reaches the RPC and the RPC still declines to delete. The two fixes do not overlap.

Origin of the rows is #141172: a run that dies before its first session commit leaves no `session_nodes` row and no `agent.run.finished`, and the `session_windows` row stays `running`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Have a cron run session whose run died before its first session commit, so only the `session_windows` row exists (`status='running'`, no `session_nodes` row for the same key).
2. Call the RPC directly, bypassing the listing resolver:

```bash
openclaw gateway call sessions.delete --json \
  --params '{"key":"agent:<agent>:cron:<jobId>:run:<runId>"}'
```

3. Re-read the store (read-only copy) and count the row.

## Expected behavior

Either the call removes the `session_windows` row — the key was accepted and nothing else references it — or it fails loudly (`ok: false` with a reason naming the missing node), so a caller can tell "removed" from "cannot remove". A row no path can reach is the one case that must not answer `ok: true`.

## Actual behavior

```
$ openclaw gateway call sessions.delete --json --params '{"key":"agent:arthur:cron:4a9a487f-9a7b-4a2e-b4ef-cc529e4f1f62:run:428d4deb-4816-4b60-89f7-a52040664ca5"}'
{
  "ok": true,
  "key": "agent:arthur:cron:4a9a487f-9a7b-4a2e-b4ef-cc529e4f1f62:run:428d4deb-4816-4b60-89f7-a52040664ca5",
  "deleted": false,
  "archived": []
}
```

The row survives. Counted against a read-only copy of the live agent store taken after the call (`node:sqlite`, never the live file):

```
== session_nodes (608 rows, key col session_key) ==
   null: 271
   done: 3

== session_windows (885 rows, key col session_key) ==
   null: 394
   done: 62
   running: 14
   failed: 2
```

All 14 `running` rows carry a `%:run:%` key, all in one agent's store, oldest 2026-08-19, newest `2026-09-28T17:08:03Z`. ~~None has a `session_nodes` row.~~ (Wrong — each has one with an invalid entry; see the correction above.)

**The control that isolates the cause.** A 15th row in the same state, `4c96f6a2-…:run:7b9e0fe7`, had rows in *both* tables. The same RPC with the same shape deleted it:

```
ok: true, deleted: true, archived: [<transcript>.zst]
```

and the count went 16 → 14 (one key, two tables). ~~Node row present → deleted. Node row absent → silent no-op.~~ Valid entry → deleted. Invalid entry (`entry_valid=-1`) → silent no-op (corrected 2026-10-08). Nothing else differs.

**No other path reaches these rows.**

```
$ openclaw gateway call sessions.get --json --params '{"key":"agent:arthur:cron:4a9a487f-…:run:428d4deb-…"}'
{ "messages": [] }

$ openclaw sessions delete agent:arthur:cron:4a9a487f-…:run:428d4deb-… --dry-run
delete agent:arthur:cron:4a9a487f-…:run:428d4deb-…: Session not found. Run openclaw sessions list --json to choose a valid key.

$ openclaw doctor --session-sqlite inspect --session-sqlite-agent arthur --json --non-interactive
… "integrityCheck": "ok" … "totals": { "issues": 0, … }
```

`doctor --session-sqlite inspect` reports `issues: 0` — the orphan window is not modelled as an integrity problem, so `--repair` has nothing to fix. The rows are also absent from `openclaw sessions list --json --agent arthur --limit all` (337 sessions, 3 `:run:` keys, all `done`), so nothing that reads the listing — including a stuck-run watchdog — can see them either.

## Environment

- openclaw `2026.9.4` (`3a9d69d`), npm global install (`/home/abacha/.local/lib`)
- Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm), Linux 7.0.12-1-pve x86_64, unprivileged LXC
- Node v24.21.0
- Model: anthropic/claude-opus-5

## Provider / routing chain

Gateway with multiple configured agents, per-agent SQLite session stores (`agents/<id>/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite`). Affected sessions are cron run sessions (`agent:<id>:cron:<jobId>:run:<runId>`) created by the internal cron scheduler.

## Additional setup details

Local `nexus-context` plugin plus a small set of dist patches, none of them touching the session lifecycle or `session_windows`. The measurement above uses only shipped commands; the store was read from a copy, never the live file.

## Impact and severity

- **A cleanup that reports success and changes nothing.** The residue-producing bug is fixed (#141172 lineage, no new rows since the 2026.9.4 bundle went live), but every row already in the table is permanent. The documented sweep — the RPC, because the CLI form is #158180 — is a no-op for 14 of 15 rows and says `ok: true` each time.
- **Time-to-notice is unbounded.** No listing, no doctor check and no watchdog surfaces these rows. They were found only by reading the SQLite store directly.
- **The remaining path is a raw `DELETE` in a live agent store**, which is not something an operator should be pushed into for garbage the framework created.
- One of these rows was read as a live turn by our restart guard and blocked every deferred gateway restart for an afternoon, which is how the whole class got measured.

# Recurrence check and what I cannot supply (update 2026-10-19)

The review of 2026-10-15 asks which admission guard rejected the run. I cannot identify it from this install, and I am not going to guess one: the receipts carry only the shared `changed while starting work. Retry.` string, the journal has no line at the failing instants, and the branch-identifying reason code that would answer it is exactly what #127195 asks for.

What I can add is the recurrence picture on the same install (`2026.9.8`, no upgrade since the 2026-10-05 failures):

- `openclaw cron runs --json` for the five cron jobs still bound to a persistent WhatsApp session (`sessionTarget: session:agent:enzo:whatsapp:…`, including the job that failed 4/4 on 2026-10-05): **33 of 33 runs `ok`**, first retained run 2026-10-12 13:30 UTC, last 2026-10-19. Run history retention is seven entries per job, so 2026-10-06 → 2026-10-11 is covered by the nine successful runs reported in the 2026-10-15 update.
- The same string appeared once more outside cron, 2026-10-17 12:29:38 UTC, as a heartbeat failure on a Discord channel session (`SessionWorkStartChangedError`, `source=replyResolver`, 90 ms). Per the review, a heartbeat occurrence does not establish cron recurrence, and I am not counting it as one.

So the failure has not recurred in cron for 14 days on this install. If it comes back I will add the receipt with timestamps here; until a reason code exists (#127195), the rejection site stays unidentifiable from operator-side output.

# Rejection site: what the installed bundle can narrow (update 2026-10-15)

Re: the review's next step ("identify the rejection site and changed ownership fields"). Two new facts, one hypothesis.

**1. The cron job no longer fails.** `8b66bb9d` ran 2026-10-06 through 2026-10-14 at 21:35 UTC, **9 of 9 `ok`**, same install (`openclaw@2026.9.8`), no upgrade (`openclaw cron runs --id 8b66bb9d-… --json`).

**2. The same text recurred outside cron, and this time the journal logged the error class.** 2026-10-14 13:58:28 UTC, a heartbeat turn on a Discord channel session of another agent, verbatim:

```
13:58:28.134 [sessions/lifecycle] slow session lifecycle operation ... operation=lifecycle ... elapsedMs=1497 ... phaseDurationsMs={"prepare":0,"run":1496,"finalize":0} signalAborted=false
13:58:28.219 [openai-transport] [responses] error provider=openai ... message=Request was aborted
13:58:28.230 [diagnostic] message dispatch completed: channel=unknown sessionId=unknown sessionKey=agent:arthur:discord:channel:155926… source=replyResolver outcome=error duration=93ms error="SessionWorkStartChangedError: Session "agent:arthur:discord:channel:155926…" changed while starting work. Retry."
13:58:28.236 [heartbeat] failed: Session "agent:arthur:discord:channel:155926…" changed while starting work. Retry.
```

`SessionWorkStartChangedError` excludes the plain-`Error` throw sites of the same text (`chat-*.js`, `chat-send-handler-*.js`, `realtime-session-harness-*.js`). In the 2026.9.8 bundle the class is raised with this exact message by `createSessionWorkStartChangedError` / `resolveSessionWorkStartError` (`lifecycle-*.js`, the `expectedSessionId` mismatch branch) and by `rejectLifecycleInvalidatedWork` inside `admitReplyTurn` (`session-entry-handle-*.js`), which carries **five** call sites with the identical string: `sessionId !== expectedSessionId` without `hasExpectedSessionRotation`; `ownerClaim.kind === "invalidated"`; `interruptedBeforeOperation || isAbortSignalAborted(params.upstreamAbortSignal)`; and two under `rotationObservation.changed()` with a recovery claim started. Only the first of those is a session rotation.

**Hypothesis, unproven:** the 2026-10-14 occurrence is the upstream-abort branch rather than rotation. The evidence is timing only: an aborted provider request 11 ms before the rejection, in the same process. The aborted request's log line carries no session key, so I cannot tie it to this session. If that holds, the receipts in the 2026-10-08 section below cannot be assumed to be rotations either: the receipt text is identical for all five branches. That is #127195 again, and it is why I cannot name the changed field. A distinct reason code per branch on `SessionWorkStartChangedError` would answer this on the next occurrence.

# Recurrence check (update 2026-10-12)

The review of 2026-10-08 asks for redacted rejection-site and ownership-field evidence from the recurring job. **I have none to add, because the failure has not recurred.** The affected job (`8b66bb9d`, `sessionTarget: "session:<WhatsApp direct key>"`) ran six times since the last failure, all `ok`, on the same install (`openclaw@2026.9.8`, no upgrade in between):

```
2026-10-05T21:35:00Z  error   (4 attempts 21:35:00–21:41:33, already listed below)
2026-10-06T21:35:00Z  ok
2026-10-07T21:35:00Z  ok
2026-10-08T21:35:00Z  ok
2026-10-09T21:35:00Z  ok
2026-10-10T21:35:00Z  ok
2026-10-11T21:35:00Z  ok
```

Source: `openclaw cron runs <job> --status all`. The two Discord-channel jobs in the list below were deleted, so they cannot recur. The rejection still carries no call site or changed-field list in the journal or `diagnostic_events`, so the next recurrence will again produce only the receipt text. If a maintainer wants the guard identified, a log line naming the guard and the differing snapshot fields at the rejection would let me answer on the next occurrence without patching the bundle.

# Live recurrence and what the trace can show (update 2026-10-08)

ClawSweeper asked which guard fires: cron preparation (`src/cron/isolated-agent/run-prepare.ts`) or reply admission. **I cannot identify the producer from this install, and I am not claiming one.** The *Summary* below attributes the rejection to `admitReplyTurn`; that attribution was read from source, never observed in a trace, and should be taken as a hypothesis. The bot's point that the cron executor invokes the agent run directly makes the cron-preparation guard the likelier producer; also unproven.

Why no trace exists here: at the failing moment on 2026.9.8 (2026-10-05 21:35:00 UTC ±2 s) the gateway journal has **no lines at all**, and `diagnostic_events` has **0 rows** in 21:34:55–21:35:10 UTC. The only record of the rejection is `cron_run_receipts.error_text`. The rejection is not logged with a stack or call site anywhere, and in 2026.9.8 the same message text appears 45 times across 10 dist files (`grep -rcF 'changed while starting work' dist`). Without instrumenting the installed bundle, a receipt cannot be tied to a guard. That is the #127195 problem, and it now blocks this issue too.

What can be shown is that it reproduces live, after the filing and on the current release. Every `cron_run_receipts` row with this error since 2026-09-28, UTC:

```
2026-09-28T18:43:56Z | 52b9ee47 | enzo   |   42ms | Session "agent:enzo:whatsapp:direct:+55…" changed while starting work. Retry.
2026-09-28T18:44:02Z | d48ffcee | enzo   |   26ms | Session "agent:enzo:whatsapp:direct:+55…" changed while starting work. Retry.
2026-09-28T18:44:27Z | 52b9ee47 | enzo   |  195ms | Session "agent:enzo:whatsapp:direct:+55…" changed while starting work. Retry.
2026-09-30T12:49:41Z | d078da16 | arthur |  903ms | Session "agent:arthur:discord:channel:1554765396014272523" changed while starting work. Retry.
2026-09-30T21:39:48Z | 8b66bb9d | enzo   |   55ms | Session "agent:enzo:whatsapp:direct:+55…" changed while starting work. Retry.
2026-09-30T21:40:19Z | 8b66bb9d | enzo   |  964ms | Session "agent:enzo:whatsapp:direct:+55…" changed while starting work. Retry.
2026-10-02T20:35:37Z | 473f37b0 | arthur |   50ms | Session "agent:arthur:discord:channel:1555671401027997798" changed while starting work. Retry.
2026-10-05T21:35:00Z | 8b66bb9d | enzo   |   43ms | Session "agent:enzo:whatsapp:direct:+55…" changed while starting work. Retry.
2026-10-05T21:35:31Z | 8b66bb9d | enzo   |   50ms | Session "agent:enzo:whatsapp:direct:+55…" changed while starting work. Retry.
2026-10-05T21:36:31Z | 8b66bb9d | enzo   |   42ms | Session "agent:enzo:whatsapp:direct:+55…" changed while starting work. Retry.
2026-10-05T21:41:33Z | 8b66bb9d | enzo   |   48ms | Session "agent:enzo:whatsapp:direct:+55…" changed while starting work. Retry.
```

- **Reproduces on 2026.9.8** (installed 2026-10-04): job `8b66bb9d` (`enzo-renata-podcast-mercado`, `35 18 * * *` America/Sao_Paulo, `sessionTarget: "session:agent:enzo:whatsapp:direct:+55…"`, enabled) died on 2026-10-05 at the scheduled minute and on all three scheduler retries (+30 s, +60 s, +300 s), 42–50 ms each, the same retry ladder as the original 2026-09-25 night. It also failed on 2026-09-30 (2 attempts).
- **Not WhatsApp-specific:** two other jobs failed the same way against Discord channel sessions of a different agent (2026-09-30, 2026-10-02). Those jobs have since been deleted, so their full definitions are not recoverable; the session key in the message is the target.
- All 11 attempts end in 26–964 ms with no model call, consistent with a rejection before execution in either guard.
- The original job `302cc0c8` is still on `sessionTarget: "isolated"` (the workaround) and has not failed this way since.

Not produced, stated rather than invented: a stack trace, the rotating writer, and a current-`main` reproduction. If a maintainer names the guard they want confirmed, I can add a stack capture at the throw sites on this install and attach the next occurrence; job `8b66bb9d` fires daily on a session that keeps reproducing it.

---

# Summary

A cron job whose `sessionTarget` is a persistent session (`session:<key>`) is **rejected at reply-turn admission** when the target session's `sessionId` does not match the id the run captured, instead of waiting for the rotation to settle and re-reading the handle. The scheduler's retries re-enter the very same rejection, so the job produces nothing at all — the turn never starts, no model call is made, no delivery is attempted.

The rejecting branch is `admitReplyTurn` in `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-turn-admission.ts` (`main` at `d769e31af2b9eca2cb566c174cd1fc0b1a2b29ab`), inside the `assertAllowed` callback passed to `beginSessionWorkAdmission`:

```ts
const activeOperationRotatedExpectedSession = rotations.hasExpectedSessionRotation({
  expectedSessionId,
  sessionId: currentEntry?.sessionId,
  databaseIdentity: admittedDatabaseClaim?.identity,
});
if (
  expectedSessionId &&
  currentEntry?.sessionId !== expectedSessionId &&
  !activeOperationRotatedExpectedSession
) {
  rejectLifecycleInvalidatedWork({
    kind: params.kind,
    message: `Session "${params.sessionKey}" changed while starting work. Retry.`,
    transientSessionChange: true,
  });
}
```

Two things make this terminal rather than transient for a cron run:

1. **The admission loop never waits for this condition.** The enclosing `while (true)` in `admitReplyTurn` has exactly one wait-and-retry path — `isReplyRunSuccessorAdmissionBlocked` → `waitForReplyRunSuccessorAdmission(...)` → `continue`. A session-id mismatch does not `continue`; `rejectLifecycleInvalidatedWork` throws straight out of the loop. The wait primitive and the `waitTimeoutMs` plumbing already exist (`params.waitTimeoutMs ?? (params.kind === "queued_followup" ? REPLY_RUN_IDLE_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_MS : undefined)`), they are simply not reachable from the rotation branch.

2. **The one tolerance that exists does not cover a cron.** `rotations.hasExpectedSessionRotation(...)` forgives the mismatch only when a *known active reply operation* owned the expected session id and rotated it. A cron run dispatched against an idle persistent session has no such operation to point at, so the tolerance is always false and the rejection is unconditional.

`src/cron/retry-hint.ts` classifies the resulting message as retryable (`SESSION_LIFECYCLE_CLAIM_ERROR_PATTERN`, `retryable: executionStarted !== true`). That is correct as far as it goes, but retrying the whole run re-captures the same expectation and re-enters the same rejection — measured below, four attempts over six minutes, every one of them dead in under 400 ms.

# Steps to reproduce

1. Create a cron job with `sessionTarget: "session:<key>"` pointing at a persistent channel session (here a WhatsApp DM lane), scheduled daily.
2. Let the target session's `sessionId` rotate between the moment the run captures `expectedSessionId` and the moment `beginSessionWorkAdmission`'s `assertAllowed` re-reads the entry.
3. The run fails before any turn exists.

# Expected behavior

The run waits for the admission window — backoff and re-read the session handle, or adopt the rotated `sessionId` the same way a rotated active operation is adopted — and then runs the turn. A session that merely rotated is still the session the job was aimed at; the job's own identity did not change.

# Actual behavior

The run is rejected in ~300 ms and every scheduler retry reproduces it.

Measured from `cron_run_receipts` in the gateway state database, job `302cc0c8-16dc-4fc0-b368-0e9c8fe23f1e` (`enzo-ig-daily-summary`, `cron 30 22 * * *` America/Sao_Paulo, `sessionTarget: session:agent:enzo:whatsapp:direct:+55…`), all timestamps UTC:

```
2026-09-25T01:30:00.033Z |  370ms | error | Session "agent:enzo:whatsapp:direct:+55…" changed while starting work. Retry.
2026-09-25T01:30:30.433Z |  368ms | error | Session "agent:enzo:whatsapp:direct:+55…" changed while starting work. Retry.
2026-09-25T01:31:30.829Z |  353ms | error | Session "agent:enzo:whatsapp:direct:+55…" changed while starting work. Retry.
2026-09-25T01:36:31.216Z |  366ms | error | Session "agent:enzo:whatsapp:direct:+55…" changed while starting work. Retry.
2026-09-26T01:30:00.026Z |  339ms | error | Session "agent:enzo:whatsapp:direct:+55…" changed while starting work. Retry.
2026-09-27T01:30:00.028Z |  280ms | error | Session "agent:enzo:whatsapp:direct:+55…" changed while starting work. Retry.
```

The four rows on the first night are the scheduler's own retry ladder (+30 s, +60 s, +300 s). All four die at the same CAS, in 353–370 ms, before the turn exists.

For contrast, the same job on the same session key, same schedule, the 24 nightly runs immediately preceding:

```
2026-09-01T01:30:00.012Z | 11088ms | ok
… 24 nightly runs, 5416–15076 ms, every one of them admitted and ran …
2026-09-24T01:30:00.028Z |  9805ms | ok
```

One of those 24 (2026-09-17) ended in a delivery error after a 10494 ms turn — it admitted and ran, and it is a different failure. So the job is not misconfigured; it admitted nightly for 24 nights and then produced nothing for three. The only thing that ended the outage was re-pointing the job at an isolated session (`2026-09-28T01:30:00.023Z | 12274ms | ok`), which is a workaround, not a fix: a cron that posts to a chat needs the persistent session precisely so the human's natural reply lands in the same lane.

Two things I could not measure and am not claiming: what rotated the session inside that window, and why the condition reproduced on three consecutive nights rather than behaving like a race. The session entry's historical state is overwritten by later turns. What is measurable is the failure shape and the fact that the admission path offers the run no way to wait.

# Environment

- Reproduced again on openclaw `2026.9.8` (`fc23bc8`), 2026-10-05; see the update above
- openclaw `2026.8.1` (original filing), installed globally via npm (`/home/abacha/.local/lib/node_modules/openclaw`)
- Node `v22.23.2`, Linux `7.0.12-1-pve` x64 (Proxmox LXC, Debian)
- Model on the affected agent: `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`
- Source re-verified against `openclaw/openclaw` `main` at `d769e31af2b9eca2cb566c174cd1fc0b1a2b29ab` (2026-09-28). The installed bundle carries the earlier shape of the same branch (`dist/session-entry-handle-*.js`, three occurrences of the message in the same function); the rejection, and the absence of a wait path for it, are identical on `main`.

# Provider / routing chain

WhatsApp channel session → cron scheduler (`src/cron`) → gateway chat-send → `admitReplyTurn` (`src/auto-reply/reply/reply-turn-admission.ts`).

# Additional setup details

Multi-agent gateway, nine agents, our own MCP servers and a small number of local `dist` patches — none of them in `reply-turn-admission`, `src/cron`, or any session-admission path. The affected job is a stock cron job created through the cron tool.

Related, and deliberately not merged into this report: [#127195](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/127195) is about this message being indistinguishable across sixteen-plus call sites, and [#131490](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/131490) is about the retry *classification* of it. This issue is about neither the text nor the classification: it is that the admission path has no wait for a condition it itself labels `transientSessionChange: true`.

# Impact and severity

A scheduled job bound to a persistent session can stop producing output indefinitely while reporting only a message that says `Retry.` — and the retries it asks for cannot succeed. Time-to-notice here was three days, and it was noticed by a human missing the nightly message, not by any alert: the run receipts said `error`, the failure alert carried the same opaque string, and nothing distinguishes "the session rotated" from the fifteen other causes that print it. The only remedy available to an operator is to unbind the job from its session, which changes the product behaviour of the job.

issues.body:
## Status 2026-10-26: reply to `clawsweeper:needs-live-repro`

**Live reproduction.** Every number in this report comes from production traffic: 949 wire-captured `POST /v1/messages` on `2026.8.1` (comment of 2026-09-10), the 2026-09-12 incident on a WhatsApp-facing agent (comment of 2026-09-21) and the fleet-wide 01/09→12/09 measurement (comment of 2026-09-27). This install runs the npm release (`openclaw@2026.9.8`), so it cannot produce a run on current `main`. Source on `main` @ `6cd627de53` (2026-10-26) still carries both constructions:

- Item 1: `src/agents/agent-command-local.ts:72` keeps `senderIsOwner: params.opts.senderIsOwner ?? true,`; the deny side is `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-tool-authority.ts:136` (`senderIsOwner === false ? { deny: [...GATEWAY_OWNER_ONLY_CORE_TOOLS] }`). #182585 (merged 2026-10-25, `201127429a0`) added `src/agents/scheduled-owner-tool-guard.ts`, which rechecks a scheduled requester's owner bit before each owner-only call. It leaves the `?? true` default of the `agent --deliver` path as it was; its effect on the tool list a cron turn submits has not been measured here.
- Item 2: `buildInboundMetaSystemPrompt` (`src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.ts:332`) is still built per message, from `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run-context.ts:237` and from `src/agents/command/session-preparation.ts:417`.
- Installed `2026.9.8`: `dist/agent-command-*.mjs:905`, same `?? true` expression.

**Correction to section 1 below.** The gate is `senderIsOwner`, threaded per message (2026-09-09 comment). The `embedded ? [] : [...]` description in section 1 is wrong; the cost numbers stand.

The latest review names an owner decision on the boundary between a session-stable prompt and live tool authority. That call is a maintainer's, and nothing further is reproducible from this side.

---

Measured on 2026.9.2 across a seven-agent fleet, 06/09→09/09: 103 sessions, 4,373 API calls,
**254 prefix rewrites costing 21.31M cache-write tokens** out of 52.06M written in total.
Anthropic caches on `tools → system → messages`, so each of those rewrites re-charges the whole
message history of a live session.

Method: `logs/cache-trace.jsonl` — `stream:context.systemDigest` (sha256 of the whole system prompt)
and `cache:state.options.snapshot.toolNames` (the tool list actually submitted) — joined with
`transcript_events.usage.cacheWrite` from every agent database. Query in
`workspace-arthur/scripts/cache-attribution.py`.

Two of the five are already closed locally by configuration; they are reported because the design
that produced them is still there.

## 1. The tool set depends on the entry path, inside one session (8.43M, 40%)

The owner tools (`gateway`, `sessions`, `terminal`, `openclaw`, `computer`, `portal`, `nodes`,
`mobile_ui`, `whatsapp_login`, `conversations_*`) are built by `embedded ? [] : [...]` in the tool
builder (`openclaw-tools-*.js`, `createOpenClawDelegateToolsForRun`). A session reached from Discord
or the Control UI submits 46 tools; the same session reached by `openclaw agent --deliver`, by cron
or by heartbeat submits 58. In one Discord session over three days: 63 calls with them, 212 without.

Every flip rewrites the prefix. **Proposal:** the submitted tool set should be a property of the
session, not of the message that woke it.

**Worked around locally** by denying the 12 tools for that agent, which levels the two paths to a
byte-identical list. That is levelling *down* — levelling up is not expressible, because on the
embedded path the tools are never constructed and `alsoAllow` cannot resurrect them.

## 2. `### Message Context` is built per message, and its channel flaps (1.68M, 8%)

`buildInboundMetaSystemPrompt` (`inbound-meta-*.js:358`) is called once per message from
`get-reply-*.js:4099` and its payload is derived from the message, not the session. On a turn that
originates from another agent's `sessions_send`, `resolveInboundChannel` returns `webchat` for one
message and nothing for the next, for the same source session — 17:42 `webchat`, 17:43 `unknown`,
17:43 `webchat`, all from `agent:enzo:main`.

When the channel does not resolve, `response_format` disappears with it, because
`resolveInboundFormattingHints` keys off the same value. So a single unresolved field drags the
channel plugin's whole formatting-hints block out of the system prompt: the deltas are ±142 bytes
and ±1.1k–1.4k bytes, alternating.

No configuration gates any of this. **Proposal:** resolve the channel once per session, or omit the
field rather than emitting a value that alternates.

## 3. Isolated finalization sends a new system prompt with the whole history (0.69M, 3%)

When a turn settles after a tool call without a final answer, `embedded-agent-*.js:6825` logs
`settled post-tool turn lacked a final answer … running isolated finalization` and re-runs with a
finalization prompt of its own. "Isolated" describes the prompt, not the conversation: the call
carries the full message history under a different system prompt, which is the worst case for the
cache. 23 events in three days across 22 sessions and three providers; in the two large sessions it
cost 288k and 271k tokens each. The gateway's own line above it reads
`cache read dropped 1014609 -> 366633 … no tracked cache input change`.

**Proposal:** reuse the system prompt of the run being finalized, since the history is already reused.

## 4. The cache observer digests only `stablePrefix`

`diagnostics.cacheTrace` records a digest of the stable prefix, so every finding above was invisible
to it: the tool list and the per-message system additions both change *after* that boundary. We only
got the attribution after computing our own digest over the whole system prompt. One-line change,
and it is the reason this took a week.

## 5. A failed MCP server silently removes its tools, with no notice to the model

While `recall-api` was down for maintenance, `bundle-mcp` failed to start the server on each turn
(`failed to start server "recall_<agent>" … ECONNREFUSED`) and **omitted its 19 tools from the
prompt** — no retry, no last-known set. 37 of 594 turns.

The cache cost (0.64M) is the smaller half. The larger one is that every agent ran without any memory
tool and **was not told**: nothing in the prompt says a tool set was truncated, so the model answers
as if the capability never existed.

## Minor: `github_identity_status` is gated on `!== undefined`

`createGitHubIdentityStatusTool` is included when `githubPublicationAvailable !== undefined`, while
its sibling `github_publish` uses `=== true`. The probe
(`github-publication-availability-*.js:48`) never returns `undefined` — it ends in `catch { return
false }` — so `undefined` only means "an entry path did not thread the field", and the tool appears
and disappears with the path. 17 rewrites, 1.91M, until we denied it.


Happy to split any of these into their own issue — they share a measurement, not a cause.

issues.body:
## Summary

Sixteen production call sites across eleven files throw or return the **byte-identical** string
`Session "<key>" changed while starting work. Retry.` No discriminator — no reason code, no call-site
tag, no cause field — reaches the log or the thrown error. When this fires in production, **which of
the sixteen branches ran is not knowable from the output.**

This is the diagnosability half of the family that #118873 / #117096 / #116694 / #121269 covered
behaviourally. Those are all closed and the stuck-session behaviour is fixed. The string is not.

## Verified against `main`

`587c7524e58`. `rg 'changed while starting work' src --type ts`, excluding tests and comments:

| File | Lines |
|---|---|
| `src/plugins/runtime/runtime-agent.ts` | 573 |
| `src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.ts` | 333 |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-admission.ts` | 259 |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts` | 166 |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/agent-session-prepare.ts` | 185 |
| `src/sessions/session-diff-baseline.ts` | 41 |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/session-entry-persistence.ts` | 98 |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-turn-admission.ts` | 241, 284, 292 |
| `src/agents/agent-command-recovery-owner.ts` | 110, 132 |
| `src/agents/agent-command.ts` | 213, 220 |
| `src/cron/isolated-agent/run-session-state.ts` | 73 |
| `src/config/sessions/lifecycle.ts` | 57 (the shared helper) |

Three of these are in one function's three branches (`reply-turn-admission.ts:241/284/292`), so even
narrowing to a single file does not narrow to a single cause.

## Why it costs an operator a diagnosis

Production, `2026.8.1-beta.2`, one Discord channel session: **27 rejected runs across 4 inbound user
messages** between `09:58:05` and `10:24:09` (-03:00), each aborting in 4–8 ms with exactly this
string. Worst case, 9 attempts over 6 min 11 s before one user message ran. Every cluster started
within ~90 s of a gateway restart.

```text
[diagnostic] message processed: channel=discord outcome=error duration=4ms
  error="Error: Session \"agent:<redacted>\" changed while starting work. Retry."
```

The three plausible causes on that path — an `expectedSessionId` mismatch, a recovery-owner claim
returning `invalidated`, and the abort check — call for three different operator responses. The log
distinguishes none of them, so triage is guesswork or a source read per occurrence. Filing this
separately because a fix here is useful whether or not any specific admission bug is open: the next
one in this family will produce the same undiagnosable line.

## The seam already exists

`src/config/sessions/lifecycle.ts` already owns the discriminating helper:

- `resolveSessionWorkStartError()` already distinguishes *deleted* / *changed* / *still initializing*
  / *archived*, and
- `SESSION_WORK_START_INVALIDATED_ERROR_CODE = "SESSION_WORK_START_INVALIDATED"` (line 24) is already
  the shared code.

Roughly fourteen sites route through that helper. The sixteen above bypass it with a hardcoded
template literal, which is what makes them indistinguishable.

## Suggested shape

Not a behaviour change and not a message rewording — the retryable contract and the operator-facing
sentence can stay exactly as they are.

1. Give the helper a `reason` discriminator alongside the message (e.g.
   `session-id-mismatch` | `recovery-owner-invalidated` | `aborted` | `entry-deleted` |
   `initializing` | `archived`).
2. Route the sixteen hardcoded literals through the helper so the reason travels with the error.
3. Log the reason on the rejection path.

Happy to send the PR if the shape is agreeable — I would rather have the reason names settled by a
maintainer first than guess at the taxonomy.

## Version

`2026.8.1-beta.2` for the production data; source claims verified against `main` at `587c7524e58`.

> **Form note (edited 2026-10-08):** this is a feature request that was filed in bug shape. The sections below add what `feature_request.yml` asks for (alternatives, implementation intent) without changing the evidence above.

## Environment (form fields)

- Production data: `2026.8.1-beta.2`, npm global install, Linux (Debian in a Proxmox LXC).
- Model / provider routing chain of the 27 rejected runs: **unknown** — not recorded with the 2026-08 occurrences. The string is emitted before any model call, so the defect is model-independent.
- Steps to reproduce / actual: this is a diagnosability gap, verified by source inspection (table above) and confirmed by ClawSweeper on current `main`; no runtime repro on current `main` was run.

## Alternatives considered

1. **Status quo — read the source per occurrence.** What we do today; it costs a source read per incident and still cannot separate the three branches inside `reply-turn-admission.ts`.
2. **Reword the sixteen messages.** Rejected: it changes an operator-facing sentence and the retryable contract, and the next caller that copies the template literal is undiagnosable again.
3. **A stable public `reason` field on the shared error.** Possible, but it creates a compatibility obligation. ClawSweeper's recommendation — bounded **diagnostic-only** labels in operational logs, retry codes and public messages unchanged — is the shape we prefer.

## Implementation intent

We will open the PR once a maintainer settles the open question (diagnostic-only labels vs public field, and the label names). Not before: we would rather not pick the taxonomy unilaterally.
