## What problem this solves

Core decided whether two Telegram routes were the same conversation by parsing Telegram's `chat:topic:N` grammar itself, in several places, each with its own rules. When those copies disagreed, users saw the result:

- **#195842:** in a DM topic, an agent that answered with the message tool (`chat:topic:N`) got its final reply sent a second time. The origin carried the topic as a separate thread id, the dedupe regex only looked inside the target string, and the two never compared equal.
- Fixing that dedupe alone exposed a fourth comparison. Telegram's `matchesToolContextTarget` ignored the current topic, so the message tool never counted an explicit `chat:topic:N` send from inside a DM topic as the source reply. With the duplicate gone, the run then posted "No answer was returned".

## What changed

One owner per question, and that owner is the channel:

- **Same conversation?** Reply dedupe and `sourceDeliveryTargetsMatch` ask the channel's existing `messaging.resolveInboundConversation` through one core helper, `deliveryRoutesShareConversation`. Channels without that resolver keep the previous comparison.
- **Base conversation of a scoped id?** Group ids, group tool-policy candidates, the `sessions` display and the conversation-resolution fallback ask the channel's existing `messaging.resolveSessionConversation` through `resolveBaseConversationId`. This replaces `stripTargetTopicSuffix` and the `:topic:` / `:sender:` regexes.
- **Telegram:** one codec in `topic-conversation.ts` (`resolveTelegramConversationRef`, `resolveTelegramTargetThread`, `buildTelegramConversationId`). Hand-built `:topic:` strings and three private parsers now go through it. Telegram's private reply-suppression matcher is deleted. `matchesToolContextTarget` also accepts the current conversation including its topic; a bare-chat send still counts as before.
- **SDK:** no new fields. `targetsMatchForReplySuppression` and `numericTopicShorthand` are marked `@deprecated` (public SDK, kept for third-party plugins); nothing in-repo sets them.
- **Guard:** `core-topic-grammar` in `check-channel-agnostic-boundaries.mts` rejects `:topic:` in string, regex or template literals under `src/`. Two exemptions: the doctor General-topic migration, and the Telegram-named store-maintenance check (next PR replaces it with a channel capability). A negative control file containing the old regex and template fails the check.

Removed the source-delivery `TOPIC_THREAD_SUFFIX` regex too. It came in with #154939 for Telegram. Its Feishu test row was a synthetic `oc:topic:456` target that Feishu cannot send to (Feishu threads always use the separate `threadId`), so that row is now a real Telegram case.

Size: runtime (`src` + `extensions`) +266 / −255; boundary rule +42; tests +111 / −64.

## Evidence

**Live Telegram, mock model, real Bot API test server.** Built with `ocx build` (no type declarations), harness `run-mock-sut-user-e2e.mjs`, Bot API requests captured at the test proxy.

| Scenario | main `2e77b6b` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| #195842 repro, DM topic: message tool sends `DUP_one` to `chat:topic:N`, then the same final text | `DUP_one` visible **twice** | visible **once**, no missing-reply notice |
| Same repro, forum topic | once (origin already carried the topic) | once |
| Golden: send, reply, streamed edits, document, buttons, exec approval with tap, in DM | baseline | identical requests |
| Golden, group | baseline | identical requests |
| Golden, forum topic | baseline | same requests (order and approval "Expires in" minute differ) |
| Golden, DM topic | baseline | same requests, plus a buttons send main lost when two inputs arrived together (harness timing) |

All runs exit 0 with no failed scenario steps.

**Tests (`ocx test`, vitest from source):**

- The #195842 regression is ported unchanged. On main it fails its 2 same-topic cases; on this branch all rows pass, plus real-plugin rows for target-form and explicit-thread cases.
- Three DM-topic rows in `session-route.test.ts` cover the matcher.
- Changed-lane run: everything passes except `doctor-session-canonical-keys.scale.test.ts`, which fails the same way at the merge base (`ocx base merge-base`).
- Earlier Telegram suite: `send.history.test.ts` "refreshes authoritative edited captions" also fails on main.

**Build and package:** `ocx build --dts` (full) and the packed install smoke (`pnpm test:install:smoke`) at this head.

**Not covered:** there is no Feishu E2E. The Feishu-facing changes (tool-policy candidates, group-id and display base ids via `resolveSessionConversation`) have unit and contract tests only.

Supersedes #195842.


### Update: head `8c88bad`

The first CI run found three failures caused by this PR. All three are fixed:

- **Boundary-rule typing:** `skip` is now optional on every rule set.
- **`conversation-resolution.test` fixture:** the fixture now declares `resolveSessionConversation`. Core asks the channel for the base conversation and no longer strips `:topic:` itself.
- **Telegram target writeback:** reverted to main, so it keeps the shorthand form the user wrote (`-100123:77`).

`send.history.test` "refreshes authoritative edited captions" also fails on main.

Re-proven at `8c88bad`:

- The live #195842 DM-topic repro shows `DUP_one` once, with no missing-reply notice (built with `ocx build`).
- `ocx build --dts` and the packed install smoke pass.
- The test-type root lane, extensions typecheck, the boundary rule, and the affected tests pass.

prs.title: fix(knowledge): queued Scribe runs are shown as running
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Knowledge Scribes reporting a queued automation as running before the scheduler reports that it started.

## User Impact

Manual runs and automatic first runs now report **Run requested**. The first-run list and detail show **in progress** or **Running now** only when the scheduler supplies a running timestamp. Scheduling, retry, permissions, and duplicate-run handling are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The run action accepts an enqueue acknowledgement, while the view treated that acknowledgement and its local first-request marker as running-state evidence. The presentation now uses the already available scheduler state for that distinction. No new state, polling, requests, or execution paths are added.

## Evidence

- **46 focused checks passed:** 29 Scribe view cases, 16 Scribe state cases, and the existing real scheduler capacity regression. Three view tests fail on main at the intended requested/running boundaries and pass after the fix. They cover manual acknowledgement, first-run list/detail, transition to observed running, retry after refusal, and no repeated automatic request.
- The scheduler regression fills capacity, acknowledges queued manual runs while no queued job has executed, and checks their eventual execution after capacity is released. It reuses the real cron service and storage with synthetic runner edges; no live automation or model is used.
- Actual Scribes component browser replay clicks **Run now**, checks the initial automatic and explicit manual requests, and captures the acknowledgement and first-run row before any running timestamp. It is the production component and styles in an isolated minimal host, with synthetic Gateway responses—not the full app shell or a live Knowledge store.
- Scoped lint, changed-plugin typecheck, formatting, i18n verification, and diff checks pass. The plugin's existing English-copy structure is preserved. Related [#195010](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195010) internationalizes these strings but retains the same running claims; it does not already fix this boundary.
- Measured checks: view/state group 3.77s; final view file 2.73s; scheduler proof 46.26s including cold worker compilation, with the test itself taking 1.36s. Remote CI and its timings are pending.
- Simplification: three files, net four production lines, ten test lines, and one documentation line. Existing fixtures and scheduler proof are reused; no helper, compatibility layer, or state owner is introduced.

Before is verified main `5328b2754d84472b6c6e05fe80c2fc4513fd7e2e`. Main through `73773a54944eb41b56cc29932a305c0ba3cd1b0b` has no drift in the affected presentation, request, or scheduler paths. The matched 1030×450 crops come from the same 1100×820 light-theme component fixture before and after. The fixture's initial syntax and SDK-resolution setup errors were corrected before either valid capture; they are not product failures or passing proof.

### Run requested, scheduler has not started it

Knowledge → Scribes → an ongoing scribe → Run now. The first-run marker and the manual acknowledgement both overclaimed progress in this state.

Before

![Before: queued Scribe run is shown as running](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ab9abf19-0058-4140-ad5e-3c4aa19ce7ec)

After

![After: Scribe run remains requested until running is observed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/27c1bbc4-f5e4-447d-8313-2d309995c5b8)

prs.title: fix: preserve script builtin hooks on stock Bun
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Script harnesses miss patched builtin calls on current stock Bun because `syncBuiltinESMExports()` does not update named ESM bindings. This makes release-priority tests execute a real `gh` lookup, bypasses receipt-persistence fault injection, misses retry-clock observations, and loses the Docker launcher's first process-ownership edge.

upstream https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/42616

## User Impact

The existing script behavior stays the same on Node. Current stock Bun can exercise the same script paths and injected faults as the pinned fork. No new runtime branch, production seam, retry, timeout, or lifecycle policy is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The production changes are bounded to four existing call sites:

- `scripts/frv.mjs` promisifies `childProcess.execFile` at the same module initialization point, reaching the existing subprocess stub used by release-priority output and protected-read deadline tests.
- `scripts/github/mobile-store-release-notify.mjs` calls `timers.setTimeout` with the existing retry delay, reaching the existing guard clock.
- `scripts/pr-lib/ci-dispatch.mjs` uses the default `fs` object for the existing receipt open/write/fsync/close/rename/unlink sequence, preserving persistence and cleanup failure handling.
- `scripts/lib/tsx-cli-shim.mjs` calls `childProcess.spawn` with unchanged arguments and options. This restores the Docker observer's launcher edge; the scheduler and shutdown owners remain unchanged.

The workflow fixture test now spies on an explicit Vitest namespace. Reachable consumer mock factories mirror their overrides on named and default surfaces, following the regression lesson from #199058 and its follow-up commit 84579cbdcc63. The earlier approach is also covered by #198788.

## Evidence

Darwin arm64 proof uses Node 26.12.1, the supplied stock Bun 1.4.4-canary.1+2596ac5d3, and repository-pinned Bun 1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1. All 56 assigned cases failed on stock for the named-binding mechanism, passed on the pinned fork and Node, and pass after the changes. No assigned case is dropped or Linux-only-unverified.

| file | ids | stock before | fork | stock after | node | control | wall s (Node before → after) |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `docker-all-harness.test.ts` | 41 | all 41 fail; 55 total failures | 76/76 pass | all 41 pass; 72/76 overall | 76/76 pass | representative ownership case fails again | 137.24 → 141.16 |
| `pr-ci-dispatch.test.ts` | 5 | 36 pass / 5 fail | 41/41 pass | 41/41 pass | 41/41 pass | same 5 persistence failures | 37.72 → 20.88 |
| `release-priority.test.ts` | 5 | 19 pass / 5 fail | 24/24 pass | 24/24 pass | 24/24 pass | same 5 missing-gh failures | 21.35 → 24.59 |
| `mobile-store-release-notify.test.ts` | 2 | 23 pass / 2 fail | 25/25 pass | 25/25 pass | 25/25 pass | same 2 missing-wait failures | 15.54 → 16.16 |
| `frv.release.test.ts` | 2 | 2 fail | 2/2 pass | 2/2 pass | 2/2 pass | same 2 deadline failures | 17.08 → 16.68 |
| `ci-workflow.test-support.test.ts` | 1 | 2 pass / 4 fail, including assigned case | 6/6 pass | 6/6 pass | 6/6 pass | same 4 spy failures | 15.17 → 12.02 |

The FRV release row runs the two protected-read deadline cases (`-t 'bounds the protected (getRun|getAttemptJobs) transport retries'`); 118 other cases are intentionally filtered. The four remaining stock Docker failures also occur in the baseline and reject a percent-encoded preload file URL before cleanup-smoke provenance can run. They are separate from the 41 assigned cases.

Owner proof: `frv.test.ts` passes 143/143 on the rebased head and `local-check-runtime.test.ts` passes 25/25 on Node, fork, and stock. The latter directly invokes the launcher. prs.title: perf(state): avoid duplicate progress-card authority checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Progress-card writes invoke the same caller authority twice in each synchronous owner assertion.

## User Impact

No behavior change. Each write performs twelve fewer caller checks while preserving current authority at worker admission and commit.

## Why This Change Was Made

`withSessionStoreTarget` supplies an owner whose `assertCurrent()` starts by invoking the exact caller assertion passed to it. The progress-card wrapper called that assertion immediately before calling the owner, with no intervening work or await. Delete the duplicate call; keep the target, database-generation, worker-store, abort, and post-await checks.

Runtime production delta: **−1 line**. Reproduction tooling adds 199 lines; the integration regression adds 26 lines, with its exact test-line allocation. No cache, schema, public API, or filesystem-probe changes.

## Evidence

The real worker-boundary regression fails on the baseline with `expected 2 to be 1` and passes with the deletion. Both focused files passed: 8 progress-card tests and 22 agent-worker-store tests. These cover transaction/commit revocation, queued cancellation, owner/resource retirement, worker loss, FIFO, and committed-reply recovery.

Formatting, changed-file core/scripts lint, `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, and the gateway-root test typecheck passed. Exact-head PR CI is pending. An initial lint invocation selected broad artifact preparation; it was stopped and replaced with the focused repository configs.

The committed benchmark uses real worker writes, 10,000 synthetic session rows, and two real composed session-source wrappers over synthetic live authority. It does not reproduce the full operator-policy graph. Count-only instrumentation is separate from timing and allocation. Timing is untraced; allocation uses 1 KiB heap sampling with collected objects included.

Initial two counterbalanced pairs, 2,000 writes per arm per timing/allocation pass (five pairs in progress):

| Per write | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Caller assertions | 29 | 17 |
| Execution operation assertions | 8 | 8 |
| Worker-store assertions | 11 | 11 |
| Progress-card owner assertions | 12 | 12 |
| Sampled allocation, paired mean | 358,801 B | 358,014 B |
| Main-thread CPU, paired mean | 2,950.6 µs | 3,020.9 µs |

The allocation change is small (−787 B/write, −0.22%). CPU changed +22.2% then −13.8% as host load changed; this is inconclusive, not a claimed speedup. The reliable improvement is the removed duplicate work. The remaining pairs will be recorded here before handoff.

Run from the repository root, with the baseline progress-card module saved outside `src`:

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/progress-card-assertion-measure.mjs --root "$PWD/.local/card-base" --source /path/to/baseline-progress-card-store.ts --mode both --iterations 2000
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/progress-card-assertion-measure.mjs --root "$PWD/.local/card-candidate" --mode both --iterations 2000
```

The benchmark deletes its synthetic database fixtures. No whole-Gateway load test was run: this is a one-line deletion of a provably duplicate synchronous call, with no scheduling, transport, or admission-boundary change. No whole-Gateway CPU/latency/GC claim is made.

prs.title: perf(diagnostics): preserve oversized heap profiles as files
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Oversized `diagnostics.heapProfile` results discard the raw sampling tree and samples, leaving a bounded inclusive summary that can omit most allocating leaves.

## User Impact

Operators receive a Chrome DevTools-loadable `.heapprofile` path and byte size alongside the existing bounded summary. The file uses the inline profile's exact redaction policy, a 64 MiB cap, owner-only permissions, and manual retention like CPU profiles. Unwritable destinations, insufficient space, cancellation, and oversized files fail the capture with partial-file cleanup.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the diagnostic artifact reservation owner and save the already-sanitized profile only when it exceeds the inline budget. An iterative encoder handles deep native trees, writing in chunks instead of recursively stringifying the whole graph. Keep summary ranking and the 1 MiB response contract; account for the artifact receipt before filling summary rows. CPU capture behavior is unchanged.

This adds 99 runtime lines because preserving a bounded, redacted artifact requires serialization and cleanup; the existing summary remains a public caller contract. The reproducible benchmark adds 82 tooling lines. Regression tests add 120 lines, covered by an exact allocation record.

## Evidence

The regression fails on baseline `37d977fd28b060e8fd964a632858e5c0a709ca1b`: the oversized capture has no `path`. Candidate proof reads the real file, checks sample order and all sampled/native self bytes, redaction, permissions, deep-tree preservation, response bounds, and failed-artifact cleanup.

Owner replay on Node 26.12.1: 9,000 native nodes, 18,000 samples, 4 GiB attributed allocation, five captures per arm in AB/BA order (10 per revision). This measures export cost from a synthetic inspector result, not live Gateway load. Means include cold first captures.

| Metric per capture | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread CPU | 50.47 ms | 63.33 ms |
| Allocated bytes | 51.66 MiB | 63.46 MiB |
| Wall time | 53.29 ms | 149.78 ms |
| Bytes attributable from inline self rows | 441.46 MiB | 441.00 MiB |
| Bytes attributable from raw artifact | unavailable | 4096 MiB (100%) |
| Artifact size | none | 2.26 MiB |
| RPC result size | 1,048,450 bytes | 1,047,437 bytes |

This is a completeness fix, not a speedup: saving the previously discarded evidence costs about 12.85 ms CPU and 11.79 MiB allocation per oversized capture. Added asynchronous disk work raises wall time; all attributed samples survive. One fewer low-ranked summary row fits after adding the receipt.

Reproduce with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/diagnostic-profile-measure.ts --mode heap-export --nodes 9000 --samples 18000 --iterations 5`. Temporary benchmark artifacts are removed. No shared perf README changes.

Local validation passed: 109 distinct tests across `diagnostic-heap-profile.test.ts`, `diagnostic-cpu-profile.test.ts`, `diagnostics.cpu-profile.test.ts`, and `diagnostics.heap-snapshot.test.ts`, including native runtime captures. Initial focused run: 248.96 s wall; final heap/snapshot run after fixture lint fixes: 120.14 s wall (primarily cold subprocess compilation; final heap file 7.99 s wall). Changed-file oxlint/oxfmt, `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.state-logging.json --incremental`, test-line allocation check, and `git diff --check` passed. Exact-head PR CI is pending.

Protocol generation passes and is byte-identical: diagnostics have request schemas only, and neither the request nor generic response schema changes (the CPU artifact precedent likewise added no response schema). RPC documentation is updated.

No whole-Gateway stress campaign: this changes an explicitly requested diagnostic export, not a hot runtime path; the scoped owner proof applies. DevTools UI import was not exercised. Independent Codex review is delegated to the maintainer before merge, as requested.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Devices silently stops responding to actions after a confirmation dialog fails to load.

## User Impact

People see the failed confirmation and can continue using other device actions without leaving the page. A failed policy-discard confirmation keeps the original target and unsaved policy. No device or policy change is sent without the existing confirmation and permission checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Destructive prompts and the dirty command-approval target-switch prompt share the Devices dialog slot. Both now report preparation failures and always release their own slot. prs.title: fix(ui): keep the chat reader's text still while scrolling and while content renders late
prs.body:
Fixes #198500

## What Problem This Solves

The text being read in the Control UI chat jumps in two situations:

- **Scrolling up through settled tool calls.**
  - Tool steps from completed runs are estimated at 240 px and render at about 34 px.
  - A row scrolled into view enters the flow at its real size while the flow's start still counts its estimate.
  - Rows prepared ahead of the scroll, and the retained row measured just above the range, are painted at their estimated slot and then move when they join the flow.
  - On a real Gateway in Chromium, visible text moves up to 206.5 px against a fast upward scroll. At phone size in WebKit, a flick through settled tool calls moves it 65 px.
- **Late content inside the top visible message.** A Mermaid diagram replacing its source block moves the text 378 px. Raw tool details opening from an off-screen control move it 440 px.

## User Impact

Scrolling up through tool-heavy history and late-rendering diagrams keeps the text being read in place, in Chromium and in phone-size WebKit.

Accepted edge cases:
- At `scrollTop` 0, native scrolling clamps a negative correction, so the first rows of a transcript can still shift.
- A size change during a bubble's 180 ms entry animation is corrected approximately.
- Near the transcript end, a correction can clamp; end-follow owns that position.
- A row above the reader whose size is not known yet, with another such row below it, stays unpainted until that row is measured, usually one frame.

## Why This Change Was Made

Production changes are in the transcript code under `ui/src/pages/chat/components/`, plus the chat boot budget below.

**Rows arriving above the reader** (`chat-transcript-forecast.ts`, `chat-transcript-initial-range.ts`, `chat-transcript-layout-solid.tsx`):
- **Held until measured:** while the reader scrolls through laid-out content, a row of unknown size arriving before it stays out of the flow until it is measured, and so do the rows before it.
- **Known sizes join at once:** rows of known size between such a row and the flow join it directly, so the flow keeps up with the reader during a fast flick. Rows revisited on a return scroll enter directly too.
- **Exact estimates:** a row that measures exactly its estimate is admitted as well. Virtual-core reports no change for it, so the range asks for a render itself.
- **Nothing laid out:** after a jump or restore, every row enters directly.
- **Painting where rows land:** a row outside the flow paints only where it will land. A row before the flow hangs at its own real height above the rows between it and the flow; a row after it sits at its virtual slot. It paints once the sizes it depends on are known; until then a row before the flow is placed there unpainted, and one after it stays parked.
- **One owner for arriving rows:** the separate path that prepared a retained row just above the range and painted it at its estimated slot is removed; the hold covers that row.

**Reader anchor** (`chat-transcript-reader-anchor.ts`, `chat-transcript-virtualizer-host.ts`):
- **Arriving rows:** when such a row's size lands, the anchor corrects `scrollTop` in the same frame, and the host redraws the flow in that frame. On an iOS user agent, virtual-core would otherwise defer its own write while the reader scrolls.
- **Landing decisions:** these follow laid-out geometry, and only rows the reader saw count as retained content. The flow is found among the mounted rows, because landings that come first in the same batch move virtual-core's range.
- **Late content in the top row:**
  - After every scroll and resize, the anchor records what the reader sees in the row crossing the top edge, the way native scroll anchoring picks an anchor.
  - When that row resizes, the recorded content's movement is corrected through the existing row-correction path.
  - Content the edge cuts that grows in place, such as a message expanding below the edge, keeps marking the reader's place, so only what follows it moves. Content that keeps its size, such as a diagram's toolbar while its image loads below it, defers to the content after it.
  - Fallbacks cover a rendered replacement that detaches what it replaced (a diagram for its source block).

**Interaction anchor** (`chat-transcript-interaction-anchor.ts`): a control the reader can't see keeps the reader's content in place, not the control's row top.

There is no correction at `scrollTop` 0, for growth below the reader's content, or while another owner (restore, scroll commands, history prepend) positions the reader.

### Changed contracts

This PR changes three existing rules, all in scope, and raises one budget:

- **#195097 (ordinary rows in normal flow, retained predecessor preparation):**
  - A row of unknown size arriving above the reader waits for one measurement before it joins the flow. That costs one render per arriving batch while scrolling into unvisited history; rows of known size still enter directly. The test "keeps ordinary incoming rows in normal flow" is replaced by "admits an incoming row above the reader once it is measured".
  - The retained row just above the range is no longer prepared on a path of its own; the hold prepares and admits it like any arriving row.
- **#196173 (forecast rows painted before measurement):** a forecast row prepared ahead of a wheel or fling paints only where it will land, so painting it at its estimate no longer makes text appear and then move. The two tests "paints the down/up forecast outside active flow before measurement" become "prepares the down/up forecast outside active flow, unpainted until measured".
- **#196001 (measuring predecessor painted at its estimated slot):** that row hangs at its real height directly above the flow. Its estimated slot was the wrong place: a 437 px row painted in a 240 px slot moved 65 px against the scroll in WebKit when it joined. The test "keeps a measuring predecessor paintable without moving retained content" keeps its name and its checks that the row is painted, inert and outside the flow and that retained content does not move; it asserts the row's bottom at the flow's top and no clip, instead of its estimated slot and a clip to the estimate.
- **Chat boot JS budget:** this PR raises `chatBootJsGzipBytes` in `scripts/check-control-ui-performance.mts` by 1,333 B gzip, from `main`'s 1,310,894 B to 1,312,227 B. That is the fix's own anchor and row-admission code, measured locally by building the merged tree with and without this PR's transcript files (1,311,778 B and 1,310,445 B). Vyctor, please accept this or push back. The other violation the check reports, 21 chat boot JS requests against a limit of 20, appears on `main` as well.

### Edits to existing tests

- **`chat-transcript-geometry-updates.browser.test.tsx`**, the #196001 case above: it pinned painting at the estimated slot, which is the jump this PR removes.
- **`chat-cold-load-anchor.e2e.test.ts`**, "paints the cached tail…": after its wheel step it read the top row of the flow as the reader at once. With this PR the two rows the wheel brings in can still be held for a frame, painted at their real place but outside the flow, so it read the row below them; after the restore all rows are in the flow and it read the first of them, failing 3 of 3 runs. The restore itself is exact: the reader row sits at y=363 before and after. The test waits until no row outside the flow overlaps the viewport before it reads the reader. It passes with this PR and with `main`'s transcript files.
- **Projected-reply fixture** (Vyctor's `43bf3602`): it delivers the native row resize before checking the deferred highlight; the highlight assertion is unchanged.

## Evidence

**Real Gateway (Chromium).** Measured at `fe5e59c5`, before the WebKit change; not re-run on the current head. Setup:
- Isolated Gateway serving 1,432 saved synthetic messages (280 turns of prose, tables, code and settled read/exec calls).
- Chromium at 1280×900, 100 wheel steps per phase, comparing `main` (`aa4bc216`) with this PR.
- Measurement: the movement of the same visible text block between consecutive painted frames.

| Phase | Worst reverse move, `main` | Worst reverse move, this PR | Jumps over 2 px, `main` | Jumps over 2 px, this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Slow up (180 px steps) | 0.5 px | 0.5 px | 0 | 0 |
| Fast up (1,100 px steps) | 206.5 px | 0.5 px | 6 (median 121 px) | 0 |

`main`, fast up: the same letters move up 206 px against the scroll; the DOM offset for this pair is 205.5 px.

![main, fast upward scroll: before and after frames, the line "I'll inspect saved file 14 for step 199" moves up 206 px](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/b0dae77bb79c39a4a826e66de7ff2b65f2771508/images/2026/11/50f6dfc8-3927-4aee-b27d-e0fd5ce27a98.png)

This PR, fast up: no reverse move over 2 px; the largest DOM offset is 0.5 px.

![This PR, fast upward scroll: before and after frames, the same line stays at y=178 px](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/b0dae77bb79c39a4a826e66de7ff2b65f2771508/images/2026/11/9d930e8d-fa1f-48ca-94b6-c0e8461a385a.png)

Recording: `main` on the left, this PR on the right, slow then fast upward scroll at 0.25× speed (76 s):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b97d858f-44fe-4b1d-8736-369a5d485929

This is browser wheel input with one run per build, not a physical trackpad.

**Phone-size WebKit.** WebKit at 390×844 with an iPhone user agent, the 280-turn mocked session, repeated flicks driven one scroll step per frame (a dragged start, then decaying momentum) over 80,000 px. Measurement: the largest move of any painted text block against the scroll between consecutive frames.

| | Worst reverse move | Runs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Without this change (`43bf3602`) | 65 px | 2 of 2 fail |
| This PR | 0 px | 2 of 2 pass in the committed test; 0 px in 3 more runs of the same harness |

This is WebKit with programmatic momentum steps, not Safari on a physical iPhone.

**Mermaid**, same message and scroll position (synthetic content):

| Before (`main`) | After late render (`main`) | After late render (this PR) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Reader marker line below a Mermaid source block](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/b0dae77bb79c39a4a826e66de7ff2b65f2771508/images/2026/11/e97e2415-51e9-45dc-958a-145cd3a39ea3.png) | ![On main the rendered diagram pushes the marker line down 377 px](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/b0dae77bb79c39a4a826e66de7ff2b65f2771508/images/2026/11/c54ae7f5-0645-49b6-aba5-93d5604bab6d.png) | ![With this PR the marker line stays in place after the diagram renders](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/b0dae77bb79c39a4a826e66de7ff2b65f2771508/images/2026/11/799f975a-6167-4a9f-a8bf-c4175697fd1a.png) |

**Regression tests:**
- **`ui/src/e2e/chat-scroll-tool-rows.e2e.test.ts`:**
  - Chromium at 1280×900 with the wheel sequence above, and WebKit at phone size with the flicks above. Both check every visible text block between painted frames, including the one the top edge cuts and rows painted outside the flow.
  - Stops well before the transcript start, where native scrolling clamps corrections.

## What Problem This Solves

Restores builtin fault injection and observation in tests on stock Bun, where `syncBuiltinESMExports()` does not update named ESM bindings.

## User Impact

Test-local builtin factories now install the same override on named and default exports. The admin CLI fixture carries its observation preload through the existing runtime-worker generation owner, preserving backend exports and loader selection, then joins the existing generation cleanup. The TTS fixture also preserves its native main-thread fsync observer; inconclusive Claude authentication cases explicitly prove their injector ran.

The only production touch is `worker-bundle-archive.ts`: the existing pipeline calls `fsSync.createReadStream` with exactly the same arguments and buffering. Its native subprocess fixture needs to observe that default builtin object. There is no new production seam, global shim, extra I/O, or lifecycle policy. prs.title: fix(plugins): allow retrying pack after a failed artifact write
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `openclaw plugins pack` leaving a corrupt final archive after a partial write (for example, a full output disk), so freeing disk space and retrying still fails with `EEXIST`.

## User Impact

Failed writes remove the newly created archive so users can retry normally. Existing approval artifacts are still refused without changing their bytes, and successful archives retain mode `0600`. No configuration or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Open the output exclusively before taking responsibility for cleanup, then close and remove that owned file on a write/close failure. Preserve the original error. This keeps the existing output contract and avoids adding another staging/publication mechanism.

Simplified to production +9/-1 and an extension of the existing artifact test (+19/-1); no new fixture or test allocation. Cleanup is best-effort for catchable failures; this does not add crash-atomic publication or a guarantee against cleanup failures.

## Evidence

Compared base `c8caba299e65a7b98bb14a4c5731376658d8c84b` with `2d88d6619dc2ab3585a4afe5f19c859e65061a54` in a non-root, secretless Linux container (Node 24, one CPU, 1.5 GiB memory). These are actual source CLI invocations through the repository recovery entry, with real esbuild/tar and filesystem operations, not mocked CLI commands or a packaged-release claim.

- On a 1 MiB output tmpfs with only one 4 KiB block free, packing a roughly 17 KiB valid artifact fails with real `ENOSPC`. **Base leaves 4,096 bytes and retry fails `EEXIST`; candidate leaves no file and retry succeeds after removing the filler.**
- A 638-byte artifact succeeds with the same one-block space boundary. Normal packing succeeds; retrying an existing complete artifact fails without modifying it; output mode remains `0600`.
- Existing native artifact-authoring suite: **17/17 passed**, 24.1 seconds total. Its new partial-write regression fails on base at the missing-output assertion, then passes with the fix. The regression injects an I/O failure after writing real partial bytes; the CLI proof above uses actual disk exhaustion.
- Targeted format and lint pass (0 warnings/errors). The targeted typecheck dependency graph exited 137 under the 1.5 GiB container cap; type/build verification is deferred to exact-head CI. No full local suite or build was run. CI timing is pending.
- Fresh independent agent review of the complete final diff: no actionable findings. No local ClawSweeper/autoreview run claimed.

<details>
<summary>Real CLI reproduction and sanitized observed output</summary>

Create a minimal tool plugin using `defineToolPlugin` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/tool-plugin`, run `plugins build`, then `plugins pack`. Mount the output directory as a 1 MiB tmpfs; write a filler occupying all but one filesystem block. A small tool packs successfully. Add an exported 16 KiB random payload to the same valid entry and pack again to a new final path. Remove only the filler, then retry exactly the same command. Finally attempt the existing output again and compare its bytes.

```text
BEFORE
openclaw plugins build --root /tmp/pack-behavior/plugin => exit=0
openclaw plugins pack --root /tmp/pack-behavior/plugin --out /tmp/pack-behavior/normal.tgz --json => exit=0 bytes=638
{"archiveSize": 638}
openclaw plugins pack --root /tmp/pack-behavior/plugin --out /output/result.tgz --json => exit=1 ENOSPC: no space left on device, write
{"failedSize": 4096}
openclaw plugins pack --root /tmp/pack-behavior/plugin --out /output/result.tgz --json => exit=1 EEXIST: file already exists, open '/output/result.tgz'
{"retryExit": 1, "files": ["result.tgz"]}
AFTER
openclaw plugins build --root /tmp/pack-behavior/plugin => exit=0
openclaw plugins pack --root /tmp/pack-behavior/plugin --out /tmp/pack-behavior/normal.tgz --json => exit=0 bytes=638
{"archiveSize": 638}
openclaw plugins pack --root /tmp/pack-behavior/plugin --out /output/boundary.tgz --json => exit=0 bytes=638
openclaw plugins pack --root /tmp/pack-behavior/plugin --out /output/result.tgz --json => exit=1 ENOSPC: no space left on device, write
{"failedSize": null}
openclaw plugins pack --root /tmp/pack-behavior/plugin --out /output/result.tgz --json => exit=0 bytes=17309
{"retryExit": 0, "files": ["result.tgz"]}
openclaw plugins pack --root /tmp/pack-behavior/plugin --out /output/result.tgz --json => exit=1 EEXIST: file already exists, open '/output/result.tgz'
{"existingPreserved": true, "mode": 384}
```
</details>

prs.title: fix: automations keep running after their conversation is deleted
prs.body:
Related: #199300

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes linked automations continuing to run after their creating conversation is deleted.

## User Impact

Deleting a conversation disables its bound automations while retaining job definitions and activity history. Commands cannot restart after their exact creating conversation is removed, including manual runs after re-enabling. Standalone automations remain unaffected.

If any job cannot be disabled, the conversation remains and the error explains that some jobs may already be disabled. Existing automation-management permissions still apply. This prevents future starts; it does not promise to kill a command already running.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the backend follow-up to #199300, not another warning-only fix. Deletion reuses the existing bound-job operation before removing the session, and command admission respects a removed parent. The existing command exceptions for archived parents and missing worktrees are unchanged. The confirmation and documentation now describe the repaired behavior.

## Evidence

- The registered deletion handler with real SQLite session/job storage and production scheduler admission reproduced both defects before the repair. Only host-command execution is synthetic.
- 7 handler scenarios pass: disablement, standalone execution, refusal to restart an orphaned command, partial persistence failure, human ownership/scopes, and model command-job policy. The model-policy regression fails without the existing policy guard and passes with it.
- 114 scheduler/binding cases and 48 existing deletion/state/worktree cases passed. Unchanged-input results were reused after integrating #199300; the updated handler cases were rerun on this candidate.
- 59 organizer cases and 2 production-built browser flows pass. Sidebar and Sessions-page flows prove Cancel sends no deletion, Confirm sends one exact-session deletion, and the client sends no separate automation mutations. Browser Gateway responses are synthetic.
- Scoped core/UI/browser typechecking, lint, formatting, i18n verification, and diff checks pass. Browser proof took 19.94s including its build; the final 7-case handler proof took 50.88s including compiler preparation. CI is pending; no live user conversation or automation was changed.
- Canonical autoreview with Codex GPT-6.1 Sol reviewed the complete final local candidate against `b9036d4f002d4a5a2d7146fe5b79766d550820e8` at P0–P2. Its first review found a missing existing model-command policy check; that was repaired and regression-tested. The final review was scoped-clean with no remaining actionable findings. A local ClawSweeper executable was unavailable. The reviewer did not independently execute tests.
- Simplification: reuse the existing session-deletion and bound-job owners; no new schema, scheduler, cache, or client-side mutation sequence.

### Before

Actual production-built Control UI, light theme, synthetic Backup maintenance conversation. The warning previously required separate automation cleanup.

![Before: linked automations may keep running](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5ff896e7-6fb7-4250-85fb-54ad5564d5e8)

### After

The same dialog now explains backend disablement and the limit for commands already running.

![After: linked automations will be disabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/20ba90a8-26b7-4a0c-b43b-b352da4b84bc)

prs.title: test: own synthetic child process stdio
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Synthetic ChildProcess fixtures fail during setup on stock Bun when they assign native readonly stream properties or read uninitialized stdio and IPC getters. In the timeout suite, four setup errors were hidden behind unresolved staging promises; the other thirteen failed directly at stream assignment.

## User Impact

Tests retain their existing assertions across Node, the pinned Bun fork, and current stock Bun. Production behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fixtures define their own stdio properties, including explicit null stdin, or use EventEmitter when they only require events and mutable lifecycle state. The shared managed-child fixture supplies its own stdin and connected state for both callers, and the local factories cover every child constructor in their files. The failed-spawn case retains undefined output streams.

Both the broker and shell environment production paths call spawn before reading stdio; neither constructs an unspawned production child. No production workaround is needed.

Follows the fixture ownership precedent in #195405. upstream https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/44933

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(ios): embedded Dashboard pages ignore device appearance
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: opening Automations or another embedded Dashboard page in the iOS app abruptly switches to the saved web theme instead of following the app’s device appearance.

## User Impact

Embedded iPhone and iPad pages use native-aligned surfaces, red accents, and sans-serif typography in the device’s light or dark mode. Saved web theme, accent, and font choices remain unchanged. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing theme owner separates rendered iOS appearance from saved web preferences. A private palette uses the existing document-start and runtime stylesheet lifecycle; only iOS embeds fetch it. The redundant first-paint theme-name table is replaced by the equivalent naming formula. Appearance explains that its theme controls customize the web Dashboard.

iOS embeds load one versioned 1,686-byte palette stylesheet, like the selected built-in web palettes; ordinary browsers do not fetch it. The existing first-paint and load/error behavior is retained.

This does not add native theme synchronization, replace native controls, or change Android/macOS appearance or navigation.

## Evidence

Addresses [ClawSweeper’s P2 byte-budget finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199394#issuecomment-6888222427) on `0e05c2920f79a7edaf17201de7d0477a9a3db3ad`. Repair head: `5ce5df3a571f247ce2043da26961b38249e56309`.

**Acceptance:** unchanged deterministic byte/request limits against base `65cf8cdc3780439cb599853f443c45fed28a98e4`; no budget or baseline increases.

| Same-toolchain measurement | Reviewed candidate | Repair | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Document gzip | 14,103 B | 13,966 B | Below the unchanged 14,026 B ceiling |
| Shared total CSS raw growth over base | +1,287 B | 0 B | Pass |
| Shared total CSS gzip growth over base | +195 B | 0 B | Pass |
| Startup CSS requests | 1 | 1 | Unchanged |
| Largest JavaScript differential gate | Within allowance | Within allowance | Pass |

- The unchanged differential performance checker passes on the repair. Existing base CSS/largest-asset debt remains visible as warnings; the PR adds no new failing budget. Startup JS grows 70 B and complete route boot JS grows 114 B over the paired base, within existing limits.
- Both strengthened production-browser scenarios pass: phone dark and iPad light, first-paint names **and background colors**, one native palette load per document, live mode changes, unchanged web preferences, and no native-palette fetch in the ordinary-browser control. Fresh production build plus E2E: 16.74 seconds; scenario execution approximately 4.4 seconds.
- 84 related tests pass across six files (4.30 seconds), including every built-in document-start theme name and palette URL in both modes. UI and selected UI app/E2E test-graph typechecks, scoped lint, stylesheet lint, formatting, i18n verification, and diff checks pass.
- Final independent Auto Review of the complete local candidate against the base found no actionable **P0–P2** issues. The reviewer did not independently execute the tests.
- Phone Automations, phone Appearance, and iPad Automations captures were regenerated on the repair and are byte-identical to the three published after images below; their existing uploaded assets are reused.
- Simplification: the global entry CSS no longer carries an iOS-only palette, and the duplicate HTML theme-name table is removed. No new preference store, configuration option, bridge, or compatibility layer. Production/docs delta: +143/−47 lines; regression coverage: +206 lines.

<details>
<summary>Reproducing the size comparison</summary>

The stock `pnpm ui:check-performance:base 65cf8cdc3780439cb599853f443c45fed28a98e4` runner exceeded this sandbox’s 1 GiB `/tmp` capacity while expanding the base archive. The exact base production inputs and frozen candidate were instead built serially in the task-owned checkout with the same installed toolchain and fixed build identity; source backups and a finally block restored the candidate before its build. The repaired build used Vite’s native config loader through the repository TypeScript loader.

The existing supported comparator was then run without changes:

```text
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-control-ui-performance.mts --base-dist <paired-base-dist>
```

It reproduces the reviewed candidate’s document/CSS failures and exits successfully on the repair. Precompressed-asset verification also passes. These are deterministic size measurements, not latency benchmarks.

</details>

**Proof boundary:** screenshots use synthetic data and the real production web bundle with the iOS document-start embed capability. They are not simulator captures; Xcode/iOS simulator verification is unavailable in this Linux sandbox. Hosted CI on `5ce5df3a571f247ce2043da26961b38249e56309` confirms that the [performance gate passes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43672048654/job/132684408743). UI E2E shards [1/7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43672048654/job/132684409028) and [3/7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43672048654/job/132684408975) fail; partial attribution is summarized below, and the aggregate gate is red. This PR is not ready to merge. Hosted timing details are not yet summarized.

**CI attribution follow-up:** the WebKit 390 px older-history failure (`190` messages expected, `30` received) matches the complete terminal failure signature in [scheduled-main job 132671550925](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43667891698/job/132671550925), main commit `41f2b981d240cab9e55b07cba991282a795317b5`. This is stronger than the report’s job-name-only classification. That main job also exhibits the same two subpixel footer geometries, with expected/received reversed. The PR’s zero-geometry footer result and Logs auto-follow-resumption failure remain **new/unknown**, not waived or called inherited. A focused replay of the cached-header connection case passes on the candidate (1 passed, 1 dashboard case not selected; 16.06 seconds including build). That is a non-reproduction, not a fix or evidence that the CI failure is unrelated. The additional local WebKit replay is blocked at browser dependency qualification in this sandbox; no test assertions were bypassed, and no CI rerun was requested. No specific introduced defect is established by this bounded investigation. The aggregate gate remains red. The retained main-log window includes the terminal summaries, not the full execution chronology.

### Before and after

Same synthetic Automations page, saved Manuscript Light appearance, and dark device mode. Browser captures of the iOS embed, not simulator screenshots.

<details>
<summary>Additional embedded contexts</summary>

Appearance settings explain the web/device distinction after a live switch to light mode:

![Appearance guidance in light mode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d0fb6d0c-8ab4-4889-9082-a9dd9188b5c0)

![iPad embedded Automations in light mode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e2a5f16c-9b34-431c-82fc-0eb750056086)

</details>

prs.title: fix(cron): cron session reports "Context overflow" when recovery compaction fails
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/199472

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an isolated cron job's session tells the user "Context overflow … Try /reset (or /new) … or use a larger-context model" when the turn overflowed and recovery compaction then failed, while the cron run record for the same run names the recovery failure.

## User Impact

User impact: when recovery compaction fails in an isolated cron run, the cron session's notice names that failure (for example, "Auto-compaction could not reach the model provider …"), matching the cron run record and what chat turns already show since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198841.

## Why This Change Was Made

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198841 stopped chat settlement from publishing the precheck's tentative overflow error once recovery fails, and its notes named the cron isolated-agent executor as a sibling left for later. The cron executor still published the deferred overflow error and its overflow observation as the session's terminal lifecycle error.

The deferred-terminal resolution (recovery error first, its `errorNotice`, and dropping the stale overflow observation) now lives in one place next to the lifecycle terminal backstop, `resolveDeferredLifecycleTerminal` in `agent-lifecycle-terminal.ts`. Chat settlement and the cron executor both call it. Chat behavior is unchanged; its inline copy of that logic is gone. The cron executor stays at its line cap (net zero lines there).

Cron now follows chat settlement's rule from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198841 (drop the overflow observation whenever a recovery error replaces the overflow). The agent command path (`agents/command/lifecycle.ts`) keeps its own rule, which keeps the observation when the recovery text is itself an overflow message; this PR does not change it.

Production delta against `main`: +30/−18 (the shared function +18, chat settlement −6, cron executor 0). Tests: +16/−9, folded into an existing cron case.

## Evidence

Tested at `ba52e416c6b` (base `main` `2928381894f`).

An isolated Gateway (its own state directory, loopback port, built from source) ran one isolated cron job through `openclaw automations run --wait`. The provider was a local OpenAI-compatible mock: it answers the first turn with a `read` tool call for a 120,000-byte workspace file, rejects the follow-up with `400 context_length_exceeded`, and answers every summarization request with `502` (`retry-after: 1`). The Gateway, cron service, embedded runner, recovery compaction and session lifecycle are the real ones.

The blocks below are summaries rendered from each run's saved JSON outputs, not raw terminal output. The commands the driver ran, in order: `automations add … --name "proof-<label>" --session isolated --no-deliver --json`, `automations run <job-id> --wait --wait-timeout 6m --poll-interval 2s`, `automations runs <job-id> --limit 5 --json`, `gateway call sessions.list --params '{"limit":50}' --json` (to find the cron session's key), and `gateway call chat.history --params '{"sessionKey":"<cron-session-key>","limit":50}' --json`. The provider line comes from the mock's request log.

Before (`main` `2928381894f`):

```text
run exit=1 seconds=82
provider requests: 23 (main: tool_call read, 400 context_length_exceeded; summary: 21 x status 502 over 78s)
cron run: status=error error="Auto-compaction could not reach the model provider after the provider rejected the prompt. Try again or run /compact."
cron session <cron-session-key>: status=(absent) lastRunError=(absent)
cron session notice (run-failed-before-reply):
  content: "⚠️ Context overflow: prompt too large for the model. Try /reset (or /new) to start a fresh session, or use a larger-context model."
  cause:   {"provider":"mock","failoverReason":"context_overflow"}
```

After (this PR):

```text
run exit=1 seconds=77
provider requests: 23 (main: tool_call read, 400 context_length_exceeded; summary: 21 x status 502 over 72s)
cron run: status=error error="Auto-compaction could not reach the model provider after the provider rejected the prompt. Try again or run /compact."
cron session <cron-session-key>: status=(absent) lastRunError=(absent)
cron session notice (run-failed-before-reply):
  content: "Auto-compaction could not reach the model provider after the provider rejected the prompt. Try again or run /compact."
  cause:   (none)
```

The same summaries with the command lines: [before.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261115-finding-198841-1-accept/before.txt), [after.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261115-finding-198841-1-accept/after.txt).

Observed result: on `main` the cron session's notice carries the overflow text and cause while the run record names the recovery failure; with this change both carry the recovery failure, and the overflow cause is gone.

Regression: the case in `run.meta-error-status.test.ts` that keeps a run-level error when delivery is pending now drives a real cron run whose turn notes the overflow and returns a `compaction_failure`, and asserts the published terminal error; its title says so. It fails on `main` and with only the cron executor change reverted. The existing chat case in `agent-runner-execution-progress.test.ts` fails when chat settlement's new call is reverted.

Checks: the touched test file and the tests of every consumer of the changed modules (`run.meta-error-status`, `run.session-lifecycle`, `agent-runner-execution-progress`, `agent-lifecycle-terminal`, `server-chat.agent-events`, `server-chat.native-provider-error`, `session-lifecycle-run-failure`, `session-lifecycle-state.persistence`, `agent-job.execution-settlement`, `agents/command/lifecycle`), all passing at the head; `pnpm check:changed` against `main` (typecheck, lint, format, line-cap ratchet) passed. Net test lines are +7, within the test-lines ratchet's per-PR allowance: "Test lines OK. Net test lines: +7; allowance: 400; allocation credit: 0." The broad suites run in this PR's CI.

| Test file | `--maxWorkers=1` wall |
| --- | --- |
| `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.meta-error-status.test.ts` | 11.8 s |

Local review: autoreview (Codex gpt-6.1-sol, high), base 2928381894fb2264c4cfb508596c95095ef99b95 to head ba52e416c6bd7f0125e1830e972715ddbdc76ba4, priority P0–P1, with `compaction-recovery-lifecycle-error.ts`, `agent-lifecycle-terminal.ts` and `run-orchestrator.ts` as source context: scoped-clean, no remaining findings.

<!-- openclaw-preflight:v1
{"v":1,"repo":"openclaw/openclaw","base":"2928381894fb2264c4cfb508596c95095ef99b95","head":"ba52e416c6bd7f0125e1830e972715ddbdc76ba4","tool":{"name":"autoreview","version":"source-a120e048f9fc"},"completion":"complete","summary":"Threshold P1; lower priorities not assessed; status scoped-clean; accepted 0; priority-filtered 0; scope/attribution-rejected 0; missing-required 0. Self-reported; see native report."}
-->

Not covered: no real model provider; the mock stages the overflow and the failed summarization. Callers that do not defer the terminal (the embedded runner's own terminal in `run-orchestrator.ts`) publish the recovery text, but, by reading the source, with the stale `context_overflow` cause that the turn's finishing event noted; this PR does not change that path and did not run it. The agent command path (`agents/command/lifecycle.ts`) keeps its own handling from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198841.

prs.title: fix(ui): speed up localized WebKit startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Localized Control UI cold boot in WebKit downloads the broad locale catalog cohort ahead of the critical entry and connection graph, delaying usable German and Chinese chat.

## User Impact

German and Chinese WebKit cold boot at 100 ms RTT becomes about 12% faster. The composer appears in the selected language on its first visible frame, with no English flash. Direction selection remains immediate.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing locale policy and hints, but append those hints at the document's `interactive` transition. This admits the existing entry/route preload graph first without waiting for module evaluation. The boot-preload owner, import-map ordering, lazy boundaries, translated readiness owner, and CSS delivery are unchanged. No new configuration or dependencies. The private policy uses a compact tuple and single-use lists stay inlined to keep HTML within its existing fixed cap.

## Evidence

Acceptance: 20 rotated base/head/base triplets with A/A for each engine (WebKit, Chromium, Firefox), locale (English, German, Chinese), network (localhost, 100 ms RTT), and boot state (cold, warm). Application readiness includes locale application. Target is at least 5% improvement for localized WebKit cold RTT boot, with other cells within the 5% median/tail guard and A/A noise. Synthetic Gateway over the production HTTP/bundle owner; headless, fresh browser per observation. Warm reload retains IndexedDB; the harness disables HTTP cache, so this is not a browser disk-cache benchmark. WebKit numbers are application elapsed time, not CPU.

| --- | --- |
| Timing matrix | 36 cells, 2,190 passed observations; 20 triplets/cell plus 10 focused German local triplets |

prs.title: fix(ios): keep chat state when the Gateway reconnects after background
prs.body:
## Problem

After the background grace ends (about 25 s), the iOS app drops its Gateway sockets. When the user comes back, it reconnects, and two things happen that throw away state the screen already has:

1. `IOSChatViewModelOwner` calls `viewModel.load()`: a full bootstrap. It raises `isLoading`, repaints from cache and re-reads history and every catalog. macOS handles the same event with the in-place `.reconnected` recovery. iOS uses `composerChrome: .clean`, which draws no spinner for `isLoading`, so this is wasted work rather than a visible glitch. The before/after recordings below look the same.
2. Media resolver health drops while the new socket is probed. `ChatMediaImageAttachment` keys its load task on that health, so a loaded image falls to "Image unavailable", then shows "Loading image…" and downloads again.

## Solution

- `OpenClawChatViewModel.recoverAfterReconnect()` (new, shared) runs the same in-place recovery as a transport `.reconnected` event. It marks health unknown, re-subscribes the active session on the new socket (before, only bootstrap did this), then runs one history read, catalog refreshes and a health probe. Run, history, outbox and progress-card state from the old socket is reset as before.
- The owner only takes this path when owner, agent and Gateway authority are unchanged; a Gateway change still detaches and rebuilds. So this recovery keeps the model, agent, source and composer catalogs on screen until their reloads replace them. Transport events can't know this, so they still clear catalogs as before. Without this, the in-place recovery made the model chip read "Default" and hid the permission shield for about half a second on every resume. Base iOS had neither.
- `IOSChatViewModelOwner` calls it instead of `load()` on operator reconnect.
- `ChatMediaImageAttachment`: a decoded image is complete without the resolver, so a health change no longer drops it.

## Evidence

`pnpm ios:behavior` gets a `resume` case. It streams a reply that ends with an image, leaves to Settings for 40 s and comes back. Setup gates confirm the image loaded first and the app logged `Background reconnect suppressed` while away. The probe now also records the loading flag, resolver health and image load states. The QA mock's `UXSTREAM` prompt takes `IMAGE`, which ends the reply with a `MEDIA:` line.

`resume`, 3 samples each, same Mac, simulator, isolated Gateway and QA mock. "Base" is this branch with the reconnect change and the image guard removed, so the probe is the same in both columns:

| Gate / metric | Base | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| connection dropped while away (setup) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| image loaded before leaving (setup) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| no transcript reload on return | **0/3** | 3/3 |
| image stays loaded | **0/3** | 3/3 |
| no remounts | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| reading position holds (≤1 pt) | **0/3** (2.7 pt) | 3/3 (0 pt) |
| image state changes on return (median) | 2 | 0 |
| health drops (median) | 1 | 1 |

Health still drops once by design: the new socket's health is unknown until its probe answers.

Recording frame about 1 s after returning: base (left) shows the image dropped to "Image unavailable" and the reply collapsed; this PR (right) keeps it.

![Resume after background: base drops the image (left), this PR keeps it (right)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b68b0c0c-3c00-4b94-947d-299c3e8b912c)

Full harness on the final code (`stream-turn`, `stream-follow`, `scrolled-up`, `keyboard`, `relaunch`, `resume` with the image): every gate 3/3, exit 0.

Unit: `ChatViewModelReconnectBurstTests` gets `owner reconnect reconciles in place without a reload`. It checks that the loading flag stays off, health isn't reused from the replaced socket, history is read once, and the model label and session controls stay through the recovery. It fails when the owner recovery clears catalogs like a transport event (label and controls assertions), and passes with this change. Local suites pass: `ChatViewModelReconnectBurstTests`, `ChatComposerParityTests`, `ChatStreamReplayTests`, `ChatViewModelOutboxTests`, `ChatViewModelUnreadTests`, `ChatViewModelReactionsTests`, `ChatSessionSidebarMenuTests`, `ChatGatewayEventSubscriptionTests`.

Local gaps, not caused here:

- `ChatViewModelTests` hangs locally past 300 s, on base as well as this branch; CI's full OpenClawKit run is the proof for it.
- `ChatStreamReplayTests` `canonical history adopts a final with different content framing` failed intermittently on base and branch in earlier runs; it passed in the final run.
- The composer briefly shows "Connect to a gateway" during the reconnect, on base too. It comes from the app model's routing identity, which this change doesn't touch.

Review: local ClawSweeper couldn't run because Codex isn't logged in on the review host (401). It's covered by the automatic hosted ClawSweeper review of this PR.

prs.title: fix(exec): keep processes the agent detaches, tracked and bounded
prs.body:
## Problem

When the agent starts a process that must keep running, OpenClaw stops it.

- A completed host `exec` call cancels its whole process tree. This stops `cmd &` and `nohup cmd &`. On Linux, the child subreaper also adopts and stops processes that left with `setsid` or a double fork, such as `nginx` and `sshd`.
- A one-shot `openclaw agent --local` run cancels every process in its exec scope when it exits. This also stops `background: true` services.
- Result: on Linux, no start style survives the CLI. The agent reports success, and the service is gone before anything can use it.
- `background: true` services also inherit the 1800 s exec timeout unless the model passes `timeoutSeconds: 0`.
- The model-facing text was wrong. `background` said "Start an independent service now; survives request Stop", but the service did not survive the CLI.

#150750 made the killing deliberate. Its real problem was that OpenClaw's own relay and owner processes stayed alive with the user's processes. It fixed that by stopping the user's processes too.

## Fix

This is PR 1: stop killing, stay bounded.

1. **Hand off on a normal exit.** When the root command exits normally, the process-group owner (anchor) does not signal its group. It reads the process table, reports every live process the command left, stops observing lineage, and exits. On Linux it exits as the subreaper, so adopted processes go to init. If a released process still holds the command's stdout or stderr pipe, the anchor keeps draining that pipe until it closes, so the service never gets SIGPIPE or EPIPE when it logs. The cap bounds these drain anchors.
2. **Every survivor is accounted for.** The report has no size limit. It includes the owner's group members, the processes the Linux subreaper adopted (these are the owner's direct children, and they stay the command's), and all of their descendants, also those in a new session (for example the `sleep` under `setsid sh -c 'sleep 300 & wait'`). If the process table cannot be read, the anchor stops the tree like a cancellation instead of releasing processes it cannot name.
3. **Adopt survivors as sessions.** Each survivor becomes an ordinary background session in the process registry, under the session that ran the command.
   - The tool result names its PID and session ID. `process list` shows it, and `process kill` stops it.
   - It is pinned to its start time. Every signal re-checks that identity, so a reused PID is never signalled.
   - OpenClaw drops it within 5 s of its exit. Gateway stop stops it.
4. **A stop counts only when the exit is observed.** OpenClaw sends SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after the 5 s grace, then waits up to 2 s for the recorded identity to disappear. If a signal is denied (for example EPERM after a UID change) or the process does not disappear, the record stays, the session is marked as cleanup-uncertain, and the result says so. This applies to `process kill`, session reset and delete, Gateway stop and over-limit survivors. A later stop retries.
5. **Admission caps.** At most 16 services per session and 64 per Gateway. A service is a background session or an adopted survivor.
   - A `background: true` start reserves its slot before approval and startup and holds it until its session runs or startup fails, so concurrent starts cannot pass the limit.
   - Over the cap, a new `background: true` start fails with an error that names `process list` and `process kill`.
   - Over the cap, a foreground command's new survivors are stopped by identity, and the result lists their PIDs and the reason. A survivor whose stop is not confirmed stays tracked over the limit, so nothing escapes custody.
   - OpenClaw never stops an older process to make room.
6. **Stopping stays the same where it matters.** Timeout, no-output timeout, cancellation, request Stop, `process kill`, memory limit, host loss and launch failure still stop the whole tree, including Linux `setsid` and double-fork escapees. Scopes with `required-all` cleanup (the local TUI shell, managed workers, cron exit watchers, update repair, desktop helpers) keep strict cleanup on exit.
7. **Every reset path stops everything the session runs.** Chat `/new` and `/reset`, Gateway `sessions.reset` and session delete all call one shared step, `stopSessionResetProcesses`, after the session's subagents stop and before the replacement conversation is committed. It stops in-flight commands, `background: true` services and adopted survivors by identity. If a stop is not confirmed, the reset fails and asks to retry. Durable processes are not affected.
8. **One-shot exit hands services off.** At the end of `openclaw agent --local`:
   - `background: true` services and adopted survivors are handed off, and only in-flight work is cancelled. The order from #177940 stays: hand-off, then scope cleanup, then join.
   - The CLI prints what it left running (PID and command) to stderr.
   - If the CLI dies without cleanup, host loss still stops work that was not handed off.
9. **No built-in timeout for services.** `background: true` no longer inherits the 1800 s default. An explicit `timeoutSeconds` or a configured `tools.exec.timeoutSeconds` still applies. In a subagent or cron run that can wait for the command with `sessions_yield`, the default still bounds that wait, as current main requires.
10. **The model sees the truth.** The tool result names every survivor and every stop, with PID and reason. The `background` description and the background-process docs state the real lifetime.

The relay and the anchor still exit after every completed command, so #150750 does not regress.

## Proof

"Base" is the behaviour without this change. "Previous head" is the head that review rated (`3549c2b`, then `bb2b295`).

| # | Proof | Tier | Base / previous head | Head |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 50 calls that each leave a survivor: 16 are adopted, 34 are stopped with the reason in the result, 0 relay or anchor processes remain (#150750); `process list` shows them; `process kill` stops one by identity; an exited one drops out within one reap interval; Gateway stop ends the rest | vitest-source, macOS | previous head: fails | pass |
| 2 | One command leaves 20 survivors: 16 tracked, 4 stopped, every PID named, none alive and untracked; then `background: true` is refused and a new survivor is stopped | vitest-source, macOS | previous head: fails (only 16 reported) | pass |
| 3 | Two concurrent `background: true` starts at 15 of 16: exactly one starts | vitest-source, macOS | previous head: fails (both start, 17 running) | pass |
| 4 | A survivor's child in a new session is tracked; stopping the session ends both | vitest-source, macOS | previous head: fails (child untracked) | pass |
| 5 | Real Linux run in `node:24-bookworm` (root, subreaper active) of `bash-tools.exec-group-cleanup.real.test.ts`, `subagent-reset.lifecycle.test.ts` and `worker.runtime.test.ts`: survivors, cap, reservation, descendant closure, `setsid sh -c 'sleep & wait'`, timeout of `setsid`/double-fork children, unconfirmed stops, chat/RPC reset | vitest-source, Linux container (fresh `pnpm install`, no skips) | `bb2b295`: 8 failed (every survivor test: the subreaper-adopted survivors were classed as helpers, so nothing was reported) | 96 of 96 passed, 0 skipped |
| 6 | Signals to a survivor are denied (EPERM): reset fails, the session stays running with cleanup uncertainty in its output, the process is still tracked; after signals work, a retry stops it and settles the record | vitest-source, macOS | previous head: fails (reset reported success, record dropped) | pass |
| 7 | Chat `/reset` (`initSessionState`) and Gateway `sessions.reset` each stop a running `background: true` service and a `cmd &` survivor before the new session is committed | vitest-source, macOS | previous head: chat path fails (both processes still alive); RPC path passes | pass, both paths |
| 9 | Detached styles (`node &`, `nohup`, plain `&`, double fork) survive a completed call; a timeout still stops what the call started; one-shot cleanup hands off and prints services and stops in-flight work; handed-off servers that log every request answer 20 of 20 requests 10 s after the run | vitest-source, macOS | — | pass |
| 10 | A timeout stops `setsid` and double-fork children | vitest-source, Linux container | — | pass (part of row 5) |
| 11 | Supervisor, relay, anchor, exec, process tool, exec follow-up (`sessions_yield`), cron exit watchers (`required-all` extinction), session reset/delete, agent delete, TUI, desktop and chat session suites | vitest-source, macOS | — | see "Test results" below |
| 12 | CLI lifecycle, real model: `openclaw agent --local` with five start styles; the server is probed 0, 3 and 10 s after the CLI exits, then sent 20 requests | source (`ocx src`), macOS | base (`669576890a1f`): 1 of 5 alive (only the double-fork daemon, which leaves the group); `background: true` answers 200 during the run, then dies at CLI exit | 5 of 5 alive, each answers 20 of 20 requests; the CLI prints every handed-off PID; 0 relay/anchor processes after the servers stop |
| 13 | Gateway lifecycle, real model, one session: start `background: true`, `nohup &` and plain `&` servers; check them in the next turn; chat `/reset`; start again; RPC `sessions.reset`; start again; stop the Gateway | source (`ocx src -- gateway run`), macOS | base: `nohup &` and plain `&` die at the end of their own call; `background: true` survives chat `/reset` and RPC reset | all 3 survive across turns; chat `/reset` stops all 3; RPC reset stops all 3; Gateway stop stops all 3; 0 relay/anchor processes left |
| 14 | Upgrade: latest stable `2026.11.3` runs on a state dir with `tools.exec.timeoutSeconds: 90`, then this head (`doctor --fix --non-interactive`, as update does) runs on the same state | stable: published npm package; head: source (`ocx src`), macOS | stable reads 90 | head still reads 90 after doctor; a `background: true` call gets a deadline 90 s after its start ("times out in 1m30s"); without a configured timeout, the same call on head has no deadline |
| 15 | Linux: five styles plus a timeout case in `node:24-bookworm` as root, `openclaw agent --local`, Node runtime | dist-nodts, Linux (this head's `dist/` laid over the `2026.11.5-beta.3` install) | published `2026.11.5-beta.2`: 0 of 5 alive | 5 of 5 alive, each answers 20 of 20 requests 10 s after the CLI exits; the timeout case stops both the `setsid` server and the double-fork daemon |

- After the CI fixes: exec, worker runtime, supervisor, relay, anchor, adapters, TUI shell, exec follow-up, process scope and subagent reset suites: 5 shards, 416 passed, 0 failed (macOS); the Linux container run in row 5.

OpenClaw does not see it, so it is not adopted, not capped, and it keeps running after session reset and Gateway stop, as in every other harness compared below. On Linux the subreaper sees it.
- A process that a tracked survivor forks after the hand-off is not tracked separately; stopping the survivor does not stop it.
- Test lines exceed the 400-line allowance by 124; `config/test-lines-allocations/199079-exec-detached-process-ownership.txt` records them. Each added test is a real-process regression for one review finding.
- Adopted services count as live background sessions, so, like `background: true` services, they block a safe Gateway restart until they exit or are stopped.

## How this compares

| Harness | Process left by a completed command | Bound while running | Session reset / new | Host stop | One-shot CLI exit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Codex | Survives; only timeout or Ctrl-C kills the group | No | Session shutdown terminates all its unified-exec processes | Killed with the session | Survives |
| Pi | Survives; only in-flight commands are tracked | No | Kills in-flight commands only | Kills in-flight commands only | Survives |
| OMP | Survives; the shell is kept while background jobs run, reaped every 5 s | 15 running background jobs; over the limit, new jobs fail | `newSession()` cancels the session's own async jobs | Kept shells and their jobs die with the harness | Killed with the harness |
| Hermes | Tracked in a session-scoped process registry | 64 tracked records; prunes only finished ones | Agent close and session end kill the session's processes, except explicitly persisted ones | — | — |
| OpenClaw before | Killed at the end of the call (Linux: daemons too) | — | Killed earlier, at the end of the call | Killed | Killed |
| OpenClaw after | Survives as a tracked background session, reaped every 5 s, named in the result and `process list` | 16 per session, 64 per Gateway; over the limit, new services are refused or stopped, old ones never evicted | Stops in-flight work, `background: true` services and survivors; durable processes stay | Stopped | Handed off and printed (as Codex and Pi) |

In every harness, a process that daemonized itself and was never tracked keeps running.

Sources: Codex `codex-rs/core/src/exec.rs`, `spawn.rs` and `core/src/session/handlers.rs` (`terminate_all_processes`); Pi `packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/bash.ts`; OMP `packages/coding-agent/src/exec/bash-executor.ts` (`RETAIN_REAP_INTERVAL_MS`), `src/async/job-manager.ts` (`DEFAULT_MAX_RUNNING_JOBS = 15`) and `newSession()` (`#cancelOwnAsyncJobs`); Hermes `tools/process_registry.py` (`MAX_PROCESSES = 64`, `kill_all`).

## Follow-ups (PR 2 and later)

- A strict process scope for cron and heartbeat runs, with a tool notice that everything ends with the run.
- A durable PID ledger so services are still owned after a Gateway crash.
- One ownership policy: remove the service-marker and platform predicates and the PTY rejection.
- cgroup and RSS memory budgets for adopted services.
- File-backed stdio for all exec, which removes the drain anchor.
