prs.body:
Fixes #194330 Related: #194338 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: Android shows an unexplained total-refresh warning when model discovery fails but a populated model catalog remains available. ## User Impact User impact: users keep their model choices and see a bounded provider or native-discovery warning when that scope is known, with an honest partial-catalog fallback when it is not. Genuine refresh failures remain visible. ## Why This Change Was Made The catalog attempt owner records provider/native failures, including an unknown scope, but previously published only an aggregate flag. This change derives live `refreshFailures` from that owner, carries the facts through the decision adapter and RPC projection, and updates Android to consume them without changing authentication outcomes or model eligibility. Partial recovery now publishes a status change even while another acquisition remains failed. The public projection omits raw errors, credentials, endpoint/profile-shaped labels, and provider identities outside the requested view. Android honors these sanitized scopes rather than recovering hidden labels from legacy outcomes; legacy fallback labels must be present in the returned catalog. **Related work:** #194338 overlaps the same producer and proposes synthesizing `providerOutcomes`. This is an alternative, not a parallel auth-state fix: it retains ready/auth outcomes, distinguishes native and unknown acquisition scopes, and includes Android handling. Reconcile the two approaches before either is merged. #159670 was also inspected; its catalog-auth retention change is not copied here. ## Evidence ### Maintainer verification — installed Android app, November 15 Both APK and isolated Gateway used the same source in each run: baseline `76b7ed16d6e5fe679dad73c6058a0c7afcf55fe9`, candidate `4260e3c6dbeff43626b4367e2df0d328e8cb54b8`. This is the installed native app on an Android API 36 emulator with a real Gateway and controlled loopback Ollama HTTP responses, not a screenshot runtime or physical phone. A forced discovery HTTP 503 preserves one available model and the exact draft in both runs. The candidate names `ollama` and explains that available models remain selectable; the picker opens with its retained row enabled, and selecting it returns to chat without losing the draft. After restoring the provider, an explicit `models.list refresh:true` performs one discovery GET and one model-detail POST; failure diagnostics and the native warning clear. **Separate inherited issue:** the chat's Refresh action did not trigger model discovery on the baseline: zero new provider requests during an 11.9-second observation, with the generic warning unchanged. Recovery above was triggered through the official RPC/CLI, not that UI action. This PR preserves that existing behavior; the Refresh wiring remains follow-up work. No live provider inference or reproduction of the reporter's exact installation is claimed. Both app builds passed; 13 focused Gateway owner/projection tests passed. Source was unmodified. Task-owned Gateway, provider, emulator and ADB processes were stopped afterward. | Before: generic warning | After: provider-specific warning | | --- | --- | | ![Installed baseline app](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a4ce4aa7-3dbd-4438-b22a-61d957b51810) | ![Installed candidate app](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e2cf82b4-0b24-4d65-b67e-e26f24792c24) | ![Retained enabled model picker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c5924371-1d93-4f71-a39d-86853f49aba3) ![Recovered app with draft preserved](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d4254c0b-2494-44d2-87f1-2737c1816922) ### Native Android rendering evidence — November 10 **Native test-fixture rendering, not installed-device/live-Gateway end-to-end proof.** These inspected Android API 34 native-graphics captures exercise the production ChatScreen → MainViewModel → NodeRuntime → ChatController → models.list path, with an isolated in-memory screenshot runtime and controlled Gateway-response I/O. Both source runs use the same 149 available choices, 412 × 892 mdpi viewport, English locale and light theme.
Before: generic partial-catalog warningAfter: scoped warning and retained choices
**Recovery:** restoring the controlled catalog response and invoking the real ViewModel/controller refresh clears the warning without losing any of the 149 choices. The native model popover was opened and searched; an available retained-model row was verified visible, clickable and enabled while the failure warning was present.

After a verified clean shutdown, candidate `doctor --fix --non-interactive` migrated that state (agent schema 27 → 40). The response excluded the fixture endpoint, key and raw error. This is real isolated Gateway/CLI transport with synthetic provider I/O, not live inference or the reporter’s deployment. Its diagnostics implementation is unchanged on the reconciled base; the full upgrade procedure was not rerun after that mechanical integration. - **Installed-app/real-Gateway qualification:** now completed on the emulator as recorded above; the older failed emulator attempt is superseded. Physical-device and live-inference proof remain outside this run. - **Managed publication recovered:** the supported canonical base refresh succeeded without conflicts and preserved the retained follow-up. The same PR and branch were updated to `4260e3c6dbeff43626b4367e2df0d328e8cb54b8`, still ready for review and not merged. The complete published Git tree matches the validated staged tree (`c2705857112ae46be533b19ab51503ed74b36edb`); all three new task commits carry the required DonnieFi co-author trailer. prs.title: fix(ui): explain transcript retention before deleting sessions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes deletion confirmations that say a session transcript is deleted even though regular sessions retain an archived copy, while other entry points describe the same operation differently.

## User Impact

Before confirming deletion, users see what happens to the selected transcripts: regular transcripts are archived, incognito transcripts are deleted without an archive, and mixed selections explain both outcomes.

Deletion requests, device cleanup, permissions, and retention policies are unchanged. This does not add a restore control or promise permanent archive retention. Incognito wording concerns OpenClaw’s transcript archive, not external-provider retention.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing deletion owner archives regular transcripts and explicitly skips archival for incognito sessions. The sidebar, chat-header operation, Sessions page, selected-session actions, and Delete all archived now use one presentation helper based on the existing incognito flag/key. Two competing selection-specific copy keys are removed. External-session catalog deletion has a different contract and is unchanged.

The existing confirmation remains the committing step. Cancel does not submit deletion, and failed or stale requests retain their existing recovery behavior. No new persistence, confirmation, or state owner was added. Confirmation copy travels with the existing deferred mutation controls rather than the shared startup catalog.

## Evidence

- 108 UI tests and 5 browser scenarios passed on the repaired tree. Five dialog regressions fail before the wording fix for the intended retention distinction, then pass for regular, incognito flag/key, all-incognito, and mixed selections. They also verify no deletion before confirmation or after Cancel. A cold-loading regression fails before the catalog repair and verifies first-use copy, preserved translations, locale, and namespace identity afterward.
- The original 3 focused backend cases use actual storage owners: normal deletion retains a readable archive file; incognito creation/deletion stays process-local with no archive; deleting nonempty memory-owned history removes its retained reset windows. Their owning code is unchanged by the repair. No real user data was deleted.
- The real sidebar flow submits the same deletion request once, then preserves the row and visible recovery on rejection. Existing selection, archived-only, stale-scope, and partial-failure checks remain intact.
- UI typecheck, scoped UI/script lint, formatting, i18n baseline/verification, and diff checks passed. The complete composed English catalog, including key order, is byte-identical before and after relocation. Generated translation memory is untouched.
- The [initial CI performance failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43638803135/job/132582020734) was reproduced with CI's Node 24.22.1, Vite 8.3.5, and Pako 3.0.3. After the repair, the unchanged base-relative performance gate passes against `10159aefda9c77cb1036298f9eb886d92c9c2445`: chat boot gzip is 224 B below base and New Session boot is 236 B below base; their request counts are unchanged. Initial-entry JS is unchanged. The copy shares the existing deferred confirmation chunk. Inherited absolute-budget debt remains; no limits were raised, and this is not a latency claim. Updated remote CI is pending.
- Before: verified main `bb905f76e55de2934e868434ea23c345893cdc6c`. Matched source-served Control UI captures use synthetic session data, light theme, and a 1280×900 viewport. Incognito/mixed images below are supplementary production-dialog fixtures, not live deletion flows. The backend tests, not screenshots, prove retention. The catalog repair changes no wording or rendering, so these verified images are reused.
- Simplification: one 28-line presentation helper replaces competing copy selection across six call sites. A small existing-pattern English registrar keeps confirmation-only copy out of shared startup. Net production growth is 51 lines; test growth is 101 lines; no deletion/storage code changes. Final focused UI checks took 11.02s and the browser file took 33.92s. Original backend runs include cold compilation.

### Sidebar deletion confirmation

Open a session’s sidebar menu, then Advanced → Delete.

After

<details>
<summary>Incognito and mixed selections — production-dialog fixtures</summary>

The actual confirmation component and shared copy selector render these synthetic selections. These images prove presentation only.

![Incognito: transcript deletion without an archive](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e6c0255f-bb82-4099-b695-d9a397a36c2b)

</details>

prs.title: fix(ui): download notices claim completion before browser saving
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Knowledge source downloads and widget HTML exports claiming a file was downloaded when OpenClaw has only handed it to the browser.

## User Impact

The fallback notices now say the download started and direct users to browser downloads to check the result. Knowledge still reports completion when its save-file writer has actually finished. File contents, destinations, permissions, clipboard behavior, and export operations are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Clicking a download link does not tell the page whether the browser saved the file. Both affected flows previously claimed completion even when Chromium explicitly refused the download.

Knowledge already knows whether it has a file writer: that path awaits the final close; the Blob fallback does not have a completion receipt. Its existing control now selects the appropriate outcome wording. Widget HTML fallback copy is corrected at its single presentation key. No new state, confirmation, browser capability, or persistence machinery is introduced.

Related: #195010 internationalizes Knowledge copy, but retains the unconditional “Original file downloaded.” outcome; it does not make this distinction.

## Evidence

- **45 focused tests passed:** 9 Knowledge control/UI cases, 35 widget export/card cases, and one built-Control-UI browser scenario. New Knowledge and widget regressions fail on verified main for the premature completion claims, then pass with the repair.
- **Real browser boundary:** the widget test uses the actual menu and exporter with an older synthetic document lacking the snapshot bridge. After the real timeout and HTML fallback, Chromium reports the download failed because the isolated context refuses downloads. The corrected notice still truthfully describes the handoff, rather than a saved file. There is no chat send.
- **Knowledge boundary:** actual download-control tests distinguish browser handoff from a pending, successful, or rejected file-writer close; canceling the picker fetches nothing. A separate Chromium capture clicks the production evidence component and observes the same browser-side refusal, with one correctly scoped attachment read. Only source bytes and file-writer responses are synthetic; the presentation and download handlers are production code. No live vault, account, printer, message, or job is used.
- Scoped lint, UI typecheck, changed plugin/browser-test typechecks, formatting, i18n baseline/verification, and diff checks pass. Canonical English and existing plugin-owned inline copy are updated; translation memory is untouched. Remote CI is pending.
- Baseline: verified main `a2892e8cd71026b10b2250b243650882acc08670`. Before/After have matched content, light theme, and viewport. Knowledge uses a **production-component fixture**, 1000×580 with an 800×215 evidence crop; this is not a full plugin-route test. The widget uses the **actual built Control UI**, 1280×900 with an 840×175 crop. Both pairs were visually inspected. Browser screenshots alone are not the saving-boundary proof; the separate download failure and writer assertions provide it.
- Simplification: one selection from existing writer state and one catalog string; **net 3 production lines**, 179 focused test lines, and 4 documentation lines. The already-correct completed-writer message remains unchanged.

### Knowledge source evidence

Open Knowledge, select a record, and use **Original file** in its source evidence. The fixture below contains synthetic planning notes. Both captures are after the download handoff; the isolated browser refused to save the file.

Before

After

<details>

In a chat containing an older widget, open **Widget actions → Download as image**. If its snapshot bridge is unavailable, the existing fallback offers the HTML document instead. This behavior is preserved; only the result notice changes.

After

</details>

prs.title: fix: honor current home paths and stabilize process-state tests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Legacy SDK detection could ignore the current `HOME`/`USERPROFILE`, and several regression fixtures depended on runtime-specific behavior for exit codes, replaced cwd functions, or the identity of `process.env`.

## User Impact

Doctor and SDK lookup use the same OS-home selection while keeping `OPENCLAW_HOME` and named-profile isolation intact. The fixture changes preserve their existing behavior checks across Node, the pinned Bun fork, and stock Bun.

## Why This Change Was Made

The four commits separate the mechanisms for review:

- Save and restore an explicit successful exit status, and assert zero while no failure has been recorded.
- Exercise real working directories in fork-based tests; use the existing temporary-directory parent seam for the media thread-worker fixture.
- Resolve the legacy SDK directory through `resolveRequiredOsHomeDir`. The previous call supplied an empty environment, discarding `HOME` and `USERPROFILE` before falling back to `os.homedir()`. Explicit `OPENCLAW_AGENT_DIR=~/.openclaw/agent` expansion also used raw `homedir()` and now uses that same OS-home resolver without changing its existing tilde syntax.
- Use the existing current-environment helpers for telemetry's test guards. The sender has no environment-identity cache: Vitest's stale proxy deleted keys from an old `process.env` after a shared-environment worker, so the sender correctly remained offline.

Runtime references: upstream https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/42607, upstream https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/42601, upstream https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/42599, and upstream https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/44371.

Three SQLite cwd-loss identities remain unchanged and deferred to the upstream path-resolution fix linked above. A real removed-directory probe still reproduces stock's stale `path.resolve` result, and the affected owners have no explicit-base seam. Replacing that boundary with a mock would manufacture the expected result.

## Evidence

| File | IDs kept / deferred | Stock before | Fork after | Stock after | Node after | Revert control | Wall s (Node before → after) |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|---:|
| `src/infra/node-runtime-recovery.shutdown.test.ts` | 10 / 0 | 10 fail | 10 pass | 10 pass | 10 pass | 10 reproduced | 8.0 → 2.8 |
| `src/infra/node-runtime-recovery.test.ts` | 3 / 0 | 3 fail | 3 pass | 3 pass | 3 pass | 3 reproduced | 9.6 → 3.9 |
| `src/infra/unhandled-rejections.fatal-detection.test.ts` | 2 / 0 | 2 fail | 2 pass | 2 pass | 2 pass | 2 reproduced | 4.8 → 2.7 |
| `src/state/openclaw-memory-write-admission.test.ts` | 3 / 0 | 3 fail | 3 pass | 3 pass | 3 pass | 3 reproduced | 191.9 → 50.6 |
| `src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-entry-state.test.ts` | 1 / 0 | 1 fail | 1 pass | 1 pass | 1 pass | 1 reproduced | 75.5 → 35.4 |
| `src/infra/push-apns-store.worker-read.test.ts` | 1 / 0 | 1 fail | 1 pass | 1 pass | 1 pass | 1 reproduced | 10.1 → 2.5 |
| `src/plugins/plugin-cache.test.ts` | 1 / 0 | 1 fail | 1 pass | 1 pass | 1 pass | 1 reproduced | 77.0 → 10.7 |
| `src/media-understanding/attachments.cache.test.ts` | 1 / 0 | 1 fail | 1 pass | 1 pass | 1 pass | 1 reproduced | 77.5 → 9.2 |
| `src/infra/sqlite-readonly-worker.test.ts` | 0 / 3 | 3 fail | baseline pass | unchanged | baseline pass | deferred | 75.7 → — |
| `src/infra/state-migrations.recoverable-legacy-state.test.ts` | 9 / 0 | 9 fail | 9 pass | 9 pass | 9 pass | 9 reproduced | 98.7 → 39.2 |
| `src/infra/state-migrations.caller-mode.storage.test.ts` | 5 / 0 | 5 fail | 5 pass | 5 pass | 5 pass | 5 reproduced | 137.2 → 57.4 |
| `src/infra/update-result-telemetry.test.ts` | 14 / 0 | 14 fail | 14 pass | 14 pass | 14 pass | 14 reproduced | 28.9 → 21.5 |

All 50 retained identities pass on all three runtimes and fail again when only their mechanism is reverted. All 53 original identities fail on Darwin stock at baseline; Linux-only-unverified: none. The OS-home helper/profile sibling run also passes.

Wall times include wrapper startup and generated worker preparation on a shared host. The existing database, SDK, and delivery integration files exercise real owner boundaries; no test cases, sleeps, or retries were added. Baseline runs also exposed unrelated SQLite cancellation/compiler/startup failures and a fork delivery timeout; those paths were not changed.

Focused Node microbenchmarks (five warmed 100,000-call samples) observed median default-profile lookup of 2.11 → 1.87 μs and explicit-tilde directory selection of 3.59 → 4.33 μs. The latter adds roughly 0.74 μs only for a tilde override; ordinary explicit paths do not call the new resolver. These are synthetic call-cost observations, not end-to-end performance claims.

Validation: scoped P2 review with no actionable findings; targeted TypeScript, lint, formatting, test-line budget, and whitespace checks. PR CI supplies the broad proof.

Node proof explicitly selected `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node` (Node v26.12.1). Stock proof used Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+2596ac5d3`; fork proof used the repository-pinned OpenClaw Bun. Earlier unqualified local runs selected the fork and are excluded from Node evidence.

No production `process.exitCode = undefined` reset was found. The telemetry owner has no environment-identity cache; only its test guard deletion required repair.

## What Problem This Solves

The Lobsterdex has pop stars, emperors and inventors, but nobody brings presents.

## User Impact

A new rare visitor, **Santa Claws**, can arrive in the Control UI and be collected in the Lobsterdex as entry #50, right after Alexander Graham Shell. The collection grows from 49 to 50 entries. Saved discoveries, names, first-visit dates and shiny sightings are kept. A finished 49/49 collection loses its golden trim until Santa Claws visits, the same current-catalog rule #159815 used.

## Why This Change Was Made

## What Problem This Solves

The first row on **Settings → Debug** is **Security audit**, and it always reads **Unavailable**. The row reads `status.securityAudit`, but the Gateway `status` method never publishes that field. Only the CLI computes an audit (`openclaw status --deep`, `openclaw security audit`). So no Control UI user could ever see a result there.

## User Impact

Debug now starts with the snapshots people open it for. Nothing that used to work is lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

A permanently unavailable status at the top of a diagnostics page reads like something is broken.

## What stays available

- `openclaw security audit --deep` and `openclaw status --deep` are unchanged.
- No Gateway, protocol or SDK change. Removed: the row component, its CSS, its English copy, its raw-copy baseline entry and tests that fed a field the Gateway never sends.

## Evidence

- Debug unit tests (18), UI typecheck, focused lint, formatting, i18n verification and the controller guard passed.
- Traced `securityAudit` across `src/`: it is only produced by `src/commands/status-*.ts` (CLI), never by `src/gateway/server-methods/health.ts` (`status`).
- Actual Control UI with the mock Gateway, dark theme, 1440×1000.

Closes #199454

Merge after the Clawnadian (#199443), which takes entry #51.

## What Problem This Solves

The Lobsterdex has no lobster from Latin America yet.

## User Impact

User impact: a new rare lobster, the Clawlombian, can visit and fill a 52nd slot in the Lobsterdex. Lobsters already found stay in the dex.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Clawlombian is a coral lobster in a cream sombrero vueltiao with black braided bands and a zigzag hatband. It wears a ruana that opens down the front, banded yellow, blue and red, and shakes a red maraca with yellow and blue bands in its right claw. Before it is found, its card hints "A cumbia beat drifts in on the tide."; once found, it reads "Dances cumbia sideways. Naturally."

It is added the same way as the other character lobsters: a palette entry with weight 1, a shell pattern for the hat and ruana, a right-claw prop for the maraca, the name and lore, and an eye glint in CSS. prs.title: fix: prompt cache misses in group chats when tools.toolsBySender restricts some senders
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/176227

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in a group chat where `tools.toolsBySender` restricts some senders, the system prompt's tool list changes whenever a different member writes. On routes that send the system prompt at the start of every request, such as the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions route used below, the provider prompt cache misses on that turn and the next one. Routes that carry system prompt changes as in-history updates (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167698) instead append a `System prompt update` message with the other sender's `## Tooling` section on every sender change (read from `session-prompt-state.ts`, not run). https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176167 now pins the tool definitions per session, but the system prompt still follows the sender, and a restricted sender's denied call gets a generic `exec is not available in this turn` refusal.

## User Impact

User impact: group sessions with per-sender restrictions on core tools keep one prompt prefix across senders, so cache reads stay high when members take turns. Permissions do not change: a restricted sender still cannot run a denied tool; the model now gets a refusal that names the sender policy. Restricted senders see the definitions and the system prompt entries of tools they cannot call, the same tradeoff https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175309 made for owner-only tools. Main already sends those definitions to a restricted sender through the pin of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176167 (Before, req#2: bob's request carries all 13 tools); this PR adds their system prompt entries and the sender-specific refusal.

## Why This Change Was Made

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175309 set the invariant: within a session, tool definitions and the system prompt depend only on session and config facts, and per-turn authority is checked when a tool runs. Global and per-agent `tools.toolsBySender` is per-turn authority (it follows the sender of each message) but still filtered the tools a turn is assembled from. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176167 keeps the request's tool block stable by pinning it per session, but the system prompt's `## Tooling` section is still built from the sender-filtered tools. Building `## Tooling` from that pinned list instead would not be enough: the pin exists only in the embedded runner, it starts from the first speaker (a restricted first speaker still costs a miss when an unrestricted sender extends it), and a pinned tool the turn did not build gets the generic refusal.

- The session surface now leaves out the sender policy, as it already leaves out a completion handoff's replayed policy. The turn surface keeps it.
- `resolveTurnToolSurface` gates the calls the sender may not make, with a refusal that names `tools.toolsBySender`.
- On a worker placement, a gated tool now runs at the Gateway, which returns the refusal, so the worker gets no launch authority for it. Before, a gated core tool kept its placement location, and the worker ran its own implementation. Main's completion-handoff gate had the same gap, since a handoff turn already offers the session surface; the same binding covers it.
- Descendant snapshots, cron-creator capture and session-event allowlists still use the sender-filtered turn tools, so children inherit the same restriction as before.

This change is limited to global and per-agent `tools.toolsBySender`. Group-level `channels.<channel>.groups.*.toolsBySender` entries live inside the group policy, whose session surface can be wider than the group default, so they keep filtering.

Codex harness: a sender restriction already turns native tools off for the turn and runs it on a transient thread, decided from the policy pipeline, not the tool list. A gated `exec` definition does not enable the native shell.

## Evidence

After re-ran on 2026-11-06 at `bf21918cf0d` (this branch merged with `upstream/main` `195efadb713`, plus the worker-placement binding) with Node 24.22.1. Before ran on 2026-10-22 against `d238c0e5ce7`; later merges change only this branch, so Before was not repeated.

Real Gateway (each side's build, `openclaw gateway run`, Ubuntu 22.04) with an isolated home and state in a loopback-only network namespace. Faked: a local IRC server with `#team` and two IRC users, and a local OpenAI-compatible provider that records each request body and answers a message containing `RUN_EXEC` with one `exec` tool call. Config: the documented example, `"id:alice!alice@127.0.0.1": {}` and `"*": { deny: [exec, process, write, edit, apply_patch] }`. Messages in one session: alice, bob, alice, bob, alice `RUN_EXEC`, bob `RUN_EXEC`.

Before (`upstream/main` `d238c0e5ce7`): every request carries the same 13 tool definitions (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176167), but on every sender change the system prompt splits at character 22,557 of 55,643. Its `## Tooling` list has 13 entries for alice and 8 for bob. Only 23,065 bytes of the previous request's messages are shared. alice's `exec` runs; bob's returns `exec is not available in this turn. Do not retry exec.`

After (this PR at `bf21918cf0d`): all 8 requests carry the same 14 tools and the same 54,673-character system prompt, and each request's messages extend the previous one. alice's `exec` runs; bob's returns `exec is not allowed for the sender of this message (tools.toolsBySender). Do not retry exec.` Main now offers 14 tools and a different system prompt in this setup; the earlier After runs at `a486c34dc3f` (13 tools, 55,643 characters) and `1e9d792086f` (14 tools, 54,110 characters) gave the same result. This setup has no worker placement; for the worker path, the tests below check that every gated tool runs at the Gateway, and a launch-authority run below shows the worker gets no grant for it.

<details>
<summary>Before: provider requests on main</summary>

```text
req#1 alice tools=13 toolsHash=00c5aaec80fa systemChars=55643 messages=3
req#2 bob   tools=13 toolsHash=00c5aaec80fa systemChars=54811 messages=6 | vs prev: toolsIdentical=true systemIdentical=false systemSplitAt=22557/55643 prevMessagesPrefix=false sharedMessageBytes=23065/58358
req#3 alice tools=13 toolsHash=00c5aaec80fa systemChars=55643 messages=9 | vs prev: toolsIdentical=true systemIdentical=false systemSplitAt=22557/54811 prevMessagesPrefix=false sharedMessageBytes=23065/58714
req#4 bob   tools=13 toolsHash=00c5aaec80fa systemChars=54811 messages=12 | vs prev: toolsIdentical=true systemIdentical=false systemSplitAt=22557/55643 prevMessagesPrefix=false sharedMessageBytes=23065/61044
req#5 alice tools=13 toolsHash=00c5aaec80fa systemChars=55643 messages=15 | vs prev: toolsIdentical=true systemIdentical=false systemSplitAt=22557/54811 prevMessagesPrefix=false sharedMessageBytes=23065/61398
req#6 alice tools=13 toolsHash=00c5aaec80fa systemChars=55643 messages=17 | vs prev: toolsIdentical=true systemIdentical=true prevMessagesPrefix=true sharedMessageBytes=63725/63725
req#7 bob   tools=13 toolsHash=00c5aaec80fa systemChars=54811 messages=20 | vs prev: toolsIdentical=true systemIdentical=false systemSplitAt=22557/55643 prevMessagesPrefix=false sharedMessageBytes=23065/63954
req#8 bob   tools=13 toolsHash=00c5aaec80fa systemChars=54811 messages=22 | vs prev: toolsIdentical=true systemIdentical=true prevMessagesPrefix=true sharedMessageBytes=64313/64313
exec result in req#6 (alice): "proof-exec-ran"
exec result in req#8 (bob): "exec is not available in this turn. Do not retry exec."
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>After: provider requests with this PR</summary>

```text
req#1 alice tools=14 toolsHash=432fab32da0d systemChars=54673 messages=3
req#2 bob   tools=14 toolsHash=432fab32da0d systemChars=54673 messages=6 | vs prev: toolsIdentical=true systemIdentical=true prevMessagesPrefix=true sharedMessageBytes=59926/59926
req#3 alice tools=14 toolsHash=432fab32da0d systemChars=54673 messages=9 | vs prev: toolsIdentical=true systemIdentical=true prevMessagesPrefix=true sharedMessageBytes=63957/63957
req#4 bob   tools=14 toolsHash=432fab32da0d systemChars=54673 messages=12 | vs prev: toolsIdentical=true systemIdentical=true prevMessagesPrefix=true sharedMessageBytes=68008/68008
req#5 alice tools=14 toolsHash=432fab32da0d systemChars=54673 messages=15 | vs prev: toolsIdentical=true systemIdentical=true prevMessagesPrefix=true sharedMessageBytes=72037/72037
req#6 alice tools=14 toolsHash=432fab32da0d systemChars=54673 messages=17 | vs prev: toolsIdentical=true systemIdentical=true prevMessagesPrefix=true sharedMessageBytes=76085/76085
req#7 bob   tools=14 toolsHash=432fab32da0d systemChars=54673 messages=20 | vs prev: toolsIdentical=true systemIdentical=true prevMessagesPrefix=true sharedMessageBytes=76314/76314
req#8 bob   tools=14 toolsHash=432fab32da0d systemChars=54673 messages=22 | vs prev: toolsIdentical=true systemIdentical=true prevMessagesPrefix=true sharedMessageBytes=80348/80348
exec result in req#6 (alice): "proof-exec-ran"
exec result in req#8 (bob): "exec is not allowed for the sender of this message (tools.toolsBySender). Do not retry exec."
```

</details>

Observed result: on main each sender change still keeps under 40% of the prefix (the system prompt differs from the tooling section on); with this PR every request extends the previous one. The original run on `847f7fade0d`, before https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176167, also showed the tool list itself changing (14 tools for alice, 9 for bob).

Tests: `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts` gains a `tools.toolsBySender` case (two senders of one group session get identical `{name, description, parameters}`; the denied sender's `write` call returns the gated refusal). Five existing sender-policy assertions changed from "tool absent" to "tool present and gated", including the requester-origin case from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/157806. A before/after test run (base `f7d9d711f86`, head `1e9d792086f`) reports all six fail on the base and pass here, with 96 guard tests passing on both; two of the six fail on the base partly because they import a new test helper, and their assertions fail there as well. Since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159863, the `sessions_spawn` description tells a sender-restricted requester that it may start only hidden helpers of the same agent, and spawn admission enforces that. The new case therefore compares every definition except that one description; the docs note it. The shared gated-tool assertion now also checks that a gated tool runs at the Gateway; without the placement binding, four sender cases fail with `expected 'placement' to be 'gateway'`. A launch-authority case in `worker-turn-execution.test.ts` (a restricted sender on a worker placement) also failed without the binding (edit, write, exec, apply_patch and process were granted) and passed with it, as did a completion-handoff variant. Neither is committed: that file is at its 1,000-line cap.

Merge with `upstream/main` `885e57e9f9d`: main renamed `isSchedulerSystemTurn` to `isHostSystemTurn` and now checks a missing turn tool before scheduler reads and owner-only, so the sender refusal sits inside main's missing-turn-tool branch next to the completion-handoff refusal. `scheduled-message-invocation.ts` keeps main's `sessionInheritedToolPolicy` line and the PR's sender-free session scope under one comment. Main removed the `resolveEffectiveToolPolicy` tests from `agent-tools-agent-config.test.ts`, so the sender case there now uses main's helpers. `agent-tools.ts` imports the turn-authority module as a namespace to stay within its 700-line limit. A second merge with `upstream/main` `eb370ce6113` (2026-11-04) had no conflicts; main had grown `agent-tools.ts` to its limit, so `completeTurnTools` now takes the policy filter's arguments, which keeps both calls on one line each. A third merge with `upstream/main` `195efadb713` (2026-11-06) conflicted only where main's https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193098 added `ownerToolCurrentAssertion` to `resolveTurnToolSurface`; both changes are kept, and this branch's patches are unchanged apart from line offsets.

Test lines: the tests add 68 net lines (+112/−44). `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` failed on `1e9d792086f` because main was then over its test-line ceiling and this branch adds lines. Two refusal checks now reuse the shared `expectSenderGated` helper instead of repeating its loop, and `config/test-lines-allocations/tools-by-sender-prefix-stability.txt` allocates exactly the 68 net lines for the regression tests above.

Checks at `bf21918cf0d` (this branch merged with `upstream/main` `195efadb713`, plus the worker-placement binding): `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base 195efadb713` passes (6,513,201 lines, ceiling 6,513,230), also with `--no-merge-base` as CI runs it. Every test file that uses the shared gated-tool assertion, plus turn-authority, retained-owner, scheduled-message-invocation, agent-tool-availability and worker-turn-execution, passes: 11 files, 213 tests. A before/after test run (base `195efadb713`) reports the six regression tests fail on the base and pass here, with 96 guard tests passing on both. `pnpm check:changed` passes typecheck, lint, import cycles and the other guards. Its four reds: the line-cap guard's `agent-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts` at 1,166 counted lines (up 1 from main's 1,165; CI reports it as advisory), a changelog attribution and a dead export in main's files, and formatting of local scratch files outside the commit.

Checks at `1e9d792086f` (pnpm 12.15.0, dependencies installed from the lockfile): the touched tests (times below), `tsgo` on the core project and on every `src` test shard, oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files, and `pnpm check:changed` (typecheck, lint, import cycles and the other guards passed; its three reds are pre-existing and name only files outside this branch's diff). The 37 test files that import a module the merge resolution touched (turn-authority, conversation-capability-profile, session-prompt-state, requester-tool-policy, scheduled-message-invocation, subagent-target-policy and the `agent-tools.*` suites; 449 passed, 6 skipped) ran at `7d8f792ad5b`; the last commit only changes how `agent-tools.ts` imports the turn-authority module and how one test builds its comparison. The docs commit passed the pre-commit hook. The broad suites run in this PR's CI. Since `1e9d792086f` the changes are the `upstream/main` merges, the test tidy-up, the behavior-neutral `completeTurnTools` change and the worker-placement binding.

| Test file | `--maxWorkers=1` wall | CI seconds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts` | 91.63 s (15 tests) | 3.14 s of test time in `agentic-agents-core-tools` (35 files, Vitest 102.24 s), CI run 39811712060 |
| `src/agents/agent-tools-agent-config.test.ts` | 37.72 s (16 tests) | 8.52 s of test time in `agentic-agents-core-tools` (35 files, Vitest 102.24 s), CI run 39811712060 |
| `src/agents/agent-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts` | 107.94 s (46 tests) | 6.08 s of test time in `core-runtime-infra-storage-state-hosted-8` (3 files, Vitest 35.37 s), CI run 39811712060 |
| `src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-tool-authority.test.ts` | 26.20 s (25 tests) | 0.49 s of test time in `agentic-gateway-core-1-hosted-2` (1 file, Vitest 51.19 s), CI run 39811712060 |

Wall times are from `1e9d792086f` on a shared host with a load average of 19 to 31, mostly transform time; at `899e6eb9206` on a quieter host they were 12.30 s, 13.66 s, 14.19 s and 12.77 s. CI seconds come from the CI run on the pre-merge head `899e6eb9206`.

Simplify pass: one decision (`resolveTurnNarrowing`) now names the per-turn policy that narrows the session surface, replacing the inline completion-handoff check in tool assembly; no new state, wrapper or option. Behavior still protected: owner-only gating, completion-handoff gating, scheduler automation reads, and descendant inheritance of sender restrictions. Delta against the merge base: production +50/−17 in 3 files, tests +112/−44 in 5 files, docs +9, one 3-line test-line allocation record.

Not covered: no real provider, so the cache-read percentage itself was not measured; the evidence is the request-prefix comparison. Group-level `toolsBySender` keeps the old behavior (see above), and so do plugin tools a sender entry denies: plugin construction drops them before the session surface is built, so their definitions still change by sender. CLI backends that get Gateway tools through the loopback MCP bridge also keep filtering by sender (`src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts`, the run-bound catalog); this PR leaves that path unchanged. The docs list these cases. Accepted edge case: a sender policy that denies `process` but allows `exec` still changes `exec`'s description and parameters for that sender, because both depend on whether `process` is callable. Likewise, a sender entry that restricts any tool changes the `sessions_spawn` description for that sender (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159863); in the embedded runner the per-session pin keeps the tool block itself unchanged, and `sessions_spawn` was not offered in the run above. For the Codex harness, owner and restricted-sender turns still use different tool sets by design (native tools on versus off), so this PR does not change Codex cache reuse across those senders.

prs.title: fix(ui): avoid no-match claims before people search is ready
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Assign to… says no people or agents match a search while the people directory is still loading or has failed to load.

## User Impact

User impact: the picker no longer tells users a teammate is missing before it can check. Desktop and phone retain the existing loading state, real error and Retry action; genuine searches with no matches still say so once the directory is available.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared picker checked its filtered rows without checking the directory’s existing loading and error facts. The same one-line condition now governs both desktop menus and the phone sheet. Known owners and agents, search behavior, assignment permissions and request ownership are unchanged. No new state, loader or recovery control is added.

## Evidence

Actual Control UI with a synthetic Gateway, light theme, at 1280×900 and an emulated 390×900 phone viewport. Before is isolated pinned main; after is the same baseline plus this fix. Red rectangles identify the premature no-match claim and the retained loading state. Images are cropped from the actual captures.

**Before — a pending search incorrectly reports no matches.**

![Before: desktop assignment reports no matches while loading the people directory](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05afbee3-9ee0-4ae3-8b3e-6ecb1700b58b)

**After — the existing loading state is sufficient.**

![After: desktop assignment waits for the people directory](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/36139fbf-2208-4117-82ae-ecb20071541e)

<details>
<summary>Phone sheet</summary>

**Before**

prs.title: fix: reduce Gateway stalls under filesystem pressure
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Synchronous pathname lookups in Gateway requests and timers turn a host I/O stall into a Gateway-wide pause. This change removes redundant polling and moves necessary filesystem work through existing async/worker owners. Session reads, locks, skills and credential paths carry prepared owner facts forward while preserving physical replacement checks, mutual exclusion, FIFO, current authority and accepted-work settlement. No new config option or lane-owned SQLite schema change is introduced.

The main reconciliation preserves RomneyDa's cold Talk reentrancy repair, adopts the shared session-reader owner and repairs two incoming #198194 regressions: usage refresh now prepares physical identity asynchronously, and pressure retirement records the idle timestamp for burst workers whose own idle timer is disabled. The latter applies to a timed primary pool; ordinary pools with a disabled primary timer keep their existing lifecycle owner.

## Measured result and limits

On packaged source **`097dad72`**, a synthetic Linux/btrfs fixture with a 35 GiB agent DB, about 5,000 sessions and 62,000 workspace files measured **39,322 → 62 selected main-thread filesystem syscalls per 60 seconds (99.84% reduction)**. The sole fully covered baseline and five fully covered candidate windows completed the workload; intercepted main-thread synchronous filesystem APIs changed **14,157 in 60.048 seconds → 0 in each candidate window**. The workload completed 35 turns and 70 provider requests.

All 62 remaining calls are Node's native `/proc/self/stat` RSS opens: real main-thread I/O outside the API spy. Cold paths outside the workload and retained artifact-cleanup source/identity guards are not proven clear. Worker I/O is outside these totals. The original 8-GiB fixture, accumulated state and A/A controls remain pinned; subsequent owner fixes and larger build-VM resources are not relabeled measurements. Unaffected owner measurements are reused, with affected correctness/work-count proofs rerun. No final-tree CPU/allocation equivalence, all-runtime-zero or outage-immunity claim is made.

<details>
<summary>Adverse costs, A/A controls and measurement limitations</summary>

Moving work off the main thread increases some total costs. These adverse results are retained:

| Actual 097 owner workload | Before → after / paired change |
| --- | --- |
| CPU sampler, five A1/B/A2 timing and allocation triplets | Process CPU 11.944/12.140 → 116.300 µs/sample; main CPU 9.969/10.132 → 66.227 µs; sampled main allocation 3.41/3.48 → 11.88 KB. Paired process CPU +871.70%, allocation +244.61%. At the existing active schedule, B projects 6.978 ms process CPU and 0.713 MB sampled allocation/minute; this is arithmetic, not a measured minute. |
| Four-file warm bootstrap, small/large fixtures | Main synchronous API calls 44 → 0/turn. Total CPU +163.29%/+246.74%, median latency +76.82%/+179.74%, total V8 heap allocation +331.44%/+1465.52%. B rereads 16 KiB/2 MiB per turn after removal of the content cache. |
| Source-mode bootstrap cold start | About 3–5 ms → 903/942 ms, including construction/import of two actual workers. One cold main-thread `realpathSync` resolves the TypeScript loader; ordinary packaged worker URLs do not take that branch. This is not a packaged Gateway startup measurement. |
| Other retained owner costs | Cold skills wall 1,048 → 1,446 ms, CPU 1,074 → 1,297 ms; detached transcript +0.54–0.65 ms and +41–43 KB sampled allocation/read; three-artifact cleanup wall 6.578 → 246.209 ms and isolate allocation 1.008 → 118.113 MB. |

All 94 CPU/bootstrap rows completed with their A/A controls. CPU controls drifted only about 0.7–2%; the owner increases are not dismissed as noise. Main allocation sampling, exact cross-isolate V8 allocation and OS-returned bytes are different measurements, not interchangeable totals.

Untraced Gateway B versus A2 showed main CPU +3.76%, process CPU +4.09%, main allocation −4.08%, median turn latency +6.49%, p95 −35.13% and process-tree RSS +11.10%. However, original A/A already drifted +25.51%/+30.86% in main/process CPU, and incoming schema/build changes, request bytes, cumulative state and a VM reboot differ. **No causal whole-Gateway CPU, allocation or latency improvement is claimed.** Auxiliary RSS observers exited 137 without completion markers, with final sampling gaps of 2.036/1.441 seconds; complete RSS coverage is not claimed. Kernel/API coverage and primary completion remain qualified.

</details>

## Evidence

**Published head: `4b4f6e812e81e9e9a625cc72629de682717aec84`; tree: `eb513481fdd9a9b42390cd066824d9271eb5ff0e`.** Its ordered parents are `a985b752e155ae88a422548f1bdd3f59d6d926f0` and main `55430c2797d8e3dacc202e1a5bdbd3cc8bd3ce2c`. The normal push is verified and GitHub reports the PR mergeable. Both RomneyDa commits remain preserved. The PR is not merged. The full changed-check passes all stages (891.995 seconds), and the integration has a clean scoped Codex review. The new artifact build is running; fresh/base/startup compatibility, exact-head CI and final-head ClawSweeper zero-open remain pending.

The only manual conflict resolution combines upstream's last cached user-footer locator with this lane's visible-pane selector and both font-readiness waits. The incoming DB maintenance keeps the existing writer, admission and settlement owners; it does not introduce main-thread filesystem/SQL work. Its new periodic worker statistics and jitter costs are outside the pinned short measurement windows above. Those measurements are not relabeled or extrapolated to this new behavior.

| Latest scope | Result and boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Published main integration | Both original chat/dashboard browser cases pass (25.587 seconds). Ten DB admission/idle/reclamation cases and 14 CLI cases pass together (65.189 seconds). Scoped Codex P0–P2 review completes with zero findings (79.104 seconds). The full changed-check passes all stages (891.995 seconds). |
| Workspace FIFO repair in a985 | The existing store-write queue now owns admission before awaited filesystem preparation and retains it through worker commit and final host authority. The 43-case owner proof and three focused cases pass; scoped review is clean. A worker-only queue admitted callers too late. No second queue owner or polling is added. |
| Process cleanup and late-PID stop repair in a985 | Cleanup settlement is attached on all cancellation paths, and explicit stop intent survives PID arrival independently of inherited cancellation. The two real Linux scope/caller cases pass, followed by all 35 process cases with two platform skips. |
| Announcement repair in a985 | Three pre-fix regressions and the decisive lost-wake trace expose a descendant-settlement wake overwritten by the parent's deferred-state write. After that write, the existing prepared reader rechecks descendants before the existing resume operation, preserving current authority. All nine owner cases and 14 lifecycle cases pass. No stored flag, timer or polling is added. The original exact-main case passed separately; that NONREPRO is not a causal-introducer claim. |
| Font-readiness fixture repair in a985 | Both original UI cases pass with unchanged geometry assertions and per-frame probes. The first controlled diagnostic intercepted no requests and is not an intervention. The corrected diagnostic measured loaded → fallback → loaded footer heights of 40.5 → 41.734375 → 40.5 px and failed the exact assertion. This is the inverse of the historical CI drift, not proof of its exact cause or a same-injection red/green pair. |
| a985 review and static follow-through | The nine-file repair review is clean. Its full changed-check fails only the 702-line exec-owner cap and the same core-lint diagnostic; other stages pass. Removing the unused fulfillment callback saves three lines, brings the owner to 699, and preserves rejection observation and cleanup settlement. All 35 process cases, formatting, core types, cap and exact lint then pass. A fresh scoped Codex review of the final repair is clean. Raw failed checks remain failed. |

Earlier proofs below retain their original source scopes and failures. The 6e711 integration awaited the existing async refresh-lock factory in the incoming usage benchmark before using its owner; preparation stays outside measured loops, with no new owner, cache or production LOC.

| Prior source scope | Retained result |
| --- | --- |
| 6e711 benchmark integration | Script types pass; five partition cases and two admission cases pass. The direct tiny benchmark completes all three scenarios with its existing log-append warnings retained. This is adapter regression smoke, not a new performance campaign or performance claim. |
| 6e711 review/check | The one-await correction has a clean Codex P0–P2 review (zero findings). The targeted changed-check passes after 250.193 seconds. Prior review/source bridges retain their actual scopes. |
| ACP repair | A single access-scope flag excludes active run-ownership fields while retaining membership, lifecycle, control-owner and policy checks. The controlled regression fails before the fix while both negative controls pass; the complete control-owner and memory-sibling files pass 13 cases, and the original ACP product case passes. This does not rewrite the failed bf740 CI record. |
| Test repairs | Startup trace: all 27 cases pass with controlled nonzero worker census. UI: the two original cases pass with visible-pane selectors and unchanged geometry assertions/deadlines. The original CI zero-geometry cause remains unexplained. |
| Prior ACP/allocation review/check | Fresh Codex P0–P2 review is scoped-clean with zero findings for the five-path runtime/test delta. Its changed-check passed after 451.644 seconds. The allocation-only follow-through has its own clean review and passing native test-budget check: 13,087 = 12,687 credit + 400. |
| Usage refresh | Before-fix guard: two synchronous stats and one native realpath. After: zero; 37 owner tests pass. This is one-refresh API counting, not another per-minute census. |
| Pressure retirement | Exact-main regression fails at burst termination; corrected full owned-pool file passes 23/23. Runtime reorder has zero net production LOC. |
| Integration | On prior frozen f186: session 35, Talk 14, automatic 25, workspace/credential/storage 28 and membership 4 qualify. They retain their original source boundaries. |
| Prior UI boundary | Both browser cases and actual real-Gateway case pass on corrected 4e209; retain that source label and narrow three-case scope. |
| Static checks | Historical full run: 37 stages pass, three fail, with exact-eb1 baseline attribution retained. Resource absorption passes 36 narrow stages; measurement-script correction passes 20/20. The 1af0 integration check failed only two reports of the same exec-owner 703-line cap. The five-line absorption is applied; final cap ratchet, formatting, exact lint and core types all pass. Raw failed runs remain failed. |
| Prior integration review | Complete 72-path integration review: two of two passes, zero findings, scoped-clean, native exit 0 and physical join (92.972 seconds). Prior full-PR review and its dispositions retain their original scope/status; the explicit coverage bridge is described below. |
| 1af0 staging integration | All 12 selected cases pass: token/shared custody and competing reclaimer, snapshot identity/live child, backup lifecycle. Original assertions/deadlines and 16 source/policy pins remain unchanged. |
| Exec integration and final delta | The reviewed integration passes 26 requester/background cases with source pins. The final mechanical exec simplification separately passes seven affected runtime/cancellation cases, plus native cap/format/lint/type checks. Prior broader results retain their original tree labels. |
| CLI native failure | Integrated 14: 13 pass, one native JIT startup trap. The sole failed case passes unchanged on the same pinned binary. NONREPRO, unknown trigger; no runtime fix or blanket green claim. |

Review coverage for published bf740 is explicit: the prior full-PR review covered 963 paths at tree 4e209 and retains its raw “findings” result. Its two findings were resolved by the exact two-reference measurement-script correction, proved through original CLI red/green and 20 passing native check stages, and the source-proven Talk false positive. The producer already observes the exact preparation promise; no redundant consumer catch was added. Published 992e has that repaired tree 8dae. The new two-pass review independently covers the entire subsequent 72-path integration to 1af0, with unchanged source/index/context hashes and zero unresolved accepted findings. Neither review is relabeled as inspecting a different tree. An independent final source bridge verifies that only the exec owner changes from reviewed 1af0 to committed 7d6458: direct lifecycle preparation replaces a forwarding closure and callback alias, while expression-style cancellation preserves the same void effect. Final seven-case proof and native checks qualify that mechanical delta; no new whole-PR engine review is claimed for it. The script regression proof is not a new performance campaign, speed comparison or LOC change.

The 33 cap violations and four SDK budget violations were reproduced and attributed on exact eb1. That is historical baseline qualification, not a waiver for main 5025 or a different final CI parent. Incoming package/patch metadata expands lint scope and exposes the existing violations. The original full check also exposed the lane-owned resource declaration growth; deriving its methods from the existing reader factory removes 23 duplicate type lines without adding an owner or runtime wrapper.

Earlier mutual-exclusion proof includes real competing processes. ## Artifact, compatibility and remaining gates

Neither the old package nor a startup source bridge qualifies that changed compressor. Build the exact successor full-DTS package and run fresh-install, latest-stable base and historical Projects-startup roles against it. No new artifact or compatibility completion is claimed here.

The completed **6e711** Linux package produced 404 declarations; its tarball is 114,222,477 bytes, SHA256 `cbd65752aaf2394549c4fd412adddc2fa84d3476f24129c401f6568226d9cdc0`. Its tarball is 114,223,285 bytes, SHA256 `0470de39f7584115a44bd57b8e471efb56450fb2f2f469dde2f2ee65d89de518`. Both native Doctor roles independently matched all **18,464 installed immutable files** and exact build metadata to that artifact with **zero source overlays**.

The historical upgrade from then-current stable `2026.11.3` passed **49 phases**, including automatic migration, Doctor, preservation, health/readiness 200 and working Gateway RPC. The historical `2026.9.4` Projects startup scenario passed **35 phases**: two healthy starts and clean stops, with explicit Doctor workspace repair between them. Six snapshots preserve both session rows, four transcript rows and their timestamps, four sentinel files and shared project/worktree rows. Only the existing nullable GC default and Doctor's expected canonical-workspace field differ. First startup leaves state unchanged; the second cycle exactly preserves post-Doctor agent/shared state. [Published bf740 CI run 43663138872](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43663138872), attempt 1, is terminal: **179 jobs, 149 successful, seven failed and 23 skipped**. ## Size, ownership and credit

Against exact main `55430c2797d8e3dacc202e1a5bdbd3cc8bd3ce2c`, production is **+8,781 lines** (+16,845/−8,064 across 498 production paths); including fifteen previously merged prerequisites (+1,696), the full lane is **+10,477**. **Net≤0 remains unmet.** Broad tests/helpers are **+13,429** across 417 paths and other/tooling **+4,896** across 55 paths, for 970 compared paths. prs.title: fix(agents): after_tool_call cannot tell a refused tool call from one that ran and failed
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a model on the Claude CLI runtime names a tool that was never offered to the run, the CLI refuses the call itself and nothing is dispatched. The Gateway still fires `after_tool_call` for that name, and the event is indistinguishable from a tool that ran and failed. This is the payload a plugin received on a production Gateway when a model called `mcp__invoke`, a name that does not exist:

```
after_tool_call {
  toolName:   "mcp__invoke"
  params:     {}
  result:     "<tool_use_error>Error: No such tool available: mcp__invoke</tool_use_error>"
  error:      "CLI tool execution failed"
}
```

`error` is the same constant a real failed tool carries, and the only text that says "no such tool" sits inside `result`, which is content a real tool can produce verbatim. A plugin that treats tool results as content therefore has two bad choices: treat the refusal as output from an unknown tool, or parse `result` and let any tool forge the exemption.

On our Gateway the first choice took sessions down. A taint-tracking plugin labelled the output of the unknown tool `mcp__invoke` as untrusted, and from then on refused every sensitive tool in that session (`exec`, `edit`, `write`, `sessions_spawn`, `process`) for a call that never ran. Two long-running coordinator sessions were lost this way in one evening.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only the host knows what a run was offered, so the host has to say so. This adds one optional field to the `after_tool_call` event, `rejected?: boolean`, and sets it in exactly one place, from registry membership:

- `resolveCliRunOfferedToolNames` (`src/agents/cli-runner/tool-policy.ts`) returns the run's exact offered set only when it is known to be complete: a run with an explicit tool-availability cap on the `claude-cli` backend, which enforces the cap through execution arguments (`--tools`, `--allowedTools mcp__openclaw__*`, `--strict-mcp-config`). It returns `undefined` for an uncapped run and for every other backend.
- `src/agents/cli-runner/execute-events.ts` sets `rejected: true` only for a client `tool_use` call, the kind the CLI dispatches or refuses itself, whose name is not in that set. Tools the provider or a connector runs (`server_tool_use`, `mcp_tool_use`) and results whose start was never seen get no claim. Offered and called names are compared by canonical name (`normalizeCliToolName`), so an offered tool reported under another spelling, such as `WebSearch` arriving as `web_search`, is never read as unoffered. The call site already excludes Gateway-mediated `mcp__openclaw__*` tools, which report through their own path.
- `src/agents/harness/hook-helpers.ts` forwards the field; `src/plugins/hook-after-tool-call.types.ts` declares it; `docs/plugins/hooks/tool-policy.md` documents it.

The flag is never derived from `isError`, from `error`, or from text inside `result`. When the offered set is unknown the field is omitted, so an absent field means "unknown", not "the call ran". The bias is deliberate: a name wrongly believed offered only loses the claim, while a name wrongly believed unoffered would exempt a call that really ran.

The event type moved from `hook-types.ts` into a sibling `hook-after-tool-call.types.ts` (re-exported unchanged) because `hook-types.ts` is over its line cap and may not grow.

Not changed: no existing field's value or meaning, no policy decision, no behavior for runtimes other than a capped `claude-cli` run. Codex and embedded runs do not set the field.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can skip a call that never ran instead of guessing from error text. For operators running a plugin that classifies tool output, a model's mistyped tool name no longer counts as output from an unknown tool, so one typo no longer disables a session's tools. Plugins that do not read the field see no change.

## Evidence

**Tested head: `2523ab301283c6147efec82e6151376ed35451c4`.** Three commits: `f32c6ad4b79` (the change and its tests), `364934bca53` (moves the event type into the sibling module; no behavior change) and `2523ab30128` (review fix: the claim is limited to client calls and compared by canonical name).

### Production Gateway, before and after

Both captures are from the journal of a long-running Gateway (systemd service, built `dist`), with real Claude CLI turns and a third-party taint-tracking plugin subscribed to `after_tool_call`. Session ids are truncated by the plugin's own logger; nothing else is edited.

**Before** (2026-11-12 19:22 MST, build without this change). The model calls `mcp__invoke`; the plugin receives the payload shown above and escalates; the session's tools are refused for the rest of the turn:

```
19:22:56.499 [provenance:7b20ad76-4300-4c]   TOOL_TAINT_ESCALATION: trusted → untrusted caused by: mcp__invoke(untrusted)
19:23:01.733 [provenance:7b20ad76-4300-4c] 🛑 BLOCKED at execution layer (real-time re-eval): exec | taint: untrusted
19:23:31.699 [provenance:7b20ad76-4300-4c] 🛑 BLOCKED at execution layer (real-time re-eval): exec | taint: untrusted
19:24:09.958 [provenance:7b20ad76-4300-4c] 🛑 BLOCKED at execution layer (real-time re-eval): edit | taint: untrusted
19:24:14.981 [provenance:7b20ad76-4300-4c] 🛑 BLOCKED at execution layer (real-time re-eval): write | taint: untrusted
19:25:07.546 [provenance:7b20ad76-4300-4c] 🛑 BLOCKED at execution layer (real-time re-eval): sessions_spawn | taint: untrusted
19:25:22.709 [provenance:7b20ad76-4300-4c] 🛑 BLOCKED at execution layer (real-time re-eval): process | taint: untrusted
19:25:50.749 [provenance:7b20ad76-4300-4c]   Final taint: untrusted
19:25:50.749 [provenance:7b20ad76-4300-4c]   External sources: mcp__invoke
```

**After** (same host, Gateway restarted 22:26 MST the same evening on a build containing this change). Five minutes later a model made the same mistake with the same name:

```
22:31:00.187 [provenance:c179b0dc-20d5-46]   TAINT_AT_START: trusted
22:31:10.005 [provenance:c179b0dc-20d5-46]   REJECTED_CALL_NO_TAINT: mcp__invoke — the harness refused the call; nothing ran, so nothing is tainted
22:31:11.920 [provenance:c179b0dc-20d5-46]   TOOL_TAINT_EVAL: tool_search(trusted) → taint unchanged at trusted
22:31:14.812 [provenance:c179b0dc-20d5-46]   TOOL_TAINT_EVAL: exec(trusted) → taint unchanged at trusted
22:31:17.263 [provenance:c179b0dc-20d5-46]   TOOL_TAINT_EVAL: exec(trusted) → taint unchanged at trusted
22:31:19.593 [provenance:c179b0dc-20d5-46]   Final taint: trusted
22:31:19.593 [provenance:c179b0dc-20d5-46]   Tools used: tool_search, exec, exec
```

The plugin prints `REJECTED_CALL_NO_TAINT` only when `event.rejected === true`, so each such line is the host-set field arriving in a real `after_tool_call` event. In the two days since, the journal holds 7 of them across 7 sessions, for the names `mcp__invoke`, `mcp__openclaw` (three times), `mcp__openclaw:read`, `mcp__openclaw:exec` and `mcp__openclaw::process`; in each session sampled the next tools ran normally. Every `TOOL_TAINT_ESCALATION` logged since the restart names a tool that actually ran (`github_read`, `web_search`, `exec` fetching a URL, and similar); none names a refused call.

What this capture is, precisely: the Gateway build is a fork integration commit (`59fa16a3c82`) that contains `f32c6ad4b79` together with other branches. It runs the code of `f32c6ad4b79`: `hook-helpers.ts` is byte-identical there to this head, `execute-events.ts` carries that commit's two hunks alongside other branches' edits, and `hook-types.ts` still holds the type inline. It predates the review fix in `2523ab30128`, so it has the membership check without the client-call and canonical-name guards. All seven marks it produced were client calls to names no run offered, so the guards would not have changed any of them. The after side also includes the plugin's own change to read the new field, which is the point of the field: without it the plugin had nothing to read.

### Regression tests, red and green

`src/agents/cli-runner/execute-events.rejected-call.test.ts` pushes real Claude CLI `tool_use` / `tool_result` records through the production stream parser into the production event handlers, with a real global hook runner capturing `after_tool_call`.

Green at this head (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/cli-runner/execute-events.rejected-call.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/tool-policy.test.ts`):

```
 ✓ after_tool_call rejected flag > marks a name the capped run never offered
 ✓ after_tool_call rejected flag > leaves an offered native tool that ran and failed unmarked
 ✓ after_tool_call rejected flag > leaves an offered discovery tool unmarked
 ✓ after_tool_call rejected flag > leaves an external MCP tool on an uncapped run unmarked
 ✓ after_tool_call rejected flag > makes no claim when the run's offered set is unknown
 ✓ after_tool_call rejected flag > leaves a server_tool_use result unmarked
 ✓ after_tool_call rejected flag > leaves a mcp_tool_use result unmarked
 ✓ after_tool_call rejected flag > leaves a call spelled differently from the offered tool unmarked
 ✓ after_tool_call rejected flag > never derives the flag from a tool's own refusal envelope
 Tests  9 passed (9)
 Tests  3 passed (3)        # tool-policy.test.ts: the offered-set predicate's two no-claim boundaries
```

Red with `execute-events.ts` restored to the base commit, same test file:

```
 × after_tool_call rejected flag > marks a name the capped run never offered
   → expected [ { toolName: 'mcp__invoke', …(6) } ] to match object [ { toolName: 'mcp__invoke', …(3) } ]
 Tests  1 failed | 8 passed (9)
```

The eight controls pass on both sides, which is what they are for: the change marks the refused call and nothing else.

Review feedback on `364934bca53`, reproduced before it was fixed: both automated reviews pointed out that a capped run offering `WebSearch` can see the search reported as a `server_tool_use` named `web_search`, and raw set membership would mark that real result rejected. With the two new server and connector cases added and the call site unchanged, they failed:

```
 × leaves a server_tool_use result unmarked   → expected { toolName: 'web_search', …(6) } to not have property "rejected"
 × leaves a mcp_tool_use result unmarked      → expected { toolName: 'echo', …(6) } to not have property "rejected"
```

`2523ab30128` closes it two ways: only a client `tool_use` can be claimed, and names are compared canonically. The `mcp_tool_use` case passes only because of the first guard and the differently spelled client call only because of the second, so each guard has its own regression. The last control is the forgery case: an offered tool whose own output is the literal refusal text, with `is_error`, stays unmarked. Per the review, the two helper tests that only restated set construction were removed.

### Gates at this head

- Focused suites above: 12 tests pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: exit 0. `pnpm tsgo:core:test`: all 29 shards pass. `pnpm plugin-sdk:check-exports` (run at `364934bca53`; no exported type changed since): synced.
- `pnpm oxlint` and `pnpm oxfmt --check` on the changed TypeScript files and the doc: clean. `git diff --check`: clean.
- Test-lines ratchet: OK with the allocation (`config/test-lines-allocations/after-tool-call-rejected-flag.txt`, 271, slack 0). Line-cap ratchet: OK.
- The branch is based on `main` as of 2026-11-11. `git merge-tree` against `main` at `669576890a1` is clean, and `main` had not changed any file in this diff as of that commit.

### Limits

- The production capture shows the field through one consumer on one host. It is not an isolated run of this branch alone, and nobody induced the model's mistake on demand; the occurrences are the ones that happened.
- Only a capped `claude-cli` run sets the field. An uncapped run hands its configured MCP servers to the CLI, so the Gateway does not hold a complete offered set and makes no claim; the same refusal there still looks like a failed tool. Codex has no `error` on this path at all and is untouched.
- This adds an optional field to a plugin hook event. Whether the plugin API should carry it is a maintainer decision.

*Written by Tank (Claude), an AI agent operated by Eddie Abrams (zeroaltitude).*

prs.title: fix(ui): deleting conversations falsely promises to pause automations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the conversation-deletion warning promising that linked automations will pause even though command automations can keep running.

## User Impact

Before deleting a conversation, the warning now says linked automations may continue and tells you to disable or remove them separately. Single and batch confirmations retain the existing automation names, Cancel and Delete anyway actions, and mandatory warning even after ordinary deletion confirmations are turned off.

## Why This Change Was Made

Deleting the conversation does not remove or disable the scheduler's command job. The shared warning now describes that boundary without changing deletion, scheduling, cancellation, permissions, or confirmation behavior. Two fresh English keys use the existing fallback pending generated translations; foreign catalogs are untouched.

Related: #161030 covers archive outcomes. This change is limited to deletion. The separate transcript-retention wording correction is in #199184.

## Evidence

- **82 focused checks pass:** 79 organizer/archive UI cases, one real deletion-to-scheduler integration, and two production-built browser flows.
- The owner regression creates a stored command job bound to a real session, proves the actual automation index flags that session, deletes it through the registered Gateway handler, then runs the retained enabled job through real occurrence admission. Only the host-command executor is synthetic; no live conversation or automation is changed.
- Single and batch warning assertions fail on main and pass after the correction. Actual built-app flows cover the sidebar and Sessions page: Cancel sends no delete, confirmation deletes the exact selected session once, and neither path sends an automation update, removal or run request. Gateway responses in the browser are synthetic.
- Scoped UI, browser and Gateway test typechecks, lint, formatting, keyless i18n baseline/verification, and diff checks pass. The initial owner fixture used the update-only source-binding option; it was corrected to the actual creation option before any product conclusion. Capture uses the visible native dialog rather than its boxless host.
- Main baseline: `7f7b16cdc243309cc9d78e3aa2c961b68739ff6c`. Browser proof: 20.04s including production build; owner proof: 14.08s including compiler preparation (test 5.61s); UI group: 2.22s. [Remote CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43651012262) passed at implementation head `10339b509b94b9a276f3e03c66a22a0386daa463`.
- Review follow-up `021b00d16dfb41b0af47b64a18716a6693e739b5` corrects the same guide's older confirmation paragraph, which still described both archive and delete as pausing jobs. This is documentation-only: the verified runtime, tests and screenshots are unchanged. Formatting and `git diff --check` pass; `pnpm docs:check-links` checked 16,644 links with zero broken links. [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43653097862) also passes; the final complete read found 50 passing checks and no failed or pending checks.
- Simplification: one net production line (formatted catalog copy), 191 net test lines and two documentation lines. No new runtime helper, state, request or compatibility layer. Existing warning tests were extended rather than replaced.

### Conversation with a linked command automation

Actual built Control UI, 1280×900 light theme, synthetic Backup maintenance conversation. Natural 540px-wide dialog crops; the longer warning adds one line without clipping or changing controls. The Sessions-page presentation matches the sidebar.

prs.title: fix(logbook): capture pause is reported before confirmation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Logbook reporting capture as paused before confirmation, leaving the scope of Pause unclear, and claiming snapshots are being collected when capture is paused or off.

## User Impact

Capture controls now say **Pause capture** and **Resume capture**. Pending changes say **Pausing capture…** or **Resuming capture…** until the confirmed state arrives. The empty timeline no longer claims collection is active. A tooltip explains that queued snapshots can still be analyzed while capture is paused.

## Why This Change Was Made

The view previously displayed its optimistic capture flag as a completed outcome. It now compares the existing optimistic and confirmed values to select pending copy and a neutral status indicator. No new state owner, request, timer, persistence, or confirmation is added.

Pausing still affects new capture attempts only. Queued analysis and captures already in progress can finish. The shared Gateway-service scope and reset-on-reload behavior are unchanged and clarified in the guide. Existing focus, polling, request admission, rollback, and model-processing behavior are preserved.

## Evidence

- **44 focused checks passed:** 27 UI cases, 15 service/lifecycle cases, and two built-Control-UI browser scenarios (desktop and emulated phone). Held-request regressions fail before the repair for the premature paused/capturing claims; the main-baseline browser flow also reproduces the misleading control and empty-state wording.
- **Capture/analysis boundary:** the registered plugin handler pauses capture before an actual scheduler wake. No node capture is invoked, but a queued SQLite batch reaches the model boundary, reports analysis running, and produces a stored timeline card. Resuming through the registered handler allows the next capture. Node/model responses and seed data are synthetic; no live screen, provider, or account is used.
- **Presentation boundary:** real controls send exactly the pause/resume requests. A held pause response displays pending, not completed, status; confirmation adopts the response. Separate regressions cover pause and resume rejection, retained focus, disabled capture, polling, retired views, and ongoing analysis. The empty-state correction works while capture is paused or off.
- Scoped lint, UI and changed-test typechecks, formatting, i18n baseline/verification, and diff checks pass. Canonical English is updated; translation memory is unchanged. Remote CI and its timings are pending.
- Measured checks: UI file group 1.61s; browser group 17.53s including its production build; backend file 45.88s including cold worker compilation, with the new registered-boundary case taking 606ms. The worker test exercises real service/storage ownership rather than mocking the decision being proved.
- Before: verified main `d6008485ec45269cd44cd0fd907735bc046d0ca1`. The final main check through `2f90c703bdf55ed99219100832b2e4c85ad5b0fc` found no drift in the affected owner/presentation paths. Matched screenshots use the actual Control UI, synthetic Gateway data, light theme, and a 1280×900 viewport, cropped to 970×330. The 400×900 phone flow was also inspected; it is browser viewport emulation, not native-device proof.
- Simplification: **net 14 production lines**, 198 test lines, and four documentation lines. The existing presentation owner uses one comparison of already available facts; execution and permission owners are untouched.

### Pause requested, reply still pending

Open the enabled Logbook page from the sidebar and select Pause. Both captures are before the deliberately held Gateway reply. The old view already claimed **Capture paused**; the corrected view makes the pending boundary explicit.
