prs.title: fix(ui): suppress link previews while Ctrl or Cmd is held
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: link hovercards cover nearby links while users hold Ctrl or Cmd to open several links.

## User Impact

User impact: holding either key keeps link previews out of the way, dismisses an open card, and cancels a pending preview. Normal hover and keyboard-focus previews resume on the next interaction after release. Modified clicks keep their normal navigation behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The lazy preview loader and mounted preview providers now share the current modifier state. Existing dismissal handles pending work and focus restoration rather than hiding an active overlay with CSS. Other hovercards and tooltips are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Four new regression cases failed on the original behavior and pass with the fix.
- 84 focused tests pass across hovercards, ordinary page previews, preview seeds, and prefetch (1.96 seconds for the final run).
- The real Control UI with synthetic Gateway responses passed Chromium checks for both Control and Meta: repeated modified clicks, hover/focus while held, open-card dismissal, pending-card cancellation, and normal hover/focus afterward. Modified click events remained unprevented by the application.
- A local autoreview finding about a delayed first-time module load was reproduced for both keys and fixed. All four source-app Chromium scenarios pass (10.95 seconds); matching delayed-module regression cases are included in the existing browser suite.
- Final local Codex autoreview of the complete working-tree candidate against `3c6bb67f82aec52a12644933434a9d5ed7e6ed01` is scoped-clean through P2, with no actionable findings.
- UI typecheck, targeted lint/format, documentation MDX validation, and whitespace checks passed.
- WebKit verification is incomplete: the test environment's egress proxy refused the local app before it loaded. This is not a verified Safari result.
- Draft scope: production build and broad CI have not run.

### Screenshots

Actual UI with synthetic content. Both show Ctrl held over the third link in the same light-theme desktop viewport.

**Before**

![Before: a hovercard covers nearby links while Ctrl is held](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cc20235e-29d9-454c-a3d2-195ad6268f52)

**After**

![After: holding Ctrl keeps the links unobstructed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e0ddca09-d49f-416c-abf8-4985e72aa325)

<details>
<summary>Scope and simplification</summary>

One transient document-level modifier state serves lazy and mounted preview activation. No persistent setting, second visibility owner, or generic overlay change was added. Production code grows by 66 net lines, with 70 regression-test lines and four documentation lines; the new shared state is needed before lazy providers load as well as after they mount.

</details>

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

prs.title: fix(cli): surface migrate blank agent remedy in JSON
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw migrate plan hermes --agent " " --json` prints the correct `--agent must not be blank` message inside its JSON envelope, but its stderr collapses to the generic `[openclaw] The CLI command failed.` plus a doctor hint, so anyone reading stderr (or any wrapper that surfaces stderr only) loses the actionable remedy. `openclaw migrate apply ... --json` behaves the same way. The guard now throws through the existing expected-CLI-error path, so JSON failures keep the concrete message.

- Problem: `resolveMigrationTargetAgentId()` threw a plain `Error` for an explicitly blank `--agent`. In JSON mode the runtime treats an unrecognized error as an unexpected failure and replaces the stderr hint with the generic failure line, even though the user-facing message already existed.
- Solution: throw the existing text through `throwExpectedCliError`, the canonical expected-CLI-error owner already used by the `sandbox explain` and `sessions compact` blank-agent guards.
- What changed: `src/commands/migrate/context.ts` imports `throwExpectedCliError` and converts the single blank-value guard; `src/commands/migrate/context.test.ts` folds the error-name assertion into the existing migration-target test and drops the now-redundant standalone case.
- What did NOT change: text-mode output, JSON stdout envelopes, exit codes, invalid-agent and unknown-agent errors, and the configured-default fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveMigrationTargetAgentId()` is the single owner shared by `migrate plan` and `migrate apply`, so one conversion covers both entry points without duplicating a guard per subcommand.

- Best fix: convert the existing guard in the shared owner. The message was already correct; only the error type was wrong, so the change introduces no new user-facing text and keeps a single source of truth for migration target validation.
- Alternative(s): adding a per-command guard in `register.migrate.ts` would duplicate ownership in two call sites; changing the global JSON failure formatter would alter behavior for unrelated commands. Both were rejected.
- Risk: the conversion only affects the explicitly blank `--agent` path. Invalid ids such as `research/../main` and unknown ids such as `missing` keep their existing plain `Error` path, which the control case below verifies. Full-repository type checking was left to CI.

## User Impact

A JSON consumer that reads stderr now receives `--agent must not be blank` instead of a generic failure line, matching the message that was already available on stdout. Text mode, stdout bytes and exit codes are unchanged, so existing scripts that parse either stream keep working.

## Evidence

Both arms are real built CLIs: the frozen `origin/main` base and the candidate were each built with `build-all.mts cliStartup`, and every cell below is a full `node openclaw.mjs ...` invocation under a minimal environment (only PATH, HOME, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, state dir and config), with 0700 scratch directories, an empty config, no credentials and no mocks. `--version` self-reports each arm.

| Case | Before (pre-fix, base c8caba2) | After (post-fix, this head 1ee8a90) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `migrate plan hermes --agent " " --json` stderr | generic `The CLI command failed.` plus doctor hint | `--agent must not be blank` |
| `migrate apply hermes --yes --agent " " --json` stderr | generic `The CLI command failed.` plus doctor hint | `--agent must not be blank` |
| `migrate plan hermes --agent " " --json` stdout | 104-byte `cli_error` envelope carrying the blank-agent message | identical 104 bytes |
| text mode `migrate plan hermes --agent " "` | blank-agent message on stderr, exit 1 | identical bytes, exit 1 |
| unknown agent control `--agent missing --json` | unknown-agent envelope and generic stderr, exit 1 | identical bytes, exit 1 |

Arm identity:

```console
# frozen base
$ node openclaw.mjs --version
OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (c8caba2)

# candidate
$ node openclaw.mjs --version
OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (1ee8a90)
```

Bug case on the launched CLI:

```console
$ node openclaw.mjs migrate plan hermes --agent " " --json

# stdout, byte-identical on both arms
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "--agent must not be blank"
  }
}

# stderr on frozen base
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.

# stderr on candidate
--agent must not be blank
```

```console
$ node openclaw.mjs migrate apply hermes --yes --agent " " --json

# stdout, byte-identical on both arms
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "--agent must not be blank"
  }
}

# stderr on frozen base
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.

# stderr on candidate
--agent must not be blank
```

Control case, unknown agent:

```console
$ node openclaw.mjs migrate plan hermes --agent missing --json

# stdout and stderr byte-identical on both arms, exit 1
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "Unknown agent id \"missing\". Run openclaw agents list to see configured agents."
  }
}
```

Full matrix as emitted by the comparison harness (`cmp` per stream, 1 = byte-identical):

```text
plan-text       exit=1/1   stdout_cmp=1   stderr_cmp=1
plan-json       exit=1/1   stdout_cmp=1   stderr_cmp=0
apply-text      exit=1/1   stdout_cmp=1   stderr_cmp=1
apply-json      exit=1/1   stdout_cmp=1   stderr_cmp=0
unknown-json    exit=1/1   stdout_cmp=1   stderr_cmp=1
```

Built bundle, proving which form actually shipped:

```console
# frozen base dist/context-*.mjs
throw new Error(`--agent must not be blank`)

# candidate dist/context-*.mjs
throwExpectedCliError(`--agent must not be blank`)
```

Regression test, same assertion on both arms:

```console
# candidate
$ npx vitest run src/commands/migrate/context.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  4 passed (4)

# frozen base with the same assertion
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  1 failed | 3 passed (4)
```

### What was not tested

- Full-repository type checking was not run locally; targeted `oxlint` (0 warnings, 0 errors), `oxfmt` and the focused suite passed, so type checking is left to CI.
- No migration was allowed to run past argument validation, so no real import path was exercised in this proof.
- Both arms emit the same Node security-patch warning and the same log-append warning in the isolated scratch HOME; they are identical across arms and unrelated to this change.

### Open PR collision check

Searched the changed-file lists of the latest 300 open PRs plus title and body searches for `migrate`, `blank agent` and `expected-cli-error`: no open PR touches `src/commands/migrate/context.ts` or `src/commands/migrate/context.test.ts`. The same-day merged #199386 converts the equivalent guard in `sessions compact` only, leaving the migrate owner untouched, so this is not a duplicate.

## What Problem This Solves

Release 2026.11.4 cannot apply the operator-approved three-job exception while retaining the fixed candidate and authenticating fresh qualification.

## User Impact

No shipped product changes. Release tooling can qualify unchanged candidate `5eb2d8052ddc363245bea3ca4ec0833815ab6e93` under Dallin Romney’s November 15, 2026, 04:13 UTC instruction to waive these failures, reseal, and publish. Raw failures remain recorded; all other required gates and publication approvals remain mandatory.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds exact-candidate grants for `checks-node-agentic-control-plane-runtime-state`, `checks-ui-e2e-real-gateway (1/2)`, and `macos-swift (tests)`. The existing policy owner receives the authenticated target SHA through collection, FRV monitoring, and strict verification. Root evidence is authenticated against its own candidate, then checked against the destination so a changelog-only descendant cannot inherit these grants. Aggregate logs must contain exactly the causes explained by the granted leaves; missing, additional, duplicate, malformed, and concealed errors are rejected.

Existing grants, including Kova, are unchanged. There are no candidate, qualification-workflow, coverage, or publisher-bypass changes. Fresh exact-source stable/full qualification with soak is still required. Failed children remain ineligible for ordinary green-child reuse.

## Evidence

- Initial focused policy/collector/FRV/strict-verifier proof: 465 passed, two existing skips. After the destination-binding correction: 172 passed, two existing skips; full qualification suite: 29 passed.
- Final test consolidation: 38 affected tests passed; tooling-test typecheck, focused lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Test-line budget: +399/400, no allocation exception. Script typecheck and documentation MDX checks also passed before the test-only consolidation.
- Actual historical aggregate log accepted under a synthetic exact-candidate policy: annotation-format compatibility only, not candidate qualification. Historical FRV 43641896010/1 tested a different candidate.
- Independent review found and verified the correction for waiver transfer through changelog-only reuse. Actual candidate-publication fixtures reproduce both invalid admissions before the fix, reject both afterward, and retain exact-candidate admission with raw CI failure. Final independent review found only the now-resolved test-line overage and no further actionable correctness issues.
- Final canonical local autoreview with unchanged verifier/policy/fixture context completed scoped-clean, with no actionable P0–P2 findings. The reviewer inspected source but did not run the tests. Hosted ClawSweeper review is queued; no duplicate request was made.
- PR CI found a new test assertion dereferencing an unknown jobs value in the root-scripts type graph. Replaced the dereference with an equivalent collection matcher retaining the gate name, accepted attempt, and failure assertions. Root-scripts typecheck, all 133 release-state tests, focused lint, formatting, and diff checks now pass locally; test budget was +398/400 before the inventory entry. A second CI finding was the explicit lint-suppression inventory: the aggregate parser intentionally strips SGR color and rejects other control bytes, so its two documented `no-control-regex` exemptions must be listed. The inventory now records exactly that file/rule/count with its reason; no parser behavior or lint policy is weakened. All 23 affected inventory/waiver tests and focused lint pass; total test budget is +400/400, with no allocation exception. Updated-head PR CI and fresh release qualification remain required.

prs.title: fix: Memory reports an unavailable provider as awake
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Memory says it is awake when the selected provider reports that it is unavailable or degraded.

## User Impact

User impact: Memory shows the provider’s actual health and explanation instead of a false healthy state. Provider-native engines no longer show an unsupported embedding test or an inferred hybrid-search mode. Refresh still checks the current provider; legacy embedding engines keep their existing controls.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already returns native provider health separately from legacy embedding readiness. It deliberately skips the embedding probe for native providers. The overview previously ignored the health result and interpreted the skipped probe as no known problem.

This is a presentation correction using the existing payload, not a provider, protocol, search or permissions change. It adds no state or helper. Related: #194982 covers a separate copy/style pass and does not consume provider health.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through the built app’s Settings → Memory page on main at 5328b2754d84472b6c6e05fe80c2fc4513fd7e2e, using the real packaged Memory Core fallback view and synthetic native-provider responses. Ready, degraded and unavailable all previously showed “Memory is awake,” inferred hybrid search and an embedding Test that could not check the provider.
- All three native-state regressions failed before the correction. All **40 focused Memory overview/search tests pass**, including legacy embedding checks, disabled engines, no search runtime, failed reads, retry, offline transitions and result presentation.
- **Seven full-app browser cases pass**: three native-health states with refresh-to-ready recovery, plus the existing packaged overview and search flows. The final simplified branch was rechecked with all 40 tests and the three native browser cases. No live provider, embedding request or paid inference was used.
- Source inspection confirms the native Doctor handler returns provider health and intentionally skips legacy embedding probing. The existing browser-safe payload already declares this health field.
- Scoped lint, the actual Memory browser TypeScript graph, i18n baseline/verification, formatting and diff checks pass. No broad CI was run. Current-main reconciliation found no intervening changes to the affected owners.

### Before

![Before: unavailable native memory is incorrectly shown as awake](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/44d0729b-97fd-43ea-b04d-2c1cfae2decd)

### After

![After: Memory shows the unavailable provider and its explanation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a692eac9-6446-4d1b-b744-131ebd6aff77)

Real built components with a synthetic “records” provider and an emulated 1280 × 900 viewport. The existing mascot rerolls its color/accessories on page load; the reading-versus-attention pose reflects the displayed state. No product imagery was replaced for the capture.

Contributor: @vyctorbrzezowski directed this audit and the user-facing correction.

prs.title: improve(workers): reduce retained database worker heap capacity
prs.body:
Related companion harness: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199420

## What Problem This Solves

Retained session readers and SQLite storage workers keep more young-generation heap capacity than this measured history workload needs.

## User Impact

Reduces the young-generation budget of existing session-reader and storage-broker workers from 32 to 16 MiB; their 512 MiB old-generation budgets, results, worker counts, lifetimes, and database admission remain unchanged. No configuration or data migration is required. Cold-read CPU increased in the comparison below. This does **not** establish that a complete Gateway fits in 2 GiB: the historical full-Gateway 2 GiB acceptance still failed and was not rerun.

## Why This Change Was Made

Change only the two existing resource-limit owners, without adding shared fallback policy, options, pools, or retirement behavior. The tradeoff for maintainer review is a smaller nursery with more first-read CPU in this workload; measured worker heap capacity is not an additive RSS saving. The cold-CPU, whole-command CPU, and sampled maximum-RSS increases below need owner acceptance before any landing; this request opens the PR only.

## Evidence

Five serial ABAB pairs on source base `940e76922e54c1880fa8594e6478f2b561fac307`, Node 26.12.1, identical frozen dependencies, fresh synthetic fixture/process per arm: 10,000 1-KiB messages, Gateway history-tail owner, 100 warm reads after the first read and five warmups. No forced GC or inspector; native worker-limit observations and cached production per-worker heap telemetry retained their sample ages. The summed heap observations are not simultaneous peak or live-set measurements; a representative broker sample was about five seconds older than the transcript sample. All ten cases completed and returned 20 of 10,000 messages. This is source-owner history-tail evidence, not a running Gateway transport or sustained mixed writer/usage/search performance test. Functional sibling coverage is listed below; those sibling workloads are not performance-qualified by this dataset.

| Metric (median of five runs) | 32 MiB | 16 MiB | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Maximum sampled target-worker heap capacity | 156,565,504 B | 116,252,672 B | -25.75% |
| Maximum sampled target-worker used heap | 80,908,352 B | 81,303,480 B | +0.49% |
| First-read elapsed | 3,012.60 ms | 3,001.95 ms | -0.35% |
| First-read CPU | 2,826.64 ms | 3,193.50 ms | +12.98% |
| Warm measured CPU, 100 reads | 246.63 ms | 223.19 ms | -9.50% |
| Warm throughput | 582.78 reads/s | 644.77 reads/s | +10.64% |
| Warm per-run p50 latency | 1.502 ms | 1.476 ms | -1.73% |
| Warm per-run p95 latency | 2.434 ms | 2.243 ms | -7.85% |
| Warm-report process RSS | 915,566,592 B | 857,538,560 B | -6.34% |
| Independently observed maximum process RSS | 960,905,216 B | 976,445,440 B | +1.62% |
| Whole-command CPU, including setup and trace | 27.77 s | 28.11 s | +1.22% |

The prespecified comparison rejects a 20% median cold/warm CPU or latency regression (including the median per-run p95), equivalent throughput loss, bad results, crashes, or old-limit drift; none occurred. Spread remains visible: per-run warm p95 ranges were 2.006–2.664 ms versus 1.892–4.853 ms, and throughput 526.54–637.48 versus 378.28–668.02 reads/s. One candidate run was a slower outlier; it was not rerun. These are medians of per-run percentiles, not a pooled p95 of all reads. Host load was recorded; this was not a constrained-host profile.

Rerunnable workload:
```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-session-history.ts \
  --profile long --operation gateway-tail --samples 100 --output report.json
```
Both arms temporarily used the exact committed benchmark script from companion PR #199420, head `cc808e0c5bc610a4838ccbc77f04dd10b878287c`, SHA-256 `9d259c0a9e674b688b90b4535a0b615822a5daaced438acaae10c4d236b82247`. The original script was restored byte-for-byte before review/commit; this PR remains independent and contains no benchmark changes. The original base script failed required runtime-config preparation before timing; that setup failure was investigated, not counted as a performance regression.

- Existing focused history/search/context/export/model-context/projection/maintenance/discovery/usage/broker/lifecycle coverage: **215 tests in 14 files passed**, 227.40 seconds through the repository wrapper with `--maxWorkers=1`. No new static-value tests.
- Core typecheck, targeted type-aware lint and formatting for both files, and `git diff --check`: passed. Broad CI remains the PR check surface; no full-Gateway or upgrade result is claimed.
- Simplification: two scalar edits, net-zero production/test lines; no new state or machinery.
- Local review: ClawSweeper runner unavailable because the installed checkout was dirty/ambiguous; shared autoreview reviewed the complete `940e769…` to working-candidate snapshot at P0–P2 and returned scoped-clean with no actionable findings. Separate independent source review found no P0–P2 defects, reproduced the summary from raw cases, and verified the exact two-value source delta and restored harness. Its cached-sampling and workload-coverage limitations are disclosed here.

Thanks @vincentkoc.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/0f0bc199-e08c-4ff0-971f-406a82b39dea)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/4a458cce-a769-45ec-ba18-f93f4ce5f875)

prs.title: fix: channel settings offer edits that read-only viewers cannot save
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: channel settings let read-only users edit fields and press Save, but nothing is saved and no explanation appears.

## User Impact

User impact: read-only viewers can inspect channel settings without entering an unsavable draft. The existing administrator-access explanation appears beside the settings, and editing and Save reflect that restriction. Existing drafts remain discardable; administrator editing is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The channel page already has a retained administrator-access fact, and the configuration owner already refuses unauthorized writes. The shared form now presents that existing decision instead of offering a silent dead end. Both core channel details and plugin-mounted configuration use this form.

No backend permission, configuration format, persistence or reconnect policy changes. The patch adds no state or helper, and reuses existing translated copy. Related: #199239 separately fixes Nostr’s plugin-owned profile editor, not this shared configuration form.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on main at a02b7418374f9b49b63ab6e34811b443cb771cd0 through Settings → Channels → Telegram and Nostr. With read-only access, toggling Enabled and clicking Save left an unsaved draft, sent no configuration request, and showed no error. Discard still worked.
- The new readonly regression failed before the fix. All **55 focused channel view/save tests pass**, including basic/advanced fields, retained-draft Save/Discard, conflicts and interrupted saves.
- Three full-app browser flows pass: readonly Telegram and Nostr now show the restriction with disabled fields; the existing packaged Nostr administrator flow still edits, saves, refreshes and navigates normally.
- UI typecheck, scoped lint, i18n verification, formatting and diff checks pass. Current-main reconciliation found no intervening changes to the affected owners. No broad CI or live messaging-service test was run.

### Before

### After

Before:

After:

Nostr’s separate Profile control is covered by #199239; it is not part of this patch.

</details>

Real built Control UI components with synthetic status/configuration and permissions, at an emulated 1280 × 1000 viewport. No real channel credentials, configuration or messages were changed.

Contributor: @vyctorbrzezowski directed this audit and the user-facing correction.

prs.title: improve: choose advertised cloud device classes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Operators must type a cloud device class even when the settings page has already loaded the provider’s available classes.

## User Impact

Editing an applied cloud profile now offers named classes for its selected operating system. Existing and custom class strings remain editable; adding a profile or editing without a matching catalog keeps manual entry. Selecting a class does not allocate a device or save configuration. The existing explicit Save and administrator boundaries remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Project the already-loaded profile catalog into the shared picker instead of adding a request or hard-coding size names. The catalog receipt retains its applied-config hash; suggestions are only used for the matching applied profile, backend, binary and setup command. Operating-system choices use that same scope. Custom drafts survive catalog refresh/failure and backend changes without losing their input or focus.

An unresolved provider-default OS after clearing a different saved target does not guess a machine catalog; custom entry remains available until the updated profile is applied. Existing unknown values are never rewritten to the first advertised choice. No provisioning, credential, configuration-schema or persistence changes.

Author simplification/review retained the existing catalog, draft and save owners. The added component owns only transient custom-entry presentation. Net change: +114 production lines, +123 test lines, +2 documentation lines; no lint/controller limits were raised.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

Existing denied-access, rejected-save and array-intent checks remain intact.

prs.title: fix(signal): align autoStart daemon bind with local connection URL port
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A path-prefixed managed-native URL is a proxy, not the daemon bind. For a saved `http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal`, autoStart reserves port 8080 for that proxy and binds the daemon on 8081. Readiness stays on the unchanged proxy URL. A URL on another port, such as `http://127.0.0.1:8082` with no `httpPort`, also stays the client endpoint. Set `httpPort` when the daemon should listen on a non-default port. Remote, HTTPS, and cross-family URLs stay independent.

Ref #116165

## Evidence

Head `4eaf1e5f323`. `extensions/signal/src/transport-prefixed-proxy.test.ts` prepares a saved `http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal` URL with no httpPort, writes that transport, and prepares it again. The proxy URL stays on 8080 and the daemon port is 8081. The same setup binds the daemon on 8080 when the path check is absent. macOS, signal-cli 0.14.9.

The production resolver reserved 8080, allocated daemon port 8081, and kept `baseUrl` at `http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal`. `spawnSignalDaemon` started signal-cli. A loopback forwarder stood in for the independent `/signal` proxy on 8080. `signalCheck` used the unchanged base URL.

```console
{
  "reserved": [8080],
  "allocated": 8081,
  "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal",
  "daemonPort": 8081,
  "signalCheck": { "ok": true, "status": 200, "error": null },
  "listeners": [
    "node ... TCP 127.0.0.1:8080 (LISTEN)",
    "signal-cl ... TCP 127.0.0.1:8081 (LISTEN)"
  ]
}
```

signal-cli listened on 8081. The readiness check against `http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal` returned HTTP 200. No phone account was registered.

Upgrade on Windows 11 10.0.26300, Node v24.19.0. Published OpenClaw 2026.11.2 (`b556fdf`) wrote `channels.signal` with `config set`: enabled, a saved account, `transport.kind` `managed-native`, and `transport.url` `http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal`. `httpPort` was left unset. `resolveSignalAccount` from the published `v2026.11.2` sources and from this head then read that same file.

```console
{
  "stable": {
    "savedUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal",
    "savedHttpPort": "omit",
    "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal",
    "httpPort": 8080,
    "urlKept": true
  },
  "head": {
    "savedUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal",
    "savedHttpPort": "omit",
    "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal",
    "httpPort": 8081,
    "urlKept": true
  }
}
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A config written by published OpenClaw 2026.11.2 with a path-prefixed loopback proxy URL stays the client endpoint on this head, and the daemon port moves to 8081. The published resolver keeps that same saved URL on port 8080.
- **Real environment tested:** Windows 11 10.0.26300, Node v24.19.0, published OpenClaw 2026.11.2 (`b556fdf`) for the saved config, head `1d08a5e9d41ee8a57dafde368361ada21a050ee8` for `resolveSignalAccount`. Earlier macOS proof used signal-cli 0.14.9 at the same head.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Published `config set` wrote `channels.signal.transport.kind` and `channels.signal.transport.url`. `resolveSignalAccount` from the v2026.11.2 Signal account owner and from this head read that file.
- **Evidence after fix:** The upgrade console block in Evidence. Published resolution reports `httpPort` 8080. This head reports `httpPort` 8081 and the same `baseUrl`.
- **Observed result after fix:** The saved proxy URL was not rewritten. This head reserves 8080 for the proxy and binds the daemon on 8081. Published 2026.11.2 still selects 8080 for that saved URL.
- **What was not tested:** A registered phone account, or two signal-cli daemons at once. This upgrade run did not start signal-cli again. The earlier macOS run already showed signal-cli listening on 8081 and a readiness check through the proxy URL.

## Summary

- Treat a non-root connection URL path as an independent proxy
- When that proxy uses port 8080, allocate the daemon on 8081 and leave the proxy URL unchanged
- Leave a saved URL on another port as the client endpoint
- A config written by OpenClaw 2026.11.2 still resolves that way on this head

## Test plan

- [x] Same-port path `http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal` starts signal-cli on 8081
- [x] `signalCheck` against that unchanged proxy URL returns HTTP 200
- [x] Saved transport URL is not rewritten
- [x] Published 2026.11.2 config resolves to daemon port 8080, and this head resolves the same file to 8081

prs.title: feat(talk): report which speech-to-text path talk.catalog uses
prs.body:
Closes #197958

## What Problem This Solves

When Talk dictation and voice notes use different providers, Settings → Talk mixes their readiness and does not explain how Talk selected its provider.

## User Impact

Settings → Talk separates speech to text into **Talk** and **Voice notes** rows so each shows its own readiness.

- **Talk** names the provider and how it was selected: the provider named in Voice Call streaming settings, the agent's voice model, automatic streaming selection from available keys, or the voice notes model. When another audio model is serving as fallback for the picked voice notes model, the row names the provider in use. **Change** and **Set up** open the settings that control that path.
- **Voice notes** keeps the audio model picker and checks that model's media-transcription credentials. **Open Models** appears only for providers Models can connect; media-only providers such as Deepgram get a Gateway environment key hint instead.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway records the selected path in the optional `talk.catalog.transcription.source` field and supplies separate `mediaProviders` readiness when Talk uses another path. `streaming` means the Voice Call config names a provider; provider options without a named provider report `streaming-auto`, because the runtime still picks by order and readiness. These fields are omitted for callers without `operator.read`; the protocol version stays unchanged.

The Talk page publishes the catalog as soon as it arrives. The Models lookup that decides whether **Open Models** applies is read on its own and never delays Talk facts.

## Evidence

**Before:** a generic status and separate preferred-model warning mix Talk's streaming provider with voice-note readiness.

![Before: generic Talk transcription status and a separate preferred-model warning](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/43c32bfc4b4396590cba933c140f07fdb10340e5/images/2026/11/caded058-6aab-4989-9ed2-d33ebb7584ed.png)

**After:** Talk shows OpenAI live transcription with its Change button. Voice notes shows Deepgram nova-3 as Not ready and explains where its key belongs.

![After: separate Talk and Voice notes rows with independent readiness and setup guidance](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/43c32bfc4b4396590cba933c140f07fdb10340e5/images/2026/11/28bdfda0-f129-4770-b37b-3979c40f0690.png)

The pair uses the real Control UI and isolated Gateways with made-up settings: OpenAI streaming enabled with a synthetic key, Deepgram nova-3 selected for voice notes without a key. The before capture is from the existing pre-change Gateway proof; the after capture exercises this PR head. No real provider transcription was requested.

Validation: 4 focused Talk test files pass (90 tests): `talk-transcription.test.ts`, `talk.test.ts`, `catalog.test.ts` and `file-transcription.test.ts`. Three of those tests fail without their fix and pass with it: the catalog renders while Models never answers, provider options without a named provider report `streaming-auto`, and the Talk row names the fallback provider. UI and core typechecks, lint on the changed files and `git diff --check` pass. The real UI capture checks the Gateway catalog, independent readiness, and the Deepgram key hint; the fallback wording and the `streaming-auto` case were not run in a live Gateway. Broad CI results are reported by the PR checks. Real-provider transcription, native clients, and the voice-model path in a live Gateway were not tested.

Known main CI failure: the latest completed full-main run has four post-cancel failures in `client-native-control.test.ts` ([job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43659747920/job/132646591715)).

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The OpenClaw ID copy-link E2E can read another parallel suite’s clipboard contents after successfully copying its own link.

## User Impact

No user-visible product change. CI keeps checking real native clipboard behavior without interference from sibling browser contexts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Give the account-menu suite its own Chromium process through the existing browser fixture option. Headless Chromium shares its native clipboard across contexts in one process; the scheduled failure read the exact pending-message text copied by the Incognito recovery suite. The production copy handler already waits for the write before showing success.

This matches other native-clipboard E2Es. All copy, keyboard, popup, geometry, animation, and ceremony assertions remain unchanged. The change adds no tests or product code and does not serialize the lane or change timeouts.

- [Scheduled run 43659747920, failed job 132646587507](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43659747920/job/132646587507): `openclaw-id-menu.e2e.test.ts` → `uses one accessible sign-in button and contains signed-in multiline rows`, native clipboard assertion at 392.
- A real Clipboard API probe deterministically reproduces the exact overwrite between sibling contexts, then verifies separate Chromium processes retain independent values. The original two-file product replay passed; it did not reproduce the timing collision.
- With the fix, the complete account-menu and competing Incognito-recovery files pass 3/3 (32.37s invocation; account-menu file 22.269s). Native clipboard assertions remain intact.
- Default UI and UI E2E typechecks (tsrs), scoped lint/format, and diff checks pass.

prs.title: fix(infra): preserve drained worker telemetry on stock Bun
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Final SQLite reader counters and worker flush samples are lost on stock Bun when diagnostics drains a queued memory-port message through `MessagePort.emit`.

## User Impact

Worker retirement and retained flushes preserve their final telemetry on stock Bun. This changes telemetry correctness only; admission and resource-limit decisions are unchanged. Node behavior stays synchronous and unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`worker-cpu` now retains the port's sole production listener and calls it directly from one shared drain helper. Retirement drains before folding SQLite counters; the metrics module only aggregates counters. The receiver is cleared with the port. The existing heap sample type also replaces duplicated field declarations.

The additional listeners in tests observe normal asynchronous delivery and are awaited or removed before drain. No runtime branch, feature probe, shim, new wait, or test change is needed.

upstream https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/45209

## Evidence

The unchanged `worker-cpu.test.ts` cases **retains task heap and GC totals across worker retirement without retaining worker ids** and **retains cumulative reader bytes across worker replacement without per-read messages** exercise queued delivery through the production flush and retirement owners.

| file | ids | stock before | fork | stock after | Node | control | wall s |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src/infra/worker-cpu.test.ts` | queued flush; queued reader registration at retirement | both fail (`pending`; 2 reads/4096 bytes instead of 4/8192) | 24/24 | both pass; full file 18/24, unrelated heap-counter failures below | 24/24 | reverting only this production change restores both failures and null-message exceptions | Node 13.27 → 32.49; fork 17.13 → 74.20; stock 75.79 → 80.20 |
| `src/infra/sqlite-reader-lifecycle.io.test.ts` | all 12 | unchanged | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | — | stock 7.73; fork 7.27; Node 11.08 |
| `src/infra/worker-cpu.postgres-bridge.test.ts` | all 3 | unchanged | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 | — | stock 70.71; fork 110.79; Node 109.36 |

Wall times include repository worker preparation and verification; no tests were added. The worker-cpu assertions themselves run in under three seconds. Restoring the reviewed change passes both focused stock cases again (172.48 s including worker compilation); the reverted failure run took 158.99 s. Targeted typecheck, lint, and format pass. Fresh isolated review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.

Stock Bun has six separate heap-counter failures: five cases require native total heap to exceed used heap, while stock reports equal values; one case underreports ArrayBuffer bytes. The isolated baseline control reproduces these with the MP change reverted. They are not included in this fix.

Consumer gates: named `worker_threads` access stays named, so no default/named mock migration is required. Close/retirement gains no asynchronous wait. Existing worker-count/close assertions pass on Node and the fork; the broker's temporary flush listener is removed before retirement.

The broker’s temporary-flush-listener test (`retains real SQLite broker forced GC in memory diagnostics`) also passes on Node and stock (25.05 s / 20.45 s wall).

prs.title: fix(ui): choose automation agents by name
prs.body:
Related: #199140, #194890

## What Problem This Solves

Automation editors ask users to type an agent ID, and their suggestions discard the names already available in the authorized agent roster.

## User Impact

Users can browse or search agents by name when creating or editing an automation. Duplicate names have identifying context, saved references remain visible when discovery fails, and supported custom agent IDs remain available without making manual entry the default.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing searchable picker now consumes the existing page-scoped agent inventory and canonical agent-label helper. It does not fetch a second catalog or change permissions. Internal system rows stay out of the ordinary choices.

**Automatic** removes the explicit agent override; the backend still resolves the linked session’s agent and then the Gateway default. It does not save a snapshot of today’s default. The old advanced clear-override checkbox and ID-only datalist are removed. Selecting a known or custom agent clears that reset flag. All changes remain drafts until Create or Save, and failed saves retain them.

Custom entry is intentional here: the existing cron contract accepts explicit agent references outside the currently discoverable roster. It is not added to closed-enum settings or unrelated fields.

Author simplification kept one cron-local control over the existing picker and form owner: net +142 production lines and +157 test/support lines. No generic picker framework, new discovery API, or cache was introduced.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

prs.title: feat(sessions): show per-session token and cost usage from the CLI
prs.body:
Closes #192616

## What Problem This Solves

The Gateway records per-session token and cost attribution and the Control UI shows it, but the terminal could not: `openclaw gateway usage-cost` prints one aggregate number, so a headless operator could not see which session, agent, or model burned the tokens.

## User Impact

`openclaw sessions usage [sessionKey]` prints one row per session (label, agent, model, messages, tokens, cost) plus range totals, with `--agent`, `--all`, `--range`, `--start/--end`, `--max-rows`, and `--group-family` selectors. `--json` returns the raw `sessions.usage` response.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The command forwards the canonical `sessions.usage` owner and only shapes output: conflicting selectors are rejected before dispatch, and the report's `partial` status is printed instead of hidden, so a time-budgeted answer is never mistaken for "no usage".
- The row cap flag is `--max-rows` rather than `--limit`, because the parent `sessions --limit` list-row cap owns that name (the sibling search command follows the same naming after review feedback).
- Registration rejects the parent list selectors, matching the other gateway-backed verbs.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/sessions-usage.test.ts src/cli/program/register.status-health-sessions.test.ts` → 27/27 passed locally.
- `oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json` → clean; `oxfmt --check` → clean.
- **Real behavior proof**: the branch was built through the shipped `build-all` and run against a real Gateway booted from this checkout (isolated state dir, `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1`):

```text
$ openclaw sessions usage --timeout 120000 --json
{ ..., "startDate": "2026-10-06", "endDate": "2026-11-04", "cacheStatus": {"status": "partial"},
  "partial": { "reason": "time-budget", "message": "Usage request exceeded its 15-second budget; ..." } }

$ openclaw sessions usage --timeout 120000
Session usage (2026-10-06 → 2026-11-04)
No session usage recorded in this range.
Totals: $0.0000 · 0 tokens · in 0 / out 0
Partial report: Usage request exceeded its 15-second budget; narrow the date range or select a session.

$ openclaw sessions usage --agent x --all          → exit 1 (conflict)
$ openclaw sessions usage --end 2026-10-31         → exit 1 (missing --start)
$ openclaw sessions usage --max-rows 500           → exit 1 (cap exceeded)
```

The live response's `partial` reason surfacing in text mode is the behavior the review asked to prove: an incomplete answer is labeled, never silent.

## Risks

- None beyond the new verb: no RPC, ledger, or config changes.

## What Problem This Solves

When a tool the agent expects is missing, the operator had to guess why. The Gateway already computes the full effective tool set for a session — each tool's status plus the profile, deny, allowlist, session, or runtime rule behind every decision — through the canonical `tools.effective` RPC, but no CLI verb exposed it.

## User Impact

`openclaw agents tools <sessionKey>` prints the effective profile, the Gateway's filtering notices, and one row per tool with its status and the deciding reasons; `--json` returns the raw diagnostics.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The command forwards the canonical owner and only shapes output; blank selectors are rejected before dispatch and transport failures exit non-zero in both output modes.
- Registered under `agents` because the `tools` root is deliberately reserved.
- The command defaults its runtime to `defaultRuntime`, matching the other agents commands that are invoked without an explicit runtime from the registration wrapper.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/agents-tools.test.ts src/cli/program/register.agent.test.ts` → 32/32 passed locally.

```text
$ openclaw agents tools "agent:main:main" --timeout 120000 --json
{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "unknown session key \"agent:main:main\"" },
  "sessionKey": "agent:main:main" }            (exit 1)

$ openclaw agents tools "agent:main:main" --timeout 120000
Tools diagnostics failed: unknown session key "agent:main:main"

```

The Gateway log confirms both live requests (`⇄ res ✗ tools.effective ... errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=unknown session key`). The isolated store has no sessions, so the populated table rendering is covered by the unit tests.

## Risks

- None beyond the new verb: no RPC, tool-policy, or config changes.

prs.title: fix(gateway): scope image capability discovery
prs.body:
## Summary

- scope attachment image-capability fallback to the selected provider instead of rebuilding every provider catalog
- keep runtime-only models by using the existing request-scoped live catalog path
- retry the complete Gateway projection when its published runtime owner is replaced during scoped discovery

## Root cause and owner

Attachment admission first reads the lifecycle-published catalog. When a selected runtime-only model is absent or has provisional text-only metadata, current main falls back to `readOnly: false`, which rebuilds the full cross-provider catalog inside the request. The provider-scoped catalog machinery exists, but this Gateway caller did not use it.

The canonical owner is the Gateway catalog projection. The second read now carries the selected provider into the existing prepared request-scoped live catalog. The projection checks the published owner before and after the asynchronous scoped read and reacquires the full owner on replacement, so catalog, config, agent identity, and auth projection never mix generations.

## ClawSweeper findings

- Early owner replacement: fixed by retrying at the Gateway projection boundary; the regression replaces the owner during scoped discovery and proves only the replacement catalog returns.
- Final provider I/O fence: the old branch tried to turn generation liveness into a public provider-auth revocation contract, but that was incomplete and added a large cross-plugin surface. This port removes that contract. Published-generation liveness governs whether results may publish; it does not retroactively revoke already-started provider requests. Results from a retired generation are discarded and the owner is reacquired.
- Runtime-only models: retained. An independent P1 review caught and rejected an intermediate static-only rewrite; the final branch uses the existing scoped live mode.
- Test-cost evidence: recorded below for the new image-capability file and the combined focused Gateway set.

## Scope

Seven Gateway files changed against integrated main: 222 insertions and 60 deletions. Reuses the existing scoped catalog owner; no provider/plugin implementation changes, new configuration, or cache.

## Validation

- Integrated main: `1f01f4944d45eb265081f8bfbf8d3e8e54ff4266`; resolved conflicts while retaining current static-capability and projection owners.
- Three focused Gateway suites: 86 tests passed (image capability, catalog projection, session utilities).
- Core production typecheck and targeted lint passed; `git diff --check` clean.
- Fresh autoreview against integrated main, P0–P2: no actionable findings in the seven-file candidate diff. Surrounding loader implementations were not included in the isolated reviewer bundle; integration assurance also relies on focused tests and source inspection.
- Previous validation counts and hosted evidence were for the old head and are not current-head proof.
- No new real-channel/live-provider proof was run.
- CI follow-up: the new catalog mock now accepts the loader's optional argument. The affected Gateway-server test-type leaf passed; 16 catalog tests passed. Current head: `8a7567d2df5d`. Replacement exact-head CI is pending, not claimed green.

Agent transcript omitted.

prs.title: ci(i18n): add non-publishing native locale refresh
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where maintainers cannot refresh secret-backed native translations for review without also creating and arming an auto-merge generated PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an explicit non-publishing dispatch mode that runs the existing bounded locale matrix and validation, then uploads an allowlisted binary patch artifact. The default publishing path remains unchanged.

Secret-backed non-publishing runs execute only from the trusted `main` workflow. The operator supplies an exact source SHA; that SHA must be the current head of one open, non-draft PR targeting `main` with GitHub's current review decision `APPROVED`. Each locale worker revalidates the exact PR head and current approval immediately before the translation-secret step. Branch-selected preflight support was removed: guards inside branch-controlled YAML cannot independently guarantee secret isolation. Manual runs use the trusted main workflow definition.

## User Impact

No direct user-facing change. Maintainers gain a review-only native translation refresh path that cannot push, open a PR, or enable auto-merge, while non-publishing source selection requires current exact-head review approval.

Related: #142663

## What Problem This Solves

`/tools verbose` advertises automation creation during management-only turns, even though execution rejects `add`. Inventory construction has no run ID, so deriving its description and schema from an exact-run execution grant incorrectly falls back to the unrestricted surface.

## User Impact

Discovery inside an admitted management-only turn no longer advertises creation. Fresh remote administrator turns retain creation through the existing `callerScopedCreation` distinction. Execution authorization is unchanged.

This fixes the discovery mismatch only; the reported Telegram creation rejection is not claimed fixed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `resolveCronToolManagementMode` reads admitted scope, deployment policy, liveness, and any supplied run ID without requiring an execution grant.
- `bindCronManagementGrant` reuses that classification while retaining its exact-run, live caller authority and operational-instance checks.
- Automation descriptions, schemas, and compact summaries use the admitted mode. Summary wording stays in the existing description-presets owner, keeping `cron-tool.ts` within its line limit.
- Discovery outside an admitted turn still describes the configuration surface, not per-turn execution authority.

## CI Repair

Rebased onto upstream `24e758688a6db34e1f9079f65faff3269bf15978`, which contains [#181647](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181647), `05d779c0c931c8c0bbccf9cce93a47fbb54e6ef9`. That upstream repair distinguishes the admitted restart source ID from the interrupted execution run ID, addressing the three failures previously reproduced on CI's upstream base without this PR.

Removed this PR's duplicate exact action-enum assertion, which had become stale when upstream added `bind`. The real command-handler regression remains; existing schema and authority tests protect permitted actions and the creation boundary. No upstream assertions, skips, retries, or approval gates were changed by this PR.

## Evidence

- Real command-handler regression covers `/tools verbose` in an admitted management-only scope. Authority coverage distinguishes discovery from execution grants and preserves fresh remote creation.
- 128 focused tests passed using repository-pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+807211511`: 20 restart-continuation cases plus 108 authority, tool, inventory, and prefix-stability cases across the six affected suites.
- [New-head native CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40344290316), including `checks-node-changed-5` and the native `openclaw/ci-gate`. The final rollup had 66 passing checks and none pending; only the maintainer-approval commit statuses remain red.
- Standalone command smoke outside Vitest, with isolated state and synthetic admitted scopes: management-only output omits `add job`; fresh remote creation output includes it. This is command-boundary proof, not a live Gateway/model session.
- Targeted production and touched-test typechecks, lint, formatting, and whitespace checks.
- Fresh independent review was attempted, but both reviewer processes failed at service capacity; no fresh review verdict is claimed. The authority implementation is unchanged from the previously reviewed patch. This update rebases that patch, removes the duplicate enum assertion, and relocates the unchanged summary expression.

The security-sensitive guard still requires current-head approval from a maintainer with `maintain` or `admin` access. A previous-head approval would not carry over after this rebase.

prs.title: fix(codex): retain native thread reasoning effort
prs.body:
## Summary

- retain Codex App Server's effective reasoning effort from thread start, resume, and fork responses
- update the same live and durable binding from matching `thread/settings/updated` notifications
- report the effective native setting through the existing `turn_starting.effort` diagnostic when a supervised turn intentionally has no per-turn collaboration override

## Root cause and canonical fix

OpenClaw's manual response types and durable session binding omitted Codex's response-backed reasoning effort. The notification controller also discarded settings notifications emitted before `turn/start` returned a turn id. Supervised attempts therefore reported a null effort even when the native thread had an effective setting.

The repair records the fact where Codex owns it: start/resume/fork responses initialize it, and `thread/settings/updated` changes it. All binding writers carry the same nullable field. Existing generation and thread guards prevent stale clients from moving live or durable state.

This current-main rewrite does not add `thread_ready.reasoningEffort` or another event field. It fills the long-standing `turn_starting.effort` field only when the per-turn request intentionally omits an override. The live harness independently verifies the effective native effort and the absent collaboration override.

## Dependency contract

The integrated plugin pins `@openai/codex` 0.164.0. The sibling Codex source was inspected directly at commit `fdf23b4097bf19adf2286c64316da2d2a9fedae6`: `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs` defines response-backed nullable `reasoning_effort` for thread start/resume and `ThreadSettings.effort` for settings updates. Native thread facts remain separate from per-turn overrides.

## Coverage and change shape

Regressions cover response capture across start/resume/fork and supervised materialization, pre-turn settings updates, durable-owner rejection, effective turn-start diagnostics, and the live supervised/native assertion boundary.

No new configuration surface, schema migration, protocol version, fallback, or parallel path. The positive production delta propagates one native fact through the existing binding writers; notification writes use the connection's current authority.

## Validation

- Current head: `ae1b83e6b0bd`; integrated main: `1f01f4944d45`.
- 89 tests passed across three affected files during conflict repair.
- After the final current-authority adaptation: all three reasoning-effort regression cases passed; extension production types and targeted lint passed.
- Fresh autoreview against integrated main, P0–P2: no actionable findings in the supplied candidate diff; unchanged surrounding source was unavailable to the isolated reviewer.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- No fresh credentialed live Codex run. Historical CI and hosted review are not current-head evidence.
- Exact-head CI pending after publication; not claimed green.

prs.title: feat(system-agent): let the system agent report backup status
prs.body:
Fixes #192657

## Summary

The system agent could report `health`, `status`, `doctor`, `models`, and `plugins`, but had no way to answer backup questions ("when did the last backup run, did it succeed, are the offsite schedules working?"). The Gateway already summarizes that through the canonical `backup.status` projection; only the model-facing surface was missing.

This PR adds a read-only `backup-status` system-agent operation plus the `backup_status` tool action, wired through the same four-step chain the `health` action established: operation type → executor case → tool action enum + `SIMPLE_ACTIONS` → assistant-prompt lists. The executor reuses the projection's own helpers (`readBackupRuns`, `summarizeBackupTargets`, `summarizeBackupSchedules`, `listStorageLocations`, `buildBackupStatusValue`), so no new projection or state access is introduced. The typed-command parser accepts `backup status` / `backup` / `backups`.

Revision 2 (`2118837348c`) closes the remaining P2 from the earlier review: when the selected Gateway is not this host (`gateway.mode=remote`), the loader now asks that Gateway's `backup.status` handler for the projection instead of reading the client's own SQLite ledger, cron partition, and storage registry. The rendered headline now states where the rows came from (`Source: local process state` or `Source: selected Gateway ws://…`), so an operator can tell which host answered.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: the `backup_status` system-agent operation now renders the recorded backup-run ledger — freshness headline, per-target `kind/target/status/age` table, enabled schedules, storage locations, plus the existing backup doctor hints — instead of having no action at all; and with `gateway.mode=remote` it renders the selected Gateway's projection rather than the client's local one.

**Real setup tested**: Windows 11 host, OpenClaw run from TypeScript source on this PR's head (`2118837348c`). Two isolated state directories, no user state touched: Gateway host `D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-prfix` (real pre-existing `state/openclaw.sqlite`, 2.0 MB, with two recorded runs) and remote client `D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-b-remote` whose own ledger holds **0 rows**. The Gateway ran on `ws://127.0.0.1:18817` with token auth, started only for this proof and stopped afterwards.
- **Runtime**: node v24.22.1, invoked as `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs` (no `dist` rebuild, so the tree under test is exactly this branch's source)
- **Selected-Gateway transport**: the shipped `backup.status` RPC over the real Gateway WebSocket, exercised through the shipped `createSystemAgentTool()` object and its `backup_status` action (not by calling `backupStatusCommand` directly, and not through a stubbed transport)

**Exact steps or command run after fix**:

```bash
# Gateway host: isolated state with real ledger rows, real Gateway on 18817
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-prfix"
export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-prfix/openclaw.json"
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway run --allow-unconfigured --port 18817

# Local mode (no gateway.mode): the same tool object the agent calls
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-prfix"
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .proof-backup-status.ts     # createSystemAgentTool({surface:"cli"}).execute({action:"backup_status"})

# Remote mode: client has gateway.mode=remote -> backup.status on the selected Gateway
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-b-remote"
export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-b-remote/openclaw.json"
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .proof-backup-status.ts

# What the client's own ledger contains (0 rows), so the two rows below can only
# have come from the Gateway's backup.status response
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .proof-ledger-rows.ts
```

The two probe files contain no stubs: they build the shipped tool with `createSystemAgentTool({ surface: "cli" })`, prepare runtime config through `captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader`, and print the tool's real text result.

**After-fix evidence**:

```text
# local mode, isolated state with two recorded runs (newest first)
Backup status last attempt failed 20h ago (external)
Source: local process state
+----------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+--------+---------+
| Kind     | Target                                                             | Status | Age     |
+----------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+--------+---------+
| external | nas-b                                                              | failed | 20h ago |
| external | nas-a                                                              | ok     | 20h ago |
+----------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+--------+---------+
----- tool result meta -----
{"ok":true,"parts":1}
```

```text
# gateway.mode=remote, client ledger has 0 rows — rows come from the selected Gateway
Backup status last attempt failed 20h ago (external)
Source: selected Gateway ws://127.0.0.1:18817
+----------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+--------+---------+
| Kind     | Target                                                             | Status | Age     |
+----------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+--------+---------+
| external | nas-b                                                              | failed | 20h ago |
| external | nas-a                                                              | ok     | 20h ago |
+----------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+--------+---------+
----- tool result meta -----
{"ok":true,"parts":1}
```

```text
# the remote client's own ledger, proving the two rows above crossed the RPC boundary
{"clientLedgerRows":0,"targets":[]}
```

The local-mode run took 254.6 s and exited 0; the remote-mode run took 142.6 s and exited 0. Both are real terminal runs, not test output.

**Observed result after the fix**: the headline moves from `Backup status none recorded` to `last ok` / `last attempt failed`, the table lists every recorded target newest-first with the ok row still visible behind a later failure, and in remote mode the same rows are rendered from the Gateway while the client's own ledger is empty. Exit code is 0 for the populated, single-row, and empty cases alike — the empty state is a normal state, not an error. `Source:` makes the answering host explicit in both modes.

**What was not tested**: no live LLM agent turn was run (this host has no model credential wired for a paid run), so the model's own tool-selection step — choosing `backup_status` and formatting its answer — is covered only by the contract assertions in `src/agents/tools/system-agent-tool.test.ts`, not by an executed agent session. Schedule rows were not exercised in this session: the isolated state has no cron backup jobs, so the "Schedules:" line did not appear (the code path is the same helper the `health` action already uses). The remote run used a loopback Gateway with token auth; a TLS/tunnel Gateway was not exercised.

**Proof limitations or environment constraints**: the runs used TypeScript source via the `tsx` loader rather than a `tsdown`-built `dist`, so the evidence is byte-identical to this branch's source but not to a packaged release artifact. The Gateway was started for the proof only and stopped afterwards; the isolated state directories and the loopback token never touch the user's real `~/.openclaw`.

## Gateway-target fix (revision 2)

| Scenario | Before this revision | After this revision |
|---|---|---|
| `gateway.mode=remote`, client ledger empty, Gateway has a failed `nas-b` run | client prints `none recorded` (its own empty SQLite ledger) | client prints `last attempt failed … nas-b`, `Source: selected Gateway ws://…` |
| Transport used | none — local file reads only | canonical `backup.status` on the selected Gateway (`callGateway`, `operator.read`) |
| Failure mode when the Gateway is unreachable | silently wrong local answer | explicit error naming the Gateway URL; no silent local fallback |
| Doctor hints | built from the client's local ledger | built from the same projection the headline/table used |

`isImplicitLocalGatewayTarget(config)` chooses the path: implicit local keeps today's local reads (no Gateway required for CLI use), `gateway.mode=remote` routes to `backup.status`. `loadBackupStatusSnapshot` is the only decision point; `renderBackupStatus` and the hint builder are shared, so both modes describe one projection.

## Tests and validation

- Unit tests landed with the PR (recorded when the branch was pushed, not re-run in this evidence session): `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/system-agent/operations-parse.test.ts src/agents/tools/system-agent-tool.test.ts` → 114/114 passed, covering the new `backup status` parse rows and the schema/description assertions.
- `oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json src/commands/backup-status.ts src/commands/backup-health.ts` → 0 warnings / 0 errors; `oxfmt --write` applied to both files.
- Type checking: a workspace-wide `tsgo` run in this checkout is red on pre-existing `@agentclientprotocol/sdk` dependency drift (`src/acp/*`, unrelated to this branch); it reported exactly one error in the touched files on the first pass (`OpenClawConfig` imported but unused), which is fixed in the pushed head.
- The end-to-end behaviour above is production code (tool dispatch → executor → projection → renderer → Gateway RPC), not a unit-test fixture.
- Read-only throughout: no backup runs, schedules, storage writes, or Gateway mutations; the operation returns `{ applied: false }` like the other reporting actions.

## Risk checklist

- **Does this change user-visible behavior?** Yes, but only additively: the system agent gains one read-only action (`backup_status`), the tool description grows by two words, and every rendered status now carries a `Source:` line. No existing action semantics change.
- **What is the release/rollback risk?** Low. The new code path is a branch inside one loader; reverting it returns to local reads without touching the ledger, the cron store, or the RPC, which remain the canonical owners.
- **Could this corrupt state or break an existing surface?** No state is written. In remote mode the command now performs a read-only `backup.status` RPC with the configured client credentials; the local path is unchanged. A defect would surface as wrong output or an explicit connection error, not as data loss.
- **Auth/secret handling**: the Gateway token is read from the existing `gateway.remote` config through `buildGatewayConnectionDetails`/`callGateway`; it is never printed, logged, or embedded in the body.

## Current review state

- **Addressed in revision 2**: the P2 "Read backup status from the selected Gateway" — `gateway.mode=remote` now routes through the selected Gateway's `backup.status`, and the evidence above shows the empty-client-ledger scenario the review described (2 rows from the Gateway, 0 rows locally).
- **Addressed in revision 1**: the "Add real behavior proof" blocker — populated, single-row, and empty states were already shown; revision 2 additionally shows the actual system-agent tool dispatch and the selected-Gateway transport the earlier review asked for.
- **Still open (author-known)**: no live LLM agent turn, no cron schedule rows, and no packaged-`dist` run (see What was not tested).
- **Next step**: maintainer review. I will not claim the remote path is release-proven until a packaged build runs against a non-loopback Gateway.

## Before / After

| State | Before this PR | After this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Agent action | no `backup_status`; fallback guidance lists doctor/status/health only | `backup_status` registered; parser maps `backup status` / `backup` / `backups` |
| Operation type | `operation-types.ts` has no backup case (0 hits on `origin/main`) | `{ kind: "backup-status" }` (1 hit) |
| Executor | no `backup-status` case (0 hits on `origin/main`) | dispatches to `backupStatusCommand` (2 hits) |
| Rendered output | — | freshness headline + source + per-target table + schedules/locations + doctor hints |
| Remote Gateway | local ledger read regardless of `gateway.mode` | `backup.status` on the selected Gateway; explicit error instead of a silent local answer |
