prs.title: improve(compaction): avoid redundant conversation checks
prs.body:
Related: #196550

## What Problem This Solves

Compaction repeats conversation classification and computes transcript byte sizes that its full-fidelity planning does not consume.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Short planning/rendering worker tasks, bounded Gateway payloads, and overlapping summary calls are preserved. **The original `12ad` comparison was negative and remains immutable. The new `a03b` snapshot-accounting repair is unmeasured and not performance-accepted. This remains a draft; no current CPU or latency gain is claimed.**

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing meaningful-content result when preparing conversation-anchor facts. In the planner’s existence-only check, stop classifying after the first real conversation message while still visiting every message and checking cancellation. The shared classifier’s full lookback behavior remains unchanged for other consumers.

For unbounded SQLite snapshots only, the shared snapshot producer now skips two eager model-size projections per navigation row (2N evaluations). An explicit size request still uses the original size SQL and existing bounded batches. Bounded snapshots and their navigation cache, PostgreSQL’s fused projection, omission handling, snapshot/fence/identity checks, cancellation, and native-writer durability remain unchanged. No work is moved outside the measurement boundary.

No cache, retained transcript payload, new configuration, changed summary selection, or persistence/authority change is introduced.

## Evidence

- **Original classification scope:** independent static owner/caller review and local autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings on `12ad15841a49778e9d9c0b6b9af1511fe5e20d0a`. The completed original 30-observation result below applies only to that head.
- **New repair source:** reviewed repair commit `7ac21e5d1b14d49e97170bd03a68738165b04c55` is published through empty metadata commit `a03b3d25606cd3c8664a6fc069c66e081f829b81`. Both have tree `94e6b6dd8350b4f1b82d9ceb08dc4e6de8dcd951`; source is identical. The exact two-file repair patch SHA-256 is `7c60e0afad0cd31cba985dab630099ff3380b71bf0b66e7116cc920cc47af437`.
- **New SQLite work-count proof:** the actual snapshot operation on original `12ad` fails the intended zero-eager-sizing assertion with six executed `octet_length` calls for a header and two inline messages. The repair performs zero eager calls, then exactly two calls when those messages’ sizes are explicitly requested, with exact byte values preserved. This proves removed SQL sizing work, not overall CPU savings.
- **New repair validation:** 53 focused tests passed across snapshot, seed, actual compaction-source integration, model-context, and selected lifetime/authority/refusal cases before a fixture type correction. The corrected selected work-count test then passed (one selected, four intentionally skipped), without double-counting it as additional coverage. The correction uses the existing `isIndexedSessionEntry` predicate; the original TS18046 failure is retained. Final independent, local autoreview, and parent hands-on reviews found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Targeted production/test type graphs, lint, line-cap, format, and diff checks exited 0.
- **New repair normal build:** normal `pnpm build` exited 0 in 181.1 seconds with Node 26.12.1 / pnpm 12.15.0, before commit at `12ad` plus the exact reviewed `7c60…` patch. Source/dependency hashes remained unchanged. This is not an `a03b`-bound native performance build. The secretless build used network-disabled private isolation, eight CPUs / 16 GiB, default heaps, absent NODE_OPTIONS, enforced zero task swap, and the existing physical exact-lockfile dependency closure. No shared dependency reconciliation or guard override occurred. Its TypeScript experimental-API warning remains retained; Control UI content-cache reuse is not a new UI-budget pass. All original warnings and failed setup/gate receipts remain retained.
- **New exact-head gates remain pending:** broad CI for `a03b` is unproven. Dirty mergeability was observed after source publication; a subsequent pre-edit metadata read returned unknown. No base integration or conflict repair has been performed. New commit-bound native builds, workload bindings, qualification, freeze, and comparison series are all pending.
- **Original classification red/green regression:** the exact new classifier test on base `8857554b178506f962068509227e5c10ebe6cc8a` fails only its two intended work-count assertions (`expected 2 to be 1`), while all 11 existing cases pass. The candidate passes all 13 cases. This proves eligible-content reads fall from two to one, not overall CPU savings. The native observer does not separately count these helper calls.
- **Original `12ad`: 94 candidate tests passed** across the classifier, safeguard-source, safeguard, actual worker compaction-source integration, context-report, and prompt-prefix stability suites. Tests ran serially through `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1` on Node 26.12.1. No separate Bun-runtime proof is claimed.
- For original `12ad`, formatting, the three-file line-cap ratchet, targeted lint, production and changed-test type graphs, and the normal `pnpm build` all exited 0. Task-private physical frozen-lockfile installations supplied the required `oxlint` 1.89.0; the shared installation was not reconciled, and no hook or content guard was overridden. Validation receipts, all 15 retained log hashes, source/dependency integrity, and exact build identity were independently audited. The earlier local hook/tool-version failure remains retained.
- **Build caveat:** the successful normal build printed eight Control UI asset-budget violations and dynamic-import warnings. This is not a passing UI-performance check. No baseline attribution was established, so these warnings are not labeled inherited or caused by this patch.
- **Original `12ad` native proof completed:** six separately tagged qualifications and all **30 original comparison observations** completed, controller exit 0. All imports/physical identities, native compactions, exact 8,192-byte seed/post-RPC follow-ups, warm-target invariance, source/build/workload/fixture bindings, default-heap/no-swap checks, independently observed main-thread CPU brackets, and graceful cleanup passed. No observation was rerun, discarded, corrected, or pooled with earlier evidence.
- **Original `12ad` broad CI remained unproven:** the complete observed exact-head inventory had six successful dispatch/metadata/scope/actionlint checks and 102 skipped checks. Skips are not broad-suite proof. The original #196550 110-observation comparison is separate and does not validate this patch.

### NEW a03 repair protocol — declared before new native sampling (pending)

Compare architecture-matched baseline `8857554b178506f962068509227e5c10ebe6cc8a` against new candidate `a03b3d25606cd3c8664a6fc069c66e081f829b81` (the same reviewed source tree as `7ac21e5d1b14d49e97170bd03a68738165b04c55`). The count goal is to remove 2N unused eager model-size evaluations from unbounded SQLite planning without moving work outside measurement or changing selected inputs, bounds, overlap, cancellation, authority, or durability.

- Use the existing committed canonical real-Gateway rig and model-mock workload, not a new benchmark framework. Native sourcePerformance builds and runtime use Node 24.22.1, eight CPUs, 16 GiB, default heaps, absent NODE_OPTIONS, enforced zero task swap, network-disabled runtime, cleared credential environment, and private exact-lock dependencies. Fixed model delays remain 250 ms for `long01` and 2,000 ms for burst. Native seed/post-RPC continuity must remain exactly 8,192 bytes.
- Run six separately tagged diagnostic qualification observations first. Their timings are excluded from acceptance. Observe actual model-request counts during qualification and bind those facts later; no new counts are assumed here.
- Acceptance contains 30 new observations: five serial interleaved main→PR pairs for whole-generation `long01` cold, five pairs for `long01` warm using a separate sacrificial warm-up session, and five pairs for cold correlated `s01` burst across ten physical sessions. Keep cold and warm populations separate.
- Use the new `repair199040-` tag namespace. Freeze the exact order, source/commit/tree/dist/lock/image/environment, committed workload, fixture, native-build bindings, and observed qualification/model-work facts before the first acceptance observation. Every required input must be bound before timing; the native build, workload binding, qualification, and series are currently pending.
- Measure whole-process CPU including all workers, separately observed main-thread CPU, complete compaction RPC wall time, process RSS, worker-local/lifecycle memory with scopes named, parse/hydration/work counts, and summary overlap. Do not sum thread RSS or noncoincident heap maxima. Main-thread CPU, memory, continuity, selected inputs, and burst concurrency must hold.
- Require a measurable process-CPU reduction, not merely avoidance of a large regression. A 20% or greater process-CPU or RPC median or p95 regression in ANY required population stops performance acceptance. Keep every smaller adverse move visible; landing with such tradeoffs requires explicit owner acceptance. This protocol grants no merge authority.
- Report n, median, nearest-rank p95, minimum/maximum and spread for each arm/population. With five observations per arm, p95 is the maximum. No pooling, outlier removal, fsync subtraction, relabeling, or retries/replacement of failed tags; retain every failure and adverse result.
- Keep prior original-199040 30 observations and six qualifiers, #196550’s 110 observations, frozen15e80 and old35 immutable and excluded. The original15e +58.2387% cold-long01 RPC-p95 landing gate is NOT waived.
- Coverage remains one whole observed generation plus one correlated source replay, not a broad corpus. Fixed mock summaries establish runtime/continuity, not provider summary quality; post-compaction unrelated RPC probes do not establish during-compaction responsiveness.

**No new native qualification or acceptance timing is reported here. The new repair remains unmeasured and performance acceptance is pending.**

### ORIGINAL 12ad protocol — completed negative comparison

Compare matching merged-main architecture base `8857554b178506f962068509227e5c10ebe6cc8a` against candidate `12ad15841a49778e9d9c0b6b9af1511fe5e20d0a`. Use the existing committed canonical real-Gateway workload with minimally adapted source admission, new build/workload bindings, default heaps, zero task swap, matched mock-model work, and separate qualifications.

- Full observed generation `long01`, cold and sacrificial-session warm: five serial interleaved pairs each.
- Correlated `s01` replay/stress burst on ten physical sessions, cold: five pairs. The workload retains synthetic seed anchors and is not ten independent real histories.
- Total: **30 new acceptance observations**, after separately tagged compatibility/continuity qualification. Exact order, source/dist/lock/image/workload/fixture bindings, and observed model-request counts must be frozen before acceptance timing. No original observations are rerun, altered, or pooled.
- Report all adverse results and cold/warm groups separately: process CPU includes workers; main-thread CPU is observed separately; nearest-rank p95 is the maximum with five samples. A 20% or greater CPU/RPC median or p95 regression in any required population stops performance acceptance. Memory and burst concurrency must hold; reduced work must produce a measured benefit before a performance-success claim.

### ORIGINAL 12ad completed comparison — no consistent CPU benefit

Five observations per arm per population, serial main→PR pairs. CPU is whole-process CPU-seconds; RPC is wall-clock seconds. With n=5, nearest-rank p95 equals the maximum.

| Population | CPU median, main→PR | Change | CPU p95, main→PR | RPC median, main→PR | RPC p95, main→PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| long01 cold | 5.087→5.229 | +2.81% | 5.358→5.763 | 2.564→2.527 | 2.629→3.005 |
| long01 warm | 2.054→2.043 | −0.56% | 2.424→2.583 | 1.645→1.641 | 1.675→1.696 |
| correlated ten-session burst | 13.942→14.057 | +0.82% | 14.158→14.677 | 12.809→12.785 | 12.901→12.999 |

No process-CPU/RPC median or p95 cell crossed 20%, but avoiding a large regression is not the required CPU benefit. Process-CPU p95 worsened **7.57%, 6.54%, 3.66%** and RPC p95 worsened **14.30%, 1.26%, 0.76%** for cold, warm and burst respectively. All values remain included. **Recommendation: do not land this as a proven CPU optimization.** No ready, merge, close or source-revert action was performed.

<details>
<summary>Main-thread CPU, memory, integrity, and exact proof bindings</summary>

| Population | Main-thread CPU median (ms), main→PR | Change | RPC-window process RSS median (MiB), main→PR | Change | Worker-local observed heap median (MiB), main→PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| long01 cold | 772.316→751.279 | −2.72% | 1818.1→1820.0 | +0.10% | 102.65→100.64 |
| long01 warm | 153.556→163.486 | +6.47% | 2002.7→2030.4 | +1.38% | 102.64→98.43 |
| correlated burst | 1558.007→1605.798 | +3.07% | 2082.5→2070.0 | −0.60% | 102.85→93.49 |

Main-thread CPU p95 changes: +0.19%, +19.05%, +1.58%. Lifecycle-process RSS median changes: +0.26%, +1.57%, −1.58%; warm lifecycle includes sacrificial warm-up. Worker-local observed heap median changes: −1.96%, −4.11%, −9.10%. Worker CPU/RSS are already included in process totals; thread RSS and noncoincident heap maxima are not summed. CPU sampling overhang and all smaller adverse tradeoffs are retained in the full distributions linked through the work session.

Both arms matched two successful agent-summary requests for long01 and forty for burst, with zero utility requests or aborted/failed requests. Burst summary overlap was ten on both arms in all ten observations. Concurrency was preserved, not increased. Fixed mock summaries prove runtime/continuity, not provider quality. The selected comparison covers one whole observed generation and one correlated source replay, not a broad corpus. Unrelated RPC probes run after compaction, so no during-compaction responsiveness benefit is claimed.

Both exact sourcePerformance builds used Node 24.22.1, eight CPUs, 16 GiB, default heaps, absent NODE_OPTIONS, zero task swap, network-disabled runtime, cleared environment and read-only source/private exact-lock dependencies. The reviewed task-local workload is commit `e2df83a57b2be282501c1d667d78406cd41e0ca6`; its five rig/turn/mock/importer/observer owners remain byte-identical to common workload `0df6facf1c0c476ad922a4cec550dd49f42b8b05`. Eleven workload-admission/native-metadata contracts passed; those synthetic contracts are separate from the actual native proof.

The canonical invocation was `python3 TOOLING/run-series.py --root ROOT --runtime-cases ROOT/runtime-cases.json --performance-order ROOT/performance-order.json`, with TOOLING staged from the committed workload and all inputs bound before timing. Full per-arm n/median/p95/min/max distributions, parse/hydration counts, model work, source/dist/lock bindings, host load and all thirty original receipt hashes are retained with the work-session report.

- Acceptance freeze: `dbeefd164fd4e6a585fc81598aa839c2ee92e0abcb524d3ed9f7121eddd20fc8`.
- Plan: `4a0e11d38f466647170a26d3657fb2729f37a8a9904fc3b66a3389a38030830d`.
- Runtime cases: `1aabdff5573ca124df9b5ae35e520043b43291f40a39093edb2c30e3a73da728`.
- Canonical aggregate: `143ac92bdf57d0049a5d4274ba5274e42ba7536b545996157f449d4b5ec250da`.

The original 110-observation comparison, frozen15e80, old35 and six qualification timings remain immutable and excluded. This result does not waive the distinct original15e +58.2387% cold-long01 RPC-p95 landing gate.

</details>

Requested by @RomneyDa; follow-up repair requested by @vincentkoc.

prs.title: fix(diagnostics): report stuck-session force-clears as force-clears
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`recoverStuckDiagnosticSession` collapses two different recovery outcomes into one. A force-clear, which releases a lane without stopping any run, is reported with `status: "aborted"` and `action: "abort_embedded_run"`:

```ts
const action = aborted || forceCleared ? "abort_embedded_run" : "release_lane";
```

Issue #145152 documents the consequence: on the reported incident the recovery path fired about 67 times in a day and every one of those lines reported a success it had not achieved. An operator reading the diagnostics cannot tell a real reclaim from a no-op, which is what kept that incident invisible for over an hour.

ClawSweeper's review of that issue names this specific defect as source-proven and points at the evidence: an existing integration case expects `status=aborted` while `aborted` is `false`.

### Scope

This change fixes **one** of the five defects listed in #145152: the misreported outcome. The other four (queue accounting, ownership validation, the generation fence across awaited cleanup, and releasing the lane by session id) are deliberately left in the issue. It does not overlap with #145444, which addresses reply-owner recovery in `runs.ts`; the only file both touch is the shared integration test.

### Change

- `force_cleared` becomes a distinct outcome status next to `aborted`, so a release that stopped nothing no longer reads as a run that was aborted.
- The action follows the outcome: an abort reports `abort_embedded_run`, a force-clear reports its own action.
- A shared type guard covers the places that legitimately treat both reclaim outcomes alike, so existing accounting keeps working.

## Evidence

The existing integration case that pinned the wrong behaviour is updated rather than removed. It asserted `status=aborted` for a run that was not aborted; it now asserts the force-clear outcome. That is the correction of a pinned misreport, not a relaxed assertion. The opposite direction is covered by the existing case `releases a wedged lane after a clean abort when session work remains queued`, which asserts `status=aborted` with `aborted=true`, `drained=true` and `forceCleared=false`, so a genuine abort is still reported as an abort.

Measured on the branch head:

- `vitest run src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-followup-recovery.integration.test.ts`: **2 files passed, 21 tests passed**
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json`: clean, exit 0


### Update after merging main (2026-10-03)

Main's #161759 added worker claim-recovery cases in `src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-launcher.claim-recovery.test.ts` that also pinned the folded values (`status: "aborted"`, `action: "abort_embedded_run"`). Those cases keep the second turn blocked past the 15-second abort settle window, so `abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun` force-clears the lane (`forceCleared=true`). Their expectation now follows the split, like the integration case above. This is the same telemetry transition described under "Operator transition", not an additional behavior change.

Measured locally on `5971deb1308` (not a claim about the GitHub CI run):

- `pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-launcher.claim-recovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 1 file, 18 tests passed
- `pnpm deadcode:full` (knip): exit 0
- `oxlint --type-aware` on both files changed in that follow-up: 0 warnings, 0 errors
- `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet` and `pnpm check:max-lines-ratchet`: OK

### Update after merging main (2026-10-11)

Merged main `89c406eb613` in `3d15547b3a0`, without conflicts. Since the previous merge (`24bdc542d27`), main had changed nine of the ten files in this PR. `94a10ebb129` adds one sentence this PR had missed: `docs/gateway/opentelemetry/model-calls-and-metrics.md` named only `aborted` and `released` as the outcomes that mark diagnostic session state idle, while the coordinator treats `force_cleared` the same way. `9763b150a1e` removes the acknowledged-abort integration case this PR had added: the existing case `releases a wedged lane after a clean abort when session work remains queued` uses the same setup and asserts a superset (`status=aborted`, `action=abort_embedded_run`, `aborted=true`, `drained=true`, `forceCleared=false`, `released=1`).

The misreport is still present outside this branch: `const action = aborted || forceCleared ? "abort_embedded_run" : "release_lane";` is at `src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts:423` on main `48a348028fb` and at line 460 in `v2026.10.1` (`e178c39e9aa`).

Measured locally (not a claim about the GitHub CI run):

- On the merge `3d15547b3a0`, `pnpm test <14 files> --maxWorkers=1`: 14 files, 316 tests passed, 582 s wall time including worker preparation. Besides the four test files of this PR, the set covers every unit and integration test that calls the real recovery owner or asserts its outcome, including files main changed or added since the previous merge (`diagnostic-stuck-session-exec-deadline`, `question.recovery`, `agent-tools.before-tool-call.approval-recovery`, the worker launcher and run-owner suites, and the diagnostics-otel and diagnostics-prometheus service tests). After `9763b150a1e` the integration file passes 16 of 16.
- The four test files of this PR against the recovery owner of main `89c406eb613` (runtime, outcome types, coordinator and event types taken from main, tests from this branch): 13 of 99 tests fail, each receiving `status: "aborted"` and `action: "abort_embedded_run"` where a force-clear is expected, for example with `aborted: false, forceCleared: true, released: 1`. On the merge all 99 pass.
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files, the conflict-marker check, `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet` and `git diff --check`: passed. The core typecheck and the type-aware lint ran out of memory on the test host; CI covers both.

CI on `94a10ebb129` ([run 38129764936](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38129764936)): `check-prod-types`, `check-test-types` (core 1 to 5), `check-lint` (core 1 to 5), `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` and `check-guards` passed. Three jobs failed, none of them in code this PR touches:

- `checks-node-changed-compact-large-25`: three `patchMany` cases in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-mutations.catalog-queue.test.ts` lose `providerOverride` and `modelOverride`. The same three cases fail today in CI runs of other branches ([run 38128733264](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38128733264), [run 38129123872](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38129123872), [run 38128804209](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38128804209)), and all 14 cases of that file pass locally on this head.
- `checks-ui-e2e (4/9)`: `ui/src/e2e/sidebar-roster.e2e.test.ts` waits for a workspace menu to close after Escape in a mobile viewport (`expected 1 to be +0`). Nothing under `ui/` imports the modules this PR changes or uses the recovery status values.
- `openclaw/ci-gate`: aggregates the two jobs above.

Still open from the review: a run through the scheduled watchdog of an installed Gateway. As stated under "Exact limits", the runtime proof below enters the coordinator directly. A Gateway run needs a built Gateway, which this update did not include.

Refs #145152


## Runtime and telemetry proof (2026-09-14)

Plain Node/tsx before/after runs exercised the actual recovery owner, command
lanes, reply and embedded-run registries, recovery coordinator, diagnostic broker,
`diagnostics-otel` service and OTLP/protobuf exporter. The 15-second settlement
windows elapsed in wall-clock time. No Vitest, fake timers or mocked recovery,
registry, event or exporter functions were used.

Tested runtime: `3e06eab3abdd39c2c9f1ab1e51d8722b5e07e9f4`. Later commits merge main and adjust
operator documentation, type exports and test expectations; the outcome
classification block is unchanged. The before comparison uses the exact pre-PR recovery-owner
file from `ee6a7ef0cb5`, with remaining components held constant; it is not a boot
of the entire old release.

| Scenario | Actual flags: aborted / drained / forceCleared | Before status | After status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reply owner never acknowledges cancellation | false / false / true | aborted | force_cleared |
| Owner acknowledges cancellation and drains | true / true / false | aborted | aborted |
| Registered handle accepts abort but never ends within 15 seconds | true / false / true | aborted | force_cleared |

The actual coordinator emitted `session.recovery.completed` with matching
status/action and no stale-result flag in all six cases. Queued work drained and
all lane queues became empty. The timeout case uses a real registered run handle,
not a mocked `abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun` result.

Selected after-run terminal output (synthetic identities omitted):

```text
stuck recovery: reply owner settlement timed out ... settleMs=15000
stuck session recovery outcome: status=force_cleared action=force_clear_embedded_run ... aborted=false drained=false forceCleared=true released=1 queuedCount=1
stuck session recovery outcome: status=aborted action=abort_embedded_run ... aborted=true drained=true forceCleared=false released=1 queuedCount=1
wait timeout: ... timeoutMs=15000
stuck session recovery outcome: status=force_cleared action=force_clear_embedded_run ... aborted=true drained=false forceCleared=true released=1 queuedCount=1
PROOF_PASS before elapsedMs=30642
PROOF_PASS after elapsedMs=30713
```

### Actual event-to-exporter receipt

The task-owned loopback HTTP collector received `application/x-protobuf` from
the real plugin exporter. `protobufjs` decoded the received OTLP wire payload;
assertions checked the metric name, values and both label dimensions:

```text
metric: openclaw.session.recovery.completed
before: value=3 openclaw.status=aborted       openclaw.action=abort_embedded_run
after:  value=2 openclaw.status=force_cleared openclaw.action=force_clear_embedded_run
after:  value=1 openclaw.status=aborted       openclaw.action=abort_embedded_run
```

### Operator transition

`docs/logging.md` now documents the new event values and exported attributes.
Queries counting all run reclaims must include `force_cleared` alongside
`aborted`, or `force_clear_embedded_run` alongside `abort_embedded_run` for action
filters. Keep them separate when measuring acknowledged aborts. Queue accounting
is unchanged. The docs-only follow-up passed the repository formatter and
`git diff --check`.

### Exact limits

The backend work and loopback collector are synthetic. SDK specifiers resolve to
the real source facades. The eligibility request enters the actual coordinator
directly; this does not claim the full scheduled watchdog, an external provider,
or an installed Gateway run. No production Gateway/configuration/credentials or
channel was used. Force-clear proves release of recovery ownership, not that
remote work stopped. The standalone driver, raw logs, protobuf payloads and
decoded assertions are preserved together for reproduction.

### Additional installed-Gateway observation (2026-10-11)

On an isolated, unchanged installed 2026.9.9-based Gateway (not this PR head), the scheduled watchdog reclaimed two sessions stalled in plugin tool calls after 905/906 seconds. A loopback synthetic provider was used; no production session was changed. Both outcomes were `status=aborted action=abort_embedded_run aborted=true drained=true forceCleared=false released=0`. Even the tool that ignored its AbortSignal ended as an acknowledged abort: stale-reply takeover superseded the session writer and the run ended about 0.3 seconds after the abort. The PR intentionally preserves this classification.

This is **not** installed-Gateway proof of the changed force-clear branch. prs.title: fix(talk): voice consults fail when the chat runs on Claude CLI or a locked native harness
prs.body:
Closes #199378

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Talk voice consults fail with `No API key found for provider anthropic` when the chat's model runs on the Claude CLI runtime, and are refused with `Model selection is locked` when the chat is locked to a native harness such as Codex, even though typed messages in the same chat work.

## User Impact

User impact: a voice consult answers from the same chat, with the same runtime, owner, sender and tool permissions, as a typed message. Claude CLI and native-harness chats can now be consulted by voice. Plugin and channel voice bridges (Google Meet, voice-call) are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway Talk adapter (`src/gateway/talk/client-agent-runtime.ts`) admitted the consult and then called the embedded runner directly, bypassing the runtime selection that a typed turn gets from the agent command owner. The embedded runner then used the direct provider API, which a CLI subscription login does not authorize.

Key tenets for review:

- **Same path as a typed turn.** The adapter keeps its exact-source acquisition, controller-input custody, retained operator authority, operational-instance binding and terminal-write drain. Only its final call changes, from `runEmbeddedAgent` to `agentCommandFromGatewayIngress`. The command's own session turn inherits the Talk claim, so no second controller input is reserved.
- **Same authority, nothing wider.** It forwards the caller's owner bit, tool cap, tool bindings, client caps, approval reviewer, elevated defaults, sender id, operator authority and source assertion. `allowModelOverride` is false; per-run thinking uses `thinkingOnce`, so the chat's persisted thinking and verbose settings are untouched. The new `normalizeThinkingLevelOverride` option is Gateway-only and cleared for public ingress.
- **Abort still revokes immediately.** It uses `closeAdmittedRunDelegatedAuthority` via `onAdmittedRunContext`, the same primitive the previous prepared admission closed.
- **Same plugin runtime as a typed turn.** The consult borrows the Gateway's published reply runtime, leased for the session's model and harness as a Gateway `agent` turn is (`client-agent-runtime-dispatch.ts`). Hosts with no published owner keep the command owner's own loading.
- **Thinking level is a preference.** A configured `talk.consultThinkingLevel` falls back to a level the chat's model supports instead of failing, matching chat-backed Talk in #194184. Without one, the chat's own level applies (the Gateway path no longer forces `"high"`). An explicit user `--thinking` is still rejected when unsupported.
- **Model-selection lock.** The Talk-side refusal is skipped only for this Gateway path (`dispatchesInSessionRuntime`), because the session's runtime now owns the lock and pinned harnesses override runtime selection. That path rejects provider/model overrides. Plugin bridges keep the refusal.
- **Workspace.** When the consult's workspace is the agent workspace, its guarded preparation uses the typed turn's bootstrap policy. Otherwise a brand-new agent whose first turn is a voice consult would hit `WorkspaceVanishedError` when the command owner prepares the same directory.
- **Metadata.** `projectOutboundPayloadPlanForJson` now keeps private `ReplyPayload` metadata on the projected objects. It never serializes, so the wire shape is unchanged. Talk still drops answers to earlier queued inputs (`precedingInputAnswer`) instead of speaking them twice.

Deliberate behavior changes:

- A Talk caller revoked mid-consult now gets the typed turn's delivery-fence rejection instead of hearing the model's text; the native effect was already fenced.
- Ordinary command-owned session bookkeeping (model and usage accounting) now happens for Gateway voice consults, as for typed turns.

<details>
<summary>Test fixture changes in existing suites</summary>

- `client-gateway-control.agent-consult.test.ts` and `client-gateway-control.mailbox.test.ts` mocked the removed seam. They now mock the command owner with `client-agent-runtime.command-owner.test-support.ts` (admission from the forwarded authority, then the run).
- `client-permission-parity.test.ts` asserts the session exec pin on `execSession`, from which exec defaults resolve. The revoked-source case expects the rejection above.
- `server.talk-consult-history.test.ts`: the per-test reset deletes the workspace directory but kept its 24-hour attestation, which the command owner's real workspace preparation correctly reads as a vanished workspace. The reset now retires the workspace state too.
- `handlers/client-native-control.test-support.ts`: the 1-second registration deadline now starts when the backend is entered, since session and model preparation now precede it. `handlers/client-native-control.test.ts` waits for typed-turn finalization before checking the spoken answer.
- `config/test-lines-allocations/talk-consult-session-runtime.txt`: 300 lines over the allowance for the real-Gateway runtime-routing, handoff-authority, lease and thinking regressions.

</details>

## Evidence

**Real Gateway, stock vs patched** (`src/gateway/server.talk-consult-session-runtime.test.ts`; real admission, runtime selection and dispatch; only `runCliAgent`/`runEmbeddedAgent` are spied):

| Case | Stock | Patched |
|---|---|---|
| Claude CLI chat, relay consult | `No API key found for provider anthropic` | reaches `runCliAgent` with `provider: claude-cli`, `senderIsOwner: true`, same session; embedded runner not called; no voice tool cap |
| Chat locked to `codex` | `Model selection is locked for this session` | routed to the pinned `codex` harness, which this fixture does not install, so it fails closed with the harness-unavailable error |

**Other red/green regressions:**

- Command owner: an unsupported machine thinking preference falls back. Stock: `Thinking level "off" is not supported for openai/account-reasoner`. The explicit-command rejection test still passes.
- Core consult: lock and thinking are left to the session runtime only on the Gateway path; bridge defaults are unchanged. Stock fails with `ModelSelectionLockedError`.
- Payload projection keeps metadata without serializing it. Stock: `undefined`.

**Affected suites, patched** (forks pool, one worker):

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `server.talk-consult-session-runtime` (new, real Gateway) | 2 passed |
| `client-agent-runtime-dispatch` (new) | 5 passed |
| `client-agent-runtime.scope` | 17 passed |
| `talk/agent-consult-runtime` / `.storage` | 17 / 8 passed |
| `client-gateway-control.agent-consult` / `.mailbox` | 17 / 6 passed |
| `client-agent-consult.terminal-writes` / `client-permission-parity` / `client-authority` | 3 / 4 / 2 passed |
| `handlers/client` / `native-consult-target` / `client-native-actions` | 16 / 38 / 14 passed |
| `server.talk-consult-history` | 19 passed, 3 Linux-only skipped |
| `infra/outbound/payloads` | 28 passed |
| `commands/agent` | 62 passed |
| `handlers/client-native-control` | 10 passed, 4 failed (see below) |

`client-native-control.test.ts` has the same four cancel-case failures with or without this change; they are #198523, red on `main`.

Scoped oxlint: 0 warnings, 0 errors on the 21 changed files. `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` pass. Test-line ratchet OK: +689 lines against a 400 allowance plus 300 allocated.

Not yet shown: a live voice consult on an authenticated Gateway. A hands-on device test is pending, and this stays a draft until it is done.

### Live prerequisite checks (November 15, 2026)

Two running Gateways were exercised with the same synthetic 24 kHz PCM question: patched `06cf0e1e961` and unpatched `1cb1b4570f9`. Both throwaway chats resolved to `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`, runtime `claude-cli`; typed turns completed as owner with `TYPED_CLI_OK`.

```text
Input transcript: Please ask the agent to count how many markdown files are in the top level of its workspace. Use its tools to check the exact count now.
xAI output transcript: Let me check that for you.
Provider event: toolCall name=openclaw_agent_consult
Server consult run: none
```

This does not establish consult completion. The xAI provider-direct relay emits a client tool call; its client handler already uses `chat.send`, outside this repair. The alternate server-owned fallback (`consultRouting=force-agent-consult`, tested only on the patched throwaway Gateway) refuses session creation because xAI requires automatic server-VAD responses. Its explicit provider guard requires `provider-direct`. The test setting was restored; the unpatched production control session was deleted and its configuration was not changed. Successful authenticated server-runner proof still requires a realtime provider that supports that route.

AI-assisted (Claude Opus 5.5 via OpenClaw); reviewed by a second model.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes /steer and /redirect reporting a finished action while it is still in progress.

prs.title: fix(talk): dictation fails to start when the voice-note model's provider has no key
prs.body:
Closes #199417

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Talk dictation fails to start when a voice-note speech-to-text model (`tools.media`) is picked whose provider has no key, even though the streaming transcription provider Talk picks by itself still has one.

## User Impact

Picking a voice-note model on Settings → Talk leaves Talk dictation working. While that model can't run, Talk keeps using the streaming provider that has a key, and `talk.catalog` reports it as ready. A voice-note model that can run keeps precedence for Talk. With no usable provider at all, the error still says to check `tools.media.models`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildTalkTranscriptionConfig` decides which path Talk transcription uses, for both `talk.session.create` and `talk.catalog`. With no Voice Call streaming provider and no `agents.defaults.voiceModel` set, it takes the `tools.media` path only when one of those models can run, or when no streaming provider can be selected automatically either. In that last case the error and the catalog still point at `tools.media.models`.

## Evidence

Isolated Gateway built from this branch and from `main` (41f2b981d24), with a placeholder `OPENAI_API_KEY`, no Deepgram key and `deepgram/nova-3` as the voice-note model:

| Run | `talk.catalog` transcription | `talk.session.create` (`mode: "transcription"`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `main` | `ready: false`, only `deepgram` listed | `UNAVAILABLE: No configured audio transcription provider is available; check tools.media.models` |
| `main` without the voice-note model | `ready: true`, `activeProvider: "openai"` | session starts on `openai` |
| this branch | `ready: true`, `activeProvider: "openai"` | session starts on `openai` |

A second live run on this branch (45dec686c37) used a real OpenAI key with the same keyless voice-note model: Talk picked `openai`, started the transcription session and accepted audio. A full transcript wasn't verified, because the test key had no credits.

Tests:

- New case in `src/gateway/talk/handlers/file-transcription.test.ts` (keyless voice-note model plus a ready streaming provider): fails on `main` (`talk.catalog` reports `ready: false`), passes with the fix. All 23 tests in that file pass, including the existing cases for a missing key with no streaming provider and for explicit provider, model and Voice Call streaming selection.
- `catalog.test.ts` (17), `catalog-speech.test.ts` (10), `provider-discovery.test.ts` (1) and `file-transcription.clawrouter.test.ts` (1) pass.
- Core and core-test typechecks, lint and formatting on the changed files are clean.

prs.title: fix(infer): sanitize terminal controls in human output
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The shared inference human-output formatters can emit terminal controls from legal input or provider/result values. For example, `infer embedding create` sends text containing screen-clear/cursor/title sequences unchanged to its configured provider, then prints those sequences as raw terminal bytes.

## User Impact

Shared human envelopes and provider summaries use the existing terminal text policy. Metadata, errors, paths and scalar displays stay on owned lines; output text retains real newlines and Unicode, and tabs display as literal `\t`. Structured `--json` output and provider input preserve their original values.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply existing `terminalText`/`sanitizeTerminalText` at the complete shared display owner. Reuse the existing transcripts per-LF pattern for multiline text. Human serialized values also need this boundary because JSON.stringify leaves C1/bidi controls. Seven inference families share the owner; no per-field renderer, new escape algorithm, public option or caller policy is added.

prs.title: fix(cli): reject nonregular model image inputs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `infer model run --file` can wait indefinitely when an image path names a FIFO without a writer. The shared image loader calls `readFile` before checking image type, so neither local nor Gateway probes reach dispatch or report an unsupported input.

## User Impact

User impact: nonregular image inputs fail promptly with the affected path and a recovery instruction. Regular images and image symlinks continue to reach the model with the original input path and exact image bytes. No new per-file or aggregate byte limit is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing core `readRegularFile` owner, resolving the input first to retain supported symlink paths. That owner rejects nonregular files before opening and validates the opened descriptor with nonblocking flags. The import stays lazy inside the image-only branch. Existing MIME detection, HEIC conversion, input metadata and local/Gateway dispatch remain with their current owners.

## Evidence

### Current-head integration and actual behavior — 2026-11-14 UTC

**Product head:** `50c1828fe4df64fb0f9e5e092bdd3c237f231075`. Integrated main: `08ae8c62b83ede02db3a8d2bc3ce36206008d253` through an ordinary two-parent merge; contributor history is retained, with no force-push.

Resolved the real model-run conflict against main while preserving the complete new nested runner, cancellation flow, MIME/conversion behavior and original descriptor-aware file admission.

- **Production entry / canonical owner:** Built `openclaw.mjs infer model run --local --model image-proof/image-proof --prompt "Describe this image" --file INPUT --json` -> shared image admission -> canonical regular-file reader -> actual completion adapter.
- **Exact frozen collector:** `node proof-model-files.mjs CHECKOUT green`. Normal build: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts cliStartup`; clean tracked tree and matching build stamp verified before and after the actual run.
- **Recorder / readback / legal controls:** Regular PNG and its symlink each dispatch one actual HTTP/SSE completion request with the original image bytes and return the recorder reply. A FIFO without a writer exits1 without opening the FIFO and without dispatch; an ordinary text file exits1 with the existing unsupported-image diagnostic and no dispatch. Full native syscall traces, CLI stdout/stderr and HTTP request payloads are linked below.
- **Acceptance RED:** retained original baseline and collector observations in the historical section below. This integration receipt claims exact-head GREEN and controls; it does not relabel earlier BASE runs as a new main execution.
- **Inspectable evidence:** [collector, complete sanitized streams, exact-head receipt, hashes and independent review](https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/tree/f54f88d71d6f05ab7c462f8e7206a806aaff4458). All uploaded bytes were read back and SHA256-verified. Proof artifacts are kept in an evidence-only orphan commit, outside this product branch.
- **Supporting checks:** 122 focused owner tests pass. Changed-file format, type-aware lint and semantic types pass; clean normal `cliStartup` build passes. Fresh independent adversarial review: PASS, no P0–P3 findings, using the user-authorized GPT6.1Sol fallback; no official autoreview-tool execution is claimed.
- **Cleanup / impact:** task-only HOME/config/state and synthetic fixtures; recorder and owned child processes stopped. No production model/account/channel/Gateway state was used or changed. No added options/defaults, dependencies, config/protocol/schema, permissions, persisted format or migration changes.
- **Limitations:** Linux FIFO/symlink admission and local production completion adapter only. No native Windows/macOS, live Gateway dispatch, external provider or whole-repository suite is claimed. Hosted required CI and the durable public review are tracked separately; local checks do not establish either.

      workerWait=fs.readFileSync(tracePath,'utf8').split('\n').find(x=>x.includes('openat(') && x.includes(JSON.stringify(file)) && x.includes('O_RDONLY') && x.includes('<unfinished ...>'));
      if (workerWait) {
        blockedAt=Date.now();
        // A controlled writer releases the observed product wait, allowing clean exit.
        setTimeout(()=>{
          const fd=fs.openSync(file,fs.constants.O_WRONLY|fs.constants.O_NONBLOCK);
          fs.writeSync(fd,'not an image\n'); fs.closeSync(fd); releasedAt=Date.now();
        },1000);
      }
    } catch {}
  },100) : undefined;
  const terminal=await new Promise((resolve,reject)=>{child.once('error',reject); child.once('close',(code,signal)=>resolve({code,signal}));});
  clearTimeout(timer); clearInterval(monitor);
  assert.equal(terminal.signal,null,'Unobserved fixture/process timeouts are not acceptance RED');
  const row={label,args,...terminal,stdout:Buffer.concat(out).toString('utf8'),stderr:Buffer.concat(err).toString('utf8'),elapsedMs:Date.now()-startedAt,blockedAt,releasedAt,workerWait,tracePath,traceSha256:f.hash(fs.readFileSync(tracePath))};
  f.receipt.runs.push(row); console.log(JSON.stringify({label,code:row.code,elapsedMs:row.elapsedMs,workerWait}));
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(f.root,'receipt.json'),JSON.stringify(f.receipt,null,2));
  return row;
}
try {
  const image=path.join(f.root,'image.png'), link=path.join(f.root,'linked.png'), fifo=path.join(f.root,'input.pipe'), text=path.join(f.root,'input.txt');
  fs.writeFileSync(image,png); fs.symlinkSync(image,link); fs.writeFileSync(text,'not an image\n'); execFileSync('mkfifo',[fifo]);
  for (const [name,file] of [['regular-png',image],['symlink-png',link]]) {
    const before=requests.length; const r=await run(name,file); assert.equal(r.code,0,r.stderr); assert.match(r.stdout,/image proof reply/); assert.equal(requests.length,before+1);
    const attached=requests.at(-1).content.find(p=>p.type==='image_url').image_url.url;
    assert.equal(attached,`data:image/png;base64,${png.toString('base64')}`);
  }
  const before=requests.length; const r=await run('fifo-rejection',fifo,true); assert.equal(r.code,1,r.stderr); assert.equal(requests.length,before);
  // JSON stdout carries the diagnostic; stderr renders the generic failure banner.
  // The acceptance boundary is the traced FIFO open and absence of provider dispatch.
  assert.match(r.stderr,/The CLI command failed/);
  if(f.phase==='red'){assert.match(r.workerWait,/openat\(.+O_RDONLY.+<unfinished/);assert.ok(r.releasedAt-r.blockedAt>=900);assert.match(JSON.parse(r.stdout).error.message,/Only image files are supported/);}
  else {assert.equal(r.blockedAt,undefined);assert.equal(fs.readFileSync(r.tracePath,'utf8').includes(JSON.stringify(fifo)),false);assert.match(JSON.parse(r.stdout).error.message,/regular file.*retry/);}
  const t=await run('text-rejection',text);assert.equal(t.code,1,t.stderr);assert.match(JSON.parse(t.stdout).error.message,/Only image files are supported/);assert.equal(requests.length,before);
  assert.deepEqual(fs.readFileSync(image),png);assert.equal(fs.statSync(fifo).isFIFO(),true);
  f.receipt.requests=requests; f.finish();
} finally {server.closeAllConnections();await new Promise(resolve=>server.close(resolve));}

prs.title: fix: Codex sign-in import fails on busy Linux hosts when process cleanup exceeds 2 s
prs.body:
Closes #195425

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw models auth login --provider openai` fails with "The Codex credential reader could not stop. No credential was imported." on a busy Linux host (~950 processes).

## User Impact

User impact: Linux users on busy or large hosts can import a Codex sign-in again. Hosts that were already fast see no change; the longer budget is only a ceiling for a stuck probe.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stopping the credential reader takes several full `/proc` snapshots under one shared deadline. At ~950 processes one snapshot took about 1.6 s, so the old 2 s budget expired, cleanup was reported `uncertain`, and the import was rejected. The budget is now one shared constant of 10 s (it was duplicated in two files). The rule that `uncertain` cleanup rejects the import, even when the root has exited, is unchanged: it protects descendant cleanup for a credential-bearing process, and an existing test asserts it.

## Evidence

- New test `completes a full snapshot of a busy host within the default containment budget` simulates 950 processes at ~3 ms each (about 2.9 s). Against the old 2 s constant it fails with `Process inspection exceeded its deadline`; with this change it passes.
- `extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-process-snapshot.test.ts`: 31 passed, 6 skipped (platform-specific).
- `extensions/codex/src/migration/provider.auth.test.ts`: 28 passed (includes the uncertain-cleanup rejection cases).
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` clean on the changed files.
- Before the fix, locally raising both constants to 15 s made the real login succeed on the affected host.

Related: #161341 reports the same message on Windows, which has a different cause (no process-tree cleanup) and is not addressed here.

prs.title: fix(systems): keep unknown device inventory neutral
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Systems claims there are no devices or search matches, and tells the user to choose a device, after its first device-inventory read fails.

## User Impact

User impact: an unknown device list stays neutral. The actual error, Retry and Refresh remain available, and accepted empty results, filtering, selection and offline recovery still work.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing accepted inventory owns whether device-dependent guidance is meaningful. The sidebar and workspace now use that fact rather than interpreting a finished request as a known inventory. Hidden placeholders retain their geometry; no new state, requests, loaders or recovery controls are introduced. Independently loaded backups remain visible.

Requested and co-authored by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/53cb60dd-b224-4e21-b03b-3e5042ea91f9)

## Evidence

- Reproduced in the actual compiled Control UI with a synthetic Gateway, at desktop 1280×900 and emulated phone 390×900. No live device or configuration changes.
- Pinned main `5fbdf6989130ed5`: the owning regression fails four assertions; both browser cases fail the six unsupported empty/choose-device assertions. Native Refresh recovery, real errors, accepted rows and genuine empty/no-match results still pass.
- Fixed independent branch: **36 focused tests and both browser cases pass**. Four additional actual-browser sibling cases pass in the combined audit checkout, covering desktop/phone reconnect recovery, touch-drawer controls and Mac desktop enablement.
- UI typecheck, touched-file lint and formatting pass. Existing strict-read diagnostics remain outside this presentation fix. Broad CI and independent automated review are not claimed complete.
- The normal inventory producer includes the Gateway host. Accepted-empty replies are explicit contract fixtures, not a claim that a running Gateway ordinarily has no host.

<details>
<summary>Ownership, history and scope</summary>

The original sidebar condition in #147519, filtering in #153224 and the Solid migration in #168871 all distinguished pending from finished without checking accepted inventory. #189365 added pending-only placeholder visibility to keep the desktop region steady; that intent is preserved across first-read failure. The authoritative environments-list handler returns an error when inventory discovery fails, not an accepted empty list.

Simplification review: one existing inventory owner, no new abstraction or persisted state; net +3 production lines. The +201 test lines cover initial failure, offline/reconnect, retained recovery, desktop/phone presentation and native Refresh follow-through. The regression lives in the bounded read-failure suite rather than exceeding the workspace suite’s line limit. Separate draft #199125 remains unchanged and is not bundled into this independent PR.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a plugin account badge that says “Connected” when OpenClaw has only read stored OAuth credentials, without checking the service.

## User Impact

The Accounts row now says **Sign-in saved**, so stored credentials are not mistaken for a working service connection. Sign-in, sign-out, credential storage, permissions, and tool execution are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The account badge comes from a read-only credential-status projection. It can report an authorized record even when its access token has expired; refresh and service access happen separately. The badge now describes that known state. The completed browser sign-in dialog remains **Signed in**, and API-key rows remain **Configured** because those controls have different meanings.

The MCP guide now distinguishes the completed sign-in dialog and saved-account badge from an actual service check. No probe, warning banner, state owner, or new interaction was added.

## Evidence

- 14 UI tests passed, covering sign-in, waiting for the authoritative account refresh, confirmation before sign-out, failed sign-out, unsupported access, navigation, reconnection, and cancellation settlement. The existing sign-in regression fails on main for the overstated badge and passes after the fix.
- 3 focused OAuth storage tests passed. The added boundary case saves a synthetic expired token through the real credential owner, reopens storage, and reads the same ordered status API consumed by plugin inspection. It still reports stored authorization without making a network request or refreshing the token. This is not a mock supplying the asserted status.
- 2 existing browser sign-in/error-recovery scenarios passed. Matched captures exercise the built Control UI plugin page with synthetic Gateway/account data, dark theme, and a 1440×1000 viewport. Before is verified main `c509b9dd44c129fec2e734f3b3590ce313577474`. Screenshots prove presentation; the storage and handler checks prove the boundary. No real account was changed or third-party service contacted.
- Scoped lint, UI typecheck, formatting, i18n baseline/verification, and diff checks passed. A first backend attempt was invalidated because I changed source during its shared worker compilation; the final unchanged-source run passed. An accidentally broad lint invocation was stopped and replaced with file-scoped checks.
- Simplification: one canonical-English string changes, with no production-code growth. The patch adds one 19-line storage-boundary case and updates an existing UI assertion; temporary capture scaffolding is not shipped. Focused UI tests took 2.44s; the backend run took 43.31s including cold compilation. PR CI timing is pending.

prs.title: fix(ui): distinguish disabling automations from pausing runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes misleading “Pause” and “Resume” controls for automations: disabling an automation cancels its active run rather than suspending it for later resumption.

## User Impact

Users see “Stop and disable” for an enabled automation with a recorded active run, “Disable” when idle, and “Enable” when disabled. Re-enabling restores eligibility for new runs; it does not resume the cancelled occurrence.

Cancellation, scheduling, permissions, saved definitions, and manual Start now behavior are unchanged. No migrations or additional confirmations.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing enablement update persists the definition and requests cancellation of active work. The shared row/detail control now describes that consequence, with matching tooltips and accessible names. Enabled/Disabled status wording also stays consistent in automation lists, filters, detail views, and desktop/mobile session summaries. An accepted update is not presented as proof that the run has stopped.

The label uses existing running-state evidence. The detail view reads the current selected-job facts, so the label changes when a run ends without replacing the control. No new state owner or operation was added.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/c4507bcf-b1bf-464e-a9df-2bc0344bbe58)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b53cbe3d-c351-4ef7-8863-86f84ec51a82)

## Evidence

- 73 focused UI tests, 14 browser scenarios, and 2 scheduler cancellation cases passed. Repeated runs are not double-counted.
- The new browser scenario fails on main for the four misleading row/detail action labels, then passes with the fix. It activates the real controls, observes the enablement update, preserves the still-running indication until authoritative runtime facts change, and verifies that enabling does not issue a manual run or chat-send request.
- Existing scheduler tests independently exercise actual disable/remove operations, cancellation signals, persisted terminal history, and run receipts. The browser fixture does not fabricate proof that cancellation completed.
- UI typecheck, formatting, i18n baseline/verification, and diff checks passed. Scoped lint passed on the original changed files. The subsequently corrected settings-layout test reports inherited max-lines debt (1,103 counted lines; limit 1,000); its unchanged-length line-cap ratchet passes. No limit or suppression was changed. Canonical English only; no foreign translation memory was hand-edited.
- [CI run 43636172945](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43636172945) exposed one old “Active / Paused” expectation in the responsive Automations layout test. Reproduced on the published head, corrected to “Enabled / Disabled,” and passed through `pnpm test:ci-failed 199163 --run`. All geometry assertions remain unchanged.
- Matched real Control UI production-build captures use synthetic Gateway data, dark theme, and a 1280×800 viewport. The displayed images crop the same page region. Before is verified main at `da85264b9eab47c6e1aba4ddbd43e3e396d66344`. No live automation or external job was triggered. The test-only CI repair does not change these images.
- Simplification/self-review: eight net production lines, existing state and controls reused. Independent agent review was not launched under this session’s no-subagent restriction.

prs.title: fix(ui): name tool interruption in the pending-message action
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a misleading “Send now” action beneath pending guidance: clicking it interrupts supported running tools, rather than simply transmitting a message.

## User Impact

The action now says “Interrupt tools and send,” so users can see the consequence before clicking. Normal Send, Stop, queue order, interruption permissions, and the continuing agent run are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The control calls the existing tool-interruption operation for the exact run holding the pending message. Tool cleanup and its interruption result precede delivery; it does not cancel the whole agent run. The new label describes that boundary without adding a warning, confirmation, or new behavior.

This translation key has one owning presentation consumer, which provides both the visible label and accessible button name. The relevant documentation and existing test selectors now use the same label. Blocked and unavailable states retain their quiet waiting text.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix: apply output reducers in headless and Code Mode calls
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes enabled tool-output reducers silently being skipped in headless runs and nested Code Mode tool calls.

## User Impact

Enabled middleware such as Tokenjuice can transform actual OpenClaw tool results before they reach the agent, including nested Code Mode shell calls. Exact file/schema results and the surrounding JavaScript envelope retain their existing contracts. Bounded-command guidance now recommends the existing terminal-result collection path instead of avoidable short-yield/poll cycles.

No new configuration, dependencies, permission changes, or migrations. Native Codex shell results remain outside this replacement path. This PR does not claim a whole-task token-savings percentage.

## Why This Change Was Made

Headless runs prepare a scoped plugin generation, but middleware discovery consulted the process-global registry and could select no callback or a different same-ID root plugin. Discovery now follows the current context and its prepared lazy-load inputs. Native catalog calls also apply the existing middleware once before guest serialization, using the arguments actually executed after policy adjustment.

The exec runtime already supports `awaitResults`; the prompt and documentation now explain when to use it. Tokenjuice guidance distinguishes real output replacement from plugin inventory status and separates native replacement, explicit wrapping, failure preservation, and complete-task measurements.

## Evidence

- Scoped-only, empty-root, and same-ID lazy-owner regressions fail on the unchanged base and pass with the fix.
- The Code Mode regression uses a real worker and shell: once-only transformation, policy-adjusted command/cwd, exit/error metadata, unchanged exact file/schema bytes, and intact outer envelope.
- Combined candidate: 43 tests pass across six focused files/four shards. Supporting lane checks cover the affected Code Mode, Tool Search, MCP, headless, native-hook, and prefix-stability consumers.
- Existing terminal-wait subprocess proof preserves exit 7, explicit background behavior, and timeout cleanup without changing runtime defaults.
- Scoped types/lint and ten-file formatting pass; the changed MDX pages pass validation.
- Local autoreview of the complete candidate at P0–P2: no actionable findings; supplied source review, not test execution. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable from a clean built runner.
- Full `pnpm build` passes (it emits UI size-budget advisory warnings; this change does not touch UI source). Built real-model headless runs pass with direct tools and Code Mode: automatic inventory compaction is 5,647 → 470 characters including the notice; exit 7/sentinel, exact file bytes, and the returned schema object are preserved. No manual CLI wrapper or global-root activation workaround.

Requested by @vincentkoc.

An installed app may not have a provider card yet. Checking only that card’s pending flag treated the earlier catalog request as a completed empty result. prs.title: fix(ci): prevent compact node shard timeouts
prs.body:
Related: #129590

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a CI problem where compact Node shards could time out after a long run when a hosted fallback exposed two cores but the workflow started three Vitest workers. The dispatch validation also hid 392 tests behind one entrypoint, so a late failure discarded too much completed work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Clamp the Vitest worker budget to the detected core count, and split dispatch validation into core, lifecycle, and delivery entrypoints with dedicated planner groups. The planner still covers every test exactly once, preserves owner routing, and does not increase timeouts or retries.

## User Impact

No product runtime behavior changes. Maintainers get smaller failure domains and less CPU oversubscription in compact CI, so a dispatch failure can be retried and diagnosed without repeating the full monolithic suite.

prs.title: fix(ui): listed ACP sessions of agents outside agents.entries cannot be opened or deleted
prs.body:
<!-- template: .github/pull_request_template.md at upstream main 65cf8cdc378 -->

Related: #199373

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI sidebar lists ACP sessions (`agent:<harness>:acp:<uuid>`) of ACP agents that are not in `agents.entries`, but opening or deleting one fails with `Unknown agent id "<harness>"`, so the row cannot be removed.

## User Impact

User impact: describe and delete requests for these ACP sessions no longer fail with `Unknown agent id` when the UI path sends the harness id, so the rows can be deleted again, single or batch, without adding the harness to `agents.entries`.

Not fixed here: opening such a session still shows "Couldn't load this conversation: Unknown agent id". The chat page also calls agent-scoped methods (`chat.metadata`, `models.list`, `board.get`, `talk.catalog` and others) that reject an agent outside `agents.entries`. That needs its own change.

## Why This Change Was Made

`sessions.list` keeps these rows on purpose since #83397. The UI then sent the harness id as an explicit `agentId` next to the session key. The Gateway rejects an explicit id outside the agent roster, and #164993 pins that rejection as intended, while the same request without the id is admitted through the key.

The shared session request builder and the describe owner now drop `agentId` when it only repeats the agent of a free ACP key. This follows the #164993 fix for `sessions_history`. A different `agentId` and every non-ACP key still send it, so roster, global alias and ownership checks are unchanged. The Gateway is not changed.

Alternative: #199398 fixes the same issue on the Gateway side, by accepting an explicit `agentId` that matches the key's agent.

## Evidence

Base 65cf8cdc378, head df871cfecc2.

- Real Gateway: isolated Gateway on a pinned port with temp state, `agents.entries: { main }`, `acp.allowedAgents: ["claude"]`, and one ACP session seeded the way an ACP spawn persists it (session row plus canonical ACP metadata). Requests use the params the Control UI's own request builders produce at each commit.
  - Base: `sessions.list` returns the row, short URL resolve works, and `sessions.describe` and `sessions.delete` fail with `Unknown agent id "claude"`. The row stays.
  - Head: describe and delete succeed and the row is gone from `sessions.list`. An explicit harness `agentId` is still rejected by the Gateway.
  - Browser run (Playwright, same kind of isolated Gateway, Control UI from source): the Sessions page lists the ACP rows, and single and batch delete there work on both base and head, because that page already sends no `agentId`. Opening a row fails on both base and head, as noted above. With only `main` configured, the sidebar does not list the ACP rows, so the sidebar delete path was not reached in the browser; it is covered by the request-level run above and the unit tests.
- Tests: new regressions for describe (redundant harness id dropped, a different id and a non-ACP key kept) and for single and batch delete. All 3 fail on the base because `agentId: "claude"` is sent, and pass with the fix. Reverting the fix turns them red again. 1250 tests pass across `ui/src/lib/sessions`, the session organizer, session details, the Sessions page and chat state refresh.
- Gates: `pnpm check:changed` passes at the head. `git diff --check` is clean.
- Local review: ClawSweeper `--local-range` (Claude runner on a Claude subscription login), base 65cf8cdc378, head df871cfecc2, full committed range, complete and checkout access verified. Outcome: no findings, patch is correct, security cleared, rating C (proof D, patch B) after 1 round. The proof tier is low because the local range review cannot see the real Gateway run below. Remaining findings: none.

## Runtime output

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Connected apps tells read-only users to sign in or create a pairing code even though their current role cannot connect an app.

## User Impact

User impact: the empty state explains the permission requirement instead of sending users toward unavailable actions. Users who can connect apps keep the existing guidance and pairing flow. No permissions, grants, or connection behavior change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The page already receives the caller’s pairing permission and uses it to show the pairing button. The empty-state explanation now uses that same fact and the existing backend’s access guidance. There is no new policy or state.

Related: #195006 covers glossary/style and translation work. Its current diff preserves the unconditional empty-state advice; this small correction does not duplicate that broader work.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on main at 4c700539aa1ac44285e3219addc246f21a76946c through the normal plugin page, loading the actual built MCP Relay entry and stylesheet. Synthetic Gateway responses cover both read-only and read/write callers; no live relay or account changes.
- The read-only regression failed before the correction. All **9 focused Connected apps tests pass**, including allowed pairing, permission changes, consent failure, refresh failure and grant revocation presentation.
- Both full-app browser flows pass. The read-only page has no pairing action or pairing request; the allowed flow opens the real dialog, creates a synthetic code with the expected scope ceiling, and closes it.
- Plugin build, scoped lint/typecheck, i18n source verification, formatting and diff checks passed. Current-main reconciliation found no intervening changes to the affected owners. No broad CI or live relay test was run.

### Before

![Before: Connected apps suggests pairing without permission](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d4b25505-b96c-4394-a403-634b35ee6cc1)

### After

![After: Connected apps explains the access requirement](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d6450ca8-fd41-4281-9897-4f207c33600d)

Real built Control UI and plugin components, synthetic Alex account, emulated 1280 × 900 desktop viewport. Captures are matched same-frame crops; full app context is retained with the test artifacts.

Contributor: @vyctorbrzezowski directed this audit and the user-facing correction.
