prs.title: fix(macos): preserve the selected CLI when inspecting a managed install
prs.body:
Closes #140128

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes macOS CLI selection changing when the app inspects a ready managed CLI while an external CLI is selected.

## User Impact

Inspecting installations no longer changes the selected CLI. A successful managed install or update still selects the verified managed CLI.

## Why This Change Was Made

Managed inspection returns status without persisting selection. Discovery retains its existing selection behavior, while installation and update record the managed CLI only after their success checks. No preference keys or formats changed, and no CLI is removed.

## Evidence

Current product head: `6fc1559689dbe9b5a355901c2aae20524c25dc36`. The 2 November merge combines the published discovery-test follow-up `64bf55b81f6573a8c14313dfa51542d21071eba7` with main `c1b0fc1415a09138c48e3f81055aca0f8e4f12aa`. Evidence below is pinned to the revision actually checked; earlier runs are not current-head native execution.

- **Current PR CI:** [Run 41518373631](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41518373631) completed successfully at product `6fc1559`, including selected preflight, security-fast, native-i18n and the CI gate. The [combined gate 41518985777](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41518985777) and security/dependency review statuses also passed. Both macOS Swift entries and macOS Node were skipped, not executed. Periphery build and scan checks passed separately; neither is native test execution.
- **Published discovery regression:** [Commit `64bf55b`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/64bf55b81f6573a8c14313dfa51542d21071eba7) strengthens the existing selection test: it clears both selection keys, calls real discovery, asserts executable/version persistence before managed inspection, and removes the debug project-path shortcut before checking the resolver. The complete delta is one test file (+11/−1), with no production seam or weakened controls. Exact source-delta, patch-application and whitespace checks passed. Independent source review and scoped AutoReview (P0–P3, `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, no findings) covered the prepared test change against `b3ee562`; native compilation/execution and baseline mutation proof were not run. Public source inspection confirms these assertions remain present at `6fc1559`.
- **Current-head review (2 November):** [ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140131#issuecomment-5559521046) completed a review of exact head `6fc1559689dbe9b5a355901c2aae20524c25dc36` with no actionable code findings. Patch quality is 4/6; overall readiness and proof remain 2/6 because actual app-entry/install-update behavior, current native execution and released-state upgrade qualification are not established. [Review run 41547046623](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/41547046623) completed; this is source review, not execution proof. The generic existing-data checklist does not identify a concrete schema or data-model defect; the bounded upgrade/preservation proof remains outstanding.

- **Prior-head native-owner proof:** [Hosted macOS run 38597006067](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/38597006067) passed with QA/workflow `4cf95ff77fae422b8b380f4a2c49c4101a8f38b1` and clean initial/final product `76ee71b`. macOS 27.0.1, Xcode 27.0, Swift 6.4 arm64: 56 Swift Testing declarations across four suites, expanding to 64 executed cases (50 single-case declarations plus 14 cases from six parameterized declarations). Selection, managed-update success/failure, and older/missing/revoked canonical-verification controls passed. These are executable fixtures, not real npm installations or signed-app proof.
- **Prior-head canonical CI:** [Run 38599555604](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38599555604) passed at exact product `76ee71b`, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. Its macOS Swift and macOS Node jobs were skipped, not executed; native proof comes from the separate owner run above.
- **Prior applicability:** Source review of then-current main `794d6500f382311cab58f5d474a9ef248598e5f2` still finds the ready `managedStatus` selection write. This is source evidence, not a new live reproduction.
- **Prior-head review (29 October):** [ClawSweeper Revision 14](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140131#issuecomment-5559521046) reviewed `a2c6197` on 29 October. It reports no findings, patch quality 4/6, and overall/proof 2/6. App-entry inspection and verified installation/update evidence, plus an existing-state upgrade from `v2026.10.9` preserving settings and data, remain required. The completed review does not establish a data-model defect.
- **Fixture follow-up:** [Commit `4298606`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4298606a9e38b4665dc014a71fd81bfb451d97af) changes exactly two positive Node fixture literals, preserving all assertions, old-runtime controls, and production source. Whitespace and exact source-delta checks passed. [Previous-head canonical CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40121014753) passed, including its CI gate, native i18n, and security-fast. The prior [combined CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40121219433) also reports success at `4298606`. Both macOS Swift entries and macOS Node were skipped, not executed; no current-head native execution proof is claimed.

### Remaining qualification

- **App entry and update:** The owner tests and retained real-npm evidence cover the affected **unbundled** discovery/inspection path at their recorded revisions. Signed packaged-app proof is separate: it must establish the actual legacy-service inspection/update routing, selection preservation, and verified canonical selection. A fresh bundled no-op or forced override cannot stand in for the original bug. The 56 owner declarations do not directly cover `install(target:)` success/compatibility-failure selection paths. The published discovery regression now asserts persistence from initially unset keys before inspection, but its new assertions still need native execution; the historical 56-declaration run predates them.
- **Existing-state upgrade:** A disposable latest-stable-to-candidate app upgrade with existing settings/data retained remains unrun. No preference/schema format changed, and source review found no data-model incompatibility; the missing upgrade run is a proof gap, not an established migration defect.
- **Current composition:** The fixtures emit `v24.22.1`, which satisfies the current runtime requirement; the 24 October change addressed the higher minimum inspected at that time. This two-line fixture-only repair is published at `4298606`; native execution of the current composition remains unverified. This does not relabel the pinned original-head result or establish a production incompatibility.

### Retained real coexisting-installation proof

[Run 37386979616](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616) compared earlier product `a38ed66158bd270bd45607411aadb5862b299b8b` with baseline `3b16db73c0b5209aad2ee7c3fb5ddfb12fb208f9`, governed by corrected QA workflow `b166bce6b7ee4fc86631cb491fd7c17990be6362`. The candidate preserved external selection through ready managed inspection and left initially unset executable/version preferences unset: one native test passed in 74.660 seconds. The baseline failed exactly the five expected selection assertions; its verifier rejected other failures.

Both jobs used two distinct real `openclaw@2026.9.8` npm installations with verified published SHA-512 integrity on disposable hosted macOS runners. Cleanup, preference/environment restoration, and pristine-source checks passed. [Candidate receipts](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616/artifacts/11380755806) and [baseline receipts](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616/artifacts/11379004102) contain selection cells, installation identities, logs, and strict verification summaries. This covers inspection only at the earlier revision, not current signed-app install/update or upgrade behavior. Preceding failed QA attempts do not establish this result.

<details>
<summary>Historical CI and source qualification</summary>

[CI 37194001816](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001816), including native Swift, [macOS Periphery 37194001640](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001640), and [shared OpenClawKit Periphery 37194001665](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001665) passed at earlier head `a38ed66158bd270bd45607411aadb5862b299b8b`. Previously reported formatting, whitespace checks, and scoped Codex AutoReview remain historical proof, not a fresh review of the current head.

</details>

Maintainer review remains separate. The fixture-only follow-up changed no production source. The current head also includes the 2 November main merge. Swift owner tests, real installation, and app upgrade remain unverified for the current head; skipped CI lanes do not supply that proof.

prs.title: improve(ios): polish native chat, floating composer, and sidebar
prs.body: Closes #141184 ## What Problem This Solves The iOS chat composer occupies a large fixed footer, preventing messages from flowing behind Liquid Glass. Connection and loading indicators compete with the conversation, and ordinary session actions look destructive. ## Why This Change Was Made Use a compact floating composer with measured trailing transcript space, native menus, and quieter navigation while preserving the existing red/gray palette, typography, attachments, and voice controls. The composer overlays the transcript instead of reducing its viewport. Upstream’s session-bound, one-shot scroll commands handle sending and jumping to the latest reply without retaining row-ID scroll constraints. Shared presentation helpers keep loading and connection chrome consistent. ## User Impact - Messages scroll behind the composer; multiline drafts grow naturally, and the latest reply remains reachable above the input. - Attachments come first in the options menu. Model, effort, context, and permission controls retain their capability restrictions and use catalog-compatible localized labels. - Selected model options remain visible to accessibility. The macOS model menu retains its sign-in action when no models are available. - Ordinary session actions use standard colors; Delete remains destructive. Unread indicators are neutral, and rows announce unread/pinned state. - Overview keeps its toolbar reachable, uses quieter counters, and opens Usage from Tokens. Small sidebar and onboarding controls meet 44-point touch targets. Reduce Motion is respected. - Upstream’s persistent iOS chat owner, gateway switcher, session attention controls, and desktop styling are preserved. ## Evidence October 12 update integrates upstream `a010ee5721f140f5da48c6c761273b5ebda4cd54`, retaining its live-reply deduplication, deferred menus, compact-width avatar treatment, session-bound scroll commands, and operator/node connection distinction. Removed the unused chat-layout parameter reported by shared dead-code CI. The previously blocked keyboard/history flow reproduced on the integrated candidate: after a multiline send, the app consumed a full CPU core in SwiftUI `LazySubviewPlacements`. Ungrouped transcript content now has one stable layout container per lazy-stack child, preserving row IDs and spacing. The unchanged keyboard/history test passes after this repair; assertions were not weakened. Local validation on iPhone 17 / iOS 26.2 with Xcode 27: - 106 iOS tests in six suites pass, including the latest upstream connection/reconnect regressions, sidebar, and typography. - 39 shared chat tests in five suites pass; shared macOS and iOS simulator builds pass. - The full keyboard/history test passes three times after the fix, covering keyboard opening, typing, sending, preserved history position, multiline anchored replies, and jumping back to the latest reply. - Composer/options sizing, restored session history, long-press actions, and Overview/Usage navigation UI tests pass. - Native lint/formatting, localization verification, and `git diff --check` pass (existing test-file length warnings remain). - Interaction proof used layout fix `5fc55fcc218`; the final `66f8e6bb317` integration adds only upstream’s connection-state changes to the native code, validated by the 106-test run. Shared transcript/composer code is identical. No new tests or CI jobs were added; the existing keyboard/history regression supplies the before/after proof. Independent reviews of the full integration and the focused layout repair found no actionable P0–P2 issues. Hosted CI on the pushed head remains separate from this local evidence. Current synthetic screenshots show keyboard-visible content and preservation of the reader’s position: | Typing | Reading older history | | --- | --- | | | | Original before/after layout comparison: | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | These original layout captures use synthetic data on the same simulator. The baseline fixture’s model label was normalized for publication; its layout is unchanged. Physical-device, iPad, largest Dynamic Type, and macOS visual comparisons remain unverified. Shared macOS compilation and chat tests are covered. Maintainer product acceptance of the floating composer and placement of advanced controls is still pending.

prs.title: improve(ui): fix core copy leftovers from the copy sweep
prs.body:
## Problem

Two leftovers from the Control UI copy sweep remained in core copy:

- In Settings › Appearance › Tab icon, the notice for a locked lobster read “This lobster is not unlocked in this browser.” The Control UI style rules call for contractions.
- Core Control UI copy spelled “cancelled” the British way, while the product uses American English.

## Solution

- Changed the English source in `ui/src/i18n/locales/en-settings.ts` to “This lobster isn’t unlocked in this browser. Using Default until it is.” Updated the matching assertion in `ui/src/pages/config/view-tab-icon.browser.test.tsx`.
- Spelled “Canceled” and “canceling” the American way, as approved by Vyctor:
  - `en.ts` `common.cancelled`: “Cancelled” → “Canceled”
  - `en-chat-session.ts` unsent and cancelled notices: “This agent update was canceled before delivery.” and “Canceled before the agent started it. …”
  - `en-github-connections.ts` GitHub sign-in: “… or try canceling again.” and the “Try canceling again” button
  - `en-openclaw-id.ts` request expiry: “This browser request expired or was canceled. …”
  - Updated assertions in `chat-thread-live-final.test.ts`, `chat-thread-input-order.test.ts` and `chat-composer-outbox.e2e.test.ts`.
- Key names (`cancelled`, `dismissCancelled`, …) are unchanged. Channel plugins and internal error-matching strings are intentionally untouched.

Lobsterdex lore, bottle fortunes and pet hover titles stay an English-only easter egg, as Peter and Ayaan designed them. An earlier revision of this PR moved them into translation files; that change has been reverted.

## Impact

Seven English strings change; no keys or behavior change. Foreign locales are untouched; the post-merge `control-ui-locale-refresh` bot owns them.

## Evidence

- `view-tab-icon` browser test: 5/5 pass.
- `chat-thread-live-final` + `chat-thread-input-order`: 29/29 pass.
- Keyless `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline` (no change) and `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`: pass.

**Not landing: requested by maintainer.**

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/8ee302fc-4575-4506-92a8-1739453b9b71)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/6f3d8cae-3016-4c59-8e2f-ed53302706a0)

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: improve(clawrouter): apply the Control UI glossary and style to ClawRouter copy
prs.body:
## Problem

The ClawRouter pool page (`extensions/clawrouter/src/control-ui.tsx`) hard-coded every English string inline. That made the copy untranslatable, and some of it didn't follow the approved Control UI style: no contractions, sentences ending fragments with periods, passive "is required" phrasing, a raw error message shown as the alert headline, two different names for the same "enabled state unknown" concept, and Gateway status messages pointing at a "Model Providers" page whose actual label is **Models**.

## Solution

- Add a plugin-owned English catalog on the Nostr/Workboard pattern: `src/i18n/locales/en.ts`, `src/i18n/locales.ts`, and `src/i18n/index.ts`, using `translateControlUiMessage`. `browserRoot` is `src/` (the dirname of `openclaw.controlUi`), so `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` picks the catalog up automatically.
- Move **70 strings** into `en.ts` (68 under `clawrouter.*`, plus the shared `common.refresh` and `common.refreshing`, which match core English exactly). Composed strings such as "Observed {date} · Policy {policy}", "{used} used / {limit} monthly limit", and "{count} subscriptions with headroom · {unknown} unknown" are now single templates instead of JSX fragments.
- Apply the glossary and style rules to every human-visible string the lane owns, including the four Gateway pool status messages in `index.ts` that this page renders.
- Errors: the alert now reads "Couldn’t load the ClawRouter pool. Try Refresh." The redacted technical detail is still shown, but as a secondary hint line under the alert. ## Problem

The **X replies** Control UI page hard-codes its English copy in `extensions/x/src/control-ui.tsx`. Several strings also break the approved Control UI glossary and style rules:

- "bot" where the copy means the agent
- "Administrator" as the role name
- "hidden helpers" for subagents
- fragment sentences that end in periods
- raw server error text shown as the only error message

The empty-state hint also put the internal config key `allowFrom` in normal copy.

## Solution

- Add a plugin-owned English catalog on the Nostr pattern: `extensions/x/src/i18n/{index.ts,locales.ts,locales/en.ts}`. The browser root is `src` because `openclaw.controlUi` points at `./src/control-ui.tsx`. **63 strings** moved into the catalog under the plugin-specific `xReplies.*` namespace, so no key collides with the shared core catalog.
- Translate the page, navigation label, and page label through `translateControlUiMessage`. The view tracks `host.locale` in its existing presentation store.
- Notices are now typed keys (`added`, `removed`, `guestsOn`, …) translated at render time instead of English strings held in state.
- Request failures are wrapped in a small `RequestFailure` that records which action failed. The alert now reads "Couldn’t {verb} {thing}. {Next step}." and the redacted server message follows inline as secondary text (`<small>`, muted). The plugin SDK host components (`ControlUiComponents`) on main have no shared "Show details" disclosure, so as the sweep brief directs, the raw detail stays visually secondary and inline.
- Copy that wraps inline elements (`<time>`, the repository link) uses a small `withSlots` helper. It splits the translated string at `{name}` placeholders, so translators control word order.
- `locales.ts` is English-only for now, and other locales fall back to English, which is today's behavior. `translated.json` isn't added, per the sweep brief. The Nostr-style lazy `translated.json` loader can't be wired until that file exists, because the bundler can't resolve a missing import.

### Notable copy changes

| Old | New |
| --- | --- |
| Choose whose mentions the bot can answer publicly. | Choose whose mentions the agent can answer publicly. |
| Administrator access is required to manage X replies. | You need admin access to manage X replies. |
| Bot account | Agent account |
| Applies to the selected bot account. Guests get repository answers with hidden helpers of the same agent. No writes, commands, visible work sessions, or other agents. Maintainers keep their normal access. | Applies to the selected agent account. Guests get repository answers from this agent and its hidden subagents. They can’t write, run commands, open visible sessions, or use other agents. Maintainers keep their normal access. |
| Per guest, per UTC day / `3 mentions` | Mentions per guest, per UTC day / `3` (no more "1 mentions") |
| Could not resolve on X: @a, @b. Check the declared profiles. | Couldn’t find @a, @b on X. Check the declared GitHub profiles. |
| No manual entries yet. Add a maintainer above or set `allowFrom` in config. | No manual entries yet. Add a maintainer above or in config. |
| *(raw server error)* / The request failed. Try again. | Couldn’t load X replies. Try again. · Couldn’t add this account. Check the handle and try again. · Couldn’t remove this entry. Try again. · Couldn’t change guest mode. Try again. *(the redacted server detail follows as secondary text)* |
| No successful sync yet.Entries update… *(missing space)* | No successful sync yet. Entries update… |

All other strings moved into the catalog with unchanged English. They were already in sentence case, used the single ellipsis character, and had no straight quotes.

### Out of scope / unchanged

- Server-generated text the page displays verbatim: the guest readiness `blockedReason` from `guests.ts`/`monitor.ts` and the GitHub sync `message` from `verified-github.ts`. That text also feeds channel status and the agent path, so it stays with its backend owners.
- Agent-facing and X-posted text (the guest policy prompt, tool text).
- Docs: `docs/channels/x.md` quotes **X replies**, **From GitHub**, **Guest mode**, and **Refresh**, and none of those labels changed.

## Impact

UI copy only. The plugin's operator RPCs (`x.allowlist.*`, `x.guests.set`), state, and authorization are unchanged. Foreign locales keep showing English until the post-merge locale refresh adds `translated.json` and the lazy loader is wired.

prs.title: fix(channels): refuse a placeholder message id as platform identity
prs.body:
Related #199070

## What Problem This Solves

A channel adapter that returns no provider event id may substitute a placeholder. The bundled Matrix adapter does exactly that: it skips falsy event ids and answers `messageId: lastMessageId || "unknown"`, while its receipt carries `platformMessageIds: []` and `parts: []`. `resolveReceiptSourceId` read that placeholder as a concrete platform identity, so shared outbound delivery recorded an identified `sent` result and fed confirmed-message bookkeeping a message the provider never identified.

## User Impact

A placeholder id with no provider ids no longer counts as a platform identity: the result stays an ambiguous/unidentified attempt instead of a confirmed send, and downstream confirmed-message bookkeeping no longer receives the sentinel. Real ids in a mixed multi-part batch are unaffected, and nothing is retried automatically — an ambiguous attempt may have reached the provider, so its custody behaviour is unchanged.

The accepted-send consumer regression now covers both dispositions: a genuine provider id still reports `sent` after its caller closes, and a placeholder-only result reports an unidentified attempt after the same caller closure instead of a confirmed send.

## Why This Change Was Made

The report's first expected behaviour and its "one shared platform-identity normalization rule": identity resolution now drops the closed set of placeholder spellings (`unknown`, `n/a`, `none`) before any source-id, receipt, or part is built from it. `resolveReceiptSourceId` is the single choke point both the part path and the aggregate `platformMessageIds` path already use, so one rule covers them.

The existing accepted-send case in `src/infra/outbound/message-action-execution.accepted-results.test.ts` returned `messageId: "unknown"` with an empty receipt and required `deliveryStatus: "sent"`. That fixture asserted the false confirmation this change removes, so it now returns a genuine provider id, and the placeholder shape moved into its own case that asserts the unidentified disposition with the caller-closure contract intact.

Scope: this is the identity gate only. Reconciliation and delivery-outcome wording are untouched, and the explicit `not_sent` distinction is unchanged.

## Evidence

![real Matrix A/B and regression A/B](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/199238/proof-199238.png)

Real rig: Synapse 1.164.2 on `oc.test` (isolated WSL `OcTestDebian`, `127.0.0.1:28798`), account `@proofbot:oc.test`, room `!VPLxOMV0cw2wGtq5SP9TtdqB3MksChOhMgEGdQ8HCO4`, shipped `openclaw message send` CLI on the built `dist/`. `main` column means this branch with only `src/channels/message/receipt.ts` reverted to `upstream/main`, rebuilt and re-run the same way.

| case (production entry point) | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| real Matrix text send | `sent`, `messageId: "$v9YiwaF2…"`, receipt `["$v9Yi…"]` | `sent`, `messageId: "$bMb_WNwT…"`, receipt `["$bMb_…"]`, 1 part |
| provider withholds the event id (real Synapse accepted it; only the `/send` response lacks `event_id`) | `failed`, `sentBeforeError: true`, no id | `failed`, `sentBeforeError: true`, no id |
| channel returns `messageId: "unknown"` + `platformMessageIds: []` + `parts: []` | `sent`, `result.messageId: "unknown"` (false confirmation) | `suppressed`, `suppressionReason: "adapter_returned_no_identity"`, `sentBeforeError: true`, `result: undefined` |

The withheld-id attempt is in the room afterwards (`$Wgl0JnR5…` as `@proofalice` reads it), so the ambiguous case is custody-preserving, not silent loss.

Two things this run established:

- Both revisions stop before the receipt gate when the provider withholds an id: the shipped `matrix-js-sdk` rejects that response with `updatePendingEvent called with status=SENT, but no new event id`. So the adapter's `lastMessageId || "unknown"` sentinel is defensive — no live Matrix send reaches it, and an unidentified live attempt already reports `failed` with `sentBeforeError` custody. That is why the placeholder A/B below is at the action + delivery layer, with the channel adapter as the only double.
- `run-tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` now runs on this checkout (the `@openclaw/proc-safe` resolution failure after main's dependency bump is gone after a clean `pnpm install`): exit 0.

Regression A/B, `src/infra/outbound/message-action-execution.accepted-results.test.ts` (real `runMessageAction` + real delivery core, production dispatch and custody):

| revision | new placeholder case | genuine-id accepted-send case | file |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main | fails: `- "deliveryStatus": "suppressed"` / `+ "deliveryStatus": "sent"` | passes | 1 failed, 35 passed |
| this branch | passes | passes | 36 passed |

Related gates on this branch: `receipt.test.ts`, `outbound-bridge.test.ts`, `deliver.test.ts`, `deliver.queue-integration.test.ts`, `message-action-execution.accepted-results.test.ts` — 135 + 36 passed, exit 0. oxfmt clean on the changed files.

## What was not tested

- No live homeserver can produce the placeholder: a real Matrix homeserver always returns an event id, and withholding one makes the SDK throw before the receipt gate (verified above). The placeholder-shape A/B therefore uses the production action and delivery stack with a constructed adapter result, not a real Matrix transport.
- The withheld-id experiment needs a wire proxy in front of the real Synapse that rewrites only the `/send` response and drops that event's sync echo; Synapse itself cannot be made to accept a message without reporting its id.
- A mixed multi-part send where one part is unidentified against a live homeserver was not run; that shape is covered by the receipt-owner test.
- The report's broader ask (reconciliation and delivery-outcome wording sharing the same rule) is out of scope here; only the identity gate is normalised.

prs.title: improve(workboard): apply the Control UI glossary and style to Workboard copy
prs.body:
## Problem

Workboard's Control UI copy didn't follow the approved Control UI glossary and style rules. It had straight apostrophes, a `...` placeholder, "could not" / "cannot" errors with no consistent form, "Board agent" capitalized mid-sentence, the British "Cancelled", and "board conversation" used for what is a session. Its errors also showed internal RPC text: `sessions.create returned no key` and `workboard response did not include a card`. About 19 user-visible English strings were still hard-coded in `extensions/workboard/browser/` instead of living in the plugin's translation source, so they could never be translated.

## Solution

- Rewrote the existing English in `browser/i18n/locales/en.ts` to follow the rules. Errors now read "Couldn’t {verb} {thing}. {Next step}." The copy uses contractions, curly apostrophes and the `…` character, sentence case, and **session** as the container noun.
- Moved the remaining hard-coded English in `browser/` (execution, loading, mutation and normalization errors; the stale-session fallback; the "Workboard is no longer active" message; widget registration labels; the board-kind suffix on duplicate sidebar names) into `en.ts` and called it through `t()`.
- `host.ts` calls `translateControlUiMessage` directly instead of `t()`, because `i18n/index.ts` imports `host.ts` and using `t()` there would create an import cycle.
- Two places that had the same stale-session fallback in different words (normalization and card alerts) now use one key.
- Updated `docs/plugins/workboard.md`, which quotes the sidebar suffix: **Planning (Cards)** / **Planning (Sessions)**.

Notable copy changes (old → new):

| Where | Old | New |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Page load failure | Workboard could not load. Check your connection and reload this page. | Couldn’t load Workboard. Check your connection and reload this page. |
| Delete without write access | Connect with write access to delete this board. | Couldn’t delete this board. Connect with write access and try again. |
| Bulk edit stopped | The operation stopped. Remaining cards are still selected; refresh and try again. | Couldn’t apply changes to every card. Remaining cards are still selected; refresh and try again. |
| Sessions board agent missing | The board conversation's agent is unavailable. Choose a configured agent or update the board's conversation. | Couldn’t open the board session. Its agent is unavailable; choose a configured agent or update the board’s session. |
| Sessions board create failed | The board conversation could not be created. Try again. | Couldn’t create the board session. Try again. |
| Rules help | The Board agent can edit column rules and session scope. | The board agent can edit column rules and session scope. |
| Note placeholder | Add a decision, blocker, or proof note... | Add a decision, blocker, or proof note… |
| Dispatch help | …this board's Ready cards… | …this board’s Ready cards… |
| Refresh status | Refresh failed | Couldn’t refresh |
| Session status | Cancelled | Canceled (American English, same as core approvals copy) |
| Widget card not loaded | This card is not loaded yet. | This card isn’t loaded yet. |
| Start, hard-coded | sessions.create returned no key | Couldn’t start a session for this card. Try again. |
| Card payload, hard-coded | workboard response did not include a card | Couldn’t read the updated card. Refresh the board and try again. |
| Gateway missing, hard-coded | Gateway client unavailable | Couldn’t refresh Workboard. Connect to the Gateway and try again. |
| Scheduled start, hard-coded | Scheduled cards cannot start before their scheduled time. | Couldn’t start this card. Scheduled cards can’t start before their scheduled time. |
| Already started, hard-coded | This card already has an execution. Refresh its details or use Edit to clear its session link before starting another. | Couldn’t start this card. It already has a linked session; refresh its details or use Edit to clear its session link. |
| Stop, hard-coded | Refresh this card's session details before stopping it, or use Edit to choose its session. | Couldn’t stop this card’s session. Refresh its session details, or use Edit to choose its session. |
| Changed card, hard-coded | This card changed. Refresh its details before starting or stopping it. | Couldn’t start or stop this card because it changed. Refresh its details and try again. |
| Stale fallback, hard-coded (×2) | Session has not reported… / Linked session has not reported recent activity. | Linked session hasn’t reported recent activity. |
| Inactive plugin, hard-coded | Workboard is no longer active. Reload the plugin to continue. | Workboard is no longer active. Reload this page to continue. |
| Unknown error, hard-coded | Unknown workboard error. | Unknown Workboard error. Refresh and try again. |
| Sidebar duplicate name | Planning (cards) | Planning (Cards) |

String count: 12 existing English values rewritten. 19 hard-coded literals moved into translation calls: 14 go to new `en.ts` keys and the rest reuse 3 existing keys (`widget.boardLabel`, `cardsBoard`, `sessionsBoard.kind`). No foreign locale, `translated.json`, `.i18n/*.tm.jsonl` or `*.meta.json` file was edited. The post-merge locale-refresh bot owns parity.

Raw Gateway error text still shows inline in the existing Workboard error toast. Workboard has no shared "Show details" disclosure on `main`, and the copy written here no longer includes internal names.

## Impact

Only copy and translation sources change; behavior doesn't. Two edge cases are accepted:
- Widget registration labels and the stale-reason fallback are resolved when they're created. A locale switch picks them up after the next refresh or reload; before this change they were always English.
- The session label `buildCardSessionLabel` writes for new card sessions, and agent-facing template drafts, stay as they are. They're stored data or model-facing text, not Control UI copy.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/workboard/browser`: 34 files, 265 tests passed (assertions updated in `index.test.ts` and `widgets/runtime.test.ts`).
- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`: green (`plugin=workboard keys=395 locales=22`).
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: green.
- `oxlint` on touched TS files: 0 warnings or errors. `oxfmt --check`: clean. `git diff --check`: clean.
- `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles`: 0 cycles.
- pr-simplify: every hunk is a copy move or rewrite. The only new code is the 4-line `inactiveMessage()` helper in `host.ts`, which avoids the import cycle. One duplicate stale fallback was merged into a shared key. Net production change is small: about +40/−30 lines, mostly `en.ts`.
- Local review: autoreview (Codex, gpt-6.1-sol, medium), branch mode, base `d59f00281eb0216` → head of this branch, max priority P2. Result: scoped-clean, "patch is correct (0.82)", no findings. The reviewer couldn't see unchanged context, so key validity and import cycles rest on the `ui:i18n:verify` and madge runs above.

Not landing: requested by maintainer; screenshots pending before merge (visual gate).

## Problem

The Nostr profile panel and the Memory overview/search views had copy that didn't follow the approved Control UI glossary and style rules: Title Case buttons and labels (`Hide Advanced`, `Import from Relays`, `Save & Publish`, `Public Key`, `Edit Profile`), straight quotes and `...`, "Could not" / "does not" with no contractions, lowercase "gateway", internal jargon ("host memory search runtime"), and error messages that didn't use the "Couldn’t {verb} {thing}. {Next step}." pattern. Nostr also had one hard-coded English label (`NIP-05`) outside its catalog.

## Solution

- Rewrote the English source catalogs in `extensions/nostr/browser/i18n/locales/en.ts` and `extensions/memory-core/browser/i18n/locales/en.ts` to follow the glossary and style rules.
- **Shared-key collision:** Nostr's `common.hideAdvanced`, `common.showAdvanced`, `common.importFromRelays`, `common.saveAndPublish` and `common.publicKey` share keys with the core catalog (`ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts`), and `ui:i18n:verify` requires a plugin's English to match the core text for any shared key. These five now live under plugin-owned `channels.nostr.*` keys.
- Removed those five core `common.*` keys from `ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts`; nothing reads them any more (approved by Vyctor; `ui:i18n:baseline`, `ui:i18n:verify` and `tsgo:ui` pass).
- Moved the hard-coded `NIP-05` profile-fact label into the Nostr catalog (`channels.nostr.nip05`). The truncated public key now uses `…`.

Before, a failed request showed only the raw server message (e.g. `Invalid profile`). Both paths share one `failure()` helper in `controller.ts`, which also removed the duplicated prefix logic.

- **Raw error detail:** the Plugin SDK has no shared "Show details" disclosure for plugin settings views, so the raw detail stays inline after the sentence. This matches the existing core pattern (`Couldn’t load cloud device profiles. Try again. {error}`).

prs.title: fix: native Codex oauth/token without a host profile should still forward unlisted models
prs.body:
Fixes #194980

### What Problem This Solves

A native Codex login that has not selected a host auth profile is an `oauth` or `token` account. `resolveCodexForwardCompatModel` forwarded a model missing from the static patch table only when `authProfileMode` was absent. Models already in the static table are unchanged.

### Why This Change Was Made

The unlisted branch now accepts `authProfileMode === undefined || authProfileMode === "oauth" || authProfileMode === "token"`. It still requires `authProfileId === undefined` and `providerConfig?.auth === undefined`. `api_key`, and `oauth` that already has an `authProfileId`, still return `undefined`.

An earlier head also passed that account mode in from agent execution and off-catalog runtime choice. That expansion did not finish runtime selection: the later membership check still reads model scope, and the Codex auth policy does not belong in core. Those callers and the account-scope readiness API are removed. The repair stays on the provider resolver.

The existing spark-routing test moved to `extensions/openai/openai-codex-spark-routing.test.ts` so the provider test file could take the new cases without growing past its line cap. That test's assertions are unchanged.

### User Impact

A profile-free native Codex `oauth` or `token` context can resolve a model id that is not yet in the static patch table when that context reaches the provider resolver. A selected host profile and API-key auth still do not receive that forward path.

### Evidence

Resolver contract, exact command `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/openai-provider.test.ts -t "delegates an unlisted first-party model|does not extend native model forwarding" --maxWorkers=1` on `bd5140669e8`: parent exit 1 for `oauth` and `token`; head exit 0. `api_key` with no profile, and `oauth` with `authProfileId` `openai:selected`, stay `undefined`.

Scheduled audit collection only admits a sole CLI-process config, so observed Gateway failures cannot produce separate audit exports.

Include the helper in the existing trusted-runner sparse checkout.

The existing private importer now validates the matching Gateway project, Bun runtime, and exact permitted Node-only exclusion; legacy CLI imports remain readable. prs.title: fix: let writer occupancy diagnostics exit after invalid time bounds
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the writer occupancy diagnostic prints an invalid time-range error but remains running when its stdin producer is still connected.

## User Impact

Operators can correct an invalid `--from`/`--until` invocation without manually interrupting the diagnostic or stopping the upstream log stream.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI now closes its readline interface after analysis settles and destroys file streams it created. Range validation and report contents stay with their existing owner.

## Evidence

**Current submitted head:** `3d0d48268f59123e9e77585f293b79af4ccc9e3c`. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42609621325) and [aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42609621325/job/129137937045) passed for this exact head. The [current-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195930#issuecomment-6739248971) reports sufficient proof and no findings or before-merge actions. Status checked November 11; runtime records below are retained, not new executions.

Real documented CLI on Node 24.22.2 in an offline, secretless 512 MiB Docker container:

| Invocation with stdin kept open | Base | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Invalid `--from` | Error printed; still alive after 2 s | Natural exit 1 in 0.44 s |
| Reversed bounds | Error printed; still alive after 2 s | Natural exit 1 in 0.32 s |

Normal empty/one-record stdin reports still exit 0. File input, invalid file bounds, missing-file errors, and help retain byte-identical stdout/stderr and exit codes. Only the hung base subprocesses needed proof cleanup.

Focused owner tests: 6/6 pass, 419 ms test time (2.19 s Vitest duration). The exact base fails only the new real-process regression. Strict narrow typecheck, Oxfmt, Node syntax, scoped Oxlint 232 rules, and diff checks pass. The 29-line allocation covers this process-lifetime regression; the shared budget is unchanged.

Local tests used a minimal isolated Vitest graph because the standard wrapper's preparation closure exceeded the available local resource scope. Standard-lane and broad coverage remain assigned to exact-head PR CI; The current-head hosted CI has since passed (linked above); no separate per-file hosted duration is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Actual subprocess receipts and reproduction</summary>

Base: `0eb84f967507089583117c874983c8358e991fcf`; fixed: `3d0d48268f59123e9e77585f293b79af4ccc9e3c`.
The parent keeps the stdin pipe open until the child exits or the 2-second observation deadline:

```python
p = subprocess.Popen(
    ["node", "scripts/diagnostic-writer-occupancy.mts", "--from", "invalid"],
    stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
)
p.wait(timeout=2)  # before: TimeoutExpired; after: returncode 1
```

The actual run also repeated this with `--from 2026-11-09T00:00:00Z --until 2026-11-08T00:00:00Z`.

```text
BEFORE invalid-from: natural_exit=false; alive after 2.009 s; cleanup SIGTERM
BEFORE reversed:     natural_exit=false; alive after 2.010 s; cleanup SIGTERM
AFTER  invalid-from: natural_exit=true; exit=1; wall_seconds=0.435
AFTER  reversed:     natural_exit=true; exit=1; wall_seconds=0.316
BOTH stderr: Writer occupancy report failed: check input readability, JSONL format and timestamp options (--help).
AFTER valid-empty: exit=0; observedReservations=0; operations=[]
AFTER valid-one:   exit=0; observedReservations=1;
                  operation=direct; count=1; reservationMs=2000;
                  queueWaitMs=1000; maxReservationMs=2000
```

The base regression kept the other 5 tests green and failed the new test with `[null, "SIGTERM"]` instead of `[1, null]`. Final committed-candidate verification: 6/6 passed, 422 ms test time, 2.27 s Vitest duration. Native staged ratchet passed with slack 6. Independent exact-diff review found no blocking issues.
</details>

prs.title: fix(skills): reject misleading meme search limits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Meme template searches silently report misleading success when `--limit` is invalid: `NaN` or `0.5` yields an empty list, while `-1` returns all but the last match.

## User Impact

Search, suggest, and refresh reject invalid limits with an actionable error. Zero still returns no templates; positive limits and default counts are unchanged. Invalid refresh limits are rejected before a network request.

## Why This Change Was Made

One limit parser serves both result-slicing paths. This corrects an existing CLI input boundary without adding dependencies or changing the curated registry. The recently merged external contribution #195043 is a related input-boundary precedent.

## Evidence

**Current candidate:** `d1b007ea8b1896b09c5896af6f43954f6c688ccf`. Its [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42642755213), including [changed tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42642755213/job/129249233105), [test-line ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42642755213/job/129249232552), and [aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42642755213/job/129253062879), passed.

The retained 18-case before/after CLI source hashes below match GitHub's exact base/head files. The [November 11 review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195201#issuecomment-6721335850) now covers this exact candidate, with sufficient proof and no findings or before-merge actions. The additional boundary run below was executed separately on November 11; no source code changed.

Rebased onto `f615e96b55becb3944b57de4e8af74a801814fab` to resolve a test conflict with merged #195929. The resolution keeps its rotated-caption rendering fix and complete rendering assertions alongside the original 30-line limit regression. The limit implementation and allocation are unchanged; the shared test-line baseline is unchanged.

Repeated the shipped standalone `skills/meme-maker/scripts/meme.mjs` against the exact upstream and rebased sources with the real curated registry. Execution used Node 24.22.2 in a secretless, network-disabled, non-root Docker container: read-only source/root, 256 MiB memory, 0.5 CPU, 64 PIDs, 32 MiB private tmp. No command implementation, search results, or numeric parser was mocked.

```text
command                                  upstream f615e96       rebased d1b007ea
search choice --limit -1 --json           exit 0, 2 matches      exit 1, limit error
suggest choice --limit NaN --json         exit 0, []             exit 1, limit error
search/suggest --limit 0 / 1 / 2 --json    0 / 1 / 2 matches      0 / 1 / 2 matches
refresh --limit -1 / NaN --json           exit 1, fetch failed   exit 1, limit error

limit error: error: --limit must be a non-negative safe integer
```

The 18-case CLI matrix covers `-1`, `0.5`, `NaN`, `Infinity`, and empty input for both search commands; zero/positive controls; and invalid refresh limits. Upstream fails all 12 invalid-input expectations and passes the six valid controls. The rebased source passes 18/18.

- Focused `test/scripts/meme-maker.test.ts`: 3 passed, 1 existing opt-in live PNG test skipped. This includes the preserved upstream rotated-caption geometry check and CLI regression. Test time 2.8 seconds; runner wall time 5.6 seconds.
- Node syntax, targeted Oxfmt/Oxlint, `git diff --check`, and the native test-line ratchet passed. Test lines and ceiling are both 6,600,471. The existing separate 30-line allocation covers this regression; no shared budget increase.
- Simplification retained one shared parser, no new state or configuration. Net production +9 lines, test +30 lines.

### Additional safe-integer boundary proof (November 11)

Ran the shipped standalone CLI and real registry from exact base `f615e96b55becb3944b57de4e8af74a801814fab` and candidate `d1b007ea8b1896b09c5896af6f43954f6c688ccf`, using Node 24.22.2 in a secretless, network-disabled container (256 MiB, 0.5 CPU, read-only source/root). No implementation or registry mocks. Command shape: `node skills/meme-maker/scripts/meme.mjs <search|suggest> choice --limit=<value> --json`; the default case omits `--limit`.

| Input (both search and suggest) | Base | Candidate |
|---|---|---|
| `-1` / `0.5` | exit 0 with misleading results | exit 1, limit error |
| `9007199254740992` (first unsafe integer) | exit 0, all 3 matches | exit 1, limit error |
| `9007199254740991` (maximum safe integer) | exit 0, all 3 matches | identical output, stderr and exit code |
| `0` / `1` | exit 0, 0 / 1 match | identical output, stderr and exit code |
| omitted (normal default) | exit 0, 3 matches | identical output, stderr and exit code |

All **14 base/candidate comparisons (28 CLI executions)** passed their assertions in **5.71 s wall time**. Every invalid candidate returned empty stdout and `error: --limit must be a non-negative safe integer`. Source hashes match the receipts below; the registry SHA-256 is identical on both sides: `414847dc28da8556bdd9a3ddf350f3d859d4668ecc237c1889b289d42d2879b8`.

The committed regression remains in the existing test file. Its original cases cover rendering, not numeric result limits; deleting unrelated rendering checks merely to eliminate the 30-line allocation would lose independent coverage. No new tests or budget changes were added for this supplementary run.

Not exercised locally: live Imgflip success, opt-in PNG rendering, full suite/build/typecheck. Current-head CI is linked above; no prior-head CI result is being substituted for it.

<details>
<summary>Exact CLI source receipts</summary>

Upstream `meme.mjs` SHA-256: `fd01ea51b17d2fa2dbc4ac0ad6909f87bb76a1149708629669c03e5b148217d3`.

Rebased `meme.mjs` SHA-256: `f0c1f7cffb41949baff2a826380182f0adf2f2fb0c442144801ba7491675f487`.

</details>

Independent Codex review covered the complete committed range `f615e96b55be..d1b007ea8b18`, including preservation of the upstream rendering fix and assertions, all limit consumers, and source-bound before/after proof. No actionable P0–P2 findings.

prs.title: fix(templates): inline review and publish fail when ClawHub handle has uppercase letters
prs.body:
Closes #199405

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: inline Template review (`templates.drafts.review`) and publication (`templates.drafts.publish`) fail with `"Your ClawHub account needs a personal publisher handle."` (`clawhub_identity_required`) when ClawHub `/api/v1/whoami` returns a mixed-case GitHub OAuth `user.handle` (such as `MertBasar0`).

## User Impact

User impact: Control UI Template creators whose ClawHub / GitHub personal handle contains uppercase characters can now review and publish Templates inline under their canonical lowercase `@<handle>/<slug>` personal namespace without false `clawhub_identity_required` failures.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawHub's `GET /api/v1/whoami` returns the GitHub-cased `user.handle` (for example `"MertBasar0"`), whereas ClawHub's publisher and package surfaces normalize personal handles to lowercase (`@mertbasar0/<slug>`, `ownerHandle: "mertbasar0"`, `https://clawhub.ai/mertbasar0/templates/<slug>`).

`personalPublisher` in `src/gateway/server-methods/templates-drafts.ts` is the sole `/api/v1/whoami` caller in `src/` (introduced in `f16e8bc092e7e`, carried through `d1c8d42588a4b` and `#196427`). Normalizing `result.user?.handle?.trim().toLowerCase()` at that producer boundary (net `0` production LOC: `+1/-1`) aligns review tokens, `prepareTemplateDraft`, upload `ownerHandle`, bound attempt status checks, and receipt URLs with ClawHub's canonical publisher handle.

## Evidence

### Live Windows Control UI Proof (Before vs After against live `https://clawhub.ai`)

**Before (`main` at `6001e95c4946`):** Clicking **Create template** in an isolated dev Gateway (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` + ephemeral port) with a ClawHub account whose `/api/v1/whoami` returns `"MertBasar0"` fails inline during `templates.drafts.review`:

![Before: Mixed-case ClawHub handle fails inline review](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ad4ef06-0a2b-4418-a445-91ff8fe21fad)

**After (this PR):** The same live Control UI flow hydrates **Review your Template** (`by @mertbasar0`) cleanly and completes end-to-end live publication (`Unpublished` -> `Publishing…` -> `Pending` -> `Published` at `https://clawhub.ai/mertbasar0/templates/pr-review-radar`, ClawScan `verdict: "benign"`, `scanStatus: "clean"`):

![After: Inline review card hydrated for @mertbasar0/pr-review-radar](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/605b909f-70e9-4b39-a0bd-45065fb330ef)

![After: Live ClawHub publication completed in Control UI](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec792831-9505-491a-ab1f-bed3cdf42801)

Live end-to-end Control UI recording (`recordVideo`, motion-trimmed):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eb7217e3-e806-41b3-b702-7718828cfe8d

Redacted live Gateway WebSocket RPC trace:

```text
# Before (unpatched main 6001e95c4946)
templates.drafts.create -> durationMs=52 ok=true
templates.drafts.review -> durationMs=942 ok=false errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage="Your ClawHub account needs a personal publisher handle."

# After (fix/templates-drafts-mixed-case-handle b761a69120a5)
templates.drafts.create -> durationMs=29 ok=true
templates.drafts.review -> durationMs=1418 ok=true
templates.drafts.publish -> durationMs=6929 ok=true publicationStatus=pending
templates.drafts.review(checkPublication=true) -> durationMs=4843 ok=true publicationStateStatus=published
```

### Tests & Checks

- Added boundary regression test `normalizes mixed-case and padded /whoami handles to lowercase personal publishers` in `src/gateway/server-methods/templates-drafts.test.ts` verifying mixed-case `/api/v1/whoami` handles (`"  MertBasar0  "`) normalize to `"mertbasar0"` across `templates.drafts.review`, `templates.drafts.publish` (`ownerHandle`), and bound attempt status polling:
  - Pre-fix run failed with `{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Your ClawHub account needs a personal publisher handle."}`.
  - Post-fix run: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/templates-drafts.test.ts` -> `31 passed (31)`.
- Production vs test LOC delta (`git diff --numstat`): `src/gateway/server-methods/templates-drafts.ts` `+1/-1` (**net `0` production LOC**); `src/gateway/server-methods/templates-drafts.test.ts` `+36/-1`.

prs.title: improve(ios): align app icon composition with Apple's design guidelines
prs.body:
Closes #187629
Related: #101411, #138002.

## What Problem This Solves

The iOS app icon’s mascot nearly fills the canvas, leaving little surrounding space instead of following Apple’s guidance to emphasize centered primary content with a simple background.

## User Impact

The iOS icon gains a more balanced composition while preserving its existing mascot, colors, and backgrounds. macOS, Debug icons, separate Watch app assets, and app behavior remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apple’s [Human Interface Guidelines for app icons](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/app-icons) recommend keeping primary content centered and using the production-template grids to guide placement. Apple also states:

> “you don’t need to fill the entire icon canvas with content.”

This reduces the iOS foreground to a centered 0.86 scale while retaining full-bleed backgrounds and leaving masking to the system. The chosen proportion is a design interpretation of Apple’s guidance, not an Apple-mandated percentage or a universal circular clipping boundary.

The unchanged macOS Original icon provides a supporting source-level sizing reference. A representative comparison with other iOS icons provides additional visual context; it is not the primary justification for this change.

The existing generator now produces release PNGs from a static, app-specific SVG rather than the animated browser favicon. Default remains opaque white, Dark retains transparency, and Tinted remains system-generated.

## Evidence

### iOS before and after

Actual baseline and regenerated PNG assets, shown with a presentation-only rounded mask. All annotations are in English. These are asset previews, **not native Home Screen screenshots**.

![iOS app icon before and after, with light and dark small-size previews](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/569b65bb-d646-4eab-8ae5-a307d1fe2316?raw=1)

### Supporting comparison with other iOS icons

Equal-size tiles using artwork returned by Apple’s US App Store lookup API for Shortcuts (915249334), WhatsApp (310633997), Signal (874139669), Telegram (686449807), Slack (618783545), and GitHub (1477376905). This representative asset comparison does not establish every app’s native appearance or system effects.

![Before and after alongside six other iOS app icons](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/23dccfd1-4ea8-4e31-ab9e-89ef0c0385b6?raw=1)

### macOS reference — unchanged

Both columns show the same source composition at 0.86 scale. Native Liquid Glass effects are omitted. No macOS source or compiled assets change.

![Unchanged macOS original icon as a sizing reference](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7187e880-ced5-4cc8-9de9-139ec6667139?raw=1)

### Validation

- All 29 release PNG assets regenerate byte-for-byte with `bash apps/ios/scripts/app-icon-variants.sh check`; existing manifest, alpha-channel, color-profile, and Debug checks pass.
- `bash -n apps/ios/scripts/app-icon-variants.sh`, `swiftc -typecheck apps/ios/scripts/app-icon-release.swift`, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Repository-pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.1: 0/1 files require formatting.
- Fresh independent source and asset review: no actionable findings. Original geometry and colors are preserved; no macOS, WatchApp, Debug, or manifest changes were found.
- Simplification pass reused the existing generation entry point and native rasterizer; no dependencies, runtime behavior, or settings were added.
- Baseline `37c408f2e32d7c8de48ea420ca5c9b1930e1d5fd`; the affected pre-existing generator/icon inputs are unchanged on fetched main `3263a51fc3a7a2ea36c48543cf62dd4035d4a7e8`.

**Draft / outstanding native proof:** native iOS asset-catalog compilation, Home Screen before/after captures, and installed-app light/dark/tinted validation have not been run. Local full Xcode/`actool` is unavailable and the paired Mac reports `COMPANION_APP_UNAVAILABLE`. Pinned SwiftLint 0.65.1 could not run because the local SourceKit framework is unavailable. No native build or lint success is claimed. Hosted CI and native visual proof remain required before marking this ready.

prs.title: feat(whatsapp): expose group membership actors to plugins
prs.body:
Related: #8495 (the group-event portion only; this proposal adds no auto-leave behavior).

## What Problem This Solves

Plugins cannot see who added the connected WhatsApp account to a group.

## User Impact

Plugins with the existing conversation-access grant can observe membership actors and affected participants, including groups whose messages are disabled. The proposed consumer is an operator-owned, read-only context plugin that uses configured trusted inviters as input to its group-admission policy.

Notifications are best effort and may repeat. A missing actor stays unknown, and a roster observation alone does not prove a new invitation. Group admission, tool access and send policy retain their current behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The observe-only `channel_group_membership_changed` hook carries event-scoped actor IDs, provider-supplied phone-number identities, affected participants and the connected account's identities. WhatsApp publishes live notifications through the existing hook runner and channel SDK subpath. The source connection owns cancellation; the timeout reference now lists the hook's two-second default.

Emitter calls rely on the existing [native plugin trust boundary](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/SECURITY.md#plugin-trust-boundary). The conversation-access grant controls observer registration and dispatch. This draft proposes the public observation contract; it adds no configuration, storage or automatic approval rule.

## Evidence

- Both new socket-to-hook tests fail on base `bde3017359ed` because no event reaches the plugin, and pass with the patch. The full WhatsApp command passes, including 1,024 Vitest tests.
- A CJS fixture loaded through the production `loadOpenClawPlugins` proves no callback without the conversation grant, delivery with it, and no callback after native replacement removes it. The retained global-runner reference also sees the revocation. This case and the neighboring replacement regression pass.
- Core and WhatsApp consumer type checks, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, SDK export synchronization and the existing test budget pass.
- Full build exited 0 on `5ca7ee39dff2`, including verification of all 160 public SDK subpaths. The review follow-up changes tests and documentation only. The build printed an advisory chat-boot gzip result of 1,276,937 B against 1,276,669 B; no budget was changed or base comparison made for that advisory.
- The committed SDK API comparison was stopped locally before completion; it produced no compatibility verdict. Current plugin/extension import-boundary checks and lint for the loader regression pass.

The local SDK declaration preflight exceeded its default five-minute limit. Generation and targeted lint passed with the supported `OPENCLAW_PLUGIN_SDK_BOUNDARY_ROOT_SHIMS_TIMEOUT_MS=1200000` setting. The broader plugin-contract aggregate was stopped after 20 minutes; reported SDK and entry guard cases passed, but there is no aggregate pass.

The simplification pass kept the existing socket, hook and SDK owners: +103 production lines and +233 testing lines, including routing, against the base. The loader test replaces weaker registration-only coverage. The tests fit the existing budget without raising its ceiling. Independent reviews found no actionable issue in the implementation or review follow-up. Fixtures are synthetic.

## Still Needed Before Merge

A redacted real WhatsApp membership notification through a loaded plugin remains outstanding; no live invitation or deployment was exercised. Maintainers also need to accept the concrete consumer and the pre-admission actor/roster disclosure under the existing conversation-access grant. The outstanding API comparison and broader required CI checks also remain before merge. This remains a draft for the contract decision.

prs.title: fix(deps): update direct Undici dependencies on stable release
prs.body:
Related: #182010, #185194

## What Problem This Solves

The `release/2026.10.9` branch still pins the directly declared Undici dependency to 8.11.2, while the fixes for published Undici advisories have already landed on `main`.

## User Impact

This brings the stable release's directly declared runtime dependencies and their resolved peer dependencies to the patched 8.12.2 release. Whether a particular advisory is exploitable depends on the application's actual use of the affected API; this PR does not establish an OpenClaw exploit.

## Why This Change Was Made

Backport the 8.11.2 to 8.12.2 dependency change already included in #182010, updating the root package and the five plugin manifests that directly pin Undici. Regenerate the workspace lock with the branch-pinned pnpm 12.15.0. A subsequent mainline refresh moved to 8.12.3 in #185194; this backport uses the previously tested 8.12.2 security fix to keep the proposed change narrow.

The relevant upstream advisories include [GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx](https://github.com/nodejs/undici/security/advisories/GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx) and [GHSA-4qv8-2p9j-2685](https://github.com/nodejs/undici/security/advisories/GHSA-4qv8-2p9j-2685). Their applicability depends on specific TLS options or EventSource usage, respectively.

**Remaining scope:** the lock still contains Undici 8.11.2 through `mailauth@7.1.0`, which pins it separately. This change does not remediate that transitive edge or prove that all packaged dependency paths are patched. The release owner should assess it separately before treating the release as fully remediated.

## Evidence

- A local manifest and lock check failed on the original six direct pins and passed after this change; it also records the remaining `mailauth` edge.
- `pnpm install --lockfile-only --ignore-scripts` completed with pnpm 12.15.0; a subsequent offline `--frozen-lockfile --lockfile-only --ignore-scripts` check passed for all 189 workspace projects. pnpm reported existing deprecated dependencies and peer warnings. Lock regeneration also records a newly published deprecation notice for `@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-base` without changing its version.
- Separately, an isolated OpenClaw 2026.10.8 installation with Undici 8.12.2 passed gateway health and authentication checks, a local OpenAI-compatible fixture, an HTTP CONNECT proxy fixture, and a synthetic TLS regression check. This is compatibility evidence for that installation, not a build or end-to-end test of this release branch.
- `git diff --check` passed. The full suite, release artifact build, and real external provider/channel operations have not been run for this PR. Hosted CI and maintainer review remain necessary.

prs.title: fix(codex): doctor --fix removes an appServer.command that points into a missing plugin generation
prs.body:
Related: #181037
Complementary prevention (merged): #191693

## What Problem This Solves

Recovery only: older cleanup versions may already have deleted the managed Codex generation referenced by `plugins.entries.codex.config.appServer.command`. The merged prevention fix #191693 keeps configured generations on disk, but cannot restore files already deleted.

## User Impact

Run `openclaw doctor --fix`, then restart the Gateway. Doctor removes only the stale command override so normal managed binary selection resumes (or `OPENCLAW_CODEX_APP_SERVER_BIN` applies). This may select a newer Codex binary. Other app-server settings, including arguments, remain unchanged. Plain Doctor previews the repair through its existing normalization flow.

Existing generation pins, unrelated custom executables, and non-missing filesystem errors remain untouched. No runtime fallback or cleanup changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the repair with the Codex plugin's existing Doctor normalizer. Recognize only the historical `openclaw-codex-8902d781d4__openclaw-generation__g-<16 lowercase hex>` directory layout beneath the state directory's `npm/projects`, and remove the override only when the generation stat returns `ENOENT` or `ENOTDIR`.

The historical name is deliberately frozen recovery data, not a second implementation of future install naming. This removes the hash-helper dependency, duplicate containment check, and nested exception scaffolding without adding SDK surface or state. Tests use an independent historical fixture and consolidate repeated setup and assertions.

Limits: no recovery of arbitrary custom paths, pinned non-default npm roots, relative command paths, external state-directory symlink aliases, or missing binaries inside an otherwise existing generation. No claim that updating alone applies this unpublished plugin repair; direct Doctor recovery is the supported scope.

## Evidence

- Simplified head: `090cc4fea9b5`; original contributor head: `5e9100d477b2`.
- Credential-free Linux ARM64 container, Node 24.22.1, frozen dependency install; no host state or credentials mounted. Tests ran with networking disconnected.
- Focused recovery and sibling Doctor suites: **60/60 passed**, two Vitest shards in 129.43s. After cleaning leftover source files from the reused image, the recovery suite was rerun: **21/21 passed**, 66.96s wrapper / 61.51s Vitest, dominated by compilation. The subsequent final change only adds required braces to a test conditional and adjusts its line allocation.
- Both primary recovery cases fail on pre-fix `c147613091ca` because the command remains configured; they pass with the repair.
- Targeted production/test TypeScript check passed using the repository test config with the two touched files as roots. Targeted source-backed lint: zero warnings/errors (23.4s). Pinned formatting, pre-commit checks, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent source review: no P0–P2 findings. Local ClawSweeper completed the full `c147613091ca..be697c268f72` range: no correctness/security findings. Final delta since that review is only the test braces and 122→124 line allocation; no production changes.
- Initial package-boundary validation encountered stale source files in the reused image; these were removed before the final focused checks. No successful full repository build is claimed.
- No new live Doctor/Gateway/model/channel or latest-stable updater run was performed. The contributor's earlier live evidence below is prior-head evidence, not a claim of current-head execution. Hosted CI is pending the push.

Compared with the original revision: production additions 62 → 44; regression test lines 394 → 124. The 124-line test allocation covers missing-generation recovery, managed selection, idempotency, preservation of settings and working pins, custom-path boundaries, symlinks, and filesystem-error distinctions.

**Live run on the current head: stable 2026.11.3 writes the state, `4087062` repairs it** (2026-11-14; Linux x64, Node 24.22.1). Added after the hosted review of `4087062da5d5`; the bullet above saying that no new live run was performed and that hosted CI was pending predates this run, and hosted CI on `4087062` has since passed (`ci-gate`). `4087062` merges main at `928c118f64db` into `090cc4fea9b5`; the four files of this PR are byte-identical in both. `openclaw@2026.11.3` was npm's latest stable release at each recorded checkpoint (`npm view openclaw dist-tags` reported latest 2026.11.3 when the sign-in window opened and at the end of the run). This head also identifies as 2026.11.3 (`OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (4087062)`), so the two builds differ by commit, not by version string. The candidate was a fresh clone of `4087062` (fetched by commit id), installed with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and built with `pnpm build` in an isolated directory. Test-host adaptation: the host also runs an unrelated, older OpenClaw Gateway as a system service under another account, and because of it this head's installed-service check refused to migrate the isolated state; every command of this head in this run, including its Gateway, therefore set `OPENCLAW_SYSTEMD_UNIT=openclaw-gateway-r5p-absent.service`, a unit that does not exist, so that check did not consider that service. That service was not changed, and the setting is unrelated to the Doctor repair under test. One isolated `HOME`, so the state directory is `<home>/.openclaw`; the Gateway listened on loopback with token auth; one real OpenAI OAuth sign-in (device code); the Telegram turns came from a self-created test bot in a private chat, with plain-text messages sent by hand; the CLI turns used `openclaw agent` through the Gateway, not `--local`. Redacted output is in the collapsed block below.

- **Stable writes the state.** `npm install -g --prefix <prefix> openclaw@2026.11.3 --allow-scripts=openclaw` (`OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (847611d)`), then `openclaw plugins install npm:@openclaw/codex@2026.11.3 --accept-capabilities`, which installed a flat managed project. The stable CLI wrote the Gateway, Telegram, tool-policy, and agent-runtime settings and the `appServer` keys `transport: "stdio"`, `homeScope: "agent"`, `mode: "guardian"`, `sandbox: "read-only"`, `approvalPolicy: "on-request"`, `requestTimeoutMs`, and `args`. At this point neither the stable CLI nor the plugin install had written `appServer.command` or `plugins.load.paths`.
- **Stable works before the stale override.** After sign-in, with the stable Gateway running, `openclaw agent --session-id r5p-cli` asked the model to remember the code word `cw-9235c2ad` and returned `CLI-PRE-OK`. After Telegram pairing, a message asking the bot to remember `tg-ab3117bc` was answered with `TG-PRE-OK`.
- **The stale override.** The Gateway was stopped, and the stable CLI set `appServer.command` to `<home>/.openclaw/npm/projects/openclaw-codex-8902d781d4__openclaw-generation__g-a727c792f2e53a82/node_modules/@openai/codex-linux-x64/vendor/x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/bin/codex`. The path was written by hand, not left behind by an update or a cleanup, and no directory existed at it while the stable build ran.
- **Before (stable 2026.11.3).** `openclaw doctor` and `openclaw doctor --fix --yes` keep the command: the preview listed no removal and left the config file byte-identical, and both runs printed core Doctor's existing custom-command warning (`Custom Codex app-server command bypasses OpenClaw's managed exact-version binary.`); `--fix` applied stable Doctor's own repairs (its output reports the agent roster, the `openai/gpt-6-astra` model entry, two session titles, a plugin-registry refresh, the OAuth directory, and three disabled skills, with two `Updated config` writes) and left `appServer.command` and the other `appServer` keys unchanged. With the stable Gateway running again, `openclaw agent --session-id r5p-cli-stable` exits 1 with `Codex catalog updater cannot run: <home>/.openclaw/npm/projects/openclaw-codex-8902d781d4__openclaw-generation__g-a727c792f2e53a82/node_modules/@openai/codex-linux-x64/vendor/x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/bin/codex or its working directory was not found`. A Telegram message asking for `STABLE-OK` got no reply within 3 minutes, and the Gateway logged `[telegram] dispatch failed: CodexAppServerSpawnError: Codex catalog updater cannot run: <home>/.openclaw/npm/projects/openclaw-codex-8902d781d4__openclaw-generation__g-a727c792f2e53a82/…`, then `spooled update <id> failed; keeping for retry`.
- **Which Codex plugin this head ran.** Two Codex plugins with the same version were present: the npm-installed `@openclaw/codex@2026.11.3` in the state, which does not contain the removal message, and the copy bundled with this head's build at `<src>/dist/extensions/codex`. In a source checkout, a compiled bundled plugin under `dist/extensions` ranks ahead of a same-id npm install regardless of version; only a `plugins.load.paths` selection ranks higher (`resolveDuplicatePrecedenceRank`, `src/plugins/manifest-registry-build.ts:151-183`, compared at `:455-470`). Observed in this run: after the hand-off, this head's `openclaw plugins inspect codex --json` reported `plugin.origin` `bundled` and `plugin.rootDir` `<src>/dist/extensions/codex`, with the npm copy listed only under `diagnostics`; Doctor printed `Kept bundled plugin "codex" from the OpenClaw source build; …`, and the CLI warned `duplicate plugin id detected; global plugin will be overridden by bundled plugin (<src>/dist/extensions/codex/index.js)`; the Gateway on this build logged `duplicate plugin id detected; global plugin will be overridden by bundled plugin (<src>/dist/extensions/codex/index.js)`; and the removal message appears in this build's copy but in no file of the npm copy.
- **After (this head, same state).** The stable Gateway was stopped, an empty directory was created at the seeded generation path, and the same `HOME` was handed to this head's build.
  - First repair, generation present: `openclaw doctor --fix --yes` ran this build's pending database migrations (state database v23–v40, listed under "Doctor changes"; agent database schema v27 -> v42; pre-migration SQLite backups saved under `<home>/.openclaw/state/` and `<home>/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/`) and kept `appServer.command`, since the generation directory existed; the `appServer` subtree was byte-identical. Config changes in this run: none (the config diff was empty).
  - The empty generation directory was then removed by hand, standing in for an older cleanup that deleted it.
  - Preview: `openclaw doctor` lists `Removed plugins.entries.codex.config.appServer.command; it pointed into an OpenClaw-managed Codex plugin generation that no longer exists. …` as a pending change and leaves the config file byte-identical.
  - Repair: `openclaw doctor --fix --yes` writes it. The only `appServer` change is the removed `command`; all config changes in this run: `plugins.entries.codex.config.appServer.command` removed, `meta.migrations.skillLibraryToolSplit` and `meta.migrations.skillWorkshopPlugin` added, and `wizard.lastRunAt` updated by Doctor's run metadata.
  - Restart: the Gateway started on this build; the Codex app-server line was `Codex app-server: using bundled 0.164.0 (no codex on PATH)`.
  - Turns: in the same CLI session, `openclaw agent --session-id r5p-cli` asked for the code word and returned `cw-9235c2ad`. In the same Telegram chat, the stable-phase message that the stable Gateway had kept for retry was answered with `STABLE-OK` after the hand-off (22:09 +09:00 in the Telegram client), before the follow-up was sent and with no other message sent to the bot in between; the follow-up was then answered with `tg-ab3117bc` (about 9 s after the Gateway received the message); no spawn error was logged after either reply.
- **Preview before migration.** On a separate state written by 2026.11.3 with the same kind of command and no directory, this build's `openclaw doctor` and `doctor --lint` exited 1 because the state-database migration had not run yet (`OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; …`, `… Client credentials require backed-up migration custody; stop the app and run openclaw doctor --fix.`), `doctor --json` reported `ok: false` with the pending migrations, and none of them listed the removal; `doctor --fix --yes` ran the migrations and removed the command in the same run. So the first Doctor command after the hand-off above was `doctor --fix --yes`, and the preview ran after it. The migration step is not part of this change.
- **Existing data still loads and works (data-model compatibility).** This head first upgraded the stored data (state database v23–v40; the agent database, which holds the sessions and the auth profile, schema v27 -> v42) and then used the state written by 2026.11.3 without a new sign-in, pairing code, or token: the CLI connected with the stored Gateway token. The CLI session and the Telegram chat that 2026.11.3 wrote before the hand-off were continued after the repair, and the code words given there were answered (above); the Telegram update that the stable Gateway had spooled for retry was processed and answered by this head after the hand-off. The Telegram turns used a self-created test bot in a private chat (BotFather Threaded Mode on), with plain-text messages sent by hand rather than through the `telegram-e2e-userbot` skill, which drives a leased Telegram Test Server user; the CLI turns used `openclaw agent` through the Gateway, not `--local`. The current-head run under **Evidence** does not depend on `openclaw update` or on the adapted run above: it is the same-state hand-off from an npm-installed 2026.11.3 to a source build of `4087062`.

**Open question:** should the update that retires a generation also prevent this first failure? That would mean treating a generation that is retired but still on disk as stale. Possible owners are core's retained-generation cleanup or the update-time Doctor; this PR does not choose between them.
