prs.title: fix: keep channel replies authorized through long-running attempts
prs.body:
Related: #145506

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes channel replies losing delivery authority while a fallback candidate is still running beyond its original attempt timeout.

## User Impact

Long-running replies can still prepare delivery until their candidate finishes or is cancelled. Cancellation revokes authority immediately, even while the model promise is still settling. Scheduled automation keeps its existing admission owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

Channel capabilities used a timeout-derived expiry although retries and approval waits can outlive one attempt. Use the existing run-owned lifetime and revoke it on the candidate's abort signal and in its existing finally block.

```diff
- expire authority at the attempt-derived deadline
+ retain authority while the candidate is active
+ revoke on cancellation, and always on settlement
```

This addresses one reproducible route to “plugin delivery capability is no longer active”; it does not claim to resolve every session-key or registry-replacement cause in the related reports. No timeout increase, new owner, or migration.

## Current real-model evidence — 7 November

[The exact-head compiled Gateway/channel flow now passes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186851#issuecomment-6713019903): 1/1, exit 0, on a7b13235d820. The existing dist/entry.js image ran the actual native model and registered qa-channel HTTP ingress/outbound path; one nonce reply reached the correct account/room. The exact inbound transport completion receipt confirmed deferred delivery/preview settlement before the 250 ms no-extra-message check and clean exit. Setup took 12.173 s and the real-model settled flow 8.077 s. No credential copy, build, install, source patch or extended deadline.

This closes the previously missing real-agent/model isolated compiled-Gateway registered-channel integration boundary. It does not turn the archived Telegram public:fallback or its CI result green, add a 41-minute real wait, or claim published-package installation/live Telegram proof. Existing simulated-clock/cancellation regressions keep their stated scope. The remaining inherited queue-context/CI disposition is separate; no empty push, manual CI retry or unqualified merge approval is inferred. Earlier dated statements that real-model proof was absent describe their then-current evidence, not this latest result.

## Evidence

### QA2 reproduced on the candidate and its exact CI main base — 7 November

The retained QA2 artifact 13046107768 from [run 41210635478/job124564973204](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41210635478/job/124564973204) was downloaded and inspected, not inferred from its job name. The historical synthetic merge 7c97777d is no longer served; no replacement is claimed to be that exact object.

Two separate private qaRuntime builds completed through the repository owner: candidate a7b13235d820b7a3b738543df5af180003077bd4 in 93.3s; actual historical CI main base 2d7376d2e6e111ae28bdf7d9e888cbb077139204 in 116s. Each build-info commit matched its checkout. Dependency declarations/lock/workspace files matched; dependencies were copied COW into an isolated baseline, not installed or reconciled. The first baseline setup missed workspace-local dependency links and stopped before runtime proof; those existing links were copied from the same declared dependency snapshot, then the qualified build succeeded. No source/config/timeout was changed to clear setup.

Both ran ONLY the original subagent-completion-direct-fallback scenario with mock-openai, crabline Telegram loopback, concurrency 1, fastMode:false and the unchanged 60s assertion. Both failed at public:fallback with the same event sequence and outcome: visible/silent controls delivered their exact markers; fallback child execution terminal/ok; fallback delivery suspended/permanent_failure; no expected fallback marker; loopback sendMessage aborted. The scenario and mock-provider source hashes match across both trees.

This establishes that the failed behavior already occurs on the CI main base without this PR delta. It is not evidence that the branch introduced the QA2 failure, and is not a passing QA verdict or proof that no other branch-specific defect can coexist. The A/B comparison alone did not identify the abort owner. [The subsequent first-abort observation and upstream source check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186851#issuecomment-6711153646) narrowed it to the current consuming async-work scope in the shared Telegram queue, not the prepared reader’s captured requestSignal. Merged PR #189457 already restores the submitted caller context before admission and dispatch; duplicate #194701 is superseded. That separate fix is not present merely because this candidate’s original QA2 artifacts exist, and this PR’s acceptance remains incomplete. No timeout, assertion, revocation check or retry protection was weakened.

The log wording about potentially sent chunks is classification, not proof of an identified delivered chunk. Existing ambiguous/post-dispatch retry protection is retained. The isolated observation and producer source work are now recorded in the linked follow-up. Reuse the merged queue-boundary correction; do not weaken the ended-scope guard, extend deadlines, or claim that these source findings pass the original scenario.

Private qaRuntime is not a public package/release build, a live Telegram test, real-model acceptance or full PR qualification. Both isolated Gateway probes completed and exited; no operator Gateway, installed package, updater attempt or workflow retry was touched. No new source commit/empty push is justified by these A/B results alone. Candidate/CI-base reports, diagnostics, raw local Gateway logs and a hashed comparison are preserved for the remaining cause investigation.


- On base `32f9477bf46d`, the two regression cases fail: authority expires after 41 simulated minutes with a 30-minute attempt timeout, and cancellation leaves authority valid until model settlement.
- With this change, all 6 execution-authority cases and 10 adjacent runner-utils cases pass: `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-message-authority.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-utils.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Focused typecheck, lint, formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Independent read-only review found no blocking issue.
- A separate isolated backport probe against the published 2026.10.8 package uses its actual channel minting and plugin delivery preparation: the baseline refuses after 41 minutes; the candidate succeeds. Wrong session/run, explicit revocation and registry replacement still reject. Zero external deliveries.
- Scope of proof: source tests use the real execute/mint/resolve path with the model and fallback selection mocked; elapsed time is simulated. No live provider retry, real approval wait or external channel delivery was exercised. Broad integration remains for CI.

Reversible code-only change; affected scope is channel reply delivery authority.

## Current source-boundary proof — 29 October

[Qualified local final-transport evidence and repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186851#issuecomment-6493700861) on head `d2c24b2642cd941ce3b4cb4c99141b64e40856c0`: three cases pass through production authority/delivery owners and actual loopback HTTP, including independent cancellation, normal settlement and candidate replacement while a started send is held before physical I/O. The existing final adapter-handoff hook now rechecks reply authority. Production core types, focused fixture types, canonical core/extension lint, formatting and native ratchet pass. The new fixture/source contains synthetic data only; raw private diagnostics remain withheld. No actual unresolved user decision prevented these local tests. This is explicit **source integration with model/fallback selection controlled by the fixture and a simulated clock jump**, not a shipped-package CLI, real-model/approval wait or live Telegram/Test Server claim. The original stronger shipped-flow request remains for fresh review to assess; no automated approval or merge acceptance is inferred.

## CI fixture repair — 29 October

Previous fixture-repair head: `8eb48f11b00270abf5635155f2a02c8b81071a4e` (fixture repair `be7378539e81` plus inventory-position-only conflict avoidance; all tested source/test blobs and lane membership unchanged). [CI diagnosis, repair and passing local checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186851#issuecomment-6494309715): move the host authority integration test out of Telegram extension-private ownership; consume the existing public test facade and route through the existing host-SQLite fork inventory. All three original observable-behavior cases and assertions are preserved. The normal wrapper now passes 3/3 without a pool override; the unchanged extension boundary suite passes 11/11, with core-import guard, focused types/lint/format and native budget checks passing. No production behavior or boundary guard changes. The previous entry and proof remain pinned to `d2c24b2642cd`; the fixture path at that revision was `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-reply-authority.telegram-http.test.ts`. New-head hosted CI is separate and not claimed green. The accepted loopback final-effect coverage remains source integration with a controlled model and simulated clock: **the required real-agent/model isolated-Gateway channel proof remains missing**. No new review request or live proof is claimed.

## Sparse type-graph repair — 29 October

Previously published head: `992fc2ee9ee6d57ec33234cdaa98cfae7fe9f178`. [Fresh CI diagnosis and proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186851#issuecomment-6494615934): the root integration owner is now `test/reply-authority.telegram-http.integration.test.ts`, still on the existing SQLite fork lane. The sparse core messaging graph drops from 264 Telegram source files to zero and the complete core tsgo boundary guard passes without any guard/config exception. The relocated three-case integration, focused root types/lint/format and native budget pass. Test bodies/assertions and production source are unchanged. Prior evidence retains its source identities. New-head hosted CI remains separate. The previous macOS job additionally invoked a tooling test absent from its PR checkout; that workflow/source-version mismatch is documented, not claimed repaired or attributed to queue capacity. **Real-agent/model isolated-Gateway proof remains outstanding**; this fresh result is still controlled-model/loopback/simulated-clock evidence.

## Current Darwin workflow/source integration — 31 October

Current published head: `a7b13235d820b7a3b738543df5af180003077bd4`, normal merge of pinned main `ef60dd054202b29fc88da7b460f0594266faf2ff`. [Qualification and limitations](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186851#issuecomment-6544754752): the required `test/scripts/pr-git-invocation.test.ts` is now present; the entire seven-file PR patch has the same stable patch-ID before and after integration. Checkout-local frozen/prefer-offline dependencies were reconciled with lifecycle scripts disabled. **13 distinct targeted tests passed**, with 12 Windows-only tooling skips on macOS. Core and focused integration types/lint, seven-file format, whitespace and the core tsgo boundary guard pass. Native ratchet against prepared main: **6,342,969 / 6,368,719**; no author budget increase. The initial default comparison against the old parent rejected inherited main allocation credit; that failure and the supported prepared-base qualification are disclosed in the evidence. GitHub confirms MERGEABLE; exact-new-head CI remains separate. **Real-agent/model Gateway proof remains outstanding**: the HTTP regression still uses controlled model/fallback selection and a simulated clock. No production installation, restart, broad core build, new grant or live-model/channel run.

## Exact-head QA failure — 31 October

At `a7b13235d820b7a3b738543df5af180003077bd4`, [QA Smoke CI profile 2/6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41210635478/job/124564973204) fails `subagent-completion-direct-fallback` at `[public:fallback]` after 60 seconds. The artifact records child execution `ok`, but delivery `suspended/permanent_failure`. Gateway logs show Telegram `sendMessage` aborting at 14:36:41.843Z, followed by an `OutboundDeliveryError` and the incomplete-send duplicate-prevention guard. Visible and silent control cases delivered.

This is the same observed failure sequence as the independently captured PR173026 run, not proof of a common root cause or an inherited-main classification. The announcement delivery owners, Telegram production sources and scenario are byte-identical to pinned main `ef60dd054202b29fc88da7b460f0594266faf2ff`; attribution still requires production-boundary reproduction. The CI gate also reports failure. No rerun or green-only push was requested.

The existing isolated reproduction attempt for this failure sequence stopped before Gateway startup at the runtime-artifact-publication guard; its checkout has no prepared `dist/entry.js`. That setup failure is not product proof, and no guard was bypassed. The source-pinned QA runtime must be qualified before identifying the abort owner and selecting a regression/fix. Previously passing focused tests are unchanged evidence, not a fix for this QA failure. **Exact-head CI and real-agent/model acceptance remain incomplete.**

prs.title: fix(browser): pages reach SSRF-blocked addresses by navigating after an action's 250 ms guard
prs.body:
Closes #198317

Builds on #198638, which moved document interception from each invocation to the tab. This PR adds the standing policy on top of it: about 190 added source lines, most of them in the new `pw-session-navigation-standing.ts`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a page reaches an address the browser SSRF policy blocks by navigating more than 250 ms after a browser action, because document interception ends when each action's guard window does.

## User Impact

User impact: in a tab OpenClaw has navigated or acted on, a document the page requests between actions is checked against the configured `browser.ssrfPolicy` and stopped before any request leaves the browser when the policy denies it.

What someone using that browser notices:

- Typing a blocked address into such a tab (or reloading or going back to one) shows Chrome's blocked page instead of loading it. To open it anyway, use a new tab or add the host to `browser.ssrfPolicy.allowedHostnames`.

  ![Chrome's "localhost is blocked" page after typing a blocked address into the tab the agent used](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/cc6765379f71c41f4d67ccd8d59a859bf622f810/images/2026/11/28e9055f-811c-4e91-9ccf-48ac4b281bca.png)

- A page keeps loading documents from the origin it is already on, so a localhost dev page opened under the automatic loopback exception can reload itself and follow its own links between tool calls. A different loopback port is a different origin and is stopped.
- A blocked navigation that a page script requested is cancelled silently and the tab keeps its page.
- Each document request in such a tab makes one round trip through the Gateway before it loads, between actions as well as during them.

Not covered, and listed in the docs: a popup's first request, Service Worker traffic, `fetch`/XHR and other subresources, tabs OpenClaw has not navigated or acted on, the time the Gateway's connection to the browser is down (a tab is covered again from its next guarded action), and speculation-rules prefetch on browsers OpenClaw did not launch.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Interception stays on for the tab's lifetime instead of only while an invocation claims it. With no claim, the tab's standing policy decides each document: the configured policy without invocation-scoped grants such as the loopback exception, which end with the invocation. Interception stays document-only, so CORS preflights and subresources stay on Chromium's native path.
- The standing policy is one small module, `pw-session-navigation-standing.ts`; the fence itself changes by about 45 lines.
- The fence never sends `Fetch.disable`, so the extension relay's refusal of `Fetch.enable` during a release, which #198638 handles, has no release to meet here. A claim only starts document tracking (`Network.enable`), after the last release is answered, once per target while the tab is claimed. It waits for that answer no longer than the navigation timeout, then fails without starting tracking; having started nothing, it only gives up its claim. A claim whose tracking fails to start fails its invocation.
- Same-origin documents are allowed because a page can already `fetch()` its own origin, so they reach nothing new.
- Whether a denial shows the blocked page or is cancelled silently depends on whether the navigation looks browser-initiated (no page request event, no referrer, top-level). A page can imitate that, so the check only picks how the denial looks; the request is denied either way.

One tradeoff for reviewers: the same-origin allowance is checked ahead of `blockedHostnames`. A tab already on a host that a config reload later blocks keeps loading that origin. `main` enforces nothing between actions, so this is not a widening against `main`.

## Evidence

- **Reproduction:** a real-Chromium test presses a key, and the page navigates to a denied address 500 ms later while a fixture server at that address counts requests. On `main` the server receives the document and it becomes the tab's page. With this change it receives nothing and the tab keeps its page.
- **Through a Gateway with a real agent and model, across an upgrade from v2026.11.3** (one run in a clean macOS VM, headed managed browser):
  - **Setup:** the Gateway of release `2026.11.3` (from npm) runs with `browser.ssrfPolicy: { dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork: false, allowedHostnames: ["127.0.0.1"] }`. One turn through `openclaw agent` with Claude Sonnet 5.5 has the agent use the browser tool to load a page, press a key, wait 3 seconds and take a snapshot. The page navigates to a policy-denied address 500 ms after the key press, and a fixture server at that address counts requests.
  - **On `2026.11.3`:** the denied server received the document and the tab ended on it.
  - **Upgrade:** the Gateway is stopped, this PR's build runs `doctor --fix` on the same state and config, and starts on them. The policy settings are the same before and after, and the browser profile that `2026.11.3` created is reused.
  - **Same turn on this PR's build:** no request reached the denied server and the tab kept its page. The agent's reply: "pressing `a` succeeded. The URL didn't change". The Gateway log has `Stopped a document the page requested between browser actions`.

    ```
    2026.11.3, after the agent turn:   denied server requests=2; tab "Denied page reached" http://localhost:DENIED_PORT/denied
    policy settings under 2026.11.3:   {"dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork":false,"allowedHostnames":["127.0.0.1"]}
    policy settings after doctor --fix: {"dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork":false,"allowedHostnames":["127.0.0.1"]}
    this PR, after the agent turn:     denied server requests=0; tab "Source page" http://127.0.0.1:SOURCE_PORT/
    ```

  - **Manual navigation afterwards**, typed into the real address bar of that upgraded profile's window:
    - The denied address in the tab the agent used: Chrome's blocked page (the screenshot under User Impact), no request reached the server.
    - An allowed address in the same tab loads:

      ![An allowed address typed into the tab the agent used loads](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/cc6765379f71c41f4d67ccd8d59a859bf622f810/images/2026/11/7742ab04-285c-400a-9ea6-c69587e9fe86.png)

    - The denied address in a tab OpenClaw never navigated or acted on loads, as the limits above say:

      ![The denied address typed into a tab OpenClaw never used loads](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/cc6765379f71c41f4d67ccd8d59a859bf622f810/images/2026/11/19a1ef2d-904d-4afc-aae2-e702ff4b08af.png)

  - The model calls leave the VM through a forwarder that adds the API key outside it, so no key is in the VM. The prompt asks for `navigate` in the existing tab, because `2026.11.3` refused `open` on a headed managed browser under this explicit strict policy.
- **Through the production extension relay:** real Chromium 156 with the bundled extension 2.3.0 loaded unpacked and paired with the Gateway's relay, in a clean macOS VM. The relay and the extension are unmodified; a tap on the relay's client socket in the test records each `Fetch`/`Network` enable and disable request and its answer. A fixture server at a policy-denied address counts requests.
  - A key press makes the page navigate to the denied address 500 ms after the action returned: no request reached the server and the tab kept its page.
  - Back-to-back key-press actions on one tab, the second making the page navigate to the denied address, and a second action started at the moment the first action's release reached the relay: blocked in 6 of 6 rounds, no request reached the server.
  - Each tab gets one `Fetch.enable` and no `Fetch.disable`; between actions only `Network.disable` and `Network.enable` cross the relay, the enable after the disable is answered.

    ```
    2222.0ms  client -> relay  Fetch.enable #256
    2222.9ms  relay -> client  Fetch.enable #256 answered
    2482.6ms  client -> relay  Network.disable #262
    2483.3ms  relay -> client  Network.disable #262 answered
    2483.7ms  client -> relay  Network.enable #263
    B rejected: Navigation blocked ...; denied server requests=0; tab kept its page
    ```

- **Live tests (real Chromium over direct CDP):** 34 pass: the between-actions suite (5), redirect authority (12), page-cancelled interception (3), download policy (7), current-document download (5) and native CORS (2). Three native-CORS cases need `127.0.0.2`, which macOS does not route; they time out there on `main` as well.
- **Unit tests:** 195 of 195 pass in the eight browser test files that cover the fence, its callers and the navigation guard, including a release answered late, a release never answered, a claim whose tracking fails to start, and the dashboard navigation test. That test holds each navigation attempt at its fence preparation, which on this branch is the claim's tracking start because interception stays on for the tab. Targeted typecheck, lint and format are clean.
- **Checked on a prior revision of this change with the same standing-policy logic, not rerun on this head:**
  - Independent adversarial runs: 34 page-initiated navigation vectors (top-level, frames, out-of-process and nested iframes, redirects, rapid and overlapping navigations) reached a denied server on an unfenced tab and none did on a fenced one. A loopback port hop, a same-origin redirect to a denied port, and a page imitating a typed navigation were each stopped before any request.
  - Page loads, cross-site iframes, reload and back, CORS preflights, downloads, form POSTs, allowed redirects, and `blob:`/`data:`/`srcdoc` frames behaved between actions as on an unfenced tab.

Not checked: Linux and Windows, and remote-CDP profiles.

prs.title: fix(codex): Gateway main thread stalls when a turn streams long reasoning
prs.body:
Closes #112698

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Gateway main thread stalls for seconds when a Codex-runtime turn streams a large amount of reasoning text; the main-thread work grows with the square of the reasoning length.

In a first reproduction run on `5e78e3516ae1` (main on 2026-11-12), one 256 KiB reasoning item streamed as 16-character deltas took about 6.5 s of main-thread CPU (four times the length cost about 16 times the CPU; about 6.8 s with no channel callback attached). When the same notifications arrived as one client-to-router write, a 0 ms timer queued before the write fired about 6.9 s late. These are component measurements on Linux x64 with Node 24.22.1; the issue reports ~22 s stalls on macOS arm64, and seconds are not compared across hosts.

## User Impact

User impact: when reasoning deltas append to the end of the streamed text, as in the measured component and client-to-router paths, the Codex reasoning projection's main-thread work now grows in proportion to the reasoning length instead of its square; other write orders keep a canonical rebuild per delta (see the accepted boundary below). In the measured component path, a 256 KiB reasoning item drops from 6,455 ms to 29.1 ms of main-thread CPU, while Web chat thinking events, channel reasoning snapshots and transcript reasoning stay byte-identical to the base across 5,000 seeded sequences. No configuration, protocol or migration change. With a synthetic Codex app-server sending one 256 KiB reasoning item of script-generated text in one burst through a built Gateway, the base spent 6,011.5 ms of Gateway main-thread CPU on the turn, its slowest `/healthz` round trip was 5,767.4 ms and it logged a `main-thread stall` warning in every sample; with this change, 557.2 ms, 135.6 ms and no warning, with the final reasoning intact (medians of five Gateway instances per side; see Evidence). A live run with a real model through an isolated Gateway with the change also kept its final reasoning intact, but its turns streamed at most 465 characters of reasoning, too short to show the cost.

## Why This Change Was Made

`CodexReasoningProjection` is the only writer of Codex reasoning text. It now keeps each item's flattened text and its last visible section, and updates both at its three writes (deltas, item started, item completed) before its first `await`. A delta that appends to that last section is appended to the item text, and to the turn-wide snapshot when this item ends it. Every other write (a hidden section becoming visible, an earlier section, whitespace written to a hidden section, an authoritative started or completed item) rebuilds with the existing rules: summary before content, sections by index, whitespace-only sections dropped, joined by blank lines. The merged CLI (#144350) and native (#123120) reasoning fixes follow the same rule: append only on a proven tail write, canonical rebuild otherwise. The per-item `thinking` events that Web chat reads (from #188076) and the cumulative `onReasoningStream` snapshots keep the same fields and values.

Left unchanged on purpose:

- Router scheduling: the thread router still drains ready notifications in order without yielding. The issue's review asked that scheduling changes follow boundary measurements; after this change the 256 KiB burst below delays a waiting timer by 69.9 ms, under the 1,000 ms event-loop-delay warning threshold.
- Snapshot coalescing per event-loop turn: it would change the cadence channels see, and the performance guide records coalescing being reverted three times.
- Callback contracts: `onReasoningStream` still receives the cumulative snapshot and `thinking` events still carry the item's full text. The issue's parse budget and timing spans are not added; no measurement points to them.

This takes over #174464 by xydt-juyaohui, which has had no new commits since 2026-10-16, reusing its idea of extending the delivered snapshot only when the touched section ends it and its "delta after an authoritative replacement" test case; the commit credits xydt-juyaohui as co-author.

## Evidence

Base `5e78e3516ae1` vs base plus this PR's production change, on Linux x64 with Node 24.22.1, in-process Vitest on Node (`OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`), main-thread CPU from `process.threadCpuUsage`. The tables below are synthetic component and client-to-router proof, not an end-to-end Gateway latency claim; the Gateway runs (a synthetic app-server run on both sides, and a live model run with the change) are reported separately below.

Acceptance rules were written before the after run: a linear shape, no regressed cell, a 1,000 ms responsiveness bound for the client-to-router burst, a work-count bound, and byte-identical output (full text in the details below). Result: all five held.

Counts are deterministic and comparable across hosts. "Long-string work" is the characters in `trim` / `startsWith` receivers and `Array.prototype.join` results that carry the stream's marker:

| Workload | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Committed burst test: 2 × 1,024 deltas (32 KiB streamed), bound 131,072 | 184,616,720 | below the bound |
| Same burst at 2 × 8,192 deltas (256 KiB streamed), bound 1,048,576 | 11,811,700,496 | 131,090 |

Main-thread CPU in ms (median / p95), 16-character deltas, five alternating base/candidate processes with samples pooled, 1-minute host load 1.00 to 3.12 during base runs and 1.02 to 1.76 during candidate runs:

| Workload | Samples per side | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| One content item with a channel callback, 16 KiB | 35 | 27.8 / 29.0 | 2.00 / 2.00 |
| Same, 64 KiB | 35 | 404 / 422 | 7.00 / 8.15 |
| Same, 256 KiB | 35 | 6,455 / 6,597 | 29.1 / 31.2 |
| 256 KiB as one client-to-router write | 15 | 6,833 / 6,879 | 59.3 / 63.3 |
| Delay of a 0 ms timer queued before that write | 15 | 6,860 / 6,904 | 69.9 / 75.0 |

After the fix, 256 KiB costs 4.15 times the 64 KiB median in the main workload (largest of the five timed workloads: 4.29; linear is about 4). Removed per delta: two full rebuilds of the item text, a prefix comparison against it, and, with a channel callback, a rebuild of every item for the snapshot. Moved the wrong way: none in CPU, timer delay or end-of-run memory. End-of-run memory of the whole probe process, including Vitest (context only): RSS 2,565 to 2,591 MiB before and 1,581 to 1,707 MiB after; heap used 1,651 to 1,693 MiB before and 704 to 716 MiB after.

Tests in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.commentary.test.ts`:

- `keeps a client-to-router reasoning burst linear for summary and content streams` writes 1,024 summary and 1,024 content deltas as one NDJSON chunk through a real `CodexAppServerClient` (in-memory transport) and thread router. It first checks that all 2,048 snapshots arrived before the spies are restored, then asserts the final snapshot, each item's last `thinking` text, concatenated deltas and event count, that completed items with the same text add nothing, the transcript reasoning, and last the long-string work bound. On the base it fails only on that last assertion; with the fix it passes.
- `preserves reasoning events and snapshots when $label` (6 cases) pins `thinking` events, snapshots and reasoning-end calls with literal expectations for each new branch: a hidden later section turning visible, a summary append before visible content, an earlier item growing after a later one, a delta after an authoritative replacement, started sections taking later deltas, and whitespace-only reasoning. Result: all six pass on the base and with the fix.
- An uncommitted seeded differential over 5,000 random sequences (summary and content deltas at varying indexes, whitespace-only and split-surrogate deltas, started and completed items, several items, with and without a channel callback, terminal snapshots) compared every `thinking` event, snapshot, reasoning-end count and final transcript reasoning between base and fix: no mismatches.

The performance guide keeps proof in the PR rather than in new tests; one regression is still committed because the root `AGENTS.md` says "Fixes prove the invariant: one or two tests of the broken behavior, red on the base, green with the fix, committed with the fix", and the ClawSweeper review on #112698 asked for "a failing client-to-router burst regression covering summary and content streams"; the table cases pin the new branches. Against `5e78e3516ae1`, production is +62 / -21 in one file and tests are +298 lines in the existing commentary test file that holds the reasoning cases, under the 400-line per-PR test-line allowance, so no allocation record is needed. The production growth is the recorded item text, last visible section and turn snapshot, plus one helper that fills the item text and last visible section at writes (the turn snapshot is rebuilt on read and extended on tail appends); that helper replaces the helper that rebuilt the text on every read, and every write other than an append to the last visible section still takes the canonical rebuild.

Targeted format, lint, type and focused-test checks all pass, as do the Codex extension lane (`pnpm test:extension codex`) and the plugin contract suite (`pnpm test:contracts:plugins`); details below. The focused file runs in 12.33 s locally (Vitest `Duration`, 2% of it in tests; the burst test itself takes 52 ms); CI: 24.70 s for this file in the Bun `changed-extensions-config-1` shard (Vitest `Duration`, 1% of it in tests; the burst test takes 38 ms).

Synthetic app-server run through a built Gateway (2026-11-15). The hosted model's reasoning summaries in the live run below stayed under 500 characters per turn, too short to show the reconstruction cost, so the same Linux x64 host (Node 24.22.1) ran an isolated Gateway with the Codex runtime against a synthetic Codex app-server: a 482-line Node script that speaks the app-server JSON-RPC protocol over stdio, built on the repository's [`scripts/e2e/lib/codex-app-server-fixture.mjs`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5e78e3516ae13a6a7612ed0ca715bc16503a3f51/scripts/e2e/lib/codex-app-server-fixture.mjs) and wired in through `plugins.entries.codex.config.appServer.command`. It answers the handshake, thread and turn requests, waits 1,000 ms after `turn/start`, then streams one reasoning item of 65,536 or 262,144 characters as 16-character `item/reasoning/textDelta` notifications (4,096 or 16,384 deltas) written to the pipe in one write, followed by the completed item, a one-line reply and `turn/completed`. The reasoning text is generated by the script, not by a model, and arrives faster than any model stream we measured; this run shows how the reconstruction cost behaves in a real Gateway, not the reported stall on the reporter's host. No provider or channel credentials were configured; no child process and no TCP or UDP socket of the synthetic app-server was seen (sampled every 200 ms during each turn); and the Gateway listened on loopback only, with the client connecting to it over loopback.

Base `5e78e3516ae1` and base plus this PR (production file identical to head `7d7c43fa222e`) were built in separate worktrees, and each Gateway ran from its tree's `openclaw.mjs` (`gateway run --bind loopback`). Five Gateway instances per side ran strictly alternating (ABAB, base first), each from fresh state, and every start checked the production file's sha256 and the built output (`reasoningSnapshotItemId`, a name this PR adds, and `reasoningItemText`, a name it removes). Each instance ran one uncounted 16 KiB warm-up turn, then a 64 KiB and a 256 KiB turn, each a Gateway `agent` request in a new session from a client that declared the `tool-events` capability and received the run's `thinking` events. Main-thread CPU is read from `/proc/<pid>/task/<pid>/stat` outside the Gateway (process CPU, all threads, from `/proc/<pid>/stat`) from the request until 1 s after the final response, minus the Gateway's idle rate from a 10 s measurement just before that turn; the window covers the whole turn, not only the reasoning. `/healthz` was polled by an independent request every 200 ms from 2 s before the request until 5 s after the final response, and `main-thread stall` warnings were counted in the Gateway file log, once per log line, from 1 s before the request until about 6 s after the final response. The stored reasoning was read back in full with `chat.message.get`, because `chat.history` replaces a message over 128 KiB with a placeholder ([`src/gateway/chat-history-budget.ts:19`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5e78e3516ae13a6a7612ed0ca715bc16503a3f51/src/gateway/chat-history-budget.ts#L19)). Acceptance rules were frozen in a file before the first counted sample (single uncounted probe turns ran before that; rules and results in the details below). Host 1-minute load: 0.03 to 0.60.

Gateway CPU, slowest `/healthz` round trip and longest `main-thread stall` warning in ms, median (min–max) over five samples per side, one per Gateway instance, rounded to 0.1 ms:

| Size | Side | Main-thread CPU | Process CPU | Slowest `/healthz` | `main-thread stall` warnings | Final reasoning intact |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| 64 KiB | Before | 516.7 (512.1–536.9) | 1,139.5 (1,119.9–1,163.7) | 227.1 (167.2–247.1) | none | 5 of 5 |
| 64 KiB | After | 361.8 (354.6–392.1) | 900.3 (822.2–991.9) | 23.1 (1.0–30.6) | none | 5 of 5 |
| 256 KiB | Before | 6,011.5 (5,957.0–6,031.7) | 7,286.1 (7,172.2–7,378.5) | 5,767.4 (5,743.7–5,816.3) | 1 per sample, 3,218 (1,003–4,588) | 5 of 5 |
| 256 KiB | After | 557.2 (534.5–704.2) | 1,328.7 (1,288.9–1,578.5) | 135.6 (109.1–263.9) | none | 5 of 5 |

On the base, each 256 KiB sample's slowest `/healthz` round trip was 5,743.7 to 5,816.3 ms, and the Gateway logged one `main-thread stall` warning per sample, of 1,003 to 4,588 ms; with this change, no sample logged a warning and the slowest round trip in any 256 KiB sample was 263.9 ms. Final reasoning: in all 20 samples, the text the client last received in `thinking` events and the reasoning stored in the session both matched the generated text (length, bytes and sha256).

Frozen rules: no regression, responsiveness, complete final reasoning, and identity and comparability held. The shape rule did not apply: it is set only when the after-fix 64 KiB median reaches 3 times the after-fix idle noise floor, and 361.8 ms is below 3 × 1,140 = 3,420 ms. That floor is the largest spread of main-thread CPU over three 3,036 ms idle windows run back to back right after each Gateway was ready; the spread was 1,020 to 1,140 ms on all ten instances, and we did not attribute it further. It is separate from the per-turn 10 s idle measurement used for the net CPU above. The Gateway run therefore makes no length-scaling claim; the shape is shown by the component table above.

The CPU above includes the Gateway's whole handling of each `thinking` event. This run does not exercise channel reasoning callbacks (`onReasoningStream`): the Gateway `agent` request used here does not attach one (the embedded reply runner passes one only when typing starts on reasoning or its caller supplies a callback, [`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-embedded-candidate.ts:270-271`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5e78e3516ae13a6a7612ed0ca715bc16503a3f51/src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-embedded-candidate.ts#L270-L271)), so that path is covered only by the component table above.

The workload is not committed to this PR. The synthetic app-server and its text generator are in the details below with their sha256; the fixture it imports is the repository file, unchanged. The host scripts that started and stopped the Gateways, sent the turns, sampled CPU, `/healthz`, the Gateway log and the app-server's descendants and sockets, ran the pause control and recomputed the tables are too long for this description and are not attached; the details below describe what they did.

Live model run (2026-11-13), with the change only: an isolated Gateway bound to loopback with no channels, the Codex runtime pinned for `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` (default reasoning effort) and an OpenAI device-code sign-in, on the same host, from a tree with the same content as head `7d7c43fa222e`, built once before the run. Each measured turn was one Gateway `agent` request asking for a hand-worked tiling count without tools, from a client that declared `tool-events` and recorded the turn's events. The three measured turns streamed 178, 287 and 465 characters of final reasoning in total (longest item 110), below the 16,384-character threshold registered before the run, so this run checks real-model correctness, not the cost. No `main-thread stall` warning was logged during them, the slowest `/healthz` round trip was 7 ms, and for all 13 reasoning items the final text in the streamed thinking events was byte-identical (sha256) to the reasoning stored in the session, which comes from the completed item. Before sign-in, a 12 s pause produced a stall warning, so the warning was visible in that setup. No live run was made on the base.

Accepted boundary: a delta that does not extend an item's last visible section, such as a summary append after content is visible or whitespace written to a later hidden section, keeps the canonical rebuild for that item (once per delta, where main rebuilt twice) and compares prefixes only when the text changed; with a channel callback, such a delta that changes the text, or any text-changing delta to an item other than the last one with text, re-joins the turn snapshot from the stored item texts, which is linear work per delta. Downstream channel consumers are unchanged; one that reads every cumulative snapshot still pays for its length (a callback reading each snapshot's last character costs 17.8 ms at 64 KiB and 776 ms at 256 KiB after the fix, against 439 ms and 6,799 ms before; reported, not gated).

Not covered: a live run on the base with a real model (none was made, so there is no live reproduction of the reported stall; the long stream above is synthetic and written in one burst, and the hosted model's reasoning summaries stayed under 500 characters per turn); the reporter's macOS arm64 host; channel reasoning callbacks in a real Gateway (covered by the component table only); a length-scaling check in the Gateway run (its shape rule did not apply); the full changed gate (`pnpm check:changed`).

Local review: autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, medium effort, P0–P2, one pass) of this patch against `5e78e3516ae1` reported `scoped-clean` with no accepted or actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper review (`--local-range`, base `5e78e3516ae1`, this diff and description) ran three times before the live Gateway run with no findings, risks, or security concerns; each run rated real-behavior proof insufficient because the live run was then missing.

<details>
<summary>Acceptance rules, workloads, full table, and Codex source</summary>

Acceptance rules as written before the after run:

1. Shape: after the fix, the 256 KiB CPU median is less than 8 times the 64 KiB median (linear is about 4, the base about 16) for the main workload and four references: no channel callback, summary deltas, a 17th item after 16 completed 16 KiB items, and one client-to-router write.
2. No regression: in each of those cells the after median is at most the before median; any cell at 1.2 times before or more stops the change.
3. Responsiveness: after the fix, a 0 ms timer queued before a 256 KiB client-to-router write fires less than 1,000 ms late (median), the diagnostic liveness `event_loop_delay` warning threshold (`src/logging/diagnostic-liveness.ts:7`).
4. Work count: long-string work stays below 4 times the streamed characters after the fix and is at least 100 times that bound on the base; the committed regression fails on the base only on that assertion.
5. Byte-identical output: a seeded differential over at least 2,000 sequences finds no mismatch; the existing reasoning tests and the new table cases pass with the fix, and the table cases also pass on the base.

A callback that reads each snapshot's content is reported only, not gated.

Workloads: an uncommitted probe in the Codex extension's test project feeds 16-character `item/reasoning/textDelta` (or `summaryTextDelta`) notifications through the public `CodexAppServerEventProjector.handleNotification` up to 16, 64 and 256 KiB. The burst workload writes them as one NDJSON chunk to a real `CodexAppServerClient` over an in-memory transport and routes them through the thread router, with a 0 ms timer queued just before the write. Main workload: 2 warmups and 7 samples per size; references: 1 and 3. Base and candidate processes alternate five times, and only the production file is switched between them. The 256 KiB count row reuses the committed test's wiring and spies. The differential is a second uncommitted probe with a deterministic PRNG. p95 is nearest-rank over the pooled samples.

Rerunnable: `pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.commentary.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. The owner bench `extensions/codex/src/test-support/event-projection.bench.ts` was not extended: by default each workload runs 100 warmups, then five samples that each time 2,000 iterations and repeat those 2,000 under allocation sampling, while this defect is growth with stream length and one 64 KiB stream alone costs about 0.4 s of CPU per iteration on the base; the deterministic committed count carries the rerunnable proof instead. The count covers `trim` and `join` as well as `startsWith` (which #123120 counted) because the per-delta rebuild is the dominant cost here; counting `startsWith` alone would let a fix that keeps both rebuilds pass.

Full table (ms, median / p95, pooled over five processes per side; main-thread CPU except the timer-delay rows):

| Workload | Size | Samples per side | Before | After |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| One content item with a channel callback | 16 KiB | 35 | 27.8 / 29.0 | 2.00 / 2.00 |

```js
function parseArgs(argv) {

  for (let index = 0; index < argv.length;) {

    if (key.startsWith("--config=")) {
      const value = key.slice("--config=".length);
      if (!value) stop("--config: 值为空");
      configOverrides.push(value);
      index += 1;

      if (!value) stop("-c: 值为空");

  for (const key of required) {

  if (!ALLOWED.delay.has(values["--delay-ms"])) stop("--delay-ms: 取值未预审");
  if (!ALLOWED.model.has(values["--model"])) stop("--model: 取值未预审");
  const marker = "/bin/";
  const scriptPath = process.argv[1].replaceAll("\\", "/");
  const splitAt = scriptPath.lastIndexOf(marker);
  if (splitAt <= 0) stop("argv[0]: 脚本路径不在 bin 目录");
  const allowedPrefix = `${scriptPath.slice(0, splitAt)}/stub/`;
  const log = values["--log"];
  const checkedLog = log.replaceAll("\\", "/");
  const leaf = checkedLog.slice(allowedPrefix.length);
  if (!checkedLog.startsWith(allowedPrefix) || !leaf || leaf.includes("/") || leaf === "." || leaf === "..") {

function stringsIn(value, into = []) {
  if (typeof value === "string") {
    into.push(value);
  } else if (Array.isArray(value)) {
    for (const item of value) stringsIn(item, into);
  } else if (value && typeof value === "object") {
    for (const item of Object.values(value)) stringsIn(item, into);
  }
  return into;
}

function readPlan(params) {
  const matches = stringsIn(params)
    .flatMap((text) => [...text.matchAll(/STUBPLAN\{([^}]*)\}/gu)].map((match) => match[1]));
  if (matches.length !== 1) return { ok: false };
  const burst = matches[0].match(/^size=([0-9]+);delta=16;mode=burst$/u);
  if (burst) {

    return Number.isSafeInteger(size) && size >= 1 && size <= 1_048_576
      ? { ok: true, size, mode: "burst" }

  const paced = matches[0].match(/^size=([0-9]+);delta=16;mode=paced;batch=([0-9]+);interval=([0-9]+)$/u);

  return `${JSON.stringify(message)}\n`;
}

function turnResult(turnId) {
  return {
    turn: {
      id: turnId,
      items: [],
      itemsView: "notLoaded",
      status: "inProgress",
      error: null,
      startedAt: null,
      completedAt: null,
      durationMs: null,
    },
  };
}

function finishMessages({ text, size, threadId, turnId, itemId, messageId }) {
  const reasoningStart = { type: "reasoning", id: itemId, summary: [], content: [] };
  const reasoningDone = { type: "reasoning", id: itemId, summary: [], content: [text] };
  const reply = { type: "agentMessage", id: messageId, text: `LP112698-STUB ${size}` };
  const messages = [
    { method: "item/started", params: { item: reasoningStart, threadId, turnId } },
  ];
  for (let offset = 0; offset < text.length; offset += 16) {
    messages.push({
      method: "item/reasoning/textDelta",
      params: { threadId, turnId, itemId, contentIndex: 0, delta: text.slice(offset, offset + 16) },
    });
  }
  messages.push(
    { method: "item/completed", params: { item: reasoningDone, threadId, turnId } },
    { method: "item/started", params: { item: reply, threadId, turnId } },
    { method: "item/completed", params: { item: reply, threadId, turnId } },
    {
      method: "turn/completed",
      params: {
        threadId,
        turn: {
          id: turnId,
          items: [reply],
          itemsView: "full",
          status: "completed",
          error: null,
          startedAt: 1,
          completedAt: 2,
          durationMs: 1,
        },
      },
    },
  );
  return messages;
}

const options = parseArgs(process.argv.slice(2));
// 第一行记完整 argv 和配置覆盖，便于采样窗口核对真实启动形状；不采集环境信息。
appendFileSync(options.requestLog, `${JSON.stringify({
  stub: "launch",
  argv: process.argv,
  configOverrides: options.configOverrides,
})}\n`);
let turnNumber = 0;
const pending = new Map();

function recordRequest(method) {
  appendFileSync(options.requestLog, `${JSON.stringify({ stub: "request-method", method })}\n`);
}

function recordRejected(kind, method) {
  appendFileSync(options.requestLog, `${JSON.stringify({ stub: kind, method })}\n`);
}

function sendMethodError(id) {
  process.stdout.write(line({
    id,
    error: { code: -32601, message: "stub: method not supported" },
  }));
}

function recordNotifications(messages) {
  const counts = {};
  const runs = [];
  for (const message of messages) {
    if (typeof message?.method !== "string") continue;
    counts[message.method] = (counts[message.method] ?? 0) + 1;
    const last = runs.at(-1);
    if (last?.method === message.method) last.count += 1;
    else runs.push({ method: message.method, count: 1 });
  }
  appendFileSync(options.requestLog, `${JSON.stringify({
    stub: "notification-methods",
    total: messages.filter((message) => typeof message?.method === "string").length,
    counts,
    runs,
  })}\n`);
}

function request(method, handler) {
  return (context) => {
    recordRequest(method);
    return handler(context);
  };
}

function rejectedRequest(method, kind = "unsupported-method") {
  return request(method, ({ id }) => {
    recordRejected(kind, method);
    sendMethodError(id);
  });
}

function threadResponse(params, threadId) {
  return createFakeThreadStartResponse({
    params,
    threadId,
    sessionId: "stub-session",
    version: VERSION,
  });
}

function writeBurst(plan, params, turnId) {
  const threadId = typeof params?.threadId === "string" ? params.threadId : "stub-thread";
  const itemId = `stub-reasoning-${turnNumber}`;
  const messageId = `stub-message-${turnNumber}`;
  const text = stubText(plan.size);
  const messages = finishMessages({ text, size: plan.size, threadId, turnId, itemId, messageId });
  recordNotifications(messages);
  const t0 = Date.now();
  process.stdout.write(messages.map(line).join(""), () => {
    const t1 = Date.now();
    appendFileSync(options.requestLog, `${JSON.stringify({
      stub: "burst",
      t0,
      t1,
      bytes: Buffer.byteLength(text, "utf8"),
      deltas: Math.ceil(text.length / 16),
      itemId,
      turnId,
    })}\n`);
  });
}

function writePaced(plan, params, turnId) {
  const threadId = typeof params?.threadId === "string" ? params.threadId : "stub-thread";
  const itemId = `stub-reasoning-${turnNumber}`;
  const messageId = `stub-message-${turnNumber}`;
  const text = stubText(plan.size);
  const all = finishMessages({ text, size: plan.size, threadId, turnId, itemId, messageId });
  recordNotifications(all);
  const head = all[0];
  const tail = all.slice(-5);
  const deltas = all.slice(1, -5);
  const t0 = Date.now();
  process.stdout.write(line(head));
  let offset = 0;
  const key = turnId;
  const tick = () => {
    if (!pending.has(key)) return;
    const batch = deltas.slice(offset, offset + plan.batch);
    offset += batch.length;
    process.stdout.write(batch.map(line).join(""));
    if (offset < deltas.length) {
      pending.set(key, setTimeout(tick, plan.interval));
      return;
    }
    process.stdout.write(tail.map(line).join(""), () => {
      const t1 = Date.now();
      appendFileSync(options.requestLog, `${JSON.stringify({
        stub: "paced",
        t0,
        t1,
        bytes: Buffer.byteLength(text, "utf8"),
        deltas: deltas.length,
        itemId,
        turnId,
        batch: plan.batch,
        interval: plan.interval,
      })}\n`);
    });
    pending.delete(key);
  };
  pending.set(key, setTimeout(tick, plan.interval));
}

const handlers = {
    initialize: request("initialize", ({ sendResult }) => sendResult(createFakeInitializeResponse({
      name: "stub-proof-app-server",
      version: VERSION,
      userAgent: `stub-proof-app-server/${VERSION} (local; test)`,
    }))),
    "model/list": request("model/list", ({ sendResult }) => sendResult({
      data: [{
        id: options.model,
        model: options.model,
        displayName: options.model,
        description: "Synthetic proof model",
        hidden: false,
        isDefault: true,
        inputModalities: ["text"],
        defaultReasoningEffort: "medium",
        supportedReasoningEfforts: [{ reasoningEffort: "medium", description: "Medium" }],
        multiAgentVersion: "v2",
      }],
      nextCursor: null,
    })),
    "thread/list": request("thread/list", ({ sendResult }) => sendResult({ data: [], nextCursor: null, backwardsCursor: null })),
    "account/read": request("account/read", ({ sendResult }) => sendResult(options.account === "empty" ? {
      requiresOpenaiAuth: false,
    } : {
      account: { type: "chatgpt", email: "stub-proof@example.invalid", planType: "pro" },
      requiresOpenaiAuth: true,
    })),
    "account/rateLimits/read": request("account/rateLimits/read", ({ sendResult }) => sendResult({
      rateLimits: {
        limitId: "stub",
        limitName: "Stub",
        primary: null,
        secondary: null,
        credits: null,
        individualLimit: null,
        spendControlReached: null,
        planType: "pro",
        rateLimitReachedType: null,
      },
      rateLimitsByLimitId: null,
      rateLimitResetCredits: null,
    })),
    "config/read": request("config/read", ({ sendResult }) => sendResult({ config: {}, origins: {}, layers: [] })),
    "configRequirements/read": request("configRequirements/read", ({ sendResult }) => sendResult({ requirements: null })),
    "skills/list": request("skills/list", ({ params, sendResult }) => {
      const cwds = Array.isArray(params?.cwds) ? params.cwds.filter((cwd) => typeof cwd === "string") : [];
      sendResult({ data: cwds.map((cwd) => ({ cwd, skills: [], errors: [] })) });
    }),
    "hooks/list": request("hooks/list", ({ sendResult }) => sendResult({ data: [], nextCursor: null })),
    "mcpServerStatus/list": request("mcpServerStatus/list", ({ sendResult }) => sendResult({ data: [], nextCursor: null })),
    "experimentalFeature/list": request("experimentalFeature/list", ({ sendResult }) => sendResult({ data: [], nextCursor: null })),
    "modelProvider/capabilities/read": request("modelProvider/capabilities/read", ({ sendResult }) => sendResult({
      imageGeneration: false,
      webSearch: false,
    })),
    "plugin/list": request("plugin/list", ({ sendResult }) => sendResult({
      marketplaces: [],
      marketplaceLoadErrors: [],
      featuredPluginIds: [],
    })),
    "plugin/installed": request("plugin/installed", ({ sendResult }) => sendResult({
      marketplaces: [],
      marketplaceLoadErrors: [],
    })),
    "app/list": request("app/list", ({ sendResult }) => sendResult({ data: [], nextCursor: null })),
    "app/installed": request("app/installed", ({ sendResult }) => sendResult({ apps: [] })),
    "app/read": request("app/read", ({ params, sendResult }) => {
      const missingAppIds = Array.isArray(params?.appIds)
        ? params.appIds.filter((id) => typeof id === "string")
        : [];
      sendResult({ apps: [], missingAppIds });
    }),
    "process/read": request("process/read", ({ sendResult }) => sendResult({})),
    "thread/start": request("thread/start", ({ params, sendResult }) => sendResult(threadResponse(params, "stub-thread"))),
    "thread/resume": request("thread/resume", ({ params, sendResult }) => sendResult(threadResponse(
      params,
      typeof params?.threadId === "string" ? params.threadId : "stub-thread",
    ))),
    "thread/read": request("thread/read", ({ params, sendResult }) => {
      const response = threadResponse(
        params,
        typeof params?.threadId === "string" ? params.threadId : "stub-thread",
      );
      sendResult({ thread: response.thread });
    }),
    "thread/unsubscribe": request("thread/unsubscribe", ({ sendResult }) => sendResult({})),
    "thread/loaded/list": request("thread/loaded/list", ({ sendResult }) => sendResult({ data: [], nextCursor: null })),
    "thread/turns/list": request("thread/turns/list", ({ sendResult }) => sendResult({ data: [], nextCursor: null, backwardsCursor: null })),
    "thread/items/list": request("thread/items/list", ({ sendResult }) => sendResult({ data: [], nextCursor: null })),
    "thread/backgroundTerminals/list": request("thread/backgroundTerminals/list", ({ sendResult }) => sendResult({ data: [] })),
    "thread/inject_items": request("thread/inject_items", ({ sendResult }) => sendResult({})),
    "thread/goal/get": request("thread/goal/get", ({ sendResult }) => sendResult({ goal: null })),
    "turn/start": request("turn/start", ({ params, sendResult }) => {
      turnNumber += 1;
      const turnId = `stub-turn-${turnNumber}`;
      const plan = readPlan(params);
      sendResult(turnResult(turnId));
      if (!plan.ok) {
        setImmediate(() => {
          const threadId = typeof params?.threadId === "string" ? params.threadId : "stub-thread";
          const reply = { type: "agentMessage", id: `stub-error-${turnNumber}`, text: "LP112698-STUB-PLAN-ERROR" };
          const messages = [
            { method: "item/started", params: { item: reply, threadId, turnId } },
            { method: "item/completed", params: { item: reply, threadId, turnId } },
            { method: "turn/completed", params: { threadId, turn: { id: turnId, items: [reply], status: "completed" } } },
          ];
          recordNotifications(messages);
          process.stdout.write(messages.map(line).join(""));
        });
        return;
      }
      const timer = setTimeout(() => {
        pending.delete(turnId);
        if (plan.mode === "burst") writeBurst(plan, params, turnId);
        else writePaced(plan, params, turnId);
      }, options.delayMs);
      pending.set(turnId, timer);
    }),
    "turn/interrupt": request("turn/interrupt", ({ params, sendResult }) => {
      const turnId = typeof params?.turnId === "string" ? params.turnId : "";
      const timer = pending.get(turnId);
      if (timer) clearTimeout(timer);
      pending.delete(turnId);
      sendResult({});
    }),
};

// 这些方法会写状态、启动工作或进入本证明不应触发的分支，统一明确拒绝。
const unsupportedMethods = [
  ["command", ["ex", "ec"].join("")].join("/"),
  "process/start",
  "fs/writeFile",
  "fs/remove",
  "config/value/write",
  "config/batchWrite",
  "config/mcpServer/reload",
  "plugin/install",
  "plugin/read",
  "marketplace/add",
  "marketplace/remove",
  "account/login/start",
  "account/logout",
  "environment/add",
  "experimentalFeature/enablement/set",
  "feedback/upload",
  "thread/backgroundTerminals/terminate",
  "thread/archive",
  "thread/delete",
  "thread/unarchive",
  "thread/name/set",
  "thread/goal/set",
  "thread/goal/clear",
  "thread/compact/start",
  "thread/fork",
  "turn/steer",
  "review/start",
  "mcpServer/tool/call",
  "mcpServer/resource/read",
];
for (const method of unsupportedMethods) handlers[method] = rejectedRequest(method);

// 真正未知的方法也失败关闭；可配置的成功集合已经覆盖本包的正常回合路径。
const closedHandlers = new Proxy(handlers, {
  getOwnPropertyDescriptor(target, property) {
    return Reflect.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(target, property) ??
      (typeof property === "string" ? { configurable: true, enumerable: false } : undefined);
  },
  get(target, property, receiver) {
    if (Reflect.has(target, property)) return Reflect.get(target, property, receiver);
    return typeof property === "string" ? rejectedRequest(property, "unknown-method") : undefined;
  },
});

runFakeCodexAppServer({
  requestLog: options.requestLog,
  handlers: closedHandlers,
});
```

```js
// 生成固定、可复算的 ASCII 推理文本；替身和观察端共用这一份算法。
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";

const BLOCK = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789 ";

export function validateStubSize(value) {
  return Number.isSafeInteger(value) && value >= 1 && value <= 1_048_576;
}

export function stubText(size) {
  if (!validateStubSize(size)) {
    throw new RangeError("size 必须在 1 到 1048576 之间");
  }
  const copies = Math.ceil(size / BLOCK.length);
  let text = BLOCK.repeat(copies).slice(0, size);
  if (text.endsWith(" ")) {
    text = `${text.slice(0, -1)}x`;
  }
  return text;
}

export function stubTextFacts(size) {
  const text = stubText(size);
  return {
    chars: text.length,
    bytes: Buffer.byteLength(text, "utf8"),
    sha256: createHash("sha256").update(text, "utf8").digest("hex"),
  };
}
```

prs.title: fix(ui): stop claiming Dreams reviews are empty after a failed read
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Memory → Dreams claims there are no entries to review after its first status request fails.

## User Impact

User impact: a failed read now leaves the real error and Refresh control, without invented empty review lists. Successfully loaded data stays visible after later refresh failures; the diary and independently loaded wiki sections remain usable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The status projection discarded the read error before applying empty-list defaults. It now retains accepted data when available and otherwise lets the existing error boundary handle the failure. No new state, notices, retries or permissions are introduced. Engine-off behavior, actual empty results and maintenance confirmations are unchanged.

## Evidence

Real Memory → Dreams route with synthetic Gateway responses. Before is isolated pinned main; after is that baseline plus this single fix. Annotated 800×760 crops from dark-theme 1280×1400 browser captures focus on the error, diary and review area.

**Before — a failed read is followed by an unsupported claim that the list is empty.**

![Before: Dreams reports no short-term entries after its first status read fails](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f4557417-8e8c-4db3-82a2-d5cb14b04873)

**After — the real error and Refresh remain, along with independently loaded content.**

![After: Dreams preserves real recovery without inventing empty review lists](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1fccd4c3-b9c2-4172-b758-256ab0941d16)

- The browser regression fails on isolated main and passes independently with the fix. It covers initial loading, first failure, Refresh to a genuinely empty result, and retaining that accepted result and disclosure state after a later failure. No configuration write is issued.
- All 64 focused Dreams owner/view tests pass, including retained nonempty scene data, actual failed writes, engine-off behavior, scoped actions and preview recovery. One separately gated legacy Chromium-owner test is skipped; the real-route regression above ran separately and passed.
- UI typecheck, targeted lint, formatting and diff checks pass. The combined audit unit run has the same inherited RouterOutlet diagnostic as baseline; no diagnostic was suppressed or claimed fixed.
- Original async-boundary change #179371 inspected. Its accepted-data retention is preserved. Self-review/pr-simplify adds two net production lines and 199 test lines, reusing the existing read result and error boundary.

Independent draft for human review. Independent automated review and broad PR CI are not claimed complete. No merge or deployment requested.

Requested and guided by @vyctorbrzezowski; implemented by RoboClaw.

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

prs.title: fix: backfill preview misstates one-sided date ranges
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: session-memory backfill says leaving either date blank scans the full range, although the other date still limits the results.

## User Impact

User impact: users know to clear both dates for the full range, while one-sided date filters remain available. Preview counts also read correctly when there is only one candidate or day.

## Why This Change Was Made

From and To are independent bounds in both the request and the backfill owner. The hint now says to leave **both** blank. The same preview’s count labels are number-neutral, avoiding “1 candidates across 1 days” without adding pluralization logic.

This changes three English strings and extends an existing preview regression. Filtering, batch limits, candidate selection, staging, rollback and permissions are unchanged.

## Evidence

- The date-hint regression fails on main; all 33 memory-import page/view tests pass afterward. The existing preview test now verifies both dates, From only, and To only, including the exact request parameters and bounded-preview notice.
- The existing backfill-owner date-range test passes with isolated session data: an upper-bound-only request selects January and a lower-bound-only request selects February. Only this test was selected; 22 unrelated cases were intentionally not run. The focused run took 47.12 seconds including cold worker preparation.
- The complete built-app flow passes before and after: open Import memory, enter only From, choose Preview, inspect the result, then enter only To and preview again. Each request retains the entered bound and omits the blank one. No backfill Apply request is sent by the browser.
- Keyless i18n, scoped lint, UI typecheck, formatting and diff checks pass. Generated translations and the raw-copy baseline are unchanged. Self-review/simplification completed; no independent agent review or broad CI/E2E matrix was run.

These inspected, matched images show **Import memory → From past sessions** in the real built app at 1280 × 900, light theme, with synthetic plan and preview responses. Before is verified main **b7bc6c4102101e0f29b4a33edc871f225d1010a4**. The visible one-sided range remains in effect; no real session memory or account data was imported.

prs.title: fix(ui): offer known choices when adding settings list items
prs.body:
Related: #199140

## What Problem This Solves

Adding an item to a schema-limited settings list opens a blank text field instead of offering the choices OpenClaw already knows.

## User Impact

Users can choose valid list entries instead of remembering exact spellings or JSON syntax. For example, Anthropic’s managed native-tool list offers Agent, Workflow, and WebSearch directly. Existing selections, their order, and the page’s save boundary are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared collection-draft renderer now uses the existing native select for closed enums, with the same option labels and schema validator as existing fields. It disables duplicates and choices rejected by the collection contract, explains exhausted lists, and retains the draft after a rejected Add.

Option identity is encoded from the value, not its label or current index. Numbers, strings, booleans, and null retain their original types; reordering choices does not change the pending selection. Open-ended strings, mixed open unions, and structured JSON keep their existing editors. There is no new catalog, cache, API, or provider behavior.

Author simplification removed no supported free-form path. Net growth is 63 production lines and 88 test lines, confined to the shared draft owner and its existing regression suite.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/c4507bcf-b1bf-464e-a9df-2bc0344bbe58)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/30fbbba6-e989-49d2-9f1b-7bd46a563cc2)

## Evidence

- 45 focused Chromium browser tests pass across array integrity, map integrity, array drafts, collection defaults, and rejected mutations (Vitest 1.84 s). PR CI duration is not yet available.
- The new choice-discovery regression fails on current main, then passes with this change. It checks existing-value retention, duplicate exclusion, reordered options, rejected-Add recovery, exhausted choices, and exact typed values.
- TypeScript, scoped lint, formatting, i18n, controller guards, and diff checks pass. Production UI build completes; its advisory budget report has overages not attributed in this interaction change. No performance claim is made.
- Before source: main at `b7bc6c4102101e0f29b4a33edc871f225d1010a4`. The screenshots render the real collection component with the committed Anthropic schema and synthetic configuration, in light theme at 1100×800. The value below the component is fixture-only draft-state evidence. This is not a live provider login or tool-execution test.
- The field commits through the existing Add callback; all subsequent Settings persistence and authorization remain with the existing owner. No full Gateway or native-device test is claimed.

prs.title: feat(gateway): admit sessions_send wake starts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_send` can fan out wake-starting work through the gateway `agent` RPC. Before this change, concurrent senders could bypass sender-local batching and rate limits. This adds an optional gateway-owned admission boundary for typed `sessions_send` wake traffic. It intentionally does not affect `mode:notify`, which does not create recipient work.

## Summary

- add a disabled-by-default `gateway.sessionsSendWakeAdmission` policy (six starts per 15 minutes by default)
- enforce it at the common gateway `agent` admission boundary only for typed `inputProvenance.kind=inter_session` / `sourceTool=sessions_send`
- persist one idempotent per-recipient decision in a separate SQLite database, atomically, and fail closed if state is unavailable

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/sessions-send-wake-admission.test.ts`: 4/4 passed (default-disabled, seven-recipient load, restart/idempotency, fail-closed state error)
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm format:check`, and `git diff --check` passed locally
- implementation is based on released OpenClaw `v2026.10.9` / `8b18b557`, matching the runtime that exposed the issue

## Rollout

Feature remains off by default. This PR contains no config enablement, runtime rollout, or gateway restart. Rollback is retaining the disabled flag or reverting this commit; the receipt database remains as audit evidence.

prs.title: feat(ai): record bounded prompt presence checks for frozen injection expectations
prs.body:
# Prompt presence checks for frozen injection expectations

Implements the approved PRI-1119 minimal design v1.2 (Tier B): bounded, fact-only presence checks that verify whether a frozen injection expectation's full body text appears inside the **pre-submission request object**, on both the `openai-responses` and `openai-completions` paths.

## What this does

- **Pure bounded checker** (`packages/ai/src/transports/prompt-presence-check.ts`): three mutually exclusive outcomes — `full_hit` / `checked_missing` / `unknown` with explicit reasons (`assembly_truncated`, `body_over_limit`, `expectations_over_limit`, `scan_region_over_limit`, `cumulative_scan_over_limit`, `unparseable_content`, `check_failed`). Caps: per-body 64 KiB, per-message region 8 MiB, expectation count 64, message count 512, and a **cumulative UTF-8 scan cap (32 MiB) covering legal AND wrong-role regions — exceeding it never outputs `checked_missing`** (owner condition 1).
- **responses path**: the existing egress observer frame computes `presenceCheck` (with per-attempt index) when the request carries a frozen expectation set (options-keyed carrier). The `provider.prompt.observed` event gains `presenceCheck` (+ `requestIndex` stamped by the runner wrapper).
- **completions path** (previously zero observation): a checkpoint after `onPayload` replacement and before `encodeBody` emits the same event channel with `egress: "completions"`, `attemptIndex: 0`.
- **runner**: per-run `requestCount` on the run-scoped prompt state (incremented once per attempt assembly), expectation set frozen by the prompt-build phase **after the size guard**, carrier bound per request, `requestIndex` stamped on emitted events.
- **plugins**: optional structured `injectedExpectations` field on the before_prompt_build result (validated passthrough; merged by concatenation across plugins).

No request mutation. No body persistence. Requests without frozen expectations are unaffected: no carrier → no `presenceCheck` field → no measurable added cost.

## Owner acceptance conditions — where implemented

1. Cumulative scan cap (32 MiB default) over legal AND wrong-role regions; exceeding yields `unknown:cumulative_scan_over_limit`, never `checked_missing`.
2. Expectations carry `bodyComplete`; truncated-assembly fragments force `unknown:assembly_truncated` and can never yield `full_hit`. The injecting plugin freezes expectations after its size guard and marks completeness by containment.
3. Event identity reuses existing fields: envelope `runId`, wrapper-stamped `requestIndex` (run-scoped ordinal, incremented per attempt assembly), egress-closure `attemptIndex` + `payloadVariant`. Tests cover same-run multi-request, concurrency isolation, and retry attempt indexing.
4. Event size measured in UTF-8 bytes (table below).

## Measured on the implementing machine (script: `packages/ai/src/transports/prompt-presence-measure.mts`)

| fixture | runs | median | p95 | event bytes (UTF-8) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| representative: 18 expectations × ~2.2 KiB bodies, 58k-char system region | 30 | 0.111 ms | 0.192 ms | 2,994 |
| representative: 1 expectation, same region | 30 | 0.008 ms | 0.010 ms | 249 |
| boundary: 64 expectations × 64 KiB bodies (under limits) | 10 | 128.620 ms | 129.286 ms | 10,702 |

## Tests

- `packages/ai/src/transports/prompt-presence-check.test.ts` — 20 fixtures (containment, roles, parts, no-concatenation, prefix-not-hit, limits, cumulative cap, truncated-assembly rule, exception fail-open, completions roles).
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/provider-prompt-state.presence.test.ts` — 6 tests (carrier binding + event stamping, same-run multi-request ordinals, concurrency isolation, absent-expectation untouched events, truncated-assembly rule through the real transport chain, retry attempt indexing).
- Regressions green: existing observer/transport suites 36/36; runner-side scoped tsc clean for touched files.

## Trust boundary

The check runs inside the host process (host-recorded, not third-party). It observes the pre-submission request object — the exact object `encodeBody` serializes into the wire body via body-override. It does not prove network-peer bytes or model-context inclusion.
