prs.title: fix(discord): preserve fenced code after marker lines with trailing text
prs.body:
Closes #127656

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

Allow edits from maintainers is enabled.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users receiving long Discord code blocks would see later code rendered as prose when the block contained a fence-like line with trailing text, such as ` ```not-a-close`. The same defect affects ordinary channel messages and webhook replies.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord's chunker closed a block after checking only the fence marker and its length. Its closing rule now matches the existing shared Markdown contract: the marker must match, be at least as long as the opener, and have only spaces or tabs after it. CRLF fence lines are recognized, while backtick-containing info strings are not misclassified as block openers. The outer reasoning italic marker is separated before scanning, and generated closing italics are placed on a separate line after code fences with space reserved in the transport budget.

The repair stays in the Discord chunk owner; no SDK, dependency, or configuration changes. Separating the existing reasoning wrapper preserves its formatting contract while enforcing actual fence endings. Wrapper restoration also runs when only one nonempty message survives, placing the closing delimiter before trailing whitespace.

## User Impact

Code remains fenced across Discord message boundaries, including code that looks like a Markdown heading. Actual closing fences still return following text to prose, and outgoing messages remain within the transport limit.

## Evidence

- September 12 integration: rebased onto main `366335ad9cd6`, preserving the allocation improvements from #142447 and all upstream webhook tests. The only manual conflict joined independent test additions; `git range-diff` confirms unchanged repair logic. **237 tests passed across four suites**, covering chunking, ordinary sends, webhooks, and native-command replies. Targeted formatting, typed lint, `git diff --check`, and a fresh independent branch review passed for the rebased candidate `e211bb56f01b`. [GitHub CI passed on this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34673184167).

- Before the repair: the three affected suites reported **9 failed, 193 passed**. The new failures cover false closers, CRLF, channel HTTP payloads, and webhook HTTP payloads.
- At the previously reviewed head `8a07c53835eb`: three suites reported **207 passed** under Vitest 5.0.0, including an additional regression for reasoning markers after synthetic closing fences. The tests use `mdast-util-from-markdown` as an independent semantic oracle and capture requests through local HTTP servers using the real Discord send paths.
- Review follow-up: the single-surviving-chunk regression failed for both `Reasoning:` and `Thinking...` before correction (**2 failed, 103 passed** in the chunk suite). Both now parse as actual emphasis, including when trailing blank lines are discarded. A further pair of cases for `__hello__` also failed before correction (**2 failed, 105 passed**) and now preserve strong emphasis rather than losing a content-adjacent underscore. The final 207-test run covers this correction.
- The initial repair passed full Discord plugin validation with isolated fork workers: **246 files, 3,343 tests passed**. A subsequent review found the synthetic-fence reasoning edge case; its new test failed before correction, and the final focused run above includes the correction. The default worker run previously exited unexpectedly after 2,812 passing tests; the isolated rerun completed without failures.
- Before the September 12 rebase, changed-scope formatting, lint, production/test typechecks, plugin boundaries, dead-export checks, and runtime import-cycle checks passed; that head also passed [GitHub CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34071825635).
- Independent `autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P2`: **scoped-clean**, with no actionable findings.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.sends-basic-channel-messages.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.webhook.chunk-limit.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/native-command-reply.test.ts
pnpm test:extension discord --pool=forks --isolate --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- extensions/discord/src/chunk.ts extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.sends-basic-channel-messages.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.webhook.chunk-limit.test.ts
git diff --check
```

Validation used Node 24.19.0 on macOS arm64. Live Discord client screenshots were not captured: this environment has no dedicated test bot/channel credentials. Local HTTP payload evidence does not claim a live Discord round trip.

Related follow-up: the shared `hasBalancedFences` test helper still uses the old marker-only closing rule. These regressions deliberately use the independent Markdown parser instead of that helper.

prs.title: fix(google): preserve medium thinking for Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw rejects `medium` for Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, or sends `HIGH` when the setting reaches the Google request builder directly.

## User Impact

`/think medium` and `--thinking medium` now select Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview's native `MEDIUM` effort. The default for this reasoning model stays adaptive.

## Why This Change Was Made

The model policy, payload sanitizer, and shared Google request builder applied the original Gemini 3 Pro level rules to 3.1 Pro Preview. The policy excluded `medium`, and the payload layers independently mapped it to `HIGH`. Use a shared model check to recognize the documented 3.1 Pro Preview IDs at all three boundaries. Original Pro mappings, fixed-tier routes, and legacy numeric budgets keep their previous behavior. [Google's thinking-level documentation](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/thinking)

## Evidence

- Ran the built OpenClaw CLI against a local Gemini-compatible test server. `agent --local --thinking medium` sent one request with `generationConfig.thinkingConfig.thinkingLevel: "MEDIUM"` and returned the expected fixture response. With no thinking override, the request omitted `thinkingLevel` and returned the same fixture response.
- The regression cases reproduced the missing level in the model policy and the `HIGH` mapping in both request formats before the fix.
- 362 focused tests passed across 10 files on the implementation commit, including GenerateContent, Interactions, provider policy, and prompt-prefix stability. Core and extension type checks, lint, and formatting passed.
- The tests-only follow-up consolidated duplicate table setup and kept all cases. All 68 tests in the touched suite passed. The test-line ratchet passed on the local merge tree with two lines of slack, and the PR now has a net test-line delta of -2.

<details>
<summary>Redacted CLI request capture for 0d900c69e</summary>

The built CLI ran `agent --local` in a fresh session against a local Gemini-compatible streaming fixture. The explicit case added `--thinking medium`. Each fixture response matched the expected synthetic text.

```jsonl

{"case":"candidate-default","override":null,"exitCode":0,"expectedText":true,"requestCount":1,"wire":[{"routeMatches":true,"level":null,"levelPresent":false,"thoughts":true,"tools":0,"fixtureAuth":true}]}
```

The upgrade check started with published OpenClaw 2026.10.10 in a separate isolated state directory. Stable saved `high` for the test session and sent `HIGH` again on reuse without a flag. The candidate ran `doctor --fix --non-interactive` for the existing migration, then reused the same session with no override. The saved choice still produced `HIGH`.

```jsonl
{"case":"candidate-doctor","exitCode":0,"providerRequests":0}
{"case":"candidate-upgrade-reuse","override":null,"exitCode":0,"expectedText":true,"requestCount":1,"wire":[{"routeMatches":true,"level":"HIGH","levelPresent":true,"thoughts":true,"tools":0,"fixtureAuth":true}]}
{"sameSessionAcrossVersions":true}
```

</details>

prs.title: improve: choose automation models and thinking levels on Android
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android automation settings require operators to type model references and thinking levels even when the task’s scoped catalog already advertises those choices.

## User Impact

Operators can search model names and provider-qualified references, select a model and its advertised thinking level, restore defaults, or enter custom values. Unlisted saved values remain intact. Selection changes only the draft; Save Changes still commits it. Catalog failures keep the task editable and offer Refresh models. No scheduler, account-binding, authorization, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing cron detail response already carries agent and session ownership. Retain those fields and read models.list for that job when its picker opens, never from the unrelated active chat. A scoped session supplies the owner when an explicit agent is absent; with neither, the Gateway resolves its ambient default.

Model choices live with the existing selected-job detail owner and use its request guard and Gateway connection scope. Late reads cannot replace a successor task, and failed refreshes retain that task’s previous choices. The shared native model-reference formatter, theme controls, draft owner, and save writer are reused. The raw-only model and thinking fields are replaced with same-window choosers; custom input remains explicit. Thinking choices come only from the selected model’s advertised capabilities, never a hard-coded ladder. Changing models preserves an existing custom thinking value. Net +278 production lines, +332 test lines, +1 documentation line, plus the generated native string inventory.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/c4507bcf-b1bf-464e-a9df-2bc0344bbe58)

prs.title: fix(models): stop blaming the API key for first-provider billing failures
prs.body:
Related: #199143 (the ordinary saved-key probe; this fixes the separate first-provider activation path).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: adding the first model provider tells users to replace a saved API key when the account is blocked by billing or quota.

## User Impact

User impact: users get billing-specific advice and can retry Save provider with the same saved key after resolving the account restriction. The real failure, retained input and existing recovery remain visible. No credentials, permissions or activation policy change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first-provider flow activates the saved profile instead of running the ordinary access probe. Its feedback still treated billing and authentication refusals alike. This change selects account-specific advice at that existing presentation owner; authentication failures still request a different key, and inconclusive checks remain warnings.

## Evidence

Actual compiled Control UI with a supported synthetic Gateway, light theme, 1280×900 desktop. These inspected, annotated 680×380 crops preserve the complete dialog. The synthetic credential is masked; no real provider or billing operation occurred.

**Before**

![Before: first-provider billing failure incorrectly asks for another API key](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a3136aef-170d-498b-b06b-fd526faad2e5)

**After**

![After: first-provider billing advice retains the saved key and Save provider recovery](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/30334fdb-a16c-47a2-b4ba-8bdb061e5796)

- On isolated current main fd3d80e432123766b3e466957cd22f7b66af442e, the actual browser scenario fails both unsupported-credential assertions; the owning regression also fails. With the fix, the browser scenario passes in 14.05s and 55 focused owner/configuration/page cases pass in 2.87s.
- The browser follows Add account → xAI → Save provider → billing refusal → retry with the same key → Start a new chat. It retains the actual diagnostic and input, offers no premature Start chat, sends two exact-profile activations and does not create a session or use the ordinary access probe.
- The owning tests preserve actual authentication rejection, inconclusive checks and transport diagnostics. Targeted UI types, focused lint, formatting, i18n verification and diff checks pass. prs.title: fix(memory): status --json keeps disabled agents visible instead of an empty array
prs.body:
Closes #199392

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw memory status --json` returned `[]` when memory search was disabled, silently dropping disabled agents from the documented machine-readable aggregate — scripts cannot distinguish "no agents" from "all agents disabled". The search path in the same CLI family already emits `{agentId, status: "disabled"}` for the same state, so the two disagreed.

## User Impact

User impact: with `memory.search.enabled: false`, `openclaw memory status --json` now reports `[{"agentId": "main", "status": "disabled"}]`, consistent with the search path's disabled document and with the human output. Human-readable status output is byte-identical to before. The plain-text notice stays off --json output at its source sites (runtime --json mode already reroutes console.log to stderr; the source-level gating makes each site contract-correct on its own).

## Why This Change Was Made

`runMemoryStatus` had no collector for the disabled path, so disabled agents never reached the aggregate. A new optional `onDisabledAgent` callback on `withMemoryCommand` feeds them in with the family's existing disabled shape; the non-json printer skips these entries so human output is unchanged. New CLI-level tests live in a self-contained sibling file, per the repo's line-cap ratchet (cli.test.ts is grandfathered over its 1000-line cap).

## Evidence

### Red on main

`./node_modules/.bin/vitest run extensions/memory-core/src/cli-json-disabled-output.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/cli.memory-slot.test.ts` on `main` (with these tests): 2 failed / 3 passed — the two --json assertions failed exactly on the defect (stray notice recorded by the log spy; aggregate `[]` vs the expected disabled entry).

### Green with this change

Same command on the fix branch: 14/14 (sibling + slot file), and the earlier full targeted run across `cli.test.ts`, `cli.memory-slot.test.ts`, `cli-runtime-common.test.ts` was 73/73.

### Real CLI before/after (isolated HOME/state/config, source checkout)

With `memory.search.enabled: false`:

```text
before (main 1c0ca31):  openclaw memory status --json   → stdout: []
after (this fix):       openclaw memory status --json   → stdout: [{"agentId": "main", "status": "disabled"}]
after:                  openclaw memory search "query" --json → stdout parses as one JSON doc
after:                  openclaw memory status (no --json)    → still prints "Memory search disabled." once
```

### Checks

- Targeted oxlint (293 rules) on all five touched files: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- Repo line-cap ratchet passes (new tests in a sibling file).

prs.title: fix(entities): C1-range numeric references decode as windows-1252 text
prs.body:
Closes #199391 ## What Problem This Solves Numeric HTML character references in the 0x80–0x9F range (for example `’`, `—`, `“`) decoded to raw Unicode C1 control characters, so any pipeline using `decodeHtmlEntities` fused words and lost smart quotes and dashes into invisible controls. ## User Impact User impact: `web_fetch` text extraction, channel inbound text (Matrix, MS Teams), DuckDuckGo result text, and tool-call argument repair now read the way browsers and the HTML5 spec read. `it’s a test — with “smart quotes” inside.` now extracts as `it’s a test — with “smart quotes” inside.` instead of a C1-laced string; file bytes and structure are otherwise unchanged. ## Why This Change Was Made The HTML5 numeric-character-reference end state maps the 0x80–0x9F range through the windows-1252 table; the vendored `entities` library already implements that table, so the fix delegates to it instead of maintaining a second copy. Undefined cp1252 slots (0x81, 0x8D, 0x8F, 0x90, 0x9D) keep their C1 control, matching WHATWG. NUL/C0-range references still decode literally — widening to the full numeric end-state table (U+FFFD mapping) is a possible follow-up, out of scope here. ## Evidence ### Red on main `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/shared/html-entities.test.ts` on `main` (`1c0ca3120c5`) with the new table-driven test: ```text Tests 1 failed | 4 passed (5) # ’ decoded to U+0092, not U+2019 ``` ### Green with this change ```text Tests 5 passed (5) ``` ### Real extraction chain before/after `htmlToMarkdown('

it’s a test — with “smart quotes” inside.

', { extractMode: "text" })`: ```text before (main): "it\u0092s a test \u0094 with \u0093smart quotes\u009d inside." (U+0092/0097/0093/0094) after (fix): "it’s a test — with “smart quotes” inside." (U+2019/2014/201C/201D) ``` ### Checks - Targeted oxlint (293 rules) on both files: 0 warnings, 0 errors. - Behavior change is asserted consciously: the updated existing test now expects `€` → `€` instead of raw U+0080.

prs.title: feat(update): keep each release in its own directory on OpenClaw-owned installs
prs.body:
Related: #197949 (design, slice 4). Builds on #198489 (linked-root Docker mode, now on `main`); this PR adds only the owned-prefix and follow-up modes to those harness files.

## What Problem This Solves

A package update on an OpenClaw-owned install displaces the old release from its path: two directory renames, whole-tree fingerprints, a launcher backup, deletion of the old tree inside the activation window, and a journal to survive a crash in between.

## User Impact

On macOS and Linux, installs made by `install-cli.sh` and the durable service copy at `<state dir>/npm` now keep each release in `<prefix>/releases/<id>/`, and `lib/node_modules/openclaw` becomes a link to the selected one. An update installs the new release beside the old one and switches the link with one rename; rollback renames a link to the previous release back. The previous release is never written and is kept for at least a day. `openclaw update status` lists the active and retained releases.

**This changes what existing installations do.** The first update by an updater with this change converts a plain package directory on those prefixes. npm prefixes you manage, `npm link` checkouts, pnpm, Bun, Git checkouts and Windows keep today's swap. A manual `npm install -g` into an owned prefix turns the link back into a directory; the next update converts it again.

## Why This Change Was Made

It implements route 3 of the [update generations design](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197949) as one cutover, because the parts only work together:

- **Install identity is the link.** `resolveUpdateInstallRoot` returns the link's own path for a release link, and maps a path inside the release the link currently selects to the link (a process finds its own root by real path). The executor key, child admission, the restart sentinel, post-core and native-receiver root checks, and the managed handoff lease key stay the same across a switch. A published updater on a linked root keys its leases by the release path, so a candidate child checking its executor grant takes the parent's spelling when `updateInstallRootsMatch` says both name one installation. Root discovery (`resolveOpenClawInstallationRootSync`, used by `resolveUpdateRoot` and Gateway update admission) maps the selected release to the link, which covers a start through the `bin` launcher. Only a link into `<prefix>/releases/<id>/lib/node_modules/openclaw` of the same prefix and owner counts.
- **Releases are installed where they stay.** `runGlobalPackageUpdateSteps` (flag set only by `openclaw update`) stages into `releases/<label>` and hands the stage to the switch instead of the swap.
- **The switch:** refuse before any change if the candidate's `bin` links differ; capture the link; stop the service; record `origin.packageRelease` (validated before the stop); create a temporary link, sync, recheck the lease and the captured link, rename, confirm, sync. Rollback decides from the link on disk (it handles a failure after the rename), and refuses a previous release whose content changed since it was recorded.
- **Adoption** (plain directory): the directory moves into `releases/` and a prepared link naming it takes its place, then the normal switch. Between those two renames the package path is missing. That moment is not journaled: the journal's candidate is a sealed tree, and nothing can run `openclaw` while the package path is missing anyway. A process killed there leaves `lib/node_modules/.openclaw.release-link-*` naming the unchanged old tree; renaming it onto `lib/node_modules/openclaw` restores the install. The docs say so. A failed second rename moves the directory back and keeps the leftover link if that fails too.
- **Run record:** optional `origin.packageRelease` (slot, from and to: path, `dev:ino`, version, build), kept exact by the codec beside `origin.packageStage` and removed from the public projection. Interrupted managed handoff reads the install identity through the link and takes the candidate from this record. `assertManagedServiceUpdateHandoffRoot` is unchanged.
- **Service bound to a release path:** a published updater run through the link writes the release's real path into the service definition, which would keep the service on the old release after a switch. The npm destination gate refuses that before any change and names `openclaw gateway install --force` from the package path. Treating it as an install-root refresh, as pnpm generation changes are, is a follow-up.
- **Retention:** after a verified update, a release is removed only when the link does not name it, no Gateway lease (`releases/.leases/`) holds it, no open update run names it, and it was not selected or changed for 24 hours. A switch stamps the release it deselects.

Not done here, by decision or for follow-up: Windows, npm-owned prefixes, the macOS app; the node host is not made a caller (it would move its activation without removing code), and its collection and `activation.lock` rule from slice 4 are left for a follow-up. A future release that adds or renames a `bin` command cannot switch on an owned prefix until a launcher-change rule is designed; the refusal names `npm install -g` as the way out. Only Gateways take leases; other processes rely on the 24-hour age. A plain CLI update killed between the switch and its post-switch Doctor is left to `openclaw update repair` (not exercised). `package-update-steps.ts` was already over the 700-line lint limit on `main`; the pnpm environment binding moved, unchanged, into `package-update-manager-preflight.ts`.

The design doc in #197949 is updated with an "as built" section for these changes.

## Evidence

Branched from `origin/main` a9a3d628b34ae; rebased onto 09d322ab2 before opening (the 45 commits between touch no update, package, root-discovery or Docker-cell path; typecheck and the release tests were rerun on the rebased head). Local runs on macOS (Node 26.12.1); Docker cells on linux/arm64.

**Red on base, green with the change** (each run with the production file reverted to `origin/main`, then restored):

| Test | Fails on base because |
| --- | --- |
| `package-release-slot.test.ts` › link path stays the installation identity across a switch | base keys the install by the release's real path |
| `package-update-release-switch.test.ts` (8 cases: record before change and before the database capture, previous release bytes unchanged, rollback, rollback after a post-rename failure, refused rollback of a rewritten release, adoption, launcher refusal, automatic rollback) | base swaps a directory over the link |
| `package-update-release-switch.process.test.ts` (real child, SIGKILL before the temporary link, after it and before the rename, after the rename and before confirmation, and between the adoption renames) | base never reaches those cuts and leaves no release layout |
| `update-command-executor-release-link.test.ts` › post-switch child runs under the installation's lease | base acquires a second lease for the new release path |
| `update-managed-service-handoff-interrupted-release.test.ts` (continue, not activated, neither) | base refuses the link as an unsafe publication object |
| `update-command-package-destination.release-link.test.ts` › service bound to a release path | base admits it |

Regression guards for defects found in review and Docker (red against the earlier version of this branch): collection age stamped at deselection, rollback reading the link after a failed `fsync`, adoption keeping its leftover link when both renames fail, restart sentinel accepting the selected release, record written before the database capture. Negative controls that pass on base too: `npm link` checkout, plain directory, another prefix's release, unselected release takes no lease, non-owned prefixes keep the swap.

**Docker published-driver cells** (`scripts/e2e/published-driver-update-docker.sh`, with #198489's linked-root mode; run before #198489 landed, with its commit cherry-picked):

| Cell | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Published 2026.11.3 → candidate on an `install-cli.sh`-shaped prefix, then candidate → second candidate (`OWNED_PREFIX=1 FOLLOW_UP=switch`) | Pass. The published updater's swap left a plain directory; the candidate's update adopted it, switched the link, kept the previous release byte for byte, restarted the Gateway on the new release (readyz 200, version checked, durable session kept), the service unit still names the package path, and `update status` listed both releases with the new one leased. |
| Same, second candidate's post-activation Doctor fails (`FOLLOW_UP=rollback`) | Pass. Switch, Doctor failure, database rollback, link pointed back, previous Gateway verified. A first run that wrote `origin.packageRelease` after the database capture failed here (database rollback refused, link left on the candidate); fixed. A control on a plain npm prefix (today's swap) rolled back. |
| Published 2026.10.9 on a linked root → candidate, then candidate update (`LINKED_ROOT=1 FOLLOW_UP=refused`) | Pass. 2026.10.9 updated in place behind the link (link kept). Its service install had written `releases/2026.10.9/.../dist/index.js` into the unit, so the candidate refused before any change (`global-install-foreign-destination`), link unchanged, Gateway ready. |
| Published 2026.11.3 on a linked root → candidate (`LINKED_ROOT=1`) | Pass, on earlier packages of this branch (first hop of superseded rollback runs). Those runs also found the post-core, native-receiver and executor-grant root checks fixed here. |

Update behavior per hop: published drivers on a plain prefix keep today's swap (plain directory stays); this candidate adopts on its first update of an owned prefix; published drivers on a linked root swap inside the release behind the link and keep it; this candidate refuses to switch a service a published driver bound to a release path.

**Suites** (`pnpm test` on all `package-update-*`, `package-release*`, `update-run-*`, `update-managed-service-handoff*`, `restart-sentinel*`, `update-plugin-cohort*`, `update-migrated*`, gateway update methods, `stale-install`, `openclaw-root`, `src/cli/update-cli/*` and `update-executor*`): 2,927 of 2,929 pass. Two `update-command-database-rollback.test.ts` variants hit the 120 s test timeout while the whole set ran in parallel; that file alone passes 16/16 on this branch (those variants 22–38 s) and on base (28–41 s). `pnpm tsgo:all` passes; oxlint and formatting clean on changed files; `pnpm lint:docker-e2e` passes; docs format and markdownlint clean.

**CI on 0225b110212, fixed in 7180dfe7401.** The local suites above covered `src/cli/update-cli/*` but not the `src/cli/update-cli.*.test.ts` files next to it, which is where most of the failures were:

| Failure | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 18 `update-cli.*.test.ts` files (compact shards) | `resolveUpdateRoot` called `resolveOpenClawInstallationRootSync`, which the shared update-cli mock of `openclaw-root.js` does not export. The destination gate also read the service layout before returning an owned destination, so tests whose layout read throws now reported `unreadable-layout`. | `resolveUpdateRoot` applies the reverse rule (`resolvePackageReleaseSlotForRootSync`) directly; the answer is the same because only a release slot was ever kept. The service layout is read early only when the package path is a release link. |
| `eager-import-closure`, `pr-wrapper-source-closure`, `pr-worktree-provision` | The PR wrapper imports `openclaw-root.ts`, which now imports `package-release-slot-path.ts`; the file was missing from `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt`, so extracted provisioners failed before receiving their private store. | Added it to the inventory. |
| `madge-import-cycles` | Type-only cycle between `package-release-slot.ts` and `package-update-swap-contract.ts`. | `PackageReleaseTarget` now lives in `package-release-slot.ts`. |
| `check-lint-core-3` | `prefer-array-find` in `package-release-slot.test.ts` (plain `oxlint` missed it; `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` reports it). | Fixed. |
| test-lines budget (+1,280 vs 400) | New subsystem tests. | Audited the touched files: three slot-level cases (adoption contents, launcher refusal, rewritten-release refusal) duplicated switch-level cases that also check that nothing stopped and that the inode is unchanged; removed them (-60 lines). The remaining +820 is recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/update-linked-package-root.txt`. |

Existing failures, the same on base 09d322ab2 with this branch's sources swapped out: `check-extension-package-tsc-boundary.test.ts` (the canary copy lacks `src/infra/directory-walk.ts`, imported by `native-declaration-emitter.mts` since #198661), `extensions/telegram/src/send.history.test.ts` › edited captions, `update-cli.fresh-doctor.test.ts` › Git version before a dry-run downgrade, and `update-cli.target-schema.test.ts` › previews explicit artifacts. On this Mac, `pr-worktree-provision.test.ts` › cold/warm PR siblings takes 184 s against its 120 s timeout when run alone; its other 17 cases pass. Rerun on 7180dfe7401: the failing files above pass apart from those cases, the release tests pass, and `pnpm tsgo:all`, madge, the test-lines ratchet, oxfmt and `run-oxlint` on changed files all pass.

**Merged `origin/main` (99157f8f8c4), CI on 7180dfe7401 fixed in af223b77056.** #198489 landed as eb1a21dad24; the merge takes `main`'s version of its five harness files and keeps only this PR's additions (owned-prefix and follow-up modes, two `package.json` scripts, the follow-up budget and env passthrough, docs). No history was rewritten. Remaining diff-caused failure on 7180dfe7401: `checks-node-changed-compact-small-11` › `update-command-executor-settlement.test.ts` (7 cases), whose hand-written mock of `update-install-root.js` lacked `updateInstallRootsMatch`, now used by the executor grant. prs.title: fix: automation model and reasoning choices follow the task
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: automation model choices follow the wrong agent, and reasoning suggestions do not reflect the selected model’s supported levels.

## User Impact

Operators can select models for the task they are actually editing instead of typing a missing reference manually. Saved/custom model references and Default remain available. Reasoning offers the selected model’s advertised levels, Default, and a custom value; switching models preserves an existing reasoning override. Changing the task agent refreshes its choices without replacing the draft; an unrelated team selection no longer changes those choices. No scheduling, model authorization, account binding, or saved-task migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing cron agent resolver for the pending task fields and the existing scoped model-catalog owner for reads, notifications, and stale-result checks. Clearing an override follows the task’s scoped session key when present; otherwise the request leaves default-agent resolution to the Gateway rather than guessing from the UI selection. A blank agent field on an existing task preserves its saved override, matching the existing update writer.

Configured and previously saved suggestions are also scoped instead of pooling every agent’s models. The existing model picker, custom-entry path, save owner, and refresh/error presentation are retained. The now-incorrect selected-agent subscription and hard-coded reasoning datalist were removed. The shared picker presents advertised reasoning metadata from that same catalog without an additional request or cache. Necessary net growth: +96 production lines, +199 test lines, +2 documentation lines; the new reasoning control owns only its transient custom-entry mode.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/c4507bcf-b1bf-464e-a9df-2bc0344bbe58)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/30fbbba6-e989-49d2-9f1b-7bd46a563cc2)

## Evidence

- Baseline: current main ee41e9e1882aef6f1b23faa2342a03b46e2accff. Opening a writer-owned task returned the page agent’s model, reproducing the new regression failure through the actual list/editor entry point.
- 73 focused tests passed across catalog notifications, page lifecycle, page interactions, and model-suggestion semantics. Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199188

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes publication status checks that look idle while their request is pending.

## User Impact

The status control stays visibly busy on desktop and mobile, with consistent menu spacing and readable feedback. Publication, retry and account-selection authority are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Completion observers no longer hold the controls’ own busy updates. The existing action and menu presentation are retained.

This is one independently reviewable case split from #199188. It targets main and does not depend on the other three split PRs.

## Evidence

The first callout marks the status-check control; the second marks the details insets. The request is held in both frames.

### Before

![Annotated before — publication](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/30c9831c-575f-4861-a38a-680d69550578)

### After

- Passed: 2 standalone browser cases (desktop/mobile pending → error → retry → settlement), 33 focused unit cases, UI TypeScript, targeted lint, stylesheet lint and formatting.
- Independent Autoreview/Codex review of the complete local candidate against bb905f76 through P2: scoped-clean. The reviewer did not independently execute tests.
- The four production patches compose byte-for-byte to the previously reviewed combined repair. Tests were separated so this case stands alone. No full CI, merge, deployment or exhaustive browser/provider matrix is claimed.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

prs.title: fix(ui): personal instructions asks to copy a nonexistent draft
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Personal instructions asks users to copy their draft after its first file read fails, even though no editor or draft exists. The same advice lingers after all edits are reverted.

## User Impact

User impact: read failures show the actual error and Reload, without unnecessary draft-recovery instructions. Unsaved edits still receive recovery guidance and discard confirmation, including an intentional deletion of the file’s contents.

## Why This Change Was Made

The error renderer appended draft-copy advice to every failure. It now consults the existing dirty-state owner, which already compares the draft with the loaded file.

Read/write permissions, version checks, draft retention, character limits and reload behavior are unchanged. No new state or recovery path is introduced.

## Evidence

Real Profile route, synthetic signed-in multi-user Gateway, light theme, 1280×1000. Before is isolated pinned main; after is the same baseline plus this independent fix. The first personal-file request is rejected before an editor has loaded.

**Before — copy advice for a draft that does not exist.**

![Before: personal instructions error asks the user to copy a nonexistent draft](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c1361a32-6b5e-4f52-9b65-5a2bbcc8f437)

**After — actual read error and Reload, without irrelevant recovery advice.**

prs.title: fix(codex): deduplicate watched-session runtime references per thread (#84662)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In the Codex app-server harness, `workspacePromptContext` already has a per-native-thread digest gate, but `watchedSessionsContext` was always supplied to `buildCodexOpenClawPromptContext` on every turn. The resulting reference envelope is persisted inside normal Codex user history, increasing subsequent model-input and compaction size. This PR **only mitigates repeated submission of unchanged watched-session references**. It does **not** solve historical retention and intentionally leaves issue #84662 open.

## Evidence

- **Before-fix evidence from affected Codex native traces:** [structured, sanitized issue comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/84662#issuecomment-4501826554) documents `response.create` with 86 runtime-reference user items (1,219,607 of 1,257,593 input text characters, 96.98%) and a compaction input containing 29 such items (593,568 of 624,822 characters, 95%). These are historical observations, **not** after-fix benchmarks.
- **Source-level cause:** the pre-patch `run-attempt-context.ts` workspace inclusion flag gated only `workspacePromptContext`, while `watchedSessionsContext` was unconditionally passed on every turn. See [the proposed diff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199361/files).
- **Patch evidence:** [new tests in `client-workspace-state.test.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199361/files) encode unchanged references over three turns, changed watches, failed admission/truncation, and reintroduction. The `run-attempt.test.ts` harness exercises `turn/start` across warm turns and after compaction/unsubscribe; the provider-review harness tests acknowledgment after accepted-then-rebound and refuses incomplete context matches.
- **Validation status (not a pass claim):** the GitHub fork PR's `CI`, CodeQL, Workflow Sanity, OpenGrep and macOS workflows report `action_required` without running test jobs; maintainers must approve first-time fork workflow execution. A separate PR-context proof check failed due to the missing required section headings; this body revision supplies the required problem/evidence sections. No local `pnpm` test run or live native `response.create` trace has been executed on this patch.

## Summary

**Partial mitigation for #84662. Does not close the issue.** This PR addresses the confirmed producer-side path where unchanged `watchedSessionsContext` is injected into every native Codex `turn/start.input` even though the existing `workspacePromptContext` already has per-thread digest gating.

The changes extend the existing native-thread reference owner to independently track the workspace and watched-session reference digests. They re-introduce references after context compaction or loss of a warm native thread subscription and acknowledge each reference only when its complete text survives prompt fitting and native `turn/start` has accepted it.

### Changes

- Track independent per-native-thread SHA-256 digests and reintroduction flags for workspace and watched-session references.
- Gate the two sections independently in `buildOpenClawPromptContext` and the turn request.
- Preserve post-`turn/start` acknowledgment even if cancellation is observed afterward; avoid acknowledging truncated or unsent sections.
- Re-arm both references when Codex sends a `contextCompaction` completion event.
- Add regression coverage for three warm turns, changes to one reference, missing/truncated sections, compaction, cold thread reattachment, native turn input, and provider-review acknowledgment.

### Deliberate limitations / security

- **This is a bounded-submission mitigation, not a fix for durable native history.** Previously stored runtime reference copies remain in Codex `role=user` history and can still enter `response.create` and compaction inputs. The full untrusted, non-persistent carrier and legacy-thread recovery contract require maintainer agreement.
- No user-editable reference material is promoted to developer/system authority.
- No `additionalContext` transport (which can retain changed fragments and truncate large values).
- No read/rewrites of production `rollout-*.jsonl`, `state_5.sqlite`, or running environments.
- No data migration or code changes outside the Codex harness.

### Validation

- Source changes and a focused test suite have been committed against upstream `main` at `5025db61e9482d95f29956f266496f32f4f94f72`.
- **Local tests and a live Codex `response.create` capture have not been run in this environment.** This is intentionally opened as a draft for CI and technical review; please do not merge until the checks and acceptance criteria are satisfied.
- Tests to run:
  - `pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/client-workspace-state.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
  - `pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-turn-request.provider-review.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
  - `pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
  - `pnpm test src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
  - Targeted types, lint, and formatting.

### Reviewer questions

1. Is the independently gated watched-session reference path appropriate as a scoped mitigation while #84662 stays open?
2. Should compaction and warm-thread tracking be extended or handled differently for failed/accepted/cancelled native turns?
3. Which Codex-supported, non-persistent, size-safe **untrusted** reference carrier and legacy-thread recovery contract should be pursued for the complete fix?

Related: #84662, previous [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/84662#issuecomment-4501154505), and [mitigation proposal](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/84662#issuecomment-6886398216).

prs.title: feat(sessions): allow same-channel thread recall without agent-wide visibility
prs.body:
Closes #163256

## What Problem This Solves

Let an agent recall sibling threads in one verified channel without exposing every session owned by that agent.

## User Impact

Opt-in `tools.sessions.visibility: "channel"` enables same-channel retrieval while excluding other agents, channels, accounts and workspaces. Existing defaults and other visibility modes are unchanged. Sibling send, status/model changes and session mutations remain denied.

Cross-session list, history, search and transcript-backed recall require a Gateway-hosted owner and fail closed when that owner, route, incarnation, or policy is withdrawn. Ordinary memory/wiki results remain available.

## Implementation

- Require matching stored provider, explicit account, opaque channel destination, chat kind and workspace/space under the same agent.
- Recheck route, incarnation, aliases, physical owner, and policy at final disclosure.
- Carry query-local transcript-owner bindings through memory and direct Wiki consumers; filter final snippets, citations, and recall side effects synchronously.
- Preserve self-only reads, ordinary memory/wiki retrieval, and archived metadata-only inventory behavior.

## Verification

Fixes: Sharing options says “No paired people yet” when its first membership read fails, on both desktop and phone.

prs.title: fix(mcp): pending Claude permission requests grow without limit in mcp serve
prs.body:
Closes #198997

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw mcp serve` keeps every Claude permission request it receives for up to an hour, with no size limit, while its event queue stops at 1000. A burst of requests grows the bridge's memory linearly, and the owner can still answer requests whose events the queue already dropped.

## User Impact

User impact: the bridge tracks at most 1000 open Claude permission requests, the same bound as its event queue. Past that it refuses new ones with a stderr line (`openclaw mcp: refused Claude permission <id>: 1000 already pending`), and Claude's local terminal prompt still answers them. Requests already pending, their `yes`/`no` replies, expiry and shutdown cleanup work as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Admission is bounded where the request enters the bridge, as the issue's review suggested. An overflow request is refused before it is queued, so no channel owner sees a prompt whose reply would be ignored, and nothing already pending is evicted (an owner may be about to answer it). Expired entries are swept before refusing, so a full map of stale requests never blocks a new one.

<details>
<summary>Claude Opus 5.5</summary>

**Cause** (at `c509b9dd44c`): `handleClaudePermissionRequest` (`src/mcp/channel-bridge.ts:344`) does an unconditional `pendingClaudePermissions.set(requestId, Date.now())`. `QUEUE_LIMIT` only trims `this.queue` in `enqueue` (`:417`). Entries leave the map only by the one-hour TTL sweep (every five minutes), a delivered owner reply, or `close()`. #71648 added the TTL and shutdown cleanup and left the cap for later.

**Change:**

- `PENDING_CLAUDE_PERMISSION_LIMIT = QUEUE_LIMIT`: never track more open permissions than the event backlog can show a poller.
- A new request id with the map at the limit first runs `sweepPendingExpired()`; if still full, it writes one stderr line (always, like the existing notification failure line) and returns without tracking or queueing. A repeated id that is already pending is still accepted, so it doesn't grow the map.
- Admission stays synchronous (no `await` between the check and the `set`), so concurrent notifications can't overshoot the limit. `close()` and the sweeper are unchanged.
- Rejected alternatives: evicting the oldest pending request (it may already be in front of the owner, whose reply would then be silently ignored), and tying map membership to queue eviction (the issue review warned against it, for the same reason).
- Docs: `docs/cli/mcp/serve.md` notes the limit and the refusal.

**Regression test:** `src/mcp/channel-server.test.ts` "refuses Claude permission requests past the pending limit" sends 1001 distinct requests through the MCP client to the registered `notifications/claude/channel/permission_request` handler. It checks the refusal line, that only 1000 request events are queued, that an owner reply to the refused id is not turned into a verdict while a reply to an admitted one is, and that a freed slot admits the refused id again. It fails on the base (no refusal line) and passes with the fix.

**Live run details:** a throwaway Gateway on each build with Telegram pointed at a local Bot API stub, the stub's user as command owner, and a real `openclaw mcp serve --claude-channel-mode on` child driven by an MCP SDK client over stdio. The script sends 1500 requests with distinct ids, reads the queue with `events_poll`, then injects the owner DMs `yes aaaaa` (the first request) and `yes zjcaa` (the last).

</details>

## Evidence

**Live, before and after:** real `openclaw mcp serve` over stdio, 1500 distinct permission requests, then owner replies over Telegram (stub Bot API) to the first and the last request.

| Build | Request events queued | Refusal lines | Owner `yes` to request 1 | Owner `yes` to request 1500 |

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Platform users cannot explicitly choose native PDF document input through the PDF tool while preserving existing upload and model-selection behavior.

## User Impact

`agents.defaults.pdfNativeOpenai: true` opts an already-selected OpenAI vision model into complete-document input. **Unset or false preserves extraction and the existing provider order**, including saved configurations upgraded from the latest stable release. Selecting an OpenAI model alone does not authorize complete-document upload.

Page selection, passwords, unknown completeness, page/text/image truncation, size-limit violations, custom endpoints, Codex/ChatGPT transports and text-only models retain bounded extraction. Completeness checks still require the configured extractor. Existing Anthropic and Google paths are unchanged.

## Implementation

This replaces the earlier automatic-upload/provider-preference proposal with one default-off core boolean at the existing PDF configuration owner. The bundled OpenAI provider implements a narrow optional media-understanding hook using the official [PDF input contract](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/file-inputs): inline `input_file`, official Platform HTTPS `/v1/responses`, `store: false`, each PDF under 50 MB and combined PDF input at most 50 MB. There is no persistent Files upload, automatic provider preference or new dependency. The official configuration generator records the single additional core leaf; channel/plugin surfaces are unchanged.

Prepared credentials, headers and symbol-attached request/auth overrides use the existing scoped egress helpers. The native branch also reuses the host-owned `withGuardedFetchRequestAuthority` scope with `assertModelCurrent`, the **original model's** credential authority and the retained provider-resource assertion. The existing HTTP guard rechecks these synchronously immediately before dispatch after asynchronous preparation and on redirects. This closes the assert-only operator/credential retirement gap across lazy provider and DNS awaits without adding an authorization abstraction or changing shared HTTP behavior.

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot reject untagged bot thread replies without also making humans repeat mentions or changing existing bot handoffs on upgrade.

## User Impact

Human follow-ups, explicit bot mentions, DMs, authorized commands, configured mention patterns, and `allowBots: true`/`false` retain their behavior.

Omitted or false preserves shipped implicit bot handoffs. This is an alternative to #160752's default change, not a downstream adoption decision. **Slack-owner acceptance of the new optional public setting remains required.**

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing bot-admission gate owns this choice. The unchanged mention classifier moves to the existing thread-mention sibling, keeping the oversized prepare module smaller. prs.title: fix(workboard): avoid unconfigured labels before the roster loads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Workboard labels an assigned agent “not configured” when the first agent-roster read fails or is still pending.

## User Impact

User impact: The existing assignment stays visible by its ID while the roster is unknown. Once a roster arrives, the picker shows the agent’s name or the genuine not-configured label. Real refresh errors, recovery, current selection and write permissions are unchanged. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared assignment-option builder treated an unavailable roster as an accepted roster without that agent. It now uses the existing nullable roster to distinguish those states. Both the inline property and card editor consume the same options; no new loading state, request or fallback owner is added.

## Evidence

Actual compiled Control UI with a supported synthetic Gateway, light theme, 1280×900 viewport. Matching right-hand crops show the assignment menu after the first roster read fails. Before is current main at 65cf8cdc3780439cb599853f443c45fed28a98e4; after is this independent fix. Orange marks unsupported configuration claims; green marks the neutral current assignment and retained real refresh error.

**Before**

![Before: unavailable roster incorrectly marks the assigned agent not configured](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3d6f046c-ba94-473f-80af-432cdc40355d)

**After**

![After: current assignment stays neutral while the actual refresh error remains](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6dccd87e-1ee8-4e91-bb35-9716456d9b4d)

- The actual browser regression fails three assertions on isolated main: the failed-read trigger, its selected menu row and the pending retry. Recovery to a named agent and later confirmation of an absent agent remain valid. No card update is sent.
- The owning regression fails on main and distinguishes unknown roster, confirmed absence and a configured name, retaining the current option, identity and default choice. Editor/detail tests also preserve rejected drafts and genuine recovery.
- The independent browser scenario passes in 14.56s and all 44 focused option/editor/detail tests pass in 2.32s. Targeted plugin production types, focused lint (zero warnings/errors), formatting and diff checks pass. Six unchanged roster/SDK cases verify failure reporting and retained accepted data.
- Source/history review traces the unconditional label to #106058, retained through plugin extraction #134943. The native picker displays the supplied label; the roster owner already distinguishes missing from accepted data. Those owners and their authority checks are unchanged.
- Self-review/simplification: seven net production lines replace the premature label at its existing owner; 115 test lines cover the live flow and distinct roster states. No new state, caching, retry policy, translation key or permission layer.

This is a draft for review. Independent automated review, broad CI and live Gateway operations are not claimed complete. Hosted CI timing is not yet known.

prs.title: feat(memory): shared memory database for multi-agent deployments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When multiple agents share a single OpenClaw instance, each agent creates its own memory database. This wastes disk space, causes inconsistent search results across agents, and triggers unnecessary full reindexing when extra memory paths change.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR introduces shared memory database support for multi-agent deployments by making four coordinated changes:

1. **Force shared memory index** (`memory-search.ts`): When the system agent is configured with an explicit default workspace (`agents.defaults.workspace`), force `memorySearch.enabled=true` and redirect `store.databasePath` to a shared sqlite keyed by workspace hash.

2. **Exclude extraPaths from scope hash** (`manager-reindex-state.ts`): Remove `extraPaths` from the scope hash calculation so adding/removing extra memory paths doesn't trigger a full reindex of the shared database.

3. **Skip shared memory ownership assertion** (`openclaw-agent-db.ts`, `openclaw-agent-db-schema-helpers.ts`): Allow multiple agents to open the same shared memory database without triggering ownership errors.

4. **Use canonical workspace for system agent** (`memory-runtime.ts`, `manager.ts`): When the system agent has an explicit default workspace, use that path directly for the shared memory database instead of a per-agent subdirectory.

## User Impact

- Multi-agent deployments share a single memory database, reducing disk usage and improving search consistency
- Adding/removing extra memory paths no longer triggers expensive full reindexing
- System agent and memory plugin lifecycle use the same canonical workspace and SQLite database

## Evidence

- Tested against OpenClaw v2026.9.2 source
- All four changes are minimal and focused on the shared memory path resolution
- No changes to memory search behavior, embedding, or ranking logic

prs.title: refactor(browser): keep one document-interception session per tab
prs.body:
Related: #198317

## What Problem This Solves

Prepares the fix for #198317. Every guarded browser navigation or action creates its own CDP session for document interception and tears it down afterwards, so nothing owns a tab's interception between actions and a policy for that gap has nowhere to live. This moves ownership to the tab without changing what is allowed or blocked, so the fix (#198452) is a small policy change on top of it.

## User Impact

User impact: none intended. Interception still runs only while a guarded navigation or action is in progress, with the same policy decisions, redirect-hop checks, source-page preservation and error precedence.

Three differences worth a reviewer's attention:

- After its first guarded navigation or action, a tab keeps one CDP session and its iframe auto-attach instead of creating them per action. A new out-of-process iframe in that tab is resumed by this session between actions too.
- A frame that attaches after an invocation lost its authority is resumed instead of left paused. Its documents are still refused and the invocation still fails with the authority error.
- An action can return slightly before a nested out-of-process iframe commits, because cleanup has fewer protocol round trips. The redirect authority live test waits for that commit instead of reading it immediately.

## Why This Change Was Made

- One tab fence per Playwright `Page` owns the session, its frame targets and the document tracking. `installNavigationAuthorityFence` keeps its signature and registers a claim: the invocation's policy, document handler and failure state.
- A paused document goes through the claims that existed when it arrived, in turn, and continues only if each one resumes it. With one claim this is the same decision as on `main`.
- Releasing the last claim sends `Fetch.disable` and `Network.disable`, and cleanup returns when they are answered, as on `main`. The next claim sends `Fetch.enable` and `Network.enable` only after that answer, once per target while the tab is claimed; claims that overlap await the same start. It waits for the answer no longer than the navigation timeout, then fails without enabling; having started nothing, it only gives up its claim. A claim whose enable fails fails its invocation. The extension relay refuses `Fetch.enable` while its `Fetch.disable` is unanswered, so sending the two in call order is not enough there.
- Cleanup that cannot confirm cancellation keeps its closed claim, which refuses every document until the tab closes, and clears the documents it was waiting on so later invocations on that tab do not wait for them.
- The fence file is edited in place (+206/−94) so the diff shows what moved from the invocation to the tab.

## Evidence

- **Through the production extension relay:** real Chromium 156 with the bundled extension 2.3.0 loaded unpacked and paired with the Gateway's relay, in a clean macOS VM. The relay and the extension are unmodified; a tap on the relay's client socket in the test records each `Fetch`/`Network` enable and disable request and its answer. A fixture server at a policy-denied address counts requests.
  - Back-to-back key-press actions on one tab, the second making the page navigate to the denied address: blocked in 3 of 3 rounds, no request reached the server, the tab kept its page.
  - The second action started at the moment the first action's `Fetch.disable` reached the relay (3 of 3 rounds): `Fetch.enable` is sent after the relay answers `Fetch.disable`, the navigation is blocked and no request reached the server.

    ```
    2493.0ms  client -> relay  Fetch.disable #255
    2493.9ms  relay -> client  Fetch.disable #255 answered
    2494.6ms  client -> relay  Fetch.enable #258
    2495.4ms  relay -> client  Fetch.enable #258 answered
    B rejected: Navigation blocked ...; denied server requests=0; tab kept its page
    ```

    The same run on this PR's first commit alone (`318c175`), which does not wait for the answer: the relay refuses the enable, the action runs with interception off and the denied server receives the document, in 3 of 3 rounds.

    ```
    2344.6ms  client -> relay  Fetch.disable #275
    2345.0ms  client -> relay  Fetch.enable #278
    2345.1ms  relay -> client  Fetch.enable #278 REFUSED: Fetch interception is owned by another session or is being released
    2345.6ms  relay -> client  Fetch.disable #275 answered
    B completed; denied server requests=2; tab is on http://localhost:DENIED_PORT/denied
    ```

  - A refused `Fetch.enable`: a second relay session takes the tab's Fetch lease between two actions. The relay refuses the next action's `Fetch.enable`, the action is rejected with the relay's error before its key press reaches the page, and no request reached the server. Once the lease is released the next action completes. On `318c175` the refusal is dropped, the key press runs and the denied server receives the document.

    ```
    5308.1ms  client -> relay  Fetch.enable #743
    5308.2ms  relay -> client  Fetch.enable #743 REFUSED: Fetch interception is owned by another session or is being released
    B rejected: send: Protocol error (Fetch.enable): Fetch interception is owned by another session or is being released; key "b" reached the page=false; denied server requests=0; tab kept its page
    ```

  - Not shown through the relay: a release that is never answered. The real relay answered every release within about 1 ms or refused, so that case has only the unit test below.
- **Unit tests for the same three cases on a mocked transport:** a delayed `Fetch.disable` answer with `Fetch.enable` refused until it arrives; a refused enable failing the invocation; and a release that is never answered, where the next invocation fails at the navigation timeout without sending an enable, stopping the page or sending the release again. Each fails without its part of the change.
- **Unit tests:** 172 of 172 pass in the seven browser test files that cover the fence and its callers, including the dashboard navigation test, which counts one fence preparation per navigation attempt. Targeted typecheck, lint and format are clean.
- **Live tests (real Chromium over direct CDP):** 29 pass: redirect authority (12), page-cancelled interception (3), download policy (7), current-document download (5) and native CORS (2).
  - Three native-CORS cases need `127.0.0.2`, which macOS does not route; they time out there on `main` as well.
  - The two nested-iframe redirect cases are intermittent in this environment and fail the same way on `main` (10 of 10 runs): a trace shows the test's click inside the nested frame starts no navigation, so the fence has no redirect to see.
- **Independent review:** reviewers who did not write the change looked for an interleaving of overlapping and back-to-back invocations, frame targets attaching or detaching, a late or missing answer, and tab or session loss in which an invocation starts with interception off. They found none.
- **Test changes:** the fence lifecycle tests assert a released claim instead of a detached session; one case that tested listener removal before detach is replaced by one that a document arriving after release loads; one case covers a later invocation not waiting on documents a timed-out cleanup left behind. The dashboard navigation test (`agent.act.dashboard-ownership.test.ts`) checks the tab-owned session: one session serves every navigation attempt and is detached, with no listeners left, when the tab closes. Its per-attempt preparation count is unchanged.

Not checked: the full Gateway with a real agent and model (the relay proof drives the browser action functions through the relay), Linux and Windows, and remote-CDP profiles.

prs.title: fix(agents): resolve transcript replay policies fresh so plugin package swaps take effect
prs.body:
### What Problem This Solves

Closes #139978.

`resolveTranscriptPolicy` memoized replay policies in a config-keyed WeakMap whose key fingerprint ignores the installed plugin inventory, so an in-process plugin package swap for the same provider id (setup-inference Codex generation install, onboarding plugin install) kept replaying with the previous package's `buildReplayPolicy` output until the config object itself was replaced. Those swap paths call `invalidatePluginRuntimeDiscoveryAfterConfigMutation` to clear the loader/metadata caches precisely so subsequent resolution observes the new package — the memo silently bypassed that invalidation.

### Why This Change Was Made

- The memo is net-negative even on its own terms: every cached-path call pays a control-plane fingerprint hash plus `JSON.stringify` of the key to save one warm registry snapshot lookup, and the loader's own load cache (which *is* invalidated on swaps) already absorbs the cold path.
- Call sites are per model turn, not per message, so fresh resolution costs nothing measurable.
- Deleting the memo restores the documented invalidation contract instead of adding a second invalidation owner for the WeakMap.

### User Impact

Replay policy decides sanitization, tool-call-id rewriting, thinking-block handling, and turn validation. After this change, an in-process plugin package swap takes effect on the next turn instead of serving transcript hygiene from the previous package for the rest of the process.

### Evidence

- **Pre-fix red / post-fix green**: driven through the committed real-package suite below (main's memo restored verbatim → stale policy served; memo removed → replacement policy served). The original mocked freshness case in `transcript-policy.test.ts` was removed (2026-10-09 review follow-up) now that the real-package suite protects the same regression end to end.
- **Mechanism source**: `src/plugins/plugin-control-plane-context.ts:59-73` — `inventoryFingerprint` is only included when an installed-plugin `index` is passed, and the memo key passes none; `src/plugins/registry-refresh.ts:60-69` — the invalidation contract the memo bypassed; swap paths at `src/system-agent/setup-inference-persist.ts:125` and `src/commands/onboarding-plugin-install.ts:132`.
- **Consumers checked for object-identity reliance**: all four call sites (`embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.ts:710,898`, `run/attempt-history.ts:419`, `runtime-plan/build.ts:197`) consume the policy by value; none compare identity.
- **LOC**: net −31 production (`git diff --numstat`: transcript-policy.ts 12+/43−), +22 net test lines.
- **Checks**: `oxfmt` clean, `oxlint --type-aware` clean on both files.
- **Review follow-up + main sync** (2026-10-09, head `f6867a60139`): fixed the unresolved `./types.openclaw.js` type import (→ `../config/types.openclaw.js`), removed the superseded mocked freshness case (−38 LOC), and synced current main (`update-branch`); `ci-gate` success, `mergeable` true.
- **Rebase onto current main** (2026-10-09): `mergeTranscriptPolicy` has since become a generic merge loop, the memo key gained `directApiKey`/`baseUrl` fields, and `inHistorySystemUpdates` post-processing was added; the fix is re-applied as pure memo removal on top of all of that (`mergeable` back to true, head `db1edffbe26c`), and the pre-fix red above was re-verified against main's *evolved* memo before this push.
- **Competition**: no open issue/PR matches (searched "transcript policy cache", "replay policy cache", "buildReplayPolicy stale", "memoize transcript"); no open PR touches `src/agents/transcript-policy.ts`.
- **Real package replacement proof** (2026-10-09, head `4b88053b8b2`): new committed suite `src/agents/transcript-policy.package-swap.test.ts` drives the real discovery → manifest-registry → jiti module-load path with no mocks: it writes a genuine provider plugin package (`openclaw.plugin.json` + `register(api)` → `api.registerProvider({...buildReplayPolicy})`) into a temp extensions dir, resolves the policy, replaces the package in place on disk (same path, same provider id, same config object), and runs the exact three lifecycle invalidation calls from `finishOnboardingPluginInstall` — `clearLoadInstalledPluginIndexInstallRecordsCache` + `clearPluginMetadataLifecycleCaches` + `invalidatePluginRuntimeDiscoveryAfterConfigMutation`.
  - Post-fix, this head: `[proof] before swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false` → `[proof] after swap sanitizeToolCallIds = true`, `Tests 1 passed (1)` (`src/agents/transcript-policy.package-swap.test.ts`).
  - Pre-fix reproduction: main's memo restored verbatim onto this tree (WeakMap + fingerprint key + cached read/write); the same suite goes red on the stale memo — `[proof] before swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false` → `[proof] after swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false`, `AssertionError: expected false to be true`. The memo was restored as a patch rather than by swapping the whole file because current main's `transcript-policy.ts` imports `@openclaw/ai/internal/openai-responses-payload-policy`, an export this checkout's workspace lockfile does not expose yet; the restored cache read/write logic is byte-identical to main's (`origin/main` `d121dc10aa1`).



### CI note (preflight red is main-inherited, not from this diff)

`preflight` fails on this fork PR with GitHub's job-outputs limit, not a test failure: every step succeeds and the job annotation is `Job outputs exceed 1,048,576 bytes` (e.g. check-run 101474152723, run 34028685031).

- Cause sits in the workflow, not this diff: `preflight` ships the whole compact Node test plan as the `checks_node_core_nondist_matrix` output (~98% of the job's total output bytes; measured locally by re-running the manifest planner for this PR's inputs: 522,685 bytes total, 513,351 of them that matrix).
- Fork PRs take `runner_profile=github` (hosted-runner-profile-contract in the `runner_profile` step), which packs 79 compact rows + 31 fallback rows instead of blacksmith's 50, and each row embeds the full test-file inventory in `groups[].includePatterns` (largest row ≈ 40KB).
- Contrast on the same day: same-repo PRs #140038 / #140040 (blacksmith profile, ~453KB) pass preflight; fork PRs #139979, #140008, #140045 fail with the same annotation. A retrigger of this same branch passed preflight once (run 34025126956) and failed twice — the payload sits at the cap edge, so fork-PR preflight is now a coin flip.
- All substantive checks on this PR's head are green (`check-test-types-*`, lint, node test shards that ran in earlier attempts); only `preflight` + the `ci-gate` aggregate are red.
