prs.title: fix(channels): unblock ingress after a transient shutdown release failure
prs.body:
Closes #193019

## Main compatibility refresh — 2026-11-06

Published merge head `3e7a10e467cf355f5a02d71b899efa3eb4068832`, integrating main `b11b610d173cc6ff87eb026b6506c20fc7e5fd62` without rewriting PR history. The single `ingress-drain.ts` conflict is resolved preserving upstream failure callback extraction, queue-cap drops, selective custody retirement and test consolidation.

**Updated scope:** main #193423 already mitigates the old indefinite hold by retiring failed drains and permitting recovery of known never-adopted claims after disposal. This PR retains the bounded, token-fenced native cancellation-release retry before disposal; it does not claim current main remains indefinitely blocked. Pinned-main production overlay fails the focused retry regression (one release instead of two). Exhaustion coverage now follows upstream recovery after joined disposal; uncertain outcomes remain fenced.

**New-head verification:** 180 tests across 13 affected files passed; final worker handoff rerun 12 passed, coordinator independent rerun 12 passed. Targeted production/test typechecking, lint, format, source-line ratchet and scoped whitespace passed. Independent exact-head semantic review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Frozen pnpm 12.15.0 install used target-identical manifests/lockfile. Test-line ratchet retains main's 25-line debt: pinned main is 25 over, candidate is 25 over, and the PR adds exactly its existing 182-line grant. No shared ceiling was changed. New-head CI is not claimed green.

**Proof provenance:** all Telegram/Claude live evidence below remains historical at `934ca4166ec58d9dc24deaf248051da44392a0a2`. Writer bytes are equivalent, but upstream custody/disposal, dependencies and test contracts changed; no live-proof equivalence or new-head live run is claimed. No production restart or new Telegram traffic occurred.

Later observed main `c63b3a2e58c45e82ea4d4955c1ac3bbb6a275d2e` also merge-probes cleanly; intervening changes are iOS tooling, so no additional merge was introduced.


## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: queued channel messages remain blocked when a pre-adoption cancellation release fails once during shutdown and the retained old drain continues holding its claim.

## User Impact

A transient known release failure can recover automatically so a replacement monitor can deliver the queued conversation. Cancellation preserves delivery retry history. No configuration or database migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retained cancellation after abort now joins at most three token-fenced release attempts, with 1s and 2s backoffs. The existing settlement owner holds custody throughout. Explicit disposal prevents another attempt; failed completion, ordinary abandonment, standalone drains, and uncertain write outcomes keep their existing safety behavior. Exhaustion or an uncertain cancellation write remains observable and retains custody. The bounded retry can add up to three seconds of backoff to shutdown, plus storage I/O.

## Evidence

- A real production ingress monitor stop/restart with an actual isolated SQLite-backed queue fails on the unchanged base and passes with the repair. One known failure is injected before the native release write; the lifecycle callback is invoked only once. The replacement processes same-lane events in order, rejects stale-token writes, and does not replay already-adopted unrelated work.
- Focused drain, monitor, handoff and claim-owner suites: 73 tests passed. Added checks cover exhausted retries, nested uncertain outcomes, explicit disposal during backoff, takeover during retry, standalone cancellation and ordinary abandonment. Existing failed-completion and retry-history controls pass.
- Targeted production/test typechecking, lint, format, line-cap/test-line ratchets and whitespace checks are recorded in the local handoff.
- Independent shared autoreview: Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, medium reasoning, P0–P2, one pass over the complete uncommitted candidate against `06d4059a3d06` and supplied unchanged owner context; no actionable findings. This is evidence-based review, without a repository mount or test execution in the reviewer sandbox. Subsequent test edits only added required braces and an explicit already-completed return and removed a redundant default type argument. The coordinating parent independently inspected the final source and clean commit and reran all 10 boundary cases successfully.

**Initial test scope (historical; supplemented by the real Telegram/model run below):** proof here is the owning monitor/SQLite boundary with a synthetic pre-write failure. Actual SQLite locking, a complete Gateway process, a real agent/model, and Telegram transport were not exercised; no live outage reproduction is claimed. Exact live Gateway channel stop/restart under an actual storage lock remains a broader integration gap. No external API or transport contract changes here.

The dedicated allocation grants exactly 182 added test lines for this recovery regression and its distinct custody bounds; the shared baseline is unchanged. The change reuses existing owners and removes redundant release wrappers; production code grows by 12 lines. The four-suite run took 41.92s including worker preparation; the final boundary file took 4.63s in Vitest (50.61s wrapper including compiler preparation), and the parent independently measured 4.92s (53.90s wrapper). CI timing is unmeasured before publication.


## Additional shipped-entry-point evidence — 2026-11-05

The earlier Evidence section describes the initial monitor tests. This additional run used the real built CLI/Gateway, its plugin loader, and the public `channels.stop` / `channels.start` RPCs. It was **not another in-process monitor test**. The channel was a task-only local diagnostic plugin (`ingress-proof/default`), not Telegram. Its delivery callback deliberately calls synthetic `onDeferred` / `onAdopted`; **no real agent/model response or external transport was exercised, so this does not claim the root real-agent/model E2E gate is fully satisfied**.

**Isolation and provenance.** Separate task HOME, config, SQLite state, workspace and loopback ports; only the diagnostic plugin enabled; no provider credentials copied, no production Gateway restart/config/state change, no real-channel messages. The same fixture and one-shot fault wrapper ran against head `934ca4166ec58d9dc24deaf248051da44392a0a2` and runtime inputs from base `06d4059a3d06e1a34a3cacfd3f635b93fe803a38`. For the base run, only the two owner files were temporarily restored byte-for-byte from the base and rebuilt through the CLI; all other runtime inputs matched base (only the new test/allocation differed). This was a documented base-runtime overlay in the head checkout, not a Git checkout whose HEAD changed. Original source was restored afterward.

The external plugin uses public SDK `createChannelIngressMonitor` and `api.runtime.state.openChannelIngressQueue`. It throws exactly once **before** calling the native release operation, logs refresh only after the real queue returns `true`, and reads the committed queue via the public API. There is no SQLite method mock, SQL reset, forced owner retirement, manual second cancellation callback, or claimed actual `SQLITE_BUSY`. The fixture SHA-256 is `d1d039654e952e53eff1e39baa8680360637a26f3e8cf0bad372773df0b7fcb3`.

**Base observation.** Real Gateway PID `95449`: the channel stop RPC reported `stopped: true`, but the internal joined monitor stop rejected the injected error. Starting the replacement channel did not drain its lane. Only `unrelated` was synthetically adopted; `task` remained claimed and `waiting` pending. Committed `claimedAt` values advanced at `2026-11-05T11:03:19.612+09:00`, `2026-11-05T11:03:21.614+09:00`, and `2026-11-05T11:03:58.706+09:00`; heartbeat commit counts were `[4, 6, 43]`. This is a bounded observation of continued old-owner renewal, not an empirical claim that it can never recover.

```text
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"cancel-callback","generation":1,"pid":95449,"id":"task","ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-abort","generation":1,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"release-attempt","generation":1,"pid":95449,"attempt":1,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"injected-known-prewrite-failure","generation":1,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-stop-rejected","generation":1,"pid":95449,"message":"Error: Synthetic known cancellation release failure before native write","ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"cancel-callback-returned","generation":1,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"heartbeat-committed","generation":1,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:21 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-started","generation":2,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":2}
11:03:21 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"heartbeat-committed","generation":2,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:58 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"heartbeat-committed","generation":2,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
```

**Head observation.** Real Gateway PID `93148` remained the same across channel generation 1→2. One cancellation callback caused one known pre-write failure, then release attempt 2 committed about one second later and joined stop succeeded. The replacement synthetically adopted `task`, then `waiting`; the already-adopted `unrelated` was not replayed. The old token's release/complete/refresh all returned `false`, the successor token differed, and re-enqueue of `unrelated` returned `completed`. Final pending and claimed sets were empty.

```text
10:58:29 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-started","generation":1,"pid":93148,"ownerGeneration":1}
10:58:59 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"adopted","generation":1,"pid":93148,"id":"unrelated","ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:55 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"cancel-callback","generation":1,"pid":93148,"id":"task","ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:55 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"release-attempt","generation":1,"pid":93148,"attempt":1,"ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:55 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"injected-known-prewrite-failure","generation":1,"pid":93148,"ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:56 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"release-attempt","generation":1,"pid":93148,"attempt":2,"ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:56 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"release-result","generation":1,"pid":93148,"id":"task","committed":true,"ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:56 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-stop-joined","generation":1,"pid":93148,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:00:11 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-started","generation":2,"pid":93148,"ownerGeneration":2}
11:00:11 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"stale-token-check","generation":2,"pid":93148,"release":false,"complete":false,"refresh":false,"changed":true}
11:00:11 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"adopted","generation":2,"pid":93148,"id":"task","ownerGeneration":2}
11:00:11 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"adopted","generation":2,"pid":93148,"id":"waiting","ownerGeneration":2}
11:00:14 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"dedupe-check","generation":2,"pid":93148,"kind":"completed"}
11:00:37 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-stop-joined","generation":2,"pid":93148,"ownerGeneration":2}
```

**Shipped command path.** Under each task-only environment: `corepack pnpm openclaw gateway run --bind loopback --auth none --verbose`; then `corepack pnpm openclaw gateway call` with `--expect-url` pinned to that task's configured loopback Gateway, using `ingressProof.seed`, `ingressProof.arm`, `channels.stop`, `ingressProof.snapshot`, `channels.start`, `ingressProof.snapshot`, and `ingressProof.dedupe` (head). Public lifecycle params were `{"channel":"ingress-proof","accountId":"default"}`. All these RPC commands exited 0; the base's reported stop success is distinguished above from its monitor failure. Both task Gateways later handled SIGTERM and exited 0 with clean shutdown. No commit/push was required for this instrumentation.

**Interpretation and limits.** A generally slow model cannot explain this comparison because no model runs; identical fixture, queue, lane and fault behavior plus the advancing native timestamps distinguish a retained old-owner claim from a delayed initial read. However, the fixture deliberately supplies deferred/cancelled work and observes its own callback receipts. Its synthetic adoption is not evidence of agent execution, outbound send, Telegram acceptance, or user-visible response. It does not prove an actual database lock, indefinite blockage beyond the observed interval, every channel adapter, or a whole-Gateway process restart. It proves a real Gateway-hosted local channel stop/replacement through shipped entry points with actual SQLite persistence. Whether this layer satisfies the requested real-behavior gate remains for review; the broader real agent/model/transport gap is explicit.


## Real Telegram and real model recovery evidence — 2026-11-05

**Observed result:** recovery eventually succeeded through the production Telegram adapter, real Claude CLI agent/model, and Telegram Bot API. It did **not** succeed on the first replacement: the task relay refused two overlapping local polls and the adapter automatically restarted twice before both replies completed. The human operator confirmed in the Telegram client that the replies arrived in A → B order. Per-event counts below are backed by the queue, transcript and Bot API receipts; the human confirmation specifically establishes client-visible order.

Pinned PR head: `934ca4166ec58d9dc24deaf248051da44392a0a2`. The requesting user confirmed their dedicated bot was unused elsewhere, then sent a fresh exact handshake and prescribed A/B prompts manually in the verified private DM. No automated user account or team QA pool was used. The isolated Gateway had task-owned config/state/workspace/ports. A parent-owned, destination-bound protected HTTPS relay consumed the stored token sentinel; no credential value was extracted or copied into the Gateway. The operator Gateway was untouched.

Temporary instrumentation held only A before real admission and injected one known error before the original claim's native cancellation release write. It never invoked synthetic adoption. Native cancellation, the PR's existing bounded writer retry, real Telegram replay, real agent/model execution and outbound delivery remained production paths. Setup `deleteWebhook` was a recorded local no-op after verified empty webhook; no upstream webhook deletion or queue flush occurred. Command-menu deletion attempts were refused locally.

Measured timeline, KST:

```text
13:31:16.764  A held before native adoption
13:31:58.907  bound B observed by real Telegram poller
13:32:36.938  read-only task SQLite: A claimed, B pending; same lane; attempts=0
13:32:38.283  one known pre-write release failure for original A token
13:32:39.285  second release attempt for that same token (+1002ms)
13:32:40      manual channel replacement starts
13:32:41      local concurrent-poll refusal; automatic restart scheduled
13:32:47–48   first automatic restart also hits local poll guard
13:32:58      second automatic restart starts
13:32:59.308  real A adoption/completion write commits with new claim token
13:33:03.954  Telegram accepts final A response
13:33:04.053  real B adoption/completion write commits
13:33:06.414  Telegram accepts final B response
```

The old long-poll request remained in the relay until its bounded upstream request returned after the downstream client was cancelled. The relay's single-poll guard refused the two successor attempts rather than starting another upstream poller. This was task relay lifecycle behavior, not a second bot consumer or a newly fixed PR behavior. No queue reset, forced retirement, manual second cancellation callback or failed-send retry was used to recover.

Final read-only SQLite inspection found exactly A and B, both `completed`, both attempts=0, with no pending/claimed work. The real agent transcript contains exactly two assistant records matching the prescribed A and B responses in order, both `provider=claude-cli`, `api=cli`, with actual usage: A input10/output181/cache-write11936; B input10/output81/cache-read11936/cache-write710. Telegram returned two distinct accepted message receipts, A then B; no duplicate-send refusal or uncertain-send event occurred. Native launch/probe/maintenance subprocess counts are not misrepresented as exactly two model requests. The separate one-shot provider setup qualification is excluded from this recovery proof.

The native Claude child used its existing login without copying credentials, with global home file writes denied by an OS policy, tools/customizations and native session persistence disabled. Gateway/OpenClaw state stayed task-owned. This was a real provider, not mock-openai or synthetic `onAdopted`. Source instrumentation was restored byte-for-byte, Git was clean at the pinned head, and the uninstrumented head build completed successfully. The Gateway logged a clean shutdown in82ms; its launcher group received SIGTERM and reported-15, so that wrapper is not reported as exit0. Parent verified the protected relay ended code0 and both task ports closed. No live task processes remain; persistent review Remote is retained.

**Client observation:** on 2026-11-05 at 13:43 KST the human operator confirmed the replies arrived in order. This is a human client observation, not an inference from Bot API acceptance.

**Limits:** Actual SQLite locking, every transport/provider, and whole-Gateway restart were not tested or required for this known pre-write failure. The earlier base/head Gateway comparison and existing safety regressions are separate supporting evidence. This run establishes eventual real-channel/model/outbound recovery with the explicit transient relay failures above; it is not presented as a clean first-restart run or proof of all client-rendering behavior.

prs.title: improve(workers): reuse verified prepared snapshots and worker code
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fresh cloud sessions repeat completed snapshot setup and worker-code extraction instead of reusing verified prepared content.

## User Impact

Fresh, unpinned default-branch sessions can reuse a compatible completed snapshot only when its revision belongs to admitted default-branch history. Explicit refs and pinned sessions retain exact-source preparation. Seed-only requests prepare the requested revision without running an unauthorized setup recipe. The actual completed base reaches preparation, inspection and binding; current repository access remains required.

Verified worker packages are reused through exact aliases; damaged or missing code falls back to verified archive installation. Legacy peers retain registration-time verification. Only negotiated peers defer verification to first binding with its full timeout; exact binding replay preserves private edits.

**Status:** `3825a67…` is published for **proof**, not landing. Broad CI, shared Swift-kit Periphery and OpenGrep precise scan **attempt 2 succeeded** after separately diagnosed download failures. At the November 9, 16:41 UTC readback, all **167 latest check runs were terminal: 124 success, 42 skipped, one neutral**, with no failed or pending checks. OpenGrep's parser-coverage limitations are recorded below. AUTH-2, UPGRADE-3 and dependency #193873 remain open. No consumer merge or server deployment occurred.

**Landing dependency:** older-snapshot behavior requires [managed publication recovery #193873](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193873). Publication is not dependency acceptance. Capture normalization and diagnostics are separately covered by #193776.

The existing admission, prepared-workspace and installer owners serve this flow. Strict registration requests exclude receipt-only fields. Negotiated verification stages preserve old/new peer compatibility without a protocol-version bump. Actual-base propagation, main's preparation callback, memoization, capture verification and diagnostics remain intact.

The admitted repository/account owner checks snapshot ancestry. Missing or oversized comparisons decline optional reuse only after repository/account revalidation; authentication, revocation, cancellation and transport failures still fail closed. The metadata size limit is unchanged.

prs.title: feat(agents): expose configured descriptions in agents_list
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent configuration accepts descriptions, but `agents_list` omits them. A requester choosing an allowed subagent cannot see the operator-authored capability summary. Fixes #7490.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expose bounded, nonblank descriptions only in on-demand discovery. Preserve the complete authorized roster, ordering, resolved model/runtime metadata, and existing child-agent restrictions. Each description is limited to 512 UTF-16 units without splitting a surrogate pair, with a shared 4096 CJK-aware weighted-unit budget. Later description text may be shortened or omitted; agent rows remain.

## User Impact

Names, descriptions and existing model/runtime metadata remain available together. Documentation at the current per-agent-entry and subagent-discovery owners describes model visibility and excludes secrets or tenant-sensitive material. There is no new configuration, authorization, persistence, provider, or automatic prompt-roster mechanism.

Existing nonblank descriptions would become model-visible to already-authorized discoverers after upgrade without an operator editing configuration. That disclosure choice requires the maintainer decision below; the spawn allowlist alone does not establish prior operator expectations.

## Evidence

All three required statuses (CI gate, dependency review and security-sensitive review) are **SUCCESS** on this head. Earlier successful runs remain prior-head evidence. No workflow rerun, duplicate review request or adoption ping was submitted. Maintainer product adoption, official distribution and employee acceptance remain separate.

Earlier validated author head: `02db206611aaf040ab37ea819889b8264483914b`. It normally merges CI-green head `1c771bb8` with official main `0372963434f6a0b79394dbe330abde2ae34f2a89` to resolve one new generated Discord-delta conflict that arose while the prior CI was running.

The current merge resolves only the later Discord delta, passes **13 snapshot-owner tests** and the canonical **six-artifact check**, and has an independent generated-resolution review plus zero-finding secret gate.

The two corrected subagent fixture files are byte-identical to CI-green `1c771bb8`. No production behavior, authorization, assertion, timeout or CI routing was changed by these integrations.

Production public/internal visible-reply requirements and every retire-count assertion are preserved.

Type-aware lint, format, diff check, independent parent review, fresh scoped Codex review and zero-finding secret gate passed. The private review snapshot is not a public ancestor.

Only fixed proof fields and the test result are retained; no credential, endpoint, IP address, configuration dump, or conversation text is included. prs.body:
## Status: superseded — do not merge

[PR #194807](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194807) already fixed this Systems dependency on main, merged at **2026-11-07 22:13:28 UTC** as `16f02454a7f8bb4e95e1a733d04303ecac193632`. That canonical implementation independently loads measurements through the existing page owner.

This draft was prepared against the older pinned baseline `fa27babf88518f243724fde005b40c90ad8e3f2a`. Current-main inspection caught the overlap. The committed early-content regression also passes when run with the Systems owning modules from inspected main `adca0b0844c71362be6da780008c642d17b2e350`. There is therefore **no additional validated performance opportunity here**, and this alternative must not replace or duplicate the current owner. The branch remains preserved as historical experiment/proof, not a proposed second cutover.

## What Problem This Solves

prs.title: fix(anthropic): retry unavailable catalog watch on elapsed time
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Anthropic catalog's `createDirtyDirectoryWatch` arms its restart backoff with `Date.now()`. When a watch becomes unavailable (health callback or start failure), it records `retryAt = Date.now() + 5_000` and only restarts once `Date.now() >= retryAt`. A wall-clock correction can distort that elapsed-time budget: rolling the clock back keeps an unavailable watch un-retried indefinitely (every catalog read degrades to a full rescan), while a forward step retries early and churns subscriptions.

Precedent: #191606 (same elapsed-TTL-vs-wall-clock shape; this PR is the same shape at the remaining Anthropic tree-watch site).

## Why This Change Was Made

The tree-watch owner (`createDirtyDirectoryWatch` in `session-catalog-tree-watch.ts`) writes and compares a single in-memory retry deadline with `Date.now()` in three spots (health-callback, start-catch, and the `takeDirty` re-check). The deadline is an elapsed-time budget and is switched to `performance.now()`, matching the clock-sweep already merged for sibling extensions in #191606. No validator, option, config, or persistence policy is added or changed.

Production LOC is `+2/-2, net 0`.

Classification: `behavior-completing`

## User Impact

A wall-clock correction no longer postpones or accelerates watch restart after an unavailable/failed filesystem watch. The five-second retry backoff fires on schedule regardless of NTP/manual clock changes; recovered coverage is re-established as before.

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `a6135571c9927fabe906cfd1c334a3b346f8be51`
- Current-main RED baseline: `0bb438485084d55ff7c760b4f5ad3f79b16346e2`
- Production entry: `createDirtyDirectoryWatch` (`extensions/anthropic/session-catalog-tree-watch.ts`)
- Canonical owner exercised: `takeDirty` retry check in `session-catalog-tree-watch.ts:75`
- Decision surface: `performance.now() >= retryAt` (watch restart backoff)
- Recorder/readback boundary: `observation.watch` call count (retry re-attaches the subscription)
- Acceptance RED: on current main the discriminating test `retries an unavailable watch on elapsed time even when the wall clock rolls back` FAILS (rollback keeps the watch un-retried), 2/3
- Acceptance GREEN: on this head the same test PASSES (elapsed retry fires on schedule), 3/3
- Legal control: existing `invalidates catalog reads at depth 2/3 and recovers lost coverage` tests still pass with forward-only clock steps
- Cleanup: test uses a temp directory via `useAutoCleanupTempDirTracker`; no production Gateway/session/token/config touched

### Inspectable RED -> GREEN terminal trace

The test drives both clocks independently: `performance.now()` (elapsed, advanced past the 5s retry window) and `Date.now()` (wall clock, rolled back an hour), with a watch that reports `unavailable`, and asserts the retry re-attaches the subscription only when the elapsed deadline has passed.

```text
# RED on current main (Date.now()-keyed retryAt): the rollback hides the expired deadline,
# the retry never re-attaches, and the watch stays unavailable.
× extension-providers extensions/anthropic/session-catalog-tree-watch.test.ts > retries an unavailable watch on elapsed time even when the wall clock rolls back
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  1 failed (3)
```

```text
# GREEN on this head (performance.now()): the elapsed retry deadline expires and the
# subscription is re-attached.
✓ extension-providers extensions/anthropic/session-catalog-tree-watch.test.ts > retries an unavailable watch on elapsed time even when the wall clock rolls back
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  3 passed (3)
```

### Real-subscription recovery trace

A real filesystem subscription drives the same unavailable->recover path (no mock): `createDirtyDirectoryWatch` watches a real directory, removing the root makes the real fs-safe watch report `unavailable`, a one-hour backward `Date.now()` step does not postpone the elapsed retry, and the rebuilt root re-attaches coverage.

```text
# HEAD (performance.now()): the elapsed retry fires on schedule despite the wall-clock rollback.
[+1201ms] attach#1 dirty="all"
[+2406ms] root removed (real unavailable)
[+2409ms] root rebuilt; Date.now rolled back 1h
[+8016ms] poll0: "all"
[+9018ms] poll1: "all"
[+10019ms] poll2: {}          # takeDirty returns an empty Set: the watch re-attached
```

`takeDirty()` returning an empty `Set` (instead of the blanket `"all"`) proves the subscription recovered coverage after the elapsed retry deadline — a real watcher, real file system, real invalidation, no mock.

### Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/anthropic/session-catalog-tree-watch.test.ts` (Node 24.18, docker) — 3/3 passed on head
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`
- Real path: the trace above exercises a real filesystem subscription (root removal drives a genuine `unavailable` health, rebuild re-attaches coverage after the elapsed deadline). The wall-clock rollback is applied only in-process to `Date.now()`; the host/system clock is untouched.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+2/-2`
- Test LOC: `+39/-2`
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses the established `performance.now()` elapsed-time pattern from #191606; no new helper, validator, or API surface
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none

prs.title: fix(gateway): scope the JSONL transcript usage estimate to the live window across boundaries
prs.body:
Refs #150579

## What Problem This Solves

A compacted session's transcript usage report (the JSONL artifact seam behind diagnostic reads) counted the whole append-only archive as live context. Content superseded by a compaction or reset stays in the file, and the chars-based estimate summed every user/assistant message ever written, so the reported total kept growing across clean compactions while the model's actual context stayed small.

A second gap sat next to it: once the estimate restarted at a boundary, eligibility was re-derived only from model-tagged assistant entries in the retained window. A summary-only window (the cut names an entry outside the message window) or a retained-user-only window (overflow compaction with a pending user message as its tail) lost the estimate until the next assistant reply, even though the summary and retained text were sitting in the model context.

## Root cause

`aggregateSessionTranscriptUsage` fills `totalTokens` from a chars estimate when no per-call usage snapshot provides one. `readLatestSessionUsageFromTranscriptFileAsync` feeds it the full JSONL transcript, and the estimate accumulated `estimatedTranscriptChars` over the whole scanned set with no notion of boundary markers or the retained window they name. The boundary restart also reset `sawEstimateModelIdentity` from the retained entries alone, while `finish()` requires that flag, so any window without a surviving model-tagged assistant reported no estimate at all.

## Fix

- The JSONL reader passes `compaction`/`reset` boundary records through with their `summary`/`firstKeptEntryId` fields, and forwards each entry's id, instead of skipping markers.
- The accumulator keeps per-entry char counts for the current window. At a boundary it keeps the retained tail named by `firstKeptEntryId` plus the compaction summary, matching the model-context contract (compactionSummary + retained entries + post-boundary messages) and the transcript tree selector's fallback (an unknown kept target drops the pre-boundary window). The previous revision restarted the estimate at zero, which undercounts a compacted session that retains a large summary or window.
- A boundary leaves the window estimate-eligible whenever it holds counted text. A compaction or reset marker is only written by a live model session, so requiring a model-tagged assistant to survive the cut only masked reads taken between the boundary and the next reply.
- Usage snapshots (input/output/cache/cost) still aggregate over the whole record, and a fresh per-call `totalTokens` snapshot still wins over any estimate, unchanged.

## Scope

This change lives entirely in the JSONL artifact seam: `readLatestSessionUsageFromTranscriptFileAsync` reads bounded transcript artifacts and its callers are diagnostic paths. The live budget-preflight path from #150579 reads the SQLite seam, which already scopes to the active context and is untouched here; that preflight symptom stays with #150579 and the PRs addressing it directly. This branch does not close the issue.

## Evidence

- New regressions in `session-usage-estimate.test.ts`: a compaction keeps its 500-char summary plus the 2000-char retained message named by `firstKeptEntryId` while dropping the 4000-char superseded prefix; a reset keeps its named retained tail; an unknown kept target drops the pre-boundary window but still counts the summary. Three further regressions end the transcript right at the boundary (summary-only window, compaction retaining only user messages, reset retaining only user text), covering the read between the boundary and the next assistant reply; earlier versions of these tests appended that reply, which masked the eligibility drop.
- Red/green: the boundary-terminal three fail on the previous head (no estimate reported). The consolidated table preserves all 10 independent scenarios, including snapshot precedence, reset boundaries, retained-user-only windows and the structural anchor.
- Runtime proof on a real compacted session (regenerated after the earlier /tmp artifact expired): isolated Gateway plus embedded agent against the scripted provider; a real injected 400 `context_length_exceeded`, one committed auto-compaction, then one more turn. The committed marker carries a 464-char summary and names a retained 91-char user message as `firstKeptEntryId`, so the boundary leaves a summary-plus-retained-user window. The artifact is the session's real settled transcript events serialized back to legacy JSONL, with redacted variants that drop usage fields and the model-snapshot entry so the chars estimate is what gets measured. The after-fix reader reports `totalTokens: 139` on the redacted prefix ending at the boundary (ceil((464 + 91) / 4), the summary plus the retained user text) and `176` on the full redacted artifact (ceil((464 + 91 + 56 + 90) / 4), adding the post-boundary assistant and user text). On the usage-carrying artifact the reader still reports the real provider aggregates (input 105 / output 25, latest context snapshot 120 total and available), so the estimate path and the snapshot path stay separate.
- Current head `dcfc49a70dfb`, including upstream main `3f2e7078de23`: `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/gateway/session-usage-estimate.test.ts src/gateway/session-transcript-derived-readers.usage.test.ts src/gateway/session-utils.fs.test.ts src/gateway/session-utils.transcript-usage.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes 4 files and 50 tests. oxfmt and direct type-aware oxlint pass on the consolidated test; the net PR diff passes `git diff --check`.
- Shipped diagnostic builder proof on `591ef68b2e9`: the real settled Gateway compaction events drive the production `buildReplyDiagnosticsPayload` raw diagnostic path through `readLatestSessionUsageFromTranscriptAsync`, not just a direct reader call. With usage fields removed, the boundary-terminal artifact emits `total=139` and the full artifact emits `total=176`. The measured control emits `input=105`, `output=25`, `cacheRead=0`, `cacheWrite=0`, `total=120`. The probe prints only the session usage block, with no transcript text, credentials or endpoints. This builder-level evidence does not satisfy Revision 17's separate shipped CLI/Gateway diagnostic request gate; that proof requirement remains open.
- Test budget: the four repeated retained-window fixtures now share one table helper, preserving all 10 scenarios while reducing the new test file from 157 to 145 lines. `config/test-lines-allocations/session-usage-active-window.txt` grants exactly those 145 added lines. The full-index ratchet on current head `dcfc49a70dfb`, using hosted CI's current main `3f2e7078de23` with `--no-merge-base`, reports `Test lines OK: 6561328; ceiling: 6561328; slack: 0.` An earlier sparse local run omitted 566 tracked test lines and produced a false slack result; materializing those files reproduced hosted CI's over-10 failure before this consolidation.

[AI-assisted] prepared with Kimi K3; verified locally as described above and reviewed line by line.

prs.title: feat: keep ask_user questions answerable after you start answering
prs.body:
Closes #199174

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an `ask_user` question expires while the person is reading its choices or typing an answer, so the answer they were writing can no longer be submitted.

## User Impact

User impact: once you click or tap into a question in the Control UI, Tab into it, choose an option, type or paste, that question stays answerable until you submit or skip it, or until the agent run is cancelled or ends. Your draft survives blur and switching between pending questions. Untouched questions still time out exactly as before (default 900 seconds, 30–3600 second clamp, unchanged model-facing arguments), so unattended automation still continues. Secret-entry questions keep their current timeout. Expired or cancelled questions are never revived.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The Gateway question manager stays the only expiry owner. A new `question.engage` RPC reports human interaction; it uses the same answer authority as `question.resolve`. The manager cancels that question's expiry job and records `expiryStoppedAtMs` only when the requester opted in (`stopExpiryOnInteraction`) and the question is not a secret question. A terminal question rejects with `QUESTION_ALREADY_TERMINAL`. While a restart or suspension is draining, `question.engage` uses the same pending-question continuation admission as `question.get` and `question.resolve`.
- `ask_user` opts in. When `question.waitAnswer` reaches its own wait deadline with the question still pending, the tool checks `question.get` and keeps waiting only if expiry was stopped; otherwise the existing wait-timeout cancellation is unchanged. Harness-owned and MCP-form requesters do not opt in, so their behavior is unchanged.
- The shared Control UI question panel (docked panel, child-session handoff, standalone question page) reports trusted pointer-down, keyboard input, Tab-driven focus, paste and input. Rendering, hover, programmatic or automatic focus, bare modifier keys, Escape and modifier shortcuts do not count. An engaged prompt drops its local countdown and its answer-request deadline. If another view's local deadline passes, it makes one `question.get` call and restores the prompt when the Gateway stopped expiry.
- Additive protocol changes (`since 2026.11`): the `question.engage` method, optional `QuestionRequestParams.stopExpiryOnInteraction`, and optional `QuestionRecord.expiryStoppedAtMs`.

Tradeoffs and limits:

- Engagement is not broadcast. Re-emitting `question.requested` would trigger web push again. Other Control UI views reconcile with one `question.get` at their local deadline instead.
- Native apps and the TUI do not send `question.engage` and still show the original countdown, so a question engaged in the Control UI may look expired there. Strict native decoders reject unknown record keys, so older native builds may not decode an engaged record that carries `expiryStoppedAtMs`. Earlier optional `since` fields set the precedent.
- A failed `question.engage` call is reported once per prompt per client and falls back to the original deadline instead of retrying on every keystroke.
- The model-facing `timeoutSeconds` description is unchanged, as scoped. It remains accurate for untouched questions.
- The run or model-attempt timeout still applies. Durability across restarts remains #167266.

## Evidence

**Reproduction on base `663611cb`.** I used a real isolated Gateway, the Control UI in Chromium, the real `ask_user` tool, a scripted local OpenAI Responses model and `timeoutSeconds: 30`. After a click and typing in the question, followed by focus moving away, the question was no longer `pending` after the original deadline. The assertion failed, which reproduces the issue.

**Acceptance proof: new `ui/src/e2e/ask-user-engaged-expiry.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`, run locally.** It passed 5/5 against a Gateway built from the change's product code at `acf841ca`. It passed 5/5 again after being routed through the real-Gateway serial project (`ui-e2e-serial-standalone`). The only later product change is the drain-time admission for `question.engage`, which these e2e cases do not exercise; a focused regression test covers it. Each case waits about 12 seconds past the original deadline.

| Case | Record after original deadline | Waiting `ask_user` result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Click, type, then blur | `pending` with `expiryStoppedAtMs` | `answered` `Teal` |
| Keyboard Tab into question, then choose an option | `pending` with `expiryStoppedAtMs` | `answered` `Green` |
| Programmatic focus, then real paste | `pending` with `expiryStoppedAtMs` | `answered` `Teal` |
| Type, wait, then Skip | `pending`, draft retained | `no_answer`; record `cancelled` |
| Untouched; hover and programmatic focus only | `expired` | `no_answer`; late `question.engage` rejected |

**CI note (corrected):** an earlier version of this body said ordinary PR CI would admit this e2e when the test changed. That was wrong. `scripts/ci-build-manifest.mjs` selects the `checks-ui-e2e-real-gateway` family on `pull_request` events only when the PR has the `ci:full` label (`OPENCLAW_CI_FULL`); main, manual and release validation run it otherwise. That is why the job shows as skipped. The local run above is the acceptance proof. A CI run needs `ci:full` added before the next PR run, or a maintainer-dispatched run; the managed publisher cannot apply labels. The file is registered in the real-Gateway, private-server and serial inventories, and the matching tooling expectations are updated. It stays release-only for automatic main selection because it takes about 4 minutes.

**Focused tests at head (all pass):**

- `src/gateway/question-manager.test.ts` covers:
  - stop after opt-in engagement, with the first stop time kept on later interaction;
  - no stop without opt-in or for secret questions;
  - no revival of expired or cancelled questions through late engagement;

prs.title: fix(acp): configured Claude binding goes offline when thinking is adaptive
prs.body:
<!-- template: .github/pull_request_template.md at upstream main 1fff14f6019 -->

Fixes #165731

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a configured ACP binding, such as Claude, is reported unavailable and its messages are dropped when the inherited thinking level (the default `adaptive`) is not one of the values the adapter accepts for `effort`.

## User Impact

User impact: operators who leave `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` at `adaptive` keep a working Claude ACP binding and get replies. The binding stays on the thinking level it already accepted. `/acp set thinking adaptive` still reports the adapter's rejection.

Risk: a configured thinking level that the adapter refuses by value is not applied to that binding. The refusal shows only in verbose logs, and the level is tried again on each readiness check with the same result. The bindings doc now says so.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reconciling an existing binding applies the configured thinking level through the live setter. The adapter answers `Invalid value for config option effort: adaptive` and the whole binding was reported unavailable. A refused thinking value now keeps the accepted level and the binding stays online. Unsupported-control errors and every other failure still fail the binding, and explicit commands are untouched. The pre-turn replay already tolerates this rejection since #113935, so it is not changed.

No new config option, no SDK or manager API change. The bindings doc is updated.

This builds on #166078, which found the reconcile path and the idea of keeping the accepted level while leaving explicit commands strict. This change keeps the tolerance inside binding reconciliation, so the plugin-facing manager setter gains no parameter, and adds proof through a real adapter.

## Evidence

Base 1fff14f6019, head e5caa63788d.

- Real adapter: isolated Gateway, real `claude-agent-acp` 0.99.1 on a Claude subscription login (no API key), `thinkingDefault: adaptive`. The adapter lists `default, low, medium, high, xhigh, max` for `effort` and answers `adaptive` with `Invalid value for config option effort: adaptive (ACP -32602)`.
  - Base: reconciling an existing binding (accepted level `high`) with the inherited `adaptive` returns `ok: false` with that error, so admission drops the message.
  - Head: the same reconcile returns `ok: true`, the binding keeps `high`, and the next message gets a reply.
  - A fresh `adaptive` binding replies on both base and head. The pre-turn replay already tolerates the rejection.
  - Not covered: no real channel plugin. The binding spec is built the way the compiler builds it. The lifecycle and manager are the shipped code.
- Tests: the new binding test fails on the base with `ok: false` and the issue's error text, and passes with the fix. Reverting only the lifecycle change turns it red again. A second case checks that an explicit `thinking` command still rejects `adaptive` and keeps the accepted level. 50 tests pass across the new file and its consumers (binding lifecycle, accepted controls, runtime config, persistent bindings, manager).
- Gates: `pnpm check:changed` passes at the head (ratchets, format, typecheck, dead-export scan, lint). `git diff --check` is clean.
- Local review: ClawSweeper `--local-range` (Claude runner on a Claude subscription login), base 1fff14f6019, head e5caa63788d, full committed range, complete and checkout access verified. Outcome: no findings, patch is correct, rating D (proof D, patch B) after 2 rounds. The proof tier is low because the local range review cannot see the real adapter run above. Round 1 at an earlier head had one P2 (a redundant pre-turn filter), which was removed. Remaining findings: none.

## Runtime output

Same harness on both commits: isolated Gateway, real `claude-agent-acp` 0.99.1 on a Claude subscription login (no API key), `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault: adaptive`. Session ids are redacted.

Base 1fff14f6019:

```
$ OPENCLAW_PROOF_ACP_ADAPTIVE=1 pnpm test:live -- src/gateway/acp-claude-adaptive-effort.proof.live.test.ts
[proof] config thinkingDefault=adaptive
[proof] ensure binding (accepted thinking high): {"ok":true,"sessionKey":"<binding-session>"}
[proof] adapter set_config_option effort=high -> accepted
[proof] reply 1: BINDING-OK-1
[proof] adapter effort option: current=high choices=default,low,medium,high,xhigh,max
[proof] adapter set_config_option effort=adaptive -> REJECTED Agent rejected session/set_config_option for "effort"="adaptive": Invalid params: Invalid value for config option effort: adaptive (ACP -32602).
[proof] ensure binding (inherited thinking adaptive): {"ok":false,"sessionKey":"<binding-session>","error":"Agent rejected session/set_config_option for \"effort\"=\"adaptive\": Invalid params: Invalid value for config option effort: adaptive (ACP -32602). | -32602"}
[proof] binding reported unavailable: configured-binding admission drops the message
```

Head e5caa63788d:

```
$ OPENCLAW_PROOF_ACP_ADAPTIVE=1 pnpm test:live -- src/gateway/acp-claude-adaptive-effort.proof.live.test.ts
[proof] config thinkingDefault=adaptive
[proof] ensure binding (accepted thinking high): {"ok":true,"sessionKey":"<binding-session>"}
[proof] adapter set_config_option effort=high -> accepted
[proof] reply 1: BINDING-OK-1
[proof] adapter effort option: current=high choices=default,low,medium,high,xhigh,max
[proof] adapter set_config_option effort=adaptive -> REJECTED Agent rejected session/set_config_option for "effort"="adaptive": Invalid params: Invalid value for config option effort: adaptive (ACP -32602).
[proof] ensure binding (inherited thinking adaptive): {"ok":true,"sessionKey":"<binding-session>"}
[proof] reply 2: BINDING-OK-2
```

The binding stays online and answers the next message. The new test asserts the accepted level stays `high`.

prs.title: fix(update): dev update replays one local-commit conflict across every candidate
prs.body:
Refs #199031

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a dev-channel update on a Git checkout with local commits replays the same failing local-commit rebase against every upstream candidate when one of those commits conflicts with upstream, then fails with only `preflight-no-good-commit` and no mention of the conflict or the conflicted files.

## User Impact

User impact: operators whose local commits conflict with upstream now get a `preflight-local-replay-conflict` failure that names the local commit and the conflicted paths, and the updater no longer replays candidates that would meet the same conflict. In the reported case (ten candidates, one conflict, about six minutes of repeated rebases) the walk-back is reduced to a single rebase whenever the conflicted files did not change across the candidate window.

The existing fallback is kept: an older candidate that predates the conflicting upstream change is still tried and can still be installed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- After a replay conflict, the updater records the unmerged paths. An older candidate is skipped only when Git resolves every conflicted path in both revisions and the object IDs are identical to the conflicted candidate's. Any candidate that differs at one of those paths is replayed as before.
- Conservative on renames, deletes and adds: if a conflicted path does not resolve in a candidate, that candidate is not skipped. Conflicts spanning more than 64 paths are not compared and are replayed as before.
- When every candidate that was tried was rejected by a replay conflict, the result reason is `preflight-local-replay-conflict` instead of `preflight-no-good-commit`. The failing `preflight-rebase` step carries failure facts with the local commit's short SHA and the conflicted paths. Mixed outcomes (a build failure, a runtime mismatch, a replay timeout) keep the existing reasons.
- The local replay block moved from `update-runner-git-preflight.ts` into a sibling module, `update-runner-git-replay.ts`, because the preflight file is at its line cap. The moved code is unchanged apart from collecting the conflicted paths before the rebase is aborted.

Known limit, stated plainly: the skip is a per-path content comparison. It assumes that identical content at the conflicted paths produces the same conflict. Git rename detection or directory-rename detection that depends on other files could in principle make an older candidate with identical content at those paths replay cleanly; such a candidate would now be skipped. This has not been observed, and the unresolved-path rule above covers the direct rename and delete cases.

Not in this PR: the issue's third ask (checking local-history replay before runtime retention) is left for a separate change, and the issue's cutoff question stays open, which is why this uses `Refs` and not a closing keyword.

Maintainer note: the issue carries `clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr` and `clawsweeper:needs-product-decision`. The maintainer chose this route (diagnostics plus a skip that preserves the walk-back) and asked for this PR despite that label.

## Evidence

- New real-Git regression tests in `src/infra/update-runner-git-replay.test.ts`:
  - identical conflicted content across ten candidates: one rebase, `preflight-local-replay-conflict`, failure facts naming the conflicted path, checkout and local `main` unchanged, no build;
  - an older candidate whose content differs at the conflicted path is still replayed (two rebases);
  - an older candidate that lacks the conflicted path is still replayed and the update succeeds on it with the local commit preserved.
- The existing `conflict` case in that file is unchanged.
- PR CI ran the full planned set once the PR was marked ready. `src/infra/update-runner-git-replay.test.ts` passed, including the three new cases and the unchanged `conflict` case, with lint and typecheck green.
- An independent read-only review of the first head found the moved block behaviourally equivalent and raised two points that are fixed in the second commit: command-runner errors while reading the paused rebase now reach the preflight owner instead of being swallowed, and an interrupted conflict probe stops the walk-back like an interrupted rebase does.
- Gaps: nothing was run locally (the task worktree had no installed dependencies), and no test injects an interrupted conflict probe or a rename-only divergence between candidates.
- The Git commands the change depends on (`git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U -z` during a paused rebase, multi-argument `git rev-parse <rev>:<path>` succeeding for identical paths and failing when a path is absent) were checked by hand in a throwaway repository.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Devices identifies a remote Gateway as “This computer” and promises automatic reconnection after rotating another device’s token without evidence that it reconnected.

## User Impact

User impact: people can identify which computer’s command policy they are viewing and understand what a cross-device token rotation confirms—and what may still require pairing again.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inventory’s Gateway row and the command-approval target always refer to the Gateway host, whether the browser is local or remote. Their label now identifies the computer running OpenClaw without changing the target.

A cross-device rotation commits the new token, invalidates the old token, and disconnects affected clients. Its reply deliberately withholds the credential from the requesting browser; it is not a reconnection receipt. The dialog now reports that the old token no longer works and explains why the new token is not shown here, while preserving the existing re-pairing instruction. It no longer promises that the token will be revealed on the other device.

This changes four English entries only. Permissions, credentials, token delivery, connection handling, command-approval policies, and layouts are unchanged. The current-device token reveal and acknowledgment remain intact. The admin-locked device hint is not changed.

## Evidence

Target changes issue the expected read requests and no approval-policy writes; rotation issues one mocked request and reveals no credential.

prs.title: fix(ui): config warning dismissal promises permanent silence
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the invalid-configuration warning promises “Don’t remind me again” even though dismissing it is temporary.

## User Impact

User impact: the button now says **Dismiss warning**, matching what it does. The warning can return after reloading or changing configuration context. Detailed validation issues stay visible.

No validation, persistence, permissions or configuration writes change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing view owns an ephemeral dismissal, not a saved reminder preference. Correcting its label is sufficient; adding persistence would unnecessarily hide future configuration warnings.

The change is one English string and one regression in the existing Config read suite. It checks dismissal, retained validation details, no save or field patch, and reset when the config context changes. No new state, helper or control is introduced.

## Evidence

- The new regression fails on the old label and passes after. 85 focused Config read/raw/navigation/route/write tests pass.
- Matched built-app flows open an invalid Logging snapshot, dismiss its warning, retain the detailed error, reload and see the warning again. They issue no configuration or preference writes. The data is synthetic; no live Gateway configuration was made invalid.
- Three additional built-app flows pass for failed-autosave recovery, schema/raw guarded writes, and rejected-save feedback/discard. These are fixture-backed flows, not live configuration changes.
- UI typecheck, scoped lint, i18n verification, formatting and diff checks pass. Broad CI is left to the PR.
- Screenshots use real components at an emulated 1280 × 960 viewport, with same-frame crops and inspected surrounding context. Baseline main: `387042f830d0586ee6c8484d95db648521c3e78b`.

prs.title: fix(memory): start default index managers at Gateway boot
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#194164 asks for memory indexing to be fresh right after a Gateway restart:
with the current demand-driven cold start, an agent's index opens on its
first search, flush, or turn, and until then `memory_index_sources`
receives nothing — the reporter observed roughly ten hours of stopped
indexing after an app relaunch.

The original draft of this PR restored eager boot-time indexing for every
configured agent. Review and history showed why that is the wrong default:
#167756 started Memory Core's index service eagerly on every Gateway start,
and #174718 (`6c050f8043`) deliberately reverted it after startup peak RSS
rose from ~1.1 GB to ~1.8 GB (startup catch-up touches every
session-transcript read lane, each spawning its own worker isolate). This
revision keeps that policy intact and adds an explicit operator opt-in
instead:

```jsonc
// memory.search.coldStart
"demand" // default — exactly today's behavior, unchanged
"eager"  // open every configured agent's index at boot and on later service starts
```

Each agent can override the global default with
`agents.entries.<id>.memory.search.coldStart`; the per-agent value wins over
the global setting in both directions, matching how the memory config
resolver treats other `memory.search` fields. Operators who need fresh
indexes immediately (the reporter's local-GGUF fleet) pay a known,
self-inflicted cost; everyone else sees zero change. The demand default, the
`liveIndexing` retention semantics, and the worker/RSS characteristics of
#174718 are untouched.

## The Change

- `memory.search.coldStart` (`"demand"` default | `"eager"`), registered in
  the config schema, field labels/help, and `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`.
- `memory-core-index` service start resolves the opt-in per agent:
  `resolveAgentConfig(cfg, agentId)?.memory?.search?.coldStart ?? global`.
  `"demand"` (effective) keeps `retainMemoryIndexingAgents` exactly as
  before; `"eager"` opens the agent's index through the existing host-aware
  runtime (`memoryRuntime.getMemorySearchManager`, which supplies the host's
  local-service acquisition — resolving the Revision 1 P2 finding). Manager
  construction marks each agent live, so later reloads retain them like any
  watched index.
- Boundary tests on untouched agents (so acquisition cannot be explained by
  prior demand): a per-agent eager override under a global demand default
  opens only that agent; a per-agent demand override under a global eager
  default keeps that agent lazy. Both fail against the previous
  global-only selector.

## Evidence

- **Unit/boundary tests** (worktree, committed source): `extensions/memory-core/index.test.ts` — 35 passed (2 new per-agent cold-start boundary cases; the previous single eager case was rewritten on untouched agents per review), and `src/config` schema regressions (config.schema-regressions, dead-config-keys, schema.hints) — 263 passed after registering the new field.
- **Regression check:** the two new boundary cases fail on the previous
  global-only selector (2 failed | 33 skipped) and pass with the per-agent
  resolution (35 passed).
- **Live redacted output, built from the committed source** (isolated
  state/workspace, local Ollama `nomic-embed-text`, synthetic data; the same
  state is upgraded in place between scenarios):

  ```text
  ===== SCENARIO 1: coldStart demand (default) =====
  gateway ready (demand)
  # memory file written + chat.send delivered, 45s watcher window, no consumer opens an index
  demand: memory_index_sources rows = 0

  ===== SCENARIO 2: upgrade in place -> coldStart eager =====
  gateway ready (eager)
  # same state, settings and sessions intact, 45s after boot, no consumer call
  eager: memory_index_sources rows = 2
      memory|memory/proof-demand-note.md
      sessions|sessions/main/34d590f2-28ad-4c95-91df-bda672a78c92.jsonl
  eager: memory_search -> {"ok":true,"results":[{"path":"memory/proof-demand-note.md",...
  ```

  Scenario 1 confirms the demand default is byte-for-byte unchanged
  (untouched agents stay lazy). Scenario 2 is the reporter's requested
  behavior, available under the explicit opt-in.

- **Latest-stable → candidate upgrade trace (redacted live output):** a
  dedicated run upgrades a state directory created by released
  **v2026.11.3** (npm, `847611d`) to the candidate built from this PR's
  head, covering both the upgrade-compatibility and data-model items:

  ```text
  ## PHASE S — stable v2026.11.3 (847611d), config without any coldStart key
  [stable] consumer memory_search -> {"ok":true,...}   # demand: index opens on first consumer
  [stable-final] memory_index_sources rows: 2          # memory/upgrade-note-a.md
  [stable-final] memory_index_chunks rows: 2           # + sessions/main/ff028686-….jsonl

  ## PHASE C-MIG — candidate refuses unmigrated DB (documented admission guard), then migrates
  "…uses schema version 27; … run openclaw doctor --fix to upgrade it to
   schema version 42 …" | gateway.maintenance_required
  $ openclaw doctor --fix --yes    ->  schema_meta primary = 42
  [post-migration] memory_index_sources: 2  memory_index_chunks: 2   # data survived

  ## PHASE C-A — candidate on migrated stable state, config UNCHANGED (demand default)
  booted healthy; memory_search retrieves the stable-era note
  [candA-final] memory_index_sources: 2                 # demand unchanged: no boot-time growth

  ## PHASE C-B — only delta: memory.search.coldStart = "eager"
  # new file written, then boot with NO consumer call
  [candB] rows BEFORE boot: sources=2 chunks=2
  [candB] rows AFTER eager boot: sources=3 chunks=3     # note B indexed at startup
      memory|memory/upgrade-note-a.md                    # stable-era data intact
      memory|memory/upgrade-note-b.md                    # newly indexed at boot
      sessions|sessions/main/ff028686-….jsonl            # stable-era session intact
  consumer memory_search("Post-upgrade synthetic") -> upgrade-note-b.md
  ```

  Existing settings are preserved (the stable-era config carries no
  `coldStart` key; the candidate boots it unchanged under the demand
  default), the stable-written database migrates via the documented
  `doctor --fix` path and loads/works (schema 27 → 42, index rows,
  session transcript, and provenance intact), demand semantics are
  unchanged after upgrade (no growth without a consumer), and the opt-in
  eager mode works on the upgraded state.

  Data-model note: this change adds an optional config field only — no
  stored index, session, or state format changes; the trace above
  demonstrates the stable-release upgrade end to end.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Teams tests duplicated parts of the inbound runner and attachment policy, while the test isolation guard treated SQLite file URIs as literal paths.

## User Impact

No user-visible production change. This strengthens internal tests and private test support; production LOC delta is zero. The test-line ratchet remains unresolved, so this is not ready to land.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixtures now use the real public inbound runner and isolated session persistence, with dispatch injected at its existing per-turn boundary. Cleanup joins session work and canonical SQLite cleanup before deleting owned roots, while explicit runtime-config reload snapshots remain intact.

Attachment checks assert ordered saved results and adapter forwarding without duplicating media policy or replacing the existing real SharePoint storage path. The SQLite guard checks NUL before canonical decoding and retains physical containment and original opener arguments. Superseded suites and the retired SQLite coordinator remain removed.

The correction is integrated on frozen base 91d08c31d14cd85be17e5ecb4d8a0ec075ef53bb. Final head is f7a21e31e0976f3ea1de083cede24f7965fd8200: 15 test/private-support source files, +500/-197 lines, plus the exact test-line allocation.

## Evidence

- **Behavioral proof:** e9275a6e52c55af0a1c3e08209ffefe65e3fca2b passed 181/181 cases across 16 modules with native --maxWorkers=1, zero filtered cases or unhandled/module errors. Both test invocations and the separate report merge completed, with all native process groups joined.
- **Unchanged guard proof:** f57774c403f83279ce2e4bbc52d26ca1f1d3f1ad passed 11/11 URI/containment cases. This earlier receipt is reused; those cases were not rerun on D or E.
- **Final static checks:** E passed repaired-path Oxlint and the full plugin-test type lane. Passing D core lint/core types/core-test types/plugin production types are retained for unchanged applicable source. E changes only truthful core-managed generic typing, Promise collection typing/equivalent iterable use, braces and a dead initializer; the 181-case run remains D evidence.
- **Final source review:** one complete review of E and its whole owner/caller context found no actionable findings. This was source-only, not another runtime or CI run.
- **Environment:** Darwin arm64, pinned Bun 1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1, Node 26.12.1 launcher. The remote backend stopped before receiver/tests; normal trusted-source local fallback supplied these results. No Linux, native Windows or live Teams proof is claimed.

<details>

These are original native report start/end intervals, not a baseline comparison or speed claim. The complete D command took 43.368s including native preparation/reporting.

The retained C src/test-utils/state-path-guard.test.ts result was 11 cases in 0.026s. The Windows-shaped filename case verifies producer/decoder assertions on this host, not Windows execution. CI seconds will be recorded when a qualifying current-head run exists.

</details>

**Budget and remaining gates:** the actual pre-grant counter ran on staged candidate source before C was signed: 6,442,408 lines against 6,441,800, +253 counted test lines, exit 1. Final E has +289 counted lines and the exact 289 allowance; the shared scalar baseline is unchanged. Frozen-input arithmetic gives 6,442,444 against a credited 6,442,089, leaving 355 over. prs.title: fix: crashed SQLite store worker leaves no reason in logs or metrics
prs.body:
<!--
Optional linked context:
Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Required PR title:
type: user-facing description
Use a parenthesized scope only when it adds clarity:
fix(auth): login redirect loops when session cookie is expired

Types: feat, fix, improve, refactor, docs, chore.
For fixes, describe the user-visible symptom and trigger:
fix: task list fails to load when user has no environments
Avoid implementation details such as:
fix: add null check to task query

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.
-->

Closes #163150

## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.
Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause.
-->

Fixes: when a SQLite store worker thread disappears, the worker lifecycle counters call it an
unattributed `exit` and the Gateway log says nothing, so an operator cannot tell a crash from a
retirement the broker asked for.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

User impact: a retirement the broker requested now shows its own reason (`closed`, or `failure`
when the slot had already failed) in the stability bundle's `workerLifecycle`, and a worker that
leaves without any request writes exactly one warning line naming its cause to the log file, so a
lost storage worker is diagnosable from the bundle and the log instead of only from a repro.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

The lifecycle registry takes the retirement reason from whatever the worker's owner recorded
before native exit; without that record it falls back to `exit`, which
`docs/gateway/prometheus.md` already defines as "an owner did not specify a reason". The task-pool
owners do record it, the SQLite store worker owner never did, so every one of its retirements
landed in the fallback. Reasons are now recorded where this owner asks the worker to leave, and on
the `error`/`messageerror` events that precede native exit. A departure that no one requested has
no other witness, so it is logged once at warn; requested retirements stay silent because their
caller already reports the outcome. Nothing in the broker's failure path changed, and the log line
carries only the redacted error text.

## Evidence

<!--
Show the most useful proof that this change works. Screenshots, screencasts,
terminal output, focused tests, CI results, live observations, redacted logs,
and artifact links are all useful. For user-visible UI changes, follow the root
AGENTS.md "Product and validation" screenshot completion/landing gate; these other
forms of evidence do not replace the required screenshots in chat AND the PR.

Reviewers will inspect the code, tests, and CI. Use this section to make the
validation easy to understand, not to restate the diff.
Summarize what was checked and the result; note meaningful gaps. Link long output
or put it in optional <details>, keeping the useful evidence summary visible.
-->

Failing test first, then the fix, on `src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts`:

```
 FAIL  src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts > SQLite worker slots > attributes a broker-requested retirement instead of an unattributed exit
AssertionError: expected +0 to be 1
    207|       await lifecycle.retire(slot);
  >  209|       expect(retirementCount("closed")).toBe(closedBefore + 1);

 FAIL  src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts > SQLite worker slots > reports a worker that leaves on its own once, naming its cause
AssertionError: expected +0 to be 1
  >  253|     expect(retirementCount("failure")).toBe(failureBefore + 1);
```

After the change the same two tests pass, and they check both halves of the symptom against the
real registry and the real log-file transport: a retirement the owner asked for adds a `closed`
count and leaves `exit` unchanged, and a worker that throws on its own adds a `failure` count while
the log file holds one `left without a retirement request` line containing the cause text.

```
 TEST  src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts
 ... > attributes a broker-requested retirement instead of an unattributed exit 87ms
 ... > reports a worker that leaves on its own once, naming its cause 178ms
```

Adjacent lanes, run locally with the same config:

```
 src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker.test.ts   Tests 10 passed, Duration 42.94s
 src/infra/worker-cpu.test.ts             Tests 7 passed with sqlite-worker-logging.test.ts,
                                          Duration 20.95s
```

Local gates: `oxfmt --check` clean on both files (28ms), `run-oxlint.mjs` on the core tsconfig
reported "Found 0 warnings and 0 errors" (68.1s), `git diff --check` clean, and
`check-line-cap-ratchet.mts` reported "Line-cap ratchet OK: 2 changed source files; no new
violations or over-cap growth". `check-changed.mjs --dry-run` listed the CI gates this diff
selects. Pre-commit hooks ran normally; no hook was skipped.

Cost of the new tests, per the repo validation rules: they add 87ms and 178ms inside a file whose
targeted run takes 26s with a warm transform cache and 212s cold on this machine. Neither test
sleeps, polls, or uses a wall-clock timer; they await the worker `online` event, the slot's own
exit promise, and `flushLogger()`.

Gaps worth naming: the run was Windows, where the six pre-existing cases in this test file already
fail at `fileURLToPath("file:///openclaw/...")` with `ERR_INVALID_FILE_URL_PATH` before this
change and in code this diff does not touch, so those cases are covered here by CI's Linux infra
lane; the two new tests derive their carrier URL from `import.meta.url` so they run on both
platforms. `pnpm tsgo:core` refuses a worktree that shares its install with the main checkout
("Declaration input escapes checkout"), so the typecheck gate was not run locally and is left to
CI. No live Gateway was started on this machine; the log-line half is proven by reading the file
the file transport actually wrote.

CI on head `e129273e8` (server-recorded base `dbb580aed`, which is 171 commits behind current `main`): 129 check runs = 67 success / 59 skipped / 1 neutral (CodeQL) / 2 failure. The two failures are `checks-windows-node-test-5` (completed 2026-10-02T08:19:37Z) and the 2 s aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` that follows it in the same run. The failing case is `test/scripts/write-unified-entry-dts.test.ts > write-unified-entry-dts > reuses unaffected canonical groups while rebuilding runtime after input edits`, and it throws `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED: Package subpath './record-coerce' is not defined by "exports"` from a `package.json` inside that test's own temporary fixture project (`%TEMP%\oc-vt-8AAiWh\openclaw-sdk-declarations-5DFbNf\Project\node_modules\@openclaw\normalization-core`), imported from `src/process/exec-result.ts` in the same temp tree. This diff is two files, both `src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.*`: it touches none of `test/scripts/`, `packages/normalization-core/`, or `src/process/`, and `packages/normalization-core/package.json` on this head does export `./record-coerce`.

What is deliberately not claimed here: inheritance is not proven. That node-id was re-run in a clean detached worktree checked out at this PR's base commit `dbb580aed`, and it fails there too - but with a different, Windows-only error while the fixture links its compiler (`EPERM: operation not permitted, symlink '..\typescript\bin\tsc' -> '...\Project\node_modules\.bin\tsgo'`), so this machine's harness cannot exercise that fixture path and no local verdict about the CI error is available. For reference, the same `checks-windows-node-test-5` check completed with `success` at 2026-10-02T15:23:03Z on unrelated head `5ce2d2d6` (#163594). No rerun, re-push, or rebase was dispatched to chase a green signal, per the repository's validation rules; naming this failure is offered so a maintainer can weigh it against the two lanes this change actually touches.
