prs.title: fix(agents): refresh provider catalogs only for the published owners
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves Fixes #194911. A scoped config publication (one agent's `agents.entries.` changed) and an auth-triggered publication rebuild only the affected agents. Both still end with `refreshCommittedProviderCatalogs(owners.values())`. That walks **every** configured owner on the Gateway and starts `loadFullModelCatalog({ changedOnly: true })` on each, which opens every agent database. On the reporter's ~470-agent Gateways, one agent's config change produced 132 slow agent-database opens, 155 main-thread stalls of up to 4.5 s, and 30–60 minute stalls of unrelated agents' turns. ## User Impact Adding, removing or editing one agent, or changing one agent's credentials, now refreshes only that agent's provider catalog. Unrelated agents on a large Gateway keep answering. ## Why This Change Was Made `refreshCommittedProviderCatalogs` now takes the publication's agent scope and skips owners outside it, using the existing `isPreparedModelRuntimeOwnerInRefreshScope` rule: - **Config publication:** passes `publicationAgentIds`, the same scope `refreshPreparedModelRuntimeSnapshotsNow` rebuilt. A full publication passes `undefined` and still refreshes every owner, so cold starts and full reloads keep all-owner discovery. - **Auth publication:** an auth transaction coalesces later credential mutations and queues only its first publisher, so the transaction now accumulates `rebuiltAgentIds` across every coalesced mutation. The auth publication refreshes that whole set, not just the first mutation's agents. - **Adopted auth during a scoped config publication:** when the config replacement adopted an auth transaction (for example, `a4`'s credentials changed while `a3` was reloading), the commit refreshes `publicationAgentIds ∪ adoptedAuthTransaction.rebuiltAgentIds`, so the adopted owner still gets its account-model refresh. - Standalone, read-only and non-configured owners keep their existing handling. ## Evidence **Regression test.** `refreshes only the published owners of a scoped publication (#194911)` in `src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.refresh-scope.test.ts`: - With the scope `{changed}`, only `changed` starts `loadFullModelCatalog({ changedOnly: true })`. - Without a scope (a full publication), the unrelated owner refreshes too. | Rev | Result | | --- | --- | | `main` | ❌ `expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times` (the unrelated owner refreshed) | | this PR | ✅ 3/3 | `accumulates the agents rebuilt by coalesced auth mutations (#194911)` in `src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.auth-recovery.test.ts` shows that a second mutation joins the queued transaction, `claimPublication` returns `false` for it, and `rebuiltAgentIds` is `["a3","a4"]`. Without the transaction change it fails with `TypeError: first.rebuiltAgentIds is not iterable`. In total, `refresh-scope`, `auth-recovery` and `scoped-refresh` pass 41/41. **Live Gateway run.** Windows 11, Node v26.12.1. Setup: - Source Gateway on loopback, with isolated state. - 9 configured agents: `main` and `a1`..`a8`, created with `openclaw agents add`. - A stub model. Each agent's owner is published at startup. - Then `config set agents.entries.a3.model "stub/n"`, which logs `[reload] config hot reload applied (agents.entries.a3.model)`. - A local-only diagnostic, identical in both builds, records every `loadFullModelCatalog({ changedOnly: true })` started by `refreshCommittedProviderCatalogs`. | Phase | `main` c61a7c0 | this PR 3de58ec | | --- | --- | --- | | startup publication (full) | main, a1..a8 (9) | main, a1..a8 (9). A full publication still refreshes every owner | | after changing only `a3` (scoped) | ❌ main, a1..a8: **9 agents** | ✅ **a3 only** | On the reporter's ~470-agent Gateway, the same fan-out means each single-agent change opened every agent database. With this change, only the changed agent's catalog is refreshed. **Gates:** - `oxfmt` and `oxlint` on the changed files: clean. - `check:line-cap-ratchet`: OK. - `check:test-lines-ratchet`: OK with `config/test-lines-allocations/194911-scoped-catalog-refresh.txt`. The allocation is 35 lines, justified there and capped at the allowed growth.

prs.title: feat(agents): make Tool Search control result character limit configurable
prs.body:
## Summary
- Adds `tools.toolSearch.maxResultChars` (`number | "auto"`) to configure the pre-wrapper character budget for network-sourced Tool Search control results (`renderToolSearchControlText` in `src/agents/tool-search-control-result.ts`).
- Preserves the existing `20,000`-character default (`19,988` characters + `\n[truncated]`) when `tools.toolSearch.maxResultChars` is unset.
- Supports `"auto"` to scale with the active model's live tool-result cap (`resolveLiveToolResultMaxChars`) minus the external-content wrapper overhead, and clamps explicit numeric limits at or under the active model's live tool-result budget so wrapped results are never cut mid-marker by the outer tool-result guard.
- Consciously raises the `core` config baseline count budget in `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` by +1 (`2638` -> `2639`) and updates `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` for the new `tools.toolSearch.maxResultChars` setting requested in #194857.

## What Problem This Solves
Network-sourced Tool Search (`dispatch_action` / `call_tool` and Code Mode) control results were hardcoded to truncate at `20,000` characters (`19,988` characters + `\n[truncated]`) in `renderToolSearchControlText` (`src/agents/tool-search-control-result.ts`) before `wrapExternalContent`, even when the active model's context window and live tool-result budget (`resolveLiveToolResultMaxChars`) could safely accommodate larger structured responses (#194857). Operators and high-context agents had no configuration knob to raise or auto-scale that pre-wrapper character limit while preserving the `<<<END_EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT ...>>>` boundary against outer truncation.

## Evidence
- Verified schema, config resolution, and runtime truncation behavior with Vitest unit tests in:
  - `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/worker-gateway-tool.test.ts` (validates `maxResultChars: "auto"` and positive integers in `AgentToolSurfacePresentationSchema.properties.toolSearch`, rejecting `0`, negative, non-integer, and unknown string values).
  - `src/agents/tool-search-config.test.ts` (verifies `resolveToolSearchConfig` omits `maxResultChars` when unset and retains `"auto"` or positive integer values).
  - `src/agents/tool-search-runtime.test.ts` (`scales network control output with maxResultChars='auto' or clamps a fixed limit to the live budget`: verifies a `30,000`-char network payload is preserved un-truncated under `maxResultChars: "auto"` with a `200,000`-token context window, and that `maxResultChars: 50_000` on a `32,000`-token context window is clamped prior to wrapping so `<<<END_EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT id="...">>>` remains intact).
- Verified `pnpm config:docs:gen` baseline artifacts (`docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` and `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json`).

Fixes #194857

prs.title: fix: show multi-question reply format
prs.body:
Closes #173760

AI-assisted. Substantially follows the shared-guidance and regression shape from #173845 by @D41910; the commit credits Winoren as co-author.

## Summary

- Show one bounded, copyable multiline example in the initial multi-question prompt and invalid-answer recovery notice.
- Document the same accepted reply format.
- Derive the regression's successful reply from the displayed example so guidance and parser behavior cannot drift.

## Issue

Closes #173760.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: messaging-channel users can be told to answer every `ask_user` question by number or id without being shown that each answer needs its own keyed line.

## User Impact

User impact: after an incomplete grouped answer is rejected, the user sees a concrete two-line reply template and can fill it in while the same question remains open.

## Root cause

The multi-question parser already accepts one keyed answer per line, but the shared prompt owner and rejection notice exposed only abstract wording. A normal one-line prose reply fills question 1 and leaves later required questions empty, so the recovery path repeated guidance that did not demonstrate the required shape.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared prompt guidance is the canonical owner for this format. Reusing one bounded constant in the initial prompt and rejection notice fixes both user-visible paths without changing parsing, validation, authorization, custody, or question lifecycle. #190513 remains complementary parser/numbering work; #193400 remains complementary correction-delivery work.

## Verification

- Exact upstream base: `c61a7c0cf6b72f9c35ad8acdc432e132f4d86a50`; the five touched files were unchanged from the reproduced `95363ce54afd893d89cc6bd6645578dba52888d0` snapshot.
- Before source oracle: exit 1. A one-line two-question answer populated `where`, left `game` empty, and found no copyable example in prompt, rejection, or docs.
- After the same oracle: exit 0. It extracted `1: <answer for question 1>\n2: <answer for question 2>`, filled it as `1: Lisbon\n2: 2000`, and mapped both keyed answers while confirming the rejection notice and docs use the same format.
- `node --experimental-strip-types --check` passed for all four touched TypeScript files.
- `node scripts/docs-list.js` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Production delta: `+6/-2` (net +4); tests `+13/-6`; docs `+10/-3`.

## Before/after

Before:

```json
{"answers":{"where":"either is fine, and lets do X","game":""},"hasExample":false,"docsExplain":false,"reproduced":true}
```

After:

```json
{"example":"1: <answer for question 1>\n2: <answer for question 2>","completeAnswer":"1: Lisbon\n2: 2000","answers":{"destination":"Lisbon","budget":"2000"},"correctionUsesShared":true,"docsExplain":true,"fixed":true}
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Multi-question text prompts and invalid-answer recovery now show the keyed multiline reply shape the existing parser accepts.
- **Real environment tested:** Exact current OpenClaw source snapshot on macOS with Node 22.22.3; source-level behavior oracle plus syntax/docs/diff checks.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Node source oracle reading the production prompt, rejection, parser contract, and docs; `node --experimental-strip-types --check` on the four TypeScript files; `node scripts/docs-list.js`; `git diff --check`.
- **Evidence after fix:** The oracle derived `1: Lisbon\n2: 2000` from the displayed example, resolved both keyed answers, confirmed both runtime messages share the guidance, and exited 0.
- **Observed result after fix:** The user-visible recovery text now contains a copyable answer that satisfies both questions without changing parser or lifecycle semantics.
- **What was not tested:** No live Telegram account, deployed Gateway, external model/API, or focused Vitest run.

## Risk and scope

Low. This changes shared bounded guidance, one recovery string, one documentation paragraph, and assertions around the existing custody flow. No config, schema, protocol, persistence, parser, validation, authorization, or delivery lifecycle changes.

## Not tested

Focused Vitest did not start. Blacksmith Testbox failed before allocation because the local `blacksmith` executable is unavailable. Local dependency installation failed first because the configured npm mirror lacks `@pnpm/macos-arm64@12.15.0`, then because Corepack's pnpm 12.15.0 cache was incomplete. The repository formatter and autoreview also could not bootstrap through the same blocked network path; no passing claim is made for them.

prs.title: fix(gateway): show claude-cli narration only once in replies that send images
prs.body:
Closes #195857

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Control UI repeats claude-cli progress narration at the top of a reply that sends images with `MEDIA:` lines. It happens again on main after #188333, most visibly when `messages.responseUsage` adds a usage footer.

## User Impact

User impact: an image reply shows the narration once, under Worked, and the bubble shows only the final caption, the usage footer and the images.

## Why This Change Was Made

#188333 drops the delivered text block when it ends with the native final caption. The delivered block still held the raw `MEDIA:` lines and the appended usage footer, so the suffix match never fired and the narration was kept.

Both sides of the comparison now go through one caption normalizer. It strips `MEDIA:` directives with the existing parser, which leaves fenced examples alone. It also strips one trailing copy of this payload's exact `responseUsageLine`, on the delivered side only. When a matched block carried the footer, the footer is added back to the rebuilt caption. Without a footer the rule is the same as before.

## Evidence

Test-budget follow-up: consolidated all six caption regressions into one 40-line table-driven file (down from 66 lines), with unchanged exact display-content assertions. The cases cover image cardinality, optional delivery usage, fenced MEDIA examples, and authored footer text; these distinct contracts cannot fit within the base tree's five-line slack. The scoped `config/test-lines-allocations/195857-native-media-captions.txt` allocates those 40 retained lines; the shared scalar is unchanged. Local budget check passes with five lines of slack. All six tests pass (17.41 s wall time, including module loading); scoped lint and diff checks pass.

Focused regression tests in `chat-transcript-persistence.native-media.test.ts`, 6 passed:
- 1 and 4 images, footer on and off: the display content is exactly `Answer ready.`, the footer when enabled, then every image. The narration and raw `MEDIA:` lines are gone.
- A fenced `MEDIA:` example in the caption stays in the visible text.
- An authored final line identical to the usage footer is kept, and the delivered footer is still shown.

Live, on two test Gateways (claude-cli, Opus, `messages.responseUsage=full`). Each sent one turn with two exec progress steps, then a final caption with 1 or 4 `MEDIA:` images. History was reloaded and Worked expanded before capture.

prs.title: fix(ui): notification test hides its Gateway-wide audience
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Settings’ browser notification test does not disclose that it sends to every registered browser on the Gateway, including other people’s browsers.

## User Impact

User impact: the existing action now says **Test all browsers**, with a nearby explanation of its audience before it is clicked. Native macOS **Send test** remains a local test.

This changes presentation only. It does not broaden delivery, change permissions or subscription ownership, send a real notification, or add a confirmation step.

## Why This Change Was Made

The documented browser test deliberately broadcasts to registered subscriptions; ordinary approval and attention notifications have narrower recipient checks. The existing status row now explains that distinction instead of letting its personal/device settings context suggest a local-only test.

The native label is preserved, browser-specific test expectations are updated, and the English notification guide names the actual control. #199223’s notification-agent picker is separate and is not duplicated. No new component, state or delivery policy is added.

## Evidence

- The existing rejected-command regression fails before because the audience explanation is absent. All 52 focused notification UI/owner tests pass after the correction, including recovery, permission and VAPID mismatch behavior, native feedback, and navigation during an admitted request.
- Four selected backend checks pass: broadcasting to registered subscriptions and the browser-test handler’s success, failure and empty-recipient outcomes. These are transport fixtures, not live browser-vendor push delivery.
- Complete built-app flows pass at 1360 and 390 pixels: open Notifications, see the audience, issue exactly one unchanged test request, hold its response, and recover the enabled control. No preference or unsubscribe write is issued. Browser subscription APIs and Gateway responses are synthetic; no real notification is sent.
- UI typecheck, scoped lint, i18n verification, formatting, the configured documentation lint and diff checks pass. No broad CI or E2E matrix was run.
- Baseline main: `a64758be048909c5c59ef781d5b4f34aaefc34af`. Matched light-theme screenshots use emulated viewports, real production components and same-frame crops. The full page and mobile wrapping were inspected. Simplification leaves one existing presentation owner, two English strings, and maintained tests/documentation.

### Before

![Before: the browser-wide action is labeled only Send test](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4ed82834-1d5a-464f-ac8c-e1b39aa59ff1)

### After

![After: Test all browsers explains that other people on the Gateway are included](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ad0c5ed5-e8ab-4aef-b92d-d8a786323506)

Contributor: @vyctorbrzezowski directed the comprehensive wording and interaction audit.

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

prs.title: fix(doctor): surface pairing store read failures in allowlist repair
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw doctor --fix` silently swallowed pairing-store read failures in `maybeRepairAllowlistPolicyAllowFrom`: `.catch(() => [])` made a failed read look like "no entries", so allowlist recovery was skipped with no operator-visible diagnostic.

The earlier revision reported that diagnostic through `changes`. That is wrong: `applyMutation` treats non-empty `changes` as a candidate-config mutation, requests a config write, and queues the message as a config-change panel even though no allowlist entry was restored.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runDoctorRepairSequence` already consumes a separate `warnings` channel (`appendNotes(warningNotes, mutation.warnings)`) and renders it as an independent "Doctor warnings" panel. The repair now returns an optional `warnings` array, keeps `changes` empty unless senders were really restored, and leaves the healthy return shape unchanged. No new type, export, schema field, or runtime mechanism is added.

The message states the outcome and the next action: recovery was skipped, retry `openclaw doctor --fix`, then run `openclaw doctor` to repair the state database. Error text goes through `formatErrorMessage` instead of raw `String(err)`.

## User Impact

Operators see the failure under `Doctor warnings` even when no config is written, and get a retry/recovery path. Doctor no longer queues a phantom config change. Healthy reads behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

### Upgrade run: released v2026.11.3 state and config, then candidate

State directory and `openclaw.json` were produced by the shipped v2026.11.3 CLI in an isolated `HOME`, then two pairing rows were inserted into the released-version `channel_pairing_allow_entries` table (the same row shape the app writes). The candidate head loaded that same state and ran the shipped CLI:

```console
released arm:  openclaw --version  ->  OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (847611d)
state schema:  user_version 22 (released)  ->  40 (candidate)
$ node --import tsx src/entry.ts doctor --fix --non-interactive
◇  Doctor changes
│  - channels.signal.allowFrom: restored 1 sender entry from pairing    │
│    store (dmPolicy="allowlist").
```

Config diff before -> after (senders redacted):

```console
channels.signal.allowFrom      : []     -> ["+86***1111"]
channels.signal.groupAllowFrom : absent -> ["+86***1111"]
meta.migrations.*, wizard.lastRun*: version bookkeeping only
```

Every other setting (agents, plugins, channel options) is unchanged, and the schema-22 to schema-40 migration preserved both pairing rows. A control arm built with the same released-version steps restores the same sender with exit 0, so the healthy path is unchanged. On the candidate the process exits 1 later at `plugin-doctor-post-session-state` with `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED` (`unicorn-magic`) from this host's pnpm layout; the allowlist repair completes before that step.

### Failure path

prs.title: fix(templates): honor the workspace bootstrap byte limit when building packages
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`templates validate` accepts a `BOOTSTRAP.md` that `templates build` later rejects. The reader (`src/templates/reader.ts`) snapshots a package-root `BOOTSTRAP.md` with the workspace bootstrap byte limit (`MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES` = 2 MiB), but the builder (`src/templates/project-build.ts`) reads the same file back through `readSelectedProjectFile` with the generic managed-file limit (`MAX_MANAGED_FILE_BYTES` = 1 MiB). A `BOOTSTRAP.md` between 1 MiB and 2 MiB passes `templates validate` (issue #198559 reproduces with a 1,680,008-byte file) and then fails `templates build` with `file exceeds limit of 1048576 bytes`.

## Solution

Make `readSelectedProjectFile` use `MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES` (2 MiB) for `BOOTSTRAP.md`, matching the reader's limit for the same file, while all other managed files keep `MAX_MANAGED_FILE_BYTES` (1 MiB). This keeps validate and build consistent for the entire accepted range.

## Evidence

### Regression test (RED → GREEN)

New test `builds a package bootstrap between the managed-file and workspace-bootstrap byte limits` in `src/templates/project.test.ts`: writes a 1,680,008-byte `BOOTSTRAP.md` (between the two limits), asserts it passes `validateTemplateProject`, then `buildTemplateProject` packages it and the extracted artifact contains the full contents.

- **RED**: before the fix the new test fails with `FsSafeError: file exceeds limit of 1048576 bytes (got 1680014)` at `project-build.ts:23` → `buildTemplateProject` at `:116`.
- **GREEN**: after the fix all 55 tests pass (3 files: `project.test.ts`, `project.bundled.test.ts`, `reader.test.ts`) plus 7 CLI tests in `templates-cli.project.test.ts`.

### Real CLI execution (post-fix, head `3876a79aecb`)

A demo Template project with a **1,680,020-byte `BOOTSTRAP.md`** (between 1 MiB and 2 MiB) at `/home/0668000622/.run-cache/198559-demo/project` (package `bootstrap-demo@1.0.0`, `CLAW.md` schemaVersion 1, `workspace.files: references/guide.md`):

**`templates validate`** (exit 0):
```
Valid Template project: /home/0668000622/.run-cache/198559-demo/project
Package: bootstrap-demo@1.0.0
```

**`templates build --out template.tgz`** (exit 0):
```
Built Template: bootstrap-demo@1.0.0
Artifact: /home/0668000622/.run-cache/198559-demo/template.tgz
Integrity: sha256:06644f3fc061c794c86a2aa35314825b72b6a8e971c2a521e2cadc464e704f4e
Excluded project paths: 0
```

**Artifact inspection** — the tar contains `package/BOOTSTRAP.md` and it is byte-for-byte identical to the source (1,680,020 bytes, `cmp` IDENTICAL, content preserved from `# Bootstrap` header through the trailing `Done.`):

```
$ tar -tzf template.tgz
package/BOOTSTRAP.md
package/CLAW.md
package/package.json
package/references/guide.md
$ cmp extract/package/BOOTSTRAP.md project/BOOTSTRAP.md && echo IDENTICAL
IDENTICAL
```

**`templates dev --json`** (exit 0, offline preview of the built artifact):
```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "openclaw.templateDev.v1",
  "offline": true,
  "mutationAllowed": false,
  "build": {
    "integrity": "sha256:06644f3fc061c794c86a2aa35314825b72b6a8e971c2a521e2cadc464e704f4e",
    "byteLength": 2129,
    "files": ["BOOTSTRAP.md", "CLAW.md", "package.json", "references/guide.md"]
  },
  "plan": { "readiness": { "ready": true }, "blockers": [], "diagnostics": [] }
}
```

The demo files contain no credentials or non-public endpoints (only this repo's own paths); the bootstrap payload is synthetic padding.

The scenario passes before and after; only its misleading label changes.

prs.title: fix(ci): spread cold release work across existing jobs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Normal full-release CI can concentrate expensive fixtures in one count-packed job when its exact selection has no measured timing. The observed [release lane](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43648749303/job/132612864388) exhausted its 120-minute limit while tests were still progressing.

## User Impact

Cold release work uses the existing relative file weights to spread work across the same compatible job slots. Coverage, Node/Bun policy, worker limits, the 64-file cap, and timeouts stay intact. This improves placement; it does not claim a measured full-release duration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the canonical striped allocator with a capacity limit. Rebalance only unmeasured compatible bundles when their maximum relative load strictly improves. Preserve measured selections and resolve regenerated selections through the existing measured splitter, so a historical timing match still controls admission.

CI tooling grows by 64 net lines to supply this missing cold-selection placement step; tests grow by 88 lines. No new planner, timing data, configuration, or product-runtime behavior.

## Evidence

- Actual base `5025db61e9482d95f29956f266496f32f4f94f72` fails the new regression at the intended unchanged maximum: `expected 640 to be less than 640` (relative weights, not seconds).
- 161 existing planner cases and all 7 release planner cases pass across the focused native runs. Both script and root-tooling test typechecks pass. [Focused release/type proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43662538110).
- Both targeted lint checks and canonical formatter/Bun parity pass on the final source bytes. [Final native static command](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43663063129) exited 0; its lease stopped and settled. Delegated Testbox Actions cancellation during lease cleanup is separate from the command result.
- Final local autoreview and independent owner review: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable in the existing dirty checkout; exact-head hosted review and required PR checks remain the landing gates.

prs.title: fix: Doctor stays silent when personal recall lacks Active Memory
prs.body:
Closes #183700

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Doctor stays silent when cross-conversation recall defaults on for a personal install but the required bundled Active Memory plugin is disabled by default.

## User Impact

Doctor and Doctor lint now warn about the missing prerequisite and name both existing choices: set `plugins.entries.active-memory.enabled=true`, or opt out with `memory.search.rememberAcrossConversations=false`. The plugin is not enabled automatically; recall defaults, privacy/session eligibility, UI/RPC behavior, and memory status are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing effective plugin-activation owner once per Doctor operation instead of a separate availability policy that treated an absent entry as enabled. Keep the plugin's internal disable switch and the existing warning severity. This is diagnostic-only: no configuration migration or automatic repair is introduced, and the excluded-session-source informational note remains unchanged.

## Evidence: latest-stable upgrade validation (2026-11-04 UTC)

**Branch status updated November 15, 2026:** the preserved candidate is now published as `dd232c362b91baca3a86e98242d001450110ef07` through the native publisher, with current-main integration based on `0bf4c979ba918ad256a0b4b79c52c03413420e01`. The native operation preserved branch history; no manual force-push or history rewrite was used. The authored delta remains three files, +106/−14. The local tracked source tree tested, built and reviewed is `0d4360b044ab7402e167ec813dc98148dde0aafa` (complete patch SHA-256 `e33ce8d543def096ad500c8aee792a6e2216894b28b4944c78bef5aa61f1d1a3`). Independent immutable GitHub commit metadata confirms that the published full tree is exactly `0d4360b044ab7402e167ec813dc98148dde0aafa`, matching the tested candidate. **Exact-head CI passed:** [CI run 43660427342, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43660427342) completed successfully; all 66 jobs reconciled (36 success, 30 skipped). The [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43660427342/job/132651709343), dependency review and applicable security-review statuses passed. Full paginated reconciliation at **2026-11-15T01:10:52Z** found **120 check instances** (54 success, 65 skipped, 1 neutral), plus three latest commit-status contexts, all successful; no failed or pending checks remained. The Gateway’s combined total of 123 includes those three status contexts. This verifies CI, not a new hosted review, grade, maintainer approval or installed-upgrade result.

**Fresh source validation for this candidate:** 155 tests across seven files passed, along with the targeted Doctor production/test typecheck, lint, format, mock/test-line/max-line ratchets and full build. The build logged advisory UI-budget warnings; no UI-budget clearance is inferred. Fresh production CLI normal Doctor exited 0, targeted memory-search lint exited 1 with two prerequisite warnings, and both explicit enablement and recall-opt-out controls cleared the findings. These are source-built CLI checks, **not an installed-upgrade run**. Canonical whole-candidate autoreview against `0bf4c979ba918ad256a0b4b79c52c03413420e01` returned `scoped-clean` with no findings in its default **P0-only** scope; it is not a broader-priority or hosted-readiness assessment. Its optional unchanged secrets-named consumer context was refused during initial preparation and was not sent or repackaged; all three changed files and required activation/configuration owners were included in the corrected completed review.

**Historical evidence boundary:** the November 4 records below retain their original scope: runs 6 and 4b exercised this PR’s diff on `main` `7c2ff8f`, not the newly published full tree. Neither full-tree equivalence to that local build nor a new-head installed-upgrade pass is claimed. The later full-policy follow-up remains separate and was not awaited for this source refresh. The quoted exact-head refusal records refer to old head `30b9fb5ff40de17ce9b0783e8ad84fd86541c990`.

Source: [supplied redacted validation records and limitations](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183729#issuecomment-6636615805). These are external macOS observations, not commands executed by this Team session.


Scope: head `30b9fb5ff40de17ce9b0783e8ad84fd86541c990`, latest stable `openclaw@2026.10.10` (`7dc3350`, `latest` dist-tag, published 2026-11-03T02:26:08.904Z). macOS arm64, Node 24.22.2, npm 11.19.1, pnpm 12.16.1. Each run used a fresh disposable HOME, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, TMPDIR, npm prefix and pnpm home/store, with inherited `OPENCLAW_*`/`npm_config_*`/`PNPM_*` variables unset. Synthetic data only. User `.npmrc` had `min-release-age=7` in every run. In pnpm runs, the pnpm global config also had `minimumReleaseAge: 10080`. Redacted records: attached `pr-183729-latest-stable-evidence-v4.zip` (README inside maps each claim to a file).

In every run, the old state was created by the installed 2026.10.10 CLI: agents `main` and `personal`, FTS-only memory, no `session.dmScope`, no `plugins.entries.active-memory`, and 3 synthetic markers indexed. On that state, 2026.10.10 Doctor prints no Active Memory line, and `doctor --lint --only core/doctor/memory-search --json` exits 0 with `findings: []`. That reproduces #183700 on the latest stable.

**Baseline install deviation (all runs).** 2026.10.10 is younger than the 7-day policy, so a plain `npm install -g openclaw@2026.10.10` fails with `ETARGET` (recorded probe). The baseline was installed with an explicit `--min-release-age=0` (npm runs). In the pnpm runs, it was installed before `minimumReleaseAge` was set. The policy was active for every upgrade step. A baseline install under the policy becomes possible at 2026-11-10T02:26:09Z; that run is not done yet.

| Run | Upgrade path | Candidate | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | published 2026.10.10 updater, npm-owned | exact head `30b9fb5` (package version 2026.10.7) | **Refused** at candidate admission: `agents.defaults: Unrecognized key: "heartbeat"` |
| 3b | same, after `openclaw config unset agents.defaults.heartbeat` (as the refusal text suggests) | exact head | **Refused and rolled back** at `candidate-gateway-startup`: binary 2026.10.7 is older than config last written by 2026.10.10 |
| 6 | published 2026.10.10 updater, npm-owned | this PR's diff on `main` 7c2ff8f (local build, version 2026.10.10) | **PASS** (diagnostic + upgrade + preservation). Not policy-preserving: npm got `--min-release-age=0` |
| 4 | published 2026.10.10 updater, pnpm-owned, `minimumReleaseAge: 10080` | same local build | **Refused by pnpm policy** (`ERR_PNPM_NO_MATURE_MATCHING_VERSION`, 11 `@openclaw/fs-safe*@0.27.0`, published 2026-10-30) and left 2026.10.10 intact. The policy held through the updater. |
| 4b | as run 4, plus `minimumReleaseAgeExclude: ["@openclaw/fs-safe", "@openclaw/fs-safe-*"]` | same local build | **PASS** (diagnostic + upgrade + preservation). Policy enforced on every other registry package |

### Runs 3/3b: the exact head cannot be installed over 2026.10.10
The head's package version is 2026.10.7, and its base predates the 2026.10.10 config schema (`agents.defaults.heartbeat` is in `src/config/zod-schema.agent-defaults.ts:24` at v2026.10.10, but not at `30b9fb5` or at `main` 7c2ff8f). The updater's downgrade and config guards correctly refuse. Both runs ended on 2026.10.10 (`7dc3350`) with memory files, chunk rows and settings unchanged. This is caused by the stale base, not the diff. The PR diff (3 files) applies cleanly to current `main` with `git apply --check`, but not to v2026.10.10. **A rebase is needed before the head itself can take the latest-stable upgrade path.**

### Run 6: npm-owned updater, PR diff on main
- `openclaw update --tag <candidate.tgz> --no-restart --yes --json` exited 0 with status `ok`. All 19 steps passed, including `candidate-gateway-startup` (a temporary check, not a service start) and `package-swap`. Version is now `2026.10.10 (d7fc880)`. No manual config step was used.
- Recorded npm step: `npm i -g ... <candidate.tgz> --no-fund --no-audit --loglevel=error --min-release-age=0`. Age audit: 16 of 494 registry name@versions were younger than 7 days at install time.

### Runs 4/4b: pnpm-owned updater route
- The updater ran `pnpm add -g --allow-build=openclaw openclaw@file:<candidate.tgz> --config.global-dir=... --config.global-bin-dir=...`, with no freshness flag. Its env still gets `npm_config_min_release_age=0` (`src/infra/update-global-env.ts:60-61`, `src/infra/npm-install-env.ts:306-324` at v2026.10.10). That is npm's key, and pnpm ignores it. Recorded probe: `pnpm add openclaw@2026.10.10` with exactly that env still fails `ERR_PNPM_NO_MATURE_MATCHING_VERSION`. Run 4 shows the same through the real updater.
- Run 4b age audit (`pnpm list -g --depth Infinity`): 438 registry name@versions. The only ones younger than 7 days are the 11 explicitly excluded `@openclaw/fs-safe*@0.27.0`. `chrome-devtools-mcp`, `playwright-core` and `@openclaw/ai` are bundled inside the candidate tarball and are not resolved from the registry, so they are outside the audit, like the candidate itself.
- For contrast, the npm-owned route always adds `--min-release-age=0` or `--before=<now>` (`src/infra/update-global.ts:1131-1163`, `src/infra/npm-install-env.ts:295-304`; documented as intentional in `docs/install/updating/update-methods.md:425-428`).

### Results after upgrade (runs 6 and 4b, identical)
- Normal `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` exits 0 and warns once for each agent: "Remember across conversations is effectively enabled for agent "main" (and "personal"), but the Active Memory plugin is disabled. Set plugins.entries.active-memory.enabled=true or set memory.search.rememberAcrossConversations to false."
- `openclaw doctor --lint --only core/doctor/memory-search --json` exits 1 with 2 findings (`main`, `personal`).
- Controls (lint exit/findings): default 1/2; `plugins.entries.active-memory.enabled=true` 0/0 (normal Doctor has no prerequisite line); enabled + `config.enabled=false` 1/2; enabled + `plugins.deny=["active-memory"]` 1/2; enabled + `plugins.enabled=false` 1/4 (adds the 2 existing `plugins.slots.memory` warnings); `rememberAcrossConversations=false` 0/0; `session.dmScope=per-peer` 0/0; restored 1/2.
- Without-PR control on the same state: in run 4, 2026.10.10 stayed installed, and the same controls gave default 0/0, back-to-default 0/0 and restored 0/0.
- Preservation:
  - The 7 workspace/memory `.md` files are sha256-identical.
  - Index chunk rows were byte-identical to baseline both before and after the first post-upgrade search: main 2 rows `9ea842df...`, personal 11 rows `86906c94...`. No rebuild was needed.
  - All 3 markers were found in the right files, and cross-agent searches returned `[]` both ways.
  - Kept: `agents.defaults.workspace`, `memory.search.{enabled,provider}`, `gateway.port`, `logging.level`, and both agent entries.
  - Changed by the updater's Doctor: removed `agents.defaults.heartbeat`, added `wizard.lastRun*`. Configuration as a whole was not unchanged.

### Not demonstrated
- An upgrade of the exact head `30b9fb5` from 2026.10.10. It is impossible until the PR is rebased (runs 3/3b). Runs 6/4b used a local build of this PR's diff on `main` 7c2ff8f, not the head.

- A pnpm run with no exclusion at all. The 11 `@openclaw/fs-safe*@0.27.0` mature at 2026-11-06T23:51:49Z.
- Any installed gateway service start or restart (`--no-restart`; service management is skipped for a non-default state dir). Docker cells. Windows or Linux.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep assistant answers out of the collapsed Worked fold
prs.body:
Related: #180490

## What Problem This Solves

On main, a completed Control UI turn collapses into one "Worked" line, and that line swallows **about a third of Claude's answers** (and those of other models that don't label commentary) along with the tools.

The fold hides every assistant text group that is not the run's last reply, unless the provider labels it as commentary. So an answer followed by any tool call (saving a note, updating a file) is hidden, and only the short closing line stays visible. A steered run that produces two replies shows only the last one.

This affects **every model that does not label its commentary**, not just Claude: as far as we know, everything except OpenAI models. Fresh GLM-5.3 Flash and DeepSeek v4.1 Flash runs on current code store their text with no phase label (examples below). Claude is where it shows most, because it routinely answers and then calls a tool to record the result.

## Why This Change Was Made

`isCollapsibleWorkGroup` treated every unphased assistant text group as completed work unless it owned the turn's final reply. That is a guess: an absent phase is unknown, not commentary, and `toolUse` is an execution stop reason, not a narration label (Claude often answers and then calls a tool to record the result).

The runtime prompt added in #159416 (refined in #178108) tells models that "Commentary is optional progress and may be hidden" and asks them to repeat every pending answer in the final response. That works for providers that tag commentary natively (OpenAI): their commentary really is throwaway progress, and the answer carries a final-answer label, so important messages stay visible.

It cannot help models that do not tag commentary, or streamed turns with no definitive final answer. The instruction does not create phase labels, so the UI still cannot tell an answer from progress, and generation ending or a later tool call does not establish that earlier text was commentary. Unlabeled text must not be folded on that assumption, hence this change.

The change adds one guard: an assistant text-only group is collapsible only when every message in it resolves to explicit `commentary` through the existing `resolveAssistantReplyPhase` (provider phase, text signatures, keyed stream-fallback commentary). Everything else is unchanged: one Worked line per turn, the same partition and ownership logic, tools and reasoning still fold, and providers that label commentary (OpenAI/Codex, Muse Spark) fold exactly as before. No CSS, renderer or layout change.

**Intentional change to existing behavior.** Main currently treats any assistant text without a phase label as narration and folds it. That assumption holds for providers that tag commentary natively, such as OpenAI, which is what the existing tests and runtime prompt (#159416, #178108) are built around. It does not hold for providers that never send a phase, where it hides real answers (34% in the replay below). This PR deliberately reverses that default. Maintainer sign-off on this behavior change is requested.

Key points for review:
- **An absent phase is unknown, not commentary.** Folding is now driven only by an explicit commentary label (provider phase, text signature, or keyed stream fallback), never by a missing one.
- **Natively tagged providers are unchanged.** OpenAI/Codex (and Muse Spark) commentary folds exactly as before.
- **OpenClaw's own rows still fold.** Host-generated assistant rows (provider `openclaw`, e.g. publication receipts) are identified with the existing `isTranscriptArtifactProvider` and fold as on main; only model-authored text is affected.
- **Layout is unchanged.** One Worked line per turn, the same rows in the same positions; every tool call still folds, and expanding Worked shows rows in transcript order.
- **Prompt guidance cannot substitute for labels.** Asking models to keep commentary throwaway does not give the UI a way to tell an untagged answer from progress.

## User Impact

**Hidden answers go from about 1 in 3 to zero.** The Worked line still collapses only the work: same count, same positions, every tool call still inside it. Expanding it shows tools between the answers they came between, as on main.

Trade-off: short unlabeled status lines (for example "Build passed; tests running now.") are now visible too, in their chronological place, for models that do not natively tag their commentary.

## Evidence

| Measure | Main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Answers hidden in the collapsed fold (1,474 sampled text blocks, two blind classifiers) | **34%** (25% if status lines count as narration) | **0%** |
| Turns that hide at least one answer | about **1 in 5** | **0** |
| Unlabeled assistant text blocks hidden (962 sessions, presentation replay) | 4,874 | **0** |
| Worked rows (same replay) | 3,483 | 3,483, **zero** differences in position, key, reply owner or duration |
| Tool cards inside Worked | 35,164 | 35,164 |
| Rows revealed, rendered A/B in the real Control UI (979 sessions) | | **4,051** across 432 sessions |
| Previously visible rows lost / sessions gone blank | | **0 / 0** |
| Expanded rows: same IDs and text, by session | | **979 / 979** |

**Method.** Every Claude Code session on one workstation (about 3 Oct to 11 Nov 2026) was replayed through main's real history import and presentation code (`840105308d2`, default View settings), then rendered on two otherwise identical scratch Gateways with and without this change. *Answer* means text that tells the user something (a result, explanation, decision, question or status), even if it also says what happens next.

**Screenshots** (synthetic conversation, same data and settings on both builds).

One streamed turn: three long answers between tool batches, ending with a notes-file write.

| | Main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Collapsed | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/9faab0a8ae958afc581c1c0b706b6ff69e4dfd8f/before-collapsed.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/9faab0a8ae958afc581c1c0b706b6ff69e4dfd8f/after-collapsed.png) |
| Expanded | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/9faab0a8ae958afc581c1c0b706b6ff69e4dfd8f/before-expanded.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/9faab0a8ae958afc581c1c0b706b6ff69e4dfd8f/after-expanded.png) |

Steered turn: both builds split the turn at the steer and show the pre-steer answer; after it, main hides both answers and this PR shows them. Expanded order is identical.

| | Main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Collapsed | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/9faab0a8ae958afc581c1c0b706b6ff69e4dfd8f/before-steer-collapsed.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/9faab0a8ae958afc581c1c0b706b6ff69e4dfd8f/after-steer-collapsed.png) |
| Expanded | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/9faab0a8ae958afc581c1c0b706b6ff69e4dfd8f/before-steer-expanded.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/9faab0a8ae958afc581c1c0b706b6ff69e4dfd8f/after-steer-expanded.png) |

**Other models** (real runs on the synthetic workspace; the prompt asks for findings before each further tool call so the turn has this shape). Neither model's stored text carries a phase label.

GLM-5.3 Flash (zai, reasoning low): main hides both findings answers; this PR shows them.

| | Main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Collapsed | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/9faab0a8ae958afc581c1c0b706b6ff69e4dfd8f/models/glm/before-collapsed.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/9faab0a8ae958afc581c1c0b706b6ff69e4dfd8f/models/glm/after-collapsed.png) |
| Expanded | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/9faab0a8ae958afc581c1c0b706b6ff69e4dfd8f/models/glm/before-expanded.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/9faab0a8ae958afc581c1c0b706b6ff69e4dfd8f/models/glm/after-expanded.png) |

DeepSeek v4.1 Flash (opencode-go): main hides both findings answers; this PR shows them.

| | Main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Collapsed | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/9faab0a8ae958afc581c1c0b706b6ff69e4dfd8f/models/deepseek/before-collapsed.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/9faab0a8ae958afc581c1c0b706b6ff69e4dfd8f/models/deepseek/after-collapsed.png) |
| Expanded | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/9faab0a8ae958afc581c1c0b706b6ff69e4dfd8f/models/deepseek/before-expanded.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/9faab0a8ae958afc581c1c0b706b6ff69e4dfd8f/models/deepseek/after-expanded.png) |

**Tests.** New regressions (answer then tool then closing line; a steered two-reply run; explicit commentary still folds; an unlabeled model answer stays visible while an OpenClaw publication receipt in the same turn still folds; tools and reasoning still fold; Worked row count and position unchanged) fail on stock and pass patched. On current main (`f7c48defb85`): UI typecheck passes; `ui/src/pages/chat` plus tool-call grouping: 8,912 passed, 3 skipped, 5 failed. Four are native-drop undo tests that fail identically on unmodified main; the fifth (an inline mock reset) passes 3/3 in isolation on both main and this branch. Existing main tests are unchanged apart from neutral fixture names.

prs.title: fix(ui): GitHub help misstates agent accounts and cloud publishing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Profile’s GitHub help incorrectly says agents always use the shared account and all cloud work must return to the current computer before personal publication.

## User Impact

User impact: the help now respects each agent’s own or inherited GitHub account and does not tell users to move work unnecessarily when a repository checkpoint already supports publication. Personal publishing still requires an explicit choice, session write access and finished, accepted work.

This is a copy-only correction. Credentials, permissions, publication eligibility and cloud-work recovery are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The account owner prefers an agent override before the shared account. Personal publication supports accepted repository-only checkpoints without a Gateway checkout; remote work sourced from a Gateway checkout retains its separate stop/reconciliation requirement. The general Profile explanation should not impose the latter restriction on every cloud session or confuse the browser computer with the Gateway.

One canonical English paragraph is shortened. The specific account explanations above it and the existing per-session publication guidance remain the owners of those details. No new controls, state, helpers or compatibility paths are added.

## Evidence

- The existing built-app personal-account flow fails on the old help and passes with the corrected paragraph. It opens and closes the real help, copies a synthetic device code, connects the personal fixture and disconnects it without changing the shared account or configuration. No live GitHub sign-in or external publication is exercised by the test.
- 61 focused GitHub UI/controller tests pass. Six selected backend contracts pass: agent-override precedence, selected-versus-effective identity, personal repository-checkpoint publication, and three busy/local-worktree refusal states. These are selected tests, not full backend suites.
- UI typecheck, scoped lint, i18n verification, formatting and diff checks pass. An initial backend proof invocation was invalidated because I edited the locale during its compilation; it ran no tests. The source was then held stable and the selected tests passed. No broad CI or E2E matrix was run.
- Matched before/after captures below use real components, synthetic responses and an emulated 1280 × 1400 viewport. The affected paragraph is fully visible after scrolling the help panel; its same-frame crop and surrounding Profile context were inspected. Baseline main: `b75177698b1cffd865aac7051237960055fae8d7`.

Contributor: @vyctorbrzezowski directed the comprehensive wording and interaction audit.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/c4507bcf-b1bf-464e-a9df-2bc0344bbe58)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/27ab8da9-7856-4f25-9b62-91d8138f1a1c)

## Screenshots

Before and after, in that order:

![Before: GitHub help requires the shared account and returning all cloud work to this computer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2a7f784d-77e3-4135-bfb3-27832aec8b40)

prs.title: fix: message from a scheduled run to a busy Claude CLI session fails once the run ends
prs.body:
<!-- Template source: .github/pull_request_template.md at origin/main 8aa2434748a. -->

Fixes #199278

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a message that a scheduled run sends with `sessions_send` to a busy Claude CLI session fails with "Cron occurrence source authority is no longer active" once the sender's run has ended. The receiver never sees the message and the sender only gets a failure notice.

## User Impact

User impact: a scheduled job can hand work to a busy Claude CLI session again. The queued turn runs after the receiver finishes its current turn, as it already does for an embedded receiver and for an interactive sender. Paced check-in jobs that message long-running Claude CLI agents no longer lose the handoff.

The queued turn still ends when the operator's role, device or access grant is revoked, and on an explicit Stop.

## Why This Change Was Made

#194798 gave accepted turns a retained continuation, and the Claude CLI receiver already holds it. The failure is somewhere else. CLI preparation projects the run's MCP tools through `captureSessionControlAuthority`, which also asserts the ambient request client's `operatorRunAuthority`. A queued CLI turn prepares inside the sender's request scope, before the CLI run installs its admitted caller identity. So the sender's run-bound authority is asserted after its occurrence ended.

#181363 already settled that an admitted caller, not the ambient client, owns continuation authority. This change applies the same rule when the admitted run's own authority is passed in, unless that authority is the ambient client's own, which keeps its live-client check. It is one expression in `src/agents/tools/sessions-operator-authority.ts`. The retained continuation keeps checking role, device and access grant.

## Evidence

**Real run.** QA lab Gateway, sender on the mock provider, receiver `claude-cli/claude-sonnet-5-5` on a Claude subscription login. The receiver runs a real `sleep 150`. A scheduled job created by an owner turn is force-run, sends with `sessions_send` while the receiver is busy, and ends.

| | Receiver after its busy turn | Sender |
|---|---|---|
| base `8aa2434748a` | never answers the handoff | `sessions_send delivery to <receiver session> failed: Cron occurrence source authority is no longer active` |
| head `0ad321660b7` | answers the handoff (`QA-CRONAUTH-HANDOFF-OK`) | no failure notice |

The scenario is a local harness of mock turns and a QA scenario, so it is not committed. A throwaway stack capture at the throw named `captureSessionControlAuthority` called from `captureMcpLoopbackScope` during `prepareCliMcpToolProjection`.

**Runtime output.** Both runs used `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 pnpm build` followed by `pnpm openclaw qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai --scenario cron-authority-mix-repro`, one run per SHA, with the scenario's recorded session history and cron run record printed in order. Times are UTC on 2026-11-15. Session keys are replaced by placeholders.

Base `8aa2434748a`:

```text
01:40:01.390 receiver  user  "Use your shell or exec tool to run exactly: sleep 150. When it finishes, reply exactly BUSY-DONE."
01:40:21.654 sender    sessions_send(sessionKey=<receiver>, message="CRONAUTH handoff reply: answer with QA-CRONAUTH-HANDOFF-OK")
01:40:51.731 sender    toolResult {"status":"accepted","sessionKey":<receiver>,"targetDisposition":"queued","delivery":{"status":"pending"}}
01:40:51.844 cron      run finished status=ok completionStatus=succeeded durationMs=30428 summary=QA-CRONAUTH-SENT
01:42:34.580 receiver  assistant "BUSY-DONE"   (no handoff message in the receiver history)
01:42:34.942 sender    assistant "sessions_send delivery to <receiver> failed: Cron occurrence source authority is no longer active. The target may not have received the message; retry or report the failure instead of assuming delivery succeeded."
```

Head `0ad321660b7`:

```text
01:34:22.064 sender    sessions_send(sessionKey=<receiver>, message="CRONAUTH handoff reply: answer with QA-CRONAUTH-HANDOFF-OK")
01:34:22.129 receiver  queued handoff message recorded in the receiver history (receiver is still running sleep 150)
01:34:52.153 sender    toolResult {"status":"accepted","sessionKey":<receiver>,"targetDisposition":"queued","delivery":{"status":"pending"}}
01:34:52.262 cron      run finished status=ok completionStatus=succeeded durationMs=30469 summary=QA-CRONAUTH-SENT
01:36:35.141 receiver  assistant "BUSY-DONE"
01:36:38.404 receiver  assistant "QA-CRONAUTH-HANDOFF-OK"   (answers the queued handoff)
01:36:38.536 sender    assistant "QA-CRONAUTH-HANDOFF-OK"   (reply flow reaches the sender, no failure notice)
```

In both runs the send is accepted and queued while the receiver runs `sleep 150`, and the sender's occurrence finishes before the receiver is idle.

**Regression tests.** `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.scheduled-handoff.test.ts` runs `prepareCliRunContext` with the real MCP tool projection, the #194798 recovery fixture, a retired occurrence and the sender's request scope still active. On base it fails with the occurrence error, with the fix it passes. Three more cases keep the revocations: the sender's device removed, the sender's role changed, and an explicit Stop each still reject the turn. Two unit cases in `sessions-control-authority.test.ts` pin the helper: the ambient client is ignored for an admitted run's own authority, and an ambient authority passed back as `prepared` keeps its live-client check.

With the fix reverted (`git apply -R`) the handoff case and the unit cases fail again. The three revocation cases reject with and without the fix, as intended.

**Checks.** Consumer suites pass (12 files): session control, MCP session controls, tool resolution, CLI prepare, and the #194798 cancellation and recovery tests. Typecheck (core and core tests), oxlint and format are clean for the touched files. The dead export scan fails on `main` the same way, on two `ui/src` test helper exports this change does not touch.

**Local review.** ClawSweeper `--local-range` (Claude runner, claude-opus-5-5), base `8aa2434748a`, head `0ad321660b7`, full committed range, review complete and checkout access verified. Outcome after 2 rounds: no findings, patch is correct, security cleared, rating overall C, proof D, patch B. Round 1 found one P3 (an ambient authority passed back as `prepared` lost its live-client check), fixed and covered by the second unit case. The proof tier reflects that the local reviewer sees the diff, not the real run above. Remaining findings: none.

**Gaps.** The occurrence in the regression tests is the #194798 fixture's retired claim, not a live cron job. The real run covers the handoff only, not revocation. The sender model in the real run is scripted. Test cost: 207 added test lines in 2 files, under the 400 line budget.

prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): name invited members from their email and ask who they are on first visit
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Someone invited to a claw through OpenClaw ID arrives as "Person c33358cb" when their account reports no display name, and stays that way in sessions, mentions and presence until they find Settings → Profile.

## User Impact

User impact: a newly approved member is named from the part of their email before the `@`, and on their first visit lands on a new session that asks for a name and then a photo before it offers a composer.

- Only invited OpenClaw ID members who have not chosen a name see the step. Owners, members whose account reports a name, and other sign-ins are unaffected.
- **Skip for now** keeps the email-derived name. The answer is saved with the member's profile on this Gateway, so they are not asked again on another device.
- The step replaces the composer on the new-session page and the chat page, and hides the starter prompts, so there is no other place to type. Nothing is sent to the agent or written to a transcript.
- An existing nameless member is named from their stored email on their next sign-in. A name someone chose is never replaced.
- Gated by the existing OpenClaw ID Labs switch.

## Why This Change Was Made

The name and photo are stored only in this Gateway's own profile. OpenClaw ID keeps holding just the account email; nothing is sent back to it.

The email-derived name is written to the profile when the member is approved, the same way an email sign-in is named, so every surface that shows a display name picks it up without a protocol change.

A member who still owes the step is taken from the default landing to a new session, because the main session is shared history. An explicit link to another session is kept, and the step replaces that session's composer.

## Evidence

**Before**: a newly approved member lands in the main session with an ordinary composer.

![A newly approved member in the main session with an ordinary composer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f244bf98-8f16-4a6c-8adc-ce355559e7b5)

**After**: the same arrival lands on a new session and is asked for a name, then a photo.

![The new-session page asking a new member for their name](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/86eb191c-a27e-4329-8d7d-e72adceffb7e)

![The photo question after the name is saved](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/727b9cd9-0d41-4c17-9e72-322636c71b95)

![The name question in a phone-sized chat page](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/55ea2dff-a666-4200-af35-1c9671ed10e3)

The screenshots are from the live runs below and show throwaway staging accounts. The "before" capture is from an earlier commit of this branch in which the chat page was still unchanged.

**Live proof.** An isolated Gateway on a Mac Studio, linked as a throwaway staging claw, with real Chromium browsers for the owner and two invited members over the tunnel against staging OpenClaw ID. 12 of 12 steps passed on `ca209c9d44cc`:

- an approved member is named from their email, never "Person";
- the member lands on `/new` with the name field focused and no composer rendered at any point before answering;

prs.title: fix(outbound): keep gateway-executed CLI send transcript writes in the gateway process
prs.body:
Fixes #199155

## Root Cause
When an external CLI process (`openclaw message send`) delegated a gateway-executed channel send via `message.action`, `src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts` unconditionally set `callerRecordsDestinationHistory: true`, causing `outbound-send-service.ts` to skip recording destination history in the Gateway process. The CLI caller then invoked `recordGatewayActionSend()` in `src/infra/outbound/message-action-send.ts` from outside the Gateway process, writing directly to `transcript_events` in SQLite without updating the Gateway resident session actor sequence state and causing subsequent Gateway appends to fail with `UNIQUE constraint failed: transcript_events.session_id, transcript_events.seq`.

## Fix
- In `src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`, only set `callerRecordsDestinationHistory` when the caller has in-process `agentRuntimeIdentity` (`Boolean(client?.internal?.agentRuntimeIdentity)`), so external CLI/WebSocket callers let the Gateway record destination history under its resident session actor ownership.
- In `src/infra/outbound/message-action-send.ts`, only call `recordGatewayActionSend()` for host-bound in-process callers (`ctx.gateway?.request`), preventing external CLI/transport callers from writing directly to the Gateway SQLite transcript.

## Verification
- Added regression test in `src/infra/outbound/message-action-gateway.test.ts`.
- Ran `pnpm test src/infra/outbound/message-action-gateway.test.ts src/infra/outbound/message-action-send.mirror-order.test.ts src/infra/outbound/outbound-send-service.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (3 files, 43 tests passed).
- Ran `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/send.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (78 tests passed).
- Ran `pnpm tsgo:core` and `npx oxlint` (0 warnings, 0 errors).

prs.title: fix(compaction): scope the transcript byte fuse to the latest compaction window
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`agents.defaults.compaction.maxActiveTranscriptBytes` is documented as an opt-in that compacts "when transcript history reaches the threshold". Once a session has compacted even once, the byte reader behind it (`readVisibleTranscriptStats`) stops scoping: it only closes its window at a `reset` boundary, so a compaction leaves it summing **every event on the active path**. Compaction cannot shrink that number, so every subsequent turn trips the fuse again and the session compacts on every single reply, wiping working context each time.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Live proof (long-running Telegram topic session, GPT-5.6 via OpenAI Responses, `maxActiveTranscriptBytes: "2mb"`, ids redacted):**

- Active path in `openclaw-agent.sqlite`: 4,432 events / 16,295,064 bytes. Post-latest-compaction window (the transcript the model actually sees): 58 events / 436,798 bytes.
- Five preflight compactions between 19:57Z and 20:59Z on the same day. Their recorded `tokensBefore` were 145,818 / 93,255 / 45,847 / 66,524 / 43,339 — each exactly the provider's last reported `totalTokens`, and all far below the ~248k token threshold for a 272k window. The token trigger was not firing; the byte fuse was (`shouldCompact = shouldCompactByTokens || shouldCompactByTranscriptBytes`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.ts`).
- Between compactions the provider-reported context sat at 35k–120k tokens, i.e. nothing was oversized.

**Root cause:** `findLatestResetMessageWindow` returns `null` unless the latest boundary is a `reset` (`src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-reset-window.ts`), and `readVisibleTranscriptStats` then falls back to the unscoped aggregate. That is correct for history readers, which intentionally span compactions and only cut at a reset, but the fuse shares the same window and so latches permanently after the first compaction.

**Why fix it here:** both byte-trigger consumers reach `readSessionTranscriptActiveStats` through `readSessionLogSnapshot`: preflight compaction uses `maxActiveTranscriptBytes`, while forced memory flush uses `memoryFlush.forceFlushTranscriptBytes`. Both thresholds should measure the model-visible window. Giving the resolver a `"history" | "context"` scope measures the kept tail, compaction summary, and everything after the latest compaction or reset without changing history readers, which keep the `"history"` default. A compaction keeps its whole tail while a reset replays only the paired subset, which the resolver now mirrors. Docs and schema help describe the shared semantics.

## User Impact

Operators who opt into `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` no longer get a compaction on every turn after the first compaction. On the session above the fuse would read ~437 KB (under the 2 MB threshold) instead of ~16 MB.

## Evidence

- Added a regression with a 20 KB discarded prefix, 3 KB retained tail, 4 KB compaction summary, and a post-compaction turn. It asserts the stats count the four model-visible events while excluding discarded history.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33027233734) on `c01fb6bd7be` → 257/257 check runs completed with zero failures, including the relocated bounded-context regression and the previously failing core lint lane.
- Before/after on the live session was computed with the equivalent SQL over the active-path projection (whole path 16,295,064 bytes vs post-boundary 436,798 bytes); the patched reader was not run against the live database.
- Fresh structured autoreview on `c01fb6bd7be` reported no actionable P0–P2 findings.

## Worked on by
- @VACInc

prs.title: feat(gateway): identify the serving process in local startup probes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A supervisor can see that its local Gateway has started and still connect through a stable routing address to a different Gateway process. Two ready processes can report the same build.

## User Impact

A supervisor can compare the boot ID from an opted-in loopback startup probe with the boot ID on its authenticated Gateway WebSocket before it sends work. The caller must still authenticate and authorize each operation on that connection.

## Why This Change Was Made

The startup checker already runs in the process that owns the WebSocket hello. It can return that same boot ID after startup without a second authenticated WebSocket handshake or a write to the Gateway’s profile store. A plain startup probe retains its existing response. The Gateway omits the field on requests with proxy identity or delegation evidence, an authorization header, a cookie, or a browser Origin. It also omits it on non-loopback traffic and requests from a configured proxy address. A same-host relay that deliberately rewrites requests as direct loopback is within the host's trust boundary.

## Evidence

The focused tests exercise a real Gateway listener and WebSocket hello, the startup and draining states, ordinary and opted-in probes, authenticated remote requests and proxy-shaped requests, and GET/HEAD response length parity.

The two owning test files passed all 21 cases in 185.65 seconds, including the cold worker build. The final focused header test passed in 32.59 seconds after adding the custom proxy-header cases. Core typechecking, scoped lint and formatting passed. Hosted CI timing is pending.

prs.title: fix(openclaw-id): reopening an approved invite link is refused as already used
prs.body:
Related: OCF-536 (Linear)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an approved OpenClaw ID member who reopens their already-used invite link from the same browser has the redemption refused as `invite_used`, with only a warn log on the Gateway and nothing on the owner's Access page.

## User Impact

User impact: a member who re-sends the invite they already redeemed, from the same account and the same device and peer keys, is accepted as a no-op instead of being refused. Reuse by a different account, by new keys, or by a removed peer is still refused, and the Gateway log now says whether the sender is already a member and whether the keys match. Invites approved before this change didn't record the approved keys, so reuse of those stays refused.

## Why This Change Was Made

The protocol authority refused every redemption for an invite that wasn't open, and approval discarded the pending account, device and peer keys, so an exact replay couldn't be recognized. The approved keys are now kept on the invite record for the rest of the invite's lifetime. An exact replay is still fully signature-verified, then accepted with no state change and no events, and the Gateway skips the pending-request and report writes for that case. The browser still gets no reply telling it the outcome; the protocol docs now describe that gap. The loader-side fix is separate (claw-loader, OCF-535).

## Evidence

- Regressions in the protocol (`invite-replay.test.ts`) and `mailbox-reader.test.ts` failed before the fix and pass after it.
- Scoped runs: 31 protocol test files with 243 tests, plus the `mailbox-reader`, `service.invites`, `authority` and `claw-store.persistence` suites with 35 tests. All passed.
- The portable protocol, core production and affected test type checks passed. Lint and format on the touched files passed.
- An independent Astra review found no verified P0–P2 findings.
- Stored-data compatibility (`claw-store.persistence.test.ts`, real SQLite state worker): a claw is saved holding one invite approved with this change and one consumed invite with no `approved` field, as an invite stored before upgrade looks. After the database is closed and reopened:
  - the record loads unchanged
  - the new invite's approved identity survives the restart, and an exact replay is accepted as a no-op without changing the authority state or the stored record
  - a replay of the pre-upgrade invite is still refused as `invite_used`
  - both members stay admitted

  All 7 tests in the file pass, and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` passes.
- Not tested: live browser and native-iroh paths (the iroh binding isn't available locally).
- After merge, claw-loader's vendored `openclaw-id-protocol` needs a sync to this commit.

prs.title: fix(ui): Profile recovery points to unavailable actions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Profile recovery messages send users to nonexistent controls when an OpenClaw ID is already linked elsewhere or their profile cannot load.

## User Impact

User impact: both messages now point to supported next steps. The account conflict explains unlinking from the other profile and administrator merging only when both profiles belong to the same person; the load failure points to the existing Refresh button.

This is an English copy correction only. It does not merge or unlink profiles, change permissions, or alter sign-in or recovery behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The stock Control UI has no Users merge view or Set identity control. The existing merge owner requires administrator access, while the actual Profile header already offers Refresh. Two canonical English strings are corrected rather than adding controls or another recovery path.

## Evidence

- The new conflict regression and the existing unavailable-profile case fail on the original messages and pass after correction. The focused Profile suites pass 58 tests; the broader model-account, Discord and GitHub owner pass passes 92 tests (overlapping selections, not additive totals).
- Two real built-app browser flows pass: Link → linked-elsewhere explanation → later successful Link; and failed profile read → Refresh → loaded account controls. They use synthetic Gateway responses and a noncredential account fixture, not live authentication. No profile merge or unlink is performed.
- UI typecheck, scoped lint, formatting, i18n verification and diff checks pass. No broad CI or full E2E matrix was run.
- Simplification pass: two production strings only; regression coverage stays in existing owner suites. No new production helpers, state or compatibility paths.

Matched current-main before/after screenshots below show the actual Profile components in an emulated 1280 × 1000 light-theme viewport. Baseline main: `5025db61e9482d95f29956f266496f32f4f94f72`; relevant Profile owners and English strings are unchanged at observed main `005850723d3c65028f8ded0580c0ba8bea4bc18d`. Crops come from their corresponding full frames; full-page context was also inspected. The refresh recovery row excludes an unrelated random test Gateway port. The linked-account example grows by one line to explain the existing administrator boundary.

prs.title: fix(update): runtime retention falls back from hard links without saying why
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `updater-runtime-retention` takes minutes and reports `linked: 0` with no explanation when the updater temporary directory cannot be hard-linked from the installation, for example an explicit `TMPDIR` on another filesystem or Btrfs subvolume.

## User Impact

User impact: operators now get one warning naming how many files could not be hard-linked and the first error code, and the step diagnostics carry the same `linkFallback` count and code, so a slow retention can be traced to its temporary-directory placement. Retention behavior and placement are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The hard-link fallback discarded the refusal reason and only incremented `copied`, which also counts files copied by policy. The retention worker now records the number of refused links and the first errno, and the updater warns once when that count is non-zero, with a cross-device hint for `EXDEV`.

Deliberately not changed:

- **Placement under an explicit `TMPDIR`.** Staging beside the installation would restore hard links on this layout, but it overrides the selected-volume placement from #178135 (#177707). That precedence needs a maintainer decision; this diagnostic is what makes the cost visible in the meantime.
- **Clone versus byte-copy counts.** The fallback already requests a clone (`clone: "auto"`), but the copy primitive does not report which method it used, so `copied` still covers both. The docs and type comments now say so instead of implying byte copies.

## Evidence

- `src/infra/update-retained-runtime-tree.test.ts`: the existing `EXDEV`, `EMLINK`, and portable-copy fallback cases now assert the reported `linkFallback` count and code; the native case asserts none is reported.
- `src/infra/update-retained-runtime-files.test.ts`: the worker reply schema round-trips `linkFallback`.
- CI on head `ac397b846ca`: `openclaw/ci-gate` passed; `checks-node-changed-5` executed both touched test files, all passing. Formatter check and the line-cap ratchet pass.
- Review: hosted ClawSweeper review on the exact head reported no findings. Local autoreview was unavailable (its isolation preflight refused the session's temporary directory), so no local reviewer ran.
- Gap: the warning line itself has no dedicated test, and no live cross-device update was run on this branch. Whether the reported host reflinked or byte-copied remains unmeasured.

Refs #199030

prs.title: fix(database): Team Reports fails to port to PostgreSQL after a successful dry run
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes database port failing before it can record a recovery manifest when a profile contains Team Reports data, even though dry-run succeeds.

## User Impact

Operators can port populated Team Reports to PostgreSQL, resume interrupted publication, and return it to SQLite without renaming existing PostgreSQL schemas or losing retained rows. No schema, configuration, permission, or durability policy changes; SQL quoting and custody checks remain in force.

## Why This Change Was Made

Team Reports already generates a quoted namespace containing `team-reports`. Anchor and recovery validation now share the restricted native-name contract, including that hyphen, while still rejecting quotes, statement separators, dots, and NUL. Catalog comparison normalizes the quoted namespace qualifier PostgreSQL emits in index definitions so the real schema and temporary reference compare equally. Existing namespaces are not renamed.

## Evidence

- **Real built CLI, isolated PostgreSQL 17.9, Node 26.12.1, synthetic populated Team Reports:** base dry-run exit 0; actual port exit 1 in capture-originals, no durable manifest, original file SHA-256 unchanged. Complete fix: forward dry-run and port exit 0; reverse dry-run and port exit 0. Retained `started_at_ms=9007199254740993` verified in PostgreSQL and returned SQLite as exact int64. Other SQLite families remain out of scope.
- **Regression red/green:** original anchor validation fails both new original/intended cases (17 existing passed, 2 new failed); repaired validation passes all 19. Removing only catalog qualifier repair makes the new real PostgreSQL Team Reports command regression fail; restoring it passes interrupted publication → resume (same anchor namespace) → SQLite return with int64 row preserved.
- **Qualified full sibling suite:** `pnpm test src/infra/database-engine/port-command.mixed.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` with task-local conformance preload: **7 passed**, including state, workboard, agent, Team Reports, scoped backup, resume and rollback. Wall 149.4s (tests 78%); the complete command/custody and native workers require this integration boundary. Isolated new case: 17.0s test time. Recovery unit suite: **19 passed**, wall 38.5s including compiled-worker preparation. Hosted PostgreSQL shard wall times: 1209.94s, 906.41s, and 975.32s.
