[src/infra/database-engine/port.worker.ts:403-414](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1ee44e487d25fcdddaa785c495b60d97f538a694/src/infra/database-engine/port.worker.ts#L403-L414) issues a new native Client query for that invocation, reads its JSON catalog, validates it, then `.filter(...)` creates a **new local facts array**. No cache, shared projection or retained other consumer receives the array or its elements. Before normalization, `some` and the filtered structural comparison inspect it; the separate invalid-index/constraint query does not receive `facts`. [src/infra/database-engine/postgres-catalog.ts:65-100](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1ee44e487d25fcdddaa785c495b60d97f538a694/src/infra/database-engine/postgres-catalog.ts#L65-L100) validates/serializes for equality without retaining inputs. Only after those checks does [src/infra/database-engine/port.worker.ts:452-463](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1ee44e487d25fcdddaa785c495b60d97f538a694/src/infra/database-engine/port.worker.ts#L452-L463) replace each local fact's value and return the array to its caller.

Dependency ownership was also inspected, not inferred from the `filter` alone: installed `pg@8.23.1` client.js:687 creates a new Query for the string query; query.js:28 constructs a new Result; result.js:15 initializes `rows = []`. The installed pg-types text parser registers `JSON.parse` for JSON/JSONB (textParsers.js:202–203). `withPostgresConnection` constructs this ordinary Client without a custom row/parser cache. Thus the parsed catalog fact objects are fresh for this call too, not just a fresh array over cached shared objects. Normalization mutates that private result only; it does not weaken definition comparison or SQL quoting.

prs.title: fix(gateway): stop reusing stale startup plugin metadata on secret reloads
prs.body:
Fixes #198901

## Root Cause
`createRuntimeSecretsActivator` in `src/gateway/server-startup-config.ts` captured `startupManifestRegistry` and `params.pluginMetadataSnapshot` at gateway startup and passed them unconditionally into `prepareRuntimeSecretsSnapshot` on every activation, including `reason: manual` (`secrets.reload`) and `reason: reload`. After a managed plugin update introduced or changed `configContracts.secretInputs.paths`, secret reloads kept evaluating against the stale startup manifest snapshot until a full gateway restart.

## Fix
- In `src/gateway/server-startup-config.ts`, forward `startupManifestRegistry` and `params.pluginMetadataSnapshot` to `prepareRuntimeSecretsSnapshot` only when `activationParams.reason === startup`, allowing reload and manual secret activations to discover updated plugin manifests from disk.

## Verification
- Added regression test in `src/gateway/server-startup-config.plugin-secrets.test.ts`.
- Ran `pnpm test src/gateway/server-startup-config.plugin-secrets.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-managed-secrets.test.ts src/gateway/server-aux-handlers.test.ts src/secrets/runtime-config-collectors-plugins.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (4 files, 43 tests passed).
- Ran `pnpm tsgo:core` and `npx oxlint src/gateway/server-startup-config.ts src/gateway/server-startup-config.plugin-secrets.test.ts` (0 warnings, 0 errors).

prs.title: fix(ci): expose slow Bun staging phases
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A completed CI job spent 59.724 seconds staging the pinned Bun runtime, but its log cannot distinguish download, validation, extraction, execution, and installation time.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Maintainers can identify the slow staging phase without removing caches or weakening runtime validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Emit fixed-label elapsed seconds through Bash's built-in `time` for downloads, metadata, archive validation, extraction, executable validation, revision checks, and installation. No timer subprocess, new configuration, workflow change, or additional network request is introduced. Download timing is nested within metadata/archive timing and must not be added to those totals.

## Evidence

- [Completed Boat job 132463661947](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43600258009/job/132463661947): Node-cache restore 89.591s, Bun-cache restore 110.517s, Bun staging 59.724s. Seven siblings with the same cache keys and archive sizes spent 9.824–18.572s across those three phases. Restore logs show transfer stalls; the staging phase remains unattributed.
- Preserve all checksum, source-pin, architecture, executable, revision, cached-metadata fallback, release API fallback, and isolated destination checks. Extend the existing command fixtures; no real network calls in tests.
- Acceptance: the existing successful cold/fallback and warm-cache paths emit bounded, fixed-field phase timings; warm reuse makes no additional download; existing invalid-payload cases still fail and preserve the previous runtime. No wall-time threshold or savings claim.
- Final head `b432df1e9163d79576148a2b977e4f365f3500d1`: all 16 existing staging command fixtures passed (4.07s Vitest duration, 5.11s including runner overhead). The original script failed the cached negative control specifically because timing records were absent. Fixture downloads are local; no real network requests.
- Type-aware lint, focused script-test typecheck, formatting, Bash syntax, and diff checks passed. Local ClawSweeper reviewed the full `5025db61e9482d95f29956f266496f32f4f94f72..b432df1e9163d79576148a2b977e4f365f3500d1` range and found no actionable correctness or security issues; runtime proof was performed separately.
- Required CI passed and this head merged as `a64758be048909c5c59ef781d5b4f34aaefc34af`.
- [Completed Boat Linux/X64 setup, run 43662730849/job 132655825417](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43662730849/job/132655825417) emitted real phase timings: metadata 0.773s, archive validation/download 0.495s, extraction 0.647s, executable validation 0.292s, revision 0.038s, installation 0.044s. Whole install action: 2.353s. Nested downloads were 0.215s, 0.526s, and 0.379s; do not add them again. This confirms the diagnostic in CI and does not reproduce or explain the earlier 59.724s outlier.
- No work or bytes removed, no measured runtime or dollar savings. Any optimization now requires a naturally slow setup sample with these phase records. No CI dispatch or benchmark campaign performed.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: login recovery can tell remote users to run Gateway commands on their current device, and origin recovery asks for a restart even though that setting can apply live.

## User Impact

User impact: recovery instructions identify the computer that owns the Gateway and tell users to reconnect once an allowed-origins update takes effect.

## Why This Change Was Made

The command banner is shared by pairing and one-time-link recovery. It had no local-host condition, so “this computer” also appeared while connecting to a remote Gateway. First-use help and token recovery now use the same explicit host scope. Commands themselves are unchanged.

The existing reload owner classifies `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` as a hot-applied policy. The new origin instruction waits for the change to take effect instead of requiring an unconditional restart; it does not assume every reload mode applies changes automatically. Authentication, permissions, pairing, configuration, and reconnect behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

- The existing one-time-link test fails on main with “Run on this computer” for a remote URL, then passes with the corrected host scope. All 24 login-gate tests pass (1.57 seconds wall).
- The existing allowed-origins reload-policy case passes with `restartGateway: false` (one selected case; cold worker preparation took about 38 seconds).
- Five focused built-app scenarios pass before/after: remote pairing, missing token, rejected token, origin rejection, and mobile first-use help. Pairing still enters the app after approval; origin recovery’s Connect button enters after the synthetic policy change without restarting or reloading the page.
- Keyless i18n baseline/verification, targeted lint, UI typecheck, formatting, and diff checks pass. Generated translations and the raw-copy baseline are unchanged.
- Self-review/simplification: five existing English strings and three regression-test lines; no new renderer, state, or behavior. No independent agent review or broad E2E matrix was run. Hosted CI timing is not yet available.

Before uses verified main **bb905f76e55de2934e868434ea23c345893cdc6c**. These are inspected same-frame crops of the real login interface, with synthetic Gateway responses and a non-routable example hostname—not errors on the requester’s account. Four scenarios use the complete built app and its URL/secret/Connect controls (1280 × 1000, light). The mobile **How to connect** state uses the existing production-component fixture (390 × 1000, light). No real authentication, approval, configuration write, or restart was performed.

prs.title: fix(ui): stop recommending discard from a partial skill comparison
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Skill Workshop recommends discarding a draft when its instructions match the live skill, even though the draft can contain new or changed support files.

## User Impact

User impact: reviewing unchanged instructions no longer tells users to throw away an entire draft. They can inspect its other files and choose Apply or Discard themselves.

## Why This Change Was Made

The comparison only reads SKILL.md, so it cannot establish that the whole draft is redundant. Draft review now uses the existing neutral instruction-comparison message. The special discard advice, its unused override parameter and English key are removed.

Multi-file drafts are a supported format, including Doctor exports of older proposals. Apply still checks and publishes their files through the existing owner; no draft is applied, deleted or classified automatically by this change.

## Evidence

Real Control UI with typed synthetic mock-Gateway data, light theme, 1280×900. The Doctor-export-style draft keeps SKILL.md unchanged and adds references/rollback.md. Before is isolated pinned main; after is that baseline plus this independent commit.

**Before — matching one file incorrectly produces whole-draft discard advice.**

![Before: partial comparison incorrectly recommends discarding the draft](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/74870d1d-a1df-4f91-9c2e-c7071c2bb7be)

**After — matching instructions are reported neutrally; the remaining files still need review.**

![After: neutral instruction comparison preserves whole-draft review](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/be7d8735-6093-40e5-ae53-6d05c2365fd9)

- The real-route regression fails on isolated main and passes on the independent branch. It opens the draft, then reads the added support file and verifies that Apply/Discard remain usable without sending either mutation.
- All 25 owning page tests pass, including actual diff rendering, apply-and-follow behavior, discard, target retirement and recovery.
- UI types, focused lint, formatting, diff checks and the keyless i18n baseline command pass. The baseline command produces no generated-file delta; translation memory was not edited.
- Original advice traced to #181747; the multi-file persistence/apply contract and existing Doctor-export tests were inspected. Self-review/pr-simplify removes net 3 production lines; tests add 149 lines. No new helper, state, copy or styles.

Independent draft for human review. Independent automated review and broad PR CI are not claimed complete. No merge or deployment requested.

prs.title: fix(ui): wait for event server inventory before suggesting setup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an event automation tells users to add MCP servers before its configuration read has answered, even when a server is already configured.

## User Impact

User impact: the editor distinguishes an unknown server inventory from a confirmed empty one. A failed first read shows its real error, and the existing Refresh action can recover without leaving the editor.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing server summary already returns unknown separately from an empty list, but the event editor discarded that distinction. It now carries the unknown result and configuration error into the existing presentation. Pending reads stay deduplicated; explicit retry re-reads a failed initial configuration request.

Event-catalog validation and save admission are unchanged. Server-inventory readiness does not become a new validation gate. Genuine empty-server advice, no-events messages, source diagnostics, permissions and retired-result protection remain.

## Evidence

Real Control UI with synthetic mock-Gateway responses, light theme, 1280×900. Before is isolated pinned main; after is that baseline plus this independent commit. The normal configuration response is held while a new automation’s Event schedule is open. Screenshots are scrolled to the same Refresh control; removing the false paragraph shortens the form above it.

**Before — an unanswered read is diagnosed as missing setup.**

![Before: premature advice to add MCP servers](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b9a6c4d8-32f2-4821-8abc-b26823affd40)

**After — the existing loading state describes the pending source.**

![After: event source loading without false server setup advice](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cadb963d-5589-49e6-99bc-88395803867f)

- The false-hint regression fails on isolated main. Both browser scenarios pass on the independent branch: pending → real configuration failure → Refresh → selectable server, and genuine empty inventory. Pending Refresh does not duplicate the config read; no automation is created.

- UI types, focused lint, formatting and diff checks pass.
- Original behavior traced to #165399; the existing configuration and event-catalog owners remain separate. Self-review/pr-simplify: net +5 production lines and +104 test lines, no new state owner, copy or styles.

prs.title: fix: keep replies running after Codex catalog timeouts
prs.body:
Fixes #198970

## What Problem This Solves

A Codex model-capability lookup can time out during reply preparation and end the reply before the configured model fallback chain runs.

## User Impact

An affected reply can continue using the current owner's retained model capabilities. The selected model still has to pass the ordinary execution checks before it can answer.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both scoped thinking-catalog reads recover only from the Codex app-server scope timeout while the owner is current. The admitted path keeps its captured catalog and the published path uses its own catalog. Cancellation, other discovery errors, and route-specific input validation keep their existing behavior.

## Evidence

- Both new focused regressions failed on `0ee1de86ce37` with the reported timeout and passed with the fix. Both exercise the production catalog read with an injected native loader failure and check that aborts and other errors still propagate.
- All 47 tests passed across `prepared-model-catalog.scoped-thinking.test.ts`, `prepared-model-runtime.native-picker-failures.test.ts`, `reply-model-levels.test.ts`, and `get-reply.auto-fallback.test.ts`. The final run took 115 seconds locally, including worker preparation.
- Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. The local tested tree matches the PR head.
- Draft pending the build and remaining changed-file checks. The isolated Gateway proof that combines a native catalog timeout, a subsequent failover-eligible model error, and visible delivery is also pending.

prs.title: feat(skills): add bundled create-blobster skill and CLI renderer
prs.body:
Closes #199162

## What Problem This Solves

Agent authors and Template creators working in chat, CLI sessions, or offline template repositories have no bundled skill guidance or offline CLI renderer to validate and render deterministic Blobster `.svg` and `256×256` `.png` avatars without going through a second Gateway LLM call.

## User Impact

User impact: Agents and developers can now design Blobster avatars directly in context using the bundled `create-blobster` skill and render validated `.svg` or `256×256` RGBA `.png` files offline via `openclaw agents render-blobster <design> --out <path> [--json]`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Extracted `renderBlobsterSvgFromDesignText(text)` and `MAX_BLOBSTER_DESIGN_CHARS` in `src/agents/blobster-generation.ts` so Gateway avatar generation (`generateBlobsterForAgent`) and CLI rendering share one parser, closed schema validator, and SVG renderer without altering `AgentsAvatarGenerateResultSchema`.
- Generalized `readBoundedCliTextInput` in `src/commands/agent-message-input.ts` and added `src/commands/agents.commands.blobster.ts` + `openclaw agents render-blobster` (`src/cli/program/register.agent.ts`, `src/cli/command-catalog.ts`) supporting file or `-` stdin inputs and `.svg` / `.png` (`@resvg/resvg-js` with `font: { loadSystemFonts: false }`) outputs.
- Added bundled skill `skills/create-blobster/` (`SKILL.md`, `references/design-guide.md`, `scripts/cli.mjs` registered in `config/knip.config.ts`) and CLI documentation in `docs/cli/agents.md`.
- Opportunistic Pathfinder fix: converted the child `--import` path in `src/gateway/server-methods/agents-avatar.test.ts` to `new URL("../../../scripts/tsx.mjs", import.meta.url).href` so the subprocess test passes on Windows Node 24 ESM (`ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME` on raw drive-letter paths).

## Evidence

Rendered `256×256` RGBA `.png` produced offline with `node skills/create-blobster/scripts/cli.mjs agents render-blobster <design.json> --out icon.png`:

![Rendered Blobster avatar preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/71af2b54-ea17-4606-a7af-857c66400b44)

Validation:
- Focused tests passed (`OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1`):
  - `src/agents/blobster-generation.test.ts` (34 passed)
  - `src/commands/agents.blobster.test.ts` (11 passed — fixture SVG parity, design-guide stdin -> 256×256 RGBA PNG header verification, invalid input rejection without partial output files)
  - `src/commands/agent-message-input.test.ts`
  - `src/gateway/server-methods/agents-avatar.test.ts` (12 passed on Windows)
  - `src/cli/help-cold-imports.test.ts` (10 passed)
  - `src/skills/loading/workspace-skill-snapshot.test.ts -t Blobster` (1 passed)
- Skill validator (`quick_validate.py skills/create-blobster`): `Skill is valid!`
- `pnpm build`, `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --timed --staged --base upstream/main`, and `pnpm tsgo:all` passed cleanly with zero new dynamic-import or unused-export warnings.
- Local `$autoreview` (`codex`, `gpt-5.6-sol`, `thinking=high`) completed with no actionable findings.

prs.title: fix(feishu): escape Markdown link destinations in incoming posts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Feishu user sends a rich-text post whose link href is `https://docs.example.com)[forged entry](https://evil.example`; the channel converts the post into the Markdown the agent reads, and the model receives two links — the sender chooses the text and the destination of the second one. `renderLinkElement` escapes the link label but interpolates the sender's `href` verbatim (`extensions/feishu/src/post.ts:78`), while the title, mention, and empty-href branches around it already escape their text. CommonMark gives `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, backslash, angle brackets, and newlines structural meaning inside a link destination, so one sender-controlled href can emit extra links and block structure. Measured on `origin/main` (file blob `b119b151af0`, byte-identical at tip `e4f55593741`):

```text
href       https://docs.example.com)[forged entry](https://evil.example
markdown   [Official Docs](https://docs.example.com)[forged entry](https://evil.example)
model sees 2 links: [Official Docs]->https://docs.example.com | [forged entry]->https://evil.example
```

A href containing raw newlines similarly forges headings and list items in the message body. This change escapes exactly the characters that carry link syntax where this renderer adds that syntax, so one incoming link stays one link with one destination.

- Problem: untrusted `href` values from inbound Feishu posts were interpolated into Markdown link structure without escaping, letting the sender close the destination early and inject new links, headings, and list items into the text the model reads.
- Solution: apply the destination rule already used for inbound link URLs in `extensions/telegram/src/bot/inbound-text-entities.ts:93` — backslash-escape `( )`, percent-encode backslash, angle brackets, and whitespace — at the single composition point.
- What changed: one interpolation expression in `extensions/feishu/src/post.ts` (+3/−1), plus the href value and expected string of the first existing case in `extensions/feishu/src/post.test.ts` (net 0 test lines, no new file, no new `describe`).
- What did NOT change: the empty-href branch, label/title/mention escaping (`escapeMarkdownText`), attachment and media handling, and every href without link punctuation (byte-identical output).

## Why This Change Was Made

The escape belongs where the syntax is added. `renderLinkElement` is the only place this parser turns a sender-controlled href into Markdown link structure, and the surrounding branches already escape their text — the destination was the one unescaped interpolation. The downstream pipeline speaks CommonMark escapes, and the same rule already ships for inbound Telegram URLs and, since #199292, for fetched web anchors, so this is the established shape rather than a new convention.

Best fix: yes — one expression at the composition point neutralizes structure without changing what the link names: after CommonMark unescaping, the destination still decodes to the sender's own href (control D below).

Alternative(s) rejected: wrapping the destination in `<…>` (CommonMark forbids raw newlines inside it, and the measured newline case shows block-level forgery survives even when the link syntax breaks); percent-encoding the entire destination (changes which resource the link names and cannot express brackets consistently across renderers); a repo-wide shared link escaper (the census over composed Markdown links found exactly two sites where externally controlled text reaches link syntax unescaped — this one and the web-fetch site fixed in #199292 — and each owner already has its own escaping helper, so a new cross-layer module would be a second policy rather than a single owner).

Risk: destinations containing parens or whitespace now carry escapes, and a renderer that ignores CommonMark backslash escapes would show them literally. Non-goal: outbound Feishu card/message composition is a different owner and is not touched here.

## User Impact

Feishu posts can no longer place links, headings, or list items in front of the model that the sender's link did not declare. Ordinary links are unaffected — the benign control below is byte-identical across arms, and a destination with balanced parens still names the same URL. No new flags, no config keys, and no documentation change.

## Compatibility

- Preserved: hrefs containing none of `\ ( ) < >` or whitespace render byte-identically; the empty-href branch still prints the escaped label; balanced parens still name the same destination after unescaping (control D); title, mention, and attachment rendering unchanged.
- Related: #199292 (the other site from the same census, merged), `extensions/telegram/src/bot/inbound-text-entities.ts:93` (the inbound destination rule this copies).
- Not claimed: no change to outbound card markdown or to other channels; no claim about renderers that ignore CommonMark backslash escapes.

## Evidence

Lead proof is the real built Gateway in both arms: `node openclaw.mjs gateway` (the launcher self-identifies `OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (86a0dd5)`), each against a fresh mode-0700 scratch profile (`HOME`, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` isolated, session bus cut). Feishu runs in webhook mode with synthetic app credentials and `dmPolicy: "open"` + `allowFrom: ["*"]`; the model side is a loopback OpenAI-compatible provider that records every chat-completions request body, so the captured text is exactly what the model receives. Each cell is a complete signed Feishu event (`sha256(timestamp + nonce + encryptKey + rawBody)`, headers `x-lark-request-timestamp` / `x-lark-request-nonce` / `x-lark-signature`) POSTed to the route the Gateway registered, and all four are accepted durably in both arms. HEAD is a full runtime build of this branch (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts cliStartup`); BASE is the same tree with only `extensions/feishu/src/post.ts` restored from `origin/main` (blob `b119b151af0`) and the bundled plugins rebuilt and re-staged (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-external-plugin-local-dist.mts --control-ui-assets-prepared`, 105 plugins). The Gateway loads the channel from the built bundle, and the two executed feishu chunks differ only in the composition line — both are printed below.

| Case (signed Feishu post → captured model request) | Before — base bundle | After — this head `86a0dd5` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A: href forges a second link | 2 links: `[Official Docs]->https://docs.example.com`, `[forged entry]->https://evil.example` | 1 link; the attacker string is literal escaped destination text |
| B: href newlines forge heading/list | raw newlines survive; `# Injected Heading` and `- injected item` appear as block structure | 1 link; destination percent-encoded (`%0A`), no raw newline, no block structure |
| C: benign href (control) | 1 link `[Guide]->https://docs.example.com/guide` | byte-identical, 1 link |
| D: balanced parens (control) | 1 link, destination `…/guide(a)` | 1 link, destination `…/guide\(a\)` — same URL after CommonMark unescaping |
| webhook acceptance, all cells | 4/4 HTTP 200, `x-openclaw-delivery-accepted: durable` | 4/4 HTTP 200, `x-openclaw-delivery-accepted: durable` (identical) |

Shipped HEAD chunk `dist/extensions/feishu/.setup/reply-delivery-result-DSslMqUD.mjs`, lines 1804–1809:

```js
function renderLinkElement(element) {
	const href = toStringOrEmpty(element.href).trim();
```

prs.title: fix(claude-cli): follow-up turns on a warm process fail with "Native tool authority capture is no longer active"
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a Gateway that keeps Claude CLI processes warm between turns, every follow-up turn that reuses a warm process can fail before the model answers, with:

```
LLM request rejected: Native tool authority capture is no longer active.
```

The user sees that string as the reply. Resending works, because the failed turn kills the warm process and the next turn starts a fresh one. In our deployment this hit follow-up turns in owner direct-message sessions: 12 failed turns in 12 hours, every one of them a reuse of a warm process.

The cause is an async-context leak. A warm CLI transport is created by a session's first turn and keeps that turn's async context for every callback it makes afterwards. `execute-plugin.ts` already says so, and already works around it for one callback:

```ts
// Warm transports retain their first turn's async context across plugin refreshes.
requestToolPermission: AsyncLocalStorage.bind(requestToolPermission),
```

The other host callbacks handed to the plugin are not bound. The Claude runtime calls the host's `assertCurrent` from transport callbacks on every record (`activeTurn()` in `extensions/anthropic/cli.runtime.ts`) and swallows any throw. On a reused process that check therefore runs in the first turn's async context, where `sessionSourceScopes` still holds the first turn's prepared session-source scope. A source assertion resolved through that stale scope can refuse, and when it does the run registry retires the current run's delegated authority (`readActiveAgentRunDelegatedAuthority` releases the claim "at detection"). A few milliseconds later the turn's `system/init` record arrives, `captureNativeToolAuthority` finds the authority closed, and the turn is failed.

A fresh process is not affected, because its transport is created inside the current turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bind every host callback on the plugin execution context to the turn that builds it, instead of one of them.

`src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin.ts` binds all eight top-level host callbacks explicitly with `AsyncLocalStorage.bind` at the existing execution boundary. The maintainer repair removes the generic cloning helper and its unchecked casts, preserving callback types without weakening the assertion-safety gate.

The bind happens where the single bind already happened, inside the turn's `runWithAgentToolSourceExecutionScope`, so a fresh process behaves exactly as before and a warm process now behaves like a fresh one.

## User Impact

Follow-up turns on a warm Claude CLI process no longer fail with "Native tool authority capture is no longer active". Warm-process reuse works, so follow-up turns keep their fast start instead of failing once and cold-starting on the retry.

## Evidence

### Maintainer verification

Repaired head: `6e31b59f9b052667cc36bd3580f8bc1c3c1c26c9`. Co-author credit for @VACInc is included in the signed repair commit.

- Independent Codex autoreview: complete P0–P3 review of the full candidate and dirty repair against base `8408f1b57558d36d7bb21bf979a6275c46c20099`; no actionable findings.
- Regression reproduced on that base: the second turn observes `turn-1` instead of `turn-2`. It passes with the repaired candidate.
- 187 tests passed in seven files, covering host execution, policy, steering, native Bash, live-session registry and Claude native transport. Three test shards completed in 89.84 seconds wall time.
- Core typecheck, scoped oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` passed. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43661446254) passed, along with Workflow Sanity, CodeQL Critical Quality, OpenGrep, CodeQL and macOS Periphery. ClawSweeper revision 2 reviewed the same head and reported no actionable findings.
- No hostile behavior identified in the reviewed changes. Existing cancellation, live-authority, permission and input checks remain intact.
- No new live Gateway/provider run was performed; the original author’s integration-fork observations and their limitations remain below.

### Original author evidence

Tested head: `8aa01786f84`.

### Real behavior: a running Gateway, before and after

This is from our production Gateway (Linux, Claude Code CLI backend, Discord channel), a real build serving real turns. It is a build of our fork's integration branch: upstream `main` at `8408f1b5755` plus our other open PR branches. The "after" build adds this change. Session keys are redacted; nothing else is edited.

**Before** (12 hours, 2026-11-12 10:12 to 22:26 MST). Twelve turns failed with this error. None of the twelve logged a `cli live session start` during the turn, meaning each reused a warm process, and each failed within a few seconds. For the affected model the log has 65 process starts and 69 completed turns alongside those 12 failures:

```
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=cli:claude-cli:owner:<redacted> durationMs=763 error="Native tool authority capture is no longer active." errorName=FailoverError
[agent/cli-backend] cli terminal failure: provider=claude-cli model=claude-fable-5-2 durationMs=3736 runId=cf1a7034-ba05-4426-af6b-822c9f953b83 error=Native tool authority capture is no longer active.
Embedded agent failed before reply: Native tool authority capture is no longer active.
```

A temporary diagnostic in that build (not part of this PR) logged why the capture was refused. The grant row was untouched; the run's own authority had been retired 18 ms after the capture was activated:

```
[mcp-loopback] native tool authority capture refused: reason=authority-closed+capture-assertion(admitted run authority is no longer active) run=ab7ad29f-1b83-4af2-b3f2-158ce686d0bb session=<redacted> lastWrite=activate-capture lastWriteRun=ab7ad29f-1b83-4af2-b3f2-158ce686d0bb lastWriteAgeMs=18 phase=probe
```

**After** (same Gateway rebuilt with this change, 14 hours from 2026-11-12 22:26 MST). Zero occurrences of the error. For the affected model the log has 18 process starts, 32 completed turns and no failed turns, so at least 14 turns completed on a reused process. The first reuse after the restart:

```
22:28:36.880 [agent/cli-backend] cli live session start: provider=claude-cli model=claude-fable-5-2 activeSessions=2
22:29:13.403 [agent/cli-backend] cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-fable-5-2 durationMs=36529 outBytes=709
22:29:49.738 [agent/cli-backend] cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-fable-5-2 durationMs=23403 outBytes=1436
```

The second `cli turn` has no `cli live session start` before it: it ran on the process started at 22:28:36. That exact sequence (a follow-up turn seconds after the first) failed every time before the change.

### Regression test

`src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin.warm-context.test.ts` runs two turns through the real `executePluginOwnedProcess`. The plugin calls the host's `assertCurrent` through an async context captured during the first turn, the way a warm transport does, and the test records which turn's context the host assertion observed.

Without the change (`origin/main` `execute-plugin.ts`):

```
 ×  unit-fast  src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin.warm-context.test.ts > plugin-owned CLI warm transport callbacks > runs host assertions in the current turn's async context, not the first turn's
   → expected [ 'turn-1' ] to deeply equal [ 'turn-2' ]
      Tests  1 failed (1)
```

With it:

```
 ✓  unit-fast  src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin.warm-context.test.ts > plugin-owned CLI warm transport callbacks > runs host assertions in the current turn's async context, not the first turn's
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

Also run at this head: `execute-plugin.test.ts`, `execute-plugin.policy.test.ts`, `execute-plugin.steering.test.ts`, `execute-plugin-native-bash.test.ts`, `cli-live-session-registry.test.ts` and `extensions/anthropic/cli-runtime.test.ts` (187 tests passed), `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint and oxfmt on the touched files, and the test-lines ratchet (the new test's 43 lines are funded in `config/test-lines-allocations/cli-warm-callback-async-context.txt`).

### Proof limits

- The before/after Gateway is a fork build that also carries our other open PR branches, not a clean build of `main` plus this change.
- We did not capture which session-source assertion refused in production. The diagnostic that would have named it shipped in the same build as the fix, and no refusal has happened since. The chain from "stale async context" to "authority retired" is read from the code; what is measured is the stale context (the regression test), the retired authority (the diagnostic line), and the failures stopping (the Gateway logs).
- The failure did not reproduce in `gateway-cli-backend.live.test.ts` with a warm process on the unfixed code. Those runs have no owner or operator session source, which is consistent with the explanation above but is not proof of it.
- The regression test proves the callbacks now run in the current turn's context. It does not itself drive the registry to retire an authority.

*Written by Tank (Claude), an AI agent operated by Eddie Abrams (zeroaltitude).*

prs.title: perf(sessions): reduce queries in full context snapshots
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reading long full-fidelity session context issues one payload query per selected message, extending the agent database's read snapshot.

## User Impact

SQLite full-context reads use less CPU and allocation while returning identical messages. There is no schema, configuration, admission, generation, or prompt-prefix change. This reduces query overhead; it does not remove cold payload I/O or move caller work outside the snapshot.

## Why This Change Was Made

The snapshot owner now streams selected payloads through primary-key cursors with at most 400 bound sequence IDs. Selection metadata retains only one batch plus lookahead. It splits at sequence reversals so compaction summaries and placed background results keep their original order. Payloads remain lazy: early termination closes the cursor, and later placement errors are observed only if the consumer reaches them.

Runtime production delta is **+59 lines**. The growth preserves three existing contracts: bounded payload residency, reordered context selections, and early-consumer error timing. Random-access seed/compaction reads still need their per-entry reader; PostgreSQL retains it because its synchronous adapter buffers an entire result. The old per-entry loop is removed from SQLite's full-context path. The separate 321-line measurement script and 61 net test lines provide reproducible evidence; the test allocation is recorded. The full non-test diff is +382 lines including the harness and allocation record.

## Evidence

Synthetic SQLite fixture: 1,024 messages with 8 KiB bodies, including large tool results; a separate variant adds a compaction boundary retaining 544 messages. Base owner: `8aa2434748afb90b64e2de12b645d61f1538b8cf`, loaded into the same tooling checkout through `--owner`. Timing used AB/BA order, 1,000 iterations per arm per pair (2,000 per revision). Allocation sampling was separate: 2,000 iterations per revision for full context and 250 per revision for the compacted shape.

| Full context metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Payload statements/read | 1,024 | 3 |
| Total statements/read | 1,029 | 8 |
| Rows returned/read, including navigation | 2,052 | 2,052 |
| Payload bytes transferred/read | 8,594,233 | 8,594,233 |
| Thread CPU ms/read, paired mean | 26.472 | 24.527 (-7.3%) |
| Untraced elapsed ms/read, paired mean | 31.682 | 28.057 (-11.4%) |
| Sampled allocation MiB/read | 33.874 | 31.560 (-6.8%) |
| Instrumented warm snapshot hold ms | 46.309 | 31.127 |
| Instrumented SQLite-pages-released hold ms | 43.473 | 35.911 |
| Warm SQL / JS inside snapshot ms | 18.500 / 27.809 | 15.363 / 15.764 |
| Pages-released SQL / JS inside snapshot ms | 16.552 / 26.921 | 18.342 / 17.570 |
| Compacted context allocation MiB/read | 20.104 | 18.896 (-6.0%) |

Message digests matched across revisions in both shapes. Compacted reads returned the same 1,574 rows and 4,566,156 payload bytes. CPU pair deltas were -9.4% and -5.1%; host one-minute loads in AB/BA order were 25.41 / 25.23 / 28.89 / 28.02. Instrumented hold samples include statement/row observation overhead and are not untraced latency claims. `PRAGMA shrink_memory` releases SQLite pages, not the OS page cache; this does not reproduce a large production database's cold disk latency.

The statement observation channel produces the same normalized SHA-256 IDs as `statementTiming`: old per-entry payload `7e92aabe2f29bce1`; new 400-row cursor `72a0461ddaa69119` and 224-row tail `3eb20cb84b771cd6`; navigation `3f0163d63bf35cf1`; maintenance report scan `686838593a7d1a5f`; maintenance suffix `1e521c4fb42592a7`.

Residuals measured, unchanged: bounded seed selection used 132 statements (127 payload probes), 1,155 rows and 1,066,133 payload bytes. Cold Code Mode maintenance used 6 statements, 1,028 rows and 429 payload bytes (138,526 total text bytes including compact report facts); its 25-event incremental suffix used 5 statements, 26 rows and 201,677 payload bytes. Maintenance already batches its suffix. Its 1 MiB guard counts original UTF-16 string length; cached UTF-8 sizes and report facts cannot replace that exact cost without changing the guard or stored shape. No maintenance/schema change is included.

Reproduce with `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/context-snapshot-holds-measure.ts --iterations 1000`; add `--owner /absolute/base-owner.ts` for the base owner, or `--iterations 250 --allocations --compaction` for the compacted allocation pass. Extract the base owner from the pinned commit at `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-model-context.ts`.

The new regression fails on base: **825 statements, expected fewer than 20**. It passes with the change and covers early termination and deferred placement errors. Existing background-placement/compaction assertions now also exercise the full reader. Focused accessor and maintenance tests (13 tests), prompt-prefix tests (14), worker context/fence tests (17), and import/wrapper closure guards (24) passed locally. Root test typechecks, `tsgo:scripts`, the config test typecheck, changed-file lint/format, export-name guard, and `git diff --check` passed. The initial base regression attempt was invalidated by an edit during fixture compilation and was rerun cleanly; an initial benchmark compaction fixture lacked a timestamp and was corrected on both arms before collecting its results.

The first CI head found a benchmark-only type error: its environment object did not explicitly declare the required state directory. The fixture now constructs that field explicitly, and the failing script typecheck passed locally. The follow-up also bounds selection metadata; its 22 accessor/worker tests passed. Fresh AB/BA timing was collected on that implementation.

No whole-Gateway or live-server stress run: this follows the scoped fast-path protocol for removing repeated owner work; SQL row/byte counts and payload residency remain unchanged. No production state or server was modified. Exact-head CI at `528bfde392db155b689b80b2e212398328f27950`: `check-test-types` is green. [Node shard 14-1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43656839531/job/132637790375) fails four existing cancellation cases in `src/gateway/talk/handlers/client-native-control.test.ts:474`: the follow-up consultation emits the fallback response instead of the expected completion. The single-file command reproduced **4 failed / 10 passed** on the head and again with the sole changed runtime file replaced by its exact parent (`92016ce978f0f638369ecd0d10fcaa9212e591ce`) source; the four cases and assertion match. The unchanged test and dependency tree were used for both, and the committed candidate was restored and verified clean afterward. No CI rerun was requested for that inherited failure. [Node shard 2-1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43656839531/job/132637790493) failed in the runner startup hook before checkout/tests because the provider's 24-hour sandbox-start limit was exhausted; this is an infrastructure coverage gap, not a test result. All four PostgreSQL conformance jobs passed. At handoff, the exact CI run has 73 successful jobs, 25 skipped jobs, the two failures above, ten queued test shards, and one running test shard. Broad CI coverage remains incomplete; this is not an all-green claim. No rerun or runner-configuration change was requested. Independent review and merge are reserved for the coordinating maintainer.

prs.title: improve(ui): move Connected apps into Settings
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Connected apps is an access-management screen, but its entry appears alongside everyday workspaces in Pages.

## User Impact

Connected apps moves to **Settings → Agents & tools**, after **Automation**, and remains searchable in Settings. Direct sign-in links, pairing, permission review, and revocation stay available. No permission changes, migration, or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing plugin page and descriptor placement rather than adding a separate core page or duplicate renderer. The Settings shell now owns its navigation, Back/Escape behavior, phone drawer, and loading layout; Pages no longer lists the entry.

## Evidence

- The original placement reproduced on base 92016ce978f0f63; the Settings-shell regression failed on that base and passed with the change.
- A focused browser flow passed with the actual Control UI and MCP Relay view: final group order, Settings search, direct consent links, code pairing, leaving Settings, and the emulated phone drawer.
- 110 focused registry, navigation, sidebar, relay-consent, and grant-management regressions passed. The affected sidebar suite was rechecked after simplifying the shared row.
- UI typecheck, scoped lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. Scoped lint retains one pre-existing reactivity warning.
- Screenshots use synthetic Gateway data at a 1280 × 900 desktop viewport; the phone check uses an emulated 400 × 820 viewport. No live ChatGPT/Claude authorization was exercised.

### Before

![Connected apps listed in Pages](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/406f2516-37fd-4232-a9f3-686359242103)

### After

![Connected apps at the bottom of Agents & tools in Settings](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/00619b10-9123-4042-87fb-70975406488a)

**Maintainer verification on the corrected head:** fixed the shared-navigation import cycle by moving the existing pure plugin-tab helpers to the route-path owner, and sorted the new test's private-server inventory entry. All helper consumers were migrated; no alternate renderer, cache, permission rule or visual change was added. Two incomplete shell test fixtures now use the existing complete context helpers, preserving their assertions.

Focused navigation, Settings, shell, keyboard, panel and plugin-slug tests passed, as did the UI typecheck, scoped lint/format, the zero-cycle guard and the exact test-ownership guard. prs.body:
Related: #196199, #190670, #170562, #194024.

## What Problem This Solves

Our earlier Gateway logs showed children losing tool access or failing to return results after the parent yielded. Accepted work could still inherit the plugin call that had just ended.

**Current-main status:** Related fixes #197658 (failed-child announcement) and #197960 (deferred auth refresh) have merged. The maintainer's Telegram test with a Codex parent and child passed on clean main. Our earlier incident came from a locally modified build, and we do not yet have a fresh current-main reproduction of the broader tool-access or result-delivery failure. The evidence below supports the tested boundaries of this patch, not a claim that every related symptom persists on current main.

## User Impact

Keep accepted child work, completion cleanup and parent wake running after the originating call ends. The original caller's authority, revocation, reload self-hold and generation checks remain enforced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Detach accepted work and queued lifecycle events from the finished invocation. Carry live self-hold facts through admission, then release them. A stale event cannot settle a replacement run.

## Evidence

Public revision: `57afbb83cb76d1beb0ce95195ff9200f3d9c34b7`.

- Focused checks passed: five event/registry/SQLite cases, three reload self-hold cases, and a real registered-tool write followed by revocation.

prs.title: fix: agent roster stays unsorted and hides unread indicators
prs.body:
Closes #198515

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI agent roster stays in configured order when users select **Last updated**, even after another agent's conversation becomes more recent. Agent rows also hide whether one of their conversations is unread.

## User Impact

User impact: unpinned agents follow their latest conversation activity and update as activity arrives, including after a cached sidebar reload. Pins, stable ties, other sort modes, and selecting an agent's main conversation keep their existing behavior. Recency uses the existing shared 300-session window, excluding archived sessions; it is not an all-history ranking.

**Draft:** focused behavior is verified, but UI typecheck and performance-budget proof remain incomplete. This is not a live deployment.

Unread dots now appear on regular and pinned agent avatars when an available non-archived, non-incognito conversation is unread, including after cached sidebar reloads. Reading the main chat does not clear a different unread conversation. This reuses the existing session badge and shared activity facts without new session fetches or polling.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing canonical conversation-activity clock instead of metadata update times, apply ordering only in the unpinned roster's Last updated view, subscribe directly to activity updates, and retain display-only recency in cached sidebar snapshots. Existing snapshots without recency remain readable.

## Evidence

- **193 focused tests passed across the latest applicable runs:** activity aggregation (9), sidebar consumers (88), snapshot model (13), snapshot lifecycle (38), shared activity store/transport/message handling (38), unread live/cache regression (1), and Chromium roster behavior (6). Coverage includes public/private unread, pinned rows, live events, cached-to-live hydration, read clearing, sorting, focus, navigation, and existing work/viewport behavior. Final Chromium rerun: 6/6 passed in 40.86 s.
- **Red/green rendering proof:** separate Chromium processes at base `51c2f42a8e029f667829c753d7098af911dd7f70` and the fixed source now committed as `0982e498e8bd9b88389ceeb957bdf0a1a6899f0a`. Selecting Last updated yields `main, recent, working` on base (failing) and `recent, main, working` with the fix (passing). Screenshots below render the production sidebar component with synthetic conversation data, not a live Gateway/model session. Both were inspected and delivered in the originating chat; generated proof media/source copies are not committed.
- **Targeted lint:** 0 warnings / 0 errors across the eight touched TypeScript files. Formatting passed for all nine changed files; `git diff --check` passed.
- **Independent read-only source review:** complete nine-file local diff against the base above (now committed unchanged as `0982e498e8bd9b88389ceeb957bdf0a1a6899f0a`); no actionable findings. Reviewed activity selection, order-neutral aggregation, pin/tie/navigation behavior, owner subscriptions, cache hydration, and the existing session window. Source review only; it did not run tests or establish CI/typecheck success.
- **UI production build:** `node scripts/ui.js build` completed with exit 0; Vite reported 71 s and verified 1,030 finalized sidecars. **This is not a clean performance gate:** it reported eight budget violations (document gzip, largest JS/CSS gzip, total CSS gzip/raw, chat boot JS requests/gzip, and new boot JS gzip). They have not been attributed against an equivalent base build; no thresholds or baselines were changed.
- **Open proof gaps:** the UI TypeScript check hit its 180 s watchdog and was terminated, not passed. No full isolated Gateway/live-model end-to-end run or broad CI proof is claimed. Automatic draft CI skips do not close these gaps; exact-head qualified validation is required before marking ready.

### Before — Last updated leaves the roster in fixed order

![Before: synthetic Harbor remains above the more recently active Scout after selecting Last updated](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/649bf242-1405-496b-bd15-7475a3397983)

### After — Last updated follows conversation activity

![After: more recently active Scout moves above Harbor while the sidebar remains rendered](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dccab4ad-435f-4d87-9424-cf8fe902ba67)

### Unread indicators — reviewed follow-up

Commit `90008fbef77f051a427cf0198cf1d3be89a31e57` adds the seven-file unread follow-up. It retains display-only unread state in snapshots (legacy snapshots remain readable), excludes incognito-only unread from the agent aggregate, and preserves the existing running indicator and sort behavior. Independent read-only review found no remaining actionable findings after reproducing and fixing cached-dot loss. Targeted lint: 0 warnings/errors across six follow-up TypeScript files; formatting passed for seven follow-up files; staged whitespace check passed. Pre-commit hooks passed through the existing task-local Windows pnpm adapter; no checks were disabled.

The production-build result above belongs to the sorting commit. The unread follow-up has not had a fresh production build or successful full UI typecheck; the existing typecheck/performance gaps remain open. This PR stays draft.

The following real-sidebar captures use synthetic conversation data. They were inspected and delivered in chat; no generated media is committed. The running ring is preserved.

#### Before — unread conversations have no agent dot

![Before: Scout and pinned Forge have no agent unread dots despite unread conversations](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/130ad97c-b8d4-4758-b266-cda4c82f9977)

prs.title: fix(agents): ask_user ignores the question number in replies like "1. Deny"
prs.body: Closes #190485 Related: #173760, #173845, #146646 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: a multi-question `ask_user` answer is saved as `1. Deny`, lands on the wrong question, or is rejected when the user numbers each reply line the way the prompt numbers the questions. ## User Impact User impact: replying `1. Deny` and `2. Approved` on separate lines answers question 1 with `Deny` and question 2 with `Approved`, in any line order. A reply that answers only some questions is still rejected and the question stays open. Multi-question prompts now label questions `Question 1: Deploy` and number each question's options from 1. On Telegram and Signal, the old `1. Deploy` header ran together with the option lines into one list (`4. Checks`), so answering by the displayed number picked the wrong question. Single-question cards rendered as Telegram messages or Teams cards now number their options to match "Reply with the number". Compatibility: in a multi-question reply, a line starting with digits, a dot and whitespace (`2. Approved`) is read as an answer to that question number. `1.5`, `Node.js: 22` and `U.S. region: East` parse as before. A line matched to a question by number or id no longer also fills another question by position. On main, `2: Approved` alone completed question 1 with the text `2: Approved`; it is now rejected as incomplete. ## Why This Change Was Made The reply parser only treated `:`, `=` and `-` as key separators. `1. Deny` stayed positional, so the agent received `1. Deny` as the answer, reordered lines landed on the wrong question, and questions with fixed options rejected the reply. Numbered lines are now a separate rule that requires whitespace after the dot, checked before the unchanged keyed syntax. The single-question card text now uses the same `1. Label - description` lines as the text prompt. Multi-question prompts numbered each question (`1. Deploy`) directly above options that also start at `1.`. Telegram and Signal render markdown lists with their own numbering, so the header and the options became one list: `1. Deploy`, `2. Staging`, `3. Production`, `4. Checks`. Questions are now labeled `Question 1: Deploy`. That is not a list marker, so each question's options render from 1, and the question number is the one the `1. answer` rule binds. The first revision of this PR also copied a single-line reply into every question. That was wrong: it invented answers the user never gave and broke the incomplete-answer contract from #146646. It is removed. The multi-question guidance wording is left to #173845, so this PR no longer touches that string. The live replies in #190485 were each a single line for a two-question card, so they were incomplete and their rejection was correct. That issue is corrected. ## Evidence - Real model, real Gateway, Telegram through a local Bot API. Two Gateways ran the bundled Telegram plugin against a loopback Bot API, with `qwen3.8-27b-uncensored-r9700` behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint: one built from main `3855c896edd`, and one built from this branch merged onto it. The Gateway and Vitest ran on macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1. The model was told the exact `ask_user` arguments and made the call itself: two questions, Ruling and Authorize, each with options Approve and Deny. Every reply reached the Gateway as a Telegram update. Two runs per build gave the same results: | | main `3855c896edd` | this branch | |---|---|---| | numbered lines in the card the bot sent | `1. Ruling`, `2. Approve`, `3. Deny`, `4. Authorize`, `5. Approve`, `6. Deny` | `Question 1: Ruling`, `1. Approve`, `2. Deny`, `Question 2: Authorize`, `1. Approve`, `2. Deny` | | reply `1. Deny` / `2. Approve` | Ruling `1. Deny`, Authorize `2. Approve` | Ruling `Deny`, Authorize `Approve` | | reply `2. Approve` / `1. Deny` | Ruling `2. Approve`, Authorize `1. Deny` | Ruling `Deny`, Authorize `Approve` | | tool result in the resumed model request, reversed reply | `Ruling: 2. Approve` / `Authorize: 1. Deny` | `Ruling: Deny` / `Authorize: Approve` | | the agent's reply, reversed | `RESULT B \| ruling=2. Approve \| authorize=1. Deny` | `RESULT B \| ruling=Deny \| authorize=Approve` | | reply `1. Deny` alone | rejected (`question 'authorize' requires an answer`), question still pending, no model request in 40 s | the same | In the in-order reply, the model got the same `Ruling: Deny` / `Authorize: Approve` on this branch, and `Ruling: 1. Deny` / `Authorize: 2. Approve` on main. After the incomplete reply, both builds sent nothing to Telegram and retried the rejected message with backoff, 6 rejections in 40 s. That is #193159, which this PR does not change. - Regression table in `src/agents/harness/user-input-bridge.test.ts` (5 rows): 5/5 pass. With `user-input-bridge.ts` from main (`1b15b48e2f3`), 2 rows fail: `1. Deny\n2. Approved` is saved as `"1. Deny"`, and a lone `2. Approved` fills question 1 with `"2. Approved"`. With the previous head (`303c244630d`), 4 rows fail: lone `2` answers both questions, `1.5\n2.5` becomes `5`/`5`, and `Node.js: 22` / `U.S. region: East` split at the dot. - Consumers: 18 test files, 354 tests pass locally, including the 3 suites that failed in [run 41326074085](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41326074085): `dispatch-from-config.question-custody` 17/17, `session-accessor.question-answer-transcript` 8/8, and `test/contracts/ask-user-msteams-presentation` 2/2 (updated to the numbered lines). - New qa-lab scenario `gateway-ask-user-numbered-text-reply` (mock-openai, real Gateway): `1. Production` alone gets "The answer was not accepted: question 'checks' requires an answer" and the question stays pending. Then `1. Production\n2. E2E\n3. Urgent` resolves it as `Production` / `E2E` / `Urgent`, and the waiting run resumes with those values. With main's parser, the same reply is stored as `1. Production` / `2. E2E` / `3. Urgent` and the scenario fails. - Multi-question prompt through Telegram's markdown renderer: on `b2b86091a7f` the numbered lines are `1. Deploy`, `2. Staging`, `3. Production`, `4. Checks`, `5. Unit`, `6. E2E`, `7. Lint`. On this head they are `1. Staging`, `2. Production`, then `1. Unit`, `2. E2E`, `3. Lint`, under `Question 1: Deploy` and `Question 2: Checks`. The new test in `test/telegram-question-gateway.test.ts` fails on `b2b86091a7f` and passes here. Signal's renderer showed the same merged list before and per-question lists after. - Telegram plugin against a local Bot API stub (scripted model, not live): after an incomplete `1. Production` was rejected, the reply `3. Urgent` / `2. E2E` / `1. Production` reached the agent with the rejected line replayed in front of it (#193159), as `1. Production` / `3. Urgent` / `2. E2E` / `1. Production`. On `b2b86091a7f` those four lines resumed the agent with Production / E2E / Urgent. On main `f5f27c3ef6e` the same four lines resumed it with `1. Production` / `3. Staging (Recommended) - Safer default`. Channels without a presentation renderer already received the numbered prompt text. - `pnpm run tsgo:all`, oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` are clean. 22 test files (474 tests) pass locally. Test-line growth is 94 lines, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/ask-user-numbered-reply-lines.txt`. Merged onto main `3855c896edd`, the ratchet reads `Test lines OK: 6592462; ceiling: 6592462; slack: 0.` - Live Telegram (2026-11-10, a throwaway bot in a DM, macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1). One isolated Gateway built from main `9a5df3d60f1` with this PR's head `6e8aec42f5e` and four of my other PR heads merged in (no file touched by two of them), on the real Telegram Bot API, with QA Lab's scripted mock provider. On this head: - The three-question card arrived as `Question 1: Deploy`, `1. Staging (Recommended) - Safer default`, `2. Production - Ship to users`, then `Question 2: Checks` with `1. Unit`, `2. E2E`, `3. Lint`, then `Question 3: Note` with `1. Routine`, `2. Urgent`. - `1. Staging (Recommended) - Safer default`, then `2. Production`). Its numbered answer was not exercised in this run; the run below covers it. - Before and after on real Telegram, each build alone (2026-11-10, the same throwaway bot's DM, macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1). Two isolated Gateways, one after the other: one built from upstream main `401a1de38b9` alone, one from this head `6e8aec42f5e` alone. QA Lab's mock provider scripted the `ask_user` calls; the cards are what each Gateway rendered and sent. Production - Ship to users`). Typing `1` (after tapping `Other…`) resolved to `Staging (Recommended)` on both builds. - Three questions: main numbers questions and options in one sequence, `1. This head labels `Question 1: Deploy`, `Question 2: Checks` and `Question 3: Note`, and numbers each question's options from 1. | | main `401a1de38b9` | this head `6e8aec42f5e` | |---|---|---| | single question | | | | three questions | | | - Test cost (`pnpm test --maxWorkers=1`, Bun, the local default, macOS arm64, two runs each): `embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts` 33.0 s (cold worker cache, 22.6 s of it compiling) and 8.6 s wall, 2.0 s and 1.4 s of tests; `user-input-bridge.test.ts` 1.4 s and 1.3 s wall, 1 ms and 1 ms of tests; `ask-user-msteams-presentation.test.ts` 10.1 s and 7.3 s wall, 1.9 s and 442 ms of tests; `telegram-question-gateway.test.ts` 18.9 s and 8.4 s wall, 14 ms and 14 ms of tests. prs.title: fix(docker): skip no-op chmod calls in the build stage permission steps (#199340)
prs.body:
Fixes #199340.

## Problem

After `COPY . .`, the Dockerfile's `build` stage runs two permission steps that call `chmod` on every entry under `/app` (except `node_modules`) and on every plugin and agent file. Most entries already have the target mode. On overlayfs, even a no-op `chmod` copies the file up into the new layer, so every `COPY . .` cache miss pays for about 64k copy-ups and the layer comes out the same.

## Solution

Both steps now call `chmod` only on entries whose mode would change:

- **Source step (`a+rX`):** skips directories that already have `-perm -0555` and regular files that already have `-perm -0444` and either all or no execute bits (`X` adds execute for all only when some execute bit is set). Every other entry still reaches `chmod a+rX`.
- **Plugin and agent step:** `! -perm 0755` for directories and `! -perm 0644` for files. These are exact matches, so special bits still get cleared as before.
- **Symlinks:** the skip conditions match only `-type d` and `-type f`, so symlinks still reach `chmod`. It follows them to their targets as before, and a dangling symlink still fails the step.
- **Portability:** the predicates use POSIX `-perm` forms only (no GNU `-perm /0111`), so the regression test runs with both BSD and GNU `find`.

## Evidence

### Regression test

`src/dockerfile.test.ts` replaces the old string match with a test that runs the Dockerfile's own two `RUN` commands. It applies them to a fixture tree through a `chmod` shim that logs its arguments. The tree contains 0000, 0600, 0744, 0755, 4755 and 0644 files, 0700 directories, plugin files and a symlink, plus a `node_modules` file that must stay at 0600.

The test asserts three things:
- every entry ends at the expected mode;
- only the entries that needed a change, plus the symlink, reach `chmod`;
- a second pass calls `chmod` only on the symlink.

On `main` it fails: 21 paths reach `chmod`, including the root and already-correct files. With the fix it passes, and the final modes match `main`'s for every fixture entry.

Local: `dockerfile.test.ts` 8/8 and `docker-build-cache.test.ts` 1/1. oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check` and the test-lines ratchet are clean.

### Docker on overlayfs

Docker 29.3.1 with the overlayfs driver on 16 CPUs. A proof Dockerfile starts from the build stage's pinned `node:24.22.1-trixie` image. It does `COPY . .` of this commit's `git archive` (863 MB, 64,291 entries after the copy) and adds a few mixed-mode files and a symlink. It then runs `main`'s or this PR's two steps, extracted verbatim from each Dockerfile, as separate timed `RUN` layers. The timed stage ran with `--no-cache-filter`:

```
== main step1 43086 ms  step2 29199 ms  entries=64291
== fix  step1   261 ms  step2   223 ms  entries=64291
== main step1 137983 ms step2 26761 ms  entries=64291
== fix  step1   120 ms  step2   102 ms  entries=64291
```

A sorted `find /app -printf '%m %u:%g %y %p\n'` dump after both steps is byte-identical between `main` and the fix across all 64,291 entries. The mixed-mode probes landed at 444, 644 and 755 as expected, setuid stayed 4755, and private directories went to 755.

prs.title: fix(mcp): pending Claude permission notices grow unbounded under unique request floods
prs.body:
<!-- Start By Cursor Rule, dsq16c418qza1ri6avv10bobouk9sxcb -->
Closes #198997

## What Problem This Solves

The MCP channel bridge records every unique Claude permission notification id in `pendingClaudePermissions` with only a one-hour TTL sweep for cleanup, so a peer that sends many unique request ids grows that map linearly while the event queue next to it stays capped at 1,000.

## User Impact

User impact: sustained MCP channel traffic can no longer accumulate one pending-permission entry per unique request for up to an hour. Pending notices are trimmed at the same 1,000-entry live bound as the event queue, oldest first, and the bridge says so once per overflow on stderr until the map drains. Close and TTL-expiry behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The event queue already carries the intended live-state policy ("Retain enough history for cursor polling without letting a long MCP session grow unbounded"); the permission map sat next to it without the same bound. Dropping the oldest entries mirrors the queue's own drop-oldest behavior, keeps both structures under one policy, and needs no new configuration surface. The single stderr line gives operators the observable signal the issue asks for without spamming during a flood.

## Evidence

### Red on main (before)

`./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/mcp/channel-bridge.test.ts` on `main` (`1c0ca3120c5`) with the two new regression tests:

```text
 FAIL  ... > bounds pending Claude permissions at the queue limit under unique request floods
AssertionError: expected 1200 to be 1000   // map grew past the queue limit
 FAIL  ... > re-arms the pending Claude permission limit warning after the pending map drains
AssertionError: expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0   // no limit warning
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  2 failed | 11 passed (13)
```

### Green with this change (after)

Same command on the fix branch:

```text
 ✓ bounds pending Claude permissions at the queue limit under unique request floods 12ms
 ✓ re-arms the pending Claude permission limit warning after the pending map drains 19ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  13 passed (13)
```

### Real-class flood probe (same shape as the issue reporter's probe, via the repo test environment)

1,200 unique `handleClaudePermissionRequest()` calls against the real bridge class: map size 1,200 → 1,000 after the fix with the oldest ids evicted, newest retained, one `openclaw mcp: pending Claude permission limit 1000 reached; dropping oldest entries` line on stderr; continued overflow stays silent; a TTL sweep that drains the map re-arms the warning; `close()` drains everything.

### Checks

- Targeted oxlint (293 rules) on both files: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- Existing suite in `src/mcp/channel-bridge.test.ts` unchanged and green (11 pre-existing tests).

Boundary: not exercised through a live Gateway MCP channel end-to-end (the bridge's start path requires a Gateway connection); the proof drives the real bridge class through the repo's test environment, mirroring the issue reporter's probe approach.

prs.title: fix(cli): cancel gateway call reads that land after Ctrl+C
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

`openclaw gateway call <method>` does not forward the command's abort signal. Ctrl+C can leave a pending diagnostic read waiting, unlike the existing dedicated read commands.

## Solution

Use the existing cancellation helper for `health`, `status`, `system-presence`, `usage.cost`, `diagnostics.stability`, and `diagnostics.capabilities`. Other methods retain their existing completion/receipt behavior. This is client-side interrupt forwarding, not an authority allowlist; it neither grants nor denies Gateway methods.

The existing Gateway descriptor owner was checked. Its scopes describe authorization, not cancellation safety: `users.github.authorize.start` and `.poll` have `operator.read` plus control-plane-write metadata, and `sessions.companion.ask` can start an interaction. The write-budget flag is not an exhaustive side-effect classification either. Reusing those classifications here would discard receipts outside the six established read-only CLI contracts, so the small interruption list remains local.

## Evidence

The retained CLI regression fails on base `7f7b16cdc243309cc9d78e3aa2c961b68739ff6c` and passes on the candidate. The compact suite passes 24 tests. Removed unused discovery and usage-renderer mocks and their two stale mock-baseline records; no test-line allocation. Whole-PR deltas: production +26/-1, tests +13/-14 (net -1), mock baseline -2 records.

Natural loopback-Gateway proof uses a cloned synthetic session containing 200,001 usage turns, a wide date range, isolated HOME/state/config/profile/ports, and no delayed peer or injected faults. [Exact-head receipts and controls](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199307#issuecomment-6886745152).

No new CLI text, options, configuration, permissions, schema, or protocol changes.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: a revert restores prior interrupt behavior without changing stored data. Blast radius is the six generic diagnostic call paths; write-capable generic calls keep their existing settlement path.

prs.title: fix(nodes): cancel interrupted camera list and location reads
prs.body:
## Summary

`nodes camera list` and `nodes location get` read a paired node through the Gateway, but neither passed an abort signal to the underlying RPC. Interrupting the CLI with Ctrl+C left the `node.invoke` request pending until its timeout, so the read hung instead of settling with the interrupt.

Follow the established read-cancel pattern from #197185 (`runNodesReadCommand`): thread the async work signal through `callNodesGatewayCli(..., { signal })` so Ctrl+C owns the exit of these inventory reads.

## Change

- `src/cli/nodes-cli/register.ts`: `camera list` and `location get` now run through `runNodesReadCommand` and pass `{ signal }` to `callNodesGatewayCli("node.invoke", ...)`. Aborted interrupts are swallowed silently by `runNodesReadCommand`, matching `status`/`list`/`pending`/`describe`.
- Tests: new `register.read-cancel.test.ts` drives the real `runNodesReadCommand` with an `AsyncWorkScope` closing mid-invoke and asserts no output/exit on interrupt; camera/location mocks updated.

Precedent: #197185

## Evidence

### Discriminant tests (base RED / head GREEN)

- Base (origin/main): `register.read-cancel.test.ts` → **2 failed**
- Head: full `src/cli/nodes-cli` suite → **8 files, 76 passed** (including the new cancel tests green)

### Shipped CLI real-behavior proof (synthetic Gateway peer + PTY Ctrl+C)

Built the `cliStartup` dist for both base and head. A synthetic WebSocket peer completes the connect-challenge handshake, answers `node.list` with one fake node, and **holds** `node.invoke` so the RPC stays pending. A PTY driver runs `openclaw nodes camera list` / `openclaw nodes location get` against the peer, sends Ctrl+C (VINTR), and records exit latency and code.

| Command | Dist | Ctrl+C → exit | Exit code |
|---|---|---|---|
| `camera list` | base | 2.03s (cleanup watchdog SIGKILL) | -9 |
| `camera list` | head | **0.08s** | **130 (SIGINT)** |
| `location get` | base | 2.03s (cleanup watchdog SIGKILL) | -9 |
| `location get` | head | **0.09s** | **130 (SIGINT)** |

Head's signal aborts the pending `node.invoke`, so cleanup completes immediately and the CLI exits 130. Base has no signal: the RPC stays pending until timeout, the signal-exit cleanup watchdog force-kills after ~2s. Peer + PTY driver archived at `/tmp/nodes-proof-assets/` (synthetic peer on 127.0.0.1, synthetic token, RFC-3849-style fake node id).

## Impact

Behavior-preserving for normal operation; only interrupt handling changes for two read-only node commands.

## Root Cause
`pollXMentions()` in `extensions/x/src/events.ts` paginated through every available page in an unbounded `for (;;)` loop, retaining all parsed `XPostEnvelope` objects and `seenTokens` in memory before sorting or delivering any mention via `onPost()`.

## Fix
- Added per-poll batch bounds (`POLL_PAGE_LIMIT = 10`, `POLL_POST_LIMIT = 100`, `POLL_CHAR_LIMIT = 1_048_576`) in `extensions/x/src/events.ts`.
- When a bound is reached with a `next_token` remaining, `pollXMentions()` stops fetching further pages, delivers the current sorted batch in ascending order, persists the existing `backfill` continuation checkpoint (`{ sinceId, backfill: { sinceId, paginationToken, newestId } }`) without prematurely advancing `sinceId`, and emits a visible backfill-deferred status via `onStatus`.
- Subsequent polls resume seamlessly from `backfill.paginationToken` until pagination completes and the high-water mark `sinceId` is committed.

## Verification
- Added 3 regression tests in `extensions/x/src/events.test.ts` covering held admission on long pagination, empty-page pagination, and large retained-content character bounds.
- Ran `pnpm test extensions/x/src/events.test.ts extensions/x/src/events-budget.test.ts extensions/x/src/monitor.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (3 files, 78 tests passed).
- Ran `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, and `npx oxlint extensions/x/src/events.ts extensions/x/src/events.test.ts` (0 warnings, 0 errors).

prs.title: fix: preserve literal Windows task environment values
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: generated Windows Gateway task scripts change environment values containing carets, exclamation marks, or quotes before the Gateway process receives them.

## User Impact

User impact: newly generated Windows task launchers preserve literal environment settings, including quoted values and surrounding whitespace. Existing installed scripts keep their legacy recovery behavior and remain recognizable during managed repair, including their previous command/cwd bang escaping; normal service reinstallation regenerates the launcher. No configuration or scheduler-policy changes are introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The task script now owns its delayed-expansion setting and uses SET-specific escaping rather than inserting carets inside quoted values. Readback recognizes that same literal format, while retaining legacy installed-script parsing. The existing CLI-shim caller uses the same serialization owner.

## Evidence

- Real native Windows / Node 24.22.1: the production renderer and encoder write a temporary CMD script which launches Node through the system CMD. Exact child environment, cwd, and argv match with inherited delayed expansion both off and on; a synthetic quote/metacharacter payload cannot create its marker file. Includes percent variables/batch parameters, carets, bangs, embedded quotes, shell operators, brackets, whitespace, an empty NODE_OPTIONS clear, and representable Unicode.
- The same native regression fails on the exact base (child exit 255); the repaired version exits 0 and passes both recovery and effective readback.
- Parser contracts: 13 passing cases, including legacy recovery and rejection of ambiguous/nonliteral assignments.
- Legacy upgrade audit regressions cover ordinary previously generated scripts and static old `^!`-escaped argv/cwd (including caret-bangs), plus custom-script negative controls. Two independent P2 review findings were reproduced and repaired rather than waived.
- Final focused proof: **25 passed** (13 parser contracts, 11 task-audit scenarios, one real-CMD matrix exercising both inherited expansion settings). Production core and services-test typechecks pass. Type-aware lint (293 rules) and formatting pass on all ten changed files.
- Independent manual and canonical full-context P0–P3 final-byte reviews are clean after both reproduced P2 compatibility findings were repaired; validated canonical status `scoped-clean`, exit 0, all ten source/test hashes unchanged. CI will validate the published head separately.
- Local broad consumer runs were not all green: 26 Windows-host platform/path-case failures matched exact-base replay. A further unchanged Darwin dangling-file-symlink fixture fails `EPERM`; a standalone Node control without repository imports reproduces that host limitation. No assertions were weakened or tests skipped to conceal these results. Native Windows CLI-shim and CMD/CIM redirection suites passed.
- Scope limitation: no real task registration, daemon installation, or live Gateway changes were performed. Launcher encoding/code-page support and existing empty-value/PATH policy are unchanged.


## Windows evidence follow-up (November 14, 2026)

[Canonical exact-head package and real published-baseline launch receipts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185511#issuecomment-6887103985). Default runtime-only package build and maintained integrity checks pass, with embedded reviewed commit and preserved artifact hash. Actual published 2026.11.3 Gateway ran in a unique synthetic canonical profile and received six literal environment values unchanged. These are supplemental only: the exact repaired candidate was not installed; no expected native Scheduled Task was observed; inherited expansion OFF/ON, native settings/env preservation and persisted-data upgrade behavior remain unproven. All reviewer holds remain; no force-stop or service guard bypass.
