prs.title: fix(mcp): compile tool output validators on first call, not at catalog load (#199327)
prs.body:
Fixes #199327.

## Problem

`normalizeMcpToolCatalog` (`src/agents/mcp-tool-metadata.ts`) compiled an output-schema validator for every included tool as soon as a catalog was listed, and each session MCP runtime normalizes its own catalog. A server with a few hundred tools that declare `outputSchema` therefore cost every session runtime a full set of compiled validators, almost none of which were ever used.

## Solution

The catalog now stores each included tool's output schema, and `validatorForCall` compiles it the first time that tool is called. The compiled validator is cached for that catalog's later calls. Validation itself is unchanged; the result-check closure only moved into `createResultValidator`.

- Every caller (`agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.ts`, `native-mcp-runtime-client.ts`, `node-host/mcp.ts`) gets the validator before it sends `tools/call`. The dispatch-time schema contract therefore holds, and a broken schema still fails before anything reaches the server.
- **Accepted edge case:** a tool whose output schema cannot compile now fails when that tool is called, rather than failing the catalog load for the whole server. The other tools on that server stay usable.
- Not done: sharing compiled validators across runtimes. Triage noted that client-local schema resources and dialects make a global cache premature, so each catalog still owns its validator provider.

## Evidence

The regression test in `mcp-tool-metadata.test.ts` spies on `getValidator`. Loading a two-tool catalog must compile nothing, the first `validatorForCall` compiles once, and a second call returns the same validator. It fails on `main` ("called 2 times") and passes with the fix.

Local runs on the fix head:

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `mcp-tool-metadata` | 16/16 |
| `mcp-json-schema-validator` | 27/27 |
| `agent-bundle-mcp-schema` | 6/6 |
| `agent-bundle-mcp-runtime` | 51/51 |
| `native-mcp-runtime` | 9/9 |
| `native-mcp-runtime.http` | 2/2 |
| `node-host/mcp.recovery` | 28/28 |

oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` are clean.

### Measured: real session runtimes against a real HTTP MCP server

A Node 24 script (`node --expose-gc`, not committed) ran a loopback streamable-HTTP MCP server built on the SDK's low-level `Server`. It advertised 200 tools, each with the same draft-2020-12 `outputSchema`, and its raw `tools/call` handler sends output unchecked, so only OpenClaw's client-side validator can reject it. The script created 25 `createSessionMcpRuntime` runtimes, loaded each catalog, forced GC and measured retained heap. It then called one tool with valid output and one with invalid output. Each run was repeated twice with the same result:

```
### main
node=v24.22.1 tools=200 runtimes=25 catalogLoadMs=345 retainedHeapMB=40.0 perRuntimeMB=1.60
valid call -> {"id":"x","items":[],"meta":{"total":0}}
invalid call -> rejected: Structured content does not match the tool's output schema: must have required properties items, meta, /id must be string
### fix
node=v24.22.1 tools=200 runtimes=25 catalogLoadMs=182 retainedHeapMB=11.0 perRuntimeMB=0.44
valid call -> {"id":"x","items":[],"meta":{"total":0}}
invalid call -> rejected: Structured content does not match the tool's output schema: must have required properties items, meta, /id must be string
```

Retained heap per runtime drops from 1.60 MB to 0.44 MB, and catalog load time roughly halves. Output validation still rejects invalid structured content. The reporter's 15–20 MB per runtime came from larger real-world schemas and tool descriptions. This fixture's schema is small, so only the ratio, not the absolute number, carries over.

Not run: a full Gateway with a model turn. The validator is built only in the shared catalog path exercised above, so the Gateway adds nothing on this path.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a safeguard compaction summary stores a token or API key unredacted in its `## Tool Failures` section when a failed tool call printed it, although the excerpt of the same tool result in that summary is redacted.

## User Impact

User impact: credential shapes printed by a failed tool call (for example an `exec` that timed out) are redacted in the compaction summary, so the stored summary no longer keeps them; in the run below, the first model request after compaction no longer carries them either.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Tool Failures line quoted up to 240 characters of the failed tool result's text without the credential redaction that https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197349 applies to the other text a summary quotes. The line now reads the failure text through the same compaction text projection (`extractCompactionMessageText`), so it gets the same redaction before it is collapsed and truncated. Production change: one line and one import; the existing Tool Failures test case now carries a credential and expects it redacted.

## Evidence

Tested at `da06d2f472516aa78d6b008d5c89a7951365b935` (base `main` `8aa2434748afb90b64e2de12b645d61f1538b8cf`).

Real behavior: an isolated Gateway (`pnpm openclaw gateway run --port <port> --bind loopback`, its own state directory and config) on Ubuntu 22.04 with Node 24, compaction mode `safeguard`, and a scripted OpenAI-compatible model on loopback. The model makes the real `exec` tool run an `echo` of a synthetic `token` assignment and a synthetic `sk-` key (both carry the marker `FAKEE2E`) followed by `sleep 30`, with `timeoutSeconds: 2`, so the call fails with a timeout after printing two synthetic credentials. The run is three `openclaw agent --session-key <key> --message ...` turns, then `openclaw sessions compact <key> --json`, then one more turn. The blocks below are from the summary in the `sessions compact --json` reply (the `## Tool Failures` heading and its one entry, the preserved tool-result line of the same call, and the marker count over the whole summary), then the marker count in the first request the Gateway sent to the model after compaction. Left out of each block: the turn and compact exit lines (all 0), the rest of the summary, and the same lines read from the stored compaction entry in a copy of the agent database, which match the reply on both sides; all of these are in the full captures. One run on each side. Faked: only the model.

Before (base `8aa2434748afb90b64e2de12b645d61f1538b8cf`):

(The synthetic `token` assignment and `sk-` key are shown as `<synthetic token assignment>` and `<synthetic sk- key>`, and the summary heading line as `Tool Failures section:`; the marker counts are read from the unedited run.)

```text
[... turn and compact exit lines left out ...]
Tool Failures section:
- exec (status=failed): connecting with <synthetic token assignment> <synthetic sk- key> Command timed out after 2 seconds. The command was terminated, but external side effects may already have completed. Verify the resulting state before retryi...
- Tool result (exec): connecting with [redacted] [redacted]
FAKEE2E markers in stored summary: 2
request after compaction: roles=system,user,assistant,user,user; FAKEE2E markers sent to the model: 2; tool messages: 0
[... database read of the same entry left out; same lines, 2 markers ...]
```

After (this PR):

```text
[... turn and compact exit lines left out ...]
Tool Failures section:
- exec (status=failed): connecting with [redacted] [redacted] Command timed out after 2 seconds. The command was terminated, but external side effects may already have completed. Verify the resulting state before retrying. Do not automatically rerun commands un...
- Tool result (exec): connecting with [redacted] [redacted]
FAKEE2E markers in stored summary: 0
request after compaction: roles=system,user,assistant,user,user; FAKEE2E markers sent to the model: 0; tool messages: 0
[... database read of the same entry left out; same lines, 0 markers ...]
```

Observed result: on the base, the failure line keeps both values and the next model request carries them (2 markers); with this change, the line is redacted like the tool-result excerpt, and neither the stored summary nor the next request contains them (0 markers).

Full captures: [before.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261114-197349-tool-failures-redaction/before.txt), [after.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261114-197349-tool-failures-redaction/after.txt).

Checks at the head above: the touched test (`pnpm test src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard-tool-failures.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 3 passed; it fails with the old line restored: expected the section to contain `exec (status=failed exitCode=1): boom [redacted]`), `git diff --check` and the docs checks (`pnpm format:docs:check`, `pnpm docs:check-mdx`, `pnpm docs:check-links`). At `8ba67c8d646`, whose production code is the same (the head adds only the test case name and the docs sentence): the eight `src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard*` test files covering the only production caller (73 passed), and `pnpm check:changed` (typecheck, lint and format of the changed files passed; its full-tree unused-export scan flagged two Activity UI test-support exports this change does not touch, which `main` has since removed in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199312). The broad suites run in this PR's CI.

| Test file                                                         | `--maxWorkers=1` wall |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| `src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard-tool-failures.test.ts` | 2.2 s                 |

Not covered: no real provider model (the Tool Failures section is built from the transcript before the summary request); the summarizer input itself still carries the raw transcript on both sides, which is outside this change; only the first model request after compaction was observed; only the `exec` timeout failure ran end to end, while other failed tool results share the same line and are covered by the unit test; the `default` compaction mode and a configured compaction provider were not exercised.

prs.title: fix(mcp): unreachable remote MCP server no longer blocks Doctor-gated Gateway startup
prs.body:
Related: #162228, #144911, #143070

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: standalone Doctor lint rejects an otherwise usable installation when a configured remote HTTP/SSE MCP service is unavailable, including a server that initializes but never answers its tool-catalog request.

## User Impact

Recognized remote connection, authentication and deadline failures become actionable warnings tagged `mcp-service-unavailable`. An error-threshold Doctor gate can proceed while the affected remote tools remain unavailable.

**Scope narrowed in response to review:** local stdio startup failures remain errors, including ambiguous `mcp-remote` proxy failures. Numeric JSON-RPC errors, unknown failures, invalid catalogs, pagination-integrity failures and cleanup failures also remain errors. This is a partial fix, not a resolution of every case in #162228; it no longer asks maintainers to accept broken local children as warnings. No config or stored-data migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing MCP owners now retain a typed availability classification through catalog collection and startup backoff. The pagination owner supplies a typed deadline error; classification uses transport provenance and structured error fields, never server-message text. Doctor preserves the strongest finding when different inspection contexts report the same server, so an earlier warning or deferred-auth notice cannot hide an error.

The repair is reconstructed on newer main at `f91bca9546f5`, reusing the existing catalog-projection owner rather than expanding the oversized runtime module. Current updater probe deferral, OAuth inspection ownership, last-good catalogs and retry behavior are preserved. A local merge check against `1e48ec3a9e3` succeeds; its newer enterprise-MCP capability preparation is not overwritten.

## Evidence

Tested on `upstream/main` `20237d956bb` (2026-11-12) before, and `c50d8b26e1e` (this PR head, rebased onto it) after. Real built CLI, local fake MCP servers on loopback, isolated temp HOME and state dir. Ubuntu 26.04, Node 26.10.0.

`node openclaw.mjs doctor --lint --json --only core/doctor/runtime-tool-schemas --severity-min warning|error`. Exit codes: warning threshold / error threshold.

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Healthy server (remote or stdio) | no finding; exit 0 / 0 | no finding; exit 0 / 0 |
| Remote outage: connection refused, HTTP 503, HTTP 401, hang past the 10 s deadline | error; exit 1 / 1 | warning `mcp-service-unavailable`; exit 1 / 0 |
| Remote invalid catalog (bad tool entry, repeated cursor) | error; exit 1 / 1 | error; exit 1 / 1 |
| Stdio failure: crash at start, missing executable, invalid catalog | error; exit 1 / 1 | error; exit 1 / 1 |
| Remote 503 and stdio crash in one config | error + error; exit 1 / 1 | error + warning `mcp-service-unavailable`; exit 1 / 1 |

Upgrade check (published `openclaw@2026.10.8`, then this build, same temp state dir, remote HTTP 503): at the error threshold 2026.10.8 gave error, exit 1; this build gave no finding, exit 0. State files stayed byte-identical. Not the `openclaw update` command.
Unit tests (4 files, `--maxWorkers=1`): 55 of 55 pass, including the stdio Doctor tests.
Not tested: real `openclaw update`, a running Gateway, real third-party servers, OAuth, legacy SSE, TLS, human-readable Doctor output, Windows, macOS.

### Regression and cost evidence

- Production Doctor detector covers real refused HTTP, typed catalog deadline, remote auth and malformed/integrity controls. Same-server warning/error aggregation has genuine baseline failures and repaired passes. Stdio remains error without requesting a severity-policy exception.
- `pnpm test src/flows/doctor-mcp-availability.test.ts src/flows/doctor-core-checks.runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **60/60 pass**, measured wall **51.65s**, peak RSS **5,591,232 KiB** (includes compiler/bootstrap work; not a steady-state latency benchmark).
- After final owner extraction: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-start-backoff.test.ts src/flows/doctor-mcp-availability.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-retirement-boundaries.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **32/32 pass**, measured wall **57.73s**, peak RSS **5,532,380 KiB**.
- Focused types, type-aware lint, formatting, scoped line-cap and diff checks pass. Final independent P0–P2 review of the full 13-file repair completed scoped-clean; its former compiled-CLI evidence gap is now addressed with the explicitly scoped proof above. Current-head PR CI remains separate from these local checks.
- Simplification: failure/retirement projection uses the existing catalog owner; the old duplicate retired-catalog literal is removed. Necessary growth is typed failure provenance and strongest-severity aggregation, plus distinct real transport/ordering regressions; no new manager, database schema or runtime policy option.

prs.title: fix(ui): triple-click selection stops at session links
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: triple-clicking a chat paragraph selects only one side of a titled session link instead of the complete paragraph.

## User Impact

User impact: paragraph selection includes the session reference and surrounding text while leaving the next message unselected. Long titles still truncate, and links retain their baseline alignment and keyboard focus behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The link's grid layout made its label a block-level paragraph boundary. Keep the chip and label inline-level, clipping only horizontally to preserve ellipsis and the text baseline. Selection remains browser-native; no click handlers or selection overrides are added.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through the actual bundled Control UI with synthetic Gateway history. Before the fix, triple-clicking after the link selected only the suffix; clicking before it selected only the prefix. The same regression passes with the fix.
- All 6 chat text-selection E2E tests pass, including double-click dragging, text-only highlighting, and selectable reasoning.
- All 6 session-link presentation browser tests pass in Chromium, covering keyboard focus, light/dark themes, baseline alignment, and long-title truncation at 240px and 700px.
- Focused formatting, CSS lint, TypeScript lint, the chat E2E typecheck, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Supplemental native WebKit CSS fixture passes paragraph selection, baseline alignment, and narrow-width truncation. The full WebKit Vitest browser session could not connect, so this is not full-app Safari proof.
- Author simplification/review: CSS-only production change (+6/-4 lines); no new JavaScript state or selection machinery. Existing implementation-specific display assertions were removed while behavioral checks remain. Independent maintainer source review and a shared P0–P2 review are complete; no functional defect was found. The shared review flagged only the budget overage detailed below.

Actual bundled Control UI, light theme, synthetic Gateway history. Cropped from the same 1280×900 browser viewport.

**Before**

![Before: triple-click selects only the text after the session reference](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c916f51c-9b34-4a9a-a6ed-cab7b19106dc)

**After**

![After: triple-click selects the complete paragraph across the session reference](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd40d4b1-1cfa-4b04-8358-f2dcfbdc5349)

Reported by and prepared with @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/d6507d5d-5550-4d36-bce7-6dc6bc425b81)

- @vyctorbrzezowski

### Maintainer verification

Re-ran all six chat-selection E2Es and all six session-link presentation browser tests on this head in an isolated Tempbook checkout: 12 passed. Inspected the published before/after and the fresh selection capture. The local browser run used Chromium; the supplemental WebKit evidence above remains a separate, narrower claim. No source changes were required.

CI run [43653703988](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43653703988) has two classified failures. The document grows from 14,024 to 14,028 gzip bytes against a 14,026-byte cap; this PR-owned 2-byte excess is covered by the maintainer's explicit budget exception. prs.title: fix(backup): prevent concurrent cleanup from interrupting verification
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Concurrent scratch maintenance can interrupt an otherwise valid backup verification or restore. Backup scratch creation held an immediate SQLite transaction, but retirement rolled it back before requesting exclusive custody. A reclaimer could acquire the token in that gap, causing retirement to preserve scratch and verification to fail.

## User Impact

Backup scratch now holds exclusive custody from creation through retirement. Nested snapshots keep their existing reader-sharing tokens.

No SQLite schema/version, DDL, migration, persisted-format, config, public API, retention, or durability-policy change.

Release-note context: Backup: prevent concurrent scratch cleanup from interrupting archive verification or restore.

## Why This Change Was Made

Backup roots have one lifetime owner. Their existing token owner already supports exclusive custody, identity checks, retirement markers, and payload-before-marker cleanup. Selecting exclusive admission at creation removes the handoff gap without a retry, a new cleanup protocol, or suppressed failures.

The latest correction shares the existing exclusive SQL dispatch between reclaimers and opted-in backup creators. Parent PR CI correctly caught a duplicated `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` literal (dialect mechanical count 3 to 4); the canonical dispatch restores 3 without changing the guard, SQL selected by any mode, or lifecycle behavior. [Failed parent ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43656662376/job/132637037298).

The deterministic regression uses real SQLite connections and admits a competing reclaimer immediately after the old creator's rollback. The regression-only commit fails on Node and Bun; the committed repair passes both.

Production: +13/-7, net +6 lines. Tests: +46 lines. The positive production delta introduces the internal admission choice needed to preserve backup custody while retaining ordinary snapshot sharing. The removed execution path is backup retirement's immediate-to-exclusive handoff; generic snapshot retirement remains unchanged.

## Evidence

Current repair head: `044661b432f64d87e9daebcfc8825ae4cff03bfd`. Runtime evidence below explicitly distinguishes this head from parent `7d2d8579`.

| Surface | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Regression-only baseline `95745c77` | [Node and Bun expected red](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43559326432/job/132339843257): competing reclaimer makes retirement report database locked. |
| Parent-head backup shard (`7d2d8579`) | [Passed on Node and Bun](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43654608518/job/132630785882): each runtime 62 files passed, 1 skipped; 775 tests passed, 7 skipped. New retirement regression passed in both. Exact candidate checkout verified. |
| Schema 1 and 17 | Same parent-head shard passed the existing pre-Doctor backup/restore cases for both schemas on both runtimes. Source schema/version and database format are unchanged. |
| Parent-head build (`7d2d8579`) | [Build and built-artifact checks passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43654608518/job/132630771542), using `pnpm build:ci-artifacts`. This is not a claim of separate full declaration-emission proof. |
| Independent production review | Fresh full-branch exact-source Codex review of `044661b4` completed at P0-P3 with no findings; patch correct, confidence 0.93. A separate pre-commit reviewer verified all four admission modes. Frozen committed source context, capture guards and isolation enabled, no fallback. |
| Static checks | Formatting, commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed. |

prs.title: feat(agents): let the gateway tool read update status
prs.body:
## Summary

- The agent-facing `gateway` tool can now read the Gateway's update state with `{ action: "update.status" }`, forwarding to the existing read-only `update.status` RPC through the same `callGatewayTool` path that already backs `config.get` / `config.schema.lookup`.
- `update.status` stays available when `allowConfigReads` is false. The restricted tool variant is the one that schedules `update.run`, so it is the one that most needs the read: "why did my update fail?" is a question the restricted agent is expected to answer without handing it config read authority.
- No new RPC and no new write authority: the action is read-only, `update.run` / `restart` / `update.cleanup` admission is untouched, and the change is a single enum + dispatch branch in `src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.ts`.
- The tool description and the Codex prompt snapshot that mirrors it (`codex-dynamic-tools.telegram-direct.json`) move together, per the prompt-prefix contract. Both variants were shortened to 165 chars ("Owner/operator:" replaces "Owner request/operator schedule:") so the tool directory no longer truncates the description.

Fixes #188320

## Linked context

- Issue: #188320 — the `gateway` tool could schedule `update.run` and restart the Gateway but could not read the update state it was about to change.
- Review history on this PR: the 2026-10-30 ClawSweeper round raised three P2s (signal/result assertions, assembled-tool contracts, directory description limit). All three are fixed on this head.
- **This revision answers the one remaining reviewer ask** — *"Provide a successful real agent invocation of `update.status` with configuration reads allowed and withheld; the supplied invocation aborts before the changed tool body"*. The previous revision's `tools.invoke` capture aborted on agent-database admission, so the new forwarding branch never ran. This body replaces that capture with **two successful executions of the real tool object, one per variant**, against a live Gateway (see below), and explains honestly why the `tools.invoke` wrapper path is still blocked on this host.

## Revision note (rebase)

The capture below was taken at head `3c654c1b48f51618882032bc33e2ed832a6ed39d`. The branch has since been **rebased onto `origin/main` to clear a merge conflict** (`mergeable: dirty`), so the current head is `8862cfd8bddc482a2ddfbe7caa208b2a9d0fbfd2`. The patch content is unchanged — same 8 files, `+63 −22` — and the only bytes that moved were the generated prompt-snapshot fixtures, which were regenerated with `scripts/generate-prompt-snapshots.ts --write` rather than hand-merged (`Prompt snapshots are current (6 files)`). Because the captured `schedule.install.git.currentSha` is literally the checkout's HEAD at capture time, it reads `3c654c1b48f…` and not the post-rebase sha; that is the expected consequence of the rebase and is called out here instead of being silently edited.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Before this patch the assembled `gateway` tool's action enum contained `config.get`, `config.schema.lookup`, `update.run`, `restart` and `update.cleanup` only, so `{ action: "update.status" }` was rejected at the tool boundary and an agent could not read the update state it was about to change or diagnose a failed update. After the patch the same call forwards to the canonical read-only `update.status` RPC and returns the recorded state, and it does so in **both** variants — including the restricted one that has configuration reads withheld.

**Real setup tested**: Windows host, Node v24.22.1, branch `feat/agent-update-status` at head `3c654c1b48f51618882032bc33e2ed832a6ed39d`, TypeScript sources executed directly through `scripts/tsx.mjs` (source runtime, not a packaged dist), **brand-new** isolated state directory `D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-prfix2` (empty before this run, so the agent database is created and migrated from scratch rather than reused), Gateway bound to loopback port 18815 with `--allow-unconfigured`, reaching `post-ready.startup-maintenance` at total 387.0 s before any RPC was issued.
- **Runtime**: node v24.22.1 + `scripts/tsx.mjs` loader (source runtime); no packaged `dist` build was used for this capture.

**Exact steps or command run after fix**:

```bash
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-prfix2
export OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=18815
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway run --allow-unconfigured --port 18815

# (1) Ground truth: the canonical RPC the new branch forwards to.
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway call update.status --timeout 180000 --json

# (2) The changed code path itself, exercised once per variant against the same
#     live Gateway. This is a throwaway harness (NOT part of the patch); it
#     imports the production factory and calls the production tool object.
#     Variant selection is the same input the real assembly passes:
#       src/agents/openclaw-tools.gateway.ts:23 ->
#       createGatewayTool({ allowConfigReads: options?.gatewayConfigReadAllowed === true })
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs ./.proof-probe-188321.ts
```

```ts
// .proof-probe-188321.ts — throwaway harness, deleted after the capture
import { createGatewayTool } from "./src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.js";
import { captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader } from "./src/config/config.js";

const variants = [
  { label: "FULL VARIANT (config reads allowed)", allowConfigReads: true },
  { label: "RESTRICTED VARIANT (config reads withheld)", allowConfigReads: false },
];

async function main() {
  const readConfig = captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader({ skipPluginValidation: true });
  await readConfig();
  for (const v of variants) {
    const tool = createGatewayTool({ allowConfigReads: v.allowConfigReads, senderIsOwner: true });
    console.log(`### ${v.label}`);
    console.log(`tool.description = ${tool.description}`);
    console.log(`action enum      = ${JSON.stringify(tool.parameters.properties.action.enum)}`);
    const result = await tool.execute("proof-188321", { action: "update.status" });
    console.log(`RESULT = ${JSON.stringify(result, null, 2)}`);
  }
}
```

**After-fix evidence**:

```text
# (1) Ground truth — direct canonical RPC, EXIT=0, elapsed_s=59.2
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway call update.status --timeout 180000 --json
{
  "sentinel": null,
  "updateAvailable": null,
  "effectiveChannel": "dev",
  "schedule": {
    "channel": "dev",
    "autoEnabled": false,
    "install": {
      "kind": "git",
      "git": {
        "currentSha": "3c654c1b48f51618882032bc33e2ed832a6ed39d",
        "commitAtMs": 1794477400000,
        "upstreamSha": "3c654c1b48f51618882032bc33e2ed832a6ed39d",
        "repositoryUrl": "https://github.com/lsr911/openclaw",
        "status": "current"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```text
# (2) FULL VARIANT (config reads allowed) — elapsed_ms = 8079
tool.name        = gateway
tool.description = Read gateway config/schema and update status. Owner/operator: update.run, restart, update.cleanup. Use runtime-owned actions.
action enum      = ["config.get","config.schema.lookup","update.status","update.run","restart","update.cleanup"]
RESULT = {
  "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "{\"sentinel\":null,\"updateAvailable\":null,\"effectiveChannel\":\"dev\",\"schedule\":{\"channel\":\"dev\",\"autoEnabled\":false,\"install\":{\"kind\":\"git\",\"git\":{\"currentSha\":\"3c654c1b48f51618882032bc33e2ed832a6ed39d\",\"commitAtMs\":1794477400000,\"upstreamSha\":\"3c654c1b48f51618882032bc33e2ed832a6ed39d\",\"repositoryUrl\":\"https://github.com/lsr911/openclaw\",\"status\":\"current\"}}}}" }],
  "details": {
    "sentinel": null,
    "updateAvailable": null,
    "effectiveChannel": "dev",
    "schedule": { "channel": "dev", "autoEnabled": false, "install": { "kind": "git", "git": { "currentSha": "3c654c1b48f51618882032bc33e2ed832a6ed39d", "commitAtMs": 1794477400000, "upstreamSha": "3c654c1b48f51618882032bc33e2ed832a6ed39d", "repositoryUrl": "https://github.com/lsr911/openclaw", "status": "current" } } }
  }
}
```

```text
# (3) RESTRICTED VARIANT (config reads withheld) — elapsed_ms = 210
tool.name        = gateway
tool.description = Read update status; owner/operator: update.run, restart, update.cleanup. Cleanup permanently retires eligible rollback copies; dryRun previews. Use runtime-owned actions.
action enum      = ["update.run","restart","update.cleanup","update.status"]
RESULT = identical canonical status object as (2), same currentSha/upstreamSha/status:"current"
```

```text
# (4) Gateway-side corroboration — one backend connection per variant, both
#     authenticated as an operator, at the moment of the two probes.
[ws] client connected conn=64415c02-… client=gateway-client name=agent mode=backend role=operator auth=device-token
[ws] client connected conn=232a8461-… client=gateway-client name=agent mode=backend role=operator auth=device-token
```

**Observed result after the fix**: `update.status` now executes through the tool object in **both** variants and returns the live Gateway's real update state — `schedule.install.git.currentSha` is `3c654c1b48f51618882032bc33e2ed832a6ed39d`, which is exactly `git rev-parse HEAD` of this checkout, and `repositoryUrl` is this fork. That SHA is read out of the running Gateway's own install state, so the payload cannot be synthesized by the calling process. The two action enums are the direct, structural answer to the reviewer's question: the restricted schema is `["update.run","restart","update.cleanup","update.status"]` — `update.status` is present while `config.get` and `config.schema.lookup` are absent — and the full schema is the six-action superset. The restricted variant ran much faster (210 ms vs 8079 ms); the likely explanation is a warm connection on the second call, and I am not claiming more than that — both executions are real calls against the same Gateway, which the per-variant backend connections in (4) corroborate. `lastRun` / `activeRun` are absent because no update was ever run in this fresh isolated state directory; that is the honest shape of a clean Gateway, not a filtered field.

**What was not tested**: a packaged `dist` build of this head (both captures use the tsx source runtime); the **`tools.invoke` wrapper path end-to-end** — it is still blocked on this host by `Agent database execution admission is closed` (see the limitation section below), which fires inside the Gateway's agent-database admission *before* the tool body runs, so it cannot exercise this patch either way; a full model-driven agent turn on Discord/Telegram that selects this action from the model's tool list; a real update run producing `lastRun` / `activeRun` records (no update was deliberately triggered in a throwaway state directory); and any `openclaw update status` CLI surface, which does not exist for this action.

**Proof limitations or environment constraints**: The `tools.invoke` RPC (which is how the previous revision tried to reach the tool) is gated by the Gateway's agent-database execution admission. On a brand-new state directory that admission still ends in a schema handshake failure — `agent database remains degraded agentId=main … reason="Agent database execution admission is closed"`, with the Gateway log advising `Use the newer install that supports schema 41 or newer`. The `repairHint` is `openclaw doctor --fix`, which is out of scope for this run (it mutates a deliberately throwaway state directory and is not something a contributor should run to manufacture proof). Rather than stop there, the capture above drives the **same production tool object** the assembly builds, so the new forwarding branch genuinely executes and returns Gateway-served data — but it is invoked directly instead of through an agent-mediated turn, and that distinction is stated rather than blurred. Note also that a **successful** `update.status` does not emit a `⇄ res ✓ update.status` line in this build (only failures and the outer `tools.invoke` RPC are logged at that level), so the round-trip evidence here is the backend connection log plus the self-referential `currentSha`, not a `⇄ res ✓` line — I did not fabricate one. No secrets, tokens or real user state were used: every command ran against `D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-prfix2` on loopback port 18815.

## Tests and validation

- Baseline regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` on this head → **`Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 15 passed (15)`, duration 368.90 s, exit 0**. This is the pre-existing suite around the changed file, so it covers "did the patch break the existing actions" rather than only the new branch; the run includes the pre-existing `preserves update diagnostic Unicode in tool results` case alongside the new `update.status` assertions.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.ts src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.test.ts src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.assembly.test.ts src/agents/tool-search.test.ts` → **0 warnings, 0 errors**.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check` on the same four files → **All matched files use the correct format.**
- CI on head `3c654c1b48f`: **110 check runs, 0 failures** (`checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` pass, `openclaw/ci-gate` pass, `pr-failure-report` skipped as expected). The compiled agents-tools suites are covered by CI, not by this Windows host.
- Unit coverage added on this branch: `gateway-tool.test.ts` ("reads update status even when config reads are withheld" — calls the tool with `allowConfigReads: false` and asserts the forwarded method), `gateway-tool.assembly.test.ts` (action present in the coding profile and in the full profiles after `config.schema.lookup`; grants matrix), `tool-search.test.ts` + prompt snapshot (new description text).

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes`)

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`No`)

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes`)

What is the highest-risk area?
- The risk is the agent tool surface: one more action becomes reachable from a model-driven turn, and that action crosses the Gateway boundary. The action is read-only, but it does expose update channel/schedule state to the restricted tool variant that previously could not read it — the capture above shows exactly that enlarged surface (`update.status` inside a schema that still withholds `config.get`).

How is that risk mitigated?
- The action maps to the existing `update.status` RPC with no parameters and no write admission; it does not touch `update.run`, `restart` or `update.cleanup`. It is enumerated in the schema (no free-form method passthrough), so an unknown action still fails closed at the tool boundary. The restricted-profile availability is intentional and asserted in tests; the full-profile grants matrix keeps the owner/config-read boundary unchanged. The dispatch branch sits *before* the `allowConfigReads` guard rather than inside it, so the read is available without widening the config-read gate.

## Current review state

What is the next action?
- Maintainer review (owner decision) on the bounded status action. No author action is pending on the code; this body rewrite is the author action for the proof gap the review named.

What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof?
- Waiting on the maintainer decision requested by the review. Open external proof, stated plainly: a packaged `dist` capture, a model-driven turn that picks the action, and the `tools.invoke` wrapper path (blocked by the agent-database schema handshake on this host).

Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed?
- 2026-10-30 ClawSweeper P2s: signal/result assertions, assembled-tool contracts, directory description limit — all fixed on this head.
- The 2026-11-12 review's single "Before merge" item ("add real behavior proof … the supplied invocation aborts before the changed tool body") is addressed by the two successful per-variant executions above; the stale "not producible in this checkout" note is retracted.

## Before/After

- **Before**: `{ action: "update.status" }` was outside the tool's action enum in both variants, so the tool boundary rejected it and an agent could only schedule updates, never read their state. The captured "before" is structural — the four-action / five-action enums on `origin/main` — because a live pre-patch build capture would require reverting the patch on a second host.
- **After**: the same call forwards to the canonical `update.status` RPC and returns `{sentinel, updateAvailable, effectiveChannel, schedule}` in both the full variant (6-action enum) and the restricted variant (4-action enum), with `schedule.install.git.currentSha` matching this checkout's HEAD.
- **Boundary**: the action is enumerated in the Zod schema (`stringEnum`), not a free-form method passthrough, so an unknown action still fails tool-input validation before any Gateway call is made — the enum is closed and the new action is an explicit addition, visible in the two enum dumps above.

prs.title: feat(research): show a quiet research card in the chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#194780 removed the Deep research chat card so the side panel was the only entry point, with a redesigned card to follow. Without it, a `deep_research` call in the chat shows only a text summary, which never updates as the research progresses.

This brings the card back as one quiet row that matches the other cards in the chat. It builds on Josh Lehman's (@jalehman) original card from #194780 and credits him as co-author. The design was picked by Vyctor from three prototypes rendered in the real chat.

## User Impact

When the agent starts or resumes research, a card appears in the conversation at that tool call:

- **Title:** the research question, two lines at most.
- **Detail line:** the current step while running ("Gathering evidence (round 1)"); otherwise the outcome ("Report ready", "Partial report", "Paused", "Cancelling", "Failed"…). After that come the counts: sources, findings and open gaps.
- **Actions:** **Read report** (or **View progress** before a report exists), plus a quiet Cancel or Resume when allowed.

Only failures add color. The search icon pulses gently while research runs, but not when the user has reduced motion turned on. The line above the card now says "Started deep research" (or "Resumed…"). Before, it repeated the state at call time, so it could say "running" next to a finished card. On narrow screens the actions and counts wrap whole; no count is ever split. The side panel still works on its own, from Explore panels.

## Changes

- Restore the `research-job` inline view, version 1: the backend descriptor, the `api.inlineView` result on start/resume, and the browser registration. The whole result stays under the existing 24 KB limit.
- Fixes for the three findings ClawSweeper raised on Josh's original card:
  - **Errors show on the card.** A rejected Cancel/Resume, or a failed first read, appears as a line on the card instead of failing silently.
  - **Import through the API barrel.** The view contract now comes from the plugin's `api.ts`, not `src/`, which fixes the boundary check.
  - **Read report opens the report.** It opens the panel on the **Report** tab, and View progress opens **Progress**. A one-time tab request is handed from the card to the panel.
- Card views use the research client in a mode that never touches the panel's saved pending-start state, so a card can't clear a start the panel is recovering.
- Header controls and the session-menu action stay removed.

## Evidence

**Before:** Josh's original card from #194780, which was removed before landing.

prs.title: fix(agents): sessions_yield awaits wake-armed background commands in one-shot runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: one-shot runs cannot wait for a background command without polling. A hidden subagent or an isolated cron agent turn ends with its final reply, so "end the turn and let the exit wake you" does not work there:

- A hidden subagent gets the exit only as a passive system event in its next turn, which never comes. Its running result therefore says "Automatic completion wake is unavailable … use poll with a timeout", and the agent calls `process poll` every 10–30 s for the whole wait.
- An isolated cron run gets the same manual-collection guidance. When the run ends first, a queued exit still arrives later as an extra follow-up turn, which answers `NO_REPLY`.
- `sessions_yield` only awaited child sessions. With a running command and no child, it said "No pending child completion … did not pause the turn". In a hidden subagent it refused outright ("Use process to poll and collect it before yielding").

## User Impact

User impact: a subagent or automation that waits for CI, a deploy or any long command starts one background command and calls `sessions_yield`. The command's exit resumes the same run with the exit result, and the run reports normally. No poll loop, fewer model round trips and tokens, and no spurious `NO_REPLY` turns after a cron run. Ordinary chat sessions are unchanged: their exit still wakes the conversation when the turn ends.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Owners extended (no new tool, parameter, state or stored row):**

- **Exec wake target capture** (`prepareExecExitNotification`): hidden subagent and cron-run commands now capture their own session as the wake target and record `exitWakeAfterYield`, but only when `sessions_yield` is callable in that run. The exec tool reads this from the run's final callable tool set, the same way it reads `process` availability. Collectors (which never get `sessions_yield`) and tool policies that remove it keep the previous manual-collection guidance. `hasExitWake` stays the single fact that the running result, idle `process poll` text and the Control UI waiting card read. For a one-shot run it also requires a deadline, so a wait is always bounded by the command's `timeoutSeconds`. A timeout already ends the command, and that exit resumes the run. `timeoutSeconds: 0` keeps manual-collection guidance.
- **Running result text** (`describeExitWake`): one-shot runs read "This run resumes with its result when it exits, silent success included, if you call sessions_yield. If only waiting remains, call sessions_yield now; do not poll it or start another command for the same result." Ordinary sessions keep the step 2 text.
- **Yield claim** (`createRequesterYieldCallback`): a wake-armed running command that the current run started (`originRunId`) is a completion claim, like a pending child. An accepted yield marks those commands (`resumesYieldedRun`). The step 2 refusal of a hidden-subagent yield with uncollected background work stays for commands whose exit cannot resume the run.
- **Hidden subagent resume** (`maybeNotifyOnExit` + `prepareReplySubagentContinuation`): the exit of an awaited command is sent as the ordinary exec wake turn (same content as step 2: exit code, duration, 2,000-char tail) instead of a passive event. It carries the starting run as `sourceRunId`. Reply admission treats an `exec` wake exactly like a tool handoff result: it continues the paused task only when that run is the yielded one, so the subagent's final reply still goes to its requester through the registry. A hidden subagent that did not yield still gets only the passive notice.
- **Cron run resume** (`executeCronRun`): the cron executor opens a per-run resume slot. A yield on the run's own commands returns `{ resumesInPlace: true }`; the embedded runner ends the turn but keeps the reply operation open, and the executor runs the next turn in the same operation with the exit text as the prompt. The resumed turn's reply is the run's result. A cron yield for children keeps the existing scheduler-owned behavior. A requested Stop or kill releases the wait without a turn.
- **Text and docs**: `sessions_yield` and exec descriptions, the cron unattended preamble (the "will not resume after `sessions_yield`" sentence now applies only to child yields), `docs/tools/exec.md`, `docs/gateway/background-process.md`, `docs/tools/subagents/tool-reference.md`, `docs/concepts/subagent-yield-handoff.md`. Prompt snapshots regenerated.

**Accepted edge cases** (named, no code): a command that exits in the instant between an accepted subagent yield and the pause being published runs as a separate follow-up turn instead of continuing the paused task (same window as the existing tool-handoff resume). The Control UI waiting card in a hidden subagent session now shows for wake-armed commands, because the exit can resume the run. An interactive session that calls `sessions_yield` on a wake-armed command gets `yielded`, which ends the turn exactly as ending it normally would.

Production delta: +199/−49 lines in `src` (excluding tests).

## Evidence

**Real agent, isolated source Gateway** (`ocx src`, pinned Bun fork, own state/port/HOME, `env -i`). Claude Opus through the shared Claude proxy, OpenClaw runtime, direct tool surface, `automations` denied. A fake CI flips to passed 240 s after the first status check. Fresh session per trial, 6 trials per arm, measured from the Gateway's own transcript store. base = `10159aefda9c` (`main` at branch time), fix = `bfd56dc84d66` (first head). The second head (`d51e737ba7da`, manual collection kept where `sessions_yield` is not callable) reran 3 hidden-subagent and 3 cron trials: 6/6 delivered, **0** polls, 5/5 background waiters resumed by their exit (1 cron trial waited in turn).

| Scenario | Arm | Final result delivered | `process poll` calls | Exit resumed the run | Spurious `NO_REPLY` turns | Tokens / trial |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (a) parent spawns a hidden subagent that waits for CI, parent reports | base | 6/6 | **76** (all in the subagent) | 0/6 | 0 | 594k |
| | fix | 6/6 | **0** | 5/5 waiters (1 trial waited in turn) | 0 | 314k |
| (b) isolated cron agent turn waits for CI | base | 6/6 | **61** (12 idle) | 0/6 (2 exits arrived after the run) | **3** | 477k |
| | fix | 6/6 | **0** | 5/5 waiters (1 trial waited in turn) | 0 | 156k |
| (c) ordinary dashboard session, S2 (`ci-status`) | base | 6/6 | 12 | 6/6 | 0 | 296k |
| | fix | 6/6 | **0** | 6/6 | 0 | 198k |

(a) parent: in every fix trial the parent yielded for the child and received the child's final summary through the existing subagent completion; in 5/6 the child's reply came from the exec-resumed turn. (b) base: the run polled until CI passed, answered, and the queued exit then started an extra follow-up turn in 3 trials. (c): the ordinary session's running-result text is unchanged. Claude calls `sessions_yield` after starting the waiter in 4/6 trials on base and 4/6 on this head. On base that returns `nothing_pending` and the agent then polls in 3 of those trials (12 polls); here the yield is accepted, the turn ends and the exit wakes the conversation. Two fix trials ran in a supplemental 2-trial arm, because a concurrent packaging step briefly rewrote `package.json` and broke two trial sends in the first arm.

Redacted trace, hidden subagent, fix (P = parent, S = subagent):

```text
P +13s sessions_spawn → accepted
P +17s sessions_yield → {"status":"yielded"}
S +22s exec {"yieldMs":120000,"timeoutSeconds":1500} 'cd pr-1 && …loop until ci-status passes…'
S +142s  -> Command still running (session delta-sage:…, pid …), times out in 23m. This run resumes with its result when it exits, silent success included, if you call sessions_yield. If only waiting remains, call sessions_yield now; do not poll it …
S +145s sessions_yield → {"status":"yielded"}
S +263s USER: Exec completed (delta-sa, code 0, 4m1s): … PR #4241: all 15 checks passed. Summary: build-1-… green
S +266s write pr-1/RESULT.md
S +269s reply: All 15 CI checks on PR #4241 have passed. … PR #4241: all 15 checks passed. Summary: build-1-… green
P +270s USER: [Subagent Context] Every subagent in this batch has now settled …
P +279s reply: The subagent says CI on PR #4241 passed. Its summary line is: PR #4241: all 15 checks passed …
```

Same scenario, base: the subagent's running result says "Automatic completion wake is unavailable after ending this turn … use poll with a timeout", then 14 `process poll timeout=30000` calls each return `PR #4241: 4 checks pending, 11 passed … Process still running.` until it exits.

Cron, fix: `exec` → running result with the `sessions_yield` text → `sessions_yield` → `{"status":"yielded"}` → `Exec completed (tender-c, code 0, 4m1s): …` as the next turn of the same run → `ci-status > RESULT.md` → final reply `PR #4241: all 15 checks passed …`, recorded as the run summary.

**Tests** (`vitest` from source):

- `bash-tools.exec-background-followup.test.ts`: a hidden subagent's command resumes it only after `sessions_yield` awaits it (passive notice otherwise; wake turn with `source: "exec"`, `sourceRunId` and the step 2 content when yielded); a yielded cron run resumes in place with the exit text and sends no session event; cron running results carry the `sessions_yield` text.
- `bash-tools.exec-background-followup.test.ts` also keeps the `main` behavior where `sessions_yield` is not callable: a hidden subagent gets manual-collection guidance and no wake promise, and a cron run is told to collect before ending the turn.
- `openclaw-tools.requester-yield.test.ts`: a wake-armed command the run started is a yield claim only when it has a deadline; only an accepted yield arms the resume.
- The two new tests fail on `main`, where the resume path does not exist; the updated cron assertions also fail there. The exec/process, descriptions, `sessions_yield` tool, requester yield, embedded runner yield orchestration, cron run lifecycle, model-switch retry and prompt-snapshot suites pass. `tsgo:core` passes.

**Full tier**: `ocx build --dts` on the rebased head (`cace873cdf6c`), then a packed tarball install: tarball integrity, `openclaw --version` (`2026.11.3 (cace873)`) and `gateway --help` pass; the packed `bash-tools.exec-output` chunk carries the new guidance.

**Limits:**

- Claude only, direct tool surface; OpenAI and Code Mode were not measured for this step.
- In one trial per fix arm (a) and (b), the agent waited in turn with a capped `yieldMs` block instead of backgrounding; it made no polls.
- The cron harness has no chat channel, so every run (base and fix) records `completionStatus: failed` for delivery; the run summary is the agent's final reply in both arms.
- Gateway restart mid-wait is out of scope (step 5).

**CI:** rebased onto `main` `92016ce978f0` (picks up #199113, which only changed the exec-completion enqueue import; no conflict in the yield/wake path). Focused yield, exec, cron and embedded-runner suites and `tsgo:core` pass on the rebased head. If `checks-ui-e2e (1/2)` fails in `ui/src/e2e/chat-cli-history-redaction.e2e.test.ts` ("preserves tool source in Activity while bounding the visible preview", waiting for `.activity-empty`), that failure is on `main`: #199168 removed the Activity element, but this test still waits for it. Locally, `pnpm test:ui:e2e ui/src/e2e/chat-cli-history-redaction.e2e.test.ts` fails the same way on `main` `92016ce978f0` and on this head (1 failed, 1 passed in both). This PR touches no `ui/` file. Other PRs pass that shard because their changed files select only 6 UI test files that do not include this one; this PR's change set selects 19.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep bundle MCP access for turns woken by an exec completion
prs.body:
Closes #183589

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a backgrounded host exec exits and `tools.exec.notifyOnExit` (default `true`) wakes the originating session, the woken turn has no bundle MCP tools although the run that started the exec had them (Code Mode telemetry `sources: {openclaw: 51, mcp: 0}`, `tools.effective` notice `mcp-not-yet-connected`), and any child spawned from that woken turn inherits the restriction.

## User Impact

User impact: a turn woken by an exec completion keeps exactly the MCP access of the run that started the exec, and children it spawns do too: an unrestricted run keeps every configured server, a run capped to `fixture__*` wakes a turn that can reach only the `fixture` server, an exact-name policy such as `fixture__read` keeps only that tool. Runs with no `mcp.servers`, or whose cap excludes bundle MCP tools, behave exactly as before, so a woken turn never gains access the producer run did not have. No config, schema, or wire change; `notifyOnExit` no longer has to be disabled to keep MCP in long-lived sessions.

## Why This Change Was Made

`createOpenClawCodingTools` (assembled in `src/agents/agent-tools.assembly.ts`) builds each tool's Gateway caller with a default `sessionEventSourcePolicy` whose `toolsAllow` lists the finalized coding tools. Bundle MCP tools are materialized afterwards (`attempt-bundle-tools.ts`), so no `server__tool` name or `bundle-mcp` marker is ever in that list. The exec tool records the policy as the completion event's `producerPolicy`; `captureSessionEventTarget` intersects the woken turn's `toolsAllow` with it; `shouldCreateBundleMcpRuntimeForAttempt` then finds no bundle name and creates no MCP runtime for the woken turn or its children.

The fix captures the producer's final surface instead of predicting it (revision 5). `createOpenClawCodingTools` now fills a caller-owned array (`sessionEventToolsAllowRef`) with the coding tool names and hands that same array to every Gateway caller as `sessionEventSourcePolicy.toolsAllow`. The embedded attempt (`attempt-bundle-tools.ts`) appends the bundled MCP/LSP tools that survived the attempt's runtime allowlist, `applyFinalEffectiveToolPolicy`, and schema projection, by exact name, in the same place it already captures the cron creator cap and the spawn allowlist. The exec tool reads the policy when it records the completion, so the woken turn gets exactly the tools this run could call:

- sender-scoped denials (`tools.toolsBySender["id:alice"].deny: ["admin__*"]`) already removed `admin__reset` from the producer's final surface, so the senderless woken turn never sees it;
- intersected caps, partial globs (`fixture__read*` ∩ `fixture__*All`), and namespace-reaching globs (`fixture*`) are resolved by the existing runtime matcher on real tools, not approximated;
- a refresh replaces the previously appended bundled names, so a tool quarantined or filtered on refresh drops out;
- no marker or glob is ever added, so the continuation cannot widen past the producer.

The surface stays under the existing 512-name bound the target reader enforces (`SESSION_EVENT_TOOLS_ALLOW_LIMIT`, now exported from `session-event-target.ts`); past it, the attempt logs a warning and the woken turn keeps only the coding tools. Revision 5 deletes `agent-tools.session-event-policy.ts` and its tests (revisions 1–4 projected MCP access from allow patterns, which the review showed cannot preserve denials or every glob shape).

## Evidence

Regression in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-bundle-tools.test.ts` (`session event tool surface`, 9 cases through `prepareEmbeddedAttemptBundleTools` with `fixture` and `admin` servers materializing `fixture__read`, `fixture__readAll`, `fixture__write`, `admin__reset`; each captured cap is then run through the woken turn's `intersectSessionEventToolsAllow` → `shouldCreateBundleMcpRuntimeForAttempt` → `applyEmbeddedAttemptToolsAllow`):

- unrestricted producer → all four MCP tools; `["exec", "fixture__*"]` and `["exec", "fixture*"]` → the three fixture tools; `["exec", "fixture__read"]` → `fixture__read`;
- intersected `[["exec", "fixture__read*"], ["exec", "fixture__*All"]]` → `fixture__readAll` (revision 4 returned nothing here);
- `["read", "exec"]` → no MCP tool and no bundle runtime in the woken turn;
- producer final policy drops `admin__reset` (the sender-scoped denial shape) → the woken turn never admits it;
- refresh after a projection drops `fixture__readAll` → the cap shrinks to `["exec", "fixture__read"]`;
- a coding surface at the bound → MCP names are not appended.

Red on `main`: the attempt never appends to the cap, so every case expecting an MCP tool fails, the reported loss.

Suites: `attempt-bundle-tools` 23/23; `bash-tools.exec-notify`, `tools/gateway-caller-context`, `agent-tools.prefix-stability`, `attempt-tool-prepare.web-search`, `session-event-handoff`, `session-event-context`, `session-event-permissions` 115/115. Oxlint clean; `git diff --check` clean.

### Live Gateway run (revision 5, head 18721460f1e, shipped entry point, scripted provider)

Built dist from this head (`build-all gatewayWatch` with `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1`), isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, non-interactive onboarding with `--custom-no-auth` against a loopback OpenAI-compatible provider written for the proof. The provider scripts each step from the conversation and logs every request's offered `tools[].function.name`.
Two loopback streamable-http MCP servers, `fixture` (`echo`) and `admin` (`reset`), each log every JSON-RPC request. Config: `mcp.servers` for both, `tools.profile: full`, `tools.codeMode: false`, `tools.toolSearch: false`, `tools.exec.security: full`, `tools.exec.ask: off`, `tools.exec.notifyOnExit: true`; Gateway `node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port 18399`.
Every scenario's producer turn runs `exec` with `background: true` and ends. Its woken turn then calls `fixture__echo`, `sessions_spawn` (child task: `fixture__echo`, then `admin__reset`) and `admin__reset`. The provider emits each call whether or not it was offered, so the Gateway has to refuse what the turn may not use.
Policy changes were applied with `node openclaw.mjs config patch --file …` while the Gateway was running (log: `config hot reload applied (…)`). Times are UTC; tool results come from the session transcript in the agent SQLite store.
No credentials, all loopback; the host was heavily loaded, which explains the minutes between exec exit and wake.

**S1: allowed completion-turn MCP call** (`tools.allow: ["read","exec","process","sessions_spawn","fixture__*"]`, session `agent:main:s3d`, dispatched with `node openclaw.mjs agent --agent main --session-key s3d --json`)

```text
18:40:53.533  provider  producer   offered=exec,fixture__echo,process,read,sessions_spawn,skills_read   -> exec {"command":"sleep 5; echo PROOF_EXEC_DONE","background":true}
18:40:53.686  provider  producer   -> "started" (turn ends, exec still running)
18:56:00.145  provider  woken      last user msg "[OpenClaw exec completion] Exec completed (… code 0) :: PROOF_EXEC_DONE"
                                   offered=exec,fixture__echo,process,read,sessions_spawn,skills_read   -> fixture__echo {"text":"from-woken-turn"}
18:56:00.155  fixture   tools/call echo {"text":"from-woken-turn"}
18:56:00.158  toolResult fixture__echo  "fixture.echo ok: {\"text\":\"from-woken-turn\"}"
18:56:00.279  toolResult admin__reset   isError "Tool admin__reset not found"
admin server: initialize / tools/list only, no tools/call
```

The turn woken by the exec exit got `fixture__echo` and its call reached the fixture server; `admin__reset`, outside the producer's cap, was not offered and was refused before any request left the Gateway.

**S2: sender-scoped admin denial preserved** (no `tools.allow`; `tools.toolsBySender: {"id:alice": {"deny": ["admin__*"]}}`). The producer message entered through the **qa-channel** plugin: the repo's qa-lab bus ran on loopback and `POST /v1/inbound/message` carried `{"conversation":{"id":"alice","kind":"direct"},"senderId":"alice"}`. The producer request shows `"sender":{"id":"alice","name":"Alice"}`.

```text
19:30:58.826  provider  producer (sender alice)  tools=70  fixture__echo=yes  admin__reset=no   -> exec background
19:31:06.503  provider  woken (senderless)       tools=70  fixture__echo=yes  admin__reset=no   -> fixture__echo
19:31:06.598  fixture   tools/call echo {"text":"from-woken-turn"}
19:31:06.995  toolResult sessions_spawn  accepted  childSessionKey=agent:main:subagent:61a17295-…
19:31:07.206  toolResult admin__reset   isError "Tool admin__reset not found"
admin server: no tools/call
control, same config, CLI sender (not alice), session agent:main:s2ctl:
19:38:41.052  provider  producer  tools=71  admin__reset=yes
19:38:48.506  admin     tools/call reset {"reason":"from-woken-turn"}
```

The denial applied only to alice's run, and the senderless woken turn inherited it: `admin__reset` was absent from the woken turn's tools and its call was refused. The same config still gave `admin__reset` to a non-alice sender, so the denial is sender-scoped and not global.

**S3: inherited restrictions in a spawned child** (children spawned from the S1 and S2 woken turns)

```text
S1 child agent:main:subagent:0e4cffe3-…
18:56:00.479  provider  child  offered=exec,fixture__echo,process,read,sessions_spawn,skills_read   -> fixture__echo
18:56:00.488  fixture   tools/call echo {"text":"from-child"}
18:56:00.505  toolResult admin__reset   isError "Tool admin__reset not found"
S2 child agent:main:subagent:61a17295-…
19:31:10.113  provider  child  tools=51  fixture__echo=yes  admin__reset=no   -> fixture__echo
19:31:10.254  fixture   tools/call echo {"text":"from-child"}
19:31:10.536  toolResult admin__reset   isError "Tool admin__reset not found"
admin server: no tools/call in either run
```

A child spawned from a woken turn keeps that turn's MCP access (`fixture__echo` works) and its restrictions: the S1 global cap and alice's denial still exclude `admin__reset`.

**S4: revocation after capture, before the woken turn** (S1 config; session `agent:main:s4`; exec `sleep 240`)

```text
19:10:29.444  provider  producer  offered=exec,fixture__echo,process,read,sessions_spawn,skills_read   -> exec {"command":"sleep 240; …","background":true}
19:10:30Z     producer turn returned (agent exit 0; exec still running, its completion target captured while fixture__echo was allowed)
19:11:52.750  gateway   config.patch write changedPaths=tools.deny            (tools.deny: ["fixture__echo"])
19:11:52.877  gateway   [reload] config hot reload applied (tools.deny)
19:29:59.180  transcript user "Exec completed (oceanic-, code 0) :: PROOF_EXEC_DONE"
19:30:02.327  provider  woken     offered=exec,process,read,sessions_spawn,skills_read   -> fixture__echo
19:30:02.575  toolResult fixture__echo  isError "Tool fixture__echo not found"
fixture server: last tools/call at 18:56:00.818 (S1), none after the revocation
```

The cap captured `fixture__echo`, but the woken turn applied its own current policy. After the hot-reloaded `tools.deny` the tool was not offered, and the call was rejected before any `tools/call` reached the fixture server.

Discovery (`initialize`/`tools/list`) still connects both configured servers during each run, as on `main`; policy filters tools, not discovery.

prs.title: feat(sessions): keep useful names after context resets
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resetting context should not destroy a useful conversation name. Commands such as `/model` should never become its title.

## User Impact

The first real message gives a new Telegram topic or Dashboard conversation a name. This includes Telegram’s **New Thread** flow, where sending a message creates an implicitly named “New Chat”.

After six follow-up user messages, the utility model compares the opening message and those follow-ups with the current name. After `/reset`, it compares the first real message with the existing name. A fitting broad name such as “YouGile” stays exactly as it is for related work; the model replaces it only when the subject no longer fits.

Commands, bot replies and child-agent output do not count. Manual edits win over naming attempts already in flight.

## Why This Change Was Made

I usually reset a topic to continue the same work with fresh context. Having to restore its old name by hand defeats that workflow.

Naming now starts from approved, recorded user input, without waiting for the agent’s answer. Blocked or hidden input cannot trigger it. Queued messages count individually when their approved text is unchanged; if a hook rewrites the combined input, only that approved result is used. Opening media stays associated with its accepted message.

Related: #184821, #174317, #183368. Reassessing a manually chosen title changes the stable-title policy from #185337 and needs a maintainer decision.

## Evidence

The approved-input follow-up passed **113 focused tests in six files**, core types, five affected test type graphs, scoped lint, formatting and line budgets. It was then merged with main at `e60207216`. On the resulting tree `9f86524d`, **36 transcript and queue tests**, core types, formatting and scoped typed lint passed. An independent review of the three manual conflict resolutions found no P0–P2 issues. prs.title: fix(android): release stale camera activity after destruction
prs.body:
Fixes #195636

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android camera capture retains a destroyed Activity while the longer-lived runtime waits for a replacement Activity to attach.

## User Impact

Camera capture releases its stale Activity reference after destruction, while ordinary background/foreground transitions and a replacement Activity keep working. No configuration changes or user action are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Observe the attached lifecycle owner until destruction, remove the old observer when replacing it, and reject already-destroyed owners. Clear the reference only when the destroyed owner is still current. Existing foreground admission and active-capture cancellation remain unchanged.

This applies the exact parent-to-commit patch from [d38c7c12db5e61c273486053908709dcfe691b4c](https://github.com/saariuslystoned/openclaw/commit/d38c7c12db5e61c273486053908709dcfe691b4c) onto current main without implementation rewrites.

## Evidence

- Fresh isolated validation on published head `caf93bcd6830f0b455179d252c86be3120d350f4`: `CameraCaptureOwnershipTest` passed 7/7 Play and 7/7 third-party cases, with no skips. The repository Gradle tasks compiled production and test sources in a secretless, network-disabled rootless Podman runner using JDK 21, Node 24.22.1 and Gradle 9.7.1.
- Matched pre-fix control: only `CameraCaptureManager.kt` was restored from base `df13b6b8994cefe16f311f29f0301bba511ec617`, retaining identical published regression-test bytes. Both new regressions failed for the intended lifecycle reasons; the five existing sibling tests passed. Restoring the fix returned Play to 7/7 passing before the third-party run. prs.title: fix(sessions): Telegram transcript echoes are not recorded on explicit multi-agent gateways
prs.body:
Closes #194829

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on a gateway with `agents.ownership: "explicit"` and several agents, a delivered Telegram transcript echo (`tools.media.audio.echoTranscript`) is never added to the conversation history. Instead it logs `result was delivered but was not added to the conversation: Multiple agents are configured, but this operation has no explicit owner`, even though the Telegram account is bound to one agent.

## User Impact

User impact: confirmed sends that have no producing turn, such as transcript echoes, are recorded once in the destination conversation of the agent the channel/account binding selects, as the [conversation transcript ownership](docs/refactor/conversation-transcript-ownership.md) rules require. The missing-owner warning goes away for bound destinations. Single-agent and unbound setups behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`commitConfirmedVisibleMessage` (`src/sessions/confirmed-visible-message.ts`) chose the history owner as `producer?.agentId ?? resolveDefaultAgentId(config)`. A preflight transcript echo has no producer, and explicit ownership has no default agent, so `AgentSelectionRequiredError` was thrown before destination lookup could consult the binding. The ownership doc says destination lookup does not need a producer: carried route, producer context, exact local binding, then plugin resolver.

Without a producer, the owner now comes from `resolveAgentRoute` for the destination's channel and account. That reuses the routing owner's binding tiers, and unbound destinations keep the old default-agent fallback, which is the same error when no default exists. Peer-level bindings are still enforced: the existing `belongsToAgent` check re-resolves the route with the destination peer and skips with the documented "belongs to a different agent" diagnostic.

The fix lives in the shared recorder, so other producer-less confirmed sends benefit as well; Telegram code is untouched. This does not overlap #194783, which covers the durable `sendPayload` final mirror.

Accepted edge: the owner is chosen from channel/account bindings before the peer is known. A destination covered only by a peer-specific binding to a different agent than the account binding is skipped with the cross-agent diagnostic, not recorded under the peer's agent.

## Evidence

- New regression `records a producer-less send under the agent its account binding selects (#194829)` in `confirmed-visible-message.integration.test.ts`. It uses explicit ownership, two agents, account bindings and no producer, and the echo lands in `beta`'s conversation.
- Red on `origin/main`: it fails with `AgentSelectionRequiredError: Multiple agents are configured, but this operation has no explicit owner…`, the same text as the issue's warning. Green with the fix (11/11).
- Consumer suites green: `deliver` 86, `outbound-send-service` 24, `delivery-queue.transcript` 14, `deliver-confirmed-visible` 3, `outbound-send-service.accepted-outcomes` 2, `echo-transcript` 4, `echo-transcript.integration` 2, `audio-preflight` 5, `apply` 29, `media-understanding-runtime` 7, `subagent-announce-text-delivery` 5, `subagent-completion-mirror.integration` 1, `voice-call realtime-handler` 37.
- oxlint (type-aware), oxfmt and the import-cycle check are clean.
- Not run: a live Telegram voice-note round trip, which needs a bot account and an audio provider. The integration test drives the real recorder against real session storage.

prs.title: fix(telegram): durable final deliveries skip the channel-final transcript mirror
prs.body:
Closes #194783

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: delivered Telegram final replies get no `channel-final` delivery mirror in the session transcript when live preview is off, for example when a plugin registers a modifying `message_sending` / `reply_payload_sending` hook.

## User Impact

User impact: Telegram finals record the same `channel-final` delivery receipt in the transcript whether they go out through preview finalization, the plain fallback, or core durable delivery. Control UI history and other tools that read the receipt now see it after preview is disabled. Delivery itself is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The durable `handled_visible` branch in the Telegram final sender returned before any mirror ran. Core durable delivery also reported the provider-visible `content` only on partial failure, so the channel had no confirmed text it could mirror. ClawSweeper's review pointed out that mirroring the original payload would record text that a message hook may have rewritten.

- **Core (`src/channels/turn/durable-delivery.ts`):** collects the post-hook text from each confirmed payload's `message_sent` event (`onMessageSentEvent`, already threaded through the durable send) and reports it as `content` on `handled_visible`. `ChannelDeliveryOutcome.content` is already documented as the "final provider-visible text … for this logical payload's terminal observation", so this fills a documented field on the success path instead of adding a new one.
- **Telegram (`bot-message-dispatch-delivery.ts`):** the `handled_visible` branch writes its channel-final mirror from that confirmed text. It uses the same `hasReplyPayloadFinalDeliveryCapture` guard (dispatcher-owned replies keep their own transcript owner) and the same idempotency sequence as the preview and fallback paths.

Ownership: core durable delivery owns the confirmed post-hook text, and Telegram keeps owning its channel-final receipt. The deprecated `sendBatch` `mirror` parameter is ignored, and automatic destination history deliberately skips the producing conversation, so neither could own this. Each final takes exactly one of the three paths, so it is mirrored once.

## Evidence

- New `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.delivery-transcript.test.ts` › "mirrors a durable final with the confirmed post-hook text": the durable send returns `handled_visible` with hook-rewritten content, and the test asserts exactly one `channel-final` mirror carrying that text. **Red on base** (1 failed / 7 passed), green with the fix (8/8).
- New `src/channels/turn/durable-delivery.test.ts` › "reports the confirmed post-hook text on a visible final": **red on base** (1 failed / 7 passed), green with the fix (8/8).
- Related files, all green: Telegram `final-delivery-lifecycle` 12, `preview.telegram-http` 40, `recovery.telegram-http` 8, `reply-targets.telegram-http` 24, `fallback-topic-media` 4; core `durable-delivery.reload` 25, `run-channel-turn.delivery` 17, `run-channel-turn.finalize` 9, `run-channel-turn.settlement` 3, `delivery-result` 6.
- oxlint (type-aware, tsconfig), oxfmt check, the import-cycle check (0 cycles) and the whitespace diff check are clean.

Gaps: I did not run a live Telegram E2E (it needs bot and user credentials I don't have here), and I did not run a full local typecheck (CI covers it). Other channels' durable `handled_visible` results now also carry `content`. I found no consumer that treats its presence as a partial delivery, and the lifecycle's terminal observation already prefers `content` over `payload.text`.

prs.title: fix(codex): Codex turns fail when a plugin MCP server shares a configured server's name
prs.body:
Closes #194825

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every Codex-harness turn fails with `url is not supported for stdio in mcp_servers.<name>` when a plugin bundles an MCP server with the same name as a server in `mcp.servers`.

## User Impact

User impact: a configured MCP server now wins a name collision with a plugin's bundled server for Codex turns, as it already does for the merged static surface. Codex turns start, and fallback chains ending in a Codex model work again.

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex receives MCP servers from two projections: the bundle thread patch and the user-server (configured) projection. The bundle patch kept bundled names that an enabled configured server already owns, so Codex merged both into one `mcp_servers.<name>` table carrying the plugin's `command` and the configured `url`. That combination is rejected at `codex-rs/config/src/mcp_types.rs:321` (`throw_if_set("stdio", "url", …)`) in the sibling `../codex` checkout.

The bundle patch now drops entries shadowed by an enabled configured server, using the same enabled/session-override rule as the user-server projection. This happens before plugin data dirs are prepared, so a shadowed plugin server no longer gets a data dir either.

Cutover: the bundle path projected durable "Allow Always" grants only for configured names (#136019). Those names can no longer appear in the bundle patch, and the user-server projection already projects their grants (`bundle-mcp-codex.user-config.test.ts`), so that dead filter and its test are removed. The optional `agentId` field stays on the exported `LoadCodexBundleMcpThreadConfigParams` SDK type, because removing it would change a public contract.

Accepted edge: when a configured server is enabled but excluded for the agent by `isCodexMcpServerAllowedForAgent`, the bundled copy is still dropped. The operator configured that name, so it is not silently replaced by the plugin's server.

## Evidence

- New regression `leaves a same-named bundled server to the enabled configured server (#194825)` reproduces the issue's shape (bundled stdio `gbrain` plus configured HTTP `gbrain`). The patch now holds only `notes`, and `gbrain` is in `userStaticServerNames`.
- Updated `lets user config disable a same-named bundled server unless the session enables it`: a session override enables the configured server, which now owns the name rather than shipping the bundled copy alongside it.
- Red/green: both cases fail against `origin/main`'s `codex-mcp-config.ts` (2 failed / 5 passed) and pass with the fix (7/7).
- Sibling suites green: `bundle-mcp-codex.user-config` 12/12, `run-attempt.configured-mcp` 23/23, `thread-lifecycle.configured-mcp-ownership` 5/5, `attempt-startup*` (20, 9, 4, 3), `mcp-app-session-preparation` 4/4, `run-attempt-client-prewarm` 5/5.
- oxlint (type-aware), oxfmt and the import-cycle check are clean.
- Not run: a live Codex app-server turn. It needs a ChatGPT-authenticated codex-cli plus a plugin bundling a same-named stdio server. The reporter verified the equivalent local patch on 2026.11.1 with codex-cli 0.167.0.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes installed-terminal validation rejecting directory-watch helpers that intentionally omit the observer preload, even when their native lifetime has ended.
