prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after Start agents, Workboard counts worker-start failures without showing their cause and describes triage cards awaiting planning as “organized.”

## User Impact

User impact: the receipt shows the first worker-start failure alongside the full failure count, and describes planning candidates as marked for planning rather than completed work. Readiness updates and released claims are named separately.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dispatcher already returns each start failure’s title and reason, but the browser normalization discarded them. The existing receipt projection now retains the first failure and the existing toast formats it through the host redactor. The preview is deliberately labeled “First start failure” rather than growing an unbounded error report; all counts remain visible.

The orchestration owner only records an idle protocol state awaiting specification or decomposition. The summary now describes that effect. Admission, execution, retry behavior, scheduling, permissions, refresh handling and model selection are unchanged. No new helper or renderer is added.

The current #194983 diff retains the affected dispatch summary. #199288 owns disabled-automation wording and #199295 owns label selection; neither is duplicated here.

## Evidence

- The new real-view action regression fails on the original copy and dropped failure detail. **37 focused UI/owner tests pass** with redaction, multiple-failure counts, bounded preview and cleared failure after a later successful receipt.
- **Two production-owner contracts pass**: triage cards remain triage and await planning; an unsandboxed target produces a start refusal before claiming work. Backend code is unchanged.
- Full built-app flow through the packaged Workboard plugin passes before/after: Start agents, planning-only receipt plus refused start, close feedback, then a successful second dispatch after simulated external preflight repair. Exactly two dispatch requests; no card creation or direct chat.send. This is synthetic transport evidence, not live worker/configuration execution.
- Both existing native lazy-page cases pass, including actual chunk-load failure and reload recovery.
- Workboard and full UI typechecks, scoped lint, i18n baseline/verification, formatting and diff checks pass. No broad local CI run.

Baseline: current main 92016ce978f0f638369ecd0d10fcaa9212e591ce at capture; affected owners are unchanged at observed main e4f55593741ed56f9bac9196847bb079f25c8d75. Fixes #198985.

Reported and requested by **Amelio Mansour (@AmelioMansour)**. AI-assisted investigation, implementation, and verification.

Fixes: opening a conversation from another agent replaces the existing cross-agent My sessions list with one agent’s conversations.

## User Impact

Keep the existing cross-agent **My sessions** conversation list visible when opening another agent’s conversation. This fixes the persistent sidebar scope reset—not the compact Show all roster, /sessions page, or sorting. No new sidebar mode.

## Why This Change Was Made

Separate the saved personal browsing scope from the effective owner query filter, which can temporarily fall back for a single-user installation. Keep all-agent owner facets valid across selected-chat agent changes. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Cloud environments labels a repository “Cold only” while its first snapshot read is pending or has failed, even when a ready snapshot exists.

## User Impact

User impact: unknown snapshot availability no longer looks like confirmed absence. Saved machine information and independently known worker progress or failures remain visible; real cold-only results and snapshot actions retain their behavior. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing read owner derives snapshot readiness from its accepted result and current capability. The shared environment classifier preserves unknown instead of defaulting to cold-only, and the sheet omits unsupported absence guidance, an empty Snapshot section and premature rebuild advice. It does not hold the whole page behind optional images or add a request, loader, stored flag or action gate.

## Evidence

Real Control UI with a synthetic Gateway, a saved repository/profile and a held ready-snapshot response, light theme and a 1280×1000 viewport. Annotated 800×550 crops show the same pending first read.

**Before** — both the repository list and sheet claim cold-only operation.

![Before: premature cold-only claims](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f954f00-ed53-4c36-8a8d-37f869f3275f)

**After** — the known repository and machine remain, without invented snapshot absence.

![After: snapshot discovery stays unknown](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/35eaf84f-e682-4cee-8ae6-a7ed1374a840)

- The real-route regression fails on isolated main `e33981dc` and passes independently through pending discovery, sustained read failure, navigation-based recovery to Ready and a confirmed cold-only result. It sends no prepare or configuration write.
- **Six browser scenarios pass** on the independent head in 17.39s, including lazy plugin activation, rebuild/cancel, failed-build dismissal, uncertain-capture acknowledgement and exact-profile pin/unpin/rollback/delete. All cloud operations are synthetic fixtures.
- **36 focused lifecycle/configuration tests pass** in 1.38s; the unchanged baseline has 35. Two owning cases fail on main. Accepted worker attention appears before optional snapshots, known data survives refresh, and unsupported-plugin behavior, true cold results, drafts and actual recovery remain covered.
- UI typecheck, formatting and diff checks pass. Targeted lint has zero errors and the same existing reactive-microtask warning as baseline. The view’s unchanged 700-line limit is respected: its existing ready-timestamp projection moved beside the classifier without changing its behavior.
- Self-review/simplification: **+12 net production lines**, **151 net test lines**. One derived readiness fact serves the list and sheet; no duplicate inventory or recovery owner.

The first failure probe recovered automatically through an already-queued refresh. The final fixture models a sustained outage before explicit recovery, rather than disabling that valid refresh path. This is an independent draft, not merged or deployed; broad PR CI, CI timing, independent automated review and live cloud-provider verification are not claimed complete.

Requested and co-authored by @vyctorbrzezowski.

prs.title: fix: recovered chat voice notes are transcribed again
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes already-transcribed voice notes becoming eligible for transcription again when a chat turn is recovered from canonical history.

## User Impact

Voice notes sent through chat clients retain their completed transcription state across persistence and recovery, avoiding redundant transcription work. This does not change live-turn transcription policy, add a schema, or require a migration. Previously stored entries are not backfilled.

## Why This Change Was Made

Audio preflight updates the runtime media facts, while the canonical user-turn input is built from separately prepared durable facts. Carry successful transcription state into those durable facts by managed URL, preserving mixed-media order, image layout, unselected audio, and durable metadata without copying runtime paths.

The fix stays in the existing Gateway producer; no new recovery policy or competing state owner. Simplification pass retained the minimal URL merge (production +8/-1 lines) and extended the existing regression rather than introducing a new suite. The exact 38-net-test-line allocation covers persistence/recovery proof and a portable path expectation; the shared budget scalar is unchanged.

## Evidence

- **base RED → 104 GREEN:** the regression fails against the pristine base producer because the completed voice note lacks `transcribed: true`; with this fix, 104/104 tests pass across seven files using the supported test wrapper and `--maxWorkers=1` on Windows/Node 24.22.1.
- Exercises `prepareChatSendUserTurn` → canonical user-turn projection → actual SQLite write/read → recovered-media normalization and selection. Mixed image/two-audio input verifies that only the completed voice note is skipped on recovery. Covers five chat-client identities, including Android and iOS, plus approval-policy and audio-preflight consumers.
- Independent source/patch reviews and a fresh final-snapshot review found no blocking findings. Verified reviewed file blobs match committed head `c34648deda828e5092e9114e0b2ca943bd4fed7d` (base `8c9310ee36391c657104e2bb3f5cd17c7154e49c`). These were independent agent reviews, not a ClawSweeper/autoreview CLI run.
- Checkout-local frozen dependency install repaired the earlier cross-checkout declaration guard. Production core typecheck and the canonical Gateway-methods test typecheck pass. The latter exposed a genuine missing fixture-narrowing assertion, now fixed without casts or weaker expectations. Final seven-file rerun passes 104/104 tests in 394.64s (including cold worker preparation); target-file type-aware lint passes 293 rules with zero warnings/errors; formatting and test-budget ratchet pass (38-line allocation, 18 lines of slack). Standard Knip production and full-tree unused-file scans both pass with zero entries. Knip needed the supported process-local Chromium executable override to an actual installed Playwright headless shell because GUI Chromium hung on `--version`; no graph/ignore/skip changes or installed-code edits.

- Normal exact-head [CI run 41940342583](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41940342583) completed successfully: production types, selected test-type/core-lint stripes, changed/consumer tests, architecture/source/ratchet guards, and selected UI end-to-end checks all passed. Dependency/security review statuses are successful; the repository watcher reports GREEN.

### Additional running-Gateway evidence (November 14, 2026)

At reviewed head `c34648deda828e5092e9114e0b2ca943bd4fed7d`, a separate loopback-only candidate-source Gateway admitted a signed WebSocket `chat.send` containing two controlled WAV attachments. The configured CLI audio model used the installed Windows offline recognizer with unconstrained dictation, not a mocked provider or canned transcript. Node was 24.22.1. The changed producer blob `ac3a80333daf11680e07e0e969aafe0fe814dab5` matches the reviewed commit.

The first WAV was actually transcribed and the second remained unselected under `attachments.mode: first`. The canonical user entry retained the real transcript and completion flag. After a shipped restart RPC cleanly closed the candidate database and a fresh candidate Gateway process reopened the same isolated state, signed `chat.history` returned that same entry and flags. A separate read-only call to the production normalization/selection functions on the persisted entry selected only the uncompleted attachment. No direct SQL or manufactured transcript records were used.

**Still limited:** the isolated default agent model was unavailable, so the agent run failed before producing a reply. This proves real admission/STT/persistence and post-restart Gateway readback, plus production recovery-selection on that record; it is **not** a successful end-to-end recovered agent/model execution, a packaged release-binary run, or a native mobile-device capture. Reviewers must decide whether further agent-runtime recovery proof is required. No maintainer design approval or merge readiness is claimed.

<details><summary>Redacted observed receipts and reproduction boundary</summary>

```text
Candidate producer blob matches reviewed head: ac3a80333daf11680e07e0e969aafe0fe814dab5
Signed Gateway connection: accepted
chat.send: started; two audio/wav files, 147950 bytes each
Real offline STT: The purple lighthouse opens at 7:00 AM
Recognition confidence: 0.6567622
Canonical user text: Controlled voice-note evidence + Heard: The purple lighthouse opens at 7:00 AM
Persisted media[0]: transcribed=true; media[1]: no completion flag
Agent run: error (isolated model unavailable; no model reply claimed)
Gateway restart RPC: scheduled; shutdown receipt: database clean close
New Gateway process, chat.history: same canonical user entry and transcript
Post-restart media[0]: transcribed=true; media[1]: no completion flag
Production normalization: alreadyTranscribed=[true,false]
Production selection from persisted media: index=[1]
```

Reproduction used an independent frozen-lock dependency install, the candidate source CLI, distinct state/config/workspace paths, loopback binding, an ephemeral signed GatewayClient, and a PowerShell System.Speech CLI recognizer registered through the normal audio-model configuration. The recognizer loaded DictationGrammar and called SetInputToWaveFile/Recognize on Gateway-staged media. Gateway RPCs created the session and admitted attachments; the captured canonical entry came from chat.history. Production recovery reads used loadTranscriptEvents, readPersistedMediaFacts, normalizeAttachments and selectAttachments without mutating state. Two identical controlled WAVs isolate selection policy; only the first was recognized.

Only synthetic, non-personal speech was used. Credentials, network addresses, device identities, session IDs, sender identities, managed filenames and local paths have been removed from these receipts. Existing regression/CI claims above are unchanged and were not rerun for this evidence-only update.

</details>

**Limitations:** the original 104-test regression uses mocked speech-provider I/O. The new capture above adds real WebSocket admission, offline STT, canonical persistence and post-restart Gateway readback, but not successful recovered agent/model execution, a packaged-release binary, Android SDK, iOS, or a native-device run. Locally unexecuted broad suites and non-core type/repository-wide lint were delegated to the normal scoped PR CI plan under `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `.agents/skills/openclaw-testing/SKILL.md`; this is not a claim that every repository test/graph ran. Full build/artifact, extension-wide lint, native/device/release jobs were skipped by the unchanged CI scope plan and were not run locally. No check, scope-plan, or approval bypasses.


## Updated running-Gateway evidence (November 14, 2026)

[Recovery execution proof and sanitized captured receipts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193077#issuecomment-6886515234): real offline recognition, persisted completion, a fresh production Gateway automatic replay, completed audio skipped and previously unselected audio recognized, successful recovered agent and zero pending inputs. Inference uses an explicitly synthetic local Responses fixture, not a commercial LLM; held-turn shutdown warnings are disclosed. This supersedes the earlier missing-successful-recovered-agent limitation, not the outstanding maintainer semantics decision.

prs.title: improve(backup): capture PostgreSQL and SQLite stores in parallel
prs.body:
Related: #183094

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw backup create` waits for the shared state PostgreSQL export to finish before it starts the SQLite agent snapshots, even though neither depends on the other's data, so capture takes about as long as both added together.

## User Impact

User impact: `backup create` and `backup create --verify` finish capture sooner when the shared state store is on PostgreSQL. On the 183094 fixture capture dropped from about 53-57 s to about 33 s, and `backup create --verify` from about 226 s to about 199 s. The archive format, compression, per-store consistency and every integrity check are unchanged. Hosts with slow disks may see less gain, because the two captures then compete for the same disk.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared state export now runs in its worker while the other stores are captured, still one at a time, so at most two captures are in flight. Their plan is built before the export supplies the agent registry. When the exported registry only names agent stores that plan already owns under the same path (the usual case: agents at their default paths), those snapshots are kept. Otherwise they are discarded and the stores are captured again from the inventory sealed with the registry, as before. So the archived registry is still the image that chose which agents were captured.

Only SQLite captures overlap the shared export. Every PostgreSQL export takes the local state owner on the state database, so another PostgreSQL-backed store (for example a retained Matrix account root) awaits the shared export before it exports, as on main.

If either side fails, the other stops: the export worker is aborted and joined, and the store loop stops before its next store (a SQLite snapshot already in progress finishes first). The first error is reported after both have settled, so nothing writes into the scratch directory after cleanup starts. Manifest order is unchanged (shared store first, then plan order).

`docs/cli/backup.md` now says the shared export runs alongside the other stores instead of "one after another". The legacy audit retry wrapper moved to its own file, unchanged, to keep `backup-sqlite-snapshot.ts` under the line cap.

## Evidence

- New `src/infra/backup-sqlite-snapshot.concurrent.test.ts` (real SQLite capture and planning; only the PostgreSQL worker is faked):
  - agent stores are captured while the export is still running, manifest order is unchanged, and the archive walk reuses the capture's header probes. Fails on main (the agent capture waits for the export).
  - the exported registry decides reuse: a new agent store, or a known agent at another path, discards the concurrent snapshots and captures from the registry; a registry naming fewer agents keeps them; a registry giving a planned store to another agent is refused, as before. Each case checks that the archived shared image is the export the registry was read from and that every registered store was archived.
  - a failing agent store aborts the export and waits for it to settle, even when the worker settles later. Fails on main (hangs).
  - a failing export stops the agent captures.
  - a second PostgreSQL-backed store never exports while the shared export runs.
  - Mutation checks: not waiting for the export, or always reusing the concurrent snapshots, each fail the matching tests.
- New PostgreSQL conformance test `src/infra/database-engine/backup-parallel-capture.postgres.test.ts`, with the real database-backup worker and a real PostgreSQL export (see below).
- `src/infra/database-engine/matrix-roots.postgres.test.ts` (three PostgreSQL-backed state roots): passes on PostgreSQL 17 (3 of 3 tests, rebased onto current main). The previous head failed it every time with `GatewayStateOwnerContentionError`, because a second export took the state owner while the shared export held it.
- Backup unit suites (`src/infra/backup-create*.test.ts`, `src/infra/backup-sqlite*.test.ts`, 16 files): 147 passed, 6 skipped.
- `pnpm check:changed`: every step passes except the dead export scan, which fails the same way on current main (unused exports in `extensions/workboard`, `ui` and `scripts/perf`, none touched here).
- Rebased onto current main: the runtime pin store that main now captures as a `services` database stays in the core inventory, sealed with the other core databases.
- Fixture timings: see below.

### Test cost

- Net test lines: 601 (`backup-sqlite-snapshot.concurrent.test.ts` +352, `backup-parallel-capture.postgres.test.ts` +249), so 201 over the 400-line allowance. `config/test-lines-allocations/197776-backup-parallel-capture.txt` records 201; `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` passes (net +601, allowance 400, credit 201).
- Why the lines are needed: each test proves a contract that no cheaper layer can. The concurrent unit file covers registry ordering and consistency (reuse or recapture, refusal when a planned store moves to another agent), abort-and-join cleanup in both directions, and PostgreSQL export serialization, using real SQLite capture and planning with only the export worker faked. The PostgreSQL file is the only check that the real database-backup worker settles and its pool is joined before scratch cleanup; a faked worker cannot show that.
- Wall time on a Mac Studio, `--maxWorkers=1`, warm runs:
  - `pnpm test src/infra/backup-sqlite-snapshot.concurrent.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: about 10.4 s wall (8.5 s Vitest duration, 8 tests). The first cold run took 39.7 s, almost all transform.
  - `backup-parallel-capture.postgres.test.ts` on PostgreSQL 17 through the database conformance runner with `--maxWorkers=1`: about 35.1 to 35.4 s wall over 3 runs (Vitest duration about 30.8 s, of which the test itself is about 4.1 s; the rest is transform). Plain `pnpm test` skips it without a PostgreSQL connection (6.2 s).
  - CI seconds: not available yet.

<details><summary>Real export worker: SQLite capture failure while the export runs</summary>

`backup-parallel-capture.postgres.test.ts` puts the shared state store on PostgreSQL 17 (20,000 rows of about 2 KB) and keeps the main agent store on SQLite. It runs `createBackupArchive` with the real database-backup worker. The SQLite agent capture throws as soon as the worker has a PostgreSQL connection open on the test database. The test asserts this order:

1. export worker run started
2. SQLite capture failed while the export was active
3. export worker run rejected
4. export worker pool close called, then joined
5. scratch cleanup started, with no export backend left in `pg_stat_activity`
6. scratch cleanup finished
7. `createBackupArchive` rejected with the SQLite error

After cleanup, the test checks for 1 s that the scratch directory stays absent. Any later write would have to recreate it.

The test does not import `database-suite-workers.test-support`, because that support shares one backup pool per worker URL and replaces its `close()` with a no-op.

The same scenario, run with timestamps and a recursive `fs.watch` on the scratch root. Paths are shown relative to the scratch directory, and the times are milliseconds from test start:

```text
3519  export worker run started (real database-backup worker, PostgreSQL export)
3706  fs.watch rename <scratch>/.../openclaw.sqlite.postgres/.pending (exists)
3834  fs.watch rename <scratch>/.../openclaw.sqlite.postgres/anchor.sqlite (exists)
3923  SQLite agent capture throws; PostgreSQL export backends active: 1
3980  export worker run settled: rejected (Error)
3980  export worker pool close called (runBackupTask finally)
3982  export worker joined; PostgreSQL export backends now 0
3986  scratch cleanup started; export backends 0
3995  fs.watch rename <scratch>/... (absent)   [11 removal events]
3995  fs.watch rename <scratch>/owner.sqlite (exists)
3996  scratch cleanup finished
3998  createBackupArchive rejected with the SQLite capture error
4046  fs.watch rename <scratch> (absent)
8040  scratch absent (ENOENT); export backends 0
```

The export had already written its `.pending` directory and anchor when the capture failed. After cleanup started, the only event for a path that still existed was the scratch's own `owner.sqlite` lock, which is removed with the directory at 4046. The scratch directory was still absent 4 s later. The scenario passed every run on this branch and on the previous head: 3 assertion-only runs and 2 timestamped runs on the final commit, plus 8 earlier runs.

</details>

<details><summary>Fixture timings</summary>

Synthetic 183094 fixture on a Mac Studio: shared state on PostgreSQL 17 (about 2.1 GB, 1 GiB blob rows), agent SQLite stores of 4.0, 1.0 and 0.5 GiB, about 4.8 GB workspace. `backup create --verify`, base and branch runs alternated, phases timed in a disposable instrumented build. Page cache was warm (no purge available), so disk-bound hosts will see different absolute numbers.

| run | capture | archive write | total (real) |
|---|---|---|---|
| main 1 | 57.1 s | 154.1 s | 226.3 s |
| branch 1 | 32.7 s | 152.7 s | 198.2 s |
| main 2 | 53.5 s | 159.5 s | 226.9 s |
| branch 2 | 32.8 s | 153.5 s | 199.7 s |

On the branch the export (about 26 s) overlaps the agent snapshots instead of preceding them. All four archives verified. The last branch archive was restored with `backup restore --target` into a fresh directory (`ok: true`, SQLite inventory verified), and the restored agent databases pass `PRAGMA quick_check`.

</details>

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the memory-import offer labels destination conflicts “Already imported,” even when nothing establishes that those files were successfully imported.

## User Impact

User impact: users can distinguish blocked files from completed imports and understand that replacement affects existing destination files, with backups.

## Why This Change Was Made

The displayed count comes from `status === "conflict"`, not import history. Claude Code import planning marks an existing destination or a nonregular target, including a dangling link, as a conflict. The first-use offer and review page now name that state consistently. The replacement control describes existing files rather than claiming they are previous imports.

Import selection, permission checks, destination safety, backups, confirmation, and actual copying are unchanged. This is five English-copy changes and a small extension of an existing semantic regression; no new renderer or state owner.

## Evidence

- Existing onboarding test fails on main with the false “Already imported” claim, then passes with this change while retaining exact item-selection and idempotency assertions.

- Self-review and simplification completed. No independent agent review or broad CI/E2E matrix was run. Existing date-input warnings in identity-retirement test scenarios are outside this string-only change.

Visual proof uses the actual built app with realistic synthetic Claude Code memory data, light theme, 1280 × 1000 viewport. prs.title: docs(mcp): state the offline ownership requirement for mcp login
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`docs/cli/mcp/transports.md` told readers that "the operator, **or an agent with shell access**, can then run
`openclaw mcp login <name>`". That is not true while a Gateway owns the state: login writes into the owner-only store, so it
refuses with `This operation requires exclusive offline state ownership`. The people most likely to hit it — agents with a
shell — are exactly the ones the sentence invites.

## Why This Change Was Made

`offlineMcpAction` runs every MCP login through `runWithLocalStateOwner` with `onForeignOwner: "refuse"`
(`src/cli/mcp-cli-state-owner.ts:10-22`), and `registerMcpLoginCommand` registers login through it
(`src/cli/mcp-cli.ts:1051`). So a shell plus a running Gateway is not enough; the state must be owned exclusively.

The replacement sentence says what the command actually needs and points at the two ways to get it (stop the Gateway, or run
where no Gateway owns the state), matching how `docs/cli/templates.md:354` and `docs/cli/plugins.md:16` already describe the
same precondition.

## User Impact

An operator reading the OAuth workflow now knows login is an offline-ownership operation instead of trying it against a
running Gateway and meeting a refusal. Nothing else in the page changes; the agent-facing behaviour is unchanged.

## Evidence

Docs-only change, verified against the current guard rather than from memory:

- `src/cli/mcp-cli-state-owner.ts:10-22` — `offlineMcpAction` → `runWithLocalStateOwner({ onForeignOwner: "refuse" })`.
- `src/cli/mcp-cli.ts:1051` — login is registered through that wrapper.
- `docs/cli/templates.md:354`, `docs/cli/plugins.md:16` — the same requirement, already documented for neighbouring paths.

Checks: `pnpm -s format:docs:check` → "Docs formatting clean (1431 files)"; `pnpm -s lint:docs` → "0 issues in 0 files";
`git diff --check` clean.

## AI Assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance from the issue report; the author reviewed the change and its evidence.

prs.title: fix(automations): choose recipients by conversation and thread
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Automation delivery reduces known conversation names to raw recipient IDs and hides the difference between threads sharing a destination.

## User Impact

With an explicit channel and sending account, **To** now offers searchable conversation names and thread context. Choosing a row keeps its exact recipient/thread pair together. Unknown and custom recipients remain supported, and selection changes only the draft until Save changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The field consumes the existing bounded conversation directory rather than inventing another discovery API or inferring an account from visible targets. Named choices are filtered to the selected channel and account. Saved routes outside that directory stay visible; custom edits use the existing owner’s thread invalidation. **No recipient override** restores existing implicit routing without claiming that a destination exists.

The last-used channel, unspecified account, webhook URLs, and failure-alert targets keep their current open-ended entry behavior. In particular, the primary account’s directory is not reused for a separate failure-alert account. Captured creating-conversation binding and delivery execution remain unchanged.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/c4507bcf-b1bf-464e-a9df-2bc0344bbe58)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/30fbbba6-e989-49d2-9f1b-7bd46a563cc2)

## Evidence

- Baseline main 4d094454859a26663978d5b77718f7ddb17d222f: the production-page regression fails because the named-recipient control is absent. Before capture shows the original numeric destination.
- 82 focused tests across six owner/consumer files pass (1.78 s Vitest wall time). Two new real-page regressions verify same-name/different-thread choices, exact account/recipient/thread save payload, accepted saved-job readback, no writes during choice, default clearing, independent failure-alert values, missing-directory/custom values, stale-thread clearing, failed-save draft/name retention, and actual input preservation. Existing directory lifetime/permission/reconnect and form/default tests remain passing.
- Full source-app Chromium flow passes in 6.16 s: pick a thread, inspect cron.update, reload saved synthetic state, search at 400 px, clear search with Escape then dismiss with Escape/focus return, and enter a custom recipient. No messages or real automations were sent.
- UI build/typecheck, scoped lint/format, i18n and controller guards pass. Build advisory budget overages are unattributed; no performance claim or ceiling change. Hosted CI duration is not yet available.
- Screenshots use actual source-app components and synthetic Gateway data, light theme, 1100×1000 desktop and 400×800 emulated phone. They are not WebKit, installed-device, live provider, or live storage proof.
- Author source review/simplification retains the existing directory/form/mutation owners, adding only the route-aware field projection: net +158 production lines, +194 test/support lines, and two documentation lines. No new API, persistent cache, permission, or backend policy. The remaining raw-input branches serve explicitly unresolved/custom route contracts, not a parallel catalog implementation. No independent reviewer/subagent, merge, auto-merge, or deployment under this task.

After

prs.title: fix(doctor): escape terminal controls in gateway-owned channel status issues
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw doctor` writes channel status issue text verbatim into the terminal. The `channels.status` RPC `statusIssues` payload carries plugin-authored `message` and `fix` strings; an ordinary plugin error can therefore clear the screen, change the terminal title, or inject misleading extra lines into the human Doctor report.

The human `channels status` command already sanitizes this exact payload through `terminalText` (Alix-007 #198304). The Doctor report renders the **same RPC field** at a second boundary (`doctor-gateway-health.ts` Channel warnings) that was left unsanitized.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing `terminalText` sanitizer at the Doctor human rendering boundary, matching the `channels status` command. Raw JSON diagnostics keep their original values; only human display escapes terminal/format controls.

This completes the same-shape boundary gap; no new option, configuration, dependency, permission, schema, protocol or migration.

## User Impact

Doctor Channel warnings display terminal-safe text with visible newline/carriage-return/tab escapes and stripped ANSI/OSC controls. JSON retains the original Gateway diagnostic values.

## Evidence

Product HEAD: `ef881ae367de294c3d5d8ba620c201418957b9c1`; BASE: `186db3a17736cf5dc7cb528c654b27b9af6ae59f`.

| Discriminating test | BASE | HEAD |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `escapes terminal controls in gateway-owned channel status issues` | RED (note receives raw `\^[[31m`/`\^[]2;`/`\^G` controls and literal newlines) | GREEN (note receives `Issue text\\nnext (fix\\rrow\\ttab)` with escaped literals) |

- **Command:** `pnpm vitest run src/commands/doctor-gateway-health.test.ts` — full file 23/23 pass on HEAD; the new discriminating test fails on BASE at the intended `note` assertion.
- **Legal controls:** existing 22 tests unchanged and green (plain-warning and structured issue rendering still match verbatim strings when no controls are present). JSON `writeJson` path untouched.
- **Boundary:** terminal human output escapes controls; JSON diagnostics keep raw Gateway values (schema `Type.String()` untouched).

### Shipped CLI proof

Real `openclaw doctor` (Node 24.22.1, glibc 2.39 container, isolated HOME/state/config) pointed at a synthetic loopback WS peer speaking the real wire protocol; the peer answers `connect`/`status`/`channels.status`/`diagnostics.stability`/`doctor.memory.status`, with `channels.status` carrying control-laden `statusIssues`. Full receipts: [EVIDENCE.md](https://github.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/blob/proof/doctor-channel-warnings-sanitize/proof/doctor-channel-warnings-sanitize/EVIDENCE.md), [base-doctor.out](https://github.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/blob/proof/doctor-channel-warnings-sanitize/proof/doctor-channel-warnings-sanitize/base-doctor.out), [head-doctor.out](https://github.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/blob/proof/doctor-channel-warnings-sanitize/proof/doctor-channel-warnings-sanitize/head-doctor.out).

| Head | "Channel warnings" report block (raw bytes) |
| --- | --- |
| BASE | `- signal default: Issue\x1b[31m text\nnext\x1b]2;forged\x07 (fix\rrow\ttab)` |
| HEAD | `- signal default: Issue text\nnext (fix\rrow\ttab)` |

BASE forwards the raw `ESC [31m` red SGR, `ESC ]2;forged BEL` OSC title change + BEL, a real newline after `text`, and real CR/TAB in `fix` into Doctor's report — a plugin could colorize, retitle the terminal, or forge an extra report line. HEAD strips the ESC/BEL sequences and renders the newline/CR/TAB as visible `\n`/`\r`/`\t` literals. Both heads exit 0 and render a second control-free diagnostic identically.

## Not tested

Real channel/provider traffic, `--json` machine output is intentionally raw (by contract), Control UI, Windows/macOS, full repository suite.

## Checks

`pnpm vitest run src/commands/doctor-gateway-health.test.ts` on HEAD: 23 passed.

Precedent: #198304 (same `statusIssues` field sanitized at the `channels status` human boundary).

prs.title: fix(ui): avoid discard warnings after reverting skill edits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: closing the Skills library editor asks to discard unsaved changes even after an edit has been completely reverted.

## User Impact

User impact: returning a skill to its saved contents lets the editor close normally, without a destructive warning or an unnecessary save. Real unsaved changes still require confirmation, including supporting-file contents, additions/removals, executable flags and the skill name.

## Why This Change Was Made

The old dirty flag remembered that an input event happened, not whether anything remained changed. The existing library owner now compares the current draft with its accepted baseline; the dialog, Save action and other editor actions use that one answer. All old dirty-flag writers are removed.

Supporting files compare their bytes and executable flags, not their transport encoding. The same comparison retains unchanged files during saves. Successful saves and rollback update the baseline; failed saves do not. No persistence format, permission rule or Gateway mutation contract changes.

## Evidence

Actual Control UI, synthetic mock-Gateway skill library, light theme, 1280×900. In both runs: open the same saved skill, change SKILL.md, restore its exact original content, then click Close.

**Before — an unnecessary destructive confirmation blocks closing.**

![Before: discard warning despite fully reverted skill content](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fad4a76a-6be1-4149-a6c1-e1786d3d9877)

**After — the unchanged editor closes and returns to the library.**

![After: reverted skill closes normally without a discard warning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5fc17957-740e-4bab-9906-05d8431009cd)

- The real route regression fails on unchanged affected main source and passes with the fix.
- All 7 owning browser tests pass, preserving real dirty-draft confirmation/cancellation, imports, supporting files, keyboard saves, read-only entries, save conflicts and rollback.
- All 54 focused unit tests pass. Added owner coverage checks actual edits versus reverted content/name/file changes, equivalent file bytes, confirmed discard for a real edit, no-op saves, and the saved baseline.
- UI types, focused lint, formatting and diff checks pass. The import test's receipt was corrected to return its submitted slug, matching the Gateway contract instead of an unrelated fixture slug.
- History review preserves the explicit in-app confirmation behavior from #192012, the Solid owner from #173770 and the lazy dialog boundary from #194827. Self-review/pr-simplify removes latched state and its writers; production net +28 lines and tests +66 lines implement the complete owner-level fix rather than hiding a dialog.

Independent one-commit draft, not stacked on other audit fixes. Independent automated review and broad PR CI are not claimed complete. No merge or deployment is requested.

Requested and guided by @vyctorbrzezowski; implemented by RoboClaw.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/53cb60dd-b224-4e21-b03b-3e5042ea91f9)

prs.title: fix(oc-path): numeric filters match blank fields as zero
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `openclaw path find` selecting records with empty or whitespace-only fields as numeric zero. A whitespace-only numeric comparison bound also behaves as zero.

## User Impact

Numeric filters no longer select blank data by accident in JSON, YAML, or JSONL. Explicit zero, padded numbers, exponent and hexadecimal notation, and string comparisons keep their existing behavior. Queries that relied on blank-to-zero coercion should use `0` explicitly.

## Why This Change Was Made

`Number("")` and `Number("   ")` both return zero. Rejecting blank operands in the shared numeric comparison owner fixes both sides without changing the supported finite-number grammar.

Related: #109789 was closed without merging after its decimal-only parser raised compatibility concerns. This change takes the narrower blank-only approach discussed in that review and leaves numeric parsing otherwise unchanged.

## Evidence

- Hosted CI has not run yet: [CI run 43633956807](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43633956807) is awaiting maintainer approval and has no test jobs. The local build and behavior proof above are complete.

- Three new format cases fail against unchanged production code, then pass with the fix. The focused find suite passes all 102 tests.
- The complete oc-path extension suite, scoped production/test typechecks, targeted lint/format, staged test-line ratchet, and whitespace checks pass. Exact counts are listed below.
- Clean `pnpm build qaRuntime` builds passed before and after the fix. Real `pnpm --silent openclaw path find` commands reproduced the bug on the baseline and verified the final commit using isolated local configuration and fixtures.
- Native local autoreview returned `scoped-clean` at P0–P3. Simplification kept the existing comparison owner: production +3, tests +25, docs +1; no new helper or state.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and captured results</summary>

Windows, Node 24.22.1. These are local built-CLI results, not a claim about hosted CI.

Baseline: `ad6738d48408b82b2e5a8925e91e465b2f5e48e9`
Final verified commit: `6f2401798347cb925e728a1f77443cb76c179857`

Save this as `scores.json` (the same JSON is valid YAML; for JSONL, write each row on its own line):

```json
{"rows":[{"id":"empty","score":""},{"id":"spaces","score":"   "},{"id":"zero","score":0},{"id":"positive","score":" 2 "},{"id":"negative","score":-1},{"id":"missing"},{"id":"null","score":null},{"id":"unknown","score":"unknown"}]}
```

With the bundled oc-path plugin enabled:

```sh
pnpm --silent openclaw path find 'oc://scores.json/rows/[score<=0]/id' --json --file scores.json
pnpm --silent openclaw path find 'oc://scores.json/rows/[score< ]/id' --json --file scores.json
pnpm --silent openclaw path find 'oc://scores.json/rows/[score=   ]/id' --json --file scores.json
```

The table projects `matches[].match.valueText` from captured stdout and shows the actual exit code. JSONL patterns omit `/rows`. Fixtures remained unchanged.

| File | Predicate | Before: IDs / exit | After: IDs / exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scores.json` | `score<=0` | `["empty", "spaces", "zero", "negative"]` / 0 | `["zero", "negative"]` / 0 |
| `scores.json` | `score< ` | `["negative"]` / 0 | `[]` / 1 |
| `scores.json` | `score=   ` | `["spaces"]` / 0 | `["spaces"]` / 0 |
| `scores.yaml` | `score<=0` | `["empty", "spaces", "zero", "negative"]` / 0 | `["zero", "negative"]` / 0 |
| `scores.yaml` | `score< ` | `["negative"]` / 0 | `[]` / 1 |
| `scores.yaml` | `score=   ` | `["spaces"]` / 0 | `["spaces"]` / 0 |
| `scores.jsonl` | `score<=0` | `["empty", "spaces", "zero", "negative"]` / 0 | `["zero", "negative"]` / 0 |
| `scores.jsonl` | `score< ` | `["negative"]` / 0 | `[]` / 1 |
| `scores.jsonl` | `score=   ` | `["spaces"]` / 0 | `["spaces"]` / 0 |

Three additional final-build commands checked the existing finite-number grammar: source values `1e2`, `0x10`, `1.`, and ` 2 ` remain numeric; `Infinity` and `NaN` remain excluded. Bounds `1e1`, `0x2`, and `1.` still work. All 12 final CLI commands passed their expected output and exit-code assertions.

Both build stamps matched their tested Git heads with `inputsClean: true`.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the saved-message warning repeatedly disappears and returns when background storage checks keep failing.

## User Impact

User impact: recovery warnings and saved draft rows stay stable during background checks, and the warning disappears only after a successful check. This fixes the flicker, not the underlying reason browser storage is unavailable. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing recovery state while its asynchronous check is pending instead of clearing it prematurely. Owner changes still clear the old state, and existing stale-result checks remain intact. No new state, timers, or storage behavior are introduced.

## Evidence

Maintainer verification on `9215ff2e066b9573ecf55fec970822a755a8b8ff`, performed on Tempbook:

- Replayed the same actual-chat browser scenario using the parent production owner. That implementation is identical to the checked main owner (`54ebe953f1c60a96dc1beb9fa0e696ff815fbdbf`). It fails because the original warning node is detached during the pending storage check.
- With the PR implementation restored, all 6 selected Chromium scenarios pass: pending/failed/successful storage checks, plus recovery-confirmation retirement for incognito, incognito toggling, session replacement, reconnection and a newer reply target.
- All 7 focused recovery-owner/import tests pass, including retained draft-row identity and stale work retirement.
- A fresh independent P0–P2 code review found no actionable defects. The tests cover distinct owner, row-identity and integrated-renderer boundaries; no extra tests or production changes were added during maintainer review.
- Author UI/browser-test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting and diff checks pass. Current-head GitHub CI is checked separately before landing.
- The browser tests use the real application renderer with a mock Gateway and controlled IndexedDB failures. They prove the warning does not flicker and the draft stays intact; they do not claim to repair the underlying reason storage is unavailable.
- The existing before/after screenshots were inspected. They show the same pending-check state, with synthetic content in an emulated 1280×820 light viewport; crops are 830×190.

prs.title: fix(pr): retain equivalent reviewed workflows for baseline proof
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Initial baseline-proof preparation rejects a reviewed workflow whenever authenticated main advances, even when the complete workflow and qualified dependency inputs remain equivalent.

## User Impact

Maintainers can retain the reviewed workflow for initial `prepare-baseline-refresh --for-proof` only after fresh main authentication, ancestry, and complete workflow/dependency/policy equivalence checks. There is no product runtime change. Later publication, recovery, custody, and merge gates remain in force.

This remains a draft. The existing Darwin arm64/ABI147 dependency audit needs a separate, genuine renewal covering the declared missing `recommended-prompts.ts` input and changed allowed-build package contracts. Until then, conservative full-tree fallback can still reject a source-only main advance. This patch does not renew that audit or claim an existing retained proof is unblocked.

## Why This Change Was Made

Dependency materialization now uses the same native Git-operation owner. Installed dependency reuse returns before computing an unused key; frozen materialization still uses the canonical complete dependency identity and conservative fallback. Lifetime, descriptor ownership, and generated-consumer checks cover that owner directly.

Production code is +735/-327 (net +408), with +17 inventory entries; tests are +371/-28 and docs +28/-5 across 13 files. The growth implements the admission and evidence-ownership boundaries, consolidates dependency materialization, and updates its dead-code consumer contract.

prs.title: fix(outbound): reject reserved placeholder delivery identities
prs.body:
Closes #199070

## What Problem This Solves

A channel adapter can finish a send without a physical platform identity. Two bundled adapters do exactly that:

- **Matrix** returns `messageId: lastMessageId || "unknown"` with an empty native receipt when the homeserver event ids were all falsy (`extensions/matrix/src/matrix/send.ts:377`).
- **iMessage** synthesizes `"ok"` when the bridge acknowledges a send without naming it (`extensions/imessage/src/send.ts:417`), and its own identity owner already classifies `"ok"` and `"unknown"` as non-identities (`extensions/imessage/src/message-guid.ts:9`).

Core held two disagreeing rules for those values:

- `normalizePlatformIds()` in `src/infra/outbound/deliver-core.ts` excluded `unknown` and `suppressed`.
- `resolveReceiptSourceId()` in `src/channels/message/receipt.ts` returned any nonblank `messageId` first, so a placeholder won the identity gate.

Because the placeholder was accepted, `observeDeliveryResult()` treated the send as identified: the delivery entered `results`, `status: "sent"` was recorded for the payload, `onDeliveryResult` persisted confirmed platform evidence, and `recordMessageSentEvent` fired with `success: true`. The record claimed confirmed delivery while the only receipt available was empty.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/channels/message/receipt.ts` owns receipt/identity semantics, so the reserved-placeholder rule now lives there as `isReservedMessageIdentity()` and both gates consume it:

- the identity gate skips a reserved placeholder in `messageId` and `pollId`, so it falls through to the nested receipt's primary id;
- `normalizePlatformIds()` keeps its existing exclusion by delegating to the same predicate.

A placeholder can no longer outrank a real multipart id, and the two gates cannot drift apart again. The reserved set is the cross-adapter placeholder vocabulary (`unknown`, `suppressed`, and the `ok` ack word that the bundled iMessage adapter documents as a bridge placeholder), so a new adapter does not have to rediscover that an acknowledged send is not an identified send.

The rest of the tree already assumes this rule, which is what made the disagreement visible:

| Owner | Current rule |
| --- | --- |
| `src/infra/outbound/deliver-core.ts` | filters `unknown` / `suppressed` out of platform ids |
| `extensions/imessage/src/message-guid.ts` | treats `ok` / `unknown` as non-identities |
| `src/infra/outbound/message-action-execution.accepted-results.test.ts` | lists `{ ok: true, messageId: "unknown" }` among payloads that stay unconfirmed |
| `src/cron/delivery.ts`, `src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.ts` | branch on `reason === "adapter_returned_no_identity"` as the uncertain case |
| `docs/plugins/sdk-channel-outbound.md` | `suppressed` + `adapter_returned_no_identity` is the ambiguous send that must not be resent; adapters should return `sent` "with the actual provider receipt" |

Fix classification: **behavior-completing** — the delivery gate now matches the receipt owner and the documented ambiguity contract.

## User Impact

A send whose transport returned only a placeholder is no longer reported as a confirmed delivery. The payload is recorded as `suppressed` with `reason: "adapter_returned_no_identity"`, the documented ambiguous bucket, so durable delivery keeps pending custody and reconciles instead of claiming success or resending.

Real identities are unchanged: a concrete `messageId`, a multipart receipt (including a case where a placeholder sits beside real event ids), a `pollId`, and `not_sent` all resolve exactly as before.

One existing fixture used the reserved placeholder as a sample *accepted* id (`message-action-execution.accepted-results.test.ts`, core-mode row). It now uses a real id so that case keeps testing caller-closure retention; the placeholder outcome is covered by the new delivery regression.

## Evidence

Base: `72f0005c889e5cb69a14ba6ef54efb2715c106ab` (current `main`; the five changed files are untouched between that commit and `84579cbdcc63`). Head: this branch.

### Red on base

Production files restored from the base commit, tests kept, then:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/channels/message/receipt.test.ts -t "reserved placeholder" --maxWorkers=1
# Tests  4 failed | 7 skipped (11)
#   AssertionError: expected 'unknown' to be undefined
#   AssertionError: expected 'suppressed' to be undefined
#   AssertionError: expected 'ok' to be undefined
#   AssertionError: expected 'unknown' to be '$event:example.org'

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/outbound/deliver-results.test.ts -t "reserved placeholder" --maxWorkers=1
# Tests  1 failed | 3 skipped (4)
#   base returns the placeholder delivery in results and records status "sent"
```

### Green on head

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/channels/message/receipt.test.ts --maxWorkers=1        # 11 passed
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/outbound/deliver-results.test.ts --maxWorkers=1  # 4 passed
```

Delivery regression (new): the adapter result is the bundled placeholder shape — reserved id plus `createMessageReceiptFromOutboundResults({ results: [] })` — driven through the real `deliverOutboundPayloadsCore` handler seam:

```
expect(results).toEqual([]);
expect(onDeliveryResult).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
expect(outcomes).toEqual([{ index: 0, status: "suppressed", reason: "adapter_returned_no_identity" }]);
```

### Shipped CLI run through the real bundled adapter and a real transport

The iMessage outbound path spawns `imsg rpc --json` and speaks newline-delimited JSON-RPC over stdio (`extensions/imessage/src/client.ts`). The proof runs the shipped CLI, the real bundled adapter, and that real subprocess transport, against a protocol-compatible bridge stand-in that acknowledges a send without naming the message — the documented path where `send.ts` synthesizes the `"ok"` placeholder.

Isolated state (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, `OPENCLAW_HOME` under `/tmp`), no Gateway process, no network:

```json5
{ gateway: { mode: "local" },
  channels: { imessage: { enabled: true, cliPath: "/tmp/proof-receipt/bin/imsg",
                          service: "imessage", allowFrom: ["*"] } } }
```

Bridge stand-in (node script, `argv=rpc --json`, answers `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":…,"result":{"ok":true}}` for `send`; it logs `imsg-stub: request method=send id=1` to prove the adapter drove it):

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts message send \
  --channel imessage --target "+15550001111" --message "proof-receipt-…" --json
```

**BASE (same command, same bridge stand-in, base source)**

```json
{ "messageId": "ok",
  "payload": { "deliveryStatus": "sent",
               "payloadOutcomes": [ { "index": 0, "status": "sent", "resultCount": 1 } ],
               "result": { "messageId": "ok",
                           "receipt": { "platformMessageIds": [], "parts": [] } } } }
# exit code 0
```

A confirmed `sent` outcome and confirmed-message bookkeeping, backed by zero platform ids.

**HEAD (same command, same bridge stand-in, this branch)**

```json
{ "messageId": null,
  "payload": { "deliveryStatus": "suppressed",
               "payloadOutcomes": [ { "index": 0, "status": "suppressed",
                                      "reason": "adapter_returned_no_identity" } ] } }
# exit code 1
```

No confirmed delivery and no confirmed-message commit; the payload keeps the documented ambiguous custody instead.

### Consumers

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  src/channels/message/outbound-bridge.test.ts \
  src/channels/plugins/contracts/outbound-payload.contract.test.ts \
  src/infra/outbound/deliver.test.ts \
  src/infra/outbound/message-action-execution.accepted-results.test.ts \
  src/infra/outbound/message-action-execution.test.ts \
  src/infra/outbound/deliver.queue-integration.test.ts \
  src/infra/outbound/delivery-completion.physical-fanout.integration.test.ts \
  extensions/matrix/src/matrix/send.test.ts extensions/imessage/src/send.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

| Surface | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `receipt.test.ts` | 11 passed |
| `deliver-results.test.ts` | 4 passed |
| `outbound-bridge.test.ts` | 9 passed |
| `outbound-payload.contract.test.ts` | passed |
| `deliver.test.ts` | 86 passed |
| `message-action-execution.accepted-results.test.ts` | 35 passed |
| `message-action-execution.test.ts` | 10 passed |
| `deliver.queue-integration.test.ts` | 13 passed |
| `delivery-completion.physical-fanout.integration.test.ts` | 30 passed |
| `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/send.test.ts` | 48 passed |
| `extensions/imessage/src/send.test.ts` | 38 passed |

### Mechanical gates

```sh
node scripts/check-line-cap-ratchet.mjs     # OK: 5 changed source files; no new violations or over-cap growth
node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts   # OK: net +55; allowance 400
node scripts/check-max-lines-ratchet.mts    # OK: 390 grandfathered suppressions
node scripts/run-format.mts --check         # All matched files use the correct format
node_modules/.bin/oxlint <5 changed files>  # 0 warnings, 0 errors
```

### Impact surface

| File | Change | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/channels/message/receipt.ts` | adds `isReservedMessageIdentity()`; `resolveReceiptSourceId()` skips reserved `messageId`/`pollId` | identity gate only; concrete ids and nested receipts unchanged |
| `src/infra/outbound/deliver-core.ts` | `normalizePlatformIds()` delegates to the shared predicate | same exclusion as before, one owner |
| `src/channels/message/receipt.test.ts` | three placeholder cases + multipart-preservation case | none |
| `src/infra/outbound/deliver-results.test.ts` | delivery regression for the placeholder shape | none |
| `src/infra/outbound/message-action-execution.accepted-results.test.ts` | sample id `unknown` → real id | keeps the caller-closure retention case honest |

## Not tested

No live Matrix homeserver or Apple bridge: the Matrix producer is pinned by source and `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/send.test.ts`, the iMessage producer by the shipped CLI run above plus `extensions/imessage/src/send.test.ts`. WhatsApp returns the same placeholder shape; it was not run against a live account. The frequency of identityless provider responses remains unmeasured, as the issue notes. The `"ok"` reserved word is intentionally narrow: it is the ack token the bundled iMessage adapter documents as a placeholder, not a general status vocabulary.

## Cleanup

Work in an isolated worktree at `72f0005c889e` with its own `node_modules`; the shipped runs used a `/tmp` state directory, a synthetic handle, and a local bridge stand-in. No live Gateway, session store, credential, user config, or Apple account was read or written.

prs.body:
Closes #195534

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a native harness seed ignores a small model window when no token budget is passed.

## User Impact

User impact: seeds for small-window models stay within the window. Runs that pass a budget are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The seed budget now follows attempt setup: explicit budget, then model window, then max tokens, then the default.

## Evidence

- New `host-seed` case with a 128-token model window and no budget: red on base (seed over 512 bytes), green with the fix.
- `host-seed` and `host-capability.annotation` tests, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxfmt and the test-line ratchet pass.
- `host-seed.test.ts`: 26 tests in about 2s on one worker. +22 test lines, allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/195534-bounded-seed-model-window.txt`.
- Not run through a live Gateway.

<!-- agent-transcript:start -->

prs.title: fix(hooks): misspelled wake modes run an immediate wake
prs.body:
Closes #178514

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `/hooks/wake` and `/hooks/agent` run an immediate wake when `mode` or `wakeMode` is misspelled (for example `next_heartbeat`), instead of the deferred wake the caller asked for.

## User Impact

Spelling variants (`next_heartbeat`, any letter case) now defer as asked. Unknown values return `400`. Omitted, null, and blank still mean `now`. Callers that sent a bad value and got an immediate wake now get a `400`.

## Why This Change Was Made

One shared normalizer replaces the two catch-all fallbacks, as recommended in the issue review.

## Evidence

- New unit test fails on `main`, passes here. `server.hooks` and early-failure suites pass (47 tests).
- Isolated Gateway from source: `next_heartbeat` and `Next-Heartbeat` now take the deferred path; `later` returns `400 mode must be now or next-heartbeat`; `/hooks/agent` with `wakeMode: "later"` returns `400`.
- `tsgo:core`, oxlint, oxfmt, docs format: clean.
- Test lines: +22 for the regression test, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/hooks-wake-mode.txt`.

## Proof

Real HTTP `POST /hooks/*` (bearer auth) against an isolated Gateway started from source by the Gateway test harness, same requests on base and on this head. The session-event handoff and the agent run are stubbed and counted (no model call): `now-wakes` is immediate wakes, `runs` is agent runs. Rows that did not change (omitted, null, blank, `next-heartbeat`) are not shown.

```
POST /hooks/wake {"text":"check inbox","mode":"next_heartbeat"}
  before: 200 {"ok":true,"mode":"now","eventOutcome":"queued"}  [now-wakes=1, runs=0]
  after:  200 {"ok":true,"mode":"next-heartbeat","eventOutcome":"queued"}  [now-wakes=0, runs=0]
POST /hooks/wake {"text":"check inbox","mode":"Next-Heartbeat"}
  before: 200 {"ok":true,"mode":"now","eventOutcome":"queued"}  [now-wakes=1, runs=0]
  after:  200 {"ok":true,"mode":"next-heartbeat","eventOutcome":"queued"}  [now-wakes=0, runs=0]
POST /hooks/wake {"text":"check inbox","mode":"later"}
  before: 200 {"ok":true,"mode":"now","eventOutcome":"queued"}  [now-wakes=1, runs=0]
  after:  400 {"ok":false,"error":"mode must be now or next-heartbeat"}  [now-wakes=0, runs=0]
POST /hooks/wake {"text":"check inbox","mode":1}
  before: 200 {"ok":true,"mode":"now","eventOutcome":"queued"}  [now-wakes=1, runs=0]
  after:  400 {"ok":false,"error":"mode must be now or next-heartbeat"}  [now-wakes=0, runs=0]
POST /hooks/wake {"text":"check inbox","mode":"next_heartbeat","sessionKey":"hook:x"}
  before: 400 {"ok":false,"error":"sessionKey is disabled for externally supplied hook payload values; set hooks.allowRequestSessionKey=true to enable"}  [now-wakes=0, runs=0]
  after:  400 {"ok":false,"error":"sessionKey requires mode=now"}  [now-wakes=0, runs=0]
POST /hooks/agent {"message":"run","wakeMode":"next_heartbeat"}
  before: 200 {"ok":true}  [now-wakes=1, runs=1]
  after:  200 {"ok":true}  [now-wakes=0, runs=1]
POST /hooks/agent {"message":"run","wakeMode":"later"}
  before: 200 {"ok":true}  [now-wakes=1, runs=1]
  after:  400 {"ok":false,"error":"wakeMode must be now or next-heartbeat"}  [now-wakes=0, runs=0]
```

### Real behavior proof (CLI-started Gateway, real model)

Head `8fd22b7`, Gateway started with `pnpm openclaw gateway run` on an isolated state dir (loopback, throwaway tokens, `hooks.enabled`), real hook HTTP requests, and a real local model (Qwen3.5 0.8B through llmman) behind the default agent. No stubs: "model requests" counts the Gateway's real calls to that model after each request. A deferred wake needs a scheduled session automation, so I first created one with `openclaw cron add --cron "0 3 * * *" --session main --system-event "nightly tick"` (without one the Gateway answers `503` to a deferred wake).

```
POST /hooks/wake {"text":"check inbox","mode":"later"}
  -> 400 {"ok":false,"error":"mode must be now or next-heartbeat"}          model requests: 0
POST /hooks/wake {"text":"check inbox","mode":1}
  -> 400 {"ok":false,"error":"mode must be now or next-heartbeat"}          model requests: 0
POST /hooks/wake {"text":"check inbox","mode":"Next-Heartbeat"}
  -> 200 {"ok":true,"mode":"next-heartbeat","eventOutcome":"queued"}       model requests: 0
POST /hooks/wake {"text":"check inbox","mode":"next_heartbeat","sessionKey":"hook:x"}
  -> 400 {"ok":false,"error":"sessionKey requires mode=now"}                model requests: 0
POST /hooks/agent {"message":"run","wakeMode":"later"}
  -> 400 {"ok":false,"error":"wakeMode must be now or next-heartbeat"}      model requests: 0
POST /hooks/wake {"text":"Reply with the single word PONG.","mode":"now"}
  -> 200 {"ok":true,"mode":"now","eventOutcome":"queued"}                  model requests: 1
POST /hooks/agent {"message":"Reply with the single word PONG.","wakeMode":"next_heartbeat"}
  -> 200 {"ok":true,"runId":"2f4a585b-..."}                                model requests: 3
     [hooks] hook agent run completed runId=2f4a585b-... status=ok model=unsloth/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF
```

Misspelled or non-string values are rejected before any dispatch, a spelling variant defers instead of waking immediately, and `mode: "now"` and the agent run reach the real model. Not run: the upgrade path from a stable release with existing hook settings, the earlier `main` behavior (see the harness table above), and the owner decision on the `400` for unknown values.

**Agent:** Added `normalizeHookWakeMode` in `src/gateway/hooks.ts` and used it for both `mode` and `wakeMode`. Added a unit test and updated `docs/gateway/config-hooks.md`.

**Agent:** Test red on base, green with the fix. Ran the related hook server suites, typecheck, lint, format.

prs.title: fix(ui): Control UI breaks under browser auto-translate
prs.body:
Closes #191961

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Control UI shows a "panel failed to load" error in Edge when browser auto-translate is on.

## User Impact

The Control UI no longer breaks under auto-translate. It already localizes itself. Browser translate of chat text is off for the page.

## Why This Change Was Made

Auto-translate rewrites text nodes under the Solid renderer, so `insertBefore` throws. The shell now sets `translate="no"` and `notranslate`.

## Evidence

- New test fails on main, passes here.
- Not tried in Edge: headless can't run its translate. Two reporters on the issue confirmed translate as the cause.

## Proof (partial)

Built Control UI (Sessions page) in real headless Chrome through the UI e2e harness, with a simulated translator that wraps every text node the browser reports as translatable in `<font>`, like a page translator:

```
            html translate attr   html.translate   text nodes replaced
main        null                  true             109
this PR     "no"                  false            0
```

Not shown: Edge's own translator, and the original `insertBefore` crash. Neither reproduces in headless, and the simulation did not trigger it on main either. This only shows the opt-out reaches the built page.

<details>
<summary>Agent transcript (trimmed)</summary>

**User:** Pick the open issue you can fix most confidently with no PR yet, and open a PR.

**Agent:** Checked open bug issues for linked PRs. #192031, #186832, #173611 already have PRs. #191043 and #193262 need maintainer decisions or Windows repro. #191961 has a confirmed cause in the thread: Edge translate rewrites text nodes while `<html lang="en">` is hardcoded.

**Agent:** `translate.ts` already sets `lang` at runtime, but Edge decides at load. Chose `translate="no"` plus `<meta name="google" content="notranslate">` in `ui/index.html`. Tradeoff: no browser translation of chat text.

**Agent:** Added a test beside the `index.html` boot test. Red on main, green with the change. `oxfmt` clean.

prs.title: fix(active-memory): Italian recall questions skip deep recall
prs.body:
Closes #188550

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Italian questions about the past never trigger Active Memory deep recall in `escalate` mode.

## User Impact

User impact: Italian users get deep recall for questions like "che motto usavo?".

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an Italian entry to the localized recall patterns, with future cues and "ti ricordi di + verb" kept quiet.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof: isolated Gateway (scratch state dir, loopback port), Active Memory in `escalate` mode, local stand-in model, each message sent with `chat.send` to `agent:main:main`. "recall" means Active Memory logs `start`; "skipped" means the main model receives the "intentionally skipped deep recall" note.

```text
                                                  main (ee75d02)   PR (d6e1b3f)
che motto usavo?                                  skipped          recall
cosa avevamo deciso sul motto, nei mesi scorsi?   skipped          recall
ricordami di comprare il latte domani             skipped          skipped
ti ricordi di chiamare Marco domani?              skipped          skipped
ciao, come stai?                                  skipped          skipped

PR gateway log, "che motto usavo?":
[plugins] active-memory: agent=main session=agent:main:main activeProvider=mock activeModel=stub thinking=off fast=inherit start timeoutMs=15000 queryChars=103 searchQueryChars=16
[plugins] active-memory: agent=main session=agent:main:main activeProvider=mock activeModel=stub thinking=off fast=inherit done status=no_relevant_memory elapsedMs=1731
main gateway log, same message: no active-memory start line
```

`resolveRecallEscalationDecision`, `escalate` mode:

```text
main: "che motto usavo?" no-recall-intent
PR:   "che motto usavo?" recall
```

Escalation tests: 7 fail on main, 148 pass here. `tsgo:extensions`, oxlint and oxfmt pass.

### Real behavior proof (real model)

Same scenarios with a real model instead of the stand-in: isolated Gateway (scratch state dir, loopback, throwaway token) built from this head (`d6e1b3f`), `qwen3.5-0.8b` (Unsloth GGUF) served by a local llmman/llama.cpp process, used as both the main model and the Active Memory recall model, `escalate` mode, each message sent with `chat.send` to `agent:main:main` and the previous run finished before the next. Base is the same tree with only `extensions/active-memory/escalation.ts` reverted to the merge base (`ee75d02`). Gateway log lines, trimmed (`recall skipped reason=session-ineligible` lines from the recall sub-run itself are omitted):

```text
                                                  base (ee75d02)            this PR (d6e1b3f)
che motto usavo?                                  skipped no-recall-intent  start ... done status=no_relevant_memory
cosa avevamo deciso sul motto, nei mesi scorsi?   skipped no-recall-intent  start ... done status=failed
ricordami di comprare il latte domani             (not run)                 skipped no-recall-intent
ti ricordi di chiamare Marco domani?              (not run)                 skipped no-recall-intent
ciao, come stai?                                  (not run)                 skipped no-recall-intent

PR, "che motto usavo?":
active-memory: agent=main session=agent:main:main activeProvider=llmman activeModel=unsloth/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF thinking=off fast=inherit start timeoutMs=60000 queryChars=16 searchQueryChars=16
active-memory: agent=main session=agent:main:main activeProvider=llmman activeModel=unsloth/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF thinking=off fast=inherit done status=no_relevant_memory elapsedMs=34775 summaryChars=0
base, same message:
active-memory: recall skipped reason=no-recall-intent
```

The recall model is tiny, so what it returns (`no_relevant_memory`, `failed`) says nothing about recall quality; this only shows the gate: the two Italian past-recall questions start a real-model recall on this head and are skipped on base, while the reminder and greeting messages stay quiet. The main turn of the fourth message ended with an error from the tiny model after its skip decision, which does not affect the gate. Not run: a populated memory with a hit, other model sizes, the upgrade path from a stable release.

prs.title: fix(acp): a failed identity save leaves a new backend session on every request
prs.body:
Closes #127371

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an ACP request succeeds on a backend identity that was never saved when the identity write fails, and the next request opens yet another backend session.

## User Impact

User impact: a failed identity save now fails the request and closes the new handle, instead of silently opening a new backend session on every call.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ensure write is now strict like session init: it must return the stored ACP entry before the handle is cached. Init and ensure share the close and persisted-entry helpers. Control and refused publications keep their handle open, as before.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof: isolated Gateway with the `acpx` backend. The backend is a tiny ACP agent I wrote over stdio (official SDK, no session resume), not a real harness. The storage failure is injected: a SQLite trigger aborts `acp_sessions` updates that store a new backend session id for session A (`database or disk is full`). Sessions A and B were created with `/acp spawn toy --mode persistent --thread off`, then the Gateway was restarted:

```text
main (74f111a):
$ openclaw agent --session-key <A> --message "A request 1"   exit=0  pong   # opened toy-1351073-1, prompt sent, identity never saved
$ openclaw agent --session-key <A> --message "A request 2"   exit=0  pong   # closed toy-1351073-1, opened toy-1351194-1, prompt sent
gateway log: acp-manager: failed persisting ACP metadata for <A>: Error: database or disk is full

PR (5059270):
$ openclaw agent --session-key <A> --message "A request 1"   exit=1  OpenClaw couldn't save your conversation because the disk is full. ...
                                                                    # opened toy-1349192-1, closed it, no prompt sent
$ openclaw agent --session-key <A> --message "A request 2"   exit=1  (same)   # opened toy-1349284-1, closed it, no prompt sent
$ openclaw agent --session-key <B> --message "B request 2"   exit=0  pong     # prompt to B's own toy-1349059-1, untouched
-- trigger dropped, storage restored --
$ openclaw agent --session-key <A> --message "A request 3"   exit=0  pong     # opened toy-1349394-1, prompt sent
$ openclaw agent --session-key <A> --message "A request 4"   exit=0  pong     # same toy-1349394-1, no new backend session
```

- `manager.runtime-handle-ensure.reset.test.ts`: red on main (resolves), green here, for a failing write and for no returned entry.
- `pnpm test:changed`, `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, lint and format pass. `check:changed` fails only the dead-export scan on files this PR does not touch.
- Test lines +38, under the ceiling.

prs.title: improve(ui): copy selected text out of the Browser panel
prs.body:
<!-- Related: #187032 and #187075 also touch the Browser panel; the three merge cleanly together -->

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: text cannot be copied out of the Control UI Browser panel. The remote page is drawn as a screenshot, Ctrl/Cmd+C was never handled, a native copy copied the panel's empty input and left the clipboard unchanged, and the actions menu only offered "Copy URL". Text the agent selected, or that a page selected itself, could not reach the user's clipboard.

## User Impact

User impact: press Ctrl/Cmd+C with the page focused, use the browser's Copy, or choose **Copy selection** in the Browser actions menu to put the remote page's selected text on your local clipboard; a "Copied" notice confirms it. An empty selection, a disconnected panel, disabled page scripting (`browser.evaluateEnabled=false`) or a clipboard failure each show a notice naming the next step, and the menu entry is disabled with a reason when there is nothing to copy. Password fields and cross-origin frames are never copied. Mac tabs still copy natively with ⌘C. Known gap: the panel cannot yet create a selection in the remote page (no drag-select, no Ctrl/Cmd+A), so copy works on selections that already exist; the notices tell users to ask the agent to select text.

## Why This Change Was Made

The panel already runs page functions through the existing `act:evaluate` route, so a small page script reads the selection back (input/textarea ranges, open shadow roots, same-origin frames, capped at 1,000,000 characters). No Gateway, protocol or model-facing tool change is needed. The clipboard write needs a live user gesture but the text only arrives after a round trip, so `copyToClipboard` now accepts a pending promise (`ClipboardItem`, then `writeText`, then `execCommand`). The tab and connection are rechecked right before the write so a stale result from another tab is dropped, a read that finishes after a newer copy never overwrites it, and selected text never reaches logs, errors, the local textarea, chat or panel state. Forwarding the key to the remote browser's clipboard was rejected because the Gateway cannot read that clipboard.

## Evidence
