prs.title: feat: watch a running command automation's output live in the Control UI
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a long-running command automation shows nothing in Automations, Run history until it finishes, so an operator cannot tell what a multi-hour job is doing. Only Settings, Logs is live, and it does not contain the script's output.

## User Impact

User impact: while a command automation runs, its Run history shows a **Live output** panel that follows the combined stdout and stderr like `tail -f`. It auto-scrolls, pauses when you scroll up (with a **Jump to latest** button), and stops polling while the browser tab is hidden. When the run ends the panel goes away and the recorded run appears in the list as before. Gateway clients can read the same tail with `cron.liveOutput`.

Risks and limits:
- Live text is redacted with the tool-payload policy, so it can be masked more strictly than the recorded summary of the same run. The recorded summary is unchanged. A private key is masked across polls; one whose start was already dropped from a full tail is masked only while its end line is still held.
- Only the most recent output is kept: at most 256 KiB, or `payload.outputMaxBytes` when that is smaller. The panel keeps the last 2000 lines.
- Agent-turn runs have no live panel. Their transcript is still available only after the run is recorded (see Evidence).

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway keeps a fixed-size in-memory ring for the active run. The command runner owns it and discards it in its existing `finally`, so exit, timeout, abort and spawn failure all clean up through one path. `cron.liveOutput` (`operator.read`, same job visibility checks as `cron.get`) returns complete lines from a byte cursor, so a reconnect neither loses nor repeats lines. The panel reuses the existing visible-poll and stream-auto-follow helpers. Cursor polling, like `logs.tail`, keeps the Gateway free of timers and per-chunk broadcasts when nobody is watching. No config key, schema or migration; `cron.history` and `cron.runs` are unchanged.

Size: about 360 lines of new production code across 3 modules, about 560 lines of tests, small edits to existing files, plus regenerated validator files.

## Evidence

Before and after screenshots (Run history of a running command job; Live output panel; paused with **Jump to latest**; hand-off when the run ends) are in the first comment below. The extra Error row in the before shot is from restarting the throwaway Gateway while testing.


- Throwaway Gateway (own state dir, port 28789, loopback, throwaway token) and a real headless Chrome against the built Control UI. A command job printed a line per second for 60 to 90 s. Follow reads returned only new lines, replaying a cursor was idempotent, stderr was interleaved in order, a fake `token=sk-...` was masked, and `active` flipped to `false` exactly when `state.runningAtMs` cleared, including after a job timeout. The recorded run was unchanged.
- Tests: buffer bounds and fixed memory, cursor, drop-oldest, UTF-8 safety, redaction (including a private key across polls) and escape stripping, cleanup on exit, timeout, abort and spawn failure; the gateway method (follow, inactive, validation, visibility, access closed mid-read); the UI line bound and panel (follow, hidden tab, hand-off, still polling before the command starts, jump to latest).
- Review round: fixes covered by focused tests and typecheck; the current-head Gateway run is under Real behavior proof below. `check:changed` passes except the dead export scan, which flags `flattenRun` in `scripts/lib/catalog-compare-released-diff.mts` (already on main, not in this PR).
- Checks run: `pnpm gateway:validators:check`, `pnpm protocol-registry:check`, the protocol since-guard (new method vintage `2026.10`), the native protocol check, scoped core and UI tests (including the existing `command-runner`, `cron.history` and `cron.runs` suites), `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, and `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main` (all lanes passed). I re-ran the validators, registry and new tests after the work finished.
- Agent-turn runs: not changed. Run history rows, including the transcript binding `cron.history` needs, are written when the run completes, so an in-flight run has no row and **View transcript** is unavailable. Live agent transcripts need an early binding row from the run owner and a follow protocol for transcript pages, which is a separate change.
- Local review: autoreview and local ClawSweeper were not run. The author read the full diff against the simplify checklist before opening.
- Not covered: hidden-tab pause in a real browser (unit-tested with a mocked `visibilityState`), narrow layout, dark theme and RTL screenshots, Windows and macOS, WebKit, the full test suite.

### Real behavior proof

Current head `1bb85c8a42c`, built with `pnpm openclaw`, against an isolated Gateway (own state dir, loopback, port 28789, throwaway token). A command job (`openclaw cron add --command`, then `openclaw cron run`) printed one line per second for 20 s, including a synthetic token, a synthetic private key split across polls, and one stderr line. I polled `cron.liveOutput` with `openclaw gateway call`, sending back the returned `cursor` and `runAtMs` (trimmed):

```
11:22:28 cursor=0   -> active:true reset:true cursor:14  "line 1 stdout\n"
11:22:31 cursor=14  -> active:true cursor:56  "line 2 stdout\nline 3 stdout\nline 4 stdout\n"
11:22:34 cursor=56  -> active:true cursor:174 "line 5 stdout\napi token=sk-pro…7890 used\nline 6 stdout\nline 7 stdout\nwarn 7 on stderr\n"
11:22:37 cursor=174 -> active:true cursor:310 "line 8 stdout\nline 9 stdout\n-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----…redacted…\n"
11:22:40 cursor=310 -> active:true cursor:381 "…redacted…-----END PRIVATE KEY-----\nline 13 stdout\n"
11:22:43 cursor=381 -> active:true cursor:426 "line 14 stdout\nline 15 stdout\nline 16 stdout\n"
11:22:46 cursor=426 -> active:true cursor:471 "line 17 stdout\nline 18 stdout\nline 19 stdout\n"
11:22:49 cursor=471 -> active:false cursor:0 ""   (run ended, buffer discarded)
```

Each poll returned only new complete lines, stderr arrived in order, the token and the private key (across polls) were masked, and `active` flipped to `false` when the run ended. `cron.runs` then recorded the finished run with its full, unchanged summary. Not re-run on this head: the Control UI panel (the screenshots above are from an earlier head).

Follow-ups: `openclaw automations runs <id> --follow` (needs a polling loop, abort handling and a `--json` decision); live agent-turn transcripts; `public-schema.ts` is at its line cap, so the new live-output schema types are not re-exported there and a maintainer may prefer a sibling file.

prs.title: fix(openai): Ark Responses fails on the turn after a tool call
prs.body:
Closes #116691

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a custom `openai-responses` model on Volcengine Ark fails with `missing input.status` on the turn after a tool call.

## User Impact

Ark and BytePlus ModelArk Responses routes keep working after tool calls. Other custom routes are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replayed `function_call` and `reasoning` items now get `status: "completed"` on Ark hosts instead of having status stripped. Other custom routes still strip it (#100831).

## Evidence

Real behavior proof, with one stand-in: no live Ark call (no key). The real Gateway and `openclaw agent` CLI use provider `custom-volces` (`api: openai-responses`, base URL host `ark.cn-beijing.volces.com`), with the Gateway's `HTTP_PROXY` pointing at a local stand-in endpoint. It returns Ark's 400 `MissingParameter ... input.status` (text from the issue log) when a replayed `function_call` or `reasoning` item has no `status`. A tool call turn, then a second user turn on the same session:

```text
main (2b9dd45):
$ openclaw agent --agent main --model custom-volces/doubao-seed-evolving --session-id ark-1 --message "read IDENTITY.md"
LLM request rejected: The request failed because it is missing \`input\.status\` parameter\. Request id\: req\-2 | MissingParameter   exit=1
  #2 -> 400 MissingParameter  replay: reasoning[status=<none>], function_call[status=<none>], function_call_output
$ openclaw agent ... --session-id ark-1 --message "read it again"
LLM request rejected: ... | MissingParameter   exit=1
  #3 -> 400 MissingParameter

PR (ee08560):
$ openclaw agent --agent main --model custom-volces/doubao-seed-evolving --session-id ark-1 --message "read IDENTITY.md"
Done, I read the file.   exit=0
  #2 -> 200  replay: reasoning[status=completed], function_call[status=completed], function_call_output
$ openclaw agent ... --session-id ark-1 --message "read it again"
Done, I read the file.   exit=0
  #3 -> 200, #4 -> 200  (older reasoning and function_call replayed with status=completed)

Other custom host (llm.example.com), main (#5) and PR (#6) alike:
  -> 200  replay: reasoning[status=<none>], function_call[status=<none>], function_call_output
```

- Policy test red on base, green here (Volcengine and BytePlus hosts, custom route still strips). Touched tests, tsgo core and core:test, oxlint, format pass.
- Test lines net -11.
- Gap: not run against the real Ark API (no key). The Ark requirement is from the issue report and docs.

prs.title: fix(worktrees): choose known repositories and base branches
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Creating a worktree requires retyping repository paths and branch names that the page already knows.

## User Impact

Choose known repositories and discovered branches by name, search the lists, or enter a custom repository path, branch, tag, or commit. **Automatic base** retains the existing Gateway decision: remote default when configured, otherwise local HEAD. Only **Create** creates a worktree.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both reference fields use the existing picker and creation model. Repository choices come from the current managed-worktree records, not a new filesystem scan or a complete project catalog. Branches still come from the selected repository’s existing discovery owner. Changing the source clears its old base selection and cancels the old branch read before it can repopulate the new source’s choices. Unknown refs, custom drafts, failed creation, offline editing, and admin boundaries remain supported.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

The existing Activity projection now keeps the Everyone count unknown until a result exists. Its People consumer accepts that same optional value; the existing row already omits an unavailable count. prs.title: ci: refresh measured test timings
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Refresh stale CI shard weights from successful jobs in completed scheduled main CI workflows, successful release-check runs, and exact compact selectors and tooling files from successful pull-request CI runs.

## Why This Change Was Made

The daily refit uses independent-run medians, rejects outliers and single samples, and keeps existing weights within the 15% replacement band. Failed main workflows contribute successful timing jobs without supplying pruning evidence. Pull-request measurements describe the merge-ref: exact compact selector keys, runtime inventory observations, and native tooling file costs can update, but partial plans never reprice unqualified compact parents or prune absent measurements. Worker timing identities must agree with observed admission. Main compact keys absent from every contributing run are removed only after three successful contributing workflows for that profile. The complete artifact report lists every change and removal.

## User Impact

Only shard balance changes; test discovery still determines the complete test inventory. This standing branch is updated automatically and never pushes to main.

## Evidence

Generated with `pnpm ci:timings:refit` from runs: 43506572021, 43533287147, 43555298196, 43555325522, 43556630588, 43559326432, 43561499832, 43566729523, 43571046461, 43575819215, 43579529335, 43579793714, 43580244890, 43580653794, 43581128526.

[Download the complete timing report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43581935636/artifacts/14109576324).

prs.title: fix: repository refresh failures hide Git diagnostics
prs.body:
Related: #197849
Follow-up to #197862.

## What Problem This Solves

Managed repository refresh failures hide the underlying Git error, and diagnostic messages must retain the next step for users rather than only directing them to operator logs.

## User Impact

Refresh preparation and branch failures explain what happened in plain language and ask users to send their message again to retry. If the failure persists, the diagnostic ID connects the session error to the operator log. The complete explanation, retry step, and diagnostic ID fit the bounded session summary; raw Git output stays out of the shared conversation.

Credentials, authentication classification, cancellation policy, retry execution, and checkout cleanup are unchanged. Clone/fetch wording from #197862 is unchanged. The original production clone/cancellation cause remains unknown, so this PR does not close the issue.

## Why This Change Was Made

Four refresh error paths bypassed the existing diagnostic logger. They now share that formatter and keep its operation names and complete process records in operator logs. An inline phrase selection restores the documented same-session retry guidance without exposing internal terms such as "seed refs" to users. No additional helper or recovery policy is introduced.

Against the original base: production **+24/-15** lines, tests **+66**, docs **+2**. The latest repair changes **5 production lines and 7 test lines in place** (+12/-12 total, no net growth), shortening the producer phrases and retry sentence. Including `ProjectCloneError: ` and a 36-character UUID, the complete messages are **149 / 154 / 158 / 156 characters** for prepare/read/seed/update respectively, all below the 160-character summary limit. Only the two existing regressions were extended; no new tests or helpers were added. The documentation sentence still matches.

## Evidence

### Current candidate: `26bc7467566cfef0695ba786fea4141a0cd7b074`

Commit: `fix(projects): fit refresh failure messages in the session summary`.

- Both existing refresh regressions fail against `ac1eb9b3c486786170660f8b872838ebe0ebf5e6` specifically because the retained summary contains the middle-elision marker. With the producer repair, the full clone-runtime file passes **25/25** (39.74 s command wall time including compiler preparation).
- The same two native-Git cases now assert the complete explanation sentence, the **Send again** step, and complete diagnostic ID in `resolveSessionRunError({ error: String(error) }, "failed")`, with no ` ... ` marker. Existing log correlation and same-checkout recovery assertions remain.
- Core and affected-test typechecks, scoped lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. The pr-simplify pass found no unrelated changes or additional abstractions.
- Independent Auto Review (OpenClaw engine, P0–P2), original base `fa155ff6f53e18f426d7b97ba3407976959380a0` → candidate snapshot published as this head: **scoped-clean**, no findings. The reviewer did not independently execute tests.

**Exact-new-head Gateway proof is pending Anmol's isolated CLI replay** (failure → same-session retry → recovery on `origin/test`). The existing capture below covers the prior head only. No hosted re-review has been requested for this repair; it will follow the new proof at the requester's direction.

### Prior-head Gateway proof: `ac1eb9b3c486786170660f8b872838ebe0ebf5e6`

**Exact-head CLI proof supplied by @anmol0b:** [failure, same-session retry, and recovery capture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198444#issuecomment-6886057504). The isolated Gateway was built from `ac1eb9b3c486786170660f8b872838ebe0ebf5e6`, used its own HOME/state/config/profile and a loopback mock model, and cloned public `octocat/Hello-World` with native Git and no GitHub token. Git and workspace preparation were not mocked. The selected base was `origin/test`, the remote-tracking ref; bare `test` does not resolve through this path.

The capture shows both failed runs retaining distinct complete IDs matching operator records, followed by a fresh recovery run after removing the lock. This closed the earlier missing-recovery gap for that head, but does not prove the latest message wording. These are the contributor's recorded observations, not an additional run performed by this agent.

<details>
<summary>Sanitized exact-head CLI excerpt: failure → failed retry → recovery</summary>

```text
Tested SHA: ac1eb9b3c486786170660f8b872838ebe0ebf5e6

sessions.create (worktreeBaseRef=origin/test; master.lock held)
  runId=b23a624c-6582-4290-ab9b-174113e2f3a0
  status=failed updatedAt=1794699589108
chat.history lastRunError:
  ProjectCloneError: Git could not update the managed ... Send again to retry; if it fails, give the operator Diagnostic ID: df514ee4-de64-4388-a915-913a3cb18643.

chat.send (same session; lock still held)
  runId=proof-retry-1
  status=failed updatedAt=1794699607333
chat.history lastRunError:
  ProjectCloneError: Git could not update the managed ... Send again to retry; if it fails, give the operator Diagnostic ID: cdd0ad3a-29c8-47e4-af67-a55a00c73adb.

Matching projects/clone records:
  diagnosticId=df514ee4-de64-4388-a915-913a3cb18643
  operation="update refs" exitCode=128 termination="exit" signal=null
  stderr="fatal: cannot lock ref 'refs/remotes/origin/master': Unable to create '<run>/state/projects/1d7ed7bd7bc9f544/hello-world/.git/refs/remotes/origin/master.lock': File exists. ..."
  stdout=""
  diagnosticId=cdd0ad3a-29c8-47e4-af67-a55a00c73adb
  operation="update refs" exitCode=128 termination="exit" signal=null
  stderr="fatal: cannot lock ref 'refs/remotes/origin/master': Unable to create '<run>/state/projects/1d7ed7bd7bc9f544/hello-world/.git/refs/remotes/origin/master.lock': File exists. ..."
  stdout=""

Lock removed; chat.send in the same session:
  before: runId=proof-retry-1 updatedAt=1794699607333
  after:  runId=proof-retry-2 updatedAt=1794699629368 status=done
  worktree branch=openclaw/ready-2
  worktree HEAD=b3cbd5bbd7e81436d2eee04537ea2b4c0cad4cdf (= origin/test)
  chat.history assistant reply="Ready."
```

Paths are redacted; credentials and loopback ports are omitted. The full commands and capture are linked above.

</details>

**Finding reproduced on that prior head and repaired in the current producer:** the 160-character summary elided part of the operation explanation. The two updated regressions now require the full sentence, retry step, and complete ID without elision. The new Gateway capture is still pending.

### Earlier-head proof (not new-head runtime evidence)

- [Public red/green CLI Gateway proof supplied by @anmol0b](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198444#issuecomment-6885395428) compares the original base with `3d6a5055c28770440894f2af3437e1503f88df61`. Native Git and an isolated Gateway demonstrate `sessions.create` and same-session `chat.send` failures, complete distinct IDs in `chat.history`, and matching operator log records with the ref-lock error and exit code 128. A loopback mock model was used. Successful Gateway recovery after lock removal was not captured.
- The earlier isolated WebSocket proof and E2E runtime build passed, but have not been repeated for the wording follow-up.

<details>
<summary>Previously investigated sibling checks and environment limitations</summary>

Refresh/default-base selection on the earlier head: 13 passed, 3 failed. One fixture was refused by the sandbox shallow-history safeguard. Two partial-clone assertions expected Git exit 1 but received 128; both reproduced with the production patch removed. No assertions were weakened.

The broader workspace preparation suite on the original base had 9 passes and 9 failures; worktree allocation encountered the sandbox's 1 GiB temporary filesystem versus the 4 GiB reserve. An isolated proof can use the supported `worktreeRoot` setting on a filesystem with sufficient free space without changing the reserve. These suites have not been rerun for this wording-only follow-up.

</details>

Hosted CI/job-second accounting is not yet available for the new head. No UI layout change or configuration changes to the running installation.

Worked on by: Anmol

prs.title: fix: Scribe setup assumes a new conversation and default model
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Scribe setup promises a new conversation and the agent’s default model even when it reuses an existing conversation, while the overview assumes every visible Scribe belongs to the viewer.

## User Impact

User impact: setup explains conversation reuse and the conversation’s model settings, without suggesting that viewing a shared Scribe transfers ownership or private access. Actions, prompts, model selection, permissions and schedules are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The start owner already reuses a saved conversation and sends the prompt without a model override. The scheduler’s visibility rules also permit administrators to inspect other people’s automations. The copy now describes those existing behaviors instead of assuming a new, viewer-owned conversation. The obsolete store-name input used only by that claim is removed; no new state or helper is added. Documentation is aligned.

This is separate from the queue wording in #199259, control wording in #199267, and the history-error correction retained in #199298. The broader copy/localization diff in #195010 retains these context claims.

## Evidence

- Two regression assertions fail against the original copy; **45 Scribe view/state tests pass** after the correction, retaining creation, reuse, archive restoration, retries and exact generated-prompt coverage.
- A full built-app flow through the real packaged plugin passes before/after on baseline 3049d421c9514b143e4632de911daf8f9b1e8cd8. It opens the Scribes list and setup dialog, expands the real prompt disclosure, starts setup, and verifies exactly one chat.send to the existing conversation, zero sessions.create calls, identical prompt bytes and no model override or schedule update.
- Scheduler visibility/ownership and Scribe discovery/start owners inspected. This does not claim live cross-person execution or access transfer testing.
- Scoped lint, browser typegraph, full UI typecheck, i18n baseline/verification, formatting and diff checks pass. No broad local suite.

Real components with synthetic sessions, an administrator-visible job owned by a different fixture profile, and mocked transport; emulated 1280 × 1100 viewport. No live Scribe, model call or private store was changed.

prs.title: fix: failed auto-compaction reply recommends /compact, which hits the same failure
prs.body:
Closes #148766

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a session overflows and auto-compaction also fails, the reply tells the user to "try again, use /compact, or use /new", then repeats "Try starting a fresh session…". Retrying and /compact rerun the compaction that just failed, and the reply never names the command that does recover the session.

## User Impact

User impact: after a failed auto-compaction, users are pointed at `/new` (fresh session) or a larger-context model. Operators who want to keep the session get a session-specific trim command. Ordinary keys are shown once and paste into cmd.exe, PowerShell, or a POSIX shell. Keys that need quoting, such as Matrix keys with `!` and `$`, get labeled forms: one for macOS, Linux, or PowerShell and one for Windows Command Prompt. When a key contains an apostrophe, POSIX and PowerShell quote it differently, so PowerShell gets its own form. A warning before the command says trimming permanently deletes older history with no backup and suggests `openclaw backup create` first. The reply no longer recommends retrying or /compact. Session handling is unchanged, and no action is required.

New reply for a typical session:

```text
⚠️ Auto-compaction could not recover this turn. I kept this conversation mapped to the current session. Use /new to start a fresh session.

Try a model with a larger context window.

To keep this session instead, an operator can trim its transcript. Trimming permanently deletes older history and keeps no backup, so run `openclaw backup create` first if that history matters, then `openclaw sessions compact agent:main:main --agent main --max-lines 200`.
```

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildContextOverflowRecoveryText` hard-coded the retry, /compact, and /new advice and never received the session key. Both production callers (the execution error handler and fallback settlement) now pass `turn.sessionKey`. The builder renders the documented `openclaw sessions compact <key> --max-lines` fallback through the existing `quoteCliArg`, `quotePowerShellArg`, and `formatCliCommand` owners. `formatCliCommand` adds `--profile`/`--container` when the Gateway runs under one. Current `main` has removed the heartbeat-bleed hint and the builder's model parameters, so the builder now takes only the agent id and session key.

Quoting:
- Ordinary keys like `agent:main:main` stay bare and work in every shell. This addresses the last open review finding on #149415.
- When a key needs quoting, the reply labels each shell's form.
  - For macOS, Linux, or PowerShell, it uses single quotes, which keep `!` and `$` literal.
  - If the key contains an apostrophe, the POSIX escape (`'\''`) is not valid PowerShell, so a separate PowerShell form is rendered with `quotePowerShellArg` (doubled apostrophes), as `config-cli-path.ts` already does.
  - For Windows Command Prompt, it uses double quotes. cmd.exe would keep single quotes as part of the key, and inside double quotes it leaves `!` and `$` literal while delayed expansion is off, which is the default.
- `sessions compact` has no key-free selector (it takes only `<key>`), so a shell-specific form is the smallest supported route.

/new stays because an explicit reset writes a `context: "clear"` boundary (`session-hooks.ts`). The issue comment's other root cause, `/new` rejected by the preflight compaction gate (#121617), was closed by #172912, which is already in this base. The Feishu/WeCom reset-remapping theory in the issue is still unverified and is out of scope here. The preflight-compaction failure copy in `agent-runner-failure-reply.ts` is a separate path, includes timeout failures that can be transient, and is left unchanged.

Builds on #149415 by @aldiz1711 (closed by its author with an invitation to continue). That PR's deletion/backup warning and session-specific command carry over. The single-quote-only rendering that review flagged for cmd.exe is replaced.

## Evidence

**Update 2026-10-31: merged current `main` (`f708b8baeb`) into this branch (merge commit `623e90aa54`, no force-push), plus `f4f249b0da` for the ClawSweeper finding.**
- Conflicts: `agent-runner-context-recovery.ts` and its test, `agent-runner-error-handler.ts`, `agent-runner-fallback-settlement.ts`, and `agent-runner-execution-context-failures.test.ts`. `main` removed the heartbeat recovery paths, and `buildContextOverflowRecoveryText()` no longer takes any parameters. I kept that streamlined builder and re-applied only this PR's change. Both callers pass `{ agentId, sessionKey }`, and the reply drops /compact and adds the warned trim command. The tests follow `main`'s new layout. Current `main` still says "Please try again, use /compact, or use /new", so the defect is still present.
- Review finding (P2, PowerShell quoting): addressed in `f4f249b0da`. The command is rendered with `quoteCliArg` (POSIX), `quotePowerShellArg` (PowerShell), and double quotes (cmd.exe). One shared form is printed when the renderings match. A key like `agent:main:bob's` now renders as:
  `openclaw sessions compact 'agent:main:bob'\''s' --agent main --max-lines 200` (macOS or Linux), `openclaw sessions compact 'agent:main:bob''s' --agent main --max-lines 200` (PowerShell), or `openclaw sessions compact "agent:main:bob's" --agent main --max-lines 200` (Windows Command Prompt).
  A new unit test covers this case. PowerShell itself was not run here (no `pwsh` on this machine), so the PowerShell form is checked against `quotePowerShellArg`'s doubling rule rather than executed.
- Merge conflict: resolved.
- Tests (`--maxWorkers=1`):
  - `agent-runner-context-recovery.test.ts`: `Tests 4 passed (4)`
  - `agent-runner-execution-context-failures.test.ts`: `Tests 4 passed (4)`
  - `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts` (registers the compaction cases): `Tests 197 passed (197)`
- `pnpm check:changed --base upstream/main`: typecheck and format pass. Lint and the dead-export scan fail only on files this PR does not touch, and fail the same way on current `main`.

The original evidence below was recorded before this merge.

Base: rebased onto `879e99cb1` (current `main`). That base includes 25acc454d, which repairs the `ui/src/pages/chat/session-snapshot-store.test.ts` failure behind the earlier red lint/test-types CI lanes. The before/after proof below was recorded on `e032d1e31`, and `main` has not changed these files since then.

**Shipped entry point: Gateway `chat.send`, the WebChat/Control UI path, before and after.**

Setup:
- Real built Gateway and CLI (`pnpm openclaw gateway run`, `node openclaw.mjs gateway call`).
- Isolated state directory and loopback ports.
- One custom `openai-completions` provider pointing at a small loopback server. The server answers every completion with HTTP 400 `context_length_exceeded`.
- One `chat.send` per session key. Replaying the same `idempotencyKey` returns the settled run result, whose error message is the reply text delivered to the chat client.

Gateway log for each turn (same on base and branch):

```text
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 1/3); attempting auto-compaction for fakeoverflow/tiny
[agent/embedded] auto-compaction failed for fakeoverflow/tiny: Nothing to compact (session too small)
[agent/embedded] [context-overflow-recovery] exhausted provider overflow recovery for fakeoverflow/tiny; livenessState=blocked suggestedAction=reset_or_new kind=context_overflow
Auto-compaction failed (400 This model's maximum context length is 8192 tokens. However, your messages resulted in 250000 tokens. Please reduce the length of the messages.). Preserving existing session mapping for agent:main:main.
```

Base build (`e032d1e31`), `sessionKey: "agent:main:main"`:

```text
$ openclaw gateway call chat.send --params '{"sessionKey":"agent:main:main","message":"hello from the proof","idempotencyKey":"proof-before-1"}'
{ "runId": "proof-before-1", "status": "started" }
$ (same call again, same idempotencyKey: settled result)
"message": "⚠️ Auto-compaction could not recover this turn. I kept this conversation mapped to the current session. Please try again, use /compact, or use /new to start a fresh session.\n\nTry starting a fresh session or using a model with a larger context window."
```

Branch build, `sessionKey: "agent:main:main"`:

```text
"message": "⚠️ Auto-compaction could not recover this turn. I kept this conversation mapped to the current session. Use /new to start a fresh session.\n\nTry a model with a larger context window.\n\nTo keep this session instead, an operator can trim its transcript. Trimming permanently deletes older history and keeps no backup, so run `openclaw backup create` first if that history matters, then `openclaw sessions compact agent:main:main --agent main --max-lines 200`."
```

Branch build, `sessionKey: "agent:main:matrix:channel:!ops:example.org:thread:$RootEvent:Example.Org"`:

```text
"message": "⚠️ Auto-compaction could not recover this turn. … then `openclaw sessions compact 'agent:main:matrix:channel:!ops:example.org:thread:$RootEvent:Example.Org' --agent main --max-lines 200` (macOS, Linux, or PowerShell) or `openclaw sessions compact \"agent:main:matrix:channel:!ops:example.org:thread:$RootEvent:Example.Org\" --agent main --max-lines 200` (Windows Command Prompt)."
```

**The displayed Matrix commands, run against that Gateway and its disposable session:**

```text
### POSIX/PowerShell form, pasted into zsh as rendered
$ openclaw sessions compact 'agent:main:matrix:channel:!ops:example.org:thread:$RootEvent:Example.Org' --agent main --max-lines 200
No compaction needed for session agent:main:matrix:channel:!ops:example.org:thread:$RootEvent:Example.Org.
exit=0

### Command Prompt form: cmd.exe strips the double quotes and leaves ! and $ literal; same argv, spawned without a shell
argv: ["sessions","compact","agent:main:matrix:channel:!ops:example.org:thread:$RootEvent:Example.Org","--agent","main","--max-lines","1"]
Compacted session agent:main:matrix:channel:!ops:example.org:thread:$RootEvent:Example.Org (kept 1 lines).
exit=0

### Single-quoted form as cmd.exe would forward it (quote characters kept): the case this PR now avoids
Compaction failed: Session 'agent:main:matrix:channel:!ops:example.org:thread:$RootEvent:Example.Org' not found. Run openclaw sessions list --json to choose a valid key.
exit=1
```

**Tests:**
- Failing before (new assertions, production code at base):
  - `agent-runner-context-recovery.test.ts`: 5 failed / 1 passed. The trim-command case fails on the old `...Please try again, use /compact, or use /new...` copy. It asserts that the reply has no `/compact` and that the no-backup warning, `openclaw backup create` and the session-specific command appear in that order. It no longer pins the whole paragraph; that was narrowed after review, and the base still fails 5 / 1 at `331be5dc9`.
  - `agent-runner-execution-context-failures.test.ts`: 3 failed / 1 passed.
  - The labeled-forms Matrix case fails on the previous single-quote-only head.
- Passing after:
  - `agent-runner-context-recovery.test.ts`: 6 passed.
  - `agent-runner-execution-context-failures.test.ts`: 4 passed. This suite runs both production callers through `executeAgentTurn`.
  - `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts` (full file): 234 passed.
- Checks:
  - `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base e032d1e31 -- <changed files>`: format, lint, core typecheck, and core test typecheck pass. The only red lanes (max-lines suppression ratchet in `ui/src/pages/**` and the core test shard root budget) are already red on the base and unrelated to these files.
  - `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles`: 0 cycles.
  - Autoreview: no P0–P2 findings.
  - Rerun after narrowing the test (`check-changed --base 879e99cb1`, madge, autoreview): format, full typecheck and the import-cycle check pass, and autoreview is clean. The remaining red lanes cover none of these files: `max-lines` in untouched files, unused exports in `src/logging/diagnostic-*` and two test-support files, and the core test shard root budget.
- Test cost, `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` wall time on a heavily loaded host:
  - `agent-runner-context-recovery.test.ts`: 22s, mostly transform.
  - `agent-runner-execution-context-failures.test.ts`: 16s.
  - `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts`: 102–245s for the existing 234-test file; only two assertions changed.
  - No new test files.

**Gaps:**
- In this run, auto-compaction fails with "nothing to compact" (one-message session) rather than because the compaction request itself overflows, as in the issue. Both outcomes reach the same "Auto-compaction failed … Preserving existing session mapping" branch and the same reply builder.
- No Windows host and no PowerShell here. The Command Prompt form is shown by spawning the exact argv cmd.exe forwards. The single-quoted form follows the same literal rules in PowerShell as in POSIX shells.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android’s automation editor requires typing an exact timezone identifier even though the device already supplies available zones.

## User Impact

The cron schedule’s Timezone field now offers searchable choices, a Gateway-default option, and explicit custom entry. Saved aliases remain intact; choosing a zone updates only the draft until Save Changes. No scheduling or default semantics change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing native editor now owns an expandable, bounded list using the device’s ZoneId catalog and existing design controls. It does not take over chat model catalogs, fetch another directory, or open a new window. Custom entry remains available because the Gateway’s supported aliases can differ from the device’s catalog. Cancel and Android Back close the choice without changing the draft; the existing save/revert flow remains authoritative.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: WhatsApp settings reports “Linked: No” and negative connection facts before its status is known, including after a first failed read or while authentication is still stabilizing.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

The packaged WhatsApp view now passes the producer’s optional facts through without converting missing values to false. It omits the unsupported linkage value and hides an empty Details disclosure while preserving its node. No new state, request, permission gate or recovery mechanism is added.

## Evidence

Actual Control UI with a synthetic Gateway, valid WhatsApp enabled/pairing configuration, light theme and a 1280×1000 viewport. Annotated 660×530 crops compare the same first-read failure on isolated main and this independent branch.

**Before** — an unavailable status invents several negative facts.

The separate core “Not configured” badge visible in both captures is addressed by [PR #199309](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199309), not bundled into this independent fix.

- **Eight real-route cases pass** in the owning checkout, including the new regression and existing save rejection, immediate login failure, confirmed/no-op logout, reconnect retirement, phone fallback and complete setup flows. - Self-review/simplification: **+1 net production line**, **187 net test lines**. Missing facts no longer become false; known values and actual recovery remain with their existing owners.

prs.title: fix(web-fetch): escape Markdown link syntax in extracted anchors
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The basic HTML-to-Markdown renderer interpolates anchor labels and destinations without escaping Markdown link delimiters. A space can invalidate a destination, an unmatched parenthesis can truncate it, and brackets in the label can turn one anchor into two links. This is a format-fidelity repair, not a security fix.

## User Impact

Fetched anchors retain their literal link text and complete destination instead of splitting into extra links or losing URL suffixes. Ordinary and balanced-parentheses links stay byte-identical.

## Why This Change Was Made

Escape brackets and backslashes in labels. For destinations containing whitespace or unbalanced parentheses, use CommonMark's angle-bracket form; escape literal angle brackets and backslashes, and percent-encode whitespace before the renderer's final prose normalization can collapse it. The follow-up narrows the original patch to leave ordinary and balanced-parentheses URLs byte-identical, including Wikipedia-style URLs.

Only Markdown link rendering changes. Text mode, links-as-text, empty-label bare URLs, visibility filtering, preformatted markers, Markdown-to-text conversion and truncation are unchanged. The Readability plugin's article selection is unchanged, but it shares this HTML renderer through the SDK, so its Markdown anchors also receive the fix.

Shared consumers include the web-fetch tool, Plugin SDK `provider-web-fetch`, `provider-web-search`, and `web-content-extractor`. The web-search and provider-web-fetch barrels expose unchanged Markdown-to-text/truncation helpers; web-content-extractor exposes the affected HTML renderer as well as unchanged Markdown-to-text conversion. The web-fetch raw-HTML fallback reaches the changed renderer; its error-body text path is unchanged.

## Evidence

The existing regression table fails twice on base `20cb257f749a` and passes all 62 cases on the narrowed candidate (vitest-source, host ocx). Focused formatter and linter pass. Test lines are net zero: retain the two regressions and remove two redundant rows already covered by the stronger attribute case and the basic-extraction Markdown case.

Built CLI proof uses a fixed loopback HTML fixture and isolated profiles with the `web-readability` plugin disabled. The `readability` setting itself stays at its default: setting it false bypasses basic HTML fallback. Returned `extractor: raw-html` identifies the intended path.

On base and candidate, the built CLI ran the article-shaped fixture twice with `extractor: raw-html`, then once with the plugin enabled and `extractor: readability`. The raw path demonstrates all three defects and their repair. The default Readability path demonstrates the unmatched-parenthesis and label repair; it already normalizes spaces in URLs. Markdown-it independently confirms one link per candidate anchor and the complete destination. Ordinary and balanced-parentheses controls are byte-identical across all six runs. The existing Readability consumer suite also passes (12 cases).

Production delta: +21/-1 lines; tests: +2/-2 lines. The original contributor commit remains in history. The follow-up replaces blanket parenthesis escaping with a single balance scan and angle destinations; no matching-index collection or new shared abstraction is needed.

Full build with declarations was attempted at this head; it emitted declarations but fails the SDK size budget (5,315,563 > 5,315,536 bytes), with no budget bypass. The self-contained tarball checker and installed-package smoke pass: the packed launcher identifies `d2478e3`, and its `infer web fetch --help` works. CI owns remaining broad validation.

Exact commands, Markdown, parsed destinations, isolation details and build/pack receipts: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199292#issuecomment-6886059148

SunnyShu's original commit and credit are retained.

## Risk

Two-way door: reverting restores the prior rendering. No state, config, dependencies or exported signatures change. Blast radius is Markdown anchor output from the basic HTML renderer, including SDK content-extractor consumers.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the model picker says “No models available” or “No models are permitted by your admin” while provider discovery is still running.

## User Impact

User impact: chat and New Session keep a neutral model label until discovery answers, instead of presenting a temporary empty catalog as a setup or administrator problem. Confirmed-empty catalogs and genuine catalog failures still show their existing guidance. No permission, model selection, request or persistence behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway can publish an empty model snapshot together with pending providers. The picker menu already treats that as unknown; its trigger did not. The shared trigger projection now withholds only the premature empty diagnosis. It adds no loader, banner, fallback model, refresh request or new state, and still asks users to choose when actual permitted options are available.

## Evidence

Real Control UI, synthetic mock-Gateway responses, light theme, 1280×900. The red rectangle marks the trigger while the same provider discovery is pending. No live team data.

**Before — a pending catalog falsely blames the administrator.**

![Before: pending provider discovery shown as an administrator restriction](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/80c73acf-5629-48f9-aa2b-7b85d34e5d0a)

**After — the default model label stays neutral until discovery answers.**

prs.title: fix(usage): show model attribution without stored session metadata
prs.body:
Fixes #198488

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing provider and model information in Usage session rows and exports when measured usage exists but session-level attribution is absent or incomplete.

## User Impact

Missing fields now use representative measured attribution without inventing a provider/model pair. Stored values remain authoritative. If one field is stored, the missing field is filled only from matching measured entries; if none match, it stays empty. No configuration, migration, or protocol changes are required.

For mixed-provider sessions, this fallback is representative metadata only—not attribution of every token or cost. Aggregate accounting and provider filters are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Initial row assembly only copied stored metadata. Packed overview summaries arrive later, and metadata restoration replaces report rows with visible rows while retaining their usage. One shared helper fills final response metadata after hydration/restoration and filtering/aggregation.

The helper selects the greatest totalTokens among eligible measured entries, keeping the first on ties. Eligibility preserves an existing provider or model. When neither field is stored, both come from the same dominant entry. Repeated application is idempotent and does not mutate source usage.

The response regression is a sibling test file because usage.sessions-usage.test.ts is at its line cap. It uses the existing isolated Gateway-methods lane. Documentation describes both representative attribution and partial-pair consistency.

## Evidence

- Base: 3ab80aba158a5c5488d9323f4352aa593fb9af1c (tree 7e4dc64cd2172b6045e63b7f35f5d38b5af13a34).
- Final candidate: 3ffbb5d752358a4b3500738ac7cc79fd4789f089 (tree 32cf975c2eb0b50588d8135fc10d5abc23516507).
- The Windows runtime proof below is supplied by @MertBasar0 and bound to afe57af5e5fdd7391263110cc8efd4dbb86a583d (tree 8393447bc9453ff991178b99a42920976a9189c5). Roboclaw did not execute those Windows commands. The final commit adds only 15 lines to one test file; every other repository file, including all production code, is byte-identical to afe57af5. The proof remains labeled with the commit actually built.
- Original RED/GREEN: detail, packed overview, and restoration failed on the pinned base due to absent attribution. Partial-pair consistency cases then failed on f303c818 (eight assertions across two tests) and passed with afe57af5.
- Final Linux verification: 53 tests pass across usage.sessions-usage.test.ts, usage-overview-report.test.ts, session-cost-usage-worker-overview.test.ts, usage-overview.test.ts, and usage.row-attribution.test.ts. Runner wall time: 22.01 seconds including preparation; attribution test bodies: 0.840 seconds. CI time is not yet available.
- Final test-file lint, format check, Gateway-methods test typecheck, and git diff --check pass. Prior core production typecheck and full-candidate review remain applicable to unchanged production code.
- Independent OpenClaw Auto Review: the full afe57af5 candidate was P0–P2 scoped-clean; a fresh review of the final test-only delta against afe57af5 is also scoped-clean, with no findings.

### Reporter measurements and explicit regression coverage

Thanks to @spacenet-Pop-OS for the [follow-up live-store measurements and requested controls](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/198488#issuecomment-6875408820). Their live-store counts, mixed-provider frequency, and client-workaround observations are reporter-provided evidence, not numbers reproduced by this PR's Windows fixture.

Both controls are in src/gateway/server-methods/usage.row-attribution.test.ts:
- **fills final detail row attribution from dominant measured usage without changing accounting**
- **fills final overview row attribution from dominant measured usage without changing accounting**

The existing **missing** case supplies two providers with 10 and 30 tokens and requires the 30-token entry's provider and model, while independently checking aggregate totals. The new **null-model-usage** case supplies totalTokens=0 and modelUsage=null and requires both row attribution fields to stay empty. Detail additionally asserts that the returned modelUsage is literally null; packed overview represents it as zero model entries and keeps attribution empty. Existing usage=null and modelUsage=[] controls remain. The null fixture is intentionally outside the current optional-array TypeScript summary type, with a localized documented expected type error; no production type was widened.

### Publication status and remaining verification

UI E2E passed locally on Windows as reported by @MertBasar0 below; this is not a passing CI claim. The inherited unused-export failures are documented rather than suppressed. Preflight found no competing #198488 PR. Main b9dacb674914f74b57155edc02cdd13f8f963486 still has the unchanged row assembly, loading, and restoration defect.

### Real behavior proof — Windows, built Gateway

A built Gateway answers the real `sessions.usage` RPC through `openclaw gateway call`. The Claude turns that create the session usage records are served by a **stub Claude CLI**, so no real inference runs. The RPC, the usage pipeline, session deletion and the overview projection are the shipped code.

Setup, identical for both builds:
- Windows 11 Home 26200 x64, Node v24.19.0. `pnpm build` of each commit from a clean checkout: base `3ab80aba` (tree `7e4dc64c`) and candidate `afe57af5` (tree `8393447b`).
- Isolated `HOME`/`USERPROFILE`, state dir, config and workspace. Model `claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-6`.
- Sequence: `openclaw gateway run` → `openclaw agent` turn in session K (kept) → turn in session D → `openclaw sessions delete <D> --yes` → `openclaw gateway call sessions.usage` with `{agentScope:"all", limit:100, startDate, endDate}`, re-polled until no row reports `computing: true` → the same call with `projection: "overview"`.

| | Base `3ab80aba` | Candidate `afe57af5` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Detail, deleted session D | `modelProvider`/`model` empty; `usage.modelUsage` = `claude-cli`/`claude-sonnet-4-6`, 2 tokens | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` |
| Detail, kept session K (stored metadata) | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` |
| Overview, deleted session D | empty | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` |
| Overview, kept session K | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` |
| Rows with `modelProvider == null` and measured usage | 1 of 2 (detail), 1 of 2 (overview) | 0 |
| `aggregates.byProvider` | `claude-cli` = 4 tokens | `claude-cli` = 4 tokens (unchanged) |

Notes:
- The deleted row first reports `computing: true` while its usage is summarized; the values above are after it settled, in both builds.
- Mixed-provider, partial stored pair and empty-usage cases are covered by the regression suite, not by this run.
- `pnpm deadcode:exports` reports the same three unused exports on base `3ab80aba` and on the candidate: `REQUIRED_ACTION_STOP`, `mergeNodeRepositoryPublication`, `WorkspaceTransferOperation`. All are in files this PR does not touch, and the new `usage-row-attribution.ts` is not flagged. So the `check:changed` red is pre-existing.
- `pnpm test:ui:e2e ui/src/e2e/usage-overview.e2e.test.ts` passes on Windows: 3 of 3 tests passed in 45.6 s, run with Playwright-managed Chromium (chromium-1248; the runner redirects `USERPROFILE`, so branded Chrome and Edge refuse remote debugging there) on candidate `afe57af5` after a clean build. The final head only adds a test case, so production and UI code are identical.

### Real behavior proof — Windows, real Claude Code

**Real Claude Code CLI 2.1.325 with a real `claude.ai` login and real `claude-sonnet-4-6` inference** serves the agent turns; the `sessions.usage` RPC, session deletion and the overview projection are the shipped code.

Setup, identical for both builds:
- Windows 11 Home 26200 x64, Node v24.19.0; `pnpm build` from a clean checkout of base `3ab80aba` (tree `7e4dc64c`) and of candidate `afe57af5` (tree `8393447b`; the later commits on this PR only add tests).
- Isolated `HOME`/`USERPROFILE`, state dir, config and workspace; Gateway env built from an allowlist, with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` pointing at a dedicated directory that holds the only Claude login. Model `claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-6`.
- Sequence: `openclaw gateway run` → `openclaw agent` turn in session K (kept) → turn in session D → `openclaw sessions delete <D> --yes` → `openclaw gateway call sessions.usage` with `{agentScope:"all", limit:100, startDate, endDate}`, re-polled until no row reports `computing: true` → the same call with `projection: "overview"`.

| | Base `3ab80aba` | Candidate `afe57af5` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Detail, deleted session D | `modelProvider`/`model` empty; `usage.modelUsage` = `claude-cli`/`claude-sonnet-4-6`, 14,073 tokens | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` (45,760 measured tokens) |
| Detail, kept session K (stored metadata) | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` |
| Overview, deleted session D | empty | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` |
| Overview, kept session K | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` |
| Rows with `modelProvider == null` and measured usage | 1 of 2 (detail), 1 of 2 (overview) | 0 |
| `aggregates.byProvider` | `claude-cli` only (59,546 tokens) | `claude-cli` only (59,919 tokens) |

Token counts differ between runs because they are real inference (cache reads included); the provider breakdown is unchanged by the patch. The captured logs contain no account email or tokens.

## Credits

Thanks to @spacenet-Pop-OS for the report, measured dominant-usage fallback idea, and follow-up live-store evidence linked above, and @MertBasar0 for the partial-pair correction and commit-bound Windows proof. All three candidate commits include MertBasar0's co-author trailer.

prs.title: improve(browser): show the agent a Browser panel note only during take-over
prs.body:
Closes #198449

## What Problem This Solves

Take-over (#197928) is opt-in by design. The operator-control module states its own contract: "Nothing changes until someone clicks Take control in the Browser panel", and #197928 promised users "Nothing changes for anyone who doesn't click the new button. Agents keep using the browser exactly as before."

The 60-second recent-use note breaks that contract. Any click or keypress in the Control UI Browser panel, with no take-over, changes what the agent receives: its browser results for the next minute carry "the user used this browser from the Browser panel N seconds ago… Check the page before acting on it." A user who only looks at or uses the panel, and never opts into take-over, still changes the agent's tool results and the text added to its context.

## User Impact

Using the Browser panel without taking control leaves the agent's browser results exactly as they are without the panel. While the user holds control, the agent still gets the take-over note on results it can still get (snapshots, screenshots), and actions still answer `user_has_control`. Take control stays the one way for a user to signal the agent that they are in the browser.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser tool adds a note only while someone holds take-over control of that browser, so the opt-in contract holds for every result. The last-input time that only fed the 60-second note is removed. Marked panel input still restarts the 5-minute idle timer of a held take-over. The Browser panel docs no longer describe the recent-use note.

## Evidence

Tests in `browser-tool.operator-control.test.ts`, through the real `browser` tool against a host browser's operator-control state:
- After panel input without take-over, an agent `act` result carries no note. This test fails on `main` (the result contains the Browser panel note) and passes with the fix.
- During take-over, a `snapshot` result ends with the take-over note, and `act` and `stop` answer `user_has_control`.

Suites run: the operator-control tool and route tests and `browser-tool.test.ts`, 105 passed. Typecheck of the extensions and their tests, lint and format of the changed files, and the assertion-safety check pass.

Live Gateway, Control UI, and real-model proof on `d0bf21a45656901fb6aa0e50e53eb50bc632fbf0`: [proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198454#issuecomment-6869218602). Both cases ran in one macOS 26.6.2 VM Gateway process and agent session, with a synthetic local page. I checked the browser tool messages sent back to the model.

Without Take control, a panel click followed by the agent's click changed the count from 1 to 2. All three browser results carried no panel-use note; the last reached the model 7.213 seconds after panel input.

![Ordinary panel input: agent action succeeds without a Browser panel note](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/068f28329ddae1f1052dd01911faedbbba21d6ba/images/2026/11/09cf973d-70e5-42fe-b357-81918a6aff76.png)

While holding Take control, the snapshot retained its takeover note, the attempted agent click returned `user_has_control`, and the count stayed at 2.

![Held Take control: snapshot note and refused agent action](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/068f28329ddae1f1052dd01911faedbbba21d6ba/images/2026/11/ffb28fed-e393-4c72-88dd-585f886feef6.png)

The runtime build completed. Its report-only Control UI performance check flagged budget overages. The focused test results above are retained from the same-head regression run; this live-proof run did not repeat those suites or broad CI.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Scribes report an empty run history when the history request actually failed.

## User Impact

User impact: a failed history read now shows an error and a way to retry by reopening the Scribe. An empty successful response is described as unavailable recent history, not proof that the automation never ran. No scheduler action or permission changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The history owner now keeps its read failure separate from an empty result and passes that fact to the existing detail renderer. Reopening performs the same read again and clears the error when history is available.

This PR has been narrowed to that distinct history correction. Queue/start wording is already covered by #199259, and enable/disable/removal wording by #199267; the overlapping portions of this PR were removed rather than retaining duplicate fixes. Conversation-context wording is separate in #199321.

## Evidence

- Original regression fails against main; **46 focused Scribe view/state tests pass** on the narrowed patch.
- The full built-app flow using the actual packaged Knowledge plugin verifies a failed cron.runs read, its error state, navigation back to Scribes, reopening and successful history recovery. No cron.run is issued.

prs.title: fix: node directory listing pages until the gateway stops
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Node directory listing stops after 32 pages so one oversized directory cannot pin the gateway. Bootstrap discovery used that stop to skip the directory, then still loaded a sibling, but it recorded no diagnostic. A configured `*/AGENTS.md` file inside the oversized directory disappeared with `diagnostics: []`.

## Evidence

Head `b06896ea3a7` on macOS Darwin arm64, Node v26.12.1. The production trace below was run on `055d09e2943`. `b06896ea3a7` merges current main and adds the 112-line test grant. It does not change the listing or the diagnostic. A real directory held 131073 empty names, which is one past 32 pages of 4096. Its sibling `keep/AGENTS.md` contained `kept instructions`. Production `createNodeWorkspaceBridge` listed that tree. Each `dir.list` call went to production `handleDirList` on that directory, not a scripted page payload. `loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics` then loaded `*/AGENTS.md`.

```console
OK: files=kept instructions diagnostics=[{"dir":"fat","reason":"io","detail":"Directory listing exceeded 32 pages"}] dirList=34 stat=0 fetch=1
```

`dir.list` ran 34 times: one page for the root, 32 pages for the oversized directory, and one page for the sibling. `file.fetch` read the sibling once. The oversized directory is named in the diagnostic and its instructions were not loaded.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Bootstrap discovery skips one directory after the real 32-page listing cap, records that skip, and still loads a sibling `AGENTS.md`.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS Darwin arm64, Node v26.12.1, head `055d09e2943` in `/tmp/oc-165805`, then merged forward as `b06896ea3a7` without changing the listing or the diagnostic. The directory was a local folder with 131073 names. The node command handler and the gateway bridge ran in one process.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Created the oversized directory and `keep/AGENTS.md`. Called `createNodeWorkspaceBridge` with `invoke` dispatching to `handleDirList`, `handleFileStat`, and `handleFileFetch`. Called `loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics` for `*/AGENTS.md`.
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from that production path:

```console
OK: files=kept instructions diagnostics=[{"dir":"fat","reason":"io","detail":"Directory listing exceeded 32 pages"}] dirList=34 fetch=1
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The sibling file was loaded. The oversized directory produced one `io` diagnostic, `Directory listing exceeded 32 pages`, after 32 real listing pages.
- **What was not tested:** A second OS process enrolled as a node over the gateway websocket. The same handlers ran in-process.

## Summary

A directory past the listing page budget is still skipped, and its sibling still loads. The skip is now a diagnostic instead of a silent omission.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): bound the sandbox scp transfer with a deadline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Sandbox media staging shells out to `scp`, and that spawn had **no deadline**: a hung transfer (dead peer, wedged ssh, a dropped TCP session that never resets) left the child process alive indefinitely and the caller awaiting a promise that never settles — one leaked `scp` per stalled staging attempt, with no bound on how long the turn could hang.

This gives the transfer a bounded deadline **through the shared process-lifecycle runner rather than by owning the spawn directly**, which is the direction #98141 was closed toward: that PR was closed as "superseded by the current process-lifecycle architecture, not because the linked defect is fixed" — so the timeout belongs on the existing runner call, not on a locally-owned `child_process.spawn`.

## Evidence

The change is two files:

```
src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.ts          |  8 +-
src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.scp.test.ts | 101 ++++++++++++++++++-
```

- `stage-sandbox-media.ts` derives the per-transfer budget (`resolveScpTransferTimeoutMs()`: size cap / supported throughput, 30s floor, `OPENCLAW_SANDBOX_SCP_TIMEOUT_MS` override) and passes it as `timeoutMs` on the existing shared-runner invocation — the runner already owns deadlines and descendant-tree termination.
- The test suite asserts the deadline reaches the runner (`expect.objectContaining({ timeoutMs: SCP_TRANSFER_TIMEOUT_MS })`) so the wiring cannot silently regress, and adds a real-process hang case: a fake `scp` on `PATH` that spawns a descendant, ignores `SIGTERM`, and never exits. The assertion is that the transfer is rejected by the deadline and **both the parent and the descendant are gone afterwards** (via the repo's existing `test-utils/process-tree` helpers), plus a negative control that a normal transfer still succeeds unchanged.

```
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.scp.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  13 passed | 2 skipped (15)
```

## Verification

The deadline wiring and the normal-transfer assertions run and pass here; the two skipped cases are the POSIX-only hang cases (`it.runIf(process.platform !== "win32")`) — this machine is Windows, so the process-tree termination assertion itself is **not exercised locally**. I am stating that rather than implying it: it needs a POSIX CI lane to run, and that is the one part of this change I could not observe directly.

Partial fix for #98468: the deadline wiring, the revised budget, and real timeout recovery (process tree + temporary cleanup) are verified here; the remaining unobserved part is a real multi-hour suspend/transfer scenario on a POSIX lane, which CI's Linux lane runs via the committed cases.

## Context worth knowing before review

- Three prior attempts exist on this issue: #98141 (closed as superseded by the lifecycle architecture — see above), #101473 (long review loop, closed), #132552 (merged, but that was the *cancellation* half of staging, not the transfer deadline).
- The issue currently also carries `clawsweeper:queueable-fix`. If the automated fix lane produces a PR for the same deadline, take that one — the intent here is to have the fix available in the architecture the maintainer pointed at, not to race a bot.

## Revision 2 — revised transfer budget + real transport proof (head `8707115c920`)

**Decision answer (the question the review asked): revise the deadline instead of an unconditional 30s cutoff.**
`resolveScpTransferTimeoutMs()` derives the per-transfer budget from the size cap and the slowest throughput still called supported, keeps it bounded, and is overridable:

| Case | Budget |
|---|---|
| 50 MiB cap at the 256 KiB/s supported floor | **200s** |
| review example: 40 MiB at 1 MiB/s (~40s) | **160s** (the old fixed 30s could never allow it) |
| small transfers | 30s floor |
| `OPENCLAW_SANDBOX_SCP_TIMEOUT_MS` | operator override (tests use it to reach the deadline in seconds) |

The deadline remains an absolute, bounded value owned by the shared runner, so an unattended hang still dies; it just no longer kills a slow-but-healthy copy. A deadline kill is also no longer retried (one bounded wait instead of three): retrying a copy that stopped progressing only re-waits the whole budget. If maintainers want a different number, or a config field instead of the env override, name it and I'll switch it.

### Real behavior proof (no mocks: real spawned transport through staging, Windows)

A compiled stand-in transport is spawned through the same argv/PATH path the runner uses, so the real spawn, deadline, tree kill, and temp cleanup all execute:

```
[proof] slow transfer staged=1 elapsed=7965ms
[proof] staged bytes=real transport bytes
[proof] hung transport pid=22892 alive=true
[proof] descendant pid=54128 alive=true
[proof] reaped by deadline: parent=true descendant=true
[proof] surface={"value":{"staged":{}}}
[proof] attempts="attempt\n"
[proof] temp dir removed=true
 ✓ windows real transport proof > publishes a real slow transport that finishes inside the budget 8044ms
 ✓ windows real transport proof > kills a real hung transport tree on the deadline without retrying 8507ms
```

Both Windows-native cases pass (17 passed | 3 skipped with the scratch cases in place) and the same file without them is **15 passed | 3 skipped, exit 0**; `oxfmt --check` clean on both files. The three skips are the POSIX-gated cases (they spawn a shebang script), which is why the Windows run above uses a compiled stand-in. `oxlint` produced no verdict for explicit paths in this junction worktree, so I am not claiming a lint verdict — CI's lint lane judges.

The new committed cases: the derived-budget unit math (including the 40 MiB / 160s case), a real slow transfer that publishes, and the hung tree + descendant reaped on the deadline with one attempt and the temp dir removed.

The reader already knows the paging unit and download path. Browser handoff is only a request; completed file writes are reported as saved. These messages now match those facts. prs.title: fix(talk): honor CLI model routing in browser calls
prs.body:
Related: #161885

## What Problem This Solves

Browser Talk consults routed through `claude-cli` request a direct Anthropic API key and fail before trying the configured fallback.

## User Impact

Browser/native GPT-Live consultations use the selected model's runtime and configured fallback chain while retaining the caller's existing authority, cancellation, session continuity and terminal ownership. No configuration or public SDK changes are required. Meeting, voice-call and FaceTime consultation paths are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Refreshed against `main` at `dab3fcdf8edd36df38144a961f8330fcbede872e` to resolve the stale branch's conflicts. Talk now uses the existing admitted turn and CLI-candidate owners, with one admission and transcript recorder across candidates. Hook-resolved routes are applied before runtime selection. Steering uses the admitted session operation; a live CLI without injection support uses the provider's existing joined replacement flow.

The refresh preserves main's exact source/Gateway binding and terminal-write draining. It removes the browser's direct embedded-only dispatch and the redundant Talk-side steering projection. Existing consumer fixtures move to the dispatcher boundary, preserving their permission, source, final-effect and lifecycle assertions.

## Evidence

Published head: [`e08988c594b`](https://github.com/ZengWen-DT/openclaw/commit/e08988c594b647757d7ce82d508f53eea8e48a5b).

- **Real baseline:** an isolated Chromium call through the genuine native Talk service on `main` `9bf3e79c823` reached a delegated consultation, then recorded `missing-provider-auth` for Anthropic despite the configured `claude-cli` runtime; fallback was not attempted. Audio input was synthetic; the browser, Gateway and service were real.
- **Focused checks:** 88 tests across six routing, steering, admission, source-scope, prompt-prefix and provider-controller files passed in 219.61 seconds. After fixing the review's hook-routing finding, the routing file passed all 16 tests in 74.10 seconds, including compilation; both new hook regressions fail on the preceding candidate.
- **Static checks:** core and plugin production types and Gateway test types passed. Formatting, conflict-marker, line-cap and mock-export guards passed. Plugin typed lint also passed. A further seven consumer files had 90 passing and four failing tests in 278.51 seconds; the four cancel-then-new-request failures reproduce with the same assertion and no speakable answer on unmodified `main` `dab3fcdf` (all four fail in the baseline run, 92.52 seconds). Running those scenarios through the actual Talk adapter produces the same four failures; they are not counted as passing. Exact-head hosted CI and its CI seconds are pending.
- **Independent review:** fresh Codex autoreview of the production adapter and then-current consumer fixtures against `dab3fcdf`, through P2: `scoped-clean`, no accepted/actionable findings. Production source is unchanged since that review; the subsequent native real-runner fixture now invokes the Talk adapter. The earlier hook-routing finding was fixed and covered by the red/green tests above. The model-lock suggestion was declined against the existing Talk owner's explicit rejection contract and tests in `src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.ts:99` and `src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.test.ts:334`.
- **Size:** production +549/-43 (net +506); tests/support +671/-53 (net +618); other +2/-5. Production growth supplies the previously missing browser-to-CLI adapter using existing runtime, auth, continuity and settlement owners; it adds no fallback loop or configuration. The test-line allocation covers distinct routing/preflight and steering-lifetime boundaries.

### Remaining validation and follow-ups

**Inherited validation failure:** native cancellation followed by a fresh delegated consultation returns the no-answer fallback in four existing tests. This reproduces on unmodified `main` as well as this candidate; underlying product-versus-fixture cause remains unconfirmed. It is recorded as follow-up, without weakening the assertions.

A successful authenticated Claude CLI after-run remains unverified because the local Claude CLI is logged out. No live CLI allowed-read/forbidden-write result is claimed. The ClawSweeper rank-up request for those final effects remains outstanding; retained-callback rejection has focused controller-boundary coverage, not a live Claude tool-call claim. Ready is a review state, not a claim that these proof gaps or required CI are cleared.

The shared CLI catalog concerns [B/C](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164229#issuecomment-6789739547) remain named follow-up work: this refresh forwards the logical `modelProvider` (A), but does not include the separate shared capability/intersection-policy patch or claim those catalog cases fixed.

Earlier [proof artifacts](https://github.com/ZengWen-DT/openclaw/tree/d530ab2f733aaf74a1e4dc1585e546b4c9f7943d/proof/issue-161885-terminal-repair) remain historical evidence for their recorded revisions; they do not validate this refreshed head. prs.title: test(update): run the published-driver cell on a linked package path
prs.body:
Related: #197949

## What Problem This Solves

The update design in #197949 proposes keeping each release in its own directory behind a linked package path. Nothing tested what an already-published updater does when it meets that layout, which a downgrade would leave behind.

## User Impact

User impact: none. This adds a mode to an existing Docker end-to-end cell, a script to run it, and documentation. No CI workflow selects the new lane, so CI cost does not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

`OPENCLAW_PUBLISHED_DRIVER_LINKED_ROOT=1` makes the published-driver update cell move the installed driver into `releases/<version>/` under the prefix and leave a relative link at the package path before the update. No shipped release produces that layout.

The update, readiness, version, and session assertions are unchanged. Three things differ in this mode:

- The incognito scan also covers the directory behind the link. Published updaters follow the link and keep their backups there, so scanning only beside the link would have checked one location instead of two.
- The installed-tree budget is measured at the link's target, because the budget check refuses a link. The default mode still passes the package path unchanged.
- The cell records where the package path points before and after the update, including after a failed update. That record is an observation and cannot fail a successful update.

Run it with `pnpm test:docker:published-driver-linked-root`. The Docker lane matches its `published-driver-scoped-restore` sibling.

## Evidence

Run locally on linux/arm64 with a candidate built from `e38fbc495a21a`, which is patch-identical to this head before a rebase onto `main`:

| Mode | Published updater | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Linked package path | 2026.11.3 | PASS, Gateway ready, version and sessions verified |
| Linked package path | 2026.10.9 | PASS, Gateway ready, version and sessions verified |
| Default (control) | 2026.11.3 | PASS |

In both linked runs the link was unchanged afterwards and the directory behind it held the new build, with the updater's activation control directory beside it. The incognito scan covered two roots in linked mode, the same count as the default mode.

Checks: `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint --type-aware`, `scripts/check-docker-e2e-boundaries.mts`, the docs MDX check, and the docs link audit pass. Seven lane and workflow test files pass (324 tests). `test/scripts/package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts` (18 cases) and one case in `test/scripts/docker-build-helper.test.ts` fail on the authoring Mac with and without this change.

Review: an independent reviewer agent found the incognito scan gap, a layout record that could throw, and three inaccurate doc statements. All are fixed here. No autoreview pass: the helper could not run on the authoring machine.

Gaps: two published updaters, Linux only, one update each. Rollback after a failed update on a linked path, a second update, and Windows are not covered.
