prs.title: fix(automations): scheduled runs can't read or save their own scratch
prs.body:
Fixes #199194

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a scheduled automation run can't read or save its own scratch. `scratch_get` and `scratch_set` return `Automation not found: <job id>` when the run's session isn't the job's owner conversation, which is always the case for isolated runs. The run still finishes `ok`, so the lost scratch goes unnoticed.

## User Impact

User impact: automations that keep notes in scratch between runs can read and save them from their own runs. Other conversations still can't see or change a job's scratch. The owner conversation still can't write the scratch of a job that runs with operator access; only a Gateway owner, an operator or the job's own run can.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scratch handlers accept the run's signed, short-lived claim for its own job, the same claim `cron.get`, `cron.remove`, `cron.runs` and `cron.history` already accept. For jobs that run with operator access (`trusted`), the write refusal exempts only a caller whose live claim names this exact job and its effective agent. The commit guard repeats that check on the locked job with a freshly read claim and the live run authority, so an expired claim or an ended run can't write.

Accepted edge case: a trusted job's run can save text it read during the run into scratch, and that text reaches its next prompt. That is what self-scoped scratch is for, and the run already holds the job's authority.

## Evidence

- **Real agent and real model** (isolated Gateway in a macOS test VM, fresh state, `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` through OpenRouter; the API key stayed outside the VM behind a forwarder that only accepts a one-off token). The PR head `176bd6045ea` and its base `8160cb00aa6` were built from `git archive` and run with the same script. As an operator it adds a trusted isolated job whose owner is a conversation, seeds scratch at revision 1, runs the job with `cron.run`, prints the run's `automations` tool calls and results from `cron.history`, and reads the scratch back with `cron.scratch.get`. The run's prompt asks the agent to call `scratch_get`, then `scratch_set` at the revision it read, then reply `read=N saved=M`. Output of both runs follows. Two kinds of line are left out: Node's security-patch warning, and the history line that repeats the prompt.

  With the fix (PR head):

  ```text
  [pr] job added: policy=trusted owner.sessionKey=agent:main:telegram:group:EXAMPLE sessionTarget=isolated
  [pr] operator seeded scratch: currentRevision=1
  [pr] run finished: status=ok completionStatus=succeeded error=none model=anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5 provider=openrouterproxy
  [pr] run session: agent:main:cron:190f399a-1cd8-4e52-8540-4ed750674c9b:run:82802cbe-a232-4324-80f6-d6697ee3649f
  [pr] tool call  automations {"action":"scratch_get"}
  [pr] tool result isError=false {"scratch":{"content":"notes r1 seeded by the operator","revision":1,"updatedAtMs":1794694148734},"currentRevision":1,"maxBytes":262144}
  [pr] tool call  automations {"action":"scratch_set","content":"notes r2 written by the run","expectedRevision":1}
  [pr] tool result isError=false {"ok":true,"scratch":{"content":"notes r2 written by the run","revision":2,"updatedAtMs":1794694153695},"currentRevision":2,"maxBytes":262144}
  [pr] assistant reply: read=1 saved=2
  [pr] stored scratch after the run (operator read): currentRevision=2 content="notes r2 written by the run"
  [pr] usage: {"input_tokens":25378,"output_tokens":165,"total_tokens":25543}
  ```

  Without the fix (base): the run still finishes `ok`, and the scratch stays at revision 1.

  ```text
  [main] job added: policy=trusted owner.sessionKey=agent:main:telegram:group:EXAMPLE sessionTarget=isolated
  [main] operator seeded scratch: currentRevision=1
  [main] run finished: status=ok completionStatus=succeeded error=none model=anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5 provider=openrouterproxy
  [main] run session: agent:main:cron:6ce42f3f-e1e8-496a-aa15-d6192c63cefc:run:d067af04-48b1-4784-b98e-f88f5d8376ef
  [main] tool call  automations {"action":"scratch_get"}
  [main] tool result isError=true {"status":"error","tool":"automations","error":"Automation not found: 6ce42f3f-e1e8-496a-aa15-d6192c63cefc. List automations and retry with a current job id. For cross-session management, use a fresh authenticated configured channel owner or Control UI administrator turn or the Automations page."}
  [main] assistant reply: Automation not found: 6ce42f3f-e1e8-496a-aa15-d6192c63cefc. List automations and retry with a current job id. For cross-session management, use a fresh authenticated configured channel owner or Control UI administrator turn or the Automations page.
  [main] stored scratch after the run (operator read): currentRevision=1 content="notes r1 seeded by the operator"
  [main] usage: {"input_tokens":16802,"output_tokens":238,"total_tokens":17040}
  ```
- **Gateway handlers** (`cron.scratch-self-run.test.ts`, real cron service and SQLite store):
  - A trusted job's own isolated run, and an account-policy job's run, read the scratch and save the next revision.
  - Without the fix, both cases are refused.
  - These callers stay refused and the stored scratch stays unchanged: another conversation (not found), the owner conversation writing a trusted job (operator-access refusal), a run of a different job, an expired claim, and a run whose authority has ended.
- **Real Gateway** (new QA scenario `cron-self-scratch`, mock-openai, isolated Gateway): an operator-created trusted job with an owner conversation runs isolated and calls `scratch_get`, then `scratch_set`.
  - With the fix: read revision 1, stored revision 2 with the run's content.
  - Without the fix: `scratch_get` returns `Automation not found`, the run finishes `ok` and the scratch stays at revision 1.
- **Existing tests that cover the changed handlers and scope check**: `cron.scratch-read`, `cron.ownership-matrix`, `cron-caller-scope`, `cron.self-removal`, `cron.validation`, `cron.list-scoped` and `cron-tool.automation`. All pass: 195 tests plus the 3 new ones.
- **Typecheck, lint and format**: typecheck (core, cron tests, extensions), oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the touched files.
- **Not covered**: a job whose run continues in a conversation session (`sessionTarget: "main"` or a named session). Those runs get the same signed claim from the same code path.

prs.title: feat(ui): edit an agent's thinking default from its Overview
prs.body:
Closes #198371

## What Problem This Solves

The agent Overview page shows an agent's **Thinking default** as plain text, so setting one agent's level (for example a `coder` agent) means using the config editor or the CLI.

## User Impact

Operators who can edit config can pick an agent's thinking default in **Agents → agent → Overview → Model selection**. The menu lists only the levels that agent's model accepts, plus **Inherit default (level)**, which removes the agent's own setting. Choices save to `agents.entries.<id>.thinkingDefault` through the page's existing autosave and affect only that agent. Message and session thinking overrides still take precedence.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The levels come from the agent's row in `agents.list` (`thinkingLevels`), which the Gateway already resolves for that agent's model and runtime.
- **Schema change (additive):** `agents.list` agent rows gain an optional `thinkingInheritedDefault`. The Gateway sends it only when the agent sets its own `thinkingDefault`. It is the level that clearing the override resolves to, using the same resolver as runs: per-agent model params, shared model params, the global default, the model's own default, then clamping to the model's levels. The core resolver gains an option to skip only the agent's own `thinkingDefault`. Existing clients can ignore the field; the Swift and Kotlin protocol contracts are unchanged. The protocol changelog is release-owned, so this description records the schema change.
- Restricted model views (a model selection policy) drop `thinkingInheritedDefault` along with the other thinking fields, because it is resolved from the agent's hidden model. Their `thinkingDefault` is the agent's own override, so with an override and no inherited level the option reads plain **Inherit default** and names no level.
- The **Inherit default (level)** label shows `thinkingInheritedDefault`, or the agent's resolved level when it has no override. Example: global Low, a per-model param of High and an agent override of Medium give "Inherit default (High)", which is what clearing produces.
- Level names come from one helper, `thinkingLevelLabel` in `ui/src/lib/chat/thinking.ts`, which this page and the Models page share. It uses the `quickSettings.model.thinkingLevels.*` translations through each page's reactive translator. The five standard levels that had no key (Minimal, Extra high, Adaptive, Maximum, Ultra) gain canonical English, and the translation pipeline supplies other locales. Provider-specific levels keep their own label.
- A saved level that the current model does not offer stays visible and selected, but greyed out, instead of being rewritten.
- The row reads the real config even when the model catalog restricts model choices, because thinking is not a model choice.
- Before config has loaded, or for users who cannot read config, the row is disabled and shows the resolved level the way the read-only row did.

**Known gaps:**

- The level list belongs to the agent's saved model. Right after changing the primary model, the list still shows the old model's levels until the agent list refreshes. Any level picked meanwhile is valid config, and the Gateway clamps it to the new model at run time.
- On a model whose only level is a harness Ultra, an agent with an Ultra override shows "Inherit default (Ultra)", though clearing it leaves no default. This is rare, and the level is visible and recoverable.

## Evidence

Live run on an isolated Gateway built from this branch, inside a macOS VM, with made-up config: agent `coder` on a stand-in reasoning model. A headless browser drove the Control UI, and the script checked the config file after each step.

Before choosing: the menu offers `Inherit default (Medium)`, `Off`, `Minimal`, `Low`, `Medium`, `High`, `Ultra`.
This frame is from the run before the label-only fix; that fix does not change this frame.

Before

![Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/8556c6104607f3ea3219925c637a008914529c98/images/2026/11/ceb177c8-6cca-4499-a032-5dade5beed5f.png)

After

![After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/8556c6104607f3ea3219925c637a008914529c98/images/2026/11/c8a71488-9023-4d9d-b278-7c958bc0880a.png)

After choosing **High**, the config file has `agents.entries.coder.thinkingDefault: "high"` and `agents.defaults` is unchanged; after a page reload the row still shows High:



Choosing **Inherit default** again removes the key from `agents.entries.coder`; after a reload the row reads Inherit default (Medium):



Second live run, same VM setup: global Low, a per-model `params.thinking` of High, and coder's own Medium.
- **Upgrade from latest stable (2026.11.3):** stable shows the read-only row. The update runs `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` with this build, then starts on the same state. coder's entry and the defaults are unchanged. `agents.list` reports `thinkingDefault: "medium"` and `thinkingInheritedDefault: "high"`, and the inherit option reads "Inherit default (High)". Choosing it removes the override, and after a reload the agent resolves to High.
- **Model-restricted operator:** a trusted-proxy person whose role has `modelPolicy.allow: ["standin/stand-in"]` and admin scope. The projected roster carries the override as `thinkingDefault` with no inherited field, and the inherit option reads plain "Inherit default".





Tests and checks:
- `ui/src/pages/agents/panels-overview.test.ts`: 21 passed; `ui/src/pages/agents/model-config.test.ts`: 13 passed; the Models page view, locale and page tests and `ui/src/lib/chat/thinking.test.ts` pass with the shared helper. They cover the levels offered, saving and clearing, inherited labels (global Low, per-model High and override Medium labelled "Inherit default (High)"; the same override on a restricted roster labelled plain "Inherit default"), a saved level the model does not offer, a restricted model catalog, and the disabled state without config. The tests that pinned the row as a read-only fact were replaced.
- `src/gateway/session-utils.agent-models.test.ts`: `agents.list` reports `thinkingInheritedDefault: "high"` for that case and omits it for an agent without an override; the real restricted projection of that roster drops the field and reports `thinkingDefault: "medium"`. The UI and Gateway tests each fail without their fix and pass with it.
- `src/gateway/session-utils-model.thinking-default.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/agents-list.test.ts` and `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/agents-models-skills.test.ts`: pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, the gateway test typecheck, oxlint and format on the touched files, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` and `pnpm protocol:check` (Swift and Kotlin contracts unchanged): pass. In a German locale the selector reads "Inherit default (Hoch)", "Aus", "Niedrig", "Mittel", "Hoch".
- Not run: the full test suite (left to CI).

prs.title: fix(android): choose automation targets without typing codes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android’s automation editor requires users to type exact run-target codes or format a session key as a target, despite knowing the supported modes and already loading recognizable sessions.

## User Impact

Users can choose a supported run mode or search the native client’s loaded sessions by name. Duplicate names show their keys as context, saved references remain intact outside the current roster, and explicit custom keys remain supported without requiring the target prefix.

## Why This Change Was Made

The target field expands inside the existing native editor and uses native radio choices, search, and the existing roster’s Load more operation. The Settings caller supplies its Gateway-scoped roster and loading/failure facts; there is no new discovery API, cache, permission request, or background polling.

This is a bounded roster, not a complete catalog: search is labeled **Search loaded sessions**, and further pages remain reachable. Archived and model-locked sessions are not offered as new targets; their saved values are not erased. The existing Gateway still owns validation and execution.

**Main session**, **Isolated run**, and **Linked run** store the existing codes. Linked run means a separate run linked to the creating conversation, not whichever chat is currently open. Choices respect the payload’s supported target shapes. Selecting an item edits only the existing draft; Save Changes, Revert Changes, failure recovery, and unrelated fields keep their current boundaries. The original raw target input and formatting hint are removed.

Author simplification retained one native field component and its two repeated option rows, with the existing draft and roster owners: net +198 production lines, +309 test lines, and one documentation line. No picker framework or backend contract was added.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/c4507bcf-b1bf-464e-a9df-2bc0344bbe58)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/30fbbba6-e989-49d2-9f1b-7bd46a563cc2)

- Play Debug compilation and 31 focused tests pass: six new target-choice Compose regressions, 23 automation mutation tests, and two existing deletion-identity UI tests. prs.title: fix(ui): dictation stops when the browser asks for microphone permission
prs.body:
Fixes #199065

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Control UI dictation stops as soon as the browser asks for microphone permission, so tapping Allow does not start listening and tapping Don't Allow shows no message.

This hits hardest on iPhone. Control UI opened from a Shortcut or as a home-screen app does not keep the microphone permission, so the browser asks on every dictation. Each time it takes three taps before you can talk: the mic, Allow, then the mic again. With speech-to-text already slow to start, dictation looks stuck.

## User Impact

One tap on the mic is enough: dictation waits while the permission prompt is open and starts listening as soon as you allow it. If you deny access, the composer says that microphone access is blocked. On the new-session page that message shows at the top of the composer, where the chat composer shows its errors.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser's permission prompt takes focus from the page and fires a window `blur` while dictation is still opening the microphone. The composer treats `blur` as the user leaving the window and ends dictation, so the start is cancelled before the user answers. This happens in Safari and in Chrome.

**This is a workaround for the permission prompt firing a window blur.** Browsers have no API that says a permission prompt is showing, so dictation ignores `blur` until it is listening. It is not tied to a browser: no browser detection, the same rule applies everywhere. From the moment dictation is listening, `blur` ends it and keeps the dictated text. A hidden page (`visibilitychange`) ends dictation at any point.

Accepted edge case: if the user switches to another app between tapping the mic and the microphone opening, dictation still starts.

On `main`, microphone and transcription errors on the new-session page render as the page-level start error, above the welcome title. With this PR they show in an alert at the top of the composer, and the next dictation clears it.

## Evidence

Real Safari 26.6 and Chrome for Testing 156 in a macOS VM, each with a fake microphone and its real permission prompt, clicked with a real mouse. The Control UI ran from source against the UI test suite's mock Gateway, so no speech was transcribed.

Before (`main`), Safari: click the mic, Safari asks, the composer drops back to idle; after Allow nothing is listening.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a8ce5595-5cfb-4f0b-ba91-acf8e644081a

After (this PR), Safari: dictation waits under the prompt, and Allow starts listening with no second click.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5f8fdb8c-36b0-4b36-ba3d-95870bf58fb0

Denying access in Chrome, `main`: no message.

![Chrome on main after denying microphone access: the new-session page shows no message](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/ac7db6f5fb85905561f8da9c1672d98bdd0b6f47/images/2026/11/d10baf5d-6df8-4d0d-9299-a9fb629f3224.png)

Denying access in Chrome, this PR: the message sits at the top of the composer.

![Chrome with this PR after denying microphone access: "Microphone access is blocked" at the top of the composer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/ac7db6f5fb85905561f8da9c1672d98bdd0b6f47/images/2026/11/a345ccfc-764c-48a7-86fb-89bdcb04dcbb.png)

Also checked: Chrome Allow on `main` drops dictation at the prompt and with this PR reaches "Listening…"; Safari Don't Allow shows the same composer message; starting dictation again clears it.

Tests: `ui/src/pages/chat/composer-dictation.test.ts` adds one test (Allow and Deny) for a blur while the microphone is opening; both cases fail on `main` and pass here. The dictation, direct-dictation and new-session page test files pass (56 of 56). UI typecheck, format and lint are clean on the touched files.

Not checked: iPhone and iOS home-screen apps, Firefox, and a real Gateway with a speech-to-text provider.

prs.title: fix: model fallback retries every model when session capability metadata was never prepared
prs.body:
Related: #194861
Related: #179290

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a turn that fails on OpenClaw's own "Session capability metadata requires worker preparation" check is retried on every configured fallback model, even though no model can fix a local session error.

## User Impact

User impact: such a turn now stops on the selected model and shows the real error, instead of silently being answered by a fallback model.

We saw this on 2026.11.3 with a Claude CLI primary and an OpenAI fallback. Turns woken by another session's completion notice hit this error on the Claude attempt and were answered by the fallback model, with no fallback notice in the chat. Those fallback turns also lacked the session tools the selected runtime had. Over three days, 15 turns in two sessions moved models this way. The trigger on that release line is addressed separately by #197434. This PR only makes sure the error can never rotate models again, from any caller.

## Why This Change Was Made

#179312 made `SessionCapabilityMetadataChangedError` stop the fallback chain. Its parent class, `SessionCapabilityReadRequired`, kept the default `Error` name, so when it escaped on its own it was classified as `unknown` and the chain moved to the next candidate. This PR gives the parent class a stable name, `SessionCapabilityReadRequiredError`, and lists it with the other local runtime coordination errors. The refresh subclass keeps its existing name.

Nothing matches on the old `Error` name or on this message; internal catches use `instanceof`. Like the other coordination errors, ending a run this way also discards a session suspension that an earlier candidate in the same run deferred.

## Evidence

- New test, "stops model fallback when an unprepared capability read escapes", next to the #179312 test. It sends a real unprepared store read through `runWithModelFallback` with one fallback.
  - Without the fix: it fails with `expected "vi.fn()" to be called once, but got 2 times`, so the chain rotated.
  - With the fix: it passes. The store test passes 22/22, and `failover-error`, `model-fallback.chain-stop` and `model-fallback` pass 124/124, including the #179312 test.
- A temporary probe, not included in the patch, also checked wrapped shapes: direct, `cause`-wrapped, `AggregateError`, `{ error }` wrapper, a 30-deep cause chain, and inside a `FailoverError`. All were `unknown` or `failover` before the fix and `coordination` after it.
- `pnpm check:changed --base upstream/main` exits 0 (format, lint, core typecheck and test typecheck, import cycles, guards). The pinned Bun fork could not be downloaded, so the documented oxfmt/oxlint fallback ran.
- Local autoreview and ClawSweeper were not run; the diff was self-reviewed.

### Live proof: real Gateway, before and after

The same scenario was run on two isolated loopback Gateways built from `v2026.11.3`:
- A: unmodified (`847611d`);
- B: `v2026.11.3` plus this commit cherry-picked (`edb3250`).

Setup on each:
- one agent on the `claude-cli` runtime with `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`;
- fallback `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`;
- a fresh state directory and no channels.

An operator started a dashboard-style parent turn that called `sessions_spawn` once and ended. The child's completion handoff then woke the parent. On 2026.11.3 that path raises the unprepared capability read (the trigger fixed separately by #197434), so the woken turn hits the real error. Redacted Gateway log lines for the woken turn:

A, before the fix: the error has no name, is classed `unknown`, and the fallback model is tried and fails the same way:
```
20:27:25.443 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=session:<id> durationMs=32 error="Session capability metadata requires worker preparation" errorName=Error
20:27:25.459 [model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 candidate=anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 reason=unknown next=anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 detail=Session capability metadata requires worker preparation
20:27:25.509 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=session:<id> durationMs=38 error="Session capability metadata requires worker preparation" errorName=Error
20:27:25.535 [agents/subagent-announce] Subagent completion direct announce failed for run <id> err={"name":"GatewayClientRequestError","message":"Session capability metadata requires worker preparation",...}
```

B, with the fix: one attempt, the error carries its new name, no fallback decision, and no second candidate:
```
20:28:15.677 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=session:<id> durationMs=47 error="Session capability metadata requires worker preparation" errorName=SessionCapabilityReadRequiredError
20:28:15.702 [agents/subagent-announce] Subagent completion direct announce failed for run <id> err={"name":"GatewayClientRequestError","message":"Session capability metadata requires worker preparation",...}
```

The announce failure itself is expected on 2026.11.3; that is the trigger #197434 fixes. This PR changes only what happens next: the turn no longer rotates through fallback models. At the default log level no explicit "chain stopped" line was printed on B. The evidence is the absence of any `model fallback decision` line and of a second attempt. Both Gateways were stopped after the run, with no listeners left.

This change was written with an AI coding agent and reviewed by the account owner before submission.

prs.title: perf(sessions): prepare event sharing only for target checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session-bearing broadcasts eagerly prepared target-sharing helpers for every connected recipient, including admin recipients whose authorization returns before reading those helpers. A fresh 10-minute synthetic Gateway attribution run on `79a72bc610cc` still attributed 47.55 MiB/min to `session-sharing-read.ts` after #199191 and #199212. The two preparers accounted for 45.34 MiB/min; 26.52 MiB/min came from event authorization and 18.63 MiB/min from row recipients.

## User Impact

Less transient allocation and main-thread work during broadcasts to admin and eligible unidentified recipients. Named viewers still receive the same current role/scope, membership, draft/incognito, and suggestion checks. Event ordering, frame bytes, session results, and audience isolation stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Let the event authorization owner invoke a preparation callback only when it needs target-sharing facts. Existing callers that already own prepared facts continue passing those facts directly. This removes unused work without retaining a viewer cache or adding an invalidation lifecycle.

The approval lookup's type previously borrowed the event-reader parameter type. It now explicitly requires already-prepared sharing facts; approval behavior is unchanged. Production LOC: **+10**, of which six are this type-only clarification. The work-count assertion adds five test lines with an exact allocation record. Benchmark usage is in the script header.

## Evidence

Acceptance declared before measurement: preserve exact frames and authority behavior; reduce owner CPU/allocation; compare counterbalanced runs and A/A controls; treat the traced whole-Gateway run as attribution, not a latency rejection gate.

The committed `scripts/perf/session-event-sharing-measure.ts` drives the real connection-state broadcaster with inert transport sinks and a committed shared row. Both changed owner modules are pinned per arm. Each cohort uses 65 recipients and five counterbalanced pairs of 5,000 publications per arm. Allocation uses separate inclusive V8 sampling passes. This exact-key owner replay is independent of roster size; the separate Gateway workload has 10,800 sessions.

| Per publication, mean of five arms | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Admin CPU | 0.04089 ms | 0.03675 ms (-10.1%) |
| Admin allocation | 152,070 B | 86,610 B (-43.0%) |
| Admin p50 / p99 | 0.03834 / 0.08726 ms | 0.03458 / 0.05967 ms |
| Admin maximum / over 180 ms | 0.817 ms / 0 of 25,000 | 0.656 ms / 0 of 25,000 |
| Eight interleaved named audiences, CPU | 0.07949 ms | 0.07775 ms |
| Named audiences, allocation | 265,102 B | 268,418 B (+1.3%) |
| Named p99 / maximum | 0.1825 / 0.659 ms | 0.1719 / 2.076 ms |

Named readers still need preparation and pay a small callback allocation cost. A/A controls: CPU 0.04150 → 0.04123 ms (-0.7%); allocation 152,166 → 152,123 B (-0.0%); p99 0.07776 → 0.07267 ms. A/A maxima: 0.681 → 0.680 ms. All timing cohorts had zero publications over 180 ms. Host load ranged 20.1–22.2 during A/B timing and 13.8–14.2 during A/A timing. Allocation-mode timings are not used as gates.

All arms produced the same complete-frame SHA-256 digest, `ecb0a46fda91d080337a83f49969cb970b65b4714e2062f4047541c177144a84`. The regression extends the existing broadcast/Stop test: two admin recipients require two presentation preparations; main performs four. It fails on main with “expected 2 times, but got 4,” and passes with this change.

Fresh-main workload: 65 sidebar clients, approximately 120 sessions.list/min, 16 transcript subscribers, 12 concurrent mock-provider turns in minute bursts, 80 seeded turns, 4 KiB tool payloads, and 40 requested plugins. Each built revision ran for ten measured minutes after warmup and completed 120 turns. Both builds used the stated baseline, with this runtime patch added to the candidate; rebasing the PR did not change the measured builds.

| Synthetic Gateway attribution | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Sharing-read allocation | 47.55 MiB/min | 20.43 MiB/min (−57.0%) |
| Two preparers under event authorization | 26.52 MiB/min | 0 |
| Total sampled allocation | 2,530.70 MiB/min | 2,465.58 MiB/min |
| Main-thread CPU | 13.53% | 15.01% |
| GC, native profiler | 0.305 s/min | 0.424 s/min |
| Event-loop p99 | 35.06 ms (28,998 samples) | 42.37 ms (28,152 samples) |
| Client sessions.list p99 | 57.18 ms (1,193 calls) | 106.05 ms (1,202 calls) |
| Server sessions.list handler p99 | 36.35 ms (1,193 calls) | 67.07 ms (1,202 calls) |
| Prepare + row + response CPU per list | 5.770 ms | 6.264 ms |
| Ending heap / RSS | 516.66 / 2,846.17 MiB | 542.76 / 2,860.31 MiB |
| Host one-minute load range | 7.14–12.71 | 12.06–36.83 |

The higher Gateway CPU/latency/GC numbers are **inconclusive for causality**, not a whole-Gateway speedup claim: these are single sequential traced attribution windows under substantially different host load, without matched Gateway A/A controls. They must not be used as a rejection or acceptance timing gate. Owner timing and A/A above are untraced. The allocation attribution is the useful result here: unused event-authorization preparation disappears, rather than moving into another owner.

For completeness, canonical telemetry reports minor GC 0.197 → 0.271 s/min (1,053 → 980 collections), major GC 0.106 → 0.150 s/min (46 → 45), and incremental GC 0.0053 → 0.0066 s/min. Minor maximum pause: 69.20 → 174.49 ms; major maximum: 39.40 → 163.40 ms. The total GC increase is material in absolute terms; untraced matched controls would be required before attributing it to this change. No pauses or maintenance windows were removed. This burst workload also does not reproduce sustained production old-generation occupancy.

Remaining scoped owners, MiB/min: event projection 43.90 → 50.49; row projection 36.26 → 38.41; child activity 34.24 → 36.77; row presentation 25.69 → 26.48; transport 24.33 → 24.26; active runs 24.91 → 26.12. Those owners are unchanged in this PR.

Validation: 32 focused tests passed across connection state, sharing events, prepared sharing, and sharing-store work; 26 approval-sharing tests passed. Focused command wall times were 50.68 s and 57.68 s, including compilation. Changed-file oxfmt/lint, `pnpm tsgo:scripts`, `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, and the gateway-server test typecheck passed. The regression's baseline run failed only at the intended work-count assertion. The branch was rebased onto current main before pushing; the benchmark comparison remains pinned to the stated baseline plus this runtime change. The initial CI script typecheck caught missing benchmark fixture/array types; those and the explicit targeted recipient set are corrected. All owner timing, allocation, and A/A results above were rerun on the corrected benchmark. CI is rerunning on head `856f4b5eadc7012d04bc0732b27f2522500396af`; it is the pending broad exact-head proof.

Independent review is delegated to the lead as requested; no local autoreview was run.

## User Impact

User impact: unchanged conversations no longer force hosted connector discovery on every message for the same unavailable plugin apps. An unavailable app can take up to one minute to be reconsidered automatically; installation, explicit invalidation, and manual refresh remain immediate. No configuration changes or migration are required, and unavailable or policy-denied apps remain unavailable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Readiness repair reuses a successful, covering forced refresh in the existing app-inventory cache for one minute, including a negative result, and joins an equivalent forced refresh already in flight. Account/thread isolation and target coverage still apply. Non-forced cold reads do not suppress the first forced repair; activation, current native policy checks, and explicit refresh retain their existing paths. There is no second cache manager, new configuration option, or permission-policy change.

Explicit runtime refresh also invalidates cached thread readiness in that account/runtime. A scoped thread refresh leaves siblings alone. Key construction and invalidation share the existing cache owner and unchanged thread-ID encoding.

## Evidence

Committed regressions use credential-free external I/O fixtures through the production config builder, manual command handler, and warm thread lifecycle/client owners. Acceptance: bound unchanged unavailable-app discovery without suppressing explicit refresh or relaxing admission.

| Scenario | Before | Current candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Three unchanged config builds, missing/inaccessible app | 3 forced reads on base | 1 |
| Three unchanged warm lifecycle turns, inaccessible app | 3 forced reads on base | 1 |
| Three unchanged builds, ready app control | 0 forced reads | 0 |
| Successful runtime refresh within the negative thread cooldown | Next warm build still excluded the connected app | Both cached same-runtime threads reconsider and admit the available, policy-allowed app |
| Other account/runtime snapshots and current native denial | Must remain isolated/enforced | Remain isolated/enforced |

- Original discovery regressions are red on `cfa40212f9c6ce442a36e6ad6b8df07eec9b6ae5` and green with bounded reuse, including the warm-lifecycle entry point with synthetic native I/O.
- Follow-up regression is red on production source matching reviewed head `2ffb9d003a19049a2db1b3a2b762f55bd1b49bd8`: the actual `/codex plugins refresh` handler succeeds at the runtime key, but the next production thread-config build still returns an empty app policy. With the clock frozen inside 60 seconds, the fix recovers two thread keys, leaves other canonical account/runtime keys untouched, and still enforces a subsequent native denial without more inventory work.
- Red/green command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/command-plugins-readiness.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "repairs warm thread readiness after runtime refresh" --reporter=dot`. A separate cache contract protects encoded sibling-thread scope during targeted invalidation.
- Current focused runs: **440 tests passed across 14 Codex files**, including the four requested modules, activation/manual refresh, migration, read-only/scheduled policy, lifecycle and run attempts. Prompt-prefix stability: **14 passed**. Total: **454 passing tests across 15 files**.
- Scoped repository typecheck covering all eight changed TypeScript files and imported consumers, oxlint on those eight files, nine-file formatting, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Fresh independent Auto Review through **P0–P2**, using `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. It covered the complete nine-file local candidate against `cfa40212…` (diff SHA-256 `13d10df931e6920eb6f0564f3b59429603b1bba58efef414b1191ba58415595a`). This supersedes the earlier P0-only local assessment; the reviewer did not independently execute tests or verify live native integration.
- Author simplification: the existing invalidation operation owns runtime/thread invalidation; the existing encoded thread-key constructor moved to that same cache/key owner and all callers migrated. No second manager, new option, generation/fence, or test-only production seam. Whole-candidate delta against the base: production +77/-20, tests +261/-3, docs +11.

Native contract inspected at pinned Codex 0.164.0 revision [6aaac694](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/6aaac694803004a63c6f393d153c96d22521a6b9/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/apps_processor/installed.rs): non-forced installed reads reuse the native snapshot, while forced reads refresh hosted runtime tools.

Limits: synthetic lifecycle/work-count proof, not an authenticated Gateway/model/connector run, macOS incident reproduction, or measured live latency/disk-I/O improvement. This does not establish a cause or fix for a separate WebSocket reset loop. Broad [exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199120/checks) is running; local proof is not a CI pass.

Contributor credit: Jacqueline Henriksen.

prs.title: fix(memory-lancedb): stop search when recall budget expires
prs.body:
Fixes #199118

## What Problem This Solves

A timed-out LanceDB recall can still start search when its embedding resolves late. Search can also give the native query time already spent preparing or refreshing the table, extending work beyond the recall deadline.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing deadline across both phase boundaries: stop before search when embedding completes too late, and deduct table preparation before dispatching the native query. A fully spent budget rejects before vector execution; a partial budget passes only the remaining whole milliseconds to LanceDB.

The outer timeout result, authority checks, native query cancellation and subsequent healthy reuse remain in place. This repairs the existing shared deadline rather than introducing another timer or a public setting.

## Evidence

The final regressions fail four ways on base: late embedding admits search both before and after timeout settlement, an expired pre-read budget still returns rows, and a partially spent budget reaches native execution unchanged. Twelve controls pass on that base.

With the fix, all 95 unique tests across eight affected/consumer suites pass. The native LanceDB fixture verifies no vector query dispatch after expiry, a 5,000 ms budget reduced to 3,499 ms after 1,500.25 ms elapsed, native cancellation and a later healthy query. Recall, explicit tools, automatic recall, provider lifecycle and external table refresh controls pass.

Executed on macOS arm64 with Node 26.12.1 and native LanceDB 0.41.0. Embedding completion and elapsed time are controlled; the database and vector queries are real. This is not a live-provider or Gateway session. Production/test typechecks, focused lint, formatting and line-cap checks pass.

```sh
node scripts/test-projects.mts \
  extensions/memory-lancedb/recall-service.test.ts \
  extensions/memory-lancedb/doctor-contract-api.test.ts \
  extensions/memory-lancedb/index.test.ts \
  extensions/memory-lancedb/auto-recall.test.ts \
  extensions/memory-lancedb/auto-recall.deadline.test.ts \
  extensions/memory-lancedb/provider-runtime.test.ts \
  extensions/memory-lancedb/embeddings.lifecycle.test.ts \
  extensions/memory-lancedb/lancedb-store.staleness.test.ts
```

### Independent review focus

Confirm that a recall whose embedding finishes after timeout does not dispatch search, and that slow table preparation consumes the same native-query budget. Then run a healthy recall on the same store to confirm recovery. The existing cold-provider initialization guards remain complementary to these later phase checks.

Plugin Settings takes unnecessarily long to render a large plugin inventory in WebKit.

## User Impact

The 1,000-plugin fixture renders faster with identical appearance in light and dark themes. No user action or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep shadow overlay resets inside shadow roots, where they are needed. Document overlays already use the canonical document reset in `base.css`; document modals no longer inject duplicate descendant and scrollbar rules. A CSS entry composes the reset and presentation rules into the same single sheet for Menu, Popover, Tooltip and shadow Modal hosts.

Default plugin fallback tiles now publish their fixed gradient directly instead of setting two inheriting custom properties on every tile. Compact prompt icons retain their custom-class CSS surface. This removes repeated matching/cascade work without changing markup, lifecycle or lazy boundaries.

prs.title: fix(matrix): persist private crypto state before key uploads
prs.body:
Closes #147450
Related: #123354 (separate received/outbound session crash paths remain outside this PR).

## What Problem This Solves

Matrix can publish one-time keys before the matching private crypto account is durable, leaving unusable keys or conflicting upload IDs after an interruption. Save the account-scoped snapshot before publication and reject the upload if that save fails. This prevents recurrence; it does not repair an already inconsistent server key pool or reset device identity.

## User Impact

Private account state must be saved before its public keys are published. Storage failures block publication until account-scoped storage is repaired and the upload is retried. Matrix-maintainer acceptance of that fail-closed tradeoff remains outstanding.

## Why This Change Was Made

The barrier runs inside the existing guarded fetch beforeRequest hook, after recovery-key persistence and message-dispatch checks. It carries originating generation, caller authority and cancellation through awaited persistence into existing SQLite action-authority admission. Ordinary requests do not load the crypto runtime. Current-main session/lifecycle owners are preserved; no snapshot-format, dependency or scope change is introduced.

## Evidence

Tested candidate: `2592b4812a4db60e8bf5a44b44f7961331724be9` (2026-10-16 UTC), compared with pinned base `0dc31f5f64309d199f12aea643452bfde54f4888`. Conflict-only rebase preserves the upload barrier and originating write authority while adopting upstream's void snapshot-lock callback.

- Focused SDK fetch-boundary proof: **10 passed / 97 unrelated cases skipped**, including stopped-before-entry, retirement during awaited persistence, storage refusal and ordinary account-data requests. Original-generation authority RED/GREEN proof remains recorded from the prior implementation; no new runtime result is claimed for the rebase.
- Current-candidate extension production/test types, seven-file lint (zero warnings/errors), formatting, diff and line-cap/assertion ratchets: **passed**. Native selected Matrix package boundary plus negative canary: **passed**, 25.59 seconds wrapper wall time; one package compiled.
- Additional current-base baseline ratchets: **passed**: conflict markers, database-worker (T1 222 → 222; deprecated compatibility 12 → 12), database-dialect (zero construct-group growth), and test-timeout-race.
- Max-lines ratchet: **exit 1 on both candidate and clean pinned base with identical diagnostics**, solely for unchanged `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx`, `ui/src/pages/config/config-page-state.ts` and `ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page-state.ts` suppressions. No baseline or suppression was changed; this check is not claimed green.
- Prior-head doctor/plugin contracts, dead-export scans and runtime checks are historical evidence, not new-base full-repository validation. Current-head CI owns broad proof. Range-diff and source inspection confirm this rebase preserves the reviewed persistence ordering, strict account-scoped state and live authority; the second commit is patch-equivalent.
- [Real SDK/Rust crypto + SQLite runtime and published v2026.10.1 upgrade evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147457#issuecomment-6108821435) was captured on prior head `7f756b78473be542b0ce1fe484dfa32ddc230262`, not rerun on this candidate. The loopback fixture proved durable-before-HTTP, storage refusal/recovery, retirement rejection, restart identity, and retained stable device/one-time-key state. Its stable-process teardown timeout and non-homeserver scope remain explicit.
- [Independent 2026.10.1 live-lab report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147457#issuecomment-6108227829) used manually ported production hunks, not this exact head; later inbound/outbound crash failures remain outside scope.

New-head CI and automated review must be assessed separately. No merge, maintainer acceptance, current-candidate real-homeserver proof or automatic background retry behavior is claimed.

prs.title: fix(cron): run keeps owner-private memory after its requester loses owner status
prs.body:
Closes #198695

## What Problem This Solves

An automation run can receive owner-private memory after its requester loses owner status while a fired condition waits for a free cron slot.

## User Impact

A run that starts after its requester is removed from the owner list receives only its parent conversation's memory audience. Runs whose requester remains an owner retain owner-private memory.

## Why This Change Was Made

Admission can happen long before payload execution. Each run rechecks requester ownership against the live runtime config when minting its execution context. Existing owner-only tool checks and intentional legacy/trusted-policy behavior are preserved.

## Evidence

[Live Gateway proof on `99181aa`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198697#issuecomment-6873644506) exercised both runtimes in one disposable VM with the repo's scripted mock provider and a CLI stub:

- Both owner-positive controls received `owner-private` and completed successfully.
- Eight occupied cron slots held both fired conditions. The requester remained in the owner list during the checks, and both runs had durable slot-wait receipts.
- The Gateway published a config removing the requester while the same wait receipts remained and neither payload had started.
- After capacity release, both payloads received `conversation` for the exact parent session key and session ID. The CLI stub recorded that same host-minted audience and run ID. Both payloads completed successfully.

A temporary observer recorded the runtime's audience; the CLI adapter passed that observed value to its stub. The Gateway scheduler, config watcher, SQLite session infrastructure, and both memory resolvers were real. The requester provenance and model transports were synthetic. No production code was changed for the proof, and the admission/resolver source hashes matched the PR head.

Two focused regressions in `src/cron/execution-context-memory-audience.test.ts` revoke a channel requester's ownership through a published config, or revoke a profile requester's access, between admission and minting. Recorded regression results: both cases fail without the fix on both runtime resolvers; the fixed test file passes all 9 tests.

## Validation Limits

The live run verifies audience assignment with synthetic model transports. It did not call a hosted model, send real Discord traffic, or read private-memory contents. The focused regression file and full suite were not rerun during the VM proof task.

prs.title: fix(bonjour): Bonjour discovery fails on npm installs of 2026.11.5 betas
prs.body:
Related: #198010
Refs #198011

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Bonjour discovery fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for `@homebridge/ciao/native.js` on npm installs of 2026.11.5-beta.1, beta.2, `release/2026.11.5` and current main.

## User Impact

User impact: npm installs advertise the Gateway over Bonjour/mDNS again. Gateways already reached ready and direct connections worked; only LAN discovery was broken. 2026.11.3 and earlier are unaffected because they import the Ciao package root.

## Why This Change Was Made

Since #182826 (`e77992dd7f9`), the core Bonjour advertiser imports `@homebridge/ciao/native.js`, an entry that only exists in the pnpm-patched Ciao (`patches/@homebridge__ciao@1.3.12.patch`). The root package declared Ciao as an ordinary dependency, so npm resolved the registry Ciao, which has no `native.js`.

Two commits:

- `8bc93455fe6`: bundle the patched Ciao in the root package, as `@openclaw/bonjour` already does, and make the tarball check require that bundling whenever `dist` imports the patched entry. This is the shape of #198011 (thanks @alfredjbclaw), re-authored with `Co-authored-by` credit for both contributor identities because the fork revision's CI is blocked on approval.
- `0456b6d46dd`: bundling alone fails the release pack. npm packs a pnpm-linked bundle's installed dependencies at their store path (`node_modules/.pnpm/@homebridge+ciao…/node_modules/{debug,fast-deep-equal,source-map-support,tslib}`), where the relocated bundle cannot resolve them and the tarball check rejects them as npm-excluded. `materializeMissingBundledDependencies` now restages a linked bundle into a flat npm layout only when npm left dependencies under that bundle's own store entry, then drops the leftover store directory. `hasMissingBundledDependencies` flags `.pnpm` entries so the pnpm-pack path also repairs them.

Rejected alternatives:

- Falling back to the Ciao package root would reintroduce the process-hook replacement #182826 removed.
- Restaging every linked bundle with installed dependencies (my first cut) also restaged `@openclaw/ai`, whose dependencies the root already installs, and pulled 346,027 entries into the tarball. The proof caught it, and the second commit narrows the rule. A negative test keeps such bundles untouched.
- No dependency version change and no new dependency.

## Evidence

- **Tests:** `test/scripts/package-bundled-links.test.ts` and `test/scripts/check-openclaw-package-tarball.test.ts` pass 105/105 on `0456b6d46dd` and on `03cff1de5e5`. With the base production files, the three new regression cases fail (102/105): store-placed restaging, store-placed tarball detection, and the patched-Ciao bundling guard. `pnpm tsgo:scripts` and `pnpm tsgo:test:root` are clean, and oxfmt/oxlint are clean on the changed files.
- **Native, pre-merge head (Crabbox AWS `cbx_4f1f6f1e39ef`, Node 24.22.1, synced source exactly `0456b6d46dd`):**
  - `package-openclaw-for-docker` pack: "OpenClaw package tarball integrity passed".
  - The tarball has 0 `node_modules/.pnpm` entries and ships `@homebridge/ciao/native.js` plus all four runtime dependencies.
  - `npm install` of the tarball works, and `import("@homebridge/ciao/native.js")` resolves (`getResponder` is a function).
  - With Bonjour enabled (it defaults on only for darwin) and `discovery.mdns.mode=full`, the Gateway logs `bonjour: advertised gateway … host=g77-proof.local. port=18799 state=announcing`, with 0 `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.
  - Installed tree: 21,248 entries / 289.1 MiB, within the 47,500 / 900 MiB budget. Ciao adds 240 entries and 1.6 MiB.
- **Before:** G76's run of the bundling-only commit failed the same pack with 66+ npm-excluded `.pnpm` entries. On published beta.2, the installed Ciao has no `native.js` (see #198010).
- **Reviews:** autoreview came back scoped-clean at P2, and an independent read-only `codex exec` review reported NO FINDINGS at P0–P2. It confirmed the existing three root bundles (acorn, chrome-devtools-mcp, playwright-core) are untouched.

**Re-proof on the merged head `03cff1de5e5`.** It merges current main to pick up #199169 (`088178a6559`), which fixes the pre-existing `extensions/telegram/src/send.history.test.ts` failure seen in this PR's first CI run.
- The merge touched no Bonjour, Ciao or packaging file. `git diff 0456b6d46dd 03cff1de5e5` is empty for `extensions/bonjour`, the Ciao patch, `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` and the packaging scripts. All six PR files are byte-identical to the pre-merge head.
- Crabbox AWS `cbx_3899e9c898d0`, synced source exactly `03cff1de5e5`:
  - the release-path pack and tarball check pass;
  - 0 `.pnpm` entries, and Ciao ships `native.js` plus all four dependencies;
  - `npm install` works and `native.js` imports;
  - the Gateway logs `bonjour: advertised gateway … state=announcing`;
  - installed tree 21,246 entries / 289.0 MiB, within the 47,500 / 900 MiB budget.
- Local: 105/105 for the two packaging test files, and 30/30 for `send.history.test.ts`.
- Autoreview: scoped-clean at P2. Independent `codex exec`: NO FINDINGS; it confirmed the six files are unchanged by the merge.

**CI diagnosis, first run on `0456b6d46dd`.** I diagnosed each failure before replacing the head, and reran no jobs:
- `check-lint-core-3`: infrastructure. apt failed in runner setup ("File has unexpected size … Mirror sync in progress?" for Google's Chrome repo) before any lint ran.
- `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-35`: `send.history` "refreshes authoritative edited captions" fails deterministically locally too. It's pre-existing on the old base and fixed on main by #199169, which is now merged in.
- `checks-node-changed-7`: `telegram-recovered-artifact` e2e passes locally twice on the same head, so it's a timing flake.
- `checks-node-changed-11`: `codex-native-hook-pressure` e2e, the known upstream bwrap metadata-mount flake.

None of these suites imports the changed files. `bundleDependencies` only affects packing.

Release note: `release/2026.11.5` carries the `native.js` import without this packaging fix. It needs both commits before 11.5 ships stable.

prs.title: perf(sandbox): reuse prepared workspace transport and unchanged packs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large local sandbox baseline replacements repeatedly encode and send unchanged content-addressed directory packs. The Gateway also expands worker-prepared mutations and serializes them again before publication.

## User Impact

Workspace preparation and recovery do less CPU and transport work, with unchanged workspace contents, checkpoint/protection semantics, stored pack bytes and tree references. No schema, migration, configuration, or protocol change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing state reader supplies only the live baseline's reachable pack digests for replacement. The computation worker skips those packs before encoding. Those packs remain protected by the live root; new packs retain the existing preparation-epoch check. Missing packs are rebuilt. No cross-request cache is added.

The computation worker also prepares source-path content and the complete compressed mutation. Main forwards that mutation unchanged and uses its prepared publication header after settlement, including lost-reply recovery. Direct large mutations retain compression because oversized checkpoint receipts must fit the broker's queue budget.

Runtime production code grows by 48 lines to carry the live pack references and prepared publication facts across existing owners. The measurement script is separate tooling. A pure receipt test moved into the existing smaller CAS test file to keep both test files within their line limits; no test coverage was deleted.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule, declared in the committed benchmark before measurement: identical roots and stored payloads, fewer preparation requests/bytes, lower CPU/allocation, and no consistent end-to-end regression. The workload alternates a one-file edit through the real worker-backed store, using synthetic contents and 10k/100k paths or the repository's 65,076 tracked path names. This is an owner replacement workload, not a full project-fetch trace.

Mean per refresh (untraced timing; five iterations per side for 10k/repository, ten for 100k in AB then BA order):

| Workload | Main-thread CPU ms | Process CPU ms | Wall ms | Preparation + mutation bytes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 10,000 files | 6.08 → 6.58 | 162.98 → 91.86 | 113.35 → 59.40 | 915,947 → 23,939 |
| 100,000 files | 50.17 → 39.54 | 1,689.15 → 759.15 | 1,345.64 → 682.95 | 9,145,594 → 144,783 |
| Repository paths | 37.91 → 28.39 | 1,145.08 → 558.08 | 876.95 → 433.58 | 6,866,480 → 12,851 |

Separate sampled-allocation passes, five iterations per side: 100k main-thread allocation **15,002,608 → 14,628,710 bytes/refresh (−2.5%)**; repository paths **12,686,619 → 11,779,094 (−7.2%)**. The small 10k main-CPU increase is 0.50 ms; total CPU falls 44%. Main allocation gains are modest compared with the reduction in native transport buffers and total worker CPU.

An untimed diagnostic refresh reports 100k preparation **1,003 → 4 packs**, **35,693,352 → 373,915 bytes before deflate**, and **9,149,914 → 144,067 compressed bytes**. Preparation writes drop **4 → 1**, followed by one mutation. Repository preparation drops **2,346 → 3 packs**, **27,875,966 → 36,857 raw bytes**, **6,877,064 → 12,140 compressed bytes**, and **10 → 1 preparation writes**. The read remains one owner snapshot per replacement. Already-incremental normal scans retain their existing selected-path behavior.

On current main, manifest/tree construction and pack deflate already run in the Git worker: their main-thread cost in this replacement path is zero. Across the first five 100k refreshes, observed main-thread v8 serialization falls **2.85 → 0.21 ms** and mutation inflation **0.48 → 0 ms**; synchronous main deflate is zero on both sides. Main thread CPU includes the actual broker and callbacks, not just these timers.

All final tree roots match. Hashes of sorted stored digest/record/children payload rows match exactly across base and candidate: `e19eee2e05e603986e08767014366a246294a94c39c4afcc11125f91b22b0e39` (100k) and `4cf67e54b24338fa09a6375dc15dbec7cfe906c3e9eaa172e2f20e32ecb6134b` (repository).

100k main GC totals over the five-refresh arms: **13.35 → 7.90 ms** and **13.59 → 4.67 ms**; max pauses **5.91 → 6.13 ms** and **4.78 → 3.62 ms**. Counts are too low for percentile gates. The first timing arms' sampled peak RSS/heap were **1,246/107 → 1,275/107 MiB** (100k) and **1,304/100 → 1,196/120 MiB** (repository); these are process samples, not a claim of reduced retained memory. One-minute host loads per 100k arm: A/B **20.82/35.60**, B/A **20.35/16.12**; repository A/B **24.03/32.71**. No metric is declared adverse from these short noisy memory windows.

Reproduce with `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/local-workspace-transport.ts --files 100000 --iterations 5`; use `--files 10000` or `--files repo`, and separate `--allocation` runs. Baseline: `7f7b16cdc243309cc9d78e3aa2c961b68739ff6c`.

Both final regressions fail on the unchanged baseline: identical replacement still issues preparation requests; prepared observation acceptance rebuilds its mutation. They pass with the fix. Focused worker-environments tests: **46 passed**; sandbox tests: **7 passed**; real warm-reuse/interrupted-base-refresh scenarios: **2 passed**. Existing rollback, expiry, stale revision, lease revocation, legacy conversion, persisted source paths, and lost-reply checks remain covered. The final focused worker test command took 56 s including compiled fixture setup. One earlier attempt was discarded because formatting changed source during fixture compilation.

The export-name guard passed; eager-import and PR-wrapper closure guards passed (24 tests). Changed-file formatting/lint and strict `pnpm tsgo:test:root` plus the matching gateway test typecheck were run. Exact-head [CI run 43651776889](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43651776889) passed on `2e10ef0151c23004a3685c89d60b2944fda749bd`; all 71 reported PR checks passed, with none pending or failed. Review and merge are reserved for the maintainer handoff; no local autoreview was launched under this lane's explicit workflow.

No Team load, production-state access, or full Gateway stress campaign was run. This follows the scoped fast-path instruction for removing duplicate preparation/transport work; these owner results do not establish whole-Gateway latency or attribute the production GC bursts to a specific project-fetch caller. Initial/direct mutations still have their existing main-thread preparation path.

prs.title: fix(skill-workshop): show what whole-file SKILL.md writes and drafts drop
prs.body:
Closes #194826

_Prepared for Cosmin Toma (RUF agentic team)._

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent silently wipes most of a live skill when it sends a short change note as the content of a whole-file `SKILL.md` write or draft.

## User Impact

User impact: when a `SKILL.md` rewrite or draft would drop most of a live skill, the agent (and the user reviewing drafts) now sees how much is removed and which sections disappear, before anyone relies on it. Nothing is blocked; writes still land and can be undone with `restore`.

## Why This Change Was Made

In #194826 (on 2026.7.1-2) an 87-line change note replaced a 387-line skill through the old proposal flow, and nothing showed the loss. On `main` that flow is gone, but `write_file` of `SKILL.md` and `draft` still replace the file whole, and the tool contract never says so.

This PR:

- adds `skillReplacementReport(before, after)` in `skill-lint.ts`: body line count before/after (`SKILL.md body: 387 → 87 lines (-78%).`), up to 8 removed `##` sections (code blocks ignored), and a non-blocking advisory when the new body is under 60% of the old one;
- shows that report on `patch`/`write_file` of an existing `SKILL.md`, on `draft` for a live skill, and on `view draft`;
- adds a `change-note` lint advisory when the title starts with Fix / Proposal / Change(s) / Changelog (only when the write introduces it, like the other rules);
- states in the tool description, the `/learn drafts` prompt and `docs/tools/skill-workshop.md` that `write_file`/`draft` content is the complete file and replaces it whole.

Advisory rather than blocking: writes are versioned with `restore`, and the codebase has no override-flag pattern for this. The Control UI already shows a diff before applying a draft.

Known nits: a legitimate title such as `# Change management` gets the change-note advisory; every `SKILL.md` patch now carries a one-line size summary; with the shrink advisory a write can end with four advisory lines instead of the documented three.

Possible follow-up, not in this PR: `skill_library` `update` with `proposal_content` also replaces `SKILL.md` whole.

## Evidence

On `main` at d44c9ad92 with this commit applied:

- `pnpm test extensions/skill-workshop`: 16 files, 140 tests passed.
- New tests: `skill-lint.test.ts` (report and `change-note` rule) and `tool.test.ts` ("shows what a whole-file SKILL.md rewrite or draft drops from the live skill"), which reproduces the incident: a 65-line skill rewritten with a `# Fix: …` note via `draft`, `view draft`, and `write_file`.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `oxlint extensions/skill-workshop`, and `git diff --check` pass. (On the original base 1ad3ec3d2 also oxfmt, `lint:docs` and the pre-commit hooks.)
- Gap: no end-to-end run against a live Gateway with a real agent; the change only adds text to tool results.

prs.title: fix(ui): avoid no-match claims before usage filters are ready
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Usage filter pickers say “No matches” while a changed reporting range is still loading or has failed to load.

## User Impact

User impact: searching providers, models, channels or tools no longer incorrectly rules out choices before their inventory is available, on desktop and phone. Existing selections, actual no-match results, report errors and recovery remain usable. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The report owner already distinguishes unknown filter options from an accepted empty inventory. The shared picker now carries that distinction through the desktop menu/chips and phone filters instead of losing it to an empty-array fallback. It adds no request, stored state, spinner or restriction.

## Evidence

Real Control UI with synthetic Gateway responses, light theme; desktop 1440×1100 and emulated phone 390×1100. Annotated crops below show the same held reporting-range request.

**Before** — the provider search claims no match while the report is still pending.

![Before: premature no-match claim](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05d845ea-5ad1-4400-897e-eb9591b183bf)

**After** — the search stays editable without inventing an empty result.

![After: search remains neutral](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/20702bbf-a853-41f0-ad6b-1c8c0efea62b)

<details>
<summary>Phone filters</summary>

**Before**

![Before: phone picker claims no match](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dcd02609-fc60-4e90-b5d5-80b2d5d2b24d)

**After**

![After: phone picker preserves unknown inventory](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0eb072ad-95dc-4685-93bd-bb6e0d9394de)

</details>

- Both new browser regressions fail on isolated main `e33981dc` and pass on this independent branch. They exercise pending → failed read → retry by reselecting the range → actual no-match search → successful provider selection. The existing failed-range/retained-totals browser scenario also passes: **3 scenarios**, 21.48s wall time.
- The owning view regression fails on main and passes here, retaining a selected provider and the same typed search through inventory recovery. **52 focused view, creator, query and ownership tests pass**, 2.61s wall time; baseline has 51 passing existing tests.
- UI typecheck, formatting and diff checks pass. Targeted lint has no errors and the same nine warnings as baseline; none was suppressed. Expected rejected-read diagnostics remain visible in test output.
- Self-review/simplification: **+6 net production lines**, **152 test lines**. One existing readiness fact is forwarded; the creator inventory keeps its separate retention policy. No shared menu lifecycle or query semantics changed.

This is an independent draft for review, not merged or deployed. Broad PR CI, CI timing, independent automated review, native-phone and live-provider verification are not claimed complete.

Requested and co-authored by @vyctorbrzezowski.

prs.title: improve(ui): remove Start if due from automation menus
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Automation menus offer **Start if due** next to **Start now**. It only starts a run when the schedule says one is already due, and the scheduler already starts due runs by itself, so in practice it almost always answers "not due" and does nothing. Beside **Start now** it reads as a second way to run a job, which it isn't.

## User Impact

The automation row menu and detail menu now offer **Clone** and **Delete**. **Start now** is unchanged and remains the one manual run action.

## Why This Change Was Made

Its only real use is testing an automation's condition check (`trigger.script`) without bypassing it. That is a developer task, and it stays available outside the Control UI.

## What stays available to plugins and integrations

- `cron.run` still accepts `mode: "due"` and the Gateway behavior is unchanged.
- `openclaw automations run <job-id> --due` and the `automations` tool (default `runMode: "due"`) are unchanged.
- Removed code was UI-only: the menu item, its `"due"` call path in the Control UI and the now-unreachable "not due yet" notice copy. No protocol, SDK or published package changed.

## Evidence

- 42 focused automation test files (360 tests), UI typecheck, focused lint, formatting and i18n verification passed. No broad CI or live Gateway claim.
- Actual Control UI (mock Gateway dev server), dark theme, 1440×1000: the row menu shows Start if due, Clone, Delete before and Clone, Delete after.
- Simplification: 26 additions / 51 deletions including tests; no new state.

prs.title: fix(ci): keep isolated Gateway tests out of methods inventory
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes inherited main CI failures in “gates Gateway method workers without changing complete coverage”: the planner selects 591 entries while the executable Gateway methods configs select 590.

## Why

Commit `55b5905ff83aed24f81dee5657e1ed39ac261b2b` moved `test/plugins/deep-research-recovery.gateway.test.ts` from database workers into isolated Gateway server tests. It updated the executable methods exclusions, but the planner's plugin filter still excluded only database workers. The recovery file became an extra, non-executable methods entry while retaining its legitimate isolated owner.

Use the existing canonical `gatewayMethodsTestExclude` in that filter. The methods inventory now exactly matches its executable configs, and recovery remains once under the isolated server owner. Existing coverage and worker assertions are unchanged. This is the same one-line correction already included in pending #198943; this focused repair excludes that PR's separate test consolidation.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. Complete test coverage and the research test's required process isolation remain intact. No new cache, configuration, schema, runner, timeout or test skip. CI tooling +1/−1; product and test LOC delta zero.

The separately reported Activity failures are already repaired on current main. #199157 (`a4fb1430366739903cdd037516b927e846b64a06`) intentionally removed Activity image galleries but left remote-image E2E assertions behind. #199168 (`a806af1be280ea36b593eee9ccaf9f8002371e00`) removed those obsolete cases/fixtures while retaining desktop/mobile recap and pull-request-preview checks. Both retained cases pass on this PR's main parent; no additional UI change is justified. The Usage removals in #199161 and #199170 are unrelated.

## Evidence

Pinned main parent: `7f7b16cdc243309cc9d78e3aa2c961b68739ff6c`.

- `pnpm test test/scripts/ci-node-test-plan.test.ts`: baseline 159 passed / 2 failed with exactly the reported 591-versus-590 mismatch; fixed 161/161 passed. Existing failing regression assertions are untouched. Wall time 104.47s before / 98.69s after; no speedup claim.
- Inventory comparison: 590 planned / 590 executable; zero extra or missing paths. Research recovery has zero methods entries and exactly one isolated-server entry.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/activity-polish.e2e.test.ts`: current main 2/2 passed at 1440 and 390 px (21.31s wall).
- Fresh independent Codex autoreview, P0–P2, reviewed the full local diff plus complete inventory and Gateway ownership source: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Simplification retains the one-line canonical-owner correction.
- `git diff --check` and the required tooling-test typecheck pass. The changed-check outcome is recorded below.

prs.title: improve: speed up Control UI device authentication
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Warm Control UI boot spends avoidable time in JavaScript Ed25519 curve math and initialization before connecting, especially in WebKit.

## User Impact

The existing device identity now signs with native WebCrypto Ed25519 where available. Noble still derives public keys and handles insecure contexts, unsupported engines, and native import/sign failures. Public keys and stored seed, token, and credential formats are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native signing owner avoids JavaScript curve math and unused noble initialization during warm connection setup, while preserving the established identity and fallback contracts.

## Result and coordinator-accepted timing band

**Coordinator-accepted:** localhost is the target flow, with a ≥5% gain required; the other conditions must not regress beyond the band. WebKit warm localhost connected readiness improves **433→365.5 ms (−15.59%)**, against A/A **−0.46%**. The 100 ms RTT guard improves **947→904 ms (−4.54%) across all 30 retained triplets**, against A/A **−0.79%**. This is a guard improvement. The coordinator corrected the earlier wording requiring a separate 5% win at RTT; that correction is explicit rather than a claim that 4.54% met the original target.

The WebKit RTT first-UI p95 is **882→904 ms (+2.49%)**, within the coordinator's tail rule of no more than 5% above the higher control; that tail did not reproduce in the extra ten (867→865 ms). All original observations remain included. No new timing runs were performed for this band call.

**Chromium and Firefox guards confirmed from the existing matrices:** cold/warm at localhost and 100 ms RTT, both first UI and connected readiness, all stay within the band. The largest median increase versus base is +0.31%. The largest p95 increase above the higher control is +0.32%; no cell exceeds 5% on either comparison.

## Signing and security contract

**WebKit signatures are randomized and still valid.** A same-seed/same-message WebKit 27.2 probe produced five distinct signatures, all verified against the RFC public key. The final-layout qualification separately delivered **50 native-signed real UI handshakes per engine accepted by a real isolated Gateway: 150 total**. The wire signatures matched successful native signing output using non-extractable, sign-only keys. A tampered signature was rejected as `device-signature` in each of Chromium, WebKit and Firefox. Deterministic signature fixtures apply only to noble fallback; native outputs are cryptographically verified.

The native owner imports the existing 32-byte seed in RFC 8410 PKCS8 form and caches only the most recent seed's non-extractable, sign-only key for the document. It stores neither signatures nor payloads. Failed native import/sign and insecure contexts retain the noble path and its input errors. Accepted edge: a rejected import stays cached until the identity changes or the document ends; noble remains usable.

Replay audit: `src/gateway/server/connection.ts:325` creates a fresh UUID challenge per WebSocket. `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-auth.ts:384-408` checks the two-minute timestamp window and exact connection nonce before signature verification. `handshake-auth-helpers.ts:217-242` reconstructs v3/v2 payloads; `src/infra/ed25519-signature.ts:177-190` calls `crypto.verify`, rather than deterministic re-signing. Watch HTTP consumes its challenge by nonce (`src/gateway/watch-node-http.ts:490-499`). Browser-pair throttling keys device ID and request ID (`src/gateway/browser-pair-http.ts:194`); pairing/token owners key device ID, role, public key, request ID or token. The actual UI (`ui/src/api/gateway-connect-plan.ts:253-271`) attaches signature bytes only as proof over the nonce/timestamp-bound v2 payload. No signature-byte replay, dedupe, idempotency or logging identity was found. The misleading V3 helper comment now describes payload reconstruction.

Fresh independent security review of randomized signing, cache identity, non-extractability, fallback and Gateway verification found **no actionable P0–P2 issues**. The subsequent benchmark correction/test simplification was independently reviewed clean. The two cap changes were separately reviewed; implementation and measured bundles are unchanged.

## Loading and bytes

Noble stays in the original lazy signer chunk but initializes only for public-key derivation or fallback. Emitted Rolldown output uses `Promise.resolve()` for the nested import: native warm signing skips noble setup, and cold identity creation adds no network request. No theme/CSS/scheduling or dependency changes.

Post-paydown comparison: base `18a62d6ff93428f15b0801ba5efe4ef0452a8f15` → reviewed head `86719414f1ee17bdb50b9d42effa469e0dd3f6d9`, same Node 26.12.1/toolchain, fixed build identity and matching canonical packaged Settings inventories (`memory-core`, `nostr`, `whatsapp`).

| Surface | Base → native | Requests |
|---|---:|---:|
| Startup JS, normalized gzip | 90,880→90,880 B | 3→3 |
| Startup CSS, normalized gzip | 40,789→40,789 B | 1→1 |
| Chat boot JS, normalized gzip | 1,309,377→1,309,615 B (+238 B) | 21→21 |
| New Session boot JS, normalized gzip | 813,185→813,423 B (+238 B) | 17→17 |
| Largest JS, normalized gzip | 569,985→569,985 B | — |

**Strict paired check passed: zero violations.** The largest chunk's existing main overage is unchanged. **Coordinator-accepted:** only the original +235 B cap edits are reapplied to #199256's refreshed main caps: **1,310,659→1,310,894 B** and **814,328→814,563 B**. No shared-checker, startup, CSS, request-count or other cap changes. This integrated graph emits +238 B per route: 3 B above the original +235 B local measurement, within the checker's 64 B variance band and below both exact requested caps. The original Linux pair emitted +236 B.

Original qualification bytes are retained for comparison: startup JS 90,945→90,945 B and CSS 40,781→40,781 B; Chat 1,315,251→1,315,486 B and New Session 818,719→818,954 B (+235 B each). Original served startup JS was 91,606→91,619 B (+13 B generated asset-name noise).

The first post-rebase local pair was discarded because generated packaged-plugin inputs differed (ten catalogs in the long-lived lane checkout versus three in the fresh base). Remeasuring the unchanged head in the existing proof checkout with the same three canonical catalogs removes that mismatch. No source or checker change was made to obtain the qualified pair.

Known WebKit warm `index.html` fetch access-control errors occurred in all RTT arms (30 rows each across 30 triplets); localhost had three base rows and one head row.
