prs.title: fix(telegram): keep DM topic approvals in their conversation
prs.body:
Closes #197907

## What Problem This Solves

An exec or plugin approval requested inside a private Telegram bot topic is sent to the root DM, not to the topic. The topic only gets "Approval required. I sent the approval request to Telegram DMs, not this chat." The user has to leave the conversation to find the card.

## User Impact

When the requester is also an approver on the same Telegram account, the approval card and its result stay in the topic where the request started. Other approvers still get their usual DM card. The requester gets one terminal result, whichever approver card is processed first.

This screenshot shows the original bug, before the fix:

![Approval sent outside its private bot topic](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw/333ff77343c75779e6d844aed454014f26c94525/docs/assets/qa/2026-11-13/telegram-dm-topic-approval.png)

## Why This Change Was Made

With `execApprovals.target: "dm"`, the delivery plan uses only approver DM targets. The approver DM target for the requester is the bare chat id, so the topic was dropped.

- The Telegram approver-DM resolver now carries the origin topic onto the requester's own DM target, only when the bot account and the numeric private chat both match the request origin.
- The redirect notice is not sent when the card already went to the origin topic.
- The terminal-result fallback waits for a later origin card in the same fan-out before it sends a separate result to the topic, so a requester that is processed second does not get two results. A failed edit of the topic card still sends one replacement result.

## Evidence

Live Telegram Test Server E2E, real Gateway + deterministic mock model, leased QA user, Threaded Mode on, `execApprovals: { enabled: true, approvers: [<qa user>], target: "dm" }`, `tools.exec.mode: "ask"`. The user sends `EXEC:/usr/bin/touch ...` inside a fresh DM topic, then taps **Allow Once**.

- `main` at `8ebe740925ca`: the card `Approval required ... /approve <id> allow-once` was posted in the root DM (no topic). The topic got `Approval required. I sent the approval request to Telegram DMs, not this chat.`, and the tap could not find the button in the topic.
- This head `b358a299a60b`: the card was posted in the topic (`topicId=200489`). The tap edited the same card to `Exec approval resolved / Allowed once`, the command ran, and one `EXEC_DONE` reply arrived in the topic. No redirect notice and no message in the root DM. A later `PING:after` in the topic was answered there.

Captured Telegram events (TDLib recorder on the QA user; `msg#` is the tail of the TDLib message id, so equal ids are the same message):

```text

```

</details>

<details>
<summary>this head b358a299a60b (after)</summary>

```text
    0.2s  user  message topic 200489 msg#953665  PING:warm
    8.4s  bot   message topic 200489 msg#147968  PONG:warm
```

prs.title: fix(release): share qualification validation across publication gates
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes valid receipt-recovered qualification being rejected at publication even though strict evidence validation accepted it. Related: #199083; this preserves that repair’s intended behavior by deleting the conflicting validator rather than adding another recovery exception.

## User Impact

Release operators get one qualification verdict across candidate readiness, publication preflight, and prepared-artifact adoption. Direct qualification and authenticated recovery remain distinct valid cases; missing admission, forged evidence, incorrect identity, uncovered failures, and out-of-scope waivers remain failures. No active release needs to adopt this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

`validateReleaseRunEvidence` is the existing authentication owner. It now exposes normalized qualification facts after validating the complete evidence graph. The publication adapter consumes those facts and retains only publication-specific eligibility. Its in-memory handoff binds the final publisher context and rechecks live authority rather than reinterpreting raw evidence.

<details>
<summary>Ownership, cutover, and retained compatibility</summary>

- Removed the parallel synchronous publication validator, its caller-supplied “strict validation” callback, the checklist manifest validator, and obsolete workflow ancestry plumbing. Scripts and workflow adapters together shrink by 402 lines against the original base.
- `full-release-receipt-recovery.mjs` still authenticates the original admission, recovered receipts, and recovery authority. Recovery does not populate the aggregate’s direct-admission field.
- Candidate checklist and preflight share the authenticated traversal and existing publication gates. Prepared npm, ClawHub, npm preflight, Docker, and readiness dispatch consume the same owner; no new service, cache, or persistent state.
- Publication eligibility still enforces actual tag, selection, covered plugin subset, and publish-purpose admission. Existing approval/publication boundaries and point-of-effect authority checks remain.
- Historical v3/v4 readers, strict JSON `qualificationAdmission`, and CLI source labels remain for existing consumers. v2 is diagnostic-only. Offline stable closeout retains its checksum-bound published-snapshot contract, not a second hosted qualification policy.
- Added transport-only direct/recovery fixtures to exercise the real owner graph, replacing fake callback tests. The larger test fixture retains original admission, child attempts, observations, and recovery seal without mocking their validators.

</details>

## Evidence

- **Before:** the authenticated recovered fixture passed strict recovery and failed the real publication evidence consumer with `Frozen publication qualification requires independently authenticated P admission`. **After:** the same path succeeds without manufacturing the direct-admission field.
- **694 passed, 2 skipped** across 14 affected consumer suites, including strict validation, recovery, checklist, preflight, publication gates, prepared npm, ClawHub, Docker, and direct/recovery readiness CLI paths.
- Compact negative matrix rejects missing/forged admission, wrong C/run/attempt/workflow, altered artifact bytes, missing recovery authentication, uncovered failures, and out-of-scope waivers. Direct and recovered evidence expose equivalent shared qualification facts.
- Independent review found a historical-main → protected-publisher handoff mismatch; fixed by binding the initial traversal to the final publisher context, with a regression. Committed-range review then caught an over-broad registry-admission requirement for older operation-based evidence. That exact guard was reproduced red, restored to the authenticated workflow contract, and verified green: **277 passed, 2 skipped** across validator, strict-reader, ClawHub, and evidence-consumption suites. After test-transport typing corrections, the historical regression passed again; the separate three-file rerun passed 154 tests with 2 skipped.
- Broader workflow/adapter run: 747 passed, 18 failed. Two stale changed-consumer expectations were then corrected and their focused rerun passed (2 tests). The remaining 16 failures are 15 instances of an inherited fixture omitting `release-qualification-admission.mjs`, plus unavailable host `zip`. The missing-module failure was reproduced from exact base-revision fixture/source bytes; no expectations were weakened. The full broad suite was not rerun after those two corrections.
- Targeted script/test lint, script and tooling-test typechecks, formatting, `git diff --check`, and docs link validation passed (16,639 links, zero broken).
- Workflow lint was attempted but blocked by missing actionlint/pre-commit and Python ensurepip/venv support on this host.
- Local ClawSweeper was unavailable. Canonical autoreview (OpenClaw engine, P0–P2) reviewed committed range `27592cd31c1d6adda9116d5b86b57eb4ac393341..91f08d0086bee97e7f2b046f7239836bb5221b8e`, finding the historical admission regression above. Its repair was independently reviewed as a local snapshot against `91f08d0086bee97e7f2b046f7239836bb5221b8e`: scoped-clean, no remaining P0–P2 findings. Subsequent test changes only align transport return types with the real client.
- Integrated main at `5a82b39b66d6` after #199083 merged. Both conflicts were in the retired validator and fake-callback tests; their replacements were retained byte-identically. After integration, the three affected production-path suites passed **24/24**, script typecheck passed, and GitHub reports the PR mergeable. Published head: `eeb6d9afe195d3393f24c97f3d686ae5b688a477`.
- ClawSweeper acknowledged the PR's initial review intake; no duplicate request was posted. Release-manager review is required by CODEOWNERS.

**Proof limits:** production entrypoints run with synthetic external transport. The real preflight provenance gate passes; unrelated synthetic registry/release gates intentionally do not, so this is not an all-gates-green live preflight. No new FRV, workflow dispatch, candidate edit, tag, registry write, release publication, cancellation, or active-release artifact/process mutation was performed.

prs.title: fix(signal): links with non-English characters are shown twice
prs.body:
Closes #199107

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes: Signal messages print a URL twice, the second time percent-encoded in parentheses, when the URL contains non-ASCII characters or `|` (for example non-English Wikipedia links).

## User Impact
User impact: Signal users see such links once, as written. Links whose label differs from the destination still show the destination, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made
Signal already leaves out the `(url)` suffix when the visible text is the URL itself, but it compared against the parser's percent-encoded destination, which never matches the visible characters. The check now also compares against the decoded destination. When decoding would produce whitespace or control characters (e.g. `%20`), the suffix is kept, so the visible text stays a usable URL.

## Evidence
- `markdownToSignalText`, main vs this branch:
  - `See https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Müller` → before: `… Müller (https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%BCller)`; after: `See https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Müller`
  - `https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/東京` → before: `… 東京 (…/%E6%9D%B1%E4%BA%AC)`; after: shown once
  - `https://example.com/?q=a|b` → before: `… (https://example.com/?q=a%7Cb)`; after: shown once
  - unchanged: `https://example.com/a%20b` and `[docs](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Müller)` keep their suffix
- New test `does not duplicate URLs whose destination is percent-encoded` (`extensions/signal/src/format.test.ts`) fails on main and passes with the fix; `format.test.ts` 5/5.
- `pnpm check:changed`: passing (format, extension lint, extension and extension-test typecheck).
- Gaps:
  - IDN hosts (punycode destinations) are unchanged.
  - Locally, `pnpm test:extension signal` timed out in `send.test.ts`, `monitor.tool-result.autostart.test.ts` and `event-handler.partial-delivery.test.ts`. None of them involve link formatting, and the same shard also hung on unmodified main here, so I'm relying on PR CI for those.

prs.title: feat(clawrouter): generate catalog-qualified OpenRouter music
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192276

## What Problem This Solves

ClawRouter's registered music tool cannot consume its qualified OpenRouter Lyria offers, and provider-wide capabilities would drop their duration or load unsupported reference images before selection.

## User Impact

When a deployment grants either supported OpenRouter Lyria model, the existing music tool can select its native or manifest transport with only the ClawRouter key. It returns one complete WAV or MP3 track and rejects reference images before loading them. A possibly paid POST cannot trigger another provider attempt after errors, cancellation, lost responses, or local persistence failure. This draft does not activate router offers or qualify live synthesis or dollar pricing.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a focused stack on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192276 at `c4fa75387b0fa42f45e47e09de25725b8d03d0e0`, carrying the exact landed SDK outer-deadline correction from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192196. Lyria production/SDK/Google behavior remains unchanged; the current parent additionally carries the exact already-qualified stored-key speech fixture correction and its +1 allocation. It consumes the two text-only declaration contracts from https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/pull/797 (`12f4815ce3c289554f60ec192cf3f01afca905cc`) and the full-output runtime landed by https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/pull/795 (`e47ecdedd4da93bb665431b81f698668468dc8ea`). Actual composed Worker qualification remains separate and pending.

The native plugin and proxy consumer share the existing SSE-audio decoder through the existing music-generation SDK barrel; native credential resolution stays in the native plugin. Optional model-specific duration and reference-image maps resolve before normalization/reference loading. Google retains its original capability projection and request/result behavior. The existing registered-tool fixture is shared rather than copied; the native decoder's former private implementation is removed.

The proxy profile requires exact model/upstream/provider/operation/formats and fresh proxy-key offers. It sends `Accept: text/event-stream`, caps the request at256KiB and prompt at32768 UTF-16 units, and requires `[DONE]` plus EOF within32MiB wire/16MiB audio/1MiB transcript. Requested duration is at most180 seconds; it does not promise an output size or completion time. The existing caller signal, remaining deadline and explicit header/body inactivity bound remain authoritative. A qualified Undici body-inactivity timeout is surfaced as a TimeoutError with its original cause, rather than an ambiguous terminated message. The final thrown error retains the post-attempt replay marker; that marker does not determine billing or refunds.

## Evidence

Current draft source: `15aeb223287b93cf26917e846f658dd53143eb4d`, tree `dd35a00f28cd0c50741431bd7c8228cd163c0ba8`, signed descendant of `49743aff29c4adf37188725b130325026d3dad18`. This is incoming author-source publication, not native preparation or READY approval.

The manifest correction uses the selected canonical `openrouter/google/lyria-3-*` ID inside the manifest body. Native requests retain the upstream `google/lyria-3-*` ID. This avoids selecting the colliding Google-owned model at the router's provider-ownership boundary. Google path parameters, selected offers, proxy credentials, deadlines, cancellation, cleanup and no-replay behavior are unchanged.

All 43 registered OpenRouter host cases are retained and are UNRUN on this head. The existing eight model/route/WAV-MP3 cases now include eligible colliding Google catalog IDs and assert the exact native or manifest body. Unknown-price, key-isolation, one-POST, zero-paid-fallback, malformed-output, abort and deadline assertions remain.

Code-only checks passed: qualified formatter, Node syntax checks, whitespace/privacy checks, normal signed-commit hooks and full-context P0-P2 source review with no actionable findings. Application semantic tests on Node and Bun, semantic typechecks, lint, required builds and current-head SDK/Worker composition remain UNRUN. Source review is not execution proof.

The test-line ratchet remains FAIL: 6,447,738 lines against a 6,447,601 ceiling, over by137. The allocation changed477 to510 for exactly33 added test LF lines. prs.title: fix(mcp-events): reject impossible event and subscription dates
prs.body:
Fixes #199101

## What Problem This Solves

MCP Events accepts impossible calendar dates in signed callbacks and subscription
expiry values because JavaScript silently normalizes them. For example, April 31
becomes May 1 when scheduling a refresh.

## User Impact

Malformed event dates and expiry dates are rejected at admission. Valid leap days,
timezones and the existing `24:00:00` end-of-day spelling continue to work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Check that the authored calendar day survives a UTC-midnight round trip, after
the existing shape and finite-instant checks. Checking the date separately avoids
rejecting a valid timestamp whose offset or end-of-day spelling crosses a UTC
day boundary. This stays inside the existing shared MCP timestamp guard, with
no new dependency or public API.

## Evidence

Extended the existing lifecycle fixture through the real HTTP callback handler,
HMAC verification and SQLite ingress queue. On base, a correctly signed event
with `2026-02-29T12:00:00Z` receives HTTP 200; after the fix it receives 400 and
no event is queued. Existing authentication, schema and size refusal controls
continue to pass. Valid leap-day, timezone and end-of-day controls receive 200
and retain their original timestamp in the queue.

The production subscription parser separately rejects impossible future expiry
dates instead of normalizing them. Valid expiry controls retain their intended
instant. Base: 3 failing tests and 21 passing controls. Fix: all 24 tests pass.
Production/test typechecks, focused lint, formatting and line-cap checks pass.

Executed with Node 26.12.1 on macOS arm64. HTTP and SQLite are real in this fixture;
the MCP source and scheduler are controlled, so this is not a live external
subscription session.

```sh
node scripts/test-projects.mts extensions/mcp-events/src/service.test.ts
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json --incremental
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --format json --tsconfig tsconfig.extensions.json \
  extensions/mcp-events/src/protocol.ts extensions/mcp-events/src/service.test.ts
pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/mcp-events/src/protocol.ts \
  extensions/mcp-events/src/service.test.ts
```

### Independent review focus

For a configured MCP Events source, compare signed invalid-date and valid-date
callbacks, then inspect the subscription refresh response with an impossible day.
The expected boundary is rejection before event admission or refresh scheduling;
a valid date with a timezone must still preserve its original occurrence time.

prs.title: fix(gateway): reduce resident memory on constrained hosts
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/192547

## Problem and change

Gateway startup and the first model turn retain unnecessary code and independent readers on memory-constrained ARM64 hosts.

This change shares bounded store readers; retires idle workers under memory pressure; loads optional runtimes on demand; skips empty-store work; and defers optional background work until memory is available. Token-only CLI requests avoid credential database machinery. Hosts with at most 1 GiB of effective memory use the existing direct-spawn path instead of retaining the optional default broker.

Shutdown leaves idle native writers to the existing reader-first drain. The final active borrower still waits for its native handle and lease to close. The memory guard rejects Node 24's unlimited-memory sentinel while retaining finite-limit pressure deferral.

Internal unused exports are removed. No new configuration options, dependencies or persistent formats. Net added test lines: 400/400; no test-line allocation file.

## Validation

- Rebased onto `989f4a6d`, preserving its independent compaction lane and bounded readers. All 52 focused reader, compaction and lifecycle checks pass.
- Final production shutdown repair: 78 pinned-Bun checks and 13 explicit Node 24 reply/idle checks pass. The four reply cases fail before the repair. Types, scoped lint, formatting and independent P0–P2 review pass.
- Real Linux ARM64 restart E2E passes with the final production guard in a freshly built native Docker image: clean-close seal, plugin cleanup and process handoff (7.817-second test). The supported prebuilt-runtime route was used after declaration preparation failed before test execution.
- Earlier import, reader-lane, lifecycle, prewarm, build-graph, restore and backend-custody proofs retain their actual revision labels in native review. The original 50-selector backend replay passed 653 cases with five skips after cleanup repair.
- Gateway fixtures now preserve worker limits, wait for committed cron state, correlate WebSocket response IDs, and join independently owned background work before cleanup. Worker-budget regression reproduces two requested workers becoming 17; the fix passes 76 config checks and 175 real Gateway cases on Linux ARM64.
- Latest test-only change retains every 30-second server wait and success assertion, and gives the transport 35 seconds to receive the response. All five subagent cases pass locally. WebSocket correlation has deterministic red/green proof and seven passing cases; the agent-deletion diagnostic group passes 486 cases. These changes do not establish the cause of earlier intermittent hosted delays.
- Scoped types, lint, formatting, line gates and fresh independent P0–P2 reviews pass. Production code is unchanged after `216ba2e7`.
- Original ARM64 memory acceptance at `523851ff`: 916.641 MiB outer peak below 928 MiB, health in 7.345 seconds, a real OpenAI `gpt-5.4-mini` reply in 19.498 seconds, and a 60.382-second healthy soak. Limits: 768 MiB service, 1 GiB outer/client, one CPU, V8 old/young 256/4 MiB. No OOM, restart or swap.

## CI and limits

Current head: `3ba05113eda4f5c037881badd2f43bb61312384e`. [CI run 43647908332](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43647908332), attempt 1, completed with 139 successful jobs, six failed test jobs, a downstream failing CI gate and 23 skipped jobs. All PostgreSQL jobs and the build-artifact job passed.

Six failed test jobs are attributed to existing baseline behavior; the aggregate gate consequently remains failed:
- Planner coverage: two cases report 591 entries instead of 590. Exact baseline `0740281e` reproduces both; upstream moved a recovery test to an isolated owner without removing it from whole-config inventory. All 12 owner inputs remain unchanged through this run's base and merge.
- Activity browser test: upstream [#199168](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199168) removed the browser-local tool feed but left a test waiting for `.activity-empty`. A fresh browser build on this run's exact base `18a62d6f` fails the same case before subscription or event injection. All 22 inspected test, UI, build and dependency inputs match the tested merge.
- Windows lifecycle: both stop/enable and suspension triage cases reproduce on baseline `27592cd3` (2 failed, 25 passed), with the same Bun-to-Node worker serialization mismatch and missing mocked task operations.
- Fresh Doctor: the split-root update case reproduces on `27592cd3` (1 failed, 11 passed), with the same deserialization error before pending-recovery reporting.
- Candidate admission: both deadline cases and fresh-profile authority reproduce on `27592cd3` (3 failed, 13 passed).
- Model list: the stale `account-a-only` presentation was reproduced on baseline `2f6061c9`; the retained native review records that run, although its raw log was not located. The failing assertion precedes replacement-time dispatch. The inspected owner still returns its retained published list while replacement discovery is pending.

All 73 inspected source inputs are unchanged between the current run's exact base and tested merge. Earlier baseline proofs retain their actual revision labels; they are not reported as new runs on the current head.

The automated failure report and the operator's baseline attribution are separate evidence. Failed CI is not described as green. Native landing must verify current review/security requirements and the exact completed attempt.

Earlier runs and revision-specific evidence remain in native review: [e1013f37](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43644412261), [a28b821e](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43640624138), [8db1930a](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43637627901), [7d758ade](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43633990403), and [88641423](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43630800382). Passing local replays do not explain historical timeouts.

The memory measurement belongs to `523851ff`, not the latest head. The physical Cardputer is offline; physical-device operation and a 512 MiB service are not qualified. Shared queues and first-use imports can add latency, and sustained memory pressure can delay optional work.

prs.title: fix(workboard): choose existing labels instead of retyping them
prs.body:
Related: #196810

## What Problem This Solves

Workboard asks users to remember and comma-format existing labels in card forms, inline editing, and bulk updates instead of offering the labels already present in their loaded cards.

## User Impact

Users can browse, search, and select existing labels in all three flows, or deliberately add a new label. Saved labels containing commas are preserved as single values. Selections stay local until Save or Apply, and cancellation, failed saves, light dismissal, and lost editability retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

A single Workboard-local control derives choices from the existing authorized card inventory in the current board and agent scope. It uses native checkboxes and the existing theme, dialog, popover, draft, and mutation owners. The loaded inventory is bounded, not a complete label catalog: saved selections remain available outside it, and custom labels remain supported. No catalog endpoint, cache, persistence system, or permission expansion was added.

Label drafts now retain arrays rather than serializing through comma-separated text. The old inputs, parser and helper copy are removed across all three consumers. Exact label strings remain the stored identities; new labels are trimmed and duplicates are not introduced.

Bulk **Keep unchanged**, **Add**, **Replace**, and **Remove** keep their distinct contracts; empty Replace clears labels. The UI respects the existing 40-character and 12-label limits, including preventing an Add operation from silently overflowing an existing card. This does not change the server’s truncation/rejection policy or duplicate the separate backend work in #196810. Bulk Remove is not artificially limited to twelve choices across several cards.

Author simplification kept one label control and existing save owners: net +183 production lines and +219 test/support lines. No universal picker or new SDK surface was introduced.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/c4507bcf-b1bf-464e-a9df-2bc0344bbe58)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/30fbbba6-e989-49d2-9f1b-7bd46a563cc2)

## Evidence

- 76 focused tests passed across six files (Vitest 2.21 s): label choices, existing card editors and bulk actions, page selection, mutations, and live refresh. The new discovery regression fails on main because no label choice exists.
- Real native-plugin assets built by the production plugin builder were loaded in the actual Control UI shell with synthetic Gateway fixtures. Chromium proof selects an existing label with Space, applies it, asserts the exact workboard.cards.update payload, reloads, and confirms the saved selection in the inline editor. Search, Escape/focus return, and an emulated 400×800 viewport also pass (5.43 s scenario).
- Regression coverage includes Add/Replace/Remove payloads, empty Replace, board scoping, unresolved saved choices, comma-bearing and new labels, save/reopen, template reapplication, partial bulk retry, failed inline saves, light dismissal, and permission/archive transitions. No live card or external system was modified.
- Plugin browser typecheck, scoped lint (with tracked-scope and SDK string-style advisories), i18n verification, controller guard, both plugin import-boundary checks, formatting, and all three line/test ratchets pass. No baseline or allocation was raised. The plugin was built and exercised; the unchanged core UI bundle and broad hosted CI were not rerun for this plugin-only change.
- Before source: main at 84579cbdcc6373edf365d459b07e8d088e372f97. Before/after use matching synthetic cards, 1100×1000 and light theme. Main capture uses the existing bulk edit entry point: select a card → Edit properties → Add labels. Narrow proof is an emulated viewport, not a physical device.
- Initial ad-hoc Vite capture did not satisfy the plugin’s same-origin/build identity contract. It was replaced by the repository’s canonical same-origin E2E server and native-plugin fixture, without changing or disabling production checks.
- WebKit and physical/native hosts are unverified. Full-diff author review and simplification completed; no independent agent was delegated. No merge, auto-merge or deployment is requested.

## User Impact

The inventory result is already filtered by the current query, type and—in Claims—assertion origin. An empty filtered result does not mean the store is empty. prs.title: fix(swabble): transcript history ignores transcripts.maxEntries
prs.body:
Closes #194843

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `transcripts.log` keeps 100 entries no matter what `transcripts.maxEntries` is set to.

## User Impact

User impact: swabble keeps at most `transcripts.maxEntries` transcripts (default 50), as the README documents.

## Why This Change Was Made

`TranscriptsStore` had a hard-coded `limit = 100`. `serve` now passes the configured limit to `append`. The store also takes an optional file URL so it can be tested without touching `~/Library`.

## Evidence

- New `TranscriptsStoreTests.testAppendKeepsConfiguredNumberOfEntries` checks the in-memory entries, the file on disk, and a reload.
  - It fails when the old fixed cap of 100 is restored.
  - It passes with the fix.
- `swift test --package-path apps/swabble`: 13 passed, 0 failed (macOS 26, Swift 6.4.2).
- `apps/swabble/scripts/lint.sh` (SwiftLint strict): 0 violations. SwiftFormat lint: clean.


**Behavior proof.** Live speech can't be captured in a headless shell. Instead, a throwaway (uncommitted) harness fed 8 `"clawd phrase N"` segments through `ServeCommand.consumeTranscripts`, the same loop `serve` runs, with `transcripts.maxEntries = 5`. The real `~/Library/Application Support/swabble/transcripts.log` lived under a temp home (`CFFIXED_USER_HOME`). The shipped `swabble tail-log` then read it back in a new process:

```
## main (before)
transcripts.log lines on disk: 8
$ swabble tail-log
phrase 1 … phrase 8

## this PR (after)
transcripts.log lines on disk: 5
$ swabble tail-log
phrase 4
phrase 5
phrase 6
phrase 7
phrase 8
```

**Existing data compatibility:** the log format (newline-separated text) is unchanged. A 100-entry `transcripts.log` from an older build loads, and the next append trims it to the newest `maxEntries`:

```
seeded transcripts.log with 100 lines from an older build
serve loop fed 8 wake phrases (maxEntries=5)
transcripts.log lines on disk: 5
$ swabble tail-log   # new process
phrase 4 … phrase 8
```


**Upgrade from the v2026.11.1 release, with existing config and history.**
- A `config.json` is created by the release binary and customized.
- History is written by the release's own `serve` transcript loop.
- This branch then loads the same `config.json` through `ConfigLoader.load` and appends through the same loop.
- The shipped `tail-log` reads the result back in a new process.

```
## v2026.11.1
$ swabble-v2026.11.1 setup --config config.json
# customized: wake.word=robot, transcripts.maxEntries=5, hook.command=/bin/echo
serve loop (config loaded from config.json) fed 8 "robot release phrase N" segments
transcripts.log lines: 8   (release ignores maxEntries=5)

## upgrade to this PR (same config.json + transcripts.log)
serve loop (config loaded from config.json) fed 3 "robot pr phrase N" segments
transcripts.log lines: 5
$ swabble-pr tail-log   # new process
release phrase 7
release phrase 8
pr phrase 1
pr phrase 2
pr phrase 3
config.json sha eb04c83bdeffc974 -> eb04c83bdeffc974 ; wake.word/maxEntries/hook.command: robot 5 /bin/echo
```

**Gap:** the shipped `swabble serve` cannot run live microphone input here. In a non-interactive shell, its Speech.framework pipeline aborts on authorization (`Abort trap: 6`) before any audio arrives, on `main` and this branch alike. So the speech-to-segment step is replaced by the synthetic segments above. Everything after it (config load, wake gating, the `serve` consumer, the on-disk log, CLI readback) is the shipped code.

The saved profile and its approval/retry behavior keep their existing owner; no authentication or approval policy changes are introduced.

prs.title: fix: keep message declarations when a turn cannot send
prs.body:
Related: #166969, #167710. Shared embedded-factory follow-up to native-Codex-specific #93813; this does not close either issue's full scope.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: temporarily disabling message execution removes its declaration from the shared embedded tool factory, changing the prompt/tool surface within the same conversation.

## User Impact

A turn can refuse message execution without removing the session's message declaration. The refusal remains non-callable and is excluded from exported/callable capability snapshots; other existing visibility policies remain in force. No configuration migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing execution gate instead of conditionally skipping message construction. Carry denied-execution metadata even without an availability binding, and preserve the current turn's refusal behind the offered session declaration. Owner/requester denials keep precedence. This separates stable declarations from current-turn authority without adding another policy owner or persistent state.

Simplification: reuse the existing factory, execution gate and availability metadata. Growth is necessary to retain refusals across declaration projection: production +48/-31 lines, tests +72/-0, plus a separate 72-line regression allocation; the shared test scalar is unchanged.

## Evidence

[Exact successful proof job](https://github.com/ensignwesley/openclaw/actions/runs/42094131686/job/127479618360): base `bf0d53d5c17a666f34cfc3ef1671e726be235a9a`, [product `e11ba635`](https://github.com/ensignwesley/openclaw/commit/e11ba635a8dcbe9191beecd646ff0d0ae556a093), proof driver `cf5e419df180143a8e06699a8b1079cecf60ffe1`. This refreshed proof retains the base's current-owner authority guard and adds its denied-gateway interaction regression; it supersedes the older-base proof.

| Production types | Passed full `tsgo:core` graph |
| Changed-test types | Passed both changed suites plus Gateway diagnostic |
| Scoped lint | Passed, zero warnings/errors |
| Exact formatting | All six matched TypeScript files passed |
| Built isolated Gateway | Three persistent-session provider requests/responses, one diagnostic test passed, joined cleanup |

Minimized excerpts from the actual captured RPCs (generated run/session IDs and unrelated fields omitted, not replaced with alleged captured values):

```json
{"method":"agent","params":{"disableMessageTool":false,"deliver":false,"message":"LANE_E1_TURN_1"},"result":{"status":"ok","summary":"completed"}}
{"method":"agent","params":{"disableMessageTool":true,"deliver":false,"message":"LANE_E1_TURN_2"},"result":{"status":"ok","summary":"completed"}}
```


Actual SSE response excerpts:

```text

data: {"type":"response.output_text.done","item_id":"e1_message_2","output_index":0,"content_index":0,"text":"LANE_E1_COMPLETE_2"}
```

prs.title: feat: recommend agent tasks during template setup and new chats
prs.body:
Related: #196643

## What Problem This Solves

Template authors can describe an agent, but users have no way to choose a first task during installation. New chats also show generic suggestions for purpose-built agents.

## User Impact

Agent authors can set an optional description and up to three recommended prompts. Users can select a prompt when adding a Template or in a new chat with the installed agent.

## Why This Change Was Made

Template Add carries the selection through the existing consent flow. The Gateway finishes installation, seeds `BOOTSTRAP.md`, and starts an opening turn before releasing the chat. The opening turn instructs the agent to ask any setup questions and wait for answers before addressing the selected task. The model handles that sequence through instructions in the opening turn. If the opening fails, the user keeps the installed agent and can continue in its chat.

## Evidence

- Published as `179a92f139d2`, imported from `f40feacd8`; all 47 feature paths match that handoff byte-for-byte. Newer upstream main changes are preserved (prepared base `f67c2396`).

prs.body:
Fixes #199216

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes bundled hooks silently disappearing when update runtime retention hard-links their installed files.

## User Impact

Bundled hooks remain discoverable after runtime retention. Rejected hook files now produce a warning naming the file and cause; hard-link warnings explain how to recover.

Already-affected files are not rewritten in place. A successful npm package replacement supplies fresh hook files, and the fixed updater preserves their independent inodes on later retention. If files remain linked, replace them with independent copies or reinstall OpenClaw with the owning package manager, then restart the Gateway. Discovery now gives that recovery guidance, so no separate Doctor mutation is added. The full upgrade recovery path remains unverified because remote capacity was unavailable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing independent-inode owner to protect `HOOK.md` and all adjacent handler candidates, so retention copies them. Keep strict hook hard-link rejection intact. Forward rejected opens to discovery's existing warning callback, leaving missing optional package manifests and handler candidates quiet.

Pr-simplify kept the existing classifier and callback; no new owner, repair state, config, schema, or protocol. Removed incidental callback-formatting churn. Net change against the base: +29 production lines and +36 test lines, needed for classification, diagnostics, and boundary regression proof.

## Evidence

- Red on base `18a62d6ff93428f15b0801ba5efe4ef0452a8f15`: retention made all four fixture hooks undiscoverable; metadata rejection emitted no warning and handler rejection lacked the rejected filename.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Automation delivery requires users to type channel account IDs, even though the page already has a channel-scoped inventory with recognizable account names; the primary account field is also hidden under Advanced.

## User Impact

Users can search and choose a named **Sending account** beside the delivery channel, and choose an **Alert account** from the failure-alert channel’s separate inventory. Saved IDs remain stable, duplicate names have identifying context, and discovery or save failures do not erase selections or unrelated drafts.

## Why This Change Was Made

One cron-local control uses the existing searchable picker and the shared channel capability. It adds no discovery API, cache, permissions, or per-row fetches. The primary account moves into Delivery, completing the existing channel → account → recipient-suggestions interaction; the old Advanced input is removed.

**Automatic** removes the explicit override and preserves existing route-based account resolution, not a snapshot of the current default. Changing an account invalidates only that route’s previous topic through the existing form owner. Selecting an account does not save: Create/Save remains the commit boundary.

Explicit custom references remain supported because the status inventory is not the schema’s complete allowed-value set. With **Last** as the channel, account entry stays open-ended: there is no single channel-specific catalog, and the UI does not guess a channel from an account name. Loading, failed discovery, unavailable inventory, and an empty known list are distinct states.

Author simplification retained a single control for the two existing account fields and removed their superseded manual paths where a channel catalog exists. prs.title: fix: Knowledge claims interrupted settings changes did not apply
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Knowledge says a store assignment or conversation-access change did not happen when its response is interrupted.

## User Impact

User impact: the error now describes an unconfirmed outcome and directs users to reopen Stores & sharing before retrying. It no longer claims nothing changed when a later read can show the change was saved. Known refusal and successful-save messages remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

A failed response does not establish whether the write committed. The existing owner returns explicit outcomes when it can, but the browser’s catch-all path previously made an unconditional “not changed” claim. Both settings surfaces now preserve that uncertainty without changing writes, permissions, retries or storage.

Related: #195010 is a broader glossary/localization pass. Its current diff changes these messages to “Couldn’t change … Try again,” so it does not resolve this outcome distinction.

## Evidence

- Reproduced both paths through the real built Knowledge plugin on main at 18a62d6ff93428f15b0801ba5efe4ef0452a8f15: select a shared store or change conversation access, receive an interrupted response, then reopen Stores & sharing. The synthetic Gateway’s readback confirms that the change applied, despite the original “not changed” message.
- Both committed browser regressions fail on the original copy and pass with the correction. They exercise the existing readback control and verify exactly one mutation, not a retry. Five existing Knowledge UI tests also pass.
- Source inspection confirms that successful assignment and access writes can be followed by a failed snapshot read, and the feature client can throw for an interrupted or invalid response. No new backend outcome or recovery mechanism was introduced.
- Focused lint, browser/E2E typechecks, i18n baseline/verification, formatting and diff checks passed. No broad local test suite or live Knowledge configuration change was performed.

### Before

![Before: an interrupted assignment reply claims nothing changed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d80d7a59-7802-4959-ac50-b0da552318e1)

### After

![After: Knowledge preserves uncertainty and names the readback step](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fc8977f3-ff2c-4376-bbe9-e06201a97b3c)

<details>
<summary>Conversation-access feedback</summary>

Before:

After:

</details>

Real built app and native plugin components; synthetic agent, store, conversation and Gateway replies; emulated 1280 × 1000 viewport. The applied-write/lost-response condition is simulated at the Gateway boundary. No live store assignment or access grant was changed.

prs.title: perf(agents): avoid token-pressure match allocations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Estimating context pressure for long, JSON-heavy conversations creates temporary arrays and strings for every lexical match, adding avoidable allocation before model requests and compaction.

## User Impact

Token-pressure estimates remain identical. The synthetic long-history workload allocates 99.07% less during estimation, with a measured 3.02% CPU increase (0.101 ms/request). No configuration, schema, provider-request, or admission behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing regex's lexical precedence, but use `test()` and `lastIndex` to find runs and count their contribution without materializing match arrays or substrings. Numeric word boundaries, encoded-run thresholds, CJK weights, and left-to-right floating-point rounding stay intact. Both old match-array paths disappear.

Frozen messages and content arrays already reuse estimates through their existing owner. No new cache is needed: a 360-message frozen history incurs 600 initial string estimates and zero history rescans on subsequent requests; the pending prompt still incurs one scan. Mutable histories incur 600 history string estimates/request (12,000 over 20 requests). The earlier reuse fix (#190952) is included in the allocation-attribution build `ef4a3c8b3abc28916f202cbf60a5c94773b08ba2`; this addresses its residual scanner cost.

Runtime production delta: **+42 LOC (51 added, 9 removed)**. The growth preserves the existing lexical and rounding contract while recovering match boundaries without allocated results. Test delta: +43 lines, with an exact allocation record. Benchmark tooling is separate from runtime code (+176 lines); the exact non-test diff is +220 lines including the two-line test allocation record. Author simplification pass completed; no new state/cache owner, export, compatibility path, or caller change.

## Evidence

Baseline: `b7bc6c4102101e0f29b4a33edc871f225d1010a4`. Local Node 26.12.1 / macOS arm64. Real `createFreshLlmBoundaryTokenEstimator` entry point, 360 messages including 120 JSON tool results, assistant tool calls, multilingual text, numeric groups, and encoded identifiers; 228,561 string characters estimated/request. Warmup/setup excluded. Five alternating base/candidate pairs, **2,000 requests/arm/pair**: 10,000 requests/side for timing and another 10,000/side for allocation. Timing is unprofiled; allocation is a separate 16 KiB sampled pass retaining minor/major-collected samples. Host one-minute load across arms: 12.86–20.02.

| Owner metric (mean) | Base | Candidate | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Sampled allocation/request | 2,284,986 B | 21,332 B | −99.07% |
| Allocation at 120 requests/min (projection) | 261.50 MiB/min | 2.44 MiB/min | −259.06 MiB/min |
| Unprofiled process CPU/request | 3.338 ms | 3.439 ms | +0.101 ms / +3.02% |
| Wall time/request | 3.364 ms | 3.679 ms | +0.315 ms / +9.37% |
| Token estimate | 123,002 | 123,002 | identical |

Allocation/request ranges: base 2,282,382–2,287,915 B; candidate 20,639–21,813 B. CPU/request ranges: base 3.301–3.381 ms; candidate 3.400–3.494 ms. All five allocation pairs improve by >99%; paired CPU changes range +1.01% to +4.98%. This is an allocation improvement with a small CPU tradeoff, not a CPU speedup. Wall timings are sensitive to host scheduling; all observations are retained.

Acceptance: exact estimates, allocation below 100,000 B/request, and no material adverse result under the campaign's paired thresholds. The committed benchmark's allocation regression fails on baseline at **2,279,668 B/request** and passes on candidate at **22,456 B/request** (1,000 requests each):

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/token-pressure-scan-measure.mjs \
  --mode allocation --iterations 1000 --max-bytes-per-turn 100000
# Add --scanner /absolute/pinned/cjk-chars.ts to test the baseline owner.
# Use --mode timing --iterations 2000 for CPU; --mode counts --iterations 20 [--frozen] for reuse.
```

Correctness: 110,000 differential estimates match the old scanner across seeded random strings, malformed Unicode, lexical boundaries, fractional ratios, and non-finite ratios. The committed golden corpus preserves 14,420 exact results (2,060 strings × seven ratios). Existing context-pressure and compaction-request tests pass: **47 tests across three files**, 6.75 s wrapper time; the new corpus takes 47 ms. Allocation regression is a manual benchmark, not a timing-sensitive CI assertion.

Validation: focused tests above; `pnpm tsgo:test:root`; package test typecheck; changed-file lint and oxfmt; export-name collision guard; eager-import/source-closure and prompt-prefix checks. Exact-head [CI run 43644371783](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43644371783) completed on head `ae4bae6d97015c31efe92c71303e88b093208ffe`: **97 successful jobs, four failing workload jobs plus the aggregate CI gate, and 23 skipped jobs**. The confirmed inherited failure is: `checks-node-compact-small-3-1` → two `ci-node-test-plan.test.ts` cases, “gates Gateway method workers without changing complete coverage” (`hybrid`, `github`). Both fail identically on PR head `ae4bae6d97015c31efe92c71303e88b093208ffe` and unchanged main parent `6ee07a446e00`: 591 actual entries versus 590 expected, with the extra `test/plugins/deep-research-recovery.gateway.test.ts`. Focused reproduction on each revision: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/ci-node-test-plan.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'gates Gateway method workers without changing complete coverage'`; head 5.07 s, base 3.36 s, both exit 1 with the same two failures. No CI rerun or unrelated repair is included.

Additional CI failure classification:

- `checks-ui (2/3)`: `plugins-page.icons.test.ts` (late publisher enrichment, expected one fetch, got zero) and `chat-header-session-menu.test.ts` (reopening focus, expected a row, got null). Both full files pass **five runs on head and five on unchanged main parent**, 26 tests/run. They do not call `estimateStringTokenPressure`; classified as unrelated flakes under the lane rule, not repaired or rerun in CI.
- `checks-ui-e2e (4/7)`: four `activity-polish.e2e.test.ts` image-preview assertions, expected four images, got zero. **Baseline attribution remains unproven**. An inspected earlier main run had different E2E failures, so it is not offered as matching evidence.
- `checks-ui-e2e (5/7)`: `route-asset-requests.e2e.test.ts` times out in `beforeAll` after 180 seconds; all four test cases are skipped. This is an unclassified setup failure, not a product assertion verdict.

The unchanged main-parent CI run skipped UI jobs and published no reusable build artifact. No local UI build or E2E campaign was launched beyond the narrow unit-file reproductions under the assigned compute limits. **Exact-head CI is not green; the two UI E2E failures remain explicit handoff gaps.** The separate report-only iOS Periphery job was still running at handoff. The PR remains ready and unmerged for maintainer review; no CI reruns or merge were performed.
 Independent Codex review is owned by the maintainer session before merge.

Scope/gaps: no new Gateway load test, production load, or Team mutation. This follows the requested owner-only fast path for removal of transient work; no whole-Gateway CPU, GC, latency, RSS/heap, or production bytes/min improvement is claimed. The per-minute row is a workload-rate projection, not an observed Gateway rate. No deployment or merge is part of this handoff.

## What Problem This Solves

The geolocation gzip overflow regression still passed when the decompression ceiling was removed, because an MMDB parse failure satisfied its URL-only assertion.

## Why This Change Was Made

Require the limit-specific rejection message preserved by `store.load()`, alongside the source URL. Reduce the decoded fixture from 700 MiB to 512 MiB + 1 byte, crossing the same production ceiling. No production edits, new exports, mocks, or injected limits.

## Evidence

| Named-file command wall | 3.949 s | 3.624 s | 0.325 s |

prs.title: feat(message): let operators confine group-turn sends to the current conversation
prs.body:
Related: #190557

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a group turn's `message` send can reach the owner's DM or another chat when the operator wants group turns kept in their own conversation, because the existing `crossContext` switches confine every kind of turn or none.

## User Impact

User impact: existing configs behave exactly as on main; no default changes. An operator who sets `tools.message.crossContext.confineChatTypes: ["group", "channel"]`, globally or per agent, gets group and channel turns that can only send to their own conversation. Any other target, on the same provider or another one, fails with `message_cross_context_denied` before a transport call. DM turns keep their current permissions. Separately, under the existing `allowWithinProvider: false`, a Telegram forum-topic send or poll that names the chat id with the current topic's `threadId`, or inherits it, is no longer denied. Other actions from a topic turn, such as renaming a topic, still have to name the current topic, as on main. Two deliberate tightenings apply under `allowWithinProvider: false`, or when group turns are confined. A turn in a Telegram forum topic can no longer create a forum topic in that chat, even through its own topic target, which main allows; the new topic is a sibling conversation in the base chat, and a turn bound to the chat itself still can. Telegram topic creation and topic edits that name another chat through `chatId`, `chat_id` or `channel_id` are denied. In every mode, a target that disagrees with one of those fields is refused as conflicting input. A numeric `target`, `to` or `channelId` is now read as its string, so it follows the same rules as the string: with a target the target wins, and alone it is the destination the check judges. Before, a numeric `channelId` skipped the check and Telegram acted on it, and a numeric `to` or `target` was dropped for the current conversation. A number that is not a safe integer is refused.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision (4b90fc67b80) flipped the shipped `allowWithinProvider` default to deny. That was the wrong shape. It reversed a deliberate default (#149875, #150157), it broke the required-delivery and context-isolation fixtures, and it changed bound broadcasts. My claim in the old body that broadcasts were exempt was wrong: child sends carry `toolContext` into the same check. Review also found a real matcher bug: the same-provider check ignored `threadId`, so a same-topic Telegram send could be denied.

This revision keeps the default and adds an opt-in inside the existing owner, `enforceCrossContextPolicy`:

- `confineChatTypes` keys on the conversation kind the host reports for the turn (`toolContext.currentChatType`). A listed kind may only target its own conversation; this overrides both `allowWithinProvider` and `allowAcrossProviders`. Unlisted kinds, and turns with no reported kind, keep those flags. A `POST /tools/invoke` call bound by the conversation headers reports the bound target's kind, so it is confined like a turn from that conversation. A per-agent list replaces the global one through the existing per-agent merge; `[]` lifts it.
- Broadcast child sends already go through this check, so a confined broadcast delivers the current conversation and reports a denial for every other target. There is no runner change.
- When same-provider sends are restricted, the check resolves the thread the send will actually use, with the same `resolveAndApplyOutboundThreadId` that delivery uses (on a copy of the params), and names the destination with the channel's own `resolveCurrentChannelId`. Policy and delivery now judge the same destination. Only `send` and `poll` are judged by that thread alone, because the runner delivers them into it. Other guarded actions only hand the thread to the plugin, so they are judged on their requested target as on main, and a thread they carry can only narrow that. `topic-create` must also name the current conversation through its parent chat, resolved with the channel's own conversation grammar (core's `resolveSessionConversation`, which asks `messaging.resolveSessionConversation`), because Telegram creates the topic in the base chat whatever topic or thread the request names. Telegram declares `chatId`, `chat_id` and `channel_id` as delivery-target aliases for `topic-create` and `topic-edit`, because its handler takes the chat from them ahead of the target. Normalization therefore canonicalizes them before the check, the same way the thread spellings are folded. Normalization also stringifies exact integer values of `target`, `to` and `channelId` before folding them: Telegram's chat reader accepts numbers, while the fold and the check read only strings.
  - When a Telegram target's encoded topic and an explicit `threadId` disagree, the check follows Telegram's delivery precedence: the explicit thread wins. Telegram's `resolveCurrentChannelId` now goes through `formatTelegramDeliveryTarget`, the helper Telegram already uses to name a delivered send (moved unchanged into `targets.ts`).
  - The shared param readers accept each key's snake_case form, and Telegram's handler reads `messageThreadId` or `message_thread_id` before `threadId` or `thread_id`. Action normalization now folds every one of those four spellings into one string `threadId` before any check, including a numeric `threadId`, which core's string reader would otherwise skip. Values that disagree are refused, and so is any value alongside an explicit `threadId: null`. On any channel, an action carrying only an alias, or a numeric `threadId`, gets that value as its string `threadId`.

What changed since `1cb5e029db3` (2026-11-10): `POST /tools/invoke` now reports the kind of the conversation its headers bind it to, so `confineChatTypes` applies to header-bound direct calls as it does to a turn from that conversation (`9aadc2bbc5c`). The Bot API traces at `1cb5e029db3` showed the gap: with only `confineChatTypes: ["group"]` set and the topic-A headers, all nine direct calls were delivered, including a `sendMessage` to the owner DM and `editForumTopic` and `createForumTopic` on it. `src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts` now sets `currentChatType` on the direct-invocation surface from the bound target, with the resolver outbound target resolution already uses, `inferChatTypeFromTarget` (now exported from `src/infra/outbound/targets.ts`; for Telegram it asks the plugin's `parseTelegramTarget`). Calls without the headers, the RPC `tools.invoke` and the MCP loopback surface are unchanged. `src/gateway/tool-resolution.direct-invoke-confinement.test.ts` fails on `1cb5e029db3` (`promise resolved "{ content: [ { …(2) } ], …(1) }" instead of rejecting` for a sibling-topic send from a header-bound call) and passes on this head; `92aee940aa8` raises the test-line allocation by its 62 lines.

pr-simplify: compared with the first revision, the default flip and its three default-denial tests are gone. No new plugin API, no runner or broadcast changes. Every remaining test group fails on a named control (below). The remaining growth is one config field (4 schema paths), the denial reason text, thread-aware matching, the tests (493 net test lines, allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/message-cross-context-confine-chat-types.txt`), and one qa-lab scenario. prs.title: fix(auto-reply): exec completions keep the requester's current sender and DM tool policy
prs.body:
Closes #177510

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a background command's completion turn loses `exec` and `process` when the sender who started it is allowed only by their own `toolsBySender` entry and the `"*"` entry denies those tools.

## User Impact

User impact: with a `toolsBySender` wildcard deny, a sender allowed by their own entry can let a background command finish its task on the completion turn, without sending another message. Guests stay denied, and changing that sender's entry, or denying the tool for the conversation they wrote in (a Telegram DM entry under `channels.telegram.direct.<chat>`, including `toolsBySender` keyed on their id, username or name, or a Discord guild or channel entry under `channels.discord.guilds.<guild>`), before the completion runs takes the tool away.

## Why This Change Was Made

A completion turn is built without a sender, so requester policy fell to the `"*"` entry. #185476 restored the sender only for command owners (`commands.ownerAllowFrom`); a sender allowed only through `toolsBySender` was never restored.

My first revisions restored too little. Review found four real gaps, all fixed:

- Without the conversation id, `resolveRequesterConversationToolPolicy` skips the channel's `security.resolveDirectToolPolicy`, so an unchanged sender entry escaped a DM-level deny. #185476's owner completions had the same gap.
- Without the sender's username and name, Telegram's `resolveTelegramDirectToolPolicy` missed a DM `toolsBySender` entry keyed `username:` or `name:`, fell back to the DM's unrestricted tools, and the requester's global id entry then allowed exec.
- Without the requester's group space and channel name, a completion in a Discord guild channel resolved group policy with no guild, so `resolveDiscordGuildKey` found no guild entry, a guild or channel deny added after launch was missed, and the requester's global id entry allowed exec.
- `combineSessionEventTargetsForHost` compared only command-owner requesters, so targets from two `toolsBySender`-only requesters could share a batch that restores only the first one.

What the PR does now:

- The session-event target keeps the requester's channel, account, sender id, E164, username, display name, group space (a Discord guild), group channel name, chat type and conversation id, taken from the host-owned tool caller. The group id comes from the completion's own route, which is the requester's conversation.
- The completion turn restores `SenderId`, `SenderE164`, `SenderUsername`, `SenderName`, `GroupSpace`, `GroupChannel` and `ChatId`, but only on the requester's own channel account and only when the turn has the requester's conversation type. A completion routed to another chat stays senderless and gets the `"*"` policy.
- The restore grants nothing by itself: a non-owner's `senderIsOwner` stays `false`, and owner-only effects still recheck at use.
- A batch refuses targets whose retained requester differs in any of those fields.
- Only exec completions and node `system.run` events retain a requester. Subagent announces, cron, heartbeats, session-state notices and adopted durable processes do not, so their authority is unchanged.
- Behavior change for #185476: an owner's sender is restored only when the chat types match; before, a matching channel and account was enough. Where they differ, the owner-effect check now fails closed.

## Evidence

Head `6fbcf9eae1e` (main `586f576` merged in), macOS arm64. Correction: the QA Lab flow and the test files in this section ran on the local default runtime, which since #172625 is OpenClaw's pinned Bun, not Node 26.12.1 as this line said. Node re-run under "Also on this head".

prs.title: fix(android): distinguish null from text in SMS and call-log commands
prs.body:
Fixes #199095

## What Problem This Solves

Android SMS and call-log commands treat JSON `null` as the literal text `"null"`.
A null SMS message or recipient passes required-field validation, and optional
null search fields become unintended filters.

## User Impact

Invalid send requests are rejected before carrier submission. Optional null
filters behave as omitted; the actual string `"null"` remains searchable text
and a valid message body.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing shared `parseJsonString` helper for the seven affected string
fields. It distinguishes JSON null from text while preserving existing trimming
and primitive conversion. Command authorization, Android permissions, numeric
filters and result formats stay at their existing owners.

## Evidence

The existing Android suites run the production SMS send method against its
carrier shadow, the SMS query parser, and call-log dispatch with its recording
data source. Four regressions fail on base and pass with this change:

- Null SMS body is rejected before submission.
- Null recipient is rejected before submission.
- Null SMS text filters remain absent.
- Null call-log text filters remain absent.

All 116 focused tests pass after the fix (112 pass on base). Controls include
literal `"null"` text, missing fields, permissions, multipart segmentation,
query defaults and pagination. ThirdParty source/test Kotlin lint and Android
lint pass. Executed on macOS arm64/JDK 21 with Robolectric 4.17; the SMS send
suite uses API 35. No real carrier or personal records were used.

```sh
cd apps/android
./gradlew :app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest \
  --tests ai.openclaw.app.node.SmsSendTest \
  --tests ai.openclaw.app.node.SmsManagerTest \
  --tests ai.openclaw.app.node.CallLogHandlerTest
./gradlew :app:ktlintThirdPartySourceSetCheck \
  :app:ktlintTestThirdPartySourceSetCheck :app:lintThirdPartyDebug
```

### Independent review focus

For a paired ThirdParty Android node, compare omitted and null SMS/call-log
filters against disposable records. Null required send fields should return
`INVALID_REQUEST` without carrier submission. The automated suite already
checks that the literal string remains intact; normal SMS submission can be
confirmed separately with a controlled recipient.
