## Problem

Related: #198259. When commands.allowFrom legitimately rejects a password-authenticated Control UI caller without a matching verified sender identity, plain-text /status previously vanished without a reply.

## Change

Internal WebChat command denials now return a visible refusal with an actionable next step: “Ask your Gateway administrator for command access.” The native-command branch remains first and preserves its existing wording. External /status text and native wrappers retain their existing silence. This changes feedback only: operator.admin does not bypass commands.allowFrom, and verified identity, authorization checks, owner attribution, and scopes are unchanged.

The correction also updates the /learn undo and /loop regressions to expect the visible refusal while retaining no-effect assertions.

## Current corrected candidate

Signed candidate: 683d6c24b54059a95ecfac1354050ea480142ec1. It adds a one-line persisted Workshop /learn undo consumer correction to bddd6464b82dfbefff03179a40470bddf89447f1; earlier corrections fixed the /loop expectation and denial-table type inference. Production remains identical to 66dbaeef42542e6f22616cb20d621c39a0bebdab; baseline remains d43de8d733674c942c8eb7bfb7333a30de4f910f.

- Exact current Workshop correction: all 34 integration tests passed under Node 24 in secretless, network-disabled Podman. Messaging typecheck, targeted type-aware lint (zero warnings/errors), formatting and whitespace passed. Independent review of blob 4fd157b30afd3bdc445c0652fa44bfd8e7e6e5e0 is READY with no findings. The persisted feed and both skill-file no-effect assertions remain unchanged. Initial dependency/cache setup failures occurred before meaningful testing; the corrected isolated setup passed.
- Previous exact loop correction: 9 tests passed; messaging typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting and whitespace passed. The no-rewrite assertion and owner-only denial remain intact. Independent exact-blob review READY, no findings.
- Previous 3817b584: 26 commands-info tests and messaging typecheck passed. These repeat prior coverage, not additional distinct tests.
- Previous 66dbaeef: four focused suites / 70 tests and full build passed (2m 19.6s). Budget warnings are not performance qualification.
- Full-delta and subsequent test-only correction reviews retained. Neither old-head results nor pending/skipped checks establish current-head broad green CI.

## Current guidance browser proof

One real-Gateway Chromium scenario passed in a secretless, network-disabled Podman container. It uses real browser pairing, a synthetic session, a nonmatching commands.allowFrom identity, and /status entered through the composer. The screenshot below visibly includes the administrator-guidance sentence. No cloud model was contacted. The image was inspected and contains synthetic content only.

Provenance: archived source and compiled Gateway/UI from 66dbaeef; all subsequent published corrections through 683d6c24 change tests only, so production source is identical. Supplemental browser harness and package build artifacts were staged separately. prs.title: fix(exec): adopted durable commands claim no exit wake after a Gateway restart
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after a Gateway restart, a still-running `durable: true` background command claims it will not wake the conversation, even though its exit does wake it. `process poll` says "Automatic completion wake is unavailable", so the agent keeps polling the command, and the Control UI hides the **Waiting on …** card for it.

## User Impact

User impact: after a restart, a durable waiter reports its exit wake correctly. An agent asked to check on it looks once and ends its turn, then the exit wakes the conversation. The Control UI shows the **Waiting on …** card for the adopted command again.

## Why This Change Was Made

Startup adoption prepared the wake destination only when the adopted process exited, so until then nothing reported a wake. Adoption now prepares it once under the session's current authority, with the same eligibility rules as before: reset, archived, incognito, subagent and cron sessions, and notifications that are turned off, still get no wake. The exit path prepares it again, so a session reset or a config change made after adoption still applies. Docs describe the adopted wake in poll and the Control UI.

## Evidence

Real-agent E2E on an isolated source Gateway (`openai/gpt-6-astra`, 6 concurrent conversations per arm). Each conversation runs one `durable: true` waiter for a fake CI that turns green about 300 s later, then ends its turn. About 60 s later the Gateway gets SIGTERM and a new Gateway starts on the same state. 20 s after restart, the harness reads `sessions.processes.list` (the Control UI card's source) and then sends each conversation "Quick check-in: the Gateway just restarted. Is your CI wait still running?".

| Arm | Waiter adopted, `wakesSession: true` | `process poll` calls after restart | Polls beyond the first status check | Finished by the exit wake | Correct final answer | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| base (`10159aefda9c`) | 0/6 | 77 | 71 | 0/6 (poll loop collected it) | 6/6 | $6.49 |
| fix | **6/6** | 6 | **0** | **6/6** | 6/6 | $4.35 |

<details><summary>Public trace, trial 2, base vs fix (paths redacted)</summary>

Base: the check-in poll says no wake is available, so the agent polls the waiter until it exits.
```
+159s USER: Quick check-in: the Gateway just restarted. Is your CI wait still running?
+165s process {"action": "poll", "timeout": 0}
+165s   -> PR #4242: 4 checks pending, 11 passed Process still running. Automatic completion wake is unavailable after ending this turn. …
+171s reply: Yes—the original durable waiter survived the restart and is still running. …
+171s process {"action": "poll", "timeout": 30000}
+201s   -> (no new output) Process still running. Automatic completion wake is unavailable after ending this turn. …
… 4 more 30 s polls …
+341s   -> PR #4242: all 15 checks passed. Summary: build-2-… green … Process exited with code 0.
+344s reply: PR #4242 is ready—all 15 checks passed. …
```

Fix: one status check, the turn ends, and the exit wakes the conversation.
```
+177s USER: Quick check-in: the Gateway just restarted. Is your CI wait still running?
+181s process {"action": "poll", "timeout": 0}
+181s   -> PR #4242: 4 checks pending, 11 passed …
+187s reply: Yes—the original durable CI wait survived the restart and is still running. …
+328s USER: Exec completed (nimble-r, code 0, 4m32s): PR #4242: … all 15 checks passed …
+334s reply: PR #4242 is ready—all 15 checks passed. …
```
</details>

- Regression: the durable adoption test now arms the exit wake, re-adopts a still-running unit, and checks that `hasExitWake` is true and `process poll` does not say the wake is unavailable. It fails on the base and passes with the fix. `bash-process-durable-notify.test.ts` passes unchanged.
- `pnpm check:changed` passes (typecheck lanes, lint, SQLite worker ratchet, dead-export scan).
- Full build with declarations, packed tarball installed into a clean prefix: `openclaw --version` and `gateway --help` run, and the packed durable adoption contains the fix.
- Not captured: a Control UI screenshot. The card code is unchanged; its data source (`sessions.processes.list` `wakesSession`) is shown above for every trial.

prs.title: fix(ios): chat reconnects load the transcript before refreshing catalogs
prs.body:
Closes #194223 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: after a reconnect on a slow or flapping connection, iOS chat repeats its model and capability catalog requests on every reconnect, ahead of the conversation history, so the transcript has to share a slow link with them. ## User Impact User impact: when iOS chat reconnects, the conversation history now loads before the model and capability catalogs are refreshed. macOS keeps the same transcript and draft behavior; this change does not guarantee history-first ordering for all macOS traffic, and no latency improvement is claimed. ## Why This Change Was Made After a reconnect, native chat can compete with model and capability catalogs while recovering its transcript. This change delays the recovery-owned catalog refreshes until history settles and coalesces overlapping recoveries. Stale state is still invalidated immediately, and session metadata needed by queued sends remains immediate. The reviewed correction by @vyctorbrzezowski (`f211a4b6c1d`) fixes two defects in the deferred path: a catalog request could target the previous conversation, and catalogs could overtake an overlapping iOS bootstrap history read. It now waits for an overlapping iOS bootstrap to finish and verifies that the captured conversation is still current before refreshing catalogs. This prevents a request for the previous agent and addresses the persistent history timeout reproduced during review. First-connect setup, live question events, cancellation, and progress-card recovery are preserved. ## Evidence ### Verified behavior Real native apps, isolated Gateway, and persisted model-generated conversations: | Scenario | Before | Corrected PR | | --- | --- | --- | | iOS: repeated cuts, 8 KiB/s downstream | 7,091 model-response bytes before the first history response on all 4 observed history-bearing connections | 0 on both observed history-bearing connections in each of 2 repetitions | | iOS: overlapping bootstrap after reconnect | Earlier PR candidate reproduced a persistent timeout from a clean start | Both final repetitions recovered without Retry or dismissing the error | | macOS native Quick Chat: 2 cuts per build | Messages and editable draft preserved | Same messages and editable draft preserved; 2 successful history reloads | Interrupted connections are excluded from the history-bearing counts. These measurements establish ordering, not a normalized request-count or latency improvement. macOS has a separate catalog loader; this change does not guarantee history-first ordering for all macOS traffic. Four focused tests and 42 related lifecycle/outbox/reaction checks passed. Both new regression cases fail on their respective earlier code and pass with the correction. Normal iOS/Watch and macOS builds passed; independent review found no actionable P0–P2 issue. These controlled-transport tests support, but do not replace, the native recordings. ### Native recordings All videos retain their complete recorded timeline and original speed. Gray masks cover model labels and adjacent metadata. No application state, Gateway response, or rendering style was injected. #### Timeout found and fixed during review The left image is the earlier corrected candidate, not main. The right is the final repetition after the bootstrap fix. #### iOS: original behavior on main https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c3d12b28-6227-47d5-b850-186355d9bccc #### iOS: final correction, repetition 1 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7d4824ba-4591-401b-9cdc-568064a81204 #### iOS: final correction, repetition 2 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dc1a207c-7e4f-4735-83cc-a14ad6d44544 #### macOS: preservation control These images are not a proposed visual change. The same saved reply and unsent draft remain usable after two network interruptions. Main: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f77dcca5-f494-4fbe-a63b-fbac021a4174 Corrected PR: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5cf819af-f4eb-46cc-a6fe-3779d1791511
Build provenance and limits - Live baseline: `4f61482980507ec61c3436f32a37eac8adabfc2e`. - Corrected PR: `f211a4b6c1da60d50ba6e3dd0d3053c026c1af84`; tested tree `35e8417f8ff722f3d1e78dd9079e85e7357a3314`. - iOS 27.2 Simulator, Xcode 27.2; native macOS Quick Chat in an isolated macOS 26.6.2 VM. - Gateway `04cc8c1e4328b873a3a5791eeecf5d4d213c34db` held constant across each comparison. Later main `74dbd7cc` was source-compared, not rebuilt; relevant Apple source is unchanged. - Response order comes from Gateway logs; request-start estimates subtract server duration with millisecond precision, not packet capture. - First final iOS recording: 85.745 seconds of sparse simulator video during 120 seconds of observation. Repeat: 114.382 seconds plus a final still after the full interval. No padding or acceleration. - Mac recordings: about 57 seconds each, two three-second network interruptions, followed by draft editing. A new send after the interruptions and node-side tools were not covered. - GitHub's full checks are separate from these local results and may still be pending. No merge or auto-merge has been requested.
Earlier contributor evidence: original head 75b5fdd69e4 The evidence below concerns the original head, before the two review corrections. Its transport fixture is supporting evidence, not the real-Gateway recording above. Xcode 27.2 (27B52), Swift 6.4.2, macOS 27.2 (26B123), Apple silicon Mac, 32 cores. Head `75b5fdd69e4` (tree `9abb6dd7fca`); the changed files on the test machine match the commit byte for byte. **Real iOS transport, wire order.** A proof-only harness (not part of this PR) runs in the OpenClaw iOS test host on an iOS 27.2 simulator (iPhone 18 Pro). It drives `OpenClawChatViewModel` through the app's `IOSGatewayChatTransport` and `IOSSourceResourceLoader`, over `GatewayNodeSession` and a real `URLSession` WebSocket, to a local Gateway fixture (`NativeGatewayWebSocketFixture` with a chat mode added). The fixture answers each `chat.history` after 1.5 s, drops the socket, sends `health` false then true, and drops the socket again; each reconnect raises the same `seqGap` the app sees on a flapping link. The harness and its driver are `rig/harness.diff` and `rig/ios-sim.sh` on the fork at [`a946eb71977`](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/tree/a946eb7197750d2d50a633939c4e27d4656e1ab1/rig). Loopback only; no credentials in the trace. | 3 runs per side, same counts each time | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | Catalog reads during the burst | 20 | 8 | | Catalog reads before the first transcript answer | 20 | 1 | | Most times one catalog was read before that answer | 5 | 1 | | Harness test | fails | passes | Catalog reads here are `models.list`, `chat.metadata`, `question.list`, `config.get` (composer and source context), `skills.status` and `tools.effective`. The `sessions.list` read for session metadata still goes out immediately on each reconnect, on purpose, and is not counted.
Wire trace, this branch (run 1, condensed: request/response pairs on one line) ``` +521ms conn1 connected +523ms conn1 -> chat.history +523ms conn1 sessions.list +527ms conn1 event health {ok: false} +629ms conn1 event health {ok: true} +629ms conn1 sessions.list +1336ms conn2 connected +1337ms conn2 health +1337ms conn2 question.list +1337ms conn2 -> chat.history +1337ms conn2 sessions.list +2847ms conn2 <- chat.history +2848ms conn2 health +2850ms conn2 models.list, question.list, chat.metadata, config.get x2, tools.effective, skills.status ``` On main the same scenario sends these catalog reads with each reconnect and again with the health recovery: 20 catalog reads, all before the first `chat.history` answer.
**Focused tests.** `ChatViewModelReconnectBurstTests` uses a fake transport that records request order and holds history open. | Test | main | previous head `6afa276f229` | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `flapping reconnects recover history before one catalog refresh` | fails (10 issues) | passes | passes | | `health recovery during a failed transcript read still refetches the progress card` | passes | fails (card never refetched) | passes | ``` main: RECONNECT_BURST requests= source,models,composer,source,models,composer,source,models,composer,questions,history,questions,swarm,questions,history.done,health,history,history.done,health branch: RECONNECT_BURST requests= history,history.done,history,history.done,health,source,models,composer,swarm,questions ``` **Suites on this branch** (in apps/shared/OpenClawKit): - `swift test --filter 'ChatViewModel|ChatModelSignIn|ChatStreamReplay|ChatQuestionCard|ChatSwarm|ChatSource|ChatComposer|ChatSessionCompletion|ChatProgress'`: 727 tests in 32 suites pass; 18 XCTest cases pass. On main the only failure is the burst test. - `swift test --parallel`: 2491 tests in 222 suites pass; 40 tests in 4 suites and 61 XCTest cases pass. On main the only failure is the burst test. - Both runs skip two clipboard tests, `ChatComposerPasteSupportTests` and `file selection remains with the captured conversation`. The test machine had no logged-in desktop session, so `NSPasteboard.writeObjects` returns false and the paste test then crashes the test process. Run alone, both fail the same way on main and on this branch. Lint: SwiftFormat 0.63.1 `--lint` with `config/swiftformat` reports no files need formatting; SwiftLint 0.65.1 with `config/swiftlint.yml` reports 0 violations; `git diff --check` is clean.
Additional runs and gaps - Same focused results with the Swift 6.4.2 Command Line Tools (MacOSX26.5 SDK) on the first head. That lane rewrote `#Preview` blocks and `@Entry` properties at build time (none in the files this PR touches) and left the XCTest files out. - Pre-existing, unrelated: `stale fallback refresh keeps retrying while run remains pending` sometimes takes about 64 s under parallel load, on main and on this branch alike (this branch: 64.0 s in the suite run, 4.5 s in the full run). It takes 0.2 s when run alone. - The simulator harness build is unsigned and leaves out the Watch app target. - Not run: a physical device on a real flapping network.
## Current integration validation Integrated current main and retained the transcript-first recovery behavior. The health-triggered composer retry now checks for an active recovery inside its task; the matching recovery keeps its marker until its catalog refreshes finish. This preserves the newer health-retry path without letting it overtake transcript recovery. Five existing reconnect and health/composer tests passed in an isolated macOS guest. The final changed source matches that tested candidate; the integrated main revision contains no intervening OpenClawKit changes relative to the test base. SwiftFormat, SwiftLint, and an independent P0–P2 review passed. The native recordings above retain their original revision and scope; they were not recreated for this integration. Fresh CI runs against `c4a20a5831ce8bcb5fcf44835c15caf3a496d2e8`.

prs.title: perf(sessions): share patch encodings across delivery histories
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Row comparisons already share work by baseline, but distinct connection histories still serialize and size the same large JSON patch repeatedly. At 16/32 subscribers the compressed replay encodes about 15/29 patches per publication for just two distinct row deltas.

## User Impact

Less synchronous broadcast CPU and allocation when subscribers receive the same session changes. Per-connection wire bytes, visibility, versions, compression, ordering, and retention semantics remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing publication-owned delta now carries the first complete patch encoding, its suffix/byte count, and encodings keyed by the exact serialized header. Identical headers share the first string; differing versions derive their string from its suffix. This avoids a second large body string even for one subscriber. Current/previous field identities preserve audience/baseline separation. Nothing is retained beyond the publication.

Connection-specific LRU admission, byte accounting, ancestor certificates, and delivery commits still consult the full connection history. Same row baseline alone is insufficient to share those decisions. Production LOC: +23; tests: −1. The growth records the prepared encoding in the existing owner and removes repeated serialization; there is no alternate delivery path or new cache owner.

## Evidence

Base `8a438e799b4eb3e3ef06c69c4a4c775cdb2b2e29` includes #199099. Node v26.12.1. Predeclared synthetic replay: changing 128 KiB text, two interleaved audiences, distinct viewers and fragmented connection histories, mixed delta/field-reference/legacy clients. Actual event projector, delivery planner, broadcaster, negotiated Control UI no-context-takeover WebSockets and subprocess receivers; only prepared presentation/access inputs are synthetic. Five alternating timing pairs × 1,000 publications/arm and five separate sampled-allocation pairs × 200. These are owner measurements, not whole-Gateway or production stall-elimination claims.

| Subscribers | Main-thread CPU ms/publication | Sampled allocation MB/publication | Patch JSON encodes/publication |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 16 | 8.895 → 5.594 (-37.1%) | 7.745 → 4.594 (-40.7%) | 14.985 → 1.998 |
| 32 | 12.378 → 5.870 (-52.6%) | 11.365 → 4.794 (-57.8%) | 28.971 → 1.998 |

Every per-connection compressed-wire and decoded receiver digest matches. Patch JSON bytes/publication fall from 2.098/4.056 MB at N16/32 to 0.280 MB. A separate 200-publication CPU profile attributes delivery planning/patch JSON at 1,550 → 216 sampled ms. Remaining candidate buckets include envelope encoding 81 ms, field preparation 62 ms, UTF-8 111 ms, compression 190 ms, and other broadcast/send work 421 ms. Field-index/envelope variants already reuse audience preparation. Ancestors are empty in this replay, so it does not measure real ancestor fan-out; existing tests protect its unchanged semantics.

Serial timing below has 5,000 samples/side. p50/p99 are means of arm percentiles; maxima are observed maxima. No arm or pause was trimmed.

| N | p50 ms | p99 ms | Max ms | >180 ms | Host load before/after, base → candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 16 | 8.78 → 5.53 | 24.29 → 7.25 | 146.72 → 15.84 | 0 → 0 | 22.7/22.8 → 23.0/20.9 |
| 32 | 12.40 → 5.73 | 18.03 → 21.57 | 58.84 → 325.40 | 0 → 1 | 21.9/23.3 → 25.4/25.0 |

N32 serial p99 is mixed-sign, including one candidate arm at 77.63 ms; its signed absolute mean delta is +3.54 ms (+19.6%). Do not infer a tail improvement from the CPU result. Same-workload unchanged-code N16 serial A/A was 126.15 versus 11.11 ms. Four synchronized N16 A/A pairs (1,000 samples/arm) had p99 10.28/9.55, 9.44/9.65, 9.42/9.30, and 13.52/13.92 ms, with zero >180 ms. Final matched N32 comparisons follow.

Final N32 large-patch matched pairs use synchronized warmed starts and swapped ports, 1,000 samples/arm/pair. Neither side exceeded 180 ms; all wire digests matched.

| Matched pair | CPU ms/publication | p99 ms | Max ms | Host load before/after, base → candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| AB | 12.021 → 5.446 | 13.396 → 6.209 | 13.658 → 6.467 | 10.79/11.40 → 10.79/11.75 |
| BA | 12.128 → 5.584 | 13.836 → 6.456 | 14.856 → 6.873 | 10.12/9.87 → 10.12/10.10 |

Single-subscriber and runtime-only controls (two swapped pairs; 2,000 timing and 400 allocation publications/side) are CPU/allocation neutral: N1 large patch 1.389 → 1.388 ms and 1.545 → 1.544 MB; N32 runtime-only 3.949 → 3.956 ms and 2.856 → 2.858 MB. N1 p99 changes by +0.36 ms. Runtime-only serial p99 was mixed-sign (7.81 → 20.38 and 5.51 → 4.88 ms), so its matched A/A/A-B results are reported below rather than treating the outlier as a verdict.

Runtime-only matched A/A p99 pairs (1,000 samples/arm) were 4.63/4.54, 4.96/4.98, 4.65/4.83, 4.70/4.94 ms, with zero >180 ms. In the first A/B pair both revisions experienced the same tail spike; the second was quiet. CPU remains neutral and the serial one-sided tail increase does not reproduce in matched windows.

| Matched pair | CPU ms/publication | p99 ms | Max ms | Host load before/after, base → candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| AB | 4.155 → 4.150 | 21.340 → 19.713 | 42.476 → 35.092 | 12.94/14.15 → 12.94/14.15 |
| BA | 3.792 → 3.812 | 4.572 → 4.516 | 5.572 → 5.233 | 10.79/10.28 → 10.79/10.28 |

| N | Heap used | Process RSS |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 16 | 37.19 → 37.22 | 288.65 → 317.39 |
| 32 | 37.36 → 37.37 | 278.96 → 305.80 |

Live retained heap is flat. RSS is higher and is not claimed as a win; matched N16 A/A RSS differed by up to 59.9 MiB on identical source while live heap stayed near 37.2 MiB, so RSS attribution is inconclusive.

Regression: the existing interleaved eight-audience/delayed-baseline test fails on main with 714 patch encodes versus 89 expected, then passes with the change. It also compares complete patch strings against independent serialization of each wire object. Focused delivery/field/audience/retention/presentation tests: 53 passed (51.68 s including transformation; test execution 9%). Broadcaster/serialized-WebSocket consumer tests: 29 passed, one existing skip. Changed-file format/lint, scripts typecheck, strict root test typecheck, and Gateway-root test typecheck passed.

Plain Codex branch autoreview (`python3 ~/.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main --engine codex`, with overrides unset) is scoped-clean at its default P0-only threshold. Exact-head CI passed at `1b8c8ff1798cb99fe77c639812280426f9cd346b`: [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43639484328), with `openclaw/ci-gate` successful. The only cancelled checks are duplicate advisory auto-response jobs. No Gateway stress run was needed for this synchronous encoding-only change; the real compressed owner replay and byte-identical frames provide the requested fast-path proof.

Caller audit: ordinary sidebar pages omit people facets. Owner counts are a separate query active only for visible, expanded Online navigation with profile users. Stable known-row events already avoid count refreshes (ten snapshots plus 125 seconds produce only the initial read); incomplete ancestor coverage/unknown membership and changed owner/run/archive/disclosure facts still need authority. Activity History requests people/pulse facets; stable unfiltered updates apply locally with a 60-second fallback, and filtered queries retain paced reads. The coordinator collects 4–5 seconds and backs off 5–15 seconds. All 56 focused UI refresh tests passed. Aggregate RPC counts do not identify each request shape’s production frequency.

Selection scaling: resolved synthetic profile and production identity projection, 1/5 parents and 1/7 archived rows, 15 live-row changes, 500 warmup updates, two 2,000-update timing runs and one separate 2,000-update allocation run. The Activity case is an all-time people/pulse query excluding subagents. No caller-side deletion is justified: bounded events cannot certify unknown whole-roster contributions.

prs.title: fix(exec): agent gets one wake turn per command when background commands exit together
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when several background commands exit close together, the agent gets one wake turn per command, so three exits cost three model turns and three replies.

## User Impact

User impact: completions that arrive while an earlier completion turn in the same conversation is still queued or running now reach the agent together in one turn, with each result's process ID, status, exit code and output tail. A single completion starts at once, exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each exit enqueued its own session event and became its own turn. The session event owner already turns a set of exact queued occurrences into one ordinary turn (`occurrences`, used by session-state notices), and `combineSessionEventTargetsForHost` already checks that a set shares one destination and requester authority. This change reuses both:

- New `session-event-batch.ts` in the session event owner keeps one in-flight completion turn per conversation. A completion with nothing in flight starts at once through `enqueueSessionEventForHost`, unchanged. A completion that arrives while that turn is queued or running claims its queued occurrence and waits. One second after the turn settles, every waiting completion that shares the same exec request owners, launching run, route and combinable target starts one turn with all of their occurrences.
- `bash-tools.exec-notify.ts` only switches its enqueue import to the batched entry point. Each result keeps the wake format from #199122 (`Exec completed (<id>, code 0, 4m3s):` plus a tail of up to 2,000 chars).
- One shared turn carries at most about 8,000 characters of results. Occurrence text must stay byte-exact, so the bound limits membership, not text: results past the budget start the next turn.
- The exec completion guidance is count-neutral ("Treat each completion result above as an internal continuation…") so a batched turn no longer says "this completion" for several results.

Choices and accepted edges:

- **A 1 s settle, only for completions that already waited.** A first or lone completion still starts at once (measured base: its turn starts within about 1 s of the exit, before later exits arrive), so no delay is added to single wakes. Without a settle, exits about 1 s apart sometimes straddle the end of the turn they waited behind: on the intermediate head, 2 of 6 trials split into three turns because the last exit arrived just after the batch started. Waiting completions now start 1 s after that turn settles, so stragglers join.
- **Only one request's completions share a turn.** Stop aborts every exec request owner of a turn, so mixing requests would let one Stop retire another request's result. Completions from different requests keep separate turns.
- **Only one launching run's completions share a turn.** The completion turn's input provenance names the run that launched the command, which plugins use to correlate a completion with its run (#179816). Request owners carry over into completion turns, so commands launched by a later run can share owners with earlier ones; the batch also requires the same launching run, and each shared turn keeps a truthful `inputProvenance.runId`.
- **Cron-run completions never wait.** They check at acceptance that the originating run is still alive; holding them could turn an accepted completion into a refused one.
- Removing one member after its shared turn is queued (for example, the model polled that result) leaves the shared prompt as is; the turn is retired only when every member is removed. Before the shared turn is queued, removal drops just that member.
- A waiting completion starts after its predecessor settles, so a human message queued in `followup` or `collect` mode meanwhile can run first.
- Rebased on #199122 (wake format) and #199085. This PR touches only the import line in `bash-tools.exec-notify.ts` and the guidance wording in `agent-runner-run-params.ts`.

## Evidence

**Real-agent E2E** (isolated source Gateway via `ocx src`, real OpenAI model, 6 concurrent trial sessions per arm). Each trial asks the agent to start three background waiters with `yieldMs`, waits until the session is idle with all three running, then releases them 1 s apart. Base = current `main` (`afeadf1c4fe0`, includes #199122); fix = this PR rebased on it.

| Arm | Wake turns (6 trials) | Results acknowledged | Wake-turn tokens (total) | Wake-turn cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| base, 3 exits | 18 (3 per trial) | 18/18 | 501,233 | $1.152 |
| fix, 3 exits | 12 (2 per trial) | 18/18 | 326,362 (-35%) | $0.930 |
| base, 1 exit | 6 | 6/6 | 153,377 | $0.402 |
| fix, 1 exit | 6 | 6/6 | 153,934 | $0.403 |

Single-exit wake latency (release to wake message, median of 6): base 0.85 s, fix 0.85 s. A single completion never waits for the settle. Time from release to the last reply in the 3-exit arm: base median 9.2 s, fix median 7.3 s.

Every fix trial: the first exit starts its turn at once; the two later exits arrive during it and share the next turn, each keeping its own id, exit code, duration and tail. Results from earlier runs before the rebase (same arms, older wake format) matched: 12 turns vs 18.

<details><summary>Redacted trace, trial 1 (times relative to release of the first waiter)</summary>

Base (before the rebase, old wake format):

```
  +8.8s USER: Exec completed (gentle-c, code 0) :: job 1 result: r11-1603127358
 +11.7s reply (26930 tok): job 1 result: r11-1603127358
 +19.1s USER: Exec completed (dawn-gla, code 0) :: job 2 result: r12-78193628
 +22.0s reply (27407 tok): job 2 result: r12-78193628
 +26.5s USER: Exec completed (kind-sum, code 0) :: job 3 result: r13-1811516849
 +29.2s reply (27885 tok): job 3 result: r13-1811516849
```

Fix (rebased head):

```
  +1.2s USER: Exec completed (tide-cov, code 0, 34s): job 1 result: r11-1383216
  +3.7s reply (26761 tok): job 1 result: r11-1383216
  +5.1s USER: Exec completed (tidy-com, code 0, 32s): job 2 result: r12-262323306
              Exec completed (rapid-bi, code 0, 29s): job 3 result: r13-179203848
  +7.7s reply (27281 tok): job 2 result: r12-262323306 / job 3 result: r13-179203848
```

</details>

**Regression tests:** `bash-tools.exec-background-followup.test.ts` runs three real background commands through the exec tool and the real session event owner with a held first model turn. Same launching run: base starts three completion turns (red); the fix starts two, the second carrying both later results and naming their run. Different launching runs with shared request owners: the later results keep separate turns, each naming its own run (red without the launch-run check). Five results of ~2,000 chars: the shared turn takes three and the fifth starts its own turn (size bound).

**Focused suites (`ocx test`, rebased head, 14 files):** `bash-tools.exec-background-followup`, `bash-tools.test`, `bash-tools.exec-runtime`, `bash-tools.exec-runtime.cleanup`, `bash-tools.visible-subagent-notify`, `bash-tools.exec-request-stop`, `bash-tools.exec.egress-lifecycle`, `bash-tools.notify-on-exit-ack`, `bash-tools.process.e2e`, `bash-tools.exec-notify.requester`, `bash-tools.exec-notify.queue-full`, `infra/exec-session-event`, `session-event-handoff`, `agent-runner-execution-session-events`: all pass. `exec-session-event`'s chained-completion case now waits for the second receipt, which starts after the 1 s settle.

**Full tier:** `ocx build --dts` (full profile) built `92847fc`; the self-contained source package passed its tarball integrity check, installed with npm into a scratch prefix, and the packed CLI reported `OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (92847fc)` with `gateway --help` exit 0. The later head commit only changes a test type.

**Gaps:** E2E covers exits from one request in an idle Control UI-style session; completions from different requests and channel-delivered sessions are covered by the shared owner's existing tests, not by a new live run.

prs.title: fix: cancel response bodies after headers with foreign signals
prs.body:
Closes #199185

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes SDK response-body reads continuing after cancellation when a foreign AbortSignal is aborted after response headers arrive.

## User Impact

Plugin developers using a foreign signal can interrupt an unfinished response body after headers, including reads through a response clone. Native signals keep their existing path; no configuration or dependency changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The foreign-to-native relay was detached when the fetch promise settled at headers. Keep it until the body finishes, fails, or is canceled by passing its cleanup to the existing response-abort lifecycle helper. Bodyless responses and fetch failures still clean up immediately. This reuses the existing lazy stream, finalizer, metadata, clone, and nonwaiting abort handling rather than adding another body owner.

The initial selection, investigation, and reproduction were supplied by the reporter. I implemented the repair, designed the regression coverage, and reran the real SDK/HTTP checks.

## Evidence

Published head `de0ccfc88f89ab380ecabf32be1bae7bd67c54e4` has the exact tested tree `785f2a1eb975643236a98d3cc9ed2d4ba190ae7e`, based on `cfa40212f9c6ce442a36e6ad6b8df07eec9b6ae5`; the tree and all three outgoing file blobs were read back from GitHub.

- **Causal red/green:** on base `cfa40212f9c6ce442a36e6ad6b8df07eec9b6ae5`, the new regression fails because the native relay signal remains un-aborted after a foreign post-header abort (17 existing cases pass). With this patch it passes and the pending body read rejects with `AbortError`.
- **Actual SDK + HTTP:** Node 26.12.1 native fetch, Undici 8.12.3 Agent over an isolated Unix socket, and `abort-controller@3.0.0`; no fetch mock. Before the fix, foreign abort stayed pending until server release, while native abort rejected. After the fix, both reject before release. Native/foreign × original/clone × abort/no-abort all pass on both source and compiled `dist/plugin-sdk/fetch-runtime.js`. Successful reads return `prefix-suffix` and EOF. Already-aborted and pre-header controls, full-body clone reads, response URL, and immutable HTTP headers also pass.
- **53 focused tests pass** across fetch, guarded body lifecycle, header normalization, timeout, and SDK release suites. This covers terminal listener cleanup even when foreign cleanup throws, original error identity/no extra unhandled rejection, lazy consumption, metadata/clones, duplex, preconnect, and wrapper identity. Command: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test src/infra/fetch.test.ts src/infra/net/guarded-body-stream.test.ts src/infra/fetch-headers.test.ts src/utils/fetch-timeout.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/fetch-runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (8.58 s wrapper wall time; changed fetch suite under 0.2 s test time). Hosted test CI seconds are unavailable while execution needs owner approval.
- Production core and infra-test typechecks, targeted typed Oxlint, local oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. Runtime compilation and canonical `pnpm build:plugin-sdk:dts` pass (SDK declarations: 76.6 s). The runtime build uses the existing local selector excluding the sealed remote-worker deployment bundle.
- **Build limit:** full `pnpm build` stopped at the unrelated sealed worker-deploy artifact because the restricted environment cannot resolve the npm registry. The full package build and Bun formatter/linter parity remain for hosted CI; no full-build success is claimed. Initial missing local workspace-resolution links were repaired using already-installed packages from the same isolated checkout, without installation or dependency changes; setup failures are excluded from causal-red evidence.
- **Hosted status (2026-11-14 20:43 UTC, published head above):** Security Review and PR context/evidence passed. [CI run 43638826857](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43638826857) and [CodeQL run 43638826772](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43638826772) report `action_required`; repository-owner workflow approval is pending, so these are not build/test results. ClawSweeper has acknowledged receipt; substantive review is pending.
- I inspected the complete diff and simplified the change around the existing lifecycle owner (+12 net production lines, +126 test lines). Author self-inspection is complete; normal hosted upstream review remains independent evidence.

Sanitized decisive capture:

```text
base, native,  abort: before release = rejected AbortError
base, foreign, abort: before release = pending; after release = suffix
fixed source and built SDK, native/foreign, original/clone:
  abort:    before release = rejected AbortError; remains rejected after release
  no abort: before release = pending; after release = suffix, EOF
```

This is SDK/HTTP proof, not evidence of a live channel, Gateway, provider, or security incident. Maintainer review and exact-head hosted CI remain required external decisions.

prs.body:
Depends on [#194755](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194755); this branch is stacked on its `5adf1572` head. Scope changes are `4ab20e2e` and `56aed841`; current head `c82b75dc` integrates the exact upstream context used for validation.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes agent session management mixing chats from different agents and hiding the selected agent’s own conversations behind an implicit personal-owner filter.

## User Impact

Authenticated agent management starts at **All owners**, showing the selected agent’s authorized conversations. Saved owner filters remain active and intersect with that agent, including when the result is empty. Restricted guests keep the **Involving me** default.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retain the selected agent in every session-list query, including reads with an explicit owner. Preserve a saved owner choice when the current or bounded owner facet omits it, rather than silently replacing that choice. Agent switching, empty results, background refreshes, and reloads therefore retain the same intended query scope. The visible agent picker subscribes to the existing authorized roster inventory for unread badges and the latest conversation, then projects it through the selected agent and owner. This avoids depending on the sidebar cache that owner changes correctly retire; no cross-agent rows enter the sidebar.

This changes the initial presentation default, not the Gateway’s authorization: session membership still comes from the Gateway, and explicit owner selections remain supported.

## Evidence

- Synthetic baseline captures reproduce the problem: selecting Mentor A can show a Main conversation while omitting Mentor A’s student discussions.
- Final browser proof passed 5/5 (18.72 s wall): three selected-agent scenarios cover the default, an explicit human owner, and an explicit agent owner; two existing page-scope regressions also pass. Assertions cover query agent/owner intersection, switching to existing and empty agents, saved-owner retention, and reload without cross-agent rows.
- Owner/query/preference unit contracts passed 68/68 (1.12 s wall), including the guest-specific default. Scoped UI, E2E and component type checks, lint, formatting, and the test-line allocation check passed.
- Fresh independent review found no actionable P0–P2 defects. These are source-branch tests with a mocked Gateway and synthetic data.

- Broader CI exposed eight expectations for the old cross-agent/default-self behavior. Owner-specific tests now explicitly select that owner. The retained resume/unread assertions also found and verify the independent picker inventory fix. The seven affected/sibling test files pass 150/150 on the exact merged head; the five browser cases and strict types also pass.
- Canonical performance against upstream `4cedec0f`: Chat boot 1,295,020 B (base 1,295,231 B; cap 1,295,248 B), New 802,413 B (base 802,603 B). Request counts remain 20/15; no budgets changed. Exact-head CI passed for `c82b75dc` (45 successful checks; 39 intentionally skipped checks).

**Mentor A selected in both captures**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Mentor view mixes Main chat and hides student conversations](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c65f93dc-4e9f-43a6-948a-e0caf0b8fdcb) | ![Mentor view shows only its authorized owner and student conversations](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4005d5a8-f2fe-4167-b13b-ea1140fe1fe6) |


### Follow-up: bounded agent inventory

At `bc2ffd8a2`, selecting an agent fetches an authorized, current agent-scoped session list with the selected owner filters rather than treating a bounded all-agent roster as complete. The result is discarded if connection, route, filter, selected agent, or latest click changes while the request is in flight. Request failure leaves the current selection in place and shows an error. Regression cases cover a truncated roster, inaccessible or deleted rows, request failure and a changed filter; 52 focused UI tests, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, targeted lint and the normal commit hook passed. Unread badges remain limited to the roster. The independent full pre-commit lint reported unrelated existing src/test errors; these tests use synthetic Gateway responses, not an installed live Gateway.


### CI follow-up

At `9b64b0d65`, picker code is lazy-loaded with intent and connection checks before and after loading. Madge reports no import cycles; seven bundled-browser cases, including the four previously failing scope/pagination scenarios, and 53 unit cases pass. `tsgo:ui`, targeted lint and line-cap checks pass. Against upstream `13ab261c`, the independently checked test-line ratchet passed without a new allocation. The integrated branch measured chat boot -212 B and New Session +3 B gzip, below their existing budgets; this is not a substitute for exact-head CI or performance-owner review.


### Final CI repair

At `9b69e34af`, the lazy loader uses Solid `lazyModule` and passes the Control UI controller guard without exceptions. Tests now await the actual agent selection and rendered state: 172 focused unit cases, three browser cases and seven E2E cases passed; typecheck, targeted lint, import-cycle and line-cap checks passed. A 239-line allocation matches the added behavioral tests on exact CI merge `9a82300` and base `74e1ecf`; the ratchet passes with no spare lines. The integrated deterministic build against `13ab261c` measured chat +128 B gzip (8 B under cap) and New Session +214 B; performance-owner evaluation is still required. Exact-head CI is pending.

prs.title: perf(ui): skip anchor fallbacks for hidden overlays
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Hidden menus retained their CSS anchor fallback lists, making WebKit spend style time on popovers that were not visible. This extends the existing closing-state fallback retirement rule to the hidden phase. The overlay lifecycle sets `opening` before showing the surface, so its original placement and flip rules return before it appears.

The change is one added selector in the existing document stylesheet. It preserves the closing workaround, the deliberate document/shadow boundary, all markup and lazy boundaries, and adds no JavaScript or state. Production LOC: 4,147 → 4,148. No changelog edit; release-note context is the faster heavy Secrets inventory with unchanged menu behavior.

## Evidence

The production builds ran 20 rotated base/head/identical-base triplets for each of four flows in WebKit 27.2, Chromium 156, and Firefox 157, with fresh headless browser processes and contexts. All **720/720** timing observations passed correctness. A single 10-triplet Firefox Secrets extension investigated its 2 ms p95 movement; **30/30** additional observations passed. Metrics are browser-local application completion, not driver wall time or CPU. Host one-minute load across the main run was 2.59–14.43.

WebKit Secrets improves **17.81%** in paired median, with median/p95 **306.5/325 → 249.5/265 ms**. Relative to the mean of both base arms the paired median improves **16.86%**, beyond the **4.77%** median absolute A/A variation. The final-head Timeline diagnostic isolates style **162.24 → 94.65 ms** (identical-base control 172.65 ms; one traced observation per arm, not acceptance timing). **201 hidden overlays with nonempty fallback lists become zero**. The existing opening lifecycle restores their original lists before display.

The Firefox extension retains the small movement transparently: across 30 triplets the paired median is **+1.15%**, p95 **144 → 146 ms**, and median absolute A/A variation is **4.67%**. That is within measured variation; it is not reported as a Firefox speedup or exact zero change. The other tested surfaces show no material regression; the win is specific to the hidden-menu workload.

| Secrets | firefox | 133 / 144 | 137.5 / 146 | 130.5 / 144 | +1.15% | -0.37% |
| Skills settings | webkit | 324 / 341 | 321.5 / 334 | 320.5 / 351 | -0.61% | +0.00% |
| Skills settings | chromium | 144.45 / 153.2 | 144.2 / 156.4 | 145 / 157.5 | -0.07% | +0.73% |
| Skills settings | firefox | 196.5 / 212 | 194.5 / 211 | 201.5 / 211 | +2.39% | +2.27% |

</details>

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| UI typecheck | `pnpm tsgo:ui` passed |
| Native menu proof | 41/41 tests passed in the three focused WebKit menu contract files; one worker |
| Styles and format | Targeted Stylelint and oxfmt passed |
| Production Knip | Passed |
| Production builds | Base and head passed |
| Strict performance comparison | Zero new violations, no cap changes |
| Startup | JS 90,945 → 90,945 B normalized gzip; CSS 40,781 → 40,789 B; 3 JS and 1 CSS requests unchanged |

| Independent review | Codex P0–P2 scoped-clean; lifecycle and cascade context included |

The copied-bundle ablation was diagnostic, not a proposed redesign: removing the shared sheet reduced Secrets style time, then rule and property bisection isolated `position-try-fallbacks`. prs.title: perf(ai): reuse Anthropic history bytes after payload hook edits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Anthropic requests re-serialize the whole conversation when a payload hook changes only an envelope field, such as the bundled service-tier wrapper's `service_tier` setting.

## User Impact

Long Anthropic histories require substantially less request-construction CPU and JavaScript allocation. Serialized request bytes, payload-hook mutability, cache checkpoints, and model settings stay unchanged. The existing weak cache retains encoded fragments while their frozen source history remains alive; its memory cost is reported below.

## Why This Change Was Made

The converter already preserves frozen history identities. Keep its existing unchanged-payload check, then reuse fragments when an edited payload remains plain data and its messages remain equal. Replacement bodies, opaque JSON, and changed messages retain full serialization.

The same fragment cache now holds private UTF-8 bytes. Assemble each request into a fresh contiguous byte array, using the existing encoded-body contract instead of intermediate Blob buffers. Cached fragments never escape the owner; request-byte reporting also recognizes the owned byte arrays. No second cache, dependency, provider option, schema, or JSON shape change.

Runtime production delta: **+10 lines**. The extra assembly loop copies private fragments into an independently owned request; it replaces Blob assembly/flattening rather than adding a parallel serializer. Regression delta: +20 lines with an exact allocation record. Benchmark extensions stay in the scripts and their header comments.

## Evidence

Base: `d4e669de5c7c` (refreshed main). Candidate: `9e69e75e3f1a19b9767d1b056d00e19206024be7`. Measurements were collected before the final rebase and benchmark-only CI fix. The rebase changed none of the measured owner, converter, immutable-data, or Anthropic plugin sources.

Acceptance was declared before timing: byte-identical requests, lower CPU/allocation, and the supplied paired GC rules. Five counterbalanced base/candidate timing pairs per size, 200 measured requests/arm (**1,000 per side**), plus two separate allocation passes (**400 per side**). Each process warms separately. Synthetic histories contain three messages/turn, large tool results, a changing mutable tail, and the actual bundled service-tier wrapper.

The owner benchmark measures conversion, hooks, serialization, and production of contiguous wire bytes. It does not measure a complete HTTP/model call, including Fetch's additional snapshot of an encoded byte-array body.

| History | Main-thread CPU ms/request | Sampled allocation MiB/request | GC ms/request |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 100 turns | 15.77 → 2.17 (-86.2%) | 11.19 → 3.03 (-72.9%) | 0.253 → 0.223 |
| 500 turns | 79.58 → 9.99 (-87.5%) | 55.96 → 14.35 (-74.3%) | 1.113 → 1.271 |

The 500-turn GC increase is **+0.158 ms/request** (+14.2%), below the declared 1 ms/request materiality threshold. One candidate arm has a 79.8 ms maximum pause versus 6.3 ms on its paired base; this is retained in the evidence. Four candidate A/A controls expose unstable short-window GC (one identical-source pair is 0.752 → 2.761 ms/request). Four fresh 1,000-request A/A pairs give 0.660–0.720 ms/request and maxima of 2.25–7.07 ms. Two longer counterbalanced base/candidate pairs (2,000 measured requests per side) give CPU **79.37 → 9.62 ms/request** and GC **1.234 → 0.735 ms/request**; maximum pauses are **93.57 → 6.37 ms** and **26.71 → 2.53 ms**. The longer matched protocol does not reproduce the adverse short-window signal; no pause was trimmed. Allocation-instrumented GC does not gate timing.

At a matched **five requests/second**, two AB/BA pairs (200 requests/arm) give 500-turn CPU **84.29 → 12.98 ms/request**, GC **3.89 → 1.92 ms/request**, RSS **501.5 → 570.3 MiB**, and heap **145.2 → 145.2 MiB**. RSS is higher by 68.8 MiB (+13.7%); the per-pair changes are +22.7% and +5.9%, below the declared mean/both-pairs rejection rule. This is a reported memory tradeoff, not a claim of lower RSS. The fixture produces a ~29.9 MB body. These are owner-process measurements, not whole-Gateway memory measurements. After releasing history, both arms collect all 1,499 source keys and 1,500 projections; the candidate releases ~29.9 MB of fragment ArrayBuffers.

Diagnostics compare cold, repeated, and appended requests at 100 and 500 turns with no hook, an observer hook, and the bundled service-tier hook, with and without 12 inline images. **All 36 full-body baseline/candidate comparisons match.** Warm text-only histories reuse 298/300 or 1,498/1,500 fragments and encode only two checkpoint messages (~55 KB). Images remain request-budget-dependent: 12 image-bearing messages plus the checkpoints encode (~1.43 MB). Deep-frozen checks remain sub-millisecond at 500 turns in the diagnostic runs. Cold history/new tails still encode as required.

The extended `anthropic-cache-transport-parity.test.ts` fails on the base: the envelope-edit case performs one whole-payload encode where zero is required. It passes on the candidate. It also mutates a sent byte array and proves later bodies remain intact, and verifies byte reporting against captured wire bytes. Existing replacement/opaque JSON/message-edit/late-hook-mutation coverage remains.

Validation: 95 focused AI tests across cache transport parity, cache carrier parity, and transport-stream tests; all 14 prefix-stability tests; the final 26-test regression file; `pnpm tsgo:test:root`; `pnpm tsgo:scripts`; the matching package-test tsconfig; changed-file lint/format; `git diff --check`. Final regression file: 0.85 s test-run duration (1.93 s wrapper wall time). No Testbox lease was used. Initial PR CI caught a benchmark-only typed-array capture mismatch under the separate script tsconfig; the capture now takes an owned snapshot without a cast. The explicit scripts/root typechecks, lint, and restored-session wire proof pass after that fix.

Complete-context **Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P2**, no accepted/actionable findings, covering the full local change against `210458b3d434db20073789863d9e493a54217358`. The subsequent rebases preserved that patch and relevant source context. A separate Codex review of the benchmark CI fix is also scoped-clean through P2. Exact-head [CI run 43642579522](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43642579522) is **successful**: 40 jobs passed, 29 intentionally skipped. The previous head’s benchmark-only script type error was fixed and the corresponding job passes on this head. Ready for TS-lead review; not merged.

Reproduce: `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/anthropic-request-construction.ts --turns 100 --hook service-tier --iterations 200` (repeat with `--turns 500`; add `--allocation` separately, `--interval-ms 200` for matched rate, or `--diagnostics` with optional `--images`). `--baseline-dir` supplies a sparse source overlay of the base request-body owner.

Scope: the requested duplicate-work fast path, with owner work-count/CPU/allocation proof. No live-provider or whole-Gateway latency claim; no Team load was started. This reproduces redundant serialization, not attribution of an individual production interrupt sample.

<details>
<summary>Per-arm GC and host-load context</summary>

| Turns / pair | GC ms/request base → candidate | Max pause ms base → candidate | Host 1-minute load base → candidate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 100 / 1 | 0.367 → 0.184 | 57.35 → 3.35 | 32.2 → 34.6 |
| 100 / 2 | 0.072 → 0.193 | 0.51 → 4.21 | 34.2 → 34.1 |
| 100 / 3 | 0.237 → 0.216 | 31.45 → 8.60 | 31.9 → 32.5 |
| 100 / 4 | 0.170 → 0.223 | 17.57 → 5.61 | 37.1 → 33.9 |
| 100 / 5 | 0.420 → 0.298 | 66.93 → 5.53 | 39.2 → 41.5 |
| 500 / 1 | 1.140 → 0.907 | 11.99 → 32.02 | 34.9 → 31.9 |
| 500 / 2 | 1.153 → 0.970 | 13.09 → 12.10 | 31.3 → 35.0 |
| 500 / 3 | 1.044 → 3.111 | 6.31 → 79.81 | 26.0 → 26.3 |
| 500 / 4 | 1.001 → 0.728 | 3.88 → 8.15 | 20.0 → 24.9 |
| 500 / 5 | 1.228 → 0.639 | 4.64 → 5.67 | 15.3 → 13.6 |

| 500 / long 1 | 1.225 → 0.791 | 93.57 → 6.37 | 15.3 → 16.5 |
| 500 / long 2 | 1.244 → 0.680 | 26.71 → 2.52 | 11.3 → 15.7 |

GC by kind, summed across 1,000 untraced requests/side:

| Turns / kind | Count base → candidate | Total ms base → candidate | Max ms base → candidate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 100 / Scavenge | 330 → 30 | 253.2 → 20.4 | 66.93 → 1.81 |
| 100 / IncrementalMarking | 0 → 65 | 0.0 → 14.1 | 0.00 → 0.99 |
| 100 / MarkSweepCompact | 0 → 64 | 0.0 → 188.3 | 0.00 → 8.60 |
| 500 / Scavenge | 6 → 183 | 8.2 → 142.4 | 1.41 → 12.45 |
| 500 / IncrementalMarking | 326 → 271 | 60.5 → 59.7 | 0.44 → 0.77 |
| 500 / MarkSweepCompact | 322 → 270 | 1044.6 → 1069.0 | 13.09 → 79.81 |

No-hook control CPU: 1.454 → 0.541 ms/request. Unchanged observer control: 2.620 → 1.628 ms/request. Two AB/BA pairs, 200 requests/arm. No p95/p99 is inferred from arm aggregates.

</details>

prs.title: fix(ios): show the main conversation in All Sessions
prs.body: Related: #192203 Vyctor requested [“a smaller PR focused on including the main conversation in All Sessions while preserving the existing navigation”](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193033#issuecomment-6733201379), noting that Home is already permanent. This PR follows that scope, not an approval to merge. #193033 remains closed. ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: the native iOS All Sessions screen omits the current agent’s existing main conversation when users look for it after switching chats. ## User Impact Users can find and reopen that same conversation in All Sessions. Home remains its permanent sidebar shortcut. Existing names, Rename, sidebar contents and limits, Overview, headers, selection styling, and navigation stay unchanged. No migration or configuration change is required. ## Why This Change Was Made The All Sessions filter now admits the main row resolved by the existing session-routing owner, while retaining the configured main key for ordinary-session filtering. The same resolved identities drive the current-row presentation and existing archive/delete/snooze protections. Opening a row still passes its existing key to the existing chat owner; no conversation is created, reset, or forked. The implementation changes one production file (+40 net lines), reusing the filter, routing, status-scope, action-menu, and navigation owners. No new state, alternate navigation, fixed title, or reserved sidebar row is introduced. The source simplification pass retained only inclusion, alias selection, and necessary lifecycle protection. The follow-up pass removed four redundant field-copy assertions and two unused fixture assignments (six test lines) while retaining the behavioral regressions; production code is unchanged. ## Evidence **Draft — native qualification remains incomplete.** This Linux execution environment has no Swift, Xcode, Simulator, SwiftFormat, or SwiftLint, and no supported authorized Mac/device capture route was exposed. The native test runner stopped before tests because `xcrun` is unavailable. There is no executed baseline-fail/candidate-pass native result, native build/typecheck, Swift test timing, or inspected before/after screenshot pair for this candidate. These are outstanding readiness gates, not passing or waived checks. Historical screenshots and test results from #193033 do not qualify this extracted tree and are not reused here. Published head: `c6898a6c7463de084afa3fd4910b0f99c2b56799`; its complete Git tree matches reviewed simplification candidate `19341686a8652fda88a4609ce7b0c89269b9e4a1`. The [earlier draft CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42628517324) belongs to `ac53b92111df` and skipped the native build and screenshot jobs; it is not proof for the new head. Completed on the candidate based on `cbe182f49c4cac33f339c03a77b983f3d7a52ccc`: - `pnpm native:i18n:verify`: passed, 4,688 entries, unchanged; native generated-artifact isolation also passed. - `git diff --cached --check`, Node syntax check of the native Gateway fixture, targeted repository oxlint, and oxfmt checks of the fixture/docs: passed. These do not establish Swift formatting or compilation. - Actual loopback WebSocket fixture smoke: main and planning have different histories and matching roster/history IDs; requesting main again returns the identical history. This validates the synthetic fixture, not the native app, production Gateway, or durable storage. - Independent bound Auto Review, `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, complete five-file candidate tree `708d9b18d2faf377a58edf081c945e9d151a895a` against the base above: scoped-clean through P2. The complete source/fixture follow-up closed the first pass’s context gap. A fresh bound review of the six-line simplification against `ac53b92111df`, also using `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, was scoped-clean through P2; it confirmed no distinct behavioral proof was lost. Native execution remains unverified. Added, **not yet executed**, native regressions cover standard/custom main aliases, duplicate aliases, incomplete rosters, selected automation and status scopes, normal title presentation, unchanged recent-chat/sidebar exclusion, protected lifecycle actions with Rename retained, and All Sessions → another chat → main with distinct history and request-trace assertions. Existing snooze/wake checks remain intact. Outstanding native commands include `pnpm ios:test CommandCenterTabSessionFilterTests`, `pnpm ios:test OpenClawUITests/SessionSnoozeUITests` with the existing isolated attention Gateway, the affected sibling `SidebarAttentionUITests`, and the configured iOS SwiftFormat/SwiftLint checks. Capture matched native before/after All Sessions evidence on the baseline and this new candidate before marking ready. Exact-head CI is not claimed as passed. ### Historical All Sessions screenshots — original issue Reused from [#192203](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/192203), credited to its reporter, @llbohacll (originally credited as @leonardobohac). The reporter identifies these as native development-app captures on the same physical iPhone 17, iOS 27.0.1, English, with the same synthetic roster: baseline `7218303550c6771d1d28dc6bb6bfdd1e2b6668d1` versus a local prototype whose exact commit was not supplied. Both original image assets were inspected and reused without alteration or duplicate upload. **These illustrate the original omission and proposed inclusion, not the current PR’s rendering or validation.** The prototype also shows a fixed “Main Session” title, distinct icon, and “default” badge; those presentation changes are not part of this narrower PR. prs.title: feat(backup): omit Doctor migration originals from archives on request
prs.body:
Closes #183277

**Decision:** Option A, approved in the [maintainer review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194823#pullrequestreview-5829109969).
`openclaw backup create` keeps Doctor's retained pre-migration originals by default, and
`--exclude-migration-backups` omits them. This follows the existing opt-in `--exclude-worktree-templates` flag
(#190822). All four items from that review are addressed (see "Why This Change Was Made").

## What Problem This Solves

Full backup archives carry every retained Doctor original as raw bytes next to the live database snapshot.
That makes archives much larger and slower after each update, with no way to leave the originals out.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can run `openclaw backup create --exclude-migration-backups` to leave Doctor's retained
pre-migration originals out of an archive. Each omitted file is listed as `excluded`. Archives made without the
flag are unchanged.

A restored archive made with the flag cannot roll back the last migration with those originals. The docs say
so. The flag never deletes or changes the originals on disk; `openclaw update cleanup` still owns their
retention.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The flag matches only the exact names Doctor writes beside the shared state database and each registered
  agent database:
  - `<database>.pre-startup-migration-<uuid>.bak` (full SQLite original)
  - `<database>.pre-startup-migration-<uuid>.scoped.bak` (scoped SQLite original)
  - `<database>.pre-startup-migration-<uuid>.postgres.bak` (PostgreSQL backup directory, omitted as a whole
    and listed once)
  - `<database>.pre-startup-migration-restart-recovery-<uuid>.bak` (SQLite original saved before a
    restart-recovery session repair)

  Look-alike names and other `.bak` files stay included. A repo-wide search found no other
  `pre-startup-migration` producers.
- The exclusion goes through the backup resource plan, like `--exclude-worktree-templates`. Each omitted file
  appears in `skipped` (kind `migration backup`, reason `excluded`) in the dry-run plan, the text and JSON
  output, and the archive manifest. The reason is not `regenerable`, because these files are recovery
  artifacts.
- Doctor's original names are built and classified in one module,
  `src/commands/doctor-migration-backup-names.ts`, next to `doctor-migration-backup.ts`. All four producers
  (`doctor-migration-backup.ts`, `doctor-postgres-migration.ts`, `doctor/shared/session-entry-rewrite.ts`)
  build their names there, and backup planning and the restore manifest classify names there, so the matcher
  cannot drift from the writers. The rule is not in `doctor-migration-backup.ts` itself because the restore
  manifest importing that file creates an import cycle (`doctor-migration-backup` ->
  `doctor-migration-backup-artifacts` -> manifest) and pulls SQLite worker code into backup planning.
- The restore manifest still accepts only the full and scoped SQLite originals, the only formats Doctor
  records in manifests. PostgreSQL and restart-recovery paths are rejected there, as before.
- `docs/cli/backup.md` documents the flag, every omitted format and the rollback tradeoff.
  `repair-and-recovery.md` points to it.
- The final test-line allocation is 214: 88 naming-test lines plus 126 archive-regression lines.
  The added coverage protects retired-store discovery and lexical/physical database aliases; current-head CI remains required.

## Evidence

### Follow-up: retained stores and physical aliases

The [signed correction](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/commit/88285352f5994b9b8f4e554b1868776fd3c64859) preserves the original contributor ancestry and fixes two additional discovery omissions without changing Option A:

- Reuse the existing complete agent-store discovery owner, including disk-only retired stores and retained registry-only custom paths, rather than only the configured roster.
- Match originals beside both lexical database locators and physical file-alias targets, matching Doctor’s canonical SQLite naming while preserving lexical-name support.
- Extend the same create/verify/archive-member/restore regression with both unconfigured-store routes and an alias-only registration. Exact archive paths prevent shared-basename false positives. Defaults, source originals, look-alikes, manifest reporting, whole PostgreSQL-directory omission and live database restoration remain covered.

The unconfigured-store defect fails on published `230674856fe149723df1b81585f277821ac2c3c4`; the physical-alias defect separately fails with the first repair already applied. Both fail at the actual archive-member omission assertion, then pass after the complete repair. Secretless focused proof passes **32 tests across four files**, focused formatting/lint, core typecheck and infra-test typecheck. The wrapped test command takes 84.01 s including cold worker preparation; the primary archive scenario takes about 6 s because it creates, verifies and restores real archives.

Local Auto Review covered the complete staged candidate against `5a2b6e131c309f6986e44509e95ee659302caab9` at P0–P2 and was scoped-clean; the staged bytes were committed unchanged as `88285352f5994b9b8f4e554b1868776fd3c64859`. A separate fresh independent source review found no likely/high-impact P0–P2 findings. The initial local review’s two INDEX-only findings were resolved by staging the already tested repairs; that earlier incorrect-index verdict is not called clean.

The optional full `check:changed` remains **failed** at the dead-export scan: the same normalized set of 58 reported exports is reproduced on a fresh unmodified copy of `230674856fe149723df1b81585f277821ac2c3c4`. All other selected checks completed successfully; no skip or baseline exception was enabled. [Exact new-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43303668867) remains the required broad proof; the local attribution does not waive it. Synthetic PostgreSQL originals exercise directory omission, not live PostgreSQL capture; Windows was not newly exercised.

The original CLI/upgrade measurements and command receipts below retain their original executing revisions and are not relabeled as executions of the corrected head.

**Shipped CLI, real Doctor originals.** On an isolated state directory, OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (latest stable)
created an agent. Current main's `openclaw doctor --fix` then migrated the databases (agent schema 27 to 41,
state 22 to 39), which left three real originals: one agent `.bak`, one state `.bak` and one state
`.scoped.bak`. Doctor writes the other two formats only during PostgreSQL migrations and restart-recovery
repairs, so I added one of each with Doctor's exact names (a restart-recovery copy of the agent database and a
`.postgres.bak` directory with a 4,096-byte file), plus two look-alikes that must stay
(`...pre-startup-migration-notauuid.bak`, `...pre-startup-migration-<uuid>.bak.old`). Each run below is
`node openclaw.mjs backup create` from a `pnpm build` of main dc0ab0240fa or of this branch rebased on it.

| Run | Members | Uncompressed bytes | Doctor originals in archive | Compressed bytes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| main, default `--verify` | 63 | 5,381,400 | 5 (3 real, 2 added) | 180,402 |
| this PR, default `--verify` | 64 | 5,494,001 | 5 | 197,093 |
| this PR, `--exclude-migration-backups --verify` | 58 | 2,648,564 | 0 | 134,488 |

- Main rejects the flag: `OpenClaw does not recognize option "--exclude-migration-backups".`
- Default archives have the same member names on main and on this PR. The one extra member on this PR,
  `state/openclaw.sqlite.seal` (112,601 bytes), is the state database's clean-close seal. It appeared on disk
  between the two runs and is unrelated to this change.
- On this PR, the flagged archive lacks exactly six members compared with the default one: the three real
  originals, the restart-recovery file, and the PostgreSQL directory with its file. Both look-alikes stay.
  The manifest grows by 1,283 bytes for the five new `skipped` entries (the directory is listed once).
- Main and the default run each warn five times about SQLite files archived as opaque bytes, four of them for
  the originals. The flagged run keeps only the unrelated warning.
- `backup restore` of the flagged archive into a fresh target returns `ok: true` and
  `sqliteInventoryVerified: true`, and restores 58 entries. The only `pre-startup-migration` names in the
  target are the two look-alikes. The restored agent and state databases pass `PRAGMA integrity_check` at
  `user_version` 41 and 39, the same as live.
- Every `pre-startup-migration` file on disk has the same SHA-256 before and after all runs.

<details>
<summary>Text output with the flag</summary>

```
Skipped 9 paths:
- workspace: ~/.openclaw/workspace (missing)
- agent: ~/.openclaw/agents/work/agent (covered by ~/.openclaw)
- plugin skills: ~/.openclaw/plugin-skills (regenerable)
- managed state: ~/.openclaw/tmp (regenerable)
- migration backup: ~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite.pre-startup-migration-11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555.postgres.bak (excluded)
- migration backup: ~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite.pre-startup-migration-cc3f463f-378c-4112-812f-e4bf675240eb.scoped.bak (excluded)
- migration backup: ~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite.pre-startup-migration-e9a1d31a-6dfc-8015-86ba-d688b1710ad5.bak (excluded)
- migration backup: ~/.openclaw/agents/work/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite.pre-startup-migration-e9a1d31a-6dfc-8015-86ba-d688b1710ad5.bak (excluded)
- migration backup: ~/.openclaw/agents/work/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite.pre-startup-migration-restart-recovery-11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555.bak (excluded)
```

</details>

**Regression tests.** In `src/infra/backup-create.ownership.test.ts` ("backup Doctor migration originals"),
a default archive contains full, scoped and restart-recovery agent originals, a full state original, and a
PostgreSQL backup directory with nested content. A flagged archive omits exactly those and keeps look-alike
names. It lists each one as `excluded` in the result and manifest, and lists the directory only once. The
archive restores, and the originals stay on disk. With only this test file applied to main dc0ab0240fa, it
fails (`AssertionError: expected true to be false` on the first flagged archive member check); with this
change it passes. In `src/commands/doctor-migration-backup-names.test.ts`, every produced name round-trips
through the classifier and look-alikes are rejected. A restore manifest accepts full and scoped originals and
rejects PostgreSQL and restart-recovery paths.

**Checks run** (rebased on main dc0ab0240fa)

- `pnpm test src/infra/backup-create.ownership.test.ts src/commands/doctor-migration-backup-names.test.ts`:
  15 and 3 passed.
- Consumers of the changed plan, names, manifest and CLI: `backup-resource-inventory`, `backup-shared`,
  `doctor-migration-backup`, `doctor-session-sqlite-recovery-inventory`, `doctor-session-entry-state`,
  `update-command-missing-originals`, `update-cleanup.stored-manifests`, `update-automatic-cleanup`:
  8 files, 102 tests passed.
- `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet`: OK (slack 0). Main dc0ab0240fa alone is 6 lines over its ceiling.
- `pnpm check:import-cycles`, `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles`, `pnpm format:docs:check`, `pnpm lint:docs`: pass.
- `pnpm check:changed`: formatting, core and test typechecks, lint, ratchets, import cycles and the other
  guards pass. The dead export scan fails on 17 files this PR does not touch (for example
  `src/process/linux-oom-score.ts`, `extensions/knowledge/src/tool-results.ts`). `pnpm deadcode:exports` on main dc0ab0240fa fails with the identical list.
- The CI `check-lint-core-4` failure on the previous head was a `no-shadow` error in
  `ui/src/e2e/sidebar-rail-alignment.e2e.test.ts`, which this PR does not touch; main has since fixed it.

Not covered: an end-to-end run against a live PostgreSQL server (the directory exclusion is covered by the
regression test and the hand-made directory above) and Windows.

## Current maintainer validation

The current branch incorporates main and retains the shared Doctor backup naming helper alongside PostgreSQL capture pruning. All 32 existing focused backup and Doctor tests pass. An isolated real CLI run verified default backup inclusion, opt-in exclusion, archive verification, and restoration: only the exact migration originals were excluded, lookalike names and source files remained intact, and the restored agent database passed its integrity check. Focused lint/format checks passed, and the matching candidate received an independent P0–P2 review with no actionable findings. CI on this published head is still pending.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Explicit standalone Session skill loading treats valid ignore patterns such as ` #private/` or a tab followed by `#private/` as comments. A matching /skill:name command can therefore expand the excluded file into a provider request.

## User Impact

User impact: Skill directories whose names begin with literal whitespace followed by a hash respect .gitignore/.ignore/.fdignore again, including nested rules. This concerns the explicit standalone Session resource loader; ordinary skills CLI/Gateway discovery is a different path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recognize comments by the raw first character, preserving authored leading whitespace. Drop a file-leading BOM before parsing so existing BOM comments still remain comments before nested prefixing and pattern-budget checks. One parser repair covers all three rule files and both depths.

## Evidence

Product head `6cd5d58d1769303cdd7eac8106918d55f11f36f9`; paired baseline `258d034391ac03a8ee3530ba33552a5cbf2062fc`.

- Production entry: Real standalone createAgentSession with DefaultResourceLoader resources_discover, bindExtensions, /skill:name prompt and the built-in OpenAI-compatible HTTP transport.
- Canonical owner exercised unmocked: src/shared/ignore-rules.ts through src/skills/loading/session.ts and the real standalone Session resource/prompt owner.
- Same scenario/command on both refs: `node proof-ignore-session.mjs CHECKOUT NEW_OUTPUT base|head`. The final version argument selects expected observations only.
- Acceptance-red: RED: three excluded leading-space/hash, tab/hash and nested-hash skill payloads appear in real loopback provider HTTP requests despite independent Git exclusions.
- Acceptance-green: GREEN: all three excluded payloads are absent. Each of seven real prompts still sends one HTTP request and completes with Proof complete.; ordinary visible, true-comment and BOM-comment skills still expand.
- Recorder/readback: Actual loopback /v1/chat/completions request bodies, final assistant replies and serialized real native Session/branch state. This is not a durable-transcript claim; excluded commands remain ordinary prompt text rather than being rejected.
- Controls: Seven real Session turns per ref. Excluded marker count is 3 on base and 0 on head; escaped-hash control stays absent on both. Three visible/comment/BOM controls remain present. Read-only Git check-ignore independently agrees on all 7 authored statuses. All skill and rule-file hashes remain unchanged.

[Collector](https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/tree/78f6550de04261970f2ffc66f08b20ef63791b60/OC/proof/2026-11-04-new-families/proof-ignore-session.mjs) · [Actual paired output/readback](https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/tree/78f6550de04261970f2ffc66f08b20ef63791b60/OC/proof/2026-11-04-new-families/ignore-comments-readback.json) · [Artifact hashes](https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/tree/78f6550de04261970f2ffc66f08b20ef63791b60/OC/proof/2026-11-04-new-families/ignore-comments-manifest.json)

```json
}
```

Tests: `pnpm test src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts --maxWorkers=1; pnpm test src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. 11 owner tests passed in 7.05s wrapper wall; independent root/nested matchers across 3 rule files; net +21 test lines. Existing prompt-prefix contract is checked separately. Prompt-prefix stability: 14 tests passed, 221.78s wrapper wall including cold agent-worker compilation.

Normal exact-head source build, commit hooks, format, typed lint, targeted typecheck and test-line ratchet passed. Independent complete-candidate code review/test-audit passed with no unresolved findings. Hosted exact-head CI and automatic PR review have not run before PR creation.
