<summary>Owner coverage, scope and limits</summary>

The explicit Session loader supplies the shared matcher at root and each nested directory. The complete fix covers .gitignore/.ignore/.fdignore. Only skill-command selection changes; provider transport, system prompt and tool definitions are unmodified.

prs.title: fix(diffs): honor empty plugin allowlists for language packs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a valid empty plugins.allow list makes diffs ignore an installed, enabled language pack and discard an explicit extended language hint.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing public SDK plugin-config normalizer for the optional renderer availability projection. Restrict only a nonempty allowlist, matching the host activation contract, and keep normalized deny/entry-disable gates in that same owner. Preserve live config reads and actual manifest/runtime asset checks.

## User Impact

User impact: explicit Nix and other extended language hints retain syntax highlighting when the optional pack is available with an unrestricted empty allowlist. Disabled or excluded packs continue to produce plain text.

## Evidence

- Scenario: An installed enabled language pack retains explicit Nix hints with allow=[]; Explicit-allow and disabled/excluded controls preserve correct rendering
- Entry: Normally built Gateway -> public tools.invoke diffs mode=view, lang=nix and path=proof.txt -> separate actual HTTP viewer response -> real Chromium hydration and computed styles; disputed owner ran unmocked: extensions/diffs/src/plugin.ts availability projection -> real diffs render/viewer
- Same command on base `b3d0977` and head `53d90ea`: `node proof-diffs-language-pack.mjs CHECKOUT NEW_OUTPUT base|head`
  - Before (base): RED: real plugin inventory includes the enabled pack, but empty allowlist viewer readback has langs=[text], uses the base runtime, and hydrated code lacks Nix syntax colors. Explicit allowed-pack control has langs=[nix] and seven computed span colors.
  - After (head): GREEN: the identical empty-allowlist viewer retains langs=[nix], loads the actual pack runtime, hydrates normally and displays Nix syntax colors like the explicit-list control.
- Readback (http): Public tool output gives a tokenized viewer URL; independent HTTP fetch and real browser read the generated payload, hydrated shadow DOM and computed code colors.
- Proof harness: https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/tree/a71e0bb1a596216a2d79d07b5fc8f8fd2c20f1b6/OC/proof/2026-11-03-distinct-families
- Control: Actual HTTP payload contains 0 Nix hints for empty allowlist base and 1 language value for fixed head. Explicit allowed-pack positive control contains 1 on both; disabled/excluded negative control contains 0 on both. Every viewer reaches the real hydrated ready flag with 0 page errors; individual policy gates and both asset layouts are covered by the existing registration fixture.
- Other callers checked: One availability producer feeds both viewer and file rendering. Normalized global enabled/deny/nonempty allow/entry gates and actual sibling assets are checked together. Native proof covers mode=view; no screenshot-file rendering claim is made. Existing language normalization/render suites cover the shared downstream owner.
- Tests: pnpm test extensions/diffs/src/plugin.test.ts extensions/diffs/src/language-hints.test.ts extensions/diffs/src/render.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 (measured cost: 10 passed across 3 files; owner-suite process 13.68s wall. Full check costs are disclosed below.)
- Screenshots: ![screenshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Alix-007/openclaw/a71e0bb1a596216a2d79d07b5fc8f8fd2c20f1b6/OC/proof/2026-11-03-distinct-families/diffs-language-pack-base-empty.png) ![screenshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Alix-007/openclaw/a71e0bb1a596216a2d79d07b5fc8f8fd2c20f1b6/OC/proof/2026-11-03-distinct-families/diffs-language-pack-head-empty.png)
- Not tested: Image/file rendering mode, optional package installation/upgrade, physically remote Gateways, Windows/macOS, installed-release upgrades and exact-head hosted CI were not run locally. This uses the real source-built optional pack and real viewer, without a model or external channel.

[Inspectable collector and paired public-entry readback](https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/tree/a71e0bb1a596216a2d79d07b5fc8f8fd2c20f1b6/OC/proof/2026-11-03-distinct-families/diffs-language-pack-readback.json). Product head `53d90ea9257325e78681e9b723aa0379da5d3848`.

<details>
<summary>Validation and scope</summary>

Normal source build, commit hooks, formatting, ordinary typed lint, targeted types and test-line ratchet passed; 10 passed across 3 files. Independent gpt6.1-sol adversarial review covered the complete production/test/allocation diff from `b3d0977b0cc484c4b472628385d1a988a794ac42` to `53d90ea9257325e78681e9b723aa0379da5d3848` (tree `a1db88ea4f07c34e52f56fc69dcd32f66bf50f7f`), with zero findings, using the user-authorized fallback for unavailable official autoreview.

Outer process wall times: format 0.90s (exit 0); lint 353.10s (exit 0); types 94.98s (exit 0); test-lines 18.60s (exit 0); tests 13.68s (exit 0).

File additions/deletions:

```text

```

Existing-solutions preflight: Empty allowlists already mean unrestricted plugin selection in the host. The optional renderer must consume that existing policy; requiring a nonempty list is not a replacement for a correct live availability projection. prs.title: fix(ui): empty model picker leaves an effort-control gap on narrow screens
prs.body:
Related: #198751

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the new-session composer keeps an empty effort-control gap before the Dictate button on narrow screens when model discovery finds no models.

## User Impact

User impact: with no models available, the composer no longer shows a blank gap or a stray Speed fallback next to the model picker; the layout matches the populated state.

## Why This Change Was Made

#198751 restored a hidden effort slot on narrow screens, so the composer's geometry stays stable while the model catalog loads. The slot is still reserved after discovery confirms there are no model choices. Now the composer keeps the reservation only while discovery is pending, or while a provider is still resolving. Once the catalog is confirmed empty, it omits the whole effort control, including the provider-default Speed fallback. This also turns the scheduled `new-session-page.model-picker-spacing` e2e green again: at 390px it measured a 46px model-to-Dictate gap, against its 32px bound.

## Evidence

![Before: reserved empty effort slot. After: no unavailable effort control](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6fe68b18-9ff8-40c7-8e59-3c68e81b7e97)

Synthetic fixture, 390px viewport, no models configured. After the fix, the gap is 2px on mobile and 3px on desktop, and it stays the same while the picker opens and closes.

- `ui/src/e2e/new-session-page.model-picker-spacing.e2e.test.ts`: fails before the fix on both the pinned Bun runtime (12.83s) and Node (16.80s). After the fix, all nine spacing and catalog-arrival cases pass on both: Bun 22.20s, Node 35.89s. Reverting the component change brings the failure back on both.
- New regression in `ui/src/pages/new-session/model-control-view.test.tsx` covers three states. An unresolved catalog reserves the slot. An empty catalog with a pending provider keeps it. An accepted empty catalog removes the whole effort control, including the Speed fallback.
- The rest of the model-control and transcript-search unit tests pass on both runtimes; scoped lint and type checks pass.
- `chat-model-controls.e2e.test.ts > keeps independent model and effort controls within the chat composer` already fails on unmodified main, on both runtimes and with a non-empty catalog. This change doesn't touch that path; it stays a separate failure.

prs.title: fix(openai): ChatGPT GPT-Live calls ignore configured voice instructions
prs.body:
Related: #183590

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: configured voice instructions (persona, when to speak, reply style) are silently ignored when GPT-Live runs as `gpt-live-1-codex` on a ChatGPT subscription. This affects Discord voice, Voice Call and browser Talk.

## User Impact

User impact: operators on the ChatGPT-subscription GPT-Live route now get their configured instructions applied. For example, a Discord bot told "your name is Lachlan, only answer when addressed by name" now calls itself Lachlan and stays out of side conversations, instead of answering as ChatGPT. The API-key and public `gpt-live-1` routes are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

On the ChatGPT route, the provider does not apply the `instructions` sent with call setup. It also rejects changing instructions afterwards (`immutable_field_update`: "Instructions cannot be updated after initialization"). It does follow `session.context.append` on the `commentary` channel.

So, on that route only, the delegation controller now repeats the call instructions once as silent commentary context when `session.started` arrives, before readiness is reported. The text is sent through the existing context-append chunker; the provider caps each append at 500 tokens. The repeated text is the configured instructions plus the host-control rules. Shared call history stays out of that channel, so earlier-call records do not arrive as live instructions. One helper in `realtime-quicksilver-wire.ts` now owns the "is this the ChatGPT call route" check, which call creation already used.

Both the Gateway relay bridge and browser Talk pass the startup context, because both create the same ChatGPT call.

## Evidence

**Live reproduction (stock 2026.11.3, Discord gateway relay bridge, ChatGPT OAuth, `gpt-live-1-codex` / `cove`).** I drove OpenClaw's own `OpenAIQuicksilverGatewayBridge` with recorded speech clips over a real WebRTC call.
- **Configured instruction only:** "Answer every single thing anyone says with exactly one word: banana."
  - "Lachlan, are you ChatGPT?" → "Yep, I'm ChatGPT."
  - "Lachlan, what's the capital of France?" → "Paris."
- **`session.update` with instructions after start:** rejected with `immutable_field_update`.
- **Same text as a `session.context.append` (`commentary`) after `session.started`:** both questions answered "banana".

**With this change's behavior** (instructions repeated as chunked commentary context on session start), a realistic persona prompt is followed:
- **Identity:** "Lachlan, are you ChatGPT?" → "Nah, I'm Lachlan."
- **Staying quiet:** prompted to answer only when addressed by name, the model stayed silent for most unaddressed group chatter, which it previously answered almost every time.
- **Prompt quality still matters:** in one run it narrated its silence ("No name, so I'll stay out of it."). That is down to how the operator writes the prompt; this PR only fixes delivery.
- **Apparatus:** this live check used a patched build of the same delivery path, not this exact branch.

**Codex reference.** In `openai/codex` at `65a5410f72`, `codex-api/src/endpoint/realtime_websocket/methods_frameless_bidi.rs` (`session_json`) sends the same call-setup shape, with `instructions`. Its protocol (`RealtimeOutboundMessage::SessionContextAppend`, `RealtimeContextAppendChannel::Commentary`) is the context channel used here.

**Regression tests (red on the parent commit, green here).**
- `realtime-quicksilver-gateway-bridge.test.ts`: ChatGPT OAuth relay sends the multi-chunk instructions plus host-control rules as commentary context once, before `onReady`, and not again on a second `session.started`.
- `realtime-quicksilver-session.test.ts`: the same for browser Talk.
- `realtime-quicksilver-wire.test.ts`: startup context excludes shared history and is absent for API-key auth.
- The existing API-key relay test still asserts that nothing extra is sent on that route.

**Checks.**
- `pnpm exec vitest run` on the gateway-bridge, session, delegation and wire suites: 73 passed.
- `pnpm check:changed`: all lanes green, including format, extension lint, and extension and extension-test typecheck. The dead-export scan fails only on unrelated compaction exports (`findTurnStartIndexFromSource`, `SessionCompactionSourcePlan`, …) that also fail on `main`.

**Review.** One independent findings-only agent review of the change. Applied:
- history excluded from the repeated context;
- a single ChatGPT-route check;
- stronger multi-chunk and ordering tests.

Remaining low-risk note: on browser Talk, host speech sent after `session.ready` but before `session.started` can precede the instructions; the window ends when the SDP answer is applied. Local ClawSweeper is not installed here; a hosted ClawSweeper review is still needed.

**Gaps.**
- No isolated-gateway Discord e2e run of this exact branch.
- The API-key `gpt-live-1-codex` route (`/v1/live`) was not tested live, so it is left unchanged.

prs.title: fix(discovery): bound wide-area TXT fields before publication
prs.body:
Fixes #199045

## What Problem This Solves

Wide-area discovery can successfully write and serve a zone whose advertised values are already damaged. CoreDNS splits a TXT field above 255 bytes into multiple wire strings; DNS-SD interprets each string as a separate key/value entry. A long `displayName` or `cliPath` is therefore shortened, and a UTF-8 character can be split between entries.

## Changes

- Check each complete `key=value` field's UTF-8 size before zone-file escaping. Keep 255-byte fields valid, including quoted text and multibyte characters.
- Reject oversized fields with an actionable field-specific error before the atomic replacement. An existing valid zone stays byte-for-byte intact; a first-time invalid publication fails clearly rather than advertising a damaged value.
- Cover the boundary through the unmocked production writer. Keep the existing OS file-size failure test effective by using valid individual TXT fields whose escaped zone text still exceeds the imposed file limit.

The existing Gateway discovery owner reports publication failures as warnings. This changes the wide-area producer, with no new dependency or discovery protocol.

## Evidence

### Production writer → CoreDNS → DNS query

Ran seven cases on the base and the fix, each with a disposable state directory, the actual `writeWideAreaGatewayZone`, CoreDNS **1.15.0** and `dig` against a loopback listener. macOS 27.0.1 arm64, Node 26.12.1. All 14 server runs completed and their owned processes stopped.

| Complete field | Base | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `displayName`, ASCII, 255 bytes | Intact | Intact |
| `displayName`, ASCII, 256 bytes | Split into field + separate `"a"` entry | Rejected; prior zone preserved and still served |
| `cliPath`, ASCII, 255 bytes | Intact | Intact |
| `cliPath`, ASCII, 256 bytes | Split into field + separate `"a"` entry | Rejected; prior zone preserved and still served |
| `displayName`, UTF-8, 255 bytes | Intact | Intact |
| `displayName`, UTF-8, 256 bytes | Last `é` split between wire strings | Rejected; prior zone preserved and still served |
| `displayName`, quoted text, 255 bytes | Intact after escaping | Intact after escaping |

For each rejection, SHA-256 of the existing zone was identical before and after; a subsequent DNS query still returned the original synthetic discovery data. The proof uses the supported zone-file boundary, with synthetic addresses and loopback-only networking. It does not require a Tailnet or install a system DNS service.

releases.body:
## 2026.11.5-beta.3

### Highlights

- **Large-session reliability:** reduce memory pressure during transcript indexing, trimming, and compaction; stream only selected hydration payloads and honor configurable summary limits. (#194099, #194066, #194536, #196207) Thanks @vincentkoc, @aniruddhaadak80, @RomneyDa, @garrytan.
- **Restart and delivery safety:** preserve queued-message permission ceilings and accepted ingress during restarts, drain final chat writes before handoff, and retain delivery ownership through the final RPC. (#196540, #196923, #196493, #197427) Thanks @joshavant, @vincentkoc.
- **Recovery and setup:** improve cold-start initialization, interrupted workspace recovery, installer permissions, and actionable iMessage Automation status. (#192552, #196423, #186782, #186117) Thanks @javiermv, @anmol0b, @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc.

### Changes

- **Models and tools:** restore context-sized default output budgets, expose effective deferred MCP tools with bounded input hints, and deduplicate wrapped structured MCP results. (#193899, #196766, #196252, #196266, #196243) Thanks @RomneyDa, @jalehman, @GrahamMcBain, @VACInc, @vincentkoc.
- **Compaction:** support a configurable summary-character limit while retaining foreground request-budget constraints and redacting credentials in quoted summary content. (#196207, #197349) Thanks @aniruddhaadak80, @RomneyDa, @garrytan, @obviyus.
- **Browser and workspaces:** route Lightpanda navigation through its supported connection path and wait for sandbox files to become ready. (#196400, #197248) Thanks @RomneyDa, @mmaps.

### Fixes

- **Startup and updates:** retry transient shared-state schema admission, defer cold-start runtime initialization, preserve external-plugin data during update rehearsals, keep idle cron workers disabled, and split timed-out SQLite header probes. Conflicting legacy exec-approval files no longer prevent startup; canonical policy remains authoritative. (#195398, #192552, #196301, #196387, #193970, #194239, #196401) Thanks @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc.
- **Sessions and storage:** bound large-transcript indexing and trimming, stream selected compaction payloads, exclude consumed inputs from actor hydration, and recover cold PostgreSQL conversations after readers close. Preserve active turns across session rollover, settle suspended descendants, and repair persisted internal-wake titles. (#194099, #194066, #194536, #196277, #189991, #197345, #197323, #196362) Thanks @vincentkoc, @etzelm, @Jo2234, @obviyus, @abacha, @wr-web, @xRyann2255, @RomneyDa.
- **Authority and delivery:** require effective authority for delegated changes, apply input-policy hooks to prepared images, preserve accepted queued ingress and original permissions through restart, and wait for final writes within the existing restart budget. Keep final-delivery ownership until its RPC settles. (#196984, #196337, #196923, #196540, #196493, #197427) Thanks @joshavant, @vincentkoc, @RomneyDa.
- **Execution and progress:** collect process results at suspended capacity, retain accepted ClawHub attempts after timeouts, settle failed Code Mode calls without unresolved sibling waits, and detect silent model streams despite tool heartbeats. Bound silent Agents API startup and release retained completion authority for finished non-announcing children. (#196927, #196929, #196435, #196517, #196672) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- **Channels:** retain iMessage Automation warnings until an accepted send, avoid Slack reasoning-stream freezes, handle empty IRC channel sender lists, and preserve local final replies in history. Cron and system replies no longer use closed plugin scopes. (#186117, #196250, #196293, #187795, #196750) Thanks @MertBasar0, @anmol0b, @RomneyDa, @mmaps, @masatohoshino, @obviyus, @ptu-gh.
- **Provider setup:** retain Z.ai Coding Plan catalog models, deduplicate concurrent provider-catalog imports, preserve model API billing settings during config writes, recover cancelled Claude CLI login refreshes, and omit enums from non-string Gemini parameter schemas. (#195390, #196448, #191326, #197032, #196742) Thanks @jason-allen-oneal, @1052326311, @WG-Mojo, @etzelm, @obviyus, @kir1ll, @vincentkoc, @RomneyDa.
- **Diagnostics:** avoid repeated redaction and serialization during opt-in OpenTelemetry content capture, bound oversized image capture, and redact raw multiline strings before JSON escaping. (#186666, #194353) Thanks @651juan, @amittell, @mmaps.
- **Platform recovery:** compare Windows state paths case-insensitively, respect installer permission masks, and recover macOS LaunchAgents when Trash access is denied. Keep iOS gateway recovery reachable while reconnecting and remove legacy plaintext setup-code preferences; pasted setup codes stay in memory. (#185917, #186782, #189321, #191560, #197049) Thanks @YangManBOBO, @javiermv, @sukhdeepjohar, @obviyus, @TameTheGame, @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc.
- **Workspace and database recovery:** recover interrupted workspace turns, avoid false admission after resumed database copies, and keep stopped-database Doctor inspection read-only on full disks. Open nested repositories outside mirror paths correctly. (#196423, #194595, #196346, #196747) Thanks @mmaps, @ylcn91, @reisball, @fuller-stack-dev.
- **Interface and release routing:** keep session links and row actions usable on touch devices, avoid freezes from deep-path progress labels, and reject incompatible release routes. (#194840, #196282, #196878) Thanks @RomneyDa, @najef1979-code, @vyctorbrzezowski, @LeizhenZhang, @obviyus.

### Complete contribution record

This audited record covers the complete v2026.11.5-beta.2..7f4704ecaf79dc747db8d7c73c614ccd08204acd history: 50 in-range PRs + 0 retained seed-only PRs = 50 unique PRs. The generation manifest also supplies direct commits as editorial input; the grouped notes above prioritize user impact.

issues.title: WebUI inline code may become a scrolling block or show only a filename
issues.body:
## Description The WebUI's Markdown renderer has two related behaviors when displaying inline code: 1. A single-line inline-code span longer than 120 JavaScript UTF-16 code units, **if it is not first classified as a file reference**, is rendered as a block with horizontal scrolling rather than flowing with the surrounding paragraph. The cutoff depends on the string length, not the available width, so even prose placed in backticks can become a separate single-line scroller. 2. Before the length check, inline code that looks like a file path is immediately replaced by a file-reference chip. The path heuristic also matches some commands or explanatory text containing a path. Because the chip normally shows only the basename, part of the inline-code text can disappear from the visible message, even when the candidate is not previewable. The original text remains in the message source and is set as an `aria-label` and tooltip on the chip; this report is about the rendered presentation, not loss of stored message data. That DOM attribute does not guarantee access via every assistive technology, and a non-interactive chip is not keyboard-focusable for its tooltip. These behaviors can make inline text harder to read or hide part of it from view. It would be helpful to understand whether they are intended and discuss whether a different rendering would be appropriate. The two behaviors have different causes, but both occur in the same renderer: changing only the length cutoff would not affect the earlier file-reference conversion. The same renderer is also used for Markdown file previews and other WebUI surfaces, so any change needs to account for those uses as well as chat. ## Steps to Reproduce ### A. Long inline code becomes a separate scroller 1. Open the WebUI at a narrow width, for example approximately 350 CSS pixels, and ensure the available message column is narrow enough that the longer string exceeds it. The block-style switch itself is independent of the viewport width. 2. Arrange for an **assistant response**, rather than an ordinary user message, to contain the following exact Markdown. Alternatively, render the same strings directly with `MarkdownTextRenderer` in a component fixture. If asking a model to echo the sample, confirm that its response contains the exact text; model output is not deterministic. ```markdown Before `word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word wordx` after. Before `word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word word wordxx` after. ``` 3. The two inline-code strings contain 120 and 121 ASCII characters, respectively. Observe their layout and try to read the entire longer span. **Actual:** The 120-character example stays inline and can wrap. The 121-character example is rendered as a block with `whitespace-pre` and its own horizontal scroll area, separating the surrounding prose. ### B. Inline text is displayed as a file reference 1. Arrange for an assistant response, or a `MarkdownTextRenderer` component fixture in chat mode, to contain exactly: ```markdown Before `这是一段说明文字，最后引用 /tmp/sample.txt` after. ``` 2. Observe the inline content. The sentence is a synthetic example meaning “This is explanatory text ending with a reference to /tmp/sample.txt.” It does not require creating the sample file: the current conversion to a chip happens before availability is determined. **Actual:** The inline-code span is treated as a file reference. The chip's visible label is `sample.txt`, rather than the whole sentence. Availability only controls whether the chip can be opened; a failed lookup does not restore the visible sentence. In the component-level static render used for this report, the sample was reduced to that filename. The assistant-response/fixture distinction matters: ordinary user-message bubbles do not use the same Markdown-rendering path. ## Suggested Behavior The following behavior is proposed for discussion; maintainers may prefer a different approach or tradeoff. - A single-line inline-code span should remain inline and wrap according to the available width, whether it contains a short token, a long command, CJK text, or prose. - Whitespace in the parsed code content, including consecutive spaces and tabs, should remain visible and selectable rather than being collapsed by the CSS change. This does not require changing normal Markdown parsing or preserving Markdown delimiter characters. - File-looking inline code should not be reduced to a basename before the UI has established that the candidate can be previewed. While a probe is pending, fails, is unavailable, or cannot be performed, show the complete parsed inline-code content. - A file candidate confirmed as previewable may still use the existing file chip, with its preview and file actions. Existing fenced and indented code-block rendering should continue to work independently of the inline-code change. ## Relevant Logs No relevant gateway logs were collected. The behavior is in WebUI rendering; the reproduced component cases did not require an LLM request. ## Environment - **nanobot Version:** `0.4.1`, source revision [`5e9810c1ad22938e5245fbe5b7a0df938782bd42`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/commit/5e9810c1ad22938e5245fbe5b7a0df938782bd42). Upstream `main` was at this revision when checked on 2026-11-14; it may have moved since. - **Python Version:** `3.12.14` in the project environment; the interpreter used by the running gateway was not independently confirmed. - **Operating System:** Linux / Ubuntu 24.04 for the component checks. - **Channel / Platform:** WebUI; the component reproduction did not require a WebSocket connection. - **LLM Provider:** Not applicable to the component reproduction; no LLM request was required. - **Browser:** Headless Chrome was used for the component-level browser checks. The exact binary and version used for those checks were not separately recorded. - **Configuration:** No special configuration was identified as necessary for the component-level reproduction. ## Additional Context ### Code paths and current behavior The following links are pinned to the source revision used for this report: - [`MarkdownTextRenderer.tsx:551–587`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/5e9810c1ad22938e5245fbe5b7a0df938782bd42/webui/src/components/MarkdownTextRenderer.tsx#L551-L587) first calls `isLikelyFilePath(raw)`, then chooses the block-like branch when `raw.includes("\n") || raw.length > 120`. The branch uses `block`, `overflow-x-auto`, and `whitespace-pre`. - [`FileReferenceChip.tsx:208–225`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/5e9810c1ad22938e5245fbe5b7a0df938782bd42/webui/src/components/FileReferenceChip.tsx#L208-L225) applies a path-shaped heuristic, not a proof of user intent. For example, it can accept a sentence ending in `/tmp/sample.txt`. It also accepts paths containing spaces, which can be legitimate and must not simply be rejected. - [`FileReferenceChip.tsx:64–67, 88–96, 111–129`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/5e9810c1ad22938e5245fbe5b7a0df938782bd42/webui/src/components/FileReferenceChip.tsx#L64-L129) defaults to displaying the basename and puts the full candidate in an `aria-label` and tooltip. When non-interactive, the inner span has no button role or tab stop; actual assistive-technology exposure has not been tested. - [`MarkdownTextRenderer.tsx:85–125`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/5e9810c1ad22938e5245fbe5b7a0df938782bd42/webui/src/components/MarkdownTextRenderer.tsx#L85-L125) already probes availability and guards against stale effects using cancellation plus the path and resolver identity. Currently it renders a chip even while the result is pending or false; the probe only affects whether the chip is interactive. - [`MarkdownTextRenderer.tsx:513–523`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/5e9810c1ad22938e5245fbe5b7a0df938782bd42/webui/src/components/MarkdownTextRenderer.tsx#L513-L523) and [`:589–608`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/5e9810c1ad22938e5245fbe5b7a0df938782bd42/webui/src/components/MarkdownTextRenderer.tsx#L589-L608) handle normal fenced/indented code through `pre` and `MarkdownCodeBlock`. The `pre` renderer also has a fallback branch, so representative real Markdown inputs should be tested rather than assuming every possible `pre` follows one path. - [`globals.css:931–942`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/5e9810c1ad22938e5245fbe5b7a0df938782bd42/webui/src/globals.css#L931-L942) declares `overflow-wrap: anywhere` and then `word-wrap: break-word`. The latter is an alias for `overflow-wrap` and wins in the observed computed style. Any new override should be limited to inline code; block code should not change. Table cells need special attention because inline-code styles inside a table can change its min-content width and wrapping. Removing only `raw.length > 120` would leave the file-chip conversion unchanged. A previous component/browser experiment also showed that the existing short-inline-code styling can visually collapse consecutive spaces and tabs when applied to long content. In that experiment, `white-space: break-spaces` preserved the tested whitespace while permitting wrapping. That is evidence for a direction, not a complete cross-browser or clipboard guarantee. ### Proposed behavior 1. Remove the existing length cutoff for single-line code. Keep the existing newline-containing fallback for now and do not redesign the `pre`/code-block renderer. 2. Apply `white-space: break-spaces` and `overflow-wrap: anywhere` specifically to `.markdown-inline-code`. Preserve the original React `kids` and passed-through props; do not replace the content with a trimmed or reconstructed path string. 3. For an **inferred** inline-code file candidate, render the ordinary code element while its availability is pending, false, rejected, or cannot be checked. Switch to the existing interactive chip only when the current path and resolver have a positive preview result and an open callback is available. Keep the existing effect cleanup and path/resolver identity checks for streaming updates and session changes. 4. A positive result must mean the service actually returned `available: true`, rather than merely failing to say false. At this revision, [`api.ts:619–635`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/5e9810c1ad22938e5245fbe5b7a0df938782bd42/webui/src/lib/api.ts#L619-L635) treats a missing `available` field as true, and [`ThreadShell.tsx:727–750`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/5e9810c1ad22938e5245fbe5b7a0df938782bd42/webui/src/components/thread/ThreadShell.tsx#L727-L750) maps an `API route not found` error to true. The illustrative diff below changes both and also requires an explicit `true` from the temporary-chat probe. 5. Do not treat a probe as authorization. The backend continues to enforce the session's workspace scope and preview rules when a file is opened. A false probe can mean a missing file, denied access, an unsupported/binary file, a size limit, or an error; it does **not** prove that the original text was not a path. ### Illustrative diff for discussion This is a candidate based on the pinned revision, **not a complete, behavior-tested patch**. It does not include the necessary test updates. `git apply --check` confirmed that the diff matches the local revision; an in-memory TypeScript check of the WebUI build configuration produced no diagnostics. Neither check establishes runtime or visual behavior.
View the illustrative diff (unverified proposal) ```diff --- a/webui/src/components/MarkdownTextRenderer.tsx +++ b/webui/src/components/MarkdownTextRenderer.tsx @@ -90,8 +90,9 @@ function AvailableFileReferenceChip({ onOpen, + fallback, ...props -}: ComponentProps) { +}: ComponentProps & { fallback?: ReactNode }) { const path = props.previewPath || props.tooltipPath || props.path; const resolve = useFilePreviewAvailabilityResolver(); const [result, setResult] = useState(null); @@ -116,6 +117,9 @@ && result.path === path && result.available ); + if (fallback !== undefined && (!resolve || !onOpen || !resolvedAvailable)) { + return <>{fallback}; + } return ( - ); - } - const widePlainBlock = raw.includes("\n") || raw.length > 120; - if (widePlainBlock) { - return ( - - {kids} - - ); - } - return ( + const plainCode = raw.includes("\n") ? ( + + {kids} + + ) : ( ); + if (!documentPath && isLikelyFilePath(raw)) { + return ( + + ); + } + return plainCode; }, pre({ children: markdownChildren }) { const kids = Children.toArray(markdownChildren); --- a/webui/src/globals.css +++ b/webui/src/globals.css @@ -941,6 +941,11 @@ word-wrap: break-word; } + .markdown-content code.markdown-inline-code { + white-space: break-spaces; + overflow-wrap: anywhere; + } + .markdown-content pre, .not-prose pre { max-width: 100%; --- a/webui/src/lib/api.ts +++ b/webui/src/lib/api.ts @@ -631,7 +631,7 @@ { cache: "no-store" }, API_READ_TIMEOUT_MS, ); - return payload.available !== false; + return payload.available === true; } export async function fetchSessionAutomations( --- a/webui/src/components/thread/ThreadShell.tsx +++ b/webui/src/components/thread/ThreadShell.tsx @@ -736,19 +736,9 @@ const request = temporary ? client.requestMutation<{ available: boolean }>("temporary_chat.file_preview", { chat_id: chatId, path, probe: true, - }).then((result) => result.available) + }).then((result) => result.available === true) : fetchFilePreviewAvailability(getToken(), previewSessionKey, path); - const pending = request.catch( - (error: unknown) => { - if (error instanceof ApiError) { - if (error.status === 404 && /API route not found/i.test(error.message)) { - return true; - } - if ([400, 403, 404, 413, 415].includes(error.status)) return false; - } - return false; - }, - ); + const pending = request.catch(() => false); const entry: FilePreviewAvailabilityCacheEntry = { promise: pending, revision: filePreviewAvailabilityRevision, ```
### Tradeoffs and limits of the proposal - This intentionally changes pending and unavailable **inferred** references from gray file chips to full inline code. They no longer have the chip's file-action menu unless confirmed. Existing tests that require an unavailable inferred reference to remain a chip must be updated to reflect the agreed behavior; explicit Markdown file links are still rendered as chips. - The stricter shared resolver also changes an edge case for **explicit** file links: if the probe route is missing or an HTTP response omits `available`, they would no longer become interactive merely because the response was treated as success. If preserving the old explicit-link behavior is required, a separate confirmed/unavailable/unknown result or separate policy would need discussion. This repository documents same-version WebUI/gateway support; the proposal does not add an old-gateway compatibility fallback. - A positive preview probe proves only that the resolved target was previewable at that moment; it cannot prove that the author intended the entire inline-code span as a file reference. A command or sentence that happens to resolve to a real file can still be misclassified. If *all* original inline-code text must always remain visible, the product needs a stronger rule, such as preserving the full text even for successful inferred references or requiring an explicit reference syntax. This diff does not provide that stronger guarantee. - Probe results are cached by session/path. At this revision a positive result can be reused, while a negative result may be retried after the displayed message count changes. Files can change after probing, so results are not a real-time guarantee. The cache is not explicitly keyed by workspace scope; if the effective scope changes without a new session key, a stale result may affect whether the chip appears interactive. The actual open must still perform the backend checks. Scope-change reachability and cache invalidation need a focused test; no authorization bypass has been established. - Unrecognized long commands and paths, including paths without a recognized extension, would change from horizontal scrolling to natural wrapping. Short inline code would also use the whitespace-preserving style. The shared renderer means Markdown file previews and other uses need checking too. In particular, the CSS selector also matches inline code in Markdown tables; `overflow-wrap: anywhere` may change cell min-content widths and table layout, and that effect has not been measured. Decide whether to accept it or exclude table cells before adopting the diff. ### Suggested regression coverage - At 120 and 121 ASCII characters, and with longer English/CJK content, verify inline flow, readable wrapping, and no horizontal overflow in narrow and wide containers. Include long unbroken strings and surrounding text before/after the code. - Check consecutive spaces and tabs in the **parsed** code content, browser selection and, separately, actual clipboard output. Include short inline code, because its whitespace styling changes too. Markdown's normal parsing/normalization still applies. - For inferred candidates, cover pending, explicit true, false, rejected probe, absent resolver, and absent open callback. Verify that a sentence or command ending in a path remains complete when not confirmed; verify an actual previewable path with spaces can become an interactive chip. - Exercise streaming content changing from candidate A to B or ordinary code, late A responses, a resolver/session change, and a reachable scope change within the same session. Check that stale results do not convert the current content to the wrong chip. Account for the existing cache's refresh and invalidation behavior. - Test strict confirmation for missing/malformed `available`, missing HTTP route and temporary-chat responses. Check explicit file links as well as inferred ones, especially the deliberate shared-resolver behavior change. - Exercise normal fenced and indented code blocks, the `pre` fallback as reachable, Markdown document preview, and a Markdown table containing long inline code. Measure any table-width/wrapping change. Check confirmed-chip interactions: click/keyboard preview, tooltip, file-action menu and image quick look, plus assistive-technology access. Check that access-denied/out-of-scope paths remain protected by the backend. ### Verification performed and gaps - **Previously reproduced:** using the actual renderer component and built CSS in headless Chrome, the 120/121 cutoff was observed in 350/700-pixel setups in streaming and completed modes. A component-level static render of the path-like Chinese sentence showed only `sample.txt` as the visible chip label. - **Rechecked the exact examples in this report:** an in-memory bundle and static render of the current component produced the inline-code class at 120 ASCII characters, the block/scroll classes at 121, and a `sample.txt` chip label for the Chinese sentence. Static rendering is not a browser-layout, streaming, or end-to-end test; it does not exercise the asynchronous probe. - **Experimented previously:** in a temporary/in-memory variant that removed only the length cutoff, the tested consecutive spaces/tabs collapsed visually and in browser selection text; `break-spaces` preserved them in that experiment. The proposed combined diff above was not applied to the project for those experiments. - **Diff applicability:** `git apply --check` on the illustrative diff against the pinned source. This does not apply the diff or establish runtime correctness. - **In-memory type check:** the source files with this diff overlaid in memory were checked using the installed TypeScript compiler and `webui/tsconfig.build.json`; both the original and candidate produced zero diagnostics. This was not a build, test run, or verification of the CSS and UI behavior, and no source files were modified. - **Not verified:** runtime behavior of the combined proposed patch, updated automated tests, full WebUI end-to-end behavior, real system clipboard behavior, supported-browser coverage, or a release build. No source fix was implemented. - **Reproduction limitation:** this report does not include a standalone runnable component fixture or script; repeating the component checks requires a reader-supplied fixture or arranging the sample text in an assistant response. ### Related report [#4693: WebUI mobile responsive layout](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/issues/4693) is a closed, broader report involving narrow-screen Markdown/long-content overflow. A limited search of open and closed issues did not find an exact report of path-like inline text being rendered as a file reference; this is not proof that no duplicate exists.

issues.title: `gpt-image-1`, `dall-e-3` and `dall-e-2` are retired but still offered in the OpenAI image model list
issues.body:
### Bug Description

OpenAI retired `gpt-image-1` on October 23, 2026, and `dall-e-3` and `dall-e-2` on May 12, 2026 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations). Requests that name them now fail, but nanobot still offers all three in the OpenAI image model list:

- https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/ce3f36983d6bee40d1f4cee58f71f3a1888ea648/nanobot/providers/image_generation.py#L1096 (`OpenAIImageGenerationClient.model_options`, which the WebUI settings show as the OpenAI image models)

### Steps to Reproduce

1. In the WebUI settings, pick OpenAI for image generation.
2. Choose `gpt-image-1`, `dall-e-3` or `dall-e-2` from the model list.
3. Generate an image. The request fails because OpenAI no longer serves that model.

### Expected Behavior

The list offers only models OpenAI still serves. The default, `gpt-image-2`, still works, so dropping the three retired ids fixes it. OpenAI's replacement for `gpt-image-1` is `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` or `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, if you want to offer one of those instead.

### Environment

Not environment-specific: found by reading the code at commit ce3f369. Provider: OpenAI. Models: `gpt-image-1`, `dall-e-3`, `dall-e-2`.

---
Found by [Since](https://since.dev), which watches code for model and API retirements and opens the fix before the date. It's free for open source, and I work on it. Full scan of this repo: https://since.dev/scan/HKUDS/nanobot

Happy to open a PR if that helps.

- Mark a result as one part of the same parent turn when sibling background tasks still owe announcements.

prs.title: fix(search): find matches in BOM-encoded text files
prs.body:
## Problem

The Python `grep` tool treats BOM-marked UTF-16 and UTF-32 files as binary and skips them. UTF-8 files with a BOM are decoded with the BOM still present, so an anchored first-line pattern such as `^needle` does not match. The same text can already be read by `read_file` and the document reader.

## Fix

Use the existing BOM decoder from the document utility before applying the ordinary binary check and UTF-8 fallback. Keep undecodable data rejected, file reads bounded, and ordinary binary-file handling unchanged.

## Tests

- Three real-file regressions exercise UTF-8 with BOM, UTF-16, and UTF-32 through `GrepTool.execute`, checking the matched text, line number, and surrounding context. All three fail on unchanged main.
- Search, filesystem, and document suites: 178 passed (`tests/tools/test_search_tools.py`, `tests/tools/test_filesystem_tools.py`, `tests/test_document_parsing.py`).
- Touched-file Ruff checks, strict BasedPyright for `search.py`, and `git diff --check` passed on Python 3.12.

Native ripgrep and channel behavior are unchanged. Cross-platform CI remains to run.

prs.title: fix(agent): preserve whitespace across streamed continuations
prs.body:
## Why

When an answer hits the output limit and continues in another model request, a newline or indentation at the join can disappear from the streamed answer. Resetting the progress buffer at every provider segment causes each segment's outer whitespace to be trimmed independently.

## What changed

- Keep the accumulated stream buffer and inline-reasoning extractor while the next segment continues the same logical answer; reset them at the actual message boundary.
- Add a runner-level regression covering trailing newlines, leading indentation, mid-word continuation, and reasoning emitted exactly once.

## Scope

This only changes streaming continuation boundaries. It does not insert separators, change the continuation policy, or change provider requests.

## Blast Radius

The shared streaming progress hook serves multiple channels. Retaining the buffer must not leak text or reasoning across tool-work or new-input boundaries; the existing runner and reasoning tests remain in place.

## Verification

- New regression before the fix: **2 failed, 1 passed**; the failures reproduce the lost newline and indentation.
- `pytest tests/agent/test_runner_progress_deltas.py tests/agent/test_progress_inline_reasoning.py tests/agent/test_runner_reasoning.py tests/agent/test_runner_core.py tests/agent/test_runner_injections.py -q`: **107 passed**.
- Ruff on the two changed files and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Isolated real gateway with a deterministic local OpenAI-compatible SSE provider: `line 61\n` ending in `length`, then `line 62` ending in `stop`. Live deltas, the terminal persisted stream snapshot, and the rendered WebUI all preserve `line 61\nline 62` after two model requests. The initial driver incorrectly concatenated cumulative history snapshots; the corrected audit verified the same recorded run without repeating model actions.

These checks were run on the unchanged source snapshot being published. Browser verification used the Vite client and synthetic model responses; no production build or external-provider rerun was performed. Full-project validation is left to remote CI.

prs.title: fix(gateway): avoid restarting stopped systemd services
prs.body:
## Why

Stopping a gateway installed as a systemd user service currently kills the process, but the generated `Restart=always` unit starts it again. Foreground conflict messages also incorrectly assume the process belongs to a terminal.

## What changed

- Restart the generated systemd service on failure rather than on a clean termination, including SIGTERM.
- Give supervisor-aware guidance for foreground start and restart conflicts.
- Document service stop and how to regenerate existing units after upgrading.

## Scope

Addresses #6624 for newly generated or reinstalled units. Existing units and custom overrides are not changed automatically. The CLI does not identify the supervising unit or stop it through systemd; a forced SIGKILL or an already-pending service restart can still cause a restart. Use `systemctl --user stop` to stop the service reliably in those cases.

## Tradeoffs

A clean gateway exit no longer triggers an automatic restart; abnormal failures still do. Service enablement is unchanged, so it may start again on a future login.

## Verification

- `/home/cyr/app/nanobot/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/gateway tests/cli/test_gateway_commands.py -q` — 101 passed, 9 skipped.
- `ruff check` on the changed Python files — passed.
- The new unit-rendering and CLI guidance assertions failed before the changes and passed afterwards.
- Real systemd lifecycle verification remains outstanding: this environment has no user systemd bus (`systemd-run --user` cannot connect). Please verify stop beyond `RestartSec` and restart after an abnormal failure on a systemd host.

## Credit

Thanks to @IndigoC for reporting the issue, providing the reproduction, and identifying the systemd restart policy.

prs.title: fix(webui): settle interrupted turns before replaying follow-ups
prs.body:
## Why

After a gateway restart, a persisted follow-up can replace an interrupted request and finish successfully while the existing WebUI page still shows Stop and treats new input as queued. Startup recovery never persisted a terminal identity for the old turn, so the client's completion fence correctly refuses to close it merely because a newer turn finished.

## What changed

- After restoring session context at startup, persist `interrupted` completion facts for the unfinished transcript tail before requeuing follow-ups.
- Exclude queued follow-up identities and leave existing completion records, including `transcript_incomplete` markers, unchanged.
- Cover interruption before model activity, after activity, and during a recovery turn, plus repeat-scan idempotence and pending-input preservation. Exercise the existing persistence-failure guard with a real incomplete history fact instead of a mocked tail predicate.

## Scope

This fixes startup recovery of the unfinished transcript tail. It does not weaken frontend completion fences, clear all client runs, change recovery confirmation, or replay completed tool work.

## Blast Radius

Startup recovery writes durable history before any new work is admitted. These completion facts must identify only the interrupted execution, never the queued follow-up; existing incomplete-transcript safeguards remain authoritative.

## Verification

- New recovery regression before the fix: **2 failed**, both missing the interrupted turn's terminal identity.
- `pytest tests/session/test_recovery.py tests/session/test_session_message_recovery_boundary.py tests/agent/test_loop_recovery.py tests/utils/test_webui_transcript.py -q`: **111 passed**.
- `bun run test src/tests/nanobot-client.test.ts src/tests/useReconnectRuns.test.tsx`: **118 passed**, including the explicit-completion and incomplete-transcript protections.
- Ruff on the two changed files and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Isolated real gateway and WebUI: keep the page open, execute a tool once, block the next model response, and send a cross-session follow-up through `send_session_message`. After a normal stop/start, the old turn has an explicit interrupted completion, the follow-up answers exactly once with its input identity, and the tool side effect remains at one. The original page becomes idle without a reload; pressing Enter sends a subsequent message normally.

These checks were run on the unchanged source snapshot being published. Browser verification used the Vite client and deterministic synthetic model responses, not a production build or external-provider rerun. Connection errors were observed during the intentional downtime. Full-project validation is left to remote CI.

prs.title: fix(webui): preserve oversized turn history with record pagination
prs.body:
## Summary

A single WebUI turn can exceed the replay budget while still fitting in SQLite. The old selector retained selected records and silently omitted the rest, with no cursor to retrieve the missing answers, reasoning, or tool activity. This changes oversized turns to contiguous record-level pages instead of sampling them.

Resolves [NAN-418](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-418/修复-webui-超大单轮历史回放被静默截断)

## Changes

- Add bidirectional record-position cursors, stable record identities, and history generations. Preserve the 4,000-record / 20 MiB selected-source page budgets, including expanded context graphs, without rewriting existing history.
- Reassemble adjacent fragments, deduplicate overlapping records, continue through invisible telemetry pages, and preserve navigation and the reader's scroll anchor.
- Make live-text coverage explicit at its owner: the existing outbound text buffers persist `text_from_seq` on end snapshots. It covers only the same turn, text phase and stream through the snapshot sequence. Tools and other streams inside that interval are not implicitly covered. The field follows actual buffer continuation/reset, including signed media and failed appends.
- Use this coverage plus installed event identities instead of client-side concatenation, text-prefix matching, or a separate snapshot/live matching map. Rebuild a fragment only when uncovered live contributions remain. Keep missing historical ranges and lifecycle completion distinct from text coverage.
- Preserve incomplete-turn canonical answer recovery, legacy missing-user backfill, Temporary Chat, and the current main input-identity contract. Recovered prompt anchors remain navigable even when the referencing answer is on another page. Exceptional canonical/navigation recovery retains its existing scope outside the selected-source page budget.

Client and gateway ship together; no old-client compatibility branch, database migration, or per-delta persistence is added. The synchronization design follows the explicit cursor/gap principles in [Matrix sync](https://spec.matrix.org/v1.16/client-server-api/#syncing) and [Telegram updates](https://core.telegram.org/api/updates), not a new generic IM framework.

## Review repairs

- Prompt navigation and whole-turn reads now use the same recovery eligibility check, including all known backfilled inputs. The six-record A/B reproducer keeps B's own answer and the incomplete marker.
- The gateway explicitly declares when a terminal fragment contains canonical replacement answers. Fragment joining withdraws the superseded stored answers, retaining reasoning and tools; deferred withdrawals survive gap filling and cache restore. An already-open transcript and a fresh read show the same final answer once.
- Accepted history acknowledges ordinary and cross-session user inputs by stable input/message identity rather than transport sequence alone. Confirmed live inputs no longer prevent accepting a recreated session, while genuinely unpersisted inputs remain protected.

## Verification of review repairs

- Focused Python record paging, prompt navigation and transcript tests: **99 passed**.
- Frontend transcript, parser, prompt history, streaming, reconnect and cache tests: **306 passed**.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.browser.json` and the history hydration browser suite: **16 passed**, including the new rendered recovery/refresh/reload regression.
- Real synthetic SQLite with the unchanged 4,000-record page budget: active `[1,4001)` and recovered `[2,4002)` payloads passed into production `ThreadTranscript.accept`. Before repair the open window showed both partial and final answers; after repair it matches a fresh window and retains one final answer when older history is loaded.
- Each reported failure was reproduced before repair. `git diff --check` passed. The first remote WebUI job stopped at TypeScript errors in the new test helper; an annotation-only follow-up narrows it to the user-message event type, and local `bun run typecheck` now passes. Full-project validation remains remote CI; no full-project PASS is claimed.

## Performance repair

The follow-up removes the measured repeated work: completion metadata no longer triggers a separate UI projection, source matching and sorted coverage ranges are indexed, and answer/wire lookups no longer scan every rendered row. Scratch replay owns its mutable collections; live projection and saved checkpoints retain copy-on-write isolation. An unchanged canonical prefix is reused for appended or repeated reads. A changed prefix, recovered answer, or changed event content invalidates replay instead of trusting the event ID alone. Prepending an earlier prefix can still require rebuilding the affected turn; it no longer performs the former quadratic matching/scanning work.

Five alternating baseline/candidate trials used the same synthetic SQLite-generated 12,000 records in three 4,000-record pages, independent headless Chrome contexts and identical workloads. The baseline is `c975ec652`; the measured candidate is `5fbb3bfa5`. Complete normalized rows, model-request state, projection cursors, closures, live-journal lengths and retained-record counts agree in every trial.

| Frontend workload | Baseline median | Optimized median | Optimized observed range |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Accept page at 4,000 accumulated records | 52.9 ms | 8.2 ms | 7.8–9.9 ms |
| Accept older page at 8,000 accumulated records | 408.9 ms | 17.6 ms | 15.9–23.2 ms |
| Accept older page at 12,000 accumulated records | 981.9 ms | 38.7 ms | 26.5–44.0 ms |
| Append page reaching 12,000 records | 678.5 ms | 21.7 ms | 18.6–23.7 ms |
| Refresh unchanged 3,000-event history | 40.42 ms | 4.34 ms | 4.22–4.54 ms |

These are synchronous component measurements, excluding HTTP/JSON parsing and React/layout/paint. A separate production-built `ThreadShell` browser fixture traversed the actual 120-message render windows and all three HTTP pages: final-page parsed-response-to-rendered-frame time fell from **1,187 ms** (1,128–1,398) to **361 ms** (285–423). The frame boundary uses two animation frames after the rendered commit; it is not a native display timestamp. The longest observed task in that interval fell from 1,112 to 275 ms, so this is not a claim of zero main-thread stalls or a sub-50-ms entire page render. No real model call or production conversation was used, and host load was not controlled.

The ordinary 40-event core path measured 0.173 → 0.220 ms; processing 4,000 live chunks in batches of ten measured 1.68 → 1.94 ms (p95 2.4 → 3.1 ms). These small absolute costs are disclosed rather than claiming zero regression. A live-to-history acknowledgement probe preserved all 64,000 answer characters and cleared the journal. The previously declared core target (<50 ms median, observed tail <100 ms for the third page) is met; the first unsuccessful optimization series and all raw trials remain preserved locally.

Current-head local verification: **456 focused frontend tests**, **25 browser tests**, import boundaries, lint, TypeScript checks, production build and `git diff --check` passed. The browser suite covers canonical recovery, cumulative hosted-tool streams, cache restore, live/history races and ordering. The previous remote active-resume test expected the old completion-only admission behavior; its fixture now uses the actual `text_from_seq` contract and asserts the saved missed prefix before accepting the next live suffix. The same catch-up behavior was independently reproduced on the prior published baseline before changing the assertion.

Full-project validation is [remote CI for this head](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/42992955792); it was still running at the publication check. No full-project PASS is claimed. Task-owned measurement servers have been stopped; source snapshots, raw results and build/test logs are retained in `D:\dev\nanobot-6586-optimize-20261111`.

## Earlier verification of the rebased follow-up

- Focused Python history/outbound/backfill/prompt/contract tests: **154 passed**.
- Focused frontend transcript/API/stream/reconnect/navigation/viewport/client tests: **486 passed**.
- History hydration browser tests: **15 passed**, including desktop/mobile live/history races, delayed covered chunks, cache return, and fragment reading position.
- Production `bun run build` and `git diff --check`: **passed**. Rebased dependencies were installed from the existing frozen lockfile. Local basedpyright was unavailable; full lint/typecheck/project checks are left to remote CI.
- Fresh isolated real gateway + built WebUI: **4,205-record** and **1,455-record / 26.76 MiB** synthetic turns. Checked older scrolling and expanded reasoning/tool activity for both, plus reload and prompt navigation followed by newer scrolling for the bytes turn. Public HTTP traversal verifies all unique event identities and equal order in both directions for both turns, and both prompts remain navigable. Records ranges are `[0,205)` + `[205,4205)` backward and `[0,4000)` + `[4000,4205)` forward; bytes ranges are `[0,115)` + `[115,1455)` backward and `[0,331)` + `[331,1455)` forward.
- Live-stream concurrency is exercised by controlled browser wire fixtures and gateway outbound/persistence/restart tests; the real gateway history acceptance does not call an external model or use the user's production conversation. Both old and new previews are stopped, with runtime/session/evidence directories preserved.

The older head's CI results do not validate this rebased head. Current full remote CI status is tracked by the PR checks; no full-project PASS is claimed here.

## Size and scope

The convergence follow-up removes 51 net lines from `thread-transcript.ts` and deletes its separate text-matching inference. Including the backend coverage contract, rebased input-backfill correction, and retained regression tests, the follow-up is **12 files, +247/-151** (implementation net **+1**, tests net **+95**). The review repair and test-type correction touch **9 files, +190/-27**. The performance follow-up touches **7 files, +339/-77**. The complete PR is now **34 files, +3,463/-377**; it has not become a small patch. The improvement is a clearer synchronization contract, not merely relocating code or dropping coverage.

prs.title: perf(webui): streamline model preset saves
prs.body:
## Why

Creating a model preset waits for two consecutive settings mutations, and each constructs a full settings response that can include expensive usage aggregation. A failure between the two mutations can leave the new preset created but not enabled in the call order.

## What changed

- Create and append a preset to the current server-side call order in one serialized configuration change, with one runtime refresh and response.
- Let capable clients omit usage from model create/update responses and retain their existing usage snapshot; other settings reads and old clients retain their previous response shape.
- Advertise the optimization as an optional WebUI capability. A client connected to an older supported host keeps the previous two-step save behavior.

## Scope

Model preset creation and edits only. The general `/api/settings` response and the separate usage endpoint remain unchanged. Legacy model configurations still require conversion before an order can be changed.

## Blast Radius

Model settings, configuration persistence, WebUI mutation compatibility across hosts, and the retained usage snapshot. A validation failure during the combined operation does not persist either change; a failure after the configuration has already been written is not claimed to be transactional with response delivery.

## Verification

- Python: `pytest tests/webui/test_settings_api.py tests/webui/test_settings_models.py tests/webui/test_settings_routes.py tests/webui/test_client_contract.py -q` — 223 passed.
- WebUI: `bun run typecheck` and `bun run test src/tests/api.test.ts src/tests/settings-models.test.tsx` — 167 passed. The test runner emitted React `act(...)` warnings.
- Ruff and focused ESLint passed; `git diff --check` passed.
- Isolated local Python operation timing, five alternating trials per side, fresh usage cache with 38,715 synthetic records and one existing preset: median 249.51 ms → 28.90 ms (ranges 243.82–257.28 ms and 27.72–29.01 ms). Each trial verified the persisted call order. This measures server operations directly, not WebSocket transport or browser end-to-end latency; no claim is made about the observed historical request.
- Real browser/remote-host compatibility and CI are not yet verified.

Resolves [NAN-436](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-436/加快模型-preset-保存并移除无关用量统计等待)

prs.title: fix(webui): correlate chat requests and cancel stale reconnects
prs.body:
## Why

Creating or forking a topic during reconnect could open an existing topic instead, and a timed-out queued request could still create a chat later. Closing the client during reconnect token refresh could also reopen it or apply stale authentication. Give chat requests and reconnect work explicit ownership so late events cannot complete a different operation.

## What changed

- Match new-topic, temporary-chat, and fork successes and expected errors by `request_id`. The gateway echoes the ID; unrelated attachments and errors cannot complete a creation request.
- Keep creation requests in one `queued / sent` owner, separate from the reconnect replay queue. Timeouts release the pending request, expired unsent work is removed, sent work is never automatically replayed, and late temporary creations are discarded.
- Abort in-flight reauthentication before applying bootstrap state, settle connection-owned requests synchronously on close, and ignore callbacks from replaced sockets. Update protocol and user-facing timeout documentation.
- Focus the added regression coverage on distinct failures: 18 added cases instead of 44. Shared request handling is tested with representative lifecycle flows; all three creation commands retain ID-correlation coverage and temporary-chat disposal remains covered. Existing UUID-shim and untagged WebSocket/TUI coverage is reused instead of adding duplicate combinations.

## Scope

Support and test coverage are limited to same-version WebUI/gateway combinations, including remote gateways. Cross-version combinations may work but have no compatibility guarantee, even when protocol checks pass; align versions first when troubleshooting. This is a support policy, not a package-version equality gate: connections are not rejected solely because package versions differ.

This PR does not add chat-request capability negotiation or untagged response matching for older gateways. It fixes the confirmed WebUI lifecycle defects without rewriting application state machines or changing cron policy, tool-result durability, process startup, ordinary-message replay, or TUI behavior.

The shared WebSocket API still accepts requests without IDs for current callers such as the TUI; this is not a WebUI fallback to an older gateway. Existing unrelated capabilities are unchanged.

## Tradeoffs

A timeout does not prove that creation failed. The user can initiate another request with a different ID, but the client does not automatically retry the old operation. Correlation IDs are not an exactly-once or deduplication promise. WebUI protocol remains 1.

## Blast Radius

WebUI connection/bootstrap handling and the gateway's chat-creation envelopes. Existing session data, execution ownership, authentication checks, workspace permissions, and message payload semantics are unchanged. No new `ready` capability field is introduced. The support-policy and test-consolidation follow-up does not change runtime code.

## Verification

- Follow-up: `cd webui && bun run test src/tests/nanobot-client.test.ts src/tests/app-layout.test.tsx src/tests/temporary-chat-navigation.test.tsx src/tests/main-randomuuid.test.tsx`: **4 files / 261 tests passed**.
- Follow-up: WebUI lint and typecheck, Ruff on both changed Python test files, Python syntax parsing, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Local Python regression execution is unavailable in the current environment because `pytest` is not installed. Full Python, browser, and TUI verification for the follow-up is delegated to the latest-head CI checks.
- Before the follow-up, [Test Suite](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/43004728027) passed for `d18fe83cff9ba8bf7addd11d9f030b857065ede7`: 12 checks succeeded; native package acceptance and Windows installer compatibility were skipped. See the PR checks for the follow-up head's results.

Resolves [NAN-432](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-432/修复-webui-会话创建与连接生命周期竞态)

prs.title: refactor(agent): clarify run-local input and checkpoint ownership
prs.body:
## Why

Changing injected-input preparation currently requires understanding queue snapshots, rollback, authorization, terminal waiting and checkpoint closures inside `_run_agent_loop`. Give the run-local queue state one owner and make the Loop–Runner adapters explicit, without replacing the existing execution or persistence model.

Resolves [NAN-188](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-188/评估并改进-agent-执行生命周期与隔离边界)

## What changed

- Extract `PendingInputs` to own each batch's FIFO boundary, rollback and shared terminal-wait deadline; keep channel/workspace/runtime-context preparation in `AgentLoop`.
- Type Runner checkpoint payloads and move persistence adaptation to a named method; retain private provider-state handling and `SessionState` commits.
- Scope existing context bindings with `ExitStack`, and cover cancellation during input conversion while another run is making its model request.

## Scope

Behavior-preserving execution-boundary refactor. FIFO barriers, input authority, follow-up acknowledgement, generation checks, recovery and background-task lifetime stay with their current owners. No new scheduler, task UI, replay behavior, persistent format or tool-reload policy.

The accompanying [design record](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/document/nanobot-执行生命周期与隔离边界评估-1cc3dbb675bc) records the existing MCP live-reload interleaving separately; this PR does not silently choose between immediate revocation, idle-only changes and retained in-flight connections.

## Tradeoffs

Moving every closure to a Loop method would leave the queue/deadline lifecycle threaded through the adapter. A small run-local buffer gives that state a coherent lifetime without receiving the entire Loop or Session. This improves ownership and readability, not net line count or measured performance.

## Blast Radius

Agent execution through both the Loop and child-task Runner checkpoint callback. The main regression risks are input order after cancellation, cross-run context leakage, terminal-wait budgeting and recovery-state persistence. Storage and client protocols are unchanged.

## Verification

- Focused execution, input, cancellation, Goal permission, recovery and follow-up commit suites: **416 passed** on Windows/Python 3.14.
- Full configured Ruff check, `uv run --no-sync basedpyright`, `uv run --no-sync python -m scripts.check_import_boundaries`, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Existing terminal-wait tests now patch the new owner while retaining the same timeout-budget assertions. The added concurrency case uses controlled events and synthetic model responses, not timing sleeps.
- [Remote CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/43206051733): passed, including Linux Python 3.11/3.14, Windows Python 3.14, Windows 3.12 process compatibility, Docker build/startup/upgrade acceptance, and the required gate. Checkout logs confirm the tested merge contains this PR head.
- Standalone WebUI/TUI/native-package lanes were not selected by the unchanged CI scope. Native update/installer tests were not run on the local interactive desktop.

## Why

A persisted empty answer-stream ending can become a streaming assistant row even when the model produced no reasoning. Treating that generic streaming flag as reasoning displays a misleading “thought process” alongside tool calls.

## What changed

## Scope

## Tradeoffs

Empty stream rows remain in the event projection for ordering and late-frame fencing, but are absorbed rather than rendered as activity. Explicit reasoning events continue to drive the reasoning UI.

## Blast Radius

The change affects thread activity rendering, history windows, fork dividers, and the running indicator. It does not alter the underlying tool execution or stream delivery.
