prs.title: perf(subagent): read saved task history by loaded turns
prs.body:
## Problem

Opening a long conversation loaded **every saved subagent task** for the session. `GET /api/sessions/{key}/subagents` had no scope, so a 500-turn session with 5000 finished tasks shipped **7.3 MB** of JSON on open — while the thread only renders a handful of messages — and the cost grew without bound as history accumulated.

## Change

Saved tasks are now read for the **turns the thread actually displays**.

- The WebUI sends the loaded user-turn ids (`?scope=window&turn_id=…&track=…`) and skips ids it already read, so growing the window reads only the new part.
- Hosts answer with tasks whose `subagent_task.origin_turn_id` falls in that window, plus every live task and any task the client still tracks. `origin_turn_id` is already persisted for every delegation, so no schema data change is needed.
- That JSON path is indexed by a **schema v6 partial index** (`sessions_subagent_origin_turn_id`), scoped to subagent child rows; `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` shows an index SEARCH instead of a table scan.
- The WebUI always uses the turn-window read, without an additional capability negotiation or a full-history fallback for older gateways. The backend's unscoped interface remains available to callers that need the complete task list.
- The window read reuses the existing session read — `read_statuses_for_session(session_key, turns=…, tracked=…)` — instead of a parallel method: stored window, one query for tracked tasks outside it, live-work reconciliation, all on one store connection. A test fails if a request opens more than one connection.
- The window is keyed by turn alone. The first version of this branch also filtered on `origin_message_id`, but the WebUI never sets that field: message frames carry only a turn id, and the message ids the thread renders are projection ids (`history-…`), not channel message ids. The dimension matched nothing while costing a second partial index, a UNION branch and up to 400 ids per request. It is gone, together with the `active=0` chunking flag — live tasks are always included and the client merges by task id.

Python: `list_subagent_session_metadata` / `read_child_session_metadata` in `SqliteSessionStore` / `SessionManager`, `SubagentSessions.load_turns` / `load_tracked`, `SubagentManager.read_statuses_for_session`, query parsing in `ws_http.py`.
WebUI: `SubagentTasks` reads per visible turn window with in-flight coalescing and an epoch/invalidate path for events, `ThreadViewport` reports the rendered turns, `api.ts` chunks long windows (≤400 ids / 5000 encoded chars per request) by tracking the encoded length instead of re-serializing the target per id.

## Measurements

These measurements were collected at `3ff53358f`, before removing the client negotiation. The backend query/index and the supported same-version request path are unchanged.

Synthetic, task-owned runtime (500 turns, 5000 finished tasks, 1024-byte results; latest 20 turns requested; no production data):

| | full read (before) | window read (after) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| response bytes | 7,283,659 | 291,358 |
| median latency | 180.7 ms | 10.7 ms |
| tasks returned | 5000 | 200 |

A second identical run measured 160.4 ms / 30.1 ms on the same commit and store, so treat the median as single-machine timing noise; the byte and row counts are exact.

Index cost, 200 subagent metadata updates per transaction, `synchronous=FULL`, 6 samples per path: **5.1–5.4 ms** with the index against **4.3–4.5 ms** without — about +4 µs per updated child row. A parent-session metadata write, the common path, never touches it because the partial predicate does not match. Building the index on a populated 5000-row store takes **26.5 ms**, a one-time startup cost on the first run after the upgrade. The write path pays that small per-row cost; the read path is where the win is.

Read-path scaling on a throwaway copy: at **50,000** stored tasks the same 20-turn read returns 200 rows in **0.3 ms**, against **283.9 ms** for the full read of the same parent.

## Verification

### Uniform-read follow-up

- `pytest tests/webui/test_client_contract.py tests/webui/test_remote_proxy_bootstrap.py tests/webui/test_subagent_persistence.py tests/session/test_subagent_metadata_query.py -q -p no:cacheprovider` → 44 passed.
- Full `bun run test --pool=forks --poolOptions.forks.maxForks=2 --poolOptions.forks.minForks=1` with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=2560` → 202 files, 3688 tests passed. An App fixture still matching the old query-free URL was corrected before this final full run.
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `bun run build`, `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.browser.json`, and `ruff check nanobot tests scripts` → passed.
- `history-boundary.spec.ts --workers=1` → 24 passed, 1 failed: `cross-path older errors never float after latest or a loaded rail jump, but boundary retry remains available` showed a blank page on its second navigation and timed out waiting for the thread. One focused diagnostic run with tracing passed on the same source; the suite failure remains unclassified. No timeout, retry, or assertion was relaxed. The task-pagination browser case passed and verified that loading older messages requests only the newly displayed turns.

### Earlier snapshot (`3ff53358f`)

The broader Python run, performance measurements, and real-gateway acceptance below were performed before this follow-up; they are retained with that snapshot identity.

- `pytest tests/session tests/webui tests/agent/test_subagent.py tests/agent/test_subagent_lifecycle.py tests/agent/test_session_manager_history.py tests/triggers/test_local_triggers.py` → 1289 passed, 22 skipped.
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `bun run build` → clean; full `bun run test` → 202 files, 3687 tests passed.
- `ruff check nanobot tests scripts` → clean. `basedpyright` 1.40.2 → 4 errors, the same pre-existing `BaseFileLock` `reportReturnType` errors; the five touched Python files report none.
- Browser acceptance on a real gateway with the synthetic 500-turn session: opening the conversation issued **one** scoped request (`content-length: 203959`, 14 turns) instead of loading 5000 tasks, each user message showed its own 10 finished tasks, scrolling into older history issued a second request covering only the newly loaded turns (0446–0485), and the console stayed clean.

CI note: on an earlier commit of this branch, `tests/webui/test_gateway_webui_smoke.py::test_real_gateway_goal_single_run_and_stop[True]` failed twice with its 30 s shutdown budget (35.5 s), then passed on a rerun of the same commit. The shutdown dump puts the wait at `nanobot/agent/loop.py:1767` — `_aclose_unlocked` draining `_background_tasks` — and no case in that file requests the subagent endpoint. It reads as a nondeterministic shutdown race in that smoke test, not a regression from this change; I recorded it instead of widening the timeout.

## Scope

Correctness work that this read depends on is *not* in this PR: the persisted `origin_turn_id` field is already on `main`, and the deeper attribution/consumption cleanup stays in a separate branch. This PR covers the window read, its index, and the WebUI integration.

Contributes to [NAN-438](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-438/按已加载消息按需读取-webui-子任务历史).

prs.title: fix(webui): prevent single-dollar math from crossing code spans
prs.body:
## Problem

The WebUI's single-dollar math scanner can start at prose such as `$ref` and consume the `$` inside a later inline code span such as `` `$defs` ``. This sends prose to KaTeX and destroys the intervening bold/code formatting. The reported full message, spaced code such as `` `$defs / definitions` ``, and preceding Windows paths are covered by regressions.

## Parsing rule

A tentative single-dollar formula must not end inside a complete CommonMark code span. Reuse micromark's `codeText` tokenizer to find the span boundary, then let the existing math scanner find its unescaped closing dollar. If that closer lies inside the code span, reject the math candidate and let Markdown parse the code normally.

This replaces the earlier identifier-tail regular expression and TeX-command guessing with a boundary check. Spaces, punctuation, and Windows paths no longer change code precedence. Ordinary formulas such as `$n$th` and `$x$2`, and backticks wholly contained within a formula such as ``$\text{`value`}$``, remain supported. The streaming fixture covers the reported reply's partial code span and completion.

When math and code delimiters cross, code wins. For example, `$th` is code in:

```text
A $x`$th`
```

An author intending a backtick inside math followed by Markdown code can use explicit TeX delimiters:

```text
A \(f(`x')\)th`code`.
```

This is a deliberate precedence choice, not an attempt to infer every author's intent. In particular, two bare dollar-prefixed identifiers without code spans remain outside this fix. Existing currency and explicit/display-math parsing rules are unchanged.

## Verification

- Focused renderer/streaming tests: 199 passed. The three added common-code regressions failed before the implementation change and passed afterward.
- Full WebUI unit suite: 205 files / 3,755 tests passed.
- Typecheck, lint, and production build passed.
- Full Chromium suite, with retries disabled: 522 passed / 1 failed. Both desktop/narrow Markdown streaming/completion cases passed, including the spaced-code and Windows-path regressions. The failing test is `history-hydration.spec.ts:319`, touch live-first history retry: `scrollTop` remained 114 instead of at most 1. Its cause is not attributed; no scroll changes or passing reruns are included in this PR.
- An initial browser command failed before tests ran because PowerShell expanded the reporter's comma. Quoting `--reporter=list,json` corrected the command; the full-suite result above is the completed run.

Earlier intermediate revisions had un-attributed full-suite failures (two `app-layout` unit cases, and `apps-connection-layout` / `history-hydration` browser cases). Their results are not reused as current-revision verification.

prs.title: refactor: drop unreferenced dead code
prs.body:
## What

Removes code that nothing in the tree references any more: leftovers from completed migrations, an SDK helper whose restore path moved, a WebUI snapshot builder and two icons that are never rendered, an unused re-export, and one unused npm dependency. No behavior changes; no public CLI, wire, config, or UI surface changes.

## How the list was produced

Two mechanical passes over every tracked file, then a manual read of each hit:

- Python: AST scan of all 1,057 `.py` files collecting every module-level and class-level definition, then counting real references (loads, attributes, keyword args, import aliases) across the whole repo. A hit means the name appears nowhere except its own definition — not in code, tests, docs, WebUI/TUI clients, or JSON/YAML data.
- TypeScript: identifier scan of every `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.mjs` file for exported symbols with zero occurrences outside their declaration, plus a check for module-private declarations with no use.

Framework-dispatched code was excluded so it cannot be mistaken for dead code: Typer command functions, pydantic `field_validator`/`model_validator` and `model_config`, pytest hooks and autouse fixtures, channel runtime classes resolved through `runtime="…:Class"` plugin strings, `ast.NodeVisitor.visit_*` overrides, pydantic-settings hooks, and SDK-private overrides called by upstream packages.

## Removed

| Location | Removed | Why it is dead |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nanobot/webui/settings_api.py` | `_parse_bool`, `_query_first_alias`, `_query_has_alias`, `_provider_requires_api_key`, `_reasoning_effort_values_for` | No importer and no in-module use. `_docs_version` and `_model_catalog_kind` stay because tests import them; `_query_first` stays because the module calls it. |
| `nanobot/sdk/types.py` | `snapshot_from_payload` | Unused since session restore moved to `snapshot_from_session`; absent from docs and from any `__all__`. |
| `nanobot/session/jsonl_migration.py` | `INTRODUCED_VERSION`, `LAST_SUPPORTED_RELEASE_LINE` | Unused; the module docstring already states both facts. `SUNSET_VERSION` stays (used by the migration guard). |
| `nanobot/providers/transcription.py` | `StepFunTranscriptionProvider._DEFAULT_URL` | Superseded by `_resolve_stepfun_asr_url`, never read. |
| `nanobot/channels/whatsapp_agent/protocol.py` | `CODE_MISSING_AUTH` | The only error-code constant that is neither exported in `__all__` nor compared anywhere; `validation.py` compares the wire value `190` directly, so the contract is unchanged. |
| `webui/src/lib/canonical-run-snapshot.ts` | `canonicalRunSnapshot` | No caller; `persistedCanonicalRunState` builds the snapshot inline. |
| `webui/src/components/icons/product-icons.tsx` | `SendIcon`, `RunningTaskIcon` | Not rendered or imported anywhere. |
| `webui/src/components/thread/AgentActivityCluster.tsx` | `export { isAgentActivityMember }` and its import | Imported only to be re-exported, and nothing imports it from this module. |
| `webui/package.json`, `webui/bun.lock` | `micromark-util-decode-string` | No import anywhere; it remains available transitively through `mdast-util-to-markdown`. |

prs.title: refactor(telegram): derive command regexes from the alias map
prs.body:
## Why

Telegram cannot render `-` in a tappable command, so `/dream-log` needs the underscore spelling `/dream_log`. The channel therefore keeps the same alias list in four places: the alias map, the display-name regex, the inline-code regex, and two routing regexes. Adding or removing a command means editing each one, and a missed edit shows up as a command that renders but does not route. Derive the spellings from the existing map instead.

## What changed

- Build the display, inline-code, and routing alternations from `_TELEGRAM_COMMAND_ALIASES`, so one map entry now feeds every spelling.
- Keep the routing split explicit: `_TELEGRAM_BUS_CANONICAL_COMMANDS` names the canonical spelling the shared handler also accepts, and `TELEGRAM_DEDICATED_COMMAND_RE` covers the rest.
- Hoist the display-name map out of `_telegram_command_text`, which rebuilt it on every call.

## Scope

Only how the patterns are assembled. The command list, handler order, matching boundaries, `@bot` suffix handling, code-fence skipping, inline-code exemption, and the text sent to the core router are unchanged. `BOT_COMMANDS` descriptions stay where they are; no command registry or dispatch framework.

## Tradeoffs

Keeping the four regexes spelled out is more readable in isolation. The cost is the silent divergence between them, which is the failure this change removes. Routing rules that differ on purpose, such as `evaluator-prompt` sharing the bus handler, remain explicit constants rather than being inferred.

## Blast Radius

Telegram command display in control replies and `/help`, and command routing through `_forward_command`. Other channels and the core command router are unaffected.

## Verification

- `nanobot/channels/telegram/tests/test_telegram_channel.py`: 178 passed, matching the pre-change result on the same base.
- `tests/channels/test_channel_plugins.py` and `tests/command` (excluding `test_compact_command.py`, which fails to import `agent.session_helpers` on this base before and after the change): 241 passed.
- `ruff check` and `basedpyright` on the changed file: clean, same as the baseline.
- The generated patterns differ from the previous literals only by `re.escape` output (`-` becomes `\-`, which matches identically); the inline-code pattern is byte-identical.
- No new tests: existing coverage already pins the observable routing and rendering behavior, and the change adds no new contract. Full CI not run locally.

prs.title: fix(models): route image input by preset capability
prs.body:
## Why

Image-aware routing lets a chain of text-only and vision models handle image requests while preserving the user's original input.

Resolves [NAN-442](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-442/模型请求失败时保留图片输入移除静默去图重试)

## What changed

- Add `supportsImages` to model presets, enabled by default. Named presets, the implicit default, and inline fallbacks each keep their own setting through save/load, migration, and runtime refresh.
- Route image requests through image-enabled presets in the configured primary and fallback order. If every candidate is text-only, return an image-input error before sending. Text requests use the full configured order.
- Preserve the original messages and images during transient retries, and return API validation errors directly. This replaces the previous image-stripping retry behavior and also preserves image blocks during DeepSeek content conversion.
- Add an **Image input** switch below the model picker using the existing settings controls and help hint. New presets start enabled; saved values stay with their preset, and cancelling discards a new draft. Include translations and configuration documentation.

## Scope

Covers preset configuration, shared provider retry and fallback selection, and the model settings UI/API.

## Tradeoffs

Users declare image capability per preset, including custom models. Enabled presets send images to their provider, which applies its image-format requirements and returns validation errors directly.

## Blast Radius

Regression coverage focuses on independent preset values, explicit `false` persistence, runtime refresh, capability-aware candidate selection, and original input/error preservation.

## Verification

Current-head local checks:

- All agent, provider and config tests plus settings API/edit-admission suites: **4052 passed, 8 skipped**.
- Focused CI-repair regression suite: **181 passed**. Attribution tests cover successful image requests and direct HTTP 400 errors with preserved input; governance and model-override mocks exercise their scripted primary/fallback paths.
- Full-project Ruff, BasedPyright, import-boundary checks, and `git diff --check`: passed.

Frontend checks carried forward from the implementation revision; frontend sources are unchanged by the test-only CI repair:

- WebUI model-settings and i18n tests: **107 passed**. `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, and `bun run build`: passed.
- Playwright preset-settings checks at 390px and 1280px: **2 passed**, covering keyboard toggling, cancellation/reset, and layout. Rendered Chinese desktop/light and narrow/dark synthetic previews and the help hint were also inspected.

Local checks use synthetic settings and controlled provider responses. Full-project verification runs in CI.

prs.title: fix(webui): scope remote health checks to visible demand
prs.body:
## Why

After opening a remote host, retained views kept triggering directory reads every five seconds—even after switching to Local or hiding the browser tab. Each read also checked every established remote connection. Tie health checks to visible demand instead of retained iframe lifetime.

## What changed

- Check only the active remote host, or established connections while the host menu/management page is visible. Pause when hidden or no longer needed; revalidate on return without discarding frames, drafts or shared tunnels. Steady polling uses the targeted response to update the directory without a separate snapshot read; existing connections remain eligible for checks after errors.
- Make ordinary directory reads snapshot-only. Explicit `check` targets use the existing gateway lifetime lock and reuse completed checks for five seconds, including overlapping requests from other tabs.
- Count distinct failed samples rather than cached responses, reject stale results after connection changes, and preserve a queued wake even if the previous request fails.

## Scope

Remote-host health observation only. No changes to chat execution, SSH/WebSocket lifetime, other settings polling, or compatibility negotiation; no new push framework.

Contributes to [NAN-338](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-338/减少-webui-空闲轮询以状态变更通知和重连同步替代重复查询)

## Tradeoffs

Unobserved hosts can have stale displayed health until revisited. Observed checks can reuse a result up to five seconds old; explicit connect/repair validation remains separate. A check already in flight may finish after hiding the tab.

## Blast Radius

The local remote-host UI and `/api/remote-instances` contract change together under the same-version WebUI/gateway support policy. Authentication, loopback restrictions, gateway/view identity checks and the existing 12-second health budget remain intact. Disconnect/Forget still own transport teardown.

## Verification

- **Before/after:** with one retained remote view and Local selected, the original hook made **6 reads / 30 simulated seconds**; the new hook makes **0**. Both new demand-scope tests fail against the original hook for the intended reasons and pass here. [Regression scenarios](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/666edb77e3bd64d40ae8e880bf9a1b48ea48107c/webui/src/tests/host-sessions.test.tsx).
- **Real Chromium visibility:** a complete isolated browser run used actual tab switching, without overriding visibility. Each steady observation lasted 6.2 seconds: hidden tab **0** new reads; Local with a retained iframe **0**; active remote **1** targeted request; open host menu **1** periodic targeted request. Showing the tab caused an immediate targeted request. The same iframe and both drafts survived. Directory/RPC/remote content were synthetic; this is not live SSH or production traffic measurement.
- Frontend remote/host suites: **199 passed across 8 files**. Backend instances/pairing/proxy suites: **239 passed**, including targeted requests, concurrent/fresh-result reuse, replacement, cancellation and shutdown safety.
- Follow-up verification: steady observed polling uses **1 request / 5-second cycle instead of 2**, discovers connections from returned snapshots, and keeps checking after setup/identity errors without reviving a mismatched view. The frontend suites, TypeScript, touched-file ESLint and `git diff --check` passed on this update.
- Backend tests, Ruff, backend basedpyright, client import boundaries, production build and browser sampling passed on `90fe91a`; they were not rerun for this two-file frontend follow-up. Vite reported large-chunk warnings.
- Live SSH acceptance and cross-version behavior were not tested. No running user gateway or remote host was changed.

prs.title: feat(webui): stabilize session transitions and add a Mac-style goal notch
prs.body:
Resolves [NAN-443](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-443/稳定-webui-session-切换的输入框布局并加入消息区淡出淡入)

## Why

Session changes should replace the conversation without making the composer jump or compete with running subagent activity. Goal details belong in a quiet, separate surface, and dismissing an informational overlay should return users to the control they were using rather than unexpectedly moving focus to a header button.

## What changed

- Add interruptible, latest-navigation-wins session transitions: fade thread content, preserve unscaled composer text and stable anchors, coordinate with theme transitions, and skip unchanged desktop panes and reduced-motion captures. Closing the active temporary chat commits its replacement immediately, without animation, so route cleanup cannot override the destination.
- Move Goal out of the composer into a Mac-style top notch with continuous inverse corners and sidebar-derived materials. Active goal details have a fixed Markdown-sized heading, independently scrolling feathered content, a 25dvh height limit, reversible expansion/collapse, and narrow-screen header controls that remain reachable. Clamp long headings to leave the objective readable on portrait and landscape screens.
- Keep blocked goals visible using the existing gateway state (`active: false`, `status: blocked`). Show the blocking reason rather than the goal title, with a muted red circular alert icon and matching text; retain the objective in expanded details. Soften the expanded shadow and add a localized, interactive Goal preview to the component gallery. A live block returns open details to the reason; loaded Markdown retains the same color as the alert icon.
- Restore Escape focus according to the actual opener across Goal, model selection, session/source information, prompt search, workspace selection and feature settings. Preserve keyboard focus indicators, outside-click targets and dialog handoffs. When saving disables the feature switch that opened a dialog, restore focus to Configure instead. Add `webui --dev-port` for isolated previews.

- Remove the unused Goal close-button translations across all 10 locales; retain the blocked-state text used by screen readers.

## Scope

History is organized into two commits: `9ab5562b9` adds `--dev-port`; `5168166cd` contains the WebUI changes and follow-up fixes. prs.title: fix(webui): keep history loading until content is ready
prs.body:
## Why

Pulling for earlier history can return a bookkeeping-only page or an incomplete turn fragment before any additional content is ready to display. Treating that first response as completion makes the nine-square indicator retract too early. Keep the pull pending until display content is admitted, history is exhausted, or a read fails.

## What changed

- Continue latest-history and navigation reads within one loading operation. Use the message list's activity filtering and include visible fork boundaries in the readiness comparison, without treating usage or timing updates as new content.
- Preserve completion metadata across discarded bookkeeping pages, in both navigation directions. Reuse the event projector with one retained terminal record per fragmented turn instead of accumulating skipped raw pages.
- Route real Blocks-button and boundary-gesture retries to the failed cursor. Publish navigation pages through one synchronous owner so a history response cannot overwrite trace details arriving in the same React batch.
- Reuse projections of immutable navigation windows and compare display fields structurally instead of serializing full tool results. Keep retry-page context only for failed reads and release it on a new read, cancellation, return to latest, or session/client change.
- Rebase the reading anchor when delayed layout hits a scroll bound, so a later prepend cannot restore an obsolete offset and jump the conversation.
- Add pagination and geometry regressions plus an opt-in browser fixture for slow, fast, multi-page, and failed reads.

## Scope

WebUI only: no gateway, protocol, persistence, or dependency changes. Reuse the existing Blocks indicator and spring; add no production delays or minimum loading duration. Deferred Markdown, images, and highlighting remain layout work rather than additional completion gates.

## Tradeoffs

One gesture may fetch several cursor pages when they add no display content. Navigation keeps a three-page raw window plus the retained terminal record for each fragmented turn. Failed reads preserve the readable window and accepted metadata and retry the failed cursor; self-contained pages extend that readable window rather than evicting it through intervening bookkeeping pages.

## Blast Radius

Latest-history pagination, reconnect fragment recovery, prompt navigation, deferred activity details, fork dividers, and reading-position compensation. Verification includes interactions with command-session snapshots and trace-detail expansion.

## Verification

Run from `webui/` on the final integrated changes:

- `bun run test src/tests/useSessions.test.tsx src/tests/usePromptHistory.test.tsx src/tests/useReconnectRuns.test.tsx src/tests/useNanobotStream.test.tsx src/tests/thread-viewport.test.tsx src/tests/thread-shell.test.tsx src/tests/thread-messages.test.tsx src/tests/thread-display-projection.test.ts src/tests/agent-activity-cluster.test.tsx` — 580 passed.
- `NANOBOT_BROWSER_TEST_PORT=4196 bun run test:browser browser/history-boundary.spec.ts browser/exec-session.spec.ts browser/session-transition.spec.ts browser/activity-wheel.spec.ts --workers=1` — 51 passed. Covers continuous loading across non-display pages, desktop wheel and mobile touch, real button/gesture retry, fast completion, exhaustion, reduced motion, bounded navigation, delayed layout, and command activity.
- Six additional synthetic lifecycle probes passed for cancellation, return to latest, session/generation replacement, and unmount during automatic continuation.
- Review regressions cover hidden task-create activity, completion metadata after more than three bookkeeping fragments and failed continuation, backward terminal-record retention, same-batch detail expansion, and fork-marker-only pages in both directions with their rendered divider (including loading parent history from the first child prompt).
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `bun run check:imports`, `bun run build`, and `git diff --check` — passed. Build retains the existing large-chunk warning.
- The top-bound layout regression reproduced a roughly 160 px jump before the anchor fix; the passing browser test requires less than 1 px drift.

### Performance and retention

Compared with the pre-fix PR head `633a2fb7c`, five alternating runs of the actual navigation hook reduced the fourth-read median from **92.98 ms to 44.76 ms** (ranges 92.11–94.58 ms and 43.55–46.26 ms). The synthetic long turn uses four 4,000-record pages, 40 model rounds per page, and two 32,000-byte tool results per round; each read produced matching displayed-content hashes and request counts. After returning to latest, all old raw-page objects were collectible instead of retaining three pages; the latest-view heap delta fell from about 10.39 MiB to 0.77 MiB in the same runs.

These are Node 22 / React + happy-dom CPU/heap measurements with mocked HTTP, not browser frame-rate or network results. Ordinary 24-event pages were also checked; very large pages can still cause long tasks.

Interactive fixture: `/browser/fixture.html?case=history-boundary&preview=pages&lang=zh-CN` on the local Vite server. Browser verification uses simulated responses, not a live authenticated gateway. Full frontend suites were not run.

Resolves [NAN-303](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-303/让-webui-历史加载头连续下拉揭示松手停靠并随用户滚动退出)

prs.title: fix(goal): make cancellation a user-only control
prs.body:
## Summary

Let users dismiss active or blocked goals with `/cancel_goal` or WebUI's **Cancel goal** button, without a model call.

- Cancellation is user-only. The agent can complete, block, or replace an active goal, but cannot cancel it.
- Active-goal cancellation reuses `/stop`, waits for work to finish stopping, then saves the cancelled state. Cancelling a blocked goal leaves unrelated replies running. `/stop` itself still keeps the saved goal.
- WebUI waits for the server state, preserves drafts, and supports retry after failure. Telegram and Discord expose the command. Chat history is kept.

## Verification

- Focused Python command, goal, persistence, and checkpoint tests: 162 passed.
- GoalIsland/ThreadShell tests: 141 passed; desktop and narrow-screen cancellation checks: 2 passed.
- WebUI typecheck, targeted Ruff/ESLint, and diff checks passed.

Browser tests use a mock gateway. Live IM accounts and real model compliance were not tested.

Resolves [NAN-444](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-444/修复受阻-goal-无法取消并持续显示)

prs.title: refactor(tools): centralize scoped file operations
prs.body:
## Why

File tools previously resolved workspace paths in the tool layer. Search then walked the tree and opened the paths it found, while edit activity reconstructed target paths separately to show changes. A check on the starting directory does not by itself authorize every file discovered below it. This change puts file access in one place so reads, writes, search, and edit previews apply the same workspace rules.

## How it works

| Layer | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| [Workspace policy](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/ad7ba91701da57577629b9a89e88b75fd37c509e/nanobot/security/workspace_policy.py) | Decide which paths the active request can access. Keep read grants, write grants, and exact-file grants separate. |
| [File execution](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/ad7ba91701da57577629b9a89e88b75fd37c509e/nanobot/execution/files.py) | Resolve the active workspace, open and check files, walk directories, and commit patch writes. Keep file and directory handles inside this layer. |
| Tool adapters | Keep argument validation, search matching and ranking, output formatting, and model-facing behavior. `read_file`, `write_file`, `edit_file`, `apply_patch`, `list_dir`, `find_files`, and Python `grep` use the scoped operations. |

- Edit activity takes its before-and-after snapshots from the authorized write target. It does not open a path taken directly from the tool arguments. An exact write grant can create the approved file without granting access to sibling names. Edit summaries and activity reuse the same line comparison when the observed contents match.
- Search checks discovered targets before reading them. It keeps authorized links to documents and their locators, such as PDF page numbers and spreadsheet cells. An exact file grant does not become a directory grant if the file is replaced by a directory.
- Mutations reject non-regular files, including named pipes. On hosts with no-follow support, a last-component symlink replacement is rejected before the write. These are application-level checks, not OS confinement against concurrent replacement of ancestor directories.
- Read deduplication remains tied to the original result being visible in the current model request. The connection to that result no longer depends on the registered tool name.

## Search cost and compatibility

Search batches filesystem checks by directory while still checking link targets. Where native directory handles are unavailable, the portable path checks directory identity before and after a batch and compares the identity of opened files. A directory replacement invalidates the scan results. Path-ordered pages stop after one extra result. Modified-time ordering still scans the eligible entries but retains only the requested prefix when a page limit applies.

The seven tool schemas serialize identically before and after. There are no new settings, data migrations, or changes to shell sandboxing, subprocess-backed `rg`, network policy, or the updater. Requests that depended on access outside an authorized path, or on writing a non-regular file, can now be rejected.

## Benchmarks

Median wall-clock time at the tool entry point, in milliseconds. macOS arm64, Python 3.11.4, warm filesystem cache. Compared base `8d64e22fb` with final PR head `db28e8b57`. Eight measured calls per version and workload, after warm-ups. All ten tested cases produced identical output, including order and pagination. The large tree contained 12,000 files; the small directory contained 32.

| Workload | Base | PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Small-directory text search | 1.18 | 1.16 |
| Large tree, sparse matches | 367.92 | 310.61 |
| Large tree, no matches | 390.81 | 319.58 |
| Large tree, dense match counts | 364.32 | 303.81 |
| Large tree, file search sorted by modification time | 104.70 | 78.38 |
| Large tree, recursive listing | 51.50 | 34.19 |

The portable path was also tested on macOS with native directory handles disabled. This is not a native Windows benchmark, and the timings do not include model calls.

## Verification

- Regression tests cover workspace grants, target replacement, special files, patch rollback, document search, cancellation, pagination, and read deduplication.
- [PR CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/43602270838) passed on `db28e8b57`: Linux and Windows Python suites, Windows process checks, and a Docker upgrade using the existing data volume.
- [Merged commit](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/commit/ad7ba91701da57577629b9a89e88b75fd37c509e) has the same source tree as the tested PR head. [Post-merge CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/43603375416) tracks that exact commit.

prs.title: Add trusted PyPI publishing for approved releases
prs.body:
## Problem

Stable PyPI uploads require a maintainer credential and manual artifact selection. Start PyPI Trusted Publishing when a maintainer publishes an approved GitHub Release. Keep a manual workflow for testing and recovery.

## Changes

- Start the protected main-branch publisher after a stable GitHub Release. Preserve the original release actor and require an independent PyPI approval.
- Verify the public final release, approval signature, tag commit and all 16 manifest-bound files before staging the five wheels and source distribution.
- Keep the OIDC-enabled publication job separate from verification. Default to TestPyPI and require an explicit production selection.
- Resume an interrupted upload with **Run workflow** on `main` for the same version and destination. A new run checks the approved files against the package index and uploads only missing files. A production upload requires a new independent approval. Stop on mismatches, unexpected files or index errors.
- Document setup, approvals and the existing manual route while the signed workflow is unavailable.

## Validation

- `pytest -q tests/scripts/test_pypi_release_trigger.py tests/test_prepare_pypi_release.py tests/test_reconcile_pypi_release.py tests/test_release_trust.py tests/scripts/test_ci_workflows.py` (54 passed)
- Executed the failure-hint shell step locally and checked both its annotation and job summary
- Ruff and actionlint on the changed Python and workflow files
- Simulated release event, manual recovery, tag mismatch and independent-approval checks
- Read-only TestPyPI check for an unpublished version

A real TestPyPI upload still requires a separately configured project and a complete, independently signed public release. Local tests do not establish end-to-end publication.

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: provider/openai
labels.description: OpenAI / Codex Responses API

labels.name: area/config
labels.description: Config system, migrations, profiles

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: cause/upstream
labels.description: A cause outside Hermes that Hermes cannot fully fix: a model provider's outage, policy change, rate

issues.body:
**Codex backend returns HTTP 400 `{"detail":"Bad Request"}` for some zstd-compressed `/responses` bodies (since #136916)**

Since the zstd request compression in #136916, `openai-codex` turns fail intermittently with a non-retryable `HTTP 400: {"detail":"Bad Request"}`. Because it is classified as non-retryable, `fallback_providers` never runs. Seen on v0.22.5 and v0.22.7, Python 3.14, official `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex`, ChatGPT OAuth.

**Minimal repro (no secrets needed in the report)**
1. Take a body the engine sent that failed (a request dump from `sessions/request_dump_*.json`).
2. POST it to `/responses` through the engine's own httpx client with the compression hook: 36/36 calls return 400.
3. POST the identical JSON with no `Content-Encoding`: 36/36 return 200.
4. Compress the same JSON myself with `compression.zstd.compress` but a different JSON whitespace or `ensure_ascii` setting: some variants return 200 and some 400, per body. So the backend accepts or rejects depending on the exact compressed bytes. Failing requests were small (1 to 3 input items, about 130 KB), so it isn't a size limit.

Because the bytes differ on every turn, it shows up as roughly random failures (about 1 in 6 on some tool-turn tests, 15 within an hour on a busy gateway).

**Suggested fix**
- Add an opt-out (for example `HERMES_CODEX_REQUEST_COMPRESSION=0` or a config key) so users can send plain JSON, which the PR said was fine before.
- Consider also replaying once without compression when the backend returns this opaque 400 on a compressed body.

Workaround: a plugin that makes `agent.codex_headers.codex_request_compression_hooks` return `None`.

issues.title: [Bug]: Weixin inbound silently stops for 90+ minutes while gateway stays up and logs nothing (iLink getupdates)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: platform/wecom
labels.description: WeCom / WeChat Work adapter

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

issues.body:
## Bug Description

The Weixin (iLink) adapter stops delivering **inbound** messages entirely while the gateway process keeps running and the adapter still reports itself connected. Nothing is logged — no `poll error`, no `Session expired`, no reconnect attempt — so there is no signal that inbound is dead. From the user's side the bot just stops answering forever.

Recovery required a full `systemctl restart hermes-gateway`; inbound resumed immediately afterwards.

## Steps to Reproduce

Not deterministic (seen once after ~2 days of uptime):

1. Run the gateway with the Weixin platform (iLink DM, single user) continuously for ~2 days.
2. Exchange a burst of messages, including outbound media (image + 3 MEDIA attachments).
3. Some time after the last exchange (here: outbound at 11:36, then no traffic), send more messages from WeChat.
4. Nothing arrives: no `[Weixin] inbound` log line, no reply, no error.

## Expected Behavior

At minimum, a stalled / failed long-poll should surface a WARN or ERROR. Ideally a receive-liveness watchdog notices "connected but no inbound for N minutes", logs it and recycles the poll session (or forces a reconnect) on its own.

## Actual Behavior

Timeline (Asia/Shanghai, single DM peer):

- `11:30:34` last `[Weixin] inbound`
- `11:36:37` last successful `Sending response`
- `11:36:37 → 13:09:52` **93 minutes**: zero `[Weixin] inbound`, zero `poll error`, zero `getUpdates failed`, zero `Disconnected`/`Connected` lines
- `12:40:55` agent cache idle-TTL evict for the weixin session (`idle=3859s`) — so the gateway itself was healthy and scheduling work
- gateway process: up 2 days 6h, `hermes gateway status` = `active (running)`, no restart in between
- `12:51:51` `systemctl restart hermes-gateway`
- `13:09:52` next `[Weixin] inbound` succeeds and the reply is sent normally

Nothing in `gateway.log` / `errors.log` between 11:36 and 12:51 mentions weixin at all. The only weixin-related errors in the preceding hours were outbound ones:

```
2026-11-14 22:29:49 WARNING [Weixin] session expired for <peer>; retrying without context_token
2026-11-14 22:42:22 ERROR   [Weixin] send failed to=<peer>: iLink sendmessage session not ready: ret=-2 errcode=None errmsg=prepare failed — the user must send the bot a message ...
```

Environment: `Hermes Agent v0.23.1+6995.g1831ce1`, Linux aarch64, Python 3.14, Weixin platform via `https://ilinkai.weixin.qq.com`, single DM peer.

## Suspected cause (for triage, not verified)

`plugins/platforms/weixin/adapter.py::_poll_loop` is the only inbound path (`ilink/bot/getupdates` long-poll, `LONG_POLL_TIMEOUT_MS = 35_000`). Two silent-stall shapes are possible and neither logs anything:

1. **Parked await** — the `get_updates` request never returns and the `asyncio.wait_for(...)` wrapping it never fires, so the loop sits in one await forever. `_running` stays true, the adapter still looks connected.
2. **Stale cursor** — the persisted `get_updates_buf` (`<hermes_home>/weixin/accounts/<account>.sync.json`) advanced past pending messages, so the server keeps returning empty batches forever. The loop is healthy, just permanently empty.

Both look identical from the outside: "online, receives nothing, logs nothing".

## Suggested fixes

- Track `last_success_ts` for `get_updates` and add a watchdog: if connected and no successful poll response for N minutes (e.g. 3× the long-poll timeout + a minute), log `WARN` and call `_recycle_poll_session()` (or reconnect the platform).
- Log a periodic heartbeat at debug level (poll ok / empty batch) so this is diagnosable after the fact.
- On stale-session recovery (`session not ready` / `ret=-2`), consider re-validating or resetting the persisted `sync_buf` instead of trusting it.
- Expose the poll-loop's last-success timestamp in `hermes gateway status` so users can tell "connected" from "actually receiving".

issues.title: [Bug]: Kanban task stuck in ready forever: stale rate-limit text in last_failure_error trips respawn guard blocker_auth after dependency promotion

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: comp/cron
labels.description: Cron scheduler and job management

labels.name: comp/plugins
labels.description: Plugin system and bundled plugins

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
### Bug Description

A kanban task that was rate-limited earlier and later parked as a dependency wait never runs again after its parent completes. `recompute_ready()` promotes it `todo -> ready` but leaves `tasks.last_failure_error` untouched. The stale text from the earlier `rate_limited` requeue ("pid N exited rate-limited (quota wall) — requeued without counting a failure") still matches `_RESPAWN_BLOCKER_RE`. The latest run's outcome is now `blocked` rather than `rate_limited`, so the rate-limit early return in `check_respawn_guard()` no longer applies. The guard therefore returns `blocker_auth` on every tick, forever.

On our board four tasks were stuck like this for ~27h: more than 1,400 `respawn_guarded {'reason': 'blocker_auth'}` events per task, a "Ready for 27.3h with no worker" diagnostic, and the gateway warning "kanban dispatcher stuck: ready queue non-empty for N consecutive ticks but 0 workers spawned. Last tick held back: blocker_auth". That warning points the operator at credentials, which is misleading here.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. A task in `ready` is spawned and the worker exits rate-limited (exit 75). `last_failure_error` gets the quota-wall text and the task is requeued to `ready`.
2. Quota returns. The next run links a new parent and blocks with `kind=dependency` (`dependency_wait`, task -> `todo`). Latest run outcome: `blocked`.
3. The parent completes. `recompute_ready()` promotes the task to `ready` (`promoted` event).
4. Every dispatcher tick now logs `respawn_guarded {'reason': 'blocker_auth'}`, and the task is never claimed.

### Expected Behavior

Once a task is promoted after a dependency wait, the respawn guard judges it on fresh state. A requeue text that the rate-limit path already declared "not a failure" should never park the task permanently.

### Actual Behavior

The task stays in `ready` indefinitely. The only way out is a manual `hermes kanban block` followed by `unblock`, because `unblock_task()` clears `consecutive_failures` and `last_failure_error`.

### Affected Component

Kanban dispatcher (`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py` `recompute_ready`, `hermes_cli/kanban_db_dispatch.py` `check_respawn_guard`)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (embedded gateway dispatcher)

### Operating System

Linux (Docker image)

### Python Version

3.13

### Hermes Version

v0.21.5 (2026.9.24), upstream 749220ef

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

- The `rate_limited` requeue stamps a quota-flavored `last_failure_error` without counting a failure. `check_respawn_guard()` only tolerates this while the **latest** run is `rate_limited` (step 1: early return).
- Any later run with a different outcome (here `blocked` via a dependency block) moves the guard to step 2. There `_RESPAWN_BLOCKER_RE` matches "rate-limited"/"quota" in the stale text, and the guard returns `blocker_auth`.
- `recompute_ready()` resets neither `last_failure_error` nor anything else on promotion. `unblock_task()` does reset both, which explains the asymmetry.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Pick either option; both would be reasonable:
1. In `recompute_ready()`, clear `last_failure_error` when promoting (at least from `todo`). A dependency promotion is a fresh start, like `unblock_task()`.
2. Don't persist the rate-limit requeue text into `last_failure_error` at all, or clear it when a later run ends with a non-`rate_limited` outcome. The requeue path already says it is "not a failure".

Also consider limiting `blocker_auth` to errors coming from the **latest** run, so that stale text can never gate a respawn.

issues.title: [Bug][Desktop] Queued turn can be stuck forever and undeletable: client persists the row in Local Storage, and its delete RPC (prompt.cancel) isn't served by the tui backend

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/gateway
labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: comp/desktop
labels.description: Electron desktop app (apps/desktop/*)

labels.name: desktop/chat
labels.description: The chat view of the desktop app: composer, sending messages, message rendering, markdown, streaming

labels.name: comp/tui-gateway
labels.description: The shared Python JSON-RPC backend that both the terminal UI and the desktop app talk to (tui_gatewa

issues.body:
## Summary

A "queued turn" badge in the desktop client can become **permanently stuck and undeletable**. The client holds a local copy of a queue entry referencing a server admission; when the admission settles server-side without the client processing the update, the badge survives tab reloads and full app restarts (it is persisted in the app's user-data dir). The UI's only removal path then fails against the backend, so the row can only be cleared by deleting the app's entire local data directory.

The failure has two independent parts, both verified in this codebase:

1. **The delete RPC the client sends is not served by the backend it talks to.** The desktop queue-slot UI removes a queued turn via `prompt.cancel` (`apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/queue-slot.tsx`, `discard-lost-prompt.ts`; the TUI has the same path with tests, e.g. "deletes a server-queued row through prompt.cancel rather than local removal"). `prompt.cancel` is registered only in the canonical gateway-authority surface (`tui_gateway/contracts/canonical.py`, dispatched in `gateway/session_controls.py` → `self.cancel`). The tui_gateway surface the desktop app speaks does **not** register it in its `METHODS` catalog, so the call returns JSON-RPC `-32601` with the text produced by `tui_gateway/contracts/registry.py::unknown_method_message()`:

   > Couldn't remove the queued turn
   > unknown method: prompt.cancel — not available on this Hermes backend

2. **The client never reconciles its local queue rows against server state.** After the server-side admission settled, the client kept rendering the row as queued across webview reloads and a full app process restart. The row is persisted in Chromium **Local Storage (LevelDB)** under the app's user-data dir — confirmed: the stuck text was present only in `Local Storage/leveldb/*.ldb` after the dir was preserved (`Cache_Data` hits are HTTP-cache echoes of the same message body, not the bug). The persisted row is not re-validated against the owner's published queue list / `prompt.receipt` on reconnect.

## Reproduction (observed incident; the reconciliation trigger is not deterministic)

1. Desktop app connected to the dashboard (port 9119).
2. Send a message to a bot while its session is mid-turn → the client shows the message as queued.
3. The message is delivered and the bot answers; the server-side admission reaches `terminal` (delivered).
4. The client does not process the settle (observed with the app running across a WS disconnect/lifecycle event; exact trigger not pinned down).
5. The "queued" badge persists across tab reloads and a full app relaunch — it lives in `Local Storage/leveldb` in the app's user-data dir.
6. Attempt to delete the queued turn from the UI → the toast above. The row cannot be removed from the UI by any supported action.
7. Workaround that succeeded: quit the app, rename its user-data dir (`~/.config/Hermes` on Linux), relaunch, and redo the gateway connection. (The app re-prompts for the connection; chat history is server-side, so nothing is lost.)

## Environment

- Desktop app: Electron 44.9.3 linux-unpacked build, productName `Hermes`, v0.0.0 (stable channel), Wayland.
- Backend: docker-managed install 0.23.1, dashboard `tui_gateway` on 9119.
- Server state verified clean at incident time: no `queued` row in `session_admissions` (the message's admission was `terminal`/delivered), no queued message rows in the session transcript, nothing in any durable store. The stuck badge was purely client-side state.

## Consequences

1. A ghost "queued" turn on a conversation that already completed — misleads the user into thinking the bot still owes a run.
2. **No supported recovery path**: every UI delete attempt returns the `-32601` toast; the only fix found is wiping the app's user-data dir and reconnecting.
3. The bug is self-concealing: the error names a missing method rather than the actual condition (a stale client row), so neither user nor operator can act on it.

## Expected behavior

Any of (a)+(b) or (c) would close this:

- (a) **Serve `prompt.cancel` on the tui surface** (proxy to the gateway authority, which implements it), so the UI delete works as designed against the desktop backend; or, if the method is deliberately absent there, the client should not offer the delete action it cannot possibly succeed with.
- (b) **Reconcile on reconnect**: on attach/resume, the client should re-validate its persisted queue rows against server state (owner's published queue list / `prompt.receipt` for the referenced `admission_id`) and retire rows whose admission has settled, instead of re-rendering them as queued forever.
- (c) **Fail the delete gracefully**: when a cancel is not honored, the client should mark the row stale/discarded locally rather than leaving an undeletable "queued" badge.

## Related

- #155955 — [Bug][Bot Mode] First DM into a pre-gateway Bot Chat silently forks the chat (separate; same "server restructures/holds state the client never learns about" family).

issues.body:
## Summary

Please consider adding a configuration knob for the same-assignee "Recent work" section that `build_worker_context` injects into every Kanban worker's context — or making it opt-in. In 0.20.0 there is no way to turn it off, and on multi-tenant boards it is a cross-task context-bleed channel that compaction can amplify into a worker executing the wrong task.

## Current behavior

`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py::build_worker_context` (0.20.0) appends a `## Recent work by @<assignee>` section: the five most recent completed runs by the same profile, drawn from **unrelated tasks** (`WHERE r.profile = ? AND r.task_id != ?`). The code comment describes it as implicit role continuity ("I'm the reviewer and my last three reviews focused on security").

There is no config key, profile setting, or board setting that disables or scopes this section.

The documented `worker_context` contract (kanban tutorial, "Structured handoff — why summary and metadata matter") describes the denominator as: the task's own body, its **prior attempts**, and **parent task results**. The same-assignee section is not mentioned anywhere in the docs, so operators discover it only when it misbehaves.

## Observed failure mode (production, multi-tenant board)

We run one board with several client matters as tenants; one analyst profile serves all of them. Sequence we hit live:

1. A worker spawned on task A (matter Alpha). Its `kanban_show` output included recent-work rows for tasks from matter Beta — same profile, unrelated tenant.
2. An automatic context compaction summarized the transcript. The compaction summary preserved the foreign matter-Beta material on equal footing with task A's own identity (the summary recorded *that* `kanban_show` had been called, but not its body).
3. Post-compaction, the worker resumed "its" task using the wrong structured context: it reported a different `case_item_id`, a different matter root, and completed run metadata that belonged to the matter-Beta workflow. The run wrote no artifacts, but the task's run history now asserts the wrong matter — a human had to catch it and route a clean retry.

The injection is bounded and clearly useful for single-tenant role continuity, but on a multi-tenant board it means every worker's context carries material from other clients' tasks by default, and any context loss (compaction, session restore) can promote that material into active authority.

## Proposal

Any of these shapes would close the gap; rough order of preference:

1. **Config knob**, e.g.:

   ```yaml
   kanban:
     worker_context:
       role_history: off   # off | titles | full (default: full)
   ```

   Per-profile override would be ideal, so orchestrator lanes can keep continuity while multi-tenant specialist lanes turn it off.

2. **Tenant scoping** — when `tenant` is set on tasks, restrict the recent-work query to the same tenant (`AND t.tenant = ?`). This preserves the feature's intent while eliminating the cross-client channel.

3. **Compaction hardening** (complementary): for dispatcher-spawned workers, have the context compressor restate the runtime-pinned `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` identity in/around the compaction summary, so task ids that appear in historical evidence cannot displace the one dispatcher-pinned work authority after compaction. The docs already treat `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` as the single task authority for a worker; making compaction restate it would keep that true across context loss.

## Why not just keep a local patch?

We currently run a local patch that removes the section and adds the compaction identity restatement, reapplied after every upgrade. It works, but it is standing divergence from the released kernel — every upgrade risks silent drift, and the behavior seems generally desirable for anyone running multi-tenant boards. Happy to submit a PR for whichever shape you prefer.

issues.body:
# Draft GitHub issue — tool_call: opaque "calls is not valid JSON" on model double-encoded `calls`

Prepared by Kenny (Master-2), 2026-11-15. For filing by Dobby/owner (needs repo credentials).
Repo: NousResearch/hermes-agent

## Title
`tool_call`: stringified `calls` with one malformed inner byte yields "not valid JSON" with no context window (no model self-correction possible)

## Summary
When a model emits the `tool_call` `calls` parameter as a JSON **string** containing a serialized array (the engine deliberately re-parses this at `tools/tool_search_validation.py:154-160`, per #114484), a single dropped/misplaced structural token inside the inner string produces:

```
tool_call 'calls' is not valid JSON: Expecting ',' delimiter: line 1 column NNN (char NNN-1)
```

The offset points into the inner string with **no context**, so the model cannot see which bytes are malformed and the next retry typically fails identically. Observed: 3 consecutive failures in one session, offsets 871/786/726 tracking message length (fault at the tail region of the inner string each time).

## Reproduction (verified from stored state)
- Profile `kenny`, model UDP-UNCENSORED-Qwen3.8-27B (custom endpoint), session `20261113_035518_11ebc82a`, messages 186/188/190 in `state.db`; engine errors at `agent.log:2372/2374/2376`.
- The model emitted `{"calls": "[{\"arguments\": {...}, \"name\": \"a2a_call\"}]"}` — a string where the bridge schema (`tools/tool_search.py:313-314`, `type: "array"`) expects an array.
- Replaying the engine's exact decode chain (`json.loads(raw_calls)` at validation.py:158) on the stored bytes reproduces all three errors byte-for-byte. The inner strings are not well-formed JSON (even quote parity, valid `\n` escapes, scanner reaches closing `]` in object context — a brace/colon structural fault).
- The same call shape with a well-formed inner string succeeded earlier the same day; the plain `terminal` path is unaffected (no re-parse of a stringified `calls`).
- No existing issue matches this exact case. Nearest: #83937 (empty-string args, fixed), #137028 (PII redaction), #25333 (Gemini `}{`), #103969 (truncation), #12731 (compression truncation) — all sibling output-shape failures.

## Suggested improvements
1. In the `validation.py:160` error, include a **±40-char context window around the failing offset** so the model can self-correct on retry (the raw bytes are already in scope at raise time).
2. Optionally: a one-shot "reserialize calls as a native array" nudge in the error text.

## Impact
Deferred-tool round trips (a2a, connectors) carrying long natural-language messages with backslash/quote runs silently burn retries until the model accidentally emits well-formed encoding, or the agent falls back to raw HTTP.

## Full evidence
Live transcript (complete tool/assistant trace):
`/home/clawski/.hermes/profiles/kenny/cache/delegation/live/deleg_c5d345ef/task-0.log`
## AI co-authorship / reproduction environment
This issue was diagnosed and drafted by the owner's local AI assistant (Kenny, `kenny` profile), on the owner's instruction.
- Model: UDP-UNCENSORED-Qwen3.8-27B (uncensored Qwen3.8-27B custom build)
- Inference engine: self-hosted NInfer (OpenAI-compatible, api_mode: chat_completions) over Tailscale at xtreme:18080
- Hermes Agent v0.23.1 (2026.9.24, stable, local 3b4215785882)
- The malformed `calls` encoding occurred in the model's own output through Hermes' custom-provider path.

issues.body:
## Bug Description

The Desktop profile rail can show **"N unread sessions"** for a profile when opening that profile shows nothing unread. In my case the rail said **5 unread sessions**. The profile has exactly one visible session, and the backend reports nothing unread: every row has `last_read_at = NULL`, which `SessionDB.session_unread` treats as read.

The count comes from the renderer's persisted markers (`localStorage["hermes.desktop.unreadFinishedSessions"]`). `profile-dot-state.ts` pass 3 adds one unread for each marker id that has no loaded row. I decoded that key from the renderer's LevelDB. The affected profile's bucket held exactly 5 ids, which matches the badge:

| marker | what it refers to (checked in every profile's `state.db`) |
|---|---|
| `<id-1>` | the profile's own Bot Chat: exists, `hidden=1`. This is the #146762 class. |
| `<id-2>` | **another profile's** Bot Chat. It exists only in the `default` profile's `state.db`, yet the same id sits in four profile buckets. |
| `<id-3>` | a `local-…` desktop chat. **No row in any profile's `state.db`.** It appears only in `gateway.log`. |
| `<id-4>` | same: deleted |
| `<id-5>` | same: deleted |

Ids 3–5 can never be cleared:

- Opening the session is impossible, because it no longer exists.
- `forgetSessionUnread` only runs on a delete or archive that Desktop itself performs. These sessions disappeared without Desktop seeing it.
- **Mark all as read** cannot reach them. `ackAllSessionsRead()` acks loaded rows only. In addition, the header button renders only when `$unreadFinishedSessionIds.length > 0` (`app/chat/sidebar/index.tsx`, `{unreadCount > 0 && (`), and the filter-menu item is disabled on the same condition. So with zero loaded unread there is no button at all.

The marker module's own comment already names the failure (`session-unread.ts`, above `MARKERS_CAP`): a marker whose session is gone "is invisible (nothing paints it) but immortal". The comment is right that nothing paints the row, but the profile rail **does** count it. The cap of 200 per profile only bounds how large the wrong count can get.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use Desktop with two profiles, A and B.
2. In profile B, have a session finish while B is not the active profile, so it gets a persisted unread marker.
3. Delete that session somewhere Desktop does not observe: the CLI, a retention/prune pass, or another client.
4. Switch Desktop to profile A.
5. B's rail square shows "1 unread session" indefinitely. Selecting B shows no such session, and there is no Mark-all-as-read affordance because no loaded row is unread.

For steps 2–3 I am working from the code path and the persisted state described above. I have not run this sequence on a clean profile.

## Expected Behavior

A marker for a session that no longer exists on any profile should be dropped, just as pins, drafts, queued prompts and interrupted sends already are.

## Actual Behavior

The rail counts dead ids forever. On this install the persisted record also holds markers in several other profile buckets (9 in one, 4 in another, 3 in three more). I have only verified the five in the affected bucket.

## Affected Component

Other: Desktop (profile rail / persisted unread markers)

## Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A. This is Desktop renderer state.

## Debug Report

Not generated. `hermes debug share` uploads logs, and everything needed to reproduce is in this report.

## Operating System

Windows 11 (packaged Desktop build)

## Python Version

3.14 (Hermes-managed venv)

## Hermes Version

v0.23.1 (commit `3b42157858`). `apps/desktop/src/store/dead-session-prune.ts` on `main` at `b2c6bc4e1e` is byte-identical to that commit, and `profile-dot-state.ts` pass 3 is unchanged there.

## Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

- The shipped bundle contains the marker store: `app.asar.unpacked/dist/assets/session-states-*.js` → ``P=l(`hermes.desktop.unreadFinishedSessions`,{},oe.json(jr))``.
- The marker ids came from the decoded LevelDB value. Each id was looked up in the root `state.db` and in every `profiles/*/state.db`, opened read-only. As a control, the same lookup found ids 1 and 2, so the misses for ids 3–5 are real.

## Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`store/dead-session-prune.ts` exists for exactly this situation ("When a session is removed from state.db (retention purge, manual delete, another surface pruning it), those keys go stale: nothing ever drops them"). Its candidate list covers pins, drafts, queued prompts and interrupted sends, **but not unread markers**, even though those are the one session-keyed store whose staleness is user-visible as a number.

A second issue I can only describe, not pin down: id 2 (a live Bot Chat that belongs to `default`) was filed into the buckets of four different profiles. `markSessionUnreadFinished` → `unlistedProfile()` falls back to `$activeGatewayProfile` when a session has no loaded row and no `profileHint`, so a hidden session completing while another profile is active would land in the wrong bucket. I have **not** identified which caller wrote these entries. The fix below does not touch them, because the session is alive on its own profile. See "B" below.

## Proposed Fix (optional)

**A, applied and tested locally.** Add the markers to the existing sweep, so they use the same "404 on every profile" verdict and the same non-404 deferral as everything else. 2 files, +39/−2.

```diff
diff --git a/apps/desktop/src/store/dead-session-prune.ts b/apps/desktop/src/store/dead-session-prune.ts
--- a/apps/desktop/src/store/dead-session-prune.ts
+++ b/apps/desktop/src/store/dead-session-prune.ts
@@ -6,8 +6,11 @@
  * (`hermes:composer-drafts:v4`, mirrored to v3), queued prompts
  * (`hermes.desktop.composerQueue.v1`) and interrupted sends
  * (`hermes:composer-outbox:v1:*`) are keyed by session id and re-asserted
- * or probed at boot. When a session is removed from state.db (retention purge,
- * manual delete, another surface pruning it), those keys go stale: nothing
+ * or probed at boot. Unread markers (`hermes.desktop.unreadFinishedSessions`)
+ * are keyed the same way and, worse, are COUNTED: the profile rail paints
+ * every marker with no loaded row as an unread session. When a session is
+ * removed from state.db (retention purge, manual delete, another surface
+ * pruning it), those keys go stale: nothing
  * ever drops them, so every boot re-requests the dead ids and the gateway
  * answers `404 {"detail":"Session not found"}` once per stale reference,
  * forever.
@@ -28,6 +31,7 @@ import { $queuedPromptsBySession, clearQueuedPrompts } from '@/store/composer-qu
 import { $pinnedSessionIds, unpinSession } from '@/store/layout'
 import { $activeGatewayProfile, $profiles, normalizeProfileKey } from '@/store/profile'
 import { $sessions } from '@/store/session'
+import { $unreadFinishedMarkers, forgetSessionUnread } from '@/store/session-unread'
 
 import { forgetPinSyncState } from './session-pin-sync'
 
@@ -154,6 +158,14 @@ function collectCandidates(): string[] {
     }
   }
 
+  for (const ids of Object.values($unreadFinishedMarkers.get())) {
+    for (const id of ids) {
+      if (!covered.has(id)) {
+        candidates.add(id)
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
   // Fresh-chat keys are never session references (they expire with the outbox entry instead).
   for (const scope of interruptedSendScopes()) {
     if (!covered.has(scope) && !isFreshDraftScope(scope)) {
@@ -197,6 +209,13 @@ function dropDeadId(id: string): void {
   }
 
   dropInterruptedSends(id)
+
+  // Dead on every profile, so every bucket holding the id is stale.
+  for (const [profile, ids] of Object.entries($unreadFinishedMarkers.get())) {
+    if (ids.includes(id)) {
+      forgetSessionUnread([id], profile)
+    }
+  }
 }
 
 async function sweepOnce(requireLoaded = true): Promise<void> {
diff --git a/apps/desktop/src/store/dead-session-prune.test.ts b/apps/desktop/src/store/dead-session-prune.test.ts
--- a/apps/desktop/src/store/dead-session-prune.test.ts
+++ b/apps/desktop/src/store/dead-session-prune.test.ts
@@ -19,6 +19,7 @@ import { $queuedPromptsBySession, enqueueQueuedPrompt, getQueuedPrompts } from '
 import { $pinnedSessionIds } from '@/store/layout'
 import { $activeGatewayProfile, $profiles } from '@/store/profile'
 import { $sessions } from '@/store/session'
+import { $unreadFinishedMarkers } from '@/store/session-unread'
 
 import { __runDeadSessionPrunePass, resetDeadSessionPrune, watchDeadSessionPrune } from './dead-session-prune'
 
@@ -48,6 +49,7 @@ beforeEach(() => {
   $sessions.set([])
   $pinnedSessionIds.set([])
   $queuedPromptsBySession.set({})
+  $unreadFinishedMarkers.set({})
   $profiles.set([profile('default'), profile('work')])
   $activeGatewayProfile.set('default')
   getSessionMock.mockReset()
@@ -113,6 +115,22 @@ describe('__runDeadSessionPrunePass', () => {
     expect($pinnedSessionIds.get()).toEqual([])
   })
 
+  it('drops unread markers for a dead session from every bucket and keeps live ones', async () => {
+    $sessions.set([row('unrelated')])
+    $unreadFinishedMarkers.set({ default: ['dead-unread', 'hidden-live'], work: ['dead-unread'] })
+    getSessionMock.mockImplementation(async id => {
+      if (id === 'hidden-live') {
+        return row(id)
+      }
+
+      throw notFound()
+    })
+
+    await __runDeadSessionPrunePass()
+
+    expect($unreadFinishedMarkers.get()).toEqual({ default: ['hidden-live'] })
+  })
+
   it('discards drafts for dead sessions but never the new-chat draft', async () => {
     $sessions.set([row('unrelated')])
     stashSessionDraft('dead-draft-session', 'stale text', [])
```

Verification on v0.23.1:

- `vitest run --project ui src/store/dead-session-prune.test.ts src/store/session-unread.test.ts src/store/profile-dot-state.test.ts`: **38/38 pass**.
- Control: with the `dropDeadId` hunk disabled, the new test **fails** (`dead-unread` stays in both buckets).
- `eslint` on both files is clean.

Notes for review:

- **Hidden sessions are kept.** `GET /api/sessions/{id}` → `resolve_session_id` / `get_session` applies no `hidden` filter, so a hidden Bot Chat is "alive" and its marker stays. I checked this in the source, not live. The `hidden-live` case in the test pins this. Whether a hidden session should count on the rail at all is #146762's question, not this one.
- **Inherits #144702.** The sweep probes the active connection only. After a gateway-connection switch, a marker for a session on the other connection would be judged dead and dropped, just as queued prompts, drafts and pins are today. For markers, the cost of that false drop is a lost dot, not lost text. #145224 changes the same sweep. I have not checked whether its fix lands in the shared verdict, which is what would cover markers too.
- **Open PRs touching the same file:** #132873, #145224, #146320, #134808, #139898. The hunks are small and should rebase cleanly, but I have not tried.

**B, not implemented: misfiled markers.** A per-bucket check (`getSession(id, bucketProfile)`; a 404 → `forgetSessionUnread([id], bucketProfile)`) would also clear id 2. The narrower fix is at the write: `unlistedProfile()` falling back to the active gateway when the owner is unknown is what lets a hidden session's completion be filed under the wrong profile.

**C, not implemented: an escape hatch.** Let Mark all as read also clear markers when nothing loaded is unread, or give the rail square its own "Mark read" action. Today the user has no way to clear the badge.

## Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

Not at this time. The diff above is ready to lift as-is.

issues.body:
## Summary

A kanban card whose worker run was **rate-limited once and then succeeded on retry** is never dispatched to its reviewer. `check_respawn_guard` keeps returning `blocker_auth` for it on every tick, indefinitely. The gateway logs `kanban dispatcher stuck: ready queue non-empty for N consecutive ticks but 0 workers spawned … blocker_auth=***`.

Observed on 4 of 4 cards that hit a provider quota wall on 2026-09-21 (checkout at `3b7eda0887`, 2026-09-20). Before the first quota wall, 114 review handoffs on the same board had never triggered it.

## Mechanism

1. The dead-worker sweep stamps `tasks.last_failure_error` with the rate-limit text (`kanban_db_dispatch.py` ≈ L1190, "requeued without counting a failure").
2. `check_respawn_guard` (≈ L1491) skips the quota regex only while the card's **latest ended run** is the `rate_limited` one (step 1 returns early). Once the retried worker finishes and calls `request_review`, the latest run is `review_requested`, so step 1 no longer applies.
3. Step 2 then matches the stale stamp against `_RESPAWN_BLOCKER_RE` (`quota`, `rate limit`, …) and returns `blocker_auth`. The review lane (`≈ L2258`) checks the guard before every spawn, so the reviewer is never started.
4. `last_failure_error` is only cleared by `complete_task` (`_clear_failure_counter`, ≈ L1480). `request_review` in `kanban_db.py` (≈ L3360, the `UPDATE tasks SET status='review' …`) does not clear it.

## Reproduce

1. Card with an implementer + reviewer profile. Make the implementer's first run exit rate-limited (provider 429).
2. Let the requeue run succeed and `request_review`.
3. `hermes kanban show <id>` → status `review`, events show `respawn_guarded {'reason': 'blocker_auth'}` every tick; the reviewer never spawns.

## Suggested fix

In `request_review`, add `last_failure_error = NULL` to the `UPDATE tasks SET status = 'review', …` statement (the same reset `complete_task` performs): a successful implementer run supersedes the rate-limit stamp. Alternatively, in `check_respawn_guard`, only consult `last_failure_error` when the latest run's outcome is itself a failure.

## Workaround we run

A cron that NULLs `last_failure_error` for cards in `review`/`ready` whose latest ended run is `review_requested` or `completed`.

prs.title: feat(display): diff-aware tool preview truncation
prs.body:
**Diff-aware tool-preview truncation** — full production path, rebased onto current `main`. Fixes #24298.

Show consecutive tool-call previews under the same ~40-char budget by eliding the shared prefix and revealing the **differing tail** (e.g. `cd /p && alpha` vs `… && beta`), instead of a dumb trailing-`...` head-cut that renders distinct commands identically (and then wrongly collapses them into `(×N)`).

### Before / After
Two consecutive distinct commands sharing a long `cd` prefix, at a ~40-char preview cap:

**Before** (dumb head-cut → identical renders → false repeat):
```
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/path && run al..."
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/path && run al..." (×2)   ← looks like a stall
```
**After** (diff-aware → differing tail shown, no false collapse):
```
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/…&& run alpha"
💻 terminal: "…&& run beta"
```
A genuine repeat of the *same* command still collapses to `(×2)` — dedup keys on raw identity, not on the rendered string.

### @teknium1's review — both points addressed on the production path
- [x] **Dedup keys on RAW identity, not rendered-truncation equality.** `_progress_emit` (gateway/run_turn_runner.py) now takes a `raw_key` derived from raw inputs (`tool_name` + raw command / preview / args) and dedups on that; truncation can no longer make two distinct commands collapse into `(×N)`. `truncate_middle()` stays presentation-only.
- [x] **The terminal/code-block path no longer head-truncates + bypasses.** `_progress_terminal_blocks` uses `truncate_middle` with a threaded `prev` (same as the ordinary preview path) instead of `cmd[:cap-3]+"..."`.

### Changes
- `agent/display.py`: `truncate_middle` / `_truncate_around_diff` / `_head_tail_truncate`; `prepare_tool_preview` gains optional `prev=`.
- `gateway/platforms/base.py::format_tool_event` **and** `gateway/run_turn_runner.py` (`_progress_build_message` / `_progress_terminal_blocks` / `_progress_emit`) thread `prev` + the raw dedup key via new `gateway/turn_context.py` fields.
- Tests: `tests/agent/test_display_truncate_middle.py` + `tests/gateway/test_run_progress_diff_aware.py` — distinct prefix-sharing commands must NOT collapse to `(×N)`; true repeats must (incl. on the `supports_code_blocks=True` path); covers a non-terminal preview. Stale expectations updated. All green.

The original branch was ~24k commits behind; this is a clean re-application onto current `main`.

prs.title: fix(batch): keep tool-search bridge trajectories
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #123817.

The batch trajectory merger previously validated `tool_stats` against a module-import-time snapshot of registered tools. Tool Search bridge tools are synthesized separately, and plugins/MCP servers can register tools after import. Valid trajectories could therefore be incorrectly discarded as corrupted.

### Changes

- Resolve the registered tool names at merge time instead of relying on a stale import-time snapshot.
- Include inline executor names and Tool Search bridge names in the valid-tool set.
- Keep the existing behavior for ordinary registered tools.

### Regression coverage

- Tool Search bridge trajectories survive batch merging.
- A tool registered after `batch_runner` import survives merging.
- Inline executor tools that bypass the registry survive merging.

### Testing status

The regression tests are committed. GitHub Actions currently report `action_required` for this fork PR, so upstream CI still needs maintainer approval.

The change is limited to trajectory merge validation; normal tool registration and execution are unchanged.
