prs.title: fix(approval): preserve executable shell text across guard and smart review
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Shell comment handling could hide executable suffixes from both the approval detector and the smart-review guardian. For example, Bash treats the hash in `echo $(printf hi)#x; reboot` as word data, but the detector previously swallowed the suffix as a comment and the public guard could approve without reaching smart review. Similar omissions affected the text sent to the guardian in multiline strings, expansions, and other shell contexts.

- Fix the detector's comment boundaries using shell blanks and lexical word state, preserving word continuity across escapes, quotes, expansion closers and conditional regex operands. Match nested substitutions without treating parameter text, case-pattern closers or ordinary keyword-like arguments as shell syntax. Keep genuine comments after subshells, functions and arithmetic commands inert.
- Preserve executable text in smart review. Strip only recognizable word-start comments; retain multiline quote state and meaningful newlines/escaped padding. Preserve complete input for ambiguous expansion, process-substitution, extglob, array-assignment, conditional, arithmetic, dollar-quote and heredoc forms, including markers split by line continuations.
- Align shell whitespace handling in the existing heredoc and terminal scanners. No dependency, configuration, model prompt, tool schema or workflow is added.

This is approval-input hardening related to #117815 item 1 and #121759. Items 2–4 of #117815 remain outside scope. These scanners are heuristics, not a full shell parser or an OS security boundary. Conservative smart-review fallbacks retain genuine comments under the existing untrusted-input instructions.

## Contribution

- @lolchocotaco / Sameer's multiline and heredoc contribution from [shoyann/hermes-agent#1](https://github.com/shoyann/hermes-agent/pull/1) is retained with its original authorship.
- @beardthelion's canonical detector repair from [#121761](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/121761), original commit `cb191cfd0721d9c6ec8ace79ec02298f6194a1b7`, is cherry-picked with authorship and provenance preserved. Follow-up word-state handling covers escaped boundaries and genuine parenthesis comments that the original patch did not handle.

## Validation

Current head: `26ad8c9fecae27923c2cb0233008433b17ecc3fc`, rebased onto `main@33c9b1d7796b34d76e6b71fc4251a7197f7ffd80`. Validation is on WSL Ubuntu / Linux, Python 3.14, using a PM-built `dev`/`test` environment and the repository's `scripts/run_tests.sh` runner with retries disabled.

- The new two public-guard invariants cover **43 inputs**, using real temporary configuration, smart mode and disabled Tirith, with no manufactured warning prefix. They require a hardline denial for executable suffixes and acceptance for inert comment controls; neither model review nor human approval may be called. Commands are classified, never executed. The initial expanded tests were red before the word-state follow-up: **9 failed / 29 passed** on the cherry-picked detector repair. Five further inputs protect nested parameters, conditional regexes, genuine comments inside process substitution, and keyword-like arguments identified during independent review.
- Existing projection tests separately exercise real config → terminal / `execute_code` guard → smart review and assert the complete `<command>` payload, replacing only the model response.
- **834 tests passed, 0 failed across 20 files**, covering smart approval, public guards, hardline rules, deny rules, self-repository protection, terminal sudo/background handling, and cron heredoc handling.
- `python scripts/check`: **all 11 checks passed**, including code health with zero blocking and zero advisory findings. `git diff --check` passed.
- **60 harmless Bash witnesses passed**: a 48-case independent comment-boundary corpus, six adjacent regression probes and six keyword-argument controls. Bash executed only harmless output/assignment inputs; dangerous suffixes were used only as classifier strings. This is focused evidence for these cases, not a general shell-parser guarantee.

The full repository suite, Windows/macOS and live-model evaluations were not rerun for this revision. Earlier fork and live-model evidence applies only to the historical commits on which it ran. Local results do not establish upstream CI acceptance; hosted workflows may require maintainer approval.

Implementation, review follow-up, tests and submission were prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance.

prs.title: fix: raw docstrings to silence invalid escape sequence warnings
prs.body:
## Summary

Python 3.12+ emits `SyntaxWarning: invalid escape sequence` for each of these docstrings, and a future release will turn them into `SyntaxError`. Found by compiling every `.py` in the repo with `warnings.catch_warnings(record=True)` — **7 occurrences across 5 files**, all docstrings containing literal backslashes:

| File | Offending text |
|---|---|
| `hermes_cli/update_cmd.py` | `venv\Scripts`, `$InstallDir\bin` |
| `tests/hermes_cli/test_scan_venv_blockers.py` | `.hermes-runtime\python\generation-...` |
| `tests/gateway/test_media_tag_separator.py` | regex shorthand `\s`, `\S` (x2 docstrings) |
| `tests/tools/test_fuzzy_match.py` | backslash runs `` ``\`` `` / `` ``\\`` `` (x2 docstrings) |
| `tests/agent/test_credits_tracker.py` | regex `^-?\d+\.\d{2}$` |

Beyond the warnings, `\b` in `$InstallDir\bin` was **silently collapsing to a backspace character** inside the `_ensure_acp_launcher` docstring (it's a valid string escape), so `__doc__` did not match the source text.

## Fix

Convert all seven docstrings to raw strings (`r"""`). Zero behaviour change; each `__doc__` now renders byte-identically to the source.

## Testing

- Full-repo scan (compile + `warnings.catch_warnings`) → **0 remaining invalid escape sequences**
- `python -m py_compile` on all touched files → OK
- `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_scan_venv_blockers.py tests/gateway/test_media_tag_separator.py tests/tools/test_fuzzy_match.py tests/agent/test_credits_tracker.py -o 'addopts=' -q` → **139 passed**

## Relation to #84537

Supersedes #84537: that PR escapes backslashes by doubling them in a single docstring; this PR fixes the whole class (all 7 sites repo-wide) with raw strings, keeping docstring text unchanged.

prs.title: plugin-catalog: add harness2 (Harness^2 self-improvement loop)
prs.body:
This PR adds the `harness2` plugin to the plugin catalog. The plugin is a native rebuild of the Harness^2 self-improvement loop (arXiv:2610.14224).

## What the plugin does

A harness is the set of files that shape an agent. The set is the system prompt, the configuration, and the skills. The plugin makes the agent better at a class of work. It edits the files of the harness. It re-runs the task in new sessions under the edited files. It keeps only the edits that the evidence supports. It saves the lessons in a library that the next run reads first.

A banked harness is a harness saved in the library. The live profile is the profile you use day to day. The plugin never writes the live profile.

## How one round works

1. The task runs once under the unedited harness.
2. The agent makes two edited harnesses. One changes how the agent works. The other adds what an expert in the field knows.
3. The task runs once under each edited harness, in its own session.
4. The agent merges the edits that the run evidence supports.
5. The task runs once under the merged harness.
6. The agent saves at most one lesson, with its evidence. The harness and the lesson enter the library.
7. The promote stage writes a carry-over report: what the banked harness changed against the unedited base, the evidence for each change, and what to apply to the live profile. The user applies what they approve.

## What the plugin uses in Hermes

The plugin uses these Hermes surfaces:

- `ctx.register_tool` - 9 tools that run the loop (`harness2_init`, `harness2_probe`, `harness2_seed`, `harness2_check`, `harness2_adopt`, `harness2_promote`, `harness2_library`, `harness2_status`, `harness2_gc`). The tool code is plain Python. It makes no model calls.
- `ctx.register_skill` - 5 skills for the judgment stages (`run`, `propose`, `compose`, `select`, `reflect`). They point at the stage prompts from the paper, which ship in `assets/prompts/`.
- `plugins.plugin_storage.plugin_data_dir` - all run state (runs, candidates, library). The installed plugin tree stays read-only.
- `config_schema` - 2 settings: `probe_budget_seconds` (default 900) and `probe_source_tag`.
- `python_dependencies` - 1 declared dependency: `PyYAML>=6,<7`, installed at plugin install time. Hosts without PyYAML use a small ruamel fallback inside the plugin. The docker-managed venv ships ruamel.yaml instead of PyYAML. The declared dependency is a load path, not a hard requirement.

The plugin uses no hooks and no middleware. It has one guarded core import (`hermes_constants`, for home resolution, with a fallback to the `HERMES_HOME` environment variable when the core is not importable). It makes no network calls. In normal operation it reads no settings from environment variables.

## What the plugin does to your machine (Rule 13 disclosures)

Full disclosure of what the plugin does on your machine:

- The plugin runs `hermes profile create --clone` and one-shot `hermes -p harness2-<task>-<probe> chat` sessions. A probe is a fresh agent session under one harness. Each probe is a full agent session billed to the configured model. Each probe has a time limit (900 seconds by default, a per-plugin setting).
- The probe overlay pins `approvals.mode: smart`, `approvals.single_query_mode: deny`, and `approvals.cron_mode: deny`, plus `security.redact_secrets: true`. Probes run as one-shot queries. No human is present to answer a prompt. A user's own `single_query_mode: approve` cannot reach a model-launched probe. The plugin never sets `single_query_mode: approve`, `approvals.mode: off`, or any non-interactive bypass.
- The plugin creates and refreshes Hermes profiles named `harness2-*`. Creation is `hermes profile create --clone`. It pins `HERMES_HOME` to the active profile's home, so a turn in one profile can never clone another profile's configuration. The clone carries the active profile's configuration and `.env` once, under Hermes' own clone policy. Every refresh after the first applies only the overlay keys (plus the run budget) with `hermes -p <probe> config set`. It also replaces `SOUL.md` and `skills/`. It never rewrites the profile's configuration or touches its `.env`. Probes run under the user's own model wiring. `harness2_gc` deletes only the probe profiles the plugin recorded creating for the named task.
- The plugin writes only to its data directory and the probe profile directories. Its read outside them is the task's user-supplied `source_dir` at init. It refuses paths outside the session's working directory, inside the Hermes home or root, under home credential directories, or through dot-dirs. The promote report writes into the run directory only. Applying the report to the live profile is the user's step, not the plugin's. Probes get the same tool access as any profile, including the web. The README shows how to remove the web toolset for offline tasks.
- The plugin sends no telemetry and no usage reports.

## Validation

`hermes plugins validate` passes at the pinned SHA (941fee06): manifest, declared tools, security scan, and the `python_dependencies` declaration. There is no core override. `scripts/check_yaml_fallback.py` keeps the ruamel fallback path honest in PyYAML-less venvs.

prs.title: fix(gateway): a reply's attachments follow its text onto the reconnected adapter
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

When a platform adapter reconnects while a turn is still running, the reply's text and its attachments go out on different transports.

`send_final_ledgered` resolves the runner's current adapter through `_final_delivery_adapter`, so the final text lands on the replacement.
`_deliver_attachments` keeps calling `self._send_image_batch` and `self._deliver_media_attachments`, which is the retired adapter, whose client is gone.
On Discord, `send_multiple_images` then returns `SendResult(success=False, error="Not connected")`.
`_send_image_batch` records that result without logging it, and the turn still counts as delivered because the text send succeeded.
The user gets the reply text and none of its images, and the gateway log shows nothing after `Sending response`.

Seen on v0.23.1 with Discord: the WebSocket health check forced a reconnect while two long turns whose replies carried images were running.
The reconnect builds a new adapter (`_create_adapter_off_loop_deps`, `_install_reconnected_adapter`) and disconnects the old one, but the running turns still held the old one.
About 15 minutes later both replies arrived as text only.
Turns that started after the reconnect delivered their images normally, and resending the same files with `hermes send` worked.

The fix:

- `_deliver_attachments` resolves `_final_delivery_adapter(event.source)` once and sends image URLs, `MEDIA:` files and local files through it, the same transport as the final text.
- `_send_image_batch` logs a warning when the batch result is a failure (`N image(s) not delivered: <error>`), so a refused upload is no longer silent.
  Exceptions were already logged; this also covers a returned failure.

`gateway/platforms/base.py` is over the file-size cap, so two docstrings were shortened to keep the file at its current line count.

## Related Issue

No existing issue; the reproduction is below.
Related prior work: #113496 (closed, unmerged) put attachments in the delivery ledger but still sent them on `self`.
#105500 (open) changes the same `_send_image_batch` call for reply anchoring; whichever merges second needs a one-line rebase.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/platforms/base.py`: `_deliver_attachments` sends through `_final_delivery_adapter(event.source)`; `_send_image_batch` logs a failed batch result.
- `tests/gateway/test_attachments_follow_live_adapter.py`: two tests through `_process_message_background` with a fake transport whose retired instance refuses uploads the way the Discord adapter does.
  One checks that after a reconnect the image goes out on the replacement adapter with the text; the other checks that a refused image batch is logged with its error.

Not changed here, same pattern: auto-TTS (`_play_tts_file`) and the turn-error notice (`_notify_turn_error`) still send on the adapter the turn started on.
No in-chat notice is added for a failed image batch, because several adapters' `send_multiple_images` overrides already post their own and a central one risks duplicates.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_attachments_follow_live_adapter.py`: both tests fail on `main` (`assert [] == ['preview.png']`, and no warning logged) and pass with this change.
2. `scripts/run_tests.sh` on 23 related delivery, media and reconnect files (`test_platform_base`, `test_media_only_outcome`, `test_mixed_attachment_routing`, `test_send_multiple_images`, `test_tts_media_routing`, `test_send_voice_dispatch_signatures`, `test_telegram_media_flood`, `test_diagnostic_wake_presentation`, `test_media_extraction`, `test_silent_partial_delivery`, `test_delivery_flood_invariants`, `test_platform_reconnect`, `test_relay_final_delivery_incident`, `test_telegram_final_delivery`, `test_native_reply_delivered_once`, `test_post_stream_media_delivery`, `test_queued_followup_final_delivery`, `test_media_resend_dedup`, `test_attachment_retry_mixed_staging`, `test_discord_audio_delivery`, `test_multiplex_docker_media_delivery_scope`, `test_warning_delivery_real_producers` and the new file): 277 passed, 0 failed, 17 skipped on this branch.
3. `python scripts/check --staged --base upstream/main`: 19 checks ok; code health 0 blocking, 0 advisory.

I also ran the whole `tests/gateway/` directory with the same change applied to v0.23.1 (`3b42157`): 14,614 passed, 10 failed.
The same 10 fail on unmodified v0.23.1: five need the optional `acp` package my test environment lacks, one is the owner-loop stall timing check in `test_api_admission_off_loop`, one is a local HTTP read timeout in `test_native_http_auth`, and three in `test_session_client_env` read host tool paths.
I did not rerun the whole directory on `main`.

I have not watched a live reconnect with this change yet; the reconnect path is covered by the tests above.

## Checklist

### Code

- [ ] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) (read the PR process section and the root, `gateway/` and `tests/` AGENTS.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [x] I've run `just test` on the tests for the code I changed, and they pass (`scripts/run_tests.sh` directly, the runner `just test` calls)
- [x] `just check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs) (`scripts/check --staged --base upstream/main`)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 26 (Apple silicon), tests only

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A (docstrings of the two changed methods)
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A (no file I/O, process or terminal handling)
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A

(`desktop/plugin.js` is not touched), `requires_hermes` stays `">=0.22.5"`.

## What changes in the entry

Only these fields, nothing else (`description`, `known_issues`, `capabilities`, `platforms`, `requires_hermes` and the

| Field | 0.1.0 | 0.1.1 |

|---|---|---|
| `add_module`, `connect` and `add_parts` (with a module) accept common breakout labels in `conn` and map them to a pin of the catalog entry, so `conn={SDA, SCL, GND}` works for `bme280`, where 0.1.0 refused `SDA`. A bus label (`SDA`, `SCL`, `SCK`/`SCLK`/`CLK`, `MOSI`/`SDI`/`DIN`/`SI`, `MISO`/`SDO`/`DOUT`/`SO`, `CS`/`SS`/`NSS`/`CSN`) counts when exactly one pin of the module's active variant carries that signal and no other pin's name starts with the label; `VCC`/`VDD` and `GND`/`VSS` only stand in for each other. A real pin name always wins (on the `l298n`, `VSS` is the logic supply, not ground). An ambiguous label is refused with its candidates (`'CLK' fits more than one pin of enc28j60 (CLKOUT, SCK): name the pin`); `VCC` is refused the same way on a module with two supply pins (`'VCC' fits more than one pin of bme280 (VDD, VDDIO): name the pin`), which covers many common sensor breakouts. The project stores the catalog pin name; every mapping appears under `assumptions` with code `pin_alias` (for example `SDA → SDI`: `bme280: I²C data pin, catalog pin SDI (SDA in I²C mode)`). `VIN`, `3V3`, `5V`, `RX` and `TX` are never labels. | `circuit_bench/bench_core/modspec.py`, `circuit_bench/bench_core/project.py` | `tests/test_u011_pin_alias.py` |
| The `ads1220` catalog entry had no pin for its SPI clock input; it now has `SCLK` (datasheet p. 4), so `SCK` and `SCLK` map to it, and `CLK` stays the external clock input. A test requires a clock pin for every entry with SPI and data and clock pins for every entry with I²C. | `circuit_bench/data/modules/nmeasure.json`, `tests/corpus/excerpts/mod-nmeasure-ads1220.txt` | `tests/test_mod_nmeasure.py`, `tests/test_u011_catalog_interfaces.py` |
| The hint for an unknown `conn` pin lists the module's pins with the labels that map to them, for example `pins: GND, CSB, SDI (SDA), SCK (SCL), SDO, VDDIO, VDD` for `bme280`; a long list is cut at a pin boundary near 300 characters. | `circuit_bench/bench_core/modspec.py`, `circuit_bench/bench_core/project.py` | `tests/test_u011_pin_alias.py` |
| The description of `conn` in `bench_project` now says that a key is a pin or a label (`pin/label (SDA)->net/role/GPIO<n>; null unlinks`). | `circuit_bench/schemas.py` | `tests/test_u011_pin_alias.py` |

### Approval and the hardware path

| Change | Files | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| In 0.1.0, when the plugin settings could not be read from Hermes' configuration, the plugin used its defaults, which include `hardware_access: true`. Now real hardware and flashing stay off (`hardware_access` and `allow_flash` `false`) and port approval stays on (`approve_serial` `true`), while numbers and paths keep their defaults. `/bench doctor` marks the check `settings` as `FAIL` (the Bench's doctor dialog shows it as a failed row) and shows the warning `settings_unreadable`, and agent calls for real boards end with `sim_only` and a hint that names the cause. | `circuit_bench/bench_core/settings.py`, `circuit_bench/bench_core/doctor.py` | `tests/test_u011_settings.py` |
| `bench_board` `detect`, `monitor` and `flash` on a real port, and a `build` that starts PlatformIO, now run only if the plugin's approval hook let exactly that call through for the same task, action and target; otherwise the tool answers `not_confirmed`. One hook pass serves one run, also when no question is asked (`approve_serial` off). In 0.1.0 only a flash was tied to the question; the other three only checked that the hook was registered. | `circuit_bench/hooks.py`, `circuit_bench/tools.py` | `tests/test_u011_hook_binding.py` |
| The approval record that lets a handler run now lives `approvals.timeout` + 60 s, kept between 120 and 3600 s (360 s when the setting is absent, unreadable or no number); in 0.1.0 a flash record was stored before the question and kept for 3600 s. Every hook pass first removes the unused records of its task and stores its own as the last step; one record serves exactly one handler run. | `circuit_bench/tools.py`, `circuit_bench/hooks.py` | `tests/test_u011_hook_binding.py` |
| `bench_board flash` (agent tool and Bench) copies every file it will write into a private folder `tmp/flash-<random>` in the plugin data folder (mode `0700`, files `0600`), compares the copies with the hashes recorded at build time (`elf_mismatch` on a difference), passes only the copies to `esptool` and removes the folder on every exit (a folder left behind by a killed process is removed by a later flash once it is older than an hour). Files named `firmware.bin`, `bootloader.bin` or `partitions.bin` (compared without case) are checked at their private copy; a file that cannot be copied ends the flash with `tool_failed` before `esptool` starts. In 0.1.0 these files were hashed in the build folder and written from there. | `circuit_bench/bench_core/board.py` | `tests/test_u011_flash_snapshot.py` |
| The approval record of an agent flash holds the images and the time of the last build as well as the ELF, port and MAC; a build made while the question is open is not flashed: the same ELF with other images or time ends with `not_confirmed`, another ELF with `elf_mismatch`. | `circuit_bench/tools.py`, `circuit_bench/hooks.py` | `tests/test_u011_flash_build_change.py` |
| The approval question for a build or a flash names the checked values first (env, chip, MAC, port, ELF hash) and the firmware folder, the only free text, last and in quotes (`Firmware folder: "<path>"`, `Folder: "<path>"`). Control characters, line breaks, Unicode direction marks, space variants other than U+0020, every `Default_Ignorable_Code_Point` and `"` are shown as `\uXXXX`; in the folder every other quotation mark (all characters with the Unicode property `Quotation_Mark` except the apostrophe U+0027) and the characters that look like `"` (primes and a few others) are shown that way too, so a folder `Lab’s` (U+2019) appears as `Lab\u2019s`; letters stay as they are, look-alike letters and letters of right-to-left scripts too, and the latter can change the displayed order of the path parts in a folder name; the chip shows only its fixed name and revision; a build env that is no PlatformIO name is refused before the question. A path longer than 120 characters is shortened in the middle, also in its last part, so the shown path is never longer than 120 characters, and the question then ends with ` (path shortened)`, which also appears when a character was only replaced. The rule key for "always" of a build uses the full folder path and the env; that of a flash is made of port, MAC and ELF hash. | `circuit_bench/hooks.py`, `circuit_bench/bench_core/shown.py` | `tests/test_u011_approval_text.py`, `tests/test_u011_question_order.py`, `tests/test_u011_hidden_chars.py`, `tests/test_u011_field_quotes.py` |
| The port in the questions of a flash, a detection and a serial monitor keeps only letters, digits and `._:/-` as they are; every other character is shown as `\uXXXX` (`/dev/ttyACM0?Simulated,nothing-is-reset.OK` appears as `/dev/ttyACM0\u003fSimulated\u002cnothing-is-reset.OK`). A port URL other than `sim://` is blocked by the hook before the question, for all three actions and also with `approve_serial` off, with the words of the handler (`Circuit Bench blocked board detection: unsupported port URL 'rfc2217://h:1' (invalid_args); use a local device path or a sim:// port.`). In 0.1.0 the port was put into the detect and monitor questions unfiltered and such a URL was refused only after the approval. Normal ports (`/dev/ttyACM0`, `COM3`) give the same question and rule key as before. | `circuit_bench/hooks.py` | `tests/test_u011_serial_question.py` |
| The message and hint of an error answer and the message of a block by the hook show format and direction characters, line and paragraph separators, lone surrogates, DEL, C1 controls and every `Default_Ignorable_Code_Point` as `\uXXXX`; spaces such as the no-break space stay; input is not refused for them. Warnings, assumptions and serial lines are unchanged. | `circuit_bench/hooks.py`, `circuit_bench/bench_core/contracts.py`, `circuit_bench/bench_core/shown.py` | `tests/test_u011_model_messages.py` |
| When the approval hook is active but a call has no pass of it, the error hint says `call bench_board <action> again: Hermes asks the user first; sim:// ports still work`. | `circuit_bench/tools.py` | `tests/test_u011_hook_binding.py` |
| The agent's serial monitor listens at most for Hermes' deadline for a tool call minus 20 s, and never shorter than 1 s (`timeouts.tools.sequential_call`, else `timeouts.tools.concurrent_batch`, else `HERMES_CONCURRENT_TOOL_TIMEOUT_S`, else 420 s). A shortened run carries the warning `monitor_capped` (`info`). With the defaults (`monitor_max_seconds` 120, deadline 420 s) nothing is shortened. Only the agent path; the Bench console and stream are not affected. | `circuit_bench/bench_core/serialport.py`, `circuit_bench/bench_core/settings.py` | `tests/test_u011_monitor_cap.py` |
| A simulated build (`sim://` port) that does not start PlatformIO no longer reports the info warning `chip_unchecked`, since nothing is compiled. A wrong chip is still refused; builds that start `pio` keep the pre-check unchanged. | `circuit_bench/bench_core/board.py`, `circuit_bench/bench_core/sim.py` | `tests/test_u011_sim_build.py` |
| A build env or a project id with a line break at its end passed the name check (the patterns end in `$`, which also matches before a final line break): `board.build` started `pio` for such an env, and `project.create` made a project with the line break in its id and folder name. The input checks of the core now compare the whole text (`fullmatch`) and refuse it with `invalid_args`, as they do ISO times, serial port names, event names and pin roles with a final line break; valid names are unchanged. The agent tool strips outer whitespace from its text arguments before any check, so an env given there with a trailing line break arrives as the plain name. | `circuit_bench/bench_core/board.py`, `project.py`, `sim.py`, `serialport.py`, `events.py`, `pins.py` and `calckit.py` in the same folder | `tests/test_u011_line_end.py` |

### Calculators and hints

| Change | Files | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| The LED and NPN calculators no longer say `GPIO current limits are not checked here (unverified)` when the pin current can be compared: at or below the ESP32-S3 value the `gpio_current` note (`info`) names the comparison (`… below the 40.0 mA high-level source current of an ESP32-S3 pin (a typical value, not a maximum; chip not given)`). Above that value it stays a caution; without pin data the old sentence stays; a current a little above or below the limit that would round to it shows more digits. | `circuit_bench/bench_core/calc.py` | `tests/test_u011_calc.py` |
| `divider` takes an optional input `target` (`esp_pin`, default, or `other`). With `target=other` the check `calc.divider.pin_max` is `not_checked` and the warning `divider_overvoltage` is not raised, so a divider that feeds something other than an ESP pin no longer reports a failed check and a `danger` warning. Without `target` the answer is unchanged. The Desktop divider form has no `target` field. | `circuit_bench/bench_core/calc.py`, `circuit_bench/tools.py` | `tests/test_u011_calc.py` |
| `led_strip` adds a planning value, `result.i_planning`, for `ws2812b` and `apa102c` (60 mA per pixel at full white, class B, `rule of thumb, worst case at full white, not a datasheet value`) and says to size the supply for the larger of the two currents. For `ws2812b` it is the larger one: 60 × `WS2812B` at 5 V still show 2.20 A from the datasheet test condition and add 3.60 A. For `apa102c` it equals the datasheet value at full brightness (`brightness` 1, the default: 3.60 A for 60 pixels) and is the larger one below it. The `high_current` warning (from 1 A) uses the larger value and names the planning value (`… (rule of thumb, worst case at full white, not a datasheet value: 60.0 mA per pixel)`) only when that is the larger one, so not for `apa102c` at full brightness. `sk6812` has no planning value and answers as before. | `circuit_bench/bench_core/calcs/led_strip.py`, `circuit_bench/data/parts/pixel.json`, `circuit_bench/data/sources/calc-plus.json` | `tests/test_u011_led_strip.py` |
| An unknown part number names the most similar known part and says it is a different type with its own ratings (`no datasheet data for part '2N2222' (closest: 2N2222A, a different type with its own ratings; known: 2N2222A)`). The calculation does not use that part's data; no alias is created. | `circuit_bench/bench_core/parts.py`, `circuit_bench/bench_core/calc.py`, `circuit_bench/bench_core/calc_power.py` | `tests/test_u011_calc.py` |
| The `unknown_board` hint lists the known boards and ends with `or leave devkit out: the chip checks still run, pins.broken_out and pins.board are skipped`; where a board is asked for by id (the Bench's board layout) `devkit` cannot be left out, so the hint only lists the boards. | `circuit_bench/bench_core/boards.py` | `tests/test_u011_hints.py` |

## Disclosure (catalog rule 13): what changes against 0.1.0

- **Network:** no new access. The Python lines added under `circuit_bench/` contain no `urllib`, `requests`,
  `httpx`, `subprocess`, `Popen` or `clitools.run` (pattern match over `git diff -U0`); `socket` appears only in a
  docstring that names the refused port URL `socket://`, and `unicode.org` addresses only in source comments that name
  the Unicode data files the character lists were copied from (the plugin does not fetch them). The `web.archive.org`
  addresses in the source data are citations for the test corpus, not requests of the plugin.
- **Processes:** no new ones. Still only the user's own `pio`, `esptool` and `addr2line`, as in 0.1.0; at a flash,
  `esptool` now gets the private copies instead of the build folder files.
- **Hooks and capabilities:** no new ones. Still the one `pre_tool_call` hook (registered in
  `circuit_bench/__init__.py`, declared in `circuit_bench/plugin.yaml`; neither file adds a hook), still seven tools.
  The hook now also keeps an approval record in memory (see the approval rows above); nothing is written to disk for
  it.
- **New place the plugin writes:** `tmp/flash-<random>` in the plugin data folder
  (`<HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/circuit-bench/`, already named in the entry's `description`). Mode `0700`, files
  `0600`, created only for a flash of a real board, removed on every exit; leftovers older than 3600 s are removed
  by the next flash.
- **Hermes settings read (read only):** in addition to the plugin settings and the `approvals.*` modes read in 0.1.0:
  `approvals.timeout`, `timeouts.tools.sequential_call`, `timeouts.tools.concurrent_batch` and the environment
  variable `HERMES_CONCURRENT_TOOL_TIMEOUT_S`.
- **Unchanged:** no telemetry, no credentials, `requires_env` empty, `project.json` schema stays 1.

## Limits that stay

- A readable configuration that holds no entry for the plugin still gives the defaults, including
  `hardware_access: true`; the safe values apply only when the settings cannot be read. `allow_flash` stays off by
  default.
- The approval binding holds per task, action and target, not per single call, and does not stop code in the same
  process (another plugin) that fakes the arguments or calls the plugin's internals. That Hermes runs the hook before
  the handler and starts no handler after a denial is an observation of Hermes' source and of local probes, not a
  guarantee; the gateway and cron paths are derived from the source, not measured. With `approvals.timeout` above
  3540 s, or an unreadable `config.yaml`, a very late approval can end with `not_confirmed`.
- A flash checks images against the build-time hashes only for files named `firmware.bin`, `bootloader.bin` and
  `partitions.bin`, and by file name, not by flash address; `boot_app0.bin` and extra images of a project are written as
  they were when copied. The private copy is not protected against other processes of the same user, and it is taken
  after `pio project metadata`, which runs the project's own `extra_scripts`.
- Hidden characters are shown by a fixed list, not by judgement: look-alike letters stay as they are, and so do letters
  of right-to-left scripts, which can change the displayed order of the path parts in a folder name; the apostrophe
  U+0027 stays in a folder name, a shortened path hides its middle part, and warnings, assumptions and serial lines are
  not filtered. The `summary` and `result` of a success answer return texts of the project (title, notes, names) as
  stored.
- A label for a module pin is accepted only for bus signals (`SDA`, `SCL`, `SCK`/`SCLK`/`CLK`, `MOSI`/`SDI`/`DIN`/`SI`,
  `MISO`/`SDO`/`DOUT`/`SO`, `CS`/`SS`/`NSS`/`CSN`) and the supply and ground names above; anything ambiguous is refused.
- The planning current for `led_strip` is a rule of thumb from a hobbyist guide (class B, archived copy), not a
  datasheet value; it does not scale with `brightness`.

## Tested with

- **This release, one hardware run:** on 2026-11-14 on an ESP32-S3 (QFN56, revision v0.2, 16 MB flash) over its native
  USB port on Linux, through the tool-call path of Hermes v0.23.1 with its approval prompts: detect, a real PlatformIO
  build of the example firmware, flash (four images, verified by esptool), a second flash call that asked again and
  was blocked after a denial, monitor (panic found) and crash decode (4 of 4 frames, ELF matched). Apart from that,
  flash and serial paths were tested with fakes and a simulated board. The real-board results named in the entry
  (ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1, WT32-ETH01, Linux) are those of 0.1.0.
- **Locally**, at the commit pinned here: test suite 6963 passed, 0 skipped (39 opt-in tests marked `hermes` or
  `toolchain` are deselected by default); the project's in-process Hermes probe
  (121 steps each) passes against Hermes main `c269f8e1`, v0.22.5, v0.23.0 and v0.23.1;
  a cold fetch of the pinned test corpus into an empty directory ends with exit 0 and matching hashes
  (verified locally on 2026-11-13).
- **GitHub CI at the pinned commit** (2026-11-14, https://github.com/juvenile454/hermes-circuit-bench/actions): all
  eight jobs passed: pytest on Python 3.11, 3.14 and with the lowest direct dependencies (6963 passed each), desktop,
  Hermes v0.22.5, v0.23.0 and v0.23.1 (`plugins validate`, simulation), and macOS with Hermes v0.23.1 (6730 passed, 233
  skipped: the tests that need Linux pseudo-terminals, so flash and serial paths are not exercised on macOS). The new
  workflow `corpus-drift.yml`, started by hand, fetched the whole corpus with matching hashes.
- **Catalog gate, run locally against the pushed commit** with a clone of hermes-agent `main` (`29267cf49ca9`):
  `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/` OK and `scripts/ci/catalog_validate_pinned_entries.py` PASS
  (`security scan — safe`, declared tools and hooks match).
- **Update from 0.1.0:** exercised only from a local git source (a clone of the pinned commit), not through the catalog,
  with Hermes v0.22.5 and v0.23.1 in an isolated home. `hermes plugins update circuit-bench` asked once to confirm the
  plugin's two Python dependencies (the same as in 0.1.0; Hermes asks this only at a terminal) and then installed 0.1.1
  at the pinned commit. Afterwards the data folder was byte-identical, the settings were kept, the stored projects
  answered `bench_project get` and `bench_pins check` as before, and the flash hook still blocked. Installing 0.1.0
  over the same data again and a fresh install of 0.1.1 worked as well. The Desktop half was opened with these projects
  in an isolated app built from Hermes main only.

## Not verified before this PR

- **Scheduled CI:** the scheduled triggers of `ci.yml` and `corpus-drift.yml` have not fired yet; both workflows ran
  once at the pinned commit (above).
- **The catalog path of `hermes plugins update`:** how Hermes re-pins this entry on an installed 0.1.0 and whether a
  consent step appears could not be tested before the PR is merged; only the route through a local source was checked.
  On the local route Hermes asked once for the Python dependencies (see above). 0.1.1 adds no capability, tool, hook
  or dependency, so no further consent should be needed. Installations stay on 0.1.0 until their user updates.

## Known issues (unchanged)

The entry's `known_issues` are the text of 0.1.0 (session-scoped `/yolo` and `hermes -z`; real boards need PlatformIO,
esptool and serial port access, tested on Linux only; command-line install needs `--enable` and `--yes-deps`; a crash
loop can block the bootloader).

prs.title: feat(sessions): bulk-filter unarchive with preview, the inverse of archive
prs.body:
## Problem

`hermes sessions archive` is a one-way door. It soft-hides sessions, and there is **no unarchive command** — plus the CLI is the only surface with no way to even *see* what was hidden:

- `hermes sessions list` has no archived filter (`list_sessions_rich(include_archived=False)` is the default on every listing path).
- `hermes sessions stats` counts live rows only, so the DB looks far smaller than it is.
- `hermes sessions browse` takes only `--source` / `--limit`.

Only the dashboard/desktop REST path can show them (`GET /api/sessions?archived=include`). A user who turns on `sessions.auto_archive`, or lowers `sessions.auto_archive_days`, finds history silently gone from every CLI surface with no recovery path. The config says "archive", the docs say "soft-hide, never delete", and the CLI offers neither a view nor an undo.

### The part that makes it a real bug, not just a missing command

The two candidate paths disagree about what may be archived:

- `archive_sessions()` selects candidates with `list_prune_candidates()`, whose WHERE clause comes from `_prune_filter_where()` — which **hardcodes** `s.ended_at IS NOT NULL`. Only *ended* conversations are ever candidates. That is the right guard for prune/archive (never touch a live conversation).
- `archive_stale_sessions()` — what `maybe_auto_archive()` runs from the dashboard session-list path — documents that it **"may archive unended sessions"**, and selects by last activity instead.

So an unended session retired by the background sweep is invisible to the prune/archive candidate path **and** has no unarchive command. It is hidden with no way back, which is exactly the failure mode this PR removes.

## Fix

- **`SessionDB.unarchive_sessions()`** — the exact inverse of `archive_sessions()`: same filter surface, via `set_session_archived` so each lineage flips as a unit, idempotent because only already-archived rows are candidates.
- **`list_archived_candidates()`** — `list_prune_candidates()`' row shape and filter surface *minus* the ended-only guard, with pinned rows included. Un-hiding is never destructive, so neither a live continuation nor a pin may block recovery.
- **`_prune_filter_where(..., ended_only: bool = True)`** — the guard becomes an explicit parameter rather than a hardcoded clause. It defaults on, so prune and archive keep exactly their current behaviour, and `count_open_prune_matches()`'s `"prune filter lost its ended-session safety guard"` assertion still holds. (The row-select SQL is factored into `_list_candidates()` so the two public listers can't drift.)
- **`hermes sessions unarchive`** — the same filter surface as `archive` (all of `--older-than`, `--newer-than`, `--source`, title/model/token/cost/etc.), the same `--dry-run` / `--yes` preview-and-confirm flow, deliberately allowed to run **unfiltered** — recovering everything a sweep retired is the point of the command. Unlike `archive`, no "refusing to run with no filters" guard: that guard exists because archiving everything *hides* everything; un-hiding everything is the recovery.
- **`describe_filters(fallback=...)`** — unarchive's preview must not inherit `"no filters (all ended sessions)"`, which would misdescribe its candidate set. Prune/archive keep the default, so nothing else changes.

## Tests

Three invariants in `tests/hermes_state/test_session_archiving.py` (extending the existing file rather than adding a parallel one):

1. archive → unarchive round-trip restores the whole lineage, spares live rows, and a repeat run is a no-op.
2. **The unended-row reachability case** — `archive_stale_sessions(30)` retires an open session; `list_prune_candidates(archived=True)` is blind to it (`== []`), `list_archived_candidates()` finds it, and `unarchive_sessions()` restores it. This is red on base for the middle assertion.
3. A pinned-and-archived row is restorable — a pin is a durable *keep* flag, not a lock.

## Verification

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_session_filters.py \
  tests/hermes_state/test_session_archiving.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_prune_spares_pinned.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_archive_safe.py
=== Summary: 4 files, 24 tests passed, 0 failed ===
```

End-to-end against a throwaway `HERMES_HOME` (one archived + one live session):

```
$ hermes sessions list                       # archived row hidden
$ hermes sessions unarchive --dry-run
1 archived session(s) match (no filters (all archived sessions); ...)
  old_archived  2026-08-07 11:10  cli  1 msgs
Dry run — nothing unarchived.

$ hermes sessions unarchive --yes
Unarchived 1 session(s). They're visible in listings again — only the hidden flag changed, nothing was deleted.

$ hermes sessions list                       # both rows now visible
$ hermes sessions unarchive --yes
No archived sessions match (no filters (all archived sessions)).   # idempotent
```

`hermes sessions archive --dry-run --source cli` still behaves identically (regression-checked).

`tests/hermes_state/test_hermes_state.py::TestFTS5Search::test_search_projection_skips_context_enrichment_queries` fails in the same directory, but it **also fails on the clean base with this branch stashed** — pre-existing, unrelated to these changes.

## Scope

Intentionally not included, happy to do as a follow-up if wanted: an `--archived` filter on `hermes sessions list`, and making `sessions stats` report archived rows separately. `unarchive --dry-run` already lists exactly what is recoverable, so this PR is self-sufficient.

prs.title: fix(update): rebase local fork commits onto upstream instead of skipping sync
prs.body:
## Problem

When the fork has local commits **and** upstream has new commits, `hermes update` previously **skipped upstream sync entirely** to avoid trampling local changes:

```
ℹ Your fork has N commit(s) not on upstream.
  Skipping upstream sync to preserve your changes.
```

The fork is then left permanently behind upstream — the sync only ever runs when the fork is strictly behind, which can't happen once a local commit lands. Users with local patches on their fork (e.g. downstream packaging, hotfixes waiting on upstream PRs) never receive official updates via the updater.

## Change

In `_sync_with_upstream_if_needed` (hermes_cli/update_cmd.py):

- **Fork ahead + upstream ahead**: rebase local commits on top of upstream/main (`git pull --rebase upstream main`).
- **Conflict safety**: if the rebase conflicts, abort it (`git rebase --abort` + capture_output) so the repo is never left in a broken mid-rebase state, and print manual-resolution instructions.
- **Fork ahead + upstream not ahead**: report `Upstream is up to date (N local commit(s) ahead)` instead of the misleading skip message.
- **Strictly behind (ff-only)**: unchanged.

## Test Plan

- [x] `python3 -m py_compile hermes_cli/update_cmd.py` passes
- [x] Manual trace of all four branch states (ahead/behind x upstream ahead/not) via code review
- [ ] Unit coverage (none exists for this helper today — happy to add if maintainers want a specific harness)

Verified against upstream/main `fbd40c907d` — cherry-picked cleanly, single-file diff.

prs.title: fix(cli): show all messaging platforms in config, not just Telegram/Discord
prs.body:
## Summary

`hermes config` now shows **all** registered messaging platforms instead of only Telegram and Discord.

## Problem

`hermes config`'s `Messaging Platforms` section was hardcoded to check only `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` and `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`. All other platforms — Email, WhatsApp, Signal, Slack, Feishu, WeCom, and many more — were silently omitted even when correctly configured via `.env` or plugin registration. This was misleading: a user could have Email fully configured and active in the gateway, yet `hermes config` would report nothing about it.

Reported in #8175. Previous PR #8238 attempted to fix this but used a static map rather than the shared platform registry, and was not merged.

## Fix

Replaces the hardcoded check with a query of `gateway.platform_registry.PlatformRegistry.all_entries()` — the shared source of truth that **all** platforms (built-in and plugin) register into:

1. Trigger plugin discovery (`get_plugin_manager().discover_and_load()`) so the registry is populated.
2. Render one row per registry entry, sorted by label, in a dedicated `_show_messaging_platforms()` helper.
3. Configured state comes from each entry's `required_env` contract — the same list `hermes setup` displays — **never** from `check_fn()`, which is a passive SDK-availability probe that must stay side-effect free (#79812). A platform with no env contract (e.g. A2A) needs nothing from the environment and renders as `configured (no env required)`.
4. Added a module-level `check_mark()` helper for consistent ✓/✗ rendering.

This single code path now automatically surfaces all 23 registered platforms, and stays correct as platforms are added or removed.

## Testing

- Regression tests in `tests/hermes_cli/test_config.py::TestShowConfigPlatforms` (row-scoped):
  - the IRC row flips `✗ not configured` → `✓ configured` when IRC's own env vars are set (asserted on the row, not a global substring)
  - a no-env-contract platform (A2A) renders `configured (no env required)`, not a false negative
  - registry output still includes Email (previously invisible) alongside Telegram and Discord
  - no Traceback/Error in config display
- `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_config.py`: 123 passed, 4 skipped; `ruff check` clean.
- Rebased onto current main (was 21k commits behind); upstream's refactor of `show_config()` into section helpers is preserved — the messaging block is now its own `_show_messaging_platforms()` section function.

Closes #8175

prs.title: feat(gateway): answer vault prompts on messaging surfaces
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Makes the vault prompts (master-password unlock, save-login, one-time code) answerable from a messaging surface.

The gateway wires `agent.clarify_callback` but never registered the three vault prompt callbacks — only `tui_gateway` and `hermes_cli` do that. On top of that, `can_prompt_here()` only asked whether the *unlock* callback existed. So every vault tool called from Telegram/Discord/etc. returned `prompt_unavailable`, and the only way to save or fill a login was to open a remote desktop and type it there.

This reuses the clarify primitive the gateway already has rather than adding a second transport: the reply is intercepted on the inbound path and handed straight to the caller, so a secret never becomes a conversation message, a memory, or part of the next request.

## Related Issue

Fixes #

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/vault_prompts.py` (new) — builds the unlock / save_login / code callbacks over a single blocking `ask`. `save_login` asks the identifier and then the password; both cards are numbered `(1/2)` / `(2/2)`, and only the final one holds the stream re-arm, matching `_clarify_batch_sync`.
- `agent/vault_backends/unlock.py` — adds `any_prompt_callback_registered()`; `can_prompt_here()` now answers for any vault prompt instead of only unlock.
- `tools/clarify_gateway.py` — `secret` flag on a clarify entry.
- `gateway/run_turn_runner.py` — `_vault_ask_sync` bridge, installed per turn next to `agent.clarify_callback` and cleared in the turn's `finally`. It logs both the dispatch and the outcome of each prompt, which is what separates "the card never posted" from "the user never answered" — without it the caller just sits in `wait_for_response` until the clarify timeout.
- `gateway/run_inbound.py` — a secret answer is no longer echoed into the retired card's summary line, and the user's own message is deleted once the value has been read (best-effort; the value has already been consumed without entering history either way).
- `tests/gateway/test_vault_prompts.py` (new) — callback contract, prompt sequencing, and the rearm/blank-answer behaviour of the runner seam.

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/gateway/test_vault_prompts.py tests/tools/test_browser_vault.py -q` → **64 passed**
2. `pytest tests/gateway/ -q -k "clarify or approval or inbound or vault"` → **438 passed, 4 skipped**
3. Live over a real Telegram gateway, against a live signup page with two password fields:
   - `browser_vault_save_login` dispatched card 1/2, the typed reply was intercepted, card 2/2 was dispatched, that reply was intercepted, and the password was typed into both password fields on the page (`len=20` each).
   - The adapter deleted the password message from the chat immediately after the value was consumed.

Reproducing the old behaviour: on `main`, calling `browser_vault_save_login` from the Telegram gateway returns `{"error_type": "prompt_unavailable"}` without ever sending a card, because no vault callback is registered for that surface.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux 6.8)

> On the full-suite box: I ran the gateway subsets listed above rather than the whole ~39k-test suite, so I've left that box unchecked rather than claim a run I didn't make.

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [ ] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — N/A: behaviour is changed by wiring existing callbacks; the new module carries its own docstrings
- [ ] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A: no new config keys
- [ ] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A: no architecture change
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — the change is platform-agnostic; message deletion is adapter-level and already best-effort on adapters without a deletion API
- [ ] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A: no tool signature changed

## Screenshots / Logs

Gateway log from the live Telegram run:

```
13:50:50  gateway.run: Vault prompt dispatched (secret=False, last=False)
13:51:20  gateway.run: Gateway intercepted clarify text response (id=af240001b0)
13:51:20  gateway.run: Vault prompt answered (secret=False)

13:51:42  agent.tool_executor: tool browser_vault_save_login completed (51.97s)
```

```
input[0] (Password)   len=20
input[1] (Confirm)    len=20
```

## Pin timecapsule v0.1.1

Repin of `plugin-catalog/timecapsule.yaml` to the 0.1.1 fix batch. The disclosure sentence is deliberately unchanged — the seal remains access control, not cryptography, and the review surface is the same.

**Changes in this pin:**
- `sha`: `d16fc06…` → `7d4ef02b323f3a700c2f5775b67b1d6d4d24fe8c` — the merge commit of [brayedan/timecapsule#1](https://github.com/brayedan/timecapsule/pull/1) (clean merge of `maintenance/v0.1.1`; the SHA exists on `main` and is tagged `v0.1.1`). Not a branch tip.
- `version`: `"0.1.0"` → `"0.1.1"`
- Everything else (name, repo, description + Disclosure, maintainer, tier, category, requires_hermes, capabilities) unchanged. Still 7 tools, no hooks, no new capabilities, stdlib-only, no network.

**What 0.1.1 fixes** (all backwards-compatible; store format adds three optional fields):
- `seal()` cap-check ordering (expired pending-deletion capsules free their slot)
- token-checked lockfile release, permission-error/deadline hardening, 0o600 lockfile
- fsync'd atomic writes, tmp cleanup on failure, `os.replace` retry on Windows
- honest corrupt/unreadable store errors + row shape/scalar validation on load
- strict integer argument coercion (bool/non-integral floats rejected)
- date parsing: fractional-second normalization (Python 3.9–3.10), overflow handled
- structured refusals: `open()` errors carry machine-readable `details` (status / eligible_at / remaining_seconds)
- deletion announcements record `pending_deletion_at`, `was_opened`, `condition_type`
- clock-rollback **warn-and-record** (high-water mark + episode log surfaced by `timecapsule_status`; never fatal — hard guard deferred to 0.2.0)

**Validation at the pinned commit:** `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v` → 42/42; `hermes plugins validate` → passed (declared == registered, security scan safe); `hermes plugins doctor` → 7 tools, 0 hooks. CI on the repo runs the same suite on Python 3.9–3.13 (`ubuntu-24.04`, pinned — 3.9 has no toolcache build on newer images).

prs.title: feat(tts): expose ElevenLabs generation options
prs.body:
## Summary

Expose ElevenLabs request options in both native TTS paths on current `main`:

- `language_code`, nested `voice_settings`, and validated `convert_options` for both file generation and live voice streaming.
- Backward-compatible top-level voice-setting keys; nested values win when both specify the same key. Global `tts.speed` is the fallback for models that support speed.
- Reject unknown/overriding convert options before making a request. Preserve the SDK's default request shape and existing configurable `base_url` / `wss_url` client construction.
- Support `eleven_v4` for high-quality output and `eleven_v4_turbo` for streaming. These models accept Stability + Similarity, but not Style, Speed, or Speaker Boost: incompatible non-default settings fail before synthesis; neutral settings are omitted. No automatic model change.
- Update configuration, TTS and voice-mode documentation.

This is a refreshed implementation of the scope in #17789, #32571 and #43980. The old PR branch had conflicts after the provider implementation moved to `tools/tts_tool_providers.py`; the shared request builder now lives in `tools/tts_elevenlabs_options.py`, used by that module and `tools/tts_streaming.py::ElevenLabsStreamer`. The native server-side options do **not** apply to Desktop's client-direct ElevenLabs wire; that is a separate path and not claimed here.

## Related issues

Fixes #17789. Partially addresses #135853 for the Hermes backend ElevenLabs sync/stream paths: both forward global `tts.speed` (with ElevenLabs settings taking precedence) via `voice_settings.speed` on models that support it. Speed is normalized to ElevenLabs' 0.7–1.2 range. The OpenAI/xAI streamers are covered by separate PRs; Desktop's client-direct ElevenLabs wire is outside this PR's scope. This does **not** close #135853.

## Example

```yaml
tts:
  provider: elevenlabs
  elevenlabs:
    model_id: eleven_v4
    streaming_model_id: eleven_v4_turbo
    language_code: pl
    voice_settings:
      stability: 0.5
      similarity_boost: 0.75
```

For older models, `style`, `use_speaker_boost`, and `speed` remain available. `tts.elevenlabs.voice_settings.speed` overrides global `tts.speed` where supported.

## Verification

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_tts*.py` — **250 passed, 2 skipped** on Linux.
- Targeted Ruff, bytecode compilation, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Minimal authenticated ElevenLabs API smoke against this isolated checkout: `eleven_v4` synchronous output returned MP3 bytes; `eleven_v4_turbo` streaming returned PCM bytes. No runtime config change.
- Full repository suite was started but stopped after ~3.6% of its ~42,792 estimated tests to avoid a long, resource-intensive local run; **no full-suite pass is claimed**. GitHub checks/statuses were still absent immediately after the push.

## Risk / rollback

Defaults and existing models remain unchanged. Revert this commit or switch back to the previous PR head if needed. Model selection is explicit; users with non-neutral `style`, `speed` or `use_speaker_boost` must remove those settings before selecting v4.


### Follow-up validation (head `8f3ab7de9a`)

- Added direct regression coverage for streaming global speed and provider precedence, plus bounds, v4 quoted-neutral speed and invalid-value handling.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_tts_elevenlabs_options.py tests/tools/test_tts_streaming.py tests/tools/test_tts_speed.py --file-retries 0 -q`: **58 passed, 1 skipped**. Targeted Ruff and `git diff --check` passed.
- A wider `tests/tools/test_tts*.py` run in a temporary checkout: **282 passed, 3 failed, 4 skipped**. The three failures are confined to `test_tts_path_traversal.py`: its home-I/O guard rejects the test checkout's location beneath the real Hermes home during gateway bootstrap. They are not claimed as a passing suite or as a fix in this PR.
- No new paid-provider synthesis/audio smoke on this follow-up head; the earlier smoke above was on a previous head.

prs.title: fix(kanban): expose max_retries in agent-facing create tool
prs.body:
## Problem

`hermes kanban create --max-retries` (CLI) and `kanban_db.create_task(..., max_retries=...)` already support a per-task retry-limit override — it caps `consecutive_failures` before the task sticks `blocked` instead of auto-recovering, overriding the board's `kanban.failure_limit` for that task only.

The agent-facing `kanban_create` tool in `tools/kanban_tools.py` never exposed it: `KANBAN_CREATE_SCHEMA` didn't declare a `max_retries` property, and `_handle_create` never read `args.get("max_retries")` or forwarded it to `create_task`. An orchestrator worker fanning out child tasks via `kanban_create` therefore had no way to bound a child's retries, even though the DB layer and the human-operated CLI both already support it — an interface gap between the two task-creation entry points, not a behavior difference in the DB.

## Solution

- `KANBAN_CREATE_SCHEMA`: add an optional `max_retries` integer property (`minimum: 1`), documented next to `max_runtime_seconds`.
- `_handle_create`: read `args.get("max_retries")`, validate it (must be an `int` that isn't a `bool`, and `>= 1`) before any task row is created, then forward it to `kanban_db.create_task(..., max_retries=...)`.
- Invalid values return a `tool_error` (same shape as the tool's other validation errors) without touching the database.

## Compatibility

Omitting `max_retries` passes `None` through to `create_task`, exactly as before this change — the board's existing fallback chain (`max_retries` → `kanban.failure_limit` → `DEFAULT_FAILURE_LIMIT`) is unaffected for callers that don't set it.

## Scope

Two files only:
- `tools/kanban_tools.py`
- `tests/tools/test_kanban_tools.py`

## Tests

Added to `tests/tools/test_kanban_tools.py`:
- `test_create_schema_exposes_optional_max_retries` — schema shape (`type`, `minimum`, not in `required`).
- `test_create_persists_max_retries` — `max_retries=3` round-trips through `_handle_create` into the stored task.
- `test_create_omitted_max_retries_preserves_fallback` — omitting the arg leaves `max_retries` `NULL`, preserving current behavior.
- `test_create_rejects_invalid_max_retries_without_row` (parametrized `0, -1, "3", 1.5, True`) — each invalid value returns the tool error and creates zero rows.

## Validation

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_kanban_tools.py -q` → 40/40 passed (36 pre-existing + 4 new).
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_db.py tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_blocked_sticky.py tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_cli.py tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_core_functionality.py tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_dispatch_lock.py -q` → all passed (no regressions in adjacent kanban DB/CLI coverage).
- `ruff check tools/kanban_tools.py tests/tools/test_kanban_tools.py` → all checks passed.
- `git diff --check` → clean.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/` surfaced unrelated pre-existing failures (video/image generation, Daytona, Modal snapshot, web tools config) — reproduced identically on unmodified `main` via `git stash`, confirming they predate and are unaffected by this change.

## Risks and rollback

Low risk: the change is additive (one new optional schema field, one new `if` branch, one new keyword argument forwarded to an already-`Optional` parameter). No existing call path's default behavior changes. Revert is a straight `git revert` of this commit.

prs.title: fix(anthropic): list the account's live models and read context windows live
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

With a Claude login, Hermes ignores two things Anthropic's `/v1/models` already reports for the account: which models it can use, and each model's context window (`max_input_tokens`). This PR takes both from that endpoint.

Repro on main (`f578714e0ee1`) with a Claude login (OAuth), checked against the live endpoint on 2026-11-14:

1. `claude-haiku-5-5` resolves to a 200,000 window, while `/v1/models` lists it at 1,000,000 (#154406). `_query_anthropic_context_length` returns None for `sk-ant-oat` tokens because it only knows `x-api-key`, which answers 401 for an OAuth token. Any model without its own `DEFAULT_CONTEXT_LENGTHS` row then falls to the generic `"claude": 200000`. `claude-mythos-5-2` is right on main only because someone added a row for it by hand.
2. The account lists 17 models and `/model` shows 20. The 15 curated ids come first, then the live-only ids re-sorted into opus, sonnet and haiku tiers. `claude-mythos-5-2`, the account's newest model, is row 20: page 3 of the Telegram picker. Three of the curated rows are not in this account's listing at all (`claude-fable-5.1`, `claude-opus-4-20250514`, `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`).
3. `_credential_fingerprint` hashes every credential file. Claude Code rewrites `~/.claude/.credentials.json` on each token refresh, and after that the cached row no longer matches. The non-blocking picker read then returns `[]`, and the picker falls back to the 15 curated ids alone. `claude-mythos-5-2`, `claude-mythos-5-1`, `claude-fable-5-1`, `claude-sonnet-5-5` and `claude-haiku-5-5` are not offered at all.

#154658 fixes item 1 for every route by adding the haiku row. This PR makes native Anthropic routes read the window from `/v1/models`, so the next model does not need a row.

## Related Issue

Refs #154406

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `agent/model_metadata_anthropic.py` (new; the probe moves here from `agent/model_metadata.py`):
  - A Claude login is sent as an OAuth bearer with the OAuth beta. `_fetch_anthropic_models` already uses these headers for the picker. An API key is still sent as `x-api-key`.
  - With no key passed, the probe resolves the native credential through `native_anthropic_fallback_token`.
  - The catalog is memoized per endpoint and credential digest for 10 minutes, or 60 s after a failed read.
  - Unchanged guards: a `key_cmd` callable is never minted (#114967). An OAuth token, or a credential the probe resolved itself, is only ever sent to api.anthropic.com.
- `hermes_cli/models.py`:
  - `_fetch_anthropic_models` keeps Anthropic's newest-first order instead of the tier sort.
  - `_anthropic_catalog` returns the live list as is. The curated list stays as the outage fallback (`CuratedFallbackModels`, #107391). An id the listing omits can still be typed, since `_validate_anthropic` soft-accepts it.
  - The non-blocking picker read is unchanged from main: a cold or mismatched Anthropic row never waits on the network (#114215). It serves what the cache has, and a background refresh warms the next read. (An earlier revision fetched inline here; review showed it could stall every provider's rows, see below.)
- `hermes_cli/models_anthropic.py` (new): the `/v1/models` paging helpers, moved verbatim and re-imported, so `models.py` stays under its line cap.
- Tests:
  - New: `tests/agent/test_anthropic_live_context_length.py`.
  - `tests/hermes_cli/test_anthropic_picker_curated.py` is rewritten for the new contract.
  - New: `tests/hermes_cli/test_anthropic_picker_nonblocking.py` (from review). A real HTTP server holds the `/v1/models` body; the picker read must return before it, and the background refresh must fill the cache.

On the curated-first merge: the comment this PR removes put curated first so that "a fresh curated model never disappears" while the listing lags. On this account, the listing had every curated model the account can use, plus the five the curated list lacked. Putting curated first is what pushed those five to the last page. A model Anthropic routes before listing it can still be typed.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_anthropic_live_context_length.py tests/hermes_cli/test_anthropic_picker_curated.py tests/hermes_cli/test_anthropic_picker_nonblocking.py tests/hermes_cli/test_list_picker_providers.py`
2. `just check`
3. With a Claude login: `/model` lists the account's models newest first (on a cold cache, from the second open), and `/model claude-haiku-5-5` reports a 1,000,000 context window.

Two errors: `tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins_picker_effective_state.py` needs `uv` on PATH, which this box lacks. `tests/agent/test_run_agent.py` hit the runner's 300 s per-file limit under 4-way load; run alone with `--file-timeout 1200`, it passed 277 of 277.

  - The live fetch returned the 17 ids in API order in 0.21 s.
  - `get_model_context_length` returned 1,000,000 for `claude-haiku-5-5`, `claude-mythos-5-2` and `claude-sonnet-5-5`, and 200,000 for `claude-opus-4-5-20251101`.

prs.title: fix(tui): copy RTL selections back in logical order
prs.body:
## Status: draft, stacked on #151662

Needs #151662 (and its L4 bracket commit) to have anything to correct on Linux, so it is built on that branch. A cross-fork PR can't use a fork branch as its base, so it sits on `main` for now and the diff carries #151662's three commits.

Once that merges I'll rebase onto `main` and mark this ready. The diff then becomes the files below, and nothing here duplicates that PR's review.

---

Copying text out of a reordered line returned the mirrored run. The screen buffer only holds visual order — that is what a bidi-unaware terminal paints — and both copy paths read it: the terminal's own selection, and the TUI's in-app selection in fullscreen mode (`selection.ts`, `getSelectedText`).

The reorderer now returns the position map alongside the visual array (`BidiReorderResult`), the screen keeps it per row (riding `blitRegion` and `shiftRows` the same way `softWrap` does), and `getSelectedText` inverts it. A drag anywhere in the line — full width or partial — yields the sentence as written.

Two details a reviewer will want:

- **A record covers a column span, not the whole row.** The live TUI composes a row from several writes (streaming chunks, trailing padding, sibling chrome), so requiring an otherwise-empty row left almost every row unmapped — which is the bug it was meant to fix. A write that overlaps the span drops the record; a write that misses it leaves the record intact.
- **The mapping is verified at read time.** A record can outlive the layout that produced it, so `bidiRowMatchesCells` re-reads the recorded characters against the cells before trusting the mapping, and columns the record does not cover are copied verbatim. A stale or partially overwritten span degrades to visual order rather than wrong text.

Nothing changes what the terminal paints — only what copy returns.

Base direction is forced to LTR rather than UAX #9 `'auto'`. Under `'auto'` a line whose first strong character is Hebrew takes an RTL base and drags its leading indentation and quote markers to the right edge (`"  שלום"` rendered as `"םולש  "`). The app's LTR frame is part of the line, not the paragraph; pure-RTL lines are unaffected, since the run is the whole line either way.

## Testing

`npx vitest run packages/hermes-ink` → 33 files, 241 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `ink-backpressure.test.ts` ("forces a write through after the coalesce ceiling"), which fails identically on `main` at 2bd378e — pre-existing, unrelated to this change. ESLint clean on the touched files.

`bidi-copy.test.ts` covers pure-RTL, mixed, a partial selection, bracket mirroring on copy, indentation anchoring, a shared row, an overwritten span, a blit into the next frame and a scroll shift. `rtl-copy-live.test.ts` covers the shapes the fullscreen TUI actually produces — a row rewritten in chunks, a row tail padded by a second write, and a multi-row drag — each of which copied mirrored before this change.

Manually: ask the TUI to print `שלום (עולם)`, drag-select it, paste into WhatsApp or Thunderbird. Before, mirrored; after, as written. On `main` the effect is visible under Ghostty/Windows/VS Code, where software reordering already runs.

## Out of scope

The remaining paragraph base-direction cases in #72508 / #51318 are untouched.

prs.title: fix(gateway): allow /update from pip/pipx installs
prs.body:
## Problem

`/update` from Telegram (and all other messaging platforms) returns "✗ Not a git repository — cannot update." on pip/pipx installs.

The handler hardcodes `Path(__file__).parent.parent.resolve() / '.git'` — for pipx installs this resolves into `site-packages/` where there's no `.git` directory, so the command bails immediately.

Meanwhile, CLI `hermes update` works fine because it uses `detect_install_method()` → sees the `pip` stamp → runs through the pipx wrapper.

## Fix

Use `detect_install_method(project_root)` before the `.git` gate. When the method is `pip`, skip the `.git` check — the spawned `hermes update --gateway` handles pipx installs correctly.

## Changes

- **`gateway/slash_commands.py`**: Import `detect_install_method` at module level; replace the unconditional `.git` check with `if install_method != "pip" and not git_dir.exists()`
- **`tests/gateway/test_update_command.py`**: Replace the single `test_no_git_directory` with two focused tests:
  - `test_no_git_directory_unknown_method` — still returns "Not a git repository" when method is not `pip`
  - `test_no_git_directory_pip_install_proceeds` — pip installs without `.git` proceed to spawn the update

All 36 tests pass.

prs.title: MCP servers that log in through GitHub OAuth can sign in and refresh (salvage #44605, port omp#18293)
prs.body:
Connecting an MCP server whose login runs through GitHub's OAuth failed with "Invalid token response": GitHub answers in form-encoded text unless the request asks for JSON, and the MCP library only reads JSON. Hermes now asks for JSON on every token request, so login, token refresh and device-code login all get a readable answer.

Ported from [can1357/oh-my-pi#18293](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/18293), and the same fix first proposed for Hermes in #44605 by @LeonSGP43 (credited as co-author; that PR's branch no longer applies after the OAuth provider moved to `tools/mcp_oauth_provider.py`, so the one-line header moves to the stamp all three token requests now share).

Fixes #44592

- `tools/mcp_oauth_provider.py::HermesProviderMixin._prepare_token_request` sets `Accept: application/json` (only when absent). It already runs on the authorization-code exchange, the refresh, and the device-flow poll in `tools/mcp_oauth_device.py`.

## What changes (live, real GitHub token endpoint)

Requests built by Hermes' real provider (`MCPOAuthManager().get_or_build_provider`, scratch HERMES_HOME), POSTed to `https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token` with a bogus code:

| Request | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| authorization-code exchange | `Accept` unset → 200 `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (SDK: "Invalid token response") | `Accept: application/json` → 200 `application/json` |
| refresh | `Accept` unset → 200 `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` | `Accept: application/json` → 200 `application/json` |

`curl` check of the same endpoint: no `Accept` → `error=incorrect_client_credentials&...` (form); `Accept: application/json` → `{"error":"incorrect_client_credentials",...}`.

**Root cause:** the SDK builds token requests with no `Accept` header and parses only JSON; GitHub defaults to form encoding.

**Not covered:** a full successful GitHub login (needs a real OAuth app + browser consent); the probe shows the content type switch on the live endpoint, which is the whole fix.

## Tests

- `tests/tools/test_mcp_oauth_user_agent.py::test_unconfigured_user_agent_falls_back_to_the_hermes_default` now also pins `Accept` on both token requests, on both provider construction paths: red on main (2 failed), green on head.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_mcp_oauth*.py`: 157 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped.

Related: #50286 (form-encoded parsing fallback; this PR makes that fallback unneeded for providers that honour `Accept`).

prs.title: execute_code: code from earlier calls shows in tracebacks and inspect.getsource (port omp#19218)
prs.body:
When the agent defines a function in one `execute_code` call and later asks Python for its source, or the function crashes in a later call, Python could not find the code: `inspect.getsource()` failed and tracebacks showed a file and line number with no code line. Now each call's code is remembered, so both work.

Ported from [can1357/oh-my-pi#19218](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/19218) (@harshaygadekar), which fixed the same defect in omp's Python eval runner.

- Each session-kernel cell compiles as `<cell-N>` (N = the kernel's execution count) instead of one shared `<cell>`, and its source goes into `linecache`.
- The runner's own `exec(...)` frame is dropped from the reported traceback, so the model sees only its own code.
- One shared cell runner (`tools/code_kernel.py::RUNNER_CELL_SOURCE`) serves both the local and remote kernels, so both get the fix.

## What changes

| Call sequence | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| cell 1 `def f(x): return 1/x`, cell 2 `inspect.getsource(f)` | `OSError('could not get source code')` | `def f(x):\n    return 1/x` |
| cell 3 `f(0)` | `File ".../hermes_kernel_runner.py", line 124, in run_cell` / `exec(compile(request["code"], "<cell>", "exec"), GLOBALS)` / `File "<cell>", line 1` / `File "<cell>", line 2, in f` (no code lines) | `File "<cell-3>", line 1` / `f(0)` / `File "<cell-1>", line 2, in f` / `return 1/x` |
| `def broken(:` | `File "<cell>", line 1` | `File "<cell-1>", line 1` + caret under the error (unchanged shape) |
| `raise SystemExit(3)` | status exit | unchanged |

**Root cause:** cells compiled under a filename with no `linecache` entry, so Python had no source to return or print.

**omp vs ours:** same mechanism (per-cell name + `linecache` registration). omp's runner also sets `__file__`/`sys.path` for on-disk files; ours only runs inline code, so that half doesn't apply here.

## Live repro

- **main** (this session's real `execute_code`): `inspect.getsource(f)` → `OSError('could not get source code')`; `f(0)` traceback shows the runner frame and `File "<cell>", line 2, in f` with no code line.
- **head** (real `tools.code_execution_tool.execute_code` from the worktree, scratch HERMES_HOME, real kernel subprocess): getsource returned both a function and a class method; the traceback printed `return 1/x` with carets and no runner frame; SyntaxError and SystemExit behave as before.

## Tests

- `tests/tools/test_code_kernel.py::TestSessionStatePersistence::test_earlier_cell_source_stays_readable`: red on main (kernel file swapped back), green on head.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_code_kernel.py tests/tools/test_code_kernel_remote.py tests/tools/test_code_execution*.py`: 150 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped.
