prs.title: fix(tui-gateway): notify memory providers when any rewind truncates the transcript
prs.body:
## Problem

`/undo` fires `memory_manager.on_session_switch(..., rewound=True)` so memory providers drop per-turn caches (#6672, #21910). Three other surfaces truncate the same transcript through `_rewind_active_session_history` and never fired it:

- `session.undo` — the Desktop/TUI undo button (`tui_gateway/methods_session.py`);
- `/retry` — undo + resend (`tui_gateway/methods_tools.py`);
- `rollback.restore` when it rewinds the newest turn (`tui_gateway/methods_tools.py`).

A provider that keeps per-turn state (e.g. "what did the assistant just ask") therefore kept answering from turns the user had just removed, while the agent itself saw the truncated history.

## Change

The notification rides the rewind itself instead of living at each call site. `_rewind_active_session_history` (`tui_gateway/session_workdir.py`) is the single choke point all four surfaces reach, so it now ends with `_notify_memory_providers_rewound(session, session_key)`:

- fires `on_session_switch(session_key, parent_session_id="", reset=False, rewound=True)` under `_session_profile_runtime_scope(session)`, the same way `/undo` did (a multiplexed manager refuses a hook naming no profile, #140058) and suppressed exactly like the old call;
- stays silent for the warm-history-only lane (no durable `session_key`) and for a session whose agent is not built yet;
- replaces `/cmd_undo`'s own copy of that call, so `/undo` notifies exactly once. `/undo` keeps `_invalidate_system_prompt()` and its `_last_flushed_db_idx` refresh — those were its own follow-ups, not the memory hook.

## Tests

New `tests/tui_gateway/test_rewind_memory_notice.py` (4 cases) drives the surfaces, not the call site:

- `session.undo` RPC → one `rewound=True` call carrying the session key;
- `command.dispatch retry` → one `rewound=True` call;
- a bare `_rewind_active_session_history` call (the lane `rollback.restore` takes) → one `rewound=True` call;
- a session without a key or without an agent → no call and no exception (control).

Verification run on this branch:

```text
tests/tui_gateway/test_rewind_memory_notice.py tests/tui_gateway/test_undo_command.py          6 passed
tests/tui_gateway (whole directory) + tests/hermes_state/test_rewind_surfaces_invariant.py    414 files, 3300 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped
python3 scripts/check --base upstream/main                                                    19 checks, ok (health 0 blocking)
```

Sabotage: with only `tui_gateway/session_workdir.py` and `tui_gateway/methods_tools.py` restored to `upstream/main` and the new test file kept, the run is `3 failed, 1 passed` — the three failures are `AssertionError: []` on the `rewound=True` call list for the RPC undo, `/retry` and the bare rewind; the control case still passes. The existing `/undo` test (`test_undo_notifies_memory_providers_from_the_session_profile`, which asserts exactly one call under a multiplexed scope) also passes, so the hook fires once, not twice.

## Risk

- The hook now runs while the caller holds `history_lock` (every rewind surface rewinds under it). Providers only invalidate their own caches there; `/undo` already called the same hook synchronously from the same code path, one line later.
- Behaviour is unchanged for `/undo` except that the memory notification is no longer a separate step in `_cmd_undo`; the prompt invalidation and the db marker still run exactly where they did.

## Not done (deliberately)

- No prompt invalidation is added to the other three surfaces: the issue asks for the memory hook, and `rollback.restore` re-persists a checkpointed tree whose prompt is rebuilt on the next agent build anyway.
- The gateway owner lane is untouched: a committed `rewind` mutation there already evicts the cached agent (`gateway/session_mutations.py`), so the next turn builds a fresh agent and a fresh memory manager.

Closes #155946

prs.title: fix(approval): hardline floor sees verbs behind wrappers, paths, multi-call binaries and literal carriers
prs.body:
**§3.2 hardening, not a security boundary.**

The hardline floor anchors its rm-root, shutdown and similar rules with `_CMDPOS`, which only consumed `sudo/env/exec/nohup/setsid/time`. So `nice reboot`, `timeout 5 rm -rf /`, `/sbin/shutdown -h now`, `busybox reboot`, `su -c reboot` and `env -S reboot` all slipped past it. The reboot family has no dangerous-layer backstop, so these spellings ran without a prompt in default mode.

**Fix (bounded):**
- Salvage #58643 (Adolanium): quote-aware wrapper peeler with a per-wrapper option grammar, plus an optional path prefix on the verb.
- Salvage #65393 (Adolanium): busybox/toybox applet prefix.
- Follow-up:
  - The peeler lives in `tools/approval_wrappers.py` and feeds only the hardline variants. Peeling the shared variants made the pipe-to-shell sink read `|| sudo bash` as `| bash`.
  - Lookup modes (`command -v`, `ionice -p`, `sudo -l`) are not runs.
  - Quote-spelled wrappers, leading assignments and the busybox/toybox applet selector are peeled.
  - Peeled and carried commands get the full detection-variant set, so quoted verbs (`nice "reboot"`, `ls; "reboot"`) are dequoted like bare ones.
  - Literal `env -S`/`--split-string` and `su`/`runuser -c` payloads are rescanned to a bounded depth, wrapper-peeled. So are wrappers inside `sh -c` payloads, and payloads behind a peeled wrapper (`xargs sh -c '…'`).

**Known gaps (heuristic, documented rather than chased):**
- `find -exec`, computed strings (`sh -c "$(…)"`, `echo … | sh`), `xargs env -S '…'`, `busybox sh -c`, `runuser -u x -- verb`, `X=1 "verb"`, and wrappers outside the fixed set (chrt/taskset/watch/flock/unbuffer).
- `sudo -l <verb>` still hits the floor through `_CMDPOS`'s own sudo prefix.
- Heredoc-body false positive: a separator followed by a quoted verb inside a heredoc body now hard-blocks. Main already hard-blocks the unquoted form in a heredoc body, so this matches main's existing heredoc handling.
- `sudo -u <verb-named-user> /bin/true` blocks (same as main).

**Tests:** `test_wrapper_paths.py`, the multicall cases in `test_hardline_blocklist.py`, and the new `test_hardline_command_carriers.py`. They are red on main, and the approval/hardline/terminal suites (1617 tests) pass.

Credits: @Adolanium (#58643, #65393). The approach overlaps #58742, #71996 and #82830 (@Sora-bluesky).

Fixes #58642
Fixes #71995
Fixes #65391
Refs #58736 (find -exec and computed strings remain)

**Merge note:** conflicts with #155269 (#7485) in the `_CMDPOS` block. Whichever lands second keeps #7485's possessive `_CMDPOS` body and appends `_MULTI_CALL_PREFIX` plus the `(?:/?(?:[^\s/]+/)*)?` path group, made possessive; then re-run `test_whitespace_runs_at_a_command_position_finish`.

**Also not caught (none of these is a regression vs main):** `xargs env -S '...'` carriers; `busybox -- <applet>`.

Builds on #58643 and #65393 by @Adolanium (commits cherry-picked, authorship kept).

**Known gaps (review round 2):**
- Resolved: `xargs env -S ...` (the earlier review's known gap) is now scanned via peeled-payload recursion.
- Known gap (unverified, unchanged): `busybox -- reboot` still is not peeled; the peel stops at an option-led argv[1].
- Known gap (minor): hex-float timeout durations (`timeout 0x1p3 ...`) are not peeled.
- Nested env options inside an `-S` split string other than `-S` itself (`env -S '-i <verb>'`, `env -S '-u X <verb>'`) are not re-walked; same on main.

**Known gaps (review follow-up):**
- ``ls `pwd`/reboot`` stays hardline: main already treats a closing backtick as a command start, and the path group joins onto it.
- Literal-heredoc exemption covers only quoted-delimiter bodies read by `cat` / `tee`; other literal readers (`sed`, `python - <<'EOF'` data, `>` into files via other tools) still get main's heredoc-body treatment, and an unquoted verb line in a heredoc body hard-blocks as on main.

**Known gaps (review follow-up):**
- Literal `cat <<'EOF'` body lines spelled as a path (`/sbin/reboot`) or a multi-call applet (`busybox reboot`) are still hardline. This is the same class as main's bare `reboot` body line.
- `rm -rf "/etc"/.` / `"$HOME"/.` and `"/"$(echo)` / `"/"${X}` are below the floor (GNU rm refuses `.` operands; the bare substitution forms are missed on main too).

**Known gaps (review follow-up):**
- An apostrophe inside a literal `cat <<'EOF'` body opens a "quote" in main's `_mask_quoted_newlines` (not heredoc-aware), which hides commands after the heredoc (`cat <<'EOF'\ndon't\nEOF\nreboot` is allowed on main and here). Needs heredoc-aware masking on main; follow-up.
- Inside a carried payload (`su -c`, `env -S`), a split-quoted heredoc delimiter (`<<'E'OF`) or an escaped `\<<'D'` after `cat`/`tee` is blanked to the end of the payload, so a command after the real closer is not scanned there. Top-level verdicts are the same as before; main allows both shapes.

**Known gaps (review follow-up):**
- A path segment no longer spans `=`, `<` or `>`, so a real directory with `=` in its name (`/a=b/reboot`) is not on the hardline floor; main does not floor it either.

**Known gaps (review follow-up):**
- Hardline-layer cost on main's 24k-line indented blank-line heredoc (#155269 test) is 1.10 s here vs 0.80 s on main (linear, extra peel/carrier variants). The end-to-end 3.0 s budget passes alone but can trip under heavy parallel test load.

## What does this PR do?

Exoplanet Period looks up one confirmed exoplanet by name and returns the orbital period in days, the discovery year, and the discovery facility. A name that is not exact stays a candidate. The pin is `bb0077aa452c9571e368132eec6144fc41dc05e1`. `requires_hermes` is `>=0.21.4` because `register_tool` and `hermes cron create --no-agent --script` are in that release. This plugin does not call an API that arrived in 0.21.6.

Submitted by the owner of the plugin repository.

## Type of Change

- [x] Catalog entry for a plugin that is not on main yet

## Changes Made

- Pin `plugin-catalog/exoplanet-period.yaml` to `bb0077aa452c9571e368132eec6144fc41dc05e1` at version 0.1.0.
- Tool: `exoplanet_lookup`. No hook is registered.
- The morning job is local only and uses no model turn. It stays off until `hermes exoplanet-period schedule`. Empty stdout sends nothing. The job does not fire until a scheduler is serving the profile.
- After `hermes plugins remove`, the cron job, `scripts/exoplanet-period-watch.py`, and `plugin-data/exoplanet-period/watch.json` remain. Copy the id from `hermes exoplanet-period status` and run `hermes cron remove` with that id, then delete those two files.

## How to Test

1. Place this catalog file in `plugin-catalog/` and run `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/`.
2. Clone the plugin repository at the pinned commit and run `hermes plugins validate` on that clone.
3. From that clone, run `python -m pytest -q`. This commit recorded 30 passed.
4. `hermes exoplanet-period call exoplanet_lookup --json '{"name":"WASP-12 b"}'` returns JSON with `ok` true, an orbital period in days, a discovery year, and a discovery facility when both catalogs answer.

## What was not verified

- No model session was run.
- A live HTTP 503 body from the NASA Exoplanet Archive was not captured on 2026-11-13. The fallback sentence is covered by a stub status.

prs.title: fix(approval): always ask a human before osascript can discard unsaved work
prs.body:
§3.2 hardening, not a security boundary.

**Problem:** `osascript -e 'tell application "Microsoft PowerPoint" to close active presentation saving no'` (and `quit saving no`) matched no approval rule, so in default smart mode it ran without asking anyone, and the operator's unsaved document was gone.

**Fix:** `tools/approval_applescript.py` classifies osascript/osacompile programs as risky (close/quit/save/delete/keystroke/`do shell script`, Terminal's `do script`, any JXA) or opaque (script from a file, pipe, heredoc, expansion or carrier). The program is matched both raw and with AppleScript layout removed (`¬` continuations, `(* *)`/`--`/`#` comments), so a phrase split by a continuation, a comment or two `-e` arguments still matches. The check runs first in `_iter_dangerous_descriptions`. Those keys skip the smart guardian, because an auxiliary LLM's APPROVE is not the consent of the person who owns the work, and the approval covers one command only (no session/always on CLI, gateway, transport or pending paths). Read-only literal scripts stay unflagged, and a carrier counts only when it names `osascript` as a whole word (`pytest tests/test_osascript_bridge.py` does not prompt). Docs updated in `security.md`.

**Known limits (heuristic):** System Events `pick`/`select menu item` and `key down` are not flagged. Routes a command line can't show are also missed: `swift -e` with NSAppleScript, `open -a "Script Editor"`, opening a prebuilt applet, `shortcuts run`, `automator`, and a Python subprocess that builds the name at run time (that one only hits the generic `-c` rule). Dialog prose that contains a risky verb still prompts.

**Tests:** `tests/tools/test_approval_applescript_documents.py` and `tests/tools/test_approval_redirect_segments.py` (fd redirections between `-e` arguments). They fail on main, and the layout/`do script`/osacompile/false-positive rows fail without the final commit. The existing approval suites still pass.

Salvaged from #151157 (@teknium1, building on @686f6c61's commits) with authorship kept, plus a follow-up commit from review.

Fixes #141346

**Known gaps (review follow-up):**
- `detect_dangerous_command` takes tens of seconds on a heredoc body of ~50k backslashes. It reproduces on main with `cat <<EOF` and is outside the osascript classifier (pre-existing; follow-up).

prs.title: feat(gateway): busy_result_mode carries mid-turn subagent and background-process results into the running turn
prs.body:
Fixes #136703

## What and why

When a background `delegate_task` child finishes while the parent is mid-turn, the session holds the result until the turn ends and then spends a separate model turn on it. This change adds an opt-in setting so the result can reach the turn that is already running:

```yaml
delegation:
  busy_result_mode: steer   # queue (default, unchanged) | steer
```

With `steer`, the gateway's completion-delivery seam (`_deliver_completion_notification`) offers a claimed async-delegation completion to the session's running agent instead of admitting it as a new turn. Classic CLI runs its turns on the gateway (one-gateway runtime), so this one seam covers CLI, TUI and messaging sessions. `agent/background_results.py` appends them to the **next tool result just before that result is persisted**. This is the same mutable tail slot the iteration-budget and run-budget notices use, so:

- past context is never rewritten, and the prompt cache holds;
- the transcript matches what the model saw;
- the text is marked as background tool-channel evidence. It is deliberately **not** the `/steer` user-authority marker, because a child's output must not be given user authority.

If no later tool batch carries an offered result (the turn ends without another tool call, or is stopped), it goes back to the completion queue and arrives as the ordinary next turn, exactly as `queue` mode delivers it. Durable claims are acknowledged when the result is accepted, the same way the idle drain acknowledges them on enqueue.

Events owned by other sessions are returned to the completion queue untouched.

## Background-process completions

The same opt-in covers `terminal(background=true, notify_on_complete=true)` completions, under their own key next to `display.background_process_notifications`:

```yaml
display:
  background_process_busy_result_mode: steer   # queue (default, unchanged) | steer
```

They go through the same seam and carrier, with a process-specific marker (`a background process you started finished…`). The settle contract differs because a process completion has no durable claim and belongs to its per-process watcher: requeuing it onto `completion_queue` would strand it. So the delivery call waits on the carry (`gateway/run_notifications_busy_result.py`). If a tool result carried it, the call returns True and no turn starts. If the turn ended without carrying it, the same call continues into the ordinary `_inject_watch_notification`, so watcher retries and fallback notices are unchanged. A cancelled delivery (shutdown) withdraws the offer, so the turn cannot carry what the watcher retries. A completion the agent already read with `process(wait/log)` (`is_completion_consumed`, checked for every process in a coalesced batch) is not shown again. Watch-pattern matches, heartbeats and API-server sessions keep queueing.

## Relation to #104434

#104434 (`result_delivery="inject"`) only injects into the **originating** parent turn and is chosen per call by the model. This PR covers the common case where the result arrives during a *later* turn, and is a user-level config default. The two are orthogonal.

## Scope

- Durable claims stay held while the result rides the turn: acknowledged once a tool result carried it (watcher tick), deferred and requeued at turn cleanup otherwise, so nothing is lost and no delivery attempt is spent. API-server sessions and per-task failure notices keep queueing. `gateway/run_busy.py` is untouched: other internal events still never steer.
- New config keys are in `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, plus the dashboard selects, `cli-config.yaml.example` and the docs (delegation, tools, gateway internals). No env var. `config_defaults.py` is over its file cap, so both keys are offset by folding neighbouring comments.
- #140296 / #142319 change how the *queue* path coalesces completions; they are orthogonal (with `queue`, the default, nothing here runs).

## Tests

- `tests/agent/test_background_results.py`: a real `run_conversation` loop. A result offered while the model is thinking appears on the tool result of the next request, never as a user row. It is red without the `tool_executor` hook.
- `tests/gateway/test_delegation_busy_result_steer.py`: a busy-session result rides the running turn's tool result and no new turn is admitted; an uncarried result is deferred and requeued as the next turn. Both red on `main`.
- `tests/gateway/test_process_busy_result_steer.py` (mode read from a real `config.yaml` through the gateway loader): a busy-session process completion rides the tool result and no turn is admitted; an uncarried one is admitted once as the next turn; one already read with `process(wait)` is not shown again. The carry test is red without the process commit: the completion is delivered at once as a new turn.

Run with `scripts/run_tests.sh`: the two new files plus `tests/gateway/test_completion_delivery.py`, `test_completion_owner_retry.py`, `test_async_delegation_session_binding.py` (all passed). Process part: 14 files incl. `test_background_process_notifications.py`, `test_gateway_shutdown.py`, `test_display_config.py`, `test_web_server.py` → 498 passed. `python scripts/check`: ok. Platform: Linux.

---

**Rebase note (2026-10-15):** rebased onto `main` @ `3dd9e4edfd` (2 commits, clean); `tests/agent/test_background_results.py` + `tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_delegation_busy_result_mode.py` → 3 passed.






**Update (2026-10-17):** the first version hooked the classic CLI's turn monitor, which no longer runs since classic CLI turns moved onto the gateway; live probe confirmed results still queued. The steer path now lives at the gateway completion-delivery seam and the dead CLI hook is removed. Rebased onto `main` @ `e7e839a5f4`.
**Update (2026-10-24):** rebased onto `main` @ `dd5bc7ee13`; added the background-process completion path (last commit) and a `config_defaults.py` line offset.

prs.title: fix(desktop): stop clipping ordered-list numbers in replies
prs.body:
## What

Ordered-list markers in a reply are clipped at the left edge: a two-digit marker renders as `|0.`, and with a monospace reply font every marker loses its first digit.

## Repro

Send a numbered list with 10 or more items, or any numbered list with a monospace reply font. The leftmost pixels of every marker are cut.

## Cause

- `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/markdown-text.tsx` puts `overflow-hidden` on `.aui-md`, so the reply body clips at its left edge.
- A marker paints inside the `<ol>`'s own `padding-inline-start`. Prose sets it to `1.625em` in the compiled sheet — a budget for a proportional face.
- At the chat font size `10.` plus its gap is wider than `1.625em`; with a monospace face even `1.` is wider. The overflow past that padding is what the clip eats.

## Fix

`apps/desktop/src/styles.css`, in the assistant-message-content block (below the `:where(h1..h4)` rule):

```css
[data-slot='aui_assistant-message-content'] .aui-md :where(ol) {
  padding-inline-start: 2.4em;
}
```

Scoped to `ol`: bullets are narrow enough and keep the prose indent.

## Verification

Headless Chromium, real compiled `dist/assets/main-*.css`, a 12-item list in four configs (15px proportional, 15px monospace, 13px proportional, 19.5px proportional). Clipping measured by diffing a render with `.aui-md { overflow: visible }` against the normal one — differing pixels are exactly the clipped part:

| config | base | with fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 15px proportional | 2.6px of `10.`/`11.`/`12.` cut | none |
| 15px monospace | all 12 markers cut | none |
| 13px proportional | 3 markers cut | none |
| 19.5px proportional | 3 markers cut | none |

No unit test: jsdom computes no layout, and this repo's test rules exclude source-reading tests. Measured on the compiled stylesheet, not in a live Electron window.

## Trade-off

An ordered list indents 0.775em (about 11px at 15px) further than before. Bullet lists do not change.

I searched open and closed issues and PRs for this (list marker, ordered list, padding-inline-start) and found no sibling.

prs.title: fix(cli): withdraw a prompt fenced behind a lost turn after submit, and say when it waits on a running turn
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Upstream now covers the main lost-turn path in the classic CLI: `_prepare_submit` refuses a prompt
when the session already holds an `unknown` admission, and `/discard <admission_id>` acknowledges it
(4e35169b2b, 342a55ebad). This PR was rebased onto that work and narrowed to the two cases it does
not cover. The `/discard` route, the pre-submit refusal and the related tests that this PR originally
carried were dropped in favour of upstream's.

1. **Fence lands after submit.** If the owner restarts while a prompt is being submitted, the
   pre-submit check passes, the prompt is admitted, and the restarted owner then fences the turn
   ahead of it as `unknown`. The new prompt sits `queued` behind it and the CLI waits for a
   `message.complete` that never comes (`Initializing agent...` with no end). `_pump` now watches
   the `pending` list from `session.info`; when its own admission is `queued` behind an `unknown`
   one, it withdraws the prompt with `prompt.cancel` and returns `failure_reason="unknown_execution"`
   with the same `/discard` recovery copy, instead of hanging.
2. **Queued behind another running turn.** When the prompt is queued behind an admission that is
   still running (for example an automation turn the restarted owner drains first), the CLI prints
   once that the message is queued and should not be resent. Previously it stayed silent, which is
   what led users to resend the same message into the queue.

Fail-closed is unchanged: nothing is replayed, and no turn is discarded without an explicit `/discard`.

## Related Issue

Refs #139532 (CLI + gateway paths; ACP is #139541)

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/gateway_agent.py`: `_pump` returns `_BLOCKED` when this turn's admission is queued
  behind a lost turn (`_queued_behind_lost`); `run_conversation` withdraws it with `prompt.cancel`
  and returns the `/discard` recovery. `_running_ahead` drives the one-time "Queued: another turn is
  still running" notice.
- `agent/turn_failure_copy.py`, `agent/error_surface.py`: `unknown_execution` is a gateway-layer
  site failure code, so the CLI shows the recovery copy as written instead of classifying it as a
  provider failure.
- `gateway/session_authority.py`, `gateway/session_ingress.py`: the `Session … paused:
  unknown_execution` log warning names the exact operator command (`hermes [-p <profile>] sessions
  discard <id>`) instead of an unnamed operator.

## How to Test

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_cli_lost_turn.py`: 2 passed. With this PR's
  `hermes_cli/gateway_agent.py` reverted to base, the file never finishes (stopped by a 200 s outer
  timeout, rc=124): the fenced prompt waits on a completion that never comes.
- Affected suites: `test_gateway_agent.py`, `test_gateway_cli_commands.py`,
  `test_native_pause_notice.py`, `test_failed_turn_site_codes.py`, `test_failed_turn_chat_copy.py`,
  `test_session_authority*.py`, `test_unknown_automation_settles.py`, `test_commands.py`,
  `test_gateway_command_parity*.py`, `test_desktop_slash_registry.py`: all pass (116 passed).
- `scripts/check`: 13 checks, ok.

## Checklist

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide.
- [x] My commit message follows Conventional Commits.
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this is not a duplicate.
- [x] My PR contains only changes related to this fix.
- [x] I've run relevant tests locally.
- [x] I've added regression coverage.
- [x] Cross-platform impact considered; protocol-level Python behavior.

prs.title: fix(cli): restore reasoning display after gateway reconnect
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Restore the classic CLI's reasoning display preference when its existing connection reconnects to the gateway.

The gateway's `live.show_reasoning` flag is intentionally session-scoped and in-memory. `GatewayAgent.reasoning_callback` sends it and caches the last `(session_id, enabled)` pair. After a gateway restart the CLI keeps that cache, but the new owner has no flag. `GatewayConnection._resubscribe` restores the subscription without restoring the preference. Replies still stream, but live reasoning no longer does; the CLI can subsequently render `last_reasoning` in its end-of-turn fallback box, below the streamed reply. Restarting the CLI masks the problem by sending the flag again.

Keep the preference in this viewer's per-session state and replay it after a successful resume, before the reconnected socket becomes ready. Use the asynchronous client already on that loop, not the blocking `connection.call`. Preserve explicit hidden preferences too; sessions without a preference are untouched. A restore failure follows the existing reconnect failure path, so no prompt is silently admitted before restoration. No prompt replay, persistent config write, transcript mutation, or new protocol/config field is introduced.

## Related Issue

Refs #134889 (classic CLI reconnect regression).
Related: #139470 restores the same live flag on ACP reattachment. This PR changes the classic CLI only; it does not duplicate ACP, Desktop, reasoning-effort persistence, or commentary routing work.

Searched open and closed/merged issues and PRs for the symptom, `show_reasoning`, reconnect/restart, and the cache symbol; checked the tracker body and comments. No existing classic CLI fix for this path was found.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/gateway_agent.py`: remember the callback-derived preference on the session's shared viewer state.
- `hermes_cli/gateway_connection.py`: restore that preference after resuming each retained session, before readiness/new requests. A refused resume is still skipped, with no config write for that session.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_connection_reconnect.py`: exercise shown/hidden preferences, first-turn ordering, same-connection write deduplication, and independent preferences for multiple sessions. Update the existing lost-turn test for the added restore request.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_reasoning_reconnect_live.py`: use a real disposable gateway daemon and a loopback fake model, restart the daemon, and verify the same CLI connection/agent receives reasoning before answer deltas on its next turn.

## How to Test

Interactive reproduction:
1. Start a classic CLI session with streaming and `/reasoning show`.
2. Finish a turn, then restart its gateway while keeping the CLI open.
3. Ask another question in the same CLI. Expected: live reasoning still arrives before the reply, without restarting the CLI. On the base, the owner loses its flag and reasoning falls back to the end-of-turn box.

Automated validation on Linux, Python 3.14.7:
- Base: `0f3eac0b8f7ccef9c469c9e9469c5b08e538d8f4`.
- New regression cases on the unchanged base: **3 failed**, at missing reasoning callbacks / missing restore writes (not collection failures).
- The real-daemon restart test also fails on a clean archive of the base: the second turn returns the answer but receives no reasoning (`'' != 'REASONING-BEFORE-THE-ANSWER'`). With the fix it passes, retaining the same connection/agent and receiving all reasoning before the first answer delta. No production gateway or external model is used.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_connection_reconnect.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_agent.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_session_store.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_disconnect_outcome.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_tools.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_chat_blocking_controls.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_reasoning_reconnect_live.py --file-retries 0 -j 2`: **126 passed, 0 failed** (7 files, no retries).
- `python scripts/check --base origin/main`: **12 checks passed**.

prs.title: Approval prompts now catch `>|` overwrite redirects to sensitive files and disks (port of QwenLM/qwen-code#17042)
prs.body:
Bash has a second overwrite redirect, `>|`, which writes even when `noclobber` is on. The approval checks only recognized a plain `>`, so `echo k >| ~/.ssh/authorized_keys` ran with no prompt and `cat f >| /dev/sda` got past the never-allow disk floor. Now `>|` is checked exactly like `>`.

Ported from QwenLM/qwen-code#17042.

## What changes

| Command | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `echo k >| ~/.ssh/authorized_keys` | runs, no prompt | approval: overwrite system file via redirection |
| `echo x >| /etc/passwd` / `>| /etc/sudoers` | runs, no prompt | approval: overwrite system config |
| `printf x >|  ~/.hermes/.env` | runs, no prompt | approval |
| `date >|'/etc/hosts'`, `cat a >|~/.bashrc` | runs, no prompt | approval |
| `cat f >| /dev/sda` | hardline floor misses it | hardline: redirect to raw block device |
| `cat f > /dev/sda` | hardline | hardline (unchanged) |
| `echo hi >| out.txt`, `ls >| /dev/null`, `echo '>|' ~/.bashrc` | allowed | allowed |

- `tools/approval_detection.py::_command_detection_variants`: the existing extra "escaped separator" variant also spells `>|` as `>`. Since it is an extra variant, the set of refused commands can only grow (nothing the base refuses becomes allowed). Zero net lines (the file is at its line-count cap).

Root cause: every redirect-write rule matches `>\s*<target>`, and the `|` of `>|` sits between the `>` and the target.

## Verification

**Live classifier A/B** (real `detect_dangerous_command` / `detect_hardline_command`, `git archive`-equivalent `origin/main` worktree vs head): 8 of 8 positives in the table above caught on head, 0 of 8 on main; the 6 harmless commands are allowed on both. Timing on 2,000 repeated `echo a >| b;` segments: 0.71 s main vs 0.77 s head (the base cost is an existing rule).

Tests: new `tests/tools/test_approval_clobber_redirect.py` (5 cases, all red on `origin/main`). All 43 `tests/tools/test_approval*.py` files: 1267 passed, 1 skipped. `scripts/check --only health` ok; ruff clean. In one full `-k approval` run under 20 workers, `test_blank_line_heredoc_finishes_end_to_end` (a 3 s wall-clock bound, no `>|` in its input) failed once from load. It passed alone on both main and head.

Not covered: a live interactive approval prompt on CLI/Desktop. The decision comes from the shared classifier, which this test exercises directly.

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep a session's subagents visible after its cached parent agent is rebuilt
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A session's delegated children disappear from `subagent.list` once the gateway rebuilds the cached agent for that route, while the children are still running. `subagent.tail`, steer and interrupt then report the child as unavailable, so the Ctrl+T monitor and the dock show an empty roster for work that is still in progress.

Root cause: `gateway/session_ancillary.py::subagent_records` ties a child to the session only through the parent agent object (`registry._is_descendant_of(record['agent'], parent)`). A child keeps a weakref to the agent that spawned it. After a cache rebuild, `authority.agent(ref)` returns the replacement agent, the old weakref no longer matches it, and the roster comes back empty. The lineage fallbacks don't cover this either, because they only list rows read-only.

The fix carries the gateway's own `LiveSession` record, which survives a parent rebuild but not a replaced conversation, and matches on that exact object:

- `gateway/local_viewer_events.py`: `wire()` binds the turn's `LiveSession` on the agent as `_canonical_session_owner` (added to `_TURN_ATTRS`, so `restore()` puts back the previous value).
- `tools/delegate_tool.py`: `_build_child_agent` copies it onto the child when it is built, because a detached child can register after the parent turn has unwired.
- `tools/delegate_tool_child_run.py`: `_register_child` stores that record as `owner_session_record`, and nested children inherit it.
- `gateway/session_ancillary.py`: `_owner_objects` passes the session's `LiveSession`, and `subagent_records` checks `record['owner_session_record'] is session_owner` before the existing parent and lineage matches.

This keeps the existing rule that an identical durable session id never transfers access to old objects. The match is object identity on `LiveSession`, so a different `LiveSession` that reuses the same id gets an empty roster. A child that carries no token is still invisible after the rebuild (`owned` in the fixture).

Overlap checked: #114420 carries owner authority across a background-thread hop, #116204 shares the roster across processes, and #135874 lists sibling sessions in `delegate_task(action=list)`. None of them covers a parent cache rebuild within the same process.

## Related Issue

No existing issue. The searches I ran are listed under Overlap checked above.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/local_viewer_events.py`, `gateway/session_ancillary.py`, `tools/delegate_tool.py`, `tools/delegate_tool_child_run.py`, as described above.
- `tests/gateway/test_subagent_live_session_owner.py` (new, 2 tests):
  - The roster and controls keep the owned child after a parent rebuild and after the parent is gone. A foreign token and an unstamped child stay hidden. Reusing the durable id with another `LiveSession` returns nothing.
  - A child registered after the parent unwired still records the session owner.
- `tests/gateway/fixtures/ancillary_reads_peer.py` (real gateway daemon probe used by `test_session_ancillary_reads.py`): adds a `rebound` child stamped with the session's `LiveSession` under an old parent. It is listed and tailable, and after `_agent_cache[route]` is replaced with a new generation it is still the only child listed. `owned` (no token) stays hidden, as before.

## How to Test

1. Plant only the test hunks on `main`: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_subagent_live_session_owner.py tests/gateway/test_session_ancillary_reads.py` gives 3 failed, including `assert [] == ['owned']` and `test_activity_snapshot_requires_current_owner_objects`.
2. Same command on this branch: 4 passed.
3. Related files (`tests/gateway/test_session_ancillary*.py`, `test_subagent*.py`, `test_local_viewer*.py`, `tests/tools/test_delegate*.py`, 51 files): 418 passed, 0 failed.
4. `python scripts/check`: 14 checks ok, 0 blocking health findings.

I've been running this change on a long-lived gateway since mid-October. Before it, a rebuilt parent left the CLI subagent monitor empty while its children kept running. With it, the children stay listed and steerable.

prs.title: fix(acp): resolve an adopted chat's owner along its compression chain
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes a regression from the gateway-owned local sessions cutover: after `hermes sessions
adopt`, an ACP editor can no longer reopen any chat that was compacted before the upgrade —
`session/load` answers `not_found`, surfaced by the editor as `Internal error`.

## Related Issue

No separate issue — this PR carries the regression report (version matrix, root cause,
minimal repro) so the fix ships with the report.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `acp_adapter/catalog.py` — `logical_session_id()` walks the compression chain tip-first
  instead of resolving the owner at `lineage[0]`.
- `tests/acp_adapter/test_gateway_catalog_adopted_chain.py` — pins the adopted shape (owner
  bound at the tip) and the un-adopted fallback.

## Root cause

`sessions adopt` can only bind a legacy receipt at the compression **tip**:
`validate_local_lineage()` (`hermes_state_local_lineage.py:22-25`) forces
`lineage[0] == legacy_lineage_root()`, and for a legacy receipt that root *is* the tip
(`hermes_state_local_migration.py:140`). So an adopted chat's receipt reads `lineage: [tip]`.

`logical_session_id()` is the only place that turns an id an editor holds into the session the
gateway owns (`acp_adapter/gateway_server.py:397-399`, `_resume()`), and it resolved the owner
at `lineage[0]` — the creation id, which such a receipt never covers. It then returned the
root unchanged, so `session.info` and the `session.resume` fallback behind it both answered
`not_found`, and the chat could not be opened at all.

A pre-gateway ACP server handed the editor the chain's **creation** id, while the receipt sits
on the **tip** — the two ends of the same chain.

## This is a regression, not a missing feature

| Version | `acp_adapter/catalog.py` | legacy adopt (`hermes_state_local_migration.py`) | resolver |
|---|---|---|---|
| ≤ v0.22.0 | absent (the editor's id *was* the session id) | absent | — |
| v0.22.1 | present | present | root only ❌ |
| v0.22.3 … v0.22.7 | present | present | root only ❌ |
| v0.23.0 / v0.23.1 (latest) | present | present | root only ❌ |
| `main` @ b2c6bc4e1e | present | present | root only ❌ |

Both files arrived in the same release: identity moved from in-process to
"gateway owns it, a receipt records the owner", and the resolver was born with a shape that
adopt never produces. The table is from `gh api contents` on each tag (v0.22.2 could not be
read that way, so it is omitted).

## How to Test

1. Take a chat that has a compression history and migrate it: `hermes sessions adopt`.
2. From any ACP client, `session/load` with the creation id the pre-gateway server handed out.
3. Before: `not_found` / `Internal error`. After: the session resumes and continues at the tip.

No client is needed for the suite: `tests/acp_adapter/test_gateway_catalog_adopted_chain.py`
seeds root → mid → tip in state.db with the receipt bound at the tip only.

- `main` + the new test: **1 failed, 1 passed** — `AssertionError: chain-root` where
  `chain-tip` is expected.
- This branch: **7 passed** across the new file and the neighbouring catalog/attach suites.
- Whole `tests/acp_adapter` with the repo's canonical runner (`scripts/run_tests.sh`: one
  subprocess per test file, `TZ=UTC LANG=C.UTF-8 PYTHONHASHSEED=0`, ambient env cleared):
  `main` → **442 passed, 1 failed, 37 skipped** (the only failure is this new case);
  branch → **443 passed, 0 failed, 37 skipped**.
- `ruff check` clean on both files (ruff 0.15.10, the pinned version).

## Note on behaviour

The only delta beyond the fix: when `get_compression_lineage()` comes back empty (the session
row was swept) but a receipt exists for that id, the id now resolves to that owner. Every other
path is unchanged — the un-adopted case is pinned by the second test — and nothing is written
to `state.db` (the read side stays `SessionDB(read_only=True)`).

Patching the receipt instead (extending `lineage` to the whole chain) is a dead end:
`validate_local_lineage` rejects it as `storage_unavailable`.

## Checklist

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits (`fix(acp):`, `test(acp):`)
- [x] I searched for existing PRs and issues (`logical_session_id`, `sessions adopt`,
      "adopted session", "logical owner") — none cover this
- [x] This PR contains only changes related to this fix (no fork-specific code)
- [x] I've run the tests for the code I changed, and they pass
- [x] I've added tests for my change
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 26.2, Python 3.14

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Documentation — N/A (behavioural fix in an internal resolver; no docs describe this path)
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example` — N/A (no config keys)
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md` — N/A (no architecture or workflow change)
- [x] Cross-platform impact considered — N/A: sqlite reads and string comparison only, paths

prs.title: fix(telegram): keep an album in one turn and admit document albums (#74965, #150720, #143001, salvage #143647)
prs.body:
If you sent several photos or files together as one Telegram album, Hermes sometimes answered the first one alone (if another was still downloading), then treated the rest as a new message. Two documents sent together were refused outright with `invalid_params: media_text_inlined_length`. Now an album waits for every item that has already arrived and reaches the agent as one message, documents included.

| Live probe (real `hermes gateway run` + real adapter vs the Bot API stand-in + FakeLLMServer) | `origin/main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 2-photo album, caption on #1, #2's download stalls 2.5 s | **2 turns**: caption + 1 image, then 2 images as a second, uncaptioned turn | **1 turn**, caption + 2 images |
| 2 `.txt` documents sent as one album | refused: "⚠️ Hermes refused this message (invalid_params: media_text_inlined_length)" | admitted; one reply; the model saw both files' content |

- **Document albums** (salvage of #143647 by @piotr-iohk): `_merge_into_pending` extended `media_urls`/`media_types` but not `media_text_inlined`, so an album whose items carry explicit flags (every document) failed native admission. The merge now goes through `MessageEvent.extend_media` with padded inline flags (shared `pad_inline_flags`), and the same per-attachment bookkeeping is fixed on the sibling paths that had the same gap: base text batching, cached reply/observed attachments, and Relay media localization.
- **Albums split by a slow sibling download** (#74965, #150720): one chat's updates run one after another and each item is downloaded before it is merged, so the 0.8 s debounce fired while a sibling's handler was still downloading. Each album item now counts as in flight from the moment its handler starts (`telegram_media_group.tracking_album_item`). When the debounce is due, the flush waits for in-flight siblings, bounded at 8 s so a stuck download cannot hold the album; a late item is still delivered, never lost. The wait happens before the event is popped, so the existing re-arm/cancel/hold semantics are unchanged.
- The debounce after the last item rises from 0.8 s to 1.5 s and is configurable as `platforms.telegram.extra.media_group_wait_seconds` (non-numeric/negative → default, capped at 10 s). This covers items Telegram delivers well apart. Documented under "Albums" in the Telegram guide.
- `_queue_media_group_event` / `_flush_media_group_event` bodies move to `plugins/platforms/telegram/telegram_media_group.py`; adapter.py 7385 → 7377.

Root cause: album bookkeeping assumed every item was merged within 0.8 s of the previous one, and only photo-shaped (flagless) events were ever merged.

Fixes #143001, fixes #74965, fixes #150720

Salvages #143647 (@piotr-iohk). The in-flight approach follows #53198 (@VKirill), re-implemented on current main: its diff predates the `_flush_buffered` hold/commit machinery and the per-chat update processor.

## Tests
- `tests/plugins/platforms/telegram/test_album_slow_sibling.py` (new, SDK-free, through `_handle_media_message` in production order): a sibling stalled past the debounce still lands in the one album turn; a stuck sibling is bounded and then delivered on its own. Sabotage: removing only the `tracking_album_item` call site → red.
- Salvaged from #143647: album/text-batch/cached-reply/relay flag tests.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh` on 13 touched/mirroring files: 139 passed, 1 skipped (PTB-gated). `scripts/check`: 15 checks ok.

## Dropped hunks
- None from #143647. #53198 is superseded, not cherry-picked: its flush body (inline sleep loop + task-slot bookkeeping) conflicts with the current `_flush_buffered` hold/commit path, and its counter is decremented only by `_queue_media_group_event`, so an item whose handler returns early (oversized, cache failure, video document) left the album waiting the full 8 s. Here the count is released when the handler returns, on every path.

## Infographic

![Infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab19c7b/wR3ZWtFNhwVeBup1eZmbn_MZwmzgbl.png)

prs.title: fix(windows): _run_git no longer hangs when a git child keeps the pipe open (#144964)
prs.body:
## Summary
Fixes #144964. On Windows, `version_info._run_git` uses `subprocess.run(capture_output=True)`. A grandchild that git starts (credential helper, fsmonitor, etc.) inherits the stdout/stderr pipe handles and keeps them open after git exits, so the read never reaches EOF. Every command that reads version info then hangs before the first API call.

## Change
- Write git's stdout/stderr to temporary files instead of pipes, and wait on the git process itself with a timeout.
- On timeout the process is killed and `None` is returned, the same contract as before.
- `--no-optional-locks` and `-uno` are kept, so the old `index.lock` behaviour does not come back.

## Tests
- New `tests/hermes_cli/test_version_info_pipe_wait.py` (6 tests). It spawns a real child that holds the pipe open.
- Fails on the current code: blocked 7.7 s past the 4.5 s bound.
- Passes with the fix on Windows 11, v0.23.1: 6/6, three consecutive runs.
- Uses `tempfile.gettempdir()`, so it also passes under Git Bash, where `TMPDIR` is a POSIX path.

We have run this as a local patch since 2026-11-14 without regressions.

prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): add elm (local reviewable memory + memory-aware routing)
prs.body:
Adds **ELM**, a third-party (`tier: community`) memory plugin, as `plugin-catalog/elm.yaml`, pinned to [`005f52c`](https://github.com/Miawd3/ELM-Hermes-plugin/tree/005f52c0bc3f6c81a6d9554df9cfdb098d8c782c/stock-plugin) (tag `v0.3.0-preview`, `subdir: stock-plugin`). I own the repository.

## What it does
Local, reviewable long-term memory for one person per profile:
- You save notes, or approve notes the model proposes.
- Matching approved notes are recalled automatically, only in chats the owner turned ELM on for.
  - Desktop/TUI `local` chats need an exact-chat `hermes elm grant` from a terminal, which expires.
  - In the classic CLI it's `/elm on`.
  - The model can never grant access.

Two optional modes:
- **Memory slot** (`memory.provider: elm`): the same rules, through `MemoryProvider` (prefetch with `RecallStatus`, `sync_turn`, `on_session_switch`).
- **Memory-aware delegation backend** (`delegation.backend: elm`): the owner names agents (model routes or profiles) under `delegation.backends.elm.agents`, and `delegate_task` gets an `agent` enum. When the model leaves it out, ELM picks the agent that did best on similar earlier tasks of that chat or scope, then `default`, then the parent route.

## Hermes surfaces used
- **General plugin** (`kind: standalone`):
  - tool `elm_memory`
  - slash command `/elm`
  - CLI `hermes elm grant|revoke|sessions|doctor|routes`
  - hooks `pre_llm_call`, `post_llm_call`, `post_compaction`, `on_session_delete`, `subagent_start`, `subagent_stop`
  - two auxiliary task slots
  - 7 skills
  - Desktop settings page, memory manager and inline cards (Desktop plugin SDK)
- `register_memory_provider` (dual-kind, as in `tests/plugins/test_memory_hook_registration.py`) and `register_delegation_provider`.
- Imports only modules listed in `plugin_api.json`.
- Storage through `plugins.plugin_storage`. No core patching.

## Disclosure (rule 13)
- **No network calls, Python dependencies, telemetry, self-updater or background daemon of its own.**
- **Storage:** data stays in `<profile>/plugin-data/elm/stock-v1.sqlite3`.
- **What reaches the model provider:** recalled notes are appended to the current user message, so they go to the configured model provider.
- **Optional model calls**, opt-in per chat, through Hermes's auxiliary model slots:
  - a search planner (query text only)
  - an organizer (captured text the user selects)
- **Capture:** opt-in per chat; it stores finished turns as plain text locally.
- **Routing:** stores the agent name, up to 12 plain-word keywords of the goal (no digits or tokens), success and duration.
  - Never task or result text.
  - Only for chats with ELM on, scoped like notes.
- **Deletion:** deleting a chat deletes its chat-only notes, captures, grant and routing rows (`on_session_delete`). Archiving keeps them.
- **Session list:** `hermes elm sessions` reads the profile's session list, to help the owner pick a chat ID.
- **Writes:** none to config, `.env` or credentials. No shell commands.

## Verification
- `hermes plugins validate stock-plugin --install-deps` at the pinned commit: passed. Security scan: safe. Capabilities match.
- `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/elm.yaml`: OK.
- `hermes plugins install "https://github.com/Miawd3/ELM-Hermes-plugin.git#stock-plugin" --ref 005f52c…`: installs and loads.
- 175 unit tests plus 4 Desktop JS checks pass. Live end-to-end tests ran in a throwaway profile on Hermes 0.23.1 (Windows 11):
  - the recall indicator
  - grant, revoke and expiry
  - chat isolation
  - compression
  - delete purge
  - routing learning in a granted chat, with nothing recorded for an ungranted chat
- An independent privacy review was done before submission; all its findings are fixed, with regression tests.

## Known limits
- Preview. Recall is keyword-based.
- macOS is not yet tested.
- No screenshots yet for the Desktop settings page; happy to add them if wanted.

prs.title: fix(redact): mask bare Google OAuth refresh tokens (1//0…)
prs.body:
**Hardening (SECURITY.md §3.2), not a boundary fix.**

## Problem
`agent/redact.py` already masks Google `GOCSPX-` client secrets and `ya29.` access tokens by prefix (#64351). The long-lived refresh token (`1//0…`) had no prefix pattern. It was masked only next to a `refresh_token` key, so a bare token in tool output, logs or request dumps went through unchanged.

## Fix
One new `_PREFIX_PATTERNS` entry: `1//0[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}`. The `1//0` anchor, the 20-char floor and the matcher's existing no-alnum lookbehind leave placeholders (`1//refresh`, `1//rt-0`), floor division (`1//2`) and URL path segments (`v1//api/…`) untouched. The control/zero-width split pass now also accepts `/` in a span. `1//0` needs it, and no other pattern can match a `/`. `1//0` also gets the same glued-identifier exemption as `GOCSPX-`/`ya29.`. The control-split pass judges that exemption per field (the live text up to the first tab or line break), so tab- or line-separated identifiers stay whole, as they do on main.

## Tests
`tests/agent/test_redact_leak_shapes.py`: the refresh token is added to the bare and no-key-name masking cases (both mask modes), plus a lookalike test that checks the text stays unchanged. The masking cases fail on main and pass with the fix. Tests cover ESC- and ZWSP-split tokens, `-`/`_`-glued tokens, and paths/URLs with control chars staying unchanged; each fails when its production line is reverted.

## Scope
This covers only the prefix half of the issue. The state.db persistence half (#54027) is a replay/design question tracked in the opt-in proposal #155050 and is not touched here. Related redact.py pattern PRs: SendGrid (#58167), `AQ.` Gemini (#66920), Tavily (#72925). This is a separate hunk.

Credit: same idea as #39697, #40092, #55467 and #117441 (@emirsaffar-collab). #117441's variant is unanchored, so it is superseded.

Refs #39654
Refs #54027

**Review notes (non-blocking):** identifiers containing `_1//0`/`-1//0` followed by 20+ token characters (e.g. `out_1//0_layer_weights_final.bin`) are now display-masked, the same trade-off the `GOCSPX-`/`ya29.` glued exemption already makes. A control character inside the 4-char `1//0` prefix itself still leaks, as it does for every other prefix.

**Merge note:** #155220 (#66920, `AQ.` Gemini keys) adds a `_PREFIX_PATTERNS` line at the same spot in `agent/redact.py`; whichever lands second keeps both lines.

The state.db half of #39654 / #54027 is left to the opt-in proposal #155050, so this PR refers to both issues rather than closing them.



**Merge note:** #155289 moves `_TOKEN_BODY_CHARS` from `agent/redact.py` into `agent/redact_control_split.py`. Whichever lands second must keep the move and add `/` in the new module.

**Known gaps (review follow-up):**
- An identifier glued by `-`/`_` to a `1//0` look-alike with 20+ body chars (e.g. `ratio=1//0_padding_identifier_long_enough`) is masked. This false positive is accepted because the `1//0` prefix is exempt from the glued-identifier check, the same as `GOCSPX-`/`ya29.`.
- A refresh token split by `\t`/`\r` mid-stream can still show its head fragment before the join completes. `ghp_` behaves the same way on main, so this is left for a separate change.

**Known gaps (review follow-up):**
- A literal `1//0` followed by a control or zero-width character can mask the identifier text after it (32 of 10k keyless prose/code samples); it fails closed.

prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Extends the session-continuity fix from #37144 to DM channels, which the original PR excluded via `channel_type_raw != "D"`.

Root DM posts had `thread_id=None`; replies carried `root_id=<root post id>`. This produced two different session keys, so the agent lost all context on the first threaded DM reply. #37144 fixed this for channels but left DMs broken.

Removing the `channel_type_raw != "D"` guard gives DMs the same treatment: `thread_id = post.get("root_id") or post_id` when `reply_mode == "thread"`.

```diff
-        if (
-            not thread_id
-            and self._reply_mode == "thread"
-            and channel_type_raw != "D"
-            and post_id
-        ):
-            thread_id = post_id
+        if thread_id is None and self._reply_mode == "thread":
+            thread_id = post_id
```

prs.title: feat(gateway): Mattermost live-thinking bubble
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds a **live-thinking bubble** to the Mattermost gateway: while the agent works, its internal thoughts are posted (and live-updated) as a `> 💭  _"..."_` blockquote message. When the agent is done, **the bubble is edited in place with the final response** — no delete/new-post sequence, no `(message deleted)` artifact.

### Changes

- `plugins/platforms/mattermost/adapter.py`: `edit_message()` and `delete_message()` implementations; `register_post_delivery_callback()` for deferred cleanup.
- `gateway/run.py`:
  - `_interim_assistant_cb` path: when `live_thinking` is enabled, post/edit the thinking bubble instead of sending commentary inline.
  - Gate `_live_thinking_adapter` on `edit_message` capability (adapters lacking it fall back silently).
  - Suppress `stream_delta_callback` when `live_thinking` is active — per-token edits would flood the MM API; the bubble IS the streaming UX.
  - Bypass `stream_consumer.on_commentary()` when `live_thinking` is active so thoughts reach the bubble path.
  - **Bubble replace on completion**: edit the bubble with the final response (3× retry + exponential backoff); `already_sent=True` + `_live_thinking_post_ids.clear()` on success. Delete fires post-delivery only as last-resort fallback after exhausted retries.
  - **Footer edit-append**: when a bubble was just replaced with the final answer, the runtime footer (`display.runtime_footer.enabled`) is edit-appended onto that same post instead of firing as its own standalone trailing post. Falls back to a separate trailing post only if that edit fails, so the footer is never lost.
  - Format thoughts as `> 💭  _"..."_` blockquote.
- `cli-config.yaml.example`: document `display.live_thinking` config key.

## Related Issue

Closes #54228

- `plugins/platforms/mattermost/adapter.py`: `edit_message`, `delete_message`, `register_post_delivery_callback`
- `gateway/run.py`: live-thinking bubble post/edit/replace pipeline; stream suppression; retry+backoff
- `cli-config.yaml.example`: `display.live_thinking` documented
- `gateway/run.py`: edit-append runtime footer onto the replaced live-thinking bubble; fallback to trailing send preserved
- `tests/gateway/test_mattermost.py`: `TestLiveThinkingFooterEditAppend` — edit-append success, edit failure fallback, edit exception fallback, no-bubble regression guard

1. Configure a Mattermost gateway with `display.live_thinking: true`
2. Send a message that requires several tool calls

5. Send a message where the agent responds immediately (no tools) — bubble should still be replaced with the final response

prs.title: feat(mattermost): seed prior thread posts into first-turn context
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

When Hermes is drawn into an existing Mattermost thread for the first time (a reply carrying `root_id`, in a thread it has no session for yet), it had no context of the conversation it just joined. The receive path in `plugins/platforms/mattermost/adapter.py` read `root_id` for session keying and reply routing only; it never called `GET /api/v4/posts/{root_id}/thread`, so the LLM saw just the triggering message.

Slack already solves this with `_fetch_thread_context()`; Mattermost was the remaining gap tracked by #37695. This adds first-turn thread-history seeding for the Mattermost adapter, mirroring the Slack approach and reusing existing infrastructure.

Design notes:

- Seeded history is attached through `MessageEvent.channel_context`, **not** prepended into the message text. The gateway (`gateway/run.py`) applies the triggering sender's prefix to `text` only, then prepends `channel_context` ahead of a `[New message]` marker. Routing history through `channel_context` keeps each prior post's own `[username]` attribution instead of letting the trigger sender's prefix swallow the whole block.
- Seeding is guarded to the **first turn only** by `_has_active_session_for_thread()`, which uses `build_session_key()` as the single source of truth so the `group_sessions_per_user` / `thread_sessions_per_user` isolation settings are honoured. Once a session exists the thread history is already carried in it, so no refetch and no duplication.
- Senders not on the allowlist are tagged `[unverified]` (via the base `_is_sender_authorized()` hook) so the model treats their content as background reference rather than authoritative input. This preserves context without dropping it, and the header switches to a security-aware variant that tells the model not to act on unverified content. Without this, injected `channel_context` would bypass the triggering-author authorization check.
- The bot's own prior replies (circular context) and slash-command posts are excluded. Command-text normalization already runs before the message-type gate on `main`, so a leading-space ` /new` is correctly classified as a command and never receives injected context.
- Policy is exposed via `config.yaml` `mattermost.thread_context` (`on` default / `off`), bridged to `MATTERMOST_THREAD_CONTEXT` through the existing `_apply_yaml_config` hook — no new bespoke `.env`-only setting.

## Related Issue

Fixes #37695

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [x] 📝 Documentation update

## Changes Made

- `plugins/platforms/mattermost/adapter.py`: add `_fetch_thread_context()`, `_has_active_session_for_thread()`, and `_resolve_thread_user_name()`; wire first-turn seeding into `_handle_ws_event()` via `MessageEvent.channel_context`; add per-root TTL cache and user-name cache; bridge `thread_context` in `_apply_yaml_config()`.
- `hermes_cli/config.py`: register `MATTERMOST_THREAD_CONTEXT` as a user-facing optional messaging setting.
- `website/docs/user-guide/messaging/mattermost.md`: document the thread-context behaviour and the `thread_context` / `MATTERMOST_THREAD_CONTEXT` knob.
- `cli-config.yaml.example`: add a `mattermost:` block including `thread_context`.
- `tests/gateway/test_mattermost.py`: 10 tests covering formatting/attribution, bot-and-command exclusion, `[unverified]` tagging, empty-root and cache behaviour, first-turn seeding via `_handle_ws_event`, no-seed on root posts, `off` disabling, and the YAML->env bridge.

## How to Test

2. `@mention` the bot in a reply to that thread. The bot's first response reflects awareness of the prior posts; posts from non-allowlisted users appear as background tagged `[unverified]`.
3. Reply again in the same thread — no refetch occurs (history is now in the session).

5. Revert-to-fail proof: `git stash push -- plugins/platforms/mattermost/adapter.py` then rerun the thread-context tests — 7 behaviour-pinning tests fail (the remaining negative-guard tests trivially hold with the feature absent); `git stash pop` restores green.

prs.title: feat(prompt): agent.skills_catalog_mode to compact the skills catalog on chat surfaces
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The messaging/chat system prompt re-sends a large stable cache prefix on every turn, and the `<available_skills>` catalog block is its single largest compressible line item. The renderer already has a names-only demotion lever (`build_skills_system_prompt(compact_categories=...)`), but it is gated behind the coding posture and the interactive-coding surface set, so it never fires on chat/messaging surfaces, which is exactly where the tokens burn.

This adds `agent.skills_catalog_mode` (`full` | `compact` | `names-only`), resolved once from session-fixed inputs (platform, config) and unioned with the existing coding-posture demotion set before the single render call, so the catalog stays a single cache-safe LRU entry that is byte-identical for the life of a conversation.

- `full`: no demotion (default for interactive coding surfaces; today's behaviour).
- `compact`: demote the non-coding category deny-list to names-only (default for messaging surfaces).
- `names-only`: demote every present category to names-only (max compaction; opt-in).

Never hides a skill: names-only demotion drops the description but keeps every name visible and loadable via `skill_view` / `skills_list`.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [x] Refactor (no behavior change)
- [x] Tests (adding or improving test coverage)

## Changes Made

- `agent/coding_context.py`: new pure resolver `resolve_skills_catalog_compaction(*, platform, config)` + `_skills_catalog_mode()` (config precedence over per-surface default). Reads no turn-varying state.
- `agent/prompt_builder.py`: `ALL_SKILL_CATEGORIES` sentinel (a distinct empty `frozenset` subclass) for names-only; renderer short-circuits "all present categories demoted" and keys the LRU cache distinctly from `full`.
- `agent/system_prompt.py`: resolve the catalog set alongside the coding-posture set and union both into the single `build_skills_system_prompt(compact_categories=...)` call.
- `cli-config.yaml.example`: documents the new `agent.skills_catalog_mode` key. No new `HERMES_*` env var, config-only.
- `tests/agent/test_coding_context.py`, `tests/agent/test_prompt_builder.py`: behavior-contract tests T1 to T7.

## How to Test

```
pytest tests/agent/test_coding_context.py tests/agent/test_prompt_builder.py -q
# 237 passed
```

Contract tests:
- **T1** chat default is `compact`, coding surface is `full`.
- **T2** every name present under `full` is still present under `compact` and `names-only` (never-hide invariant).
- **T3** `compact` drops only non-coding descriptions; `names-only` drops all, each category rendered as a `[names only]` line.
- **T4** determinism: resolver + renderer are byte-identical for identical inputs (cache-safety).
- **T5** config precedence: profile/base override the per-surface default; empty string falls through.
- **T6** measured saving gate (see below).
- **T7** no `HERMES_*` env var / `os.environ` read for the mode.

## T6, measured catalog reduction

Measured against a representative 204-skill catalog, `<available_skills>` block only, tokens via `tiktoken` `cl100k_base`:

| mode | chars | tokens | token reduction |
|---|---|---|---|
| `full` | 19,786 | 4,678 | n/a |
| `compact` | 16,176 | 3,859 | **17.5%** |
| `names-only` | 5,295 | 1,390 | **70.3%** |

The reduction from `compact` varies with the category mix. On a coding-heavy catalog (many `github` / `gitlab` / `devops` / `software-development` skills that `compact` deliberately keeps full), `compact` reclaims ~17.5%; the full cut comes from `names-only` at ~70.3%, which strips coding descriptions too and is therefore opt-in, not the chat default. The synthetic-catalog unit test (`test_t6_compact_shrinks_block_at_least_50pct`) asserts >=50% on a non-coding-heavy catalog to guard the mechanism; the table above is a real-profile figure.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added and passing (237 passed)
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example` updated for the new config key
- [x] No new env var introduced (config-only, per repo `.env`-is-secrets-only rule)
- [x] Cache-safety preserved: resolver reads only session-fixed inputs; result joins the existing LRU cache key

prs.body:
Bumps policy-backtester from 0.5.2 to 0.5.3 (pin `c2a15a2843b28d975ef90bc0a1082dd5a0d81cae`, the `v0.5.3` tag).
I own the repository.

The hackathon entry as submitted and judged is 0.5.2 at `2fdaade`. This bump doesn't change that.

## What changes for users

`hermes backtest enforce` waits until `hermes backtest log` says the policy is ready on that profile. Until 0.5.3 it
accepted any past shadow run plus older job history, so it could turn a policy on before shadow had seen a single job
run under it.

Ready now means that, since shadow started on that exact policy:

- every scheduled job Hermes will run has completed a run that started after shadow did (a profile with no
  scheduled jobs needs at least one tool call);
- shadow would have stopped nothing in a job, in a job's subagents or Kanban tasks, or in a session Hermes didn't
  save;
- shadow logged no call it couldn't check.

Turning the guard off, shadowing a different policy, or setting the mode by hand starts the wait again. Jobs that
Hermes has paused don't hold enforce. `--force` still overrides, and the promotion record now lists what was
overridden.

## Commit range

[`2fdaade...c2a15a2`](https://github.com/noviceadam666/policy-backtester/compare/2fdaade2a2e34a01b611fd074d8deb8d9853c7be...c2a15a2843b28d975ef90bc0a1082dd5a0d81cae):
three commits. Two only reword the README's proof line. The third is the change above, in `backtester/cli.py`,
`ingest.py`, `demo.py` and `fixture.py`, plus tests and the README.

- The live hook (`backtester/live.py`) and the bundled policies are byte-identical to 0.5.2, so calls are checked
  exactly as before.
- No new reads, writes, network calls or subprocesses. The promotion records in `promotions.jsonl` gain a few fields
  (`shadow_since`, `overrode`, `again`, `forced_before`). The disclosure in the entry still holds.

## Entry change

Only `sha` and `version` change, starting from the entry as it is on main. `requires_hermes` (`>=0.22.5`, the same
floor as `plugin.yaml`) and `capabilities` (one `pre_tool_call` hook) are unchanged.

## Checks

- `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py` passes on this entry.
- `hermes plugins validate` on the pinned tree (Hermes v0.22.5): 15 of 15 checks, scan `caution` for the same quoted
  commands as 0.5.2, validation passed.
- The plugin's suite, 463 tests, passes on Hermes v0.22.5. That includes 8 end-to-end runs through Hermes's real
  plugin manager and `pre_tool_call` dispatch. `hermes backtest demo` passes 12 of 12; it now runs a night of jobs
