releases.name: v2026.11.0-beta.3
releases.body:
NanoClaw 2026.11.0-beta.3 is the third beta of 2026.11.0: an early test build, so expect rough edges. The November release takes the place of 2026.10.1, which never becomes a stable release; its two release candidates stay published, and everything they brought is in this entry. Installs on the `beta` channel get this beta; `stable` stays on 2026.10.0 until 2026.11.0 is published. Since 2026.11.0-beta.2, gateway approval cards mark anything they shorten, an approval card changes only after NanoClaw accepts the click, long Slack replies are sent as several messages, and installs that set `NANOCLAW_INSTALL_ID` use it in the shell scripts and the installed service. Since 2026.11.0-beta.1, locally built agent images move to Claude Code 2.1.321 and Agent SDK 0.3.321, the first pair that knows Claude Fable 5.2, `/update-nanoclaw` no longer stops on a lockfile conflict at the first update of a default install, setup installs jq when it's missing so channel setup works on WSL and minimal Ubuntu images, setup restarts NanoClaw after it installs a provider, mention-sticky threads no longer wake the agent for chatter it was never mentioned in, answered question cards keep their question text on every channel, and setup warns when a OneCLI gateway on another machine would send your agents to their own machine. Since 2026.10.1-rc.2, a stuck channel send no longer silences a conversation, agents can put KPI fields, a table and charts in cards, setup on Linux and WSL asks for your password in the open before it installs Node or Docker, setup on Linux reaches Docker right after it adds you to the docker group, setup names the NanoClaw account a machine is signed in to and lets you switch it, Discord server messages that @mention someone reach the agent, agent reactions reach Telegram, Mattermost recovers by itself from a short outage at startup, the OneCLI upgrade guide deletes the Dial key only when it has to, and locally built agent images clear every known High and Critical advisory that had a fix. Since 2026.10.0 it moves OneCLI to 1.45, where new agent groups get only their model key and other keys go to the groups you choose, makes the webhook server listen only on this machine by default, applies egress lockdown to agents that were already running, asks for Node's October 2026 security releases, and lets Claude agents read PDFs; Google Chat now checks that its webhooks come from your app. It also lets agents create other agents from templates, adds Cursor as an agent provider, and moves locally built agent images to Claude Code 2.1.321 with Claude Haiku 5.5. Seven changes need action from some installs, among them the OneCLI upgrade, the webhook address and two new Google Chat settings, so check the section below before you update.

### ⚠️ Before you update

- [BREAKING] **Chat SDK channels move to adapter 4.41.1, which fixes Telegram messages with links that were never delivered.** Affected: installs where `grep -o '"@chat-adapter/[a-z]*"' package.json` prints anything (Telegram, Slack, Discord, Google Chat, Teams, WhatsApp Cloud, GitHub, Linear). Fix: `/update-nanoclaw` refreshes installed channels; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-<channel>` for each one. Google Chat: @mentions in spaces now need `GOOGLE_CHAT_BOT_USER_ID=users/<id>` in `.env` (DMs work without it; without it the log says "Google Chat botUserId is not configured" at startup): once the app has replied to you in a DM, list that DM's messages with the Chat API (`spaces.messages.list`), copy the `sender.name` of a message whose sender `type` is `BOT`, and restart the service. Slack agent-to-agent rooms: a sibling bot now arrives as `slack:bot:U…` instead of `slack:bot:B…`, so approve each sibling bot once more. Check: each channel answers a test message. Rollback: `pnpm exec tsx scripts/update-nanoclaw.ts rollback --id <transaction-id>` ([rolling back](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/operate/upgrading#rolling-back)).
- [BREAKING] **Iron Proxy installs that connected Codex with ChatGPT before this release must sign in to Codex again.** Detect, from the NanoClaw folder (works while the service is stopped): `f=data/session-materials/iron-control/codex.json; [ -f "$f" ] && grep -q '"mode":"chatgpt"' "$f" && ! grep -q '"accountId"' "$f" && echo affected`. Once running, an affected install's Codex agents answer only with the failure notice ("Sorry, something went wrong and I couldn't answer") and the agent container log shows `selected workspace missing from routing discovery`. Why: Codex 0.156 and later check the login's workspace id, and older Iron logins never recorded it. Fix: `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step provider-auth codex`, then check that a Codex agent answers. OneCLI installs are affected only when the vault holds several ChatGPT logins or one without a recorded id; the host log then says "OneCLI login stand-in keeps its placeholder account id": delete the extra or stale login (`onecli secrets list`, then `onecli secrets delete --id <id>`), run the same command, and grant the new secret to each agent that had the old one, as `docs/onecli-upgrades.md` in your install describes. Rollback: return to the previous release.
- [BREAKING] **Forks and hand-made templates: the template code moved and `templates/` is now ignored by git.** Affected: fork code that imports `cloneRegistry`, `listTemplatesFromDir`, `copyTemplate` or `DEFAULT_TEMPLATES_SOURCE` from `setup/templates.ts` (it stops compiling), forks that edit the `GROUP_SCOPE_RESOURCES` line or the stamper's `ensureContainerConfig` line, forks that point setup at their own template library, and anyone who keeps a hand-made template in `templates/`. Why: templates fetched by setup or by an agent are install state and must not block `/update-nanoclaw`, and setup now lists a library from its `index.json`. Fix: import `cloneRegistry` and `listTemplatesFromDir` from `src/templates/library.ts` and `await cloneRegistry()`; `copyTemplate` is gone, so call `ensureTemplateLocal`; a fork that changed `DEFAULT_TEMPLATES_SOURCE` edits `LIBRARY_REPO` (`owner/repo`) and `LIBRARY_BRANCH` in `src/templates/library.ts` instead; re-anchor fork edits on the new lines; keep a new hand-made template in git with `git add -f templates/<ref>`; give your own library an `index.json` at its root in the same shape as `nanocoai/nanoclaw-templates` (`{ "schema": 1, "categories": { "<category>": [{ "ref": "<folder>", "name": "...", "description": "..." }] } }`). Check: `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` passes and setup's library picker lists your templates ([building templates](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/templates/building)). Rollback: revert this release; fetched templates then show as untracked in `git status`, so delete them or `git add` the ones to keep.
- [BREAKING] **OneCLI installs: upgrade the gateway to 1.45.0 and the `onecli` CLI to 2.11.0, where agents get only the keys you grant them.** Detect: the gateway's `/api/health` reports a version older than 1.45.0, or `unknown` (Iron Proxy installs skip this). Why: OneCLI 1.44 replaced secret modes with per-agent grants, and 1.45 is the last version that converts existing installs, so do not skip past it. Fix: before restarting, follow `docs/onecli-upgrades.md` in your install ([the same guide on GitHub](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/blob/main/.claude/skills/add-onecli/payload/docs/onecli-upgrades.md)); it backs up the gateway database, stops if the conversion would delete your rules, and covers the CLI binary. If you use `/add-dial-tool`, run the guide's Dial check before you pull; it deletes the Dial key only when the upgrade could hand it to agents you kept away from Dial (see the Dial item below). Existing groups keep what the conversion gives them; new groups get only their model credential, and on a 1.42 gateway new groups still get every key until you upgrade. To give a group a tool, re-run that tool's skill (for example `/add-vercel`) and pick the group; with `/add-tavily-tool`, re-run its Phase 5 so paid-key upgrades attach the key. `/add-vercel`, `/add-tavily-tool` and `/add-dial-tool` refuse a gateway that is not 1.45. If your Claude key in OneCLI is not named `Anthropic` (or your Codex key `Codex` or `openai`), new groups get no key: run that provider's login again after upgrading (`pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step gateway-auth claude`, or `codex`). Check: `/api/health` reports 1.45.0 and a new agent group answers. Rollback: restore the database backup the guide takes.
- [BREAKING] **The webhook server now listens on 127.0.0.1 by default.** Tunnels and reverse proxies on the same machine keep working. Affected: a proxy on another machine, or anything in Docker on Linux that calls back to the host, such as a Mattermost server; webhooks stop arriving, and the log shows `Webhook server started host="127.0.0.1"`. Fix: set `WEBHOOK_HOST=0.0.0.0` (or one interface's IP address; a name such as `localhost` stops the host at startup) in `.env` and restart. Check: a message on that channel gets an answer. Rollback: the same setting restores the old behavior.
- [BREAKING] **Google Chat installs need two new settings, or the channel does not start.** Google Chat now verifies that webhooks come from your Workspace add-on Chat app, using `GOOGLE_CHAT_ENDPOINT_URL` and `GOOGLE_CHAT_PROJECT_NUMBER` (digits) in `.env`; `/update-nanoclaw` brings the new adapter but cannot ask for them. Detect: the log says "Google Chat needs GOOGLE_CHAT_ENDPOINT_URL and GOOGLE_CHAT_PROJECT_NUMBER (digits) in .env to verify webhooks". Fix: re-run `/add-gchat`, which keeps your existing values and asks for the endpoint URL, the project number and the bot user id for @mentions in spaces, or set both values by hand and restart. The Chat app must be a Google Workspace add-on, and converting an app to one cannot be undone. Check: a test message gets an answer. Rollback: `pnpm exec tsx scripts/update-nanoclaw.ts rollback --id <transaction-id>`.
- [BREAKING] **Custom skills and forks: a card's response handler must say what the click did.** Affected: your own skill or fork code that registers a response handler for card clicks, or that calls `finalizeReject` with a reason. Detect: a response handler that returns `true` still compiles, but its card no longer changes and the host logs `legacy_true`; a `finalizeReject` call with a 4th string argument no longer compiles. Why: a card may show only what the host decided. Fix: return `'accepted'`, `'refused'`, `'closed'` or `'ignored'` (or `false` to pass the click on), and pass a reject reason as `finalizeReject(approval, session, userId, { reason })`. Check: `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` passes and a clicked card changes. Rollback: return to the previous release; handlers that return `true` then redraw as before.
- **`/add-dial-tool` users: run the upgrade guide's Dial check before upgrading OneCLI.** It reads only, and says `delete` only when the gateway has not converted yet (1.43 or older) and the upgrade could remove what keeps agents away from Dial, such as `Dial: blocked agents`, or when it cannot read all the rules that decide; a gateway already on 1.44 or later keeps its Dial key and its grants. When it says `delete`, the guide's `--delete` command removes the key; re-run `/add-dial-tool` after the upgrade, which gives the Dial key only to the agent groups you choose, and new groups get Dial only when you add them. NanoClaw's `ONECLI_PROJECT_ID` and the `onecli` CLI's project (`onecli config set project`, or `ONECLI_PROJECT`) must match or both be unset: when they differ, the re-run stops and writes nothing to OneCLI. An agent group name with a line break no longer changes which groups keep Dial.
- **Update Node to its October 2026 security release.** Setup now requires Node 22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1 or newer and refuses the end-of-life 23 and 25; locally built agent images move to Node 22.23.4, pinned by digest, and hardened installs get it with a later image. NanoClaw keeps running on an older Node; re-running setup picks a Node that meets the minimum, and stops only when it finds none. After `/update-nanoclaw`, run `bash setup/install-node.sh`, then re-run `bash nanoclaw.sh` so the service uses the new Node. If Node comes from nvm, fnm, volta or asdf, update it there. Groups with extra packages also need `ncl groups restart --id <group-id> --rebuild`.
- **Egress lockdown now covers agents that were already running when it was turned on**: they restart on the locked network when the host restarts. If the lockdown network exists but is not internal (only a network made by hand, or a setting that points at an ordinary one), agents no longer start and the host log says "Refusing to spawn with open egress". Fix: list what is attached with `docker network inspect nanoclaw-egress`, detach it (`docker network disconnect nanoclaw-egress <container>`), then `docker network rm nanoclaw-egress`; the next agent start recreates it as internal. Iron Proxy installs name it `nanoclaw-egress-<slug>`, and `NANOCLAW_EGRESS_NETWORK` can set another name.
- **Locally built agent images move to Claude Code 2.1.321 and Agent SDK 0.3.321, where Claude Haiku 5.5 replaces Haiku 4.5.** They are the first pair that knows Claude Fable 5.2. On the Anthropic API, Claude Code's background requests and groups set to `haiku` move to Haiku 5.5, which costs a tenth of Haiku 4.5's price for prompts up to 100K tokens. Hardened installs keep Claude Code 2.1.280 and Haiku 4.5 until an image for this release is listed.
- **Hardened installs move to the image built from v2026.10.0.** A pull now takes the image listed in `agent-images.json` on `main` for the newest release in the install's history, so a new hardened image reaches installs without a new release. Betas and release candidates never get an image of their own, so this beta uses v2026.10.0's (Claude Code 2.1.280, newer than the old pinned build), and the pull's "agent-runner lock drift" warning is expected. This beta lists a newer build of that image, made on 2026-11-03, so `/update-nanoclaw` pulls it again. Run `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step registry -- --refresh` to move onto it ([hardened runtime](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/guides/echo-hardened-runtime)).
- **Codex groups with no model set start new threads on GPT-6.1 Sol.** `/add-codex` now pins `@openai/codex` 0.162.1; existing threads keep their model. To stay on the old one, run `ncl groups config update --id <group-id> --model gpt-6-astra`, then `ncl groups restart --id <group-id>`.

### ✨ New

- **Agents can create other agents from templates.** Ask for one in chat, pick from `ncl templates list` or the public library, and the agent builds it. Setup's template library list now shows what each template does ([using templates](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/templates/using-templates)).
- **Cursor is an agent provider.** The new `/add-cursor` skill runs Cursor's Agent SDK, and setup offers Cursor in the provider picker; it needs a locally built agent image ([providers](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/extend/providers)).
- **Setup waits for a slow first reply instead of failing.** The first-chat check waits 2 minutes, then asks whether to keep waiting, and shows each stage (sandbox, agent runtime, model) with its time, so local models that take minutes to load no longer fail setup. Runs without a terminal now stop after 2 minutes instead of 30 seconds.
- **Agents on slow local models are no longer cut off mid-turn.** Raise `NANOCLAW_ABSOLUTE_CEILING_MS` (default 30 minutes) or `NANOCLAW_CLAIM_STUCK_MS` (default 60 seconds) in `.env`; the host log names which one fired. Restart the service after a change; installs that set neither are unaffected ([environment variables](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/reference/environment-variables)).
- **Agents can put KPI fields, a table and charts in a `send_card` card.** Slack draws them natively and Teams shows a chart as a table; WhatsApp Cloud doesn't show tables or charts yet, and Mattermost doesn't show charts, so agents put those numbers in text there. The linked-device WhatsApp channel (`/add-whatsapp`) doesn't show cards at all. A card's whole text, title and description included, may be up to about 12,000 characters; `send_card` refuses a longer card with the reason, so the agent can send a smaller one. Channels have lower limits of their own, such as 4,096 characters for a whole card on Telegram, and 150 for the title and 3,000 for the description on Slack; a card over them can be cut off or not posted.
- **Early test builds are now called betas.** They are tagged `vX.Y.Z-beta.N`, and `-rc.N` (release candidate) is kept for the last build or two before a release. The `beta` channel offers the newest beta or release candidate that is newer than stable, and `stable` never offers either. `/update-nanoclaw` reads this rule from `main`, so beta installs on 2026.10.1-rc.2 get this beta as they are.

### 🛠️ Fixes

- **Setup tells you when your assistant's first reply failed.** Instead of saying the assistant is ready (for example after a bad API key), it shows the agent's error, names the log files and links the troubleshooting docs; `pnpm run chat` exits with code 4 on a failure notice. When an agent has no error of its own to share, every channel's failure notice now reads "Sorry, something went wrong and I couldn't answer" and links the troubleshooting docs.
- **Setup on Linux and WSL asks for your password up front.** It asks in the open, right before it installs Node or Docker, instead of hiding the sudo prompt behind the progress spinner. On WSL, the docker-group message now tells you to run `wsl --shutdown`.
- **Setup on Linux reaches Docker right after it adds you to the docker group.** The service kept the groups it started with, so it could not open Docker and kept restarting; setup's workaround needs the `acl` package, which stock and minimal Ubuntu lack. Setup now installs `acl` on apt systems, gives your user access to Docker until Docker restarts, and starts the service without a crash wait; a reboot (or `wsl --shutdown` on WSL) makes it last. If it still can't reach Docker, setup prints the commands to run.
- **Setup names the NanoClaw account this machine is signed in to.** At the hardened image and managed Slack steps it asks "Continue as <email>" or "Use a different account", so switching no longer means deleting `account.json`. A first sign-in prints a short code in the terminal: approve only if the sign-in page shows the same code.
- **Channel setup works on WSL and minimal Ubuntu images.** Setup now installs jq when it's missing, so Slack, Discord, Telegram, Teams and Dial setup work there. Slack and Discord setup now stop when the API reply has no id, instead of saving an empty one.
- **Setup restarts NanoClaw after it installs a provider.** `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step provider-auth <provider>` now restarts NanoClaw after installing a provider, so Codex, Cursor and OpenCode work without a manual host restart. The restart runs before sign-in, so an OpenCode install or re-auth that sets a new endpoint needs one more `bash setup/lib/restart.sh`.
- **Setup warns when a OneCLI gateway on another machine would send your agents to their own machine.** They would never reply, so setup prints the `GATEWAY_BASE_URL` line to set.
- **Agents no longer lose or repeat a reply around `send_message`.** An agent that sent something with `send_message` and then left its answer unwrapped is shown what it already sent and asked to finish, and an exact repeat is not sent twice. On streaming providers, a reply sent with `send_message` and followed by plain closing text costs one extra model turn.
- **Agents reply in the language of the message they are answering**, unless you ask for another one. They no longer pick a language from earlier history, other people's messages or the timezone.
- **A stuck channel no longer silences agents.** NanoClaw stops waiting on a send after 60 seconds, logs `Message delivery passed its deadline`, and keeps delivering that conversation's later replies until 3 of its sends are stuck at once; chats wired to share one session (`agent-shared`) count as one conversation. A stuck message is retried if its send fails, and marked failed if there is still no answer an hour later. Other conversations keep going while up to 8 are stuck; with more, their replies can wait a minute or more.
- **Fewer failed agent runs.** On Docker Desktop, a message that arrives while an agent is replying no longer fails the run, and "Permission denied" replies to admin-only commands are sent directly to the chat. On every install, `ncl` and agent tools no longer hit intermittent "database is locked" errors.
- **Mention-sticky threads no longer wake the agent for chatter it was never mentioned in.** A thread keeps going without a mention only after the agent was woken there. A message sent while the thread's first mention is still in its admin-command check (such as `/clear`) no longer wakes the agent: it is dropped under `ignored_message_policy='drop'` (the default) and kept as context under `'accumulate'`. The gap is near zero unless the role lookup is slow, as with a remote database.
- **Approval cards appear where you are waiting and are easier to read.** When an agent in a thread of your own DM asks for approval, the card and its "Reject with reason" prompt appear in that thread. Cards show command arguments and agent-to-agent messages in a code block, and names and the install reason quoted on one line. An approval an agent asks for, or an `ask_user_question`, whose title and question together run over 2,000 characters is refused, and the agent is told the limit so it can shorten it; `ask_user_question` also returns an error within seconds of the host giving up on delivering its card, instead of waiting out its 300-second timeout.
- **Answered question cards keep their question text** on every channel, not just Discord.
- **Gateway approval cards show the action in the card text and mark anything they shorten.** Card text is no longer cut at a fixed length: a shortened value ends with "… N more characters not shown", and left-out details are counted. Card text shows as typed on Slack, Google Chat and Discord. On Telegram, Discord and WhatsApp Cloud a card too long to show whole is refused instead of cut: nothing is approved, and the approver is told the request was not shown. `/update-nanoclaw` brings the channel side; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-<channel>` for each one.
- **An approval card changes only after NanoClaw accepts the click.** A click from someone who can't answer the card leaves its buttons in place. WhatsApp, iMessage and the local web chat confirm an answer only after it is accepted; a refused answer leaves the question open. On Discord, clicks on cards from a durable approval gateway are now recorded (they were ignored), a stalled click acknowledgement no longer holds later events in its channel, and a decided gateway approval card no longer keeps its buttons. `/update-nanoclaw` brings the channel side; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-<channel>` for each one.
- **The background service finds the tools it was installed with.** On macOS it now includes `/opt/homebrew/bin` and the Node.js folder, so Apple Silicon installs using Homebrew or Apple Container no longer crash at start; on Linux it includes the Node.js folder (for example from nvm). Existing installs get it by running `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step service` once.
- **Installs that set `NANOCLAW_INSTALL_ID` now use it in the shell scripts and the installed service.** The shell scripts (image build and pull, restart, skill steps) and the launchd or systemd service that setup installs use the id, and an invalid value stops them with a clear error. An existing install gets the id into its service by running `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step service` once. Without launchd or systemd, NanoClaw still takes the id from the shell that starts it.
- **`/update-nanoclaw` no longer stops at its validate step on installs with Slack.** The skill refresh now credits each channel import to the skill that adds it, so it stops looking for Slack skills that don't exist. The fix comes with the update itself.
- **`/update-nanoclaw` no longer stops on a lockfile conflict at the first update of a default install.** It now regenerates `pnpm-lock.yaml` and the agent-runner `bun.lock` when they are the only merge conflicts. After a manual merge, take the new lockfile and run `pnpm install --lockfile-only` (for `bun.lock`, `bun install --lockfile-only` in `container/agent-runner`).
- **Discord: Approve on an approval card now approves.** Button clicks were misread, so approvals were recorded as rejections and answers to questions came back garbled.
- **Discord: server messages that @mention someone reach the agent.** Chat SDK adapter 4.41.1 dropped every server message with an @mention, including ones that mention the bot; `/add-discord` and `/update-nanoclaw` now apply a patch with the upstream fix. After a manual merge, rerun `/add-discord`.
- **Agent reactions reach Telegram and other Chat SDK channels.** They failed with "message to react not found" and were dropped after three tries.
- **Errors the Chat SDK hits while handling an incoming message show in the NanoClaw log** instead of being dropped silently.
- **Mattermost recovers by itself from a short outage at startup.** When the server, or a proxy in front of it, is unreachable or answers with a server error, it tries 3 more times, waiting 2, 5 and then 10 seconds, instead of staying offline until NanoClaw is restarted; after a longer outage, restart NanoClaw once the server is back. `/update-nanoclaw` brings it; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-mattermost`.
- **Slack: long replies are sent as several messages instead of failing.** Slack refuses a message over 12,000 characters, so a reply over 10,000 is now split. `/update-nanoclaw` brings it; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-slack`.
- **Claude agents can read long PDFs you send them.** Installs that build their own agent image get it from the image rebuild in `/update-nanoclaw`; groups that installed their own packages also need `ncl groups restart --id <group-id> --rebuild`. Hardened installs get it with a later image.
- **Google Chat attachments reach the agent.** On channels whose message ids contain `/`, such as Google Chat, files were dropped and the agent saw only the file name. When someone shares a file from Google Drive, the agent now says it can't open Drive files and asks for the file to be pasted or dragged into the chat.
- **Resend email replies are sent.** Agent replies and the "Connect yourself" hello failed with `Invalid thread ID format`; they now go out, and a reply lands in the email thread the person last wrote in. `/update-nanoclaw` brings it; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-resend`.
- **Installing extra packages for an agent works when NanoClaw lives in a folder whose name has a space.** Setup and uninstall now stop only this install's own host process.
- **Smaller fixes.** An agent reads its own replies from other threads of the same chat as its own, not as another agent's; `ncl groups delete` also removes the group's host bookkeeping rows, and agents that could message it stop listing it right away; creating an agent from a template no longer fails when an agent that has not run yet holds that name; a Slack bot set up for channels only no longer sends you an FYI each time it turns away a DM; `ncl messaging-groups delete` also removes the group's wirings, its own sessions and pending approvals instead of failing with a foreign key error, and removing iMessage uses it; creating an agent refuses a name whose group folder would be invalid (too long, or reserved such as "Global") before anything is written, and says why; setup accepts Anthropic's newer API key types (`sk-ant-usr`, `sk-ant-svc`), which must be scoped to one workspace; Linux Signal setup installs signal-cli 0.14.9, which fixes sends to new contacts hanging (rerun `setup/install-signal-cli.sh`, then restart the service); when `ncl` can't reach the host, it also shows the restart command for Linux without systemd (for example WSL); and the `/add-dashboard` dashboard keeps updating when a transcript grows past about 512 MB and no longer re-reads every transcript each minute (rerun `/add-dashboard` to get it).

### 🔒 Security

- **`/add-resend` installs a Resend adapter with no known advisories.** The pin moves from 0.1.1 (4 moderate findings through `uuid`) to 0.3.0, and `/update-nanoclaw` moves existing email installs to it (after a manual merge, rerun `/add-resend`). The webhook now answers before the message is processed, so a message that fails is not retried, and replies are sent as HTML with a plain-text part that drops link targets.
- **Signal setup checks the signal-cli download's sha256** before installing it.
- **OneCLI setup keeps keys off the command line.** Setup now gives keys to the `onecli` CLI through a private temporary file or stdin, and hides them in error messages. If setup ever failed while saving your Anthropic key or OneCLI API key, rotate that key and delete the old files in `logs/setup-steps/` and `logs/setup.log`.
- **Dial setup no longer leaves the account token readable by other users on the machine** while it pins the default sender number.
- **Registry sign-in opens your browser only for a plain https link**, and says so when it starts no browser. On WSL without `wslview` or `xdg-open` it no longer tries `cmd.exe`; open the link it prints instead.
- **Locally built agent images move to Bun 1.4.4, which no longer trusts the revoked eMudhra certificates.** `/update-nanoclaw` rebuilds the image; hardened installs get it with a later image.
- **Locally built agent images clear every known High and Critical advisory that had a fix.** The image ships npm 11, pnpm 10.34.9, a fresh build of its Node 22.23.4 base and updated agent-runner libraries. `/update-nanoclaw` rebuilds the image; hardened installs get it with a later image.
- **Re-applying a template to an agent (restamp) can no longer be pointed outside its group folder.** It refuses, with an error, to write a context file or skill through a folder in the group folder that was swapped for a link, and checks template file names more strictly. On a Mac this needs the NanoClaw folder on an APFS or HFS+ disk (the usual Mac disk); on other disks these writes are refused.

### 🔧 For custom installations

- **Custom container code that reads `inbound.db`** through `openInboundDb()` or `getInboundDb()` (`mailbox/sqlite/connection.ts`) must use `readInbound((db) => ...)`: `openInboundDb()` is gone, and `getInboundDb()` now works only in tests.
- **Custom mailbox stores that create storage on first write**: a new thread or conversation now gets its earlier context there. The default SQLite store was not affected.
- **`/add-codex` ships its provider inside the skill**, so installs and forks no longer need the providers branch; on an older core its instructions tell you to update core first. Codex archives pick up core's header fix (the thread-id line no longer renders as a heading).
- **Provider skills can archive exchanges through core.** Use `container/agent-runner/src/provider-contracts/exchange-archive.ts`; refreshing `/add-codex` deletes the old copy in `providers/exchange-archive.ts`, so a custom provider that imports it must switch.
- **A gateway credential can target one exact path on a host.** The provider credential seam moves to version 2: a custom provider skill that requires exactly version 1 must accept 1 or later, a skill that sets `path` must require 2, and a custom gateway must declare `connectionPaths: true` to accept path-scoped credentials.
- **The agent image no longer installs `cron-parser`** or its `luxon` dependency (about 4.9 MB); scheduling still runs on the host. Custom container code that imported them must add them back.
- **Forks that pointed the `versions.json` agent-image pin at their own mirror** must move that reference to `NANOCLAW_AGENT_IMAGE_REF`, because the `agent-images.json` list now comes first.
- **Forks no longer run the agent-image refresh workflow**, which failed every 6 hours outside `nanocoai/nanoclaw`.
- **OpenCode: `OPENCODE_NATIVE_ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES` and `OPENCODE_NATIVE_ATTACHMENT_MAX_COUNT` are gone**; they never took effect.
- **Forks that move `@chat-adapter/discord` off 4.41.1** must also remove the `pnpm.patchedDependencies` entry `/add-discord` adds, or pnpm stops with `ERR_PNPM_UNUSED_PATCH`; 4.42.0 and later carry the fix.

issues.body:
## Summary

Replace the current iteration-count and wall-clock caps (50 iterations, 5-minute Python VM timeout, 500 worker iterations) with a **cost-based (USD) budget system** that cascades across a new explicit hierarchy — **user → project → mission → thread → sub-thread**. Background invocations (heartbeat, routines, missions, jobs) are scheduled with a concrete per-invocation budget rather than an arbitrary step cap. Users set their own daily/monthly spend caps; exceeding them is an explicit approval event, not a silent death.

This is a **full rework**, not an incremental patch. Partial fixes (\"raise max_iterations to 200\") have already been rejected because they re-introduce the same failure mode one rung up. The goal is that IronClaw can run autonomously **for hours** when the work warrants it, and stop within **seconds** when it is wasting money.

**Expected size:** ~1500–2500 LoC across 15–20 files, 3 DB migrations, 2 new crates modules. Plan for 2–3 weeks.

---

## Problem

Two failure modes today, rooted in the same miscalibration:

1. **Too restrictive for real work.** Engine v2's `ThreadConfig::max_iterations = 50` (`crates/ironclaw_engine/src/types/thread.rs:164`) and the orchestrator Python VM's `ORCHESTRATOR_DEFAULT_MAX_DURATION_SECS = 300` (`crates/ironclaw_engine/src/executor/orchestrator.rs:101`) cap autonomous runs at roughly 5 minutes of agent work. Comparable coding agents run for hours without a turn or session cap (see reference research: Claude Code has no hard session timeout, no tool-call cap — stops are budget-driven via token-delta / diminishing-return detection).

2. **Permissive for waste.** Once a run is under the cap, nothing restrains an agent that is re-calling the same tool with the same args, bouncing between two dead ends, or burning LLM spend on a task that has already plateaued. Compaction is off by default (`enable_compaction: false`, `thread.rs:174`), `max_budget_usd` is `None` by default (`thread.rs:172`), and there is no project-level or user-level aggregate spend limit anywhere in the codebase.

The caps are arbitrary because the dimension is wrong. **Iterations and seconds are proxies for cost.** Measure cost directly; let iterations and seconds float.

---

## Design Principles

1. **USD is the primary budget.** Tokens, iterations, and wall-clock are secondary signals used for telemetry and backstops. Every budget decision resolves to a dollar amount.
2. **Budgets cascade and are enforced at every level.** A thread cannot exceed its own budget, nor its mission's remaining budget, nor its project's remaining daily budget, nor the user's remaining daily budget. The minimum of the four is the effective ceiling.
3. **Pre-flight reservation, post-flight reconciliation.** Before each LLM call, we reserve a conservative estimate of the upcoming cost against all relevant budgets. After the call completes, we reconcile the reservation with the actual cost and release the delta. This prevents the \"many concurrent threads each individually under budget, collectively 10× over\" race.
4. **Graduated intervention.** At 50% utilization: log. At 75%: emit a `BudgetWarning` event visible in UI. At 90%: require approval to continue (surface an approval gate, same mechanism as tool approval). At 100%: hard stop, mark thread `Failed(BudgetExhausted)`.
5. **Background work is explicitly budgeted at schedule time.** Heartbeat, routines, and missions declare a per-invocation budget when scheduled. No silent defaults — if the user did not set one, the system applies a conservative per-invocation default (e.g. $0.10) and shows it in the UI.
6. **User override is explicit and audited.** Increasing a budget is a first-class action (`budget_increase`) with an `ActionRecord`, visible in the audit log. No env-var-only escape hatches that bypass the UI.
7. **Progress detection is orthogonal.** Loop detection, diminishing-returns detection, and repeated-tool-call detection run *alongside* budget enforcement, not as a substitute. A thread can be killed for being stuck even with budget remaining; conversely, a productive thread is never killed for iteration count.
8. **Hard caps remain as backstops.** We keep an absolute maximum (e.g. `MAX_HARD_CAP_ITERATIONS = 10_000`, `MAX_HARD_WALL_CLOCK = 24h`) to prevent a budget-config bug from ruining a week's spend. These are **invariants, not defaults**.

---

## Architecture

### Type Model

Introduce `crates/ironclaw_engine/src/types/budget.rs`:

```rust
/// Immutable budget allocation for one scope.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Budget {
    pub id: BudgetId,
    pub scope: BudgetScope,
    pub limit: BudgetLimit,
    pub period: BudgetPeriod,
    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    pub created_by: UserId,         // audit: who set this
    pub source: BudgetSource,       // Default | UserOverride | InheritedFromParent
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum BudgetScope {
    User(UserId),
    Project(ProjectId),
    Mission(MissionId),
    Thread(ThreadId),
    BackgroundInvocation { kind: BackgroundKind, scope_id: String },
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct BudgetLimit {
    pub usd: Decimal,               // primary
    pub tokens: Option<u64>,        // optional secondary cap
    pub wall_clock: Option<Duration>, // optional secondary cap
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum BudgetPeriod {
    PerInvocation,                  // resets on each run (threads, jobs)
    Rolling24h,                     // rolling window (user/project daily)
    Calendar { tz: Tz, unit: PeriodUnit },  // day/week/month in user's tz
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct BudgetLedger {
    pub budget_id: BudgetId,
    pub period_start: DateTime<Utc>,
    pub period_end: DateTime<Utc>,
    pub spent_usd: Decimal,
    pub reserved_usd: Decimal,      // in-flight reservations
    pub tokens_used: u64,
    pub updated_at: DateTime<Utc>,
}
```

All IDs are newtypes per `.claude/rules/types.md`. `BudgetId`, `BackgroundKind` (enum: `Heartbeat | RoutineCron | MissionTick | ContainerJob | UserInitiated`), and `PeriodUnit` (enum: `Day | Week | Month`) follow the canonical newtype template.

### The Enforcer

New module `crates/ironclaw_engine/src/runtime/budget.rs`:

```rust
pub struct BudgetEnforcer {
    store: Arc<dyn BudgetStore>,
    cache: Arc<RwLock<HashMap<BudgetId, BudgetLedger>>>,
}

impl BudgetEnforcer {
    /// Called before every LLM call and before every costed tool.
    /// Returns a Reservation token OR a Deny reason. Never silently allows.
    pub async fn reserve(
        &self,
        scopes: &[BudgetScope],       // user, project, mission, thread — cascade
        estimated_usd: Decimal,
        estimated_tokens: u64,
    ) -> Result<BudgetReservation, BudgetDenial> { ... }

    /// Called after the LLM call with actual costs. Never fails silently.
    pub async fn reconcile(
        &self,
        reservation: BudgetReservation,
        actual_usd: Decimal,
        actual_tokens: u64,
    ) -> Result<(), BudgetError> { ... }

    /// Release a reservation without recording spend (e.g., call aborted).
    pub async fn release(&self, reservation: BudgetReservation) -> Result<(), BudgetError> { ... }
}

pub enum BudgetDenial {
    ExhaustedUsd { scope: BudgetScope, limit: Decimal, spent: Decimal },
    ExhaustedTokens { scope: BudgetScope, limit: u64, used: u64 },
    RequiresApproval { scope: BudgetScope, utilization: f64 },  // the 90% gate
}
```

**Invariant:** `ExecutionLoop::step()` in `crates/ironclaw_engine/src/executor/loop_engine.rs` MUST call `enforcer.reserve()` before every `LlmBackend::complete()` call. There is no bypass path. Any new LLM call site added later is a reviewer-flagged diff if it doesn't route through the enforcer.

**Estimation for reservation:** use `LlmProvider::cost_per_token()` × worst-case output estimate (model's max output tokens, or configured reservation factor). After the call, `reconcile()` releases the overshoot. This is conservative — we briefly \"over-reserve\" to guarantee we never spend more than the budget.

### Cascade Resolution

When a thread starts, `BudgetEnforcer::scopes_for_thread(thread)` returns the ordered cascade:

```
[user:alice, project:yc-demo, mission:daily-standup, thread:xyz]
```

A reservation must succeed against **all** of them. The first to fail is the first to deny. The ledger of each is updated on `reconcile`. This means a $0.02 thread can still be denied if the user is at $50/$50 today even though the thread has $4.98/$5.00 of its own allocation left.

### Sub-threads (`llm_query` recursion)

Sub-threads inherit their parent's remaining budget by default — not a fresh budget. A parent with $1 remaining can spawn a child with $1; the child's spending eats the parent's ledger. The engine already tracks `Thread::parent_id` and `depth`. Use the existing recursion depth field; add the budget inheritance rule in `ExecutionLoop::spawn_child_thread()`.

### Background Invocations

For each background kind, the scheduler computes budget at dispatch time:

| Kind | Default | Source of authority |
|------|---------|---------------------|
| Heartbeat tick | $0.05 per tick | `HeartbeatConfig::per_tick_budget_usd` |
| Routine (lightweight) | $0.02 per fire | `RoutineConfig::lightweight_budget_usd` |
| Routine (standard) | $0.10 per fire | `RoutineConfig::standard_budget_usd` |
| Mission tick | $0.50 per tick | `Mission.per_tick_budget_usd` (new field) |
| Container job | $1.00 per job | `JobSpec.budget_usd` (new field) |

Each background dispatch constructs a `BudgetScope::BackgroundInvocation { kind, scope_id }` with a `PerInvocation` period. The scheduler calls `enforcer.reserve()` with this scope plus the user/project/mission cascade. If the user's daily budget is exhausted, the invocation is **skipped**, a `BudgetExhausted` event is recorded, and the next tick is attempted. Skipped ticks do NOT delete their schedule — the schedule continues; only the individual tick is dropped.

### Graduated Intervention

`reserve()` returns a warning tier when utilization crosses thresholds:

- 50%: `ReservationGranted { warnings: [Tier::Info] }` — log only.
- 75%: `ReservationGranted { warnings: [Tier::Warn] }` — emit `ThreadEvent::BudgetWarning` that channels surface to the user.
- 90%: `BudgetDenial::RequiresApproval` — thread transitions to `ThreadState::Waiting` with an approval gate. User can `budget_extend` or `budget_cancel`. Same wire shape as tool approval gates (`request_id`, resume via `/api/chat/gate/resolve`).
- 100%: `BudgetDenial::ExhaustedUsd` — thread transitions to `ThreadState::Failed { reason: BudgetExhausted }`.

Thresholds are themselves configurable per-scope with sensible defaults.

### Progress Detection (Orthogonal)

In the same PR (this work is \"fundamental fix\"; progress detection completes the story), add `crates/ironclaw_engine/src/runtime/progress.rs`:

- **Diminishing returns**: if the last 3 steps added < 500 tokens of non-boilerplate content AND < $0.01 of tool work, emit `ThreadEvent::NoProgress`. After 2 consecutive `NoProgress` events, fail the thread with `StuckNoProgress`.
- **Repeated tool call**: if the same `(tool_name, normalized_params_hash)` appears 3× consecutively, inject a nudge message. 5× → fail with `StuckLoop`.
- Normalization: strip timestamps, request IDs, random UUIDs from params before hashing. Helper in `crates/ironclaw_engine/src/util/param_hash.rs`.

These run independently of budget checks. A thread can be killed for being stuck while under budget.

---

## Database Schema

Three new tables. All must work against both PostgreSQL and libSQL per `.claude/rules/database.md`.

**`budgets`:**

```sql
CREATE TABLE budgets (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    scope_kind TEXT NOT NULL,         -- 'user' | 'project' | 'mission' | 'thread' | 'background'
    scope_id TEXT NOT NULL,           -- opaque string, meaning depends on scope_kind
    limit_usd NUMERIC(10, 6) NOT NULL,
    limit_tokens BIGINT,
    limit_wall_clock_secs INTEGER,
    period_kind TEXT NOT NULL,        -- 'per_invocation' | 'rolling_24h' | 'calendar'
    period_tz TEXT,
    period_unit TEXT,                 -- 'day' | 'week' | 'month'
    source TEXT NOT NULL,             -- 'default' | 'user_override' | 'inherited'
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    created_by TEXT NOT NULL,
    active BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
    UNIQUE (scope_kind, scope_id, period_kind, period_unit)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_budgets_scope ON budgets(scope_kind, scope_id, active);
```

**`budget_ledgers`:**

```sql
CREATE TABLE budget_ledgers (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    budget_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES budgets(id),
    period_start TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    period_end TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    spent_usd NUMERIC(10, 6) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    reserved_usd NUMERIC(10, 6) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    tokens_used BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    UNIQUE (budget_id, period_start)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_ledgers_budget_period ON budget_ledgers(budget_id, period_end DESC);
```

**`budget_events`** (audit trail):

```sql
CREATE TABLE budget_events (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    budget_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES budgets(id),
    thread_id UUID,                   -- if triggered by a thread
    event_kind TEXT NOT NULL,         -- 'reserve' | 'reconcile' | 'release' | 'deny' | 'approve' | 'override'
    amount_usd NUMERIC(10, 6),
    tokens BIGINT,
    reason TEXT,
    actor_user_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX idx_budget_events_budget_created ON budget_events(budget_id, created_at DESC);
```

### Reservation Atomicity

The \"reserve then reconcile\" pattern **must** be atomic against concurrent readers. Two threads under the same user cannot both reserve the last $0.01. Implementation:

- **PostgreSQL**: `UPDATE budget_ledgers SET reserved_usd = reserved_usd + $1 WHERE budget_id = $2 AND reserved_usd + spent_usd + $1 <= (SELECT limit_usd FROM budgets WHERE id = $2) RETURNING id;` — single-row atomic; empty result = denied.
- **libSQL**: same approach inside a `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction (libSQL doesn't support `FOR UPDATE`).

The database is the coordination point. In-memory cache is populated from the DB after every successful write and is **only a read cache**; every write goes through the DB first.

---

## Code Changes (Enumerated)

### Remove

- `crates/ironclaw_engine/src/executor/orchestrator.rs:101–122` — `ORCHESTRATOR_DEFAULT_MAX_DURATION_SECS` and env-var override are deleted. The Python VM inherits the thread's remaining wall-clock from the budget system. (Keep `ORCHESTRATOR_HARD_CAP_SECS = 86400` as a 24h invariant backstop.)
- `crates/ironclaw_common/src/lib.rs` — `MAX_WORKER_ITERATIONS = 500` is deleted. Worker jobs use `JobSpec.budget_usd`.
- `crates/ironclaw_engine/src/types/thread.rs:117–159` — `ThreadConfig::max_iterations` is deleted. `max_tokens_total` and `max_budget_usd` are replaced by a single `budget: BudgetScope` handle that indirects through the enforcer.
- `src/config/routines.rs:17,21` — `max_lightweight_tokens` and `lightweight_max_iterations` are replaced by `lightweight_budget_usd`, `standard_budget_usd`.

### Add

- `crates/ironclaw_engine/src/types/budget.rs` — types above.
- `crates/ironclaw_engine/src/runtime/budget.rs` — `BudgetEnforcer`.
- `crates/ironclaw_engine/src/runtime/progress.rs` — diminishing-returns + loop detection.
- `crates/ironclaw_engine/src/traits/store.rs` — add `BudgetStore` methods to the existing `Store` trait: `get_budget`, `list_budgets_for_scope`, `reserve_atomic`, `reconcile`, `release`, `record_budget_event`.
- `src/db/libsql/budgets.rs`, `src/db/postgres/budgets.rs` — backend implementations.
- `src/db/migrations/` — one migration per backend for the three tables.
- `src/config/budget.rs` — `BudgetConfig` with defaults (user-daily $5, project-daily $2, mission-per-tick $0.50, heartbeat-per-tick $0.05, routine-lightweight $0.02, routine-standard $0.10, job-default $1.00). Env vars `BUDGET_USER_DAILY_USD`, etc.
- `src/cli/budget.rs` — CLI subcommand: `ironclaw budget show`, `ironclaw budget set --scope project:<id> --daily-usd 10`, `ironclaw budget history`, `ironclaw budget approve <thread_id>`.
- `src/tools/builtin/budget_tools.rs` — tools `budget_show`, `budget_increase`, `budget_history` routed through `ToolDispatcher` per `.claude/rules/tools.md`.
- Web UI: new `crates/ironclaw_gateway/static/js/core/budget.js` with status chip + override dialog + approval gate handling. Do not inline into `app.js` — follow the onboarding split pattern documented in the Extension/Auth Invariants section of `CLAUDE.md`.

### Modify

- `crates/ironclaw_engine/src/executor/loop_engine.rs` — wrap every LLM call with `reserve` / `reconcile`. Handle `BudgetDenial` as a distinct termination path (`ThreadState::Failed { reason: BudgetExhausted }` or `ThreadState::Waiting` for approval).
- `crates/ironclaw_engine/src/runtime/manager.rs` — when spawning threads, resolve and persist the scope cascade.
- `crates/ironclaw_engine/src/runtime/mission.rs` — on each mission tick, allocate a per-tick budget; skip tick if user/project daily exhausted (record `BudgetExhausted` event, do NOT delete schedule).
- `src/agent/heartbeat.rs` — same pattern for heartbeat ticks.
- `src/worker/job.rs` + `src/worker/container.rs` — jobs accept a `budget_usd` in their spec; enforce via the enforcer; on exhaustion, terminate gracefully and surface via job status.
- `src/channels/web/server.rs` — rehydrate budget approval gates alongside existing auth gates. (Reuse the same `request_id`/`gate/resolve` path.)
- `src/orchestrator/job_manager.rs` — remove the iteration clamp; replace with budget check.

### Keep

- `max_consecutive_errors` — this is error-rate safety, not cost; unaffected.
- `max_tool_intent_nudges`, `max_action_requirement_nudges` — UX nudges, unaffected.
- Per-tool timeouts (shell 120s, HTTP 30s/300s, memory 15s) — these are per-*call* timeouts, not session-wide, and remain correct. **Add** bash output cap (30KB default, 150KB max, persisted to disk) — missing today and causes context blowup on `cargo build 2>&1`-style commands.

### Invariants & Backstops

In `crates/ironclaw_common/src/lib.rs`:

```rust
pub const HARD_CAP_WALL_CLOCK_SECS: u64 = 86_400;     // 24h absolute
pub const HARD_CAP_ITERATIONS: usize = 10_000;        // catches runaway loops even under budget
pub const HARD_CAP_BUDGET_USD: &str = \"100.00\";       // Decimal; per-thread ceiling regardless of config
```

These are **invariants, not defaults**. A config that tries to exceed them should fail validation at load time with a clear error.

---

## Configuration Surface

`.env.example` additions (no new required vars — everything has a sensible default):

```
# Budget defaults (USD)
BUDGET_USER_DAILY_USD=5.00
BUDGET_PROJECT_DAILY_USD=2.00
BUDGET_MISSION_PER_TICK_USD=0.50
BUDGET_HEARTBEAT_PER_TICK_USD=0.05
BUDGET_ROUTINE_LIGHTWEIGHT_USD=0.02
BUDGET_ROUTINE_STANDARD_USD=0.10
BUDGET_JOB_DEFAULT_USD=1.00

# Intervention thresholds (fractions)
BUDGET_WARN_THRESHOLD=0.75
BUDGET_APPROVAL_THRESHOLD=0.90

# Progress detection
PROGRESS_DIMINISHING_TOKENS=500
PROGRESS_NOPROGRESS_WINDOW=3
PROGRESS_LOOP_THRESHOLD=3
```

All defaults land in `src/config/budget.rs`. Per-user overrides live in the `budgets` table (user scope). Per-project in the same table (project scope).

---

## Migration & Rollout

**Phased, behind `BUDGET_ENFORCEMENT_MODE` env var:**

| Mode | Behavior |
|------|----------|
| `off` | Current behavior; enforcer records nothing. (Default for existing deployments on first release.) |
| `shadow` | Enforcer records reservations/reconciles but never denies. Warnings and denials are logged only. Used to calibrate default budgets against real traffic. |
| `warn` | Enforcer denies at 100% but approval gate at 90% is a soft warning instead of a hard gate. |
| `enforce` | Full enforcement. |

Phases:

1. **Phase A** (this issue): schema + enforcer + `shadow` mode. Ship to staging, run for 1 week, review `budget_events` logs, calibrate default budgets.
2. **Phase B**: flip to `warn` in staging. Watch for false-positive denials.
3. **Phase C**: `enforce` in staging, `warn` in production.
4. **Phase D**: `enforce` everywhere. Delete the mode flag and the old iteration caps.

The old `max_iterations` field remains deserializable from existing DB rows during Phase A–C (`#[serde(default)]`), ignored by the enforcer. Deleted in Phase D.

---

## Testing Criteria

A junior engineer's work on this issue is **not accepted** unless every bullet below is covered by a passing test and the reviewer can find the test by the name indicated.

### Unit tests (`cargo test -p ironclaw_engine`)

1. `budget_reserve_denies_when_user_exhausted` — user at $5.00/$5.00 denies a $0.01 request.
2. `budget_reserve_denies_when_project_exhausted` — user has $4/$5, project has $2/$2, denies.
3. `budget_reserve_returns_first_denying_scope` — cascade order is user, project, mission, thread; test names each.
4. `budget_reconcile_releases_overshoot` — reserve $0.10, actual $0.03, ledger shows `spent=0.03, reserved=0.00`.
5. `budget_release_on_abort_zeroes_reservation` — reserve then release, ledger shows `spent=0, reserved=0`.
6. `budget_concurrent_reservations_do_not_oversubscribe` — 100 concurrent reservations of $0.10 against a $5.00 budget: exactly 50 succeed, 50 denied, `reserved+spent <= 5.00` throughout. Run with `tokio::spawn` + `JoinSet`.
7. `budget_period_rolls_over_at_midnight_user_tz` — rolling-24h and calendar-day semantics.
8. `budget_hard_cap_rejects_config_exceeding_invariant` — `BudgetConfig::load()` with `$1000.00` per-thread returns `Err(ConfigError::ExceedsHardCap)`.
9. `progress_diminishing_returns_fires_after_3_low_delta_steps` — fabricate step history, assert event fired.
10. `progress_loop_detection_normalizes_timestamps_in_params` — same tool with timestamps `t1`, `t2`, `t3` in otherwise-identical params counts as 3 consecutive.
11. `budget_denial_does_not_update_spent_only_fails_reservation` — a denied reserve leaves `spent` unchanged; important for audit correctness.
12. `budget_subthread_inherits_parent_remaining` — parent at $0.50/$1.00; child gets $0.50 budget, not $1.00.
13. `budget_ledger_period_unique_constraint` — two ledger rows for same `(budget_id, period_start)` fail; test against both backends.

### Integration tests (`cargo test --features integration`)

14. `test_budget_end_to_end_user_daily_blocks_new_thread` — real PostgreSQL; spend $5 across threads; next thread fails at spawn.
15. `test_budget_background_invocation_skipped_when_user_exhausted` — mock scheduler, user at cap, heartbeat fires, invocation is dropped, `BudgetExhausted` event recorded, schedule persists for next tick.
16. `test_budget_approval_gate_pauses_and_resumes` — thread hits 90%, enters `Waiting`, user calls `budget_extend`, thread resumes and completes.
17. `test_budget_approval_gate_cancel_marks_thread_failed_budget_exhausted` — same as above but user cancels.
18. `test_budget_mode_shadow_never_denies_but_records_all_events` — run with `BUDGET_ENFORCEMENT_MODE=shadow`, saturate user daily, every LLM call still succeeds, `budget_events` shows every reservation.
19. `test_budget_mode_off_is_no_op` — with mode `off`, no `budget_events` rows created, existing iteration-cap behavior preserved (temporary — Phase A).
20. `test_budget_persists_across_process_restart` — reserve, reconcile, restart process, ledger state matches. (Catches in-memory-cache-only bugs.)
21. `test_budget_libsql_and_postgres_produce_identical_ledgers` — run the same sequence of operations against both backends, assert `spent_usd` and `reserved_usd` are byte-identical.
22. `test_budget_tool_goes_through_dispatcher` — `budget_increase` called directly without `ToolDispatcher::dispatch` fails the pre-commit hook. (Rule enforcement per `.claude/rules/tools.md`.)
23. `test_budget_denial_error_does_not_leak_internals_to_user` — user-facing message says \"daily budget exhausted\" not \"postgres connection failed\" or raw error variant name. (Error-boundary rule per `.claude/rules/error-handling.md`.)

### E2E tests (`tests/e2e/`)

24. `test_e2e_user_sets_daily_budget_via_cli_and_it_takes_effect` — `ironclaw budget set ...`, start a thread, verify enforcement.
25. `test_e2e_web_ui_shows_budget_chip_and_approval_gate` — Playwright; spawn expensive thread, expect approval modal at 90%, click \"extend $5\", thread resumes.
26. `test_e2e_long_running_thread_1_hour_under_generous_budget_completes` — with a $10 budget, run a genuinely long agentic task (e.g., a multi-tool research task), verify it completes and is not killed by any iteration cap. This is the \"can run for hours\" acceptance test; allocate 60 minutes of CI time. If CI can't accommodate, mark `#[ignore]` and run manually before merge.
27. `test_e2e_stuck_thread_killed_in_seconds_despite_budget` — craft a prompt that induces a tool loop; thread must be killed by `StuckLoop` within 10 seconds, well under budget. This is the \"doesn't waste cycles\" acceptance test.

### Regression tests (catch the specific failure modes this rework is motivated by)

28. `regression_orchestrator_5min_cap_no_longer_applies` — run a Python orchestrator step that takes 8 minutes wall-clock under a 15-minute thread budget; completes successfully.
29. `regression_50_iteration_cap_no_longer_applies` — run a synthetic thread that legitimately needs 200 LLM calls under a sufficient budget; completes successfully.

### Manual verification checklist (PR description must confirm each)

- [ ] Started a fresh DB, ran migration, inserted a user, verified `budgets` table has default user-daily row auto-created at first thread spawn.
- [ ] Ran `ironclaw budget show` — output renders.
- [ ] Hit the 75% warning on a real LLM call — warning surfaced in CLI and web UI.
- [ ] Hit the 90% approval gate — approved via CLI, resumed.
- [ ] Hit the 90% approval gate — cancelled via CLI, thread failed gracefully.
- [ ] Started heartbeat under exhausted daily budget — heartbeat skipped, logged, did not loop-crash.
- [ ] Removed the old `max_iterations` flag in Phase D and rebuilt — no callers remain (grep `max_iterations` returns zero hits outside tests and historical docs).

---

## Observability

- Every `reserve`, `reconcile`, `release`, `deny`, `approve`, `override` writes a row to `budget_events`.
- Emit tracing spans: `budget.reserve`, `budget.reconcile`, `budget.deny`.
- Add structured log lines at `debug!` (not `info!` — REPL/TUI corruption rule from `CLAUDE.md`).
- Web UI shows a budget status chip in the thread header: `$X.XX / $Y.YY today (ZZ%)`. Green < 50, yellow 50–75, orange 75–90, red ≥ 90.

---

## Out of Scope

- Charging real money / billing integration. This is a **spend cap**, not a payment system.
- Per-tool costing beyond LLM cost (we do not currently track tool-specific dollar cost like \"Brave Search API calls cost $0.001 each\"). Design leaves room for it (`BudgetLedger::reserved_usd` is already tool-agnostic) but wiring per-tool pricing is a follow-up.
- Dynamic pricing fetching from providers. `src/llm/costs.rs` remains a static table; pricing updates remain manual.
- Retroactive budget limits (you cannot set a limit at $2, run $5 of work, and have it retroactively fail).

---

## Open Questions (pre-implementation review)

1. **Budget reset on project delete?** If a project is deleted, do its spent dollars still count toward the user's daily? **Recommendation:** yes, keep the ledger (don't cascade-delete). Spend already happened.
2. **Cross-user mission?** Missions are currently single-user (`mission.rs:108`). Confirm — if they ever become multi-user, the cascade needs revisiting.
3. **Currency.** We assume USD everywhere. OK for v1 but document the assumption.
4. **Free models.** Local models return $0 cost. Should they still count against a token budget? **Recommendation:** yes, tokens bypass \"zero cost\" denial but still enforce `max_tokens_total` if set. Prevents an ollama thread from running 10M tokens.
5. **Trial / onboarding mode.** New users get $N free today — set a first-day $5 budget, surface it in onboarding? Defer.

---

## Acceptance Checklist for Merge

- [ ] All 29 tests listed above pass locally and in CI.
- [ ] `cargo clippy --all --benches --tests --examples --all-features` is zero-warning.
- [ ] `cargo fmt` is clean.
- [ ] Migration runs forward **and** backward cleanly on both PostgreSQL and libSQL; verified by migration-specific integration test.
- [ ] Pre-commit hook (`scripts/pre-commit-safety.sh`) passes — no direct `state.store.*` bypass lines added.
- [ ] Every new tool goes through `ToolDispatcher::dispatch` per `.claude/rules/tools.md`.
- [ ] Every new newtype follows the canonical template in `.claude/rules/types.md`.
- [ ] No `info!` logs on background paths (heartbeat, missions) per `CLAUDE.md` code style.
- [ ] No `.unwrap_or_default()` on DB reads without a `// silent-ok:` justification.
- [ ] Docs updated: `CLAUDE.md` gets a new \"Budgets\" section, `crates/ironclaw_engine/CLAUDE.md` documents the `BudgetEnforcer` primitive, `.env.example` lists all new vars.
- [ ] PR description includes a table of measured costs for five representative threads (e.g. \"simple Q&A: $0.003\", \"code refactor: $0.12\", \"research mission: $0.87\") so reviewers can sanity-check default budgets.
- [ ] Phase A (shadow mode) deployed to staging for 7 days, `budget_events` reviewed, defaults tuned before Phase B.

---

## References

- Reference research comparing IronClaw's current limits to Claude Code's budget-driven approach (conversation transcript; summary: Claude Code has no hard session timeout, uses diminishing-returns detection, auto-compaction at ~13K tokens below context limit, per-tool output caps with disk persistence).
- `crates/ironclaw_engine/src/types/thread.rs:117–180` — current `ThreadConfig` and defaults.
- `crates/ironclaw_engine/src/executor/orchestrator.rs:101–129` — current orchestrator caps.
- `crates/ironclaw_common/src/lib.rs` — `MAX_WORKER_ITERATIONS`.
- `src/llm/costs.rs` — existing per-token pricing table.
- `.claude/rules/database.md`, `.claude/rules/tools.md`, `.claude/rules/types.md`, `.claude/rules/error-handling.md` — mandatory conventions.

prs.title: fix(common): price models from the llm-prices table
prs.body:
## Summary

- Several prices in `model_cost()` no longer match the providers. gpt-5.5 was at $2/$8 but costs $5/$30. gpt-5.2-pro was at $2/$8 when it's $21/$168. Opus 4.5 and 4.6 were at $15/$75, but they're $5/$25. Haiku 4.5 was at $0.80/$4 instead of $1/$5. The USD budget work in #2843 depends on this table, so these errors go straight into budgets.
- `cache_read_discount()` gave every GPT model 2x, but GPT-5 cache reads are 10x cheaper and GPT-4.1/o4-mini are 4x.
- `model_cost()` and `cache_read_discount()` now look a model up in [llm-prices](https://crates.io/crates/llm-prices) first. I wrote and maintain that crate. It has no dependencies and records each price with the provider's pricing page and the date it was checked.
- Unlisted `gpt-5*` ids (Codex variants, a new minor release) bill at their nearest listed row: `gpt-5.5-codex` -> `gpt-5.5`, `gpt-5.3-codex-spark` -> `gpt-5.3-codex`, `gpt-5.1-codex-max` -> `gpt-5.1`, `*-mini`/`*-nano` -> the matching small-tier row. The old local Codex rows and the `gpt-5*` $2/$8 fallback are gone, so a Codex id can no longer be priced below its base model.
- Rates are converted to `Decimal` from their exact decimal form (`1.1` -> `"1.1"`), not through `Decimal::from_f64`, so no binary float error reaches the money math. The local table stays for ids the crate doesn't list (Claude 3.x, dated gpt-4o snapshots, o1-mini). The vendor census for `llm_costs.rs` drops from 91 to 32 occurrences and 9 to 8 vendors.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] CI/Infrastructure
- [ ] Security
- [x] Dependencies

## Linked Issue

Related #2843

## Validation

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (rustfmt `--check` on the changed files)
- [x] `cargo clippy -p ironclaw_common --tests -- -D warnings` (owning crate only)
- [ ] `cargo build` (built the crates the tests below pull in, not the full workspace)
- [x] Relevant tests pass: `cargo test -p ironclaw_common --lib llm_costs` (19 tests), `cargo test -p ironclaw_architecture_tests --test reborn_contracts_vendor_census`
- [ ] `cargo test -p <owning-crate> --features integration`: not applicable, no database or runtime-integration behavior changed
- [ ] Manual testing: not applicable, pure pricing function
- [ ] If a coding agent was used and supports it, `pr-shepherd` was run before requesting review

## Test Strategy

User behavior: per-run USD cost and budget accounting use current published prices for listed models. Unlisted Codex variants price at their base model.

Risk areas:
- [ ] Model behavior
- [ ] Browser
- [ ] Side effect
- [ ] Persistence
- [ ] Security or permissions
- [ ] External provider
- [x] Cross-component behavior (budget accounting and the OpenAI-compatible cost fields read this table)

Tests added or updated:
- Unit or contract: `llm_costs` tests for listed prices, exact decimal conversion, Codex variants billing at their listed base, small-tier fallbacks, local/`:free` models, cache-read ratios. The two Opus cache tests in `openai_compat_serve/tests.rs` now use the $5 input rate.
- Reborn integration: Not applicable: no runtime wiring changed, only the values the pricing function returns.
- Recorded fixture: Not applicable: no provider traffic.
- Browser E2E: Not applicable: no UI change.
- Backend or runtime: Not applicable: covered by the unit tests above.
- Live canary: Not applicable: pricing is a pure lookup.

What the tests prove: listed ids return the published per-token rate as an exact `Decimal`, Codex and new `gpt-5*` ids return the same rate as their listed base row, local and `:free` models stay at zero, and unknown ids still fall back to `default_cost()`.

Commands run: `cargo test -p ironclaw_common --lib llm_costs`, `cargo test -p ironclaw_architecture_tests --test reborn_contracts_vendor_census --test reborn_extension_specificity`, `cargo clippy -p ironclaw_common --tests -- -D warnings`

## Security Impact

None. `llm-prices` is a compile-time data table with no dependencies, no build script, no network calls, no I/O and no unsafe code. It's a `[dependencies]` entry pinned through `Cargo.lock`.

## Reborn Trust-Boundary Checklist

N/A: no policy, evidence, prompt, hash, status, serde, queue or sandbox types change. The public API of `llm_costs` is unchanged.

## Database Impact

None.

## Blast Radius

`ironclaw_common::llm_costs` and everything that reads it: per-run cost in the OpenAI-compatible API and WebChat v2, budget accounting in `ironclaw_loop_host`, and the provider cost lookups in `ironclaw_llm`. The worst case is a wrong price for a model, which only changes reported cost and budget math.

## Rollback Plan

Revert the PR. The lookup is additive and the public API didn't change, so a revert restores the old table without touching callers.

## Review Follow-Through

`crates/contracts/AGENTS.md` lists `llm_costs` as shrink-only vendor residue pending an owner decision on moving it beside the llm providers. This PR only shrinks it (91 -> 32 in the census) and doesn't do the move, since that's the owner call. If you want the move, I can do it as a follow-up. Happy to put the lookup behind a feature flag instead if you'd prefer.

---

**Review track**: B

prs.title: fix(cowork): clarify file edit progress and details
prs.body:
## Summary

File edit steps showed live green/red `+N / -N` counters without units, which could be mistaken for credit charges. Show file actions and outcomes by default, with an explicit **View changes** control for before/after details.

## Related Issue

User-reported usability issue; no linked GitHub issue.

## Changes Made

- Remove line-count badges from running steps, timeline rows, and folded activity summaries.
- Add visible change/error disclosure controls. Opening a file-change summary reveals its file details in one click.
- Default edit details to a localized Before/After comparison with neutral, unit-labeled line counts; show written content when no previous version is available.
- Deduplicate successful file changes in summaries and distinguish failed or incomplete edits from completed work.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Testing

- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added new tests
- [x] Updated existing tests
- [x] Manual testing performed

Validation:
- **123 targeted Vitest tests passed** across `AssistantTurnBlock`, `ActivityGroupBlock`, `ActivityIndicator`, `messageDisplayUtils`, and `mediaTaskPresentation`.
- Renderer TypeScript (`tsc --noEmit`), `npm run compile:electron`, changed-file ESLint with zero warnings, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Electron renderer fixtures verified running, successful, failed, interrupted, write, and mixed outcomes; deduplicated totals; expansion/collapse; Chinese/English; light/dark themes; and a 420px panel. This was fixture-based UI validation, not a live agent run.

## Screenshots

Actual components rendered in Electron with representative fixture data:

![File-change disclosure and before/after details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/2674a56962e579ad79948525e5fbc80702e96324/docs/res/screenshots/file-change-disclosure.png)

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing relevant unit tests pass locally with my changes

## Electron-Specific Changes

- [x] None

Renderer presentation only; no changes to main/preload, IPC, storage, runtime, window management, or OpenClaw configuration/restart behavior.
