prs.title: feat(mcp): generic OAuth 2.1 authorization-code + PKCE sign-in for remote MCP servers
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Remote MCP HTTP/SSE servers can now authenticate with a real OAuth 2.x authorization-code + PKCE flow via one config opt-in: `oauth = true` (`mcp.servers.<name>`, plus optional `oauth_client_id` / `oauth_scopes`). Before this, remote MCP endpoints were limited to static headers, which fails against real-world MCP gateways fronted by OAuth identity providers.
  - Full RFC stack, provider-agnostic (zero hardcoded provider specifics): RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata, RFC 8414 AS metadata, RFC 7591 dynamic client registration (public `none` client), RFC 8707 resource binding, RFC 9207 `iss` validation, RFC 8252 loopback redirects, RFC 6749 §6 refresh-token retention semantics.
  - Grants live in the existing encrypted `auth-profiles.json` store (fail-closed when `secrets.encrypt = false`), single process-wide owner, shared across transport clones and agents; proactive expiry refresh, 401-driven forced refresh, issuer-drift = drop + re-sign-in.
  - Interactive posture (stdin AND stderr TTY) waits up to 5 minutes for the browser callback; headless/daemon posture never hangs startup: it logs an actionable "connect once from an interactive ZeroClaw" error instead. Sign-in runs OUTSIDE the per-request timeout budgets (`prepare_auth`), so a slow human never has the loopback listener canceled mid-flow.
  - Docs: a full operator section in `docs/book/src/tools/mcp.md` (lifecycle, security posture, Silpo example, troubleshooting shapes).
- **Scope boundary:** does NOT add any OAuth provider specifics, discovery beyond RFCs, device-code flow, dashboard-hosted redirects, or tool-policy changes. Static-header MCP behavior remains unchanged except for the new fail-closed rejection of server-advertised CROSS-ORIGIN SSE message endpoints; bundles, risk profiles, approvals, and outcome-unknown recovery semantics are byte-identical.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-config` schema (three new fields + two new config errors), `zeroclaw-tools` (new `mcp_oauth` module; `mcp_transport` and `mcp_client` gained auth hooks), `zeroclaw-runtime` (process-wide manager assembly + interactive-posture plumbing). One deliberate behavior hardening beyond opt-in scope: every `sse` server's server-advertised message endpoint must now share the configured origin (a cross-origin advertisement is rejected even without `oauth` — session-header exfiltration), while the additional https requirement applies only with `oauth = true`, so plain-http LAN servers advertising their own origin keep working unchanged (see Compatibility).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related — planned (create at PR filing).
- **Maintainer question:** per ADR-016, the transitional runtime wiring (`tools/mcp_oauth_wiring.rs`, scoped assembly, daemon heartbeat hookup) likely needs a `zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md` exception-table row naming the MCP-OAuth scope. Master already carries such rows for #12274, #12342 and #12417 (this branch is rebased on the latter), so the pattern and owners columns are established; I deliberately do not draft the row's text or owner names here — flagged for Core Team disposition.

### What this does, simply

Many hosted MCP servers (e.g. shopping, banking, SaaS assistants) hide behind a login: they only accept requests carrying an OAuth token that a browser flow obtained. ZeroClaw previously had no way to get such a token, so these servers were unusable. This PR teaches ZeroClaw to knock on the server's door (`/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp`), discover where the login service lives, register itself as a public client, ask the user's browser to log in once, catch the resulting code on a loopback socket, exchange it for tokens (with PKCE, so no client secret can leak), and inject the token into every request to that server — refreshing it for the user from then on. Tokens are stored encrypted with the rest of ZeroClaw's credentials and are bound to the exact server resource. If sign-in is not possible (a daemon with no terminal), ZeroClaw says so plainly and keeps the server on hold rather than hanging.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes — deterministic, local mocks only, and one optional real-provider check if you have a Silpo account.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` (`cli`, `tui`) + MCP transports (streamable HTTP, SSE) against wiremock servers; gateway/daemon headless paths via unit/integration tests.
- **Setup / preconditions:** any checkout; `secrets.encrypt = true` (default).
- **Steps to run:** `cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools mcp_oauth` (127 tests, ~36 s — includes the 35 s slow-human connect regression), `cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib mcp_` (374), `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib mcp` (65, 1 ignored pre-existing), `cargo test -p zeroclaw-config oauth` (schema/validation/generated-fields). Optional live A/B (account required): config block `[[mcp.servers]] name=... transport="http" url="https://mcp.silpo.ua/mcp" oauth=true` + a bundle grant, then `zeroclaw agent -a <agent> -m "list MCP tools"`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** first connect prints an authorization URL and waits (up to 5 min, interactive); after consent the server's tools appear (`<name>__*`); restart reuses the encrypted grant silently (no browser); `zeroclaw` in a non-TTY environment logs "connect once from an interactive ZeroClaw" instead of hanging.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `McpServerConfig` does not deny unknown fields, so master silently IGNORES `oauth = true`, connects without a token, gets HTTP 401 from the gateway, and the server is skipped with a generic auth error — observed live when the same config ran on a master build. Remote MCP servers were static-header only.

### How I tested

All gates from clean `git worktree` checkouts of the exact SHAs (never the working tree), plus a production smoke against the real `mcp.silpo.ua` authorization server (Docker deployment; no fixtures with personal data).

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                   # 0
cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets \
  --features ci-all -- -D warnings                           # 0 warnings
cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools mcp_oauth                       # 127 passed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib mcp_                      # 374 passed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib mcp                     # 65 passed, 1 ignored (pre-existing npx)
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config                                # all binaries green
cargo test --workspace                                       # all green except two
                                                             # environment-bound component tests
                                                             # (missing `expect` binary / AppImage
                                                             # smoke), reproduced identically on
                                                             # unmodified master in the same box
DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/tools/mcp.md scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh   # 0 errors
DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/tools/mcp.md scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh     # pass (lychee absent locally; CI runs it)
```

Per-commit verification: every commit in the stack was gated in a detached clean worktree at its exact SHA (an automated per-SHA sweep — fmt + config-oauth + tools mcp_oauth + tools mcp_ + runtime mcp + wiring — plus the same suites re-run by each reviewer at the SHA under review). Result: all green except the `zeroclaw-runtime` **test build** at the three slices before the wiring commit (`error[E0063]: missing fields oauth, oauth_client_id, oauth_scopes in initializer of McpServerConfig` — a pre-existing daemon test struct literal without a `Default` fill; library/binary builds are green at every commit; repaired in the runtime-wiring commit, reproduced identically at every later rewrite of those commits).

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the exact gate commands above are the CI strict quality/test surfaces for the touched crates; docs/link gates cover the changed Markdown lines.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** live authorization-server interop is CI-unprovable (no credentials in CI); mitigated by the RFC-strict wiremock matrix + the documented live validation below. `./dev/ci.sh all` not run on the dev box (no Docker); native equivalents were run individually.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** A production deployment (Docker on a NAS, real `mcp.silpo.ua` OAuth 2.1 AS) plus a clean-room re-test built from this branch's final tip: fresh sign-in from a wiped grant store — the printed URL survived a multi-minute manual login (listener alive, single token exchange), a second run reused the encrypted grant silently (no browser at all: `enc2:` access+refresh profiles in `auth-profiles.json`), and the headless gateway then exercised real cart, delivery-settings, loyalty, and time-slot reads through the agent (38 tools). NOT verified in CI (no credentials); refresh/rotation paths are proven against mocks only. No PII committed.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (no layout-bearing surfaces; printed sign-in URL + record lines only).
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Docker-based `./dev/ci.sh all` (daemon unavailable on the dev box) — replaced by the native gate commands listed above.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes** — a loopback TCP listener on an ephemeral 127.0.0.1 port during interactive sign-in only (bind to loopback, host-equality gate on private targets, state + PKCE validation on every callback; RAII-closed after the flow).
- New external network calls? **Yes** — AS metadata/registration/token endpoints discovered from the protected-resource metadata; all HTTPS enforced, pinned to the configured host's DNS resolutions, proxy fail-closed when the `tool.mcp` policy applies; no telemetry.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes** — new `mcp:oauth@<hash>` profiles in the existing `auth-profiles.json` (encrypted-at-rest, fail-closed with `secrets.encrypt = false`); tokens redacted from logs/errors/tool results; resource+issuer-bound grants. Trust-boundary precision to state plainly: a private/loopback CONFIGURED MCP host trusts other ports on that same host for discovered AS/token endpoints (needed for local mock pairs and co-located private IdPs); public configured hosts never reach private ranges. This is host-equality, not origin-equality.
- Grant identity (deliberate): OAuth grants are intentionally bound to the canonical MCP resource URI, not to the configuration name. A configuration name is an operator alias and is not a user or security boundary; multiple aliases for the same resource therefore share the same audience-bound grant. Per-principal grants are out of scope and need a separate design (authenticated principal propagation, cache isolation, storage identity, DCR/client ownership, rate-limit attribution).
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No** — fixtures are synthetic; the docs example names only the public Silpo MCP URL.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No.**

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes**, one narrow exception: an SSE server that advertises a message endpoint on a DIFFERENT origin is now rejected even without `oauth` (session-header exfiltration guard). Servers advertising their own origin (the norm, including plain-http LAN servers) are unaffected — including the custom-CA https rule for non-OAuth servers, which is pre-existing and unchanged. Mid-session interactive re-authorization (token revoked while a tool call is in flight) is bounded by that call's timeout, not the full 5-minute browser window; it fails closed and the next attempt re-enters the sign-in with a fresh listener.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes** — three additive fields (`mcp.servers.<name>.oauth|oauth_client_id|oauth_scopes`); two new config validation errors (`oauth` on stdio; `oauth` + configured `Authorization` header). Upgrade steps: none for existing users. Known limitations: mid-session interactive re-authorization (token revoked during an in-flight tool call) is bounded by that call's timeout, not the 5-minute browser window — it fails closed and the next attempt re-enters the sign-in with a fresh listener (review-accepted NIT). Sign-in UX for container/remote deployments currently requires a terminal on the host (loopback callback); an operator onboarding follow-up (paste-the-redirect fallback, `zeroclaw mcp signin`, fixed redirect port) is designed and queued as a stacked PR.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No** (one new internal dependency on the `url` crate already used across the ecosystem).

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the PR's commits (stack of six conventional commits, each independently revertable); or downgrade the binary — older versions silently ignore the `oauth*` fields, so also remove or disable the affected `mcp.servers` entries (their connections would otherwise 401 and be skipped).
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** per-server `oauth = false` is the toggle; an unused stored grant is inert for older versions.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** grep records for `mcp_oauth` (`manager-init` errors typically mean `secrets.encrypt = false`; `browser-flow`/`refresh` errors carry the RFC-shaped reason: `invalid_client` → AS without DCR, use `oauth_client_id`; `redirect_uri_mismatch` → AS rejects ephemeral loopback ports; `invalid_scope` → adjust `oauth_scopes`; `issuer-drift` + `store-clear` mean the AS issuer moved and a fresh sign-in is required).

## Supersede Attribution

N/A

---

Privacy contract respected: no real identities/secrets in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs.

prs.title: feat(memory): store embeddings + hybrid recall for PostgresMemory
prs.body:
### Problem

`PostgresMemory` creates the pgvector `embedding` column but **never writes to it**: Postgres recall is always keyword-only (full-text), `reindex()` returns `Ok(0)`, and there is no embedder wiring on the postgres branch. The SQLite backend has had functional embeddings + hybrid recall all along; this makes the postgres backend functionally comparable.

### What changes

- **Embed-on-write**: the store path embeds when a vector column and a live embedder are present (upsert keeps the prior vector when a re-embed fails).
- **Two-stage hybrid recall**: cosine nearest-neighbours fused with the full-text ranking via the existing `hybrid_merge`. Falls back to the keyword path verbatim when the vector stage is not live (noop embedder, `search_mode = bm25`, empty query, provider error, or pgvector unavailable) — **the stock no-embedder default behavior is unchanged**.
- **Real `reindex()`**: backfills missing embedding vectors in batches (returning the number backfilled) and reindexes the derived keyword indexes.
- **`refresh_embedder()`** rebuilds and swaps the embedder in place, matching SQLite; `PostgresMemory::with_embedder(..)` added; `build_memory_with_storage` wires the resolved embedder/weights/search-mode into the postgres branch.
- **Migration guard fix** (first commit): the V3 constraint checks matched constraint names across the whole schema instead of the target table, so a second memory schema in the same database falsely reported "already initialized" and skipped its own migration.

### Tests

- `cargo test -p zeroclaw-memory --all-features`: 580 unit tests pass (feature-on and feature-off check clean, clippy + rustfmt clean).
- 6 live integration tests against a fresh `pgvector/pgvector:pg17` (isolated schemas, `ZEROCLAW_TEST_POSTGRES_URL`), including an end-to-end test that asserts embed-on-write populates the column with the expected vector **and** that the vector stage ranks a document whose keywords do *not* match the query (so the vector contribution is real, not keyword recall in disguise).

prs.title: feat(providers): support multiple models per provider profile
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Separate schema-v4 connections, capability models, presets and fallback graphs. Complete TOML keys are opaque, including dots and case. Historical profile/section and embedding inputs are normalized only in `zeroclaw-config`; V3→V4 migration retires profile-local fallback with actionable notices. Loading and disk migration share route conversion, including older V4 input, and loading converts historical model lists and speech bindings before any consumer receives Config.
  - Centralize chat, embedding, TTS, ASR and native decision protocols in `zeroclaw-providers`, behind capability contracts in `zeroclaw-api`. Share wire implementations across vendor adapters; model-specific text reasoning/tool extraction runs before empty-response validation, independently of native structured calls.
  - Make runtime, channels, memory, delegation, SOP, Doctor, CLI, gateway and UI consume canonical models. Gemini OAuth selects connection-owned credentials through a connection or model key, preserving implicit historical OAuth clients at the input boundary. Quickstart locality and route validation/display use the same admitted canonical registry as construction; model-switch and factory guidance use canonical model/connection names. Model identity is the exact ref plus upstream ID; every route, fallback and switch rematerializes the target model's full policy while connection descriptors may be reused within construction.
  - Use one validated registry editor for exact-key changes, secret restoration/encryption and dangling-reference validation. Editors no longer migrate historical source tables. Provider CLI CRUD manages connections/models/presets/fallback; renames update config consumers and refuse environment-owned references. CLI writes hold exclusive offline ownership; live edits use the daemon's existing transaction. Config deserialization and schema migration share one provider-input normalizer, with generated transient fields from the Config declarations. Historical driver, nested-model, OAuth and memory environment names are adapted at the same input transaction; file migration and environment input share driver field mappings. Environment snapshots follow relocated fields; external op:// references use the same exact-key secret traversal as encryption and survive unchanged saves or connection renames, while edited/deleted references are pruned.
  - Keep model bindings, RPC session refresh and embedding refresh in the admitted config generation lifecycle. Canonical Quickstart/Web/Zerocode pickers and Doctor/pricing use exact keys; context-window discovery addresses `/api/config/models/{model_ref}/refresh-context-window` and rechecks the target after network I/O.
- **Scope boundary:** Provider/model configuration and its consumers; no unrelated dependency/security upgrade or tool-permission expansion.
- **Blast radius:** Config migration/loading, provider construction/protocols, model routing/rebuild, agent turns, gateway sessions, channels, voice, memory embedding, delegation, and summaries.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.

### What this does, simply

A connection owns one endpoint and credential. Several independently named models can reuse it, including models for different capabilities. Consumers select a complete model key; model names may contain dots without becoming a path.

```toml
[providers.connections."gateway.prod"]
kind = "openai-compatible"
uri = "https://gateway.example.com/v1"
auth = { mode = "api_key", api_key = "<API_KEY>" }

[providers.connections."gateway.prod".api.chat]
wire_api = "chat_completions"
preset = "chat.balanced"
request_timeout_secs = 120
read_timeout_secs = 300

[providers.model_presets."chat.balanced"]
capability = "chat"
options = { max_tokens = 4096, extract_text_reasoning = true, extract_text_tool_calls = true }

[providers.models."chat.fast.us"]
capability = "chat"
provider = "gateway.prod"
model = "gpt-4o-mini"
options = { temperature = 0.2, extract_text_tool_calls = false }

[providers.models."chat.backup"]
capability = "chat"
provider = "gateway.prod"
model = "gpt-4o"

[providers.fallback]
"chat.fast.us" = ["chat.backup"]
```

An agent selects `model_provider = "chat.fast.us"`. Its model options override inherited preset values. Each selected fallback or switched model applies its own extraction policy; disabling text tool extraction does not disable native structured tool calls. Existing channel delivery sanitization and permission checks still apply.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=cli` and `surface=web`; gateway/channel consumers use the same admitted model registry.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A synthetic test account or a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint, a connection and two models as above, and an existing agent/risk profile with `model_provider = "chat.fast.us"`. Use a deterministic local fixture when checking textual extraction rather than relying on a model to repeat markup.
- **Steps to run:** Load the config, run `zeroclaw doctor`, then `zeroclaw agent -a assistant -m "hello"`. Repeat with each extraction option enabled/disabled, a native structured tool response, and a failed primary followed by the configured fallback. Switch the selected model and repeat.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Exact dotted model keys resolve, including in `llm_task`; model presets and invocation overrides apply. Route credentials override the primary only; backups use their own credentials. Fallback and switching use complete model settings. A tool-bearing request explicitly rejects a fallback chain mixing native and text protocols before dispatch; homogeneous chains and scalar calls remain supported. Registry Save all locks editing until its masked server baseline is refreshed.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The canonical connection/model/preset arrangement and per-model extraction switches are unavailable; text tool parsing is controlled by a runtime-profile `strict_tool_parsing` setting and reasoning markup is stripped unconditionally.

### How I tested

- **Current follow-up (2026-11-12, `da09279218`):** Formatting, working/staged diff checks, migration-fixture TOML parsing and static call-site audits passed. Local compilation, Clippy and tests were intentionally deferred; no historical result below is claimed for this head.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Format`, `Lint`, the Rust `Check` lanes and `Test` are pending for this revision. `Test` runs workspace nextest, including config migration/editor, provider OAuth, projected model locality/routes and heartbeat request-body regressions. `Docs Style` covers the documentation edits.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Compilation, tests and lint for the new input-admission boundary and adapted fixtures are pending. Added regressions cover V3/V4 admission, disk migration idempotence, mixed canonical/historical fallback, encryption and exact-key external-reference retention. No new live-vendor, manual terminal or browser capture was performed for this follow-up; existing screenshots retain their recorded revision.
- **Commands run and tail output:** For follow-up commit `dd2116a081`, `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` completed successfully. Source checks cover moved API call sites and test-only fixture boundaries; standard TOML parsing checked the new admission fixtures. No Rust build, test or Clippy was run locally for this follow-up; those results remain pending in CI.
- Added CI regression cases for V3/older-V4 route migration equivalence and idempotency, legacy-only model lists, speech namespace normalization/promotion/rename, explicit capability rejection, selected-connection key inheritance, heartbeat preset/options/clear behavior, and Gemini OAuth connection/model references plus active-profile selection. Follow-up cases also cover projected local models in mixed configs, route validation without canonical fixture injection, implicit Gemini OAuth clients across V3 migration/editor save/reload, masked secrets, and explicit API-key priority. These cases have not been executed locally.
- Added regression coverage for exact dotted keys, complete temporary model policy/fallback inheritance, canonical/legacy environment override restoration and promotion, exact rename/delete atomicity, environment-owned consumer refusal and canonical provider CLI parsing. These tests have not been run locally for this follow-up.
- The preceding CI run identified an exact-model pricing test expectation; the fixture now expects independent entries for both configured models. An inherited dependency advisory and a Landlock tool-install timeout remain outside this PR's scope.
- **Historical evidence:** Earlier revisions passed the targeted provider/config/gateway/Zerocode and Web checks recorded in the PR history. They do not establish compilation or behavioral correctness of this consumer refactor. The existing Web screenshots below cover the earlier UI revision; this follow-up does not change Web layout.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Chrome rendered the production Web bundle against isolated synthetic API fixtures. Selecting `chat.fast.us`, clearing and selecting `main`, following an exact model key into the registry Models tab, and requiring Azure `extra.resource` before staging all passed, with zero page script errors. This is interface evidence rather than real-backend/vendor evidence.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Six existing screenshots and the browser record are in [`.pr-evidence/pr9809/canonical-ui-20261110`](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/tree/worktree-providers-multi-model/.pr-evidence/pr9809/canonical-ui-20261110). The older registry-save captures in the parent evidence directory are historical.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `surface=web`, production bundle routes `/quickstart` and `/config/providers.registry?model=chat.fast.us`, Chrome `en-US`, desktop 1280×900 and mobile 390×844. The [browser record](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/worktree-providers-multi-model/.pr-evidence/pr9809/canonical-ui-20261110/observations.json) records the tested Web tree and bundle digest.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** [Quickstart desktop](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/worktree-providers-multi-model/.pr-evidence/pr9809/canonical-ui-20261110/quickstart-desktop.png), [selected model](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/worktree-providers-multi-model/.pr-evidence/pr9809/canonical-ui-20261110/quickstart-selected.png), [Azure required field](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/worktree-providers-multi-model/.pr-evidence/pr9809/canonical-ui-20261110/quickstart-azure-required.png), [Quickstart mobile](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/worktree-providers-multi-model/.pr-evidence/pr9809/canonical-ui-20261110/quickstart-mobile.png), [registry desktop](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/worktree-providers-multi-model/.pr-evidence/pr9809/canonical-ui-20261110/registry-desktop.png), and [registry mobile](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/worktree-providers-multi-model/.pr-evidence/pr9809/canonical-ui-20261110/registry-mobile.png). All data is synthetic and credentials are masked.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** HTTP and RPC configuration navigation expose one registry editor. UI and catalog consumers keep complete opaque model keys. Cost accounting reads canonical model metadata, response-cache identity includes connections/presets, and channel/voice consumers construct canonical ASR/TTS managers without legacy enable flags. Quickstart, factory dispatch, embedding construction and semantic-search diagnostics consume normalized definitions; the production family factory no longer accepts an optional Config for historical profile lookup. Doctor enumerates canonical chat models, retains single-part cache keys, and recognizes Codex authentication on connections. Quickstart writes typed connections plus models and validates required connection fields before publishing. CLI flag prefills, authentication prompts, and subscription login use the same canonical field names; Anthropic setup tokens update the exact connection and use the existing encrypted persistence lifecycle. Existing model selection no longer derives a provider kind from name segments.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Local compilation, Rust tests and Clippy were intentionally deferred to CI at the requested validation scope. No unrelated dependency/security upgrades were added. Live-vendor and manual terminal checks require their configured environments.


## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes, provider capability support and authenticated registry editing.** The whole-registry editor requires Config read/create/update/delete grants and root `providers` write scope; narrower scopes cannot use replacement to bypass existing restrictions. Native decision and shared audio protocols are available on supported provider adapters; this does not grant new tool permissions or filesystem access. Model capability admission and configured connection restrictions remain enforced.
- New external network calls? **Yes, supported native protocol endpoints.** Requests use the selected configured connection, authentication, transport policy, and timeouts; native decision calls are not synthesized through chat.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes.** Typed connection authentication and all `extra_headers` values follow the existing credential encryption policy. Both editors receive masked snapshots and restore unchanged masks under the config commit lock. Models reference connections rather than duplicating credentials.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.** Examples use synthetic credentials and endpoints.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** Text tool instructions/extraction now follow the selected model's boolean policy. Only admitted tools can execute, and existing approval, permission, and channel delivery sanitization boundaries remain in place.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Selecting the wrong connection or protocol can send a request to an unintended configured provider or expose incompatible model output. Exact-key resolution, capability/type validation, admitted generations, explicit factory errors, encryption, and unchanged execution authorization constrain those changes.

## Compatibility (required)

- Provider CLI CRUD now addresses canonical registry sections and complete keys; legacy category/family/alias arguments are removed. `models set` edits the selected model's upstream ID. These writes require offline ownership; use the running daemon's configuration editor for live updates.
- `ModelIdentity` exposes exact `model_ref` and effective `model_id`; ASR manager construction accepts full `Config`. Context-window discovery uses the exact-model HTTP route documented above; the family/alias route is removed.
- Registry rename updates in-config model/connection/preset bindings and fallback edges, and refuses environment-owned changes. External SOP files must be updated separately. Config loading retires historical source tables before internal consumers run; registry writes edit only those admitted definitions, so deletion cannot regenerate removed models. Historical fixture adapters live in the config migration module and are gated to tests/test-helpers.

- Backward compatible? **No for removed config fields; historical provider input is normalized at the config boundary, including legacy route input in already-versioned V4 files.** Canonical exact keys take precedence when both forms are admitted.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** Canonical provider tables and boolean extraction options are available; `strict_tool_parsing` is removed.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: This PR is part of schema v4, not a v5 change. Run `zeroclaw config migrate` for v3 input, review retirement notices, define shared connections and capability models, and update consumers to exact model keys. Replace an old `strict_tool_parsing = true` intent with `options.extract_text_tool_calls = false` on the corresponding chat model/preset. Omit a boolean to inherit; use `true`/`false` to override. The two extraction booleans do not accept the `"null"` clear sentinel used by nullable request options.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the PR commits through a reviewed branch. Keep a pre-migration config backup when evaluating the new layout.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** No feature flag. Textual extraction can be adjusted per model/preset through the two boolean options.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Config admission/capability mismatch errors, unresolved exact model keys, provider construction or model-switch failures, exhausted fallback chains, and voice/embedding initialization failures. Text extraction regressions appear as unexpected markup in replies or missing textual tool calls.

prs.title: fix(web): show a detached chat turn and load its answer when it ends
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - When a dashboard chat socket closes mid-turn and reopens while the turn is still running, the page reloads the transcript once, before the turn is stored, and nothing reloads it again: the answer stays missing until a page reload or a conversation switch (#12107).
  - Hydration now asks `GET /api/sessions/{id}/state` before it loads the stored transcript (asked after it, a turn ending between the two reads would leave its answer unloaded). While the turn is `running` there, the page shows it as running (before the composer unlocks, so it does not offer to send into it) and asks again every 2 s. Once the state leaves `running`, it loads the transcript once more. The gateway sets `idle` or `error` only after it has persisted the turn (`ws.rs`), so that load has the answer, or the stored outcome of a failed turn.
  - The watch ends without a reload on the next hydration, a conversation switch or clear, a model switch (a clear or model switch also stops one that has not started yet, while the first check or the transcript load is still out), unmount, and when its socket closes (the reopen reloads and asks again). A check still in flight when the watch ends is ignored. A failed check, including the 404 of a gateway without session persistence, reads as "not running": the page keeps today's single load and never retries in a loop. So does a check without an answer within 10 s (`STATE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS`): each check has its own deadline, and the page stops awaiting it at the deadline or when the watch ends, so a stuck request can neither keep the composer locked nor keep the turn shown as running. A daemon restarted mid-turn settles the abandoned turn to `error` (`recover_abandoned_session_turns`), which also ends the watch.
  - Because the check runs after any hydration, a page loaded while its conversation's turn runs (a reload, or a return from another conversation) also shows the turn and loads the answer when it ends.
- **Scope boundary:** Web dashboard only (`web/src`); no gateway or API change: the state route already exists. A turn streaming on the page's own socket is not watched. A conversation switch still does not abort a detached turn (it aborts a live one, as before); Stop aborts a watched turn through the existing abort route, and the watch then loads the outcome. Accounts whose chat goes through the core (one conversation per socket) are unchanged: there is nothing to reload. No partial-answer replay while the turn runs; the answer appears when it is stored. Not covered, as possible follow-ups: an "outcome unknown" notice or tool-card settling across a reload; a deadline on the transcript load itself (`GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages`, unchanged here and signal-less on master); a turn that another client starts in the same conversation, which this page does not see live at any time (a dashboard socket receives turn frames only for its own prompts; the multi-viewer direction is #9002 and #11185), so a turn started while the transcript loads is shown at the next load, as one started just after it would be; and the known limit pinned in `chatHydration.logic.test.ts` (#11571), where a prompt another client committed with identical text hides the same prompt in flight here: transcript rows carry no turn id, so that needs a server change.
- **Blast radius:** `AgentContext` hydration and the socket close handler. One extra `GET /api/sessions/{id}/state` per transcript load (a gateway without session persistence answers it with 404), plus one every 2 s only while a detached turn runs.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12107. Related #9002 (the wider reconnect contract), #11571 (keeps the in-flight prompt on reload), #11965 (introduced the reload on reopen), #11185 (server-side session-owned turns for RPC clients; no dashboard change).

### What this does, simply

The gateway keeps working on a chat turn after the browser loses its connection, but it saves the turn only when it finishes. If the browser reconnected before that, it fetched the conversation too early, got no answer, and never looked again, so the chat sat idle with the answer missing. Now the browser asks the gateway whether the turn is still running, shows it as running if so, and fetches the conversation again as soon as the gateway reports it finished. It stops asking when the turn ends, when the user moves on, or when anything goes wrong, so it cannot loop.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface: web`
- **Setup / preconditions:** Session persistence on (the default) and a turn that runs at least ~20 s (for example a shell tool running `sleep 20`).
- **Steps to run:** Send the turn. While it runs, drop the connection briefly (devtools offline for a few seconds, or restart a proxy in front of the gateway) so the socket closes and reopens. Wait for the turn to finish. Separately: reload the page while a turn runs.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** After the reopen (or reload) the turn shows as running and the composer stays locked; when the turn finishes, the answer appears on its own and the composer unlocks. The prompt appears once.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** After the reopen the page stops showing the turn; the answer does not appear until the page is reloaded or the conversation switched.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the web test jobs run `test:contexts`, which includes `sessionLifecycle.test.ts`, where the new tests live next to the existing reopen test.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI has no browser test; the network-drop behaviour is covered by the manual browser check below.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (on this head, Node with the generated API files from an xtask web build)
  - `npx tsc -b`: clean
  - `npm run test:contexts`: `ℹ pass 151` / `ℹ fail 0` (`sessionLifecycle.test.ts`: 83 pass, 20 new)
  - `npm test`: 166 pass, 0 fail; `npm run test:auth`: 239 pass, 0 fail; `npm run test:navigation`: 9 pass, 0 fail; `npm run test:permissions`: 34 pass, 0 fail
  - `git diff --check`, `scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` on the changed files: clean
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - The new tests fail against master's `AgentContext.tsx` (same tests, master's production file): the reopen, page-load, Stop, switch and close scenarios fail at the first "shows the turn as running" assertion.
  - Reverting each guard one at a time (live-turn guard; switch keeps a detached turn; close, clear, model switch and unmount end the watch; the abort checks after the wait and after the last check; a failed check reads as not running; the reload when the turn ends; the per-check deadline, the race that stops awaiting a stuck request, the cancellation of a check when the watch ends; a hydration's pending check registered, and cancelled by clear and by model switch; no watch once cancelled before the load) fails at least one test each: 17 of 17.
  - The tests also assert the prompt shows exactly once while the turn runs and after the answer loads, and that the page never re-sends it.
  - A turn that ends while the transcript loads (the test's gateway flips to `idle` when the snapshot is read) still gets its answer loaded; this fails with the state asked after the load.
  - A state check that never answers: hydration finishes at the deadline with the single load (no watch), and a stuck check during the watch ends it with one reload; the stuck request's signal is aborted in both, and on a conversation switch.
  - **Browser check against a real gateway with a real network drop** (added 2026-11-15; headless Chromium, isolated `zeroclaw gateway` built from this head's two commits, patch-id identical, plus unrelated carried changes). A fake OpenAI-compatible model streams a fixed answer over 20 s; a TCP proxy between browser and gateway drops every connection, with no close frames, and refuses new ones for a set time. Each trial opens `/agent/<alias>`, sends a message, cuts the network once the model's first words are on screen, then waits for the complete answer without any reload or navigation. Control: the same tree with this PR's two commits reverted and nothing else.

    | Network outage | Without this PR | With this PR |
    |---|---|---|
    | 3 s (the socket reopens while the turn still runs) | 0/5: one transcript load while the turn runs, the composer back to "Type a message...", the answer never shown | 5/5: "Running…" shown, `/state` polled every 2 s, the answer loaded when the turn ends |
    | 12 s (the turn ends during the outage) | 2/2 | 2/2 |

  - **Gateway side, without a browser:** over 30 drop-and-reopen trials (clean close, close then reopen, abrupt TCP drop), `/state` stayed `running` during the detached turn, and at the first non-`running` read (polled every 50 ms) `/messages` already held the complete answer: the turn is stored before the state reports `idle`, which this change relies on.
  - Not covered: mobile background-tab timer throttling and tab eviction.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact final-interface output. No new UI: the change only drives the existing running state (`typing`); one test renders the real chat page (`AgentChatInner`) and asserts the composer is disabled while the detached turn runs and enabled once its answer has loaded.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `e3bb49a3591b54e131a6a018faa2ad96ac2b5a2b`, `web/src/contexts/sessionLifecycle.test.ts` ("a page that loads while its turn runs shows the turn and loads the outcome once it ends").
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** the assertions above, on the rendered `AgentChatInner` textarea's `disabled` prop.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** turn running on the gateway at hydration → composer disabled, running state shown; state leaves `running` → transcript reloaded, answer shown, composer enabled.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** no Rust checks: no Rust file changed.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No (an existing same-origin route, with the page's existing auth)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk: `git revert <sha>`.

prs.title: feat(web): manage write-only plugin TLS credentials
prs.body:
## Summary

- Base branch is `master`.
- Add a write-only operator panel under Config → Storage → Secrets for credentials already referenced by a plugin TLS profile.
- Reuse the canonical encrypted plugin configuration and existing host-mediated TLS authorization. The catalog returns instance, property, destinations and configured state.
- This is the first implementation slice of Related #12373. The broader catalog, reversible disable, and references usable by other consumers are open design work. This PR leaves the issue open.

### What this does, simply

An authenticated operator can provision a PEM value for a configured plugin TLS profile without putting the value in a chat. Rotation and deletion use the existing configuration commit path. New connections continue to use the existing instance and destination checks.

## Testing

### How you can test

- Reviewer testing requested. Surface is web.
- Pair the dashboard, enable encryption with an initialized key, and configure a plugin TLS profile referencing a schema-declared secret.
- Open Storage → Secrets → Plugin TLS credentials. Set, replace, refresh and delete a synthetic PEM value. Inspect the responses and verify they contain only metadata or configured state.
- On master, the dedicated panel is absent.

### How I tested

- `cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --tests -j2` completed successfully.
- Web TypeScript type checking passed. The four existing read-only configuration UI regression tests passed.
- Rust formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Added a real config-router test for scoped-principal rejection, missing key, encrypted persistence, duplicate creation, replacement and deletion. The gateway test exposed a deletion failure. The follow-up persists only the selected credential and tests that neighboring ciphertext and the TLS profile survive. The current-head gateway test is pending CI. A Chrome walkthrough of the real WebUI with a synthetic API passed create, replace, refresh, delete, and draft clearing on cancel. This browser test did not use a live gateway.

## Security & Privacy Impact

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. The new route requires a current authenticated administrator. It accepts only existing TLS binding slots.
- New external network calls? No.
- Credential handling changed? Yes. Bounded request bodies carry write-only values. The route requires encryption and an existing key, returns metadata with no-store, and emits mutation metadata without the submitted value.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in the diff or fixtures? No.
- Model-visible inputs or prompt injection surface changed? No.

## Compatibility

- Backward compatible? Yes.
- Config, env or CLI surface changed? No. The API and dashboard gain a panel for existing bindings.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.

## Rollback

Revert this change to remove the panel and route. Values already saved remain standard plugin configuration. Restore a known-good encrypted configuration backup to undo a credential rotation or deletion, and retain the corresponding encryption key. Watch for unexpected 403, 409 or 412 responses on the new route and for connection failures after credential edits.

prs.title: fix(config): bind cached HTTP clients to their Tokio runtime
prs.body:
## Summary



- **Base branch:** `master`

- **What changed and why:** Match cached HTTP clients to their owning Tokio runtime, so a client whose dispatcher ended cannot be reused by a later runtime. Preserve one existing cache entry per service/timeout profile and the current proxy-generation invalidation.

- **Scope boundary:** No global test serialization, disabled HTTP pooling, new proxy authority, or provider retry policy.

- **Blast radius:** Shared runtime proxy HTTP client builders, including provider calls.

- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12236 and #12238. This addresses the production cache ownership rather than disabling pooling only in tests.



### What this does, simply



A cached client could outlive the runtime that owned its connection tasks. A later request then failed with “dispatch task is gone”. Cache lookup now checks the current runtime identity, and clients built without a current runtime are not cached. Ordinary calls on one runtime still reuse their client.



## Testing (required)



### How you can test (when useful)



- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A; the regression starts a real local HTTP server and performs requests from two successive runtimes.



### How I tested



- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Fresh CI requested; pending.

- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Full workspace and platform CI pending; no live provider credentials used.

- **Commands run and tail output:**



```text

cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib runtime_proxy_client_cache -j 4

5 passed; 0 failed

cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config --all-targets -j 4 -- -D warnings

Finished dev profile; exit 0

cargo fmt --all

exit 0

```



- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The test drops the first runtime before the second request, uses one unchanged service/timeout cache profile, and verifies both HTTP responses. Existing generation-invalidation and same-runtime cache tests pass.

- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no presentation change.

- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** 0298c72bede70858ee5e80aec76616cedc6b3a67; native Linux HTTP cache tests.

- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Test output above.

- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Both runtimes receive HTTP 200 and body ok.

- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No full workspace run locally; fresh CI supplies wider coverage. SQLite advisory on master remains a separate issue #12320 and is fixed separately in #12322.



## Security & Privacy Impact (required)



- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No

- New external network calls? No production change; test uses loopback

- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No

- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No

- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: None. Proxy selection and invalidation remain authoritative.



## Compatibility (required)



- Backward compatible? Yes

- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No

- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No; enables Tokio rt already present at runtime.



## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)



- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the commit; cache may again reuse a dispatcher owned by an ended runtime.

- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.

- **Observable failure symptoms:** Failed cache regression or HTTP dispatcher errors. Cache remains bounded to its existing service profiles.




SQLite follow-up: the workspace-only bridge from #12322 was removed from this independent PR after review identified the crates.io consumer limitation. Registry dependency compatibility is preserved. The shared security advisory remains tracked in #12320; #12322 is not a merge prerequisite for this PR.

prs.title: feat(web): add paired-device voice settings and chat controls
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** master.
- Add opt-in browser dictation and narration in agent chat, with paired-device voice preferences and a localized guide under Config â†’ Other â†’ Browser Voice and Audio.
- Save microphone, recognition mode, language, voice, speed and automatic narration on the authenticated paired-device record, not browser storage. Operators can select another paired device's record without changing the current browser's identity.
- Add one global `gateway.voice_silence_timeout_secs` setting in that same voice screen: default 15 seconds, accepted range 0â€“300, with 0 disabling automatic submission. It applies to every device/conversation and uses the existing authenticated configuration property API.
- Speak rendered Markdown text rather than hidden delimiters; omit only a trailing crab signature. Preserve meaningful literal code punctuation. Formatting-only replies do not block the continuous reading queue.
- **Scope boundary:** browser speech APIs, paired-device preferences, one gateway configuration field and normal chat submission. No server STT/TTS backend, microphone-audio upload endpoint, new identity or external service is added.
- **Blast radius:** web Config/chat, existing device-registry migration, gateway configuration and same-origin microphone Permissions Policy.
- **Linked issues:** none.

### What this does, simply

A paired browser can enable microphone and speaker controls next to the composer. Recognition starts only when the user clicks the microphone and grants browser permission. Local recognition is the default and never falls back online automatically; browser-service recognition is an explicit choice.

Dictation appends final recognized text to the draft. After the global silence interval, capture stops and final results are accepted before the normal send path is invoked once. Empty captures, hidden/cancelled chats, disconnected/busy sessions and stale conversation requests do not auto-send. A browser ending recognition early still honors the remaining silence interval. Local slash commands remain for manual submission. Set the global value to 0 for manual sending only.

The speaker reads a reply once, stops it, or enables continuous reading through a hold/Shift+Enter gesture. Automatic reading skips restored history and consumes unreadable formatting/signature-only replies so later responses can play. Changing the speech text never changes the displayed/stored response.

<!-- jarvis-validation-update:start -->
## Validation update (2026-11-10)

Updated to master a11a5ce5b at 9a9f6a1be. Combined voice controls with scoped chat while retaining operator-only image uploads. Voice submission honors the existing canSend/first-conversation path. A regression drives the actual voice callback through a restricted account's first WebSocket conversation, verifies exactly one message after session_start, and verifies that file uploads remain unavailable. Canonical API generation, the auth suite, all 31 voice tests, and the production build passed. Five gateway voice authorization tests also passed, including revocation during a write. This update was validated locally; earlier installed-browser evidence below describes its recorded revisions.

CI results and maintainer decisions on the published revision remain authoritative.
<!-- jarvis-validation-update:end -->

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interfaces:** web Config and agent chat; authenticated gateway configuration/device APIs.
- **Preconditions:** HTTPS or localhost, a paired browser, browser/OS speech support; select a locally available voice to test playback.
- **Steps:**
  1. Open Config â†’ Other â†’ Browser Voice and Audio. Enable dictation/narration, select language/voice and try the sample.
  2. Change global silence to 15, dictate and pause: verify exactly one send after the interval. Test 0 (manual only), another value, empty capture, manual stop, conversation switch and hidden chat. Confirm the same value appears on another paired device.
  3. Read a response with headings, emphasis, lists, a link and a horizontal rule. Formatting must not be spoken; code such as `apt-get --yes` must retain literal punctuation. A final crab signature is silent, but a crab in the body remains content.
  4. Enable continuous reading; place `---` or a signature-only reply before another readable answer. The latter must play. Restored history and trim notices remain silent.
  5. Reload settings and switch the device selector: per-device choices remain isolated, while the silence timeout stays global. Revoke a technical device and confirm its voice API refuses access. No voice preference storage key is added to browser storage.
  6. Try unavailable local recognition: no online fallback. Browser-service mode and online voices remain explicit choices.
- **Expected after:** documented opt-in controls, durable per-device voice choices, one adjustable global silence deadline and readable narration.
- **Before on master:** these browser speech controls and preference APIs are absent.

### Earlier validation (historical)

- **Latest functional/layout revision:** 61aeff4bb (global silence, narration fixes and responsive settings/toolbar spacing); the corresponding integrated candidate uses the same feature changes.
- **Latest checks actually run:** 24 voice tests passed; configuration default/range test passed; canonical `cargo run -p xtask --bin web -- gen-api` passed; integrated TypeScript check and production WebUI build passed. The checks exercise the actual component speech-submission callback, global property save, zero-disable, final-results ordering, activity resets, empty/hidden/cancelled capture, early recognition end, signature filtering and continuous queue progress.
- **Historical baseline checks:** gateway paired-device tests (14), security-header tests (5), auth/session/UI tests and format/diff checks passed at earlier documented revisions. These are not reattributed to the new head.
- **CI status:** current head includes master755bc9a4e. Its SQLite exception was approved and merged by maintainers in#12321; this PR does not introduce its own exception. The functional/layout source and installed bundle remain unchanged by that policy-only merge. Current-head CI is authoritative. The independent PR's shared SQLite advisory remains tracked by #12320; the checkout-only #12322 bridge was removed here after its registry-publication limitation was found. No advisory ignore was added. The preceding head's 32-bit check failed during runner `apt install` timeouts, before checking this code.
- **Coverage limits:** component tests simulate speech APIs. Actual microphone hardware, audible OS voice output, language pack downloads and browser-provider network behavior require device testing. New browser validation/deployment results will be reported separately, not inferred from unit tests.
- **Installed-browser validation:** synthetic microphone transcript, actual WebSocket/model completion, exactly one automatic send after **15,131 ms**, technical conversation deleted, global field verified at15 in Browser Voice and Audio; a nondefault16-second value was saved, verified on disk/after reload, then restored to15. Actual microphone hardware/audio playback are not claimed.
- **Responsive layout follow-up at61aeff4bb:** label above the numeric input (8px gap), separate help and save row (16px gap), and nonshrinking40px microphone/speaker buttons. Verified the installed UI at1280px and390px wide; both controls remain visible. The layout-only static update preserved configuration and binary and did not restart the daemon.

![Current desktop voice settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/0cc369ed976c610335df3a05e7fc6db4bfc0b6c1/.pr-evidence/web-voice-layout-desktop.png)

![Current mobile voice settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/0cc369ed976c610335df3a05e7fc6db4bfc0b6c1/.pr-evidence/web-voice-layout-mobile.png)

- **Earlier functional-field evidence (before the spacing follow-up):** cropped from the installed UI matching the feature changes at3f70b1efc; the evidence branch adds only this image, without changing the reviewed feature head.

![Global browser voice silence setting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/6423d16e3db0b77a369c815b7839f81bbe79d357/.pr-evidence/web-voice-global-silence-live.png)

- **Visual evidence provenance:** the following captures were originally recorded at 6338a726b3297bd18fa3d3a3cc06f5b6a7d109ae and retained at the evidence revision below. They show the prior device selector, guide and controls; they do not show the newly added global field.

![Paired-device selector](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/183d5eaed671ebc6d8e8621ea71a46cc1bc22c02/.pr-evidence/web-voice-devices-other-desktop.png)

![Settings and usage guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/183d5eaed671ebc6d8e8621ea71a46cc1bc22c02/.pr-evidence/web-voice-guide-desktop.png)

[Mobile chat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/183d5eaed671ebc6d8e8621ea71a46cc1bc22c02/.pr-evidence/web-voice-chat-mobile.png) Â· [Portuguese guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/183d5eaed671ebc6d8e8621ea71a46cc1bc22c02/.pr-evidence/web-voice-guide-pt.png)

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- **Permissions:** same-origin microphone/on-device recognition is permitted; microphone and narration default disabled per device. Browser consent and user initiation are still required. Global silence defaults to 15 only after dictation is explicitly started.
- **External calls:** optional browser language-pack downloads, explicitly selected online recognition/voices; no microphone audio reaches the gateway.
- **Credentials:** own-device routes resolve the existing paired bearer under the live pairing guard; other-device management uses existing operator authorization. Global timeout reads/writes use the existing config property API and its authorization/validation. No credential is returned or logged by this feature.
- **Personal data in fixtures/docs:** none; synthetic content only.
- **Model-visible text:** recognized text follows the existing user draft/send path; no approval bypass or additional execution capability.

## Compatibility (required)

- **HTTP/config:** existing paired records receive disabled voice defaults; the new global field defaults to 15 when absent. Its range is validated on configuration writes/load. Rust struct-literal callers may need the new field or `..Default::default()`.
- **Config surface:** `gateway.voice_silence_timeout_secs`; existing device preference routes remain per-device. No new environment variable or transport endpoint.
- **Toolchain floor:** unchanged.
- **Upgrade:** build matching gateway/WebUI, enable desired device controls and adjust the global interval in Browser Voice and Audio. Cookie-only sessions without a paired-device identity cannot edit device preferences.

## Rollback

- Disable automatic sending by setting global silence to 0; microphone/narration/continuous reading can be disabled independently in the voice screen.
- For binary rollback, restore a verified prior binary; remove the new configuration key if rolling back to a version rejecting unknown fields. The nullable device-preference column can remain. Preserve state and credentials rather than blindly restoring an old database after accepted work.
- Observable failures: Config save/load errors, browser capture/playback errors or preference-API refusals. Global-setting load failure disables automatic submission rather than guessing a deadline.

### Localization

The existing voice guide/device strings retain their ten-language translations and English fallback. The six new global-setting strings are provided in English and Portuguese; other locales use the existing English fallback.


<!-- followup-20261110-b:start -->
## Additional review follow-up
Continuous reading now checks readiness, listening and speaking before parsing a queued Markdown answer. Added a regression demonstrating no repeated DOM conversion while the parent rerenders during playback; it fails before the fix and passes after. All 32 voice tests pass; the integrated WebUI production build passes.

Local evidence above is from the integrated candidate. Fresh hosted CI will run on the published branch commit; maintainer architecture/merge decisions remain unchanged.
<!-- followup-20261110-b:end -->

prs.title: feat(tools): add opt-in task-owned SSH transport reuse
prs.body:
## Summary





Base branch: `master`.





Add opt-in task-owned SSH transport reuse. Related #11867.





### What this does, simply





One logical task owns its transport pool. Healthy idle connections can be recreated; failed or unexpectedly dead transports remain unavailable until the task ends.





## Testing (required)





### How you can test (when useful)





Run `python3 scripts/ssh/test_ssh_task.py -v` and `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --lib task_ssh::tests`. Native Linux/OpenSSH lifecycle checks should cover process death, expiry and task cleanup.





### How I tested





Current-head CI Required Gate and all executed checks pass at 1add22e4e970f98fb1e018e0c07d9e56b4876515, including CLI-only artifact ratchet, parallel Runtime Test and Windows coverage. All 14 helper regressions and 20 native Linux/OpenSSH candidate checks passed. The integrated composition c67330cc221ffdee48494424071833f8b2165230 passed 13 follow-up validation groups: the actual opt-in helper steering test observed one task ID across both tool rounds; five streamed lifecycle tests, two task-scope tests, strict Clippy and release passed. Alias/effective-configuration isolation, per-key network setup, 8 KiB in-memory stderr and idle retirement/generation leases are covered. Earlier recommended maintainer commits retain their authorship. The Core ownership decision remains pending.





Visual interface evidence: this follow-up changes integration, lifecycle or tests; prior feature UI evidence remains linked in the review discussion. No new presentation claim is made from source inspection. Remaining platform/integration gaps are those not covered by current-head hosted CI and the named local checks.





## Security & Privacy Impact (required)





The feature reuses existing SSH authentication and host-trust settings. No credential export or trust override is added. The failure-cache repair reclaims process/log/socket resources while retaining the task failure record. New transport access remains opt-in and task-scoped.

prs.title: feat(ssh): use scoped credentials in task-owned transports
prs.body:
## Summary

Depends on #11869 and #12408. Related #12373.

The task SSH broker reads a configured SSH alias and checks the effective OpenSSH host, port, and user before granting access to a connection. It supports local encrypted keys and OpenBao references. The key is loaded over stdin into a private per-connection ssh-agent. SSH trust checks, task cleanup and idle expiry remain in force.

## Testing

- All 15 existing SSH broker tests passed.
- On a Linux integration host, an OpenBao reference provisioned through the WebUI authenticated on two approved destinations with the host's legacy agent removed from the test environment.
- Three commands used two masters. The wrong port was refused. Task completion removed the socket directory. A same-task test removed one destination grant from an isolated temporary policy while both masters were open. The revoked destination was denied and the other still worked. After a full host reboot the service recovered OpenBao authentication and both approved SSH destinations worked again.

## Security and compatibility

The operator opts in by setting the credential directory and optionally a default alias. The broker checks configuration before granting each command. Private key bytes are excluded from command arguments and written to the private agent over stdin. Existing deployments continue to use their configured agent when the scoped mode is not enabled. This Linux helper requires Python cryptography for scoped mode. Roll back by reverting the helper and restoring the previous service environment.

### SSH key custody and transport lifetime

The operator registers a write-only OpenSSH key or an external reference and explicit host, port, and remote-user grants. For OpenBao, the daemon persists the encrypted reference, fetches the key under its narrowly scoped service identity, and passes it over stdin to an ephemeral OpenSSH agent. The helper does not create a private-key file or expose the value to the model, command arguments, or tool output. The signer socket is under a mode-0700 task directory owned by the service user, and agent forwarding is disabled. The broker requires strict server host-key verification.

Once OpenSSH creates its authenticated multiplex listener, the broker shuts down the signer and unlinks its socket before granting the first command. Later commands reuse the authenticated connection and recheck the current destination grant. A revoked grant blocks subsequent broker commands even if a transport already exists. The master itself is closed on task completion, cancellation, or idle expiry.

The service account and root remain trusted. A process with the same UID may reach the signing socket during authentication or the authenticated multiplex socket during the task. Per-destination grants are enforced by the broker. Host isolation and least-privilege vault policy bound the impact of same-UID compromise. This design does not claim a security boundary against a compromised daemon or unrestricted same-UID execution.

prs.title: feat(channels): opt-in owner notice for turned-away Matrix senders
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A Matrix message turned away by the sender allowlist is dropped silently: the sender gets no stub, and the operator learns about the attempt only from DEBUG logs. This adds an opt-in `owner_user_id` field to `[channels.matrix.<alias>]`; when set, the channel also delivers a short heads-up DM to that user (typically the operator) naming the sender MXID, the source room, and a bounded preview of the turned-away message, plus a `peer_groups` authorization hint.
  - The DM room is created lazily (`is_direct`, encrypted under the SDK's e2e feature), cached, and re-resolved when the configured owner changes; an existing DM with the owner is reused.
  - Notices are throttled to one per (sender, room) pair per 5 minutes. Matrix has no transport-level flood gate like Telegram's Bot API, so without this a determined spammer could turn the operator's DM into a firehose.
- **Scope boundary:** trigger v1 is the sender-allowlist drop only — room-allowlist drops (operator configuration errors) and mention-gate drops (polite group silence) do not notify. No public stub is sent to the turned-away sender; authorization decisions, peer resolution, and other channels are unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** Matrix channel ingress only. `HandlerCtx` and the channel struct gain shared owner-notice state; two test-only `HandlerCtx` literals and one full `MatrixConfig` test literal are updated.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12346 (Telegram `owner_chat_id` owner notice — same design vocabulary, deliberately adapted)

### What this does, simply

In Matrix, when someone who is not on the bot's peer list writes to a room the bot watches, the message is currently dropped with only a DEBUG log line — neither the sender nor the operator hears anything. With this PR an operator who sets `owner_user_id = "@you:your-server"` on the channel alias gets a direct message from the bot: who tried, from which room, a 160-character preview of what they said, and a hint that authorizing means adding their MXID to the channel's `peer_groups` entry. The notice is deliberately sent even when the operator themselves is the turned-away sender (unlike the Telegram version, which skips that echo) because Matrix sends no public reply at all — the DM is the only signal, and an operator testing from an unauthorized account wants to see it.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — ingress behavior is covered by unit tests at the decision layer; end-to-end DM delivery needs a live homeserver and was verified against a real Synapse (see below).
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` (matrix)

### How I tested

```sh
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib --features channel-matrix        # full channel suite incl. new owner_notice_gates module
cargo check -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-matrix --tests     # feature-gated compile gate
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                             # clean (cargo +1.98.0 fmt)
```

- New `owner_notice_gates` tests pin the pure decision layer: preview collapse/truncation with ellipsis, throttle admit/suppress/readmit per (sender, room) pair, notice composition naming sender/room/preview/alias, and `prepare_owner_notice` gating (no owner, blank owner, no logged-in client all yield no notice).
- The full channel suite was run **with `--features channel-matrix`** so the feature-gated matrix module is actually compiled and exercised (an earlier PR of ours missed this — see #12426 — and the lesson is applied here).
- Delivery itself (DM creation, encrypted send) requires a logged-in client; it was verified end-to-end against a live Synapse 1.165 stand during development (turned-away sender → operator DM received, throttle suppressing rapid repeats). A homeserver is not available in CI for this path.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** required CI builds the workspace across the feature matrix, compiling `channel-matrix` and the updated config schema.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** DM delivery has no CI integration test (no homeserver); the decision layer is unit-covered and delivery is a thin `get_dm_room`/`create_dm` + `room.send` wrapper with failure logging.
- **Beyond CI, what did I manually verify?** Live Synase stand: unauthorized sender → owner DM delivered with correct fields; repeat attempt within 5 minutes produced no second DM; the DM room was reused (no duplicate room created). Not verified: owner switching mid-run against a live server (covered by cache-key design, exercised only at unit level).
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A — no user-visible interface state changed.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (No)
- New external network calls? (No — the DM send goes to the already-configured homeserver, like every other channel send)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? (No)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? (No — examples use `example.org` placeholders)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? (No — the notice text is delivered to the configured operator only; message bodies reach the notice preview unchanged from what the sender wrote, and the notice is never fed back into an agent turn)
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? (Yes — default off; without `owner_user_id` the drop stays exactly as silent as before)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? (Yes — one new optional key `[channels.matrix.<alias>] owner_user_id`, default unset)
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? (No)
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: to opt in, add `owner_user_id = "@you:your-server"` under the Matrix alias in `config.toml`; the change is visible to the next turn-away event without a restart when the config is published through the live-config authority.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>` — single commit, no migration.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** remove `owner_user_id` from the alias (or set it to an empty value) — the notice path disables immediately on the next read.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** operator receives owner DMs for ordinary traffic (misconfigured `owner_user_id` pointing at a user who is also an authorized sender — the notice only fires on allowlist drops, so this means the allowlist is wrong, not the notice); WARN records `matrix: owner notice delivery failed` when the homeserver rejects DM creation or send.
